gru.english: Then I disagree that a rabbit's antlers are the reverse of all which is different from a coffee cup. Let's again consider a rabbit's antlers.  They are too the reverse of all which is different from a coffee cup! Why do you say that? Because they are not different from a coffee cup!

gru.wylie: ma grub na, ri bong rva chos can, bum pa dang tha dad ma yin par thal, bum pa dang tha mi dad yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that a rabbit's antlers are not different from a coffee cup. Let's again consider a rabbit's antlers.  They are too something which is not different from a coffee cup! Why do you say that? Because they are not different from a coffee cup!

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, RI BONG RVA CHOS CAN, BUM PA DANG THA MI DAD YIN PAR THAL, MED NGES YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, ri bong rva chos can, bum pa dang tha mi dad yin par thal, med nges yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that a rabbit's antlers are not different from a coffee cup. If you disagree, then let's again consider a rabbit's antlers.  They are too something which is not different from a coffee cup! Why do you say that? Because they don't even exist!

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, BUM PA CHOS CAN, KHYOD KHYOD DANG GCIG MA YIN PA LAS LDOG PAR THAL, KHYOD KHYOD DANG GCIG MA YIN PA LAS LOG PA YIN PA'I PHYIR,

It is too the reverse of everything which is not one with it. Why do you say that? Because it is the opposite of all which is not one with it!

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, BUM PA CHOS CAN, KHYOD KHYOD DANG GCIG MA YIN PA LAS LOG PA YIN PAR THAL, KHYOD KHYOD DANG GCIG YIN PA'I PHYIR,

gru.english: I disagree that a coffee cup is the opposite of all which isn't one with it. If you do disagree, then let's again consider a coffee cup.  It is too the opposite of all which isn't one with it! Why do you say that? Because it's one with itself! 8 Are Rabbit Antlers The Reverse of All Which Is Not One With a Coffee Cup?

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, RI BONG RVA CHOS CAN, BUM PA DANG GCIG MA YIN PA LAS LOG PA MA YIN PAR THAL, BUM PA DANG GCIG MA YIN PA'I PHYIR,

No, they're not the opposite of all which is not one with a coffee cup! Why do you say that? Because they're not one with a coffee cup!

gru.acip: BUM PA'I LDOG PA DANG, BUM PA DANG GCIG GNYIS YIN KHYAB MNYAM YIN TE, GZHI GRUB NA KHYOD KHYOD KYI LDOG PA YIN PAS KHYAB PA DANG, GZHI GRUB NA, KHYOD KHYOD DANG GCIG YIN PAS KHYAB PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: bum pa'i ldog pa dang, bum pa dang gcig gnyis yin khyab mnyam yin te, gzhi grub na khyod khyod kyi ldog pa yin pas khyab pa dang, gzhi grub na, khyod khyod dang gcig yin pas khyab pa'i phyir
gru.english: The two of “the reverse of all which is not a coffee cup” and “that which is one with a coffee cup” amount to the same thing, because if something can be established as existing, then it is always the reverse of all that it is not; and if that thing can be established as existing, then it is also always one with itself.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, GZHI GRUB NA KHYOD KHYOD DANG GCIG YIN PAS KHYAB PAR THAL, GZHI GRUB NA KHYOD KHYOD DANG THA DAD MA YIN PAS KHYAB PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, gzhi grub na khyod khyod dang gcig yin pas khyab par thal, gzhi grub na khyod khyod dang tha dad ma yin pas khyab pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree! Suppose you do disagree.  And yet it is the case that if something can be established as existing, then it is always one with itself. Why do you say that? Because if something can be established as existing, then it can never be separate from itself.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, DNGOS PO DANG MI RTAG PA GNYIS CHOS CAN, NGO BO GCIG YIN PAR THAL, BDAG NYID GCIG YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, dngos po dang mi rtag pa gnyis chos can, ngo bo gcig yin par thal, bdag nyid gcig yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: Then I disagree that the two of working things and changing things are such that to be one is to be the other. If you do disagree, then let's again consider the two of working things and changing things.  They are too such that to be one is to be the other! Why do you say that? Because they're such that to be one is to automatically be the other!

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, DNGOS PO DANG MI RTAG PA GNYIS CHOS CAN, DU MA YIN PAR THAL, PHAN TSUN THA DAD YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, dngos po dang mi rtag pa gnyis chos can, du ma yin par thal, phan tshun tha dad yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that the two of working things and changing things are many. If you do disagree, then let's again consider working things and changing things.  Yes, they are many! Why do you say that? Because they are separate from each other!

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, DNGOS PO DANG MI RTAG PA GNYIS PHAN TSUN THA DAD YIN PAR THAL, DNGOS PO MI RTAG PA DANG THA DAD YIN PA GANG ZHIG MI RTAG PA DNGOS PO DANG THA DAD YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, dngos po dang mi rtag pa gnyis phan tshun tha dad yin par thal, dngos po mi rtag pa dang tha dad yin pa gang zhig mi rtag pa dngos po dang tha dad yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that the two of working things and changing things are separate from each other. Suppose you do disagree.  And yet the two of working things and changing things are indeed separate from each other! Why do you say that? Because, first of all, working things are separate from changing things; and secondly, changing things are separate from working things.

gru.acip: RTAGS RE RE NAS GRUB STE, BDAG MED YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: rtags re re nas grub ste, bdag med yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: Each of the reasons we've given is correct, for neither of these is themselves! 2 If Something Is Such That to Be It Is to Be The Something Else, Then Must It Always Be The Other Thing Substantially?

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, SHES BYA DANG RTAG PA GNYIS CHOS CAN, NGO BO GCIG YIN PAR THAL, BDAG NYID GCIG YIN PA'I PHYIR,

gru.english: Then I disagree that to be things is to be an unchanging thing. If you do disagree, then let's consider the two of things and unchanging things.  It certainly is true that to be the one is to be the other. Why do you say that? Because they're such that to be one is automatically to be the other!

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, SHES BYA DANG RTAG PA GNYIS BDAG NYID GCIG YIN PAR THAL, SHES BYA RTAG PA DANG BDAG NYID GCIG YIN PA GANG ZHIG, RTAG PA SHES BYA DANG BDAG NYID GCIG YIN PA'I PHYIR,

gru.english: I disagree that to be things is to automatically be an unchanging thing. Suppose you do disagree.  And yet it is true that to be things is to be an unchanging thing. Why do you say that? Because, first of all, to be things is to automatically be an unchanging thing.  And secondly, to be an unchanging thing is to automatically be a thing.

gru.acip: RTAGS DANG PO MA GRUB NA, SHES BYA CHOS CAN, RTAG PA DANG BDAG NYID GCIG YIN PAR THAL, RTAG PA YIN PA'I PHYIR,

gru.english: I disagree with the first half of your reason; that is, it's not true that to be things is to automatically be an unchanging thing. If you do disagree, then let's consider things.  It is too the case that to be things is to automatically be an unchanging thing. Why do you say that? Because “things” is an unchanging thing!

gru.acip: RTAGS GNYIS PA MA GRUB NA, RTAG PA CHOS CAN, SHES BYA DANG BDAG NYID GCIG YIN PAR THAL, SHES BYA YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: rtags gnyis pa ma grub na, rtag pa chos can, shes bya dang bdag nyid gcig yin par thal, shes bya yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: Well then, I disagree with the second part of your reason; that is, it's not true that to be an unchanging thing is to automatically be a thing. If you disagree, then let's consider unchanging things.  It is too true that to be one of them is to be, automatically, a thing. Why do you say that? Because they are knowable things!

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, SHES BYA DANG RTAG PA GNYIS CHOS CAN, RDZAS MA YIN PAR THAL, DNGOS PO MA YIN PA'I PHYIR,

gru.english: I disagree that the two of things and unchanging things are not substantial. Suppose you do disagree.  Then let's again consider the two of things and unchanging things.  In fact, they are not substantial! Why do you say that? Because they're not working things!

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, KVA BA DANG BUM PA GNYIS CHOS CAN, DNGOS PO DANG RDZAS GCIG YIN PAR THAL, DNGOS PO'I BYE BRAG YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, kva ba dang bum pa gnyis chos can, dngos po dang rdzas gcig yin par thal, dngos po'i bye brag yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: Then I disagree that the two of a coffee table and a coffee cup are such that to be them is to be a working thing, substantially. If you do disagree, then let's again consider the two of a coffee table and a coffee cup.  They are too such that to be them is to be a working thing, substantially. Why do you say that? Because they are characteristic of the quality “working thing”!

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, KVA BA DANG BUM PA GNYIS CHOS CAN, RDZAS THA DAD YIN PAR THAL, DNGOS PO GANG ZHIG RDZAS PHAN TSUN 'BREL MED DON GZHAN YIN PA'I PHYIR,

They are too separate substances! Why do you say that? Because, first of all, they are working things.  And secondly, they are substantial entities which are completely separate objects, neither of which shares any necessary relationship with the other! 4 If Something Is Such That to Be It Is to Automatically Be A Knowable Thing, Then Does It Necessarily Have to Be An Autonomous Entity?

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, KVA BA DANG BUM PA GNYIS CHOS CAN, SHES BYA DANG BDAG NYID GCIG YIN PAR THAL, SHES BYA YIN PA'I PHYIR,

Because they are objects which any person at all, in a single glance as they turn their mind towards them, would have the thought arise in their mind, all of its own, that “These two are similar.”

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, BA LANG DKAR ZAL DANG BA LANG NAG RGUR GNYIS CHOS CAN, BDAG NYID THA DAD YIN PAR THAL, PHAN TSUN 'BREL MED DON GZHAN YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, ba lang dkar zal dang ba lang nag rgur gnyis chos can, bdag nyid tha dad yin par thal, phan tshun 'brel med don gzhan yin pa'i phyir

It is too the case that they are both negatives in the sense of being an absence, in the form of the simple exclusion of what they exclude, which is the same type of thing. Why do you say that? They are too both an absence in the form of the simple exclusion of the same type of concreteness. Why do you say that? Because they're both absences in the form of the simple exclusion of concreteness.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, BUM PA'I NAM MKHA' DANG KHANG PA'I NAM MKHA' GNYIS CHOS CAN, THOGS REG BKAG TZAM GYI MED DGAG YIN PAR THAL, 'DUS MA BYAS KYI NAM MKHA' YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, bum pa'i nam mkha' dang khang pa'i nam mkha' gnyis chos can, thogs reg bkag tsam gyi med dgag yin par thal, 'dus ma byas kyi nam mkha' yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that these two are both absences in the form of the simple exclusion of concreteness. If you do disagree, then let's again consider the two of the empty space occupied by a coffee cup and the empty space occupied by a coffee shop.  They are too both absences in the form of the simple exclusion of concreteness. Why do you say that? Because they're both examples of unproduced space!

gru.acip: RTZA BAR 'DOD NA, BUM PA'I NAM MKHA' DANG KHANG PA'I NAM MKHA' GNYIS CHOS CAN, SGRUB PAR GYUR PA'I LDOG PA RIGS GCIG MA YIN PAR THAL, SGRUB PA MA YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: rtsa bar 'dod na, bum pa'i nam mkha' dang khang pa'i nam mkha' gnyis chos can, sgrub par gyur pa'i ldog pa rigs gcig ma yin par thal, sgrub pa ma yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: Then I agree to your original statement: these two are of the same kind in being the positive expression of the reverse of what they are, in a certain way, not. If you do agree, then let's again consider the two of the empty space occupied by a coffee cup and the empty space occupied by a coffee shop.  No, they're not the same kind in being the positive expression of the reverse of what they are, in a certain way, not. Why do you say that? Because they're not positive entities!

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, BUM PA'I NAM MKHA' DANG KHANG PA'I NAM MKHA' GNYIS CHOS CAN, SGRUB PA MA YIN PAR THAL, DGAG PA YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, bum pa'i nam mkha' dang khang pa'i nam mkha' gnyis chos can, sgrub pa ma yin par thal, dgag pa yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that these two are not positive entities. If you do disagree, then let's again consider the empty space occupied by a coffee cup and the empty space occupied by a coffee shop.  It is so true that they are not positive entities. Why do you say that? Because they're negative entities!

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, BUM PA'I NAM MKHA' DANG KHANG PA'I NAM MKHA' GNYIS CHOS CAN, DGAG PA YIN PAR THAL, 'DUS MA BYAS KYI NAM MKHA' YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, bum pa'i nam mkha' dang khang pa'i nam mkha' gnyis chos can, dgag pa yin par thal, 'dus ma byas kyi nam mkha' yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that these two are negative entities. If you do disagree, then let's again consider the two of the empty space occupied by a coffee cup and the empty space occupied by a coffee shop.  They are too negative entitites. Why do you say that? Because they're examples of unproduced space! 8 If Two Things Belong To a Single Unit, Then Are They Necessarily a Unit Such That to Be One Is to Be the Other, Substantially?

gru.acip: KHA CIG NA RE, GRUB BDE GCIG YIN NA, GRUB BDE RDZAS GCIG YIN PAS KHYAB ZER NA,
gru.wylie: kha cig na re, grub bde gcig yin na, grub bde rdzas gcig yin pas khyab zer na
gru.english: Suppose someone comes and makes the following claim: If two things belong to a single unit, then they're necessarily a unit such that to be one is to be the other, substantially.

gru.acip: BU RAM GYI KHA DOG DANG BU RAM GYI DRI GNYIS CHOS CAN, GRUB BDE RDZAS GCIG YIN PAR THAL, GRUB BDE GCIG YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: bu ram gyi kha dog dang bu ram gyi dri gnyis chos can, grub bde rdzas gcig yin par thal, grub bde gcig yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: Let's consider the two of the color of brown sugar and the smell of brown sugar.  So, are you saying that they are a unit such that to be one is to be the other, substantially? Why do you say that? Because they belong to a single unit!

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, BU RAM GYI KHA DOG DANG BU RAM GYI DRI GNYIS CHOS CAN, GRUB BDE GCIG YIN PAR THAL, GRUB PA DUS MNYAM GNAS PA DUS MNYAM 'JIG PA DUS MNYAM YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, bu ram gyi kha dog dang bu ram gyi dri gnyis chos can, grub bde gcig yin par thal, grub pa dus mnyam gnas pa dus mnyam 'jig pa dus mnyam yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: Then I disagree that the two of the color of brown sugar and the smell of brown sugar belong to a single unit. If you do disagree, then let's again consider the two of the color of brown sugar and the smell of brown sugar.  They do too belong to a single unit! Why do you say that? Because they come about at the same time; they remain for the same length of time; and they stop at the same time!

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, BU RAM CHOS CAN, KHYOD KYI KHA DOG DANG KHYOD KYI DRI GNYIS GRUB PA DUS MNYAM GNAS PA DUS MNYAM 'JIG PA DUS MNYAM YIN PAR THAL, KHYOD RDUL RDZAS BRGYAD 'DUS KYI GONG BU YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, bu ram chos can, khyod kyi kha dog dang khyod kyi dri gnyis grub pa dus mnyam gnas pa dus mnyam 'jig pa dus mnyam yin par thal, khyod rdul rdzas brgyad 'dus kyi gong bu yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that the color of brown sugar and smell of brown sugar come about at the same time; remain for the same length of time; and stop at the same time. If you do disagree, then let's consider brown sugar.  Its color and its smell do too come about at the same time, remain for the same length of time, and stop at the same time. Why do you say that? Because the brown sugar is a conglomerate of molecules which are themselves composed of the eight different substances!

gru.acip: RTZA BAR 'DOD NA, BU RAM GYI KHA DOG DANG BU RAM GYI DRI GNYIS CHOS CAN, GRUB BDE RDZAS GCIG MA YIN PAR THAL, RDZAS GCIG MA YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: rtsa bar 'dod na, bu ram gyi kha dog dang bu ram gyi dri gnyis chos can, grub bde rdzas gcig ma yin par thal, rdzas gcig ma yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: Then I agree to your original statement: the two of the color of brown sugar and the smell of brown sugar are a unit such that to be one is to be the other, substantially. If you do agree, then let's consider the two of the color of brown sugar and the smell of brown sugar.  No, they're not a unit such that to be one is to be the other, substantially. Why do you say that? Because they're not such that to be one is to be the other, substantially!

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, BU RAM GYI KHA DOG DANG BU RAM GYI DRI GNYIS CHOS CAN, RDZAS GCIG MA YIN PAR THAL, RDZAS THA DAD YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, bu ram gyi kha dog dang bu ram gyi dri gnyis chos can, rdzas gcig ma yin par thal, rdzas tha dad yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that the two of the color of brown sugar and the smell of brown sugar are not such that to be one is to be the other, substantially! If you do disagree, then let's again consider the color and smell of brown sugar.  It is indeed true that they are not such that to be one is to be the other, substantially. Why do you say that? Because they are such that to be one is not to be the other, substantially!

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, BU RAM CHOS CAN, KHYOD KYI KHA DOG DANG KHYOD KYI DRI GNYIS RDZAS THA DAD YIN PAR THAL, KHYOD RDUL RDZAS BRGYAD 'DUS KYI GONG BU YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, bu ram chos can, khyod kyi kha dog dang khyod kyi dri gnyis rdzas tha dad yin par thal, khyod rdul rdzas brgyad 'dus kyi gong bu yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that the two of the color of brown sugar and the smell of brown sugar are such that to be one is not to be the other, substantially! If you do disagree, then let's consider brown sugar.  Its color and its smell are too such that to be one is not to be the other, substantially. Why do you say that? Because the brown sugar is a conglomerate of molecules which are themselves composed of the eight different substances. 9 If Things Are of The Same Type of Substance, Then Do They Necessarily Have to Be Such That to Be One Is to Be the Other, Substantially?

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, NYER LEN NAS LDOG GCIG LAS SKYES PA'I NAS 'BRU CHE CHUNG GNYIS PO CHOS CAN, RDZAS RIGS GCIG YIN PAR THAL, THA DAD GANG ZHIG, RANG GI NYER LEN GCIG LAS SKYES PA YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, nyer len nas ldog gcig las skyes pa'i nas 'bru che chung gnyis po chos can, rdzas rigs gcig yin par thal, tha dad gang zhig, rang gi nyer len gcig las skyes pa yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: Then I disagree that the two of a larger grain and a smaller grain of barley that grow from a material cause which is the same, in the sense of being the reverse of a specific thing that it is not, are of the same type of substance. If you do disagree, then let's again consider the two of a larger grain and a smaller grain of barley that grow from a material cause which is the same, in the sense of being the reverse of a specific thing that it is not.  They are too of the same type of substance. Why do you say that? Because, first of all, they are separate things.  And secondly, they've grown from the same single material cause!

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, NYER LEN NAS LDOG GCIG LAS SKYES PA'I NAS 'BRU CHE CHUNG GNYIS PO DE CHOS CAN, BDAG NYID GCIG MA YIN PAR THAL, NGO BO THA DAD YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, nyer len nas ldog gcig las skyes pa'i nas 'bru che chung gnyis po de chos can, bdag nyid gcig ma yin par thal, ngo bo tha dad yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that it is not the case that to be one of these two is to be, automatically, the other. If you do disagree, then let's again consider the two of a larger grain and a smaller grain of barley that grow from a material cause which is the same, in the sense of being the reverse of a specific thing that it is not.  It is true that it is not the case that to be one of these two is to be, automatically, the other. Why do you say that? Because to be one is not to be, essentially, the other.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, NYER LEN NAS LDOG GCIG LAS SKYES PA'I NAS 'BRU CHE CHUNG GNYIS PO DE CHOS CAN, NGO BO THA DAD YIN PAR THAL, PHAN TSUN 'BREL MED DON GZHAN YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, nyer len nas ldog gcig las skyes pa'i nas 'bru che chung gnyis po de chos can, ngo bo tha dad yin par thal, phan tshun 'brel med don gzhan yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that to be one of these two is not to be, essentially, the other. If you do disagree, then let's again consider the two of a larger grain and a smaller grain of barley that grow from a material cause which is the same, in the sense of being the reverse of a specific thing that it is not.  It is so the case that to be one of these two is not to be, essentially, the other. Why do you say that? Because they are separate objects which share no necessary relation to one other! B. Our own school's position on the topic of Oneness & Separateness 10 Our Own Position on Oneness & Separateness

gru.acip: LDOG PA RIGS GCIG PA LA DBYE NA GNYIS YOD DE, SGRUB PAR GYUR PA'I LDOG PA RIGS GCIG PA DANG, DGAG PAR GYUR PA'I LDOG PA RIGS GCIG PA GNYIS YOD PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ldog pa rigs gcig pa la dbye na gnyis yod de, sgrub par gyur pa'i ldog pa rigs gcig pa dang, dgag par gyur pa'i ldog pa rigs gcig pa gnyis yod pa'i phyir
gru.english: There are two further divisions to things of the same kind where they are the same in being the reverse of what they are, in a certain way, not.  The first is a case where this reverse is a positive entity; and the second is where this reverse is a negative entity.

gru.acip: SGRUB PAR GYUR PA'I LDOG PA RIGS GCIG GI MTSAN NYID YOD DE, GANG ZAG GANG DANG GANG GIS YID GTAD PAS MTHONG TZAM NYID NAS 'DI DANG 'DI 'DRA'O SNYAM PA'I BLO NGANG GIS SKYED NUS PA'I CHOS DE YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: sgrub par gyur pa'i ldog pa rigs gcig gi mtshan nyid yod de, gang zag gang dang gang gis yid gtad pas mthong tsam nyid nas 'di dang 'di 'dra'o snyam pa'i blo ngang gis skyed nus pa'i chos de yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: There is a specific definition for things that are positive entities which are the same in being the reverse of what they are, in a certain way, not.  And that is: “Objects which any person at all, in a single glance as they turn their mind towards them, would have the thought arise in their mind, all of its own, that 'These two are similar'.”

gru.acip: SGRUB PAR GYUR PA'I LDOG PA RIGS GCIG PA LA DBYE NA GSUM YOD DE, SHES PAR GYUR PA'I LDOG PA RIGS GCIG PA DANG, GZUGS SU GYUR PA'I LDOG PA RIGS GCIG PA DANG, LDAN MIN 'DU BYED DU GYUR PA'I LDOG PA RIGS GCIG PA DANG GSUM YOD PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: sgrub par gyur pa'i ldog pa rigs gcig pa la dbye na gsum yod de, shes par gyur pa'i ldog pa rigs gcig pa dang, gzugs su gyur pa'i ldog pa rigs gcig pa dang, ldan min 'du byed du gyur pa'i ldog pa rigs gcig pa dang gsum yod pa'i phyir
gru.english: There are three different divisions to these things that are positive entities which are the same in being the reverse of what they are, in a certain way, not.  First are those things of this type which are awareness; second are things of this type which are form; and third are those things of this type which are active entities that are neither awareness nor form.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, GSER BUM ZANGS BUM GNYIS CHOS CAN, RIGS THA DAD YIN PAR THAL, RDZAS RIGS THA DAD YIN PA'I PHYIR ZER NA
gru.wylie: ma grub na, gser bum zangs bum gnyis chos can, rigs tha dad yin par thal, rdzas rigs tha dad yin pa'i phyir zer na
gru.english: I disagree that they are of separate kinds. Suppose you do disagree.  Consider again the two of a gold coffee cup and a copper coffee cup. They are too of separate kinds, Because they are a case where their substances are of separate kinds.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, GSER BUM ZANGS BUM GNYIS CHOS CAN, RDZAS RIGS THA DAD YIN PAR THAL, RANG GI DNGOS KYI NYER LEN SO SO LAS SKYES PA'I THA DAD PA'I 'DU BYAS YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, gser bum zangs bum gnyis chos can, rdzas rigs tha dad yin par thal, rang gi dngos kyi nyer len so so las skyes pa'i tha dad pa'i 'du byas yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that these things themselves are of separate kinds. If you do disagree that these things themselves are of separate kinds, then let's again consider the two of a gold coffee cup and a copper coffee cup. They are too of separate kinds, Because they are produced things that are separate from each other which have each come from their own individual direct material cause.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, GSER BUM ZANGS BUM GNYIS CHOS CAN, RANG GI DNGOS KYI NYER LEN SO SO LAS SKYES PA'I THA DAD PA'I 'DU BYAS YIN PAR THAL, RANG GI DNGOS KYI NYER LEN SO SO LAS SKYES PA GANG ZHIG ,THA DAD PA'I 'DU BYAS YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, gser bum zangs bum gnyis chos can, rang gi dngos kyi nyer len so so las skyes pa'i tha dad pa'i 'du byas yin par thal, rang gi dngos kyi nyer len so so las skyes pa gang zhig ,tha dad pa'i 'du byas yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that the two cups are produced things that are separate from each other which have each come from their own individual direct material cause. If you do disagree, then let's again consider the two of the gold coffee cup and the copper coffee cup. They are so produced things that are separate from each other which have each come from their own individual direct material cause, Because (1) they have each come from their own individual direct material cause; and (2) they are produced things which are separate from each other.

gru.acip: RTAGS DANG PO MA GRUB NA, GSER BUM ZANGS BUM GNYIS CHOS CAN, RANG GI DNGOS KYI NYER LEN SO SO LAS SKYES PA YIN PAR THAL, GSER BUM DE GSER LAS SKYES PA YIN KYANG, ZANGS LAS SKYES PA MA YIN, ZANGS BUM DE ZANGS LAS SKYES PA YIN KYANG, GSER LAS SKYES PA MA YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: rtags dang po ma grub na, gser bum zangs bum gnyis chos can, rang gi dngos kyi nyer len so so las skyes pa yin par thal, gser bum de gser las skyes pa yin kyang, zangs las skyes pa ma yin, zangs bum de zangs las skyes pa yin kyang, gser las skyes pa ma yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree with the first half of your reason: the two cups have not each come from their own individual direct material cause. Suppose that you do disagree with the first half of our reason.  Consider then again the gold coffee cup and the copper coffee cup.  They have too each come from their own individual direct material cause, because first of all the gold coffee cup—although it has come from gold—has not come from copper; whereas the copper coffee cup—although it has come from copper—has not come from gold. 12 Do Things Have to Be Of the Same Substance, If They Are Not Entities Of Individual Substances?

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, SHES BYA DANG RTAG PA GNYIS CHOS CAN, RDZAS SO SO BA MA YIN PA'I CHOS YIN PAR THAL, RDZAS SO SO BA MA YIN PA GANG ZHIG ,CHOS YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, shes bya dang rtag pa gnyis chos can, rdzas so so ba ma yin pa'i chos yin par thal, rdzas so so ba ma yin pa gang zhig ,chos yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: Well I disagree that the two of knowable things and the quality of never changing are not entities of individual substances. Suppose you do disagree.  Let's consider, again, the two of knowable things and the quality of never changing.  They are so not entities of individual substances, Because (1) they are not of individual substances, and (2) they are entities.

gru.acip: RTAGS DANG PO MA GRUB NA, SHES BYA DANG RTAG PA GNYIS CHOS CAN, RDZAS SO SO BA MA YIN PAR THAL, RDZAS THA DAD MA YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: rtags dang po ma grub na, shes bya dang rtag pa gnyis chos can, rdzas so so ba ma yin par thal, rdzas tha dad ma yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree with the first half of your reason; that is, I disagree that the two of knowable things and the quality of never changing are not of individual substances. If you do disagree with the first half of our reason, then let's again consider the two of knowable things, and the quality of never changing. They are so not of individual substances, because they are not of separate substances.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, SHES BYA DANG RTAG PA GNYIS CHOS CAN, RDZAS THA DAD MA YIN PAR THAL, RDZAS MA YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, shes bya dang rtag pa gnyis chos can, rdzas tha dad ma yin par thal, rdzas ma yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that the two of knowable things and the quality of never changing are not of separate substances. Suppose you do disagree.  Consider then yet again the two of knowable things and the quality of never changing. They are so not of separate substances, Because they are not substances at all!

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, SHES BYA DANG RTAG PA GNYIS CHOS CAN, RDZAS MA YIN PAR THAL, RTAG PA YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, shes bya dang rtag pa gnyis chos can, rdzas ma yin par thal, rtag pa yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that the two of knowable things and the quality of never changing are not substances at all. Suppose you do disagree.  Consider one last time the two of knowable things and the quality of never changing. No, they're not at all substances, Because they are unchanging entities! 13 Are Existence and Non-existence Separate Expressions?

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, YOD PA DANG MED PA GNYIS CHOS CAN, RANG LDOG SO SO BA'I CHOS YIN PAR THAL, RANG LDOG SO SO BA YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, yod pa dang med pa gnyis chos can, rang ldog so so ba'i chos yin par thal, rang ldog so so ba yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that they are entities with separate expressions. Suppose you do disagree.  Consider then these two, of existence and non-existence. They are too entities with separate expressions, Because they are entities with individual expressions.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, YOD PA DANG MED PA GNYIS CHOS CAN, RANG LDOG SO SO BA YIN PAR THAL, RANG LDOG GCIG MA YIN PA'I PHYIR ZER NA
gru.wylie: ma grub na, yod pa dang med pa gnyis chos can, rang ldog so so ba yin par thal, rang ldog gcig ma yin pa'i phyir zer na
gru.english: I disagree that they are entities with individual expressions. Suppose you do disagree.  Let's consider again then these two, of existence and non-existence. They are too entities with individual expressions, Because they are not entities with the same expression.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, YOD PA DANG MED PA GNYIS CHOS CAN, RANG LDOG GCIG MA YIN PAR THAL, KHYOD KYI RANG LDOG MED PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, yod pa dang med pa gnyis chos can, rang ldog gcig ma yin par thal, khyod kyi rang ldog med pa'i phyir
gru.english: And suppose you disagree that they are not entities with the same expression. Let's consider the two of existence and non-existence. They are so not entities with the same expression, Because they don't even have their own expressions.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, YOD PA DANG MED PA GNYIS CHOS CAN, KHYOD KYI RANG LDOG MED PAR THAL, KHYOD MED PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, yod pa dang med pa gnyis chos can, khyod kyi rang ldog med par thal, khyod med pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that they don't even have their own expressions. Then let's again consider the two of existence and non-existence. No, they don't have their own expressions, Because they don't even exist! 14 If Things Are Not Of the Same Substance, Do They Have to Be Of Separate Substances?

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, DNGOS PO KHO NA DANG DNGOS PO GNYIS CHOS CAN, RDZAS GCIG MA YIN PAR THAL, RDZAS MA YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, dngos po kho na dang dngos po gnyis chos can, rdzas gcig ma yin par thal, rdzas ma yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: And I disagree that only a working thing and a working thing are not of the same substance. Suppose you do disagree.  Then let's again consider the two of only a working thing and a working thing. No, they're not of the same substance, Because they are not of any substance.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, DNGOS PO KHO NA DANG DNGOS PO GNYIS CHOS CAN, RDZAS MA YIN PAR THAL, DNGOS PO MA YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, dngos po kho na dang dngos po gnyis chos can, rdzas ma yin par thal, dngos po ma yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that the two of only a working thing and a working thing are not of any substance. If you do disagree, then let's again consider the two of only a working thing and a working thing. They are so not of any substance, Because they are not working things.

gru.acip: KHA CIG NA RE, GZHI GRUB NA, RGYU 'BRAS GANG RUNG YIN PAS KHYAB ZER NA,
gru.wylie: kha cig na re, gzhi grub na, rgyu 'bras gang rung yin pas khyab zer na
gru.english: Suppose someone comes and makes the following claim: If something can be established as existing, then it is necessarily either a cause, or a result, or both.

gru.acip: SHES BYA CHOS CAN, RGYU 'BRAS GANG RUNG YIN PAR THAL, GZHI GRUB PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: shes bya chos can, rgyu 'bras gang rung yin par thal, gzhi grub pa'i phyir
gru.english: Well then, let's consider all knowable things. Are you saying it's either a cause, or a result, or both a cause and a result? Why do you say that? Because it can be established as existing.

gru.acip: RTAGS DANG PO MA GRUB NA, SHES BYA CHOS CAN, RGYU MA YIN PAR THAL, KHYOD KYI 'BRAS BU MED PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: rtags dang po ma grub na, shes bya chos can, rgyu ma yin par thal, khyod kyi 'bras bu med pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree to the first part of that last reason. Suppose you do disagree to the first part of that last reason. Let's again consider all knowable things. No, it's not a cause, Because it has no result.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, SHES BYA CHOS CAN, KHYOD KYI 'BRAS BU MED PAR THAL, KHYOD RTAG PA YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, shes bya chos can, khyod kyi 'bras bu med par thal, khyod rtag pa yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that it has no result. If you do disagree, then let's again consider all knowable things. No, it doesn't have a result, Because it is unchanging.

gru.acip: RTAGS GNYIS PA MA GRUB NA, SHES BYA CHOS CAN, 'BRAS BU MA YIN PAR THAL, KHYOD KYI RGYU MED PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: rtags gnyis pa ma grub na, shes bya chos can, 'bras bu ma yin par thal, khyod kyi rgyu med pa'i phyir
gru.english: Well then I disagree with the second part of the reason you gave: I disagree that all knowable things cannot be a result. Suppose you do disagree with that second part. Let's again consider all knowable things. No, it's not a result, Because it has no cause.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, SHES BYA CHOS CAN, KHYOD KYI RGYU MED PAR THAL, KHYOD KYI SKYED BYED MED PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, shes bya chos can, khyod kyi rgyu med par thal, khyod kyi skyed byed med pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that all knowable things has no cause. Suppose you do disagree. Let's again consider all knowable things. No, it doesn't have a cause, Because there is nothing which makes it happen.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, SHES BYA CHOS CAN, KHYOD KYI SKYED BYED MED PAR THAL, KHYOD MA SKYES PA YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, shes bya chos can, khyod kyi skyed byed med par thal, khyod ma skyes pa yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that there is nothing which makes all knowable things happen. Suppose you do disagree. Let's consider, again, all knowable things. It is so true that there is nothing which makes it happen, Because it is not something which ever started.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, SHES BYA CHOS CAN, KHYOD MA SKYES PA YIN PAR THAL, KHYOD RTAG PA YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, shes bya chos can, khyod ma skyes pa yin par thal, khyod rtag pa yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that all knowable things is not something which ever started. If you do disagree, then let's again consider all knowable things. It is so true that it is not something which ever started, Because it is unchanging. 2 Can Something Also Be a Result, If It's Already a Cause?

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, GZUGS CHOS CAN, RGYU YIN PAR THAL, GZUGS KYI PHYI LOGS SU BYUNG BA'I RGYU YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, gzugs chos can, rgyu yin par thal, gzugs kyi phyi logs su byung ba'i rgyu yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: Then I disagree that form is a cause. If you do disagree, then let's consider form again. It is so a cause, Because it is a cause of what comes out from form just after the form.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, GZUGS CHOS CAN, KHYOD KHYOD KYI PHYI LOGS SU BYUNG BA'I RGYU YIN PAR THAL, KHYOD DNGOS PO YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, gzugs chos can, khyod khyod kyi phyi logs su byung ba'i rgyu yin par thal, khyod dngos po yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that form is a cause of what comes out from form just after the form. Suppose you do disagree. Let's again consider the form. It is too the cause of what comes out of it just after it, Because it is a working entity.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, GZUGS CHOS CAN, KHYOD KYI RGYU YOD PAR THAL, KHYOD SKYES PA YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, gzugs chos can, khyod kyi rgyu yod par thal, khyod skyes pa yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that form has its cause. Suppose you do disagree. Let's again consider form. It does too have its cause, Because it is something that started!

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, GZUGS CHOS CAN, KHYOD SKYES PA YIN PAR THAL, KHYOD DNGOS PO YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, gzugs chos can, khyod skyes pa yin par thal, khyod dngos po yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that form is something that started. Then again consider form. It is so something which has started, Because it is a working thing! 3 Does Everything Which Is a Cause Have to Be a Material Cause?

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, GLOG SKAD CIG THA MA CHOS CAN, RGYU YIN PAR THAL, KHYOD KYI 'BRAS BU YOD PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, glog skad cig tha ma chos can, rgyu yin par thal, khyod kyi 'bras bu yod pa'i phyir
gru.english: Then I disagree that the last moment of a bolt of lightning is a cause. If you do disagree, then let's again consider the last moment of a bolt of lightning. It is too a cause! Why do you say that? Because it has a result!

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, GLOG SKAD CIG THA MA CHOS CAN, KHYOD KYI 'BRAS BU YOD PAR THAL, KHYOD DNGOS PO YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, glog skad cig tha ma chos can, khyod kyi 'bras bu yod par thal, khyod dngos po yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that the last moment of a bolt of lightning has a result. If you do disagree, then let's again consider the last moment of a bolt of lightning. It does too have a result! Because it's a working thing!

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, GLOG CHOS CAN, KHYOD SKAD CIG THA MA DNGOS PO YIN PAR THAL, KHYOD GZUGS YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, glog chos can, khyod skad cig tha ma dngos po yin par thal, khyod gzugs yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that the last moment of a bolt of lightning is a working thing. If you do disagree, then let's consider lightning.  The last moment of it is too a working thing! Why do you say that? Because it's physical!

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, GLOG SKAD CIG THA MA CHOS CAN, RANG GI RDZAS RGYUN PHYI MA GTZO BOR SKYED BYED MA YIN PAR THAL, KHYOD KYI RDZAS RGYUN PHYI MA MED PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, glog skad cig tha ma chos can, rang gi rdzas rgyun phyi ma gtso bor skyed byed ma yin par thal, khyod kyi rdzas rgyun phyi ma med pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that the last moment of a bolt of lightning isn't primarily a thing which creates its subsequent, substantial stream. If you do disagree, then let's again consider the last moment of a bolt of lightning. No, it's not primarily a thing which creates its subsequent, substantial stream, Because it has no subsequent, substantial stream.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, GLOG SKAD CIG THA MA CHOS CAN, KHYOD KYI RDZAS RGYUN PHYI MA MED PAR THAL, KHYOD RDZAS RGYUN 'CHAD KA MA YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, glog skad cig tha ma chos can, khyod kyi rdzas rgyun phyi ma med par thal, khyod rdzas rgyun 'chad ka ma yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that the last moment of a bolt of lightning has no subsequent, substantial stream. If you do disagree, then let's consider once more the last moment of a bolt of lightning. No, it doesn't have any subsequent, substantial stream. Because it represents the very edge at which its stream cuts off.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, GLOG CHOS CAN, KHYOD SKAD CIG THA MA RDZAS RGYUN 'CHAD KA MA YIN PAR THAL, KHYOD SKAD CIG TZAM GYIS RGYUN 'CHAD NGES KYI DNGOS PO YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, glog chos can, khyod skad cig tha ma rdzas rgyun 'chad ka ma yin par thal, khyod skad cig tsam gyis rgyun 'chad nges kyi dngos po yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that the last moment of a bolt of lightning represents the very edge at which its stream cuts off. If you do disagree, then let's once more consider the bolt of lightning. It does too represent the very edge at which its stream cuts off, Because it is a working thing whose flow is certain to discontinue within nothing more than a single second. 4 Can Something Be the Cause Of a Coffee Cup, Without Being Its Material Cause?

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, BUM PA'I RGYUR GYUR PA'I SKYES BU BUM PA'I RGYU YIN PAR THAL, BUM PA'I RGYUR GYUR PA'I SKYES BU YOD PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, bum pa'i rgyur gyur pa'i skyes bu bum pa'i rgyu yin par thal, bum pa'i rgyur gyur pa'i skyes bu yod pa'i phyir
gru.english: Then I disagree that the individual who acts as a cause of the coffee cup is a cause for the coffee cup. But the individual who acts as a cause for the coffee cup is too a cause of the coffee cup! Because there exists an individual who acts as a cause for a coffee cup!

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, BUM PA CHOS CAN, KHYOD KYI RGYUR GYUR PA'I SKYES BU YOD PAR THAL, KHYOD SKYES BU'I RTZOL BA LAS BYUNG BA'I CHOS YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, bum pa chos can, khyod kyi rgyur gyur pa'i skyes bu yod par thal, khyod skyes bu'i rtsol ba las byung ba'i chos yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that there exists an individual who acts as a cause for a coffee cup. If you do disagree, then let's consider a coffee cup. It is so true, that there exists an individual who acts as a cause for it! Because it is something which comes about through the conscious effort of an individual person.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, BUM PA'I RGYUR GYUR PA'I SKYES BU CHOS CAN, BUM PA RANG GI RDZAS RGYUN DU RDZAS SU GTZO BOR SKYED BYED MA YIN PAR THAL, BUM PA KHYOD KYI RDZAS RGYUN PHYI MA MA YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, bum pa'i rgyur gyur pa'i skyes bu chos can, bum pa rang gi rdzas rgyun du rdzas su gtso bor skyed byed ma yin par thal, bum pa khyod kyi rdzas rgyun phyi ma ma yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that the individual who acts as a cause for a coffee cup is not that thing which—acting primarily as a material entity—creates the material continuation of the original cup. If you do disagree, then consider once again this individual who acts as a cause for a coffee cup. No, they're not that thing which—acting primarily as a material entity—creates the material continuation of the coffee cup, Because the coffee cup is not their later, material continuation.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, BUM PA'I RGYUR GYUR PA'I SKYES BU CHOS CAN, BUM PA KHYOD KYI RDZAS RGYUN PHYI MA MA YIN PAR THAL, BUM PA KHYOD KYI RGYUN PHYI MA MA YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, bum pa'i rgyur gyur pa'i skyes bu chos can, bum pa khyod kyi rdzas rgyun phyi ma ma yin par thal, bum pa khyod kyi rgyun phyi ma ma yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that the coffee cup is not this individual's later, material continuation. If you do disagree, then let's consider this individual who acts as a cause for a coffee cup. No, the coffee cup is not their later, material continuation. Because the coffee cup is not their later continuation at all!

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, BUM PA'I RGYUR GYUR PA'I SKYES BU CHOS CAN, BUM PA KHYOD KYI RGYUN PHYI MA MA YIN PAR THAL, KHYOD GANG ZAG YIN PA GANG ZHIG BUM PA DE BEM PO YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, bum pa'i rgyur gyur pa'i skyes bu chos can, bum pa khyod kyi rgyun phyi ma ma yin par thal, khyod gang zag yin pa gang zhig bum pa de bem po yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that the coffee cup is not this individual's later continuation at all. If you do disagree, then let's once more consider the individual who acts as a cause for the coffee cup. No, the cup is not their later continuation, Because this individual is a person, whereas the coffee cup is matter. 5 If Something Exists Just Prior to Something, Is It Necessarily That Thing's Cause?

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, BUM PA'I DGAG GZHI CHOS CAN, DNGOS PO'I RGYUR GYUR BA'I BUM PA MED PAR THAL, BUM PA MED PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, bum pa'i dgag gzhi chos can, dngos po'i rgyur gyur ba'i bum pa med par thal, bum pa med pa'i phyir
gru.english: Well then, I disagree that there is no coffee cup which could act as the cause of working things. Then let's consider a spot where there is no coffee cup. No, there isn't any coffee cup which acts as a cause for working things, Because there's no coffee cup!

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, BUM PA'I DGAG GZHI CHOS CAN, BUM PA MED PAR THAL, BUM PA'I DGAG GZHI YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, bum pa'i dgag gzhi chos can, bum pa med par thal, bum pa'i dgag gzhi yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that there's no coffee cup. If you do disagree, then let's consider a spot where there's no coffee cup. No, there's not any coffee cup, Because it's a spot where there is no coffee cup.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, TZANDAN GYI ME CHOS CAN, DU BA KHYOD KYI 'BRAS BU MA YIN PAR THAL, DU BA KHYOD DANG RTEN BYUNG 'BREL MA YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, tsandan gyi me chos can, du ba khyod kyi 'bras bu ma yin par thal, du ba khyod dang rten byung 'brel ma yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that smoke could never be the result of a fire made from sandalwood tree logs. Suppose you do disagree.  Let's consider then a fire made from sandalwood tree logs. And yet it is in fact the case that smoke could never be its result, Because smoke could never share an interdependent relationship with this fire.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, TZANDAN GYI ME CHOS CAN, DU BA KHYOD DANG RTEN BYUNG 'BREL MA YIN PAR THAL, KHYOD MED NA DU BA MED MI DGOS PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, tsandan gyi me chos can, du ba khyod dang rten byung 'brel ma yin par thal, khyod med na du ba med mi dgos pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that smoke could never share an interdependent relationship with this fire. Suppose you do disagree.  Consider then, once again, a fire made from sandalwood tree logs. No, it's not the case that smoke could share an interdependent relationship with it, Because it's not the case that—if this fire were absent—there could be no smoke.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, TZANDAN MED PA'I SA PHYOGS CHOS CAN, DU BA MED PAR THAL, TZANDAN GYI ME MED PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, tsandan med pa'i sa phyogs chos can, du ba med par thal, tsandan gyi me med pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that it's not the case that—if this fire were absent—there could be no smoke. If you do disagree, then let's consider an area where there are never any sandalwood logs around. There must be, then, no smoke! Why do you say that? Because there can be no fire made from sandalwood tree logs there.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, TZANDAN MED PA'I SA PHYOGS CHOS CAN, TZANDAN GYI ME MED PAR THAL, TZANDAN MED PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, tsandan med pa'i sa phyogs chos can, tsandan gyi me med par thal, tsandan med pa'i phyir
gru.english: Then I disagree that there can be no fire made from sandalwood logs in that particular location. If you do disagree, then let's once again consider an area where there are never any sandalwood logs around. No, there isn't any fire made from sandalwood logs there, Because there are no sandalwood logs there!

gru.acip: MA GRUB PA NA, TZANDAN MED PA'I SA PHYOGS CHOS CAN, TZANDAN MED PAR THAL, TZANDAN GYI DGAG GZHI YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub pa na, tsandan med pa'i sa phyogs chos can, tsandan med par thal, tsandan gyi dgag gzhi yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: And suppose that you disagree that there are no sandalwood logs there. Let's once more consider an area where there are never any sandalwood logs around. No, there aren't any sandalwood logs there, Because it's a spot where there are no sandalwood logs!

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, TZANDAN MED PA'I SA PHYOGS DER, SHUG PA'I ME'I DU BA YOD PAR THAL, TZANDAN MED PA'I SA PHYOGS DER, SHUG PA'I ME YOD PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, tsandan med pa'i sa phyogs der, shug pa'i me'i du ba yod par thal, tsandan med pa'i sa phyogs der, shug pa'i me yod pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that there is smoke made from juniper logs. Suppose you do disagree.  And yet there is smoke made from juniper logs! Because there in an area where there are never any sandalwood logs around, there is smoke made from juniper logs! 7 If Something Is Certain To Become a Coffee Cup, Does It Have to Be a Cause Of Coffee Cups?

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, RDZA BUM GYI NYER LEN DU GYUR PA'I 'JIM PA CHOS CAN, BUM PAR 'GYUR NGES YIN PAR THAL, RDZA BUM DU 'GYUR NGES YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, rdza bum gyi nyer len du gyur pa'i 'jim pa chos can, bum par 'gyur nges yin par thal, rdza bum du 'gyur nges yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: Then I disagree with that last reason: the clay that serves as a material cause of a ceramic coffee cup is not certain to become a coffee cup. Let's say you do disagree.  Consider once again the clay that serves as a material cause of a ceramic coffee cup. It is too certain to become a coffee cup, Because it is certain to become a ceramic coffee cup.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, RDZA BUM CHOS CAN, KHYOD KYI NYER LEN DU GYUR PA'I 'JIM PA KHYOD DU 'GYUR NGES YIN PAR THAL, KHYOD KYI NYER LEN DU GYUR PA'I 'JIM PA YOD PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, rdza bum chos can, khyod kyi nyer len du gyur pa'i 'jim pa khyod du 'gyur nges yin par thal, khyod kyi nyer len du gyur pa'i 'jim pa yod pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that the clay which serves as a material cause of a ceramic coffee cup is certain to become a ceramic coffee cup. Suppose you do disagree. Let's consider then a ceramic coffee cup. The clay which serves as a material cause of the ceramic coffee cup is so certain to become a ceramic coffee cup, Because there is indeed clay which serves as a material cause of the ceramic coffee cup.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, RDZA BUM CHOS CAN, KHYOD KYI NYER LEN DU GYUR PA'I 'JIM PA YOD PAR THAL, KHYOD RDZA BUM YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, rdza bum chos can, khyod kyi nyer len du gyur pa'i 'jim pa yod par thal, khyod rdza bum yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: Then I disagree that it is indeed clay which serves as a material cause of the ceramic coffee cup. If you do disagree, then let's again consider the ceramic coffee cup. There is so clay which serves as a material cause of the cup, Because the cup is a ceramic one!

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, RDZA BUM GYI NYER LEN DU GYUR BA'I 'JIM PA CHOS CAN, BUM PA KHYOD KYI 'BRAS BU MA YIN PAR THAL, KHYOD MED NA BUM PA MED PAS MA KHYAB PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, rdza bum gyi nyer len du gyur ba'i 'jim pa chos can, bum pa khyod kyi 'bras bu ma yin par thal, khyod med na bum pa med pas ma khyab pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that coffee cups are not the result of the clay that serves as a material cause of a coffee cup. If you do disagree, then let's once more consider the clay that serves as a material cause of a ceramic coffee cup. No, it's not the case the coffee cups are its result, Because it's not necessarily the case that if this clay is absent, then coffee cups are absent.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, RDZA BUM MED PA'I SA PHYOGS CHOS CAN, BUM PA MED PAR THAL, RDZA BUM GYI NYER LEN DU GYUR PA'I 'JIM PA MED PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, rdza bum med pa'i sa phyogs chos can, bum pa med par thal, rdza bum gyi nyer len du gyur pa'i 'jim pa med pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that it's not necessarily the case that if this clay is absent, then coffee cups are absent. If you do disagree, then let's consider a certain area where there are no ceramic coffee cups. Are you saying that there are no coffee cups? Why do you say that? Because in this area there is none of the clay that serves as a material cause of a ceramic coffee cup.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, RDZA BUM MED PA'I SA PHYOGS CHOS CAN, RDZA BUM GYI NYER LEN DU GYUR PA'I 'JIM PA MED PAR THAL, RDZA BUM GYI DGAG GZHI YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, rdza bum med pa'i sa phyogs chos can, rdza bum gyi nyer len du gyur pa'i 'jim pa med par thal, rdza bum gyi dgag gzhi yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: Then I disagree that, in this area, there is none of the clay that serves as a material cause of a ceramic coffee cup. If you do disagree, the let's again consider the area where there is no ceramic coffee cup. It is so the case that in this area there is none of the clay that serves as a material cause of a ceramic coffee cup, Because this is an area where there are no ceramic coffee cups.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, RDZA BUM MED PA'I SA PHYOGS CHOS CAN, GSER BUM YOD PAR THAL, GSER BUM GYI DGAG GZHI MA YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, rdza bum med pa'i sa phyogs chos can, gser bum yod par thal, gser bum gyi dgag gzhi ma yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that there are golden coffee cups. If you do disagree, then let's again consider an area where there are no ceramic coffee cups. There are too golden coffee cups, Because this is not an area where there can be no golden coffee cups. 8 Does a Material Cause Of Consciousness Have to Be Consciousness?

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, RNAM SHES KYI SA BON CHOS CAN, RNAM SHES KYI NYER LEN YIN PAR THAL, RNAM SHES RANG GI RDZAS RGYUN DU RDZAS SU GTZO BOR SKYED BYED YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, rnam shes kyi sa bon chos can, rnam shes kyi nyer len yin par thal, rnam shes rang gi rdzas rgyun du rdzas su gtso bor skyed byed yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree then that a seed for consciousness is a material cause of consciousness. Suppose that you do then disagree.  Let's consider the seed for consciousness. It is so a material cause of consciousness, Because it is that thing which—acting primarily as a material entity—creates the material continuation of the original consciousness.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, RNAM SHES CHOS CAN, KHYOD KYI SA BON KHYOD RANG GI RDZAS RGYUN DU RDZAS SU GTZO BOR SKYED BYED YIN PAR THAL, KHYOD SHES PA YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, rnam shes chos can, khyod kyi sa bon khyod rang gi rdzas rgyun du rdzas su gtso bor skyed byed yin par thal, khyod shes pa yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that a seed for consciousness is that thing which—acting primarily as a material entity—creates the material continuation of the original consciousness. Suppose you do disagree.  Consider then consciousness. Its seed is too that thing which—acting primarily as a material entity—creates the material continuation of the original consciousness. Because it is a kind of awareness.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, RNAM SHES KYI SA BON CHOS CAN, SHES PA MA YIN PAR THAL, LDAN MIN 'DU BYED YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, rnam shes kyi sa bon chos can, shes pa ma yin par thal, ldan min 'du byed yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that the seed of a consciousness is not a kind of awareness. If you do disagree, then let's consider this seed of a consciousness. No, it's not a kind of awareness, Because it's an active entity which is neither awareness nor form.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, RNAM SHES CHOS CAN, KHYOD KYI SA BON LDAN MIN 'DU BYED YIN PAR THAL, KHYOD KYI SA BON YOD PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, rnam shes chos can, khyod kyi sa bon ldan min 'du byed yin par thal, khyod kyi sa bon yod pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that the seed of a consciousness is an active entity which is neither awareness nor form. If you do disagree, then let's consider consciousness. Its seed is so an active entity which is neither awareness nor form, Because the consciousness has its seed.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, RNAM SHES CHOS CAN, KHYOD KYI SA BON YOD PAR THAL, KHYOD DNGOS PO YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, rnam shes chos can, khyod kyi sa bon yod par thal, khyod dngos po yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that the consciousness has its seed. If you do disagree, then consider again the consciousness. It does too have its seed, Because it is a working thing. 9 If Something Is the Direct Result Of a Working Thing, Then Does It Have to Be The Direct Result Of the Working Thing?

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, DNGOS PO'I PHYI LOGS SU BYUNG BA CHOS CAN, KHYOD DNGOS PO'I DNGOS 'BRAS YIN PAR THAL, DNGOS PO KHYOD KYI DNGOS RGYU YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, dngos po'i phyi logs su byung ba chos can, khyod dngos po'i dngos 'bras yin par thal, dngos po khyod kyi dngos rgyu yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: Then I disagree that something which is the working thing of the next moment after a working thing is the direct result of the working thing. If you do disagree, then let's consider the working thing of the next moment after a working thing. It is too the direct result of the working thing, Because the working thing is its direct cause.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, DNGOS PO CHOS CAN, KHYOD KHYOD KYI PHYI LOGS SU BYUNG BA'I DNGOS RGYU YIN PAR THAL, KHYOD DNGOS PO YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, dngos po chos can, khyod khyod kyi phyi logs su byung ba'i dngos rgyu yin par thal, khyod dngos po yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that the working thing is the direct cause of the working thing of the next moment after it. If you do disagree, then let's consider the working thing. It is so the direct cause of the working thing of the next moment after it, Because it is a working thing!

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, DNGOS PO CHOS CAN, DNGOS PO'I PHYI LOGS SU BYUNG BA'I PHYI LOGS SU BYUNG BA'I SNGA LOGS SU BYUNG BA YIN PAR THAL, DNGOS PO'I PHYI LOGS SU BYUNG BA'I PHYI LOGS SU BYUNG BA'I RGYU YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, dngos po chos can, dngos po'i phyi logs su byung ba'i phyi logs su byung ba'i snga logs su byung ba yin par thal, dngos po'i phyi logs su byung ba'i phyi logs su byung ba'i rgyu yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: Well then, I disagree that the working thing is the working thing of the moment before the working thing of the moment after the working thing of the moment after the working thing. If you do disagree, then let's consider the working thing. It is so the working thing of the moment before the working thing of the moment after the working thing of the moment after the working thing, Because it is the cause of the working thing of the moment after the working thing of the moment after the working thing.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, DNGOS PO CHOS CAN, DNGOS PO'I PHYI LOGS SU BYUNG BA'I PHYI LOGS SU BYUNG BA'I RGYU YIN PAR THAL, DNGOS PO'I PHYI LOGS SU BYUNG BA'I PHYI LOGS SU BYUNG BA KHYOD KYI 'BRAS BU YIN PA'I PHYIR,

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, DNGOS PO CHOS CAN, KHYOD KYI PHYI LOGS SU BYUNG BA'I PHYI LOGS SU BYUNG BA KHYOD KYI 'BRAS BU YIN PAR THAL, KHYOD DNGOS PO YIN PA'I PHYIR,

gru.english: I disagree that the working thing of the moment after the working thing of the moment after the working thing is the working thing's result. If you do disagree, then consider the working thing. The working thing of the moment after the working thing of the moment after it is so its result, Because it is a working thing! 10 If Something Is the Result of a Form, Does It Have to Be Either The Direct Result or the Indirect Result Of That Form?

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, GZUGS CHOS CAN, KHYOD KHYOD KYI PHYI LOGS SU BYUNG BA DANG KHYOD KYI PHYI LOGS SU BYUNG BA'I PHYI LOGS SU BYUNG BA GNYIS KA'I RGYU YIN PAR THAL, KHYOD DNGOS PO YIN PA'I PHYIR,

gru.english: I disagree that a form is the cause of both the form of the moment after the form, and the form of the moment after the form of the moment after the form. Suppose you do disagree. A form is so the cause of both the form of the moment after the form, and the form of the moment after the form of the moment after the form, Because the form is a working thing!

gru.acip: RTAGS DANG PO MA GRUB NA, GZUGS KYI PHYI LOGS SU BYUNG BA'I PHYI LOGS SU BYUNG BA GZUGS KYI DNGOS 'BRAS YIN PAR THAL, GZUGS KYI PHYI LOGS SU BYUNG BA DANG GZUGS KYI PHYI LOGS SU BYUNG BA'I PHYI LOGS SU BYUNG BA GNYIS KA GZUGS KYI DNGOS 'BRAS YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: rtags dang po ma grub na, gzugs kyi phyi logs su byung ba'i phyi logs su byung ba gzugs kyi dngos 'bras yin par thal, gzugs kyi phyi logs su byung ba dang gzugs kyi phyi logs su byung ba'i phyi logs su byung ba gnyis ka gzugs kyi dngos 'bras yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree with the first part of this last reason of yours: I disagree that both the form of the moment after a form, and the form of the moment after the form of the moment after the form, cannot be the direct result of the form. Suppose you do disagree with that first part.  Are you saying then that the form of the moment after the form of the moment after a form is the direct result of that form? Why do you say that? Because, according to you, both the form of the moment after a form and the form of the moment after the form of the moment after the form are the direct result of the form.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, GZUGS KYI PHYI LOGS SU BYUNG BA'I PHYI LOGS SU BYUNG BA CHOS CAN, GZUGS KYI BRGYUD 'BRAS YIN PAR THAL, GZUGS KHYOD KYI BRGYUD RGYU YIN PA'I PHYIR,

If you do disagree, then let's consider the form of the moment after the form of the moment after a form. It is so the indirect result of the form, Because the form is its indirect cause!

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, GZUGS CHOS CAN, KHYOD KHYOD KYI PHYI LOGS SU BYUNG BA'I PHYI LOGS SU BYUNG BA'I BRGYUD RGYU YIN PAR THAL, KHYOD DNGOS PO YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, gzugs chos can, khyod khyod kyi phyi logs su byung ba'i phyi logs su byung ba'i brgyud rgyu yin par thal, khyod dngos po yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that a form is the indirect cause of the form of the moment after the form of the moment after the form. Suppose you do disagree.  Then let's consider the form. It is so the indirect cause of the form of the moment after the form of the moment after it, Because it is a working thing!

gru.acip: RTAGS GNYIS PA MA GRUB NA, GZUGS KYI PHYI LOGS SU BYUNG BA GZUGS KYI BRGYUD 'BRAS YIN PAR THAL, GZUGS KYI PHYI LOGS SU BYUNG BA DANG, GZUGS KYI PHYI LOGS SU BYUNG BA'I PHYI LOGS SU BYUNG BA GNYIS KA GZUGS KYI BRGYUD 'BRAS YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: rtags gnyis pa ma grub na, gzugs kyi phyi logs su byung ba gzugs kyi brgyud 'bras yin par thal, gzugs kyi phyi logs su byung ba dang, gzugs kyi phyi logs su byung ba'i phyi logs su byung ba gnyis ka gzugs kyi brgyud 'bras yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: Well then, I disagree with the second part of the reason given above: I disagree that both the form of the moment after a form, and the form of the moment after the form of the moment after the form, cannot be the indirect result of the form. Suppose you do disagree with the second part of the reason we gave above. Are you saying then that the form of the moment after a form is its indirect result? Why do you say that? Because—according to you—both the form of the moment after a form, and the form of the moment after the form of the moment after the form, can be the indirect result of the form.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, GZUGS CHOS CAN, KHYOD KHYOD KYI PHYI LOGS SU BYUNG BA'I BRGYUD RGYU MA YIN PAR THAL, KHYOD DNGOS PO YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, gzugs chos can, khyod khyod kyi phyi logs su byung ba'i brgyud rgyu ma yin par thal, khyod dngos po yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that the form is not its indirect cause. If you do disagree, then let's again consider that form. No, it's not the indirect cause of the form of the moment after it, Because it is a working thing! 11 Can the Form of the Moment Before The Form of the Moment Before The Form of the Moment after a Form Be a Direct Cause of That Form?

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, SHES BYA CHOS CAN, DNGOS PO'I SKYED BYED YIN PAR THAL, DNGOS PO SKYED BYED YIN PA'I PHYIR ZER NA
gru.wylie: ma grub na, shes bya chos can, dngos po'i skyed byed yin par thal, dngos po skyed byed yin pa'i phyir zer na
gru.english: And suppose you disagree that all knowable things act to create working things. Let's consider again all knowable things. They do too act to create working things, Because they are working things act to create.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, SHES BYA CHOS CAN, DNGOS PO SKYED BYED YIN PAR THAL, DNGOS PO RGYU YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, shes bya chos can, dngos po skyed byed yin par thal, dngos po rgyu yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: And suppose you disagree that all knowable things are working things act to create. Let's then consider, again, all knowable things. They are so working things act to create, Because they are working things are causes.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, SHES BYA CHOS CAN, DNGOS PO RGYU YIN PAR THAL, DNGOS PO DNGOS PO'I PHYI LOGS SU BYUNG BA'I RGYU YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, shes bya chos can, dngos po rgyu yin par thal, dngos po dngos po'i phyi logs su byung ba'i rgyu yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that all knowable things are working things are causes. If you do disagree, then let's once again consider all knowable things. They are too working things are causes, Because they are working things are causes of the working things that come after working things.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, SHES BYA CHOS CAN, DNGOS PO DNGOS PO'I PHYI LOGS SU BYUNG BA'I RGYU YIN PAR THAL, DNGOS PO YOD PA'I PHYIR,

gru.english: I disagree that all knowable things are working things are causes of the working things that come after working things. If you do disagree, then consider all knowable things. They are too working things are causes of the working things that come after working things, Because working things do exist.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, SHES BYA CHOS CAN, DNGOS PO YOD PAR THAL, GANG ZAG GI BDAG MED YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, shes bya chos can, dngos po yod par thal, gang zag gi bdag med yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that working things do exist. Suppose you do disagree.  Consider then all knowable things. Working things do too exist, Because individuals are not individuals with them. 15 Is It True That a Working Thing Cannot Be the Cause Of What Comes Just After The Working Thing?

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, DNGOS PO CHOS CAN, DNGOS PO DANG DUS MNYAM DU BYUNG BA'I RGYU YIN PAR THAL, DNGOS PO DANG DUS MNYAM DU BYUNG BA'I DNGOS PO YIN PA'I PHYIR ZER NA
gru.wylie: ma grub na, dngos po chos can, dngos po dang dus mnyam du byung ba'i rgyu yin par thal, dngos po dang dus mnyam du byung ba'i dngos po yin pa'i phyir zer na
gru.english: I disagree that a working thing is a cause which happens at the same time as the working thing. If you do disagree, then let's again consider the working thing. It is so a cause which happens at the same time as the working thing, Because it is a working thing that happens at the same time as the working thing.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, DNGOS PO CHOS CAN, KHYOD KHYOD DANG DUS MNYAM DU BYUNG BA'I DNGOS PO YIN PAR THAL, KHYOD DNGOS PO YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, dngos po chos can, khyod khyod dang dus mnyam du byung ba'i dngos po yin par thal, khyod dngos po yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that the working thing is a working thing that happens at the same time as the working thing. Suppose you do disagree.  Consider then the working thing. It is so a working thing that happens at the same time as the working thing, Because it's a working thing! 16 Isn't a Working Thing The Cause of What Happens Just After a Working Thing?

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, DNGOS PO CHOS CAN, KHYOD KHYOD KYI PHYI LOGS SU BYUNG BA'I DNGOS PO MA YIN PAR THAL, KHYOD GANG ZAG GI BDAG MED YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, dngos po chos can, khyod khyod kyi phyi logs su byung ba'i dngos po ma yin par thal, khyod gang zag gi bdag med yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: And you could never disagree that a working thing was not a working thing that happens just after the working thing. If you did, then you would have to consider a working thing. No, it's not a working thing that happens just after the working thing, Because an individual is not an individual with it. 17 Could It Be True That Working Things Could Not Be the Causes Of What Happens Just After the Working Things?

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, DNGOS PO CHOS CAN, DNGOS PO'I PHYI LOGS SU BYUNG BA'I DNGOS PO MA YIN PAR THAL, DNGOS PO DANG DUS MNYAM DU BYUNG BA'I DNGOS PO YIN PA'I PHYIR,
