gru.english: And suppose you disagree that the working thing is not a working thing that happens just after a working thing. Consider, in that case, the working thing. No, it's not a working thing that happens just after a working thing, Because it's a working thing that happens at the same time as the working thing.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, DNGOS PO CHOS CAN, KHYOD KHYOD DANG DUS MNYAM DU BYUNG BA'I DNGOS PO YIN PAR THAL, KHYOD DNGOS PO YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, dngos po chos can, khyod khyod dang dus mnyam du byung ba'i dngos po yin par thal, khyod dngos po yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that the working thing is a working thing that happens at the same time as the working thing. Suppose you do disagree.  Consider then, once more, the working thing. It is so a working thing that happens at the same time as the working thing, Because it's a working thing! 18 Does What Happens Just After a Working Thing Have to Be a Result Of What Happens Just After The Working Thing?

gru.acip: RTAGS DANG PO MA GRUB NA, DNGOS PO'I PHYI LOGS SU BYUNG BA CHOS CAN, DNGOS PO'I PHYI LOGS SU BYUNG BA YIN PAR THAL, DNGOS PO'I 'BRAS BU YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: rtags dang po ma grub na, dngos po'i phyi logs su byung ba chos can, dngos po'i phyi logs su byung ba yin par thal, dngos po'i 'bras bu yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: Well then, I disagree with the first half of the reason here: what happens just after a working thing is not something that happens just after a working thing. Suppose you do disagree.  In that case, let's consider what happens just after a working thing. It is so something that happens just after a working thing, Because it is the result of a working thing.

gru.acip: RTAGS GNYIS PA MA GRUB NA, DNGOS PO'I PHYI LOGS SU BYUNG BA CHOS CAN, 'BRAS BU YIN PAR THAL, DNGOS PO YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: rtags gnyis pa ma grub na, dngos po'i phyi logs su byung ba chos can, 'bras bu yin par thal, dngos po yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: So then I disagree with the second half of your reason: what happens just after a working thing is not a result. Suppose you do disagree with the second half of that reason.  Let's consider, once again, what happens just after a working thing. It is so a result, Because it is a working thing!

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, RTAG PA MA YIN PA'I RGYU YOD PAR THAL, RTAG PA MA YIN PAR GYUR PA'I RGYU YOD PA'I PHYIR ZER NA
gru.wylie: ma grub na, rtag pa ma yin pa'i rgyu yod par thal, rtag pa ma yin par gyur pa'i rgyu yod pa'i phyir zer na
gru.english: I disagree that there is always a cause of something which is not unchanging. Suppose you do disagree. And yet there is too a cause of something which is not unchanging, Because there do exist causes which are themselves not unchanging.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, RTAG PA MA YIN PAR GYUR PA'I RGYU YOD PAR THAL, GZUGS DE YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, rtag pa ma yin par gyur pa'i rgyu yod par thal, gzugs de yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: Well then I disagree with that reason above: I say there do not exist any causes which are themselves not unchanging. Suppose you do disagree.  And yet there do exist causes which are themselves not unchanging, Because form would be an example of one.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, GZUGS CHOS CAN, RTAG PA MA YIN PAR GYUR PA'I RGYU YIN PAR THAL, RTAG PA MA YIN PA DANG RGYU GNYIS KA YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, gzugs chos can, rtag pa ma yin par gyur pa'i rgyu yin par thal, rtag pa ma yin pa dang rgyu gnyis ka yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that form would be an example of a cause which was itself not unchanging. If you do disagree, then let's consider form. It is too an example of a cause which is itself not unchanging, Because it is something which is both (1) not unchanging and (2) a cause.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, GZUGS CHOS CAN, RTAG PA MA YIN PA DANG RGYU GNYIS KA YIN PAR THAL, RGYU YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, gzugs chos can, rtag pa ma yin pa dang rgyu gnyis ka yin par thal, rgyu yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that form is something which is both (1) not unchanging and (2) a cause. Suppose you do disagree.  Let's consider then form. It is so something which is both (1) not unchanging and (2) a cause, Because it is a cause! 20 Is It the Case That That Which Is Not Unchanging Has to Be the Result Of Form?

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, KVA BUM GNYIS KA'I SNGA LOGS SU BYUNG BA CHOS CAN, KVA BA KHYOD KYI 'BRAS BU MA YIN PAR THAL, KHYOD MED NA KVA BA MED PAS MA KHYAB PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, kva bum gnyis ka'i snga logs su byung ba chos can, kva ba khyod kyi 'bras bu ma yin par thal, khyod med na kva ba med pas ma khyab pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that the coffee table is not a result of what comes just before both a coffee table and a coffee cup. If you do disagree, then let's once more consider what comes just before both a coffee table and a coffee cup. No, the coffee table is not a result of it, Because it's not necessarily the case that—if what comes just before both a coffee table and a coffee cup were absent—then the coffee table would also have to be absent.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, BUM PA'I DGAG GZHI CHOS CAN, KVA BA MED PAR THAL, KVA BUM GNYIS KA'I SNGA LOGS SU BYUNG BA MED PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, bum pa'i dgag gzhi chos can, kva ba med par thal, kva bum gnyis ka'i snga logs su byung ba med pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that it's not necessarily the case that—if what comes just before both a coffee table and a coffee cup were absent—then the coffee table would also have to be absent. And suppose you do disagree.  In that case, let's consider an area where there are no coffee cups. It must then be the case that there could be no coffee tables there, Because what comes just before a coffee table and a coffee cup would be absent there.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, BUM PA'I DGAG GZHI CHOS CAN, KVA BUM GNYIS KA'I SNGA LOGS SU BYUNG BA MED PAR THAL, KVA BUM GNYIS MED PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, bum pa'i dgag gzhi chos can, kva bum gnyis ka'i snga logs su byung ba med par thal, kva bum gnyis med pa'i phyir
gru.english: Then I disagree that what comes just before a coffee table and a coffee cup would be absent in an area where there are no coffee cups. Suppose you do disagree.  Let's consider then again an area where there are no coffee cups. It is so the case that what comes just before a coffee table and a coffee cup would be absent there, Because the two of a coffee table and a coffee cup would be absent.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, BUM PA'I DGAG GZHI CHOS CAN, KVA BUM GNYIS MED PAR THAL, BUM PA MED PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, bum pa'i dgag gzhi chos can, kva bum gnyis med par thal, bum pa med pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that the two of a coffee table and a coffee cup would be absent. Suppose you do disagree.  Let's consider then an area where there are no coffee cups. The two of a coffee table and a coffee cup would too be absent, Because there would be no coffee cups!

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, BUM PA'I DGAG GZHI CHOS CAN, BUM PA MED PAR THAL, BUM PA'I DGAG GZHI YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, bum pa'i dgag gzhi chos can, bum pa med par thal, bum pa'i dgag gzhi yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that there would be no coffee cups in an area where there are no coffee cups. Suppose you do disagree.  Let's consider then an area where there are no coffee cups. No, there wouldn't be any coffee cups there, Because it's an area where there are no coffee cups!

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, KVA BUM GNYIS CHOS CAN, KVA BA'I SNGA LOGS SU BYUNG BA'I 'BRAS BU MA YIN PAR THAL, KVA BA'I SNGA LOGS SU BYUNG BA KHYOD KYI RGYU MA YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, kva bum gnyis chos can, kva ba'i snga logs su byung ba'i 'bras bu ma yin par thal, kva ba'i snga logs su byung ba khyod kyi rgyu ma yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that the two of a coffee table and a coffee cup are not a result of what comes just before a coffee table. Suppose you do disagree.  Let's consider then the two of a coffee table and a coffee cup. No, it's not a result of what comes just before a coffee table, Because what comes just before a coffee table is not its cause.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, KVA BA'I SNGA LOGS SU BYUNG BA CHOS CAN, KVA BUM GNYIS KA'I RGYU MA YIN PAR THAL, KVA BA'I RGYU YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, kva ba'i snga logs su byung ba chos can, kva bum gnyis ka'i rgyu ma yin par thal, kva ba'i rgyu yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that what comes just before a coffee table is not a cause of the two of a coffee table and a coffee cup. Suppose you do disagree.  In that case, let's consider what comes just before a coffee table. No, it's not a cause of the two of a coffee table and a coffee cup, Because it's not a cause of a coffee table. 24 Is There a Working Thing At the Time Of What Comes Just Before A Working Thing?

gru.acip: RTAGS DANG PO MA GRUB NA, DNGOS PO'I SNGA LOGS SU BYUNG BA CHOS CAN, DNGOS PO YIN PAR THAL, DNGOS PO'I RGYU YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: rtags dang po ma grub na, dngos po'i snga logs su byung ba chos can, dngos po yin par thal, dngos po'i rgyu yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree with the first part of your reason above: it's not true that what comes just before a working thing is itself a working thing. If you do disagree, then let's again consider what comes just before a working thing. It is too a working thing, Because it's the cause of a working thing.

gru.acip: RTAGS GNYIS PA MA GRUB NA, DNGOS PO'I SNGA LOGS SU BYUNG BA CHOS CAN, KHYOD KYI DUS SU KHYOD YOD PAR THAL, KHYOD DNGOS PO YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: rtags gnyis pa ma grub na, dngos po'i snga logs su byung ba chos can, khyod kyi dus su khyod yod par thal, khyod dngos po yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: Then I disagree with the second part of your reason above: it's not true that such a thing as what comes just before a working thing exists. Suppose you do disagree to that second part.  Consider then again what comes just before a working thing. It does so exist at its time, Because it is a working thing. 25 Is What Comes Just Before A Working Thing A Material Cause Of That Thing?

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, DNGOS PO'I SNGA LOGS SU BYUNG BA CHOS CAN, DNGOS PO'I NYER LEN MA YIN PAR THAL, DNGOS POR 'GYUR NGES MA YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, dngos po'i snga logs su byung ba chos can, dngos po'i nyer len ma yin par thal, dngos por 'gyur nges ma yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that what comes just before a working thing is not the material cause of the working thing. Suppose you do disagree.  Let's consider then what comes just before a working thing. Isn't it not the material cause of the working thing? Why do you say that? Because it is not certain to turn into the working thing.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, DNGOS PO'I SNGA LOGS SU BYUNG BA CHOS CAN, DNGOS POR 'GYUR NGES MA YIN PAR THAL, DNGOS POR GYUR ZIN PA YIN PA'I PHYIR ZER NA
gru.wylie: ma grub na, dngos po'i snga logs su byung ba chos can, dngos por 'gyur nges ma yin par thal, dngos por gyur zin pa yin pa'i phyir zer na
gru.english: I disagree that what comes just before a working thing is not certain to turn into the working thing. Suppose you do disagree.  Let's consider then what comes just before a working thing. Isn't it true that it is not certain to turn into the working thing? Why do you say that? Because it has already turned into a working thing.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, DNGOS PO'I SNGA LOGS SU BYUNG BA CHOS CAN, DNGOS POR GYUR ZIN PA YIN PAR THAL, DNGOS PO YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, dngos po'i snga logs su byung ba chos can, dngos por gyur zin pa yin par thal, dngos po yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: Well then, I disagree that what comes just before a working thing has already turned into a working thing. If you do disagree, then let's again consider what comes just before a working thing. It has too already turned into a working thing, Because it is a working thing! 26 Do the Two Of a Coffee Table & a Coffee Cup Have a Material Cause?

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, RI BONG RVA CHOS CAN, BLO GANG YANG RUNG BA GCIG GI YUL YIN PAR THAL, RI BONG RVA 'DZIN RTOG PA'I YUL YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, ri bong rva chos can, blo gang yang rung ba gcig gi yul yin par thal, ri bong rva 'dzin rtog pa'i yul yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: Well then, I disagree that the antlers on top of a rabbit's head are the object of a particular state of mind. If you do disagree, then let's consider the antlers on top of a rabbit's head. They are too the object of a particular state of mind, Because they are the object of a state of mind that thinks it sees antlers on top of a rabbit's head!

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, RI BONG RVA CHOS CAN, RI BONG RVA 'DZIN RTOG PA'I YUL YIN PAR THAL, RI BONG RVA 'DZIN RTOG PA'I ZHEN YUL YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, ri bong rva chos can, ri bong rva 'dzin rtog pa'i yul yin par thal, ri bong rva 'dzin rtog pa'i zhen yul yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that the antlers on top of a rabbit's head are the object of a state of mind that thinks it sees antlers on top of a rabbit's head. If you do disagree, then let's again consider the antlers on top of a rabbit's head. They are too the object of a state of mind that thinks it sees antlers on top of a rabbit's head, Because they are the object that a state of mind that thinks it sees antlers on top of a rabbit's head believes in.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, RI BONG RVA CHOS CAN, KHYOD KHYOD 'DZIN RTOG PA'I ZHEN YUL YIN PAR THAL, KHYOD GANG ZAG GI BDAG MED YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, ri bong rva chos can, khyod khyod 'dzin rtog pa'i zhen yul yin par thal, khyod gang zag gi bdag med yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that the antlers on top of a rabbit's head are the object that a state of mind that thinks it sees antlers on top of a rabbit's head believes in. If you do disagree, then consider the antlers on top of a rabbit's head. They are too the object that a state of mind that thinks it sees antlers on top of a rabbit's head believes in, Because an individual is not an individual with it.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, YUL DANG GZHAL BYA GNYIS DON GCIG YIN PAR THAL, YUL DANG TSAD MAS DMIGS PA GNYIS DON GCIG YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, yul dang gzhal bya gnyis don gcig yin par thal, yul dang tshad mas dmigs pa gnyis don gcig yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that the two of “object” and “object under consideration” are synonymous. Suppose you do disagree.  And yet the two of “object” and “object under consideration” are too synonymous, Because the two of “object” and “something which is perceived by an accurate perception” are synonymous. 2 Are All Subjects States of Mind?

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, BUM PA ZHES BRJOD PA'I SGRA CHOS CAN, YUL CAN YIN PAR THAL, KHYOD KYI YUL YOD PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, bum pa zhes brjod pa'i sgra chos can, yul can yin par thal, khyod kyi yul yod pa'i phyir
gru.english: Well then, I disagree that the sound “coffee cup” is a subject. Suppose that you do disagree.  Let's consider the sound “coffee cup.” It is too a subject, Because it has its object.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, BUM PA ZHES BRJOD PA'I SGRA CHOS CAN, KHYOD KYI YUL YOD PAR THAL, KHYOD KYI BRJOD BYA YOD PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, bum pa zhes brjod pa'i sgra chos can, khyod kyi yul yod par thal, khyod kyi brjod bya yod pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that the sound “coffee cup” has its object. Suppose you do disagree.  Let's consider then this same sound, “coffee cup.” It does too have its object, Because there does exist an object which it expresses.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, BUM PA ZHES BRJOD PA'I SGRA CHOS CAN, KHYOD KYI BRJOD BYA YOD PAR THAL, BUM PA DE YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, bum pa zhes brjod pa'i sgra chos can, khyod kyi brjod bya yod par thal, bum pa de yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that there does exist an object which the sound “coffee cup” expresses. Suppose you do disagree.  Let's then again consider the sound “coffee cup.” There does too exist an object which it expresses, Because a coffee cup is that object.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, BUM PA CHOS CAN, KHYOD KHYOD ZHES BRJOD PA'I SGRA'I BRJOD BYA YIN PAR THAL, KHYOD GANG ZAG GI BDAG MED YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, bum pa chos can, khyod khyod zhes brjod pa'i sgra'i brjod bya yin par thal, khyod gang zag gi bdag med yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that a coffee cup is the object which the sound “coffee cup” expresses. Suppose you do disagree.  Let's again consider that coffee cup. It is too the object which the sound for the same object expresses, Because an individual is not an individual with it.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, BUM PA ZHES BRJOD PA'I SGRA CHOS CAN, GSAL ZHING RIG PA MA YIN PAR THAL, BEM PO YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, bum pa zhes brjod pa'i sgra chos can, gsal zhing rig pa ma yin par thal, bem po yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that the sound “coffee cup” is not clear and knowing. If you do disagree, then again consider the sound “coffee cup.” No, it's not clear and knowing, Because it's physical matter!

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, BUM PA ZHES BRJOD PA'I SGRA CHOS CAN, BEM PO YIN PAR THAL, SGRA YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, bum pa zhes brjod pa'i sgra chos can, bem po yin par thal, sgra yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that the sound “coffee cup” is physical matter. Suppose you do disagree.  Consider then, once more, the sound “coffee cup.” It is too physical matter, Because it's a sound!

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, BUM PA CHOS CAN, KHYOD ZHES BRJOD PA'I SGRA SGRA YIN PAR THAL, KHYOD GANG ZAG GI BDAG MED YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, bum pa chos can, khyod zhes brjod pa'i sgra sgra yin par thal, khyod gang zag gi bdag med yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that the sound “coffee cup” is a sound. If you disagree, then consider a coffee cup. It is too the object which the sound for the same object expresses, Because an individual is not an individual with it. 3 If Something Is a Subject, Does It Have to Be A State of Mind?

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, MIG DBANG CHOS CAN, YUL CAN YIN PAR THAL, KHYOD KYI YUL YOD PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, mig dbang chos can, yul can yin par thal, khyod kyi yul yod pa'i phyir
gru.english: Then I disagree that a state of mind is a subject. Suppose you do disagree. Let's consider the sense power of the eye. It is too a subject, Because it has its object!

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, MIG DBANG CHOS CAN, KHYOD KYI YUL YOD PAR THAL, SNGON PO DE YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, mig dbang chos can, khyod kyi yul yod par thal, sngon po de yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that the sense power of the eye has its object. If you do disagree, then let's consider the sense power of the eye. It does too have its object, Because blue is one of those objects.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, SNGON PO CHOS CAN, KHYOD MIG DBANG GI YUL YIN PAR THAL, MIG SHES KYI BZUNG BYA YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, sngon po chos can, khyod mig dbang gi yul yin par thal, mig shes kyi bzung bya yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that blue is an object of the sense power of the eye. Suppose you do disagree. Let's consider then blue. It is too an object of the sense power of the eye, Because it is a thing that the sense power of the eye apprehends.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, SNGON PO CHOS CAN, MIG SHES KYI BZUNG BYA YIN PAR THAL, GZUGS KYI SKYE MCHED YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, sngon po chos can, mig shes kyi bzung bya yin par thal, gzugs kyi skye mched yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that blue is a thing that the sense power of the eye apprehends. Suppose you do disagree. Let's consider then blue. It is too a thing that the sense power of the eye apprehends, Because it belongs to the category of form.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, MIG DBANG CHOS CAN, BEM PO YIN PAR THAL, GZUGS YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, mig dbang chos can, bem po yin par thal, gzugs yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that the sense power of the eye is physical matter. Suppose you do disagree. Let's again consider the sense power of the eye. It is too physical matter, Because it's form!

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, MIG DBANG CHOS CAN, GZUGS YIN PAR THAL, MIG GI SKYE MCHED YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, mig dbang chos can, gzugs yin par thal, mig gi skye mched yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that the sense power of the eye is form. Suppose you do disagree. Let's consider the sense power of the eye. It is too form, Because it is the door of sense of the eye.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, MIG DBANG CHOS CAN, MIG GI SKYE MCHED YIN PAR THAL, MIG YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, mig dbang chos can, mig gi skye mched yin par thal, mig yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that the sense power of the eye is the door of sense of the eye. If you do disagree, then let's again consider the sense power of the eye. It is too the door of sense of the eye, Because it's the eye! 4 Are All Subjects States of Mind, Reprised

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, SANGS RGYAS 'PHAGS PA CHOS CAN, YUL CAN YIN PAR THAL, KHYOD KYI YUL YOD PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, sangs rgyas 'phags pa chos can, yul can yin par thal, khyod kyi yul yod pa'i phyir
gru.english: Then I disagree that a realized being who is also an enlightened being is a subject. Suppose you do disagree. Let's consider then a realized being who is also an enlightened being. They are too a subject, Because they have their object.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, SANGS RGYAS 'PHAGS PA CHOS CAN, KHYOD KYI YUL YOD PAR THAL, KHYOD KYI GZHAL BYA YOD PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, sangs rgyas 'phags pa chos can, khyod kyi yul yod par thal, khyod kyi gzhal bya yod pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that a realized being who is also an enlightened being has their object. If you do disagree, then let's consider this realized being who is also an enlightened being. They do too have their object, Because they have something under consideration.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, SANGS RGYAS 'PHAGS PA CHOS CAN, KHYOD KYI GZHAL BYA YOD PAR THAL, GZHI GRUB NA KHYOD KYI GZHAL BYA YIN PAS KHYAB PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, sangs rgyas 'phags pa chos can, khyod kyi gzhal bya yod par thal, gzhi grub na khyod kyi gzhal bya yin pas khyab pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that a realized being who is also an enlightened being has something under consideration. If you do disagree, then let's again consider this realized being who is also an enlightened being. They do too have something under consideration. Because anything which is an example of reality is something under their consideration.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, SANGS RGYAS 'PHAGS PA CHOS CAN, LDAN MIN 'DU BYED YIN PAR THAL, GANG ZAG YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, sangs rgyas 'phags pa chos can, ldan min 'du byed yin par thal, gang zag yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that a realized being who is also an enlightened being is an active entity which is neither awareness nor form. Suppose you do disagree. Let's consider again this realized being who is also an enlightened being. They are so an active entity which is neither awareness nor form, Because they are an individual.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, SANGS RGYAS 'PHAGS PA CHOS CAN, GANG ZAG YIN PAR THAL, SANGS RGYAS 'PHAGS PA YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, sangs rgyas 'phags pa chos can, gang zag yin par thal, sangs rgyas 'phags pa yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that a realized being who is also an enlightened being is an individual. If you do disagree, then let's consider once more this realized being who is also an enlightened being. They are too an individual, Because they are a realized being who is also an enlightened being. 5 Are All Objects Direct Objects Of Direct Perception?

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, 'DUS MA BYAS KYI NAM MKHA' CHOS CAN, YUL YIN PAR THAL, BLO'I YUL YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, 'dus ma byas kyi nam mkha' chos can, yul yin par thal, blo'i yul yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: Then I disagree: the unproduced form of space is not an object. Suppose you do disagree. Let's again then consider the unproduced form of space. It is too an object, Because it is an object of the mind.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, 'DUS MA BYAS KYI NAM MKHA' CHOS CAN, BLO'I YUL YIN PAR THAL, BLO'I YUL DU BYA RUNG YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, 'dus ma byas kyi nam mkha' chos can, blo'i yul yin par thal, blo'i yul du bya rung yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: Then I disagree that the unproduced form of space is an object of the mind. Suppose you do disagree. Let's consider again the unproduced form of space. It is too an object of the mind, Because it can be taken as an object of the mind.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, 'DUS MA BYAS KYI NAM MKHA' CHOS CAN, BLO'I YUL DU BYA RUNG YIN PAR THAL, SHES BYA YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, 'dus ma byas kyi nam mkha' chos can, blo'i yul du bya rung yin par thal, shes bya yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that the unproduced form of space can be taken as an object of the mind. If you do disagree, then let's once more consider this unproduced form of space. It can too be taken as an object of the mind, Because it is a knowable thing.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, 'DUS MA BYAS KYI NAM MKHA' CHOS CAN, RNAM MKHYEN GYI DNGOS YUL MA YIN PAR THAL, RNAM MKHYEN GYI DNGOS GZHAL MA YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, 'dus ma byas kyi nam mkha' chos can, rnam mkhyen gyi dngos yul ma yin par thal, rnam mkhyen gyi dngos gzhal ma yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that the unproduced form of space is not the direct object of omniscience. If you do disagree, then let's again consider the unproduced form of space. No, it's not the direct object of omniscience, Because it's not an object which omniscience considers directly.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, 'DUS MA BYAS KYI NAM MKHA' CHOS CAN, RNAM MKHYEN GYI DNGOS GZHAL MA YIN PAR THAL, DNGOS PO MA YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, 'dus ma byas kyi nam mkha' chos can, rnam mkhyen gyi dngos gzhal ma yin par thal, dngos po ma yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that the unproduced form of space is not an object which omniscience considers directly. If you do disagree, the let's once more consider the unproduced form of space. No, it's not an object which omniscience considers directly, Because it's not a working thing.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, BUM 'DZIN RTOG PA LA BUM PA MA YIN PA LAS LOG PAR SNANG BA CHOS CAN, BUM 'DZIN RTOG PA'I BZUNG YUL YIN PAR THAL, BUM 'DZIN RTOG PA'I SNANG YUL YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, bum 'dzin rtog pa la bum pa ma yin pa las log par snang ba chos can, bum 'dzin rtog pa'i bzung yul yin par thal, bum 'dzin rtog pa'i snang yul yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: Then I disagree that a case where the opposite of everything which is not a coffee cup is making its appearance to a perception holding to a coffee cup is a case where the object is apprehended by a perception holding to a coffee cup. Suppose you do disagree.  Let's consider then this case, where the opposite of everything which is not a coffee cup is making its appearance to a perception holding to a coffee cup. This opposite is too an object apprehended by a perception holding to a coffee cup, Because it is the object which is making its appearance to a perception holding to a coffee cup.

gru.acip: GONG GI MA KHYAB MTSAMS LA RTAGS MA GRUB ZER NA, BUM PA CHOS CAN, KHYOD 'DZIN RTOG PA LA KHYOD MA YIN PA LAS LOG PAR SNANG BA KHYOD 'DZIN RTOG PA'I SNANG YUL YIN PAR THAL, KHYOD GANG ZAG GI BDAG MED YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: gong gi ma khyab mtshams la rtags ma grub zer na, bum pa chos can, khyod 'dzin rtog pa la khyod ma yin pa las log par snang ba khyod 'dzin rtog pa'i snang yul yin par thal, khyod gang zag gi bdag med yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: And suppose you reply “I disagree with the reason,” instead of saying that one didn't imply the other, in that last exchange. Let's consider then a coffee cup. The opposite of everything which is not a coffee cup, as it makes its appearance to a perception holding to a coffee cup, is so the object which is making its appearance to a perception holding to a coffee cup, Because an individual is not an individual with it.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, BUM 'DZIN RTOG PA LA BUM PA MA YIN PA LAS LOG PAR SNANG BA CHOS CAN, BUM 'DZIN RTOG PA'I 'DZIN STANGS KYI YUL MA YIN PAR THAL, BUM 'DZIN RTOG PA'I SNANG YUL YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, bum 'dzin rtog pa la bum pa ma yin pa las log par snang ba chos can, bum 'dzin rtog pa'i 'dzin stangs kyi yul ma yin par thal, bum 'dzin rtog pa'i snang yul yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that the opposite of everything which is not a coffee cup, as it makes its appearance to a perception holding a coffee cup, is not the object that a perception holding to a coffee cup is holding to. Suppose you do disagree. And yet that is not the object that a perception holding to a coffee cup is holding to, Because it is the object making its appearance to the perception holding to a coffee cup.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, BUM PA CHOS CAN, KHYOD 'DZIN RTOG PA'I 'DZIN STANGS KYI YUL DANG KHYOD 'DZIN RTOG PA'I SNANG YUL GNYIS 'GAL BA YIN PAR THAL, KHYOD GANG ZAG GI BDAG MED YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, bum pa chos can, khyod 'dzin rtog pa'i 'dzin stangs kyi yul dang khyod 'dzin rtog pa'i snang yul gnyis 'gal ba yin par thal, khyod gang zag gi bdag med yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that it's a contradiction for one thing to be both the object that the perception holding to a coffee cup is holding to; and at the same time be the object making its appearance to this same perception. Suppose you do disagree. Let's take then a coffee cup. It is so a contradiction for it to be both the object that a perception of something is holding to; and at the same time be the object making its appearance to that same perception, Because an individual is not an individual with it. 7 If Something Is Not Apprehended by a Perception, Is It Then Never The Object Apprehended By That Perception?

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, BUM 'DZIN RTOG PA LA BUM PA MA YIN PA LAS LOG PAR SNANG BA CHOS CAN, BUM 'DZIN RTOG PAS MA BZUNG BAR THAL, BUM 'DZIN RTOG PA'I SNANG YUL YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, bum 'dzin rtog pa la bum pa ma yin pa las log par snang ba chos can, bum 'dzin rtog pas ma bzung bar thal, bum 'dzin rtog pa'i snang yul yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: Then I disagree that the opposite of everything which is not a coffee cup, as it makes its appearance to a perception holding a coffee cup, is not apprehended by a perception holding to a coffee cup. Suppose you do disagree. Let's consider the opposite of everything which is not a coffee cup, as it makes its appearance to a perception holding a coffee cup. Not it's not apprehended by a perception holding a coffee cup, Because it is the object making its appearance to a perception holding a coffee cup! 8 If a Perception Believes in an Object, Does the Object Have to Exist?

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, SGRA CHOS CAN, KHYOD RTAG PAR 'DZIN PA'I RTOG PA DE RTOG PA YIN PAR THAL, KHYOD RTAG PAR 'DZIN PA'I RTOG PA YOD PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, sgra chos can, khyod rtag par 'dzin pa'i rtog pa de rtog pa yin par thal, khyod rtag par 'dzin pa'i rtog pa yod pa'i phyir
gru.english: Well then, I disagree that the perception which holds that sound is an unchanging thing is a perception. Suppose you do disagree. Let's consider then sound. The perception which holds that it is an unchanging thing is too a perception, Because there does exist a perception that it is an unchanging thing.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, SGRA CHOS CAN, KHYOD RTAG PAR 'DZIN PA'I RTOG PA YOD PAR THAL, KHYOD GANG ZAG GI BDAG MED YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, sgra chos can, khyod rtag par 'dzin pa'i rtog pa yod par thal, khyod gang zag gi bdag med yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that there does exist a perception that sound is an unchanging thing. If you do disagree, then let's again consider sound. There does too exist a perception which holds that it is an unchanging thing, Because an individual is not an individual with it.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, SGRA RTAG PAR 'DZIN PA'I RTOG PA CHOS CAN, KHYOD KYI 'DZIN STANGS KYI YUL MED PAR THAL, KHYOD LOG SHES YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, sgra rtag par 'dzin pa'i rtog pa chos can, khyod kyi 'dzin stangs kyi yul med par thal, khyod log shes yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that there is no object that a perception which holds that sound is an unchanging thing is holding to. If you do disagree, then let's consider the perception which holds that sound is an unchanging thing. No, there isn't any object that it is holding to, Because it is a mistaken perception!

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, SGRA CHOS CAN, KHYOD RTAG PAR 'DZIN PA'I RTOG PA DE LOG SHES YIN PAR THAL, KHYOD RTAG PA MA YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, sgra chos can, khyod rtag par 'dzin pa'i rtog pa de log shes yin par thal, khyod rtag pa ma yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that the perception which holds that sound is an unchanging thing is a mistaken perception. If you do disagree, then let's consider sound. The perception which holds it to be an unchanging thing is so a mistaken perception, Because it is not an unchanging thing. 9 If a Perception Focuses on an Object, Does That Object Have to Exist?

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, SGRA RTAG PAR 'DZIN PA'I RTOG PA CHOS CAN, KHYOD KYI DMIGS YUL YOD PAR THAL, SGRA DE YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, sgra rtag par 'dzin pa'i rtog pa chos can, khyod kyi dmigs yul yod par thal, sgra de yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that the perception which holds that sound is an unchanging thing does have an object which it is focusing upon. If you do disagree, then let's consider the perception which holds that sound is an unchanging thing. Yes, it does have an object which it is focusing upon, Because sound is that object.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, SGRA CHOS CAN, KHYOD SGRA RTAG PAR 'DZIN PA'I RTOG PA'I DMIGS YUL YIN PAR THAL, KHYOD SGRA MI RTAG PAR RTOGS PA'I RJES DPAG GI DMIGS YUL YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, sgra chos can, khyod sgra rtag par 'dzin pa'i rtog pa'i dmigs yul yin par thal, khyod sgra mi rtag par rtogs pa'i rjes dpag gi dmigs yul yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that sound is the object that the perception which holds that sound is an unchanging thing is focusing upon. Suppose you do disagree. Consider then sound. It is too the object that the perception which holds that sound is an unchanging thing is focusing upon, Because it is the object that the deductive realization that sound is a changing thing is focusing upon.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, BUM PA CHOS CAN, KHYOD SGRA SPYI TZAM GYI SGO NAS 'DZIN PA'I RTOG PA DE KHYOD 'DZIN RTOGS YIN PAR THAL, KHYOD SGRA SPYI TZAM GYI SGO NAS 'DZIN PA'I RTOG PA YOD PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, bum pa chos can, khyod sgra spyi tsam gyi sgo nas 'dzin pa'i rtog pa de khyod 'dzin rtogs yin par thal, khyod sgra spyi tsam gyi sgo nas 'dzin pa'i rtog pa yod pa'i phyir
gru.english: Then I disagree that a perception that holds to a coffee cup through nothing more than the sound which is its general archetype is a perception that holds to a coffee cup. Suppose you do disagree. Consider then a coffee cup. The perception that holds to it through nothing more than the sound which is its general archetype is too a perception that holds to a coffee cup, Because there does exist a perception that holds to the coffee cup through nothing more than the sound which is its general archetype.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, BUM PA CHOS CAN, KHYOD SGRA SPYI TZAM GYI SGO NAS 'DZIN PA'I RTOG PA YOD PAR THAL, KHYOD GANG ZAG GI BDAG MED YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, bum pa chos can, khyod sgra spyi tsam gyi sgo nas 'dzin pa'i rtog pa yod par thal, khyod gang zag gi bdag med yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that there does exist a perception that holds to the coffee cup through nothing more than the sound which is its general archetype. If you do disagree, then let's again consider a coffee cup. There does too exist a perception that holds to the coffee cup through nothing more than the sound which is its general archetype, Because an individual is not an individual with it.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, BUM PA CHOS CAN, KHYOD KHYOD SGRA SPYI TZAM GYI SGO NAS 'DZIN PA'I RTOG PA'I SHUGS YUL YIN PAR THAL, KHYOD BUM PA YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, bum pa chos can, khyod khyod sgra spyi tsam gyi sgo nas 'dzin pa'i rtog pa'i shugs yul yin par thal, khyod bum pa yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that a coffee cup is the indirect object of a perception that holds to a coffee cup through nothing more than the sound which is its general archetype. Suppose you do disagree. The coffee cup is too the indirect object of a perception that holds to it through nothing more than the sound which is its general archetype, Because it is a coffee cup! 11 If Something Is the Consciousness Of the Thought, Does It Have to Be The Thought?

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, SNGO 'DZIN MIG SHES NYAMS MYONG GI RANG RIG CHOS CAN, YID SHES YIN PAR THAL, RANG RIG YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, sngo 'dzin mig shes nyams myong gi rang rig chos can, yid shes yin par thal, rang rig yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: Well then, I disagree that the apperception which experiences a visual consciousness which is holding to the color blue is the consciousness of the thought. Suppose you do disagree. Consider then that apperception which experiences a visual consciousness which is holding to the color blue. It is too the consciousness of the thought, Because it is apperception!

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, SNGO 'DZIN MIG SHES CHOS CAN, KHYOD NYAMS MYONG GI RANG RIG DE RANG RIG YIN PAR THAL, KHYOD NYAMS MYONG GI RANG RIG YOD PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, sngo 'dzin mig shes chos can, khyod nyams myong gi rang rig de rang rig yin par thal, khyod nyams myong gi rang rig yod pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that the apperception which experiences a visual consciousness which is holding to the color blue is apperception. If you do disagree, then consider a visual consciousness which is holding to the color blue. The apperception which experiences it is so an apperception! Because it is an apperception which experiences it!

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, SNGO 'DZIN MIG SHES CHOS CAN, KHYOD NYAMS MYONG GI RANG RIG YOD PAR THAL, KHYOD GZHAN RIG GI SHES PA YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, sngo 'dzin mig shes chos can, khyod nyams myong gi rang rig yod par thal, khyod gzhan rig gi shes pa yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that that apperception is an apperception which experiences that consciousness. Suppose you do disagree.  Let's consider then the visual consciousness which is holding to the color blue. There does too exist an apperception which is experiencing it, Because it is a state of mind which is perceiving something other than itself!

gru.acip: GONG GI MA KHYAB MTSAMS LA RTAGS MA GRUB ZER NA, SNGO 'DZIN MIG SHES NYAMS MYONG GI RANG RIG CHOS CAN, RNAM SHES MA YIN PAR THAL, SEMS MA YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: gong gi ma khyab mtshams la rtags ma grub zer na, sngo 'dzin mig shes nyams myong gi rang rig chos can, rnam shes ma yin par thal, sems ma yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: Then I change my answer: where I said above that “It's not necessarily the case that if something is not consciousness it can't be the thought,” I instead say “It's not true that the apperception which experiences a visual consciousness which is holding to the color blue is not consciousness.” Suppose you do disagree that it's true. In that case, let's consider again the apperception which experiences a visual consciousness which is holding to the color blue. No, it's not consciousness, Because it's not the mind!

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, SNGO 'DZIN MIG SHES NYAMS MYONG GI RANG RIG CHOS CAN, SEMS MA YIN PAR THAL, SEMS DANG SEMS BYUNG GANG RUNG MA YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, sngo 'dzin mig shes nyams myong gi rang rig chos can, sems ma yin par thal, sems dang sems byung gang rung ma yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that the mind's perception of itself in which it experiences the eye consciousness of the color blue is not the mind. If you do disagree, then let's once again consider the mind's perception of itself in which it experiences the eye consciousness of the color blue. No, it's not the mind, Because it is neither mind nor a mental function.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, SNGO 'DZIN MIG SHES NYAMS MYONG GI RANG RIG CHOS CAN, SEMS DANG SEMS BYUNG GANG RUNG MA YIN PAR THAL, RANG RIG YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, sngo 'dzin mig shes nyams myong gi rang rig chos can, sems dang sems byung gang rung ma yin par thal, rang rig yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that the mind's perception of itself in which it experiences the eye consciousness of the color blue is neither mind nor a mental function. If you do disagree, then let's consider again the mind's perception of itself in which it experiences the eye consciousness of the color blue. No, it's neither mind nor a mental function, Because it is apperception!

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, YID KYI RNAM PAR SHES PA'I 'KHOR DU GYUR PA'I TSOR BA CHOS CAN, YID SHES YIN PAR THAL, YID KYI RNAM PAR SHES PA'I 'KHOR DU GYUR PA'I SEMS BYUNG YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, yid kyi rnam par shes pa'i 'khor du gyur pa'i tshor ba chos can, yid shes yin par thal, yid kyi rnam par shes pa'i 'khor du gyur pa'i sems byung yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: Then I disagree that the capacity of feeling as it exists attendant to the consciousness of the thought is the consciousness of the thought. Suppose you do disagree. Let's again then consider the capacity of feeling as it exists attendant to the consciousness of the thought. It is too consciousness of the thought, Because it is a mental function existing attendant to the consciousness of the thought.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, GANGS RI SNGON POR SNANG BA'I DBANG SHES CHOS CAN, SHES PA YIN PAR THAL, DBANG SHES YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, gangs ri sngon por snang ba'i dbang shes chos can, shes pa yin par thal, dbang shes yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: Then I disagree that a sense consciousness where a white snow mountain is appearing to be blue is a state of mind. Suppose you do disagree. Let's consider then this sense consciousness where a white snow mountain is appearing to be blue. It is so a state of mind, Because it is a sense perception.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, SGRA MI RTAG PAR RTOGS PA'I RJES DPAG CHOS CAN, TSAD MA YIN PAR THAL, GSAR DU MI BSLU BA'I RIG PA YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, sgra mi rtag par rtogs pa'i rjes dpag chos can, tshad ma yin par thal, gsar du mi bslu ba'i rig pa yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: Then I disagree with your reason: the deductive perception where we realize that sound is a changing thing is not an accurate perception. Suppose you do disagree. Let's consider then the deductive perception where we realize that sound is a changing thing. It is too an accurate perception, Because it is a state of awareness which is fresh and unmistaken.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, SGRA MI RTAG PAR RTOGS PA'I RJES DPAG CHOS CAN, MNGON SUM MA YIN PAR THAL, RTOG BRAL GYI SHES PA MA YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, sgra mi rtag par rtogs pa'i rjes dpag chos can, mngon sum ma yin par thal, rtog bral gyi shes pa ma yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that the deductive perception where we realize that sound is a changing thing is not a direct perception at all. If you do disagree, then let's consider the deductive perception where we realize that sound is a changing thing. No, it's not a direct perception, Because it is not a state of mind which is free of conceptual thought.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, SGRA MI RTAG PAR RTOGS PA'I RJES DPAG CHOS CAN, RTOG BRAL GYI SHES PA MA YIN PAR THAL, RTOG PA YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, sgra mi rtag par rtogs pa'i rjes dpag chos can, rtog bral gyi shes pa ma yin par thal, rtog pa yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that the deductive perception where we realize that sound is a changing thing is not a state of mind which is free of conceptual thought. If you do disagree, the let's consider again the deductive perception where we realize that sound is a changing thing. No, it's not a state of mind which is free of conceptual thought, Because it is a conceptual thought!

gru.acip: DGE BA BCU GCIG 'DREN TSUL YOD DE, NGO TSA SHES PA DANG, KHREL YOD PA DANG, 'DOD CHAGS MED PA DANG, ZHE SDANG MED PA DANG, GTI MUG MED PA DANG, DAD PA DANG, SHIN SBYANGS DANG, BAG YOD DANG, BTANG SNYOMS DANG, BRTZON 'GRUS DANG, RNAM PAR MI 'TSE BA DANG BCU GCIG PO DE 'DREN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: dge ba bcu gcig 'dren tshul yod de, ngo tsha shes pa dang, khrel yod pa dang, 'dod chags med pa dang, zhe sdang med pa dang, gti mug med pa dang, dad pa dang, shin sbyangs dang, bag yod dang, btang snyoms dang, brtson 'grus dang, rnam par mi 'tshe ba dang bcu gcig po de 'dren pa'i phyir
gru.english: There is a way of enumerating the eleven virtuous mental functions, because there is the enumeration into the eleven of shame; consideration; freedom from ignorant liking; freedom from ignorant disliking; freedom from ignorance; faith; pliancy; mindfulness; seeing people as equal; joyful effort; and not wishing to harm.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, 'DUS MA BYAS KYI NAM MKHA' CHOS CAN, MNGON SUM GYI TSAD MAS DNGOS SU RTOGS PAR BYA BA YIN PAR THAL, RNAM MKHYEN GYIS DNGOS SU RTOGS PAR BYA BA YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, 'dus ma byas kyi nam mkha' chos can, mngon sum gyi tshad mas dngos su rtogs par bya ba yin par thal, rnam mkhyen gyis dngos su rtogs par bya ba yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: And suppose you disagree that the unproduced form of space is an object which is grasped directly by an accurate perception which is direct. Let's then consider this unproduced form of space. It is too an object which is grasped directly by an accurate perception which is direct. Because it is something which is grasped directly by omniscience.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, 'DUS MA BYAS KYI NAM MKHA' CHOS CAN, RNAM MKHYEN GYIS DNGOS SU RTOGS PAR BYA BA YIN PAR THAL, RNAM MKHYEN GYIS RTOGS PAR BYA BA YIN PA'I PHYIR ZER NA
gru.wylie: ma grub na, 'dus ma byas kyi nam mkha' chos can, rnam mkhyen gyis dngos su rtogs par bya ba yin par thal, rnam mkhyen gyis rtogs par bya ba yin pa'i phyir zer na
gru.english: Suppose next you disagree that the unproduced form of space is something grasped directly by omniscience. Let's then again consider this unproduced form of space. It is too something grasped directly by omniscience, Because it is something grasped by omniscience.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, 'DUS MA BYAS KYI NAM MKHA' CHOS CAN, RNAM MKHYEN GYIS RTOGS PAR BYA BA YIN PAR THAL, RNAM MKHYEN GYI GZHAL BYA YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, 'dus ma byas kyi nam mkha' chos can, rnam mkhyen gyis rtogs par bya ba yin par thal, rnam mkhyen gyi gzhal bya yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: And suppose one was to disagree that the unproduced form of space is something grasped by omniscience. In that case, let us consider the unproduced form of space. It is so something grasped by omniscience, Because it is something considered by omniscience.

gru.acip: DER THAL, GZHI GRUB PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: der thal, gzhi grub pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that the unproduced form of space is something considered by omniscience. And yet it is, Because it is an example of reality.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, SGRA MI RTAG PA CHOS CAN, RJES DPAG GI TSAD MAS DNGOS SU RTOGS PAR BYA BA YIN PAR THAL, SGRA MI RTAG PAR RTOGS PA'I RJES DPAG GI TSAD MAS DNGOS SU RTOGS PAR BYA BA YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, sgra mi rtag pa chos can, rjes dpag gi tshad mas dngos su rtogs par bya ba yin par thal, sgra mi rtag par rtogs pa'i rjes dpag gi tshad mas dngos su rtogs par bya ba yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: And suppose that you disagree that the fact that sound is a changing thing is an object which is grasped directly by a deductive form of accurate perception. In that case, let us consider this fact, that sound is a changing thing. It is so an object which is grasped directly by a deductive form of accurate perception, Because it is something which is grasped directly by a deductive form of accurate perception where one grasps that sound is a changing thing.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, SGRA MI RTAG PA CHOS CAN, KHYOD KHYOD RTOGS PA'I RJES DPAG GI TSAD MAS DNGOS SU RTOGS PAR BYA BA YIN PAR THAL, KHYOD RTOGS PA'I RJES DPAG GI TSAD MA YOD PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, sgra mi rtag pa chos can, khyod khyod rtogs pa'i rjes dpag gi tshad mas dngos su rtogs par bya ba yin par thal, khyod rtogs pa'i rjes dpag gi tshad ma yod pa'i phyir
gru.english: And suppose you disagree that the fact that sound is a changing thing is something which is grasped directly by a deductive form of accurate perception where one grasps that sound is a changing thing. In that case, let's consider the fact that sound is a changing thing. It is so something which is grasped directly by the deductive form of accurate perception which grasps it, Because there does exist a deductive form of accurate perception which grasps it.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, SGRA MI RTAG PA CHOS CAN, KHYOD RTOGS PA'I RJES DPAG GI TSAD MA YOD PAR THAL, KHYOD GZHI GRUB PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, sgra mi rtag pa chos can, khyod rtogs pa'i rjes dpag gi tshad ma yod par thal, khyod gzhi grub pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that there does exist a deductive form of accurate perception which grasps that sound is a changing thing. Suppose you do disagree. In that case, let us consider the fact that sound is a changing thing. There does too exist a deductive form of accurate perception which grasps it, Because it is an example of reality.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, SGRA MI RTAG PA CHOS CAN, LKOG GYUR YIN PAR THAL, GZHI GRUB PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, sgra mi rtag pa chos can, lkog gyur yin par thal, gzhi grub pa'i phyir
gru.english: Well then, I disagree that the fact that sound is a changing thing is an example of hidden reality. Suppose you do disagree. Consider then the fact that sound is a changing thing. It is so an example of hidden reality, Because it is an example of reality. 19 Does Something Have to Be A State of Mind To Be Totally Accurate?

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, BSTAN BCOS MNGON RTOGS RGYAN CHOS CAN, TSAD MA YIN PAR THAL, LUNG GI TSAD MA YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, bstan bcos mngon rtogs rgyan chos can, tshad ma yin par thal, lung gi tshad ma yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: And suppose you do disagree that the Jewel of Realizations is totally accurate. Let's consider this particular classical commentary. It is so totally accurate, Because it is total accuracy in the form of scripture.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, BSTAN BCOS MNGON RTOGS RGYAN CHOS CAN, LUNG GI TSAD MA YIN PAR THAL, KHYOD LUNG TSAD MA YIN PA'I PHYIR ZER NA
gru.wylie: ma grub na, bstan bcos mngon rtogs rgyan chos can, lung gi tshad ma yin par thal, khyod lung tshad ma yin pa'i phyir zer na
gru.english: And suppose you disagree that the Jewel of Realizations is total accuracy in the form of scripture. Let's then consider, once again the Jewel of Realizations. It is so total accuracy in the form of scripture, Because it is scripture which is totally accurate.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, BSTAN BCOS MNGON RTOGS RGYAN CHOS CAN, KHYOD LUNG TSAD MA YIN PAR THAL, KHYOD BSTAN BCOS RNAM DAG YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, bstan bcos mngon rtogs rgyan chos can, khyod lung tshad ma yin par thal, khyod bstan bcos rnam dag yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: And if you disagree that the Jewel of Realizations is scripture which is totally accurate, Let's once again consider the Jewel of Realizations. It is so scripture which is totally accurate, Because it is an absolutely correct classical commentary. 20 If Something Is an Object Considered by a Deductive Form Of Accurate Perception, Does It Have to Be an Example Of Hidden Reality?

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, RI BONG RVA CHOS CAN, RJES DPAG GI TSAD MA'I GZHAL BYA YIN PAR THAL, RJES DPAG TSAD MA'I GZHAL BYA YIN PA'I PHYIR ZER NA
gru.wylie: ma grub na, ri bong rva chos can, rjes dpag gi tshad ma'i gzhal bya yin par thal, rjes dpag tshad ma'i gzhal bya yin pa'i phyir zer na
gru.english: And suppose you disagree that the antlers on top of a rabbit's head are an object which is considered by a deductive form of accurate perception. In that case, let us consider again the antlers on top of a rabbit's head. They are too an object which is considered by a deductive form of accurate perception, Because they are a deductive accurate perception, object of consideration.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, RI BONG RVA CHOS CAN, RJES DPAG TSAD MA'I GZHAL BYA YIN PAR THAL, RJES DPAG RNAM MKHYEN GYI GZHAL BYA YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, ri bong rva chos can, rjes dpag tshad ma'i gzhal bya yin par thal, rjes dpag rnam mkhyen gyi gzhal bya yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: And suppose you disagree that the antlers on top of a rabbit's head are a deductive accurate perception, object of consideration. Let's consider then the antlers on top of a rabbit's head. They are too a deductive accurate perception, object of consideration, Because they are deductive accurate perception is an object considered by omniscience.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, RI BONG RVA CHOS CAN, RJES DPAG RNAM MKHYEN GYI GZHAL BYA YIN PAR THAL, RJES DPAG YOD PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, ri bong rva chos can, rjes dpag rnam mkhyen gyi gzhal bya yin par thal, rjes dpag yod pa'i phyir
gru.english: And suppose you disagree that the antlers on top of a rabbit's head are deductive accurate perception is an object considered by omniscience. Let's consider then again the antlers on top of a rabbit's head. They are too deductive accurate perception is an object considered by omniscience, Because they are deductive accurate perception exists!

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, RI BONG RVA CHOS CAN, RJES DPAG YOD PAR THAL, GANG ZAG GI BDAG MED YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, ri bong rva chos can, rjes dpag yod par thal, gang zag gi bdag med yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: And suppose you disagree that the antlers on top of a rabbit's head are deductive accurate perception exists. Let's consider then, one last time, the antlers on top of a rabbit's head. They are too deductive accurate perception exists, Because an individual is not an individual with them. 21 If Something Is An Object Held by a Perception, Is It Necessarily Apprehended by That Perception?

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, BUM PA'I DON SPYI CHOS CAN, BUM 'DZIN RTOG PA'I BZUNG YUL YIN PAR THAL, BUM 'DZIN RTOG PA'I SNANG YUL YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, bum pa'i don spyi chos can, bum 'dzin rtog pa'i bzung yul yin par thal, bum 'dzin rtog pa'i snang yul yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: And suppose you disagree that a mental image of a coffee cup is the object held by a perception that holds to a coffee cup. Let's consider then the mental image of a coffee cup. It is so the object held by a perception that holds to a coffee cup, Because it is the object that appears to a perception that holds to a coffee cup.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, SPYI DANG BYE BRAG GANG RUNG YIN NA YOD PAS KHYAB PAR THAL, SPYI YIN NA YOD PAS KHYAB PA GANG ZHIG ,BYE BRAG YIN NA YOD PAS KHYAB PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, spyi dang bye brag gang rung yin na yod pas khyab par thal, spyi yin na yod pas khyab pa gang zhig ,bye brag yin na yod pas khyab pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that it is a fact that if something is a quality or a characteristic, it is an existing thing. And yet it is true that, if something is a quality or a characteristic, it is an existing thing, Because (1) if something is a quality, then it must exist; and (2) if something is a characteristic, then it must exist.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, DNGOS PO CHOS CAN, SPYI YIN PAR THAL, KHYOD KYI BYE BRAG YOD PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, dngos po chos can, spyi yin par thal, khyod kyi bye brag yod pa'i phyir
gru.english: Then I disagree that working thing is a quality. If you do disagree, then let's consider working thing. It is too a quality, Because there are things that are characteristic of it.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, DNGOS PO CHOS CAN, KHYOD KYI BYE BRAG YOD PAR THAL, BUM PA DE YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, dngos po chos can, khyod kyi bye brag yod par thal, bum pa de yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that there are things that are characteristic of the quality “working thing.” Suppose you do disagree. Let's then again consider working thing. There are too things which are characteristic of it, Because a coffee cup would be just such an example.

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, BUM PA CHOS CAN, KHYOD DNGOS PO'I BYE BRAG YIN PAR THAL, KHYOD DNGOS PO YIN KHYOD DNGOS PO DANG BDAG GCIG TU 'BREL, KHYOD MA YIN ZHING DNGOS PO YIN PA'I GZHI MTHUN PA DU MA GRUB PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: ma grub na, bum pa chos can, khyod dngos po'i bye brag yin par thal, khyod dngos po yin khyod dngos po dang bdag gcig tu 'brel, khyod ma yin zhing dngos po yin pa'i gzhi mthun pa du ma grub pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that a coffee cup would be characteristic of working thing. If you do disagree, then let's consider a coffee cup. It is too characteristic of working thing, Because (1) a coffee cup is a working thing; (2) it shares a relationship with working thing such that to be it—the coffee cup—is to be a working thing; and (3) there do exist many examples of other things which are not coffee cups but which are still working things.

gru.acip: RTAGS DANG PO MA GRUB NA, BUM PA CHOS CAN, DNGOS PO YIN PAR THAL, MI RTAG PA YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: rtags dang po ma grub na, bum pa chos can, dngos po yin par thal, mi rtag pa yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree with the first part of your reason; that is, it's not true that a coffee cup is a working thing. If you do disagree, then let's consider a coffee cup. It is too a working thing, Because it is a changing thing!

gru.acip: RTAGS GNYIS PA MA GRUB NA, BUM PA CHOS CAN, DNGOS PO DANG BDAG GCIG 'BREL YIN PAR THAL, DNGOS PO DANG BDAG NYID GCIG GI SGO NAS THA DAD DNGOS PO MED NA KHYOD MED DGOS PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: rtags gnyis pa ma grub na, bum pa chos can, dngos po dang bdag gcig 'brel yin par thal, dngos po dang bdag nyid gcig gi sgo nas tha dad dngos po med na khyod med dgos pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree with the second part of your reason: it is not true that the coffee cup shares a relationship with working thing such that to be it—the coffee cup—is to be a working thing. Suppose you do disagree. Consider then a coffee cup. It does too share a relationship with working thing such that to be it—the coffee cup—is to be a working thing, Because the coffee cup is separate from working thing in such a way that to be the coffee cup is to be a working thing; and if there is no working thing, then there can be no coffee cup.

gru.acip: RTAGS DANG PO MA GRUB NA, BUM PA CHOS CAN, DNGOS PO DANG BDAG NYID GCIG YIN PAR THAL, BUM PA DANG GCIG YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: rtags dang po ma grub na, bum pa chos can, dngos po dang bdag nyid gcig yin par thal, bum pa dang gcig yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree with that part of your last reason: it is not true that to be the coffee cup is to be a working thing. If you do disagree, then let us consider a coffee cup. To be a coffee cup is so to be a working thing, Because to be a coffee cup is to be a coffee cup!

gru.acip: RTAGS GNYIS PA MA GRUB NA, BUM PA CHOS CAN, DNGOS PO DANG THA DAD YIN PAR THAL, GZUGS YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: rtags gnyis pa ma grub na, bum pa chos can, dngos po dang tha dad yin par thal, gzugs yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: Then I disagree with that other part of your last reason: it's not true that the coffee cup is separate from working thing. Suppose you do disagree. Let's again consider a coffee cup. It is so separate from working thing, Because it is a physical thing!

gru.acip: RTAGS GSUM PA MA GRUB NA, BUM PA CHOS CAN, DNGOS PO MED NA KHYOD MED DGOS PAR THAL, DNGOS PO MED NA GANG DRAN DRAN YIN DGOS PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: rtags gsum pa ma grub na, bum pa chos can, dngos po med na khyod med dgos par thal, dngos po med na gang dran dran yin dgos pa'i phyir
gru.english: Then I disagree with that other part of your last reason: it is not true that—if there is no working thing—then there can be no coffee cup. Suppose you do disagree. Let's consider then, again, the coffee cup. gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, RTAG PA CHOS CAN, KHYOD KHYOD DANG GCIG YANG YIN, KVA BUM GNYIS DANG 'GAL BA YANG YIN PA'I GZHI MTHUN PA YIN PAR THAL, KHYOD KVA BUM GNYIS DANG 'GAL BA YIN PA'I PHYIR,

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, RTAG PA CHOS CAN, KHYOD KVA BUM GNYIS DANG 'GAL BA YIN PAR THAL, KHYOD KVA BUM GNYIS DANG THA DAD, KHYOD YANG YIN, KVA BUM GNYIS YIN PA'I GZHI MTHUN PA MED PA'I PHYIR,

gru.acip: MA GRUB NA, ME DU GNYIS CHOS CAN, RTEN BYUNG 'BREL YIN PAR THAL, RGYU 'BRAS YIN PA'I PHYIR,

gru.english: I disagree that the pair of fire and smoke are an example of a relationship of dependent origination. Suppose you do disagree. In that case, let's consider the two of fire and smoke. They are too an example of a relationship of dependent origination, Because they are cause and result.

They are too cause and result, Because their relationship to one another is that of something which is started, and something which starts it. 9 If Something Is A Cause and Result, Does It Have to Be A Relationship Of Dependent Origination?

gru.english: And neither can you deny that a coffee cup is both a cause and a result, Because a coffee cup is a working thing! 10 If Something Is Characteristic of a Class, Does It Have to Be A General Class?

gru.english: And both parts of our reason here do hold true, Because being a working thing is a quality of a coffee cup.

gru.acip: ,SMRA BA ZLA MED 'DREN PA ZAS GTZANG SRAS, ,BYAMS BRTZE'I GTER CHEN MI PHAM 'JAM PA'I DBYANGS, ,SHING RTA CHEN PO KLU SGRUB THOGS MED SOGS, ,'DZAM GLING RGYAN GYUR MKHAS PA'I TSOGS LA 'DUD,
gru.wylie: smra ba zla med 'dren pa zas gtsang sras, ,byams brtse'i gter chen mi pham 'jam pa'i dbyangs, ,shing rta chen po klu sgrub thogs med sogs, ,'dzam gling rgyan gyur mkhas pa'i tshogs la 'dud
gru.english: I bow down to the mass of sages, The jewels of this world: To the son of Shuddhodana, Matchless teacher and guide; To the Invincible One and to Gentle Voice, Who are a goldmine of love and affection; To the innovators, Nagarjuna and Asanga; And all their company.

gru.acip: RTOGS BYA'I BDAG MED LA PHRA RAGS KYIS PHYE NA MANG YANG 'BYED PA'I TSE, GRUB MTHA' RNAM PA BZHI'I 'DOD TSUL DANG BSTUN DGOS KYI, DE BZHI PO GANG RUNG DANG MI MTHUN PA'I BDAG MED RTOGS PA'I LTA BA YOD PAR KHAS LEN DU MI RUNG STE, BDAG MED KHAS LEN PA'I TSUL LA NI GRUB MTHA' BZHIR NGES PA'I PHYIR TE,
gru.wylie: rtogs bya'i bdag med la phra rags kyis phye na mang yang 'byed pa'i tshe, grub mtha' rnam pa bzhi'i 'dod tshul dang bstun dgos kyi, de bzhi po gang rung dang mi mthun pa'i bdag med rtogs pa'i lta ba yod par khas len du mi rung ste, bdag med khas len pa'i tshul la ni grub mtha' bzhir nges pa'i phyir te
gru.english: This fact that nothing is itself may be divided in many different ways, according to relative subtlety. But when you do make these distinctions, you must do so following the positions taken by the four different schools—it is a mistake to accept any view of emptiness which fails to fit into one of the four classical schools. This is because all valid ways of treating the fact that nothing is itself are covered in these four: no more, and no less.

gru.acip: MKHAS GRUB RJES, DE YANG BDE BAR GSHEGS PA'I BSTAN PA LA BDAG MED KHAS LEN PA'I GRUB MTHA' BZHIR NGES KYI, BZHI PO GANG DANG YANG MI MTHUN PA'I BDAG MED PA'I LTA BA DANG DE NYID GOMS PAR BYED PA'I RNAM GZHAG SU ZHIG GIS CI TZAM SMRAS SU ZIN KYANG, RGYAL BA'I BSTAN PA LAS PHYI ROL TU GYUR PAR BRJOD PAR BYA'I, MKHAS PA DGYES PA'I LAM DU BLO GROS DANG LDAN PA DAG GIS YID CHES PAR BYA BA MIN NO, ZHES GSUNGS PA'I PHYIR RO,,
gru.wylie: mkhas grub rjes, de yang bde bar gshegs pa'i bstan pa la bdag med khas len pa'i grub mtha' bzhir nges kyi, bzhi po gang dang yang mi mthun pa'i bdag med pa'i lta ba dang de nyid goms par byed pa'i rnam gzhag su zhig gis ci tsam smras su zin kyang, rgyal ba'i bstan pa las phyi rol tu gyur par brjod par bya'i, mkhas pa dgyes pa'i lam du blo gros dang ldan pa dag gis yid ches par bya ba min no, zhes gsungs pa'i phyir ro
gru.english: This fact is repeated by Kedrup Je: Moreover, within the teachings of Those Who Have Gone to Bliss, there are four—and only four—schools of thought for presenting how nothing is itself. Now it's possible that a person might come up with a presentation for some kind of view about no self-nature, and some way of meditating on suchness, which is not in keeping with one of these four schools. But we would have to say that they had then wandered outside of the Buddha's own teachings. People of intelligence should not trust in such presentations as being the path which pleases the wise.

gru.acip: DES NA BDAG MED PHRA RAGS RNAMS GRUB MTHA' BZHI'I 'DOD TSUL GYI RIM PA DANG MTHUN PAR RJE YAB SRAS KYI BZHED PA JI LTA BA BZHIN GTAN LA DBAB PAR BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: des na bdag med phra rags rnams grub mtha' bzhi'i 'dod tshul gyi rim pa dang mthun par rje yab sras kyi bzhed pa ji lta ba bzhin gtan la dbab par bya'o
gru.english: As such, I will give my current presentation in keeping with how the four schools describe the subtle and gross forms of the fact that nothing is itself, following the positions taken by the spiritual father—the Lord—and his sons.

gru.acip: DES NA GRUB MTHA' BZHI POS KYANG BDAG MED RTOGS PA'I LTA BA DE, THAR PAR BGROD PA'I LAM GYI SROG YIN PAR 'DOD PA LA KHYAD PAR MED DE, BDAG MED MA RTOGS PAR THAR PA THOB PA MI SRID CES 'DOD PA LA KHYAD PAR MED PA'I PHYIR RO,,
gru.wylie: des na grub mtha' bzhi pos kyang bdag med rtogs pa'i lta ba de, thar par bgrod pa'i lam gyi srog yin par 'dod pa la khyad par med de, bdag med ma rtogs par thar pa thob pa mi srid ces 'dod pa la khyad par med pa'i phyir ro
gru.english: And thus it is that all four schools agree that the very life of the path—for those who wish to travel to freedom—is to perceive that things are not themselves. On this, there is no difference between these schools; that is, there is a consensus among them that if you don't come to the realization that things are not themselves, it is impossible for you to attain freedom.

gru.acip: MKHAS GRUB RIN PO CHES, BYE BRAG SMRA BA DANG MDO SDE PA DANG SEMS TZAM PA DANG DBU MA RANG RGYUD PA DAG GANG ZAG RANG RKYA THUB PA'I RDZAS YOD RNAM PAR BCAD TZAM RTOGS PAS GANG ZAG GI BDAG MED MTSAN NYID RDZOGS RTOGS PAR BZHED PA LA 'DRA MOD, ZHES GSUNGS SHING,
gru.wylie: mkhas grub rin po ches, bye brag smra ba dang mdo sde pa dang sems tsam pa dang dbu ma rang rgyud pa dag gang zag rang rkya thub pa'i rdzas yod rnam par bcad tsam rtogs pas gang zag gi bdag med mtshan nyid rdzogs rtogs par bzhed pa la 'dra mod, zhes gsungs shing
gru.english: As Kedrup Je again has put it: Admittedly, followers of the Detailist, Sutrist, and Mind Only Schools, as well as those of the Independent branch within the Middle Way School, are similar in accepting that—by realizing the simple absence of a person who is substantial, in the sense of being self-standing—one realizes the lack of a self-nature to a person, in its full and definitive form.

gru.acip: TSUL DE BZHIN DU RJE'I DRANG NGES RNAM 'BYED DANG, MKHAS GRUB KYI STONG THUN SOGS DU MA LAS BSHAD PA'I PHYIR RO,,
gru.wylie: tshul de bzhin du rje'i drang nges rnam 'byed dang, mkhas grub kyi stong thun sogs du ma las bshad pa'i phyir ro
gru.english: This position is expressed by Je Tsongkapa in his Essence of Eloquence on the Art of Interpretation, and by Kedrup Je in his Interlude on Emptiness, as well as by many others.

gru.acip: DE 'KHOR LO DANG POS BSTAN PA'I BDAG MED KYI DON YIN PAR GRUB MTHA' SMRA BA BZHIS 'DOD LA, THAL 'GYUR BAS NI DE TZAM MIN PAR YANG BZHED DO,,
gru.wylie: de 'khor lo dang pos bstan pa'i bdag med kyi don yin par grub mtha' smra ba bzhis 'dod la, thal 'gyur bas ni de tsam min par yang bzhed do
gru.english: All four schools accept that that is the meaning of no-self as taught by Lord Buddha in the first turning of the wheel. The Consequence branch of the Middle Way School, though, would also assert that it's not limited to that.

gru.acip: DE LTAR YIN KYANG, 'JUG PA'I tIKKA LAS, GANG ZAG RANG RKYA THUB PA'I RDZAS YOD DU 'DZIN PA NI, GRUB MTHAS BLO MA BSGYUR BA LA YANG YOD MOD KYANG, GANG ZAG PHUNG PO DANG MTSAN NYID MI MTHUN PAR GZHAN DU YOD PAR 'DZIN PA NI GRUB MTHAS BLO MA BSGYUR BA LA MED DO,,
gru.wylie: de ltar yin kyang, 'jug pa'i Tikka las, gang zag rang rkya thub pa'i rdzas yod du 'dzin pa ni, grub mthas blo ma bsgyur ba la yang yod mod kyang, gang zag phung po dang mtshan nyid mi mthun par gzhan du yod par 'dzin pa ni grub mthas blo ma bsgyur ba la med do
gru.english: And that's true, but the commentary to Entering the Middle Way says: Admittedly, there are people whose minds have not been influenced by philosophical schools who believe that the person is substantial, in the sense of self-standing. But the belief that the basic nature of the person is separate and inconsistent with body and mind is never found with someone who has not been influenced by some system of thought.

gru.acip: RJE'I DRANG NGES RNAM 'BYED LAS, GANG ZAG GI BDAG MED NI, RANG SDE THEG PA CHE CHUNG GI GRUB MTHA' SMRA BA GZHAN GYI LTAR NA, GANG ZAG PHUNG PO DANG MTSAN NYID MI MTHUN PA'I RANG RKYA THUB PA'I RDZAS SU MED PA TZAM LA 'DOD DO,,
gru.wylie: rje'i drang nges rnam 'byed las, gang zag gi bdag med ni, rang sde theg pa che chung gi grub mtha' smra ba gzhan gyi ltar na, gang zag phung po dang mtshan nyid mi mthun pa'i rang rkya thub pa'i rdzas su med pa tsam la 'dod do
gru.english: We begin with a statement from Je Tsongkapa's Distinguishing between the Literal and the Figurative: According to proponents of other Buddhist schools—whether these schools belong to the greater way or to the lesser—the lack of a self-nature to the person refers to no more than the person's not being substantial, in the sense of not being something which is self-standing, while still being inconsistent in its nature with the parts of a person.

gru.acip: DE 'DRA'I BDAG MED GTAN LA 'BEB BYED KYI RIGS PA MANG YANG, 'DIR CUNG ZAD BRJOD PA LA GNYIS, RTAGS 'GOD PA DANG, TSUL SGRUB PA'O,,
gru.wylie: de 'dra'i bdag med gtan la 'beb byed kyi rigs pa mang yang, 'dir cung zad brjod pa la gnyis, rtags 'god pa dang, tshul sgrub pa'o
gru.english: There are many different proofs that are used for establishing this way in which things are not themselves; but here I will describe one of them briefly. We proceed in two steps: setting forth the proof, and then establishing its validity.

gru.acip: DANG PO NI, RANG RKYA THUB PAR SNANG BA'I BDAG CHOS CAN, PHUNG PO DANG MTSAN NYID MI MTHUN PA'I RANG RKYA THUB PA'I BDAG TU MED DE, PHUNG PO DANG RANG RKYA THUB PA'I GCIG DANG RANG RKYA THUB PA'I THA DAD GANG RUNG DU MA GRUB PA'I PHYIR, DPER NA, RI BONG GI RVA BZHIN ZHES PA NI, 'BREL ZLA MA DMIGS PA'I RTAGS SO,,
gru.wylie: dang po ni, rang rkya thub par snang ba'i bdag chos can, phung po dang mtshan nyid mi mthun pa'i rang rkya thub pa'i bdag tu med de, phung po dang rang rkya thub pa'i gcig dang rang rkya thub pa'i tha dad gang rung du ma grub pa'i phyir, dper na, ri bong gi rva bzhin zhes pa ni, 'brel zla ma dmigs pa'i rtags so
gru.english: Here is the first, which happens to be a syllogism of the type which depends on the absence of something which is necessarily related. Consider a self which seems to be self-standing. It doesn't exist as a self which is self-standing, and which has an essentially different nature from the body & mind, Because it is neither something which is self-standing and is one and the same as the body & mind; nor is it something which is self-standing and is different from the body & mind. It is, for example, like the antlers of a rabbit.

gru.acip: TSUL SGRUB PA LA GNYIS, KHYAB PA DANG, PHYOGS CHOS SO,,
gru.wylie: tshul sgrub pa la gnyis, khyab pa dang, phyogs chos so
gru.english: Next I'll establish that the relationships in this syllogism do hold true. I'll do so in two steps. First I'll establish that the relationship between the reason and the quality to be proven holds true. And then I'll establish that the relationship between the reason and the subject holds true.

gru.acip: DANG PO NI, SPYIR GCIG DANG THA DAD GRUB DU MED NA MED PAR NGES PA DNGOS PO'I STOBS GYIS 'GRUB LA,
gru.wylie: dang po ni, spyir gcig dang tha dad grub du med na med par nges pa dngos po'i stobs gyis 'grub la
gru.english: Here is the first. Generally speaking, the very nature of things demands that if a thing is neither one and the same as some other existing thing, nor separate from that same thing, then it cannot exist at all.

gru.acip: RTAGS SNGA MA SGRUB PA NI, DE CHOS CAN, PHUNG PO DANG THA DAD DU SNANG BA YIN TE, DE DANG RANG RKYA BAR SNANG BA'I PHYIR RO,,
gru.wylie: rtags snga ma sgrub pa ni, de chos can, phung po dang tha dad du snang ba yin te, de dang rang rkya bar snang ba'i phyir ro
gru.english: Let's go back and prove the reason given just before this last one: the one that says, “A self that seems to be self-standing appears to be different from the body & mind.” Consider this self—the one that seems to be self-standing. It is too something which appears to be different from the body & mind, Because it appears to be standing by itself, apart from the body & mind.

gru.acip: RTAGS RTZOD GZHI'I STENG DU GRUB BO,,
gru.wylie: rtags rtsod gzhi'i steng du grub bo
gru.english: For it is true that what I've just given as the reason—the fact that the self appears to be standing by itself, apart from the body & mind—does apply to the subject under discussion here: to this self that seems to be self-standing.

gru.acip: GONG GI RTAGS PHYI MA DE SGRUB PA NI, DE CHOS CAN, PHUNG PO LAS DON GZHAN DU MED DE, PHUNG PO'I STENG DU BTAGS NAS BZHAG PA'I PHYIR RO,,
gru.wylie: gong gi rtags phyi ma de sgrub pa ni, de chos can, phung po las don gzhan du med de, phung po'i steng du btags nas bzhag pa'i phyir ro
gru.english: Now let's discuss the latter of the reasons I gave above—where I said that a self which appears to be self-standing did not exist as an object which is different from the body & mind. Let's consider this same thing: the self which appears to be self-standing. It does not exist as an object which is different from the body & mind; Because it exists as an idea applied to the body & mind.

gru.acip: CHOS KYI BDAG MED 'JOG TSUL NI GNYIS TE, NGO BO DANG KHYAD PAR LA KUN BTAGS PA'I KUN BTAGS RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS MA GRUB PA DANG, GZUGS SGRA SOGS PHYI DON GYIS STONG BA'O,,
gru.wylie: chos kyi bdag med 'jog tshul ni gnyis te, ngo bo dang khyad par la kun btags pa'i kun btags rang gi mtshan nyid kyis ma grub pa dang, gzugs sgra sogs phyi don gyis stong ba'o
gru.english: As for the lack of a self-nature to things, this is described by the Mind Only School in two ways. The first is where the basic nature and various features attributed to an object cannot exist by definition. The second is where things like visible forms and sounds are devoid of being outside objects.

gru.acip: DE GNYIS KA'ANG 'KHOR LO BAR PA'I BSTAN DON YIN PAR 'KHOR LO THA MAS BSGRUB PAR 'DOD LA,
gru.wylie: de gnyis ka'ang 'khor lo bar pa'i bstan don yin par 'khor lo tha mas bsgrub par 'dod la
gru.english: Moreover, they believe that these two are established by the final turning of the wheel as being the true meaning of the teachings of the middle turning. An examination of how things are called things

gru.acip: DGONGS 'GREL, BYANG SA, THEG BSDUS, BSDU BA SOGS NAS BSHAD PA'I DON RJE NYID GYIS LEGS BSHAD SNYING PO LAS GTAN LA PHAB PA LTAR, MKHAS GRUB RIN PO CHES STONG THUN NAS RGYAS PAR BSHAD PA'I SNYING PO BSDU NA 'DI LTAR YIN TE,
gru.wylie: dgongs 'grel, byang sa, theg bsdus, bsdu ba sogs nas bshad pa'i don rje nyid gyis legs bshad snying po las gtan la phab pa ltar, mkhas grub rin po ches stong thun nas rgyas par bshad pa'i snying po bsdu na 'di ltar yin te
gru.english: I'll summarize here the essence of Kedrup Je's detailed explanation of these points, as found in his Interlude on Emptiness. This itself is based upon the Lord's own presentation in the Essence of Eloquence—which in turn unlocks the points made in works such as Unraveling the True Thought; The Levels of the Bodhisattva; A Summary of the Greater Way; and A Brief Presentation.

gru.acip: NYAN THOS SDE GNYIS KYIS GZUGS SOGS NGO BO DANG KHYAD PAR DU KUN BTAGS KYI GZHIR RANG GI GNAS LUGS GYI DBANG GIS GRUB PAR 'DOD LA,
gru.wylie: nyan thos sde gnyis kyis gzugs sogs ngo bo dang khyad par du kun btags kyi gzhir rang gi gnas lugs gyi dbang gis grub par 'dod la
gru.english: The two listener schools believe that the fact that things like visible form and so on are what their basic nature and various features are attributed to is something that exists by the very nature of these objects.

gru.acip: SNGON PO SOGS NGO BO DANG KHYAD PAR DE TZAM DU YOD PAS MI 'GOG CING DER RANG GI MTSAN NYID GYIS GRUB PA 'GOG PA YIN NO,,
gru.wylie: sngon po sogs ngo bo dang khyad par de tsam du yod pas mi 'gog cing der rang gi mtshan nyid gyis grub pa 'gog pa yin no
gru.english: Now things like blue do exist with precisely these kinds of basic natures, and various features; so this is not what is being denied. What's being denied is that blue and the rest could possess the natures and features by definition.

gru.acip: DE YANG GZUGS SOGS NGO BO DANG KHYAD PAR GYI THA SNYAD KYI GZHI YIN PA NI, MING BRDAS BZHAG BA TZAM YIN YANG YOD LA, DER RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PA NI MED PAS DE LTAR SNANG BA LTAR GRUB PA KHEGS DGOS SO,,
gru.wylie: de yang gzugs sogs ngo bo dang khyad par gyi tha snyad kyi gzhi yin pa ni, ming brdas bzhag ba tsam yin yang yod la, der rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub pa ni med pas de ltar snang ba ltar grub pa khegs dgos so
gru.english: Now it is true that the fact that visible form and the like are things that we refer to with expressions that describe their basic natures and various features is a case where things are being established using no more than names and terms; and yet these things do in fact exist. They do not though exist this way by definition. As such, we need to deny that these could actually exist in the way they seem to: by definition.

gru.acip: DE LA GZUGS SOGS NGO BO DANG KHYAD PAR GYI THA SNYAD KYI GZHIR RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PA RTOG PA LA SNANG BA'I SNANG BA TZAM NI, RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS MA GRUB PA'I SGRO BTAGS SU MDO SDE PAS KYANG GRUB CING,
gru.wylie: de la gzugs sogs ngo bo dang khyad par gyi tha snyad kyi gzhir rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub pa rtog pa la snang ba'i snang ba tsam ni, rang gi mtshan nyid kyis ma grub pa'i sgro btags su mdo sde pas kyang grub cing
gru.english: Let's look at the mere appearance though that presents itself to our imagination here: where things like visible form seem by definition to be what is referred to with the terms that describe their basic natures and various features. Even members of the Sutrist School recognize that what we have here is a case where the mind overrates the situation: where these things are actually not what they are by definition.

gru.acip: RTOG PA DE 'KHRUL SHES SU'ANG DES GRUB PAS SNANG BA DE RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS MA GRUB PA TZAM CHOS KYI BDAG MED PHRA MO MIN NO,,
gru.wylie: rtog pa de 'khrul shes su'ang des grub pas snang ba de rang gi mtshan nyid kyis ma grub pa tsam chos kyi bdag med phra mo min no
gru.english: And even these Sutrists would recognize that our imagination at this point is a mistaken state of mind. As such, it cannot be that the mere fact that the appearance here cannot exist by definition is what the subtle lack of a self-nature to things refers to.
