gru.english: We can, in short, say that there is no object in the universe which exists through any nature of its own—which exists in and of itself, without depending on a process where its existence is established through the application of words and mental pictures to its assembled parts.

gru.acip: 'DI LA BZHED PA MI 'DRA BA YOD KYANG, MKHAS GRUB NOR BZANG RGYA MTSO'I BZHED PA BZHIN BSHAD NA, DE'I GSUNG 'BUM THOR BU LAS,
gru.wylie: 'di la bzhed pa mi 'dra ba yod kyang, mkhas grub nor bzang rgya mtsho'i bzhed pa bzhin bshad na, de'i gsung 'bum thor bu las
gru.english: There are a variety of different opinions on this question; but let's look at the explanation given by the wise and accomplished Norsang Gyatso. We see the following lines in the collection of his miscellaneous works:

gru.acip: LTA BA DNGOS GZHI SKYONG BA'I TSE, RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA LTA BU'I DGAG BYA DE YOD NA, RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA'I GCIG DANG THA DAD GANG RUNG LAS MA 'DAS PA'I NGES PA BSKYED DE,
gru.wylie: lta ba dngos gzhi skyong ba'i tshe, rang bzhin gyis grub pa lta bu'i dgag bya de yod na, rang bzhin gyis grub pa'i gcig dang tha dad gang rung las ma 'das pa'i nges pa bskyed de
gru.english: As they arrive at the main stage in learning to maintain this view of things, they should try to come to a firm conviction that, if the thing we're denying could actually exist—if something could exist, for example, through some nature of its own; then it would either have to be one thing that existed through its own nature, or separate things that existed through their own natures: there is no other option.

gru.acip: DE NAS NGA LTA BU RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA'I GCIG DANG DU MA GANG RUNG DU GRUB MA GRUB DPYAD PAS GANG DU YANG MA GRUB PA'I NGES PA RNYED PA NA,
gru.wylie: de nas nga lta bu rang bzhin gyis grub pa'i gcig dang du ma gang rung du grub ma grub dpyad pas gang du yang ma grub pa'i nges pa rnyed pa na
gru.english: After that, practitioners should examine the question of whether—for example—even they themselves exist as either one thing which exists through some nature of its own; or as more than one thing which exists through just such a nature. They will then come to a decision that they could never exist in either of these two ways.

gru.acip: RGYU MTSAN DE NYID KYIS NA, NGA RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA LTA BU'I DGAG BYA ZHE PHUG LA BZHAG NAS MED MED SNYAM PA'I MED DGAG GI 'DZIN STANGS NYID SKYONG BA YIN NO, ,ZHES GSUNGS PA LTAR BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: rgyu mtshan de nyid kyis na, nga rang bzhin gyis grub pa lta bu'i dgag bya zhe phug la bzhag nas med med snyam pa'i med dgag gi 'dzin stangs nyid skyong ba yin no, ,zhes gsungs pa ltar bya'o
gru.english: For this one reason, then, they can take a version of themselves which does for example exist through some nature of its own and set it deep down there in the center of their heart, as that very thing that emptiness seeks to deny. And then they can review, over and over again, how this version of themselves could never, ever, exist. This then is how they should conduct their actual practice of emptiness. And this then is how we ourselves should put all these ideas into actual practice!

gru.acip: 'DZIN STANGS ZHEN DU SONG NA, RIGS PA DRAN TZAM BYAS TE, SNANG TSUL DE LTAR DU GRUB PA MED MED SNYAM DU BSAM ZHING SKYUR NAS BSGOM PAR BYA LA,
gru.wylie: 'dzin stangs zhen du song na, rigs pa dran tsam byas te, snang tshul de ltar du grub pa med med snyam du bsam zhing skyur nas bsgom par bya la
gru.english: When you start sliding into believing in things again, then give yourself just a small reminder. Come back to thinking about how none of these things could ever, ever, possibly exist in this way that they appear to. Continue meditating and practicing this way, where you throw those mistaken beliefs away from you.

gru.acip: RJES THOB TU GZUGS SOGS BDEN GRUB TU LAM LAM 'CHAR BA NA, 'DI RNAMS DE LTAR DU GRUB PA MED MOD SNANG STONG TSOGS PA'I SGYU MA LTA BU STE AE MA NGO MTSAR CHE'O, ,SNYAM DU BLTA BAR BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: rjes thob tu gzugs sogs bden grub tu lam lam 'char ba na, 'di rnams de ltar du grub pa med mod snang stong tshogs pa'i sgyu ma lta bu ste ae ma ngo mtshar che'o, ,snyam du blta bar bya'o
gru.english: During the periods after these meditations—during those times between meditations—things like the visible world around you will suddenly appear to you as if they existed in truth. In these moments, here is how you should view things: “Now of course none of these things I see exists as it appears to; it is all like some kind of grand illusion—as a grand marriage between things appearing to exist in a certain way, and those same things being empty of any such existence. The universe is truly a wonder!”

gru.acip: KHA CIG ,NGA DE KHA DOG DANG DBYIBS GANG DU'ANG BZUNG DU MED PAS RANG BZHIN GYIS MA GRUB PA'O SNYAM DU SGOM PA DE, GNAS LUGS SGOM PA'O ZER BA
gru.wylie: kha cig ,nga de kha dog dang dbyibs gang du'ang bzung du med pas rang bzhin gyis ma grub pa'o snyam du sgom pa de, gnas lugs sgom pa'o zer ba
gru.english: Here's another argument they make: Meditating on the way things really are is where we sit down and think to ourselves, “The 'me' is something we could never hold on to—neither in colors, nor in shapes. It is not, therefore, something that could ever exist through any nature of its own.”

gru.acip: YANG MI 'THAD DE, NGA'I KHA DOG DANG DBYIBS NI YOD PAS MI RIGS LA, NGA KHA DOG DANG DBYIBS SU MA GRUB PAR RTOGS PA NYID KYIS, NGA RANG BZHIN MED PAR RTOGS MI NUS PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: yang mi 'thad de, nga'i kha dog dang dbyibs ni yod pas mi rigs la, nga kha dog dang dbyibs su ma grub par rtogs pa nyid kyis, nga rang bzhin med par rtogs mi nus pa'i phyir
gru.english: This position though is inaccurate; it is illogical simply for the reason that the shape and color of “me” actually do exist. And it is not the case that we could ever come to the realization that the “me” has no nature of its own simply by realizing that the “me” does not exist as color or shape.

gru.acip: KHA CIG ,SEMS KHA DOG DANG DBYIBS SU MA GRUB PAS, SEMS CI YANG MED DO SNYAM PA DANG, SEMS RANG BZHIN GYIS MED DO SNYAM DU SGOM PA DE, GNAS LUGS SGOM PA'O ZER BA
gru.wylie: kha cig ,sems kha dog dang dbyibs su ma grub pas, sems ci yang med do snyam pa dang, sems rang bzhin gyis med do snyam du sgom pa de, gnas lugs sgom pa'o zer ba
gru.english: Here's another one: The mind is made of neither colors nor shapes; therefore, there is no mind at all, and the mind cannot exist through any nature of its own. Sitting down and following this train of thought is what it means to meditate on the way things really are.

gru.acip: DER THAL, SEMS SHES PA YIN PAS, KHA DOG DANG DBYIBS SU MA GRUB PA SHIN TU NGES SLA BAS, DE TZAM GYIS NI SEMS RANG BZHIN GYIS MED PAR NGES MI NUS PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: der thal, sems shes pa yin pas, kha dog dang dbyibs su ma grub pa shin tu nges sla bas, de tsam gyis ni sems rang bzhin gyis med par nges mi nus pa'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree! And yet that is the case. After all, since the mind is made of awareness, it's an extremely simple exercise to perceive that it's not something made of color and shape. As such, it would be a mistake to say that perceiving this fact would be enough to determine that the mind cannot exist through any nature of its own. 6) The argument that the mind neither comes nor goes

gru.acip: YANG KHA CIG, SEMS DANG POR KHYI TSANG GI NANG NAS 'BYUNG BA LTAR GANG NAS KYANG MA 'ONGS, BAR DU RGYAL PO GDAN LA BZHUGS PA LTAR GANG DU'ANG MI GNAS, MTHAR BYI BA KHUNG DU 'DZUL BA LTAR GANG DU'ANG MI 'GRO BA'I GZHI MED RTZA BRAL DU RTOGS NAS RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA MED DO SNYAM DU SGOM PA DE, SEMS KYI GNAS LUGS SGOM PA'O ZER BA
gru.wylie: yang kha cig, sems dang por khyi tshang gi nang nas 'byung ba ltar gang nas kyang ma 'ongs, bar du rgyal po gdan la bzhugs pa ltar gang du'ang mi gnas, mthar byi ba khung du 'dzul ba ltar gang du'ang mi 'gro ba'i gzhi med rtsa bral du rtogs nas rang bzhin gyis grub pa med do snyam du sgom pa de, sems kyi gnas lugs sgom pa'o zer ba
gru.english: Here's yet another argument you hear: There is nowhere that the mind ever first comes from; it's not as if it pops up like a dog departing the door of its doghouse. And there is nowhere where the mind—in the interim—sits itself down, like a king or queen upon a throne. And there is nowhere, at the end of things, that the mind finally returns to, like a mouse squeezing back into its hole. When we finally understand all this about the mind—when we finally realize that it has no foundation, and is devoid of all roots; and thus begin to meditate upon the idea that it cannot exist through any nature of its own—then this truly is what it means to perform a meditation upon the way our mind really is.

gru.acip: DER THAL, TSUL DES SEMS GZUGS CAN DU GRUB PA'I SKYE 'GAG GNAS GSUM DANG BRAL BAR RTOGS KYANG, SEMS RANG BZHIN MED PA RTOGS MI NUS PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: der thal, tshul des sems gzugs can du grub pa'i skye 'gag gnas gsum dang bral bar rtogs kyang, sems rang bzhin med pa rtogs mi nus pa'i phyir
gru.english: But I disagree! And yet you cannot. Following the thinking you've laid out here would be enough, if all you wanted to grasp was that the mind was devoid of the three of starting, stopping, and staying in the form of a physical entity. It would not be enough, though, to come to the realization that the mind is not something that could ever exist through any nature of its own.

gru.acip: GZHAN YANG, DE MI 'THAD DE, SKYE 'GAG GNAS GSUM RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA MED PA'I 'TSOL TSUL DE LTAR MA YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: gzhan yang, de mi 'thad de, skye 'gag gnas gsum rang bzhin gyis grub pa med pa'i 'tshol tshul de ltar ma yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: And this position is wrong for another reason. The way you've described it is not, in fact, the way in which we look to discover whether or not the three of starting, stopping, and staying are things that exist through some nature of their own.

gru.acip: DER THAL, DE 'TSOL TSUL NI, SEMS SNGAR MED GSAR DU RANG BZHIN GYIS MI SKYE BA DANG, RANG DUS SU RANG BZHIN GYIS MI GNAS PA DANG, RANG GRUB PA'I DUS SKAD CIG GNYIS PAR RANG BZHIN GYIS MI 'GAG PAR DPYOD DGOS PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: der thal, de 'tshol tshul ni, sems sngar med gsar du rang bzhin gyis mi skye ba dang, rang dus su rang bzhin gyis mi gnas pa dang, rang grub pa'i dus skad cig gnyis par rang bzhin gyis mi 'gag par dpyod dgos pa'i phyir
gru.english: But I disagree! And yet you cannot disagree, because the way we look to discover that is, rather, done differently: first you have to check and find out that a mind which was not there before could not now start, through some nature of its own. Nor could it—during the time in which it is present—be staying, through any nature of its own. And nor, in the moment following the moment in which it was staying, could it come to a stop through any nature of its own. 7) The argument that seeing the clearness of the mind is a meditation on emptiness

gru.acip: KHA CIG ,SEMS GRUB TZAM NAS GSAL BA'I NGO BOR SKYES SHING, GSAL TZAM DE LA BRTAGS SHING DPYAD NA, KHA DOG DANG DBYIBS GANG DU'ANG MI RNYED PAS, GSAL BA'I DUS NA STONG PA STONG PA'I DUS NA GSAL BAS GSAL STONG DBYER MED DU SGOM PA DE, GNAS LUGS SGOM PA'O ZER BA
gru.wylie: kha cig ,sems grub tsam nas gsal ba'i ngo bor skyes shing, gsal tsam de la brtags shing dpyad na, kha dog dang dbyibs gang du'ang mi rnyed pas, gsal ba'i dus na stong pa stong pa'i dus na gsal bas gsal stong dbyer med du sgom pa de, gnas lugs sgom pa'o zer ba
gru.english: Yet another argument: The mind, as soon as it comes into being, starts as something with a nature of being clear. If we take that simple clarity and examine it—go deeper—then we discover that we could never find it within some color, or some shape. We then meditate on how—during the time that it is clear—the mind is also empty; and how—during the time that it is empty—it is also clear. That is, we meditate on how the clarity and the emptiness are indivisible. This then is what it means to meditate upon the way things really are.

gru.acip: DE NI KHYOD 'DOD PA LTAR MIN GYI, NAM MKHA' DE THOGS BCAS KYI REG BYA BKAG TZAM YIN PA DE BZHIN DU SEMS LA SOGS PA'I CHOS THAMS CAD KYI CHOS NYID DE, DGAG BYA BDEN GRUB BKAG TZAM LA 'JOG ZHES PA'I DON YIN PAS SO,,
gru.wylie: de ni khyod 'dod pa ltar min gyi, nam mkha' de thogs bcas kyi reg bya bkag tsam yin pa de bzhin du sems la sogs pa'i chos thams cad kyi chos nyid de, dgag bya bden grub bkag tsam la 'jog zhes pa'i don yin pas so
gru.english: It does, but not in the way that you say it does. Empty space consists of the simple denial of tangibles in the form of concrete physicality; while the real nature of every entity in the universe is similar—but only in the sense that they are established through the simple denial of the object we refuse: anything that could exist in truth. This is the only point that the metaphor is meant to convey. 13) The argument that all mental states following the analysis are a meditation on the way things really are

gru.acip: YANG CUNG MI 'THAD DE, LAS DANG PO BAS ZHI GNAS MA THOB TSUN LTA BA DNGOS GZHI'I TSE BAR BAR DU CUNG ZAD RE DPYAD NAS 'JOG SGOM BYED PA YIN GYI, 'JOG SGOM KHO NAS LHAG MTHONG MI 'GRUB LA, DPYAD PA HA CANG MANG NA, RGOD PA SKYE BAS ZHI GNAS MI 'GRUB PA'I PHYIR RO,,
gru.wylie: yang cung mi 'thad de, las dang po bas zhi gnas ma thob tshun lta ba dngos gzhi'i tshe bar bar du cung zad re dpyad nas 'jog sgom byed pa yin gyi, 'jog sgom kho nas lhag mthong mi 'grub la, dpyad pa ha cang mang na, rgod pa skye bas zhi gnas mi 'grub pa'i phyir ro
gru.english: These positions though are, again, just a bit defective. Starting off with raw beginners, who have yet to achieve meditative quietude, then during the main stage of the practice they're going to have to be doing a fixed meditation where—from time to time—they drop back into a bit of analytical meditation. It's not the case though that you can achieve what we call “special insight” into the real nature of things only through the fixed type of meditation. On the other hand, if the time spent in analysis at this point is too much, you will start to experience mental agitation inside of your meditation, and never reach the state of quietude. Our own position

gru.acip: ,BSTAN PA'I SNYING PO BDAG MED LTA BA NYID, ,GRUB MTHA' RNAM BZHI'I DBYE BA DANG 'BREL BAR, ,RJE BTZUN CHOS KYI RGYAL PO BTZONG KHA PA'I, ,DGONGS PA JI BZHIN MDOR BSDUS BDAG GIS BSHAD,
gru.wylie: bstan pa'i snying po bdag med lta ba nyid, ,grub mtha' rnam bzhi'i dbye ba dang 'brel bar, ,rje btsun chos kyi rgyal po btsong kha pa'i, ,dgongs pa ji bzhin mdor bsdus bdag gis bshad
gru.english: Thus then have I given My brief and summary explanation Of that heart of all the teachings, Which is none other than the view That says nothing is itself. I have done so by relating The parts of my explanation To the division of all the schools Into the major four; And I have followed The true thought of That high and holy one, The King of the Dharma, Tsongkapa.

gru.acip: (,CES GRUB MTHA' BZHI DANG 'BREL BAR LTA BA'I RIM PA RNAM PAR BSHAD PA THAR LAM GSAL BYED CES BYA BA 'DI NI,
gru.wylie: (,ces grub mtha' bzhi dang 'brel bar lta ba'i rim pa rnam par bshad pa thar lam gsal byed ces bya ba 'di ni
gru.english: And so there it is—Light on the Path to Freedom, an explication of the steps for developing an accurate view of reality, based on the beliefs of the four great schools of ancient Buddhism. And here is the story of how I came to write it.

gru.acip: RIGS PA'I TSUL LA BLO GROS KYI SNANG BA CUNG ZAD THOB PA SH'AKYA'I DGE SLONG GRAGS PA BSHAD SGRUB KYIS, SHING SBRUL NAG PA ZLA BA'I YAR TSES LA SBYAR BA STE, 'DIS KYANG RJE BLA MA'I BSTAN PA LA PHAN THOGS PAR GYUR CIG
gru.wylie: rigs pa'i tshul la blo gros kyi snang ba cung zad thob pa shAkya'i dge slong grags pa bshad sgrub kyis, shing sbrul nag pa zla ba'i yar tshes la sbyar ba ste, 'dis kyang rje bla ma'i bstan pa la phan thogs par gyur cig
gru.english: And so it is that I—a Buddhist monk and follower of Shakyamuni Buddha by the name of Drakpa Shedrup, who has been able to reach a tiny bit of understanding in the ways of reasoning—have undertaken to compose the work here, in the waxing of the moon during the month of Chitra, in the Wood Snake year. And I pray that it will be of some help towards keeping the teachings of Je Tsongkapa here in this world.

gru.acip: [N10] ,STONG ZHING DNGOS PO MA GRUB PAS, ,SGYU MA'I DNGOS PO SKYE BA MED, ,DE BZHIN YOD PA MA YIN TE, ,DNGOS PO RMI LAM LTA BU YIN,
gru.wylie: [n10] ,stong zhing dngos po ma grub pas, ,sgyu ma'i dngos po skye ba med, ,de bzhin yod pa ma yin te, ,dngos po rmi lam lta bu yin
gru.english: Things that are only illusion Can never start at all; For they are empty, And cannot be real. Everything else Is just the same; They are like a dream, And cannot exist at all.

gru.acip: [N58] ,DE LTAR SHES RAB DAG PA YIS, ,RANG GI NGO BO DON DAM 'DI, ,SHIN TU YANG NI GRUB PA NA, ,BRTAG PA'I GZHAN DNGOS 'BYUNG MA YIN,
gru.wylie: [n58] ,de ltar shes rab dag pa yis, ,rang gi ngo bo don dam 'di, ,shin tu yang ni grub pa na, ,brtag pa'i gzhan dngos 'byung ma yin
gru.english: Anyone who learns to use Pure wisdom in this way Then proves to themselves, And perfectly, The ultimate nature Of the wisdom itself; At this point there can come None of those other entities— The ones that pictures create.

gru.acip: [N59] ,'PHAGS PA KLU SGRUB KYI ZHAL SNGA NAS MDZAD PA'I BSGOM PA'I RIM PA RDZOGS SO,,
gru.wylie: [n59] ,'phags pa klu sgrub kyi zhal snga nas mdzad pa'i bsgom pa'i rim pa rdzogs so
gru.english: This then completes The Stages of Meditation, which has come from the holy lips of Nagarjuna—The Arya.

gru.acip: DE LTA BAS NA BCOM LDAN 'DAS KYIS RNAL 'BYOR PA RNAMS KYI DMIGS PA'I DNGOS PO BZHI BSTAN TE, RNAM PAR MI RTOG PA'I GZUGS BRNYAN DANG, RNAM PAR RTOG PA DANG BCAS PA'I GZUGS BRNYAN DANG, DNGOS PO'I MTHA' DANG, DGOS PA YONGS SU GRUB PA'O,,
gru.wylie: de lta bas na bcom ldan 'das kyis rnal 'byor pa rnams kyi dmigs pa'i dngos po bzhi bstan te, rnam par mi rtog pa'i gzugs brnyan dang, rnam par rtog pa dang bcas pa'i gzugs brnyan dang, dngos po'i mtha' dang, dgos pa yongs su grub pa'o
gru.english: Thus it is that the Conqueror has taught us four different points that deep practitioners should focus upon: the reflection of going beyond all thoughts; the reflection where we still have thoughts; the end of all things; and the final accomplishment of the goal.

gru.acip: DES NA SMAN BCUD KYIS LEN ZA BA BZHIN DU BSGOM PA'I LAM GYIS SA LHAG MA RNAMS SU RIM GYIS SHIN TU RAB TU RNAM PAR DAG PA'I SKAD CIG BYUNG BAS GNAS GYUR NAS, GANG GI TSE SGRIB PA MA LUS PA SPANGS PA'I MTSAN NYID DGOS PA YONGS SU RDZOGS PAR GYUR PA DE'I TSE SANGS RGYAS KYI SA LA YE SHES DE NYID DGOS PA YONGS SU GRUB PA LA DMIGS PA ZHES BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: des na sman bcud kyis len za ba bzhin du bsgom pa'i lam gyis sa lhag ma rnams su rim gyis shin tu rab tu rnam par dag pa'i skad cig byung bas gnas gyur nas, gang gi tshe sgrib pa ma lus pa spangs pa'i mtshan nyid dgos pa yongs su rdzogs par gyur pa de'i tshe sangs rgyas kyi sa la ye shes de nyid dgos pa yongs su grub pa la dmigs pa zhes bya'o
gru.english: And then it's just the same as where we learn to live on nothing more than a tiny pill made from the essence of some medicinal plant. Utilizing the path of habituation, we work our way gradually through the rest of the bodhisattva levels, transforming things with mere instants of absolute purity. At some point, we fulfill the goal characterized by eliminating each and every one of our obstacles. When we do reach this juncture, we say that this same state of wisdom, at the level of an Enlightened Being, is “focused upon final accomplishment of the goal.”

gru.acip: DE LTA BU 'DIS CI BSTAN PA YIN ZHE NA, ZHI GNAS DANG LHAG MTHONG GOMS PAR BYAS PAS DNGOS PO'I MTHA' RTOGS PAR 'GYUR TE, DES SGRIB PA MTHA' DAG SPONG BA'I MTSAN NYID DGOS PA YONGS SU GRUB PA 'THOB BO,,
gru.wylie: de lta bu 'dis ci bstan pa yin zhe na, zhi gnas dang lhag mthong goms par byas pas dngos po'i mtha' rtogs par 'gyur te, des sgrib pa mtha' dag spong ba'i mtshan nyid dgos pa yongs su grub pa 'thob bo
gru.english: “And what is it,” you may ask, “that reveals these things to us?” It is when we engage in the practices of quietude and insight that we come to this realization of the ultimate end of things. It is these practices which enable us to reach the accomplishment of the final goal, characterized as it is by having eliminated each and every obstacle there is.

gru.acip: GANG DE GNYIS LA MI SGOM PA DE DAG NI DNGOS PO'I MTHA' YANG MI RTOGS, DGOS PA YONGS SU GRUB PAR YANG MI 'GYUR RO ZHES BSTAN PAR 'GYUR RO,,
gru.wylie: gang de gnyis la mi sgom pa de dag ni dngos po'i mtha' yang mi rtogs, dgos pa yongs su grub par yang mi 'gyur ro zhes bstan par 'gyur ro
gru.english: What this is also telling us is that—if we fail to meditate upon these two—then we will never come to that realization of the end of all things; and then neither will we ever attain that final goal.

gru.acip: DBUGS PHYI NANG DU RGYU BA YANG SGRA CAN DANG, RNGAM PA DANG, DBUGS RGOD PA CAN DU MI BTANG GI ,CI NAS KYANG MI TSOR BAR DAL BU DAL BUS LHUN GYIS GRUB PA'I TSUL GYIS DBUGS NANG DU RNGUB PA DANG PHYIR 'BYUNG BAR 'GYUR BA DE LTAR BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: dbugs phyi nang du rgyu ba yang sgra can dang, rngam pa dang, dbugs rgod pa can du mi btang gi ,ci nas kyang mi tshor bar dal bu dal bus lhun gyis grub pa'i tshul gyis dbugs nang du rngub pa dang phyir 'byung bar 'gyur ba de ltar bya'o
gru.english: Watch your breathing. The breath should not make any sound, as it flows out and in. Don't start panting or breathing irregularly. That is, you should do your best to invite the breath in, and then send it out to the world, completely unnoticed: let it travel in a leisurely and spontaneous way. Starting from a visualization

gru.acip: DE LA RNAL 'BYOR PAS THOG MAR DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA'I SKU GZUGS JI LTAR MTHONG BA DANG JI LTAR THOS PA LA SEMS GTAD DE BZHAG NAS ZHI GNAS BSGRUB PAR BYA STE,
gru.wylie: de la rnal 'byor pas thog mar de bzhin gshegs pa'i sku gzugs ji ltar mthong ba dang ji ltar thos pa la sems gtad de bzhag nas zhi gnas bsgrub par bya ste
gru.english: Now in the beginning, the deep practitioner should focus their mind on the holy body of the One Gone Thus, with the feeling that they could actually see their form and hear their words. This is how we build up our capacity for quietude.

gru.acip: RNAM PA GCIG TU NA RNAM PA JI SNYED KYIS CHOS THAMS CAD BSDUS PAR GYUR PA DE LA SEMS BZHAG STE BYING BA DANG RGOD PA LA SOGS PA RAB TU ZHI BAR ZHI GNAS BSGRUB PAR BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: rnam pa gcig tu na rnam pa ji snyed kyis chos thams cad bsdus par gyur pa de la sems bzhag ste bying ba dang rgod pa la sogs pa rab tu zhi bar zhi gnas bsgrub par bya'o
gru.english: Set your mind here, on the aspect of every existing entity in the universe combined into a single aspect. Put a final stop to feelings like mental dullness and agitation, and thus attain the state of quietude.

gru.acip: DE DAG GI PHYIN CI LOG BSAL BA'I PHYIR DE DAG LA SNYING RJE CHEN PO MNGON DU BYAS LA, RNAL 'BYOR PA'I ZHI GNAS GRUB NAS DE KHO NA RTOGS PAR BYA BA'I PHYIR, DE NAS LHAG MTHONG BSGOM PAR BYA STE, YANG DAG PAR SO SOR RTOG PA NI LHAG MTHONG ZHES BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: de dag gi phyin ci log bsal ba'i phyir de dag la snying rje chen po mngon du byas la, rnal 'byor pa'i zhi gnas grub nas de kho na rtogs par bya ba'i phyir, de nas lhag mthong bsgom par bya ste, yang dag par so sor rtog pa ni lhag mthong zhes bya'o
gru.english: Bring up in your heart feelings of great compassion for these infants, so that you can begin the work of helping them clear away their mistaken impressions. Once the deep practitioner has attained quietude, then they can begin meditating upon insight so that they can come to the realization of suchness. This pure analysis of entities is what we call “insight.”

gru.acip: DE'I TSE ZHI GNAS DANG LHAG MTHONG ZUNG DU 'BREL PA'I LAM GRUB PA YIN PAR RIG PAR BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: de'i tshe zhi gnas dang lhag mthong zung du 'brel pa'i lam grub pa yin par rig par bya'o
gru.english: You should understand that—at this juncture—you have achieved that path where quietude and insight are joined together, as one.

gru.acip: DE NAS 'DOD PAR GYUR PAS BRTZON 'GRUS RTZOM MO, DE NAS BRTZON 'GRUS LA BRTEN PAS LUS DANG SEMS LAS SU RUNG BA NYID DU BYED DO,,
gru.wylie: de nas 'dod par gyur pas brtson 'grus rtsom mo, de nas brtson 'grus la brten pas lus dang sems las su rung ba nyid du byed do
gru.english: This desire then inspires us to undertake [3] efforts to meditate. And then—due to our efforts—[4] our body and mind become especially suited to the task at hand.

gru.acip: SGYU MA MKHAN BZHIN DU BLO PHYIN CI LOG TU MA GYUR PAS BSOD NAMS DANG YE SHES KYI TSOGS RGYA CHEN PO YONGS SU SGRUB PA DE DAG NI DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA'I GO 'PHANG BRNYES NAS 'KHOR BA NA 'GRO BA MA LUS PA LA PHAN PA DANG BDE BA'I RNAM PA THAMS CAD YANG DAG PAR SGRUB CING BZHUGS SO,,
gru.wylie: sgyu ma mkhan bzhin du blo phyin ci log tu ma gyur pas bsod nams dang ye shes kyi tshogs rgya chen po yongs su sgrub pa de dag ni de bzhin gshegs pa'i go 'phang brnyes nas 'khor ba na 'gro ba ma lus pa la phan pa dang bde ba'i rnam pa thams cad yang dag par sgrub cing bzhugs so
gru.english: Like the magician who directs the magic show, they are not fooled; and so they are able to accomplish massive collections of both merit and wisdom. People like this attain the level of the Ones Who Have Gone That Way; they live every minute of their life accomplishing each and every form of help and happiness for each and every being caught in the cycle of pain.

gru.acip: SEMS CAN THAMS CAD KYI NYE BAR 'TSO BAR YANG 'GYUR RO, ,DE LTA BAS NA SEMS CAN MTHA' DAG LA PHAN PA DANG BDE BA BSKYED PAR 'DOD PA MI GNAS PA'I MYA NGAN LAS 'DAS PA THOB PAR 'DOD PA DAG GIS BSOD NAMS DANG YE SHES KYI TSOGS RGYA CHEN PO SGRUB PA LA DUS THAMS CAD DU MNGON PAR BRTZON PAR BYA'O SNYAM DU BSAM MO,
gru.wylie: sems can thams cad kyi nye bar 'tsho bar yang 'gyur ro, ,de lta bas na sems can mtha' dag la phan pa dang bde ba bskyed par 'dod pa mi gnas pa'i mya ngan las 'das pa thob par 'dod pa dag gis bsod nams dang ye shes kyi tshogs rgya chen po sgrub pa la dus thams cad du mngon par brtson par bya'o snyam du bsam mo
gru.english: They sustain, as well, every living being there is. People like this, therefore, seek to attain the nirvana where they no longer stay—a nirvana where they can create help and happiness for every living creature in the universe. These ones accomplish a tremendous accumulation of both merit and wisdom. Decide, deep within your meditation, that you too will make efforts in every moment of the day to do the same.

gru.acip: 'PHAGS PA DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA SKYE BA 'BYUNG BA'I MDO LAS KYANG BKA' STZAL TE, GANG DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA RNAMS 'BYUNG BA DE NI RGYU GCIG PU MA YIN NO, ,DE CI'I PHYIR ZHE NA, KYE RGYAL BA'I SRAS DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA RNAMS NI YANG DAG PAR 'GRUB PA'I RGYU TSAD MED PA 'BUM PHRAG BCUS YANG DAG PAR 'GRUB STE, BCU GANG ZHE NA, 'DI LTA STE, BSOD NAMS DANG YE SHES KYI TSOGS TSAD MED PAS MI NGOMS PA YANG DAG PAR 'GRUB PA'I RGYU DANG ZHES BYA BA LA SOGS PA RGYAS PAR 'BYUNG NGO,,
gru.wylie: 'phags pa de bzhin gshegs pa skye ba 'byung ba'i mdo las kyang bka' stsal te, gang de bzhin gshegs pa rnams 'byung ba de ni rgyu gcig pu ma yin no, ,de ci'i phyir zhe na, kye rgyal ba'i sras de bzhin gshegs pa rnams ni yang dag par 'grub pa'i rgyu tshad med pa 'bum phrag bcus yang dag par 'grub ste, bcu gang zhe na, 'di lta ste, bsod nams dang ye shes kyi tshogs tshad med pas mi ngoms pa yang dag par 'grub pa'i rgyu dang zhes bya ba la sogs pa rgyas par 'byung ngo
gru.english: The Scripture on How the Birth of Those Gone Thus Occurs concurs, in great detail, with lines like the following: It is not that the Ones Gone Thus could ever come into being from but a single cause. And why is that? Ah, wonders, you daughters and sons of the Victorious Ones! The state of One Gone Thus is achieved, in its perfection, through ten times a hundred thousand groups of causes that we call “infinites.” And what do these ten consist of? It's like this: each cause is itself accomplished through the relentless pursuit of collections of merit and wisdom which are themselves beyond all measure.

gru.acip: DE NAS STONG PA NYID DANG SNYING RJE'I SNYING PO CAN BLA NA MED PA'I BYANG CHUB TU YONGS SU BSNGOS PA'I SBYIN PA LA SOGS PA'I BSOD NAMS KYI TSOGS SGRUB PA LA MNGON PAR BRTZON PAR BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: de nas stong pa nyid dang snying rje'i snying po can bla na med pa'i byang chub tu yongs su bsngos pa'i sbyin pa la sogs pa'i bsod nams kyi tshogs sgrub pa la mngon par brtson par bya'o
gru.english: Then go and apply great efforts in accomplishing the collection of good deeds—giving and the rest, with emptiness and compassion at their core—deeply dedicated to matchless enlightenment. The foolish mistake of trying to meditate on nothing

gru.acip: DE LTA BAS NA BDAG NI SHES RAB CHUNG NGU, BRTZON 'GRUS CHUNG NGU STE, MANG DU THOS PA YONGS SU TSOL MI NUS SO ZHES DE SKAD BYA BA'I RIGS KYI, BCOM LDAN 'DAS KYIS MANG DU THOS PA BSNGAGS PA'I PHYIR DUS THAMS CAD DU YANG DE SPANG BAR NI MI RIGS SO,,
gru.wylie: de lta bas na bdag ni shes rab chung ngu, brtson 'grus chung ngu ste, mang du thos pa yongs su tshol mi nus so zhes de skad bya ba'i rigs kyi, bcom ldan 'das kyis mang du thos pa bsngags pa'i phyir dus thams cad du yang de spang bar ni mi rigs so
gru.english: And so perhaps it may be alright to say, “I am a person of little wisdom, and little effort; as such, I am unable to spend much of my time seeking more learning.” But given that the Conqueror himself has lavished such praise on the act of trying to accumulate great learning, it would never—at any moment in one's life—be alright to abandon such learning.

gru.acip: YANG DE NYID LAS JI LTAR NA BRTZON 'GRUS DANG LDAN PA LAGS, BKA' STZAL PA, GANG GI TSE THAMS CAD MKHYEN PA'I YE SHES LA BRTAGS NAS MA DMIGS PA'O ZHES GSUNGS SO,,
gru.wylie: yang de nyid las ji ltar na brtson 'grus dang ldan pa lags, bka' stsal pa, gang gi tshe thams cad mkhyen pa'i ye shes la brtags nas ma dmigs pa'o zhes gsungs so
gru.english: The same sutra also says: What does it mean to be possessed of effort? I will tell you: it is when you examine the state of mind of knowing all things, and find nothing there.

gru.acip: CI STE NYON MONGS PA ZAD PAR BYA BA'I PHYIR LHAG MTHONG LA BRTEN PAR BYA'O SNYAM DU SEMS NA NI DE'I TSE NYON MONGS PA ZAD PA NYID KYIS GROL BAR 'GRUB STE, LAS ZAD PAR BYA BA'I TSIG DON MED PAR 'GYUR RO,,
gru.wylie: ci ste nyon mongs pa zad par bya ba'i phyir lhag mthong la brten par bya'o snyam du sems na ni de'i tshe nyon mongs pa zad pa nyid kyis grol bar 'grub ste, las zad par bya ba'i tshig don med par 'gyur ro
gru.english: So suppose now that you think to yourself, “Well then, I am going to start relying on the practice of insight, in order to put a stop to everything connected to the negative emotions.” In this case, you will come to attain liberation, simply because everything to do with the negative emotions will come to a stop. And then it becomes pointless to talk about wearing out all your karmas.

gru.acip: DE SKAD 'PHAGS PA SA BCU PA LAS KYANG BKA' STZAL TE, DGE BA BCU'I LAS KYI LAM DE DAG NYID BSNGO BA LA SOGS PA YONGS SU SBYANG BA BYAS PA'I BYE BRAG GIS NI NYAN THOS DANG, RANG SANGS RGYAS DANG, BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA' DANG, SANGS RGYAS NYID SGRUB PAR BYED DO ZHES 'BYUNG NGO,,
gru.wylie: de skad 'phags pa sa bcu pa las kyang bka' stsal te, dge ba bcu'i las kyi lam de dag nyid bsngo ba la sogs pa yongs su sbyang ba byas pa'i bye brag gis ni nyan thos dang, rang sangs rgyas dang, byang chub sems dpa' dang, sangs rgyas nyid sgrub par byed do zhes 'byung ngo
gru.english: The same sentiment has been expressed in the exalted sutra entitled The Ten Levels: Certain details of how the one karmic path of the ten good deeds is followed—that is, whether it is dedicated to a higher purpose and so on—determine the extent to which it is purified, and whether it will accomplish the goal of a listener; or that of a self-made buddha; or of a bodhisattva; or of an Enlightened Being themselves.

gru.acip: PHUNG PO GSUM PA'I YONGS SU BSNGO BA LAS KYANG BKA' STZAL PA, GANG BDAG GIS SBYIN PA DANG, TSUL KHRIMS DANG, BZOD PA DANG, BRTZON 'GRUS DANG, BSAM GTAN DANG, SHES RAB MNYAM PA NYID DU MA 'TSAL NAS DMIGS PAR LTUNG BAS SBYIN PA LA BRTZAL BA DANG, TSUL KHRIMS MCHOG TU 'DZIN PAS TSUL KHRIMS SRUNG BA DANG, BDAG DANG GZHAN DU 'DU SHES PAS BZOD PA BSGOMS PA LA SOGS PA GANG LAG PA DE DAG THAMS CAD SO SOR BSHAGS PAR BGYI'O ZHES 'BYUNG BA GANG YIN PA
gru.wylie: phung po gsum pa'i yongs su bsngo ba las kyang bka' stsal pa, gang bdag gis sbyin pa dang, tshul khrims dang, bzod pa dang, brtson 'grus dang, bsam gtan dang, shes rab mnyam pa nyid du ma 'tshal nas dmigs par ltung bas sbyin pa la brtsal ba dang, tshul khrims mchog tu 'dzin pas tshul khrims srung ba dang, bdag dang gzhan du 'du shes pas bzod pa bsgoms pa la sogs pa gang lag pa de dag thams cad so sor bshags par bgyi'o zhes 'byung ba gang yin pa
gru.english: The Dedication of the Three Heaps also says: Suppose a person fails to seek the absolute sameness within the acts of giving; the pursuit of an ethical life; refusing to be angered; joyful effort; meditation; and wisdom. That is, suppose they slip into the objects of perception, and then make efforts in giving; or they hold morality to be supreme, and then protect that morality; or they engage in the act of patience, even as they distinguish between self and others—or anything else of the like. You should understand that any such act is one that you would have to confess as a misdeed.

gru.acip: MDO KUN LAS BTUS PA LAS KYANG, PHA ROL TU PHYIN PA DRUG LA SOGS PA SGRUB PA DANG LDAN PA'I BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA' RNAMS NI DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA'I RDZU 'PHRUL GYIS 'GRO BA YIN NO ZHES BSNGAGS TE, DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA'I RDZU 'PHRUL GYIS 'GRO BA LAS MGYOGS PA NI GZHAN MED DO,,
gru.wylie: mdo kun las btus pa las kyang, pha rol tu phyin pa drug la sogs pa sgrub pa dang ldan pa'i byang chub sems dpa' rnams ni de bzhin gshegs pa'i rdzu 'phrul gyis 'gro ba yin no zhes bsngags te, de bzhin gshegs pa'i rdzu 'phrul gyis 'gro ba las mgyogs pa ni gzhan med do
gru.english: The Compendium of the Sutras also says: Bodhisattvas who possess the achievement of practices such as the six perfections are traveling with the miracle powers of One who has Gone That Way. This is high praise, since there is no faster form of travel than using the miracle powers of One Gone Thus.

gru.acip: DE SKAD 'PHAGS PA CHOS THAMS CAD SHIN TU RGYAS PA LAS KYANG BKA' STZAL TE, BYAMS PA BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA' RNAMS KYI PHA ROL TU PHYIN PA DRUG YANG DAG PAR BSGRUBS PA 'DI NI RDZOGS PA'I BYANG CHUB KYI PHYIR YIN NA, DE LA YANG MI BLUN PO DAG 'DI SKAD DU BYANG CHUB SEMS DPAS SHES RAB KYI PHA ROL TU PHYIN PA KHO NA LA BSLAB PAR BYA'I, PHA ROL TU PHYIN PA LHAG MA RNAMS KYIS CI ZHIG BYA ZHES ZER ZHING, DE DAG PHA ROL TU PHYIN PA GZHAN DAG LA SUN 'BYIN PAR SEMS SO,,
gru.wylie: de skad 'phags pa chos thams cad shin tu rgyas pa las kyang bka' stsal te, byams pa byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi pha rol tu phyin pa drug yang dag par bsgrubs pa 'di ni rdzogs pa'i byang chub kyi phyir yin na, de la yang mi blun po dag 'di skad du byang chub sems dpas shes rab kyi pha rol tu phyin pa kho na la bslab par bya'i, pha rol tu phyin pa lhag ma rnams kyis ci zhig bya zhes zer zhing, de dag pha rol tu phyin pa gzhan dag la sun 'byin par sems so
gru.english: We see the same thought expressed in places like this one, from the exalted scripture entitled The Incredible Extant of Everything There Is: O Loving One, the way that the bodhisattvas practice the six perfections is all for the purpose of attaining a total enlightenment. And yet some fools say things like: “Oh, bodhisattvas only practice the one perfection—the perfection of wisdom. What use do they have with the other perfections?” In speaking thus, they propose to abolish all the other perfections.

gru.acip: BCOM LDAN 'DAS KYIS BKA' STZAL PA, MA PHAM PA KHYOD KYIS KYANG BSKAL PA DRUG CUR SBYIN PA'I PHA ROL TU PHYIN PA YANG DAG PAR BSGRUBS, DE BZHIN DU BSKAL PA DRUG CUR SHES RAB KYI PHA ROL TU PHYIN PA'I BAR DU YANG DAG PAR BSGRUBS NA, DE LA MI BLUN PO DAG 'DI SKAD CES TSUL GCIG KHO NAS BYANG CHUB STE, 'DI LTA STE, STONG PA NYID KYI TSUL GYIS SO ZHES ZER TE, DE DAG NI SPYOD PA YONGS SU MA DAG PAR 'GYUR RO ZHES BYA BA LA SOGS PA 'BYUNG NGO,,
gru.wylie: bcom ldan 'das kyis bka' stsal pa, ma pham pa khyod kyis kyang bskal pa drug cur sbyin pa'i pha rol tu phyin pa yang dag par bsgrubs, de bzhin du bskal pa drug cur shes rab kyi pha rol tu phyin pa'i bar du yang dag par bsgrubs na, de la mi blun po dag 'di skad ces tshul gcig kho nas byang chub ste, 'di lta ste, stong pa nyid kyi tshul gyis so zhes zer te, de dag ni spyod pa yongs su ma dag par 'gyur ro zhes bya ba la sogs pa 'byung ngo
gru.english: And then the Conqueror said: Undefeatable One, you practiced the perfection of giving for sixty million years. In the same way, you practiced the perfection of wisdom over a period of sixty million years. And yet there are some foolish people who say that there is only one way you can use to reach enlightenment; and they claim that the way you need to use is but emptiness. Their behavior is completely impure.

gru.acip: DE LTA BAS NA SLOB DPON KLU SGRUB KYI ZHAL SNGA NAS KYI MDO KUN LAS BTUS PA LAS BSHAD PA, THABS MKHAS PA DANG BRAL BA'I BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA' CHOS ZAB MO NYID LA MNGON PAR BRTZON PAR MI BYA'O ZHES 'BYUNG NGO,,
gru.wylie: de lta bas na slob dpon klu sgrub kyi zhal snga nas kyi mdo kun las btus pa las bshad pa, thabs mkhas pa dang bral ba'i byang chub sems dpa' chos zab mo nyid la mngon par brtson par mi bya'o zhes 'byung ngo
gru.english: This is why the following is spoken from the holy lips of Master Nagarjuna, in his Compendium of the Sutras: A bodhisattva who is not utilizing spiritual strategies should never make efforts in that most profound of objects.

gru.acip: 'DIR YANG 'PHAGS PA DRI MA MED PAR GRAGS PAS BSTAN PA LA SOGS PA KHUNGS BSTAN CING BSHAD KYI, DE YANG SLOB DPON KLU SGRUB KYI ZHAL SNGA NAS KYI BKA' NI MA YIN NO,,
gru.wylie: 'dir yang 'phags pa dri ma med par grags pas bstan pa la sogs pa khungs bstan cing bshad kyi, de yang slob dpon klu sgrub kyi zhal snga nas kyi bka' ni ma yin no
gru.english: This statement is made and explained according to authentic sources such as the exalted teaching given by Vimala Kirti; it is not Master Nagarjuna saying something of his own.

gru.acip: YANG BKA' STZAL PA, DE LTAR NA BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA'I DMIGS PA GANG CI YANG RUNG, DE THAMS CAD NI THAMS CAD MKHYEN PA'I YE SHES MNGON PAR BSGRUB PA'I PHYIR MI GNAS PA MED DO,,
gru.wylie: yang bka' stsal pa, de ltar na byang chub sems dpa'i dmigs pa gang ci yang rung, de thams cad ni thams cad mkhyen pa'i ye shes mngon par bsgrub pa'i phyir mi gnas pa med do
gru.english: It is further stated: You can take any object at all that a bodhisattva is looking at; there is not a single one among all of them in which the bodhisattva does not reside, for the purpose of attaining that wisdom which knows all things.

gru.acip: DE BZHIN DU MDO SDE MTHA' YAS PA LAS BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA' RNAMS KYI THABS DANG SHES RAB KYI TSUL SGRUB PA BSTAN TO,,
gru.wylie: de bzhin du mdo sde mtha' yas pa las byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi thabs dang shes rab kyi tshul sgrub pa bstan to
gru.english: We see as well countless other scriptures that describe how bodhisattvas master the ways of wisdom combined with spiritual strategies.

gru.acip: DE LA BDAG NYID SBYIN PA LA SOGS PA BSOD NAMS KYI TSOGS LA BRTZON 'GRUS RTZOM MI NUS SU ZIN KYANG, GZHAN DAG LA DE SKAD DU BSTAN PA NI MI RIGS SO, ,DE LTAR BYAS NA BDAG DANG GZHAN LA 'KHU BA BYAS PAR 'GYUR RO,,
gru.wylie: de la bdag nyid sbyin pa la sogs pa bsod nams kyi tshogs la brtson 'grus rtsom mi nus su zin kyang, gzhan dag la de skad du bstan pa ni mi rigs so, ,de ltar byas na bdag dang gzhan la 'khu ba byas par 'gyur ro
gru.english: Now you yourself may be a person who is unable to put out the effort required to complete the collection of merit—with deeds like giving and the rest. But it's wrong then to teach others to do the same thing. If you did, then you would be striving against both yourself and other people, at the same time.

gru.acip: DE LTAR BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA' CI NAS KYANG YANG DAG PAR SO SOR BRTAG PAR BYA ZHING SBYIN PA LA SOGS PA BSOD NAMS KYI TSOGS MTHA' DAG BSGRUB PAR BYA ZHES RIGS PA DANG LUNG GIS BSTAN PA YIN NO,,
gru.wylie: de ltar byang chub sems dpa' ci nas kyang yang dag par so sor brtag par bya zhing sbyin pa la sogs pa bsod nams kyi tshogs mtha' dag bsgrub par bya zhes rigs pa dang lung gis bstan pa yin no
gru.english: And so we can say that we are instructed, by both reason and by scriptural authority, that as bodhisattvas we should—no matter what—indeed engage in a careful examination of things, and in doing everything we can to accomplish every detail of the accumulation of merit.

gru.acip: DE'I PHYIR RTOG PA DANG LDAN PAS THOS PA NYUNG BA MNGON PA'I NGA RGYAL CAN RNAMS KYI TSIG DUG BZHIN DU SPANGS LA, SLOB DPON KLU SGRUB LA SOGS PA SKYE BO MKHAS PA'I TSIG BDUD RTZI'I RJES SU 'JUG PAS
gru.wylie: de'i phyir rtog pa dang ldan pas thos pa nyung ba mngon pa'i nga rgyal can rnams kyi tshig dug bzhin du spangs la, slob dpon klu sgrub la sogs pa skye bo mkhas pa'i tshig bdud rtsi'i rjes su 'jug pas
gru.english: Given all this, those of you who can understand things should take the words of those arrogant ones of little learning, and throw them out—as you would a bottle of poison. And then become a regular user of that deathless nectar provided to us by people who are true masters: people like Nagarjuna and the rest. Come and rescue every living creature there is

gru.acip: CHAGS PA MED PA DANG, THOGS PA MED PA'I YE SHES THOB NAS YON TAN MA LUS PA'I GZHI SANGS RGYAS KYI SA THOB PAR 'GYUR TE, DGOS PA YONGS SU GRUB PA LA DMIGS PA YANG THOB PA YIN NO,,
gru.wylie: chags pa med pa dang, thogs pa med pa'i ye shes thob nas yon tan ma lus pa'i gzhi sangs rgyas kyi sa thob par 'gyur te, dgos pa yongs su grub pa la dmigs pa yang thob pa yin no
gru.english: You will go beyond all desire, and attain unstoppable wisdom. With that, you will reach that state of every good quality in the universe: you will come to the level of a Buddha. You will also attain the vision—you will look upon the object—of the ability to fulfil all needs.

gru.acip: [T1] , ,THEG PA GSUM GYI YON TAN THAMS CAD ZHI LHAG DNGOS SAM RJES MTHUN GYI SGOM GANG YANG RUNG BA'I 'BRAS BUR GSUNGS SHING, ZHI GNAS GRUB NAS DGE SBYOR GANG BYAS STOBS CHE BA SOGS PHAN YON DANG DGOS PA SHIN TU CHE BAS, THAR PA DON DU GNYER BA'I RNAL 'BYOR PA RNAMS KYIS ZHI GNAS SGRUB PA GAL CHE ZHING,
gru.wylie: [t1] , ,theg pa gsum gyi yon tan thams cad zhi lhag dngos sam rjes mthun gyi sgom gang yang rung ba'i 'bras bur gsungs shing, zhi gnas grub nas dge sbyor gang byas stobs che ba sogs phan yon dang dgos pa shin tu che bas, thar pa don du gnyer ba'i rnal 'byor pa rnams kyis zhi gnas sgrub pa gal che zhing
gru.english: It has been spoken that each and every high spiritual quality of all three ways is a result of meditation, either in the form of quietude [which is called shamatha in Sanskrit], or some state which is close to it. The benefits of meditation are many, beginning with the fact that once you have attained quietude then any virtuous practice you undertake becomes extremely powerful. It is an absolute necessity, and so attaining the state of quietude is extremely important for any deep practitioner who really hopes to reach freedom.

gru.acip: [T4] GNYIS PA'I GNYEN POR DRAN PA, GSUM PA'I GNYEN POR SHES BZHIN, BZHI BA'I GNYEN POR 'DU BYED PA, LNGA PA'I GNYEN POR BTANG SNYOMS TE GNYEN PO 'DU BYED BRGYAD BSTEN NAS SGRUB DGOS LA,
gru.wylie: [t4] gnyis pa'i gnyen por dran pa, gsum pa'i gnyen por shes bzhin, bzhi ba'i gnyen por 'du byed pa, lnga pa'i gnyen por btang snyoms te gnyen po 'du byed brgyad bsten nas sgrub dgos la
gru.english: The correction for the second obstacle is to bring the mind back to the object. The correction for the third problem is watchfulness, and the correction for the fourth is taking the necessary action. The correction for the fifth problem is to leave well enough alone. Thus one must attain quietude through undertaking eight different corrective actions.

gru.acip: [T5] DE DAG KYANG SEMS GNAS DGUR PHYE BA DANG, DE RNAMS STOBS DRUG GIS 'GRUB LUGS DANG, YID BYED BZHIR SDUD TSUL RNAMS SHES NA TING 'DZIN SKYON MED BDE BLAG TU 'GRUB PAR GSUNGS PAS,
gru.wylie: [t5] de dag kyang sems gnas dgur phye ba dang, de rnams stobs drug gis 'grub lugs dang, yid byed bzhir sdud tshul rnams shes na ting 'dzin skyon med bde blag tu 'grub par gsungs pas
gru.english: It is further stated that if you come to understand how these can be divided into nine mental states, and how these in turn are achieved through six different powers and grouped into four modes of focus, then you can quite easily attain a state of single-pointed concentration which is perfect.

gru.acip: [T9] DE DAG STOBS DRUG GIS 'GRUB LUGS NI, BLA MA'I GDAMS NGAG THOS PA'I STOBS KYIS SEMS GNAS DANG PO 'GRUB, BSAM PA'I STOBS KYIS GNYIS PA 'GRUB, DRAN PA'I STOBS KYIS GSUM PA DANG BZHI PA 'GRUB, SHES BZHIN GYI STOBS KYIS LNGA PA DANG DRUG PA 'GRUB, BRTZON 'GRUS KYI STOBS KYIS BDUN PA DANG BRGYAD PA 'GRUB, 'DRIS PA'I STOBS KYIS DGU PA 'GRUB BO,,
gru.wylie: [t9] de dag stobs drug gis 'grub lugs ni, bla ma'i gdams ngag thos pa'i stobs kyis sems gnas dang po 'grub, bsam pa'i stobs kyis gnyis pa 'grub, dran pa'i stobs kyis gsum pa dang bzhi pa 'grub, shes bzhin gyi stobs kyis lnga pa dang drug pa 'grub, brtson 'grus kyi stobs kyis bdun pa dang brgyad pa 'grub, 'dris pa'i stobs kyis dgu pa 'grub bo
gru.english: Here is how you use the six powers to attain these nine states. The first of the states is attained through the power of learning the instructions for meditation from your Teacher. The second is reached through the power of contemplating these instructions. You achieve the third and fourth mental states through the power of bringing your mind back to the object. The fifth and sixth are attained by the power of watchfulness. The seventh and eighth you bring about through the power of effort, and the ninth with the power of complete habituation.

gru.acip: [T10] DE DAG YID BYED BZHIR SDUD TSUL NI, DANG PO DANG GNYIS PA'I SKABS BSGRIMS TE 'JUG PA'I YID BYED DANG, BAR PA LNGA'I SKABS CHAD CING 'JUG PA'I YID BYED DANG, BRGYAD PA NI CHAD PA MED PAR 'JUG PA'I YID BYED DANG, DGU PA NI LHUN GYIS 'GRUB PA'I YID BYED DU 'JOG PA YIN NO,,
gru.wylie: [t10] de dag yid byed bzhir sdud tshul ni, dang po dang gnyis pa'i skabs bsgrims te 'jug pa'i yid byed dang, bar pa lnga'i skabs chad cing 'jug pa'i yid byed dang, brgyad pa ni chad pa med par 'jug pa'i yid byed dang, dgu pa ni lhun gyis 'grub pa'i yid byed du 'jog pa yin no
gru.english: Here is how these nine are grouped into four different modes of focus. During the first and second mental states, you focus by forcefully concentrating the mind. Over the course of the middle five states, you focus in a stream, but with interruptions. In the eighth mental state you focus in an uninterrupted stream, and during the ninth you focus on the object completely effortlessly.

gru.acip: [T11] DE LTAR SEMS GNAS DGU RIM GYIS 'GRUB PA'I MTHAR SHIN SBYANGS MI G-YO BA THOB PA DANG DUS MNYAM DU BSAM GTAN DANG PO'I NYER BSDOGS KYIS BSDUS PA'I ZHI GNAS GRUB PA YIN NO,,
gru.wylie: [t11] de ltar sems gnas dgu rim gyis 'grub pa'i mthar shin sbyangs mi g-yo ba thob pa dang dus mnyam du bsam gtan dang po'i nyer bsdogs kyis bsdus pa'i zhi gnas grub pa yin no
gru.english: The final result of attaining these nine states, one by one, is that you reach an unshakeable state of physical and mental meditative pleasure. Simultaneous to achieving this pleasure, you attain a state of quietude, which is taken in by the preparatory stage of the first concentration level [which in turn is the meditative platform needed to see emptiness directly].

gru.acip: [T12] DE LTA BUS ZHI GNAS GRUB PA'I RJES SU ZAB MO DBU MA'I LTA BA LA RTZE GCIG TU DPYAD 'JOG CHA MNYAM DU GOMS PAR BYAS PAS,
gru.wylie: [t12] de lta bus zhi gnas grub pa'i rjes su zab mo dbu ma'i lta ba la rtse gcig tu dpyad 'jog cha mnyam du goms par byas pas
gru.english: Suppose that, after achieving quietude in the way described above, you go on to meditate one-pointedly upon the profound worldview of the middle way, reaching a balance in your practice between the ability to analyze reality and the ability to hold your mind fixed in meditation on the conclusions gained from your analysis.

gru.acip: [T15] SKU BZHI'I RGYAL THABS CHEN PO MNGON DU BYAS TE NAM MKHA' JI SRID BAR 'GRO BA'I RE BA SKONG BA'I 'PHRIN LAS LHUN GRUB RGYUN MI CHAD PA 'BYUNG BA YIN NO,,
gru.wylie: [t15] sku bzhi'i rgyal thabs chen po mngon du byas te nam mkha' ji srid bar 'gro ba'i re ba skong ba'i 'phrin las lhun grub rgyun mi chad pa 'byung ba yin no
gru.english: With this you will win the great victory of the four bodies of a Buddha, and find yourself able to perform enlightened deeds, constantly and spontaneously, without any conscious thought—fulfilling the hopes of every living creature, for as long as space itself endures.

gru.acip: [T25] 4) LAM GYI KHUG PA DRUG STOBS DRUG DANG SBYAR BA LAS DANG PO THOS PA'I STOBS SO, ,'DI LA BRTEN NAS SEMS GNAS DANG PO 'GRUB PA YIN,,
gru.wylie: [t25] 4) lam gyi khug pa drug stobs drug dang sbyar ba las dang po thos pa'i stobs so, ,'di la brten nas sems gnas dang po 'grub pa yin
gru.english: 4) The six bends in the road represent the six powers. The first stands for the power of learning the instructions. Based on this, one achieves the first mental state.

gru.acip: [T29] 8) BSAM PA'I STOBS SO, ,'DIS SEMS GNAS GNYIS PA 'GRUB,
gru.wylie: [t29] 8) bsam pa'i stobs so, ,'dis sems gnas gnyis pa 'grub
gru.english: 8) The power of contemplating the instructions. You use this to reach the second mental state.

gru.acip: [T33] 12) DRAN PA'I STOBS SO, ,'DIS SEMS GNAS GSUM PA DANG BZHI PA 'GRUB,
gru.wylie: [t33] 12) dran pa'i stobs so, ,'dis sems gnas gsum pa dang bzhi pa 'grub
gru.english: 12) The power of bringing the mind back to the object. This allows you to attain the third and fourth mental states.

gru.acip: [T38] 17) SHES BZHIN GYI STOBS SO, ,'DIS SEMS GNAS LNGA PA DANG DRUG PA 'GRUB,,
gru.wylie: [t38] 17) shes bzhin gyi stobs so, ,'dis sems gnas lnga pa dang drug pa 'grub
gru.english: 17) The power of watchfulness. This allows you to reach the fifth and sixth mental states.

gru.acip: [T40] 19) ZHI GNAS SGRUB SKABS SEMS DGE BA'I PHYOGS LA 'PHRO BA'ANG BAR GCOD YIN PAS 'GOG DGOS KYANG, SKABS GZHAN DU MI 'GOG PAR DON GNYIS KYI 'BRAS BU LEN PA,
gru.wylie: [t40] 19) zhi gnas sgrub skabs sems dge ba'i phyogs la 'phro ba'ang bar gcod yin pas 'gog dgos kyang, skabs gzhan du mi 'gog par don gnyis kyi 'bras bu len pa
gru.english: 19) When you are trying to develop quietude, even allowing your mind to be distracted to a virtuous object becomes an obstacle, and you must seek to stop it. When you are doing other practices though you do not have to stop it. And so we see the monkey reaching for the fruit of a second activity.

gru.acip: [T44] 23) BRTZON 'GRUS KYI STOBS MO, ,'DIS SEMS GNAS BDUN PA DANG BRGYAD PA 'GRUB,
gru.wylie: [t44] 23) brtson 'grus kyi stobs mo, ,'dis sems gnas bdun pa dang brgyad pa 'grub
gru.english: 23) The power of effort. This allows you to reach the seventh and eighth mental states.

gru.acip: [T48] 27) YONGS SU 'BRIS PA'I STOBS SO, ,'DIS SEMS GNAS DGU PA 'GRUB,
gru.wylie: [t48] 27) yongs su 'bris pa'i stobs so, ,'dis sems gnas dgu pa 'grub
gru.english: 27) The power of complete habituation, which enables you to reach the ninth mental state

gru.acip: DANG PO LA DRUG ,ZHI GNAS KYI TSOGS BSTEN PA, ZHI GNAS SGRUB TSUL DNGOS, DE LA BRTEN NAS SEMS GNAS DGU SGRUB TSUL, DE STOBS DRUG GIS 'GRUB LUGS, DE LA YID BYED BZHI YOD TSUL, DE LAS ZHI GNAS DNGOS SKYE TSUL LO,,
gru.wylie: dang po la drug ,zhi gnas kyi tshogs bsten pa, zhi gnas sgrub tshul dngos, de la brten nas sems gnas dgu sgrub tshul, de stobs drug gis 'grub lugs, de la yid byed bzhi yod tshul, de las zhi gnas dngos skye tshul lo
gru.english: The first of these two sections has six parts of its own: [1] Gathering together the conditions which are conducive to meditation; [2] Actual instructions for attaining quietude; [3] How we attain nine mental states by utilizing these instructions; [4] How to use six different powers to attain those nine states; [5] Four modes of focus that we'll find with the nine states; and [6] A description of the actual state of quietude that we attain through the above process.

gru.acip: MDO SNGAGS KYI TING NGE 'DZIN GYI YON TAN JI 'DRA ZHIG SKYE BAR 'DOD KYANG CHU BLUGS PA LA CHU SDOD SA'I SNOD LTAR MED DU MI RUNG BA NI ZHI GNAS NYID YIN PAS, THOG MAR 'DI BRTAN PO ZHIG SGRUB PA GAL CHE,
gru.wylie: mdo sngags kyi ting nge 'dzin gyi yon tan ji 'dra zhig skye bar 'dod kyang chu blugs pa la chu sdod sa'i snod ltar med du mi rung ba ni zhi gnas nyid yin pas, thog mar 'di brtan po zhig sgrub pa gal che
gru.english: It doesn't matter which high quality of concentration from either the open teachings or the secret teachings that you hope to develop; in every case, quietude is something you absolutely can't do without. It's like the case where—if you want to pour some water someplace—you're surely going to need something to hold it in first.

gru.acip: DER MA ZAD ZHI GNAS GRUB NA DAL 'BYOR RNYED DKA' DANG MI RTAG BSGOM PA'I RTOGS PA TSUN LA SKYED THON PA SLA,
gru.wylie: der ma zad zhi gnas grub na dal 'byor rnyed dka' dang mi rtag bsgom pa'i rtogs pa tshun la skyed thon pa sla
gru.english: And not only that; when you're trying to develop the practice of quietude, it will be easier for you to get results if you start off from realizations that you've developed from meditating on how difficult it is to get the necessary leisure and fortune for spiritual practice; and meditating on how impermanent everything about your life is.

gru.acip: LAM SGRON LAS, MNGON SHES SGRUB PA'I PHYIR SKYED PAR GSUNGS KYANG, DE MTSON PA TZAM LAS, DGOS PA'I GTZO BO NI, ZHI BA LHAS,
gru.wylie: lam sgron las, mngon shes sgrub pa'i phyir skyed par gsungs kyang, de mtshon pa tsam las, dgos pa'i gtso bo ni, zhi ba lhas
gru.english: Now it is true that the Light on the Path states that you will have to develop quietude if you hope to achieve clairvoyance; but that is just meant to offer one example. As for the principal necessity of quietude, we need to turn to Master Shantideva:

gru.acip: ZHES GSUNGS PA 'DI YIN PAS THOG MAR ZHI GNAS BSGRUB DGOS LA, DE YANG SEMS BSKYED KYI RJES KHO NAR MI DGOS PAR SNGA PHYI GANG DU BSGRUB KYANG CHOG
gru.wylie: zhes gsungs pa 'di yin pas thog mar zhi gnas bsgrub dgos la, de yang sems bskyed kyi rjes kho nar mi dgos par snga phyi gang du bsgrub kyang chog
gru.english: And since the necessity is thus, then first we need to attain quietude. This by the way is not something that need come only after you have been able to reach the Wish for enlightenment; rather, you can develop it either before or after.

gru.acip: ,DE 'GRUB NA, THEG PA GSUM GYI NYAMS LEN GANG BSGOMS KYANG, SA CHOD SHIN TU CHE BA 'ONG,
gru.wylie: de 'grub na, theg pa gsum gyi nyams len gang bsgoms kyang, sa chod shin tu che ba 'ong
gru.english: Once you do attain quietude though, you can achieve great leaps in your spiritual progress—no matter which practice in any of the three ways that you are focusing on. Conditions you will need to develop quietude

gru.acip: DE LA THOG MAR ZHI GNAS KYI TSOGS BSTEN DGOS KYI, DE MED PAR MI 'GRUB STE, LAM SGRON LAS, ,ZHI GNAS YAN LAG RNAM NYAMS PAS, ,RAB TU 'BAD DE BSGOM BYAS KYANG, ,LO NI STONG PHRAG DAG GIS KYANG, ,TING 'DZIN 'GRUB PAR MI 'GYUR RO,, ZHES GSUNGS,
gru.wylie: de la thog mar zhi gnas kyi tshogs bsten dgos kyi, de med par mi 'grub ste, lam sgron las, ,zhi gnas yan lag rnam nyams pas, ,rab tu 'bad de bsgom byas kyang, ,lo ni stong phrag dag gis kyang, ,ting 'dzin 'grub par mi 'gyur ro,, zhes gsungs
gru.english: In order to develop quietude, we need to first assemble the necessary conditions for it; without these, we will never be able to reach it. As the Light on the Path again puts it: If the different components In the practice of quietude are lost, We can make all the efforts we like— But we'll find ourselves unable To reach a state of concentration Even in thousands of years.

gru.acip: 'DI SGRUB PA'I YUL YANG KHYAD PAR LNGA LDAN TE, MDO SDE RGYAN LAS, ,BLO LDAN GANG DU SGRUB PA'I YUL, ,LEGS PAR RNYED DANG GNAS BZANG DANG, ,SA BZANG BA DANG GROGS BZANG DANG, ,RNAL 'BYOR BDE BA'I YO BYAD LDAN, ,ZHES GSUNGS PA LTAR DGOS,
gru.wylie: 'di sgrub pa'i yul yang khyad par lnga ldan te, mdo sde rgyan las, ,blo ldan gang du sgrub pa'i yul, ,legs par rnyed dang gnas bzang dang, ,sa bzang ba dang grogs bzang dang, ,rnal 'byor bde ba'i yo byad ldan, ,zhes gsungs pa ltar dgos
gru.english: Now the area that we choose for trying to develop quietude should have five different qualities. As the Jewel of the Sutras says: The area where intelligent ones Choose to do their practice Should be one where Physical necessities are easily found; A pure place, a good place, A place with good companions; Where we are blessed with all the needs Of a deep practitioner.

gru.acip: SGRUB PA RTZE GCIG BYED PA LA, SKAR RTZIS DANG, SMAN, MO 'DEBS, GRONG CHOG SOGS KYANG 'DU 'DZI YIN PAS SPONG DGOS,
gru.wylie: sgrub pa rtse gcig byed pa la, skar rtsis dang, sman, mo 'debs, grong chog sogs kyang 'du 'dzi yin pas spong dgos
gru.english: Once we monks and nuns decide to stay single-pointed in the pursuit of our spiritual practice, then we'll have to give up lesser activities such as studying topics like astrology and medicine; or learning to tell others their future; doing a lot of rituals at the request of families who want them, and so forth. This is because these in themselves will become distractions.

gru.acip: 'DIS RANG RE LTA BU'I LAS DANG PO PAR LTA CI, SKYES BU DAM PA YIN YANG GNOD TSABS CHE STE, BU STON DANG BLA MA DAM PA GNYIS LA'ANG RGYAL PO PE KAR GYIS MTHO BRTZAMS NAS, LCAGS SMYUG PHUL BAS SKU TSE DE LA LCAGS SMYUG STONG PHRAG ZAD ZAD RTZIS LA G-YENGS TE MCHOG MA 'GRUB PAR GSUNGS,
gru.wylie: 'dis rang re lta bu'i las dang po par lta ci, skyes bu dam pa yin yang gnod tshabs che ste, bu ston dang bla ma dam pa gnyis la'ang rgyal po pe kar gyis mtho brtsams nas, lcags smyug phul bas sku tshe de la lcags smyug stong phrag zad zad rtsis la g-yengs te mchog ma 'grub par gsungs
gru.english: Distractions like this can be very destructive not only for beginners like ourselves, but even for advanced spiritual practitioners. For example, the spirit king by the name of Pekar was once hoping to belittle people no less than Buton Rinpoche and Lama Dampa. He offered each of them an iron stylus; and from then on, they wore out a thousand such pens wasting their time on calculations—with the result, our Lama said, that they were unable to reach the ultimate goal in their lifetimes.

gru.acip: RJE RIN PO CHES KYANG GSUNG POD BCO BRGYAD PO LA'ANG, DBU LA SUM PHAB SOGS MA MDZAD PA KHONG GIS BRi TTA DANG DZA TI MA MKHYEN PA MIN, SGRUB PA NYAMS LEN LA GNOD DOGS TE MA MDZAD PA YIN,
gru.wylie: rje rin po ches kyang gsung pod bco brgyad po la'ang, dbu la sum phab sogs ma mdzad pa khong gis bri tta dang dza ti ma mkhyen pa min, sgrub pa nyams len la gnod dogs te ma mdzad pa yin
gru.english: And Tsongkapa, Je Rinpoche, composed a total of 18 entire volumes filled with different titles; but he never followed the tradition of writing the titles of his books in three lines with ornamental Sanskrit followed by Sanskrit in Tibetan letters, and then the Tibetan itself. This is not because he was ignorant of the finer points of Sanskrit grammar such as word formation or the treatment of nominal stems; rather, he was afraid that spending his time on such matters would be detrimental to his spiritual practice.

gru.acip: KHO BOS RTZA SGRUB RNAM DAG GCIG PU'ANG LO GCIG TZAM SBYANGS PAS MDZUB MO BUG CING, SAM tA'ANG GNYIS GSUM TZAM RGYUS PA HRENG HRENG DU ZAD MOD, DE DAG KYANG 'DU 'DZIR SONG BA LAS, NYAMS LEN LA PHAN PA MA BYUNG,
gru.wylie: kho bos rtsa sgrub rnam dag gcig pu'ang lo gcig tsam sbyangs pas mdzub mo bug cing, sam Ta'ang gnyis gsum tsam rgyus pa hreng hreng du zad mod, de dag kyang 'du 'dzir song ba las, nyams len la phan pa ma byung
gru.english: I myself spent an entire year devoted to the single aspect of Sanskrit where you try to isolate the roots correctly. I sat by myself and wore holes in my fingers, going through two or three practice slates at a time, one after the other. It ended up just being a kind of busy work, and didn't help my spiritual practice at all.

gru.acip: DES NA BU RAM MI LEN PAR BUR SHING LA CHAGS PA LTAR DON GYI SNYING PO MI SGRUB PAR, RIG GNAS PHRAN TSEGS LTA BU DON CHUNG CHUNG ZHIG LA BRTZON PAS CI BYED,
gru.wylie: des na bu ram mi len par bur shing la chags pa ltar don gyi snying po mi sgrub par, rig gnas phran tshegs lta bu don chung chung zhig la brtson pas ci byed
gru.english: What's the use then, of focusing on the insignificant goal of mastering things like some minor academic subject, and missing out on the ultimate goal of all? That's like getting attached to used-up sugar cane sticks and missing out on the yummy sugar inside.

gru.acip: DES NA RGYU TSOGS 'DI DAG TSANG BA ZHIG GIS BRTZON PAS SGRUB NA, ZHI GNAS 'GRUB PA LA ZLA BA DRUG LAS MI 'GOR BAR GSUNGS,
gru.wylie: des na rgyu tshogs 'di dag tshang ba zhig gis brtson pas sgrub na, zhi gnas 'grub pa la zla ba drug las mi 'gor bar gsungs
gru.english: It is stated in the scriptures that if a person takes the time to bring together all these conditions for developing their meditation, and then really puts forth some effort, then it won't take them longer than six months to attain the high state of quietude. The actual method for developing quietude

gru.acip: GNYIS PA ZHI GNAS SGRUB TSUL DNGOS NI, DBUS MTHA' LAS, ,NYES PA LNGA SPONG 'DU BYED BRGYAD, ,BSTEN PA'I RGYU LAS BYUNG BA'O,,
gru.wylie: gnyis pa zhi gnas sgrub tshul dngos ni, dbus mtha' las, ,nyes pa lnga spong 'du byed brgyad, ,bsten pa'i rgyu las byung ba'o
gru.english: Which brings us to our second point from above: the actual method for developing quietude. Distinguishing the Middle from the Extremes says that: The cause that will bring it to you Is avoiding five different problems, And making use of eight Different kinds of action. The five classic problems that come up during meditation

gru.acip: ,ZHES NYES PA LNGA'I GNYEN POR 'DU BYED BRGYAD BSTEN PAR GSUNGS LA, TING 'DZIN SGRUB PA'I MAN NGAG NI, BYAMS CHOS DANG SA SDE DANG DBU MA SGOM RIM SOGS GZHUNG CHEN MO RNAMS SU GSUNGS PA LAS LHAG PA MED PAS NA, RANG CAG GIS MAN NGAG 'DI LTA BU BTZAL NAS BSGOM PA ZHIG DGOS KYI,
gru.wylie: zhes nyes pa lnga'i gnyen por 'du byed brgyad bsten par gsungs la, ting 'dzin sgrub pa'i man ngag ni, byams chos dang sa sde dang dbu ma sgom rim sogs gzhung chen mo rnams su gsungs pa las lhag pa med pas na, rang cag gis man ngag 'di lta bu btsal nas bsgom pa zhig dgos kyi
gru.english: These lines then are describing the five problems that can arise during our meditation, and how we can rely on eight different corrective actions as the antidotes to these problems. And so we see instructions on how to develop our meditative concentration in great classics such as the Five Books of Maitreya; the group of works by Master Asanga on the various spiritual levels; Master Kamalashila's stages of meditation for the middle way; and so on. People like you and I need to seek out great books of instruction like this, to develop our own meditation practice.

gru.acip: RJE TZONG KHA PA CHEN POS LTA SGOM SPYOD GSUM GANG GI CHA LA'ANG RGYA GAR GYI PAn GRUB MTHAR THUG RNAMS KYI GSUNG LA GTUGS NAS DPANG POR MDZAD PAR
gru.wylie: rje tsong kha pa chen pos lta sgom spyod gsum gang gi cha la'ang rgya gar gyi paN grub mthar thug rnams kyi gsung la gtugs nas dpang por mdzad par
gru.english: The great Je Tsongkapa though was different. No matter which of the three you're talking about—his viewpoints, his meditation, or the way he led his life—you can see that he paid witness to the words of the very greatest of the scholars and practitioners of the classical Buddhism of India.

gru.acip: DES NA GSANG SNGAGS KYI BSKYED RDZOGS NAS BZUNG STE, THA NA TING NGE 'DZIN CHUNG NGU RE SGOM PA YAN LA BSTAN BCOS KHUNGS MA NAS GSUNGS PA'I ZHI GNAS SGRUB PA'I MAN NGAG NYES PA LNGA SPONG ZHING 'DU BYED BRGYAD BSTEN PA 'DI MED THABS MED,
gru.wylie: des na gsang sngags kyi bskyed rdzogs nas bzung ste, tha na ting nge 'dzin chung ngu re sgom pa yan la bstan bcos khungs ma nas gsungs pa'i zhi gnas sgrub pa'i man ngag nyes pa lnga spong zhing 'du byed brgyad bsten pa 'di med thabs med
gru.english: And so let's look at the whole range of spiritual practice; starting all the way down to trying to have a tiny experience of true focus during one of your meditation sessions, and going all the way up to reaching the two stages—the stage of creation, and the stage of completion—within the secret teachings for attaining enlightenment in a single life. There is no way that you're ever going to get anywhere, with any of this, if you don't learn and follow the instructions found in authentic, ancient scriptures: if you fail to follow the true instructions for attaining the meditative state of quietude, by eliminating the five problems and relying upon the eight corrective actions. 1) Laziness

gru.acip: DE LA NYES PA DANG PO LE LO'I GNYEN POR TING NGE 'DZIN GYI YON TAN MTHONG BA'I DAD PA, TING NGE 'DZIN LA DON GNYER GYI 'DUN PA, TING NGE 'DZIN LA RTZOL BA'I BRTZON 'GRUS, RTZOL BA'I 'BRAS BU SHIN SBYANGS TE BZHI LAS,
gru.wylie: de la nyes pa dang po le lo'i gnyen por ting nge 'dzin gyi yon tan mthong ba'i dad pa, ting nge 'dzin la don gnyer gyi 'dun pa, ting nge 'dzin la rtsol ba'i brtson 'grus, rtsol ba'i 'bras bu shin sbyangs te bzhi las
gru.english: Now the first of the classic problems that comes up when we try to meditate is laziness, and there are four antidotes we use to stop it. These are [1] faith in the practice, because we can see the great benefits of being able to meditate; [2] aspiration, where we would really like to gain this ability ourselves; [3] effort, where we are willing to put in the work needed to learn to meditate properly; and [4] that physical and mental pliancy—the practiced ease—which is the result of this effort.

gru.acip: ,ZHES GSUNGS PA BZHIN SEMS G-YENG BA'I SKYON RNAMS BSAMS SHING ZHI GNAS 'GRUB NA DGE BA LA 'JUG PA'I TSE, YUL DMIGS PA LA 'JUG PA BRTAN CING, DE BRTAN PAS DNGOS GRUB MYUR LA,
gru.wylie: zhes gsungs pa bzhin sems g-yeng ba'i skyon rnams bsams shing zhi gnas 'grub na dge ba la 'jug pa'i tshe, yul dmigs pa la 'jug pa brtan cing, de brtan pas dngos grub myur la
gru.english: What this is saying is that—if we think carefully about the problems that happen when our mind is distracted, and instead manage to develop meditative quietude—then when we engage in any kind of good deed we will be unshakable in our focus on our goal; and because we are, then spiritual achievements will arrive with speed.

gru.acip: THUN MONG GI MNGON SHES RDZU 'PHRUL SOGS KYANG 'DIS 'GRUB CING, GNYID TING 'DZIN DU 'GRO BA DANG, NYON MONGS SHAS CHUNG DU 'GRO BA DANG, KHYAD PAR DU BSHES GNYEN BSTEN TSUL NAS BRTZAMS TE BSKYED RDZOGS BAR GYI LAM THAMS CAD MYUR DU SKYE SLA BA SOGS 'BYUNG BA'I YON TAN RNAMS
gru.wylie: thun mong gi mngon shes rdzu 'phrul sogs kyang 'dis 'grub cing, gnyid ting 'dzin du 'gro ba dang, nyon mongs shas chung du 'gro ba dang, khyad par du bshes gnyen bsten tshul nas brtsams te bskyed rdzogs bar gyi lam thams cad myur du skye sla ba sogs 'byung ba'i yon tan rnams
gru.english: The attainments that are shared with lesser traditions—things like clairvoyance, the ability to perform miracles, and other skills of the like—are also attained through this same quietude. So too, if we do reach quietude, then other good things will start to happen as well. These include for example seeing our negative emotions begin to dwindle away; and more especially finding it easy to master all the aspects of the spiritual path with ease—everything from the very first step of learning how to take ourselves to a true master; on up to mastering the final steps: the stages of creation and completion.

gru.acip: DE BYUNG NA 'DUN PA, BRTZON 'GRUS, SHIN SBYANGS RNAMS RIM BZHIN SNGA MA SNGA MAS PHYI MA PHYI MA DRANGS 'ONG BAS 'DI BZHI RGYU 'BRAS KYI TSUL DU 'GRO,
gru.wylie: de byung na 'dun pa, brtson 'grus, shin sbyangs rnams rim bzhin snga ma snga mas phyi ma phyi ma drangs 'ong bas 'di bzhi rgyu 'bras kyi tshul du 'gro
gru.english: Once you do reach this kind of faith, then that will naturally lead you to the other three antidotes for laziness here: aspiration; effort; and then physical & mental pliancy. Each one will act to bring on the next in the list: you will see a pattern of cause & effect between the four. 2) Forgetting the instructions

gru.acip: DE YANG DMIGS RTEN NI CHOS GANG LA DMIGS KYANG 'GRUB PA YIN, PHYI ROL PA DAG GIS RDE'U DANG SHING BU LA DMIGS PA DANG, BON GYIS AA LA DMIGS TE ZHI GNAS SGRUB PA RNAMS
gru.wylie: de yang dmigs rten ni chos gang la dmigs kyang 'grub pa yin, phyi rol pa dag gis rde'u dang shing bu la dmigs pa dang, bon gyis aa la dmigs te zhi gnas sgrub pa rnams
gru.english: Now as far as selecting a meditation object, you can develop concentration towards just about anything. To try to reach the state of quietude, there were certain non-Buddhist schools of ancient India that would use a small stone, or a little piece of wood, to focus their meditation on; while followers of Bon—the native shamanistic religion of Tibet—would concentrate on the letter “a”.

gru.acip: DMIGS RTEN DE DANG DE YID YUL DU BYED PA LAS MIG GIS BLTAS TE SGRUB PA MIN, GZHAN PHYOGS KHA CIG GIS DMIGS RTEN LA MIG GIS BLTAS TE SGRUB PA NI SNGA MA GNYIS LAS KYANG DMAN TE,
gru.wylie: dmigs rten de dang de yid yul du byed pa las mig gis bltas te sgrub pa min, gzhan phyogs kha cig gis dmigs rten la mig gis bltas te sgrub pa ni snga ma gnyis las kyang dman te
gru.english: It's important to say though that to actually reach quietude, the meditation object you select has to be something inside the mind: there's no way to achieve quietude just by staring at something on the outside. Those groups of practitioners who have recommended simply sitting down and staring at some visible object in front of you are even worse than the two traditions we've just mentioned.

gru.acip: ZHI GNAS YID SHES LA SGRUB DGOS KYI, MIG LA SGRUB PA MA YIN PAS, DE DAG LA LNGA PA CHEN PO SOGS MANG POS DGAG PA MDZAD YOD,
gru.wylie: zhi gnas yid shes la sgrub dgos kyi, mig la sgrub pa ma yin pas, de dag la lnga pa chen po sogs mang pos dgag pa mdzad yod
gru.english: And that's because quietude is something that we attain by using our awareness of our thoughts—it is not something you can achieve with your eyeballs. Thus it is that a great many thinkers, including His Holiness the Great Fifth Dalai Lama, have rejected this kind of practice.

gru.acip: SNGON RGYA GAR NAS GCIG GIS SEMS GNAS DMIGS RTEN GZHAN LA MA 'GRUB PAR BA LANG GI RVA LA DMIGS RTEN BYAS TE BSGRUBS PAS 'GRUB PA BYUNG BA BZHIN DU YUL GANG GOMS PA LA DMIGS RTEN BYAS KYANG 'GRUB,
gru.wylie: sngon rgya gar nas gcig gis sems gnas dmigs rten gzhan la ma 'grub par ba lang gi rva la dmigs rten byas te bsgrubs pas 'grub pa byung ba bzhin du yul gang goms pa la dmigs rten byas kyang 'grub
gru.english: There was a meditator in ancient India who didn't have anything else to meditate on, and so he chose as his meditation object the horns of a bull. And he actually succeeded, with this object. And so you can learn to meditate using just about anything you get used to as your object.

gru.acip: 'ON KYANG RANG CAG RNAMS KYIS RJE BDAG NYID CHEN PO'I BKA' SROL LTAR, ZHI GNAS SGRUB PA'I TSE SANGS RGYAS KYI SKU LA DMIGS NA TSOGS GSOG SGRIB SBYONG GI ZHING DMIGS PA LA KHYAD CHE BA DANG,
gru.wylie: 'on kyang rang cag rnams kyis rje bdag nyid chen po'i bka' srol ltar, zhi gnas sgrub pa'i tshe sangs rgyas kyi sku la dmigs na tshogs gsog sgrib sbyong gi zhing dmigs pa la khyad che ba dang
gru.english: At the same time though, people like you and I should try to follow the advice given to us by that mighty being, Lord Tsongkapa. If, rather, as we try to develop the capacity of quietude we choose to visualize something like the physical form of a Buddha, then at the same time this acts as a spiritual garden in which we can plant piles of good seeds, and also remove our inner obstacles. It makes a huge difference.

gru.acip: DGA' LDAN PHYAG RGYA CHEN PO'I KHRID LAS SEMS LA DMIGS PA'I ZHI GNAS SGRUB TSUL GSUNGS PA LTAR BYA CHOG CING, DE NI GRUB MTHA' GZHAN PHYOGS KYIS SEMS NGO BLTA BA DANG PHYOGS MTSUNGS,
gru.wylie: dga' ldan phyag rgya chen po'i khrid las sems la dmigs pa'i zhi gnas sgrub tshul gsungs pa ltar bya chog cing, de ni grub mtha' gzhan phyogs kyis sems ngo blta ba dang phyogs mtshungs
gru.english: These instructions are known as the “Great Seal—Mahamudra—in the Tradition of the Followers of the Heaven of Bliss”; and so as an alternative you could profitably follow the instructions there on how to develop meditative quietude by focusing on your own mind as your meditation object. This approach bears some broad similarity to the practice of meeting the mind, as taught in other traditions.

gru.acip: YANG BSKYED RIM DANG SBRAGS NAS LHA SKU DANG, RDZOGS RIM DANG SBRAGS NAS AA SHAD LA DMIGS NAS SKYANG SGRUB TU RUNG NGO,,
gru.wylie: yang bskyed rim dang sbrags nas lha sku dang, rdzogs rim dang sbrags nas aa shad la dmigs nas skyang sgrub tu rung ngo
gru.english: It is also quite appropriate if—as an adjunct to your practice of the stage of creation in the secret teachings, when you have reached that point—you work on developing quietude using the holy body of the deity. Or, if you are focusing on the stage of completion, you could also reach quietude by using the traditional practice based on visualizing the stroke used for a long “a” vowel in Sanskrit.

gru.acip: LAG LEN LA RANG NYID GANG 'CHAR BDE BA GCIG LA BYAS TE MA GRUB BAR DU DMIGS PA KHA MA SPOS PAR BSGOM DGOS PA LAS MDO LAS GSUNGS PA'I DMIGS PA BZHI PO TSANG MA BSGOM DGOS PA MIN PAS RANG GI SEMS LA GANG 'PHROD PA GCIG LA SEMS BZHAG DGOS,
gru.wylie: lag len la rang nyid gang 'char bde ba gcig la byas te ma grub bar du dmigs pa kha ma spos par bsgom dgos pa las mdo las gsungs pa'i dmigs pa bzhi po tshang ma bsgom dgos pa min pas rang gi sems la gang 'phrod pa gcig la sems bzhag dgos
gru.english: At any rate, in actual practice you should select a meditation object which is easy for you to watch within your mind. Then you need to stick with this object in your meditation, without skipping around to others. It's not by the way that you have to meditate on all four of the possible types of objects described in the scriptures; rather, you need to choose one that fits you, and then glue your mind to that.

gru.acip: ,ZHES GSUNGS PA LTAR BSGOM PA'I SKABS DMIGS PA GCIG LA BZHAG PA LAS, DMIGS PA SPOS NA MI 'GRUB STE, DPER NA GTZUB SHING GTZUB PA'I TSE SHING SPOS PA NA ME MI 'BAR BA DANG 'DRA,
gru.wylie: zhes gsungs pa ltar bsgom pa'i skabs dmigs pa gcig la bzhag pa las, dmigs pa spos na mi 'grub ste, dper na gtsub shing gtsub pa'i tshe shing spos pa na me mi 'bar ba dang 'dra
gru.english: And so whenever you are meditating, it's better to put the mind on just one object. If you keep switching to another object, you'll never succeed. It's like the case where you are trying to start a fire by rubbing two sticks together, but you keep switching out the sticks—then the fire will never light.

gru.acip: DER MA ZAD ZHI GNAS BSGOM PA NA GNYID DANG ZAS DANG, BSHANG GCI 'DOR SKABS TZAM MA GTOGS GZHAN GTZUB SHING BAR MA CHAD PAR GTZUB PA LTAR BAR MA CHAD DU LO'AM ZLA BA DRUG SOGS JI TZAM BSGRUB PA DE'I RING RGYUN MI GCOD PAR BYA DGOS KYI,
gru.wylie: der ma zad zhi gnas bsgom pa na gnyid dang zas dang, bshang gci 'dor skabs tsam ma gtogs gzhan gtsub shing bar ma chad par gtsub pa ltar bar ma chad du lo'am zla ba drug sogs ji tsam bsgrub pa de'i ring rgyun mi gcod par bya dgos kyi
gru.english: And that's not all. Even if you keep to the same sticks, you still have to continue rubbing them together until you get a fire. And so you will need to keep up your meditation sessions—just stopping for things like getting in your night's sleep; going to the toilet; and so forth. You have to keep going—in a flow, without a stop—whether it takes a year, or six months, or whatever it may be.

gru.acip: DE'I GNYEN PO 'DU BYED BRGYAD LAS LNGA PA DRAN PA STE, LAG PAS PHRENG BA BZUNG BA LTAR DRAN PA SHUGS CHEN POS DMIGS RTEN THU RE BZUNG BA DGOS LA, GANG ZAG SO SO'I DRAN PA BRTAN MI BRTAN GYIS KYANG ZHI GNAS 'GRUB DKA' SLA'I KHYAD YOD,
gru.wylie: de'i gnyen po 'du byed brgyad las lnga pa dran pa ste, lag pas phreng ba bzung ba ltar dran pa shugs chen pos dmigs rten thu re bzung ba dgos la, gang zag so so'i dran pa brtan mi brtan gyis kyang zhi gnas 'grub dka' sla'i khyad yod
gru.english: The antidote for this particular problem is to take the fifth of the eight corrective actions: to bring our mind back to the object. Holding this object should feel like holding some meditation beads in your fist: you need to keep a continuous hold on it, using considerable mental strength to keep the mind there. The natural capacity of different individuals to hold their mind on an object is different—some are able to stay there steadily, and others not so steady. This difference will determine whether it is easy or difficult for the particular person to reach the state of quietude.

gru.acip: BYING BA PHRA MO LA SGOM DU 'KHRUL NA, 'BRAS BU GZUGS GZUGS MED KYI RGYU TZAM DU'ANG MI 'GRO ZHING, TSE 'DIR YANG BRJED NGES CHE BA DANG, SHES RAB MI GSAL DU 'GRO BAS DUD 'GRO'I SGRUB THABS CHED DU BSGOM PA LTA BU LAS MA BYUNG BAR GSUNGS,
gru.wylie: bying ba phra mo la sgom du 'khrul na, 'bras bu gzugs gzugs med kyi rgyu tsam du'ang mi 'gro zhing, tshe 'dir yang brjed nges che ba dang, shes rab mi gsal du 'gro bas dud 'gro'i sgrub thabs ched du bsgom pa lta bu las ma byung bar gsungs
gru.english: And suppose we do mistake this subtle dullness for real meditation. The only result it can lead us to then is nothing greater than a birth into the form or formless realms. And even in this life, we'll start to become forgetful in little things all day long; our level of intelligence itself will also suffer. And then—our Lama pointed out—it's almost as if this entire exercise of meditating has become nothing but a spiritual method for attaining rebirth as some mindless kind of animal.

gru.acip: DE 'DRA NYER GCIG TZAM RE SEMS MA YENGS PAR BZUNG THUB NA, SEMS GNAS DANG PO GRUB TSAD YIN,
gru.wylie: de 'dra nyer gcig tsam re sems ma yengs par bzung thub na, sems gnas dang po grub tshad yin
gru.english: If you can reach a count of 21 this way, without the mind getting distracted, then that is the point at which we would say you have reached the first level of meditation.

gru.acip: SNGAR YER PA'I GRUB CHEN PHUN TSOGS RGYA MTSO YANG, RANG GI SKU MCHED CIG SDE SRID SANGS RGYAS RGYA MTSO'I ZHABS 'BRING YIN PAS, SDE SRID ZHABS 'BRING BCAS LA DBU NYES BYUNG BAS SGOM LA THUGS MA ZIN PAR GYUR PA NA DBUGS BGRANGS PA 'DIS GRUB PA'I RABS YOD,
gru.wylie: sngar yer pa'i grub chen phun tshogs rgya mtsho yang, rang gi sku mched cig sde srid sangs rgyas rgya mtsho'i zhabs 'bring yin pas, sde srid zhabs 'bring bcas la dbu nyes byung bas sgom la thugs ma zin par gyur pa na dbugs bgrangs pa 'dis grub pa'i rabs yod
