gru.english: There is a story, said our Lama, about a great practitioner in past times: his name was Puntsok Gyatso, and he hailed from the area of Yerpa. One of his brothers was an assistant to the government official Desi Sangye Gyatso. The brother once tried to do some meditation practice, but he couldn't take his mind off of some problems that the Desi and his staff were having. Then though, he tried this exercise of counting his breaths, and was later able to succeed.

gru.acip: SNGAR GRUB MCHOG BLO BZANG RNAM RGYAL GYIS BKA' GDAMS GSUNG THOR BU'I LJAGS LUNG STZAL BA NA, DENG SANG SNYIGS MA'I DUS RANG RGYUD 'DUL BA'I DUS YIN GYI GZHAN RGYUD 'DUL BA'I DUS MIN ZHES PA'I MTSAMS SU BSHUM NAS GNANG MA THUB PAR CHOS MTSAMS BZHAG PAS PHYI NYIN DANG YANG NYIN KYANG TSIG MTSAMS DE KAR BYUNG BAS GNANG MA THUB PA'I RABS BZHIN YIN,
gru.wylie: sngar grub mchog blo bzang rnam rgyal gyis bka' gdams gsung thor bu'i ljags lung stsal ba na, deng sang snyigs ma'i dus rang rgyud 'dul ba'i dus yin gyi gzhan rgyud 'dul ba'i dus min zhes pa'i mtshams su bshum nas gnang ma thub par chos mtshams bzhag pas phyi nyin dang yang nyin kyang tshig mtshams de kar byung bas gnang ma thub pa'i rabs bzhin yin
gru.english: The great practitioner Lobsang Namgyal was once giving an oral transmission of a collection of briefer works from the Seers of the Word. He reached a line that said, “Times of degeneration in history are times when we have to be careful to watch our own morality, and not the morality of others.” With this, he suddenly broke out in tears and couldn't go on, and so the teaching session was ended there. The same thing happened the following day, and then again on the day after that—he just couldn't go on. This same sort of thing could happen with our meditation sessions.

gru.acip: ,DE'ANG DANG PO NAS DMIGS PA GSAL BA ZHIG MI 'BYUNG ZHING, SGRUB KYANG MI DGOS LA, DBU DANG PHYAG ZHABS SOGS CHA SHAS SPYI TZAM DANG, SER SBAM ME BA LTA BU LAM TZAM ZHIG 'CHAR BYUNG NA,
gru.wylie: de'ang dang po nas dmigs pa gsal ba zhig mi 'byung zhing, sgrub kyang mi dgos la, dbu dang phyag zhabs sogs cha shas spyi tsam dang, ser sbam me ba lta bu lam tsam zhig 'char byung na
gru.english: Here at the beginning, the image of this Buddha won't be all that clear—nor do you have to attempt to make it so. Just try to get it to the point where you have all the different parts there in a general way—the holy head, arms, legs, and so on. There should though be this sudden, soft golden glow to the scene.

gru.acip: DES NA SGRUB PA ZHIG BRGYAG KHUL BYED KYANG SGRUB RGYU'I TING 'DZIN LA GANG 'DRA ZHIG DGOS PA MI SHES PA DE LTA BU MIN PAR, SPYIR GNAS CHA DANG, GTZO BOR GSAL CHA, DE YANG 'DZIN STANGS DAM PAR BYED PA'I KHYAD CHOS GNYIS LDAN GYI TING NGE 'DZIN ZHIG NGES PAR DU BSGRUB DGOS,
gru.wylie: des na sgrub pa zhig brgyag khul byed kyang sgrub rgyu'i ting 'dzin la gang 'dra zhig dgos pa mi shes pa de lta bu min par, spyir gnas cha dang, gtso bor gsal cha, de yang 'dzin stangs dam par byed pa'i khyad chos gnyis ldan gyi ting nge 'dzin zhig nges par du bsgrub dgos
gru.english: You can see then that a person can look like they're making some efforts in spiritual practice, but without any real understanding of what the meditative focus they're looking for looks like. You and I shouldn't go this way—rather, we definitely have to try to achieve a kind of meditative concentration which is complete in two different aspects. Generally, there should be fixation; and, more especially, clarity—both characterized by a firm hold on the object.

gru.acip: RGYAS PAR NI DGE LDAN PHYAG RGYA CHEN PO'I KHRID KYI SKABS SU 'BYUNG BAS, SEMS LA DMIGS NAS ZHI GNAS SGRUB 'DOD PA RNAMS KYIS DE LAS SHES DGOS GSUNGS,
gru.wylie: rgyas par ni dge ldan phyag rgya chen po'i khrid kyi skabs su 'byung bas, sems la dmigs nas zhi gnas sgrub 'dod pa rnams kyis de las shes dgos gsungs
gru.english: Our Lama concluded this thought by saying that we could learn more details on this practice during teachings on the practice of the Great Seal in the tradition of the Virtuous Ones. He advised us that those who were interested in learning to develop quietude by using the mind itself as their meditation object could do so that way. The nine levels of meditation

gru.acip: GSUM PA DE LAS BRTEN NAS SEMS GNAS DGU SGRUB TSUL NI,
gru.wylie: gsum pa de las brten nas sems gnas dgu sgrub tshul ni
gru.english: This brings us to the third major topic of our discussion of how to develop quietude: a presentation on the nine mental states that we pass through as we follow the instructions on developing this deepest form of meditation.

gru.acip: DANG PO NI, BLA MA LAS DMIGS PA'I GDAMS NGAG THOS STOBS KYIS 'GRUB CING, DE YANG DMIGS PA LA BZHAG TZAM BZHAG TZAM LAS SHAS CHER MI GNAS PAS RGYUN MTHUD MI THUB PA STE,
gru.wylie: dang po ni, bla ma las dmigs pa'i gdams ngag thos stobs kyis 'grub cing, de yang dmigs pa la bzhag tsam bzhag tsam las shas cher mi gnas pas rgyun mthud mi thub pa ste
gru.english: The first of the nine levels—setting the mind on the object—is reached through the first of the six powers: listening to our teacher's personal advices about the object we should choose for our meditation. At this point, we are capable only of placing our mind on the object in brief spurts—we spend most of our time off the object. As such, we aren't yet able to maintain any continuity in our meditation.

gru.acip: 'DI'I TSE SKABS RE RNAM RTOG ZHI ZHING SKABS RE RNAM RTOG SKYE BAS RNAM RTOG NGAL BSO BA'I NYAMS 'ONG, 'DI BSAM PA'I STOBS KYIS 'GRUB,
gru.wylie: 'di'i tshe skabs re rnam rtog zhi zhing skabs re rnam rtog skye bas rnam rtog ngal bso ba'i nyams 'ong, 'di bsam pa'i stobs kyis 'grub
gru.english: At this level, we get the impression that our random thoughts have somehow revived, because there are times when they are quiet, followed by times when they come back up. The level is achieved by the power of contemplating the instructions we originally received.

gru.acip: SEMS GNAS GSUM PA DANG BZHI PA 'DI GNYIS DRAN PA'I STOBS KYIS 'GRUB, 'DI NAS NAR SON PA'I MI LTAR DRAN PA NAR SON PA'AM, DRAN PA'I STOBS RDZOGS PA YIN GSUNGS,
gru.wylie: sems gnas gsum pa dang bzhi pa 'di gnyis dran pa'i stobs kyis 'grub, 'di nas nar son pa'i mi ltar dran pa nar son pa'am, dran pa'i stobs rdzogs pa yin gsungs
gru.english: The third and fourth levels are achieved through the power of bringing the mind back to the object. Our ability to hold the mind on the object, and bring it back there, has at this point “grown up”—meaning that it's like a person who has finally grown up from being a child into having the strength of an adult. You could also just say that the power of holding the mind on the object is now complete. 5) Controlling the mind

gru.acip: SNGA MA LAS 'DI SKABS BYING BA PHRA MO'I NYEN CHE BA MED PA'I KHYAD YOD, LNGA PA DANG DRUG PA GNYIS SHES BZHIN GYI STOBS KYIS 'GRUB, 'DI NAS SHES BZHIN GYI STOBS RDZOGS PAR GSUNGS,
gru.wylie: snga ma las 'di skabs bying ba phra mo'i nyen che ba med pa'i khyad yod, lnga pa dang drug pa gnyis shes bzhin gyi stobs kyis 'grub, 'di nas shes bzhin gyi stobs rdzogs par gsungs
gru.english: The difference between this level and the one before it is that—at this point—there is no great danger that subtle dullness will be coming up. The fifth and sixth levels are achieved through the power of watchfulness; and from this point—our Lama told us—the power of our watchfulness is complete. 7) Completely quieting the mind

gru.acip: BDUN PA'I SKABS SU DRAN SHES KYI STOBS RDZOGS PAS BYING RGOD SKYE DKA' YANG, DE NAS BRTZON 'GRUS KYI STOBS BSKYED DE BYING RGOD PHRA MO LA'ANG SKYON DU BLTAS NAS SPONG GANG THUB BYED DGOS,
gru.wylie: bdun pa'i skabs su dran shes kyi stobs rdzogs pas bying rgod skye dka' yang, de nas brtson 'grus kyi stobs bskyed de bying rgod phra mo la'ang skyon du bltas nas spong gang thub byed dgos
gru.english: At the seventh meditation level, the power of our holding the mind on the object, and our watchfulness, are both complete. As such, it is difficult for any form of dullness or agitation to appear. We will though, from this point, need to develop the power of effort. Here we view even the most subtle forms of dullness and agitation as problems, and try as hard as we can to eliminate them.

gru.acip: LNGA PA DANG DRUG PA'I SKABS BYING RGOD KYIS TSUR GNOD PA'I DOGS PA YOD LA, BDUN PA'I SKABS 'DIR BYING RGOD BYUNG YANG BRTZON 'GRUS KYIS BKAG THUB PAS BYING RGOD KYIS TSUR BAR DU CHER GCOD MI NUS GSUNGS,
gru.wylie: lnga pa dang drug pa'i skabs bying rgod kyis tshur gnod pa'i dogs pa yod la, bdun pa'i skabs 'dir bying rgod byung yang brtson 'grus kyis bkag thub pas bying rgod kyis tshur bar du cher gcod mi nus gsungs
gru.english: At the fifth and sixth levels, we still need to have some concern that dullness and agitation will hurt us, instead of us hurting them. Here at the seventh level, dullness and agitation can possibly occur, but the effort we put out is able to stop them. As such, said our Lama, the dullness and agitation never get so great that they could cause us any significant interruption.

gru.acip: SEMS GNAS BDUN PA DANG BRGYAD PA BRTZON 'GRUS KYIS STOBS KYIS 'GRUB, DGU PA NI 'BAD RTZOL DANG BRAL BAR 'JUG PA STE, DE YANG BRGYAD PA'I SKABS YANG YANG 'DRIS PA LA BRTEN NAS 'DIR 'BAD RTZOL MED PAR LHUN GYIS GRUB PA YIN PAS
gru.wylie: sems gnas bdun pa dang brgyad pa brtson 'grus kyis stobs kyis 'grub, dgu pa ni 'bad rtsol dang bral bar 'jug pa ste, de yang brgyad pa'i skabs yang yang 'dris pa la brten nas 'dir 'bad rtsol med par lhun gyis grub pa yin pas
gru.english: The seventh and eighth meditation levels are achieved through the power of effort. At the ninth, we are engaging in our meditation without any conscious effort at all. Due to the familiarity that we developed over and again at the eighth level, the process at the ninth is effortless—completely spontaneous.

gru.acip: DGU PA 'DI YONGS SU 'DRIS PA'I STOBS KYIS 'GRUB,
gru.wylie: dgu pa 'di yongs su 'dris pa'i stobs kyis 'grub
gru.english: This ninth of the meditation levels is achieved through the power of complete habituation.

gru.acip: ZHI GNAS LA SLOB TSUL GYI TSOGS BSTEN PA LNGA'AM DRUG DANG, SGRUB TSUL DNGOS KYI, NYES PA LNGA'I GNYEN PO 'DU BYED BRGYAD BSTEN TSUL DANG, DE LA BRTEN NAS SEMS GNAS DGU BSGRUB LUGS RNAMS LA BSKYAR BSHAD GNANG,
gru.wylie: zhi gnas la slob tshul gyi tshogs bsten pa lnga'am drug dang, sgrub tshul dngos kyi, nyes pa lnga'i gnyen po 'du byed brgyad bsten tshul dang, de la brten nas sems gnas dgu bsgrub lugs rnams la bskyar bshad gnang
gru.english: The Lama also reviewed for us the five or six conducive conditions that we would need to assemble together for our attempt to develop quietude; and then as far as the actual procedure for reaching quietude, he went back over the way in which we should rely on eight corrective actions as antidotes to five classic problems in meditation. Finally, he repeated his explanation of how—based on all of this—we would be reaching nine progressive levels of meditation.

gru.acip: BZHI PA, DE STOBS DRUG GIS 'GRUB LUGS NI,
gru.wylie: bzhi pa, de stobs drug gis 'grub lugs ni
gru.english: Which brings us to the fourth section in our overall outline: how we use the six different powers to attain those nine states.

gru.acip: BDUN PA BRGYAD PA GNYIS BRTZON 'GRUS, DGU PA 'DRIS PA'I STOBS KYIS 'GRUB PA STE ZHIB PA SNGAR SEMS GNAS DGU SO SO'I SKABS SU BSHAD ZIN,
gru.wylie: bdun pa brgyad pa gnyis brtson 'grus, dgu pa 'dris pa'i stobs kyis 'grub pa ste zhib pa sngar sems gnas dgu so so'i skabs su bshad zin
gru.english: The seventh and eighth levels of meditation we attain through [5] the power of effort. And then the ninth level is reached through [6] the power of complete habituation. The details for all this have already been covered, back in our presentation of each of the nine meditative levels. The four modes of focus

gru.acip: LNGA PA DE LA YID BYED BZHI YOD TSUL NI, SEMS GNAS DANG PO GNYIS BSGRIMS TE 'JUG PA DANG, BAR PA LNGA CHAD CING 'JUG PA, BRGYAD PA NI RTZOL BA DANG BCAS TE CHAD PA MED PAR 'JUG PA, DGU PA RTZOL MED DU LHUN GYIS GRUB PAR 'JUG PA YIN,
gru.wylie: lnga pa de la yid byed bzhi yod tshul ni, sems gnas dang po gnyis bsgrims te 'jug pa dang, bar pa lnga chad cing 'jug pa, brgyad pa ni rtsol ba dang bcas te chad pa med par 'jug pa, dgu pa rtsol med du lhun gyis grub par 'jug pa yin
gru.english: Which brings us to the fifth section of our original outline, treating the way in which there are four different modes of focus here. At the first two meditation levels, we are [1] forcefully concentrating the mind. During the five intermediate levels, we are [2] focusing in a stream, but with interruptions. At the eighth level, we are [3] focusing in an uninterrupted stream, but with conscious effort. And then at the ninth level, we are [4] focusing on the object spontaneously, without any conscious effort.

gru.acip: DGU PA RTZOL MED DU DMIGS PAR 'JOG PAS LHUN GYIS GRUB PAR 'JUG PA ZHES KHYAD PAR SO SOR BZHAG PA YIN,
gru.wylie: dgu pa rtsol med du dmigs par 'jog pas lhun gyis grub par 'jug pa zhes khyad par so sor bzhag pa yin
gru.english: At the ninth level, we engage in our meditation object without applying any conscious effort; and so we call it “focusing spontaneously.” This then explains the differences in focus throughout each of the nine levels. The actual state of quietude

gru.acip: DRUG PA DE LAS ZHI GNAS DNGOS 'GRUB TSUL NI, SEMS GNAS DGU PA THOB NAS BYING RGOD PHRA MO DANG BRAL BAR TING 'DZIN LA 'BAD MED DU YUN RING GNAS THUB PA BYUNG NA'ANG DE ZHI GNAS RJES MTHUN PA LAS DNGOS MIN,
gru.wylie: drug pa de las zhi gnas dngos 'grub tshul ni, sems gnas dgu pa thob nas bying rgod phra mo dang bral bar ting 'dzin la 'bad med du yun ring gnas thub pa byung na'ang de zhi gnas rjes mthun pa las dngos min
gru.english: Which brings us to the sixth and final topic of our conversation: a description of the actual state of quietude that we attain through the entire process we've presented here. When we do reach that ninth level of meditation, and we come to a point where we can stay in meditative concentration for an extended period of time—effortlessly—without seeing any of the subtle forms of dullness or agitation, even that is only an approximation of the state of quietude: it is not yet the real thing.

gru.acip: DE NAS NYER BSDOGS PHYI MA RNAMS BSGRUBS NAS RIM GYIS BSAM GZUGS BRGYAD KA BSGRUB NA'ANG THOB NUS MOD, 'ON KYANG DGOS PA CHUNG BAS RANG RES DE SKYED PA MIN ZHING,
gru.wylie: de nas nyer bsdogs phyi ma rnams bsgrubs nas rim gyis bsam gzugs brgyad ka bsgrub na'ang thob nus mod, 'on kyang dgos pa chung bas rang res de skyed pa min zhing
gru.english: Now at this point, we could go on to other preliminary stages and—step by step—work our way through achieving all eight of the concentration and formless-realm levels. There is actually though no great point to going through this exercise, and we needn't focus on trying to reach those particular forms of meditation. Final advice to focus on authentic meditations

gru.acip: BSNGAGS 'OS BSNGAGS BSTOD LAS, ,KHYOD KYI CHOS LA MI PHYOGS PA'I, ,SKYE BO GTI MUG GIS LDONGS PA, ,SRID RTZE'I BAR DU SONG NAS KYANG, ,SDUG BSNGAL YANG 'BYUNG SRID PA SGRUB, ,CES DANG,
gru.wylie: bsngags 'os bsngags bstod las, ,khyod kyi chos la mi phyogs pa'i, ,skye bo gti mug gis ldongs pa, ,srid rtse'i bar du song nas kyang, ,sdug bsngal yang 'byung srid pa sgrub, ,ces dang
gru.english: As the scripture called The Praise of What Deserves Praise puts it: There are though people Who are blinded by ignorance, And have no attraction To the Dharma you teach. Yes they may get as far As the Peak of Existence, But all they've achieved Is the cycle of pain, And the return of suffering.

gru.acip: DE LTAR ZHI GNAS LEGS PAR GRUB NA, RTZIG PA LA SOGS PA'I RDUL PHRA RAB TSUN KYANG BGRANG NUS PA'I TSOD KYI SEMS GSAL NYAMS DANG,
gru.wylie: de ltar zhi gnas legs par grub na, rtsig pa la sogs pa'i rdul phra rab tshun kyang bgrang nus pa'i tshod kyi sems gsal nyams dang
gru.english: If we follow the instructions here and thus perfectly arrive at the state of quietude, we can attain a great number of high personal qualities. Here are some examples. We experience such a degree of mental clarity that we can look at something like a wall, and go down so deep that we can count the number of atoms inside of it.

gru.acip: BYING BA BSAGS PA LA SGOM DU 'KHRUL NAS BSGOM PAS NI, KHAMS GONG MAR YANG 'PHEN MI NUS SHING, DUD 'GRO'I RGYU SGRUB PA LTA BU BYUNG BA YIN TE,
gru.wylie: bying ba bsags pa la sgom du 'khrul nas bsgom pas ni, khams gong mar yang 'phen mi nus shing, dud 'gro'i rgyu sgrub pa lta bu byung ba yin te
gru.english: Spending your time doing a meditation where you pile up experiences of mental dullness and mistake that for real meditation won't actually even help you get to the higher realms of suffering life: it's more like you're working hard to achieve the cause that will bring you a rebirth as an animal.

gru.acip: ,,GRUB MTHA' THAMS CAD KYI SNYING PO BSDUS PA ZHES BYA BA BZHUGS SO,,
gru.wylie: grub mtha' thams cad kyi snying po bsdus pa zhes bya ba bzhugs so
gru.english: Herein lies A Brief Survey of the Essence of Existing Belief Systems Preface The opening obeisance

gru.acip: ,TSOGS GNYIS RGYA MTSOR BRTZON PA'I MANDHA RAS, ,LEGS PAR BSRUBS LAS DON GNYIS 'GRUB PA'I NOR, ,MNGON DU GYUR NAS 'GRO LA PHAN BDE YI, ,'DOD DGU MCHOG STZOL STON PA GANG DER 'DUD,
gru.wylie: tshogs gnyis rgya mtshor brtson pa'i mandha ras, ,legs par bsrubs las don gnyis 'grub pa'i nor, ,mngon du gyur nas 'gro la phan bde yi, ,'dod dgu mchog stsol ston pa gang der 'dud
gru.english: Your effort, like Mount Mandhara, Churned deeply the ocean Of the two collections, And thus caused the treasure Of the two goals to emerge. I bow to you, the Teacher, Who grants every highest wish Of benefit and joy, for all beings.

gru.acip: ,BRTZON PA 'PHUL {%PHUL} GYIS RIG GNAS DU MA LA, ,LEGS SBYANGS RANG GZHAN GRUB MTHA'I MTHAR SON ZHING, ,'CHAD RTZOD RTZOM LA NGAG GI DBANG PHYUG DANG, ,DBYER MED DGE BA'I BSHES GNYEN RTAG TU RGYAL,
gru.wylie: brtson pa 'phul {%phul} gyis rig gnas du ma la, ,legs sbyangs rang gzhan grub mtha'i mthar son zhing, ,'chad rtsod rtsom la ngag gi dbang phyug dang, ,dbyer med dge ba'i bshes gnyen rtag tu rgyal
gru.english: My spiritual guides, You've mastered The many sciences, Through your extraordinary efforts— And thus come to the end Of all the systems of belief, Both our own and others'. In your explanation, argument, And composition, You are none other than Lords of The Spoken Word; May you be forever victorious.

gru.acip: DE LTAR MCHOD PAR BRJOD NAS GANG BSHAD PAR BYA BA NI, BLO GROS DON DU GNYER BA 'GA' LA PHAN PA'I CHED DU RANG GZHAN GYI GRUB MTHA'I SNYING PO'I DON BSDUS NAS 'CHAD PAR BYED LA, DE YANG LUNG 'DREN SOGS MANG NA BLO DMAN DAG GIS RTOGS MI NUS PAS NA, DE'I PHYIR LUNG CUNG ZAD RES BRGYAN TE BSHAD PAR BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: de ltar mchod par brjod nas gang bshad par bya ba ni, blo gros don du gnyer ba 'ga' la phan pa'i ched du rang gzhan gyi grub mtha'i snying po'i don bsdus nas 'chad par byed la, de yang lung 'dren sogs mang na blo dman dag gis rtogs mi nus pas na, de'i phyir lung cung zad res brgyan te bshad par bya'o
gru.english: Now that our offering of praise is complete, what topic are we going to explain? This will be a summary of the very essence of the belief systems followed by both ourselves and others.  I do hope it may be of some use to a few hard-working students who aspire to reaching true wisdom. That said, if I quote too many scriptures and such, then students who are less intelligent won't be able to understand; so I'll just dress up my explanation with a few textual citations here and there!

gru.acip: 'DI LA GNYIS, PHYI NANG GI KHYAD PAR NGOS BZUNG BA DANG, GRUB MTHA'I KHYAD PAR SO SOR BSHAD PA'O, ,DANG PO NI,
gru.wylie: 'di la gnyis, phyi nang gi khyad par ngos bzung ba dang, grub mtha'i khyad par so sor bshad pa'o, ,dang po ni
gru.english: There will be two parts to this presentation.  First I'll describe the difference between an “outer” and an “inner” belief system; and then I'll go into the unique concepts espoused by each of the different systems of belief.  Here then we begin, with that first distinction. The meaning of siddhanta

gru.acip: GRUB MTHA'I THA SNYAD 'DI GANG GIS BYAS PA YIN ZHE NA,
gru.wylie: grub mtha'i tha snyad 'di gang gis byas pa yin zhe na
gru.english: We might start with a simple question: “Who came up with the original Sanskrit term for 'belief system'; that is, where does the word siddhanta come from, in the first place?”

gru.acip: 'DI LA RANG SDE'I GRUB MTHA'I THA SNYAD GI {%NI} STON PA NYID KYIS GSUNGS PA YIN TE,
gru.wylie: 'di la rang sde'i grub mtha'i tha snyad gi {%ni} ston pa nyid kyis gsungs pa yin te
gru.english: The answer is that our Teacher himself referred to our own various belief systems with this term.

gru.acip: ,LANG KAR GANG GSHEGS PA'I MDO LAS, ,NGA YI CHOS TSUL RNAM GNYIS TE, ,BSTAN PA DANG NI GRUB MTHA' 'O,, ZHES GSUNGS PAS SO,,
gru.wylie: lang kar gang gshegs pa'i mdo las, ,nga yi chos tshul rnam gnyis te, ,bstan pa dang ni grub mtha' 'o,, zhes gsungs pas so
gru.english: In A Journey to Langka he says: I make my presentation Of great ideas in two different ways: Either I give a teaching, Or a system of belief.

gru.acip: GRUB MTHA'I SGRA DON NI, RNAM RTOG GIS SGRO BTAGS PA'I CHA GZHAN BZLOG NAS RANG GI BLO NGOR 'THAD PAR GRUB PAS NA, GRUB MTHA' 'O,,
gru.wylie: grub mtha'i sgra don ni, rnam rtog gis sgro btags pa'i cha gzhan bzlog nas rang gi blo ngor 'thad par grub pas na, grub mtha' 'o
gru.english: Here's the literal meaning of siddhanta, the original Sanskrit word for “belief system”: when you eliminate all of the conceptual exaggerations that your imagination lays upon things, then the more accurate understanding which—in the end (anta)—you have thereby reached (siddha) is called a “belief system” (siddhanta).

gru.acip: GRUB MTHA' LA GNYIS SU NGES PAS, DE LA ZHUGS PA LA YANG PHYI NANG GI GANG ZAG GNYIS SU NGES SO,,
gru.wylie: grub mtha' la gnyis su nges pas, de la zhugs pa la yang phyi nang gi gang zag gnyis su nges so
gru.english: Now belief systems are fixed at two types; and so the types of people who follow these systems are also fixed at two: we call them “outer” and “inner.”

gru.acip: BLO GROS DMAN PA RNAMS KYIS RANG GI STON PA'I RJES SU 'JUG PA DANG DES BSTAN PA'I CHOS BSGRUB BYA YIN PAR BZUNG NAS SKYABS SU 'GRO BA NI, MOS MNO TZAM DANG YID DPYOD TZAM GYIS {%GYI} SGO NAS YIN GYI, BLO CHE BA RNAMS KYIS THOG MA NYID NAS PHYOGS LHUNG DANG 'DOD ZHEN GYIS RANG GI STON PA'O SNYAM PA DANG DES GSUNGS PA'O SNYAM DU MI 'DZIN PAR PHYI NANG GI STON PA GNYIS LAS GANG GI BSHAD PA DE RIGS PA YIN,
gru.wylie: blo gros dman pa rnams kyis rang gi ston pa'i rjes su 'jug pa dang des bstan pa'i chos bsgrub bya yin par bzung nas skyabs su 'gro ba ni, mos mno tsam dang yid dpyod tsam gyis {%gyi} sgo nas yin gyi, blo che ba rnams kyis thog ma nyid nas phyogs lhung dang 'dod zhen gyis rang gi ston pa'o snyam pa dang des gsungs pa'o snyam du mi 'dzin par phyi nang gi ston pa gnyis las gang gi bshad pa de rigs pa yin
gru.english: People of lesser intellectual capacity tend to follow their own teacher and practice whatever that teacher teaches, and in this way take their refuge in them.  It's all done out of blind faith and guesswork.  Those of greater intellect don't think in terms of sticking to their teacher and their teacher's words from nothing more than prejudice or favoritism.  Whether they encounter a teacher from an outer belief system or an inner one, in either case they wait to see if the explanations given make sense.

gru.acip: DES NA BSTAN PA LA YANG SANGS RGYAS KYI LUNG RTOGS KYI BSTAN PA NI, GDUL BYA RNAMS KYI GNAS SKABS DANG MTHAR THUG GI PHAN BDE SGRUB PA'I THABS DANG, GZHAN GIS {%GYIS} BSTAN PA NI DE LAS LDOG PAR NGES PAR 'GYUR RO,,
gru.wylie: des na bstan pa la yang sangs rgyas kyi lung rtogs kyi bstan pa ni, gdul bya rnams kyi gnas skabs dang mthar thug gi phan bde sgrub pa'i thabs dang, gzhan gis {%gyis} bstan pa ni de las ldog par nges par 'gyur ro
gru.english: This approach leads students to a certainty that the teachings of the Buddhas—in the form of both scripture and realizations—are a method that brings benefit and joy to disciples on both an immediate and an ultimate level.  And the students gain equal certainty that what is taught by others is the opposite.

gru.acip: GNYIS PA KHYAD PAR SO SOR BSHAD PA LA, PHYI NANG GI GRUB MTHA' GNYIS LAS, DANG PO LA GSUM, BYUNG RIM, MING DON, SO SOR BSHAD PA'O,,
gru.wylie: gnyis pa khyad par so sor bshad pa la, phyi nang gi grub mtha' gnyis las, dang po la gsum, byung rim, ming don, so sor bshad pa'o
gru.english: Now that we've covered the general difference between outer and inner systems of belief, let's look at the differences between specific systems.  We'll begin with the outer belief systems, covering this topic in three steps: how such systems started; how they got the name “outer”; and finally the details of each one.

gru.acip: DANG PO LA GSUM, STON PA MING DON GRUB MTHA' 'O,,
gru.wylie: dang po la gsum, ston pa ming don grub mtha' 'o
gru.english: We'll cover the beliefs in three parts.  Who are their teachers?  What do the names of their systems mean?  And what exactly is the system they believe in?

gru.acip: GNYIS {%GSUM} PA GRUB MTHA' NI, 'DIS RNAM 'GREL LAS, ,DPER NA TSER MA LA SOGS PA'I, ,RNO SOGS RGYU MED PA NYID DE, ,ZHES SOGS DANG,
gru.wylie: gnyis {%gsum} pa grub mtha' ni, 'dis rnam 'grel las, ,dper na tsher ma la sogs pa'i, ,rno sogs rgyu med pa nyid de, ,zhes sogs dang
gru.english: Here third is the actual belief system of the Nihilists.  We see it described in the Commentary on Accurate Perception: It is for example like the idea That things like the sharpness Of a thorn have no cause.

gru.acip: YANG TSE 'DI LA SER SNA CAN KHA CIG PHYUG PA DANG, SBYIN PA GTONG PA {%BA} KHA CIG DBUL BA DANG, YANG 'DIR CHOS SGRUB PA KHA CIG SDUG BSNGAL BA DANG, SDIG PA BYED PA KHA CIG BDE BAR MTHONG NAS DGE MI DGE'I LAS 'BRAS MI BDEN PAR 'DOD PA DANG,
gru.wylie: yang tshe 'di la ser sna can kha cig phyug pa dang, sbyin pa gtong pa {%ba} kha cig dbul ba dang, yang 'dir chos sgrub pa kha cig sdug bsngal ba dang, sdig pa byed pa kha cig bde bar mthong nas dge mi dge'i las 'bras mi bden par 'dod pa dang
gru.english: In this life too we can see people who dislike sharing what they have, and yet who are rich.  We also see people who are very generous, and yet poor.  We see those who practice the teachings, and still suffer.  And we see people who do a lot of bad things to others, and yet still seem happy.  In light of all this, the Outcasts believe that the idea that good deeds and bad deeds bear their respective fruits cannot be true.

gru.acip: ,ZHES SOGS KYIS SPYIR RGYU MED LAS MI SKYE BA DANG, KHYAD PAR BYIS PA BTZAS MA THAG PA DANG, 'CHI KHA MA'I RIG PAS MTSON NAS SKYE BA SNGA PHYI YOD PA'I SGRUB BYED DU {%DU MA} DANG, BLO SOGS GOMS NA RIM GYIS GSAL BA 'ONG BA SOGS KYIS KUN MKHYEN YOD PA DANG, TSER MA'I RNO BA DE RANG RGYU TSER MA 'GYUR BA'I NUS PA'I BYED PAS 'GRUB PAS,
gru.wylie: zhes sogs kyis spyir rgyu med las mi skye ba dang, khyad par byis pa btsas ma thag pa dang, 'chi kha ma'i rig pas mtshon nas skye ba snga phyi yod pa'i sgrub byed du {%du ma} dang, blo sogs goms na rim gyis gsal ba 'ong ba sogs kyis kun mkhyen yod pa dang, tsher ma'i rno ba de rang rgyu tsher ma 'gyur ba'i nus pa'i byed pas 'grub pas
gru.english: Here we've given quotations to show that, generally speaking, things cannot start without a cause.  More specifically, we've given citations about a child just after birth and the mind at the moment of death, as examples of proofs of past and future lives.  We've added further references to show that—through steady practice—you will gradually clean your mind till you come to know all things.  We've also demonstrated that a thorn's sharpness is caused by the same power that caused the thorn itself.

gru.acip: DE LTA BU LA RGYU YOD PA DANG, SKYE BA PHYI MA RGYANG BAN LTA BU'I MNGON SUM GYIS MI MTHONG YANG YOD PA'I SGRUB BYED SOGS SGRUB BYED DU MA MDZAD LA,
gru.wylie: de lta bu la rgyu yod pa dang, skye ba phyi ma rgyang ban lta bu'i mngon sum gyis mi mthong yang yod pa'i sgrub byed sogs sgrub byed du ma mdzad la
gru.english: All these kinds of things really do have causes.  And even though people like the Outcasts can't directly see future births, we have presented here a wide variety of proofs that establish the existence of these and other such entities.

gru.acip: DE YANG SPYIR DNGOS STOBS KYI RIGS PAS SGRUB NUS PA NI, DES SGRUB LA, DE TZAM GYIS MI NUS PA NI DPYAD PA GSUM GYIS DAG PA'I LUNG GIS SGRUB TSUL RNAM 'GREL DANG DE'I tIKKA MTHA' DPYOD SOGS NA GSAL LO,,
gru.wylie: de yang spyir dngos stobs kyi rigs pas sgrub nus pa ni, des sgrub la, de tsam gyis mi nus pa ni dpyad pa gsum gyis dag pa'i lung gis sgrub tshul rnam 'grel dang de'i Tikka mtha' dpyod sogs na gsal lo
gru.english: In general, we should use the logic based on the nature of things to prove what can be proven that way.  In cases where this type of logic is not sufficient, we can use scriptural authority which has been confirmed with the three tests, to accomplish the proof.  This methodology is clearly presented in works such as the Commentary on Accurate Perception; its classical commentaries; and the various analytical textbooks based upon those. Chapter 3 Eleven Eternalist Belief Systems 1) The Numerist belief system

gru.acip: ,,GNYIS PA RTAG SMRA BA'I GRUB MTHA' LA GNYIS, DE'I LUGS BRJOD PA DANG, DE DGAG PA'O,,
gru.wylie: gnyis pa rtag smra ba'i grub mtha' la gnyis, de'i lugs brjod pa dang, de dgag pa'o
gru.english: This brings us to the second major section of our book: a description of the belief systems followed by the Eternalists.  First we'll present their position, and then we'll refute it.

gru.acip: DANG PO LA STON PA, MING, GRUB MTHA'I KHYAD PAR RO,,
gru.wylie: dang po la ston pa, ming, grub mtha'i khyad par ro
gru.english: We'll treat the first of these eleven systems in three parts.  Who are their teachers?  Why are they called “Numerists”?  And what are the details of their belief system?

gru.acip: DE SNGAR GYI RGYU DUS SU YOD CES KHAS LEN PAS BDAG SKYE 'DOD PAR MTSUNGS LA, KHYAD PAR NI RANG GI RGYU DANG NGO BO GCIG PA MI GSAL BA'I TSUL DU YOD PA ZHIG GSAL BAR 'BYUNG DGOS PAR 'DOD PA DANG, YANG 'O MA ZHOR 'GYUR BA LTAR GRUB ZIN SLAR YANG SKYE BAR 'DOD PA'I TSUL GNYIS YOD DO,,
gru.wylie: de sngar gyi rgyu dus su yod ces khas len pas bdag skye 'dod par mtshungs la, khyad par ni rang gi rgyu dang ngo bo gcig pa mi gsal ba'i tshul du yod pa zhig gsal bar 'byung dgos par 'dod pa dang, yang 'o ma zhor 'gyur ba ltar grub zin slar yang skye bar 'dod pa'i tshul gnyis yod do
gru.english: Now saying that the sprout somehow existed back at the time of its cause is the same thing as saying that the sprout was born from itself; but there are two ways that Numerists distance themselves from that position.  Sometimes they say that the sprout exists in some obscure form within its own cause, and that it must be revealed.  At other times they describe the sprout as already being present there in its cause, but as something that must come out once again.  They compare it to the way in which milk, which has already come out, must make an additional transformation to become yogurt.

gru.acip: ,GNYIS PA TSANGS PA'I 'DOD PA LA, STON PA, MING, GRUB MTHA' RNAMS LAS,
gru.wylie: gnyis pa tshangs pa'i 'dod pa la, ston pa, ming, grub mtha' rnams las
gru.english: We'll address the ideas of the Purists, the second group of Eternalists, using the same three sections as before: Who are their teachers?  Why are they called “Purists”?  And what are the details of their belief system?

gru.acip: YANG RTA 'GA' ZHIG LA KHAB LNGA BRGYA RE BTZUGS NAS SBYIN SREG BYED DE, DE LAS LHAG TSANGS PA SGRUB PA'I THABS KHYAD PAR CAN GZHAN MED PAR 'DOD,
gru.wylie: yang rta 'ga' zhig la khab lnga brgya re btsugs nas sbyin sreg byed de, de las lhag tshangs pa sgrub pa'i thabs khyad par can gzhan med par 'dod
gru.english: They may also take some of these horses and pierce each one with 500 nails before offering them into the fire.  They believe there is no higher way than this to reach the Pure One.

gru.acip: ,,GSUM PA BRDA SPROD PA LA, STON PA MING GRUB MTHA' RNAMS LAS,
gru.wylie: gsum pa brda sprod pa la, ston pa ming grub mtha' rnams las
gru.english: Here third we'll address the beliefs of the Linguists in the same three sections: Who is their teacher?  Why are they called “Linguists”?  And what are the details of their belief system?

gru.acip: ,,BZHI PA RIG BYED PA LA, STON PA MING GRUB MTHA' RNAMS LAS,
gru.wylie: bzhi pa rig byed pa la, ston pa ming grub mtha' rnams las
gru.english: The “Knowers” are the fourth Eternalist system of belief.  We'll discuss their teacher, their name, and their beliefs.

gru.acip: ,,LNGA PA GSANG BA PA LA, STON PA MING GRUB MTHA' RNAMS LAS,
gru.wylie: lnga pa gsang ba pa la, ston pa ming grub mtha' rnams las
gru.english: The fifth of the Eternalist belief systems is that of the “Hidden Ones”; again, we'll discuss their teacher, their name, and their beliefs.

gru.acip: ,,DRUG PA KHYAB 'JUG PA LA, STON PA MING GRUB MTHA' RNAMS LAS,
gru.wylie: drug pa khyab 'jug pa la, ston pa ming grub mtha' rnams las
gru.english: The sixth of the Eternalist systems is that of the Universalists, which we will again cover in terms of their teacher; their name; and their beliefs.

gru.acip: ,,BDUN PA DPYOD PA {%PA BA} LA, STON {%PA} MING GRUB MTHA' LAS,
gru.wylie: bdun pa dpyod pa {%pa ba} la, ston {%pa} ming grub mtha' las
gru.english: The “Analyzers” are the seventh Eternalist belief system.  Again, we'll discuss their teacher, their name, and their beliefs.

gru.acip: ,,BRGYAD PA ZHI BA PA LA, STON {%STON PA} MING GRUB MTHA' RNAMS LAS,
gru.wylie: brgyad pa zhi ba pa la, ston {%ston pa} ming grub mtha' rnams las
gru.english: The Followers of the Destroyer are the eighth Eternalist system.  We'll again discuss their teacher, their name, and their beliefs.

gru.acip: 'KHRIG PA'I GRUB PA NI THAR PA YIN LA, ZHES SOGS GSUNGS PA'I PHYIR RO,,
gru.wylie: 'khrig pa'i grub pa ni thar pa yin la, zhes sogs gsungs pa'i phyir ro
gru.english: So too we see lines like— The practice of sex is liberation. 9) The belief system of the Detailers

gru.acip: ,,DGU PA BYE BRAG PA LA, STON PA MING GRUB MTHA' RNAMS LAS,
gru.wylie: dgu pa bye brag pa la, ston pa ming grub mtha' rnams las
gru.english: The “Detailers” are the ninth of the Eternalist systems.  We'll discuss their teacher, their name, and their beliefs.

gru.acip: ,,BCU PA RIG {%RIGS} PA CAN PA LA, STON PA MING GRUB MTHA' RNAMS LAS,
gru.wylie: bcu pa rig {%rigs} pa can pa la, ston pa ming grub mtha' rnams las
gru.english: The “Logicians” are the tenth system among the Eternalists.  We'll discuss their teacher, their name, and their beliefs.

gru.acip: ,,BCU GCIG BZAD {%PA ZAD} BYED PA LA, STON PA MING GRUB MTHA' RNAMS LAS,
gru.wylie: bcu gcig bzad {%pa zad} byed pa la, ston pa ming grub mtha' rnams las
gru.english: The Removers are the eleventh and final Eternalist system.  Again we cover their teachers, their name, and their beliefs.

gru.acip: GNYIS PA RTAG SMRA BA'I LUGS DE DAG THUN MONG DU DGAG PA NI, MDO LAS KYANG GSUNGS SHING KLU SGRUB SOGS MKHAS GRUB GZHAN MANG POS KYANG BSHAD YOD,
gru.wylie: gnyis pa rtag smra ba'i lugs de dag thun mong du dgag pa ni, mdo las kyang gsungs shing klu sgrub sogs mkhas grub gzhan mang pos kyang bshad yod
gru.english: We've now reached step two on the topic of the Eternalist schools.  We'll refute all of their positions together, for this refutation has been covered both in the sutras, and by many wise and accomplished masters such as Nagarjuna.

gru.acip: DE NYID SNANG BAR, ,RANG GI BDAG NYID SKYED PA MED, ,GRUB PA YIN NA DBYER MED PHYIR, ,ZHES SOGS DANG,
gru.wylie: de nyid snang bar, ,rang gi bdag nyid skyed pa med, ,grub pa yin na dbyer med phyir, ,zhes sogs dang
gru.english: And the Illumination of Suchness says things like: Nothing could give birth to itself; Or else you could never tell things apart.

gru.acip: ,NGES PAR KHYAD PAR LDAN PA YIS {%YI}, [,RANG BZHIN DBYER MED GCIG NYID DE, ,DE LTA YIN NA THA DAD NYID, ,JI LTAR YANG NI BSGRUB DKA' STE,] ,ZHES SOGS DANG,
gru.wylie: nges par khyad par ldan pa yis {%yi}, [,rang bzhin dbyer med gcig nyid de, ,de lta yin na tha dad nyid, ,ji ltar yang ni bsgrub dka' ste,] ,zhes sogs dang
gru.english: And we see others, from the same work, including: It is a certainty That any indivisible, Singular supreme Nature Which possessed Its different variations Would therefore need To be separate from them; Which in any case Would be a difficult thing Ever to establish.

gru.acip: 'ON KYANG MU STEGS BYED DE DAG NI RANG GI GRUB MTHA' {%MTHA'I} RIG {%RIGS} PA LA SBYANGS PA'I DBANG GIS SGRUB BYED DU MA YOD CING, LOG LTA CAN DE RNAMS NI RIG {%RIGS} PA GANG LA YANG MA SBYANGS PAS SHIN TU RMONGS PA'I MUN PA DANG, LOG PAR ZHUGS PA'O,,
gru.wylie: 'on kyang mu stegs byed de dag ni rang gi grub mtha' {%mtha'i} rig {%rigs} pa la sbyangs pa'i dbang gis sgrub byed du ma yod cing, log lta can de rnams ni rig {%rigs} pa gang la yang ma sbyangs pas shin tu rmongs pa'i mun pa dang, log par zhugs pa'o
gru.english: We should say though that these River schools have spent considerable time working through the logic for their own systems of belief—and thus do have many proofs of their own.  The fact though is that they have failed to devote any time at all to mastering the process of reasoning itself, and so remain in the deepest darkness of confusion, and mistaken positions.

gru.acip: LAS 'BRAS YOD PAR BDEN GRUB TU BZUNGS NAS DGE BA BYED PA NI, THAR PA'I RGYU KHYAD PAR CAN MIN KYANG BDE 'GRO'I RGYUR 'GRO LA, LAS 'BRAS MED PAR LTA BA DANG DE LA YID MI CHES PA NI, NGAN 'GRO'I RGYU DNGOS YIN TE,
gru.wylie: las 'bras yod par bden grub tu bzungs nas dge ba byed pa ni, thar pa'i rgyu khyad par can min kyang bde 'gro'i rgyur 'gro la, las 'bras med par lta ba dang de la yid mi ches pa ni, ngan 'gro'i rgyu dngos yin te
gru.english: Holding to the perception that the law of karma and its consequences does exist—but that it exists as something ultimately real—and then engaging in good deeds cannot serve as any exceptional cause for reaching freedom.  Nonetheless, it can provide a cause for us to take a birth into the higher realms of existence—whereas the belief that there is no such law, and thus failing to believe in it, is a genuine cause for a birth in the realms of misery.

gru.acip: KHA CIG 'DI SNYAM DU NANG PA'I GRUB MTHA' SHES DGOS KYANG PHYI ROL BA'I {%PA'I} GRUB MTHAS CI BYA ZHE NA,
gru.wylie: kha cig 'di snyam du nang pa'i grub mtha' shes dgos kyang phyi rol ba'i {%pa'i} grub mthas ci bya zhe na
gru.english: The following thought may occur to some of our readers: I can appreciate why we should understand our Buddhist belief systems; but I don't see why you are covering here systems outside of that.

gru.acip: DE LA MKHAS PA RNAMS KYIS RANG DANG GZHAN GYI GRUB MTHA' KUN SHES DGOS PA YIN TE, DE MI SHES NA GZHAN SDE'I GRUB MTHA' NI DMAN PA DANG, RANG SDE'I GRUB MTHA' NI MCHOG YIN PAR LEGS PAR MI SHES PAS DE LTAR MI SHES BZHIN DU MCHOG DMAN DU 'DZIN PA NI RANG PHYOGS MCHOG 'DZIN NAM, RANG GI 'DOD PHYOGS TZAM DU 'GYUR BA'I PHYIR RO,,
gru.wylie: de la mkhas pa rnams kyis rang dang gzhan gyi grub mtha' kun shes dgos pa yin te, de mi shes na gzhan sde'i grub mtha' ni dman pa dang, rang sde'i grub mtha' ni mchog yin par legs par mi shes pas de ltar mi shes bzhin du mchog dman du 'dzin pa ni rang phyogs mchog 'dzin nam, rang gi 'dod phyogs tsam du 'gyur ba'i phyir ro
gru.english: The answer is that true sages need to have a thorough understanding of both their own belief system, and the systems of others as well.  If we don't understand both, we can't really come to an appreciation of why other belief systems might be less rational, and our own the most rational.  And if we lack such an appreciation, and still hold to a difference like this between systems, then we are simply being biased towards our own belief system.  And then that system becomes nothing more than personal prejudice.

gru.acip: GZHAN YANG DE LTAR SHES DGOS TE, DPER NA RGYA MTSO'I PHA ROL TU 'GRO BA LA GRU DGOS PA BZHIN DU GRUB MTHA' RGYA MTSO'I PHA ROL TU 'GRO BA LA DE LTAR SHES DGOS PA'I PHYIR TE,
gru.wylie: gzhan yang de ltar shes dgos te, dper na rgya mtsho'i pha rol tu 'gro ba la gru dgos pa bzhin du grub mtha' rgya mtsho'i pha rol tu 'gro ba la de ltar shes dgos pa'i phyir te
gru.english: And there is, moreover, a good reason why we should learn about all these different systems.  To draw a metaphor, a person who hopes to travel to the land on the other side of an ocean is going to need a ship; and the journey across the ocean of different belief systems that we see in the world is best accomplished with an appreciation of the many different systems that people hold to.

whole_word_matches.context: es dgos te, dper na rgya mtsho'i pha rol tu 'gro ba la gru dgos pa bzhin du grub mtha' rgya mtsho'i pha rol tu 'g

gru.acip: RANG RE'I RJE BLA MA YAB SRAS KYIS RANG GZHAN GYI GRUB MTHA' KUN LA YANG NA {%KUN LA MKHAS} MKHAS PAR SBYANGS PA YIN TE, RTOGS BRJOD LAS, ,DE NYID PHYIR NA MI PHAM CHOS RJE DANG, [,'DZAM GLING RGYAN DRUG MCHOG GNYIS ZHES GRAGS PA'I, ,GZHUNG LA PHYOGS RE BA DANG RAGS PA RES,] ,TSIM PAR MA BYAS KUN LA ZHIB TU SBYANGS, ,ZHES PA'I BAR DANG,
gru.wylie: rang re'i rje bla ma yab sras kyis rang gzhan gyi grub mtha' kun la yang na {%kun la mkhas} mkhas par sbyangs pa yin te, rtogs brjod las, ,de nyid phyir na mi pham chos rje dang, [,'dzam gling rgyan drug mchog gnyis zhes grags pa'i, ,gzhung la phyogs re ba dang rags pa res,] ,tshim par ma byas kun la zhib tu sbyangs, ,zhes pa'i bar dang
gru.english: The masters of our own lineage—the Lord, Tsongkapa, and his two spiritual sons—closely studied and thoroughly grasped the details of all the major belief systems of their time.  The Spiritual Life puts it this way: Learn then to be insatiable: Dig deep into the details Of all the classics you can find, Looking for details, And overviews as well. You could start with those Of the Undefeatable, The Lord of the Dharma, And the masters we know As the Six Jewels of the World, Along with the Two Supreme.

gru.acip: RGYAL TSAB KYI BSTOD PAR, ,RANG GZHAN GRUB MTHA'I PHA ROL SON, ,ZHES SOGS DANG,
gru.wylie: rgyal tshab kyi bstod par, ,rang gzhan grub mtha'i pha rol son, ,zhes sogs dang
gru.english: The praise of Gyaltsab puts it this way: You travelled to the farthest shore Of the systems of belief Followed by both ourselves and others.

gru.acip: MKHAS GRUB KYI GSUNG RAB DU MA LAS KYANG RANG NYID GRUB MTHA' KUN LA MKHAS PAR ZHAL GYIS BZHES PA'I PHYIR RO,,
gru.wylie: mkhas grub kyi gsung rab du ma las kyang rang nyid grub mtha' kun la mkhas par zhal gyis bzhes pa'i phyir ro
gru.english: And we see many writings by Kedrup Je in which he also describes himself as being a master of all the various systems of belief. Concluding lines for Part One

gru.acip: ,RANG GZHAN GRUB MTHA' MCHOG DMAN YOD DO ZHES, ,KUN GYI {%GYIS} 'BRUG SGRA JI BZHIN SGROGS MOD KYANG, ,KHYAD PAR MA {%MI} SHES RANG PHYOGS MCHOG 'DZIN PA, ,PHYOGS LHUNG GDON GYIS ZIN PAR GSUNGS PAS NA,
gru.wylie: rang gzhan grub mtha' mchog dman yod do zhes, ,kun gyi {%gyis} 'brug sgra ji bzhin sgrogs mod kyang, ,khyad par ma {%mi} shes rang phyogs mchog 'dzin pa, ,phyogs lhung gdon gyis zin par gsungs pas na
gru.english: You see everybody Shouting to the sky, Loud as a dragon's roar, That their system of belief Is the very best of all; While those of others Are the very worst. But please remember How it's been stated That a person who clings To their school as best Without any understanding Of how it differs from others Is simply themselves A victim Of the demon of prejudice.

gru.acip: ,CES RANG GZHAN GYI GRUB MTHA' KUN GYI SNYING PO'I DON BSDUS PA BLO GSAL 'JUG PA'I KHANG BZANG LAS, GZHAN SDE'I LUGS BKOD NAS BKAG PA'I SKABS SO,, ,,
gru.wylie: ces rang gzhan gyi grub mtha' kun gyi snying po'i don bsdus pa blo gsal 'jug pa'i khang bzang las, gzhan sde'i lugs bkod nas bkag pa'i skabs so,,
gru.english: This concludes then the section on presenting and refuting the systems of other groups, from that veritable palace built for the entertainment of those with clearest minds: A Brief Survey of the Essence of Every Existing Belief System, Whether Ours or Others'. Part Two The 62 Mistaken Views The 62 Mistaken Views The sutra entitled Endless Jewels, taught by Lord Buddha 25 centuries ago, is one of the best original sources for a famous teaching called “The 62 Mistaken Views.”  We start with the Buddha addressing his disciples, well into the work— Lord Buddha lists the 62

gru.acip: 'DI LA KHA CIG DAG 'DI SKAD SMRA ZHING 'DI LTAR LTA BA YOD DE, GANG GI TSE BDAG GZUGS CAN DE 'BYUNG BA CHEN PO BZHI LAS GYUR PA CHAD PAR 'GYUR, RNAM PAR 'JUG {%'JIG} PAR 'GYUR, MI 'GRUB PAR 'GYUR TE, DE TZAM GYI SA {%GYIS} BDAG DE YANG DAG PAR CHAD PAR 'GYUR RO,,
gru.wylie: 'di la kha cig dag 'di skad smra zhing 'di ltar lta ba yod de, gang gi tshe bdag gzugs can de 'byung ba chen po bzhi las gyur pa chad par 'gyur, rnam par 'jug {%'jig} par 'gyur, mi 'grub par 'gyur te, de tsam gyi sa {%gyis} bdag de yang dag par chad par 'gyur ro
gru.english: (56) So there are some people who say the following, as how they view things: “There comes a point where my physical self—the one which is derived from the four great elements—is discontinued.  It is destroyed; it goes out of existence.  And with nothing more than that, my self discontinues as well.”

gru.acip: GANG GI TSE BDAG DE LHA'I 'DOD PA'I YON TAN DAG LA YONGS SU SPYAD NAS CHAD PAR 'GYUR, RNAM PAR 'JIG PAR 'GYUR, MI 'GRUB PAR 'GYUR TE, DE TZAM GYIS BDAG DE YANG DAG PAR CHAD PAR 'GYUR RO,,
gru.wylie: gang gi tshe bdag de lha'i 'dod pa'i yon tan dag la yongs su spyad nas chad par 'gyur, rnam par 'jig par 'gyur, mi 'grub par 'gyur te, de tsam gyis bdag de yang dag par chad par 'gyur ro
gru.english: (57) Others say: “There is a point at which my self revels in the objects of desire enjoyed by the worldly gods, and then simply discontinues.  It is destroyed; it goes out of existence.  And with nothing more than that, my self discontinues completely.”

gru.acip: DE LA GZHAN DAG 'DI SKAD SMRA STE, BDAG DE DE TZAM GYIS YANG DAG PAR CHAD PAR MI 'GYUR RO, ,GANG GI TSE BDAG GZUGS CAN DE 'JIG RTEN PHA ROL NAS SHI NAS MI'I BZANG PO YONGS SU SPYAD DE CHAD PAR 'GYUR, RNAM PAR 'JIG PAR 'GYUR, MI 'GRUB PAR 'GYUR TE, BDAG DE YANG DAG PAR CHAD PAR 'GYUR RO, DE BZHIN DU SBYAR TE,
gru.wylie: de la gzhan dag 'di skad smra ste, bdag de de tsam gyis yang dag par chad par mi 'gyur ro, ,gang gi tshe bdag gzugs can de 'jig rten pha rol nas shi nas mi'i bzang po yongs su spyad de chad par 'gyur, rnam par 'jig par 'gyur, mi 'grub par 'gyur te, bdag de yang dag par chad par 'gyur ro, de bzhin du sbyar te
gru.english: (58) Others have this to say about that last idea: “Actually that point is not enough to say that the self has discontinued.  Rather, there is a point at which the physical version of our self—in the world to come—dies there; and all its experience of good things in the world of humans comes to a stop.  It is destroyed; it goes out of existence.  And then the self too comes to a total stop.”  This pattern of the wording is continued next.

gru.acip: DE LA GZHAN DAG 'DI SKAD SMRA STE, BDAG DE DE TZAM GYIS YANG DAG PAR CHAD PAR MI 'GYUR RO, ,GANG GI TSE BDAG GZUGS CAN MA YIN PA DE 'JIG RTEN PHA ROL NAS SHI NAS NAM MKHA' LA 'DU SHES SKYE MCHED DU NYE BAR SONG STE CHAD PAR 'GYUR, RNAM PAR 'JIG PAR 'GYUR, MI 'GRUB PAR 'GYUR TE, DE TZAM GYIS ZHES BYA BA NAS DE BZHIN DU SBYAR RO,,
gru.wylie: de la gzhan dag 'di skad smra ste, bdag de de tsam gyis yang dag par chad par mi 'gyur ro, ,gang gi tshe bdag gzugs can ma yin pa de 'jig rten pha rol nas shi nas nam mkha' la 'du shes skye mched du nye bar song ste chad par 'gyur, rnam par 'jig par 'gyur, mi 'grub par 'gyur te, de tsam gyis zhes bya ba nas de bzhin du sbyar ro
gru.english: (59) Still further, you find people who say, “No, that alone is not the point at which the self discontinues completely.  Rather, there comes a point where the self—in a form with no physicality, in the world to come—dies there.  It then passes into the sky, into a certain realm of thought, and discontinues.  It is destroyed, and goes out of existence…”  (And then you can complete the viewpoint in the same pattern you see above: “And with nothing more than that” and so on.)

gru.acip: DE LA GZHAN DAG 'DI SKAD SMRA STE, BDAG DE DE TZAM GYIS YANG DAG PAR CHAD PAR MI 'GYUR RO, ,GANG GI TSE BDAG GZUGS CAN MA YIN PA DE 'JIG RTEN PHA ROL NAS SHI NAS RNAM SHES 'DU SHES SKYE MCHED DU NYE BAR SONG STE CHAD PAR 'GYUR, RNAM PAR 'JIG PAR 'GYUR, MI 'GRUB PAR 'GYUR TE, BDAG DE YANG DAG PAR CHAD PAR 'GYUR BA'I BAR DE BZHIN DU SBYAR RO,,
gru.wylie: de la gzhan dag 'di skad smra ste, bdag de de tsam gyis yang dag par chad par mi 'gyur ro, ,gang gi tshe bdag gzugs can ma yin pa de 'jig rten pha rol nas shi nas rnam shes 'du shes skye mched du nye bar song ste chad par 'gyur, rnam par 'jig par 'gyur, mi 'grub par 'gyur te, bdag de yang dag par chad par 'gyur ba'i bar de bzhin du sbyar ro
gru.english: (60) And even further, we see those who say: “All that in itself is not enough to say that the self has discontinued altogether.  Instead, there comes a point where the self—indeed in a form with no physicality, in the world to come—dies there.  The consciousness then passes into a certain realm of thought, and discontinues.  It is destroyed, and goes out of existence.”  And then the wording of the position follows the same pattern, up to the point about the self reaching a point where it discontinues completely.

gru.acip: DE LA GZHAN DAG 'DI SKAD SMRA STE, BDAG DE DE TZAM GYIS YANG DAG PAR CHAD PAR MI 'GYUR RO, ,GANG GI TSE BDAG GZUGS CAN MA YIN PA DE 'JIG RTEN PHA ROL NAS SHI NAS CI'ANG MED PA'I SKYE MCHED DU NYE BAR SONG STE CHAD PAR 'GYUR, RNAM PAR 'JIG PAR 'GYUR, MI 'GRUB PAR 'GYUR TE, BDAG DE YANG DAG PAR CHAD PAR 'GYUR BA'I BAR DE BZHIN DU SBYAR RO,,
gru.wylie: de la gzhan dag 'di skad smra ste, bdag de de tsam gyis yang dag par chad par mi 'gyur ro, ,gang gi tshe bdag gzugs can ma yin pa de 'jig rten pha rol nas shi nas ci'ang med pa'i skye mched du nye bar song ste chad par 'gyur, rnam par 'jig par 'gyur, mi 'grub par 'gyur te, bdag de yang dag par chad par 'gyur ba'i bar de bzhin du sbyar ro
gru.english: (61) Along come others who say, rather: “Everything presented thus far is not enough to say that the self has discontinued altogether.  Rather, there comes a point where the self—and we agree, in a form with no physicality, in the world to come—dies there.  This self then passes into a realm where there is nothing at all, and simply stops.  It is destroyed, and goes out of existence.”  And they continue with the same sort of wording, up to the part about the self reaching a point where it discontinues completely.

gru.acip: DE LA GZHAN DAG 'DI SKAD SMRA STE, BDAG DE DE TZAM GYIS YANG DAG PAR CHAD PAR MI 'GYUR RO, ,GANG GI TSE BDAG DE 'JIG RTEN PHA ROL NAS SHI NAS 'DU SHES MED 'DU SHES MED MIN SKYE MCHED DU NYE BAR SONG STE CHAD PAR 'GYUR, RNAM PAR 'JIG PAR 'GYUR, MI 'GRUB PAR 'GYUR TE, DE TZAM GYIS BDAG DE YANG DAG PAR 'CHAD PAR 'GYUR RO, ,
gru.wylie: de la gzhan dag 'di skad smra ste, bdag de de tsam gyis yang dag par chad par mi 'gyur ro, ,gang gi tshe bdag de 'jig rten pha rol nas shi nas 'du shes med 'du shes med min skye mched du nye bar song ste chad par 'gyur, rnam par 'jig par 'gyur, mi 'grub par 'gyur te, de tsam gyis bdag de yang dag par 'chad par 'gyur ro,
gru.english: (62) And then finally, some say: “All of that is not enough to say that the self has discontinued altogether.  Rather, what happens is that the self is in the world to come, and dies there.  It then passes into a realm that we can describe as 'neither a place of thoughts, nor a place of no thoughts.'  And in this process, the self discontinues.  It is destroyed, and goes out of existence.  This is the point at which we can say that the self has discontinued, completely.”

gru.acip: ,RANG SDE'I GRUB MTHA' SPYI DANG KHYAD PAR RNAMS, ,MKHAS GRUB RNAMS KYI BZHED PA JI BZHIN DU, ,DON BSDUS GO SLA'I NGAG GIS 'DIR BSHAD KYI, ,GZUR GNAS BLO LDAN MCHIS NA 'JUG PAR RIGS,
gru.wylie: rang sde'i grub mtha' spyi dang khyad par rnams, ,mkhas grub rnams kyi bzhed pa ji bzhin du, ,don bsdus go sla'i ngag gis 'dir bshad kyi, ,gzur gnas blo ldan mchis na 'jug par rigs
gru.english: In words both brief And easily understood, I will now present a description Of the general principles, And also specifics, For the systems of belief Followed by our own tradition. And I will do so In keeping with the Positions accepted By our accomplished masters. This section then Could be very helpful To anyone out there Who is both unbiased And intelligent. Why the inner systems are four

gru.acip: ,GNYIS PA RANG SDE'I GRUB MTHA' RNAM PAR BZHAG PA LA GNYIS, SPYIR BSTAN PA DANG, SO SOR BSHAD PA'O,,
gru.wylie: gnyis pa rang sde'i grub mtha' rnam par bzhag pa la gnyis, spyir bstan pa dang, so sor bshad pa'o
gru.english: Here begins the second part of our explanation: a presentation on the belief systems of our own tradition.  We will proceed in two sections—a general description, and then an explanation of each different system.

gru.acip: DANG PO NI, RANG SDE'I GRUB MTHA' THUN MONG BA RNAM PA BZHIR NGES PA YIN TE, BYE BRAG SMRA BA, MDO SDE BA {%PA}, SEMS TZAM PA, DBU MA PA'I GRUB MTHA' DANG BZHIR NGES PA'I PHYIR TE,
gru.wylie: dang po ni, rang sde'i grub mtha' thun mong ba rnam pa bzhir nges pa yin te, bye brag smra ba, mdo sde ba {%pa}, sems tsam pa, dbu ma pa'i grub mtha' dang bzhir nges pa'i phyir te
gru.english: Here is the first.  The general belief systems of our own tradition number exactly four—no more, no less.  And that's true because this number is fixed precisely at the four systems of the Detailists, the Sutrists, the Mind Only, and the Middle Way.

gru.acip: BZHI PO DE DAG KYANG BSDU NA THEG PA CHE CHUNG GI GRUB MTHA' GNYIS SU 'DU BA YIN TE, BYE MDO GNYIS KYI GRUB MTHA' NI THEG DMAN GYI GRUB MTHA' DANG, DBU SEMS GNYIS KYI GRUB MTHA' NI THEG CHEN GYI GRUB MTHAR 'DU BA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: bzhi po de dag kyang bsdu na theg pa che chung gi grub mtha' gnyis su 'du ba yin te, bye mdo gnyis kyi grub mtha' ni theg dman gyi grub mtha' dang, dbu sems gnyis kyi grub mtha' ni theg chen gyi grub mthar 'du ba'i phyir
gru.english: These four different belief systems can be abbreviated into just two: the belief systems of the lesser and higher ways.  When treated in this manner, the systems of the Detailists and Sutrists are grouped within the system of the lesser way; whereas the systems of the Mind Only and the Middle Way are grouped within the system of the greater way. The role of the historical innovators

gru.acip: DE YANG KLU SGRUB KYIS DBU MA PA DANG, THOGS MED KYI {%KYIS} SEMS TZAM PA'I SHING RTA'I SROL PHYE ZHING DE GNYIS KAS KYANG THEG CHEN GYI SHING RTA'I SROL PHYE LA, DE'I ZHAR BYUNG DU THEG DMAN GYI GRUB MTHA' LA BLTOS PA'I SHING RTA'I SROL YANG PHYE BA YIN NO,,
gru.wylie: de yang klu sgrub kyis dbu ma pa dang, thogs med kyi {%kyis} sems tsam pa'i shing rta'i srol phye zhing de gnyis kas kyang theg chen gyi shing rta'i srol phye la, de'i zhar byung du theg dman gyi grub mtha' la bltos pa'i shing rta'i srol yang phye ba yin no
gru.english: It was Arya Nagarjuna who first formalized the belief system of the Middle Way; and Arya Asanga who did the same for that of the Mind Only.  We can say thus that it was these two who—by doing so—formalized the system of the higher way.  We can even go so far as to say that, by implication, they also thereby formalized the belief systems of the lower way.

gru.acip: GRUB MTHA' BZHI PO SO SO NAS RANG RANG GI LUGS DE STON PA SANGS RGYAS KYI RANG LUGS DANG, RANG GI LUGS DE YANG RTAG CHAD KYI MTHA' GNYIS DANG MA 'DRES PAR 'DOD LA,
gru.wylie: grub mtha' bzhi po so so nas rang rang gi lugs de ston pa sangs rgyas kyi rang lugs dang, rang gi lugs de yang rtag chad kyi mtha' gnyis dang ma 'dres par 'dod la
gru.english: When each of these four systems describes its own beliefs, they are in fact describing the beliefs that the Buddha himself would describe as his own.  We further hold the position that none of their own beliefs here would cross the line into ideas which would necessitate everything lasting forever; or else stopping altogether.

gru.acip: BYE BRAG SMRA BAS 'DUS MA BYAS LA RDZAS GRUB 'DOD PA DE, MDO SDE PAS 'GOG
gru.wylie: bye brag smra bas 'dus ma byas la rdzas grub 'dod pa de, mdo sde pas 'gog
gru.english: These same Detailists would say though that an existing thing which was not produced by the coming together of causes & conditions would still exist in a substantial way; whereas the Sutrists would refute this idea.

gru.acip: ,DES RANG MTSAN RNAMS RANG RANG GI MING GI THA SNYAD KYI GZHIR GNAS TSOD KYI DBANG GIS GRUB PAR 'DOD PA DE, SEMS TZAM PAS 'GOG
gru.wylie: des rang mtshan rnams rang rang gi ming gi tha snyad kyi gzhir gnas tshod kyi dbang gis grub par 'dod pa de, sems tsam pas 'gog
gru.english: The Sutrists, in turn, would assert that the actual manifestation of an entity into reality would be—by its very nature—that thing which was given its name.  And this idea, in its turn, would be refuted by the Mind Only system.

gru.acip: ,SEMS TZAM PAS DNGOS PO BDEN GRUB TU 'DOD PA DE, DBU MA PAS 'GOG PAS GRUB MTHA' 'OG MA 'OG MA LAS GONG MA GONG MA MCHOG YIN NO,,
gru.wylie: sems tsam pas dngos po bden grub tu 'dod pa de, dbu ma pas 'gog pas grub mtha' 'og ma 'og ma las gong ma gong ma mchog yin no
gru.english: The Mind Only, in their turn, would say that functioning things exist in truth; whereas those of the Middle Way would deny it.  We can say then that each of the four belief systems represents an improvement upon the one that precedes it. The stairway of the four systems

gru.acip: DES NA GRUB MTHA' BZHI PO RNAMS LAS SNGA MA RNAMS PHYI MA'I STEGS SU 'GYUR TE, DE'I TSUL YANG PHYI ROL BAS {%PAS} BDAG DANG SKYE BA SNGA PHYI LTA BU 'JOG MA SHES LA, BYE SMRAS DE LTAR SHES PA DE,
gru.wylie: des na grub mtha' bzhi po rnams las snga ma rnams phyi ma'i stegs su 'gyur te, de'i tshul yang phyi rol bas {%pas} bdag dang skye ba snga phyi lta bu 'jog ma shes la, bye smras de ltar shes pa de
gru.english: Thus we might compare these four belief systems to steps up a stairway, where each one serves as an impetus for the next.  The way this works—to name one example—would be the way in which the outside belief systems fail to describe, accurately, things like either the self, or past & future lives.  The Detailists then tread there and use it to climb up to the next step, where they do describe these with accuracy.

gru.acip: MDO SDE BAS {%PAS} DE LTAR SHES PA DE, SEMS TZAM PA {%PAS} CHOS THAMS CAD RANG NYID RANG NYID ZHES {%CES} PA'I THA SNYAD 'JUG PA'I GZHIR RANG DBANG GIS MA GRUB KYANG BYA BYED 'THAD PA DANG,
gru.wylie: mdo sde bas {%pas} de ltar shes pa de, sems tsam pa {%pas} chos thams cad rang nyid rang nyid zhes {%ces} pa'i tha snyad 'jug pa'i gzhir rang dbang gis ma grub kyang bya byed 'thad pa dang
gru.english: Those of the Mind Only then use this understanding of the Sutrist system as a springboard, so that they can further climb to their own idea which says that—even though things are never naturally the thing which is given the particular name they are given—nonetheless we can still say that the way in which the world works, and does things, is all entirely correct.

gru.acip: KUN BTAGS RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS MA GRUB PAR 'JOG SHES PA'I STEGS DANG, SEMS TZAM PAS DE LTAR SHES PA DE, DBU MA BAS {%PAS} CHOS THAMS CAD MING BRDAS BZHAG PA LAS GZHAN DU BDEN PAR GRUB PA RDUL TZAM YANG MED PA LA BYA BYED 'THAD PAR GO BA'I STEGS SU 'GYUR BA'I PHYIR RO,,
gru.wylie: kun btags rang gi mtshan nyid kyis ma grub par 'jog shes pa'i stegs dang, sems tsam pas de ltar shes pa de, dbu ma bas {%pas} chos thams cad ming brdas bzhag pa las gzhan du bden par grub pa rdul tsam yang med pa la bya byed 'thad par go ba'i stegs su 'gyur ba'i phyir ro
gru.english: Those of the Middle Way then utilize this position of the Mind Only—where they know how to describe conceptualizations as things that could never exist by nature—as a stepping stone from which to ascend to the Middle Way realization that every object in the universe is a creation of names & terms; or, to express it the other way, that there is not a single atom of any object in the entire universe which exists in reality; and yet still all the ways in which things in the world do what they do is entirely reasonable.

gru.acip: [,KHA CIG LAS NI SDIG PA LAS, ,RNAM PAR BZLOG PHYIR CHOS STON TE, ,KHA CIG BSOD NAMS 'GRUB BYA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: [,kha cig las ni sdig pa las, ,rnam par bzlog phyir chos ston te, ,kha cig bsod nams 'grub bya'i phyir
gru.english: To some he teaches the Dharma In order to deter them Forever from bad deeds; To others he does the same, To encourage them To undertake good deeds.

gru.acip: ,STONG NYID SNYING RJE'I SNYING PO CAN, ,BYANG CHUB SGRUB PA KHA CIG LA'O, ,ZHES PA'I BAR GSUNGS PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: stong nyid snying rje'i snying po can, ,byang chub sgrub pa kha cig la'o, ,zhes pa'i bar gsungs pa'i phyir
gru.english: Only for the few Who seek to reach Total enlightenment Does he teach emptiness With compassion At its heart. The highest system of all

gru.acip: RJE BLA MAS, [,KHYOD KYI BLA MED THEG PA'I TSUL,] ,YOD DANG MED PA'I MTHA' SPANGS PA, [,JI BZHIN 'GREL PAR LUNG BSTAN PA, ,KLU SGRUB GZHUNG LUGS KUNDA'I TSAL,] ZHES SOGS GSUNGS PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: rje bla mas, [,khyod kyi bla med theg pa'i tshul,] ,yod dang med pa'i mtha' spangs pa, [,ji bzhin 'grel par lung bstan pa, ,klu sgrub gzhung lugs kunda'i tshal,] zhes sogs gsungs pa'i phyir
gru.english: And Je Tsongkapa puts it this way— Then I entered The Jasmine Garden: The way of the great books Of the realized one, Nagarjuna; The one who you foretold Would come and clarify for us Your system, the unsurpassed way, Where we discard the extremes Of saying things exist, Or saying that they don't.

gru.acip: NANG PA'I THUN MONG GI GRUB MTHA' LA BZHIR NGES PAS DE SMRA BA'I GANG ZAG LA YANG BZHIR NGES LA, DE DAG NI 'CHAD PAR 'GYUR RO,,
gru.wylie: nang pa'i thun mong gi grub mtha' la bzhir nges pas de smra ba'i gang zag la yang bzhir nges la, de dag ni 'chad par 'gyur ro
gru.english: Given that the general number of inner belief systems is fixed at four, the types of people who profess these systems are also set at four.  We'll explain this point in more detail below. Chapter 6 The Detailist System of Belief The definition of a Detailist

gru.acip: ,,GNYIS PA SO SOR BSHAD PA LA BZHI, BYE BRAG SMRA BA, MDO SDE PA, SEMS TZAM PA, DBU MA PA'I GRUB MTHA' 'O,,
gru.wylie: gnyis pa so sor bshad pa la bzhi, bye brag smra ba, mdo sde pa, sems tsam pa, dbu ma pa'i grub mtha' 'o
gru.english: This brings us to our second point promised above, which is a separate explanation of each of the four inner systems.  We proceed, naturally, through four sections, covering the belief systems of the Detailists; the Sutrists; the Mind Only; and the Middle Way.

gru.acip: DANG PO LA BZHI, MTSAN NYID, SGRA DON, DBYE BA, GRUB MTHA'I 'DOD TSUL LO,,
gru.wylie: dang po la bzhi, mtshan nyid, sgra don, dbye ba, grub mtha'i 'dod tshul lo
gru.english: We cover the Detailists in four further points: their definition; the literal meaning of their name; the divisions among them; and the beliefs that their system adheres to.

gru.acip: DANG PO NI, RANG RIG MI 'DOD CING PHYI DON YOD PAR BDEN ZHEN GYIS 'DOD PA'I THEG DMAN GYI GRUB MTHA' SMRA BA'I GANG ZAG BYE BRAG SMRA BA'I MTSAN NYID,
gru.wylie: dang po ni, rang rig mi 'dod cing phyi don yod par bden zhen gyis 'dod pa'i theg dman gyi grub mtha' smra ba'i gang zag bye brag smra ba'i mtshan nyid
gru.english: The definition of a follower of the Detailist belief system is: Any person who professes a system of belief which denies apperception, and yet—due to the person's habit of seeing them as real—accepts the existence of outside objects. Literal meaning of the name “Detailist”

gru.acip: 'DI DAG GI KHYAD PAR RGYAS PAR NI 'DUL BA SOGS NAS SHES PAR BYA ZHING THEG DMAN GYI GANG ZAG DANG THEG DMAN GYI GRUB MTHA' SMRA BA'I GANG ZAG LA NI KHYAD PAR YOD PA YANG SHES DGOS SO,,
gru.wylie: 'di dag gi khyad par rgyas par ni 'dul ba sogs nas shes par bya zhing theg dman gyi gang zag dang theg dman gyi grub mtha' smra ba'i gang zag la ni khyad par yod pa yang shes dgos so
gru.english: You can find more detail about the distinctions between these different groups in places such as the literature on vowed morality.  You should also educate yourself about the difference that exists between a person who belongs to the lower way, and a person who professes a belief system within the lower way. Some detail on the 18 groups of Detailists [In keeping with these instructions from our author, Choney Lama, we add here a very useful description of the various groups of Detailists from an overview of vowed morality composed by the great Sera Jetsun Chukyi Gyeltsen:

gru.acip: DE RNAMS 'GA' ZHIG GNAS KYI MING, 'GA' ZHIG GRUB MTHA'I MING, 'GA' ZHIG GANG GI RJES SU 'BRANG BA'I SLOB DPON GYI SGO NAS MING BTAGS PA YIN TE,
gru.wylie: de rnams 'ga' zhig gnas kyi ming, 'ga' zhig grub mtha'i ming, 'ga' zhig gang gi rjes su 'brang ba'i slob dpon gyi sgo nas ming btags pa yin te
gru.english: The names of these various groups are applied by different criteria: sometimes the name is based upon a place name; sometimes upon the name of a belief system; and then sometimes upon the name of the master whom they follow.

gru.acip: BZHI PA GRUB MTHA'I 'DOD TSUL LA GSUM, GZHI DANG, LAM DANG, 'BRAS BU'O,,
gru.wylie: bzhi pa grub mtha'i 'dod tshul la gsum, gzhi dang, lam dang, 'bras bu'o
gru.english: This brings us to our fourth point from above—an explanation of the beliefs of the Detailist system.  We cover this in three sections: their description of our original condition; of the path that we should follow to change it; and the results we can achieve by traveling that path.

gru.acip: SHES BYA THAMS CAD KHAMS BCO BRGYAD DANG, SKYE MCHED BCU GNYIS SU 'DUS PAR 'DOD LA, 'DI TZAM ZHIG NI GRUB MTHA' GONG MA THAMS CAD DANG THUN MONG DU KHAS LEN NO,,
gru.wylie: shes bya thams cad khams bco brgyad dang, skye mched bcu gnyis su 'dus par 'dod la, 'di tsam zhig ni grub mtha' gong ma thams cad dang thun mong du khas len no
gru.english: The Detailists say that each and every knowable object there is can be included into either the group of 18 categories, or that of the 12 doors of sense.  Just this much of their belief system is something that the schools above this one also accept, as a group.

gru.acip: ,,GNYIS PA MDO SDE PA'I LUGS LA BZHI, MTSAN NYID, SGRA DON, DBYE BA, GRUB MTHA' 'O,,
gru.wylie: gnyis pa mdo sde pa'i lugs la bzhi, mtshan nyid, sgra don, dbye ba, grub mtha' 'o
gru.english: With this, we have reached the second of the four inner belief systems—that of the Sutrists.  We will cover this group in the same sections of their definition; the literal meaning of their name; their divisions; and their beliefs.

gru.acip: DANG PO NI, RANG RIG DANG PHYI DON GNYIS KA KHAS LEN PA'I THEG DMAN GYI GRUB MTHA' SMRA BA'I GANG ZAG DE, MDO SDE PA'I MTSAN NYID,
gru.wylie: dang po ni, rang rig dang phyi don gnyis ka khas len pa'i theg dman gyi grub mtha' smra ba'i gang zag de, mdo sde pa'i mtshan nyid
gru.english: Here is the first.  The definition of a Sutrist is: “A person who professes the belief system of the lower way which accepts both apperception and outer objects.” Literal meaning of the name “Sutrist”

gru.acip: ,,BZHI PA GRUB MTHA' LA GSUM, GZHI, LAM, 'BRAS BU'O,,
gru.wylie: bzhi pa grub mtha' la gsum, gzhi, lam, 'bras bu'o
gru.english: Here next is the fourth point from above, concerning the beliefs of the Sutrist system.  We'll cover three topics: how they see our original condition; the path to repair this condition; and the final result of the path.

gru.acip: GANG ZAG GI BDAG MED RTOGS PA'I YE SHES NI, GROL LAM GYI NGO BO DANG, GANG ZAG GI BDAG MED NI, GANG ZAG RANG RKYA THUB PA'I RDZAS YOD KYIS STONG PA'I STONG NYID LTA BU LA 'DOD LA, STONG NYID DE YANG DE BZHIN NYID DANG, YONGS GRUB KYANG YIN NO,,
gru.wylie: gang zag gi bdag med rtogs pa'i ye shes ni, grol lam gyi ngo bo dang, gang zag gi bdag med ni, gang zag rang rkya thub pa'i rdzas yod kyis stong pa'i stong nyid lta bu la 'dod la, stong nyid de yang de bzhin nyid dang, yongs grub kyang yin no
gru.english: The Sutrists do, further, accept that the wisdom with which we realize that the person has no self-nature represents the very essence of the path to liberation; and they also accept that this lack of any self-nature to the person can be described as emptiness, in the form of a person being devoid of any substantial, self-supporting existence.  They would also use the terms “suchness”—and even “totality”—to describe this emptiness.

gru.acip: ,,GSUM PA SEMS TZAM PA'I LUGS LA BZHI, MTSAN NYID, SGRA DON, DBYE BA, GRUB MTHA'O,,
gru.wylie: gsum pa sems tsam pa'i lugs la bzhi, mtshan nyid, sgra don, dbye ba, grub mtha'o
gru.english: This brings us to our third inner belief system: that of the Mind Only.  Here again we proceed in divisions of the definition of someone who follows this system; the literal meaning of the name “Mind Only”; the divisions within the system; and then finally a description of their beliefs.

gru.acip: DANG PO NI, PHYI DON KHAS MI LEN CING RANG RIG SOGS DNGOS PO BDEN GRUB TU KHAS LEN PA'I THEG CHEN GYI GRUB MTHA' SMRA BA'I GANG ZAG DE, SEMS TZAM PA'I MTSAN NYID,
gru.wylie: dang po ni, phyi don khas mi len cing rang rig sogs dngos po bden grub tu khas len pa'i theg chen gyi grub mtha' smra ba'i gang zag de, sems tsam pa'i mtshan nyid
gru.english: Here is the first.  The definition of a follower of the Mind Only system is— A person who professes a system of belief which belongs to the greater way, and which denies the existence of outer objects; but which does accept the concept of apperception, as well as the idea that functional entities exist in truth. Literal meaning of the name “Mind Only”

gru.acip: RNAM BRDZUN PAS DE LA DE LTAR SNANG BA DE SNANG BA LTAR MA GRUB PAR 'DOD LA, RNAM BDEN PAS DE LTAR GRUB PAR 'DOD DO,,
gru.wylie: rnam brdzun pas de la de ltar snang ba de snang ba ltar ma grub par 'dod la, rnam bden pas de ltar grub par 'dod do
gru.english: The Falsists say that—when such an object appears to this kind of person—it cannot exist in the way that it appears to.  The Truists though would say that it does.

gru.acip: ,,BZHI PA GRUB MTHA' LA GSUM, GZHI, LAM, 'BRAS BU'O,,
gru.wylie: bzhi pa grub mtha' la gsum, gzhi, lam, 'bras bu'o
gru.english: Which brings us to the fourth section in our present discussion: a description of the beliefs of the Mind Only system.  Here again we cover their version of our original condition; of the path we take to change it; and the result we can expect from following this path.

gru.acip: 'DI RANG RGYUD PA SOGS KYIS DON DAM BDEN PAR MI 'DOD KYANG 'DI PAS DON DAM BDEN PA DANG YONGS GRUB TU 'DOD DO,,
gru.wylie: 'di rang rgyud pa sogs kyis don dam bden par mi 'dod kyang 'di pas don dam bden pa dang yongs grub tu 'dod do
gru.english: This last is not something that groups like the Independent branch within the Middle Way system would accept as being ultimate reality; nonetheless, it is accepted by the present system as being both ultimate reality, and what they term “totality.”

gru.acip: MTSAN NYID GSUM GYI NANG NAS GZHAN DBANG DANG 'DUS BYAS DON GCIG PA DANG, STONG NYID MIN PA'I 'DUS MA BYAS RNAMS KUN BTAGS DANG, STONG NYID DANG YONGS GRUB DON GCIG
gru.wylie: mtshan nyid gsum gyi nang nas gzhan dbang dang 'dus byas don gcig pa dang, stong nyid min pa'i 'dus ma byas rnams kun btags dang, stong nyid dang yongs grub don gcig
gru.english: Now when we look at the three qualities which the Mind Only system speaks of, the one known as “dominated things” consists of exactly the same components as the group we commonly know as “all things produced by causes & conditions.”  And all things which exist but which are not produced by causes & conditions—but which are also not emptiness itself—they refer to as the second quality: “imaginary things.”  The third quality, known as “totality,” is then just another way of saying “emptiness.”

gru.acip: 'DI TZAM ZHIG DBU MA PA YANG 'DOD KYANG BDEN GRUB 'DOD MI 'DOD KYI KHYAD PAR CHE STE,
gru.wylie: 'di tsam zhig dbu ma pa yang 'dod kyang bden grub 'dod mi 'dod kyi khyad par che ste
gru.english: Just this much for the third quality is also accepted by those who follow the Middle Way system; but there is a huge difference between the two systems as to whether they would say that this third one exists in truth, or not.

gru.acip: 'DIS KUN BTAGS BDEN PAR MA GRUB CING, GZHAN DBANG DANG YONGS GRUB GNYIS SO SO NAS BDEN PAR GRUB PAR 'DOD LA, DBU MA PAS BDEN GRUB KYI CHOS YOD PAR MI 'DOD PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: 'dis kun btags bden par ma grub cing, gzhan dbang dang yongs grub gnyis so so nas bden par grub par 'dod la, dbu ma pas bden grub kyi chos yod par mi 'dod pa'i phyir
gru.english: And that's because the followers of the Mind Only would say that—although imaginary things do not exist in truth—dominated things and objects included into totality do exist in truth; whereas those of the Middle Way deny the existence of anything in the universe which could exist in truth.

gru.acip: DE YANG RGYU 'BRAS KYI RNAM GZHAG GZHAN DBANG LA 'THAD PAS DE BDEN PAR GRUB PA DANG YONGS GRUB 'PHAGS PA'I MNYAM GZHAG GI NGO BOR BDEN PAS DE BDEN PAR GRUB PA'O,,
gru.wylie: de yang rgyu 'bras kyi rnam gzhag gzhan dbang la 'thad pas de bden par grub pa dang yongs grub 'phags pa'i mnyam gzhag gi ngo bor bden pas de bden par grub pa'o
gru.english: The position of the Mind Only here derives from the fact that they hold that—since the whole structure of cause & effect is fully proper for dominated things—they must then exist in truth.  And since totality appears to the mind as true during the balanced meditation of a realized being, it too must exist in truth.

gru.acip: KUN BTAGS BDEN PAR 'DZIN PA'I BDEN 'DZIN SGRIB PA YIN KYANG, DNGOS PO BDEN PAR GRUB PAS DE BDEN PAR 'DZIN PA'I BDEN 'DZIN NI SGRIB PA MIN NO,,
gru.wylie: kun btags bden par 'dzin pa'i bden 'dzin sgrib pa yin kyang, dngos po bden par grub pas de bden par 'dzin pa'i bden 'dzin ni sgrib pa min no
gru.english: They would further say that grasping to things as real—in the form of considering imaginary objects to be real—is indeed a spiritual obstacle; but that holding functioning things to be real—since they are real—does not represent a spiritual obstacle.

gru.acip: MNGON DU BYED TSUL NI GONG DU RAGS TZAM BRJOD PA BZHIN DANG, RGYAS PAR NI GZHUNG GZHAN DANG, GRUB MTHA'I KHYAD PAR RNAMS DRANG NGES RNAM 'BYED NA GSAL ZHING,
gru.wylie: mngon du byed tshul ni gong du rags tsam brjod pa bzhin dang, rgyas par ni gzhung gzhan dang, grub mtha'i khyad par rnams drang nges rnam 'byed na gsal zhing
gru.english: The way we achieve the goals here is similar to what we've already described in just a general way; for more detail, consult other major texts on the topic.  As for the differences in beliefs between the schools mentioned in this part of our text, you can find a comprehensive clarification in Careful Distinctions between Teachings That Are to Be Taken Literally, and Those to Be Taken Figuratively.

gru.acip: DE YANG 'DIS NI MTHAR THUG THEG PA GCIG TU GRUB PAR 'DOD PA DANG, RNAM BDEN PA MTHAR THUG THEG PA GSUM DU GRUB PAR 'DOD PA'I DBANG GIS YIN NO,,
gru.wylie: de yang 'dis ni mthar thug theg pa gcig tu grub par 'dod pa dang, rnam bden pa mthar thug theg pa gsum du grub par 'dod pa'i dbang gis yin no
gru.english: This distinction between the two groups is due to the fact that the Falsists assert that—in the end—all the various paths represent but one grand highway; whereas the Truists believe, rather, that in the end there are indeed three separate ways. Chapter 9 Lower Middle Way System: The Independent Branch Introduction to the Middle Way system

gru.acip: DANG PO NI, BDEN GRUB KYI CHOS RDUL TZAM YANG MED PAR 'DOD PA'I THEG CHEN GYI GRUB MTHA' SMRA BA'I GANG ZAG DE, DBU MA PA'I MTSAN NYID,
gru.wylie: dang po ni, bden grub kyi chos rdul tsam yang med par 'dod pa'i theg chen gyi grub mtha' smra ba'i gang zag de, dbu ma pa'i mtshan nyid
gru.english: Here is the first.  The definition of a follower of the Middle Way is— A person who professes a system of belief which is part of the higher way, and where it is asserted that there does not exist even a single atom of any object in the universe which could exist in truth.

gru.acip: CHOS THAMS CAD LA BDEN PAR GRUB PA'I NGO BO CUNG ZAD KYANG MED PAR SMRA BAS NA NGO BO NYID MED PAR SMRA BA'O,,
gru.wylie: chos thams cad la bden par grub pa'i ngo bo cung zad kyang med par smra bas na ngo bo nyid med par smra ba'o
gru.english: The members of this system are also spoken of as “those who assert that nothing has any essence at all,” because they hold that no object in the entire universe has even the slightest nature of existing in truth.

gru.acip: DANG PO LA BZHI, MTSAN NYID, SGRA DON, DBYE BA, GRUB MTHA' 'O,,
gru.wylie: dang po la bzhi, mtshan nyid, sgra don, dbye ba, grub mtha' 'o
gru.english: We'll cover the first of the two branches in four sections.  We begin with the definition of a follower of this Independent branch; then go to the literal meaning of this name, “Independent”; next the divisions within this branch; and then finally the beliefs that this branch adheres to.

gru.acip: DANG PO NI, RANG RGYUD KYI RTAGS SAM RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PA'I RTAGS ZHAL GYIS BZHES SHING BDEN GRUB THA SNYAD DU YANG MI 'DOD PA'I DBU MA PA DE, DBU MA RANG RGYUD PA'I MTSAN NYID ,
gru.wylie: dang po ni, rang rgyud kyi rtags sam rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub pa'i rtags zhal gyis bzhes shing bden grub tha snyad du yang mi 'dod pa'i dbu ma pa de, dbu ma rang rgyud pa'i mtshan nyid
gru.english: Here is the first.  The definition of a member of the Independent branch within the Middle Way system is— A member of the Middle Way belief system who accepts the idea of an “independent” logical reason—which is to say, a reason which exists by definition—but who does not agree that there exists, even in a nominal way, any entity in the universe which could exist in truth. Literal meaning of the name, “Independent”

gru.acip: BZHI PA GRUB MTHA' LA GSUM, GZHI, LAM, 'BRAS BU'O,,
gru.wylie: bzhi pa grub mtha' la gsum, gzhi, lam, 'bras bu'o
gru.english: With this, we have reached our fourth point, on the beliefs of the Independent branch.  This we cover in terms of our original condition; the path we follow to free ourselves from this condition; and the result we can expect by following this path.

gru.acip: DANG {%PO} NI, GRUB MTHA' 'OG MA DANG THUN MONG BA'I 'DOD TSUL DANG KHYAD PAR SEMS TZAM PA DANG 'DOD TSUL THUN MONG BA PHAL CHER NI SNGAR BSHAD ZIN LA, 'DI PAS BDEN GRUB MI 'DOD KYANG, RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA DANG, RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PA, RANG NGOS NAS GRUB PA GSUM THA SNYAD DU YOD PAR 'DOD,
gru.wylie: dang {%po} ni, grub mtha' 'og ma dang thun mong ba'i 'dod tshul dang khyad par sems tsam pa dang 'dod tshul thun mong ba phal cher ni sngar bshad zin la, 'di pas bden grub mi 'dod kyang, rang bzhin gyis grub pa dang, rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub pa, rang ngos nas grub pa gsum tha snyad du yod par 'dod
gru.english: Here is the first.
