gru.wylie: brgyad pa kun gzhi rnam shes la yang ngo bo nyid kyi kun gzhi zhes sangs rgyas 'grub pa'i don dang ldan pa zhig dang, rnam smin gyi kun gzhi zhes khams bco brgyad la dmigs pa zhig dang, kun nas nyon mongs pa'i kun gzhi zhes chos kyi bdag 'dzin zhig ste, gsum du 'chad pa dang
gru.english: Master Paramartha then explains [8] the eighth type of consciousness—foundation consciousness—by dividing it further into three different kinds.  The first he calls “the foundation consciousness of the very essence,” referring to a foundation consciousness which contains the very point of attaining enlightenment.  Second is “foundation consciousness as a ripening,” which is a form of this consciousness that is focused upon the eighteen categories.  And third comes “foundation consciousness for total negativity,” which is another particular kind of grasping to self-existence: one which holds to the self-existence of things.

gru.acip: ,TSOGS BRGYAD DAG LAS LOGS PA YI, ,GTZO BO RNAM SHES YOD GYUR NA, ,RTAG PA'I DNGOS POR 'GYUR BA'I PHYIR, ,TSOGS DGUR 'DOD LA SGRUB BYED MED,
gru.wylie: tshogs brgyad dag las logs pa yi, ,gtso bo rnam shes yod gyur na, ,rtag pa'i dngos por 'gyur ba'i phyir, ,tshogs dgur 'dod la sgrub byed med
gru.english: If there were a primary consciousness Distinct from the group of eight, Then there would have to exist A functional thing that never changed. As such, there is no support For the position of a group of nine.

gru.acip: DES NA TSOGS DGUR 'DOD PA LA LUNG RIGS KYIS SGRUB BYED MED DO,,
gru.wylie: des na tshogs dgur 'dod pa la lung rigs kyis sgrub byed med do
gru.english: As such, we can say there is no support—either scriptural or logical—for the position that there exists a group of nine different types of consciousness. Why all minds are but one

gru.acip: ,DE PHYIR YID CHES LUNG RIGS KYIS, ,GRUB PA RNAM SHES BRGYAD YIN PHYIR, ,GSANG BA'I GNAS LA MI ZHUM PA'I, ,MKHAS PAS BRGYAD NYID 'DOD PAR BYA,
gru.wylie: de phyir yid ches lung rigs kyis, ,grub pa rnam shes brgyad yin phyir, ,gsang ba'i gnas la mi zhum pa'i, ,mkhas pas brgyad nyid 'dod par bya
gru.english: As such then, It is the concept Of eight types of consciousness Which can be established With credible scriptural authority, And logic. Wise ones who refuse To shy away from The deepest secret points Should themselves embrace The idea of exactly eight.

gru.acip: SNGAR BSHAD PA LTAR RNAM SHES TSOGS BRGYAD 'DOD PA LA LUNG RIGS KYIS SGRUB BYED DANG, DE LAS GZHAN DU 'DOD PA LA GNOD PA YOD PA DE'I PHYIR RNAM RIG PA'I MKHAS PAS JI SKAD BSHAD PA LTAR, YID CHES LUNG RIGS KYIS, ,LEGS PAR GRUB PA NI RNAM SHES TSOGS BRGYAD NYID YIN PA'I PHYIR NA,
gru.wylie: sngar bshad pa ltar rnam shes tshogs brgyad 'dod pa la lung rigs kyis sgrub byed dang, de las gzhan du 'dod pa la gnod pa yod pa de'i phyir rnam rig pa'i mkhas pas ji skad bshad pa ltar, yid ches lung rigs kyis, ,legs par grub pa ni rnam shes tshogs brgyad nyid yin pa'i phyir na
gru.english: And so, as we have heretofore explained, we have demonstrated that there exist both scriptural and logical support for the position that the types of consciousness come in a group that numbers eight.  We have also shown that there are problems with taking any other position.  As such then, it is only the concept of a group of eight types of consciousness—no less, and no more—which can (as the masters of the Conceptualist School itself explain) be established, perfectly, with both credible scriptural authority, and logic.

gru.acip: ,RNAM RIG PA'I GRUB MTHA'I GSANG BA STE LKOG TU GYUR PA'AM RTOGS DKA' BA'I GNAS ZAB MO KUN GZHI DANG, GNYIS STONG GI DE KHO NA NYID LA MI ZHUM PA'I, ,MKHAS PAS LUGS DER RNAM SHES TSOGS BRGYAD NYID 'DOD PAR BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: rnam rig pa'i grub mtha'i gsang ba ste lkog tu gyur pa'am rtogs dka' ba'i gnas zab mo kun gzhi dang, gnyis stong gi de kho na nyid la mi zhum pa'i, ,mkhas pas lugs der rnam shes tshogs brgyad nyid 'dod par bya'o
gru.english: As such, wise ones who refuse to shy away from the deepest secrets of the Conceptualist School—from these hidden truths, the deep and difficult points of foundation consciousness, and suchness in the form of the emptiness of the two—should themselves embrace (for this school, at least) the idea that the group of the types of consciousness includes exactly eight members. The author of the root text dedicates the goodness

gru.acip: ,CES CHOS 'DI LA SLOB GNYER BYED SKABS SEMS DPA' CHEN PO ^ BLO BZANG MCHOG GRUB KYI BKA' DRIN LAS RANG GIS GO TSUL BLO BZANG 'JIGS MED KYIS BRJED GSO'I TSUL DU YI GER BKOD PA'O,,
gru.wylie: ces chos 'di la slob gnyer byed skabs sems dpa' chen po ^ blo bzang mchog grub kyi bka' drin las rang gis go tshul blo bzang 'jigs med kyis brjed gso'i tshul du yi ger bkod pa'o
gru.english: This work consists of notes that were taken by myself, Lobsang Jikme, as I was studying this topic at the feet of the great bodhisattva Lobsang Chokdrup, who in his great kindness shared it with me.  I have put these ideas down into writing as best I understood them, in the hopes that I would prevent myself from forgetting what he had taught me.

gru.acip: ,STENG 'OG PHYOGS MTSAMS BZHUGS PA'I SANGS RGYAS LA, ,PHYAG 'TSAL SKYABS MCHIS BDAG CAG GAR 'GRO YANG, ,DGRA JAG CHOM RKUN ME CHU GCAN GZAN SOGS, ,'JIGS PA KUN SKYOBS BSAM DON LHUN GRUB MDZOD, (,PAn CHEN RIN PO CHES MDZAD PA'I PHYOGS BCU MUN SEL BZHUGS SO,,)
gru.wylie: steng 'og phyogs mtshams bzhugs pa'i sangs rgyas la, ,phyag 'tshal skyabs mchis bdag cag gar 'gro yang, ,dgra jag chom rkun me chu gcan gzan sogs, ,'jigs pa kun skyobs bsam don lhun grub mdzod, (,paN chen rin po ches mdzad pa'i phyogs bcu mun sel bzhugs so,,)
gru.english: Here is a small prayer composed by Panchen Rinpoche entitled “Clearing Away the Darkness in Every Corner of the Universe”: All of us bow down, And take shelter in All the Buddhas who live In the four main directions, And the four directions between them, And above and below as well— In every corner of the universe. Protect us we ask From enemies, And robbers & thieves, And fire & flood, And wild beasts Or any other such danger. Help us see our hopes & dreams Accomplished almost Automatically. Original printing prayer for this edition

gru.acip: ,,AOm SVA STI, ,YID DANG KUN GZHIS {%GZHI'I} 'GREL BA {%PA} 'DI, ,AA BA GA YI WANG SHOG GI ,DGE SLONG DPAL DAN {%LDAN} RGYA MTSO YIS, ,CHOS SDE SKU 'BUM BYAMS GLING DU, ,MTHUN RKYEN SBYAR TE PAR DU BSGRUBS,
gru.wylie: aoM sva sti, ,yid dang kun gzhis {%gzhi'i} 'grel ba {%pa} 'di, ,aa ba ga yi wang shog gi ,dge slong dpal dan {%ldan} rgya mtsho yis, ,chos sde sku 'bum byams gling du, ,mthun rkyen sbyar te par du bsgrubs
gru.english: Om svasti! May all be good! This printing of A commentary upon Negative and foundation consciousness Was completed at Kumbum Jampa Ling With the financial assistance Of the Buddhist monk Pelden Gyatso From the abbey of Abaga Wangshok.

gru.acip: ,MTSAN NYID SGRUB PAR BYED PA DANG, ,DGU DANG GCIG PUR 'DOD PA DGAG ,DON RNAM BZHI YIS KUN GZHI DANG, ,NYON MONGS CAN YID SHES PAR BYA,
gru.wylie: mtshan nyid sgrub par byed pa dang, ,dgu dang gcig pur 'dod pa dgag ,don rnam bzhi yis kun gzhi dang, ,nyon mongs can yid shes par bya
gru.english: Use four different strategies to understand Foundation and negative consciousness: Definitions; arguments for their existence; Refuting the belief that consciousness Can be grouped into nine; and the belief That they can be put in a single group. (6)

gru.acip: ,DGE DANG MI DGE MTSAN NYID PAR, ,'DOD LA SGRUB PAR BYED PA MED,
gru.wylie: dge dang mi dge mtshan nyid par, ,'dod la sgrub par byed pa med
gru.english: There is nothing that constitutes Proof for positions that Seeds can consist of Definitive virtue or non-virtue. (30)

gru.acip: [D13] RNAL 'BYOR GYIS {%GYI SA} GSUM PA NI, SNGON PO DE BDEN PAR GRUB NA, RANG SNANG YUL DU BYED PA'I SHES PA LA JI LTAR SNANG BA LTAR GRUB DGOS SHING, DE LTAR NA SNGO SNANG DBANG SHES LA RGYANGS CHAD DU SNANG BA LTAR BDEN PAR GRUB DGOS PA LA JI SKAD BSHAD PA'I RTAGS KYIS DA {%DE} KHEGS BA'I {%PA'I} PHYIR, SNGON PO BDEN PAR MA GRUB CING,
gru.wylie: [d13] rnal 'byor gyis {%gyi sa} gsum pa ni, sngon po de bden par grub na, rang snang yul du byed pa'i shes pa la ji ltar snang ba ltar grub dgos shing, de ltar na sngo snang dbang shes la rgyangs chad du snang ba ltar bden par grub dgos pa la ji skad bshad pa'i rtags kyis da {%de} khegs ba'i {%pa'i} phyir, sngon po bden par ma grub cing
gru.english: Moving on to the third level of deep practice.  If the blue color were to exist in reality, then it would have to in fact exist the way it appears to exist to the state of mind which takes it as the object appearing to it.  And if that were the case, then the blue—which appears to the state of mind taking on an aspect of blue as if it existed at a distance—would have to in fact exist that way.  This possibility though is disproven by the logical reasoning presented above; and so we can say that actually the blue does not in reality exist.

gru.acip: [D20] GSUM PA NI, DE LTAR 'JIG RTEN PA'I LAM GYIS BSGOMS PA'I STOBS GRUB PA NA BLO GSAL BA KHA CIG GIS
gru.wylie: [d20] gsum pa ni, de ltar 'jig rten pa'i lam gyis bsgoms pa'i stobs grub pa na blo gsal ba kha cig gis
gru.english: Here third is how the meditation eliminates the obstacles.  The methods used so far are still considered a worldly path to enlightenment; but as the power of having done these meditations is perfected, a number of particularly clear-minded practitioners are able to go further.

gru.acip: [E1] GNYIS PA RIGS PA LA GNYIS LAS, KUN GZHI'I RIGS PA NI, ,RNAL 'BYOR SPYOD PA'I GZHUNG LUGS NAS, ,SGRUB BYED RIGS PA MTHA' YAS PA, ,GSUNGS KYANG LEN DANG DANG PO GSAL, ,SA BON LAS DANG LUS TSOR DANG, ,SNYOMS 'JUG 'CHI 'PHO MI RUNG BA, ,BRGYAD DU 'DUS PHYIR 'DI BSHAD BYA, ,ZHES GSUNGS SO,,
gru.wylie: [e1] gnyis pa rigs pa la gnyis las, kun gzhi'i rigs pa ni, ,rnal 'byor spyod pa'i gzhung lugs nas, ,sgrub byed rigs pa mtha' yas pa, ,gsungs kyang len dang dang po gsal, ,sa bon las dang lus tshor dang, ,snyoms 'jug 'chi 'pho mi rung ba, ,brgyad du 'dus phyir 'di bshad bya, ,zhes gsungs so
gru.english: This brings us to our second section, where we discuss the reasoning in support of foundation and negative consciousnesses.  The first of these two is expressed in the following lines from Je Tsongkapa's Difficult Points: Limitless reasoning Is spoken in the scriptural tradition Of the way of deep practice. Nonetheless, these can be summarized In eight arguments concerning Problems with taking birth; Arising first; the clarity; The seeds; the operation; Feeling and the body; Deep meditation; And dying and moving on. These I will now explain.

gru.acip: [E2] KUN GZHI SGRUB BYED KYI RIGS PA THEG BSDUS DANG PHUNG PO LNGA'I RA BA {%LNGA'I RAB} BYED DANG PA'I {%SA'I} STONG {%STOD or BSTOD} 'GREL SOGS LAS GSUNGS PA'I RNAM GRANGS MANG YANG, 'DIR BSHAD BA'I {%PA'I} RIGS PA BRGYAD DU PHAL CHER 'DUS PAR GSUNGS SHING,
gru.wylie: [e2] kun gzhi sgrub byed kyi rigs pa theg bsdus dang phung po lnga'i ra ba {%lnga'i rab} byed dang pa'i {%sa'i} stong {%stod or bstod} 'grel sogs las gsungs pa'i rnam grangs mang yang, 'dir bshad ba'i {%pa'i} rigs pa brgyad du phal cher 'dus par gsungs shing
gru.english: What this is saying is that logical arguments in support of the concept of foundation consciousness are found in a great many forms, spoken in works such as A Summary of the Greater Way; Verses on the Five Heaps; and Lines of Commentary in Praise of the Levels.  Nonetheless, these arguments are for the most part summed up in the eight classical arguments I will explain here.

gru.acip: [E4] SEMS CAN RNAMS NI RNAM PAR SHES PA RGYUD RE RE BA'O, ,ZHES PA'I MDO DANG 'GAL BA'I RTZOD SPONG GI RIGS PA YIN LA, GZHAN LNGA NI KUN GZHI YOD PAR SGRUB PA'I RIGS PA DNGOS YIN NO,,
gru.wylie: [e4] sems can rnams ni rnam par shes pa rgyud re re ba'o, ,zhes pa'i mdo dang 'gal ba'i rtsod spong gi rigs pa yin la, gzhan lnga ni kun gzhi yod par sgrub pa'i rigs pa dngos yin no
gru.english: These three are all arguments where the supporters of the Mind Only view must try to refute apparent contradictions with the statement, in sutra, that “the flows of consciousness in living beings are separate from one another.”  The other five arguments then are the actual reasoning used to establish the existence of foundation consciousness. First argument: How could we take birth?

gru.acip: [E7] DANG PO GRUB STE, NYON YID YOD NA KUN GZHI YANG YOD DGOS PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: [e7] dang po grub ste, nyon yid yod na kun gzhi yang yod dgos pa'i phyir
gru.english: The first of these two statements is correct, because if there were a negative consciousness present at that point, then a foundation consciousness would have to be there too.

gru.acip: [E8] GNYIS PA GRUB STE, TSOGS DRUG RGYU MCHAN {%MTSAN} LNGAS LUS LEN BYED DU MI RUNG BA'I PHYIR, DER THAL,
gru.wylie: [e8] gnyis pa grub ste, tshogs drug rgyu mchan {%mtshan} lngas lus len byed du mi rung ba'i phyir, der thal
gru.english: The second statement is also correct, given the five reasons why there would be a problem for the collection of six different types of consciousness to be the entity taking on the body.

gru.acip: [E10] DANG PO GRUB STE, TSOGS DRUG NI LUS GRUB ZIN PA'I RJES SU TSE 'DI'I RKYEN YUL DBANG YID BYED GSUM 'DUS BA LAS 'BYUNG DGOS PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: [e10] dang po grub ste, tshogs drug ni lus grub zin pa'i rjes su tshe 'di'i rkyen yul dbang yid byed gsum 'dus ba las 'byung dgos pa'i phyir
gru.english: The first reason listed is correct, because the collection of six—only after the body has come into being—must occur, in the new life, through the convening of their three conditions: object, sense power, and turning one's attention to the object.

gru.acip: [E11] GNYIS BA {%PA} GRUB STE, TSOGS DRUG LA DGE MI DGE MED NA DGE MI DGE'I SEMS MED PAR 'GYUR BA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: [e11] gnyis ba {%pa} grub ste, tshogs drug la dge mi dge med na dge mi dge'i sems med par 'gyur ba'i phyir
gru.english: And the second reason is correct because—if the collection of six were to lack good deeds and bad—then there would be no state of mind which was virtuous, or non-virtuous.

gru.acip: [E12] GSUM PA GRUB STE, TSOGS DRUG LA TSE JI SRID KYI BAR DU RGYUN MA CHAD PAR 'JUG PA'I RNAM SMIN MED PA'I PHYIR TE, TSOGS DRUG NI RES 'GA' 'BYUNG RES 'GA' MI 'BYUNG BA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: [e12] gsum pa grub ste, tshogs drug la tshe ji srid kyi bar du rgyun ma chad par 'jug pa'i rnam smin med pa'i phyir te, tshogs drug ni res 'ga' 'byung res 'ga' mi 'byung ba'i phyir
gru.english: The third reason is correct because there is no ripening of karma of the kind where these six types of consciousness engage for the entire length of one's life.  This is because these six occur, and stop occurring, intermittently throughout our life.

gru.acip: [E13] BZHI PA GRUB STE, DBANG SHES RNAMS LUS KYI PHYOGS LA BRTEN PA GANG ZHIG ,YID SHES NI LUS KYI CHA SHAS LA MI GNAS KYANG LUS THAMS CAD LA KHYAB NAS 'DZIN PA'I NUS PA MED PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: [e13] bzhi pa grub ste, dbang shes rnams lus kyi phyogs la brten pa gang zhig ,yid shes ni lus kyi cha shas la mi gnas kyang lus thams cad la khyab nas 'dzin pa'i nus pa med pa'i phyir
gru.english: The fourth reason is correct because the sense consciousnesses are something that depend upon different areas of the physical body; whereas the consciousness of the thought—although it is not situated at any one part of the body—still lacks the capacity to grasp its object even as it extends over the entire body.

gru.acip: [E14] LNGA PA GRUB STE, TSOGS DRUG GIS LUS LEN NA TSOGS DRUG PA'I {%DRUG MI 'BYUNG BA'I} TSE LUS 'DOR BA DANG TSOGS DRUG SLAR 'BYUNG BA'I TSE LUS LEN PAR 'GYUR BA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: [e14] lnga pa grub ste, tshogs drug gis lus len na tshogs drug pa'i {%drug mi 'byung ba'i} tshe lus 'dor ba dang tshogs drug slar 'byung ba'i tshe lus len par 'gyur ba'i phyir
gru.english: The fifth reason holds because—if it were the collection of six which took on the body—then when these are not occurring, we would have to lose that body; and when they return to occurring, we would have to take on another body.

gru.acip: [E21] DANG PO LTAR NA, RANG NYID KYIS RNAM SHES DU MA GCIG CAR MI SKYE BAR 'DOD DGOS PA LAS, RNAM SHES DU MA GCIG CAR MI SKYE BAR 'DOD MKHAN SU ZHIG YIN GRAGS MI CHE BA'I PHYIR TE, GRUB MTHA' SMRA BA RNAMS KYIS RNAM SHES DU MA GCIG CAR SKYE BAR 'DOD PA SHA STAG YIN PAR SNANG BA'I PHYIR RO,
gru.wylie: [e21] dang po ltar na, rang nyid kyis rnam shes du ma gcig car mi skye bar 'dod dgos pa las, rnam shes du ma gcig car mi skye bar 'dod mkhan su zhig yin grags mi che ba'i phyir te, grub mtha' smra ba rnams kyis rnam shes du ma gcig car skye bar 'dod pa sha stag yin par snang ba'i phyir ro
gru.english: If it's the former, then you would have to say that our side in this argument was some school which asserted that it was not possible for multiple types of consciousness to arise at the same time.  But the fact of the matter is that it isn't generally known here who it is that would assert that multiple types of consciousness cannot arise simultaneously.  And that's because, as far as we can tell, the major schools of philosophy are unanimous in saying that—indeed—many different kinds of consciousness can arise at the same time.

gru.acip: [E22] ,GNYIS PA LTAR NA, DE LA RIGS MI MTHUN PA'I RNAM SHES DU MA GCIG CAR SKYE BAR SGRUB PA'I RIGS BA {%PA} BKOD PA NI GRUB ZIN SGRUB PA'I SKYON DU 'GYUR BA'I PHYIR MI 'THAD DO ZHE NA DPYOD DGOS SO,,
gru.wylie: [e22] ,gnyis pa ltar na, de la rigs mi mthun pa'i rnam shes du ma gcig car skye bar sgrub pa'i rigs ba {%pa} bkod pa ni grub zin sgrub pa'i skyon du 'gyur ba'i phyir mi 'thad do zhe na dpyod dgos so
gru.english: And suppose instead that the latter were the case; you'd have to consider what you would respond with, if someone said, “Then setting forth arguments in favor of the idea that multiple types of consciousness which are not of the same consistent type can arise at the same time is itself incorrect—for these arguments incur the error of proving what has already been proven.”

gru.acip: [E28] MA KHYAB MTSAMS KYI RTAGS GRUB STE, GZUGS SHES PA NI RNAM GNYIS TE, ,MIG DANG YID LA BRTEN PA'O, ,ZHES GSUNGS PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: [e28] ma khyab mtshams kyi rtags grub ste, gzugs shes pa ni rnam gnyis te, ,mig dang yid la brten pa'o, ,zhes gsungs pa'i phyir
gru.english: And suppose someone were to respond to that itself by saying, “But the one does not always imply the other.”  We would say then, “Our reason holds true; remember the lines that state: The perception of visible form Has two different aspects, For it depends upon eye and thoughts.”

gru.acip: [E46] MA GRUB NA, DE DAG GI LUS SHI LUS SU THAL BA DANG, DE DAG GANG ZAG MA YIN PAR 'GYUR BA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: [e46] ma grub na, de dag gi lus shi lus su thal ba dang, de dag gang zag ma yin par 'gyur ba'i phyir
gru.english: I disagree that their bodies are imbued with awareness. If you do disagree, then their bodies must be dead ones; and they cannot be people.

gru.acip: ,DUS GSUM BDE BAR GSHEGS PA'I THUGS KYI BCUD, ,MTHA' BRAL DBU MA RTEN CING 'BREL 'BYUNG LAM, ,JI BZHIN 'GREL PAR LUNG BSTAN KLU SGRUB LA, ,SNYING NAS 'DUD DO BRTZE BA'I LCAGS KYUS ZUNGS,
gru.wylie: dus gsum bde bar gshegs pa'i thugs kyi bcud, ,mtha' bral dbu ma rten cing 'brel 'byung lam, ,ji bzhin 'grel par lung bstan klu sgrub la, ,snying nas 'dud do brtse ba'i lcags kyus zungs
gru.english: The very cream Within the holy minds Of all who have Gone To Bliss, Past & present & future, Is the Middle Way, Free of extremes: The path of dependence. From the depths of my heart I bow myself To Master Nagarjuna, The one who it was foretold would come And unfold this way. Set, I pray, the iron hook Of your love within my breast.

gru.acip: ,RJE BTZUN 'JAM PA'I DBYANGS KYI BKA' GRUB CING, ,'PHAGS PA'I DGONGS PA MTHAR THUG GSAL BAR MDZAD, ,GRUB PA'I RIG 'DZIN GNAS SU GSHEGS GYUR PA, ,SANGS RGYAS BSKYANGS KYI ZHABS LA MGOS PHYAG 'TSAL,
gru.wylie: rje btsun 'jam pa'i dbyangs kyi bka' grub cing, ,'phags pa'i dgongs pa mthar thug gsal bar mdzad, ,grub pa'i rig 'dzin gnas su gshegs gyur pa, ,sangs rgyas bskyangs kyi zhabs la mgos phyag 'tshal
gru.english: I bow and touch My head as well To the feet of Buddha Palita, Who carried out The command of the holy Gentle Voice; Who clarified The ultimate intent Of the Realized One, And who reached the state Of an accomplished one, A keeper of the knowledge.

gru.acip: ,PHRA LA RTOGS DKA' DRANG SRONG CHEN PO'I LAM, ,KLU SGRUB LUGS KYI THUN MONG MIN PA'I GNAD, ,YONGS SU RDZOGS PAR STON MDZAD ZLA BA'I ZHABS, ,ZHI BA LHA DANG BCAS PA'I ZHABS LA 'DUD,
gru.wylie: phra la rtogs dka' drang srong chen po'i lam, ,klu sgrub lugs kyi thun mong min pa'i gnad, ,yongs su rdzogs par ston mdzad zla ba'i zhabs, ,zhi ba lha dang bcas pa'i zhabs la 'dud
gru.english: I bow as well At the feet of the holy Chandrakirti, Who along with Master Shantideva Has instructed us In every single one Of the unique & crucial points Found in the system Of Master Nagarjuna: In the path of this great saint, A way which is subtle And difficult to grasp.

gru.acip: ,KLU SGRUB 'PHAGS PA LHA YI GRUB PA'I MTHA', ,SHING RTA CHEN PO GSUM GYIS BKRAL BA NYID, ,THUN MONG MA YIN GNAD DON KUN RDZOGS PAR, ,DRI MED BLO GROS MIG GIS LEGS MTHONG ZHING,
gru.wylie: klu sgrub 'phags pa lha yi grub pa'i mtha', ,shing rta chen po gsum gyis bkral ba nyid, ,thun mong ma yin gnad don kun rdzogs par, ,dri med blo gros mig gis legs mthong zhing
gru.english: I have seen, perfectly, With the eyes of Immaculate wisdom, Each & every one Of the unique And crucial points In the philosophical system Of Nagarjuna and Aryadeva, Just as this was commented upon By every one of the three Magnificent innovators.

gru.acip: MA DHY'A MA KA'I SKAD KYI BYINGS LA BRTZAMS NAS, DBU MA'I BSTAN BCOS SAM DBU MA'I GRUB MTHA' LA DBU MAR BYAS PAR SHES RAB SGRON MAR YANG BSHAD PAS, DBU MA ZHES PA TZAM LAS MA BYUNG YANG, 'DIR DBU MA'I BSTAN BCOS LA GO BAR BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: ma dhyA ma ka'i skad kyi byings la brtsams nas, dbu ma'i bstan bcos sam dbu ma'i grub mtha' la dbu mar byas par shes rab sgron mar yang bshad pas, dbu ma zhes pa tsam las ma byung yang, 'dir dbu ma'i bstan bcos la go bar bya'o
gru.english: The Lamp on Wisdom, which of course is working from the original Sanskrit term madhyamaka, also refers both to the Classical Commentary on the Middle Way and to the philosophical system of the Middle Way as “middle way.” Thus we can say that here in the title of Master Chandrakirti's work we are meant to understand that he is referring to the Classical Commentary on the Middle Way even when he directly mentions no more than “the middle way.”

gru.acip: NYES PA MED DE LAM DE SGROG PA BYED PA NYID YIN GYI, RJES SU MTHUN PA TZAM YANG RANG GIS MI SGRUB PAR BSAMS PA YIN PAS SO,,
gru.wylie: nyes pa med de lam de sgrog pa byed pa nyid yin gyi, rjes su mthun pa tsam yang rang gis mi sgrub par bsams pa yin pas so
gru.english: And yet there's no such issue. The idea behind the term “listener” here is that they only spread this path, and fail to actually practice it themselves, in even an approximate way. What is a “medium Buddha”?

gru.acip: MI RIGS TE, LUGS 'DIR CHOS THAMS CAD RANG BZHIN MED PAR RTOGS PA NYAN RANG GNYIS KA LA YOD PAR GSUNGS PA'I PHYIR DANG, DE SKAD SMRA BA DES KYANG GRUB MTHA' DE 'DOD PAR 'DUG PA'I PHYIR RO,,
gru.wylie: mi rigs te, lugs 'dir chos thams cad rang bzhin med par rtogs pa nyan rang gnyis ka la yod par gsungs pa'i phyir dang, de skad smra ba des kyang grub mtha' de 'dod par 'dug pa'i phyir ro
gru.english: This though is a mistaken opinion, since it is taught in the current system that both listeners & self-made buddhas possess the realization that nothing has any nature of its own. In fact, even the person who wrote that line was someone who followed this system.

gru.acip: YANG DAG PAR 'GRUB PA'I NGO BOS BYANG CHUB CHEN PO 'DZIN PAR BYED PA'I PHYIR NA, SNYING RJE CHEN PO LA SOGS PA NI TSOGS YIN PAS,
gru.wylie: yang dag par 'grub pa'i ngo bos byang chub chen po 'dzin par byed pa'i phyir na, snying rje chen po la sogs pa ni tshogs yin pas
gru.english: Qualities such as great compassion are considered “accumulated” insofar as the very nature of their proper practice is that they bring one to embrace the great enlightenment.

gru.acip: ZHES BLA NA MED PA'I BYANG CHUB PHYIN CI MA LOG PAR SGRUB PA'I THABS KYIS, 'BRAS BUR 'DZIN PA LA GSUNGS PA LTAR GYI DON TSANG BA'I BSOD NAMS DANG YE SHES SO, ,DON DE MA TSANG BA GNYIS NI TSOGS PHAL PA'O,,
gru.wylie: zhes bla na med pa'i byang chub phyin ci ma log par sgrub pa'i thabs kyis, 'bras bur 'dzin pa la gsungs pa ltar gyi don tshang ba'i bsod nams dang ye shes so, ,don de ma tshang ba gnyis ni tshogs phal pa'o
gru.english: We can thus say that the principal reference of the word “accumulation” is to merit & wisdom in a form in which the stated elements are complete: where they serve as a method of attaining matchless enlightenment in a way which is flawless, leading one to embrace the final goal. In any case where these elements are not complete, we can only refer to them as “accumulated” in an ordinary sense of the term.

gru.acip: SANGS RGYAS KYIS RTEN 'BREL BSTAN PA'I RANG RGYAL GYI SGRUB PA POS, MYONG NGES KYI LAS BSAGS PAS LAS SOG PA'I TSE DE NYID LA 'BRAS BU MA MYONG YANG, SKYE BA GZHAN DU NGES PAR MYONG BA LTAR,
gru.wylie: sangs rgyas kyis rten 'brel bstan pa'i rang rgyal gyi sgrub pa pos, myong nges kyi las bsags pas las sog pa'i tshe de nyid la 'bras bu ma myong yang, skye ba gzhan du nges par myong ba ltar
gru.english: Nonetheless, a practitioner of the self-made buddha type who receives teachings on dependent events from an Enlightened Being collects karma of the kind which is “certain to be experienced”; and so even though they may not experience the attainment of the goal in the very same life in which they collected this karma, it is certain that they will have this experience in another lifetime.

gru.acip: 'DIS NI BYANG SEMS GZHAN GYIS THOB BYA'I SANGS RGYAS DANG, RGYUD THA DAD PA'I BYANG SEMS KYIS SANGS RGYAS DE'I LHAN CIG BYED RKYEN BYAS PA'I SGO NAS, SANGS RGYAS BYANG SEMS LAS 'KHRUNGS PAR SGRUB PA YIN NO,,
gru.wylie: 'dis ni byang sems gzhan gyis thob bya'i sangs rgyas dang, rgyud tha dad pa'i byang sems kyis sangs rgyas de'i lhan cig byed rkyen byas pa'i sgo nas, sangs rgyas byang sems las 'khrungs par sgrub pa yin no
gru.english: This then would be a case where the holy birth of a Buddha from a bodhisattva was accomplished in such a way that the bodhisattva acted as a contributing cause for a particular Buddha: the bodhisattva who did this was a separate person from the bodhisattva who would later attain their own Buddhahood.

gru.acip: BYANG SEMS LAS SANGS RGYAS 'KHRUNGS PAR SGRUB PA MI RIGS TE, DE LTAR BSGRUBS PA LA YANG DA DUNG DOGS PA SNGA MA SKYE BAS, DOGS PA DE MI CHOD PA'I PHYIR RO SNYAM NA,
gru.wylie: byang sems las sangs rgyas 'khrungs par sgrub pa mi rigs te, de ltar bsgrubs pa la yang da dung dogs pa snga ma skye bas, dogs pa de mi chod pa'i phyir ro snyam na
gru.english: As such it remains the case that it is wrong to assert that Buddhas take their holy birth from bodhisattvas; for even if you persist in doing so, the same question that we expressed before must be raised—you have done nothing to resolve this issue in our minds.

gru.acip: 'DIS NI SANGS RGYAS BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA' LAS 'KHRUNGS PAR LUNG GIS BSGRUBS LA, RGYU MTSAN SNGA MA GNYIS KYIS NI RIGS PAS BSGRUBS SO,,
gru.wylie: 'dis ni sangs rgyas byang chub sems dpa' las 'khrungs par lung gis bsgrubs la, rgyu mtshan snga ma gnyis kyis ni rigs pas bsgrubs so
gru.english: This statement by the way serves to prove, through the use of authoritative scripture, the fact that Enlightened Beings take their holy birth from bodhisattvas; whereas the two reasons given before serve to prove this fact through logical reasoning.

gru.acip: DE 'DRA BA'I DAM BCA' BA DE YANG GNYIS SU MED PA'I YE SHES KYIS MTSON PA'I SBYIN SOGS KYI SPYOD PA DOR NA MI 'GRUB PAR MTHONG NAS, YE SHES GTZO BOR GYUR PA'I SPYOD PA LA YANG NGES PA KHO NAR 'JUG PAS NA, SANGS RGYAS KYI CHOS KUN GYI SA BON NI SNYING RJE CHEN PO YIN NO,,
gru.wylie: de 'dra ba'i dam bca' ba de yang gnyis su med pa'i ye shes kyis mtshon pa'i sbyin sogs kyi spyod pa dor na mi 'grub par mthong nas, ye shes gtso bor gyur pa'i spyod pa la yang nges pa kho nar 'jug pas na, sangs rgyas kyi chos kun gyi sa bon ni snying rje chen po yin no
gru.english: They recognize another thing too: that they will never be able to fulfill this commitment if they give up on the way of life represented here in the expression “wisdom beyond duality”—that is, giving & the rest. As such they know that they have no choice but to engage in this way of life, where wisdom plays the principal role. Thus it is that great compassion is the seed of all the qualities of an Enlightened Being.

gru.acip: DE'I DANG PO NI DER SKYE BA'I DON DU 'BAD MI DGOS PAR NGANG GIS 'JUG PA DANG, PHYI MA NI DE'I RGYU RNAMS 'BAD PA CHEN POS SGRUB DGOS PAS DKA' BA STE,
gru.wylie: de'i dang po ni der skye ba'i don du 'bad mi dgos par ngang gis 'jug pa dang, phyi ma ni de'i rgyu rnams 'bad pa chen pos sgrub dgos pas dka' ba ste
gru.english: And we tend to slide automatically into the first of these two, taking birth there without expending any special effort. The causes to bring about the second, though, are difficult to assemble—for they can be achieved only through intense work.

gru.acip: DE BZHIN DU 'GRO BA CHU'I NANG GI ZLA GZUGS LTAR, RANG BZHIN NYID KYIS GRUB PAR SNANG YANG DES STONG PAR MTHONG NAS, DE LA SNYING RJER GYUR PA LA 'DUD DO ZHES PA DANG SBYAR BA NI, ,DMIGS PA MED PA'I SNYING RJE LA PHYAG 'TSAL BA'O,,
gru.wylie: de bzhin du 'gro ba chu'i nang gi zla gzugs ltar, rang bzhin nyid kyis grub par snang yang des stong par mthong nas, de la snying rjer gyur pa la 'dud do zhes pa dang sbyar ba ni, ,dmigs pa med pa'i snying rje la phyag 'tshal ba'o
gru.english: He is also bowing down to the form of compassion which is focused upon the way in which beings are not even there; to relate this one to the root text, Master Chandrakirti is saying, “I bow down to that thing which is compassion where we first see that every living creature is like an image of the moon reflected in some water (that is, they may seem to exist through some nature of their own, but in fact they are empty of any such nature); and then experience the feelings of compassion.”

gru.acip: SKAD CIG RE RE LA 'JIG PA'I 'DU BYED KYI SDUG BSNGAL THOG TU 'BAB PA DANG, RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAS STONG PAR MTHONG BA NA, DE RNAMS LA DMIGS NAS SNYING RJE CHEN PO SKYE BAR 'GYUR TE,
gru.wylie: skad cig re re la 'jig pa'i 'du byed kyi sdug bsngal thog tu 'bab pa dang, rang bzhin gyis grub pas stong par mthong ba na, de rnams la dmigs nas snying rje chen po skye bar 'gyur te
gru.english: In every passing moment of their lives, they are stricken by a special kind of suffering: the fact that certain forces have given them their birth—and so they must in turn be destroyed. And they are devoid of possessing any nature which is their own. The bodhisattvas see these beings thus, and in their hearts rises that great compassion which focuses upon them.

gru.acip: DMIGS PA MED PA LA DMIGS PA'I SNYING RJES KYANG SEMS CAN TZAM LA DMIGS PA MIN GYI, DMIGS PA KHYAD PAR BA RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAS STONG PA'I SEMS CAN LA DMIGS SO,,
gru.wylie: dmigs pa med pa la dmigs pa'i snying rjes kyang sems can tsam la dmigs pa min gyi, dmigs pa khyad par ba rang bzhin gyis grub pas stong pa'i sems can la dmigs so
gru.english: The form of compassion which we say is “focused upon something which is not even there” is another case where we are focused upon something more than a simple living being. That is, there is a certain distinction in how we focus: we are focusing on a living being that we see as being devoid of existing through any nature of their own.

gru.acip: DANG PO NI, GAL TE BSTAN BCOS 'DIR BYANG SEMS KYI ZAB PA DANG RGYA CHE BA'I LAM KLU SGRUB KYI RJES SU 'BRANGS TE GTAN LA 'BEBS NA, RE ZHIG MGON PO KLU SGRUB KYI LUGS KYIS SANGS RGYAS KYI SAR BGROD PA'I LAM GYI RIM PA CI 'DRA BA ZHIG BZHED CE NA,
gru.wylie: dang po ni, gal te bstan bcos 'dir byang sems kyi zab pa dang rgya che ba'i lam klu sgrub kyi rjes su 'brangs te gtan la 'bebs na, re zhig mgon po klu sgrub kyi lugs kyis sangs rgyas kyi sar bgrod pa'i lam gyi rim pa ci 'dra ba zhig bzhed ce na
gru.english: For the first, one may begin with the following question: So the goal of this classical commentary is to provide a presentation of the profound & widespread paths of the bodhisattva, following the teachings of Nagarjuna. Here then at the beginning, can you give us an outline of the steps of the path for travelling to the state of a Buddha, according to the system accepted by our savior, Nagarjuna?

gru.acip: DE LA SANGS RGYAS GNYIS PA KLU SGRUB ZHABS LA SOGS PA'I LUGS THOS BSAM GYIS GTAN LA 'BEBS PA NI, RANG GIS YANG DAG PA'I LAM NYAMS SU LEN TSUL LA NGES PA CHEN PO RNYED NAS, LAM LTAR SNANG RNAMS KYIS BKRI BAR MI NUS PA'I CHED DU YIN NO,,
gru.wylie: de la sangs rgyas gnyis pa klu sgrub zhabs la sogs pa'i lugs thos bsam gyis gtan la 'bebs pa ni, rang gis yang dag pa'i lam nyams su len tshul la nges pa chen po rnyed nas, lam ltar snang rnams kyis bkri bar mi nus pa'i ched du yin no
gru.english: Now the whole purpose of undertaking learning & contemplation in order to come to an understanding of the system of that second Buddha, the great Nagarjuna, is so that—by reaching a deep place of certainty in our own practice of the correct path—we can assure that it is impossible for us ever to be misdirected to some mistaken path.

gru.acip: ,DE LA BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA' YI, ,YON TAN MDOR BSTAN BYA BA NI, ,SBYIN DANG TSUL KHRIMS BZOD BRTZON 'GRUS, ,BSAM GTAN SHES RAB SNYING RJE SOGS,
gru.wylie: de la byang chub sems dpa' yi, ,yon tan mdor bstan bya ba ni, ,sbyin dang tshul khrims bzod brtson 'grus, ,bsam gtan shes rab snying rje sogs
gru.english: We may summarize, briefly, The high qualities of the bodhisattva As giving; an ethical way of life; Patience; joyful effort; Meditation; wisdom; Compassion; and others as well.

gru.acip: ,SBYIN PA RANG DON YONGS BTANG BA, ,TSUL KHRIMS GZHAN PHAN BYA BA'O,, BZOD PA KHRO BA SPANGS PA STE, ,DKAR PO'I CHOS SPEL BRTZON 'GRUS SO,
gru.wylie: sbyin pa rang don yongs btang ba, ,tshul khrims gzhan phan bya ba'o,, bzod pa khro ba spangs pa ste, ,dkar po'i chos spel brtson 'grus so
gru.english: Giving is to give away All that you ever wanted; The ethical life means doing things Of benefit to others. Patience is to give up anger, And effort is working to increase The good parts of ourselves.

gru.acip: ,SBYIN PAS LONGS SPYOD KHRIMS KYIS BDE, ,BZOD PAS MDANGS LDAN BRTZON PAS BRJID, ,BSAM GTAN GYIS ZHI BLO YIS GROL, ,SNYING BRTZE BAS NI DON KUN SGRUB,
gru.wylie: sbyin pas longs spyod khrims kyis bde, ,bzod pas mdangs ldan brtson pas brjid, ,bsam gtan gyis zhi blo yis grol, ,snying brtse bas ni don kun sgrub
gru.english: Giving brings us prosperity; An ethical life brings happiness; Patience brings a lovely face, And effort brings respect. Meditation leads to peace, Understanding liberates us, And compassion accomplishes all things.

gru.acip: NYAN RANG GNYIS THUB DBANG LAS SKYES PA DANG, SANGS RGYAS BYANG SEMS LAS 'KHRUNGS PAR LUNG RIGS KYIS BSGRUBS PA SOGS THAMS CAD DBU MA LA 'JUG PA'I LUGS MIN PAR 'GYUR ZHING,
gru.wylie: nyan rang gnyis thub dbang las skyes pa dang, sangs rgyas byang sems las 'khrungs par lung rigs kyis bsgrubs pa sogs thams cad dbu ma la 'jug pa'i lugs min par 'gyur zhing
gru.english: And by that point, nothing like this whole exercise where we use both scriptural authority and logical reasoning to establish that the two of listeners & self-made buddhas are born from the Lords of the Able—and that Buddhas themselves take their holy birth from bodhisattvas—can any longer represent the system of Entering the Middle Way.

gru.acip: RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAS STONG PA'I SEMS CAN ZO CHUN DANG CHOS MTHUN DRUG GIS 'KHOR BAR BSHAD PA RNAMS 'GAL 'DU 'BA' ZHIG TU 'GYUR BAS,
gru.wylie: rang bzhin gyis grub pas stong pa'i sems can zo chun dang chos mthun drug gis 'khor bar bshad pa rnams 'gal 'du 'ba' zhig tu 'gyur bas
gru.english: Their thinking stands in total contradiction to the presentation on how living beings who are devoid of any natural existence spin through the cycle of life in a manner which is similar, in six different ways, to the way in which a water wheel turns.

gru.acip: BSLAB BTUS LAS KYANG, SO SO SKYE BO LA BYANG CHUB KYI SEMS BSKYED PA YOD PAR MDO MANG POS BSGRUBS PAS BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA' BTAGS PA BAR 'DOD PA NI LOG PAR 'CHAD PA'O,,
gru.wylie: bslab btus las kyang, so so skye bo la byang chub kyi sems bskyed pa yod par mdo mang pos bsgrubs pas byang chub sems dpa' btags pa bar 'dod pa ni log par 'chad pa'o
gru.english: The Compendium of All the Trainings also uses many references from sutra to establish that common beings can also possess the Wish for enlightenment; as such, it is an error to think that such practitioners are only “nominal” bodhisattvas.

gru.acip: NYAN THOS KYI SBYOR LAM STAN GCIG PA NAS BZUNG STE, 'BRAS BU DANG PO MA THOB PA'I BAR RNAMS RGYUN ZHUGS ZHUGS PAR MNGON PA KUN LAS BTUS LAS BSHAD PAS ,DPE MA GRUB BO SNYAM NA,
gru.wylie: nyan thos kyi sbyor lam stan gcig pa nas bzung ste, 'bras bu dang po ma thob pa'i bar rnams rgyun zhugs zhugs par mngon pa kun las btus las bshad pas ,dpe ma grub bo snyam na
gru.english: One might raise the following objection: The Compendium of All the Teachings on Higher Knowledge describes listeners on the path of preparation who pass up to the achievement of the first of the fruits in a single sitting as practitioners who are at the “entrance” stage of entering the stream; as such, your example is disproved.

gru.acip: SA DANG PO 'DI NI GANG ZAG RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PA MED PA'I GANG ZAG GI BDAG MED MNGON SUM DU MTHONG BAS, 'JIG LTA DANG PHRA RGYAS KYI THE TSOM DANG, TSUL KHRIMS DANG BRTUL ZHUGS MCHOG 'DZIN GYI KUN TU SBYOR BA GSUM PO THAMS CAD SPANGS PA YIN TE, SLAR MI SKYE BA'I PHYIR RO,,
gru.wylie: sa dang po 'di ni gang zag rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub pa med pa'i gang zag gi bdag med mngon sum du mthong bas, 'jig lta dang phra rgyas kyi the tshom dang, tshul khrims dang brtul zhugs mchog 'dzin gyi kun tu sbyor ba gsum po thams cad spangs pa yin te, slar mi skye ba'i phyir ro
gru.english: This practitioner at the first bodhisattva level has seen, directly, the lack of a self-nature to the person: the fact that the person possesses no nature of existing by definition. They have thus eliminated, within themselves, all three of what we call the “bonds”: the view of destruction; forms of doubt which are infectious negative thoughts; and the belief that mistaken forms of morality & asceticism are perfect. They have “eliminated” the three because these will never again make their appearance within the bodhisattva.

gru.acip: GNYIS PA LA GSUM, SA 'DIR NYAN RANG RNAMS RIGS KYI SGO NAS ZIL GYIS GNON PA DANG, SA BDUN PAR NYAN RANG GNYIS BLO'I SGO NAS ZIL GYIS GNON PA DANG, DE LTAR GSUNGS PAS GRUB PA'I DON BSHAD PA'O,,
gru.wylie: gnyis pa la gsum, sa 'dir nyan rang rnams rigs kyi sgo nas zil gyis gnon pa dang, sa bdun par nyan rang gnyis blo'i sgo nas zil gyis gnon pa dang, de ltar gsungs pas grub pa'i don bshad pa'o
gru.english: With this we have reached the second of our more general sections above—the high quality where our being outshines those of others. This we also cover in three steps: how a bodhisattva at this level outshines the listeners & self-made buddhas, by virtue of the family to which they belong; how, at the seventh bodhisattva level, they outshine these two by virtue of their state of mind; and then an explanation of the conclusion we can draw from statements to this effect.

gru.acip: GSUM PA LA GSUM, SA BCU PA'I MDOS NYAN RANG LA CHOS RANG BZHIN MED PAR RTOGS PA YOD PAR BSTAN PA DANG, DE SGRUB PA'I KHUNGS BSTAN PA DANG, DE LTAR BSTAN PA LA RTZOD PA SPANG BA'O,,
gru.wylie: gsum pa la gsum, sa bcu pa'i mdos nyan rang la chos rang bzhin med par rtogs pa yod par bstan pa dang, de sgrub pa'i khungs bstan pa dang, de ltar bstan pa la rtsod pa spang ba'o
gru.english: This brings us to our third step from above: an explanation of the conclusion that we can draw from statements about how the bodhisattva outshines others. Here we will cover three topics: how the Sutra on the Ten Levels indicates that the listeners & self-made buddhas do possess the realization that things have no nature of their own; a presentation of authentic sources which prove this point; and a refutation of arguments concerning these presentations.

gru.acip: DE BYAS NA GANG ZAG GI BDAG MED DE MNGON SUM DU RTOGS PA 'ONG BA NI, RNAL 'BYOR MNGON SUM SGRUB PA'I RIGS PA RNAMS KYIS 'GRUB BO,,
gru.wylie: de byas na gang zag gi bdag med de mngon sum du rtogs pa 'ong ba ni, rnal 'byor mngon sum sgrub pa'i rigs pa rnams kyis 'grub bo
gru.english: And if they were, then they would come to be able to perceive—directly—the fact that the person is not themselves. This fact is established by the logic with which we establish the existence of a direct, mystic perception.

gru.acip: DE LTAR NA DE RTOGS PA'I MTHONG LAM GYIS NYON MONGS KUN BRTAGS RNAMS SPONG BA 'GRUB BO, ,DE GRUB NA GANG ZAG GI BDAG MED MNGON SUM DU MTHONG ZIN GOMS PAR BYED PA'I SGOM LAM YANG 'GRUB PAS, LHAN SKYES KYI NYON MONGS KYANG SPONG NUS PAS,
gru.wylie: de ltar na de rtogs pa'i mthong lam gyis nyon mongs kun brtags rnams spong ba 'grub bo, ,de grub na gang zag gi bdag med mngon sum du mthong zin goms par byed pa'i sgom lam yang 'grub pas, lhan skyes kyi nyon mongs kyang spong nus pas
gru.english: If this is the case, then we can establish that the path of seeing whereby we perceive this fact eliminates the learned forms of negative emotions. And if we can establish that, then we can in turn establish the existence of a path of habituation, where we accustom ourselves to the lack of a self to the person which we have already seen directly. This then means that we also have the capacity to eliminate the inborn forms of negative emotions.

gru.acip: NYON MONGS PA'I ZAG PA THAMS CAD ZAD PA 'GRUB PAS STONG NYID MA RTOGS KYANG, KHAMS GSUM GYI PHRA RGYAS THAMS CAD SA BON DANG BCAS PA SPONG BAR NUS TE,
gru.wylie: nyon mongs pa'i zag pa thams cad zad pa 'grub pas stong nyid ma rtogs kyang, khams gsum gyi phra rgyas thams cad sa bon dang bcas pa spong bar nus te
gru.english: Having thus established that we would have eliminated all forms of the impurity caused by the negative emotions; we can say that—even without realizing emptiness—one can eliminate each & every widespread, negative emotion of all three of the realms, along with the seeds for these emotions.

gru.acip: DPER NA SEMS TZAM PAS RDUL CHA MED DANG, DE BSAGS PA'I PHYI DON DANG, DE LAS RDZAS THA DAD PA'I 'DZIN PA GNYIS BKAG PA YANG TSAD MAS 'GRUB CING, DES 'DUL BA'I GDUL BYAS RING DU GOMS PAR BYAS NA, DON DE MNGON SUM DU MTHONG BA DANG, MTHONG ZIN GOMS PAR BYED PA 'GRUB TU CHUG KYANG, DE'I STENG NAS SA BCU DANG, LAM PHYI MA GSUM BGROD PA DBU MA PAS DRANG DON DU 'GREL BA BZHIN NO,,
gru.wylie: dper na sems tsam pas rdul cha med dang, de bsags pa'i phyi don dang, de las rdzas tha dad pa'i 'dzin pa gnyis bkag pa yang tshad mas 'grub cing, des 'dul ba'i gdul byas ring du goms par byas na, don de mngon sum du mthong ba dang, mthong zin goms par byed pa 'grub tu chug kyang, de'i steng nas sa bcu dang, lam phyi ma gsum bgrod pa dbu ma pas drang don du 'grel ba bzhin no
gru.english: Followers of the Middle Way school can, for example, accept the idea that those of the Mind Only school might disprove, through an accurate perception, the two ideas that (1) atoms could have sides, and that outer objects composed of such atoms could exist; and (2) there could exist a perception of these objects which was substantially separate from them—and that students for whom this school was meant might then accustom themselves to these positions over a long period of time; and finally come to perceive them directly; and then get used to what they had at that point seen directly. But as for saying that this process could be used to go higher, to the ten levels; or to travel the latter three paths; those of the middle way would interpret any such pronouncements as only metaphoric.

gru.acip: ZHES RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAS STONG PAR MTHONG BA'I LAM 'DI MED PAR, BYANG CHUB GSUM GANG YANG THOB PA MED PAR GSUNGS TE,
gru.wylie: zhes rang bzhin gyis grub pas stong par mthong ba'i lam 'di med par, byang chub gsum gang yang thob pa med par gsungs te
gru.english: What this is saying is that—if we lack this path where we see how things are empty of existing through any nature of their own—then we cannot achieve any of the three forms of enlightenment.

gru.acip: DES NA GANG ZAG RANG RKYA THUB PA'I RDZAS YOD DU 'DZIN PA'I BDAG 'DZIN GYIS DRANGS PA'I SRED PA MNGON GYUR BA RE ZHIG SPANGS KYANG, GANG ZAG NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB PAR 'DZIN PA'I 'JIG LTAS DRANGS PA'I SRED PA CI STE MED CES PA YIN PAS, SNGAR BSHAD PA'I MNGON GYUR SPANGS PA LA NI, BSHAD MA THAG PA'I 'JIG LTA DANG SRED PA MNGON GYUR BA YANG MI LDOG GO ,
gru.wylie: des na gang zag rang rkya thub pa'i rdzas yod du 'dzin pa'i bdag 'dzin gyis drangs pa'i sred pa mngon gyur ba re zhig spangs kyang, gang zag ngo bo nyid kyis grub par 'dzin pa'i 'jig ltas drangs pa'i sred pa ci ste med ces pa yin pas, sngar bshad pa'i mngon gyur spangs pa la ni, bshad ma thag pa'i 'jig lta dang sred pa mngon gyur ba yang mi ldog go
gru.english: Therefore what we are saying here is: “It may indeed be the case that one has eliminated, for the time being, manifest forms of that initial desire which is brought on by the tendency to grasp to some self-nature which holds that the individual is substantial, in the sense of being self-standing. Why though would this preclude the form of initial desire that is brought on by the view of destruction which grasps to the idea that the individual could exist in & of itself?” The point is that a person who has eliminated the manifest form that we mentioned earlier will not have eliminated, in addition, the view of destruction that we just described; nor the manifest form of initial desire.

gru.acip: ZHES SPYOD 'JUG LAS GSUNGS PA LTAR YIN TE, TSOR BA PO DANG TSOR BA 'GA' YANG RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA MED PAR MTHONG BA GOMS NA, SRED PA LDOG PAR BSTAN PAS, DE 'DRA BA'I LAM MED NA SRED PA THAMS CAD CI'I PHYIR LDOG CES PAR YANG STON NO,,
gru.wylie: zhes spyod 'jug las gsungs pa ltar yin te, tshor ba po dang tshor ba 'ga' yang rang bzhin gyis grub pa med par mthong ba goms na, sred pa ldog par bstan pas, de 'dra ba'i lam med na sred pa thams cad ci'i phyir ldog ces par yang ston no
gru.english: It's just as the Guide is putting it here. At some point, the lines are teaching us, we are able to see—and become accustomed to the fact—that there is no one at all doing the feeling, and no feeling at all for them to have, which exist through some nature of their own. And it is at this point that we are able to stop initial desire. The lines are also, in effect, saying: “How then, in the absence of such a path, would you ever be able to stop all forms of initial desire?”

gru.acip: TSOR BA YOD PA'I RGYU MTSAN GYIS SRED PA YOD PAR GSUNGS PA LA, RGYU YOD PAS 'BRAS BU YOD PAR SGRUB MI NUS PAS LEGS PA MIN ZHES CHA PA DANG, RTZEGS DBANG PHYUG SENG GES SPYOD 'JUG 'GOG PA NI,
gru.wylie: tshor ba yod pa'i rgyu mtshan gyis sred pa yod par gsungs pa la, rgyu yod pas 'bras bu yod par sgrub mi nus pas legs pa min zhes cha pa dang, rtsegs dbang phyug seng ges spyod 'jug 'gog pa ni
gru.english: Chapa and Tsek Wangchuk Senge have attempted to refute the Guide to the Bodhisattva's Way of Life, claiming that this statement that “A person possesses initial desire for the reason that they possess feelings” is imperfect, since the presence of a cause does not necessarily establish the presence of its result.

gru.acip: BDEN PA'I PHUNG PO DMIGS PAR BYAS NAS MI RTAG SOGS SU YID LA BYED PA CIG KYANG YOD LA, DE NI ZHEN YUL LA 'KHRUL BA'I LOG SHES RKYANG PA YIN PAS, TSAD MAS GRUB PA MIN KYANG
gru.wylie: bden pa'i phung po dmigs par byas nas mi rtag sogs su yid la byed pa cig kyang yod la, de ni zhen yul la 'khrul ba'i log shes rkyang pa yin pas, tshad mas grub pa min kyang
gru.english: And so there are people who think they are looking at parts to a person which are real, and who think of them as impermanent and such—but their state of mind is a total misperception, mistaken in the object that it believes it sees. Therefore we can go further and say the object here is not even one which is established by an accurate perception.

gru.acip: BDEN 'DZIN GYI YUL SUN PHYUNG BA'I LTA BA MA RNYED PA'I RGYUD LA, BDEN BRDZUN GANG GIS KYANG KHYAD PAR DU MA BYAS PA'I PHUNG PO LA DMIGS NAS, DE GNYIS GANG GIS KYANG KHYAD PAR DU MA BYAS PA'I MI RTAG PA SOGS SU THA SNYAD PA'I TSAD MAS GRUB PA DU MA ZHIG 'ONG LA, SGOM PA'I TSE YANG DON DE BSGOMS PAS SNGAR BSHAD PA BZHIN GYI LAM RGYUD LA SKYE'O,,
gru.wylie: bden 'dzin gyi yul sun phyung ba'i lta ba ma rnyed pa'i rgyud la, bden brdzun gang gis kyang khyad par du ma byas pa'i phung po la dmigs nas, de gnyis gang gis kyang khyad par du ma byas pa'i mi rtag pa sogs su tha snyad pa'i tshad mas grub pa du ma zhig 'ong la, sgom pa'i tshe yang don de bsgoms pas sngar bshad pa bzhin gyi lam rgyud la skye'o
gru.english: The mind of this person—one who has yet to arrive at the viewpoint in which the object of the tendency to hold things as real has been demolished—is focusing on the parts of the person and failing to make any distinction at all between what is real & what is false. And then they do manage to establish, but only with accurate perception operating at a nominal level, no small number of facts such as impermanence & the rest—even as they fail to make the distinction between these two. And since when they then meditate they are meditating on these particular kinds of facts, the path that arises in their mind looks like the one we described above.

gru.acip: 'DIS NI BDEN BZHI RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA MED PAR MTHONG BA DES, 'KHOR BA LAS GROL BAR BYED LA, BDEN 'DZIN DANG MA BRAL BA'I LAM GYIS 'KHOR BA LAS MI 'DA' BA SHIN TU GSAL BAR GSUNGS PAS,
gru.wylie: 'dis ni bden bzhi rang bzhin gyis grub pa med par mthong ba des, 'khor ba las grol bar byed la, bden 'dzin dang ma bral ba'i lam gyis 'khor ba las mi 'da' ba shin tu gsal bar gsungs pas
gru.english: The point being made is that people who see that the four truths cannot exist through any nature of their own are able to liberate themselves from the cycle of pain—meaning that the Buddha is very clearly stating that one cannot go beyond this cycle by using a path where one is still not free of the tendency to think that things are real.

gru.acip: DE LTAR NA LUNG DE DAG GIS NI DE KHO NA NYID KYI LTA BA DANG BRAL NA, 'KHOR BA LAS MI GROL BA DANG, 'KHOR BA LAS GROL BA LA LTA BA DE DGOS PAR GSAL BAR BSTAN LA, NYAN RANG DGRA BCOM PA 'KHOR BA'I 'CHING BA LAS MA GROL BA NI, MKHAS PA SU YANG MI 'DOD CING MI 'THAD PAS, NYAN RANG LA CHOS RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA MED PA RTOGS PA YOD PAR GSAL BAR BSTAN NO,,
gru.wylie: de ltar na lung de dag gis ni de kho na nyid kyi lta ba dang bral na, 'khor ba las mi grol ba dang, 'khor ba las grol ba la lta ba de dgos par gsal bar bstan la, nyan rang dgra bcom pa 'khor ba'i 'ching ba las ma grol ba ni, mkhas pa su yang mi 'dod cing mi 'thad pas, nyan rang la chos rang bzhin gyis grub pa med pa rtogs pa yod par gsal bar bstan no
gru.english: These citations then are clearly indicating that, so long as one still lacks the view of suchness, they cannot be liberated from the cycle of pain; and in order to achieve such a liberation, one must possess this view. And since there is no sage anywhere who would ever agree to the idea that enemy destroyers who are listeners or self-made buddhas have not yet achieved liberation from the shackles of the cycle of suffering—and since it would be wrong in any case to do so—then what these citations are also indicating clearly is that these listeners & self-made buddhas do possess the realization that nothing exists through any nature of its own.

gru.acip: DE LTAR NA BDEN 'DZIN GYI ZHEN YUL SUN MA PHYUNG BAR DU, 'JIG LTA'I ZHEN YUL SUN MI PHYIN PAS, THEG PA CHE CHUNG GI GRUB MTHA' SMRA BA LA THUN MONG DU GRAGS PA'I GANG ZAG GI BDAG MED NI, RAGS PA'I GANG ZAG GI BDAG TZAM BKAG PA YIN GYI, PHRA BA'I GANG ZAG GI BDAG MED MIN PAR SHES SO,,
gru.wylie: de ltar na bden 'dzin gyi zhen yul sun ma phyung bar du, 'jig lta'i zhen yul sun mi phyin pas, theg pa che chung gi grub mtha' smra ba la thun mong du grags pa'i gang zag gi bdag med ni, rags pa'i gang zag gi bdag tsam bkag pa yin gyi, phra ba'i gang zag gi bdag med min par shes so
gru.english: As such, we cannot demolish the object that the view of destruction thinks it sees, until we manage to demolish the object that the tendency to think that things are real thinks it sees. And so you should understand that the version of the lack of a self-nature to the person which is generally understood to be held in common by those who follow the schools of the greater way and those who follow the schools of the lesser way is a denial of a self-nature to the person in no more than its gross form; and is not the subtle form of the lack of a self-nature to the person.

gru.acip: DE'I PHYIR SLOB DPON 'DI'I LUGS KYIS NYAN RANG GIS GANG ZAG GI BDAG MED RTOGS TSUL, GRUB MTHA' SMRA BA GZHAN DANG 'DRA BA BZUNG NAS, CHOS KYI BDAG MED RTOGS PA YOD MED LA MI MTHUN PAR SMRA BAS NI, 'DI'I LUGS LEGS PAR MA RTOGS PA YIN TE,
gru.wylie: de'i phyir slob dpon 'di'i lugs kyis nyan rang gis gang zag gi bdag med rtogs tshul, grub mtha' smra ba gzhan dang 'dra ba bzung nas, chos kyi bdag med rtogs pa yod med la mi mthun par smra bas ni, 'di'i lugs legs par ma rtogs pa yin te
gru.english: Therefore those who make contradictory statements about whether listeners & self-made buddhas perceive the lack of a self-nature to things—because they have interpreted this particular master's presentation on how these two types of practitioners perceive the lack of a self-nature to the person in accordance with proponents of other schools—have in fact failed to grasp this presentation correctly.

gru.acip: DE LTAR THUN MONG MA YIN PA'I GANG ZAG GI BDAG MED KYI 'JOG TSUL MDZAD PHYIN CHAD, GANG ZAG GI BDAG MED THUN MONG BA TZAM GYI DBANG DU MDZAD NAS, 'JIG LTA LA SOGS PA'I NGOS 'DZIN MDZAD PA'I NYON MONGS KYI RNAM GZHAG RNAMS SOR BZHAG TU MDZAD NA, THUN MONG MA YIN PA'I GRUB MTHA', MTHA' MA CHOD PA'I NOR PA CHEN POR 'GYUR BAS, DE LA MKHAS PA'I DBANG PO 'DI 'KHRUL BA GA LA SRID,
gru.wylie: de ltar thun mong ma yin pa'i gang zag gi bdag med kyi 'jog tshul mdzad phyin chad, gang zag gi bdag med thun mong ba tsam gyi dbang du mdzad nas, 'jig lta la sogs pa'i ngos 'dzin mdzad pa'i nyon mongs kyi rnam gzhag rnams sor bzhag tu mdzad na, thun mong ma yin pa'i grub mtha', mtha' ma chod pa'i nor pa chen por 'gyur bas, de la mkhas pa'i dbang po 'di 'khrul ba ga la srid
gru.english: And so suppose we start with a thinker who was actually the one who set forth the way of defining the lack of a self-nature to the person in a way which was not shared by the different systems; and who supposedly then limited themselves to the shared concept of this particular lack of a self-nature; and who then set aside the presentation of the negative emotions which correctly identifies the view of destruction and so on; and thus made the stupendous error of failing to thresh out the views of this very unique school of thought…how could this Lord of All Sages ever possibly make such a mistake?

gru.acip: ZHES PA'I PHYOGS SNGA MA SMRA BA NI SLOB DPON LEGS LDAN YIN TE, SANGS RGYAS BSKYANGS KYIS RAB BYED BDUN PA'I 'GREL PAR THEG DMAN GYI MDOR CHOS THAMS CAD BDAG MED PAR GSUNGS PA'I DON, CHOS RNAMS NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB PA MED PA'I DON DU BSHAD PA LA, SHES RAB SGRON MAR DE LTA YIN NA, THEG CHEN BSTAN PA DON MED DU 'GYUR RO ZHES DGAG PA MDZAD DO,,
gru.wylie: zhes pa'i phyogs snga ma smra ba ni slob dpon legs ldan yin te, sangs rgyas bskyangs kyis rab byed bdun pa'i 'grel par theg dman gyi mdor chos thams cad bdag med par gsungs pa'i don, chos rnams ngo bo nyid kyis grub pa med pa'i don du bshad pa la, shes rab sgron mar de lta yin na, theg chen bstan pa don med du 'gyur ro zhes dgag pa mdzad do
gru.english: The person who expressed the first position found in this citation is Master Bhavaviveka. Master Buddha Palita, in commenting upon the seventh section of Wisdom, had described the statement that the sutras of the lower way speak of how nothing has any nature of its own as referring to the way in which nothing exists through any unique quality of its own. And then in his Lamp on Wisdom, Master Bhavaviveka tries to refute this position, saying that if this were the case, then the presentation found in the greater way would be pointless.

gru.acip: DE NI THEG CHEN PA LA SHES BYA THAMS CAD RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA MED PAR RTOGS PA YOD LA, NYAN RANG LA DE MED PAR SHES BYA PHYOGS GCIG PA 'GA' RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA MED PAR RTOGS PA YOD CES PA NI, GTAN MIN TE
gru.wylie: de ni theg chen pa la shes bya thams cad rang bzhin gyis grub pa med par rtogs pa yod la, nyan rang la de med par shes bya phyogs gcig pa 'ga' rang bzhin gyis grub pa med par rtogs pa yod ces pa ni, gtan min te
gru.english: It is not at all the case, as some have put it, that this presentation is meant to convey that those of the greater way possess a realization that no existing object exists through any nature of its own; whereas those of the ways of the listener and the self-made buddha lack this same realization—since they realize only that some portion of all the things there are exist through no nature of their own.

gru.acip: GZHI GRUB PA CIG GI STENG DU, CHOS KYI BDAG MED TSAD MAS GRUB PA CIG BYUNG NA, DE NAS GZHI GZHAN LA BDEN PAR YOD MED KYI DPYOD PA ZHUGS NA, RIGS PA SNGA MA LA BRTEN NAS BDEN MED DU RTOGS PAR NUS PA'I PHYIR RO,,
gru.wylie: gzhi grub pa cig gi steng du, chos kyi bdag med tshad mas grub pa cig byung na, de nas gzhi gzhan la bden par yod med kyi dpyod pa zhugs na, rigs pa snga ma la brten nas bden med du rtogs par nus pa'i phyir ro
gru.english: And this is because—if one is able to establish, by using an accurate perception, that the lack of a self-nature to things is true with regard to any single existent thing—then when one engages in an examination of whether things exist in truth with regard to any other object, they will be able to perceive that in fact it does not exist in truth, simply by using the same reasoning that they have employed previously.

gru.acip: DBU MA PAR 'DOD PA KHA CIG GIS DNGOS PO BDEN GRUB KHEGS PA'I LUGS SU BYAS NAS, BDEN STONG BDEN GRUB TU 'DOD PA DANG, KHA CIG GIS CHOS NYID SGRUB PA'ANG DBANG BA {%SGRUB PA RANG DBANG BA} BDEN GRUB TU 'DOD PA'I
gru.wylie: dbu ma par 'dod pa kha cig gis dngos po bden grub khegs pa'i lugs su byas nas, bden stong bden grub tu 'dod pa dang, kha cig gis chos nyid sgrub pa'ang dbang ba {%sgrub pa rang dbang ba} bden grub tu 'dod pa'i
gru.english: Now some people who consider themselves to be followers of the Middle Way school—thinking to use it as a way of denying that functional things could exist in truth—have expressed the opinion that this lack of real existence itself does exist in truth. And others believe that the proof of the very nature of things is itself something which has its own inherent power: that it exists in truth.

gru.acip: DES NA THEG CHEN PAS NI RTZA SHE LAS GSUNGS PA BZHIN DU, GZHI GCIG BDEN MED DU SGRUB PA LA YANG, SGRUB BYED KYI RIGS PA MI 'DRA BA MTHA' YAS PAS BSGRUBS PAS, DE KHO NA NYID LA BLO SHIN TU RGYAS PAR 'GYUR LA,
gru.wylie: des na theg chen pas ni rtsa she las gsungs pa bzhin du, gzhi gcig bden med du sgrub pa la yang, sgrub byed kyi rigs pa mi 'dra ba mtha' yas pas bsgrubs pas, de kho na nyid la blo shin tu rgyas par 'gyur la
gru.english: Thus it is that when, as described in Wisdom, those of the greater way undertake to prove that any single object is devoid of true existence, they do so by using a limitless number of proofs to make their point—and their minds are thereby made wide open towards suchness.

gru.acip: THEG DMAN LA NI RIGS PA MDOR BSDUS PA CIG GIS DE KHO NA NYID TSAD MAS GRUB NA, SNGA MA LTAR MI BYED PAS DE KHO NA NYID LA BLO RGYAS PA MED PAS RGYAS BSDUS DANG, BDAG MED SGOM PA RDZOGS MA RDZOGS SU GSUNGS SO,,
gru.wylie: theg dman la ni rigs pa mdor bsdus pa cig gis de kho na nyid tshad mas grub na, snga ma ltar mi byed pas de kho na nyid la blo rgyas pa med pas rgyas bsdus dang, bdag med sgom pa rdzogs ma rdzogs su gsungs so
gru.english: Those of the lower way, on the other hand, employ only abbreviated forms of reasoning to prove suchness with accurate perception. Since they fail to do what those other ones do, they lack any broadening of their mind towards suchness. Thus it is that pronouncements have been made about the relative detail of the two approaches; and whether or not one has meditated in a complete way upon the lack of a self-nature.

gru.acip: DE LA GZUNG BA PHYI ROL LA ZHEN PA SPONG BA'I DON NI, PHYI ROL GYI DON TSAD MAS GRUB KYANG, PHYI ROL BDEN GRUB RIGS PAS KHEGS PA DBU MA PA LTAR GTAN LA PHAB PA'I DON BSGOMS NAS BDEN ZHEN SPONG BA DANG,
gru.wylie: de la gzung ba phyi rol la zhen pa spong ba'i don ni, phyi rol gyi don tshad mas grub kyang, phyi rol bden grub rigs pas khegs pa dbu ma pa ltar gtan la phab pa'i don bsgoms nas bden zhen spong ba dang
gru.english: What does it mean then when we say that a person has “rid oneself of a belief in objects of the mind—outer objects”? It could mean that we have meditated upon the way as those of the Middle Way school describe it—showing how, although outer objects are confirmed by accurate perception, the idea that outer objects could exist in truth is disproved by reasoning—and through this meditation we have been able to rid ourselves of this particular belief that a thing could exist in truth.

gru.acip: GNYIS PA LTAR 'DOD PA NI SLOB DPON SENG GE BZANG PO LA SOGS PA'I 'GREL PA'I LUGS YIN PAS, DE'I LTAR NA PHYI ROL MED PAR TSAD MAS GRUB PA YIN NO,,
gru.wylie: gnyis pa ltar 'dod pa ni slob dpon seng ge bzang po la sogs pa'i 'grel pa'i lugs yin pas, de'i ltar na phyi rol med par tshad mas grub pa yin no
gru.english: Accepting the second option is what we see done in the commentarial tradition of Master Haribhadra and others; and in this case then, it would be established through accurate perception that there are no outer objects.

gru.acip: PHYI ROL MED PAR GRUB NA DE 'DZIN PA'I SHES PA, GZUNG BA LAS RDZAS THA DAD PA MED PAR NI, SU DBANG PO RTUL YANG 'GRUB PAS,
gru.wylie: phyi rol med par grub na de 'dzin pa'i shes pa, gzung ba las rdzas tha dad pa med par ni, su dbang po rtul yang 'grub pas
gru.english: Once a person has established that there are no outer objects, then they can figure out—regardless of how dull they might be—that the state of mind holding to an object cannot be substantially separate from the object being held.

gru.acip: 'DZIN PA LA BDEN ZHEN MI SPONG BA NI, SPYIR SHES PA BDEN GRUB TU KHAS LEN PA LA BYED KYI, GZUNG 'DZIN RDZAS THA DAD KYI PHYED KHEGS SHING PHYED BDEN PAR 'DZIN PA GTAN MIN PAS,
gru.wylie: 'dzin pa la bden zhen mi spong ba ni, spyir shes pa bden grub tu khas len pa la byed kyi, gzung 'dzin rdzas tha dad kyi phyed khegs shing phyed bden par 'dzin pa gtan min pas
gru.english: And so when we say that someone has yet to rid themselves—with respect to the state of mind holding to an object—of the belief that it exists in truth, what we are referring to is someone who accepts the idea that the mind could exist in truth. It is not at all as if they deny half of the idea that subjects & objects could be separate from each other, and believe that the rest exists in truth.

gru.acip: 'DZIN PA BDEN PAR SMRA BA'I RANG RGYAL DANG, GZUNG 'DZIN GNYIS MED KYI SHES PA DON DAM DU GRUB PAR SMRA BA'I RNAM RIG PA GNYIS GRUB MTHA' MTSUNGS PA MTSAR ZHES PA NI, GSAL BYED PA'I BZHAD GAD DO,,
gru.wylie: 'dzin pa bden par smra ba'i rang rgyal dang, gzung 'dzin gnyis med kyi shes pa don dam du grub par smra ba'i rnam rig pa gnyis grub mtha' mtshungs pa mtshar zhes pa ni, gsal byed pa'i bzhad gad do
gru.english: Thus they are having an illuminating laugh when they say, “Isn't it weird that self-made buddhas who say that the state of mind holding to an object exists in truth; and those that believe everything is the mind who go on to say that the perception that objects and subjects are no two things exists in an ultimate way, are actually sharing the very same school of thought?”

gru.acip: DES NA 'DIS NI CHOS KYI DBYINGS NYID 'PHAGS PA'I CHOS RNAMS KYI RGYU YIN PA'I PHYIR, ,RANG BZHIN DU GNAS PA'I RIGS SGRUB PA'I RTEN YIN NO ZHES STON PAR BYED DO,
gru.wylie: des na 'dis ni chos kyi dbyings nyid 'phags pa'i chos rnams kyi rgyu yin pa'i phyir, ,rang bzhin du gnas pa'i rigs sgrub pa'i rten yin no zhes ston par byed do
gru.english: Thus it has been taught that—because this sphere of reality is in fact the cause of the qualities of a realized being—the family quality that exists in all beings by nature is the foundation of all Buddhist practice.

gru.acip: RTEN NI 'DIR DMIGS PA DANG, BRTEN PA NI DMIGS BYED YIN LA, DMIGS BYED LA NYAN RANG GI THEG PA GNYIS KYANG YOD CING, CHOS NYID LA DMIGS PA LA DE BLO NGOR 'GRUB DGOS LA, BDEN GRUB BLO NGOR MA BCAD PAR, BDEN STONG BLO NGOR MI 'GRUB CING, DE MA GRUB NA CHOS NYID BLO NGOR MI 'GRUB BO,,
gru.wylie: rten ni 'dir dmigs pa dang, brten pa ni dmigs byed yin la, dmigs byed la nyan rang gi theg pa gnyis kyang yod cing, chos nyid la dmigs pa la de blo ngor 'grub dgos la, bden grub blo ngor ma bcad par, bden stong blo ngor mi 'grub cing, de ma grub na chos nyid blo ngor mi 'grub bo
gru.english: The thing being relied upon here is the object of the perception; while what relies upon it is the state of mind doing the perceiving—and the mind doing the perceiving can also include the minds of those who belong to the two ways of the listener or the self-made buddha. And to say that one is perceiving the way things are, this way must have presented itself to the mind. Yet if one has yet to exclude the idea that things exist in truth from presenting itself to the mind, the idea that things are void of existing in truth cannot present itself—and so long as it does not, then the way things really are cannot.

gru.acip: DE NI RDO RJE GCOD PA LAS SANGS RGYAS PA'I CHOS DANG, DES BSTAN PA'I CHOS THAMS CAD MA MCHIS SO, ZHES PA'I SGRUB BYED DU 'PHAGS PA'I GANG ZAG RNAMS NI 'DUS MA BYAS KYIS RAB TU PHYE BA'I SLAD DU'O,
gru.wylie: de ni rdo rje gcod pa las sangs rgyas pa'i chos dang, des bstan pa'i chos thams cad ma mchis so, zhes pa'i sgrub byed du 'phags pa'i gang zag rnams ni 'dus ma byas kyis rab tu phye ba'i slad du'o
gru.english: This statement recalls the mention in the Diamond Cutter Sutra that it is impossible for there to be any such thing as a being who becomes enlightened; and for there to be any such thing as the teaching which this being gives. And in support of this idea, it is then stated that people who are realized beings are distinguished by something which is unproduced.

gru.acip: ZHES GSUNGS PA'I DON NI THEG PA CHE CHUNG GI 'PHAGS PA'I GANG ZAG THAMS CAD NI CHOS RNAMS DE KHO NAR MA GRUB PA'I DON DAM 'DUS MA BYAS MNGON DU BYAS PAS BZHAG PA'I PHYIR ZHES PA'O,,
gru.wylie: zhes gsungs pa'i don ni theg pa che chung gi 'phags pa'i gang zag thams cad ni chos rnams de kho nar ma grub pa'i don dam 'dus ma byas mngon du byas pas bzhag pa'i phyir zhes pa'o
gru.english: The point being made in these words is that all realized beings—whether they belong to the greater way or the lesser—are established as what they are by actualizing the ultimate unproduced thing: the fact that nothing in the universe is only what it is.

gru.acip: DES NA DE RNAMS NI SBYIN PA'I 'BRAS BU MNGON SUM DU MI MTHONG BA'I PHYIR SBYIN PA LA MI 'JUG PA YANG SRID NA, 'GRO BA THAMS CAD LA PHUGS SU PHAN PA DANG, 'PHRAL DU BDE BA SGRUB PAR DAM BCAS PA'I YID CAN GYI BYANG SEMS RNAMS, SBYIN PAS RING POR MI THOGS PAR SLONG BA PO TSIM PAR BYAS PA MTHONG BA'I MJUG THOGS NYID DU, SBYIN PA'I 'BRAS BU DGA' BA MCHOG TU GYUR BA 'THOB CING SBYIN 'BRAS LA LONGS SPYOD PAS, DUS THAMS CAD KYI TSE SBYIN PA BYED PA LA DGA' BAR 'GYUR RO,,
gru.wylie: des na de rnams ni sbyin pa'i 'bras bu mngon sum du mi mthong ba'i phyir sbyin pa la mi 'jug pa yang srid na, 'gro ba thams cad la phugs su phan pa dang, 'phral du bde ba sgrub par dam bcas pa'i yid can gyi byang sems rnams, sbyin pas ring por mi thogs par slong ba po tshim par byas pa mthong ba'i mjug thogs nyid du, sbyin pa'i 'bras bu dga' ba mchog tu gyur ba 'thob cing sbyin 'bras la longs spyod pas, dus thams cad kyi tshe sbyin pa byed pa la dga' bar 'gyur ro
gru.english: As such—because they don't see the results of their giving in a direct way—there is a possibility that they will fail to engage in the act of giving. But the bodhisattvas—who have resolved in their hearts to be of benefit to every living being in the long run, and in the short run to make them happy—undertake acts of giving and then not long afterwards (meaning immediately subsequent to seeing that their giving has satisfied the needs of those who have asked them for something) these acts make them feel a supreme form of happiness as the result of their giving. Having thus enjoyed the fruits of their giving, they are at all times very pleased to engage in giving. Why giving is the most important [I.13b]

gru.acip: ,LUS BCAD STER ZHING BDAG GI SDUG BSNGAL GYIS, ,GZHAN DAG RNAMS KYI DMYAL BA LA SOGS PA'I, ,SDUG BSNGAL RANG RIG NYID DU MTHONG NAS NI, ,DE BCAD BYA PHYIR MYUR DU BRTZON 'GRUS RTZOM,
gru.wylie: lus bcad ster zhing bdag gi sdug bsngal gyis, ,gzhan dag rnams kyi dmyal ba la sogs pa'i, ,sdug bsngal rang rig nyid du mthong nas ni, ,de bcad bya phyir myur du brtson 'grus rtsom
gru.english: What do they do with the pain Of cutting off & giving away Their own flesh? When they have seen for themselves The pain of others— Those in the hells & the rest— They leap to do the deed, In order to cut that pain.

gru.acip: SLONG BA PO LA RANG LUS BCAD NAS STER BA'I BDAG GI SDUG BSNGAL GYIS TE SDUG BSNGAL LA RTZIS MED PAR BYAS NAS, RANG GIS SDUG BSNGAL NYAMS SU MYONG BA DE NYID KYI RGYU MTSAN LAS, SEMS CAN GZHAN DAG RNAMS KYI DMYAL BA LA SOGS PA'I SDUG BSNGAL DE GCAD PA'I PHYIR DU CHOS {%CHES} MYUR DU BRTZON 'GRUS RTZOM MO,,
gru.wylie: slong ba po la rang lus bcad nas ster ba'i bdag gi sdug bsngal gyis te sdug bsngal la rtsis med par byas nas, rang gis sdug bsngal nyams su myong ba de nyid kyi rgyu mtshan las, sems can gzhan dag rnams kyi dmyal ba la sogs pa'i sdug bsngal de gcad pa'i phyir du chos {%ches} myur du brtson 'grus rtsom mo
gru.english: And when the bodhisattva cuts the flesh from their own body and gives it away to someone who asks them for it, the first words they say are “With this pain of mine”—meaning they pay no attention at all to their own pain, but rather see this same suffering they are undergoing themselves as a reason: as something whose purpose is to cut off the suffering of other living beings—those living in the hell realms, and so on. And so they immediately leap to do the deed.

gru.acip: SPYOD 'JUG LAS, ,LUS DANG DE BZHIN LONGS SPYOD DANG, ,DUS GSUM DGE BA THAMS CAD KYANG, ,SEMS CAN KUN GYI DON BSGRUB PHYIR, ,PHANGS PA MED PAR GTANG BAR BYA, ZHES DANG,
gru.wylie: spyod 'jug las, ,lus dang de bzhin longs spyod dang, ,dus gsum dge ba thams cad kyang, ,sems can kun gyi don bsgrub phyir, ,phangs pa med par gtang bar bya, zhes dang
gru.english: As the Guide to the Bodhisattva's Way of Life puts it, Give up everything you have: Your own flesh, the things you own, And the good things you do In the past, in the present, in the future— All for the sake Of every living being.

gru.acip: ,THAMS CAD BTANG BAS MYA NGAN 'DA', ,BDAG BLO MYA NGAN 'DAS PA SGRUB, ,THAMS CAD GTONG BAR CHABS CIG LA, ,SEMS CAN RNAMS LA BTANG BA MCHOG ,CES GSUNGS PA LTAR BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: thams cad btang bas mya ngan 'da', ,bdag blo mya ngan 'das pa sgrub, ,thams cad gtong bar chabs cig la, ,sems can rnams la btang ba mchog ,ces gsungs pa ltar bya'o
gru.english: We reach nirvana Giving up all we have; Let me reach it then Within my own mind: It's best, when I give it all up, To do the giving To every living being. The moonstone

gru.acip: DE YANG DGAG BCAS KYI MTSAMS LAS LDOG PAR MA ZAD, TSUL KHRIMS LAS BRTZAMS PA'I SGRUB BCAS KYI PHYOGS KUN RDZOGS PAR BYED PA'O,,
gru.wylie: de yang dgag bcas kyi mtshams las ldog par ma zad, tshul khrims las brtsams pa'i sgrub bcas kyi phyogs kun rdzogs par byed pa'o
gru.english: The point here, by the way, is not only that a person leading an ethical way of life has been able to turn away from transgressing deeds pronounced to be things that we shouldn't do; but they have been able as well to accomplish the opposite: deeds which, from a moral viewpoint, have been pronounced to be things that we should do. Our life is even more ethical

gru.acip: BZHI PA NI, GANG GI PHYIR DGE SLONG KHA CIG SO THAR LAS BRTZAMS TE, TSUL KHRIMS CHES YONGS SU DAG PA YIN KYANG, GAL TE DE NI CHOS RNAMS LA RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAR LTA BA MI SPONG NA, DE'I PHYIR RGYU MTSAN DES DGE SLONG DE TSUL KHRIMS DAG PAR MI 'GYUR TE,
gru.wylie: bzhi pa ni, gang gi phyir dge slong kha cig so thar las brtsams te, tshul khrims ches yongs su dag pa yin kyang, gal te de ni chos rnams la rang bzhin gyis grub par lta ba mi spong na, de'i phyir rgyu mtshan des dge slong de tshul khrims dag par mi 'gyur te
gru.english: Here finally is the fourth division from above: a presentation of additional causes that make our ethical life totally pure. Now there are certain monks who, with regard to the way in which they follow the vows of individual freedom, possess an ethical way of life which is incredibly pure. And yet if a monk like this has failed to rid themselves of the viewpoint in which they think that objects exist through some nature of their own, then because of this—for this reason—that same monk's observance of an ethical life would no longer be pure.

gru.acip: BDAG TU SMRA BA NI DMIGS PAR LTA BA'O, ,DE YANG NGA DANG NGA YIR 'DZIN PA LA GNAS PAS BSTAN TE, DE'I DON NI THUN MONG BA'I 'JIG LTA LA MI BYA'I, NGA DANG NGA YI BA RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PAR 'DZIN PA MI SPONG BA LA BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: bdag tu smra ba ni dmigs par lta ba'o, ,de yang nga dang nga yir 'dzin pa la gnas pas bstan te, de'i don ni thun mong ba'i 'jig lta la mi bya'i, nga dang nga yi ba rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub par 'dzin pa mi spong ba la bya'o
gru.english: By the way, when the text here refers to a monk who “asserts that things are themselves,” it is actually referring to a monk who views things as being themselves. This is as well what the words “they are still living in a way where they grasp to some kind of 'me,' and some kind of 'mine'” are referring to: the point is that they have yet to rid themselves of the idea that they & theirs exist by definition.

gru.acip: DMIGS PA CAN GYI LTA BA MI SPONG NA TSUL KHRIMS MI DAG PA DE'I PHYIR, SA GNYIS PA BA DE NI, RTAG TU SEMS CAN GANG LA TSUL 'CHAL SPONG BA DANG, SPONG GNYEN GANG ZHIG BYED PA DANG, GANG GIS SPONG BA GSUM CHAR LA'ANG DNGOS PO DANG DNGOS MED LA SOGS PA'I GNYIS KYI CHOS LA RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAR LTA BA'I GNYIS SU 'DZIN PA'I BLO'I RGYU BA YANG DAG PAR BRAL BAR TE SPONG BAR BYED PAR 'GYUR RO,,
gru.wylie: dmigs pa can gyi lta ba mi spong na tshul khrims mi dag pa de'i phyir, sa gnyis pa ba de ni, rtag tu sems can gang la tshul 'chal spong ba dang, spong gnyen gang zhig byed pa dang, gang gis spong ba gsum char la'ang dngos po dang dngos med la sogs pa'i gnyis kyi chos la rang bzhin gyis grub par lta ba'i gnyis su 'dzin pa'i blo'i rgyu ba yang dag par bral bar te spong bar byed par 'gyur ro
gru.english: If then we fail to rid ourselves of a point of view which still holds that there is something to view, then our attempt to follow an ethical way of life is no longer pure. Thus it is, that a person at the second level is always “free of”—meaning, they have rid themselves of—their mind running in a way where it grasps to duality: where it looks upon dual divisions such as things which function & things which do not, and views them as existing by nature; and this applies to having this view towards any of the three of (1) the living beings towards whom one has rid themselves of failing to live an ethical way of life; (2) the spiritual antidote which one has employed to do so; and (3) the person who is ridding themselves of this failure. An ethical life makes us pure

gru.acip: SHIN TU BLUN PAS GSAR DU SBYIN SOGS SGRUB PA MED PA'I PHYIR, SKYED DANG BCAS PA'I DNGOS PO 'DU BA STE RTZA BA LA SPYAD PAS YONGS SU ZAD PAS NA, SNGON GYI SBYIN 'BRAS MA LUS PA LONGS SPYOD PA PHYIN CHAD NAS GANG ZAG DE LA LONGS SPYOD 'BYUNG BAR MI 'GYUR RO,,
gru.wylie: shin tu blun pas gsar du sbyin sogs sgrub pa med pa'i phyir, skyed dang bcas pa'i dngos po 'du ba ste rtsa ba la spyad pas yongs su zad pas na, sngon gyi sbyin 'bras ma lus pa longs spyod pa phyin chad nas gang zag de la longs spyod 'byung bar mi 'gyur ro
gru.english: And then—since in our new circumstances our mind is so foolish—we will follow none of the practices of giving & the rest. That is, we will splurge the accumulated capital from which we are earning our interest: we will use up all our equity. A person like this enjoys every one of the fruits of our previous acts of giving, and then later on they have nothing more that can bring them any wealth.

gru.acip: NGAN 'GRO'I RTEN LA NI DGE BA SGRUB PA SHIN TU DKON LA, SDIG PA SOG PA LA SHIN TU THU BAS NA, NGAN 'GRO KHO NAR BRGYUD DGOS SO,,
gru.wylie: ngan 'gro'i rten la ni dge ba sgrub pa shin tu dkon la, sdig pa sog pa la shin tu thu bas na, ngan 'gro kho nar brgyud dgos so
gru.english: It is extremely rare for a person who possesses the body & mind of a being in the lower realms to accomplish any good deeds at all; their tendency to accumulate even more negative deeds is infinitely worse, and so they enter a downward cycle, which keeps them only in these realms of misery.

gru.acip: DE NYID KYI PHYIR MDO SDE LAS KYANG, BRGYA LA GAL TE MI RNAMS KYI NANG DU SKYES NA YANG, RNAM PAR SMIN PA GNYIS SGRUB STE, ZHES MIR SKYE BA DKA' BAR GSUNGS SO,,
gru.wylie: de nyid kyi phyir mdo sde las kyang, brgya la gal te mi rnams kyi nang du skyes na yang, rnam par smin pa gnyis sgrub ste, zhes mir skye ba dka' bar gsungs so
gru.english: This is exactly why the sutras describe how difficult it is to be born as a human being, in lines like— Even in the remote chance That they are born among humans, Their previous deeds Will come back to them in two ways…

gru.acip: ,BZHI PA NI, GANG GI PHYIR TSUL KHRIMS 'CHAL BA NI NGAN 'GROR 'KHRID PA SOGS NYES PA DU MA'I GNAS SU GYUR PA DE'I PHYIR, SDIG PA MTHA' DAG PHAM PAR MDZAD PA'I RGYAL BAS, SBYIN PA LA SOGS PA'I YON TAN CHUD MI ZA BAR BYA BA'I PHYIR SBYIN PA'I GTAM MDZAD NAS, DE'I MJUG THOGS SU TSUL KHRIMS SBYIN PA'I RJES SU 'GRO BA STE SGRUB PA'I GTAM NYID MDZAD PA YIN NO,,
gru.wylie: bzhi pa ni, gang gi phyir tshul khrims 'chal ba ni ngan 'gror 'khrid pa sogs nyes pa du ma'i gnas su gyur pa de'i phyir, sdig pa mtha' dag pham par mdzad pa'i rgyal bas, sbyin pa la sogs pa'i yon tan chud mi za bar bya ba'i phyir sbyin pa'i gtam mdzad nas, de'i mjug thogs su tshul khrims sbyin pa'i rjes su 'gro ba ste sgrub pa'i gtam nyid mdzad pa yin no
gru.english: This brings us to our fourth point from above: the reason why leading an ethical life is discussed after the discussion of giving. And so when a person fails in leading an ethical life, they incur many problems—such as this failure leading them to the lower realms.
