gru.acip: GANG ZAG DANG CHOS RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA NI, DE 'GOG PA'I RIGS PA RNAMS KYIS KHEGS PAR 'GYUR ZHING, DE'I TSE DE LTAR 'DZIN PA DE ZHEN YUL LA 'KHRUL PA'I BDEN 'DZIN DU 'GRUB LA, DE GRUB NA GANG ZAG DANG CHOS GNYIS BDEN GRUB TU 'DZIN PA BDAG 'DZIN GNYIS SU 'GRUB BO,,
gru.wylie: gang zag dang chos rang bzhin gyis grub pa ni, de 'gog pa'i rigs pa rnams kyis khegs par 'gyur zhing, de'i tshe de ltar 'dzin pa de zhen yul la 'khrul pa'i bden 'dzin du 'grub la, de grub na gang zag dang chos gnyis bden grub tu 'dzin pa bdag 'dzin gnyis su 'grub bo
gru.english: They refute the idea that the person & things could exist through some nature of their own by employing different forms of reasoning which disproves it. They would establish, at this point, the tendency to hold these things this way as being a tendency to hold that things are real where we are mistaken about the object that we think we see. Once this is established, they establish that the tendencies to hold the person and things as being real are what constitute the two forms of holding that things are themselves.

gru.acip: DE RNAMS GRUB NA BDEN 'DZIN DE DE KHO NA NYID KYI DON RIG PA'I 'GAL BA MI MTHUN PHYOGS SU 'GRUB PAS, MA RIG PAR 'GRUB CING, DE MA ZAD PAR {%BAR} DU 'JIG LTA YANG MI 'DZAD PAR SGRUB NUS PAS, NYON MONGS CAN GYI MA RIG PAR 'GRUB PAS NYON MONGS KYI RNAM GZHAG THUN MONG MA YIN PA 'JOG SHES PA SHIN TU GAL CHE'O,,
gru.wylie: de rnams grub na bden 'dzin de de kho na nyid kyi don rig pa'i 'gal ba mi mthun phyogs su 'grub pas, ma rig par 'grub cing, de ma zad par {%bar} du 'jig lta yang mi 'dzad par sgrub nus pas, nyon mongs can gyi ma rig par 'grub pas nyon mongs kyi rnam gzhag thun mong ma yin pa 'jog shes pa shin tu gal che'o
gru.english: Once these things are established, they can establish that the tendency to see things as real constitutes the direct, contradictory opposite of understanding suchness. With this, they have established what constitutes misunderstanding. Since we can prove that—until we finish this off—we could never finish off the view of destruction either, then once we have established what misunderstanding involved with negative emotions is, we can posit a unique presentation on the negative emotions. Understanding all this is extremely important.

gru.acip: DES NA GTI MUG GIS KUN BRTAGS PA KHO NA LA ZHES SOGS NI, RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA KHO NA'I YID DU 'ONG MI 'ONG SGRO BTAGS PA LA BRTEN NAS CHAGS SDANG GNYIS 'JUG PA'I PHYIR ZHES PA'O,,
gru.wylie: des na gti mug gis kun brtags pa kho na la zhes sogs ni, rang bzhin gyis grub pa kho na'i yid du 'ong mi 'ong sgro btags pa la brten nas chags sdang gnyis 'jug pa'i phyir zhes pa'o
gru.english: And thus the words “engage, exclusively, in a nature to things which has been imputed to them by this dark ignorance.” What this is saying is that attachment & repulsion can only engage in objects that are attractive or unattractive in a way which makes them more real than they are: these objects are exclusively those that would be existing through some nature of their own.

gru.acip: GTI MUG GIS BTAGS PA'I BDEN GRUB KHO NA CHAGS SOGS KYI DMIGS RNAM GNYIS KYI NANG NAS DMIGS PAR STON PA MIN TE, BDAG 'DZIN LHAN SKYES GNYIS KA'I DMIGS RNAM GNYIS KYI DMIGS PA GZHI GRUB PA YIN LA, CHAGS SOGS KYANG GTI MUG DANG MTSUNGS LDAN YIN PAS DMIGS PA MTSUNGS PA'I PHYIR RO,,
gru.wylie: gti mug gis btags pa'i bden grub kho na chags sogs kyi dmigs rnam gnyis kyi nang nas dmigs par ston pa min te, bdag 'dzin lhan skyes gnyis ka'i dmigs rnam gnyis kyi dmigs pa gzhi grub pa yin la, chags sogs kyang gti mug dang mtshungs ldan yin pas dmigs pa mtshungs pa'i phyir ro
gru.english: This is not to say though that it is only the real existence imputed by dark ignorance which can serve as one of the things belonging to the two sets of objects perceived by attachment or the like. For objects in the form of the two aspects of objects perceived by both the inborn forms of the tendency to believe that things are themselves are in fact existing entitites. And since the attachment or whatever shares a mental link with the dark ignorance, the objects of the two are also shared.

gru.acip: GTI MUG LA BRTEN PAR YANG 'GYUR TE ZHES PA NI, RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PAR 'DZIN PA'I GTI MUG SNGON DU SONG BAS CHAGS SOGS 'DREN PA'I DON NO,,
gru.wylie: gti mug la brten par yang 'gyur te zhes pa ni, rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub par 'dzin pa'i gti mug sngon du song bas chags sogs 'dren pa'i don no
gru.english: Now when the citation states that “they all rely upon this ignorance,” the point is that dark ignorance where we hold that things exist by definition comes first, and then this elicits the attachment or whatever it may be.

gru.acip: DES NA GTI MUG BCOM PA NYID KYIS NYON MONGS THAMS CAD 'JOMS PAR 'GYUR BAS, 'DI'I GNYEN PO RTEN 'BYUNG RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAS STONG PA'I GTAM NYID LA GUS PAR BYA BAR GSUNGS SO,,
gru.wylie: des na gti mug bcom pa nyid kyis nyon mongs thams cad 'joms par 'gyur bas, 'di'i gnyen po rten 'byung rang bzhin gyis grub pas stong pa'i gtam nyid la gus par bya bar gsungs so
gru.english: As such, the one & only way to destroy all our negative emotions is to destroy dark ignorance. And because of that, the text is saying, we should honor this one antidote to the ignorance: the teachings upon dependence, the fact that things are empty of existing through any nature of their own.

gru.acip: YUL DE YID DU 'ONG MI 'ONG GANG YANG MIN PA ZHIG NA'ANG MA RIG PA SKYE BAR 'GREL PA LAS GSUNGS TE, YUL DE RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PAR 'DZIN PA CIG RGYUD LA 'JUG BZHIN PA NA, YANG NA 'DOD CHAGS, YANG NA ZHE SDANG SKYE DE GNYIS MIN NA'ANG GTI MUG GI RIGS 'DRA 'JUG PAR BZHED LA,
gru.wylie: yul de yid du 'ong mi 'ong gang yang min pa zhig na'ang ma rig pa skye bar 'grel pa las gsungs te, yul de rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub par 'dzin pa cig rgyud la 'jug bzhin pa na, yang na 'dod chags, yang na zhe sdang skye de gnyis min na'ang gti mug gi rigs 'dra 'jug par bzhed la
gru.english: The commentary also says that misunderstanding will still arise even in a case where the object is neither attractive nor unattractive; for it takes the position that, so long as any tendency to hold things as existing by definition is operating within the mind, then desire or repulsion will arise and—even if neither does, at the moment—then a continued form of the dark ignorance will be in operation.

gru.acip: DE BZHIN DU CHOS RNAMS BDEN GRUB TU 'DZIN PA'I RNAM RTOG LA SGOM SPANG CHE 'BRING DGUR BYAS NAS, GNYEN PO SGOM LAM DGU DANG SBYOR BA YANG,
gru.wylie: de bzhin du chos rnams bden grub tu 'dzin pa'i rnam rtog la sgom spang che 'bring dgur byas nas, gnyen po sgom lam dgu dang sbyor ba yang
gru.english: In the same manner, there has been presented a division of the misperception where we hold all objects to exist in truth into nine different states of mind that we must rid ourselves of during the path of habituation, based on whether they are greater or middling. These are then matched to nine different antidotes during this path of habituation.

gru.acip: DES NA SHES SGRIB KYI MA RIG PA SPYOD PA'I PHYIR, ZHES PA NI SNANG BA YOD PA'I RGYU MTSAN MIN GYI, MNYAM RJES SU SNANG BA YOD MED RES 'JOG TU 'BYUNG BA'I SGRUB BYED DO,,
gru.wylie: des na shes sgrib kyi ma rig pa spyod pa'i phyir, zhes pa ni snang ba yod pa'i rgyu mtshan min gyi, mnyam rjes su snang ba yod med res 'jog tu 'byung ba'i sgrub byed do
gru.english: Therefore when we speak of “misunderstanding engaging in the form of an obstacle to knowledge,” it's not because there is an appearance of things as being self-existence; rather, we are simply establishing that things are alternating at that point: one possesses, and then doesn't possess, an appearance of things as self-existent, in states inside of the deep meditation and then subsequent to that state.

gru.acip: SNGA MA'I DON NI, SO SKYES DON DAM PAR GRUB PAR BZUNG BA'I BUM SOGS DE NYID, SNGAR BSHAD PA'I 'PHAGS PA GSUM MNYAM GZHAG LAS LANGS PA'I RJES THOB SNANG BA CAN RNAMS KYI KUN RDZOB TZAM YIN PAR BSTAN PAS,
gru.wylie: snga ma'i don ni, so skyes don dam par grub par bzung ba'i bum sogs de nyid, sngar bshad pa'i 'phags pa gsum mnyam gzhag las langs pa'i rjes thob snang ba can rnams kyi kun rdzob tsam yin par bstan pas
gru.english: What the first part of this last statement is saying is that those same objects which common beings hold to exist in an ultimate way—water pitchers and the like—are nothing more than deceptive objects for perceptions of the three types of realized beings described before who have come out of their deep meditation on emptiness, and to whom objects are appearing in a self-existent way.

gru.acip: DE RNAMS KYI NGOR BDEN PA TZAM GCOD KYI KUN RDZOB BDEN PA YIN PA MI GCOD CING, SO SKYES BUM SOGS LA DON DAM DU GRUB PAR 'DZIN PA'I ZHEN YUL 'PHAGS PA LA KUN RDZOB TU 'GYUR BAR STON PA MIN TE DE MI SRID PA'I PHYIR RO,,
gru.wylie: de rnams kyi ngor bden pa tsam gcod kyi kun rdzob bden pa yin pa mi gcod cing, so skyes bum sogs la don dam du grub par 'dzin pa'i zhen yul 'phags pa la kun rdzob tu 'gyur bar ston pa min te de mi srid pa'i phyir ro
gru.english: To their perceptions, deceptive reality in the form of the simple exclusion of a thing having real existence is not itself prevented; and we are not saying that, to a realized being, the things that common beings believe are there when they hold a water pitcher or the like to exist ultimately are present in a deceptive way—for that would be impossible.

gru.acip: DE YANG ZHES SOGS KYI DON NI DON DAM BDEN PA'I BDEN PA DE BDEN GRUB MA YIN PAR BSTAN PAR BZHED NAS, DE KHO NA NYID GZIGS PA'I NGOR SLU BA MED PAR GNAS PA BDEN PA'I DON DU BSHAD DO,,
gru.wylie: de yang zhes sogs kyi don ni don dam bden pa'i bden pa de bden grub ma yin par bstan par bzhed nas, de kho na nyid gzigs pa'i ngor slu ba med par gnas pa bden pa'i don du bshad do
gru.english: Moreover, the part in this citation which begins with “and this is” is meant by the author to indicate that the reality in ultimate reality is not something which exists really: what he's saying is that what it means to be “real” is where—to the perceptions of these beings as they view suchness—things exist in a way where they are no longer deceiving anyone. Not, in fact, indescribable

gru.acip: 'DI RTZOD PA'I LAN DU 'GRO TSUL NI, JI LTA BA MKHYEN PA'I YE SHES DES PHUNG SOGS KYI DE KHO NA NYID MNGON SUM DU GZIGS PA'I PHYIR DANG, PHUNG SOGS RNAMS GZIGS NGO DER MA GRUB PA DE DAG GI DE KHO NA NYID YIN PA'I PHYIR DANG, PHUNG SOGS MA GZIGS PA'I TSUL GYIS DE DAG GI DE KHO NA NYID GZIGS DGOS PA'I PHYIR TE,
gru.wylie: 'di rtsod pa'i lan du 'gro tshul ni, ji lta ba mkhyen pa'i ye shes des phung sogs kyi de kho na nyid mngon sum du gzigs pa'i phyir dang, phung sogs rnams gzigs ngo der ma grub pa de dag gi de kho na nyid yin pa'i phyir dang, phung sogs ma gzigs pa'i tshul gyis de dag gi de kho na nyid gzigs dgos pa'i phyir te
gru.english: How exactly does this point function to address that last objection? First of all, the wisdom of a Buddha which perceives the way in which all things exist sees—directly—the true nature of the parts to the person, and so on. And the way that these parts and the like do not exist to these perceptions is in fact the true nature of those entities. Finally, these beings have to perceive the true nature of these objects through their way of not seeing these parts, and the rest.

gru.acip: TSAD MA DANG GZHAL BYA YANG TSIG GSAL LAS GSUNGS PA LTAR NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB PA BKAG NAS, LTOS 'JOG GI TSAD MA DANG GZHAL BYA 'JOG PAR BSHAD PA LTA BUR BYED DGOS TE 'OG TU 'CHAD PAR 'GYUR RO,,
gru.wylie: tshad ma dang gzhal bya yang tshig gsal las gsungs pa ltar ngo bo nyid kyis grub pa bkag nas, ltos 'jog gi tshad ma dang gzhal bya 'jog par bshad pa lta bur byed dgos te 'og tu 'chad par 'gyur ro
gru.english: As for the concepts of accurate perception and the objects under its consideration, we need to deny—in the same way as we seen this done in A Clarification of the Verses—that they could ever exist through any nature of their own. And then we need to go further and do things like explaining how it is that we ourselves posit an accurate type of perception which could establish that things exist in reliance; and what the object under its consideration would be like. The world contradicts the world

gru.acip: 'JIG RTEN NYID LAS GRAGS SHING GRUB PA'I DON NI, 'JIG RTEN GYI GRAGS PA NYID KYIS GAL TE SEL NA, GANG ZAG DE LA 'JIG RTEN GYIS GNOD PAR 'GYUR RO,,
gru.wylie: 'jig rten nyid las grags shing grub pa'i don ni, 'jig rten gyi grags pa nyid kyis gal te sel na, gang zag de la 'jig rten gyis gnod par 'gyur ro
gru.english: Consider, in reply, the state of things as this is generally considered, and established, in the everyday world itself. Suppose this were itself disallowed by the very conventions of this same world; in this case, we could say that this same person was contradicted by the world.

gru.acip: GANG GI PHYIR PHA 'DI BU DE'I LUS KYI RGYU BLUGS NAS RANG GI BU STON PAR BYED PA DE'I PHYIR, SA BON DANG BU GNYIS RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PA'I GZHAN DU 'DZIN PA MA YIN NO, ZHES BYA BAR 'JIG RTEN DU GSAL BAR NGES SO,,
gru.wylie: gang gi phyir pha 'di bu de'i lus kyi rgyu blugs nas rang gi bu ston par byed pa de'i phyir, sa bon dang bu gnyis rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub pa'i gzhan du 'dzin pa ma yin no, zhes bya bar 'jig rten du gsal bar nges so
gru.english: And so the father points to the child as his child, since it was he who deposited the cause for the child's body. As such, it is beyond question that—in the world—the case is clear: neither of the two, the seed nor the child, is being considered something other which exists in & of itself.

gru.acip: GAL TE RANG GI NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB PA'I GZHAN DU 'DZIN NA NI, GANG ZAG GZHAN LTAR BU DE BSTAN NAS 'DI NGAS BSKYED DO ZHES STON PAR MI 'GYUR RO,,
gru.wylie: gal te rang gi ngo bo nyid kyis grub pa'i gzhan du 'dzin na ni, gang zag gzhan ltar bu de bstan nas 'di ngas bskyed do zhes ston par mi 'gyur ro
gru.english: If the world did adhere to something other which did exist in & of itself, then it would never happen that—as we saw with that other person—people pointed to a child and said “I was the one who gave them birth.”

gru.acip: DE'I PHYIR GRUB MTHA' SMRA BA GZHAN GYIS GZHAN SKYE KHAS BLANGS PA'I DON NI, RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PA'I GZHAN SKYE YIN GYI, NGO BO GZHAN DU GRUB PA TZAM MA YIN LA, DE TZAM 'JIG RTEN GYI NGOR MA GRUB PA YANG MIN NO,,
gru.wylie: de'i phyir grub mtha' smra ba gzhan gyis gzhan skye khas blangs pa'i don ni, rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub pa'i gzhan skye yin gyi, ngo bo gzhan du grub pa tsam ma yin la, de tsam 'jig rten gyi ngor ma grub pa yang min no
gru.english: As such, when those who profess other schools of thought say that they accept the idea that things grow from other things, what they are referring to actually is a growing from other things which could exist by definition. It is not simply the fact that the essence of the things is that they exist as other than each other; just that much is not something that cannot be established to the perceptions of the everyday world.

gru.acip: GZHAN LAS SKYE BA 'JIG RTEN LAS KYANG MED, CES PA'I DON NI, 'JIG RTEN RANG DGA' BAS SA MYUG LA SOGS PA'I NYER LEN GYI RGYU 'BRAS LA RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PA'I GZHAN DU 'DZIN PA MED CES PA TZAM MIN GYI,
gru.wylie: gzhan las skye ba 'jig rten las kyang med, ces pa'i don ni, 'jig rten rang dga' bas sa myug la sogs pa'i nyer len gyi rgyu 'bras la rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub pa'i gzhan du 'dzin pa med ces pa tsam min gyi
gru.english: But then our verse here says, “Things growing from things that are other than them is not something that we see even in the everyday world.” This is not simply saying that just normal people of the everyday world never hold that things like the soil and the sprout—examples of cause & effect where the cause turns into the result directly—exist as entities that are other than each other by definition.

gru.acip: CI KUN RDZOB KYI RNAM PAR GZHAG PA BRJOD PAR BYA BA YIN NAM ZHES PA'I LAN DU, RKYEN NYID 'DI PA TZAM GYIS KUN RDZOB GRUB PAR KHAS LEN GYI, PHYOGS BZHI KHAS BLANGS PA'I SGO NAS NI MA YIN TE,
gru.wylie: ci kun rdzob kyi rnam par gzhag pa brjod par bya ba yin nam zhes pa'i lan du, rkyen nyid 'di pa tsam gyis kun rdzob grub par khas len gyi, phyogs bzhi khas blangs pa'i sgo nas ni ma yin te
gru.english: And the same work concludes with: And you may ask, “What do you mean, when you say this is all happening in a deceptive way?” In response we can say that we accept that something exists in a deceptive way as soon as we mention no more than “this particular factor.” It is not though because we are accepting any one of the four options at this point.

gru.acip: DE'I PHYIR DE LTAR DNGOS PO RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA MED PAR JI SKAD BSHAD PA'I TSUL LA, RTEN 'BYUNG RTAG CHAD MED PAR GRUB PA'I SGO NAS RTAG CHAD KYI MTHAR MI LTUNG BA'I YON TAN BSTAN PA'I PHYIR BSHAD PA,
gru.wylie: de'i phyir de ltar dngos po rang bzhin gyis grub pa med par ji skad bshad pa'i tshul la, rten 'byung rtag chad med par grub pa'i sgo nas rtag chad kyi mthar mi ltung ba'i yon tan bstan pa'i phyir bshad pa
gru.english: For all these reasons, then, we have established that the way in which things occur in dependence is free of the extremes of lasting forever or simply discontinuing, in the way we have explained how things are free of existing through any nature of their own. And then now we seek to demonstrate the benefits of avoiding, thus, falling into these extremes of things lasting forever, or discontinuing; which is why we continue on here to explain the following point.

gru.acip: GAL TE MYU GU SA BON LAS RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA'I GZHAN YIN NA NI, SA MYUG GNYIS RGYU 'BRAS SU MI RUNG BA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: gal te myu gu sa bon las rang bzhin gyis grub pa'i gzhan yin na ni, sa myug gnyis rgyu 'bras su mi rung ba'i phyir
gru.english: That is, if a sprout were something other than its seed in a way where the sprout existed through some nature of its own, it would be inappropriate to say that the seed and the sprout were a cause and its effect.

gru.acip: DE LTAR YIN PA LA RGYU MTSAN GANG GI PHYIR MYU GU SA BON LAS RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA'I GZHAN MIN PA'I PHYOGS LA, DE GNYIS RGYU 'BRAS SU MI 'GAL BA DE'I PHYIR MYU GU YOD PA'I TSE SA BON ZHIG PA STE DE'I RIGS BRGYUD CHAD PA MED PAS CHAD PA SPANGS SO,,
gru.wylie: de ltar yin pa la rgyu mtshan gang gi phyir myu gu sa bon las rang bzhin gyis grub pa'i gzhan min pa'i phyogs la, de gnyis rgyu 'bras su mi 'gal ba de'i phyir myu gu yod pa'i tshe sa bon zhig pa ste de'i rigs brgyud chad pa med pas chad pa spangs so
gru.english: Why—for what reason—is this the case? Suppose we take the position that a sprout is not something which exists as something other than the seed—at least as something which is other through some nature of its own. The fact is that it is no contradiction to say that these two exist as cause & effect; which means that, therefore, we can say that by the time that the sprout is in existence, the seed has gone out of existence. It's not though that the the seed type in itself has undergone any discontinuation here; that it no longer exists. As such, we avoid the extreme of saying that things have stopped altogether.

gru.acip: DE'I RGYU MTSAN CI'I PHYIR ZHE NA, MYU GU DE SA BON LAS RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA'I GZHAN DANG, RANG BZHIN GCIG PA NYID DE YANG MIN PA'I PHYIR RO,,
gru.wylie: de'i rgyu mtshan ci'i phyir zhe na, myu gu de sa bon las rang bzhin gyis grub pa'i gzhan dang, rang bzhin gcig pa nyid de yang min pa'i phyir ro
gru.english: And why is that? Because the sprout is not something that exists through some nature of its own which is other than the seed; nor is it something which is such that to be it is to be no other than the seed.

gru.acip: RKANG PA DANG POS NI 'DU BYED MA RIG PA LA BRTEN NAS 'BYUNG BA'I GTAN TSIGS DANG, GNYIS PAS NI 'DU BYED DE KHO NA NYID DU YOD PA MIN ZHES PA'I BSGRUB BYA DANG, GSUM PAS NI RGYU 'BRAS GNYIS KA STONG PAR BSTAN LA, BZHI PAS NI STONG TSUL STON TE, G-YO BA NI MNGON PAR 'DU BYED PA YIN LA, DE DANG BRAL BA NI 'DU BYED 'DU BYED KYIS STONG PA'O,,
gru.wylie: rkang pa dang pos ni 'du byed ma rig pa la brten nas 'byung ba'i gtan tshigs dang, gnyis pas ni 'du byed de kho na nyid du yod pa min zhes pa'i bsgrub bya dang, gsum pas ni rgyu 'bras gnyis ka stong par bstan la, bzhi pas ni stong tshul ston te, g-yo ba ni mngon par 'du byed pa yin la, de dang bral ba ni 'du byed 'du byed kyis stong pa'o
gru.english: The first of the four sections here presents the logical statement, that fresh karma occurs through its dependence upon misunderstanding. The second of the four presents the assertion to be proven, which is that fresh karma is not something which could exist in & of itself. The third presents the idea that both cause and effect are empty; and then the fourth section describes the way in which they are empty. Here, the word “shifting” connotes occurrence through conscious undertaking; and mentioning “free of” is meant to indicate that fresh karma is empty of any such undertaking.

gru.acip: DE YANG RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA DANG BRAL LO ZHES DGAG BYA'I KHYAD PAR BSTAN TE, DE KHO NA NYID DU MED PA DANG DON 'DRA'O,,
gru.wylie: de yang rang bzhin gyis grub pa dang bral lo zhes dgag bya'i khyad par bstan te, de kho na nyid du med pa dang don 'dra'o
gru.english: And then when it's saying here that “things are devoid of existing through any nature of their own”—which is to indicate the logical feature of what it is we deny. This is similar to saying that these things are devoid of existing in & of themselves.

gru.acip: BZHI PA LA GNYIS, RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PA YOD PAR 'DOD PA DGAG PA DANG, DE LTAR BKAG PA LA RTZOD PA SPANG BA'O,,
gru.wylie: bzhi pa la gnyis, rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub pa yod par 'dod pa dgag pa dang, de ltar bkag pa la rtsod pa spang ba'o
gru.english: Here then is our fourth point from above, demonstrating that there is no possible instance where it would be correct to say that things could grow through any nature of their own. Here we proceed in two steps: denying the belief that things could exist by definition; and then disproving any argument against this denial.

gru.acip: DE LTA MA YIN TE GAL TE GZUGS DANG TSOR BA LA SOGS PA'I RANG GI MTSAN NYID DE RANG GI NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB PA'I RANG BZHIN, RGYU DANG RKYEN LA BRTEN NAS SKYE BAR 'GYUR NA NI, RNAL 'BYOR PAS CHOS RNAMS RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAS STONG PAR MNGON SUM DU RTOGS PA'I TSE, DNGOS PO'I RANG BZHIN DE LA SKUR PA BTAB PA'I TSUL GYIS STONG PA NYID RTOGS PAR 'GYUR TE,
gru.wylie: de lta ma yin te gal te gzugs dang tshor ba la sogs pa'i rang gi mtshan nyid de rang gi ngo bo nyid kyis grub pa'i rang bzhin, rgyu dang rkyen la brten nas skye bar 'gyur na ni, rnal 'byor pas chos rnams rang bzhin gyis grub pas stong par mngon sum du rtogs pa'i tshe, dngos po'i rang bzhin de la skur pa btab pa'i tshul gyis stong pa nyid rtogs par 'gyur te
gru.english: And that is indeed the case, since—well, suppose it were not. Suppose that physical form and feelings and the rest had a nature of existing by definition; which is to say, through some nature of their own. If that nature were something that started by depending upon causes & conditions, then when a deep practitioner perceived, directly, that entities were empty of existing through any nature of their own, then they would be perceiving emptiness itself in a manner where they were discounting the very nature of all these entities.

gru.acip: MNYAM GZHAG GIS GZUGS SOGS RNAMS MA DMIGS PA DGOS LA, DE RNAMS RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB NA MNYAM GZHAG GIS DMIGS DGOS PA LAS MA DMIGS PA'I PHYIR, DE'I TSE DNGOS PO DE RNAMS MED PAR 'GYUR RO,,
gru.wylie: mnyam gzhag gis gzugs sogs rnams ma dmigs pa dgos la, de rnams rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub na mnyam gzhag gis dmigs dgos pa las ma dmigs pa'i phyir, de'i tshe dngos po de rnams med par 'gyur ro
gru.english: And the simple fact is that—when we are in this particular deep meditation—we would then have to be focusing upon physical form and the like; and if these things existed by definition, then the meditation would have to be perceiving that fact. But in fact, it does not. And for this reason then, those entities—at that moment in time—would have to be non-existent.

gru.acip: DE NI RIGS PA YANG MIN PA DE'I PHYIR DNGOS PO RNAMS KYI RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PA NI YOD PA MIN PAS, DUS THAMS CAD KYI TSE RANG BZHIN GYIS SKYE BA KHAS BLANG BAR MI BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: de ni rigs pa yang min pa de'i phyir dngos po rnams kyi rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub pa ni yod pa min pas, dus thams cad kyi tshe rang bzhin gyis skye ba khas blang bar mi bya'o
gru.english: And yet neither is that a reasonable thing to say happened; as such, it could never occur that objects could exist by definition. And thus we could never accept that things had started through any nature of their own, at any particular point in time at all.

gru.acip: 'DI LA DBU MA PA RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PA'I SKYE BA KHAS LEN PA RNAMS, RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB KYANG BDEN GRUB TU MI 'GRO BAR 'DOD PA'I RGYU MTSAN GYIS, GZUGS SOGS RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB NA DE KHO NA NYID MNGON SUM DU GZIGS PAS DMIGS MI DGOS SO, ZHES SMRA MOD KYANG,
gru.wylie: 'di la dbu ma pa rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub pa'i skye ba khas len pa rnams, rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub kyang bden grub tu mi 'gro bar 'dod pa'i rgyu mtshan gyis, gzugs sogs rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub na de kho na nyid mngon sum du gzigs pas dmigs mi dgos so, zhes smra mod kyang
gru.english: Now there are certain members of the Middle Way school who accept the idea that the starting of things could exist by definition; and they would say that a thing's existing by definition does not necessitate that it exists in truth. And then for this reason they would say that it's not necessarily the case that—if physical form and the rest exist by definition—then that would have to be perceived by someone who was seeing, directly, the way things really are.

gru.acip: DE TZAM NAS BDEN GRUB YIN PAR SNGAR YANG BSHAD CING, SLAR YANG 'CHAD PAR 'GYUR BA'I RIGS PAS NYES PA SPONG MI NUS SO,,
gru.wylie: de tsam nas bden grub yin par sngar yang bshad cing, slar yang 'chad par 'gyur ba'i rigs pas nyes pa spong mi nus so
gru.english: From this standpoint alone they would have to be accepting, as we explained earlier, that things existed in truth; and it's not as though we would be able to disabuse them of their mistake by repeated any further logic.

gru.acip: CHOS RNAMS LA RANG MTSAN GYIS GRUB PA'I RANG BZHIN YOD NA, CHOS DE RNAMS RANG NGOS NAS STONG PAR MA SONG BAS CHOS RNAMS NYID STONG PA DANG ZHES PA MI 'THAD LA,
gru.wylie: chos rnams la rang mtshan gyis grub pa'i rang bzhin yod na, chos de rnams rang ngos nas stong par ma song bas chos rnams nyid stong pa dang zhes pa mi 'thad la
gru.english: If things did have a nature to them which existed by definition, then we could never say that these same things were, from their side, empty. And then it would be incorrect to say things like we just saw: “The very nature of those things is their emptiness.”

gru.acip: DBU MA'I LAM GYIS CHOS RNAMS KYI RANG BZHIN LA SO SOR RTOG PA NA, CHOS RNAMS RANG NGOS NAS RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAS STONG PAR STON PAR YIN PAR BSTAN NO,,
gru.wylie: dbu ma'i lam gyis chos rnams kyi rang bzhin la so sor rtog pa na, chos rnams rang ngos nas rang bzhin gyis grub pas stong par ston par yin par bstan no
gru.english: And so all this would mean that what's being said is that—when we use the path of the middle way to make a thorough investigation of the nature of things—what we're learning is that things are empty of existing through any nature where they could be coming from their own side.

gru.acip: MDO 'DIS NI RNAM RIG PAS GZHAN DBANG RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PAS MI STONG BA DANG, DE GZUNG 'DZIN RDZAS THA DAD PA MED PAS STONG ZHES PA YANG BKAG LA,
gru.wylie: mdo 'dis ni rnam rig pas gzhan dbang rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub pas mi stong ba dang, de gzung 'dzin rdzas tha dad pa med pas stong zhes pa yang bkag la
gru.english: This sutra is also serving to deny the idea of the Mentalists that those entities which arise at the pleasure of their causes & conditions are not empty of existing by definition; and the idea that these things are empty because there cannot exist any state of mind holding to an object, and any object being held by it, which are such that it is not true that to be one is to be the other.

gru.acip: RTZA SHE LAS KYANG, ,STONG NYID LTA BA THAMS CAD NI, ,NGES PAR 'BYIN PAR RGYAL BAS GSUNGS, ,GANG DAG STONG PA NYID LTA BA, ,DE DAG BSGRUB TU MED PAR GSUNGS, ZHES PAS KYANG SNGAR GYI MDO'I DON DE NYID 'CHAD DO,,
gru.wylie: rtsa she las kyang, ,stong nyid lta ba thams cad ni, ,nges par 'byin par rgyal bas gsungs, ,gang dag stong pa nyid lta ba, ,de dag bsgrub tu med par gsungs, zhes pas kyang sngar gyi mdo'i don de nyid 'chad do
gru.english: Wisdom also says— The victorious Buddhas have stated That emptiness functions To destroy all of those views. And they say as well That those with a view Of emptiness can never Be sustained. These lines as well are expressing the same point as the sutra listed above.

gru.acip: DE 'DRA BA'I STONG PA DE KHA CIG YANG DAG TU SMRA LA, GZHAN DAG CHAD STONG DU 'DOD PA GNYIS KA YANG RTEN 'BREL RTAG CHAD KYI MTHA' DANG BRAL BAR RGYAL BA RGYAL SRAS KYIS LAN CIG MA YIN PAR BSGRUBS PA LAS PHYI ROL TU GYUR PA YIN NO,,
gru.wylie: de 'dra ba'i stong pa de kha cig yang dag tu smra la, gzhan dag chad stong du 'dod pa gnyis ka yang rten 'brel rtag chad kyi mtha' dang bral bar rgyal ba rgyal sras kyis lan cig ma yin par bsgrubs pa las phyi rol tu gyur pa yin no
gru.english: And so some people say that these kinds of emptiness are correct forms of emptiness; while others say that they represent an emptiness of things simply discontinuing. Both of these parties though have left behind what the Victors and the children of these Victors have established—have “sustained,” and certainly no single time—as dependent events, free of the extremes of all things remaining forever unchanging, or simply discontinuing.

gru.acip: KHYAD PAR DU KUN RDZOB BDEN PA THAMS CAD KHO RANG KHO RANG GIS STONG PAR GTAN LA 'BEBS DGOS ZER NAS, DE CHAD STONG DU 'DOD PA NI MI RIGS PA KHO NA STE, GRUB MTHA' BZHI PO SU YANG LTA BA DE CHAD LTA YIN PAR SHES NAS, DE RANG GI RGYUD LA SKYED PAR BYED PA SU YANG MED PA'I PHYIR RO,,
gru.wylie: khyad par du kun rdzob bden pa thams cad kho rang kho rang gis stong par gtan la 'bebs dgos zer nas, de chad stong du 'dod pa ni mi rigs pa kho na ste, grub mtha' bzhi po su yang lta ba de chad lta yin par shes nas, de rang gi rgyud la skyed par byed pa su yang med pa'i phyir ro
gru.english: Let's look more particularly at the claim here that we must establish all instances of deceptive reality through saying that they are empty of being themselves. The belief that this then represents the emptiness of things simply discontinuing is nothing but mistaken. It doesn't matter which of the four classical schools a person might belong to; everybody in all the schools realizes that this is simply the view that things would, indeed, have simply discontinued. As such, there is not a single person in all these schools that would attempt to engender this viewpoint within their own mindstream.

gru.acip: DES NA DGAG GZHI DE DGAG BYA'I NGO BOR MED PA DANG, GZHI DE DGAG BYAS STONG TSUL YANG YIN PAS STONG PAR 'DRA BZHIN DU, CHOS RNAMS RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PAS STONG PA NI RANG GI NGO BOS STONG PA'I DON YIN LA,
gru.wylie: des na dgag gzhi de dgag bya'i ngo bor med pa dang, gzhi de dgag byas stong tshul yang yin pas stong par 'dra bzhin du, chos rnams rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub pas stong pa ni rang gi ngo bos stong pa'i don yin la
gru.english: As such, we can say that the object which we assert lacks a certain quality represents an absence of sharing any essence of that quality; and we can also say that this is equivalent to the way in which this object is empty of the particular quality that we deny about it. These two are both ways in which we can describe the object as “empty.” Similarly, the fact that entities are empty of existing in any way by definition is exactly what it means when we say they are empty of any essence of their own.

gru.acip: DE LAS GZHAN PA'I STONG TSUL RNAMS RANG GI NGO BOS STONG PA MIN PA'I RGYU MTSAN NI, STONG TSUL SNGA MA TSAD MAS GRUB ZIN BYED PA MA NYAMS PA'I RING LA, GRUB MTHAS GZHI DE BDEN PA'AM DE'I DON DU YOD PAR 'DZIN PA'I SGRO 'DOGS SKYE MI SRID LA, PHYI MA RNAMS KYI DON TSAD MAS GRUB CING BYED PA MA NYAMS KYANG, GRUB MTHA' BDEN PA'AM BDEN PA'I DON DU SGRO 'DOGS PA MI 'GAL BA'O,,
gru.wylie: de las gzhan pa'i stong tshul rnams rang gi ngo bos stong pa min pa'i rgyu mtshan ni, stong tshul snga ma tshad mas grub zin byed pa ma nyams pa'i ring la, grub mthas gzhi de bden pa'am de'i don du yod par 'dzin pa'i sgro 'dogs skye mi srid la, phyi ma rnams kyi don tshad mas grub cing byed pa ma nyams kyang, grub mtha' bden pa'am bden pa'i don du sgro 'dogs pa mi 'gal ba'o
gru.english: And what then is the reason why we say that ways in which things could be empty that are different than these particular ways do not represent an emptiness of some kind of self-essence? Suppose that those previous ways in which we described things as being empty had already been confirmed by accurate perception; and we were all still sitting in a place where none of those confirmations had in any way declined. It would in that state be impossible for us to hold a school of thought which took those same examples of things to exist in truth; neither would it be possible for there to grow, within our minds, that form of overestimation where we held that things could exist in this same kind of truth. The idea in the latter cases here would be that a certain point had been confirmed by an accurate perception, and that the working of this perception had in no way declined; and yet this would not preclude overestimation through a learned philosophical school which said that a certain object was real; or even described what it was to be real. Normal reality cannot stand up under true analysis

gru.acip: DON BSDU NA CHOS RNAMS RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB NA 'DU BYED RNAMS BRDZUN PA SLU BA'I CHOS CAN DU MI 'GRUB PAS, KUN RDZOB BDEN PA MED PA'I PHYIR BDEN PA GNYIS MED PAR 'GYUR LA, RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PA MED PA'I PHYOGS LA NI, KUN RDZOB DANG DON DAM BDEN PA GNYIS KA YOD CES PA'I DON NO,,
gru.wylie: don bsdu na chos rnams rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub na 'du byed rnams brdzun pa slu ba'i chos can du mi 'grub pas, kun rdzob bden pa med pa'i phyir bden pa gnyis med par 'gyur la, rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub pa med pa'i phyogs la ni, kun rdzob dang don dam bden pa gnyis ka yod ces pa'i don no
gru.english: To summarize, we can say that if things existed by definition, then it would not be the case that the various factors were things that were lying to us: deceiving us. And in this case, there would be no deceptive form of reality; which means that there would then be no two realities. And what this is all really saying is that—when we take the position that there is nothing in the universe that exists by definition—then there can exist the two realities: deceptive and ultimate.

gru.acip: GAL TE SNGAR GYI LUNG GIS MYANG 'DAS GCIG PU BDEN GYI, 'DU BYED GZHAN BRDZUN PAR GSUNGS PAS 'DUS BYAS RNAMS RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS MA GRUB KYANG, MYANG 'DAS DON DAM PA'I BDEN PA RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PA MA YIN NAM SNYAM NA,
gru.wylie: gal te sngar gyi lung gis myang 'das gcig pu bden gyi, 'du byed gzhan brdzun par gsungs pas 'dus byas rnams rang gi mtshan nyid kyis ma grub kyang, myang 'das don dam pa'i bden pa rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub pa ma yin nam snyam na
gru.english: Now someone might think to themselves the following: Well then, the lines you just quoted were saying that only nirvana is true; and that other things, factors, were false. Wouldn't this then imply that—although produced things are not things which exist by definition—nirvana, or ultimate reality, does exist by definition?

gru.acip: DE'I BDEN PA NI MDO NYID LAS MI SLU BA'I CHOS CAN ZHES GSUNGS PAS MI SLU BA'I DON DU BSHAD KYI, RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA'I BDEN PA NI MA YIN NA, ,'DU BYED THAMS CAD NI BRDZUN PA SLU BA'I CHOS CAN ZHES GSUNGS PAS KYANG SNGA MA'I BDEN PA MI SLU BA'I DON DU SHES SO,,
gru.wylie: de'i bden pa ni mdo nyid las mi slu ba'i chos can zhes gsungs pas mi slu ba'i don du bshad kyi, rang bzhin gyis grub pa'i bden pa ni ma yin na, ,'du byed thams cad ni brdzun pa slu ba'i chos can zhes gsungs pas kyang snga ma'i bden pa mi slu ba'i don du shes so
gru.english: That type of reality is described in the sutra itself as being something that never deceives us; as such, this is what's being explained as the meaning of “never deceives.” But if saying that a truth existed by definition were not what “never deceives” refers to, then we would have to understand that “all the factors there are lie to us: they deceive us” was what it meant for the first truth to be something that did not deceive us.

gru.acip: RANG RGYUD PA RNAMS KYIS NI DE TZAM NAS DE KHO NA NYID LA DPYOD PAR MI 'JOG GI ,SNGAR BSHAD PA BZHIN GYI SHES PA LA SNANG BA'I DBANG GIS YOD PAR BZHAG GAM, DE'I DBANG GIS BZHAG PA MIN PA'I DON GYI SDOD LUGS NAS GRUB PA YIN DPYOD PA NAS,
gru.wylie: rang rgyud pa rnams kyis ni de tsam nas de kho na nyid la dpyod par mi 'jog gi ,sngar bshad pa bzhin gyi shes pa la snang ba'i dbang gis yod par bzhag gam, de'i dbang gis bzhag pa min pa'i don gyi sdod lugs nas grub pa yin dpyod pa nas
gru.english: This in itself though is not enough—according to those who belong to the Independent group within this same Middle Way school—to say that we are examining the way that things really are. They would investigate whether, first of all, things are established as existing by force of their making their appearance to a state of mind, as we described it before. Or else they would try to see if things were not established in this manner; but, rather, simply from the way that the object itself existed in the world.

gru.acip: MA DPYAD PA'I RNAM GZHAG THAMS CAD LOG PA'I DON CAN KHO NA DANG, DPYAD PA'I RNAM GZHAG RNAMS MA LOG PAR 'DOD PA NI DBU TSAD GANG GI YANG LUGS MA YIN TE, GNYIS KA'I LUGS KYIS MA DPYAD PA'I RNAM GZHAG LA TSAD MAS GRUB PA DU MA ZHIG 'BYUNG BA'I PHYIR RO, ,RGYAS PAR GZHAN DU BSHAD ZIN PAS MA SPROS SO,,
gru.wylie: ma dpyad pa'i rnam gzhag thams cad log pa'i don can kho na dang, dpyad pa'i rnam gzhag rnams ma log par 'dod pa ni dbu tshad gang gi yang lugs ma yin te, gnyis ka'i lugs kyis ma dpyad pa'i rnam gzhag la tshad mas grub pa du ma zhig 'byung ba'i phyir ro, ,rgyas par gzhan du bshad zin pas ma spros so
gru.english: Just so, all determinations that we make about things without any real examination result in nothing other than erroneous conclusions. And claiming that different ways of making the examination are not mistaken is not the position of any school which counts itself part of the Middle Way; since, for that matter, there are many points in positions not examined by either system which can indeed be confirmed by accurate perception. I have in the past expanded on these points significantly elsewhere; and so I will not present more detail on them here.

gru.acip: CI STE YANG DE LTAR DNGOS PO LA BDEN PAR MNGON PAR ZHEN PA THAMS CAD GCOD PA NA, BRED SHA 'THON PA THA SNYAD KYI BDEN PA LA BDEN PAR ZHEN PA 'DI GANG KUN BYANG GNYIS KYI 'CHING GROL GYI RGYUR 'GYUR BA, RDZAS TE RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PA'I BDAG NYID 'GA' ZHIG TU SKYE BAR 'GYUR BA CIG BYA DGOS SO ZHES SMRA NA, DE SKAD DU SMRA BA LA NI TSIG TZAM ZHIG LHAG MAR LUS PAR 'GYUR RO,,
gru.wylie: ci ste yang de ltar dngos po la bden par mngon par zhen pa thams cad gcod pa na, bred sha 'thon pa tha snyad kyi bden pa la bden par zhen pa 'di gang kun byang gnyis kyi 'ching grol gyi rgyur 'gyur ba, rdzas te rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub pa'i bdag nyid 'ga' zhig tu skye bar 'gyur ba cig bya dgos so zhes smra na, de skad du smra ba la ni tshig tsam zhig lhag mar lus par 'gyur ro
gru.english: Well now, how is it? Suppose that, as we've described it, people start to eliminate all of their tendencies to grasp to things existing in reality. Then though their faces take on a certain look of panic, and they start feeling a strong belief that nominal reality though must be real. That is, they begin to say that there must exist objects which act as causes behind the bondage and the liberation going on with the negative side of things, and the enlightened side of things. And they feel that these causes must be creating some number of entities which are substantial; that is, which exist by definition. But these kinds of proclamations end up just being all words, and nothing else.

gru.acip: CI'I PHYIR ZHE NA, JI LTAR DE KHO NA NYID DON DAM PA LA DPYOD PA'I SKABS SU, JI SKAD BSHAD PA'I RIGS PA GANG ZHIG GIS GZUGS SOGS BDAG DANG GZHAN LAS SKYE BA RIGS PA MIN PA DE BZHIN DU, THA SNYAD DU YANG RIGS PA DE NYID KYIS SKYE BAR RIGS PA MIN PAS, KHYOD KYI RANG BZHIN GYIS SKYE BA TSAD MA GANG GIS 'GRUB PAR 'GYUR TE MI 'GYUR RO,,
gru.wylie: ci'i phyir zhe na, ji ltar de kho na nyid don dam pa la dpyod pa'i skabs su, ji skad bshad pa'i rigs pa gang zhig gis gzugs sogs bdag dang gzhan las skye ba rigs pa min pa de bzhin du, tha snyad du yang rigs pa de nyid kyis skye bar rigs pa min pas, khyod kyi rang bzhin gyis skye ba tshad ma gang gis 'grub par 'gyur te mi 'gyur ro
gru.english: And why can we say that? The fact is that the case here is just the same as it was at the point where we were examining the way things really are; that is, the ultimate. We can use the same rationale that we expressed there, and say that it would be illogical to say that physical form or the like could have grown either from itself, or from something other than itself. This very same reasoning applies in nominal cases as well, to show that it could not be logical to say that things were growing. Thus the question remains, of what kind of accurate perception you can point to in order to establish things' growing through some nature of their own. Because, in fact, no such perception exists.

gru.acip: DE KHO NA NYID LA DPYOD PA'I RIGS PAS THA SNYAD DU RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PA'I SKYE BA MI KHEGS NA, DON DAM PAR GRUB PA'I SKYE BA YANG MI KHEGS PAR BZHED PA NI RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PA TZAM NAS BDEN GRUB TU 'GYUR BAS, DE LA THA SNYAD DU ZHES SBYAR MA SBYAR 'DRA BAR BZHED PA'O,,
gru.wylie: de kho na nyid la dpyod pa'i rigs pas tha snyad du rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub pa'i skye ba mi khegs na, don dam par grub pa'i skye ba yang mi khegs par bzhed pa ni rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub pa tsam nas bden grub tu 'gyur bas, de la tha snyad du zhes sbyar ma sbyar 'dra bar bzhed pa'o
gru.english: Some would take the position that—if we cannot use reasoning which is examining the way things really are to deny a case of growing which exists by definition in a nominal sense—then neither could we deny a case of growing which exists ultimately. But taking this position is, then, to take the position that—since something exists in truth as soon as it exists by definition—it would be the same whether or not you went on to add the qualifier “in a nominal sense.”

gru.acip: DE LTA NA DON DAM PAR YOD PAR 'GYUR BA DANG, GZUGS SOGS KUN RDZOB PAR MI 'GYUR ZHES GZUGS SOGS DON DAM DU GRUB PAR KHAS MI LEN PA DANG, KUN RDZOB PAR 'JOG PA CIG LA 'PHEN LA, DE YANG DNGOS POR SMRA BA LA MIN PAS DBU MA RANG RGYUD PA YIN PAR SHIN TU GSAL LO,,
gru.wylie: de lta na don dam par yod par 'gyur ba dang, gzugs sogs kun rdzob par mi 'gyur zhes gzugs sogs don dam du grub par khas mi len pa dang, kun rdzob par 'jog pa cig la 'phen la, de yang dngos por smra ba la min pas dbu ma rang rgyud pa yin par shin tu gsal lo
gru.english: In this case what you're saying is that things do exist in an ultimate way, but that physical form and the like don't exist in a deceptive way. Which is to say, by implication, that there must be someone else who takes the position that form and the rest cannot exist in an ultimate way, and must then be said to exist in a deceptive way. And there is no one among the Functionalists who would fit this description; which means that it's very clear that you are referring to someone who belongs to the Independent group with in the Middle Way school.

gru.acip: 'DI YANG, DE LTAR 'GREL PA'I GTAN TSIGS MED PAR MI 'GRUB PAS, DE SKAD DU SMRA BA LA NI BRGAL ZHING BRTAG PAR BYA BA KHO NA'O, ZHES BSHAD PA'I PHYOGS SNGA SMRA BA NI, SNGA RABS PA KHA CIG SLOB DPON BLO BRTAN LA SOGS PA YIN PAR SMRA MOD KYANG, DE'I GZHUNG NA DE LTAR BSHAD PA MI SNANG NGO,,
gru.wylie: 'di yang, de ltar 'grel pa'i gtan tshigs med par mi 'grub pas, de skad du smra ba la ni brgal zhing brtag par bya ba kho na'o, zhes bshad pa'i phyogs snga smra ba ni, snga rabs pa kha cig slob dpon blo brtan la sogs pa yin par smra mod kyang, de'i gzhung na de ltar bshad pa mi snang ngo
gru.english: At this point, the autocommentary says that “since without a proper syllogism the point could not be made, making this statement is simple argumentation, and conjecture.” Now admitted that some thinkers of the earlier generation here in Tibet have expressed the opinion that the opponent in the argument here is Master Sthiramati, or someone like that; but I have not observed in his writings any such explanation.

gru.acip: SLOB DPON DBYIG GNYEN LA SOGS PA'I CHEN PO RNAMS KYI GZHUNG NA, KLU SGRUB KYI GZHUNG GI DON 'DI LTAR 'GREL PA YIN ZHES GSAL BAR MI SNANG YANG,
gru.wylie: slob dpon dbyig gnyen la sogs pa'i chen po rnams kyi gzhung na, klu sgrub kyi gzhung gi don 'di ltar 'grel pa yin zhes gsal bar mi snang yang
gru.english: Now it is not the case that we see clear references in the great books of great masters like Vasubandhu which interpret the import of Nagarjuna in this way.

gru.acip: 'ON KYANG CHOS THAMS CAD DON DAM PAR MA GRUB PA DANG, RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS MA GRUB PAR BSHAD PA RNAMS SGRA JI LTA BA BZHIN DU RIGS PAS 'GRUB PAS, SGRA JI BZHIN PA LA GNOD PA MED PA'I PHYIR, DRANG DON DU 'GREL MI NUS PA LA DGONGS NAS, BRGAL ZHING BRTAG PAR BYA BA KHO NA'O ZHES GSUNGS TE,
gru.wylie: 'on kyang chos thams cad don dam par ma grub pa dang, rang gi mtshan nyid kyis ma grub par bshad pa rnams sgra ji lta ba bzhin du rigs pas 'grub pas, sgra ji bzhin pa la gnod pa med pa'i phyir, drang don du 'grel mi nus pa la dgongs nas, brgal zhing brtag par bya ba kho na'o zhes gsungs te
gru.english: The fact though is that explanations which say that nothing in the universe exists in an ultimate way; and that nothing exists by definition; can be established, by correct reasoning, as being literal. Given this, people have thought that—since there is nothing to prevent us from taking the points literally—there is no way that we can explain them as being figurative. And thus we come up with statements like “this is simple argumentation, and conjecture.”

gru.acip: SGRA JI BZHIN PA'I BZLOG PHYOGS LA GNOD BYED DANG, DRANG THAD LA SGRUB BYED MTHA' YAS PA CIG STON PA NI, GZHUNG GI DON RNAM PA GZHAN DU DRANG DU MI RUNG BAR SGRUB PA YIN PAS 'DIR MDO TZAM LAS MA GSUNGS SO,,
gru.wylie: sgra ji bzhin pa'i bzlog phyogs la gnod byed dang, drang thad la sgrub byed mtha' yas pa cig ston pa ni, gzhung gi don rnam pa gzhan du drang du mi rung bar sgrub pa yin pas 'dir mdo tsam las ma gsungs so
gru.english: Once we present problems with doing the opposite of taking something as literal, and once we have offered innumerable arguments in support of leaving off taking them as figurative, then we have established that it would be incorrect to interpret the meaning of a text as referring to something other than what it says directly. As such, I have said no more than a tiny bit on the point here. Illusions in the world

gru.acip: GAL TE RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PA'I SKYE BA BDEN LA {%PA scan is wrong = LA} GNYIS CAR DU YANG MED NA, GZUGS LA SOGS PA RNAMS MED PAR 'GYUR LA, DE LTA NA GZUGS LA SOGS PA'I NGO BO MIG LA SOGS PA'I SHES PA LA 'JIG RTEN DU DMIGS PAR MI 'GYUR TE, DE LTA MA YIN NA RI BONG GI RVA LA SOGS PA YANG MIG LA SOGS PA'I SHES PA LA SNANG BAR 'GYUR TE, RGYU MTSAN KUN NAS MTSUNGS PA'I PHYIR RO ZHE NA,
gru.wylie: gal te rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub pa'i skye ba bden la {%pa ScaN iS wroNg = la} gnyis car du yang med na, gzugs la sogs pa rnams med par 'gyur la, de lta na gzugs la sogs pa'i ngo bo mig la sogs pa'i shes pa la 'jig rten du dmigs par mi 'gyur te, de lta ma yin na ri bong gi rva la sogs pa yang mig la sogs pa'i shes pa la snang bar 'gyur te, rgyu mtshan kun nas mtshungs pa'i phyir ro zhe na
gru.english: One may begin with the following question— Suppose then that it really is the case that a growing of things by definition exists with neither one of the two realities. In this case, physical form and the rest could would have to be non-existent. And in that case, then things that have the essential nature of form and the like could never be something that the awarenesses of the eye and such ever perceive, here in the everyday world. And if that were the case, then even things like rabbit horns could make their appearance to the awarenesses of the eye and the like. And that's because the reasoning would be equivalent, in every respect.

gru.acip: BRDZUN PA'I GZUGS BRNYAN LAS BRDZUN PA'I RNAM PA CAN GYI SHES PA SKYE BA DE BZHIN DU, DNGOS PO THAMS CAD RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PAS STONG NA'ANG, DES STONG PA'I RGYU DAG LAS DES STONG PA'I 'BRAS BU RAB TU SKYE BAR 'GYUR RO,,
gru.wylie: brdzun pa'i gzugs brnyan las brdzun pa'i rnam pa can gyi shes pa skye ba de bzhin du, dngos po thams cad rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub pas stong na'ang, des stong pa'i rgyu dag las des stong pa'i 'bras bu rab tu skye bar 'gyur ro
gru.english: Just as a type of awareness can grow which has assumed the false form of the reflection which is itself false, all the functioning things there are—even though they are empty of existing by definition—quite certainly grow, as results that are empty of that existence flowing from causes that are also empty of it.

gru.acip: DE LTAR NA DBANG SHES 'KHRUL PA LA SNANG BA'I BYAD DANG ZLA GNYIS DANG SKRA SHAD SOGS NI, DBANG PO LA 'PHRAL GYI GNOD PA MED PA'I SHES PA LNGA LA SNANG BA'I RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PA DANG 'DRA'O,,
gru.wylie: de ltar na dbang shes 'khrul pa la snang ba'i byad dang zla gnyis dang skra shad sogs ni, dbang po la 'phral gyi gnod pa med pa'i shes pa lnga la snang ba'i rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub pa dang 'dra'o
gru.english: And so what's being said here is that when our sense perceptions are mistaken, and an object which is actually just a reflection in the mirror appears to us—or we see things like the two moons, or a hair lying there—it is similar to the case with our five sense perceptions when they are not affected by any adventitious defect, but things appear to them to exist by definition.

gru.acip: BYAD BZHIN SOGS MI SRID KYANG DER SNANG BA NI RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PA NI {%carving: add also MI} SRID KYANG DER SNANG BA DANG 'DRA'O,,
gru.wylie: byad bzhin sogs mi srid kyang der snang ba ni rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub pa ni {%carviNg: aDD alSo mi} srid kyang der snang ba dang 'dra'o
gru.english: A reflection which is actually the object reflected is an impossibility; but it can seem as though it is. It is an impossibility for something to exist by definition; but it can seem as though it does—the cases are similar.

gru.acip: GZUGS BRNYAN DANG SGRA BRNYAN LA SOGS PA NI GZUGS DANG SGRA LA SOGS PA DANG 'DRA BAS, DES NA GZUGS SOGS LNGA RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA PHYI ROL TU MI 'JOG KYANG DER SNANG BA'I GZUGS SOGS PHYI ROL TU 'JOG PA BZHIN DU, GZUGS BRNYAN SOGS BYAD BZHIN YIN PA SOGS PHYI ROL TU MI 'JOG KYANG, GZUGS BRNYAN SOGS PHYI ROL TU 'JOG STE DE GNYIS PHYI ROL TU 'JOG MI 'JOG MTSUNGS PA YIN NO,,
gru.wylie: gzugs brnyan dang sgra brnyan la sogs pa ni gzugs dang sgra la sogs pa dang 'dra bas, des na gzugs sogs lnga rang bzhin gyis grub pa phyi rol tu mi 'jog kyang der snang ba'i gzugs sogs phyi rol tu 'jog pa bzhin du, gzugs brnyan sogs byad bzhin yin pa sogs phyi rol tu mi 'jog kyang, gzugs brnyan sogs phyi rol tu 'jog ste de gnyis phyi rol tu 'jog mi 'jog mtshungs pa yin no
gru.english: Reflections in a mirror, and echoes in a cave, and other such things are similar to actual visible forms, and sounds, and the like. As such, even though we do not say that visible forms and the other four exist as outside objects which exist through some nature of their own, we can say that the visible form and such which appear to be this way are on the outside. Similarly, we do not say that reflections and the like which are the actual image standing before the mirror and such exist on the outside; but we can say that the reflection and such themselves are on the outside—that is, the case here is the equivalent, when we are making the determination of whether these two are outside objects, or not.

gru.acip: GZUGS BRNYAN BYAD BZHIN GYIS STONG PA TZAM GYI BRDZUN PA NI, STONG NYID STON PA'I LUNG RIGS GANG LA YANG BLO KHA MA PHYOGS PA'I 'JIG RTEN PA'I RGAN PO BRDA BYANG THAMS CAD KYIS 'GRUB PAS, DE LTAR RTOGS PA DE RIGS SHES RAGS PA CIG TU 'DOD PA NI MI RIGS PA KHO NA'O,,
gru.wylie: gzugs brnyan byad bzhin gyis stong pa tsam gyi brdzun pa ni, stong nyid ston pa'i lung rigs gang la yang blo kha ma phyogs pa'i 'jig rten pa'i rgan po brda byang thams cad kyis 'grub pas, de ltar rtogs pa de rigs shes rags pa cig tu 'dod pa ni mi rigs pa kho na'o
gru.english: The concept of falseness in the form of a reflection in the mirror being simply empty of existing as the object standing in front of the mirror is something that even old geezers in the everyday world who understand the words we are using can establish as fact, without directing their minds in any way to forms of scripture and logic which present the concept of emptiness. As such, portraying this kind of understanding as a coarse version of logical thinking is simply in error.

gru.acip: GAL TE DE LTA NA NI GZUGS BRNYAN BRDZUN PAR GRAGS PA DE GRUB KYANG, DBU MA PAS BZHAG PA'I BRDZUN PAR MI 'GRUB PAS, SNGA MA DE PHYI MA'I DPER JI LTAR 'GYUR ZHE NA,
gru.wylie: gal te de lta na ni gzugs brnyan brdzun par grags pa de grub kyang, dbu ma pas bzhag pa'i brdzun par mi 'grub pas, snga ma de phyi ma'i dper ji ltar 'gyur zhe na
gru.english: One may come with the following question— If that's the way it is, and there really does exist a reflection which everyone admits is false, then it wouldn't be false in the same was as the those of the Middle Way school describe it. How then can you say that the former stands as an illustration of the latter?

gru.acip: SKABS 'DIR GZUGS BRNYAN SOGS DPER BKOD PA NI 'JIG RTEN PAS GRUB ZIN DPER 'GOD PA YIN GYI, DBU MA PAS BRDZUN PAR BZHAG PA GRUB ZIN PA CIG DPER 'GOD PA MIN NO,,
gru.wylie: skabs 'dir gzugs brnyan sogs dper bkod pa ni 'jig rten pas grub zin dper 'god pa yin gyi, dbu ma pas brdzun par bzhag pa grub zin pa cig dper 'god pa min no
gru.english: When we present the reflection in a mirror and so on as examples in this particular context, we are only putting them forth as instances which are already accepted in the everyday world. We are not putting them forth as examples of something which those of the Middle Way have already completed demonstrating as false.

gru.acip: BYAD BZHIN GYI GANG SNANG GI CHA THAMS CAD NAS SNANG BA LTAR DU YOD PAS STONG YANG, RANG GI RGYU LA BRTEN NAS SKYE BA MI 'GAL BA DPER BYAS NAS DE BZHIN DU SNGON PO RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PAR SNANG BA NA YANG, SNGON PO'I STENG NAS RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAR SNANG MI SNANG GI CHA GNYIS DBYER MED PAR SNANG LA,
gru.wylie: byad bzhin gyi gang snang gi cha thams cad nas snang ba ltar du yod pas stong yang, rang gi rgyu la brten nas skye ba mi 'gal ba dper byas nas de bzhin du sngon po rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub par snang ba na yang, sngon po'i steng nas rang bzhin gyis grub par snang mi snang gi cha gnyis dbyer med par snang la
gru.english: Rather, the reflection is appearing in a way where it is empty of existing as the object in front of the mirror in all of the parts of it which are making their appearance. And yet there is still no contradiction in saying that this reflection is growing through reliance upon its particular causes. And we can go ahead and use this as an illustration for describing how the color blue might act. That is, the blue may appear as though it exists by definition; but it appears this way in a manner where we could never divide out a part of the blue which is appearing as though it exists by definition, and another part which does not appear as though it exists by definition.

gru.acip: DE LTAR SNANG BA YANG GANG SNANG GI CHA THAMS CAD NAS SNANG BA LTAR DU YOD PAS STONG YANG, RANG GI RGYUS BSKYED PA DANG RANG GIS 'BRAS BU BSKYED PA MI 'GAL BAR SGRUB PA YIN TE,
gru.wylie: de ltar snang ba yang gang snang gi cha thams cad nas snang ba ltar du yod pas stong yang, rang gi rgyus bskyed pa dang rang gis 'bras bu bskyed pa mi 'gal bar sgrub pa yin te
gru.english: And even though the blue does appear this way, it is empty of actually being the way that it appears to be, in all of its various parts making such an appearance. Nonetheless, we have shown how it is no contradiction here to go further and say it has been produced by its causes; and is in turn producing its own results.

gru.acip: BYAD BZHIN KYI GZUGS BRNYAN LA DER GANG SNANG GI CHA THAMS CAD NAS SNANG BA LTAR DU MED KYANG GZUGS BRNYAN MED PAR MI 'GRO BA CIG 'JOG SHES NA, SNGON PO LA YANG RANG MTSAN GYIS GRUB PAR SNANG BA'I CHA THAMS CAD NAS SNANG BA LTAR GYI DON DU MED KYANG, SNGON PO YOD PAR NGES PAR 'JOG NUS PA CIG 'ONG NGO,,
gru.wylie: byad bzhin kyi gzugs brnyan la der gang snang gi cha thams cad nas snang ba ltar du med kyang gzugs brnyan med par mi 'gro ba cig 'jog shes na, sngon po la yang rang mtshan gyis grub par snang ba'i cha thams cad nas snang ba ltar gyi don du med kyang, sngon po yod par nges par 'jog nus pa cig 'ong ngo
gru.english: The reflection of an object in the mirror is not something which exists in the way it appears, in each and every one of the parts of it which appear to actually be that object. But this in no way requires us to say that there is no reflection there at all. If we understand how we can say all this, then in the case of the color blue as well we can say that it does not, in reality, exist in the way that it appears to exist, in any single one of the multiple parts of it which appear to exist by definition. At the same time though, there certainly does exist a color blue there; and we can in this way learn to establish that fact, with complete certainty.

gru.acip: GANG GI PHYIR DNGOS PO THAMS CAD GZUGS BRNYAN LTAR RANG BZHIN GYIS YOD PAS STONG PA DE NYID KYI PHYIR, DON DAM PA DANG KUN RDZOB BDEN PA GNYIS SU'AM GNYIS CAR DU'ANG RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA MED PA'I PHYIR, GZUGS SOGS DE DAG RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA'I RTAG PA MA YIN LA, DER MA ZAD CHAD PA'ANG MIN TE, CHAD PA NI MYUG TSE SA BON ZHIG PA MED PA'I SKABS SU BSHAD PA LTA BU'I CHAD PA DANG,
gru.wylie: gang gi phyir dngos po thams cad gzugs brnyan ltar rang bzhin gyis yod pas stong pa de nyid kyi phyir, don dam pa dang kun rdzob bden pa gnyis su'am gnyis car du'ang rang bzhin gyis grub pa med pa'i phyir, gzugs sogs de dag rang bzhin gyis grub pa'i rtag pa ma yin la, der ma zad chad pa'ang min te, chad pa ni myug tshe sa bon zhig pa med pa'i skabs su bshad pa lta bu'i chad pa dang
gru.english: Due to the fact that all entities are similar to reflections in a mirror, they are empty of existing through any nature of their own. And for this very reason, they can exist through a nature of their own neither with regard to ultimate reality, nor deceptive reality. And this then is why these things—physical form and the rest—are neither things that could last forever, and which exist by nature; nor things that could simply discontinue, in the same way. And when we say “discontinue” here, what we're referring to is a kind of discontinuation such as where a seed could ever not have ended at the time of its sprout.

gru.acip: ZHES DNGOS PO RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA KHAS BLANGS PAS SNGAR YOD KYI DNGOS PO PHYIS MED PA'AM, ZHIG PA'I MI RTAG PAR 'DOD NA'ANG CHAD LTAR 'GYUR TE, DNGOS PO RANG BZHIN GYIS YOD PAR KHAS LEN NA DE RTAG MI RTAG GANG DU 'DOD KYANG, RTAG CHAD KYI MTHAR LTUNG BA'I LTA BAR GSUNGS PA'I PHYIR RO,,
gru.wylie: zhes dngos po rang bzhin gyis grub pa khas blangs pas sngar yod kyi dngos po phyis med pa'am, zhig pa'i mi rtag par 'dod na'ang chad ltar 'gyur te, dngos po rang bzhin gyis yod par khas len na de rtag mi rtag gang du 'dod kyang, rtag chad kyi mthar ltung ba'i lta bar gsungs pa'i phyir ro
gru.english: What this refers to is where we accept that idea that things could exist through any nature of their own; and where something that was there before is not there afterwards—which is to say, it has stopped. This constitutes agreeing to the thing being changing; but it amounts to things simply discontinuing. Once you accept the idea that a thing could exist through any nature of its own, it doesn't matter whether you assert that it's unchanging or changing; you are still holding a viewpoint where you have fallen into the extremes of things lasting forever, or simply discontinuing altogether. This is what's being said in these lines.

gru.acip: 'DIR 'GREL PAR RTZA SHE LAS, STON PAS SPRUL PA ZHIG SPRUL LA NGES KYANG GZHAN ZHIG SPRUL PA DE BZHIN DU, BYED PA PO DANG LAS DANG DES BYAS PA RNAMS KYANG DE RNAMS DANG 'DRA BAR GSUNGS PAS, RANG BZHIN MED PA LAS RANG BZHIN MED PA RNAMS SKYE BAR BSTAN TO, ZHES GSUNGS PAS NI, RANG BZHIN GYIS MA GRUB PA LA BYA BYED THAMS CAD 'JOG PAS CHAD LTA MED PAR STON PA'O,,
gru.wylie: 'dir 'grel par rtsa she las, ston pas sprul pa zhig sprul la nges kyang gzhan zhig sprul pa de bzhin du, byed pa po dang las dang des byas pa rnams kyang de rnams dang 'dra bar gsungs pas, rang bzhin med pa las rang bzhin med pa rnams skye bar bstan to, zhes gsungs pas ni, rang bzhin gyis ma grub pa la bya byed thams cad 'jog pas chad lta med par ston pa'o
gru.english: At this point in the autocommentary they talk about how we can ascertain that the Teacher has sent out an emanation, but then that emanation can emanate yet another. And what it's saying is that the agent of an action; and the action itself; and what that does are similar. The wording here is “Things without any nature of their own grow from things with no nature of their own.” What these words are indicating is that—in a case where we establish the working of things while nothing exists through any nature of its own—we avoid the view that things could have simply discontinued.

gru.acip: 'DIR KUN RDZOB TU RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PA MA BKAG NA SHIN TU PHRA BA'I BDAG MED MI RTOGS PAS, SHIN TU PHRA BA'I RTAG CHAD KYI LTA BA RGYUD LA MI SKYE BA YANG BYA DKA' BAS, RTAG CHAD KYI LTA BA MA LUS PAR SPONG BA NI, DGAG BYA DE KUN RDZOB TU BKAG PA'I YON TAN NO,,
gru.wylie: 'dir kun rdzob tu rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub pa ma bkag na shin tu phra ba'i bdag med mi rtogs pas, shin tu phra ba'i rtag chad kyi lta ba rgyud la mi skye ba yang bya dka' bas, rtag chad kyi lta ba ma lus par spong ba ni, dgag bya de kun rdzob tu bkag pa'i yon tan no
gru.english: If we are unable to disprove the idea that—from a deceptive point of view—things could ever exist through some nature of their own, then we will never grasp the extremely subtle form of the lack of self-existence. It is an extremely difficult task to prevent the viewpoint of the extremely subtle forms of staying forever and simply discontinuing from growing within our mind; and it is one of the great features of blocking the object which we deny when we speak of no-self-nature even deceptively, when our goal is to eliminate, within ourselves, each and every case of the views that things could stay forever, or simply discontinue.

gru.acip: GNYIS PA LA GSUM, RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA MI 'DOD PA LA KUN GZHI SOGS KHAS BLANG MI DGOS PAR BSTAN PA DANG, LAS 'GAGS PA LAS 'BRAS BU 'BYUNG BA'I DPE BSTAN PA DANG, DE LTAR BSTAN PA LA RTZOD PA SPANG BA'O,,
gru.wylie: gnyis pa la gsum, rang bzhin gyis grub pa mi 'dod pa la kun gzhi sogs khas blang mi dgos par bstan pa dang, las 'gags pa las 'bras bu 'byung ba'i dpe bstan pa dang, de ltar bstan pa la rtsod pa spang ba'o
gru.english: Which brings us to our second point from above: The advantage of showing that the connection between karma and its consequences is eminently correct. Here we proceed in three steps: a demonstration that it is not the case that if we deny that things could exist through any nature of their own, we must then accept things like foundation consciousness; the presentation of a metaphor to illustrate how a karmic consequence can come from the karma itself having stopped; and then finally disproving any debate that may arise about this presentation.

gru.acip: ZHES RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PA THA SNYAD DU YANG MED PA'I PHYOGS LA RTAG CHAD KYI LTA BA RGYANG RING DU BSRINGS PA'I YON TAN YOD PAR MA ZAD KUN GZHI LA SOGS PA KHAS MA BLANGS KYANG LAS 'BRAS KYI 'BREL BA SHIN TU 'THAD PA'I YON TAN YOD PAR BSTAN NO,,
gru.wylie: zhes rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub pa tha snyad du yang med pa'i phyogs la rtag chad kyi lta ba rgyang ring du bsrings pa'i yon tan yod par ma zad kun gzhi la sogs pa khas ma blangs kyang las 'bras kyi 'brel ba shin tu 'thad pa'i yon tan yod par bstan no
gru.english: What this is saying is that—yes—with those who take the position that things cannot exist by definition, even nominally, there is that benefit that they are able to banish, to a great distance, the viewpoints either that things could last forever as they are, or else simply discontinue. But that's not all; there is also the benefit that the connection between karma and its consequences is, for them, something which is extremely correct, even if they refuse to accept concepts such as foundation consciousness, or the like.

gru.acip: 'PHAGS PA'I GZHUNG 'GREL TSUL LA RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PA RDUL TZAM MED KYANG, BYA BYED THAMS CAD BZHAG PAS CHOG PA'I 'GREL TSUL GYI LUGS THUN MONG MA YIN PA 'DI LA BRTEN NAS, RNAM PAR DAG PA'I GRUB MTHA' 'GREL BYED GZHAN DANG THUN MONG MA YIN PA MANG DU YOD DE,
gru.wylie: 'phags pa'i gzhung 'grel tshul la rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub pa rdul tsam med kyang, bya byed thams cad bzhag pas chog pa'i 'grel tshul gyi lugs thun mong ma yin pa 'di la brten nas, rnam par dag pa'i grub mtha' 'grel byed gzhan dang thun mong ma yin pa mang du yod de
gru.english: As far as commenting upon the classic of the Realized One, this is a truly unique way of doing it; where we say that—even though there does not exist even the tiniest bit of anything which could ever exist by definition—still we can go ahead and posit the entire system in which things do what they do. And based upon this kind of presentation, there are many other points here that are not held in common even with other commentators who belong to quite accurate schools of thought.

gru.acip: DE'I DANG PO NI SKABS 'DIR BSTAN LA, RANG RIG KHAS MI LEN PA RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA MI 'DOD PA LA THUG TSUL NI 'CHAD PAR 'GYUR RO,,
gru.wylie: de'i dang po ni skabs 'dir bstan la, rang rig khas mi len pa rang bzhin gyis grub pa mi 'dod pa la thug tshul ni 'chad par 'gyur ro
gru.english: The first of all these is presented at this juncture; and we will go on to explain how our refusal to accept apperception stems from our denial that things could exist through any nature of their own.

gru.acip: PHYI ROL KHAS LEN PA 'DI LA THUG PA NI 'CHAD PAR 'GYUR LA, LNGA PA YANG 'DI LA THUG TSUL NI SANGS RGYAS BSKYANGS KYIS NYAN THOS KYI SDE SNOD LAS CHOS THAMS CAD BDAG MED DO ZHES GSUNGS PA'I MED RGYU'I BDAG NI, NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB PA LA BSHAD PA LTAR 'DIR YANG BZHED DE, DE YANG BDAG MED MTSAN NYID RDZOGS PA'I DON NO,,
gru.wylie: phyi rol khas len pa 'di la thug pa ni 'chad par 'gyur la, lnga pa yang 'di la thug tshul ni sangs rgyas bskyangs kyis nyan thos kyi sde snod las chos thams cad bdag med do zhes gsungs pa'i med rgyu'i bdag ni, ngo bo nyid kyis grub pa la bshad pa ltar 'dir yang bzhed de, de yang bdag med mtshan nyid rdzogs pa'i don no
gru.english: The way in which our accepting the existence of outside objects comes down to this is something we will be explaining. The fifth point also comes down to this same concept; Master Buddha Palita has made that reference to “the lack of a self-nature to all things, covered in the collections of the listeners.” The self-nature lacking here is explained as referring to things existing through some essence of their own; and that idea is accepted here as well. This is moreover the point of saying that things have no self-nature; it describes this concept definitively.

gru.acip: DE'I PHYIR GANG ZAG GI BDAG MED MTSAN NYID RDZOGS PA YANG GANG ZAG RANG GI NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB PA MED PA LA BYA DGOS LA, DE JI BZHIN DU RTOGS PA LA NI CHOS KYI BDAG MED JI BZHIN PA YANG RTOGS DGOS PA'I GNAD DO,,
gru.wylie: de'i phyir gang zag gi bdag med mtshan nyid rdzogs pa yang gang zag rang gi ngo bo nyid kyis grub pa med pa la bya dgos la, de ji bzhin du rtogs pa la ni chos kyi bdag med ji bzhin pa yang rtogs dgos pa'i gnad do
gru.english: Therefore when you describe the lack of a self-nature to the person in its definitive form, you have to tie it to how the person cannot exist through any essential nature of their own. And the crucial point here is that you have to understand how to describe the lack of a self-nature to things in the same way that you have grasped that other fact.

gru.acip: DE LTA NA LAM DES CHOS KYI BDAG 'DZIN KUN BRTAGS MTHONG LAM NAS SPONG BA DANG, BDAG 'DZIN DE LHAN SKYES, DE'I SGOM LAM NAS KYANG SPONG BA 'DOD DGOS PAS, DNGOS PO RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PAR 'DZIN PA'I DBU MA PA'I LUGS LA YANG CHOS KYI BDAG 'DZIN LA NYON MONGS CAN YIN MIN GNYIS 'DOD DAM SNYAM NA,
gru.wylie: de lta na lam des chos kyi bdag 'dzin kun brtags mthong lam nas spong ba dang, bdag 'dzin de lhan skyes, de'i sgom lam nas kyang spong ba 'dod dgos pas, dngos po rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub par 'dzin pa'i dbu ma pa'i lugs la yang chos kyi bdag 'dzin la nyon mongs can yin min gnyis 'dod dam snyam na
gru.english: One might wonder about something here. In such a case, we would have to agree that a person could use this particular path to eliminate the learned form of grasping to a self-nature to things at the point of the path of seeing; and then could eliminate the innate form of grasping to this self-nature at the point of the path of habituation. Wouldn't it then be the case that—in systems of the Middle Way which hold that functional things exist by definition, as well—there would be both a belief that the tendency to hold to a self-nature of things was wrapped up with negative thoughts, and a belief that it was not?

gru.acip: DNGOS PO RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA MED PAR 'DOD PA'I PHYOGS LA, KUN GZHI SOGS KHAS MA BLANGS KYANG LAS 'BRAS KYI 'BREL PA 'THAD TSUL JI LTAR YIN ZHE NA,
gru.wylie: dngos po rang bzhin gyis grub pa med par 'dod pa'i phyogs la, kun gzhi sogs khas ma blangs kyang las 'bras kyi 'brel pa 'thad tshul ji ltar yin zhe na
gru.english: One may begin with the following question: Just how is it—in the case of those who assert that there is nothing at all which exists through any nature of its own—that we can we can say that the connection between karma and its consequences is all perfectly acceptable, even without accepting concepts such as foundation consciousness?

gru.acip: DE RNAMS KYI DON NI SNGAR BZHIN BRTZAD PA'I LAN SMRA BA PO BZHI GAS KYANG, LAS LA SKYE BA DANG 'GAG PA RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PA KHAS LEN ZHING, LAS BYAS PA'I 'OG TU 'GAGS PA DE RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAR 'DOD DO,,
gru.wylie: de rnams kyi don ni sngar bzhin brtsad pa'i lan smra ba po bzhi gas kyang, las la skye ba dang 'gag pa rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub pa khas len zhing, las byas pa'i 'og tu 'gags pa de rang bzhin gyis grub par 'dod do
gru.english: The import of all these points is to provide an answer to the arguments presented earlier, as all four presenters here accept the idea that karma can start & stop, by definition; and that when karma stops after we have committed it, this is something which occurs by nature.

gru.acip: DE LA SLOB DPON 'DIS DE 'DRA BA'I 'GAGS PA YIN KYANG KUN GZHI SOGS KHAS LEN PAS SKYON MED CES LAN 'DEBS PA MI RIGS TE, RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA'I TSUL GYIS LAS SKYE BA DANG 'GAGS PA MED PA'I PHYIR RO ZHES 'GOG PA YIN NO,,
gru.wylie: de la slob dpon 'dis de 'dra ba'i 'gags pa yin kyang kun gzhi sogs khas len pas skyon med ces lan 'debs pa mi rigs te, rang bzhin gyis grub pa'i tshul gyis las skye ba dang 'gags pa med pa'i phyir ro zhes 'gog pa yin no
gru.english: And what this master is saying here is that it would be wrong to reply, at this point, that—even though it is true that the stopping of the karma is happening the way it was described—nonetheless there is no problem, since we accept concepts such as foundation consciousness and the like. That is, he is denying that there could exist any such thing as karma starting and stopping in a way where things existed through some nature of their own.

gru.acip: LAN 'DEBS TSUL DE NYID 'PHAGS PA'I BZHED PA YIN PAR STON PA LA, ,GANG PHYIR LAS NI SKYE BA MED, ,'DI LTAR RANG BZHIN MED DE'I PHYIR, ,GANG PHYIR DE NI MA SKYES PA, ,DE PHYIR CHUD ZAR MI 'GYUR RO, ZHES RTZA SHER GSUNGS PA DRANGS TE, LAS RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA MED PA'I PHYIR RANG GI BDAG NYID KYIS SKYE BA MED DO,,
gru.wylie: lan 'debs tshul de nyid 'phags pa'i bzhed pa yin par ston pa la, ,gang phyir las ni skye ba med, ,'di ltar rang bzhin med de'i phyir, ,gang phyir de ni ma skyes pa, ,de phyir chud zar mi 'gyur ro, zhes rtsa sher gsungs pa drangs te, las rang bzhin gyis grub pa med pa'i phyir rang gi bdag nyid kyis skye ba med do
gru.english: In order to show that this exact way of responding reflects the viewpoint of the Realized One, our master at this point cites the following lines from Wisdom: Karma never starts; And for this reason, It has, as we have seen, No nature of its own. And for the reason too That it never started, It can never be that it Simply fades away. What this is saying is that—because there is no such thing as karma which exists through some nature of its own—there is no such thing as karma which starts in and of itself.

gru.acip: DE'I PHYIR LAS RANG BZHIN GYIS 'GAG PA MI SRID PA'I PHYIR, LAS BYAS PA'I 'OG TU 'GAGS PA DE RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAR BZUNG NAS CHUD MI ZA BAR RTOG PA RIGS PA MIN NO, ZHES PA'I DON NO,,
gru.wylie: de'i phyir las rang bzhin gyis 'gag pa mi srid pa'i phyir, las byas pa'i 'og tu 'gags pa de rang bzhin gyis grub par bzung nas chud mi za bar rtog pa rigs pa min no, zhes pa'i don no
gru.english: As such—for the reason that it is impossible for karma to come to a stop through some nature of its own—what's being said here is that it's illogical to imagine that karma never just fades away, if you are still holding that the stopping of karma subsequent to its commission is something that does exist through some nature of its own.

gru.acip: YANG MDO LAS, ,MI YI TSE TSAD LO BRGYA STE, ,DE SRID 'TSO ZHES BRJOD MOD KYI, ,LO LA PHUNG POR SPUNGS PA MED, ,SGRUB PA DE YANG DE DANG MTSUNGS, ,ZAD PA MED CES GANG SMRAS DANG, ,LAS ZAD CES NI GANG SMRAS PA, ,STONG PA'I TSUL DU ZAD PA MED, ,THA SNYAD TSUL DU ZAD PAR BSTAN,
gru.wylie: yang mdo las, ,mi yi tshe tshad lo brgya ste, ,de srid 'tsho zhes brjod mod kyi, ,lo la phung por spungs pa med, ,sgrub pa de yang de dang mtshungs, ,zad pa med ces gang smras dang, ,las zad ces ni gang smras pa, ,stong pa'i tshul du zad pa med, ,tha snyad tshul du zad par bstan
gru.english: We can quote the following sutra— The span of a human life May be a hundred years, And people may talk about Staying alive for that long; But years are not things That you can pile upon each other; And doing practice Is something the same as that. When it was said that There was no ending, And when they said That karma did end, It was in the sense of emptiness That there was no ending; And in the sense of expression That things were said to end.

gru.acip: ZHES GSUNGS PA DRANGS TE, RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA'I ZAD PA'AM 'GAG PA MED PA DANG, DE GNYIS THA SNYAD KYI DBANG GIS BZHAG PA'I KHUNGS SO,,
gru.wylie: zhes gsungs pa drangs te, rang bzhin gyis grub pa'i zad pa'am 'gag pa med pa dang, de gnyis tha snyad kyi dbang gis bzhag pa'i khungs so
gru.english: This is a source for saying that there is no such thing as an ending, or a stopping, which could exist through any nature of its own; and for saying that these two are established nominally.

gru.acip: DANG PO NI, GAL TE RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA'I 'GAG PA MED KYANG RANG GI LUGS LA YANG LA LAR LAS 'GAGS ZHES DANG, 'GAGS SHING RANG BZHIN YOD MIN PA'I, ZHES GSUNGS PAS, THA SNYAD TSUL DU ZAD PAR BSTAN, ZHES PA LTAR
gru.wylie: dang po ni, gal te rang bzhin gyis grub pa'i 'gag pa med kyang rang gi lugs la yang la lar las 'gags zhes dang, 'gags shing rang bzhin yod min pa'i, zhes gsungs pas, tha snyad tshul du zad par bstan, zhes pa ltar
gru.english: Here is the first. One may begin with the following question— Now in your presentation, you say that even though there is no such thing as the karma stopping through some nature of its own, nonetheless “In particular ones, karma can stop,” and one “which is not something that exists with any nature of its own can stop.” And thus you have quoted “In the sense of expression, things were said to end.”

gru.acip: SKYON MED DE, GANG PHYIR RANG BZHIN GYIS DE MI 'GAG PA, DE PHYIR ZHES PA'I RGYU MTSAN NYID KYIS LAS ZHIG PA'I ZHIG PA LAS PHYIS KYI 'BRAS BU 'BYUNG BA 'GRUB PAS LAN ZUR PA MA GSUNGS SO,,
gru.wylie: skyon med de, gang phyir rang bzhin gyis de mi 'gag pa, de phyir zhes pa'i rgyu mtshan nyid kyis las zhig pa'i zhig pa las phyis kyi 'bras bu 'byung ba 'grub pas lan zur pa ma gsungs so
gru.english: And yet there is no such problem. Remember, “For the reason that it never stopped through any nature of its own; and for that reason too.” This is expressing the very reason why we can say that—from the stopping of a karma which has stopped—a later result can be given forth; as such, no further, separate reason is offered.

gru.acip: DE YANG DNGOS PO RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAR 'DOD PA'I PHYOGS THAMS CAD LA, ZHIG PA DNGOS POR MI RUNG LA RANG BZHIN GYIS MA GRUB PAR 'DOD PA'I DBU MA'I PHYOGS LA ZHIG PA DNGOS POR GRUB PA'I GNAD DO,,
gru.wylie: de yang dngos po rang bzhin gyis grub par 'dod pa'i phyogs thams cad la, zhig pa dngos por mi rung la rang bzhin gyis ma grub par 'dod pa'i dbu ma'i phyogs la zhig pa dngos por grub pa'i gnad do
gru.english: Beyond that—according to the views of all those groups which accept the idea that a functional object could exist through some nature of its own—it would be incorrect to say that the stopping could itself be a functional thing; whereas according to the views of the followers of the Middle Way school, the stopping itself is proved to be a functional thing. This is the crucial point here.

gru.acip: DE SGRUB PA LA LUNG RIGS GNYIS TSIG GSAL LAS GSUNGS PA'I DANG PO NI,
gru.wylie: de sgrub pa la lung rigs gnyis tshig gsal las gsungs pa'i dang po ni
gru.english: A Clarification of the Verses presents both scriptural reasoning and logical support which corroborate this position; let's speak about the first.

gru.acip: SGRUB BYED LHAG MA NI RGYAS PAR RTZA SHE'I t'IKKA LAS SHES PAR BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: sgrub byed lhag ma ni rgyas par rtsa she'i TIkka las shes par bya'o
gru.english: The remaining logical argument in support of this idea is something that you can learn by studying the commentary on Wisdom.
