gru.acip: LAN DE DAG KYANG BDAG 'DRA BAS LUGS CHEN PO RNAMS LA RANG STOBS KYIS BRJOD PAR GA LA NUS, 'ON KYANG MGON PO KLU SGRUB KYI DGONGS PA JI LTA BA BZHIN DU RDZOGS PAR 'JOG SHES PA'I SHING RTA CHEN PO DAG GI LUGS LA BRTEN NAS SMRAS PA YIN NO,,
gru.wylie: lan de dag kyang bdag 'dra bas lugs chen po rnams la rang stobs kyis brjod par ga la nus, 'on kyang mgon po klu sgrub kyi dgongs pa ji lta ba bzhin du rdzogs par 'jog shes pa'i shing rta chen po dag gi lugs la brten nas smras pa yin no
gru.english: As for these responses, how could anyone like me ever display my own capacity to speak to the positions of the great ones? I have though made my comments here relying upon the system of those magnificent innovators who possess themselves the knowledge of how to set forth, in their entirety, positions which represent the true intent of our Savior, Nagarjuna.

gru.acip: DE RNAMS LA DPAGS NA KUN GZHI SGRUB PA'I RIGS PA LHAG MA RNAMS KYIS KYANG LUGS 'DI LA MI GNOD PAR MNGON TE, BLO GROS CHE ZHING ZHIB LA RNO BA RNAMS KYIS RTZAD GCAD PAR BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: de rnams la dpags na kun gzhi sgrub pa'i rigs pa lhag ma rnams kyis kyang lugs 'di la mi gnod par mngon te, blo gros che zhing zhib la rno ba rnams kyis rtsad gcad par bya'o
gru.english: It would seem that we can extrapolate from the points we have covered here what we need to show that remaining arguments in favor of a foundation consciousness in no way challenge the present system; and so those of you who possess a great degree of understanding—a detailed degree, and sharp—can go ahead and dissect those accordingly. Karma in a dream

gru.acip: LAS BYAS MA THAG TU 'GAGS PA NI THA SNYAD DU DANG, LHAG MAS NI 'GAG PA NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB PA BKAG GO
gru.wylie: las byas ma thag tu 'gags pa ni tha snyad du dang, lhag mas ni 'gag pa ngo bo nyid kyis grub pa bkag go
gru.english: When the sutra mentions karma stopping just after its commission, this is meant in a nominal sense. And then the remainder is denying that the stopping could occur through some essential nature of its own.

gru.acip: DE BZHIN DU LAS RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA MIN PAR MTSUNGS BZHIN DU, SMIN MA ZIN PA LAS SMIN PA DANG, SMIN ZIN PA LAS SLAR YANG SMIN PA MIN PAR SHES PAR GYIS SHIG
gru.wylie: de bzhin du las rang bzhin gyis grub pa min par mtshungs bzhin du, smin ma zin pa las smin pa dang, smin zin pa las slar yang smin pa min par shes par gyis shig
gru.english: Similarly, karma is equivalent in that it is not something which can exist through any nature of its own. You should understand that—when the karma has not yet ripened—it can go on to ripen; but it's not as if karma which has already ripened is going to go ahead and ripen once again.

gru.acip: ,DPE 'DI LAS LAS RNAMS KYI 'BRAS BU NGES PAR 'GRUB PA 'BA' ZHIG TU MA ZAD KYI, DGE MI DGE'I LAS LAS YID DU 'ONG MI 'ONG GI 'BRAS BU YANG SO SOR NGES SO ZHES BSHAD PA,
gru.wylie: dpe 'di las las rnams kyi 'bras bu nges par 'grub pa 'ba' zhig tu ma zad kyi, dge mi dge'i las las yid du 'ong mi 'ong gi 'bras bu yang so sor nges so zhes bshad pa
gru.english: This example serves not only to inform us about how consequences come, with certainty, from karma. Rather, we also hear about how either pleasant or unpleasant consequences respectively come, with certainty, from virtuous and non-virtuous karma.

gru.acip: DGE BA DANG MI DGE BA'I LAS MED PA'I BLO CAN TE RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA MI DMIGS PAR RTOGS PA NI 'KHOR BA LAS THAR BAR 'GYUR RO,,
gru.wylie: dge ba dang mi dge ba'i las med pa'i blo can te rang bzhin gyis grub pa mi dmigs par rtogs pa ni 'khor ba las thar bar 'gyur ro
gru.english: And also, those intelligent ones who understand that there exists no virtuous karma, nor non-virtuous karma—that is, those who realize that it is an impossibility for karma to exist through any nature of its own—come to be freed from the cycle of suffering.

gru.acip: DE'I PHYIR RGYAL BAS SO SO SKYE BO LAS KYI KHYAD PAR 'DI DANG 'DI LAS 'BRAS BU'I KHYAD PAR 'DI DANG 'DI 'BYUNG BA'I RGYU MTSAN 'THAD SGRUB KYI RIGS PAS ZHIB PAR NGES PAR DPYOD PAR BYED PA RNAMS LA, LAS DANG 'BRAS BU LA SKUR PA BTAB PA LAS KUN RDZOB 'JIG PAR 'GYUR DU 'ONG SNYAM STE, LAS RNAMS KYI 'BRAS BU RNAM PAR SMIN PA NI BSAM GYIS MI KHYAB BO, ZHES LAS DANG 'BRAS BU RNAMS LA BRTEN PA'I SEMS PA STE DPYAD PA'ANG DGAG PAR MDZAD DO,,
gru.wylie: de'i phyir rgyal bas so so skye bo las kyi khyad par 'di dang 'di las 'bras bu'i khyad par 'di dang 'di 'byung ba'i rgyu mtshan 'thad sgrub kyi rigs pas zhib par nges par dpyod par byed pa rnams la, las dang 'bras bu la skur pa btab pa las kun rdzob 'jig par 'gyur du 'ong snyam ste, las rnams kyi 'bras bu rnam par smin pa ni bsam gyis mi khyab bo, zhes las dang 'bras bu rnams la brten pa'i sems pa ste dpyad pa'ang dgag par mdzad do
gru.english: And so the Victors have undertaken to prove the correctness of karma to common beings, with reasons such as “You will get this or that particular kind of consequence from committing this or that particular karma”; for they know that, on a conventional level, it will be the destruction of these individuals if they discount the laws of karma & its consequences. And so they undertake to prevent these types of people from overthinking things—from overanalyzing them—with regard to the laws of karma & its consequences; they tell them, “Oh, the way that consequences ripen from karma is simply inconceivable.”

gru.acip: GANG LA DGONGS NAS GSUNGS PA'I DGONGS GZHI NI, RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAS STONG PA'I STONG PA NYID KHO NA LA DGONGS NAS, KUN GZHI RNAM SHES KYI SGRAS BSTAN PAR RIG PAR BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: gang la dgongs nas gsungs pa'i dgongs gzhi ni, rang bzhin gyis grub pas stong pa'i stong pa nyid kho na la dgongs nas, kun gzhi rnam shes kyi sgras bstan par rig par bya'o
gru.english: What is it our real intention to say, when we make such references? What we only ever intend to refer to with these statements is emptiness: the fact that existence is devoid of anything that could exist through some nature of its own. You should understand then that we are only using the expression “foundation consciousness” to say this very thing.

gru.acip: ,CES GSUNGS PA LTAR CHOS NYID THOG MAR BSTAN PA NA SKRAG NAS, SANGS RGYAS KYI BSTAN PA LA G-YANG SA DANG 'DRA BAR SEMS PA DE DAG BSTAN PA LA RGYAB KYIS PHYOGS SHING MI 'JUG PAS DON CHEN PO SGRUB PAR MI 'GYUR RO,,
gru.wylie: ces gsungs pa ltar chos nyid thog mar bstan pa na skrag nas, sangs rgyas kyi bstan pa la g-yang sa dang 'dra bar sems pa de dag bstan pa la rgyab kyis phyogs shing mi 'jug pas don chen po sgrub par mi 'gyur ro
gru.english: As this is pointing out, people will be terrified if—from the very beginning—we teach them the true nature of things. They will perceive the teachings of the Buddha as if they were a high cliff that a person might fall from. And then they turn away from those teachings, and refuse to enter into them. As such there is no great meaning thus served.

gru.acip: THEG BSDUS SU KUN GZHI RNAM SHES KYI SGRUB BYED DU DRANGS PA'I CHOS MNGON PA'I LUNG, RGYUD BLA MA'I 'GREL PA LAS, SEMS CAN LA DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA'I KHAMS GRUB PA SNYING POR GYUR PA YOD MOD KYI, SEMS CAN DE DAG GIS SHES PA MA YIN NO, ZHES GSUNGS SO,,
gru.wylie: theg bsdus su kun gzhi rnam shes kyi sgrub byed du drangs pa'i chos mngon pa'i lung, rgyud bla ma'i 'grel pa las, sems can la de bzhin gshegs pa'i khams grub pa snying por gyur pa yod mod kyi, sems can de dag gis shes pa ma yin no, zhes gsungs so
gru.english: In A Compendium of the Greater Way, we do see citations from teachings on higher knowledge used in support of the idea of foundation consciousness. And in the commentary to The Higher Line we read: It is said that, admittedly, living beings do possess what is the essence of attainment, the element of the Ones Gone Thus; but it is not something that they are even aware of.

gru.acip: DE SKAD DU, ,THOG MA MED PA'I DUS KYI KHAMS, ,CHOS RNAMS KUN GYI GNAS YIN TE, ,DE YOD PAS NA 'GRO KUN DANG, ,MYA NGAN 'DAS PA'ANG THOB PA YIN, ZHES SEMS CAN LA CHOS NYID KYI RIGS YOD PA'I SGRUB BYED DU DRANGS PAS,
gru.wylie: de skad du, ,thog ma med pa'i dus kyi khams, ,chos rnams kun gyi gnas yin te, ,de yod pas na 'gro kun dang, ,mya ngan 'das pa'ang thob pa yin, zhes sems can la chos nyid kyi rigs yod pa'i sgrub byed du drangs pas
gru.english: We also see the following lines quoted in support of the idea that living beings do possess the nature of the very essence of all things: It is an element That has been there For time with no beginning; It is a place Of all the things there are; Because it is here, We have all the different Types of beings, And can attain nirvana As well.

gru.acip: DE NI SEMS LAS DON GZHAN PA'I PHYI ROL BKAG NAS SEMS TZAM ZHIG RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA MA BKAG PA'I SEMS TZAM GSUNGS PA NI, BYIS PA THAMS CAD STONG PAR BSTAN PA LA SKRAG PA SPANG BA'I PHYIR YIN GYI, NGES DON GYI DE NYID MIN PA DANG,
gru.wylie: de ni sems las don gzhan pa'i phyi rol bkag nas sems tsam zhig rang bzhin gyis grub pa ma bkag pa'i sems tsam gsungs pa ni, byis pa thams cad stong par bstan pa la skrag pa spang ba'i phyir yin gyi, nges don gyi de nyid min pa dang
gru.english: Let's consider this statement, where we talk about a way in which things are mind only, in the sense of denying that there could exist external objects that were not part & parcel with the mind itself. This description is made only with the intention of avoiding any panic that infants might feel when we describe emptiness; it is not though describing a nature of things which is meant to be taken literally.

gru.acip: RNAL 'BYOR SPYOD PA BA RNAMS KYIS GNAS GYUR PA'I SEMS KYI DAG PA RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA CIG, SO SO RANG GIS RIG PA'I SPYOD YUL DU GRUB PA KHAS BLANGS PA BKAG PA'I TSE,
gru.wylie: rnal 'byor spyod pa ba rnams kyis gnas gyur pa'i sems kyi dag pa rang bzhin gyis grub pa cig, so so rang gis rig pa'i spyod yul du grub pa khas blangs pa bkag pa'i tshe
gru.english: Let's consider the point at which we deny the position of those who belong to the school of deep practice, as they assert an adventitious purity of the mind which could exist through some nature of its own, and which could serve as the sphere of activity for the state of mind which could perceive itself, in the same moment that it perceives other objects.

gru.acip: LCAGS DANG SHING LA SEMS MED KYANG YOD PA LTAR G-YO BA BZHIN DU, KUN GZHI BDEN PAR MED KYANG BDEN PAR YOD PA LTAR 'GRO 'ONG GI G-YO BA DANG BCAS PAR SNANG NGO, ZHES STON PA YIN PAS GZHUNG GZHAN NAS BSHAD PA LTAR GYI KUN GZHI RNAM SHES RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PA KHAS LEN PA NI MIN NO,,
gru.wylie: lcags dang shing la sems med kyang yod pa ltar g-yo ba bzhin du, kun gzhi bden par med kyang bden par yod pa ltar 'gro 'ong gi g-yo ba dang bcas par snang ngo, zhes ston pa yin pas gzhung gzhan nas bshad pa ltar gyi kun gzhi rnam shes rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub pa khas len pa ni min no
gru.english: And then what's being indicated here is that—even though foundation consciousness is not something that exists in truth—it can appear to be involved with the shifts of going & coming as if it did exist in truth; it's just like the way that the iron or a tree could shift here & there, as if they had a mind, despite the fact that they do not. As such, it is not that in this case a kind of foundation consciousness is—as we see it described in other texts—being accepted as existing by definition.

gru.acip: GAL TE KUN GZHI RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PAR KHAS MI LEN KYANG, TSOGS DRUG LAS NGO BO THA DAD PA'I SGYU MA LTA BU KUN BYANG GI CHOS KUN GYI SA BON THAMS CAD PA KHAS LEN NO SNYAM NA,
gru.wylie: gal te kun gzhi rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub par khas mi len kyang, tshogs drug las ngo bo tha dad pa'i sgyu ma lta bu kun byang gi chos kun gyi sa bon thams cad pa khas len no snyam na
gru.english: Which may lead one to the following thought— Even if it is the case that foundation consciousness is not being accepted here as something which could exist by definition, don't we still accept it as something that is essentially separate from the combination of six kinds of consciousness; as being like an illusion; and as the combination of all the seeds there are?

gru.acip: SEMS SPYI TZAM RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA BKAG PA'I LAN DU, SEMS BDEN PAR MED PA LA BYA BYED RUNG BA'I TSUL YIN PA'I PHYIR DANG, SRID PAR SKYE BA 'DZIN PA'I SEMS YID SHES YIN PA'I PHYIR DANG, YID KYI SHES PA NI KUN NAS NYON MONGS DANG RNAM BYANG THAMS CAD KYI GZHI YIN PA'I PHYIR RO,,
gru.wylie: sems spyi tsam rang bzhin gyis grub pa bkag pa'i lan du, sems bden par med pa la bya byed rung ba'i tshul yin pa'i phyir dang, srid par skye ba 'dzin pa'i sems yid shes yin pa'i phyir dang, yid kyi shes pa ni kun nas nyon mongs dang rnam byang thams cad kyi gzhi yin pa'i phyir ro
gru.english: That is, as we reply by denying that the mind in general could exist through any nature of its own, we are describing a way in which all the workings of things is something completely consistent with the idea of a mind which cannot exist in truth; and where the mind that takes a new birth in the cycle of pain is our awareness of our thoughts; and how our awareness of our thoughts is the foundation of everything there is, in both the side of life which is entirely negative, and the side which is totally enlightened.

gru.acip: SANGS RGYAS BCOM LDAN 'DAS KYIS NGA DANG NGA YI ZHES JI SKAD BSTAN PA DE BZHIN DU, DNGOS PO RNAMS RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA MED MOD KYI STE KYANG, RANG BZHIN GYIS YOD CES DRANG DON NYID DU BSTAN PA NI, 'JIG RTEN GYI RIM GYIS DE KHO NA NYID KHONG DU CHUD PA'I THABS YIN NO,,
gru.wylie: sangs rgyas bcom ldan 'das kyis nga dang nga yi zhes ji skad bstan pa de bzhin du, dngos po rnams rang bzhin gyis grub pa med mod kyi ste kyang, rang bzhin gyis yod ces drang don nyid du bstan pa ni, 'jig rten gyi rim gyis de kho na nyid khong du chud pa'i thabs yin no
gru.english: As such, the Conqueror—the Buddha—did give teachings using the expressions “me” and “mine.” It's a similar case with the way in which things admittedly have no manner of existing though some nature of their own, and yet only in a figurative sense it was stated that things did exist through just such a nature. It was only meant as a stratagem for getting those of the world to begin to grasp, very gradually, the way things really are.

gru.acip: BZHIN DU CHOS RNAMS RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAR STON PA DE SANGS RGYAS KYI DGONGS PA LTAR SNANG YANG CHOS RNAMS DE LTAR MED PA DE NGES PA'I DON NO ZHES PA'O,,
gru.wylie: bzhin du chos rnams rang bzhin gyis grub par ston pa de sangs rgyas kyi dgongs pa ltar snang yang chos rnams de ltar med pa de nges pa'i don no zhes pa'o
gru.english: In the same way, it would appear that Lord Buddha's intention was to indicate that things existed through some nature of their own; but what he really meant to say was that things didn't exist that way at all.

gru.acip: GNYIS PA SEMS TZAM PA'I LUGS BYE BRAG TU DGAG PA LA GSUM, PHYI ROL MED PA'I SHES PA RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA DGAG ,GZHAN DBANG RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA'I SGRUB BYED TSAD MA DGAG ,SEMS TZAM DU GSUNGS PA'I TZAM GYI SGRAS PHYI DON 'GOG PA MIN PAR BSTAN PA'O,,
gru.wylie: gnyis pa sems tsam pa'i lugs bye brag tu dgag pa la gsum, phyi rol med pa'i shes pa rang bzhin gyis grub pa dgag ,gzhan dbang rang bzhin gyis grub pa'i sgrub byed tshad ma dgag ,sems tsam du gsungs pa'i tsam gyi sgras phyi don 'gog pa min par bstan pa'o
gru.english: This brings us, at last, to the second section in showing how we disprove the position that things can grow from something other than themselves; that is, a more specific denial of this point by the Mind Only school. Here we have three parts: a denial that the understanding that there are no outer objects could ever exist through some nature of its own; denying the accurate perception which is supposed to prove that dominated things exist through some nature of their own; and a demonstration that the word “only” in the expression “Mind Only” is not meant to deny outer objects.

gru.acip: RTEN 'BREL MDO 'GREL DU, KUN GZHI RNAMS KYI RKYEN GYIS MING GZUGS 'GRUB PAR BSHAD PA'I MING PHUNG PO LHAG MA BZHI DANG, GZUGS 'BYUNG BA 'BYUNG 'GYUR GYI GZUGS LA 'CHAD CING, DE 'DRA DE GZUGS MED NA MED KYANG KHAMS GZHAN GNYIS NA YOD PAR BSHAD PA SOGS SEMS TZAM GYI LUGS LA GZUGS KHAS LEN PA MTHA' YAS PA CIG SNANG NGO,,
gru.wylie: rten 'brel mdo 'grel du, kun gzhi rnams kyi rkyen gyis ming gzugs 'grub par bshad pa'i ming phung po lhag ma bzhi dang, gzugs 'byung ba 'byung 'gyur gyi gzugs la 'chad cing, de 'dra de gzugs med na med kyang khams gzhan gnyis na yod par bshad pa sogs sems tsam gyi lugs la gzugs khas len pa mtha' yas pa cig snang ngo
gru.english: The commentary to the Sutra on Interdependence speaks of how the factor of foundation consciousness brings about the link of name & form; this latter is explaned as referring to “name” in the sense of the remaining four parts to the person, and to “form” in the sense of form composed either of the elements themselves, or the products of the elements. This kind of thing is explained as something that does not occur in the formless realm, but which does exist in the other two realms. It would appear that—with these and other such ideas—there are almost an infinite number of special positions, in the Mind Only school, relating to form.

gru.acip: DE LTA MA YIN NA SEMS TZAM GYI SKABS SU GZUGS PHUNG GI STENG NAS, DE LTAR GZUGS SGRA SOGS THA SNYAD MDZAD PA THAMS CAD LA, GSAR DU MA BCOS PA THA SNYAD BTAGS PA DE NYID KYIS THA SNYAD BYED DU MI RUNG BA KHO NAR 'GYUR BAR SNANG LA, DE 'DRA BA'I THA SNYAD BYAR MI RUNG BAR MTHONG YANG DA DUNG GRUB MTHA' 'DI LEGS SO ZHES PA NI 'PHAGS YUL GYI SANGS RGYAS PA SU LA YANG MI SNANG NGO,,
gru.wylie: de lta ma yin na sems tsam gyi skabs su gzugs phung gi steng nas, de ltar gzugs sgra sogs tha snyad mdzad pa thams cad la, gsar du ma bcos pa tha snyad btags pa de nyid kyis tha snyad byed du mi rung ba kho nar 'gyur bar snang la, de 'dra ba'i tha snyad byar mi rung bar mthong yang da dung grub mtha' 'di legs so zhes pa ni 'phags yul gyi sangs rgyas pa su la yang mi snang ngo
gru.english: If it were not this way, it would appear that in the context of the Mind Only school we would have the following problem. That is—in every case where we used the terms “visible form” or “sound”—it would always be inappropriate to apply the terms in this specific way of their not being created fresh. We can see that it would be inappropriate to apply terms in this way; and yet to continue to insist then that “This is a really great system” is something that we would never see any follower of Buddhism in the Land of the Realized Ones do.

gru.acip: 'DI DANG DBU MA PAS GZUGS SOGS RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PA BKAG NAS GZUGS SOGS 'JOG PA LA, RANG MTSAN GYIS GRUB PAR SNANG BA'I GZUGS SOGS 'DI NYID RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PAR 'JOG PA'I PHYIR, DE YOD MED LA RTZOD PA MED LA RTZOD PA'O ZHES PA DANG 'DRA STE,
gru.wylie: 'di dang dbu ma pas gzugs sogs rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub pa bkag nas gzugs sogs 'jog pa la, rang mtshan gyis grub par snang ba'i gzugs sogs 'di nyid rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub par 'jog pa'i phyir, de yod med la rtsod pa med la rtsod pa'o zhes pa dang 'dra ste
gru.english: This argument would be similar to talking about those who belong to the Middle Way school in the following way: These thinkers deny that form and the rest could ever exist by definition; but when they do posit the existence of form and the like, they are talking about form and such which appear to exist by definition—and so they must be saying that these things exist in fact by definition. And so when they debate about whether these things exist this way or not, they are debating, literally, about nothing.

gru.acip: GRUB MTHA' GNYIS KA'I DKA' GNAS CHEN POR SNANG BAS, DBU MA'I TSUL DKA' BAR MA ZAD SEMS TZAM PA'I LUGS 'DI LA YANG, PHYI ROL BKAG NA GZUGS SOGS KYANG MED PAR 'GRO ZHING, GZUGS SOGS BZHAG NA PHYI ROL YANG BZHAG DGOS PAR MTHONG BAR 'DUG PA'I PHYIR RO,,
gru.wylie: grub mtha' gnyis ka'i dka' gnas chen por snang bas, dbu ma'i tshul dka' bar ma zad sems tsam pa'i lugs 'di la yang, phyi rol bkag na gzugs sogs kyang med par 'gro zhing, gzugs sogs bzhag na phyi rol yang bzhag dgos par mthong bar 'dug pa'i phyir ro
gru.english: This would appear to be a point of great difficulty in both of these schools of thought; as such, it's not just that the system of the Middle Way is something difficult—there is also this point in the tradition of the Mind Only. That is, if we deny the existence of outer objects, then form and the rest would also have to be things that did not exist; whereas if we do posit things such as form and so on, we can see that we would have to posit them as things with an outside existence.

gru.acip: GANG GI PHYIR GSUNG RAB KYI RNAM PAR BZHAG PA NI SNGAR BSHAD PA 'DI YIN PAR GRAGS PA DE'I PHYIR GZHAN GYI DBANG RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA'I NGO BO GANG YIN PA 'DI NI GDON MI ZA BAR KHAS BLANG BAR BYA STE, GANG GI PHYIR GZUNG 'DZIN GYI DNGOS PO BTAGS PAR YOD PA STE RDZAS THA DAD DU YOD PAR 'DZIN PA SOGS KYI RTOG PA'I DRA BA MA LUS PA'I RGYU STE GZHIR 'GYUR BAR 'DOD PA'I PHYIR RO,,
gru.wylie: gang gi phyir gsung rab kyi rnam par bzhag pa ni sngar bshad pa 'di yin par grags pa de'i phyir gzhan gyi dbang rang bzhin gyis grub pa'i ngo bo gang yin pa 'di ni gdon mi za bar khas blang bar bya ste, gang gi phyir gzung 'dzin gyi dngos po btags par yod pa ste rdzas tha dad du yod par 'dzin pa sogs kyi rtog pa'i dra ba ma lus pa'i rgyu ste gzhir 'gyur bar 'dod pa'i phyir ro
gru.english: The presentation of the teachings we have made then is known to be as we have described it; and therefore the idea that an essential nature to dominated things which exists through some quality of its own is something that—beyond any shadow of a doubt—we must accept. And why is this the case? Because we accept the idea that things like objects of perception and the corresponding perceiving subjects exist only as things that are given these names; and that to hold them as being such that to be one is not automatically to be the other is the cause—which is to say, the foundation—of this entire trap of conceptual thought.

gru.acip: SEMS CAN RANG DGA' BA RNAMS KYIS BDEN PAR ZHEN PA'I ZHEN YUL SUN PHYUNG BA'I STONG NYID RTOGS PA LAM DU MI BYED PAR STONG PA GZHAN CIG BDEN PAR SGRUB PA NI, THOG MA MED PA NAS ZHUGS PA'I BDEN ZHEN PHRA RAGS GANG GI YANG GNYEN POR MI 'GRO BAS NGAL BA 'BRAS MED DO,,
gru.wylie: sems can rang dga' ba rnams kyis bden par zhen pa'i zhen yul sun phyung ba'i stong nyid rtogs pa lam du mi byed par stong pa gzhan cig bden par sgrub pa ni, thog ma med pa nas zhugs pa'i bden zhen phra rags gang gi yang gnyen por mi 'gro bas ngal ba 'bras med do
gru.english: And suppose we fail to make a path out of coming to a realization of emptiness—an emptiness where we have overthrown that object of belief: the belief of just normal people of the world that things exist in reality. That is, suppose we take some other kind of emptiness to exist, really. This could never serve as an antidote for either one of the forms—more subtle, or more coarse—of the belief in something real which has resided in the hearts of beings for time with no beginning. And as such, the whole exercise would be one in futility.

gru.acip: DANG PO LA GSUM, PHYI ROL MED PA'I SHES PA RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA'I DPE DGAG ,BAG CHAGS KYI NUS PA LAS DON GYIS STONG PA'I SHES PA SKYE BA'I DON DGAG ,DE LTAR BKAG PA DANG MI SDUG PA SGOM PA GNYIS MI 'GAL BAR BSTAN PA'O,,
gru.wylie: dang po la gsum, phyi rol med pa'i shes pa rang bzhin gyis grub pa'i dpe dgag ,bag chags kyi nus pa las don gyis stong pa'i shes pa skye ba'i don dgag ,de ltar bkag pa dang mi sdug pa sgom pa gnyis mi 'gal bar bstan pa'o
gru.english: The expanded description has three sections of its own: denying a metaphor which is meant to show that awareness where there are no outer objects could exist through some nature of its own; denying the referent of the metaphor in a case where awareness arises from the power of a deep seed, and is empty of the referent; and finally a demonstration that there is no contradiction between this particular denial, and the meditation on the repulsive.

gru.acip: DANG PO LA GSUM, RMI LAM GYI DPES SHES PA RANG BZHIN GYIS YOD PA MI 'GRUB PA, RMI LAM GYI DPES SAD DUS SU PHYI ROL MED PA MI 'GRUB PA, RMI LAM GYI DPES DNGOS PO THAMS CAD BRDZUN PAR 'GRUB PA'O,,
gru.wylie: dang po la gsum, rmi lam gyi dpes shes pa rang bzhin gyis yod pa mi 'grub pa, rmi lam gyi dpes sad dus su phyi rol med pa mi 'grub pa, rmi lam gyi dpes dngos po thams cad brdzun par 'grub pa'o
gru.english: And then finally the first of these steps has three points: how it is that the metaphor of a dream fails to establish that awareness exists through some nature of its own; how it is that the metaphor of a dream fails to establish the idea that, when we awake, there are no outer objects; and finally establishing—through the metaphor of a dream—that all entities are deceptive.

gru.acip: DANG PO NI, SEMS TZAM PA KHYED PHYI ROL MED LA, RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PA'I SEMS YOD PAR 'DOD NA, DPER NA 'DI BZHIN ZHES 'DI'I DPE NI GANG DU YOD CES 'DI NYID DPYAD PAR BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: dang po ni, sems tsam pa khyed phyi rol med la, rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub pa'i sems yod par 'dod na, dper na 'di bzhin zhes 'di'i dpe ni gang du yod ces 'di nyid dpyad par bya'o
gru.english: Here is the first. Suppose that you proponents of the Mind Only school assert that there are no outer objects; but that there does exist a mind which exists by definition. In that case, we need to examine this point more closely; we want you to tell us, “It's like this particular metaphor.” Where then is the metaphor you think there might be for this?

gru.acip: DE'I PHYIR RMI LAM JI LTA BA BZHIN DU PHYI ROL GYI YUL MED BZHIN DU, RNAM SHES RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA 'DI NGES PAR KHAS BLANG BAR BYA'O ZHE NA, 'DI YANG SNYING PO MED PA NYID DU BSTAN PA'I PHYIR BSHAD PA, DPE DE NYID 'DIR BSAM PA STE DPYAD PAR BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: de'i phyir rmi lam ji lta ba bzhin du phyi rol gyi yul med bzhin du, rnam shes rang bzhin gyis grub pa 'di nges par khas blang bar bya'o zhe na, 'di yang snying po med pa nyid du bstan pa'i phyir bshad pa, dpe de nyid 'dir bsam pa ste dpyad par bya'o
gru.english: Suppose then you say that the case here is just the same as a dream, where no outer objects exist; and so we must definitely accept the idea that awareness exists through some nature of its own. Since this is something described to indicate how nothing has any essence of its own, we need to consider this very metaphor here, in our case—we need to examine it.

gru.acip: YANG DPYAD PAR BYA BA DE CI ZHIG CE NA, GANG GI TSE RMI LAM NA YANG BA LANG MYOS PA'I KHYU'I RNAM PA CAN GYI SEMS RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PA DE NI, YUL GLANG PO CHE MED PA LTAR NGA'I LUGS LA YOD PA MIN TE, MA SKYES PA'I PHYIR RO,,
gru.wylie: yang dpyad par bya ba de ci zhig ce na, gang gi tshe rmi lam na yang ba lang myos pa'i khyu'i rnam pa can gyi sems rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub pa de ni, yul glang po che med pa ltar nga'i lugs la yod pa min te, ma skyes pa'i phyir ro
gru.english: And how should this examination proceed? Suppose that—even just in a dream—we have a state of mind that exists by definition, and which is holding the image of a herd of crazed elephants. Here in our system too there is no such existence; it never started, just as the object mentioned—the elephants—never existed.

gru.acip: RNAM SHES RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PA MED NA, DE'I TSE GNYIS KA LA GRUB PA'I KHYED KYI DPE YOD PA MIN PAS, PHYI ROL MED PAR RNAM PAR SHES PA YOD PA MIN NO,,
gru.wylie: rnam shes rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub pa med na, de'i tshe gnyis ka la grub pa'i khyed kyi dpe yod pa min pas, phyi rol med par rnam par shes pa yod pa min no
gru.english: But suppose that there is no such thing as a consciousness which could exist by definition. In that case, you would have no metaphor that existed here which was valid for both parties. And as such, there could be no awareness that existed without outer objects.

gru.acip: 'DIR RMI LAM NA SNANG BA'I GLANG PO CHE MED PA BZHIN DU YUL CAN SHES PA YANG MED PAR STON PA NI MIN GYI RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA'I SHES PA MED PAR STON PA LA NGES PAR 'DOD DGOS TE,
gru.wylie: 'dir rmi lam na snang ba'i glang po che med pa bzhin du yul can shes pa yang med par ston pa ni min gyi rang bzhin gyis grub pa'i shes pa med par ston pa la nges par 'dod dgos te
gru.english: This is not a demonstration that—just as an elephant which appears in a dream cannot be something which exists—an awareness which holds an object cannot exist either. Rather, we have to agree that it is indicating how there exists no awareness which could exist through some nature of its own.

gru.acip: SNGAR BSHAD PA LTAR SEMS TZAM PAS PHYI ROL MED PA'I GZHAN DBANG KHAS BLANGS PA NI, GZHAN DBANG RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA YIN PA'I PHYIR DANG,
gru.wylie: sngar bshad pa ltar sems tsam pas phyi rol med pa'i gzhan dbang khas blangs pa ni, gzhan dbang rang bzhin gyis grub pa yin pa'i phyir dang
gru.english: And so let's consider this assertion by the Mind Only that—as we described it earlier—there do exist dominated entitites where there are no outer objects. It goes back to the idea that dominated entities exist through some nature of their own.

gru.acip: 'DI NI SHES PA RANG GI NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB PA MED NA, SHES PA YE MED PAR BSAMS PA'I RTZOD PA'O,,
gru.wylie: 'di ni shes pa rang gi ngo bo nyid kyis grub pa med na, shes pa ye med par bsams pa'i rtsod pa'o
gru.english: This is an argument based on thinking that—if awareness is not something that exists through some essential nature of its own—then it cannot exist at all.

gru.acip: DE LTAR RTZOD PA 'DI YANG MI RUNG STE, GAL TE GNYID SAD PA'I TSE RMI LAM GYI NYAMS SU MYONG BA DRAN PA LAS, RMI LAM GYI YID RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA YOD NA, RMI LAM GYI GLANG PO CHE LA SOGS PA PHYI ROL TU SNANG BA'I YUL YANG YID DE BZHIN DU YOD PAR 'GYUR TE,
gru.wylie: de ltar rtsod pa 'di yang mi rung ste, gal te gnyid sad pa'i tshe rmi lam gyi nyams su myong ba dran pa las, rmi lam gyi yid rang bzhin gyis grub pa yod na, rmi lam gyi glang po che la sogs pa phyi rol tu snang ba'i yul yang yid de bzhin du yod par 'gyur te
gru.english: And making this kind of argument is, further, incorrect, for the following reason. Suppose that—when we have woken from a dream—we remember what we experienced in the dream. And then suppose further that our mind in the dream existed through some nature of its own. In that case, from our remembering then, things like the elephant in the dream would also become just as that state of mind dictated: they would exist as objects appearing in the outside world.

gru.acip: DE LTAR NA PHYI ROL GYIS STONG PA'I GZHAN DBANG RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PA NI 'JOG PAR MI NUS TE, DNGOS KYI DPE YANG MI SRID LA SKYE BA SNGA PHYI YOD PAR SGRUB PA LTA BU LA DNGOS KYI DPE MED KYANG, SBYOR BA'I 'GOD TSUL GZHAN GYIS SGRUB PA LTA BU'I DPE YANG 'DI LA MED PAS, SEMS TZAM PA 'GOG PA NI RIGS PA SHIN TU STOBS CHE BAR SHES PAR BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: de ltar na phyi rol gyis stong pa'i gzhan dbang rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub pa ni 'jog par mi nus te, dngos kyi dpe yang mi srid la skye ba snga phyi yod par sgrub pa lta bu la dngos kyi dpe med kyang, sbyor ba'i 'god tshul gzhan gyis sgrub pa lta bu'i dpe yang 'di la med pas, sems tsam pa 'gog pa ni rigs pa shin tu stobs che bar shes par bya'o
gru.english: And so thus we can say that there is no way one could establish the existence of dominated entitites that exist by definition and are devoid of objects existing on the outside. There is no outright example of this possibility; and whereas—in the case of proving the existence of past & future lives, there is no outright example either, but we can establish it by other means, such as by positing a logical proof based on a metaphor—there is nothing like that here in this case. As such, you should understand that the denial of the Mind Only position is an extremely powerful expression of logic. The failure of the dream

gru.acip: 'DI NI SNGAR GYI DPE DE MA GRUB TU CHUG KYANG RMI LAM GYI DPES SAD PA'I SKABS SU PHYI ROL MED PA'I RNAM SHES 'GRUB BO SNYAM PA'O,,
gru.wylie: 'di ni sngar gyi dpe de ma grub tu chug kyang rmi lam gyi dpes sad pa'i skabs su phyi rol med pa'i rnam shes 'grub bo snyam pa'o
gru.english: It would appear that—in these lines—it is being allowed that the previous metaphor was not successful, but at the same time there is an assertion that the metaphor of a dream works to establish the fact that, when we awake, there is present a consciousness which has no outer objects.

gru.acip: DE NI MA YIN TE RMI LAM DU YID KYI RNAM SHES 'BYUNG BA MI SRID PA'I PHYIR RO, ZHES GSUNGS PA NI, RMI LAM DU GZUGS KYI SKYE MCHED MED DU CHUG KYANG, DA {%DE} MED PA'I YID KYI RNAM SHES RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA RMI LAM NA'ANG MI SRID PAS, PHYI ROL MED PA DANG YID SHES RANG BZHIN GYIS YOD PA GNYIS TSOGS PA DE DPER MI RUNG ZHES PA'O,,
gru.wylie: de ni ma yin te rmi lam du yid kyi rnam shes 'byung ba mi srid pa'i phyir ro, zhes gsungs pa ni, rmi lam du gzugs kyi skye mched med du chug kyang, da {%de} med pa'i yid kyi rnam shes rang bzhin gyis grub pa rmi lam na'ang mi srid pas, phyi rol med pa dang yid shes rang bzhin gyis yod pa gnyis tshogs pa de dper mi rung zhes pa'o
gru.english: And then we have a statement that this is not the way it is; that it's impossible for consciousness of the thoughts to occur within a dream. What this is saying is that—even if we accede the point that there is no door of sense of visible form in a dream—it is further the case that in a dream it is impossible for there to exist a consciousness of the thoughts which indeed has no such door, and which exists through some nature of its own. As such, it's being said, it is inappropriate to offer this metaphor to illustrate the combination of there being no outer objects, and the awareness of our thoughts existing through some nature of its own.

gru.acip: BOD KYI MKHAS PAR RLOM PA 'GA' ZHIG LA, 'DI 'DRA BA'I GRUB MTHA' LA MKHAS PA'I DBANG PO SEMS DPA' CHEN PO YIN, NGO SHES PA RNAMS KYI LUGS RAGS PA'ANG MA GO BAR, DE RNAMS BSOD NAMS MA YIN PA RGYUN LDAN DU GSOG PA'I ZHING DU GZUNG NAS, SEMS CAN DU MA ZHIG BSOD NAMS MA YIN PA LA SBYOR BAR SNANG BAS BAG YOD PAR BYOS SHIG
gru.wylie: bod kyi mkhas par rlom pa 'ga' zhig la, 'di 'dra ba'i grub mtha' la mkhas pa'i dbang po sems dpa' chen po yin, ngo shes pa rnams kyi lugs rags pa'ang ma go bar, de rnams bsod nams ma yin pa rgyun ldan du gsog pa'i zhing du gzung nas, sems can du ma zhig bsod nams ma yin pa la sbyor bar snang bas bag yod par byos shig
gru.english: And I address this comment to a number of Tibetans who imagine themselves to be great masters: Those who are lords among masters within schools of thought like this are themselves great bodhisattvas; and you have failed to achieve an understanding of even the roughest outline of their system, for those who really recognize who they are. It would appear though that you are taking these lords to be like a garden for harvesting steady flows of negative karma, and are guiding many innocent others to wrongful deeds. And so I ask you, please: Be careful!

gru.acip: ,'DIR SEMS TZAM PAS GAL TE GNYID NANG ZHES SOGS KYIS BSHAD PA BZHIN DU RANG LUGS BZHAG PA LA, SLOB DPON LEGS LDAN GYIS KYANG DPE MA GRUB PA'I LAN MDZAD PA NA, CHOS KYI SKYE MCHED DU GTOGS PA'I GZUGS YID KYI SHES PAS GZUNG BAR BYA BA CIG ,RMI LAM NA YOD PAS RNAM PAR SHES PA NI YUL MED PAR 'GAR YANG YOD PA MA YIN NO ZHES SMRA'O,,
gru.wylie: 'dir sems tsam pas gal te gnyid nang zhes sogs kyis bshad pa bzhin du rang lugs bzhag pa la, slob dpon legs ldan gyis kyang dpe ma grub pa'i lan mdzad pa na, chos kyi skye mched du gtogs pa'i gzugs yid kyi shes pas gzung bar bya ba cig ,rmi lam na yod pas rnam par shes pa ni yul med par 'gar yang yod pa ma yin no zhes smra'o
gru.english: When those of the Mind Only put forth their own system as expressed in the lines that include “If, in our sleep,” Master Bhavaviveka also responds to it saying that the metaphor doesn't work out; that there is something grasped by the awareness of the thought which is subsumed by the door of sense of all things, and this is present in the dream. As such, as it says, “It is not at all the case that the consciousness here is one for which there is no object.”

gru.acip: ZHES GSUNGS PA'I DON NI YUL DBANG RNAM SHES GSUM RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA NI RMI LAM NA YANG RNAM PA THAMS CAD DU MI SRID PA'I PHYIR, CHOS KYI SKYE MCHED KYI GZUGS SHES PA LAS DON GZHAN RMI LAM NA YOD PA MI RIGS ZHES BSHAD RGYU YIN LA,
gru.wylie: zhes gsungs pa'i don ni yul dbang rnam shes gsum rang bzhin gyis grub pa ni rmi lam na yang rnam pa thams cad du mi srid pa'i phyir, chos kyi skye mched kyi gzugs shes pa las don gzhan rmi lam na yod pa mi rigs zhes bshad rgyu yin la
gru.english: What this is saying is that—if the three of the object, the power, and the consciousness existed through some nature of their own—then even in a dream they would be, in every respect, an impossibility. And that means that we would have to say that it is wrong to posit form of the door of sense of all things which could exist in a dream as something discrete from awareness itself.

gru.acip: DE'I TSE GZUGS DE RANG GIS KYANG BZHED DGOS LA, DE RMI LAM NA YANG YOD PA MI 'GAL BAS, GZUGS DE LEGS LDAN GYIS RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PAR ZHAL GYIS BZHES BAR GSAL BAS DE MED PA'I RGYU MTSAN DU BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: de'i tshe gzugs de rang gis kyang bzhed dgos la, de rmi lam na yang yod pa mi 'gal bas, gzugs de legs ldan gyis rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub par zhal gyis bzhes bar gsal bas de med pa'i rgyu mtshan du bya'o
gru.english: In such a case, one would also have to accept this particular form. And since there would be no contradiction for it to exist, even in a dream, then it is clear that Bhavaviveka would have to agree that it existed through some nature of its own. And then we could use that as a reason for saying that it didn't exist.

gru.acip: CI STE SEMS TZAM PA'I LUGS PHYI'I SKYE MCHED DU GTOGS PA'I GZUGS DON GZHAN MED PA LA, RMI LAM DPER 'JOG PA DES SEL NUS PAS, DE BSAL BA'I PHYIR GZUGS DE RANG MTSAN GYIS GRUB PAR KHAS LEN NA NI, DE'I TSE DBU MA PAS BDEN MED SGRUB PA LA RMI LAM GYI DPE BKOD PA DON MED DO,,
gru.wylie: ci ste sems tsam pa'i lugs phyi'i skye mched du gtogs pa'i gzugs don gzhan med pa la, rmi lam dper 'jog pa des sel nus pas, de bsal ba'i phyir gzugs de rang mtshan gyis grub par khas len na ni, de'i tshe dbu ma pas bden med sgrub pa la rmi lam gyi dpe bkod pa don med do
gru.english: And it being the case that in the Mind Only system there could exist no other aspect of form which was taken in by the outer doors of sense, the form that we posit in the metaphor of the dream would be able to remove this problem. If to clarify this point we accept the idea that the form would exist by definition, then it would serve no purpose for those of the Middle Way school to offer the metaphor of a dream in establishing that nothing exists in reality.

gru.acip: RMI LAM DE BRDZUN PA MA YIN PA'I DON CAN TE, RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PA NYID KYIS DPE LAS BYUNG BA STE, DES MTSON PA'I DNGOS KYI DON BRDZUN PA NYID DU GRUB PA MI SRID PA'I PHYIR TE, RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA MA BKAG BAR DU, BDEN MED SGRUB PA'I RTAGS CHOS DPE DE LA RJES SU 'GRO BA MED PA'I PHYIR RO,,
gru.wylie: rmi lam de brdzun pa ma yin pa'i don can te, rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub pa nyid kyis dpe las byung ba ste, des mtshon pa'i dngos kyi don brdzun pa nyid du grub pa mi srid pa'i phyir te, rang bzhin gyis grub pa ma bkag bar du, bden med sgrub pa'i rtags chos dpe de la rjes su 'gro ba med pa'i phyir ro
gru.english: A dream then would carry the connotation of something that was not false. If because of the very fact that it existed by definition, a point were derived from the metaphor, then it would be impossible for the direct referent represented by the metaphor to be established as something that was, in fact, deceptive. And that's because—until such point as we have succeeded in denying that something could exist through some nature of its own—there would be no way that the reason and the quality to be proven in a syllogism to prove that things were not real would ever match the metaphor.

gru.acip: DES NA SNGAR RANG GI LUGS KYIS RMI LAM NA GANG SNANG THAMS CAD RANG BZHIN GYIS MA GRUB PA'I LAN BTAB PA CHES LEGS SO,,
gru.wylie: des na sngar rang gi lugs kyis rmi lam na gang snang thams cad rang bzhin gyis ma grub pa'i lan btab pa ches legs so
gru.english: As such, it is excellent in the extreme for those who belong to our own system to offer the reply that not a single object which appears in a dream could ever exist through some nature of its own.

gru.acip: GANG GI PHYIR RMI LAM NA YUL DBANG RNAM SHES SU SNANG BA GSUM CHAR YANG MI BDEN PA DE'I PHYIR, RMI LAM BDEN MED DU RAB TU GRUB PA'I SGO NAS CHOS GZHAN BDEN MED DU MA GRUB PA RNAMS BSGRUB PA'I PHYIR, SAD PA'I TSE NA YANG CHOS THAMS CAD RANG BZHIN MED PA NYID DU BSGRUBS PAR 'GYUR RO ZHES BSHAD PA,
gru.wylie: gang gi phyir rmi lam na yul dbang rnam shes su snang ba gsum char yang mi bden pa de'i phyir, rmi lam bden med du rab tu grub pa'i sgo nas chos gzhan bden med du ma grub pa rnams bsgrub pa'i phyir, sad pa'i tshe na yang chos thams cad rang bzhin med pa nyid du bsgrubs par 'gyur ro zhes bshad pa
gru.english: In a dream, none of the three that make their appearance are real: neither the object, nor the sense power, nor the awareness. And for this very reason, we can establish that things which we have yet to establish as being unreal—by demonstrating, perfectly, that a dream has no reality. And then for this reason we can say that—when we are awake as well—every entity that exists can be established as having absolutely no nature of its own. To express all this then, we have the following.

gru.acip: MDO DE DAG GIS RMI LAM GYI DPES CHOS THAMS CAD DE KHO NAR MA GRUB PAR BSHAD PA DE DBU MA LA 'GRIG GI ,SEMS TZAM LA MI 'GRIGS PAS LEGS PAR BSHAD PAR 'GYUR ZHES GSUNGS SO,,
gru.wylie: mdo de dag gis rmi lam gyi dpes chos thams cad de kho nar ma grub par bshad pa de dbu ma la 'grig gi ,sems tsam la mi 'grigs pas legs par bshad par 'gyur zhes gsungs so
gru.english: When these sutras use the metaphor of a dream to describe how nothing in the universe exists in & of itself, it is fine with those of the Middle Way school—but it would not be fine with the Mind Only school. As such, it is “a fine explanation.”

gru.acip: DE LTA MA YIN TE GAL TE RAB RIB CAN LA SHES BYA SKRA SHAD MED PAR SKRA SHAD KYI RNAM PA CAN GYI RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA'I BLO SKYE BA YOD NA
gru.wylie: de lta ma yin te gal te rab rib can la shes bya skra shad med par skra shad kyi rnam pa can gyi rang bzhin gyis grub pa'i blo skye ba yod na
gru.english: And suppose it were not this way; suppose a state of mind were there—that it started—with the person who had the cataracts, which existed through some nature of its own and held the appearance of a strand of hair even in the absence of any strand of hair which was an existing object.

gru.acip: 'DI NI RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA'I GZHAN LAS SKYE NA, GZHAN YIN TSAD THAMS CAD LAS SKYE BAR 'PHEN PA BZHIN DU RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA'I SHES PA CIG SKYE NA, YUL SKRA SHAD MED PAR MTSUNGS PA LA, RAB RIB CAN LA DE MTHONG BA SKYE LA, RAB RIB MED PA LA DE MTHONG BA MI SKYE BA MI 'THAD DE, SHES PA DE RAB RIB LA MI LTOS PAR 'PHUL NUS PAS 'BREL MED DU 'GRO BA'I PHYIR RO,,
gru.wylie: 'di ni rang bzhin gyis grub pa'i gzhan las skye na, gzhan yin tshad thams cad las skye bar 'phen pa bzhin du rang bzhin gyis grub pa'i shes pa cig skye na, yul skra shad med par mtshungs pa la, rab rib can la de mthong ba skye la, rab rib med pa la de mthong ba mi skye ba mi 'thad de, shes pa de rab rib la mi ltos par 'phul nus pas 'brel med du 'gro ba'i phyir ro
gru.english: If something could grow from something other than it which existed through some nature of its own, then that implies that it could grow as well from each & every other object in the universe which was other than it. Just so, if it were possible for one state of mind to grow which existed through some nature of its own, then it would be incorrect to say that—in a case where the strand of hair were equally absent—the sight of it would grow in a person who had cataracts but the sight of it would not grow in a person who had no cataracts. That is, since there would be the potential for this state of mind to make itself known without any dependence upon cataracts, everything would happen without any connection to anything.

gru.acip: RAB RIB MED PA LA SGRA SHAD DU SNANG BA'I BLO SKYE BA DE LTA MA YIN PA DE'I PHYIR PHYI ROL MED PAR RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA'I SHES PA DE YOD PA MIN NO,,
gru.wylie: rab rib med pa la sgra shad du snang ba'i blo skye ba de lta ma yin pa de'i phyir phyi rol med par rang bzhin gyis grub pa'i shes pa de yod pa min no
gru.english: And so it is not the case that a state of mind which holds the appearance of a strand of hair could start with the person who had no cataracts; and for this reason, that state of mind which exists through some nature of its own—in the absence of outer objects—is not something which could ever exist. Denying others on deep seeds

gru.acip: GNYIS PA LA GSUM, DA LTAR BA LA NUS PA RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA DGAG ,MA 'ONGS PA'I NUS PA RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA DGAG, 'DAS PA LA NUS PA RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA DGAG PA'O, ,DANG PO NI,
gru.wylie: gnyis pa la gsum, da ltar ba la nus pa rang bzhin gyis grub pa dgag ,ma 'ongs pa'i nus pa rang bzhin gyis grub pa dgag, 'das pa la nus pa rang bzhin gyis grub pa dgag pa'o, ,dang po ni
gru.english: Which brings us to our second part from above: a denial of our opponent's position. We'll cover this point in three steps: a denial that the present could possess a potential that existed through some nature of its own; a denial that the potential of the future could exist through some nature of its own; and a denial that the potential of the past could exist through some nature of its own. Here is the first.

gru.acip: [VI.56b] ,NUS DE MED [207a] PAS 'DI NI 'GRUB MA YIN,
gru.wylie: [vi.56b] ,nus de med [207a] pas 'di ni 'grub ma yin
gru.english: Since there is no such thing As a potential like this Which exists [f. 207a], That is not something Which could be established.

gru.acip: GAL TE NUS PA ZHES PA RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA CIG YOD NA NI, DE'I TSE NUS PA DE SMIN MA SMIN LAS RNAM SHES 'BYUNG MI 'BYUNG YOD DU CHUG NA YANG, NUS PA NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB PA DE MED PAS, 'DI NI 'GRUB PA MA YIN NO,,
gru.wylie: gal te nus pa zhes pa rang bzhin gyis grub pa cig yod na ni, de'i tshe nus pa de smin ma smin las rnam shes 'byung mi 'byung yod du chug na yang, nus pa ngo bo nyid kyis grub pa de med pas, 'di ni 'grub pa ma yin no
gru.english: If what we call “potential” here were one that could exist through some nature of its own, then admittedly we could say that awareness would occur, or not occur, when that potential had ripened, or not yet ripened. But since there is no such thing as a potential like this which exists in & of itself, then that is not something which could be established.

gru.acip: JI LTAR MI 'GRUB CE NA,
gru.wylie: ji ltar mi 'grub ce na
gru.english: “And just how is it,” one may ask, “that this could not be established?”

gru.acip: DE LA RE ZHIG SKYES PA STE DA LTAR BA LA NUS PA NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB PA SRID PA NYID YOD PA MA YIN LA, MA SKYES PA MA 'ONGS PA'I NGO BO LA YANG NUS PA YOD PA MA YIN NO,,
gru.wylie: de la re zhig skyes pa ste da ltar ba la nus pa ngo bo nyid kyis grub pa srid pa nyid yod pa ma yin la, ma skyes pa ma 'ongs pa'i ngo bo la yang nus pa yod pa ma yin no
gru.english: On this question, to start with, we would say that it is not at all a possibility that there could exist a potential to the present—to what had already grown—which also existed in & of itself. Neither could there exist any potential that had a nature of being future; that is, of not having yet grown.

gru.acip: DE LA RNAM SHES MA SKYES PA MA 'ONGS PA NI, RNAM PAR SHES PA'O ZHES SGRUB PA'I NGO BOR BSTAN PAR MI NUS LA, RNAM PAR SHES PA MA YIN ZHES RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA'I DGAG PA'I NGO BOR BSTAN PAR MI NUS SO,,
gru.wylie: de la rnam shes ma skyes pa ma 'ongs pa ni, rnam par shes pa'o zhes sgrub pa'i ngo bor bstan par mi nus la, rnam par shes pa ma yin zhes rang bzhin gyis grub pa'i dgag pa'i ngo bor bstan par mi nus so
gru.english: Suppose here though that the consciousness had not yet grown; that it was future. In this case you could not speak of it as having an established existence: “The consciousness.” But neither could you speak of it as “not being consciousness”: as having a nature where you denied that it could exist through some nature of its own.

gru.acip: ,GAL TE 'BYUNG BAR 'GYUR BAS BSNYAD 'DOD NA, ,NUS PA MED PAR 'DI YI 'BYUNG 'GYUR MED, ,PHAN TSUN DON LA BRTEN PA'I 'GRUB PA NI, ,GRUB MIN NYID CES DAM PA RNAMS KYIS GSUNGS,
gru.wylie: gal te 'byung bar 'gyur bas bsnyad 'dod na, ,nus pa med par 'di yi 'byung 'gyur med, ,phan tshun don la brten pa'i 'grub pa ni, ,grub min nyid ces dam pa rnams kyis gsungs
gru.english: Suppose you assert That you apply a term To that which is Yet to come. But there cannot exist Any which could arise In the absence Of a potential. These are things Which occur in a Codependent relationship; The holy ones Would say that That is something Which could only never exist.

gru.acip: DE'I PHYIR GAL TE RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA'I NUS PA YOD NA RNAM SHES 'BYUNG DU CHUG KYANG, GANG GI TSE DA LTA MA 'ONGS PA'I RNAM SHES RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA NI DUS NAM YANG MED PAS, DE SKYED PA'I NUS PA GTAN MED PA DE'I TSE, MO GSHAM GYI BU LA SOGS PA BZHIN DU RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA'I RNAM SHES SKYED PA'I NUS PA MED PAR RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA'I RNAM SHES 'DI YI 'BYUNG BAR 'GYUR BA MED DO,,
gru.wylie: de'i phyir gal te rang bzhin gyis grub pa'i nus pa yod na rnam shes 'byung du chug kyang, gang gi tshe da lta ma 'ongs pa'i rnam shes rang bzhin gyis grub pa ni dus nam yang med pas, de skyed pa'i nus pa gtan med pa de'i tshe, mo gsham gyi bu la sogs pa bzhin du rang bzhin gyis grub pa'i rnam shes skyed pa'i nus pa med par rang bzhin gyis grub pa'i rnam shes 'di yi 'byung bar 'gyur ba med do
gru.english: And so we can say that—if there did exist a potential that existed through some nature of its own—we could allow that consciousness might then occur. But in a situation where there is never, upon any occasion, any present or future consciousness which could exist through a nature of its own, there cannot exist at all any potential which could trigger it. And in this case, there cannot exist any consciousness that existed through its own nature and which could arise in the absence of a potential that triggered a consciousness that existed through some nature of its own: the whole thing would be like the child of a barren woman, or something of that ilk.

gru.acip: DBU MA PAS MYU GU SKYE BA RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PA 'GOG PA'I SKABS MANG POR, MYU GU SA BON GYI DUS SU MED KYANG SKYE NA, RI BONG GI RVA LA SOGS PA YANG SKYE BAR 'GYUR RO, ,ZHES HA CANG THAL BA 'PHEN PA'I
gru.wylie: dbu ma pas myu gu skye ba rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub pa 'gog pa'i skabs mang por, myu gu sa bon gyi dus su med kyang skye na, ri bong gi rva la sogs pa yang skye bar 'gyur ro, ,zhes ha cang thal ba 'phen pa'i
gru.english: In many contexts where those of the Middle Way school deny that the growing of a sprout could happen by definition, they say things like “If the sprout could be absent at the time of the seed and yet still grow, then the horn of a rabbit or the like would also grow.” That is, they point to an absurd consequence that would be necessitated.

gru.acip: GNAD NI RANG MTSAN GYIS GRUB PA'I MYU GU NI SKABS GCIG TU MED NA DUS NAM YANG MED DGOS PAS, GZHI MA GRUB DANG KHYAD MED DU 'GRO BA'I RGYU MTSAN GYIS YIN GYI, SPYIR MYU GU SA BON GYI DUS NA MED KYANG SKYE NA, RI BONG GI RVA YANG SKYE BAR THAL ZHES 'GOG PA GTAN MIN NO,,
gru.wylie: gnad ni rang mtshan gyis grub pa'i myu gu ni skabs gcig tu med na dus nam yang med dgos pas, gzhi ma grub dang khyad med du 'gro ba'i rgyu mtshan gyis yin gyi, spyir myu gu sa bon gyi dus na med kyang skye na, ri bong gi rva yang skye bar thal zhes 'gog pa gtan min no
gru.english: The point of such statements is to say that—if there were any single occasion upon which a sprout that existed by definition were absent—then it would have to always be absent. And then there wouldn't be any difference from saying that it never existed in the first place. This is the rationale being employed at this point; it is not the point though to say that—generally speaking—if a sprout were absent in the time of the seed but were still able to grow, then a rabbit horn would also have to grow. This is not at all the denial being made here.

gru.acip: GZHAN YANG RNAM SHES 'BYUNG 'GYUR YOD PA LA LTOS NAS DE'I NUS PA 'JOG LA, NUS PA LAS RNAM SHES 'BYUNG NGO ZHES NUS PA LA LTOS NAS RNAM SHES 'JOG NA, PHAN TSUN GYI DON LA BRTEN PA'I 'GRUB PAR 'GYUR RO,,
gru.wylie: gzhan yang rnam shes 'byung 'gyur yod pa la ltos nas de'i nus pa 'jog la, nus pa las rnam shes 'byung ngo zhes nus pa la ltos nas rnam shes 'jog na, phan tshun gyi don la brten pa'i 'grub par 'gyur ro
gru.english: Moreover, the potential for a consciousness is posited relative to a consciousness which is yet to occur; and we posit the consciousness relative to the potential; we say: “The consciousness is going to rise from the potential.” As such, these are things which occur in a codependent relationship.

gru.acip: DE 'DOD DO ZHE NA, DE LTAR NA RNAM SHES RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA MIN PA NYID CES DAM PA MKHYEN RAB MNGA' BA RNAMS KYIS GSUNGS SO,,
gru.wylie: de 'dod do zhe na, de ltar na rnam shes rang bzhin gyis grub pa min pa nyid ces dam pa mkhyen rab mnga' ba rnams kyis gsungs so
gru.english: And if you say that all this seems like something you could agree to, then in that case the holy ones—which is to say, those who possess supreme intellect—would say that, in that case, a consciousness which could exist through some nature of its own is something which could only never exist.

gru.acip: 'GREL PAR RING THUNG DANG PHA ROL TSUL {%TSUR} ROL LTA BU'I LTOS 'GRUB RNAMS NI BTAGS PAR YOD PAR 'GYUR GYI, GRUB PA RANG BZHIN PA MED PAR GSUNGS PAS DE DAG LA GRUB PA SPYIR 'GOG PA MIN GYIS RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA 'GOG PA'I KHYAD PAR RNAMS SHES PAR BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: 'grel par ring thung dang pha rol tshul {%tshur} rol lta bu'i ltos 'grub rnams ni btags par yod par 'gyur gyi, grub pa rang bzhin pa med par gsungs pas de dag la grub pa spyir 'gog pa min gyis rang bzhin gyis grub pa 'gog pa'i khyad par rnams shes par bya'o
gru.english: In the autocommentary, they talk about how things like long & short—and “over there” & “over here”—exist as designated relative to each other; but since it is said that their existence is not one which has any quality of being natural, it is not the case that we are denying, in general, that they could have any existence at all. As such, you need to understand the details of how we deny that things could exist through any nature of their own.

gru.acip: RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA'I GZHAN GYI NUS PA LAS 'BRAS BU'I RNAM SHES GZHAN 'BYUNG BAR 'GYUR RO,,
gru.wylie: rang bzhin gyis grub pa'i gzhan gyi nus pa las 'bras bu'i rnam shes gzhan 'byung bar 'gyur ro
gru.english: And so something other—a resulting consciousness—is arising from a potential which is something other, and which exists through some nature of its own.

gru.acip: SKAD CIG SNGA PHYI DE DAG PHAN TSUN GZHAN DANG GZHAN DU THA DAD CING, RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PA'I GZHAN NYID DU PHA ROL POS KHAS BLANGS PA YIN NO,,
gru.wylie: skad cig snga phyi de dag phan tshun gzhan dang gzhan du tha dad cing, rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub pa'i gzhan nyid du pha rol pos khas blangs pa yin no
gru.english: The other party here accepts the idea that the earlier and later seconds are discrete, each one from the other; and that they are invariably others from each other which exist by definition.

gru.acip: DE LTAR NA RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA'I GZHAN GYI NUS PA LAS GZHAN 'BYUNG BAR 'GYUR RO,,
gru.wylie: de ltar na rang bzhin gyis grub pa'i gzhan gyi nus pa las gzhan 'byung bar 'gyur ro
gru.english: As such, we can say then that one thing which is other comes from a potential which is also other and which exists by definition.

gru.acip: ,GAL TE DER NI RGYUN CAN THA DAD KYI, ,DE DAG LA RGYUN THA DAD MED DE'I PHYIR, ,NYES MED CE NA 'DI NI BSGRUB BYA ZHIG ,THA MI DAD RGYUN SKABS MI RIGS PHYIR RO,
gru.wylie: gal te der ni rgyun can tha dad kyi, ,de dag la rgyun tha dad med de'i phyir, ,nyes med ce na 'di ni bsgrub bya zhig ,tha mi dad rgyun skabs mi rigs phyir ro
gru.english: Suppose then There is the composite Flow of those That are different From each other. But suppose you say That the flow for those Could never involve Separate things; And so there is No such problem. This idea though Is something that You would still Have to prove. It is illogical to say That there could be Any opportunity For a flow of things That were not separate.

gru.acip: GAL TE YANG SKAD CIG SNGA PHYI RIM GYIS 'JUG PA DER NI RGYUN CAN RDZAS KYI SKAD CIG MA RNAMS PHAN TSUN NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB PA'I THA DAD DE GZHAN NYID YOD MOD KYI,
gru.wylie: gal te yang skad cig snga phyi rim gyis 'jug pa der ni rgyun can rdzas kyi skad cig ma rnams phan tshun ngo bo nyid kyis grub pa'i tha dad de gzhan nyid yod mod kyi
gru.english: Suppose then that we do accept the idea that there in the progressive flow of the earlier & later seconds there are seconds of the material, the composite flow, which are different from each other, by their very nature.

gru.acip: SNGA PHYI NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB PA'I SO SO BA LA RGYUD GCIG GRUB NA, SKYON MED DU CHUG KYANG RGYUD GCIG PA 'DI MA GRUB PAS NA RGYUD GCIG PA 'DI NI BSGRUB PAR BYA BA ZHIG GO
gru.wylie: snga phyi ngo bo nyid kyis grub pa'i so so ba la rgyud gcig grub na, skyon med du chug kyang rgyud gcig pa 'di ma grub pas na rgyud gcig pa 'di ni bsgrub par bya ba zhig go
gru.english: Let's say that a single flow is composed of earlier and later parts that are separate and which exist through some essential nature of their own. Even if you allow that there is no problem here, they could never constitute a single flow. As such, this idea of a single flow is something that you would still have to prove.

gru.acip: ,CI'I PHYIR ZHE NA, SNGA PHYI NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB PA'I THA DAD RNAMS LA THA MI DAD PA'I RGYUN TE RGYUD GCIG PA'I GO SKABS MI RIGS PA'I PHYIR TE,
gru.wylie: ci'i phyir zhe na, snga phyi ngo bo nyid kyis grub pa'i tha dad rnams la tha mi dad pa'i rgyun te rgyud gcig pa'i go skabs mi rigs pa'i phyir te
gru.english: And why is that? Because it is illogical to say that there could be any opportunity for a single stream, a flow, of things that were not separate with these separate parts of earlier and later that existed in and of themselves.

gru.acip: DE BZHIN DU, SNGA PHYI BA GANG DAG RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PA'I SO SO BA DE DAG NI, RGYUD GCIG TU GTOGS PA STE GCIG PA NYID RIGS PA DANG LDAN PA MA YIN NO,,
gru.wylie: de bzhin du, snga phyi ba gang dag rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub pa'i so so ba de dag ni, rgyud gcig tu gtogs pa ste gcig pa nyid rigs pa dang ldan pa ma yin no
gru.english: The same would hold true with those earlier and later parts that were separate things that existed by definition. It would not be something that was logical to say that they were all one and the same: that they were sharing a single flow.

gru.acip: DE LTAR NA GZHAN SKYE LA HA CANG THAL BA 'PHANGS PA'I SKYON SPONG LA, SA LU'I SA MYUG RGYUD GCIG YIN LA NAS KYI SA MYUG DANG RGYUD MI GCIG PAS THAMS CAD LAS THAMS CAD MI SKYE ZHES ZER BAS, SKYON SPONG MI NUS PA'I GNAD PHA ROL POS, RANG MTSAN GYIS GRUB PA'I GZHAN KHAS BLANGS PA LA THUG PAR BSTAN PAS,
gru.wylie: de ltar na gzhan skye la ha cang thal ba 'phangs pa'i skyon spong la, sa lu'i sa myug rgyud gcig yin la nas kyi sa myug dang rgyud mi gcig pas thams cad las thams cad mi skye zhes zer bas, skyon spong mi nus pa'i gnad pha rol pos, rang mtshan gyis grub pa'i gzhan khas blangs pa la thug par bstan pas
gru.english: As such, people have to say the following sort of thing to avoid the problem that is raised by the idea that things grow from things other than themselves—the problem that it would all be too much. That is, for this they make the claim that “The seed & the sprout for a rice plant constitute a single flow; but they are not a single flow with the seed & the sprout for a barley plant; as such, it is not the case that everything grows from everything else.” The fact that this does not allow them to avoid the problem comes down to one crucial point: that these other parties accept the idea that one thing could be other than another thing by definition. And we have shown them this.

gru.acip: GZHAN TZAM LA 'PHEN PA MIN PAR SHIN TU GSAL BA LA LDOG PA GCIG PA'I DPUNG 'PHUL SOGS BYED PA DANG, RANG MTSAN GYIS GRUB PA'I GZHAN CES GSUNGS PA DGAG BYA'I KHYAD PAR SBYAR BA MA GO BAS,
gru.wylie: gzhan tsam la 'phen pa min par shin tu gsal ba la ldog pa gcig pa'i dpung 'phul sogs byed pa dang, rang mtshan gyis grub pa'i gzhan ces gsungs pa dgag bya'i khyad par sbyar ba ma go bas
gru.english: Here those other parties though have misunderstood how totally clear it is that none of these problems comes up when we accept something which is a simple other; they continue to toss out examples where they pile up items as if they were all stuck together into one thing. It seems as though they are just completely incapable of understanding it when we apply the term for the thing whose existence we deny to something which is other, by saying that it would exist “through some nature of its own.”

gru.acip: DPAL LDAN ZLA BA NYID KYIS SKYON SPONG MI NUS PAR GSUNGS PA'I RGYU MTSAN BZHAG NAS MA GSUNGS PA'I RTOG BZO BYED PA NI YANG DAG PA'I GRUB MTHA' SLOD PA'O,,
gru.wylie: dpal ldan zla ba nyid kyis skyon spong mi nus par gsungs pa'i rgyu mtshan bzhag nas ma gsungs pa'i rtog bzo byed pa ni yang dag pa'i grub mtha' slod pa'o
gru.english: They throw out to us, as one of their reasons, the idea that the glorious Chandrakirti himself made statements in which he was unable to avoid certain problems; and in this way they make up ideas that this Master never did express, polluting what is in actuality the very purest school of thought. The Mind Only on outer objects

gru.acip: DE SKAD BSTAN PA YIN DANG SLAR YANG SEMS TZAM PAS RANG GI LUGS BRJOD PA GTZO BOR BYAS PA NYID KYIS RANG GI 'DOD DON 'GRUB PAR BSAMS SHING SMRAS PA,
gru.wylie: de skad bstan pa yin dang slar yang sems tsam pas rang gi lugs brjod pa gtso bor byas pa nyid kyis rang gi 'dod don 'grub par bsams shing smras pa
gru.english: And so this is the presentation; and then once again the followers of the Mind Only hope to focus on describing, primarily, their own position—thus then they consider ways of establishing it and present the following.

gru.acip: 'DI YANG PHYI'I GZUGS SOGS MED PAR RNAM SHES RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA SKYE NA, RMI LAM DANG SAD PA GNYIS KA LA KHYAD MED PA'I GNAD KYIS YIN NO,,
gru.wylie: 'di yang phyi'i gzugs sogs med par rnam shes rang bzhin gyis grub pa skye na, rmi lam dang sad pa gnyis ka la khyad med pa'i gnad kyis yin no
gru.english: And there is another crucial point to back this up: If an awareness that existed through some nature of its own could arise even in the absence of outer visible form and the like, then there would be no difference between the dream state and the waking state.

gru.acip: DE'I PHYIR MIG MED PA SAD PA'I LONG BA 'DI LA DON SNANG GI BAG CHAGS SMIN PA RGYU MIN PA JI LTA BA DE LTAR RMI LAM DU YANG GNYID NI DON SNANG GI BAG CHAGS SMIN PA'I RGYU MA YIN TE, PHYI ROL MED PAR SHES PA RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA SKYE NA BAG CHAGS SMIN PA LA MI LTOS PA'I PHYIR RO,,
gru.wylie: de'i phyir mig med pa sad pa'i long ba 'di la don snang gi bag chags smin pa rgyu min pa ji lta ba de ltar rmi lam du yang gnyid ni don snang gi bag chags smin pa'i rgyu ma yin te, phyi rol med par shes pa rang bzhin gyis grub pa skye na bag chags smin pa la mi ltos pa'i phyir ro
gru.english: As such, it's not as if things are happening here as they do when there is no eye: where, for this person who is blind during the waking state, the ripening of a deep seed for the mind to take on the appearance of the object is not acting as a cause. Just so, in a dream as well, sleep could not be a cause for the ripening of the deep seed of the mind taking on the aspect of the object. And that's because—if it were the case that a state of mind that existed through some nature of its own could grow in the absence of outer objects, then it wouldn't have to rely upon the ripening of some deep seed.

gru.acip: DE GSUM MIG SOGS SU GRUB PAR 'DOD PA MIN TE, SGYU MA'I RTA GLANG DANG SGYU MA'I MI KHAS LEN KYANG, DE DAG RTA GLANG DANG MIR 'DOD MI DGOS PA BZHIN NO,,
gru.wylie: de gsum mig sogs su grub par 'dod pa min te, sgyu ma'i rta glang dang sgyu ma'i mi khas len kyang, de dag rta glang dang mir 'dod mi dgos pa bzhin no
gru.english: It's not saying though that we would have to say that these three actually existed as an eye or the like. That is, we would have to agree that there do exist illusory horses and cows, and illusory people; but that doesn't mean that we would have to agree that they were horses, or cows, or people.

gru.acip: DE'I PHYIR DE LTAR NA SEMS TZAM PA 'DI YIS DBU MA PA LA LAN NI GANG DANG GANG BTAB PA DE DANG DE NI, DAM BCA' BA STE BSGRUB BYA MA GRUB PA DANG MTSUNGS PAR MTHONG BAS, RTZOD 'DI STE RNAM PAR RIG PA TZAM DU SMRA BA 'DI SEL BA STE ZLOG PAR BYAD {%BYED} DO,,
gru.wylie: de'i phyir de ltar na sems tsam pa 'di yis dbu ma pa la lan ni gang dang gang btab pa de dang de ni, dam bca' ba ste bsgrub bya ma grub pa dang mtshungs par mthong bas, rtsod 'di ste rnam par rig pa tsam du smra ba 'di sel ba ste zlog par byad {%byed} do
gru.english: And so thus, given this we can say that whatever response it is that these proponents of the Mind Only school might make to those of the Middle Way, we can see that this assertion is equivalent to a logical proof which doesn't hold. As such, this particular argument actually “clears” the beliefs of those who say that there is nothing but awareness; which is to say, it blocks them.

gru.acip: DE DAG DPER BRJOD NA DBU MA PAS SAD PA'I SKABS KYI YUL DBANG RNAM SHES GSUM RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAS STONG PA YIN TE, DMIGS PA YIN PA'I PHYIR RMI LAM BZHIN NO, ZHES BKOD PA NA
gru.wylie: de dag dper brjod na dbu ma pas sad pa'i skabs kyi yul dbang rnam shes gsum rang bzhin gyis grub pas stong pa yin te, dmigs pa yin pa'i phyir rmi lam bzhin no, zhes bkod pa na
gru.english: And so let's say for example that those of the Middle Way were to set forth the logic that these three, when we are awake—the object, the sense power, and the consciousness—are empty of existing through any nature of their own, simply because they are observed: they are like a dream.

gru.acip: DE LA SBYOR BA DANG PO GNYIS NI, DPE MA GRUB PAS SGRUB BYED BSGRUB BYA DANG MTSUNGS PA YIN TE, RMI LAM NA YID KYI SHES PA LAS NGO BO THA DAD PA'I CHOS KYI SKYE MCHED KYI GZUGS YOD PA'I PHYIR RO,,
gru.wylie: de la sbyor ba dang po gnyis ni, dpe ma grub pas sgrub byed bsgrub bya dang mtshungs pa yin te, rmi lam na yid kyi shes pa las ngo bo tha dad pa'i chos kyi skye mched kyi gzugs yod pa'i phyir ro
gru.english: As for the first two logical sentiments expressed here, we can say that since the example cited isn't correct, what is being used to prove the idea and the idea that they are trying to prove end up being equivalent. And that's because, in a dream, there does exist form of the sense door of phenomena which is essentially separate from consciousness of the thought.

gru.acip: SBYOR BA GSUM PA NI, KUN BYANG GI RTEN RANG MTSAN GYIS GRUB PA CIG SGRUB 'DOD PA YIN PAS DE LA NI, RTEN TZAM MED PA MA GRUB PA YIN LA, RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PA LA BSAMS NA NI MA NGES PA'O,,
gru.wylie: sbyor ba gsum pa ni, kun byang gi rten rang mtshan gyis grub pa cig sgrub 'dod pa yin pas de la ni, rten tsam med pa ma grub pa yin la, rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub pa la bsams na ni ma nges pa'o
gru.english: As for the third logical thought expessed above, they seek to establish that there is a foundation to the negative side of things—and to the enlightened side of things—which could exist by definition. Proving this foundation in its simple form is simply an argument that is not proven to be true; whereas if what they have in mind is specifically something that could exist by definition, then the proof is inconclusive. Scripture can deny Mind Only

gru.acip: RKANG PA DANG POS SRID GSUM BLOS BTAGS PA TZAM DU YOD PAR BSTAN LA, RKANG PA GNYIS PAS NI DE'I DON BSTAN TE, DE YANG NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB PA'I DNGOS PO MED PAR BSTAN PAS, NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB PA MED PA YIN GYI DNGOS PO YE MED MIN ZHES PA'O,,
gru.wylie: rkang pa dang pos srid gsum blos btags pa tsam du yod par bstan la, rkang pa gnyis pas ni de'i don bstan te, de yang ngo bo nyid kyis grub pa'i dngos po med par bstan pas, ngo bo nyid kyis grub pa med pa yin gyi dngos po ye med min zhes pa'o
gru.english: The first line here [in the Tibetan; the first two lines in the English] are meant to indicate that the three realms into which the entire universe is divided exist only as something labeled by the mind. The second line [third and fourth in the English] are meant to explain what this means; that is—by showing how there can be no entity which exists in & of itself—we are saying that there is nothing which exists in & of itself, but not that nothing exists at all.

gru.acip: DE LTAR BLOS BTAGS PA TZAM LA NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB PA'I DNGOS POR DE KHO NA NYID KYI DON MA RNYED PA'I RTOG GE PAS 'DOD DO ZHES PA NI, BTAGS PA ZHES PA GNYIS KYIS STON NO,,
gru.wylie: de ltar blos btags pa tsam la ngo bo nyid kyis grub pa'i dngos por de kho na nyid kyi don ma rnyed pa'i rtog ge pas 'dod do zhes pa ni, btags pa zhes pa gnyis kyis ston no
gru.english: And what the two mentions of “labels” are meant to indicate is that the idea that what is—in actuality—merely a creation of the mind could exist as an entity which existed in & of itself is only something that could be asserted by a person trying to think logically who had yet to discover the true meaning of suchness.

gru.acip: NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB PA MED PAR SPYIR BSTAN PA STE, BYE BRAG TU PHYE STE STON PA NI, R'U PA ZHES PA RANG BZHIN DANG GZUGS GNYIS KA LA 'JUG PA LAS 'DIR GZUGS CAN LA BYA STE, RNAM RIG CES PA'I ZLA STOBS KYIS SO,,
gru.wylie: ngo bo nyid kyis grub pa med par spyir bstan pa ste, bye brag tu phye ste ston pa ni, rU pa zhes pa rang bzhin dang gzugs gnyis ka la 'jug pa las 'dir gzugs can la bya ste, rnam rig ces pa'i zla stobs kyis so
gru.english: Saying that things don't exist in & of themselves is the general presentation; if we were to break things down more particularly, we would point out that the Sanskrit word rūpa can refer both to “nature” and to “form”; and that here, it is meant to allude to things which possess physical form. This physicality is indicated here in the lines in the form of what they call a “contrasting poeticism,” with the word “awareness.”

gru.acip: GCIG LA CIG SHOS MED PA'I STONG PA 'DI DPER BRJOD DE DANG 'DRA BAR 'GYUR TSUL NI BCOM LDAN 'DAS KYI RANG BZHIN GYIS DBEN PA'I STONG NYID GSUNGS PA NI SEMS CAN RNAMS THOG MA MED PA NAS GZUGS SOGS KYI DNGOS PO LA BDEN PAR GRUB PAR 'DZIN PA'I MNGON ZHEN BZLOG PA'I PHYIR DU YIN PA LA,
gru.wylie: gcig la cig shos med pa'i stong pa 'di dper brjod de dang 'dra bar 'gyur tshul ni bcom ldan 'das kyi rang bzhin gyis dben pa'i stong nyid gsungs pa ni sems can rnams thog ma med pa nas gzugs sogs kyi dngos po la bden par grub par 'dzin pa'i mngon zhen bzlog pa'i phyir du yin pa la
gru.english: Now let's consider this approach, where—as in the example just cited—we speak of emptiness as one thing lacking another. When the conquering Buddhas make statements like this, about an emptiness where things are devoid of any nature, the reason they do so is to stop the belief of living beings, for time with no beginning, where they grasp to the idea that entities such as form and the like could exist as real.

gru.acip: DE LA GZUGS SOGS SU SNANG BA'I GZHAN DBANG 'DI NYID BDEN PAR MA GRUB PAR BSTAN DGOS PA LA, DE LTAR MI STON PAR GZHAN DBANG 'DI GZUNG 'DZIN RDZAS THA DAD PAR MI BDEN NO ZHES BSTAN PA NA, BA LANG MED PA'I RGYU MTSAN DU BA LANG LTAR MED CES ZER BA DANG 'DRA'O,,
gru.wylie: de la gzugs sogs su snang ba'i gzhan dbang 'di nyid bden par ma grub par bstan dgos pa la, de ltar mi ston par gzhan dbang 'di gzung 'dzin rdzas tha dad par mi bden no zhes bstan pa na, ba lang med pa'i rgyu mtshan du ba lang ltar med ces zer ba dang 'dra'o
gru.english: To this point, one has to demonstrate that dominated entities which appear as form or the like cannot exist in reality. And suppose that we do not present it that way, and only indicate that these dominated things are not real in the sense of objects & subjects which are essentially different. This would be like saying—as a reason for asserting that a cow doesn't exist—that “it doesn't exist, because it's similar to the case with a cow.”

gru.acip: DBU MA PA LTAR NA ZHEN TSUL NI SNANG BA LA THA SNYAD PA'I BLOS BZHAG PA MIN PA'I BDEN GRUB TU ZHEN PA YIN LA, DE'I GNYEN POR SNANG BA 'DI CHOS CAN DU BZUNG NAS, DE 'DRA BA'I BDEN PAR MED CES 'GOG STE,
gru.wylie: dbu ma pa ltar na zhen tshul ni snang ba la tha snyad pa'i blos bzhag pa min pa'i bden grub tu zhen pa yin la, de'i gnyen por snang ba 'di chos can du bzung nas, de 'dra ba'i bden par med ces 'gog ste
gru.english: Those of the Middle Way describe the belief with which we hold to things in a different way. They say that we hold that things exist in reality—which is to say, we believe that what appears to us is not being established by a nominal state of mind. And then as an antidote for this belief, we start by taking this way that things appear to us as the subject under our logical consideration. Then we deny this appearance by saying, “This is not something which exists as real, in the way we have described that.”

gru.acip: DE LTAR NA SEMS TZAM PA NGES DON MTHAR THUG PA RTOGS PA'I SHES RAB KYI RTZAL MED PAR GRUB PA'I MTHAR SBYAR BA 'DI BSAL BAR BYA BA KHO NA'O,,
gru.wylie: de ltar na sems tsam pa nges don mthar thug pa rtogs pa'i shes rab kyi rtsal med par grub pa'i mthar sbyar ba 'di bsal bar bya ba kho na'o
gru.english: And so we can say that this attempt to depict the Mind Only as a school of thought that completely lacks any dexterity in the wisdom needed to perceive the ultimate intended meaning is an idea that should only be refused. No contradiction with the repulsive

gru.acip: GAL TE PHYI YI YUL MED PAR GZUGS SGRA SOGS GSAL BAR SNANG BA'I SHES PA RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA MED NA, BLA MA'I MAN NGAG LAS MI SDUG PA SGOM PA'I RNAL 'BYOR PA RNAMS KYIS, SA GZHI KENG RUS KYIS GANG BAR MTHONG BA DE JI LTAR 'THAD DE, KENG RUS NI MED KYANG RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA'I RNAM SHES NI YOD PA'I PHYIR RO SNYAM NA,
gru.wylie: gal te phyi yi yul med par gzugs sgra sogs gsal bar snang ba'i shes pa rang bzhin gyis grub pa med na, bla ma'i man ngag las mi sdug pa sgom pa'i rnal 'byor pa rnams kyis, sa gzhi keng rus kyis gang bar mthong ba de ji ltar 'thad de, keng rus ni med kyang rang bzhin gyis grub pa'i rnam shes ni yod pa'i phyir ro snyam na
gru.english: One may come next with the following thought: Well then, suppose it is the case that—even in a total absence of outer objects—the consciousness which so clearly takes on the aspect of visual form, sound, and the rest does not exist as something with some nature of its own. How then can it be correct for those great pracitioners who are following the advices of their spiritual teachers, and meditating upon the repulsive, to see the entire surface of the earth covered with skeletons? Because it must then be the case that—even though these skeletons don't actually exist—there is present some awareness which exists through a nature of its own.

gru.acip: KENG RUS SNANG BA'I SHES PA RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB NA, DE'I SNANG BA YANG DE LTAR 'GYUR BAS YID BYED DE DE KHO NA NYID KYI YUL CAN DU 'GYUR RO,,
gru.wylie: keng rus snang ba'i shes pa rang bzhin gyis grub na, de'i snang ba yang de ltar 'gyur bas yid byed de de kho na nyid kyi yul can du 'gyur ro
gru.english: If awareness that had taken on the aspect of skeletons existed through some nature of its own, then the aspect that it takes on would also have to be the same. And in that case, this particular way of focusing the mind would have to have, as its object, something that represented the way that things actually are.

gru.acip: RNAL 'BYOR PA YIN MIN MGO MTSUNGS MDZAD PA YANG, SHES PA RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA YIN NA KENG RUS KYI MAN NGAG SGOM PA LA LTOS PA 'GOG NUS PA'I GNAD KYIS YIN NO,,
gru.wylie: rnal 'byor pa yin min mgo mtshungs mdzad pa yang, shes pa rang bzhin gyis grub pa yin na keng rus kyi man ngag sgom pa la ltos pa 'gog nus pa'i gnad kyis yin no
gru.english: This is true because of a crucial point here. Even if we were to say that the two observers were the same—in either being a deep practitioner, or not—in a case where their states of mind existed through some nature of their own, we would be able to deny that they were relying on a meditation upon the advices for the practice of the skeletons.

gru.acip: DE LA CHOS KYI SKYE MCHED KYI GZUGS LNGA NI DNGOS POR SMRA BA'I GRUB MTHAS BTAGS PA MIN GYI, MDO LAS GSUNGS SHING RANG NYID KYANG DE LTAR DU BZHED DO,,
gru.wylie: de la chos kyi skye mched kyi gzugs lnga ni dngos por smra ba'i grub mthas btags pa min gyi, mdo las gsungs shing rang nyid kyang de ltar du bzhed do
gru.english: Now the five types of form relating to the sense door of all things are not something simply imputed by the school of thought known as the Functionalists. Rather, they have been stated in sutra, and we also accept them as being such.

gru.acip: THEG BSDUS LAS KYANG, ,YI DVAGS DUD 'GRO MI RNAMS DANG, ,LHA RNAMS JI LTAR RIGS RIGS SU, ,DNGOS GCIG YID NI THA DAD PHYIR, ,DON MA GRUB PAR 'DOD PA YIN, ZHES GSUNGS SHING,
gru.wylie: theg bsdus las kyang, ,yi dvags dud 'gro mi rnams dang, ,lha rnams ji ltar rigs rigs su, ,dngos gcig yid ni tha dad phyir, ,don ma grub par 'dod pa yin, zhes gsungs shing
gru.english: The Compendium of the Greater Way puts it this way: Since a single entity Is separate things To a craving spirit, And a human, And a worldly god, Each according To their type, We assert that It cannot exist In fact.

gru.acip: 'DI LA 'DI SNYAM DU 'GRO BA DE DAG GI MTHONG BA NI THA SNYAD PA'I TSAD MA YIN LA, GZHI GCIG MI MTHUN PA DE DAG TU TSAD MAS GRUB NA RNAG KHRAG DANG RNAL KHRAG MA YIN PA GNYIS MI 'GAL ZHING, TSAD MAS GRUB PA LA YANG YID BRTAN MED PAR 'GYUR RO ZHE NA,
gru.wylie: 'di la 'di snyam du 'gro ba de dag gi mthong ba ni tha snyad pa'i tshad ma yin la, gzhi gcig mi mthun pa de dag tu tshad mas grub na rnag khrag dang rnal khrag ma yin pa gnyis mi 'gal zhing, tshad mas grub pa la yang yid brtan med par 'gyur ro zhe na
gru.english: One may feel the following concerns about this citation: The way that these different beings see things is a nominal form of accurate perception; and if these incompatible perceptions of a single base object are all confirmed with an accurate perception, then it must be the case that being blood and pus, and not being blood and pus, are not two incompatible states. It also throws into the question the whole process of confirming things with accurate perception.

gru.acip: DE LTAR GO BA DE'I DON YIN PAR BZUNG NAS TSAD MAS GRUB PA LA YID BRTAN MED DO ZHES SMRA NA NI, DON 'DI KHO BOS 'DI LTAR RTOGS SO ZHES PA GCIG KYANG GZHAG TU MED CING, TSAD MA THAMS CAD LA SKUR PA 'DEBS PAS NA SHIN TU MI 'THAD PA'O,,
