gru.wylie: de ltar go ba de'i don yin par bzung nas tshad mas grub pa la yid brtan med do zhes smra na ni, don 'di kho bos 'di ltar rtogs so zhes pa gcig kyang gzhag tu med cing, tshad ma thams cad la skur pa 'debs pas na shin tu mi 'thad pa'o
gru.english: But if you do take this interpretation of the matter as what the lines are referring to, and say that they draw into question the principle of things being confirmed with accurate perception, it doesn't seem as though you have a single concept to point to which you from your side would say represented your stand on the question. And it would be a massive error to discount each and every form of accurate perception.

gru.acip: DE LTAR NA MI SREG PA DANG SREG PA'I REG BYA GNYIS KA LCAGS GONG GCIG PU DE'I REG BYAR NI BYA DGOS LA, LUS SHES TSAD MA GNYIS GCIG GIS GRUB PA'I REG BYA CIG SHOS KYIS GRUB PA NI MIN PAS GNYIS KA TSAD MAR KHAS BLANGS KYANG TSAD MA GCIG GIS GRUB PA CIG SHOS KYIS 'GOG PA MIN NO,,
gru.wylie: de ltar na mi sreg pa dang sreg pa'i reg bya gnyis ka lcags gong gcig pu de'i reg byar ni bya dgos la, lus shes tshad ma gnyis gcig gis grub pa'i reg bya cig shos kyis grub pa ni min pas gnyis ka tshad mar khas blangs kyang tshad ma gcig gis grub pa cig shos kyis 'gog pa min no
gru.english: As such, we would have to say that both tangible objects—not being burning, and being burning—must be tangible objects of the single length of steel. And we can say that, of these two different accurate perceptions of the awareness of the tangible, one is confirming a tangible object which by the other is not confirmed; and that, as such, we would have to accept both as being accurate. It is not though the case that the confirmation by one accurate perception would have to invalidate the other.

gru.acip: DE GNYIS KA CHU KLUNG GCIG GI CHA SHAS RE YIN PAS, YI DVAGS KYI MIG SHES TSAD MAS GRUB PA'I DON DANG, MI'I MIG SHES TSAD MAS GRUB PA'I DON GNYIS KYANG DNGOS PO SO SO BA YIN PAS DE GNYIS GCIG GIS GRUB PA'I DON DE NYID, CIG SHOS KYIS DE'I BZLOG PHYOGS SU GRUB PA GA LA YIN,
gru.wylie: de gnyis ka chu klung gcig gi cha shas re yin pas, yi dvags kyi mig shes tshad mas grub pa'i don dang, mi'i mig shes tshad mas grub pa'i don gnyis kyang dngos po so so ba yin pas de gnyis gcig gis grub pa'i don de nyid, cig shos kyis de'i bzlog phyogs su grub pa ga la yin
gru.english: Each one of the two represents a section of a single stream of water; and we can also say that the object as confirmed by the accurate perception of the craving spirit's visual consciousness, and the object as confirmed by the accurate perception of the human being's visual consciousness—these two—are discrete entities in their own right. How then could one ever assert that these two were such that the very object confirmed by one were the incompatible opposite of that confirmed by the other?

gru.acip: SNGAR RGYAS PAR BSHAD PA RNAMS KYI DON MDOR BSDU NA SHES BYA RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA MED PA JI LTA BA DE BZHIN DU SHES BYA'I RNAM PA CAN GYI BLO YANG RANG GI BDAG NYID KYIS SKYES PA MED CES DON 'DI SHES PAR GYIS SHING GCES GSUNGS PAS,
gru.wylie: sngar rgyas par bshad pa rnams kyi don mdor bsdu na shes bya rang bzhin gyis grub pa med pa ji lta ba de bzhin du shes bya'i rnam pa can gyi blo yang rang gi bdag nyid kyis skyes pa med ces don 'di shes par gyis shing gces gsungs pas
gru.english: Suppose then we were to summarize the points that we have covered in detail so far. The fact is that there is nothing in the universe which exists through some nature of its own. Just so, there is no state of mind which takes on the aspect of these existing entities which could arise in & of itself. This, the root text is telling us, is the point which we need to understand.

gru.acip: GNYIS PA LA BZHI, GZHAN DBANG GI SGRUB BYED RANG RIG DGAG PA, SEMS TZAM PA'I LUGS BDEN PA GNYIS CHAR LAS NYAMS PAR BSTAN PA, DES NA KLU SGRUB KYI LUGS KHO NA'I RJES SU 'BRANG BAR RIGS PA, GZHAN DBANG DANG 'JIG RTEN PA'I THA SNYAD 'GOG PA GNYIS MI MTSUNGS PAR BSTAN PA'O,,
gru.wylie: gnyis pa la bzhi, gzhan dbang gi sgrub byed rang rig dgag pa, sems tsam pa'i lugs bden pa gnyis char las nyams par bstan pa, des na klu sgrub kyi lugs kho na'i rjes su 'brang bar rigs pa, gzhan dbang dang 'jig rten pa'i tha snyad 'gog pa gnyis mi mtshungs par bstan pa'o
gru.english: Here next is the second general part of this discussion: denying the accurate perception which is supposed to prove that dominated things exist through some nature of their own. We proceed in four steps: a denial of apperception, which is used to establish dominated entities; a demonstration that the Mind Only system fails from the viewpoint of both of the realities; a description of how—therefore—it is appropriate to follow the system of Arya Nagarjuna, exclusively; and showing that denying dominated entities and denying the verbiage of the world are not equivalent.

gru.acip: DANG PO LA BZHI, GZHAN DBANG GI SGRUB BYED DRIS NAS DE MI 'THAD PAR BSTAN PA, DE 'THAD PA'I GZHAN GYI LAN DGAG PA, RIGS PA GZHAN GYIS KYANG RANG RIG MI 'THAD PAR BSTAN PA, GZHAN DBANG RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA MO GSHAM KYI BU DANG MTSUNGS PAR BSTAN PA'O, ,DANG PO NI,
gru.wylie: dang po la bzhi, gzhan dbang gi sgrub byed dris nas de mi 'thad par bstan pa, de 'thad pa'i gzhan gyi lan dgag pa, rigs pa gzhan gyis kyang rang rig mi 'thad par bstan pa, gzhan dbang rang bzhin gyis grub pa mo gsham kyi bu dang mtshungs par bstan pa'o, ,dang po ni
gru.english: The first of these steps has four parts of its own. These are (1) a request for proof to substantiate the existence of dominated entities, and then a demonstration that the attempted proof is incorrect; (2) a denial of the response by others that the proof is indeed correct; (3) a demonstration that apperception is illogical even according to other proofs; and (4) establishing that dominated entities which existed through some nature of their own would be the equivalent of the child of a barren woman.

gru.acip: DE LTAR PHYI ROL MED PAR RNAM SHES PA MI SRID PAR BSTAN NAS, DA NI PHYI ROL MED PAS KHYAD PAR DU MA BYAS PA'I GZHAN DBANG GI DNGOS PO TZAM ZHIG RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA DGAG PA'I PHYIR BSHAD PA,
gru.wylie: de ltar phyi rol med par rnam shes pa mi srid par bstan nas, da ni phyi rol med pas khyad par du ma byas pa'i gzhan dbang gi dngos po tsam zhig rang bzhin gyis grub pa dgag pa'i phyir bshad pa
gru.english: We have demonstrated, then, that a kind of consciousness which could have no outer objects would be impossible. We will now give an explanation which is meant to deny that the simple form of entities which are dominated—meaning, when we do not distinguish these as not being outer objects—could exist through any nature of their own.

gru.acip: SHES PA DE NI RANG LAS DON GZHAN PA'I SHES PAS KYANG 'DZIN PA MA YIN TE, SEMS TZAM PA RANG GI GRUB MTHA' DANG 'GAL BA'I PHYIR TE, GAL TE 'BRAS BU'I GNAS GYUR MA THOB PA'I SKABS SU RNAM PAR RIG PA DON GZHAN CIG RNAM PAR RIG PA'I SNANG YUL YIN NA RNAM PAR RIG PA TZAM NYID DU SMRA BA NYAMS PAR 'GYUR RO, ZHES SEMS TZAM GYI GZHUNG LAS 'BYUNG BA'I PHYIR RO,,
gru.wylie: shes pa de ni rang las don gzhan pa'i shes pas kyang 'dzin pa ma yin te, sems tsam pa rang gi grub mtha' dang 'gal ba'i phyir te, gal te 'bras bu'i gnas gyur ma thob pa'i skabs su rnam par rig pa don gzhan cig rnam par rig pa'i snang yul yin na rnam par rig pa tsam nyid du smra ba nyams par 'gyur ro, zhes sems tsam gyi gzhung las 'byung ba'i phyir ro
gru.english: It is not by the way the case that this particular state of mind is being held by a state of mind which is different from it; for that would contradict the Mind Only's own school of thought. This is because we see, in the great books of the Mind Only themselves, sentiments like “You would lose your status as a person who is professing that things are awareness alone, if you were to say that, even before this entity had reached that point where it had become a result, one state of awareness could act as the object which that same state of awareness were taking as its aspect of focus.”

gru.acip: [VI.73a] ,DE NYID KYIS DE MYONG BAR 'GRUB MA YIN,
gru.wylie: [vi.73a] ,de nyid kyis de myong bar 'grub ma yin
gru.english: This particular one Is not something That could establish these, By experiencing them.

gru.acip: SHES PA DE NYID KYIS DE MYONG BAR GRUB PA MA YIN NO,,
gru.wylie: shes pa de nyid kyis de myong bar grub pa ma yin no
gru.english: But then we would say that this particular state of mind is not something that could establish these, by experiencing them.

gru.acip: SEMS TZAM PAS GZHAN DBANG GZUNG 'DZIN RDZAS GZHAN GYI KUN BRTAGS KYIS STONG PAR BSGRUBS PA NA, SHES PA GZHAN DBANG NI GNYIS SNANG GIS DBEN PA'I NGO BO RIG PAR 'BYUNG BA'I RANG RIG GRUB NA, DE NAS GZHI DE GZUNG 'DZIN RDZAS GZHAN DU MED PA SHES KYI, DE LTAR SNGON DU GZHI DE RANG RIG GIS MA GRUB NA, DE GZHIR BZUNG NAS KUN BRTAGS KYIS STONG PA MI 'GRUB BO ZHES BSHAD DE,
gru.wylie: sems tsam pas gzhan dbang gzung 'dzin rdzas gzhan gyi kun brtags kyis stong par bsgrubs pa na, shes pa gzhan dbang ni gnyis snang gis dben pa'i ngo bo rig par 'byung ba'i rang rig grub na, de nas gzhi de gzung 'dzin rdzas gzhan du med pa shes kyi, de ltar sngon du gzhi de rang rig gis ma grub na, de gzhir bzung nas kun brtags kyis stong pa mi 'grub bo zhes bshad de
gru.english: That is, suppose that those of the Mind Only are trying to prove that dominated entities are devoid of constructs, in the sense of an object held and a holding consciousness which could be materially different from one another. If they can establish a state of apperception which can perceive that the nature of the dominated entity of awareness is to be devoid of any duality of object & subject, then we could understand that this base entity had no quality where objects & subjects were materially different. And they would say that if we take this as the base we could never establish that it was empty of these constructs.

gru.acip: KHYOD KYI LTAR NA GZHAN DBANG GI SGRUB BYED GNYIS SNANG DANG BRAL BA'I RANG RIG GIS GRUB DGOS PA LA, DE MI 'GRUB CES BKAG GO
gru.wylie: khyod kyi ltar na gzhan dbang gi sgrub byed gnyis snang dang bral ba'i rang rig gis grub dgos pa la, de mi 'grub ces bkag go
gru.english: That is, this master is making his denial by saying that—according to you—the support for dominated entities would have to be established by an apperception which was free of all duality; whereas it is not so established.

gru.acip: 'DIR KHA CIG GIS TE SEMS TZAM PAS MDO SDE PA'I PHYOGS KHAS BLANGS NAS RANG RIG BSGRUB PA'I PHYIR, JI LTAR ME NI SKYES PA NYID NA RANG DANG BUM PA LA SOGS PA DAG RIM GYIS GNYIS SU GSAL BA LA MI 'JUG PAR CIG CAR GSAL BAR BYED LA,
gru.wylie: 'dir kha cig gis te sems tsam pas mdo sde pa'i phyogs khas blangs nas rang rig bsgrub pa'i phyir, ji ltar me ni skyes pa nyid na rang dang bum pa la sogs pa dag rim gyis gnyis su gsal ba la mi 'jug par cig car gsal bar byed la
gru.english: On this point, some make the following assertion: Those of the Mind Only accept the position of the Sutrists on this point, and give the following description to substantiate the existence of apperception. Think of how—when a fire starts—it illuminates both itself and something like a vase at the same instant; it is not the case that it acts in stages, first illuminating itself and then only afterwards illuminating the vase or whatever it may be.

gru.acip: CI'I PHYIR ZHE NA, SNGAR NYAMS SU MA MYONG BA LA DRAN PA SKYE MI SRID PAS DRAN PA NI SNGAR GYI NYAMS SU MYONG BA'I YUL CAN YIN NA, KHYOD RANG RIG MI 'DOD PA LTAR NA SNGAR GYI SNGO 'DZIN LTA BU'I SHES PA YANG RANG DUS SU NYAMS SU MA MYONG BAS, PHYIS KYI DRAN PA YOD PAR MI 'GRUB BO,,
gru.wylie: ci'i phyir zhe na, sngar nyams su ma myong ba la dran pa skye mi srid pas dran pa ni sngar gyi nyams su myong ba'i yul can yin na, khyod rang rig mi 'dod pa ltar na sngar gyi sngo 'dzin lta bu'i shes pa yang rang dus su nyams su ma myong bas, phyis kyi dran pa yod par mi 'grub bo
gru.english: And why is that? It is impossible for us to have a memory of something that we have not experienced earlier on. As such, memory is a subject state of mind which holds as its object a previous experience. According to you all though—those of you who do not accept the concept of apperception—a previous perception such as having perceived a patch of blue could not have experienced this object within its own time, which means that you cannot say that there was a later memory.

gru.acip: 'DIS NI SNGAR GYI SNGO 'DZIN DE LA MYONG BA YOD PAR PHYIS DE DRAN PA'I RTAGS LAS SGRUB PA YIN TE, SNGAR GYI SNGO 'DZIN LA RANG MYONG BA'I RANG RIG YOD DE ZHES SGRUB NA NI, GZHAN LA GRUB PA'I DPE MI SNYED PAS DE LTAR MI SGRUB BO,,
gru.wylie: 'dis ni sngar gyi sngo 'dzin de la myong ba yod par phyis de dran pa'i rtags las sgrub pa yin te, sngar gyi sngo 'dzin la rang myong ba'i rang rig yod de zhes sgrub na ni, gzhan la grub pa'i dpe mi snyed pas de ltar mi sgrub bo
gru.english: What this is saying is that the existence of an earlier experience with the perception of blue is proven from the logical reason that we have a memory of it later. If we were to phrase it like “during that previous perception of blue, there was present an occurrence of apperception which experienced this perception, because…” one would be unable to find a common example that the other party accepted as valid; so this is not how this would be proven.

gru.acip: SNGO 'DZIN LA MYONG BA YOD PAR GRUB NA NI, DE'I MYONG BA LA RANG GIS DANG GZHAN GYIS MYONG BA GNYIS SU KHA TSON BCAD NAS DANG PO KHYOD LA MI RUNG LA, GNYIS PA RANG LUGS KYIS BKAG PA NA MYONG BA'I KHYAB BYED KHEGS PA NA, MYONG BA TZAM YANG MI 'THAD PAR 'GYUR RO
gru.wylie: sngo 'dzin la myong ba yod par grub na ni, de'i myong ba la rang gis dang gzhan gyis myong ba gnyis su kha tshon bcad nas dang po khyod la mi rung la, gnyis pa rang lugs kyis bkag pa na myong ba'i khyab byed khegs pa na, myong ba tsam yang mi 'thad par 'gyur ro
gru.english: If we are seeking to prove that there exists an experience of a perception of blue, then we can narrow the possibilities down to two: either this perception experiences itself, or something else experiences it. According to you, the first would be incorrect. But if the second were denied by our own system, then we would be denying the general entire category of the possibility of experience. In this case then, any experience at all would become incorrect here.

gru.acip: ZHES 'GOG PA YIN TE, RANG RIG SGRUB PA'I RIGS PA DRAG SHOS YIN NO,,
gru.wylie: zhes 'gog pa yin te, rang rig sgrub pa'i rigs pa drag shos yin no
gru.english: The denial presented thus actually represents the very best attempt at a reasoning to establish the existence of apperception.

gru.acip: MI DGOS NA SHES PA SNGA MA LA YANG MI DGOS PAR 'GYUR LA, DGOS NA DE LA YANG GZHAN DGOS PAS THUG PA MED PA'I SKYON DU 'GYUR ZHING, THUG MED DU SONG NA NI SNGO 'DZIN DANG PO LA MYONG BA MI GRUB PA'I SKYON YOD DO,,
gru.wylie: mi dgos na shes pa snga ma la yang mi dgos par 'gyur la, dgos na de la yang gzhan dgos pas thug pa med pa'i skyon du 'gyur zhing, thug med du song na ni sngo 'dzin dang po la myong ba mi grub pa'i skyon yod do
gru.english: If you say that this following state of mind were not required, then it wouldn't be required either with the state of mind previous to it. If it were required, then yet another state of mind would be required, and you'd have the problem that the process would become endless. And if it did become endless, then you'd have the problem that there was nothing you could establish as experiencing the first perception of blue.

gru.acip: SHIN TU MI RIGS TE, RANG RIG SGRUB PA'I MDO SDE PA DANG SEMS TZAM PAS NI SEMS CAN RNAMS NI RNAM PAR SHES PA'I RGYUD RE RE BA'O,
gru.wylie: shin tu mi rigs te, rang rig sgrub pa'i mdo sde pa dang sems tsam pas ni sems can rnams ni rnam par shes pa'i rgyud re re ba'o
gru.english: And yet this would be wrong in the extreme, for the Sutrists and members of the Mind Only who seek to prove the existence of apperception would say that living beings have flows of consciousness that are discrete from one another.

gru.acip: RANG RIG SGRUB MKHAN DE GNYIS KYIS 'JUG PA MYUR BA CIG CAR DU 'KHRUL BA'I RGYU YIN PA YANG RNAM 'GREL DU BKAG PAS NA, GZHUNG 'DI DE GNYIS KYI LUGS SU 'JOG DKA' BAR SNANG STE
gru.wylie: rang rig sgrub mkhan de gnyis kyis 'jug pa myur ba cig car du 'khrul ba'i rgyu yin pa yang rnam 'grel du bkag pas na, gzhung 'di de gnyis kyi lugs su 'jog dka' bar snang ste
gru.english: As for these two groups though who are trying to establish the existence of apperception, the fact is that the Commentary on Accurate Perception denies this idea about the speed of their engagement being the cause of mistaking these awarenesses as being simultaneous. As such, it would seem that in the system of these two groups there is some difficulty in establishing the meaning of this classical source.

gru.acip: DE LTAR RANG MYONG BA'I RANG RIG YOD NA YANG GZHAN DBANG YOD PAR RANG RIG DES 'GRUB PAS, 'DI NI YOD PAR GANG GIS SHES PAR 'GYUR, ZHES DBU MA PAS DRIS PA LA LAN 'DI NYE BAR BSTAN PA YIN NO, ZHES SMRA'O,,
gru.wylie: de ltar rang myong ba'i rang rig yod na yang gzhan dbang yod par rang rig des 'grub pas, 'di ni yod par gang gis shes par 'gyur, zhes dbu ma pas dris pa la lan 'di nye bar bstan pa yin no, zhes smra'o
gru.english: And so what's being said in this entire section is the following. Thus—given that there exists a state of apperception which can experience itself—then this apperception can be used to establish the existence of dominated entities; and this is the reply which is presented in response to the question of those of the Middle Way school when they said, “What is it that allows you to say that this state of mind exists?” Assumptions from recollection

gru.acip: [VI.73b] ,GAL TE PHYI DUS DRAN PA LAS 'GRUB NA, ,MA GRUB BSGRUB PAR BYA PHYIR BRJOD PA YI, ,MA GRUB 'DI NI SGRUB PAR BYED PA MIN,
gru.wylie: [vi.73b] ,gal te phyi dus dran pa las 'grub na, ,ma grub bsgrub par bya phyir brjod pa yi, ,ma grub 'di ni sgrub par byed pa min
gru.english: Suppose we were To establish it From recollection At a later time. They are Bringing it up In order to substantiate That which has not yet Been established. The fact that this Does not exist Is not something Which serves to establish it.

gru.acip: GAL TE RDZAS RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PA'I DBANG DU BYAS NAS PHYIS KYI DUS KYI DRAN PA LAS, DRAN YUL GYI SHES PA SNGA MA RANG RIG PAR 'GRUB NA, PHYIR RGOL LA RANG RIG MA GRUB PA BSGRUB PAR BYA BA'I PHYIR DU, BRJOD PA YI DRAN PA RANG BZHIN GYIS YOD PAR MA GRUB PA 'DI NI, RANG RIG SGRUB PAR BYED PA MIN TE, SGRA MI RTAG PAR SGRUB PA LA MIG GI GZUNG BYA BZHIN NO,,
gru.wylie: gal te rdzas rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub pa'i dbang du byas nas phyis kyi dus kyi dran pa las, dran yul gyi shes pa snga ma rang rig par 'grub na, phyir rgol la rang rig ma grub pa bsgrub par bya ba'i phyir du, brjod pa yi dran pa rang bzhin gyis yod par ma grub pa 'di ni, rang rig sgrub par byed pa min te, sgra mi rtag par sgrub pa la mig gi gzung bya bzhin no
gru.english: Suppose then that—with reference to a substance which existed by definition—we were to establish the existence of a previous case of apperception, an awareness of the original object we are now remembering, from the presence of a recollection at a later time. Here, the opponent in the debate is bringing up a state of recollection in order to substantiate the existence of an apperception which has not yet been established. And yet the fact that this recollection does not exist through any nature of its own is not something which serves to establish the apperception here; it would be like saying that sound is a changing thing because it is an object which the eye perceives.

gru.acip: CI'I PHYIR ZHE NA, GAL TE 'DIR MI GRUB NA DU BA DE'I 'BRAS BUR SHES PAR 'GYUR BA BZHIN DU, RANG RIG GRUB NA DE LAS DRAN PA 'BYUNG BA'I 'BREL PA GRUB NA, DRAN PA LAS RANG RIG YOD PAR NGES PAR 'GYUR BA ZHIG NA, RANG RIG DE DA DUNG DU YANG PHYIR RGOL LA MA GRUB PAS, RANG RIG GI 'BRAS BU RANG RIG MED PAR MI 'BYUNG BA'I DRAN PA GA LA YOD,
gru.wylie: ci'i phyir zhe na, gal te 'dir mi grub na du ba de'i 'bras bur shes par 'gyur ba bzhin du, rang rig grub na de las dran pa 'byung ba'i 'brel pa grub na, dran pa las rang rig yod par nges par 'gyur ba zhig na, rang rig de da dung du yang phyir rgol la ma grub pas, rang rig gi 'bras bu rang rig med par mi 'byung ba'i dran pa ga la yod
gru.english: And why is that? If the point were not made here, then it would be the same as when we deduce the presence of something from its result, of smoke. If establishing apperception allows us establish a connection to a recollection that occurs from it, then we could confirm the existence of apperception from recollection; but in that case apperception would stil not have been confirmed to the opponent. And as such, how could we ever say that there was a recollection which were a result of apperception, and which could never occur without apperception?

gru.acip: 'BREL PA MED PAR MI 'GRUB PA'I DPE NI, CHU TZAM DANG ME TZAM MTHONG BA LAS NOR BU CHU SHEL DANG ME SHEL DPOG PA NI MA YIN TE, DE GNYIS MED PAR YANG CHAR LA SOGS PA DANG, GTZUB SHING GTZUB PA SOGS LAS CHU DANG ME DAG 'BYUNG BA'I PHYIR RO,,
gru.wylie: 'brel pa med par mi 'grub pa'i dpe ni, chu tsam dang me tsam mthong ba las nor bu chu shel dang me shel dpog pa ni ma yin te, de gnyis med par yang char la sogs pa dang, gtsub shing gtsub pa sogs las chu dang me dag 'byung ba'i phyir ro
gru.english: What are some examples of a failure to occur without a connection? We cannot for example deduce the presence of the precious stones water crystal or fire crystal from seeing only water, or only fire. This is because water and fire can also occur in the absence of these minerals; for example, from rain or the like, or from “fire sticks” that are rubbed together to help start a fire.

gru.acip: DGAG PA 'DI LA LAN DU DRAN PA DANG RANG RIG MED {%ME} DU BZHIN DU RGYU 'BRAS SU BSGRUBS PA'I SGO NAS, DRAN PAS RANG RIG DPOG PA MIN GYI, SNGAR BSHAD PA LTAR DRAN PAS SNGAR GYI SHES PA LA MYONG BA YOD PAR DPOG LA,
gru.wylie: dgag pa 'di la lan du dran pa dang rang rig med {%me} du bzhin du rgyu 'bras su bsgrubs pa'i sgo nas, dran pas rang rig dpog pa min gyi, sngar bshad pa ltar dran pas sngar gyi shes pa la myong ba yod par dpog la
gru.english: For a reply to this denial, we can say that when you try to use a proof based on recollection and apperception being cause and effect in the way that fire and smoke are, it's not the case that we can deduce apperception from recollection; rather, as we explained before, recollection helps us deduce the fact that the mind had a previous experience.

gru.acip: DE LA RANG GIS DANG GZHAN GYIS MYONG BA GNYIS SU BCAD NAS BKAG PA NA, RANG GIS RANG MYONG BA 'GRUB BO ZHES SMRA MOD KYANG SHES PAS RIG PA LA MDO SDE PA DANG SEMS TZAM PAS BZHAG PA DE GNYIS SU KHA TSON MA CHOD PA'I PHYIR TE,
gru.wylie: de la rang gis dang gzhan gyis myong ba gnyis su bcad nas bkag pa na, rang gis rang myong ba 'grub bo zhes smra mod kyang shes pas rig pa la mdo sde pa dang sems tsam pas bzhag pa de gnyis su kha tshon ma chod pa'i phyir te
gru.english: Suppose we were to attempt making the denial here by eliminating both the possibility that the mind was experienced by itself, and by something else. Now you could say that the determination was made by the mind's knowing itself, but in fact when the Sutrists and the Mind Only present how it is that awareness knows things, they would not make the division into those two possibilities.

gru.acip: ,RANG RIG PA NI GRUB LA RAG MOD KYI, ,DE LTA'ANG DRAN PA'I DRAN PA RIGS MIN TE, ,GZHAN PHYIR MA SHES RGYUD LA SKYES PA BZHIN, ,GTAN TSIGS 'DIS NI KHYAD PAR DAG KYANG 'JOMS,
gru.wylie: rang rig pa ni grub la rag mod kyi, ,de lta'ang dran pa'i dran pa rigs min te, ,gzhan phyir ma shes rgyud la skyes pa bzhin, ,gtan tshigs 'dis ni khyad par dag kyang 'joms
gru.english: In the end, your proofs Are going to rely upon It knowing itself; But it is still Not logical For recollection To recall, Because they are Other than each other. It's the same as What could have arisen In the mindstream of one Who has not known; That logical statement Would also obviate details.

gru.acip: CI STE DE LTAR RNAM PAR DPYOD PA BTANG NAS KYANG, SHES PAS RANG GI BDAG NYID RIG PA DANG, YUL RIG PAR BYED PA NI GRUB LA RAG MOD KYI STE GRUB TU CHUG KYANG, DRAN PA'I SHES PAS YUL DANG YUL CAN DE DAG DRAN PA NI RIGS PA MIN TE, PHYIS KYI DRAN SHES DANG SNGAR GYI YUL MYONG GI SHES PA GNYIS RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA'I GZHAN NYID DU KHYED KYIS KHAS BLANGS PA'I PHYIR RO,,
gru.wylie: ci ste de ltar rnam par dpyod pa btang nas kyang, shes pas rang gi bdag nyid rig pa dang, yul rig par byed pa ni grub la rag mod kyi ste grub tu chug kyang, dran pa'i shes pas yul dang yul can de dag dran pa ni rigs pa min te, phyis kyi dran shes dang sngar gyi yul myong gi shes pa gnyis rang bzhin gyis grub pa'i gzhan nyid du khyed kyis khas blangs pa'i phyir ro
gru.english: You may undertake some different forms of examination, but in the end your proofs are going to rely upon the idea of a state of mind knowing itself—its own self—and also knowing the particular object. But still it is not logical to say that the state of mind of recollection can recall both the subject and the object involved. And this is simply because you have accepted the idea that both the later recollecting state of mind and the earlier awareness which perceived the object are objects that are other than each other and which exist through some nature of their own.

gru.acip: DE BZHIN DU, SNGAR MA SHES PA STE MA MYONG BA'I RGYUD LA SKYES PA BZHIN DU RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA'I GZHAN YIN PA'I PHYIR NA, RANG GI RGYUD DU GTOGS PA'I RNAM PAR SHES PA DUS PHYIS 'BYUNG BAS KYANG SHES PA DANG DON DAG NYAMS SU MA MYONG BA'I PHYIR DRAN PAR MI 'GYUR RO,,
gru.wylie: de bzhin du, sngar ma shes pa ste ma myong ba'i rgyud la skyes pa bzhin du rang bzhin gyis grub pa'i gzhan yin pa'i phyir na, rang gi rgyud du gtogs pa'i rnam par shes pa dus phyis 'byung bas kyang shes pa dang don dag nyams su ma myong ba'i phyir dran par mi 'gyur ro
gru.english: The case here is the same as with what could have arisen in the mindstream of a person who has not known or had a certain experience. Because this person constitutes an “other” who exists through their own nature, even if a state of awareness taken in by their mindstream were to occur later on, there would be no recollection here, since they had not undergone an experience of the state of mind and corresponding object.

gru.acip: SA MYUG LTA BU'I NYER LEN GYI RGYU 'BRAS LA RANG MTSAN GYIS GRUB PA'I GZHAN DU 'DZIN PA, 'JIG RTEN GYI BLO RANG DGA' BA LA MED PA YANG SNGAR BSHAD ZIN PAS SNGAR GYI YUL MYONG DANG PHYIS KYI DRAN PA'I RGYU 'BRAS LA YANG, 'JIG RTEN PA'I BLO LHAN SKYES LA RANG MTSAN GYIS GRUB PA'I GZHAN DU 'DZIN PA MED DO,,
gru.wylie: sa myug lta bu'i nyer len gyi rgyu 'bras la rang mtshan gyis grub pa'i gzhan du 'dzin pa, 'jig rten gyi blo rang dga' ba la med pa yang sngar bshad zin pas sngar gyi yul myong dang phyis kyi dran pa'i rgyu 'bras la yang, 'jig rten pa'i blo lhan skyes la rang mtshan gyis grub pa'i gzhan du 'dzin pa med do
gru.english: There is not even any normal state of mind of a person in the everyday world which—with regard to cause & effect in the sense of a material cause such as a seed for a plant producing a sprout—would hold to the idea that these things were other than each other, by definition. Further, as we have already explained, there is no tendency for the natural state of mind of people in the world to hold to things as being other than each other by definition, in the case of the cause & effect represented by the earlier experience of an object and a later recollection.

gru.acip: RANG 'GREL LAS RDZAS RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PA'I RANG RIG DANG DRAN PA BKAG PA'I 'OG TU, 'ON TE 'JIG RTEN GYI THA SNYAD KYI DBANG DU YIN NA NI, DE LTA NA YANG RANG RIG PA'I RGYU CAN GYI DRAN PA MI SRID PA NYID DO,
gru.wylie: rang 'grel las rdzas rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub pa'i rang rig dang dran pa bkag pa'i 'og tu, 'on te 'jig rten gyi tha snyad kyi dbang du yin na ni, de lta na yang rang rig pa'i rgyu can gyi dran pa mi srid pa nyid do
gru.english: Subsequent to denying both apperception and recollection that could exist substantially—by definition—the autocommentary states, “But even if you were to restrict yourself to the terminology of the everyday world, still a recollection that had, as its cause, apperception would be completely impossible.”

gru.acip: GZHAN GYI LUGS KYIS MYONG DRAN DANG DE'I DUS KYI YUL GNYIS RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PA'I GZHAN DU 'JOG PAS, MYONG DRAN GNYIS YUL GCIG PA DANG DE GNYIS RGYUD GCIG TU 'DOD MOS KYANG DER 'JOG MI NUS PA NI SNGAR MANG DU BSHAD ZIN TO,,
gru.wylie: gzhan gyi lugs kyis myong dran dang de'i dus kyi yul gnyis rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub pa'i gzhan du 'jog pas, myong dran gnyis yul gcig pa dang de gnyis rgyud gcig tu 'dod mos kyang der 'jog mi nus pa ni sngar mang du bshad zin to
gru.english: The other party in the debate here posits things which are other than each other which also exist be definition, with both the original experience and the recollection; as well as with the two objects of each of these, in their own time. And admittedly one may assert that the two of the experience and the recollection share the same object; and that the pair constitute part of a single stream of awareness; but we have gone in to some great detail already to show how one might fail to establish this.

gru.acip: 'DI NI SPYIR PHYIS KYI RNAM SHES KYI DRAN PA MI 'THAD PAR THAL, SNGAR GYI RNAM SHES DES RANG GIS RANG MA MYONG BA'I PHYIR, ZHES PA LA KHYAB MA GRUB KYI LAN BTAB PA YIN PAS, SPYOD 'JUG GI DGONGS PA NI THA SNYAD DU RANG RIG 'GOG PA MIN ZHES PA NI RGYAL SRAS CHEN PO'I BZHED PA GTAN MIN NO,,
gru.wylie: 'di ni spyir phyis kyi rnam shes kyi dran pa mi 'thad par thal, sngar gyi rnam shes des rang gis rang ma myong ba'i phyir, zhes pa la khyab ma grub kyi lan btab pa yin pas, spyod 'jug gi dgongs pa ni tha snyad du rang rig 'gog pa min zhes pa ni rgyal sras chen po'i bzhed pa gtan min no
gru.english: Generally speaking, this reasoning is a reply of “that's not necessarily the case” to the argument that it must be incorrect to say that we have a later recollection of a state of mind, since earlier on this state of mind did not experience itself by itself. As such, it is not at all the position of his great child of the Victors to say that it was not the intent of The Guide to deny apperception, in a nominal sense. Rejecting rebuttal about direct accurate perception

gru.acip: DE LA YUL DRAN PA NYID KYIS YUL CAN YANG DRAN PAS, YUL CAN DRAN PA ZUR PA MI DGOS PA BZHIN DU SNGO 'DZIN LTA BU'I YUL SNGON PO GRUB PA NYID KYIS SNGON PO 'JAL BYED 'GRUB KYI, SNGON PO 'GRUB TSUL LAS GZHAN PA'I SNGON PO 'JAL BYED 'GRUB TSUL MI DGOS SO,,
gru.wylie: de la yul dran pa nyid kyis yul can yang dran pas, yul can dran pa zur pa mi dgos pa bzhin du sngo 'dzin lta bu'i yul sngon po grub pa nyid kyis sngon po 'jal byed 'grub kyi, sngon po 'grub tshul las gzhan pa'i sngon po 'jal byed 'grub tshul mi dgos so
gru.english: Here we can start by saying that the recollection of an object itself also recalls the original subject state of mind. As such, there is no need for a different, additional recollection of that subject. That is, the very establishment of the object—the patch of blue, say, for a perception of blue—establishes the state of mind which took the blue under consideration. It is not though as if we would require some way of establishing the state of mind which took the blue under consideration which were different from the way we were establishing the blue itself.

gru.acip: DE YANG SNGON POS SNGO 'DZIN LA RANG 'DRA'I RNAM PA GTAD PA SHAR BA NYID KYIS, SNGON PO 'GRUB PA NI LUGS GZHAN DANG YANG 'DRA'O,,
gru.wylie: de yang sngon pos sngo 'dzin la rang 'dra'i rnam pa gtad pa shar ba nyid kyis, sngon po 'grub pa ni lugs gzhan dang yang 'dra'o
gru.english: That is, when the blue directs the particular aspect that reflects it towards the perception of the blue, the very manifestation of this perception is sufficient to establish the existence of that blue—this much is similar in other schools of thought as well.

gru.acip: 'ON KYANG MI 'DRA BA NI SNGO 'DZIN DE 'GRUB PA NA GNYIS SNANG DANG BRAL BA'I 'DZIN RNAM YAN GAR BA MYONG BA'I RANG RIG GI SGO NAS 'GRUB PA YIN LA, DE YANG SHES PA THAMS CAD LA 'DRA BAR LUGS GZHAN DAG 'DOD LA,
gru.wylie: 'on kyang mi 'dra ba ni sngo 'dzin de 'grub pa na gnyis snang dang bral ba'i 'dzin rnam yan gar ba myong ba'i rang rig gi sgo nas 'grub pa yin la, de yang shes pa thams cad la 'dra bar lugs gzhan dag 'dod la
gru.english: A point on which the presentations diverge here though is where certain other systems would say that—when they establish the existence of the perception of the blue—they must do so by pointing to an apperception which experiences a discrete aspect of perceiving which is devoid of all duality between subject & object. And they would say that this is the same for all other states of mind.

gru.acip: 'DIR NI DBU MA SNYING PO DANG BDEN GNYIS RTZA 'GREL LAS GSUNGS PA BZHIN DU DE 'DRA BA'I 'DZIN RNAM YAN GAR BA MI SRID PAR BZHED PAS, DE MYONG BA'I RANG RIG GIS MI 'GRUB KYI, SNGON PO GRUB PA NYID KYIS SNGO 'DZIN DE 'GRUB STE,
gru.wylie: 'dir ni dbu ma snying po dang bden gnyis rtsa 'grel las gsungs pa bzhin du de 'dra ba'i 'dzin rnam yan gar ba mi srid par bzhed pas, de myong ba'i rang rig gis mi 'grub kyi, sngon po grub pa nyid kyis sngo 'dzin de 'grub ste
gru.english: On this, we would ourselves take the same position here as that expressed in Heart of the Middle Way and both the root text and commentary to the Two Realities—which say that it is impossible for there to be any such discrete aspect of perceiving. As such, we cannot say that there is established any state of apperception which would further establish the subject here; rather, it is simply establishing that the blue itself is present, which establishes the presence of the perception of this blue.

gru.acip: TZAM GYIS ZHES PA NI SEMS TZAM PA DANG MDO SDE PA 'DOD PA LTAR TSAD MA GZHAL BYA JI 'DRA PA DE 'DRA BA'I RNAM PA'I RJE SU BYED PAS GZHAL BYA 'GRUB LA,
gru.wylie: tsam gyis zhes pa ni sems tsam pa dang mdo sde pa 'dod pa ltar tshad ma gzhal bya ji 'dra pa de 'dra ba'i rnam pa'i rje su byed pas gzhal bya 'grub la
gru.english: When they utilize the word “only” in the citation above, what they're saying is that—according to the beliefs of those who belong to the school of Only Mind, and the Sutrists—the aspect that accurate perceptions take on always follows from the objects they take under consideration, and this then leads to the confirmation of these objects.

gru.acip: DE NAS TSAD MA 'GRUB TSUL NI SNGA MA LAS ZUR DU TSAD MA RANG GI NGO BO LA GNYIS SNANG DANG BRAL BA'I 'DZIN RNAM YAN GAR BA MYONG BA'I RANG RIG GIS 'GRUB PA 'GOG STE, GZHAL BYA 'GRUB PA TZAM GYIS 'GRUB PA'I DON NO,,
gru.wylie: de nas tshad ma 'grub tshul ni snga ma las zur du tshad ma rang gi ngo bo la gnyis snang dang bral ba'i 'dzin rnam yan gar ba myong ba'i rang rig gis 'grub pa 'gog ste, gzhal bya 'grub pa tsam gyis 'grub pa'i don no
gru.english: And so then we can say that this way in which accurate perception is established acts in turn to deny the idea that things could be established by an apperception which undergoes a discrete experience in an aspect of being the perceiver, free of all subject-object duality in its nature—an accurate perception which has a separate experience from the one that came before.

gru.acip: 'DI NI 'PHAGS PA NYID KYIS, ,GAL TE RANG LAS TSAD MA GRUB, ,GZHAL BYA RNAMS LA MA LTOS PAR, ,KHYOD KYI TSAD MA GRUB GYUR 'DIR, ,GZHAN LA MI LTOS RAB GRUB 'GYUR, ZHES GSUNGS PA'I DGONGS PA YIN TE,
gru.wylie: 'di ni 'phags pa nyid kyis, ,gal te rang las tshad ma grub, ,gzhal bya rnams la ma ltos par, ,khyod kyi tshad ma grub gyur 'dir, ,gzhan la mi ltos rab grub 'gyur, zhes gsungs pa'i dgongs pa yin te
gru.english: This is in fact what he had in mind when The Arya himself stated, Suppose this state of mind Were established As an accurate perception All on its own, Without depending Upon the objects It takes under consideration. When you then Are establishing What it is that makes A thing an accurate Form of perception, Your proof itself Is perfectly free Of relying on Anything else at all.

gru.acip: TSAD MA 'GRUB PA LA GZHAL BYA GRUB PA TZAM GYIS MI CHOG PAR TSAD MA RANG LAS TSAD MA 'GRUB PA GZHAN DAG 'DOD PA LTAR YIN NA, GZHAL BYA LA MA LTOS PAR TSAD MA 'GRUB PAR 'GYUR RO,,
gru.wylie: tshad ma 'grub pa la gzhal bya grub pa tsam gyis mi chog par tshad ma rang las tshad ma 'grub pa gzhan dag 'dod pa ltar yin na, gzhal bya la ma ltos par tshad ma 'grub par 'gyur ro
gru.english: Suppose it were as others would have it: suppose that—in order to establish an accurate perception—we could not simply be satisfied by establishing what that perception takes under its consideration. Suppose, as others would have it, that accurate perception is established through accurate perception itself. In that case, something would be established as an accurate perception without relying upon that thing which it takes under consideration.

gru.acip: DE 'DOD NA DNGOS PO RNAMS RGYU RKYEN GZHAN LA MA LTOS PAR RAB TU GRUB PAR 'GYUR RO, ZHES BKAG PAS GZHAL BYA GRUB PA TZAM GYIS TSAD MA GRUB PAR SHUGS KYIS BSTAN NO,,
gru.wylie: de 'dod na dngos po rnams rgyu rkyen gzhan la ma ltos par rab tu grub par 'gyur ro, zhes bkag pas gzhal bya grub pa tsam gyis tshad ma grub par shugs kyis bstan no
gru.english: And if one were to accept that, then functional entities could be established without relying on any other causes or conditions. This is how the denial here is made; as such, what's being said, by implication, is that accurate perceptions are to be established only by establishing those objects which they take under consideration.

gru.acip: DE LTAR NA SNGO 'DZIN NI GZHAN LUGS LTAR RANG RIG GIS MI 'GRUB KYI, DBANG PO'I MNGON SUM TSAD MAS 'GRUB PAR BSTAN TE, DE YOD PA NI SNGO 'DZIN GYIS GZHAL BYA GRUB PA DE NYID KYIS RTOGS PA'I PHYIR RO,,
gru.wylie: de ltar na sngo 'dzin ni gzhan lugs ltar rang rig gis mi 'grub kyi, dbang po'i mngon sum tshad mas 'grub par bstan te, de yod pa ni sngo 'dzin gyis gzhal bya grub pa de nyid kyis rtogs pa'i phyir ro
gru.english: As such, what's being presented here is the idea that the perception of a patch of blue is not—as other schools would have it—established through some apperception; but rather, through a direct form of accurate perception. And the fact that that exists can be grasped from the very fact that the perception of blue confirms its own object of consideration.

gru.acip: DE'I PHYIR TSAD MA GANG YIN THAMS CAD RANG GI GZHAL BYA GRUB PA DE NYID KYIS 'GRUB BO,,
gru.wylie: de'i phyir tshad ma gang yin thams cad rang gi gzhal bya grub pa de nyid kyis 'grub bo
gru.english: And so the fact is that every accurate perception there is, is itself established through the object that it takes under its consideration. Rejecting rebuttal about deductive accurate perception

gru.acip: DE'I PHYIR DBANG PO'I SHES PA 'JIG RTEN RANG DGA' BA LA LTOS PA'I 'KHRUL MA 'KHRUL GANG YIN KYANG, RANG GI GZHAL BYA GRUB PAS YUL CAN 'GRUB BO,,
gru.wylie: de'i phyir dbang po'i shes pa 'jig rten rang dga' ba la ltos pa'i 'khrul ma 'khrul gang yin kyang, rang gi gzhal bya grub pas yul can 'grub bo
gru.english: And so we can say that whether or not a sense perception is mistaken with reference to the normal perceptions of the world, the object that it takes under consideration is established; which means that the subject state of mind is also established.

gru.acip: 'ON KYANG RANG RIG KHAS MI LEN PA LA GZHI DUS KYI YID SHES SNANG BA DANG, ZHEN YUL LA 'KHRUL BA RNAMS YOD PAR MI 'GRUB STE, DE RNAMS LA RANG GI GZHAL BYA 'JAL BAS YUL CAN GRUB PA MED PA'I PHYIR RO ZHE NA,
gru.wylie: 'on kyang rang rig khas mi len pa la gzhi dus kyi yid shes snang ba dang, zhen yul la 'khrul ba rnams yod par mi 'grub ste, de rnams la rang gi gzhal bya 'jal bas yul can grub pa med pa'i phyir ro zhe na
gru.english: One may come then with the following question: But isn't it the case that—with someone who does not accept the idea of apperception—the consciousness of the thought (assuming one is still in their original state of evolution) and types of perception which are mistaken towards what one thinks that they see, cannot be demonstrated to exist? Because it is the case that there is no confirmation of the subject states of mind here, as they take under consideration their particular objects of consideration.

gru.acip: 'DI YANG YID SHES KYI DBANG DU BYAS KYI DBANG SHES KYI TSOR BA GSUM GYIS GZUGS SGRA SOGS YONGS SU GCOD DE, DE'I 'GRUB TSUL NI SNGAR BSHAD PA BZHIN NO,,
gru.wylie: 'di yang yid shes kyi dbang du byas kyi dbang shes kyi tshor ba gsum gyis gzugs sgra sogs yongs su gcod de, de'i 'grub tshul ni sngar bshad pa bzhin no
gru.english: Now the three types of feeling for awareness of the senses relative to the consciousness of the thought discern objects such as visual form and sound; how we establish this follows what we described earlier.

gru.acip: MYONG BYA DANG MYONG BYED THA DAD PA NYID DU SNANG BA'I PHYIR NA PHYOGS SNGA MA'I RANG RIG DANG MI GCIG GO ,DE'I PHYIR BDE BA SOGS NYAMS SU MYONG BAS GRUB PA NYID KYIS TSOR BA GRUB BO,,
gru.wylie: myong bya dang myong byed tha dad pa nyid du snang ba'i phyir na phyogs snga ma'i rang rig dang mi gcig go ,de'i phyir bde ba sogs nyams su myong bas grub pa nyid kyis tshor ba grub bo
gru.english: And so because the thing experienced and the thing experiencing it appear with certainty as separate from one another, what we're describing here is not the same as the apperception accepted by the earlier opponent. As such, we can say that an occurrence of feeling is confirmed by the very fact of there having been an experience of pleasure or the like.

gru.acip: YID SHES KYI NGOR KENG RUS GSAL SNANG SOGS CHOS KYI SKYE MCHED PA'I GZUGS SNANG BA NA, YID SHES LA DE RNAMS KYI RNAM PA SHAR BA'I SGO NAS DES DE RNAMS GRUB PA NA DE 'DZIN GYI SHES PA 'GRUB PA NI SNGAR DANG 'DRA STE, YUL DE RNAMS NI YID KYI SHES PA LAS NGO BO THA DAD PA'O,,
gru.wylie: yid shes kyi ngor keng rus gsal snang sogs chos kyi skye mched pa'i gzugs snang ba na, yid shes la de rnams kyi rnam pa shar ba'i sgo nas des de rnams grub pa na de 'dzin gyi shes pa 'grub pa ni sngar dang 'dra ste, yul de rnams ni yid kyi shes pa las ngo bo tha dad pa'o
gru.english: And so let's say that form which is part of the door of sense of all things makes its appearance, in the form of a vivid image of skeletons for the consciousness of the thought. The consciousness of the thought here confirms these images by way of their having appeared to this consciousness. And then establishing that an awareness is perceiving these objects is accomplished in the same way as we described it before. That is, these objects are essentially separate from the awareness of the thoughts.

gru.acip: BDAG 'DZIN GNYIS LTA BU'I YID SHES KYI SHES PA DE JI LTAR 'GRUB PA NI, TSIG GSAL LAS, GAL TE MTSAN GZHI'AM RANG GI MTSAN NYID DAM SPYI'I MTSAN NYID KYANG RUNG STE, 'JIG RTEN NA YOD NA NI THAMS CAD MNGON SUM DU DMIGS PAR BYA BA YIN PA'I PHYIR LKOG TU MA GYUR BA YIN TE, DE'I PHYIR DE'I YUL CAN GYI RNAM PAR SHES PA DANG LHAN CIG TU MNGON SUM NYID DU RNAM PAR BZHAG GO ,ZHES GSUNGS PA 'DIS SHES PAR BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: bdag 'dzin gnyis lta bu'i yid shes kyi shes pa de ji ltar 'grub pa ni, tshig gsal las, gal te mtshan gzhi'am rang gi mtshan nyid dam spyi'i mtshan nyid kyang rung ste, 'jig rten na yod na ni thams cad mngon sum du dmigs par bya ba yin pa'i phyir lkog tu ma gyur ba yin te, de'i phyir de'i yul can gyi rnam par shes pa dang lhan cig tu mngon sum nyid du rnam par bzhag go ,zhes gsungs pa 'dis shes par bya'o
gru.english: How is it then that we establish perceptions of the consciousness of the thought for things like the two forms of the tendency to believe in some kind of self-existence? The answer to this question can be understood from the following description found in A Clarification of the Verses— It doesn't matter whether we're talking about a defining occurrence of something; or the definition of something; or the general characteristics of the thing. When things are said to exist in the everyday world, then all of them are objects which can be observed directly. As such, they are not what we would call “recondite.” And for this reason, they are established exclusively as being direct, part & parcel with the relevant subject state of awareness.

gru.acip: 'DI NYID KYI MJUG THOGS SU LKOG TU GYUR PA'I YUL CAN RTAGS BSGRUB PAR BYA BA LA MI 'KHRUL BA LAS SKYES PA'I SHES PA NI RJES SU DPAG PA'O,
gru.wylie: 'di nyid kyi mjug thogs su lkog tu gyur pa'i yul can rtags bsgrub par bya ba la mi 'khrul ba las skyes pa'i shes pa ni rjes su dpag pa'o
gru.english: And then just below the section in A Clarification of the Verses mentioned above, we have the statement that— Deduction then we describe as a state of mind where the subject state that holds to an object which is recondite is unmistaken, due to confirmation by a logical reason.

gru.acip: DE'I TSE GZHAL BYA SNANG BA DE SHES PA DE'I GRUB PA NA YUL CAN 'GRUB PA NI SNGAR BZHIN YIN NO,,
gru.wylie: de'i tshe gzhal bya snang ba de shes pa de'i grub pa na yul can 'grub pa ni sngar bzhin yin no
gru.english: At this point then, if the object under consideration—the appearance—is confirmed for that state of mind, then that state is confirmed as the subject; just as we described it earlier on.

gru.acip: DE'I PHYIR BDAG 'DZIN GNYIS LTA BU LA YANG BDAG GNYIS KYI SNANG BA MNGON SUM DU 'CHAR LA, DE'I TSE GZHAL BYA SNANG BA MNGON GYUR DE YUL CAN DES 'GRUB PA SOGS SNGAR DANG 'DRA STE, DES ZHEN YUL LA 'KHRUL PA GZHAN YANG SHES PAR BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: de'i phyir bdag 'dzin gnyis lta bu la yang bdag gnyis kyi snang ba mngon sum du 'char la, de'i tshe gzhal bya snang ba mngon gyur de yul can des 'grub pa sogs sngar dang 'dra ste, des zhen yul la 'khrul pa gzhan yang shes par bya'o
gru.english: As such, we can say even with things like the two forms of the tendency to grasp to some self-nature of things that the appearance of two “selfs” here is made directly. And we can also say at that point things like the fact that the object under consideration is making its appearance directly is confirmed by the subject state of mind; just as we did this earlier. And from this we can also understand moreover that this state of mind is mistaken towards the object that it thinks it sees.

gru.acip: DE LTAR SHES PA RNAMS YUL DU SNANG BA'I SNANG YUL MNGON GYUR GRUB PAR 'DRA LA, BDAG GNYIS DANG BDAG MED GNYIS DANG, GZUGS SOGS RTAG MI RTAG SOGS LA TSAD MAR 'GRO MI 'GRO'I KHYAD PAR CHEN PO YOD PAS, BLO LA TSAD MA DANG TSAD MIN GYI RNAM PAR BZHAG PA'ANG 'GRUB BO,,
gru.wylie: de ltar shes pa rnams yul du snang ba'i snang yul mngon gyur grub par 'dra la, bdag gnyis dang bdag med gnyis dang, gzugs sogs rtag mi rtag sogs la tshad mar 'gro mi 'gro'i khyad par chen po yod pas, blo la tshad ma dang tshad min gyi rnam par bzhag pa'ang 'grub bo
gru.english: As such, it is in a similar way that we establish that the objects which make their appearance, showing themselves as objects to different states of mind, are direct objects. At the same time, there is a huge difference between whether or not states of mind are accurate perception relative to the two supposed self-natures and the two absences of any self-nature; and between form and the rest, and things being unchanging & changing. And thus it is that we can set forth the entire presentation of states of mind being accurate perception, or perception which is not accurate.

gru.acip: PHYI MA LA NI GRUB MTHAS BTAGS PA'I YUL YUL CAN TZAM MA GTOGS PA RTOG PAS YID CI TZAM GTAD KYANG RIG BYA DANG RIG BYED KYI SNANG BA GNYIS MI 'CHAR LA, SNGA MA LA NI YID GTAD DE BLTAS PA NA YUL CAN SHES PA DANG YUL CHOS NYID KYI RNAM PA THA DAD PA NGES PAR 'CHAR BA'I PHYIR RO,,
gru.wylie: phyi ma la ni grub mthas btags pa'i yul yul can tsam ma gtogs pa rtog pas yid ci tsam gtad kyang rig bya dang rig byed kyi snang ba gnyis mi 'char la, snga ma la ni yid gtad de bltas pa na yul can shes pa dang yul chos nyid kyi rnam pa tha dad pa nges par 'char ba'i phyir ro
gru.english: In the latter case, there is nothing more than an object and subject which are imputed by certain schools of thought; that is, no matter how much you direct your thoughts towards them, there will appear to you neither the aspect of something to be known, nor something which knows it. If though you direct your thoughts towards the former—if you observe it—it is a certainty that a discrete subject state of mind and object of the very nature of things will make their appearance.

gru.acip: MNYAM GZHAG RNAM PAR MI RTOG PA'I YE SHES KYIS RANG GI GZHAL BYA CHOS NYID GRUB PA NA, DE'I STOBS KYIS YUL CAN GYI YE SHES 'GRUB PA LA,
gru.wylie: mnyam gzhag rnam par mi rtog pa'i ye shes kyis rang gi gzhal bya chos nyid grub pa na, de'i stobs kyis yul can gyi ye shes 'grub pa la
gru.english: When the non-conceptual wisdom of deep, balanced meditation acts to confirm the object that it takes under consideration—that is, the very nature of things—then by the power of this happening, the subject state of wisdom is then established.

gru.acip: DES NA DE GNYIS KYI RIG BYA RIG BYED DANG PHYOGS KYI CHA MED NI GRUB MTHAS BTAGS PA 'BA' ZHIG GO ,DES NA DE GNYIS SNANG YANG MA NGES PA YIN PA YANG BKAG STE, BDEN GNYIS RANG 'GREL LAS, GAL TE SNANG BA BZHIN DU YANG DE NGES PAR MI ZIN SNYAM NA, DES NA CI DE LTA BU LA NI THA SNYAD MED DO, ,SNANG ZHES BYA BA YANG YID CHES PA MED PA'I PHYIR MNA' CHU BTUNG DGOS SO, ZHES SNANG BA LA YANG SGRUB BYED MNA' TZAM DU ZAD DO, ZHES GSUNGS SO,,
gru.wylie: des na de gnyis kyi rig bya rig byed dang phyogs kyi cha med ni grub mthas btags pa 'ba' zhig go ,des na de gnyis snang yang ma nges pa yin pa yang bkag ste, bden gnyis rang 'grel las, gal te snang ba bzhin du yang de nges par mi zin snyam na, des na ci de lta bu la ni tha snyad med do, ,snang zhes bya ba yang yid ches pa med pa'i phyir mna' chu btung dgos so, zhes snang ba la yang sgrub byed mna' tsam du zad do, zhes gsungs so
gru.english: As such, we can say that the ideas of these two groups—something we know which is also the knower; and particles with no directions to them—are nothing more than inventions of their respective systems. And as such, we are in addition denying the idea that the way things appear as subjects & objects could itself be indefinite; as the autocommentary to the Two Realities again puts it, Suppose you think to yourself, “Even as this makes its appearance, it is not with certainty perceived.” But the fact is that when something is like that, there can be no term to describe it. To simply state that something was appearing would have to be just something that you swore was true. Which is to say, the only proof you could give for the thing indeed making an appearance would be no more than your swearing it were so.

gru.acip: GAL TE RANG BZHIN GYIS SKYE BA MED CING TSAD MAS MA SHES PA'I BDAG NYID CAN GYI GZHAN DBANG RANG GIS NGO BOS GRUB PA'I DNGOS PO YOD NA, RGYU MTSAN GANG GIS NA 'DI YOD PAR MI RIGS PA GZHAN TE
gru.wylie: gal te rang bzhin gyis skye ba med cing tshad mas ma shes pa'i bdag nyid can gyi gzhan dbang rang gis ngo bos grub pa'i dngos po yod na, rgyu mtshan gang gis na 'di yod par mi rigs pa gzhan te
gru.english: Suppose then that there is nothing which can start through any nature of its own; but that there does exist an entity which exists through some nature of its own which is a dominated entity and has a nature such that it is not perceived by any accurate perception. There is yet another reasoning why it would be illogical to say that such a thing existed.

gru.acip: GANG GI TSE GZHAN DBANG RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA CUNG ZAD KYANG YOD PA MIN NA, THA SNYAD KUN RDZOB PA'I 'KHRUL PA'I RGYU STE GZHI RDZAS SU GRUB PAR NI GANG ZHIG 'GYUR TE CUNG ZAD KYANG MED DO,,
gru.wylie: gang gi tshe gzhan dbang rang bzhin gyis grub pa cung zad kyang yod pa min na, tha snyad kun rdzob pa'i 'khrul pa'i rgyu ste gzhi rdzas su grub par ni gang zhig 'gyur te cung zad kyang med do
gru.english: At such point that there did not exist even the slightest dominated entities which existed through some nature of their own, then how could something ever exist as a deceptive, a nominal, reason for error—how could the foundation here exist substantially? There could exist not the slightest such thing.

gru.acip: DES NI GZHAN DBANG DON DAM DU GRUB PAR 'DOD PAS DON DAM LAS NYAMS PAR BSTAN NO,,
gru.wylie: des ni gzhan dbang don dam du grub par 'dod pas don dam las nyams par bstan no
gru.english: What this is saying is that those who accept the idea that dominated entities could exist in some ultimate way have degenerated from the idea of the ultimate.

gru.acip: TSUL MIN GYI DPYAD PA CHU DANG 'DRA BA BLUGS NAS, RANG GI BLO GROS KYI TSUL NGAN PA'I PHYIR TE RGYU MTSAN GYIS, 'JIG RTEN LA GRAGS PA'I RNAM GZHAG 'JIG RTEN KHO NA LAS GRUB PA 'DUG CIG SONG ZHIG BYOS SHIG ,CES PA SOGS DANG
gru.wylie: tshul min gyi dpyad pa chu dang 'dra ba blugs nas, rang gi blo gros kyi tshul ngan pa'i phyir te rgyu mtshan gyis, 'jig rten la grags pa'i rnam gzhag 'jig rten kho na las grub pa 'dug cig song zhig byos shig ,ces pa sogs dang
gru.english: And then into this unready vessel they pour the water of their faulty thinking, which demonstrates the awful workings of their level of intelligence—the thinking that forces them to say things like “the way that the everyday world posits how things exist is something that only works for the world. This is how it is, and this is how we should take it.”

gru.acip: ,SLOB DPON KLU SGRUB ZHABS KYI LAM LAS NI, ,PHYI ROL GYUR LA ZHI BA'I THABS MED DO, ,DE DAG KUN RDZOB DE NYID BDEN LAS NYAMS, ,DE LAS NYAMS PAS THAR PA 'GRUB YOD MIN,
gru.wylie: slob dpon klu sgrub zhabs kyi lam las ni, ,phyi rol gyur la zhi ba'i thabs med do, ,de dag kun rdzob de nyid bden las nyams, ,de las nyams pas thar pa 'grub yod min
gru.english: Those who have Wandered away From the path of Our master, Nagarjuna, Lack the method Needed to attain peace. These people have lost The true concepts Of deceptive reality And the reality Of suchness. Once we have lost this, There is no possibility That we can achieve freedom.

gru.acip: SLOB DPON 'PHAGS PA KLU SGRUB ZHABS KYIS SROL PHYE BA'I LAM LAS NI PHYI ROL TU GYUR PA LA ZHI BA MYANG 'DAS 'THOB PA'I THABS KYI GTZO BO MED DO,,
gru.wylie: slob dpon 'phags pa klu sgrub zhabs kyis srol phye ba'i lam las ni phyi rol tu gyur pa la zhi ba myang 'das 'thob pa'i thabs kyi gtso bo med do
gru.english: They have wandered away from the path of the system introduced by our master, the Realized One, Nagarjuna; and they lack the primary method which is needed to attain peace—nirvana.

gru.acip: CI'I PHYIR ZHE NA, 'DI LTAR PHYI ROL TU GYUR PA DE DAG NI KUN RDZOB KYI BDEN PA DANG DE NYID DON DAM BDEN PA LAS NGES PAR NYAMS PAR 'GYUR LA, BDEN GNYIS DE LAS NYAMS PAS KYANG DE MA BTANG GI BAR DU THAR PA 'GRUB PA YOD PA MIN NO,,
gru.wylie: ci'i phyir zhe na, 'di ltar phyi rol tu gyur pa de dag ni kun rdzob kyi bden pa dang de nyid don dam bden pa las nges par nyams par 'gyur la, bden gnyis de las nyams pas kyang de ma btang gi bar du thar pa 'grub pa yod pa min no
gru.english: And why is this the case? People who have wandered away from this particular system have—quite certainly—lost the true concepts of deceptive reality and ultimate reality: suchness. And once we have lost this teaching on the two realities, then until we have given up those mistaken ideas there is no possibility that we can achieve freedom.

gru.acip: YANG CI'I PHYIR BDEN GNYIS LAS NYAMS PAS THAR PA MI 'GRUB CE NA,
gru.wylie: yang ci'i phyir bden gnyis las nyams pas thar pa mi 'grub ce na
gru.english: “And how is it,” one may ask, “that they have lost the concepts of the two realities, and thus cannot reach freedom?”

gru.acip: DE'I PHYIR KLU SGRUB KYIS SROL PHYE BA'I LUGS KHO NA'I RJES SU 'BRANG BAR BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: de'i phyir klu sgrub kyis srol phye ba'i lugs kho na'i rjes su 'brang bar bya'o
gru.english: As such, we should seek to follow only that system which was introduced to the world by Nagarjuna.

gru.acip: TSUL DE NYID MDOS SGRUB PA LA DE KHO NA NYID NGES PAR BSTAN PA'I TING NGE 'DZIN LAS, ,'JIG RTEN MKHYEN PAS GZHAN LA MA GSAN PAR, ,BDEN PA 'DI GNYIS NYID KYIS BSTAN PAR MDZAD, ,GANG ZHIG KUN RDZOB DE BZHIN DON DAM STE, ,BDEN PA GSUM PA GANG YANG MA MCHIS SO,
gru.wylie: tshul de nyid mdos sgrub pa la de kho na nyid nges par bstan pa'i ting nge 'dzin las, ,'jig rten mkhyen pas gzhan la ma gsan par, ,bden pa 'di gnyis nyid kyis bstan par mdzad, ,gang zhig kun rdzob de bzhin don dam ste, ,bden pa gsum pa gang yang ma mchis so
gru.english: The exact way this works is established in sutra, and described as follows in Concentration which Reveals Suchness— The Knower of the World, Without hearing These things from others, Undertook to teach By using these two different Types of reality. These were the deceptive And the ultimate; And it's an impossibility For there to exist Any kind of third reality.

gru.acip: ,KUN RDZOB DE LA DON DAM SU SMRA BA, ,DE DAG NOR PA'I BLO LDAN SHES PAR BYA, ZHES PAS NI KUN RDZOB PA 'GRO BA DRUG LA SOGS PA LA DON DAM STE BDEN PAR GRUB PA ZHES SU SMRA BA DE DAG PHYIN CI LOG GI BLO CAN DU SHES PAR BYA BAR GSUNGS PAS RANG SDE DE LTAR 'DOD PA RNAMS GRUB MTHA' NOR BAR GSUNGS SO,,
gru.wylie: kun rdzob de la don dam su smra ba, ,de dag nor pa'i blo ldan shes par bya, zhes pas ni kun rdzob pa 'gro ba drug la sogs pa la don dam ste bden par grub pa zhes su smra ba de dag phyin ci log gi blo can du shes par bya bar gsungs pas rang sde de ltar 'dod pa rnams grub mtha' nor bar gsungs so
gru.english: You should understand That those who describe The deceptive as being The ultimate possess A mind that is mistaken. And what this is saying is that those who profess that the deceptive—a reference to things like the six forms of suffering life—is “ultimate,” meaning something that exists as real, should be understood as having minds which are mistaken. That is to say, those whose schools of thought accept this kind of idea are being described as mistaken systems.

gru.acip: ZHES PAS NI PHYIN CI LOG BZHI LA GOMS PA DANG DE 'THAD PA'I GRUB MTHAS BSLAD PA PHYI ROL PA RNAMS NI, SANGS RGYAS KYI GSUNG THOS NA SPONG ZHING DE'I MTHUS SEMS CAN DMYAL BAR 'GRO BA DANG, DE DAG GIS THAR PA'I BDE BA TSUL BZHIN MIN PA'I THABS KYIS BTZAL YANG, DE MI RNYED PAR MA ZAD SDUG BSNGAL DU MAS MNAR BAR 'GYUR BAR BSTAN NO,,
gru.wylie: zhes pas ni phyin ci log bzhi la goms pa dang de 'thad pa'i grub mthas bslad pa phyi rol pa rnams ni, sangs rgyas kyi gsung thos na spong zhing de'i mthus sems can dmyal bar 'gro ba dang, de dag gis thar pa'i bde ba tshul bzhin min pa'i thabs kyis btsal yang, de mi rnyed par ma zad sdug bsngal du mas mnar bar 'gyur bar bstan no
gru.english: What this is teaching us is that there are non-Buddhists who become very accustomed to the four different reversed ways of thinking mentioned here, and who are infected by schools of thought which believe that they are correct. When people like this happen to hear the words of the Buddha, they reject them; and by the power of this they pass to the realms of hell. These kinds of individuals undertake a search for the happiness of freedom through mistaken means; but not only do they fail to find this happiness, they instead come to be tortured by a great many sufferings.

gru.acip: GAL TE KHYOD KYIS DE SKAD DU KHO BO CAG LA SHIN TU LTOS PA MED PAR SMRA NA, DA NI NGED CAG KYANG KHYED LA BZOD PA MI BYED DE, GAL TE BDAG NYID GZHAN GYI PHYOGS SUN 'BYIN PA TZAM LA MKHAS PAR MNGON PAR BYED CING, RIGS PA'I 'THAD PAS MI RIGS PA'I PHYIR GZHAN DBANG RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA'I NGO BO SEL BAR BYED NA, 'O NA DA NI BDAG DANG GZHAN LAS SKYE BA SOGS 'GOG PA'I 'THAD PA KHO NAS, MI RIGS PA'I PHYIR KHYOD LA GRAGS PA'I KUN RDZOB SEL BAR BYED DO ZHE NA,
gru.wylie: gal te khyod kyis de skad du kho bo cag la shin tu ltos pa med par smra na, da ni nged cag kyang khyed la bzod pa mi byed de, gal te bdag nyid gzhan gyi phyogs sun 'byin pa tsam la mkhas par mngon par byed cing, rigs pa'i 'thad pas mi rigs pa'i phyir gzhan dbang rang bzhin gyis grub pa'i ngo bo sel bar byed na, 'o na da ni bdag dang gzhan las skye ba sogs 'gog pa'i 'thad pa kho nas, mi rigs pa'i phyir khyod la grags pa'i kun rdzob sel bar byed do zhe na
gru.english: And so suppose someone comes now with the following response— You have said things about us in those words which have nothing to do with the situation. And so now we can no longer be so patient with you. So suppose it is the case that a person starts to look like they are a master, just because they can attack the positions that someone else holds. But you are just trying to disprove the essential nature of dominated entities, something which does exist through a nature of its own, reasoning which is not itself rational. What we will do now then is just to show that it is correct to deny that things could grow either from themselves or from other things; and with nothing more than that, we will be able to disprove the kind of deceptive reality that you speak about—for in the end it is illogical.

gru.acip: 'DI LTAR JI LTAR SEMS TZAM PA KHYOD KYIS GZHAN DBANG DNGOS POR TE NGO BOS GRUB PA, SUM CU PA LAS, DE MA MTHONG BAR DE MI MTHONG ZHES GSUNGS PA LTAR 'PHAGS PA'I YE SHES KYIS THUGS SU CHUD PAR BYAS PA ZHIG GI RANG DBANG DU BYAS NAS, RANG LUGS KYIS YOD DO ZHES 'DOD PA DE LTAR KUN RDZOB KYANG NI RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAR BDAG GIS KHAS MA BLANGS SO,,
gru.wylie: 'di ltar ji ltar sems tsam pa khyod kyis gzhan dbang dngos por te ngo bos grub pa, sum cu pa las, de ma mthong bar de mi mthong zhes gsungs pa ltar 'phags pa'i ye shes kyis thugs su chud par byas pa zhig gi rang dbang du byas nas, rang lugs kyis yod do zhes 'dod pa de ltar kun rdzob kyang ni rang bzhin gyis grub par bdag gis khas ma blangs so
gru.english: And here's how that happens. You followers of the Mind Only say that dominated entities are real things; which is to say, that they exist through some essential nature of their own. As the Thirty Verses puts it, “It's something you fail to see, being something that cannot be seen.” That is, you are saying that there is something which is comprehended by the wisdom of a realized being which has some independent nature of its own. And then when you say that your own system says that something does exist, and you agree to it, you are talking about a deceptive reality which could exist through some nature of its own. This is not something though which we can accept.

gru.acip: GZHAN NGOR DE LTAR KHAS LEN PA NI 'BRAS BU STE DGOS PA'I PHYIR YIN LA, DE YANG GDUL BYA DE GRUB MTHA' NGAN PA GZHAN LAS LDOG PA DANG, RIM GYIS DE KHO NA NYID RTOGS PA'I THABS YIN PA'I PHYIR RO,,
gru.wylie: gzhan ngor de ltar khas len pa ni 'bras bu ste dgos pa'i phyir yin la, de yang gdul bya de grub mtha' ngan pa gzhan las ldog pa dang, rim gyis de kho na nyid rtogs pa'i thabs yin pa'i phyir ro
gru.english: Accepting these things in the eyes of those others is something meant for a certain effect; which is to say, to satisfy a certain need. In fact it is meant as a means of turning disciples away from these other, defective systems of thought and bringing them, gradually, to the means of realizing suchness.

gru.acip: DE LTAR NA PHYI ROL MED PA LA THA SNYAD PA'I TSAD MAS GNOD PAS PHYI ROL MED PAR SGRUB MI NUS SO,,
gru.wylie: de ltar na phyi rol med pa la tha snyad pa'i tshad mas gnod pas phyi rol med par sgrub mi nus so
gru.english: As such, nominal forms of accurate perception draw into question the idea that there exist no outer objects; as such, you are unable to prove the idea that no such objects exist.

gru.acip: DANG PO LA GSUM, TZAM GYI SGRAS PHYI ROL MI 'GOG PA SA BCU PA'I LUNG GIS BSGRUB PA, DON DE NYID MDO GZHAN GYIS KYANG BSGRUB PA, TZAM GYI SGRAS SEMS GTZO BO NYID DU BSGRUB PA'O, ,DANG PO NI,
gru.wylie: dang po la gsum, tsam gyi sgras phyi rol mi 'gog pa sa bcu pa'i lung gis bsgrub pa, don de nyid mdo gzhan gyis kyang bsgrub pa, tsam gyi sgras sems gtso bo nyid du bsgrub pa'o, ,dang po ni
gru.english: We'll cover the first of these three in another three of its own: showing how a citation from The Ten Levels supports the idea that the word “only” is not meant to deny outer objects; demonstrating how this very same point is made in other sutras as well; and establishing that the intent of the word “only” is to say only that the mind is the primary thing. Here is the first of these.

gru.acip: GAL TE DE KHO NA NYID LA DPYOD PA'I 'THAD PA STE RIGS PAS GRUB PA DANG BRAL YANG, 'JIG RTEN PA'I GNOD PAS 'JIGS NAS KHYOD KYIS KUN RDZOB KHAS BLANGS NA NI, LUNG GI GNOD PAS 'JIGS PAS SEMS TZAM DU YANG KHAS BLANG DGOS TE, SA BCU PA LAS, DE 'DI SNYAM DU SEMS TE, 'DI LTAR KHAMS GSUM PO 'DI NI SEMS TZAM STE, ZHES GSUNGS PA LTA BU'O ZHE NA,
gru.wylie: gal te de kho na nyid la dpyod pa'i 'thad pa ste rigs pas grub pa dang bral yang, 'jig rten pa'i gnod pas 'jigs nas khyod kyis kun rdzob khas blangs na ni, lung gi gnod pas 'jigs pas sems tsam du yang khas blang dgos te, sa bcu pa las, de 'di snyam du sems te, 'di ltar khams gsum po 'di ni sems tsam ste, zhes gsungs pa lta bu'o zhe na
gru.english: And so suppose you come and say the following— I was bereft of the correctness of learning to examine suchness; which is to say, I felt I was without any solid proof for it. Fearing then that the ideas of the world would harm my position, I accepted the idea of a deceptive reality. And when I did that, I feared further that I would be disproven by scripture; and so I found myself having to accept the ideas of the Mind Only. Here I found support from The Ten Levels, where it says: “And then one comes to the following thoughts, saying to oneself, 'All three of the realms of existence are only the mind.”

gru.acip: SA BCU PA LAS, LUGS SU BYUNG BA'I RNAM PAR RTEN CING 'BREL PAR 'BYUNG BA LA RAB TU RTOG GO ,DE LTAR NA SDUG BSNGAL GYI PHUNG PO SDUG BSNGAL GYI LJON PA BYED PA PO DANG, TSOR BA PO MED PA 'BA' ZHIG PO 'DI MNGON PAR 'GRUB PAR 'GYUR RO SNYAM MO,,
gru.wylie: sa bcu pa las, lugs su byung ba'i rnam par rten cing 'brel par 'byung ba la rab tu rtog go ,de ltar na sdug bsngal gyi phung po sdug bsngal gyi ljon pa byed pa po dang, tshor ba po med pa 'ba' zhig po 'di mngon par 'grub par 'gyur ro snyam mo
gru.english: The way that The Ten Levels puts it, in great detail, is as follows: They have a great understanding of all it is that occurs in dependence and relationship, in the forward order of this progression. And so they think to themselves, “The great tree of this heap of suffering, of pain, had no maker; and there is no one to feel it either. This is all there is; this is how this came to be.”

gru.acip: MDO DES NI BYED PA PO DANG TSOR BA PO MED PA'I 'BA' ZHIG PA 'GRUB PA DANG, SEMS TZAM GYI DON BSHAD PA NA YAN LAG BCU GNYIS SEMS GCIG LA BRTEN PAR GSUNGS PAS,
gru.wylie: mdo des ni byed pa po dang tshor ba po med pa'i 'ba' zhig pa 'grub pa dang, sems tsam gyi don bshad pa na yan lag bcu gnyis sems gcig la brten par gsungs pas
gru.english: These lines of the sutra are establishing a singularity where there is no agent, and no one who has feelings. And when it gets into explaining the meaning of “mind only,” it states that the twelve links of dependence depend upon the one thing, mind.

gru.acip: MDO 'DI'I DON DGROL BA'I PHYIR BSHAD PA, JI BZHIN TE JI LTAR RANG RANG GI BSTAN BCOS KYI GRUB PA'I MTHA' DE DANG DE LAS, MU STEGS RNAMS KYIS GANG ZAG DANG SOGS PAS RGYUN DANG PHUNG PO SOGS BYED PA POR SMRAS PA DE DAG BYED PA POR MA GZIGS NAS, RGYAL BAS SEMS TZAM ZHIG 'JIG RTEN GYI BYED PA POR GSUNGS SO,,
gru.wylie: mdo 'di'i don dgrol ba'i phyir bshad pa, ji bzhin te ji ltar rang rang gi bstan bcos kyi grub pa'i mtha' de dang de las, mu stegs rnams kyis gang zag dang sogs pas rgyun dang phung po sogs byed pa por smras pa de dag byed pa por ma gzigs nas, rgyal bas sems tsam zhig 'jig rten gyi byed pa por gsungs so
gru.english: And so the following is stated, to unravel the intent of these lines from sutra. Look at the way—the manner—in which the River Schools, in this or that of the commentaries of their respective systems, speak of the person “and such”—which is meant to include a flow or the heaps or such as the creator. The Victors though do not see these as being creators, and so have stated that it is only the mind which is the creator of the world.

gru.acip: DE'I PHYIR SEMS TZAM MO ZHES PA 'DIR NI STE 'DIS NI, GZUGS LA SOGS PA RNAMS KHAMS GSUM 'GRUB PA LA GTZO BO YIN PA SEL BAR BYED KYI, SEMS TZAM ZHIG KHO NA RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA YIN GYI PHYI ROL GYI GZUGS NI MED DO ZHES 'GOG PA DE LTAR 'CHAD PA NI MDO YI DON MA YIN NO,,
gru.wylie: de'i phyir sems tsam mo zhes pa 'dir ni ste 'dis ni, gzugs la sogs pa rnams khams gsum 'grub pa la gtso bo yin pa sel bar byed kyi, sems tsam zhig kho na rang bzhin gyis grub pa yin gyi phyi rol gyi gzugs ni med do zhes 'gog pa de ltar 'chad pa ni mdo yi don ma yin no
gru.english: And so let's look at the term here in the expression “mind only.” It serves, first of all, to preclude the possibility that—in the formation of the three realms—physical matter is the main thing. But it is not the meaning of sutra here when people explain it as some kind of denial; that is, as saying that it is just—that is, only—the mind which exists through its own nature, and there is then no outer form.

gru.acip: KHYOD KYI LUGS LTAR NA GAL TE KHAMS GSUM PO 'DI DAG RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA'I SEMS TZAM MO ZHES MKHYEN NAS, SA BCU PA DE LAS PHYI ROL GYI GZUGS NYID DGAG PAR MDZAD NA NI,
gru.wylie: khyod kyi lugs ltar na gal te khams gsum po 'di dag rang bzhin gyis grub pa'i sems tsam mo zhes mkhyen nas, sa bcu pa de las phyi rol gyi gzugs nyid dgag par mdzad na ni
gru.english: Suppose then it were the way that your system would have it. That is, suppose all these three realms of existence were referred to as “only the mind,” as something which existed through its own nature. And suppose the Buddha knew this, and so meant—in this Ten Levels—to deny “form itself,” in the sense of outer form.

gru.acip: SA BCU PA'I MDO DE NYID LAS RNAM SHES MA RIG PA DANG 'DU BYED KYI 'BRAS BUR GSUNGS KYI, RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PAR NI MA GSUNGS SO,,
gru.wylie: sa bcu pa'i mdo de nyid las rnam shes ma rig pa dang 'du byed kyi 'bras bur gsungs kyi, rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub par ni ma gsungs so
gru.english: That is, this same Ten Levels does state that consciousness is a result of misunderstanding and fresh karma; but it doesn't say anything about things existing by definition.

gru.acip: RTEN 'BYUNG DU YANG GSUNGS LA RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PAR YANG GSUNGS NA NI GSUNG BA PO 'KHRUL ZAD LA DE GNYIS KA RANG LUGS SU BZHED PA MI SRID PAS, GDUL BYA GZHAN BKRI PA'I PHYIR GZHAN NGOR ZHAL GYIS BZHES PAR SHES PAR BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: rten 'byung du yang gsungs la rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub par yang gsungs na ni gsung ba po 'khrul zad la de gnyis ka rang lugs su bzhed pa mi srid pas, gdul bya gzhan bkri pa'i phyir gzhan ngor zhal gyis bzhes par shes par bya'o
gru.english: That is, it would be nothing less than a gross error for the person making these statements to say that things were arising out of dependence, and at the same time to say that they existed by definition. Which is to say, it would be impossible to say that your own system was that you accepted both concepts. As such, you should understand that that they were accepted only in front of certain disciples, in order lead them—in time—to something higher.

gru.acip: GNYIS KA RANG LUGS SU MI RUNG BA NI GAL TE RNAM PAR SHES PA RANG GI BDAG NYID KYIS GRUB PAR GYUR NA NI, RNAM SHES DE MA RIG PA'AM 'DU BYED LA MI LTOS PAR 'GYUR BA ZHIG NA, LTOS PA YANG YIN TE, DE'I PHYIR RANG GI BDAG NYID KYIS GRUB PA NI MED DO,,
gru.wylie: gnyis ka rang lugs su mi rung ba ni gal te rnam par shes pa rang gi bdag nyid kyis grub par gyur na ni, rnam shes de ma rig pa'am 'du byed la mi ltos par 'gyur ba zhig na, ltos pa yang yin te, de'i phyir rang gi bdag nyid kyis grub pa ni med do
gru.english: And just how is it that both could never represent our own system? Say for example that consciousness were something that could exist in & of itself. In that case, consciousness would come to a stop, but without relying on misunderstanding, or on fresh karma; which means that it did depend on something. And that would mean that it couldn't be something that existed in & of itself.

gru.acip: DE LTAR BYED PA NI NANG GI BDEN 'DZIN GYI GRUB MTHAS BYAS PAR 'GYUR RO,,
gru.wylie: de ltar byed pa ni nang gi bden 'dzin gyi grub mthas byas par 'gyur ro
gru.english: When people do act this way, it is caused by beliefs of a school of an inner tendency to hold to things as real.

gru.acip: ZHES GSUNGS TE, RANG GI NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB NA GNAS LUGS SU GRUB PAR 'GYUR LA, DE'I TSE 'KHRUL PA LOG PA NA GSAL DU 'GRO DGOS KYI, LDOG PAR MI 'GYUR RO, ZHES PA'I DON NO,,
gru.wylie: zhes gsungs te, rang gi ngo bo nyid kyis grub na gnas lugs su grub par 'gyur la, de'i tshe 'khrul pa log pa na gsal du 'gro dgos kyi, ldog par mi 'gyur ro, zhes pa'i don no
gru.english: The point here is that—if things could exist through some essential nature of their own—then they would exist by the very nature of things. In that case, if we were able to correct our error, the truth would have to be brought to light. But in the opposite case, it would not.

gru.acip: YAN LAG BCU GNYIS PO THAMS CAD KYANG SEMS GCIG LA BRTEN PAR GSUNGS PA LA BRTEN NAS, TZAM GYI SGRAS SEMS GTZO BOR GYUR PAR BSTAN TE, BSHAD PA SNGA MA DGAG PHYOGS DANG PHYI MA SGRUB PHYOGS NAS YIN NO,,
gru.wylie: yan lag bcu gnyis po thams cad kyang sems gcig la brten par gsungs pa la brten nas, tsam gyi sgras sems gtso bor gyur par bstan te, bshad pa snga ma dgag phyogs dang phyi ma sgrub phyogs nas yin no
gru.english: And so we see statements that all of the twelve links of dependence rely on but one thing, the mind. Relying on these statements, we can say then that the word “only” is meant to indicate that it is the mind which is primary. The former of the two statements is made from the negative side of things; while the latter is meant from the positive side of things.

gru.acip: ,GANG GI TSE BTAGS DON 'TSOL BA'I 'THAD PAS DPYAD PA NA PHYI'I GZUGS MED PAR RTOG NA NI DE'I TSE PHYI NANG GNYIS KA'I YOD PA 'THAD PAS LAS 'GRUB PA DANG BRAL BA'I PHYIR NANG GI SEMS MED PAR YANG RTOGS PAR BYA DGOS LA,
gru.wylie: gang gi tshe btags don 'tshol ba'i 'thad pas dpyad pa na phyi'i gzugs med par rtog na ni de'i tshe phyi nang gnyis ka'i yod pa 'thad pas las 'grub pa dang bral ba'i phyir nang gi sems med par yang rtogs par bya dgos la
gru.english: And suppose you use reasoning to go looking for the the thing that is given the name, and thus come to the idea that there is no outer form. At that point, you would fail to be able to establish karma, through reasoning which establishes both the existence of the outer and the inner. And at that juncture, you would have to come to a realization that there was no mind, on the inside.

gru.acip: GAL TE SEMS TZAM PAS GZUGS CAN KHAS MI LEN NA SEMS TZAM PAS KUN GZHI SGRUB PA'I RIGS PA STON PA NA, THEG BSDUS LAS, NYING MTSAMS SBYOR BA SBREL {%SPREL} ZIN PA RNAMS KYI DBANG PO GZUGS CAN 'DZIN PAR BYED PA YANG DE LAS GZHAN RNAM PAR SMIN PA'I RNAM PAR SHES PA MED PAR {%this med-pa not in Teng!} MI 'THAD DE ZHES DANG,
gru.wylie: gal te sems tsam pas gzugs can khas mi len na sems tsam pas kun gzhi sgrub pa'i rigs pa ston pa na, theg bsdus las, nying mtshams sbyor ba sbrel {%sprel} zin pa rnams kyi dbang po gzugs can 'dzin par byed pa yang de las gzhan rnam par smin pa'i rnam par shes pa med par {%ThiS MeD-pa NoT iN teNg!} mi 'thad de zhes dang
gru.english: And suppose you say that the Mind Only did not accept things with form. In such a case, it would be a sheer contradiction for A Compendium of the Greater Way to make certain statements that it does, in its presentation of the reasoning that the Mind Only uses for for establishing foundation consciousness. One of these is— It would be incorrect to say that those who have already made the connection of the crossing between death & birth—and who were thus holding to sense powers consisting of form—possessed none of the consciousness that was other than these and which had then ripened.

gru.acip: LUNG LAS KYANG PHYI ROL GYI DON DANG NANG GI SHES PA YOD MED MTSUNGS PA DE LTAR RTOGS PAR BYA STE, 'DI LTAR GZUGS LA SOGS PA'I PHUNG PO LNGA PO DE DAG NI SHES RAB KYI PHA ROL TU PHYIN PA'I TSUL GYI MDOR NI SANGS RGYAS KYIS LNGA CHAR YANG MTSUNGS PAR RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA SPANGS SHING STE BKAG PA YIN TE,
gru.wylie: lung las kyang phyi rol gyi don dang nang gi shes pa yod med mtshungs pa de ltar rtogs par bya ste, 'di ltar gzugs la sogs pa'i phung po lnga po de dag ni shes rab kyi pha rol tu phyin pa'i tshul gyi mdor ni sangs rgyas kyis lnga char yang mtshungs par rang bzhin gyis grub pa spangs shing ste bkag pa yin te
gru.english: We can also understand, from scripture, how outside objects and inside awareness must be equivalent, in either existing or not existing. We can look thus at physical form and the rest of the five parts to the person as these are presented in sutras on the ways of the perfection of wisdom. Here, the Buddha treated all five as equivalent, in rejecting—that is, denying—that they could exist through any nature of their own.

gru.acip: ,BDEN GNYIS RIM PA 'DI DAG BSHIG NAS KYANG, ,KHYOD KYI RDZAS NI BKAG PAS 'GRUB MI 'GYUR, ,DE PHYIR DE LTA'I RIM PAS DNGOS GDOD NAS, ,DE NYID MA SKYES 'JIG RTEN SKYES RIG BYA,
gru.wylie: bden gnyis rim pa 'di dag bshig nas kyang, ,khyod kyi rdzas ni bkag pas 'grub mi 'gyur, ,de phyir de lta'i rim pas dngos gdod nas, ,de nyid ma skyes 'jig rten skyes rig bya
gru.english: Even though These stages Of the two realities Are destroyed, That doesn't mean That your idea Of the substantial Is established; For it was disproved. Thus it is that, Because of stages Like that, Entities have Never arisen, For all the time There ever was. It is reasonable To say, In the world, That they have arisen.

gru.acip: DE'I PHYIR PHA ROL GYIS NI SNGAR BSHAD PA DE LTAR PHYI ROL DANG SEMS GNYIS DON DAM PAR MED MNYAM DANG, KUN RDZOB TU YOD MNYAM DU LUNG DANG RIGS PAS GRUB PA'I BDEN GNYIS KYI RIM PA 'DI DAG BSHIG PAR 'GYUR RO,,
gru.wylie: de'i phyir pha rol gyis ni sngar bshad pa de ltar phyi rol dang sems gnyis don dam par med mnyam dang, kun rdzob tu yod mnyam du lung dang rigs pas grub pa'i bden gnyis kyi rim pa 'di dag bshig par 'gyur ro
gru.english: As such, the explanation of the other side about these stages of the two realities is destroyed: where it is established by both scripture & reasoning that the two of outside things and the mind are equivalent in not existing in an ultimate way, and equivalent as well in existing in a deceptive way.

gru.acip: DE LTAR BSHIG NAS KYANG SEMS TZAM PA KHYOD KYI GZHAN DBANG RDZAS SU GRUB PA NI 'GRUB PAR MI 'GYUR RO,,
gru.wylie: de ltar bshig nas kyang sems tsam pa khyod kyi gzhan dbang rdzas su grub pa ni 'grub par mi 'gyur ro
gru.english: And even though these things are thus destroyed, that doesn't mean that your Mind Only idea of dominated entities that exist substantially is established.

gru.acip: CI'I PHYIR ZHE NA, GANG GI PHYIR SNGAR GZHAN DBANG RDZAS SU GRUB PA LAN DU MAR BKAG PA DE'I PHYIR, KHYOD KYI NGAL BA DON MED PAR 'GYUR RO,,
gru.wylie: ci'i phyir zhe na, gang gi phyir sngar gzhan dbang rdzas su grub pa lan du mar bkag pa de'i phyir, khyod kyi ngal ba don med par 'gyur ro
