gru.english: And why is that? Because all your efforts to exhaust yourself here are simply pointless, given that we have earlier on disproved—many times over—your idea that dominated entities could exist substantially.

gru.acip: PHYI ROL MED PAR SEMS TZAM MO ZHES GSUNGS PA 'DI NI, STON PAS DRANG DON NYID DU GSUNGS PAS LUNG LAS DRANG DON DU 'GRUB LA, MDO 'DI NI DRANG DON NYID DU RIGS PAS KYANG 'THAD PA STE 'GRUB BO,,
gru.wylie: phyi rol med par sems tsam mo zhes gsungs pa 'di ni, ston pas drang don nyid du gsungs pas lung las drang don du 'grub la, mdo 'di ni drang don nyid du rigs pas kyang 'thad pa ste 'grub bo
gru.english: Let's consider then this statement that things are only the mind—and that there are no outer things. It was indeed made by the Teacher only as something that was meant to be taken figuratively; and we have shown that it can be established as such, from scripture itself. So too though it can also be established—shown that it was only meant as metaphorical, and nothing more—through logical reasoning as well.

gru.acip: BDAG GNYIS SU KUN BRTAGS PA LTA BU DANG, CHOS RNAMS LA NGO BO DANG KHYAD PAR DU BTAGS PA RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PA NI, DE'I LUGS KYIS SHES BYA LA MI SRID KYANG NGO BO DANG KHYAD PAR DU BTAGS PA'I KUN BRTAGS DU MA ZHIG NI GZHI GRUB PA YIN NO,,
gru.wylie: bdag gnyis su kun brtags pa lta bu dang, chos rnams la ngo bo dang khyad par du btags pa rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub pa ni, de'i lugs kyis shes bya la mi srid kyang ngo bo dang khyad par du btags pa'i kun brtags du ma zhig ni gzhi grub pa yin no
gru.english: And so first we have fabricated things such as that into the two realities; and where entities are labelled into the essence and the features, as things that exist by definition. Even though—in this system—these things are impossible with reference to existing objects, many examples of fabricated things labelled as essence and features do indeed exist.

gru.acip: MDO DER GZHAN DBANG DANG YONGS GRUB GNYIS KA RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PAR GSUNGS KYANG, 'GREL PAR GZHAN DBANG TZAM LAS MA GSUNGS PA NI DBU SEMS BDEN PAR YOD MED RTZOD PA'I GZHI'I GTZO BO NI GZHAN DBANG YIN TE KUN BRTAGS 'DOGS PA'I GZHI YANG GZHAN DBANG YIN LA, YONGS GRUB KYANG GZHAN DBANG LA BRTEN NAS GZHAG DGOS PA'I PHYIR RO,,
gru.wylie: mdo der gzhan dbang dang yongs grub gnyis ka rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub par gsungs kyang, 'grel par gzhan dbang tsam las ma gsungs pa ni dbu sems bden par yod med rtsod pa'i gzhi'i gtso bo ni gzhan dbang yin te kun brtags 'dogs pa'i gzhi yang gzhan dbang yin la, yongs grub kyang gzhan dbang la brten nas gzhag dgos pa'i phyir ro
gru.english: In the sutra, both dominated entities and totality are said to exist by definition; but in the commentary we only see mention here of the dominated ones. This is because the main point of contention between the Middle Way and the Mind Only schools—as far as the question of whether they exist in truth or not—is the dominated entities. That is, the basis upon which we label things as fabrications consists of these entities; and we must also posit totality itself on the basis of of these same dominated entities.

gru.acip: 'DI LA YANG MTHAR THUG THEG PA GSUM DU BSHAD PA NI 'PHAGS PA NYID KYIS MDO KUN LAS BTUS PA LAS MTHAR THUG THEG PA GCIG TU SGRUB PA LAS GO NUS PAR DGONGS NAS 'JUG 'GREL DU MA SMOS SO,,
gru.wylie: 'di la yang mthar thug theg pa gsum du bshad pa ni 'phags pa nyid kyis mdo kun las btus pa las mthar thug theg pa gcig tu sgrub pa las go nus par dgongs nas 'jug 'grel du ma smos so
gru.english: Along the same lines, the explanation that—ultimately—there are three ways is something that can be understood from the substantiation in A Compendium of All the Sutras of that ultimately there is only on way. This is why we don't see it stated in the autocommentary to Entering the Middle Way.

gru.acip: LHAG MA GSUM GYI PHYI ROL MED PAR SEMS TZAM ZHIG RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAR BSTAN PA DRANG DON DU LUNG GIS GSAL BAR BYED PA NI, LANG KAR GSHEGS PA LAS, ,JI LTAR NAD PA NAD PA LA, ,SMAN PA SMAN RNAMS GTONG BA LTAR, ,SANGS RGYAS DE BZHIN SEMS CAN LA, ,SEMS TZAM DU YANG RAB TU GSUNGS, ZHES PA 'DI YIN TE
gru.wylie: lhag ma gsum gyi phyi rol med par sems tsam zhig rang bzhin gyis grub par bstan pa drang don du lung gis gsal bar byed pa ni, lang kar gshegs pa las, ,ji ltar nad pa nad pa la, ,sman pa sman rnams gtong ba ltar, ,sangs rgyas de bzhin sems can la, ,sems tsam du yang rab tu gsungs, zhes pa 'di yin te
gru.english: Things not existing on the outside, and being the mind only, and existing through some nature of their own—according the remaining three points—are ideas that are clarified in citations from scripture as being metaphoric. Here for example is what the Journey to Langka says: Doctors deliver medicines To those who are ill According to the disease; In the same way, The Buddhas keep telling Beings that it is all Only the mind.

gru.acip: DES JI LTAR NAD PA ZHES SOGS KYIS SEMS TZAM DU SMRA BA DRANG DON DU BSHAD PA BZHIN DU RTAG BRTAN GYI SNYING PO DRANG DON DU GSUNGS PAS KYANG DGONGS 'GREL SOGS LAS KUN GZHI RNAM SHES GSUNGS PA SGRA JI BZHIN PA MIN PAR SGRUB PA YIN NO,,
gru.wylie: des ji ltar nad pa zhes sogs kyis sems tsam du smra ba drang don du bshad pa bzhin du rtag brtan gyi snying po drang don du gsungs pas kyang dgongs 'grel sogs las kun gzhi rnam shes gsungs pa sgra ji bzhin pa min par sgrub pa yin no
gru.english: That is, this part in the autocommentary is expressing the point that the statement “in the same way with people that are ill” can be used to show that—just as statements that things are mind only are explained as being metaphors—statements about a heart which is unchanging & firm are metaphoric. And then it is for this reason that we can establish that statements in sources such as What I Really Meant about a foundation consciousness were never meant to be taken literally.

gru.acip: RTAG BRTAN GYI SNYING PO YOD PAR BSTAN PA DRANG DON YIN PAS KUN GZHI DRANG DON DU JI LTAR 'GRUB CE NA,
gru.wylie: rtag brtan gyi snying po yod par bstan pa drang don yin pas kun gzhi drang don du ji ltar 'grub ce na
gru.english: “How is it,” one may ask then, “that foundation consciousness is proven to be meant in a figurative way, just because that teaching about the existence of a heart to things which is unchanging and stable was intended figuratively?”

gru.acip: ,DE LTAR NA SNGA MA DRANG DON DU BSTAN PA NYID KYIS PHYI MA YANG DRANG DON DU 'GRUB BO,,
gru.wylie: de ltar na snga ma drang don du bstan pa nyid kyis phyi ma yang drang don du 'grub bo
gru.english: As such, we can say that—since the former is explained as being meant figuratively—the latter is established as being figurative as well.

gru.acip: ,SHES BYA MED NA SHES PA BSAL BA NI, ,BDE BLAG RNYED CES SANGS RGYAS RNAMS KYIS GSUNGS, ,SHES BYA MED NA SHES PA BKAG 'GRUB PAS, ,DANG POR SHES BYA DGAG PA MDZAD PA YIN,
gru.wylie: shes bya med na shes pa bsal ba ni, ,bde blag rnyed ces sangs rgyas rnams kyis gsungs, ,shes bya med na shes pa bkag 'grub pas, ,dang por shes bya dgag pa mdzad pa yin
gru.english: The Buddhas Have stated that If no objects exist, And then we Clear away The idea of a State of mind, Then people can Come to this idea More easily. If there are no Objects of knowledge, We can deny Any perception, And establish that. Therefore At the beginning We focus on denying Objects of knowledge.

gru.acip: DE 'DRA BA LA SNGON DU SHES BYA PHYI ROL LA MED PA BSTAN NA, DE'I 'OG TU SHES PA RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA GSAL BA NI, BDE BLAG TU RNYED CES SANGS RGYAS RNAMS KYIS GSUNGS SO,,
gru.wylie: de 'dra ba la sngon du shes bya phyi rol la med pa bstan na, de'i 'og tu shes pa rang bzhin gyis grub pa gsal ba ni, bde blag tu rnyed ces sangs rgyas rnams kyis gsungs so
gru.english: And so the Buddhas have stated that if, before we take such a step, we teach people that no objects exist on the outside—and only after that clear away the idea of any state of mind which could exist through some nature of its own—then they can come to this idea more easily.

gru.acip: SANGS RGYAS RNAMS KYIS DANG POR SHES BYA PHYI ROL DGAG PAR MDZAD PA KHO NA GSUNGS PA YIN TE SHES BYA MED NA STE PHYI ROL GYI BDAG MED PA RIG PA RNAMS SHES PA BKAG PA STE DE'I BDAG MED PA BDE BLAG TU 'GRUB PA'I PHYIR RO,,
gru.wylie: sangs rgyas rnams kyis dang por shes bya phyi rol dgag par mdzad pa kho na gsungs pa yin te shes bya med na ste phyi rol gyi bdag med pa rig pa rnams shes pa bkag pa ste de'i bdag med pa bde blag tu 'grub pa'i phyir ro
gru.english: Thus it is then that the Buddhas say things, at the beginning, which focus only on denying the existence of outer objects of knowledge. And that's because—if there are no objects of knowledge—then we can go on to deny any perception or knowledge of what on the outside lacks any self-nature, and thus easily establish that lack of a self-nature to things.

gru.acip: DE GNYIS KA KHAS BLANG DGOS PA LA DE DAG GI DE KHO NA NYID STON PA NA DE RNAMS RANG GI NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB NA 'BYUNG BA MIG GI GZUNG BYA'AM, YANG NA YUL GZUGS MIG GI GZUNG BYA MIN PAR KHAS BLANG DGOS PAR
gru.wylie: de gnyis ka khas blang dgos pa la de dag gi de kho na nyid ston pa na de rnams rang gi ngo bo nyid kyis grub na 'byung ba mig gi gzung bya'am, yang na yul gzugs mig gi gzung bya min par khas blang dgos par
gru.english: In fact we have to accept both of these; but when we teach the suchness that they possess, we would have to say that—if they existed through some nature of their own—then we would have to accept that the elements were something that the eye could grasp; or else that the object of form were not something that the eye could grasp.

gru.acip: SBRUL DNGOS LA NI YONGS SU GRUB PA YIN TE MED BZHIN DU KUN TU MA BTAGS PA'I PHYIR RO,,
gru.wylie: sbrul dngos la ni yongs su grub pa yin te med bzhin du kun tu ma btags pa'i phyir ro
gru.english: A genuine snake is something we could call “totality”—“completely established”—in the sense that it is in no way just called what it is, without being there at all.

gru.acip: DE LA GANG ZAG DANG BDAG GCES PA'I SROG DANG, DBANG PO LA SOGS PA SROG MA YIN PA DANG, MNGON MTHO DANG NGES LEGS 'GRUB PA'I CHOS DANG, DE LAS BZLOG PA'I CHOS MIN PA DANG, NYON MONGS PA'I ZAG PA DANG 'CHAL KHRIMS 'GOG PA'I SDOM PA DANG, LA SOGS PAS BDE BA DANG, SDUG BSNGAL BA DANG, SHES PA LAS SKYES SHING SHES PA'I RGYUR GYUR PA'I 'DU BYA BA'I SHUGS TE, TSIG GI DON DGU'I RNAM GZHAG BYAS NAS
gru.wylie: de la gang zag dang bdag gces pa'i srog dang, dbang po la sogs pa srog ma yin pa dang, mngon mtho dang nges legs 'grub pa'i chos dang, de las bzlog pa'i chos min pa dang, nyon mongs pa'i zag pa dang 'chal khrims 'gog pa'i sdom pa dang, la sogs pas bde ba dang, sdug bsngal ba dang, shes pa las skyes shing shes pa'i rgyur gyur pa'i 'du bya ba'i shugs te, tshig gi don dgu'i rnam gzhag byas nas
gru.english: They set forth nine different principles, which involve the person and the life which is cherished by the self; those things which are not the life, such as the powers and so forth; the teachings which help us achieve the higher rebirths and definite goodness; the opposite of these teachings, negative teachings; the impurities of the negativities; the commitments which help prevent immoral behavior; and “so on”—which would include pleasure, pain, the power that brings things together born from mind and supplying the causes for mind.

gru.acip: ,GNYIS LAS SKYE BA'ANG RIGS PA'I NGO BO MA YIN GANG GI PHYIR, ,BSHAD ZIN NYES PA DE DAG THOG TU 'BAB PA YIN PHYIR RO, ,'DI NI 'JIG RTEN LAS MIN DE NYID DU YANG 'DOD MIN TE, ,GANG PHYIR RE RE LAS NI SKYE BA 'GRUB PA YOD MA YIN,
gru.wylie: gnyis las skye ba'ang rigs pa'i ngo bo ma yin gang gi phyir, ,bshad zin nyes pa de dag thog tu 'bab pa yin phyir ro, ,'di ni 'jig rten las min de nyid du yang 'dod min te, ,gang phyir re re las ni skye ba 'grub pa yod ma yin
gru.english: It is also not the nature Of clear thinking To say that things Could arise from A combination. Why is that? Because those same Problems already raised Would strike Like lightning. From the point Of the everyday world There are none; And speaking as well From the point of view Of suchness, Neither is this idea Something that We can accept. The reason That this is true Is that there Is no such thing As an arising Accomplished separately.

gru.acip: GANG GI PHYIR BDAG GZHAN RE RE LAS NI SKYE BA 'GRUB PA YOD PA MA YIN PAS GNYIS KA LAS SKYE BA YANG RIGS PA MA YIN NO,,
gru.wylie: gang gi phyir bdag gzhan re re las ni skye ba 'grub pa yod pa ma yin pas gnyis ka las skye ba yang rigs pa ma yin no
gru.english: The reason that this is true is that there is no such thing as an arising of things which is accomplished separately, either from the thing itself, or from things other than itself. As such, it would be illogical then to say that something could arise from both together. And never with no cause

gru.acip: SPYIR MNGON SUM DU MA ZAD RJES DPAG LAS RAB TU GRUB PAS KYANG SKYES BU'I DON SGRUB PA YIN NA RJES DPAG 'DI NI KHYOD KYIS KHAS BLANGS PA YANG MA YIN TE, ,JI TZAM DBANG PO'I SPYOD YUL BA, ,SKYES BU DE TZAM KHO NAR ZAD, ,BZANG MO MANG THOS GANG SMRA BA, ,DE NI SPYANG KI'I RJES DANG 'DRA,
gru.wylie: spyir mngon sum du ma zad rjes dpag las rab tu grub pas kyang skyes bu'i don sgrub pa yin na rjes dpag 'di ni khyod kyis khas blangs pa yang ma yin te, ,ji tsam dbang po'i spyod yul ba, ,skyes bu de tsam kho nar zad, ,bzang mo mang thos gang smra ba, ,de ni spyang ki'i rjes dang 'dra
gru.english: Generally speaking, it is not only through direct forms of accurate perception that people can achieve their ends; they also use deductive forms of accurate perception. Therefore, it's not as if this kind of deduction is not something that you would accept. As the lines go, There are those who say That it ends with the Objects of the activity Of the physical senses. O pure lady, Those like this Who are called learned Are as much a wolf As its tracks.

gru.acip: CI STE 'BYUNG BA BDEN PAR RTOGS PA'I TSE YANG PHYIN CI MA LOG PAS MTHONG BA'I DPE BSGRUB BYA'I CHOS KYIS STONG PA YIN NO SNYAM NA,
gru.wylie: ci ste 'byung ba bden par rtogs pa'i tshe yang phyin ci ma log pas mthong ba'i dpe bsgrub bya'i chos kyis stong pa yin no snyam na
gru.english: In response to this, you might think to yourself the following— When we perceive the elements as existing in truth, that is an unmistaken perception. The example then you use of something we can supposedly see is itself totally devoid of the quality you are trying to establish.

gru.acip: DE YANG YOD PA MA YIN TE RANG BZHIN GYIS MA SKYES PA DANG YOD PA MIN PA'I 'BYUNG BA LA RANG BZHIN GYIS YOD PA DANG SKYE BA NYID DU RTOGS PAS PHYIN CI LOG TU LTA BA NYID GRUB PA'I PHYIR RO,,
gru.wylie: de yang yod pa ma yin te rang bzhin gyis ma skyes pa dang yod pa min pa'i 'byung ba la rang bzhin gyis yod pa dang skye ba nyid du rtogs pas phyin ci log tu lta ba nyid grub pa'i phyir ro
gru.english: But this is not the case either. Suppose you perceive that elements which do not actually exist through any nature of their own, and which in fact do not have any existence, could exist through just such a nature, or could arise in just the way you think. This kind of view of things is established as being one which is completely mistaken.

gru.acip: 'DIS NI RANG GI RTAGS YANG DAG GI SBYOR BA RNAMS LA DPER BZUNG BA LA BSGRUB BYA'I CHOS KYIS MI STONG BA DGOS PAR BSTAN TE, RTAGS SU BZUNG BA LA YANG 'DRA LA, SNGAR SGRA MI RTAG PAR SGRUB PA LA MIG GIS GZUNG BYA BKOD PA MA GRUB PA'I RTAGS SU YANG BSHAD PAS DAM BCA' RTAGS KYIS SGRUB PA LA TSUL GSUM DGOS PAR BSTAN NO,,
gru.wylie: 'dis ni rang gi rtags yang dag gi sbyor ba rnams la dper bzung ba la bsgrub bya'i chos kyis mi stong ba dgos par bstan te, rtags su bzung ba la yang 'dra la, sngar sgra mi rtag par sgrub pa la mig gis gzung bya bkod pa ma grub pa'i rtags su yang bshad pas dam bca' rtags kyis sgrub pa la tshul gsum dgos par bstan no
gru.english: What all this is showing is that when we present a representative example to accompany an accurate logical statement, it must in fact not be empty of the quality that we are trying to prove. That is, what we take as the reason in the proof remains as it was; if we have been trying to prove that sound is something changing, and then give “because it is something perceived by the sense power of the eye” as the reason, then we would say that this is an invalid reason. And so the point is that—in order to establish an assertion by using a certain reason—all three relationships of a valid proof must be present.

gru.acip: 'BYUNG BA RANG BZHIN GYIS MA SKYES PA DE NYID BSGRUB PAR BYA DGOS SO ZHE NA,
gru.wylie: 'byung ba rang bzhin gyis ma skyes pa de nyid bsgrub par bya dgos so zhe na
gru.english: And suppose you say, Well the thing that you should be proving is that one thing: that the elements never arise through any nature of their own.

gru.acip: GANG GI PHYIR NA GONG DU RANG DANG, GZHAN LAS DANG, GNYIS KA LAS SKYE BA DANG, RGYU MED DU SKYE BA 'GOG PAR BYED PA NA 'BYUNG BA RANG BZHIN GYIS SKYE BA YANG BDAG GIS THUN MONG DU NI STE SPYIR BKAG ZIN PA DE YI PHYIR, 'BYUNG BA 'DI DAG LTA ZHIG STE GANG YANG SNGAR SPYI'I TSUL GYIS BKAG PAS MA BSHAD PA YOD PA MA YIN PAS DPE GRUB BO,,
gru.wylie: gang gi phyir na gong du rang dang, gzhan las dang, gnyis ka las skye ba dang, rgyu med du skye ba 'gog par byed pa na 'byung ba rang bzhin gyis skye ba yang bdag gis thun mong du ni ste spyir bkag zin pa de yi phyir, 'byung ba 'di dag lta zhig ste gang yang sngar spyi'i tshul gyis bkag pas ma bshad pa yod pa ma yin pas dpe grub bo
gru.english: And how was it that we explained that? We undertook to deny, previously, that things could grow from themselves; from something other than themselves; from both themselves and from something other than themselves; or without any cause at all. As such, we have already denied the common or general idea that the elements could grow through any nature of their own. Therefore much less with these elements, but with anything at all, in very general terms, we have made our denial; this is not something where we have given no explanation of the case; and thus the example is proof.

gru.acip: DE BZHIN DU THAMS CAD MKHYEN PA LA SKUR PA 'DEBS PA DANG, DE LAS GZHAN PA'I RANG BZHIN GYI DNGOS POR SMRA BA RNAMS KYI GRUB PA'I MTHA' 'GOG PA NA YANG, RTOGS PA PHYIN CI LOG PA SBYAR BAR BYA STE,
gru.wylie: de bzhin du thams cad mkhyen pa la skur pa 'debs pa dang, de las gzhan pa'i rang bzhin gyi dngos por smra ba rnams kyi grub pa'i mtha' 'gog pa na yang, rtogs pa phyin ci log pa sbyar bar bya ste
gru.english: We need to disprove the positions of those who discount any state of omniscience, and any other such ideas of those who profess some entities which could exist through some nature of their own, by making reference to the same sorts of basic wrong ideas.

gru.acip: CI STE KHYOD LA YANG THAL BAR 'GYUR BA 'DI MTSUNGS SO SNYAM NA DE YANG YOD PA MA YIN TE, KHO BO CAG PHYIN CI LOG PAR SGRUB PA LA DPE MED PA'I PHYIR RO,,
gru.wylie: ci ste khyod la yang thal bar 'gyur ba 'di mtshungs so snyam na de yang yod pa ma yin te, kho bo cag phyin ci log par sgrub pa la dpe med pa'i phyir ro
gru.english: And suppose you think to yourself that the necessary implications raised here are just the same for our own beliefs. But that is in fact not the case, for we have presented no example that is meant to prove something that is entirely mistaken.

gru.acip: DE'I PHYIR TSUL 'DIS NI, ,DE NYID DE LAS 'BYUNG MIN GZHAN DAG LAS LTA GA LA ZHIG ,GNYIS KA LAS KYANG MA YIN RGYU MED PAR NI GA LA YOD, CES GANG DAM BCAS BAR {%PAR} GYUR PA BZHI PO RAB TU BSGRUBS PA YIN NO, ZHES GSUNGS PAS GZHAN LUGS BKAG PA YIN GYI RANG LUGS MA BSGRUBS SO ZHES SMRA BAR MI BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: de'i phyir tshul 'dis ni, ,de nyid de las 'byung min gzhan dag las lta ga la zhig ,gnyis ka las kyang ma yin rgyu med par ni ga la yod, ces gang dam bcas bar {%par} gyur pa bzhi po rab tu bsgrubs pa yin no, zhes gsungs pas gzhan lugs bkag pa yin gyi rang lugs ma bsgrubs so zhes smra bar mi bya'o
gru.english: The autocommentary concludes here with— And so we see it stated that (the four points) which we assert are perfectly established: That never came From that thing itself; And so how Could it ever have come From other things? Neither did it come From both; And how could it Ever have come Without a cause at all? Thus we would have to ask you not to make the claim here that the position of the other side has been denied, but that our own position has not been substantiated. Where the four take us

gru.acip: RGYU MTSAN GANG GI PHYIR NA BDAG DANG GZHAN DANG GNYIS KA LAS SKYE BA DANG, RGYU LAM {%LA MA} LTOS PAR SKYE BA YOD PA MIN PAS DNGOS PO RNAMS RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA DANG BRAL LO, ZHES SMOS SO,,
gru.wylie: rgyu mtshan gang gi phyir na bdag dang gzhan dang gnyis ka las skye ba dang, rgyu lam {%la ma} ltos par skye ba yod pa min pas dngos po rnams rang bzhin gyis grub pa dang bral lo, zhes smos so
gru.english: For the reason that there can exist no arising of a thing which could occur from itself, or from something other than itself, or from both, or without relying upon any cause at all, we can say that entities are devoid of existing through some nature of their own.

gru.acip: DNGOS PO RNAMS ZHES PA NI CHOS CAN NO, ,RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA DANG BRAL BA NI DAM BCA'O,,
gru.wylie: dngos po rnams zhes pa ni chos can no, ,rang bzhin gyis grub pa dang bral ba ni dam bca'o
gru.english: The subject under consideration here is provided by the phrase, “all entities.” And the assertion is provided by saying “they are devoid of existing through any nature of their own.” Refuting debate about the denial

gru.acip: RANG GI NGO BOS GRUB PA MIN BZHIN DU DER SNANG BA NI, GTI MUG GI DBANG GIS YIN NO ZHES PHYI'I DPE'I SGO NAS BSTAN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: rang gi ngo bos grub pa min bzhin du der snang ba ni, gti mug gi dbang gis yin no zhes phyi'i dpe'i sgo nas bstan pa'i phyir
gru.english: The answer is that what comes next in the root text is meant to present a follow-up metaphor to indicate how the fact that things appear to exist through some essential nature of their own—even though they have no such nature—is due to dark ignorance.

gru.acip: DE'I PHYIR 'DI NI RNAL 'BYOR PA RNAMS LA BRGAL ZHING BRTAG PA MA YIN TE, DE DAG GIS NI KUN RDZOB TU YANG CHOS 'GA' ZHIG LA NGO BOS GRUB PA'I RANG BZHIN 'GA' YANG MA GZIGS LA, DON DAM PAR YANG CI YANG MA GZIGS SO,,
gru.wylie: de'i phyir 'di ni rnal 'byor pa rnams la brgal zhing brtag pa ma yin te, de dag gis ni kun rdzob tu yang chos 'ga' zhig la ngo bos grub pa'i rang bzhin 'ga' yang ma gzigs la, don dam par yang ci yang ma gzigs so
gru.english: As such, it is not the case that all this is meant to be conjecture or argument with those deep practitioners. They for their part see no kind of nature in any kind of thing at all, where these could exist through some essential nature of their own, even deceptively. Neither do they see how these could have any such nature in an ultimate way.

gru.acip: DE'I RGYU MTSAN YANG GAL TE 'GA' ZHIG LA RANG BZHIN TE NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB PA YOD NA, DE SKYE BAR 'GYUR NA RANG BZHIN DE YANG YOD PA MIN PAS CI ZHIG SKYE BAR 'GYUR, DE'I PHYIR MYA NGAN LAS 'DAS PA STE RNAM PAR DAG PA'O,,
gru.wylie: de'i rgyu mtshan yang gal te 'ga' zhig la rang bzhin te ngo bo nyid kyis grub pa yod na, de skye bar 'gyur na rang bzhin de yang yod pa min pas ci zhig skye bar 'gyur, de'i phyir mya ngan las 'das pa ste rnam par dag pa'o
gru.english: And this in itself has a reason. Suppose that there did exist some number of entities that did exist through some nature of their own—through some essential quality. If they were to grow then, then they could no longer have that nature; what then is it that grew? As such, these things are described as “nirvana”; which is to say, as being completely pure.

gru.acip: GAL TE BUM PA LA SOGS PAR GDAGS PA'I RTEN 'BYUNG BA BZHI DANG, 'BYUNG 'GYUR BZHI LA SOGS PA RNAMS RDZAS GRUB TU YOD PA'I PHYIR, BUM PA LA SOGS PAR BTAGS PA NI RGYU 'AM GZHI DANG BCAS PAR RIGS NA DBU MA PA LTAR NA CHOS THAMS CAD BTAGS PA TZAM KHO NA YIN GYI, BTAGS PA'I RTEN RDZAS SU GRUB PA CI YANG MED PA LA MO GSHAM GYI BU DANG 'DRA BAR THAL BA LDOG PA MED DO SNYAM NA,
gru.wylie: gal te bum pa la sogs par gdags pa'i rten 'byung ba bzhi dang, 'byung 'gyur bzhi la sogs pa rnams rdzas grub tu yod pa'i phyir, bum pa la sogs par btags pa ni rgyu 'am gzhi dang bcas par rigs na dbu ma pa ltar na chos thams cad btags pa tsam kho na yin gyi, btags pa'i rten rdzas su grub pa ci yang med pa la mo gsham gyi bu dang 'dra bar thal ba ldog pa med do snyam na
gru.english: One might then have the following thought— Let's consider the four elements, and the four products of the elements, and so on which provide the basis for labeling something as a pitcher or the like. These exist substantially, and so suppose that it is acceptable to say that when we label a pitcher or something similar, there is an accompanying cause or basis. According to those of the Middle Way, every object in the universe exists only as something labeled, but there is never any basis for the labeling that could substantially. As such there is no avoiding the necessary implication that everything would be like the child of a barren woman.

gru.acip: DE YANG MI RIGS TE, BTAGS PA'I RTEN RDZAS SU GRUB PAR SGRUB PAR MI NUS PA'I PHYIR RO,,
gru.wylie: de yang mi rigs te, btags pa'i rten rdzas su grub par sgrub par mi nus pa'i phyir ro
gru.english: And yet this is incorrect, since there is no way of proving that the basis for the labeling exists in a substantial manner.

gru.acip: RTZA SHE LAS KYANG, ,BYED PO LAS LA BRTEN BYAS SHING, ,LAS KYANG BYED PO DE NYID LA, ,BRTEN NAS 'BYUNG BA MA GTOGS PAR, ,'GRUB PA'I RGYU NI MA MTHONG NGO,
gru.wylie: rtsa she las kyang, ,byed po las la brten byas shing, ,las kyang byed po de nyid la, ,brten nas 'byung ba ma gtogs par, ,'grub pa'i rgyu ni ma mthong ngo
gru.english: Wisdom says as well— An agent is created Dependent upon its action. An action as well Comes about in dependence On nothing less Than its agent. Aside from this, We can see No cause which would Establish them.

gru.acip: SLOB DPON 'DIS SPYIR SKYE BA GZHAG DGOS PA DANG, MTHA' BZHI LAS MI SKYE BA'I PHYIR BRTEN NAS SKYE BAR 'GYUR RO, ZHES 'BAD PA DU MAS BSGRUBS PA LA,
gru.wylie: slob dpon 'dis spyir skye ba gzhag dgos pa dang, mtha' bzhi las mi skye ba'i phyir brten nas skye bar 'gyur ro, zhes 'bad pa du mas bsgrubs pa la
gru.english: Our master here must necessarily set forth how it is that things arise; and he is establishing—by expending quite considerable efforts—how it is that they arise through dependence, since they cannot arise through any of the four extreme options.

gru.acip: RANG BZHIN GYIS YOD PAR SGRO 'DOGS PA'I RTAG PAR LTA BA DANG, BYA BYED MI 'THAD PA'I CHAD PAR LTA BA DANG, DUS SNGA MA NA YOD PA DE NYID DUS PHYI MA RNAMS SU 'ANG YOD PA'I RTOG PA DANG, RANG BZHIN GYIS SNGA PHYI SO SO BA'I SKAD CIG MA'I MI RTAG PA DANG, DNGOS PO DANG DNGOS POR MED PA GNYIS NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB PA LA SOGS PAR RTOG PA'ANG BRTAGS PA'I YUL GZHAN DAG KYANG, MI SRID DO ZHES BSTAN PA'I PHYIR BSHAD PA,
gru.wylie: rang bzhin gyis yod par sgro 'dogs pa'i rtag par lta ba dang, bya byed mi 'thad pa'i chad par lta ba dang, dus snga ma na yod pa de nyid dus phyi ma rnams su 'ang yod pa'i rtog pa dang, rang bzhin gyis snga phyi so so ba'i skad cig ma'i mi rtag pa dang, dngos po dang dngos por med pa gnyis ngo bo nyid kyis grub pa la sogs par rtog pa'ang brtags pa'i yul gzhan dag kyang, mi srid do zhes bstan pa'i phyir bshad pa
gru.english: Because now, with the following lines of the root text, we will describe how other options here that are products of sheer imagination are flatly impossible. These include ideas like the following— The view that things could never change, due to overrating these things and holding them to exist through some nature of their own; The view that things would simply discontinue, due to the belief that the way everything works in the world is something mistaken; The notion that the very same things which existed at some previous point in time could also exist at a later point in time; The idea of a changing nature to things consisting of discrete milliseconds of time which exist, through some nature of their own, either earlier or later; or else The concept of existents and non-existents—both of them—that could through some essential nature of their own.

gru.acip: 'DI LTAR RKYEN NYID 'DI PA TZAM ZHIG RTEN 'BREL GYI DON DU 'JOG PA'I DBU MA PAS NI, DNGOS PO 'GA' LA YANG RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA KHAS MA BLANGS TE,
gru.wylie: 'di ltar rkyen nyid 'di pa tsam zhig rten 'brel gyi don du 'jog pa'i dbu ma pas ni, dngos po 'ga' la yang rang bzhin gyis grub pa khas ma blangs te
gru.english: And thus it is that those of the Middle Way establish the meaning of dependence, as nothing more complicated than talking about this particular factor for things. They do not agree that any entity that ever exists could come about through some nature of its own.

gru.acip: ZHES RTEN 'BYUNG YIN PA NYID KYIS RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAS STONG PAR GSUNGS SHING,
gru.wylie: zhes rten 'byung yin pa nyid kyis rang bzhin gyis grub pas stong par gsungs shing
gru.english: What this is saying is that the very fact that something has occurred through dependence is enough to say that it is empty of existing through any nature of its own.

gru.acip: BSGRUB PAR BYA BA MA SKYES ZHES PA'I DON NI RKANG PA GNYIS PAS BSTAN TE, RANG BZHIN GYIS MA SKYES TE ZHES PA'I DON YIN GYI, DGAG BYA LA KHYAD PAR MA SBYAR BA MIN TE,
gru.wylie: bsgrub par bya ba ma skyes zhes pa'i don ni rkang pa gnyis pas bstan te, rang bzhin gyis ma skyes te zhes pa'i don yin gyi, dgag bya la khyad par ma sbyar ba min te
gru.english: What the reason is proving is expressed in the words, “never arose”; and its meaning is expressed in the second line of the verse [in Tibetan, corresponding to the second section in the English translation], where it says “that would not be something that had a nature of arising.” But it's not as if there is no distinction in the wording for what it is we're denying.

gru.acip: GANG GI TSE DE LTAR DNGOS PO RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA KHAS MA BLANGS PA DE'I TSE RANG BZHIN MED PA NI BDAG GZHAN LAS SKYE BA LA SOGS PA GANG ZHIG TU 'BYUNG BAR 'GYUR,
gru.wylie: gang gi tshe de ltar dngos po rang bzhin gyis grub pa khas ma blangs pa de'i tshe rang bzhin med pa ni bdag gzhan las skye ba la sogs pa gang zhig tu 'byung bar 'gyur
gru.english: At the point where we refuse to accept that idea that things could exist through some nature of their own, then the general lack of a self-nature to things begins to refer to the fact that—for example—things might arise from themselves, or from something other than themselves.

gru.acip: GAL TE RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA 'GA' ZHIG YOD NA NI DE'I TSE SKYE BA NGO BO NYID LAS SAM BDAG GZHAN DANG DBANG PHYUG SOGS LAS SKYE BAR 'GYUR ZHING,
gru.wylie: gal te rang bzhin gyis grub pa 'ga' zhig yod na ni de'i tshe skye ba ngo bo nyid las sam bdag gzhan dang dbang phyug sogs las skye bar 'gyur zhing
gru.english: If there did exist some kind of natural existence to things, then the arising of things could be something that happened in and of itself; or from itself or something other than itself; or from some supreme being—or something else of the like.

gru.acip: MTHAR 'DZIN PA'I RTOG PA RNAMS DNGOS PO RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAR 'DZIN PA YOD NA 'BYUNG BAR 'GYUR BA STE, JI SKAD BSHAD PA'I RIGS PAS DNGOS PO RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA JI LTAR YANG MED PAR YONGS SU DPYAD ZIN LA,
gru.wylie: mthar 'dzin pa'i rtog pa rnams dngos po rang bzhin gyis grub par 'dzin pa yod na 'byung bar 'gyur ba ste, ji skad bshad pa'i rigs pas dngos po rang bzhin gyis grub pa ji ltar yang med par yongs su dpyad zin la
gru.english: Suppose it happens that these notions that hold to the extremes come up, and they begin to hold that things could exist through some nature of their own. We have already examined in depth—with the logic we covered—how any existence of things through this kind of nature is something that could never be.

gru.acip: DNGOS PO RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAR 'DZIN PA MED PAR MTHAR 'DZIN GYI RTOG PA 'DI RNAMS MI 'BYUNG STE, DPER NA RGYU BUD SHING MED PAR 'BRAS BU ME YOD PA MIN PA DE BZHIN NO,,
gru.wylie: dngos po rang bzhin gyis grub par 'dzin pa med par mthar 'dzin gyi rtog pa 'di rnams mi 'byung ste, dper na rgyu bud shing med par 'bras bu me yod pa min pa de bzhin no
gru.english: In the absence though of the habit of holding that things could exist through some nature of their own, these kinds of notions will never come up; it's like, for example, the way that the result of fire can never occur in the absence of its cause: the firewood.

gru.acip: BDAG GZHAN GYI PHYOGS LA CHAGS PA DANG KHRO BA'I PHYOGS LHUNG DOR NAS GZU BO'I BLOS MA DPYAD NA, GRUB MTHA' LA DPYOD PAR SGOM PA DE NYID LA BRTEN NAS 'KHOR BAR DAM DU 'CHING BAR GSUNGS PA 'DI NYID, BDAG CAG RNAMS LA THUGS BRTZE BAS MAN NGAG KHYAD PAR CAN BYIN PAR SHES PAR GYIS SHIG
gru.wylie: bdag gzhan gyi phyogs la chags pa dang khro ba'i phyogs lhung dor nas gzu bo'i blos ma dpyad na, grub mtha' la dpyod par sgom pa de nyid la brten nas 'khor bar dam du 'ching bar gsungs pa 'di nyid, bdag cag rnams la thugs brtse bas man ngag khyad par can byin par shes par gyis shig
gru.english: Suppose we are unable to let go of this kind of prejudice, of attachment and hatred towards the positions we ourselves hold, and those of others—we are unable to think out things with an unbiased state of mind. What this very citation is saying is that—when we accustom ourselves to just this kind of analysis of the various schools of thought—it will chain us ever more tightly to the circle of pain. And so all of us should understand that we have thus been granted some very special words of advice, from a person who really loves us.

gru.acip: GNYIS PA GANG ZAG GI BDAG MED RIGS PAS BSGRUB PA LA GSUM, THAR 'DOD KYIS THOG MAR BDAG RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA NYID DGAG DGOS PAR BSTAN PA, BDAG DANG BDAG GI BA GNYIS RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA 'GOG PA'I TSUL, BDAG DANG SHING RTA'I DPYAD PA DNGOS PO GZHAN LA YANG BSGRE BAR BSTAN PA'O, ,DANG PO NI,
gru.wylie: gnyis pa gang zag gi bdag med rigs pas bsgrub pa la gsum, thar 'dod kyis thog mar bdag rang bzhin gyis grub pa nyid dgag dgos par bstan pa, bdag dang bdag gi ba gnyis rang bzhin gyis grub pa 'gog pa'i tshul, bdag dang shing rta'i dpyad pa dngos po gzhan la yang bsgre bar bstan pa'o, ,dang po ni
gru.english: With this we have reached our second major part from above, on using reasoning to prove that the person has no self-nature. This itself we will cover in three sections: (1) showing how those who wish to achieve freedom need, before anything else, to deny that the self is something that could exist through any nature of its own; (2) how it is that we deny the idea that either me or mine could exist through any nature of their own; and (3) the way in which we can apply our examination of the self, and of a wagon, to other entities as well. Here is the first.

gru.acip: DE LTAR BRTAGS PA NA NYON MONGS PA NI 'DOD CHAGS LA SOGS PA DANG, SKYON RNAMS NI SKYE RGA NA 'CHI LA SOGS PA STE DE RNAMS MA LUS PAR NGA DANG NGA'I 'O SNYAM PA'I RNAM PA CAN DE GNYIS RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAR 'DZIN PA'I SHES RAB NYON MONGS PA CAN GYI 'JIG TSOGS LA LTA BA LAS BYUNG BAR BLO YIS MTHONG BAR 'GYUR TE, DE DAG NI MA LUS PAR 'JIG TSOGS LA LTA BA'I 'BRAS BU YIN NO,,
gru.wylie: de ltar brtags pa na nyon mongs pa ni 'dod chags la sogs pa dang, skyon rnams ni skye rga na 'chi la sogs pa ste de rnams ma lus par nga dang nga'i 'o snyam pa'i rnam pa can de gnyis rang bzhin gyis grub par 'dzin pa'i shes rab nyon mongs pa can gyi 'jig tshogs la lta ba las byung bar blo yis mthong bar 'gyur te, de dag ni ma lus par 'jig tshogs la lta ba'i 'bras bu yin no
gru.english: And when we examine this question, our intellect comes to see where it is that everything related to negative emotions—ignorant desire and the like—as well as all the rest of our problems (birth, aging, death, and so on) really comes from. And the fact is that each & every one of these troubles comes the view of destruction, which is a kind of negative intelligence where we have thoughts about “me” and “mine” and hold these two to exist through some nature of their own. That is, each and every one of those pains is a result of the view of destruction.

gru.acip: DE YANG DE'I DMIGS PA BDAG GI BDAG STE NGO BOS GRUB PA MED PAR KHONG DU CHUD PA LAS SPONG BAR 'GYUR BAS, RNAL 'BYOR PAS GANG ZHIG BDAG TU 'DZIN PA'I YUL BDAG CES BYA BA 'DI, NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB MA GRUB CI 'DRA BA ZHIG CES THOG MAR BDAG KHO NA LA RTOG PAR BYED DO,,
gru.wylie: de yang de'i dmigs pa bdag gi bdag ste ngo bos grub pa med par khong du chud pa las spong bar 'gyur bas, rnal 'byor pas gang zhig bdag tu 'dzin pa'i yul bdag ces bya ba 'di, ngo bo nyid kyis grub ma grub ci 'dra ba zhig ces thog mar bdag kho na la rtog par byed do
gru.english: This in itself is something that we have to eliminate by coming to a realization that my “me”—the object that this view focuses upon—has nothing about it which could exist through some essential nature of its own. And so it is that that the deep practitioner is going to have to decide—at the beginning, only with regard to themselves—the question of whether this “self” that the tendency to hold to a self grasps on to is something that could exist though some essential nature of its own, or not.

gru.acip: RNAL 'BYOR PA YIS BDAG DE NI RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA 'GOG PAR BYED PA LAS, 'JIG LTA SPANGS NA NYES SKYON KUN LDOG PAS NA, BDAG LA RNAM PAR DPYAD PA 'DI NI THAR PA SGRUB PA'I THABS YIN TE,
gru.wylie: rnal 'byor pa yis bdag de ni rang bzhin gyis grub pa 'gog par byed pa las, 'jig lta spangs na nyes skyon kun ldog pas na, bdag la rnam par dpyad pa 'di ni thar pa sgrub pa'i thabs yin te
gru.english: The way it goes is that the deep practitioner works to stop the idea that the self is something that could exist through some nature of its own; this then eliminates the view of destruction, which in turn puts a stop to all the problems there ever were. As such, the examination of whether a self exists or not is itself the method for attaining freedom.

gru.acip: BSLAB BTUS LAS, GANG ZAG STONG PA NYID NI DE LTAR SHIN TU GRUB PA YIN NA, ,DE'I PHYIR RTZA BA CHAD PAS NYON MONGS PA THAMS CAD KUN TU MI 'BYUNG NGO,,
gru.wylie: bslab btus las, gang zag stong pa nyid ni de ltar shin tu grub pa yin na, ,de'i phyir rtsa ba chad pas nyon mongs pa thams cad kun tu mi 'byung ngo
gru.english: As the Compendium of All the Trainings puts it, Suppose that a person is able to prove, beyond the shadow of a doubt, the emptiness of the person. This has the effect of stopping each and everyone one of the negative emotions, completely—because it severs their very root.

gru.acip: GNYIS KA YANG RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PAR 'DZIN PA'I RNAM PA CAN YIN PA'I PHYIR DANG, 'KHOR BA'I RTZA BA GNYIS 'GAL BA NA YUL LA 'JUG PA'I 'DZIN STANGS MI MTHUN PA GNYIS 'KHOR BA'I RTZA BAR 'JOG PA LA BYED PA'I PHYIR,,
gru.wylie: gnyis ka yang rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub par 'dzin pa'i rnam pa can yin pa'i phyir dang, 'khor ba'i rtsa ba gnyis 'gal ba na yul la 'jug pa'i 'dzin stangs mi mthun pa gnyis 'khor ba'i rtsa bar 'jog pa la byed pa'i phyir
gru.english: And that's because both of them display an aspect where they hold their object to exist through some nature of its own. And if the two roots of the circle of pain were to contradict each other, then one would have to establish the root of this cycle as consisting of two manners of engaging in an object which were internally inconsistent with each other.

gru.acip: GNYIS PA LA GNYIS, BDAG RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA DGAG PA DANG, BDAG GI BA RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA DGAG PA'O,,
gru.wylie: gnyis pa la gnyis, bdag rang bzhin gyis grub pa dgag pa dang, bdag gi ba rang bzhin gyis grub pa dgag pa'o
gru.english: Which brings us to our second section from above: how it is that we deny the idea that either me or mine could exist through any nature of their own. We proceed in two steps: denying that the self could exist through any nature of its own; and then denying that what belongs to the self could exist through any nature of its own.

gru.acip: 'BAD PA NI DON BSGRUB PAR BYA BA LA DE'I MTHAR THUG PAR SEMS KYI MKHAS PA NYID DO,,
gru.wylie: 'bad pa ni don bsgrub par bya ba la de'i mthar thug par sems kyi mkhas pa nyid do
gru.english: (6) Endeavor consists of a special mental fluency in achieving the final ends of attempts to accomplish some goal.

gru.acip: GANG LAS MNGON PAR MTHO BA DANG NGES PAR LEGS PA 'GRUB PA DE NI CHOS SO,,
gru.wylie: gang las mngon par mtho ba dang nges par legs pa 'grub pa de ni chos so
gru.english: (7) Teachings are those things which allow us to achieve higher rebirths and final good.

gru.acip: BDAG GI YON TAN DGU PO DE JI SRID DU BDAG LA 'DU ZHING YOD PA DE SRID DU, DE DAG GIS SBYAR BA'I DGE BA DANG MI DGE BA'I LAS SGRUB PA'I PHYIR 'KHOR BAR 'GYUR LA,
gru.wylie: bdag gi yon tan dgu po de ji srid du bdag la 'du zhing yod pa de srid du, de dag gis sbyar ba'i dge ba dang mi dge ba'i las sgrub pa'i phyir 'khor bar 'gyur la
gru.english: As long as these nine attributes of the self are incorporated into ourselves—as long as they are present there—then we tend to undertake good deeds and bad karma utilizing the nine. This then causes us to circle in the wheel of pain.

gru.acip: RNAM PA'I YUL NI GANG ZAG GI BDAG YIN PAS DE NI THA SNYAD TZAM DU YANG MA GRUB PA YIN PAS, MA SKYES PA DANG MI 'GAL LO,,
gru.wylie: rnam pa'i yul ni gang zag gi bdag yin pas de ni tha snyad tsam du yang ma grub pa yin pas, ma skyes pa dang mi 'gal lo
gru.english: Then there is the object as represented by the aspect here—which would refer to the self-nature of the person. This is not something which can exist even in a nominal sense, and so it would not contradict the idea of things never arising.

gru.acip: DE'I PHYIR 'DI'I LUGS KYIS GANG ZAG GI BDAG THA SNYAD DU YOD PAR 'DOD DO ZHES PA NI 'DI PA'I GRUB MTHA'I 'GANGS DANG, 'JIG LTA'I DMIGS RNAM GYI YUL ZHIB TU MA PHYED PAR BYUNG RGYAL DU SMRA BA'O,,
gru.wylie: de'i phyir 'di'i lugs kyis gang zag gi bdag tha snyad du yod par 'dod do zhes pa ni 'di pa'i grub mtha'i 'gangs dang, 'jig lta'i dmigs rnam gyi yul zhib tu ma phyed par byung rgyal du smra ba'o
gru.english: Therefore those who say that “The way that this present system accepts the existence of the self-nature to the person, at least nominally, is its one most crucial concept” and then failing to distinguish this carefully from the object represented by the aspect of focus taken on by the view of destruction represents no more than blurting out whatever comes to their minds.

gru.acip: ,DE PHYIR PHUNG PO LAS GZHAN BDAG MED DE, ,PHUNG PO MA GTOGS DE 'DZIN MA GRUB PHYIR, ,'JIG RTEN NGAR 'DZIN BLO YI RTEN DU YANG, ,MI 'DOD DE RIG MIN PA'ANG BDAG LTA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: de phyir phung po las gzhan bdag med de, ,phung po ma gtogs de 'dzin ma grub phyir, ,'jig rten ngar 'dzin blo yi rten du yang, ,mi 'dod de rig min pa'ang bdag lta'i phyir
gru.english: And this is why There is no self Separate from the Parts of the person: Because you could Never establish The capacity to hold To some that didn't Involve the parts. Neither are we saying That it is the basis For the tendency To hold to some “me” That the world Thinks of; That is not something Which could ever Make sense. And that's because Even then we could View something As the self.

gru.acip: DE'I PHYIR PHUNG PO LAS NGO BO GZHAN PA'I BDAG MED DE, PHUNG PO BZUNG BA MA GTOGS PAR BDAG DE YAN GAR DU 'DZIN PA MA GRUB PA'I PHYIR RO,,
gru.wylie: de'i phyir phung po las ngo bo gzhan pa'i bdag med de, phung po bzung ba ma gtogs par bdag de yan gar du 'dzin pa ma grub pa'i phyir ro
gru.english: And this is why we can say that there is no self which is essentially separate from the parts of the person; and that's because you could never establish the capacity to hold to some discrete self that didn't involve holding to the parts of the person.

gru.acip: DE NI MA YIN TE GRUB MTHA' NGAN PAS BLO BSGYUR BA KHO NA LA, PHUNG PO LAS NGO BO THA DAD PA'I BDAG NGAR 'DZIN GYI RTEN DU 'DZIN PA YOD PA YIN PA'I PHYIR RO,,
gru.wylie: de ni ma yin te grub mtha' ngan pas blo bsgyur ba kho na la, phung po las ngo bo tha dad pa'i bdag ngar 'dzin gyi rten du 'dzin pa yod pa yin pa'i phyir ro
gru.english: Our answer is that it would not be the case. And that's because it is only with those individuals whose minds have been influenced by inferior schools of thought that the tendency to hold to some “me” grasps onto, as its basis, a self which is essentially separate from the parts to a person.

gru.acip: SEMS CAN GANG DAG LA SNGAR GRUB MTHA' NGAN PA'I GOMS PA MED PA DE DAG LA YANG 'DIR NGAR 'DZIN 'JUG PAR MTHONG STE, 'DI LTA STE,
gru.wylie: sems can gang dag la sngar grub mtha' ngan pa'i goms pa med pa de dag la yang 'dir ngar 'dzin 'jug par mthong ste, 'di lta ste
gru.english: We do however also see here—with individuals who have not previously become accustomed to some inferior school of thought—the mind engaging in the tendency to hold to some “me.” And here is how that works.

gru.acip: GNYIS PA LA LNGA, PHUNG PO BDAG TU 'DOD PA LA GNOD BYED BSTAN PA, DE LTAR 'DOD PAR MI RIGS PA'I SGRUB BYED BSTAN PA, PHUNG PO BDAG TU SMRA BA LA GNOD BYED GZHAN BSTAN PA, PHUNG PO BDAG TU GSUNGS PA SOGS KYI DGONGS PA BSHAD PA, GZHAN GYI LUGS 'BREL MED DU BSTAN PA'O,,
gru.wylie: gnyis pa la lnga, phung po bdag tu 'dod pa la gnod byed bstan pa, de ltar 'dod par mi rigs pa'i sgrub byed bstan pa, phung po bdag tu smra ba la gnod byed gzhan bstan pa, phung po bdag tu gsungs pa sogs kyi dgongs pa bshad pa, gzhan gyi lugs 'brel med du bstan pa'o
gru.english: These brings us to our second topic from above: denying the position concocted by some of our own groups, who believe that the parts to the person themselves represent the self. This we offer in five different sections— 1) A presentation of problems with the position that the parts to the person constitute the self; 2) A presentation of support for saying that this kind of belief is incorrect; 3) A presentation of other problems with saying that the parts to the person are the self; 4) An explanation of the actual intent behind statements that the parts to the person are the self, and so on; and 5) A demonstration that the position of others here is irrelevant to the case.

gru.acip: ,PHUNG PO LAS GZHAN BDAG GRUB MED PA'I PHYIR, ,BDAG LTA'I DMIGS PA PHUNG PO KHO NA'O, ,KHA CIG BDAG LTA'I RTEN DU PHUNG PO NI, ,LNGA CHAR YANG 'DOD KHA CIG SEMS GCIG 'DOD,
gru.wylie: phung po las gzhan bdag grub med pa'i phyir, ,bdag lta'i dmigs pa phung po kho na'o, ,kha cig bdag lta'i rten du phung po ni, ,lnga char yang 'dod kha cig sems gcig 'dod
gru.english: There is no self Which exists As separate from The parts to The person. As such, Seeing a self Takes as its Object of focus Only the parts. Some number Describe the support Of the view of a self As consisting Of all five Of the parts. Some assert That it is only The mind.

gru.acip: 'DIR RANG GI SDE PA DAG NA RE PHUNG PO LAS NGO BO GZHAN PA'I BDAG GRUB PA MED PA'I PHYIR BDAG TU LTA BA STE 'JIG TSOGS LA LTA BA'I DMIGS RNAM GNYIS KYI NANG GI DMIGS PA NI PHUNG PO KHO NA YIN TE, PHUNG PO LAS NGO BO THA DAD PA DANG NANG GI PHUNG PO DMIGS PAR 'JOG PA GNYIS SU NGES PA LAS SNGA MA MI RUNG BA'I PHYIR RO,,
gru.wylie: 'dir rang gi sde pa dag na re phung po las ngo bo gzhan pa'i bdag grub pa med pa'i phyir bdag tu lta ba ste 'jig tshogs la lta ba'i dmigs rnam gnyis kyi nang gi dmigs pa ni phung po kho na yin te, phung po las ngo bo tha dad pa dang nang gi phung po dmigs par 'jog pa gnyis su nges pa las snga ma mi rung ba'i phyir ro
gru.english: Here certain of our own groups make the following argument: There is no self which exists as essentially separate from the parts to the person; as such, the tendency to see a self—which is to say, the view of destruction, which has two objects of its focus—takes as its inner object of focus only the parts to the person. And that's due to the fact that the objects of focus here are fixed at two—no more, no less: one which is essentially separate from these parts to a person, and a second which is focused on the heaps inside; and it would be inappropriate here to include the former.

gru.acip: PHUNG PO LEN MKHAN NI BDAG YIN LA RNAM SHES KYIS YANG SRID LEN PA'I PHYIR RNAM SHES BDAG TU BZHAG GO ZHES RIGS PA'I SGRUB BYED SMRA'O,,
gru.wylie: phung po len mkhan ni bdag yin la rnam shes kyis yang srid len pa'i phyir rnam shes bdag tu bzhag go zhes rigs pa'i sgrub byed smra'o
gru.english: We also see statements of the supporting logic here: “The one who takes on the parts to a person is the self; and since it is our consciousness which takes on the next rebirth, then we can say that it is consciousness which must be the self.”

gru.acip: GZHAN YANG PHUNG PO DER LTA BA'I 'JIG TSOGS LA LTA BA RDZAS LA 'JUG PA STE RDZAS SU GRUB PA'I YUL CAN YIN PAS, SNGON PO DANG SER PO LA SOGS PA'I SHES PA LTAR PHYIN CI LOG NYID DU MI 'GYUR RO,,
gru.wylie: gzhan yang phung po der lta ba'i 'jig tshogs la lta ba rdzas la 'jug pa ste rdzas su grub pa'i yul can yin pas, sngon po dang ser po la sogs pa'i shes pa ltar phyin ci log nyid du mi 'gyur ro
gru.english: We can moreover say that the view of destruction that acts to view these parts to the person engages in substance; which is to say, it is a subject which takes as its object things which exist substantially. As such, in the sense that it is aware of things like blue and yellow and the like, it is not something which is exclusively mistaken.

gru.acip: DE YANG NANG GI BYED PA'I SKYES BU LA BSAMS NAS 'DRI NA NI, KHYAD GZHI MA GRUB PAS KHYAD PAR GYI CHOS LUNG BSTAN DU MED DO,,
gru.wylie: de yang nang gi byed pa'i skyes bu la bsams nas 'dri na ni, khyad gzhi ma grub pas khyad par gyi chos lung bstan du med do
gru.english: If these questions about things are intended as starting off from an individual considered as something inner, then—since the basis that we are considering doesn't exist at all—then it would be impossible to express an opinion about a quality that this basis supposedly possessed.

gru.acip: 'DI LA RIGS PA PHRA MO MA RTOGS NA LAN MI THEBS PAS BSHAD PAR BYA STE, PHA ROL POS PHUNG PO DANG SEMS BDAG TU 'DOD PA NI BDAG DANG GANG ZAG RNAMS THA SNYAD KYI DBANG GIS BZHAG PA TZAM DU MA RTOGS PAR BTAGS DON BTZAL NAS BZHAG PA YIN LA, DE LTAR NA PHUNG PO DANG SEMS BDAG YIN PA DE RANG GI NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB PA'I BDAG TU 'GYUR LA,
gru.wylie: 'di la rigs pa phra mo ma rtogs na lan mi thebs pas bshad par bya ste, pha rol pos phung po dang sems bdag tu 'dod pa ni bdag dang gang zag rnams tha snyad kyi dbang gis bzhag pa tsam du ma rtogs par btags don btsal nas bzhag pa yin la, de ltar na phung po dang sems bdag yin pa de rang gi ngo bo nyid kyis grub pa'i bdag tu 'gyur la
gru.english: There is some subtle reasoning here that—if you cannot grasp it—will prevent you from giving a proper answer here; so we'd better explain it. When the other side here holds that the parts to the person, or the mind, are the self, they are at the same time failing to realize that both the self and the person are things that are established only by force of terms. And then on this basis they are looking for what it is that we gave the name, and making a decision about what it should be. And then in this way the parts to the person and the mind that are supposed to be the self turn into a self that could exist through some essential nature of its own.

gru.acip: DANG PO LA GSUM, LUNG GI DGONGS PA DGAG BYA GCOD PA'I DGAG PHYOGS NAS YIN PAR BSTAN PA, SGRUB PHYOGS NAS YIN DU CHUG KYANG PHUNG PO BDAG TU STON PA MIN PA, DE DAG LA GZHAN GYI RTZOD PA SPANG BA'O, ,DANG PO NI,
gru.wylie: dang po la gsum, lung gi dgongs pa dgag bya gcod pa'i dgag phyogs nas yin par bstan pa, sgrub phyogs nas yin du chug kyang phung po bdag tu ston pa min pa, de dag la gzhan gyi rtsod pa spang ba'o, ,dang po ni
gru.english: The first of these five sections has three parts of its own: (1) a demonstration that the intent of the scriptural reference is meant in a negative connotation, where we are eliminating what we deny; (2) how this reference is not saying that the parts to the person are a self, even if we allow that the reference was meant in a positive sense; and (3) refuting additional argument on these points. Here then is the first of these.

gru.acip: MDO GANG LAS GZUGS SOGS RNAMS KYANG BDAG YIN PA BKAG PA DE LAS NI, BRTEN NAS BTAGS PA'I BDAG 'JIG LTA'I DMIGS PA 'DIS PHUNG PO LEN PA'I PHUNG PO'I NYE BAR LEN PA CAN RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA BKAG PAR RIG PAR BYA STE, GZUGS SOGS BDAG MIN PAR GSUNGS PA DE NI DE KHO NA NYID LA SEMS PA'I SKABS YIN PA'I PHYIR RO,,
gru.wylie: mdo gang las gzugs sogs rnams kyang bdag yin pa bkag pa de las ni, brten nas btags pa'i bdag 'jig lta'i dmigs pa 'dis phung po len pa'i phung po'i nye bar len pa can rang bzhin gyis grub pa bkag par rig par bya ste, gzugs sogs bdag min par gsungs pa de ni de kho na nyid la sems pa'i skabs yin pa'i phyir ro
gru.english: There are other sutras in which it is also denied that form and the rest could be the self; and from this we should understand that the self as labeled in dependence—what it is that the view of destruction focuses upon—serves to deny the idea that the one it is that takes on the parts to the person as these parts are taken could exist through any nature of its own. That is, statements that form and the rest are not the self are made in the context of considering the topic of suchness.

gru.acip: DE LTAR NYE BAR LEN PA PO RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA MA DMIGS NA, BDAG DE'I NYE BAR BLANG BAR BYA BA PHUNG PO YANG RANG BZHIN GYIS YOD PA MA YIN NO, ZHES GZUGS SOGS LA YANG BDEN PAR ZHEN PA'I 'DOD CHAGS DANG BRAL BA 'THAD PA NYID DO,,
gru.wylie: de ltar nye bar len pa po rang bzhin gyis grub pa ma dmigs na, bdag de'i nye bar blang bar bya ba phung po yang rang bzhin gyis yod pa ma yin no, zhes gzugs sogs la yang bden par zhen pa'i 'dod chags dang bral ba 'thad pa nyid do
gru.english: And so what we have here is the statement, “Suppose then that the one who does take these things on could not be someone who existed through some nature of their own. We would have to say in that case that what they did take on—the parts to the person—could never be entities that existed through some nature of their own either.” In that case then it would be perfectly appropriate to say that we were free from the desire which is so hungry to believe that form and the rest are real.

gru.acip: GAL TE NYE BAR LEN PA'I PHUNG PO LNGA PO 'DI DAG KHO NA LA LTA'O ZHES PA 'DI NI, SGRUB PHYOGS KYI SGO NAS PHUNG PO BDAG TU STON PA YIN KYANG, PHUNG PO RE RE NAS BDAG TU STON PA MIN NO,,
gru.wylie: gal te nye bar len pa'i phung po lnga po 'di dag kho na la lta'o zhes pa 'di ni, sgrub phyogs kyi sgo nas phung po bdag tu ston pa yin kyang, phung po re re nas bdag tu ston pa min no
gru.english: What then about statements that say, “It can only be considering the five parts to the person that we have taken on”? This is expressing the point positively, describing the parts to the person as the self; but it is not saying that each separate part to the person is the self.

gru.acip: DPER NA SHING RNAMS NI NAGS TSAL LO ZHES BRJOD PA NA, SHING GI TSOGS PA NAGS TSAL YIN GYI, SHING RE RE BA NAGS SU 'GYUR BAS SHING GI NGO BOR RE {%BO RE RE} BA NAGS SU BRJOD PA MIN PA BZHIN NO, ZHES GZHAN LA GRUB PA DPER BRJOD PA'O,,
gru.wylie: dper na shing rnams ni nags tshal lo zhes brjod pa na, shing gi tshogs pa nags tshal yin gyi, shing re re ba nags su 'gyur bas shing gi ngo bor re {%bo re re} ba nags su brjod pa min pa bzhin no, zhes gzhan la grub pa dper brjod pa'o
gru.english: Think for example when we use the expression “the forest of the trees.” It's the collection of the trees which is the forest; it is not though the case that each separate tree represents the forest, and that we are then referring to the essential nature of each tree and calling it a forest. All this then is being used as an example meant to apply to other things.

gru.acip: DE NYID SGRUB PA'I NGAG GIS GSAL BAR BYED PA NI, GANG ZHIG LA BRTEN NAS GANG BRTAGS PA DE NI BTAGS PA NYE BAR LEN PA'I YAN LAG TSOGS PA TZAM MA YIN TE, BRTEN NAS BTAGS PA'I PHYIR 'BYUNG BA LAS GYUR PA BZHIN NO,,
gru.wylie: de nyid sgrub pa'i ngag gis gsal bar byed pa ni, gang zhig la brten nas gang brtags pa de ni btags pa nye bar len pa'i yan lag tshogs pa tsam ma yin te, brten nas btags pa'i phyir 'byung ba las gyur pa bzhin no
gru.english: Here is a clarification of this very point, made through the use of supporting logic. That is, any entity which is ascribed on the basis of something is not the simple collection of the component parts that were taken on. The case is similar to one in which something has come from the elements, as it is labeled on their basis.

gru.acip: DE YANG YOD PA MA YIN TE, BUM PA LA SOGS PA RNAMS KYANG GZUGS LA SOGS PA TSOGS PA TZAM NYID YIN PAR MA GRUB PA'I PHYIR DANG, DER YANG BDAG DANG 'DRA BAR BRGAL ZHING BRTAG PA MTSUNGS PA'I PHYIR RO,,
gru.wylie: de yang yod pa ma yin te, bum pa la sogs pa rnams kyang gzugs la sogs pa tshogs pa tsam nyid yin par ma grub pa'i phyir dang, der yang bdag dang 'dra bar brgal zhing brtag pa mtshungs pa'i phyir ro
gru.english: This though is not the case. This is first of all because it is not the case that water pitchers and the like are simply the collection of form and the rest. And secondly, the examination and the final conclusions we draw with them are just the same as we do with the self.

gru.acip: LAS DANG BYED PA PO RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA BKAG PA'I RIGS PAS NYE BAR BLANG BA DANG LEN PA PO YANG RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA BKAG PA YANG SHES PAR BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: las dang byed pa po rang bzhin gyis grub pa bkag pa'i rigs pas nye bar blang ba dang len pa po yang rang bzhin gyis grub pa bkag pa yang shes par bya'o
gru.english: You should understand that—using the same logic we employ to deny that the action & the agent could exist through some nature of their own—we deny that the agent of taking things on, and the one who does the taking, could exist either through any nature of their own.

gru.acip: DNGOS PO LHAG MA NI TSIG GSAL LAS, BSKYED BYA SKYED BYED DANG 'GRO BA DANG 'GRO BA PO DANG, BLTA BYA LTA BYED DANG, MTSAN NYID DANG MTSAN GZHI DANG, 'BYUNG BAR BYA BA DANG, {%no ,} 'BYUNG BAR BYED PA DANG, YAN LAG DANG YAN LAG CAN DANG, YON TAN DANG YON TAN CAN DANG, TSAD MA DANG GZHAL BYA LA SOGS PA'I DNGOS PO MA LUS PA NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB PA BKAG STE, PHAN TSUN LTOS PA'I GRUB PA NYID YIN PAR SHES RAB CAN GYIS SHES PAR BYA'O,
gru.wylie: dngos po lhag ma ni tshig gsal las, bskyed bya skyed byed dang 'gro ba dang 'gro ba po dang, blta bya lta byed dang, mtshan nyid dang mtshan gzhi dang, 'byung bar bya ba dang, {%No ,} 'byung bar byed pa dang, yan lag dang yan lag can dang, yon tan dang yon tan can dang, tshad ma dang gzhal bya la sogs pa'i dngos po ma lus pa ngo bo nyid kyis grub pa bkag ste, phan tshun ltos pa'i grub pa nyid yin par shes rab can gyis shes par bya'o
gru.english: As for the rest of functioning things, we can follow the words of A Clarification of the Verses: We deny that any functional entity at all could ever exist through some nature of its own, whether we're talking about things that start or the things that start them; or goings or the one who goes; or what is viewed, and the the one who views it; or definitions or things defined; or the fact of things happening or what makes them happen; or the component parts of things or the wholes made up of those parts; or specific qualities and those that possess those qualities; or accurate perceptions and the objects which those perceptions hold under their consideration. And this is all because those who possess wisdom understand that all these are nothing but things which occur in mutual reliance.

gru.acip: ZHES GSUNGS PAS BYA BYED SPYI DANG, KHYAD PAR DU TSAD MA DANG GZHAL BYA'I BYA BYED RNAMS NGO BO NYID KYIS MA GRUB CING, LTOS 'GRUB KYI TSUL GYIS KHAS LEN PA YIN TE,
gru.wylie: zhes gsungs pas bya byed spyi dang, khyad par du tshad ma dang gzhal bya'i bya byed rnams ngo bo nyid kyis ma grub cing, ltos 'grub kyi tshul gyis khas len pa yin te
gru.english: Given this kind of statement, what we accept is that neither actions & agents in general—nor, more particularly, actions & agents in the form of accurate perceptions and the objects under their consideration—could ever exist through some essential nature of their own; but rather through a process of reliance.

gru.acip: LTOS 'GRUB 'DI LA GNYIS KA PHAN TSUN LTOS PA'I THUN MONG MA YIN PA'I 'JOG LUGS YOD PA RNAMS SHES DGOS PAR YOD DO,,
gru.wylie: ltos 'grub 'di la gnyis ka phan tshun ltos pa'i thun mong ma yin pa'i 'jog lugs yod pa rnams shes dgos par yod do
gru.english: And as regards this process of reliance, you should understand the unique methods in which we establish both of the two here as sharing a mutual reliance.

gru.acip: DNGOS PO YANG RANG GI SGRUB PAR BYED PA MED PAR 'BYUNG BA MA YIN PAS, RANG GI SGRUB PAR BYED PA NYE BAR BLANG BA DANG, NYE BAR LEN PA PO GNYIS KA YANG NYE BAR LEN PA ZHES PAR 'JOG GO
gru.wylie: dngos po yang rang gi sgrub par byed pa med par 'byung ba ma yin pas, rang gi sgrub par byed pa nye bar blang ba dang, nye bar len pa po gnyis ka yang nye bar len pa zhes par 'jog go
gru.english: Working things are not entities that can occur in an absence of what produces them; and so we can speak of what produces them as both that taking them on, and as the entity it is which takes them on.

gru.acip: DE LAS NI, BYED PA PO RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA BKAG PAR SHES PAR BYA'I, RTEN NAS GDAGS PAR BYA BA THA SNYAD KYI YAN LAG TU GYUR PA YANG BKAG GO ,ZHES BYA BAR NI SHES PAR MI BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: de las ni, byed pa po rang bzhin gyis grub pa bkag par shes par bya'i, rten nas gdags par bya ba tha snyad kyi yan lag tu gyur pa yang bkag go ,zhes bya bar ni shes par mi bya'o
gru.english: What this says is that we should understand that the agent existing through some nature of its own is denied; but that we are not to entertain the understanding that we deny something which can be, nominally, the adjunct here: something which is labeled through reliance.

gru.acip: NGAR 'DZIN GYI DMIGS YUL RANG BZHIN GYIS YOD PA MA YIN PAS, RNAL 'BYOR BAS BDAG RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA MA DMIGS PA LAS, BDAG GI BA YANG RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA'I SNYING PO DANG LDAN PA MA YIN PA NYID DU SHES SHING,
gru.wylie: ngar 'dzin gyi dmigs yul rang bzhin gyis yod pa ma yin pas, rnal 'byor bas bdag rang bzhin gyis grub pa ma dmigs pa las, bdag gi ba yang rang bzhin gyis grub pa'i snying po dang ldan pa ma yin pa nyid du shes shing
gru.english: The object of focus for the tendency to hold to some “me” is not something which could exist through some nature of its own. As such, we should understand that when the deep practitioner fails to perceive any self that could exist through some nature of its own, what belongs to the self can only be something which could never have possessed any essence of existing through any nature of its own, either.

gru.acip: RGYU MTSAN DE DAG LA BRTEN NAS GANG ZAG RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAS STONG PAR 'JOG PA'I RNAM PAR DPYOD PA 'DI NI, THAR PA 'DOD PA'I DBANG PO SHIN TU RNON PO LA CHES MDZES PA YIN TE, 'DIS YID 'PHROG PA 'DRA BA GRUB PA'I MTHA' GZHAN LA MED PA'I PHYIR RO,,
gru.wylie: rgyu mtshan de dag la brten nas gang zag rang bzhin gyis grub pas stong par 'jog pa'i rnam par dpyod pa 'di ni, thar pa 'dod pa'i dbang po shin tu rnon po la ches mdzes pa yin te, 'dis yid 'phrog pa 'dra ba grub pa'i mtha' gzhan la med pa'i phyir ro
gru.english: We can also say that—based on all these reasons—this particular logical examination where we establish how the person is empty of existing through any nature of its own is something extremely beautiful for those individuals of sharp faculties who hope for freedom. There is no presentation found in any other school of thought which can so completely steal our hearts as this one does. The irrelevance of others' position

gru.acip: DE LTAR BDAG PHUNG PO DANG RANG BZHIN GCIG DANG THA DAD GANG DU YANG MA GRUB PAR BSTAN NAS, BDAG PHUNG PO DANG PHAN TSUN RTEN DANG BRTEN PA NYID DU YANG NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB PA MED PAR BRJOD PA'I PHYIR BSHAD PA,
gru.wylie: de ltar bdag phung po dang rang bzhin gcig dang tha dad gang du yang ma grub par bstan nas, bdag phung po dang phan tshun rten dang brten pa nyid du yang ngo bo nyid kyis grub pa med par brjod pa'i phyir bshad pa
gru.english: Having thus presented how the self is neither essentially the same nor separate from the parts to the person, we will now make an explanation which is meant to express how the self and the parts to the person cannot exist, mutually, either exactly as a basis or what relies upon this basis, at least in a way where this exists through some essence of its own.

gru.acip: RGYU MTSAN GANG GI PHYIR NA PHUNG PO DANG BDAG 'DIR NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB PA'I GZHAN NYID YOD NA, RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA'I RTEN DANG BRTEN PA'I RTOG PA GNYIS PO 'DIR 'GYUR NA, RANG BZHIN GYIS GZHAN NYID DU GRUB PA DE MED PA DE'I PHYIR RTEN DANG BRTEN PAR NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB PA 'DI PHYIN CI LOG GI RTOG PAS BZHAG PA TZAM STE,
gru.wylie: rgyu mtshan gang gi phyir na phung po dang bdag 'dir ngo bo nyid kyis grub pa'i gzhan nyid yod na, rang bzhin gyis grub pa'i rten dang brten pa'i rtog pa gnyis po 'dir 'gyur na, rang bzhin gyis gzhan nyid du grub pa de med pa de'i phyir rten dang brten par ngo bo nyid kyis grub pa 'di phyin ci log gi rtog pas bzhag pa tsam ste
gru.english: And what is the reason why we can say this? Suppose it were the case that the parts to the person and the self “here” (meaning, in a way in which they existed through some essence of their own) were perfectly separate from one another. If these two ideas—of a basis and something relying upon that basis that existed through some nature of their own—were indeed the case here, then for the reason that there could be no possibility of their being essentially other than each other by nature, we can say that this essential existence of a basis and something relying upon this basis is a proposal that is established by nothing more than a mistaken imagining.

gru.acip: DPER NA 'JIG RTEN NA 'KHAR GZHONG DANG ZHO GNYIS NGO BO THA DAD PA LA RTEN DANG BRTEN PA MTHONG BA LTAR PHUNG PO DANG BDAG GNYIS LA DE LTAR MTHONG BA MED PAS RTEN DANG BRTEN PA'I NGO BOR RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA MED DO,,
gru.wylie: dper na 'jig rten na 'khar gzhong dang zho gnyis ngo bo tha dad pa la rten dang brten pa mthong ba ltar phung po dang bdag gnyis la de ltar mthong ba med pas rten dang brten pa'i ngo bor rang bzhin gyis grub pa med do
gru.english: In the everyday world, for example, we can see an example of a basis and something relying upon that basis where some yogurt—and the metal dish that might hold that yogurt—are essentially separate entities. We do not though see this sort of thing with the pair of the parts to the person and the self. As such, it is not the case that there is a relationship here of a basis and what depends upon that basis existing through some essential nature of their own.

gru.acip: BDAG NI GZUGS KYI PHUNG PO DANG LDAN PA NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB PAR MI 'DOD DE, RGYU MTSAN GANG GI PHYIR NA BDAG PHUNG PO RNAMS LAS RANG BZHIN GYIS GCIG DANG THA DAD PA NI BKAG ZIN PAS YOD PA MIN PA DE'I PHYIR, BDAG PHUNG PO DANG LDAN PA'I SBYOR BA RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA MED DE,
gru.wylie: bdag ni gzugs kyi phung po dang ldan pa ngo bo nyid kyis grub par mi 'dod de, rgyu mtshan gang gi phyir na bdag phung po rnams las rang bzhin gyis gcig dang tha dad pa ni bkag zin pas yod pa min pa de'i phyir, bdag phung po dang ldan pa'i sbyor ba rang bzhin gyis grub pa med de
gru.english: We do not then accept the idea that the self is something that could possess the heap of form in a way where this occurred through some nature of its own. Our reason for saying this, why we say it's so, is that there is no possibility of asserting that the self is either—by nature—one with or separate from the parts to the person; we have already disproved these possibilities. Therefore the connection possessed by the self and the parts to the person is not something that could exist through any nature of its own.

gru.acip: LHA SBYIN GZUGS DANG LDAN ZHES PA LTA BU NI NGO BO GZHAN MIN PA LA SBYOR BA YIN NA, BDAG NI GZUGS LAS DE NYID DE GCIG DANG, GZHAN NYID DE THA DAD PA MED PAS, BDAG GZUGS DANG LDAN PA RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA 'DI YANG MI SRID DO,,
gru.wylie: lha sbyin gzugs dang ldan zhes pa lta bu ni ngo bo gzhan min pa la sbyor ba yin na, bdag ni gzugs las de nyid de gcig dang, gzhan nyid de tha dad pa med pas, bdag gzugs dang ldan pa rang bzhin gyis grub pa 'di yang mi srid do
gru.english: And then suppose we posed a connection where we said that “John is possessed of a physical form,” where there was no essentially separate thing. The relationship of the self to the form is neither that they are essentially the same, or one; nor are they essentially different, where they are things distinct from each other. As such, neither is it a possibility that the self could be possessed of form in a way that existed through some nature of its own.

gru.acip: DE DAG GIS NI PHUNG PO LHAG MA BZHI DANG LDAN PA NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB PA YANG BKAG PAR SHES PAR BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: de dag gis ni phung po lhag ma bzhi dang ldan pa ngo bo nyid kyis grub pa yang bkag par shes par bya'o
gru.english: You should understand that the points here further serve to deny that the self could be possessed of any of the remaining four parts to the person in a way that existed in & of itself. How destruction is mistaken

gru.acip: DMIGS PA NGA LA DMIGS NAS RNAM PA RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAR 'DZIN PA'I 'JIG TSOGS LA LTA BA'I RI BO 'PHAGS PA'I YE SHES KYI RDO RJE MA BABS PAS,
gru.wylie: dmigs pa nga la dmigs nas rnam pa rang bzhin gyis grub par 'dzin pa'i 'jig tshogs la lta ba'i ri bo 'phags pa'i ye shes kyi rdo rje ma babs pas
gru.english: And so let's consider that mountain of the view of destruction which takes, as its object of focus, the “me” and maintains an aspect of it which holds it to exist through some nature of its own. Here is what will happen, if we don't manage to bring the diamond weapon of wisdom down upon it.

gru.acip: GANG DANG LHAN CIG TU NYI SHU RGYUN ZHUGS KYIS SPANGS PA'I RTZA BA'I 'JIG LTA YANG KUN BRTAGS YIN LA, DE YANG DE RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PAR 'DZIN PA TZAM LA MI BYED KYI, DE'I 'DZIN STANGS 'THAD LDAN DU GRUB MTHA' NGAN PA LA BRTEN NAS 'DZIN PA'I SA BON RGYUN ZHUGS KYIS SPANGS PA'O,,
gru.wylie: gang dang lhan cig tu nyi shu rgyun zhugs kyis spangs pa'i rtsa ba'i 'jig lta yang kun brtags yin la, de yang de rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub par 'dzin pa tsam la mi byed kyi, de'i 'dzin stangs 'thad ldan du grub mtha' ngan pa la brten nas 'dzin pa'i sa bon rgyun zhugs kyis spangs pa'o
gru.english: The fundamental form of the view of destruction when we speak of how one who enters the stream eliminates its twenty concomitant forms, moreover, is a learned form. And it moreover does not refer only to holding that things could exist by definition; rather, the stream enterer eliminates as well the seeds for that stance here—itself brought about by relying upon mistaken schools of thought—that how this view considers things must be correct. Others on the substantial person

gru.acip: RANG GI SDE PA MANG POS BKUR BA PA KHA CIG NI, PHUNG PO MA GTOGS DE 'DZIN MA GRUB PHYIR, ZHES PA'I RIGS PAS GANG ZAG PHUNG PO LAS NGO BO THA DAD PA MIN LA, PHUNG PO'I RANG BZHIN CAN YANG MIN TE, YIN NA BDAG DE SKYE 'JIG DANG LDAN PAR 'GYUR BA'I PHYIR RO,,
gru.wylie: rang gi sde pa mang pos bkur ba pa kha cig ni, phung po ma gtogs de 'dzin ma grub phyir, zhes pa'i rigs pas gang zag phung po las ngo bo tha dad pa min la, phung po'i rang bzhin can yang min te, yin na bdag de skye 'jig dang ldan par 'gyur ba'i phyir ro
gru.english: Here then is the idea of some people who belong to the Widely Respected group. They would reference the verse that includes, “Because you could never establish the capacity to hold to some that didn't involve the parts,” and say that there is no person who is essentially separate from the parts to the person. They would say as well that this is not something which possesses the nature of these parts; since if it were, then the self would be something which exhibited started & stopping.

gru.acip: ,GANG PHYIR GZUGS LAS SEMS BRJOD MED MI RTOGS, ,DNGOS YOD BRJOD MED RTOGS PA MA YIN NYID, ,GAL TE BDAG 'GA' DNGOS POR GRUB GYUR NA, ,SEMS LTAR GRUB DNGOS BRJOD DU MED MI 'GYUR,
gru.wylie: gang phyir gzugs las sems brjod med mi rtogs, ,dngos yod brjod med rtogs pa ma yin nyid, ,gal te bdag 'ga' dngos por grub gyur na, ,sems ltar grub dngos brjod du med mi 'gyur
gru.english: For what reason? We don't understand How the mind's Relationship to form Cannot be described. This same idea Can never be described As things that exist As entitites. Suppose that There were some Possible cases Of the self That existed As entities. Entities that existed In a way similar To the mind Would have to be Indescribable.

gru.acip: DNGOS PO STE RDZAS SU YOD PA RNAMS LA DE NYID DANG GZHAN NYID DU BRJOD DU MED PAR RTOGS PA MA YIN PA NYID DE, 'DI LTAR GAL TE BDAG 'GA' ZHIG DNGOS POR TE RDZAS SU GRUB PAR GYUR NA, SEMS LTAR DU GRUB PA'I DNGOS PO SGO GNYIS GANG DU BRJOD DU MED PAR MI 'GYUR RO,,
gru.wylie: dngos po ste rdzas su yod pa rnams la de nyid dang gzhan nyid du brjod du med par rtogs pa ma yin pa nyid de, 'di ltar gal te bdag 'ga' zhig dngos por te rdzas su grub par gyur na, sems ltar du grub pa'i dngos po sgo gnyis gang du brjod du med par mi 'gyur ro
gru.english: And let's also consider this same idea that the mind can never be described either as the very same as, or as perfectly distinct from, things that exist as entities—which is to say, as substantial. Because suppose that there were some possible cases of the self that existed as entities; which here means, in a substantial way. In that scenario, entities that existed in a way similar to the mind would have to be indescribable, in either of the two senses.

gru.acip: ,GANG PHYIR KHYOD BUM DNGOS POR MA GRUB PA'I, ,NGO BO GZUGS SOGS LAS BRJOD MED 'GYUR BAS, ,BDAG GANG PHUNG PO LAS BRJOD MED 'GYUR TE, ,RANG GIS YOD PAR GRUB PAR RTOGS MI BYA,
gru.wylie: gang phyir khyod bum dngos por ma grub pa'i, ,ngo bo gzugs sogs las brjod med 'gyur bas, ,bdag gang phung po las brjod med 'gyur te, ,rang gis yod par grub par rtogs mi bya
gru.english: What is the reason? The relationship Of your water pitcher— Which has an Essential nature Where it cannot exist As an entity— To form and the rest Is not something Which can be described. As such, that self Is something whose Relationship to The parts To the person Cannot be described. You cannot understand That it itself exists.

gru.acip: RGYU MTSAN GANG GI PHYIR KHYOD KYI LTAR NA BUM PA RANG RKYA THUB PA'I DNGOS POR MA GRUB PA'I NGO BO DE RANG GI YAN LAG GI GZUGS SOGS LAS DE NYID DE GCIG DANG NGO BO THA DAD DU BRJOD DU MED PAR 'GYUR BAR 'DOD PAS,
gru.wylie: rgyu mtshan gang gi phyir khyod kyi ltar na bum pa rang rkya thub pa'i dngos por ma grub pa'i ngo bo de rang gi yan lag gi gzugs sogs las de nyid de gcig dang ngo bo tha dad du brjod du med par 'gyur bar 'dod pas
gru.english: And what is the reason why we can say that? According to you, the relationship of a water pitcher—which has an essential nature where it cannot exist as an entity which stands of its own accord—to its parts of form and the rest is not something which can be described as being just that (the very same) or essentially different.

gru.acip: DE'I PHYIR GANG ZAG RANG GI NGO BO NYID KYIS YOD PAR GRUB PAR RTOGS PA STE GZUNG BAR MI BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: de'i phyir gang zag rang gi ngo bo nyid kyis yod par grub par rtogs pa ste gzung bar mi bya'o
gru.english: As such, you cannot “understand”—which is to say, hold—that the person exists in & of itself: through some nature of its own.

gru.acip: DE LTAR TSIGS SU BCAD PA GNYIS KYIS RDZAS SU YOD PA DGAG PA DANG, BTAGS YOD DU SGRUB PA NYE BAR BSTAN NAS, DA NI DE NYID DANG GZHAN GNYIS DNGOS PO'I RTEN NYID DU BRJOD NAS, RTEN DE MA YIN PA NYID KYIS BDAG RDZAS SU YOD PA 'GOG PAR RTZOM PA,
gru.wylie: de ltar tshigs su bcad pa gnyis kyis rdzas su yod pa dgag pa dang, btags yod du sgrub pa nye bar bstan nas, da ni de nyid dang gzhan gnyis dngos po'i rten nyid du brjod nas, rten de ma yin pa nyid kyis bdag rdzas su yod pa 'gog par rtsom pa
gru.english: As such then we have two verses which are indicating here that things cannot exist in any substantial manner; but can be established as existing by imputation. Now then we will move on to undertaking our denial that the self could exist in a substantial way, as it does not in any way provide a basis, described as the very basis of things of things either as those things themselves, or as something other than them.

gru.acip: DNGOS PO LA GCIG DANG THA DAD KYI RNAM PA DE GNYIS NGES PAR MTHONG BAR 'GYUR BA DE'I PHYIR BDAG RDZAS SU MED DE, DNGOS PO'I CHOS DE NYID DANG GZHAN GNYIS SU GRUB PA DANG BRAL BA'I PHYIR RO,,
gru.wylie: dngos po la gcig dang tha dad kyi rnam pa de gnyis nges par mthong bar 'gyur ba de'i phyir bdag rdzas su med de, dngos po'i chos de nyid dang gzhan gnyis su grub pa dang bral ba'i phyir ro
gru.english: And with entities we see that things are fixed at two types: either they are one & the same, or they are separate. For this reason, the self cannot exist as a substantial entity, for it is devoid of existing either way: as the essence or quality of an entity itself, or as something other than it. The seven extremes

gru.acip: LNGA PA LA BZHI, BDAG MTHA' BDUN DU MED KYANG BRTEN NAS BTAGS PA SHING RTA DANG 'DRA BAR BSTAN PA, SNGAR MA BSHAD PA'I PHYOGS LHAG MA GNYIS RGYAS PAR BSHAD PA, DE LTAR BSHAD PA LA GZHAN GYI RTZOD PA SPANG BA, MING GI THA SNYAD KYI DON GZHAN YANG GRUB PAR BSTAN PA'O, ,DANG PO NI,
gru.wylie: lnga pa la bzhi, bdag mtha' bdun du med kyang brten nas btags pa shing rta dang 'dra bar bstan pa, sngar ma bshad pa'i phyogs lhag ma gnyis rgyas par bshad pa, de ltar bshad pa la gzhan gyi rtsod pa spang ba, ming gi tha snyad kyi don gzhan yang grub par bstan pa'o, ,dang po ni
gru.english: The fifth section here—explaining, with the use of a metaphor, how it is that we establish that the self is something labelled through dependence—has four parts of its own: (1) a demonstration that, even though the self is devoid of the seven extremes, it is still similar to a wagon, in being labeled in dependence; (2) an extended explanation of two additional positions which have not been covered so far; (3) rejecting arguments by others concerning this way of explaining things; and (4) a demonstration how there is another interpretation of the meaning of terms used as names. Here then is the first of these.

gru.acip: ,DE PHYIR NGAR 'DZIN RTEN NI DNGOS PO MIN, ,PHUNG LAS GZHAN MIN PHUNG PO'I NGO BO MIN, ,PHUNG PO RTEN MIN 'DI NI DE LDAN MIN, ,'DI NI PHUNG PO RNAMS BRTEN 'GRUB PAR 'GYUR,
gru.wylie: de phyir ngar 'dzin rten ni dngos po min, ,phung las gzhan min phung po'i ngo bo min, ,phung po rten min 'di ni de ldan min, ,'di ni phung po rnams brten 'grub par 'gyur
gru.english: For that reason, The basis for Holding to some “Me” is not A substantial thing. It is not Something other Than the parts To the person. Neither is it The essence Of the parts To the person. Neither is it The basis; Neither is this Possessed of those. This is something That exists through Dependence upon The parts of the person.

gru.acip: GANG GI PHYIR SNGAR BSHAD PA DE LTAR RNAM PAR DPYAD PA NA GANG ZAG RDZAS SU YOD PA MI 'THAD PA DE'I PHYIR NGAR 'DZIN PA'I RTEN TE DMIGS PA NI, DNGOS PO STE RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA MIN TE,
