gru.wylie: gang gi phyir sngar bshad pa de ltar rnam par dpyad pa na gang zag rdzas su yod pa mi 'thad pa de'i phyir ngar 'dzin pa'i rten te dmigs pa ni, dngos po ste rang bzhin gyis grub pa min te
gru.english: Now if one does the examination as we have previously described it, we see that it is incorrect to say that the person exists substantially. For that reason, (1) the basis—which is to say, the object of focus—for holding to some “me” is not something which is a substantial thing, which is to say, something that could exist through any nature of its own.

gru.acip: DE'I PHYIR RANG GI SDE PA GANG DAG BDAG BTAGS PAR YOD CES PA'AM, BDAG DON DAM PAR MA DMIGS PAR 'DOD PAS KYANG RUNG STE JI SKAD SMRAS PA'I RNAM PAS BDAG KHAS BLANG BAR MI BYA'O ZHES BSHAD PA NI, BDAG 'DI NI PHUNG PO RNAMS LA BRTEN NAS GRUB PAR 'GYUR BA'O,,
gru.wylie: de'i phyir rang gi sde pa gang dag bdag btags par yod ces pa'am, bdag don dam par ma dmigs par 'dod pas kyang rung ste ji skad smras pa'i rnam pas bdag khas blang bar mi bya'o zhes bshad pa ni, bdag 'di ni phung po rnams la brten nas grub par 'gyur ba'o
gru.english: As such, it is appropriate for any of our own groups to assert either that the self is something that exists as labeled; or to say that it is not something which exists in an ultimate manner. That is, when we say that we cannot accept a self that exists in any of the different aspects described above, what we are saying is that this “self” is something that exists through dependence upon the parts of the person.

gru.acip: BDAG BTAGS PA TZAM DU GRUB PAR BYA BA'I DON DU JI SKAD BSHAD PA'I DON NYID GSAL BAR BYA BA'I PHYIR, PHYI ROL GYI DPE STON CING BSHAD PA,
gru.wylie: bdag btags pa tsam du grub par bya ba'i don du ji skad bshad pa'i don nyid gsal bar bya ba'i phyir, phyi rol gyi dpe ston cing bshad pa
gru.english: The next section here is presented in order to make even more clear the point we have just made—with an eye towards establishing that the self is only something which exists as labeled. Towards that end, we present and then explain a metaphor from the normal, outside world.

gru.acip: SHING RTA RANG GI YAN LAG LAS DON GZHAN DU 'DOD PA MIN LA, GZHAN MIN TE GCIG TU YANG GRUB PA MA YIN PA DANG, PHUNG PO DE DANG LDAN PA DANG, YAN LAG LA PHAR BRTEN PA DANG, YAN LAG DAG BDAG DER BRTEN PA RANG BZHIN GYIS YOD PA MIN PA DANG, YAN LAG 'DUS PA TZAM DANG YAN LAG GI DBYIBS MIN PA JI LTA BA DE BZHIN DU, BDAG DANG PHUNG PO GNYIS KYANG DE BZHIN DU SHES PAR BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: shing rta rang gi yan lag las don gzhan du 'dod pa min la, gzhan min te gcig tu yang grub pa ma yin pa dang, phung po de dang ldan pa dang, yan lag la phar brten pa dang, yan lag dag bdag der brten pa rang bzhin gyis yod pa min pa dang, yan lag 'dus pa tsam dang yan lag gi dbyibs min pa ji lta ba de bzhin du, bdag dang phung po gnyis kyang de bzhin du shes par bya'o
gru.english: That is, (1) we are not saying that a wagon is something other than its component parts. But (2) neither are we saying that it could be the other: that it could exist as one and the same as these parts. And neither are we saying (3) that the self is possessed of those parts to the person; or (4) that it depends out upon its component parts; or (5) that the component parts depend there upon the self—when we are talking about each of these possibilities existing through some nature of its own. Neither are we saying (6) that the wagon is the simple collection of its component parts, or (7) that it consists of the outline of the parts put together. Which is to say, one should understand that all this applies as well to the pair of the self and the parts to the person. Denying the collection is the wagon

gru.acip: PHYOGS SNGA MA LNGA NI SNGAR BSTAN ZIN PAS 'DIR TSOGS PA'I PHYOGS DANG, DBYIBS KYI PHYOGS GNYIS SHING RTA YIN PA 'GOG PA NI BSGRUB PAR BYA DGOS PAS DE DAG STON PA BRTZAM PAR BYA STE,
gru.wylie: phyogs snga ma lnga ni sngar bstan zin pas 'dir tshogs pa'i phyogs dang, dbyibs kyi phyogs gnyis shing rta yin pa 'gog pa ni bsgrub par bya dgos pas de dag ston pa brtsam par bya ste
gru.english: We have finished then presenting the first five of the positions indicated; as such, the time has come for us to establish how we deny first the idea that collection could be the wagon; and then secondly the idea that the outline could be the wagon. Here is how we start with that.

gru.acip: CI'I PHYIR ZHE NA, KHYOD KYI LTAR NA SHING RTA'I 'PHANG LO LA SOGS PA'I YAN LAG RE RE LA SNGAR MA BSGRIGS PA'I DUS SU DBYIBS JI LTAR YOD PAR GYUR PA BZHIN DU, PHYIS BSGRIGS TE SHING RTAR RTOGS {%GTOGS} PA STE GRUB PA'I DUS SU'ANG SNGA MA DE BZHIN DU YOD PA YIN NA,
gru.wylie: ci'i phyir zhe na, khyod kyi ltar na shing rta'i 'phang lo la sogs pa'i yan lag re re la sngar ma bsgrigs pa'i dus su dbyibs ji ltar yod par gyur pa bzhin du, phyis bsgrigs te shing rtar rtogs {%gtogs} pa ste grub pa'i dus su'ang snga ma de bzhin du yod pa yin na
gru.english: And why is that? According to you, we should first consider the shape of each separate component part of the wagon—the wheels and all the rest—as they existed prior to the point that they were assembled into the wagon. And then their shape after they have been incorporated into the wagon—that is, after the wagon has been completed—should as well be something that exists in just the same way as it was before.

gru.acip: GAL TE DA LTA SHING RTA NYID DU GRUB PA'I DUS 'DIR 'PHANG LO DANG LA SOGS PAS SROG SHING DANG, GZER BU LA SOGS PA SHING RTA'I YAN LAG RNAMS KYI DBYIBS KYI KHYAD PAR SO SOR LHAM PA STE GRU BZHI DANG, RING PO DANG ZLUM PO LA SOGS PA'I DBYIBS SNGAR MA BSGRIGS PA'I DUS DANG, MI MTHUN PA'I THA DAD PA YOD NA,
gru.wylie: gal te da lta shing rta nyid du grub pa'i dus 'dir 'phang lo dang la sogs pas srog shing dang, gzer bu la sogs pa shing rta'i yan lag rnams kyi dbyibs kyi khyad par so sor lham pa ste gru bzhi dang, ring po dang zlum po la sogs pa'i dbyibs sngar ma bsgrigs pa'i dus dang, mi mthun pa'i tha dad pa yod na
gru.english: Suppose then we refer to that point in time now when the wagon itself is already completed, and consider the particular of the shape of the wheels & “the rest”—which would include things like the axle, or the pins that hold the wagon together, or other things of the like. There would be, say, things that were rectangular or squarish, or long, or rounded, or any other kind of shape that the components might have had before they were assembled together. These shapes would be separate, inconsistent with each other.

whole_word_matches.context: lag rnams kyi dbyibs kyi khyad par so sor lham pa ste gru bzhi dang, ring po dang zlum po la sogs pa'i dbyibs sn

gru.acip: JI LTAR YIN SNYAM NA, KHYOD KYIS SHING RTA'I BTAGS DON RNAM PAR DPYAD PA STE BTZAL NAS, SHING RTA 'JOG PAR BYED CING BTAGS DON MA BTZAL BAR 'GRUB PA'I THABS GZHAN KHAS MA BLANGS PA'I PHYIR DANG,
gru.wylie: ji ltar yin snyam na, khyod kyis shing rta'i btags don rnam par dpyad pa ste btsal nas, shing rta 'jog par byed cing btags don ma btsal bar 'grub pa'i thabs gzhan khas ma blangs pa'i phyir dang
gru.english: And how would that work? Let's say that you are examining—or seeking—that thing which we label “wagon.” The fact is that you have failed to express your support for any method of establishing the wagon other than looking at how we say something is a wagon, and looking for what it is that we've called “wagon.”

gru.acip: BTAGS DON RNAM PA BDUN DU BTZAL BA NA, SHING RTA 'ON CIG CES BYA BA SOGS KYI 'JIG RTEN GYI THA SNYAD RNAMS KHYOD LA JI LTAR 'GRUB PAR 'GYUR TE MI 'GYUR RO,,
gru.wylie: btags don rnam pa bdun du btsal ba na, shing rta 'on cig ces bya ba sogs kyi 'jig rten gyi tha snyad rnams khyod la ji ltar 'grub par 'gyur te mi 'gyur ro
gru.english: Moreover, when we look—in seven different ways—for what it is that we label “the wagon,” we don't see how it is that this can be established according to you, as the terms are applied in the way of the world at large, with expressions such as “bring the wagon” and the like. In fact, it could not be established.

gru.acip: ,DE NI DE NYID DU 'AM 'JIG RTEN DU, ,RNAM PA BDUN GYIS 'GRUB 'GYUR MIN MOD KYI, ,RNAM DPYAD MED PAR 'JIG RTEN NYID LAS 'DIR, ,RANG GI YAN LAG BRTEN NAS 'DOGS PA YIN,
gru.wylie: de ni de nyid du 'am 'jig rten du, ,rnam pa bdun gyis 'grub 'gyur min mod kyi, ,rnam dpyad med par 'jig rten nyid las 'dir, ,rang gi yan lag brten nas 'dogs pa yin
gru.english: Looking at that In and of itself, Or even in the way That the world does, Admittedly this doesn't End up something That could be established. But leaving off This close examination, Confining ourselves To the world, Here the labeling Has been done In reliance upon The component parts.

gru.acip: KHO BO CAG LA NI SNGAR BSHAD PA'I RTZOD PA'I NYES PA DE MED DE, SHING RTA DE NI DE NYID DU STE DON DAM PA'AM, 'JIG RTEN GYI KUN RDZOB TU BTAGS DON RNAM PA BDUN GYIS BTZAL BA NA SHING RTA 'GRUB PAR 'GYUR BA MIN MOD KYI,
gru.wylie: kho bo cag la ni sngar bshad pa'i rtsod pa'i nyes pa de med de, shing rta de ni de nyid du ste don dam pa'am, 'jig rten gyi kun rdzob tu btags don rnam pa bdun gyis btsal ba na shing rta 'grub par 'gyur ba min mod kyi
gru.english: Now the fact is that the problems raised in these previous arguments don't apply to us ourselves at all. That is, suppose we look—in those seven different ways—for that wagon that we have given the name in and of itself; which is to say, in an ultimate sense. Or even, in the way that the world does, in a deceptive sense. Admittedly this doesn't end up something that could be established as a wagon.

gru.acip: DBU MA PA'I PHYOGS 'DIR 'JIG RTEN LA GRAGS PA'I SGO NAS SHING RTAS THA SNYAD 'DOGS PA CHES GSAL BAR GRUB PA 'BA' ZHIG TU MA ZAD KYI, SHING RTA'I MING GI KHYAD PAR GZHAN DAG KYANG BTAGS DON 'TSOL BA'I TSUL GYIS RNAM PAR DPYAD PA MED PAR 'JIG RTEN LA GRAGS PA'I SGO NAS KHAS BLANG PAR BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: dbu ma pa'i phyogs 'dir 'jig rten la grags pa'i sgo nas shing rtas tha snyad 'dogs pa ches gsal bar grub pa 'ba' zhig tu ma zad kyi, shing rta'i ming gi khyad par gzhan dag kyang btags don 'tshol ba'i tshul gyis rnam par dpyad pa med par 'jig rten la grags pa'i sgo nas khas blang par bya'o
gru.english: Here in the standpoint of the Middle Way, it is exceedingly clear that this object has been labeled a “wagon” in keeping with the way that things are spoken of in the everyday world. Not only that, but we can say that we accept other details of the naming of the wagon in just the way that these are commonly spoken of in the everyday world, without reference to any close examination utilizing a search for what it was that received the label.

gru.acip: ,DE NYID YAN LAG CAN DE CHA SHAS CAN, ,SHING RTA DE NYID BYED PO ZHES 'GROR BSNYAD, ,SKYE BO RNAMS LA LEN PO NYID DU 'GRUB, ,'JIG RTEN GRAGS PA'I KUN RDZOB MA BRLAG CIG,
gru.wylie: de nyid yan lag can de cha shas can, ,shing rta de nyid byed po zhes 'gror bsnyad, ,skye bo rnams la len po nyid du 'grub, ,'jig rten grags pa'i kun rdzob ma brlag cig
gru.english: The thing itself Is a composite; This same thing Is a whole. This same wagon We can call “An agent.” Living beings Are designated In the same way. People are thus Established as Nothing other than The ones that do This incorporating. The deceptive In the common parlance Of the world would be “Don't ruin that.”

gru.acip: SHING RTA DE NYID 'PHANG LO LA SOGS PA NYE BAR BLANG BAR BYA BA NYE BAR LEN PA'I BYA BA LA LTOS NAS NI, BYED PA PO ZHES 'GRO BA LA BSNYAD PA DANG, RANG GI NYE BAR LEN PA GZUGS LA SOGS PA'I GDAGS GZHI LA LTOS NAS NI, SKYE BO RNAMS LA LEN PA PO NYID DU YANG 'GRUB BO,,
gru.wylie: shing rta de nyid 'phang lo la sogs pa nye bar blang bar bya ba nye bar len pa'i bya ba la ltos nas ni, byed pa po zhes 'gro ba la bsnyad pa dang, rang gi nye bar len pa gzugs la sogs pa'i gdags gzhi la ltos nas ni, skye bo rnams la len pa po nyid du yang 'grub bo
gru.english: We can also say that this same wagon is an incorporation of the the wheels and the rest. And then since it relies upon what it has incorporated, we can call it an “agent.” Living beings are designated in the same way; that is, dependent upon what it is they incorporate—their form and the rest—we can also say that people are thus established as nothing other than the ones that do this kind of taking on or incorporating.

gru.acip: DE'I PHYIR SHING RTA SOGS MING DU BTAGS PA TZAM DU MI 'DOD PAS SHING RTA LA SOGS PA RNAMS RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PAR 'DOD PA YIN PAS,
gru.wylie: de'i phyir shing rta sogs ming du btags pa tsam du mi 'dod pas shing rta la sogs pa rnams rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub par 'dod pa yin pas
gru.english: As such—given that they cannot accept that things like a wagon and so forth are simply labeled what they are—they have to take the position that wagons and the like exist by definition.

gru.acip: DE JI LTAR YIN ZHE NA, SHING RTA RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA ZHIG YIN NA RNAM PA BDUN GYIS BTZAL BA NA NGES PAR BDUN PO GANG RUNG ZHIG TU RNYED DGOS PA LA, RNAL 'BYOR PAS SHING RTA 'DI'I YOD PA NYID MI RNYED DO,,
gru.wylie: de ji ltar yin zhe na, shing rta rang bzhin gyis grub pa zhig yin na rnam pa bdun gyis btsal ba na nges par bdun po gang rung zhig tu rnyed dgos pa la, rnal 'byor pas shing rta 'di'i yod pa nyid mi rnyed do
gru.english: “Just what does that look like?” you may inquire. Suppose that a wagon were something that existed through some nature of its own. In that case, if we did our search in those seven different aspects, we would without doubt have to locate the wagon in some one of the seven options. The fact is though is that the deep practitioner does not arrive at any pure existence of this wagon.

gru.acip: ,RNAM BDUN GYIS MED GANG DE JI LTA BUR, ,YOD CES RNAL 'BYOR PAS 'DI'I YOD MI RNYED, ,DES DE NYID LA'ANG BDE BLAG 'JUG 'GYUR BAS, ,'DIR DE'I GRUB PA DE BZHIN 'DOD PAR BYA,
gru.wylie: rnam bdun gyis med gang de ji lta bur, ,yod ces rnal 'byor pas 'di'i yod mi rnyed, ,des de nyid la'ang bde blag 'jug 'gyur bas, ,'dir de'i grub pa de bzhin 'dod par bya
gru.english: Not finding anything Using seven different Options means that The way things Really are is something Which is devoid Of existing. In this, the Deep practitioner Also engages with ease In suchness. As such, Here we are Also to accept This, in the Same manner.

gru.acip: DE'I PHYIR SHING RTA NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB PA ZHES BYA BA NI, MA RIG PA'I LING TOG GIS BLO'I MIG NYAMS PAR BYAS PA KHO NAS BRTAGS PA YIN GYI,
gru.wylie: de'i phyir shing rta ngo bo nyid kyis grub pa zhes bya ba ni, ma rig pa'i ling tog gis blo'i mig nyams par byas pa kho nas brtags pa yin gyi
gru.english: As such, we can say that the very expression that “a wagon is something which exists through some essential nature of its own” is only something imputed by an individual who has seen the eyes of their intellect degraded by the cataract of misunderstanding.

gru.acip: RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA NI YOD PA MA YIN NO SNYAM PA DE LTAR RNAL 'BYOR PA LA NGES PA SKYE BAR 'GYUR ZHING, TSUL DES DE KHO NA NYID LA YANG RNAL 'BYOR PA BDE BLAG TU 'JUG PAR 'GYUR RO,,
gru.wylie: rang bzhin gyis grub pa ni yod pa ma yin no snyam pa de ltar rnal 'byor pa la nges pa skye bar 'gyur zhing, tshul des de kho na nyid la yang rnal 'byor pa bde blag tu 'jug par 'gyur ro
gru.english: The deep pracititioner though is someone who gives birth to a certain certainty, as they think to themselves that there is no such thing as something existing through some nature of its own. And in this manner, as well, the deep practitioner engages with ease in suchness.

gru.acip: DE BAS NA DBU MA PA'I SKABS 'DIR SHING RTA DE'I GRUB PA'I TSUL NI MA BRTAGS PAR GRUB PA DE BZHIN DU 'DOD PAR BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: de bas na dbu ma pa'i skabs 'dir shing rta de'i grub pa'i tshul ni ma brtags par grub pa de bzhin du 'dod par bya'o
gru.english: As such, then, here in the context of a follower of the Middle Way, we are also to accept—in the same manner—a way in which this wagon can exist without being examined.

gru.acip: GZHAN YANG SHING RTA RANG BZHIN GYIS MA GRUB NA DE'I YAN LAG KYANG RANG BZHIN GYIS YOD PA MIN PA'I DON 'DI NI, DPE 'DI LAS SHES PAR BYA STE,
gru.wylie: gzhan yang shing rta rang bzhin gyis ma grub na de'i yan lag kyang rang bzhin gyis yod pa min pa'i don 'di ni, dpe 'di las shes par bya ste
gru.english: Moreover, the point that if a wagon is not something that could exist through some nature of its own, then its component parts cannot either be things that exist through some nature of their own is something that we can understand from this metaphor.

gru.acip: YAN LAG CAN SHING RTA RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA LUS PA MED PAR BSREGS PA NA, SHES RAB KYI ME'I BUD SHING DU GYUR PA'I YAN LAG DAG GIS KYANG BDAG NYID ZUG TSUGS PAR TE RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAR SDAD PAR BYED MI NUS TE, SHES RAB KYI MES NGES PAR BSREGS PA'I PHYIR RO,,
gru.wylie: yan lag can shing rta rang bzhin gyis grub pa lus pa med par bsregs pa na, shes rab kyi me'i bud shing du gyur pa'i yan lag dag gis kyang bdag nyid zug tshugs par te rang bzhin gyis grub par sdad par byed mi nus te, shes rab kyi mes nges par bsregs pa'i phyir ro
gru.english: This fire burns up, without a single thing left over, that idea that the whole of the component parts—the wagon—could exist through any nature of its own. And those types of component parts themselves—which provide the firewood for the fire of wisdom—cannot stand on their own; that is, nothing can make them capable of staying there through some nature of their own. Which is to say, they are with certainty burned up completely in these flames of wisdom. The wagon & the self

gru.acip: BDAG BRTEN NAS GDAGS PA LA 'JOG PA NA, BRTAN PA DANG MI BRTAN PA LA SOGS PA'I MTHAR 'DZIN GYI RTOG PA'I RTEN MIN PAS MI RTAG PA LA SOGS PAR NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB PAR 'DZIN PA'I RTOG PA BZLOG PAR SLA BAR 'GYUR RO ZHES BSHAD PA,
gru.wylie: bdag brten nas gdags pa la 'jog pa na, brtan pa dang mi brtan pa la sogs pa'i mthar 'dzin gyi rtog pa'i rten min pas mi rtag pa la sogs par ngo bo nyid kyis grub par 'dzin pa'i rtog pa bzlog par sla bar 'gyur ro zhes bshad pa
gru.english: Our next section here is presented in order to make the following point. Suppose we can establish that the self is something which is labeled in dependence. In this case, it would no longer serve as a foundation for the kind of thinking where we hold to the extremes of believing that things are either solid, or not solid. It then becomes relatively easy to stop the idea where we hold that things like impermanence could exist through some essence of their own.

gru.acip: 'DI LAS NA 'DI NI SKYE 'JIG MIN ZHES PA'I KHYAD PAR GNYIS BKOD PA SLOB DPON GYI BZHED PA YIN NO, ZHES GSUNGS TE, SKYE 'JIG NI NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB PA'O,,
gru.wylie: 'di las na 'di ni skye 'jig min zhes pa'i khyad par gnyis bkod pa slob dpon gyi bzhed pa yin no, zhes gsungs te, skye 'jig ni ngo bo nyid kyis grub pa'o
gru.english: Here we see “it is the Master's position that we mention both characteristics, that 'this neither starts nor stops.'” This is referring to a starting & stopping that would exist through some essence of its own.

gru.acip: DE RNAMS KYI RGYU MTSAN NI BDAG CES BYA BA'I DNGOS PO RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA YOD PA MIN PA'I PHYIR RO,,
gru.wylie: de rnams kyi rgyu mtshan ni bdag ces bya ba'i dngos po rang bzhin gyis grub pa yod pa min pa'i phyir ro
gru.english: And that's all because—the reason for saying these things is—that entity which we refer to as the “self” is not something that exists through any nature of its own.

gru.acip: GANG ZHIG BTAGS DON RNAM PA BDUN GYIS BTZAL BA NA, RTAG PA DANG MI RTAG PA NYID DU MI SRID CING, BDAG GANG ZHIG RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA MED PA NYID MA MTHONG ZHING,
gru.wylie: gang zhig btags don rnam pa bdun gyis btsal ba na, rtag pa dang mi rtag pa nyid du mi srid cing, bdag gang zhig rang bzhin gyis grub pa med pa nyid ma mthong zhing
gru.english: Now there are those who fail to seek—in those seven different ways—what it is that receives the label; and thus cannot come to see that it is simply not possible for it to be unchanging or changing—and cannot recognize that there is absolutely no self anywhere that could exist through some nature of its own.

gru.acip: MA RIG PA'I DBANG GIS RANG BZHIN GYIS YOD PA NYID DU ZHEN NAS, 'JIG LTAS BDAG 'DI NI RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAR MNGON PAR ZHEN PA RNAMS 'KHOR BAR 'GYUR LA,
gru.wylie: ma rig pa'i dbang gis rang bzhin gyis yod pa nyid du zhen nas, 'jig ltas bdag 'di ni rang bzhin gyis grub par mngon par zhen pa rnams 'khor bar 'gyur la
gru.english: Due to misunderstanding then they are strongly attracted to the idea that things must exist through some nature of their own. And due to this, they hold strongly—through that view of destruction—to the idea that this self could exist through some nature of its own. And because of this, they must make their circle.

gru.acip: BDAG DE YI BDAG GI BA GANG YIN PA DER, NGA YI BAR 'DZIN PA'I BLO 'BYUNG BA'I BDAG DE NI, MA BRTAGS PA'I GRAGS PA'I NGOR GTI MUG STE MI SHES PA LAS GRUB PA YIN GYI RANG GI NGO BOS GRUB PA NI MA YIN NO,,
gru.wylie: bdag de yi bdag gi ba gang yin pa der, nga yi bar 'dzin pa'i blo 'byung ba'i bdag de ni, ma brtags pa'i grags pa'i ngor gti mug ste mi shes pa las grub pa yin gyi rang gi ngo bos grub pa ni ma yin no
gru.english: In short then, let us consider everything there is which is of it, the self: which belongs to the self. This is everything that makes up that self towards which there arises the state of mind that holds to “me.” And it is something that stems from misunderstanding: from that dark state of ignorance focused towards a self that is unexamined, and accepted on face value, in the parlance of the world. It is not though something that could exist through some essence of its own.

gru.acip: DE MA DMIGS NA'ANG MIG LA SOGS PA BDAG RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA DE'I NYE BAR LEN PA RNAMS DMIGS PAR MI 'GYUR TE, 'DI LTAR RNAL 'BYOR PAS NI BDAG DANG BDAG GI BA'I GZHI'I DNGOS PO 'GA' LA YANG RANG GI NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB PA DMIGS PA MED DE, DE'I PHYIR 'KHOR BA LAS GROL BAR 'GYUR TE,
gru.wylie: de ma dmigs na'ang mig la sogs pa bdag rang bzhin gyis grub pa de'i nye bar len pa rnams dmigs par mi 'gyur te, 'di ltar rnal 'byor pas ni bdag dang bdag gi ba'i gzhi'i dngos po 'ga' la yang rang gi ngo bo nyid kyis grub pa dmigs pa med de, de'i phyir 'khor ba las grol bar 'gyur te
gru.english: And even though they never perceive such a thing, neither do they perceive anything it is that this self-existent self could incorporate. Thus it is that there is nothing at all that the deep practitioner perceives as existing through some essence of its own, when we are talking about that base entity for the self, and what belongs to the self. And because of that not seeing, this practitioner comes to be free of the cycle of pain.

gru.acip: JI LTAR BYED PA PO RDZA MKHAN MED PA CAN GYI LAS SU BYA BA RDZA BUM MED PA DE'I PHYIR BDAG GI BA RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA NI, BDAG RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA MED PAR YOD PA MIN NO,,
gru.wylie: ji ltar byed pa po rdza mkhan med pa can gyi las su bya ba rdza bum med pa de'i phyir bdag gi ba rang bzhin gyis grub pa ni, bdag rang bzhin gyis grub pa med par yod pa min no
gru.english: It's just the way in which an agent—say, the potter—is something that has no existence; and what they act towards—the clay pot itself—has no existence either. As such, let's consider something belonging to the self that could exist through some nature of its own. This is not something that could ever exist, with a self that could not itself exist through any nature of its own.

gru.acip: DE'I PHYIR BDAG DANG BDAG GI BA GNYIS RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAS STONG PAR LTA ZHING, DE'I DON GOMS PAR BYED PA NA RNAL 'BYOR PA DE 'KHOR BA LAS RNAM PAR GROL BAR 'GYUR RO,,
gru.wylie: de'i phyir bdag dang bdag gi ba gnyis rang bzhin gyis grub pas stong par lta zhing, de'i don goms par byed pa na rnal 'byor pa de 'khor ba las rnam par grol bar 'gyur ro
gru.english: As such, let's consider that deep practitioner who sees that both the self and what belongs to the self are empty of existing through any nature of their own; and who then undertakes to accustom themselves to this fact. This then is a person who is completely liberated from the cycle of suffering.

gru.acip: GZUGS LA SOGS PA RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA MA DMIGS PA NA, GZUGS LA SOGS PA RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAR RTOG PA'I CHAGS SOGS KYI NYON MONGS RNAMS ZAD PAR 'GYUR BAS,
gru.wylie: gzugs la sogs pa rang bzhin gyis grub pa ma dmigs pa na, gzugs la sogs pa rang bzhin gyis grub par rtog pa'i chags sogs kyi nyon mongs rnams zad par 'gyur bas
gru.english: Suppose that we no longer look at form and the rest as being things that could exist through some nature of their own. In that case, negative thoughts such as attachment and the rest—thoughts where we imagine that form and such could indeed exist through some nature of their own—will come to a stop.

gru.acip: YAN LAG LA SOGS PA RNAMS PHAN TSUN LTOS PA'I GRUB PA YIN PA 'BA' ZHIG TU MA ZAD KYI, RGYU DANG 'BRAS BU GNYIS KYANG PHAN TSUN LTOS NAS GRUB PA YIN NO ZHES BSHAD PA,
gru.wylie: yan lag la sogs pa rnams phan tshun ltos pa'i grub pa yin pa 'ba' zhig tu ma zad kyi, rgyu dang 'bras bu gnyis kyang phan tshun ltos nas grub pa yin no zhes bshad pa
gru.english: This next section is meant to explain how not only is it the case that the component parts of things exist in reliance upon each other; but that causes and effects as well exist in this kind of mutual reliance as well.

gru.acip: CI STE RGYU 'BRAS RANG GI NGO BOS GRUB PAR SEMS NA,
gru.wylie: ci ste rgyu 'bras rang gi ngo bos grub par sems na
gru.english: And suppose now that you think to yourself that causes & effects could exist through some essential nature of their own.

gru.acip: DE LTA RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA LA RGYU SNGA BA MI RIGS TE, RGYU'I DUS SU RGYU'I LTOS SA 'BRAS BU DE GRUB DGOS PAS SO,,
gru.wylie: de lta rang bzhin gyis grub pa la rgyu snga ba mi rigs te, rgyu'i dus su rgyu'i ltos sa 'bras bu de grub dgos pas so
gru.english: If things were like that, and they existed through some nature of their own, then it would be illogical to say that the cause had come earlier—since there would have had to exist a result in the same time period as the cause, for the cause to rely upon.

gru.acip: DE'I PHYIR RGYU DANG 'BRAS BUR GDAGS PA YANG SHING RTA LTAR PHAN TSUN BRTEN NAS GRUB PAR RIG PAR BYA'I RANG BZHIN LAS GYUR PA NI MA YIN NO,,
gru.wylie: de'i phyir rgyu dang 'bras bur gdags pa yang shing rta ltar phan tshun brten nas grub par rig par bya'i rang bzhin las gyur pa ni ma yin no
gru.english: As such then we should understand the labelling of causes and effects as being something that occurs in a mutual dependence, as we saw with the wagon. It is not though something that could occur through any nature of its own.

gru.acip: CI STE SO SOR TE MA PHRAD PAR SKYED NA NI, 'BRAS BU'I RGYUR 'DOD PA 'DI, DE'I RGYU MIN PA RNAMS DANG SKYED MI SKYED KHYAD PAR MED PAR 'GYUR TE, RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA'I SO SO BA RNAMS 'BREL MED DON GZHAN DU 'GYUR BA'I PHYIR RO,,
gru.wylie: ci ste so sor te ma phrad par skyed na ni, 'bras bu'i rgyur 'dod pa 'di, de'i rgyu min pa rnams dang skyed mi skyed khyad par med par 'gyur te, rang bzhin gyis grub pa'i so so ba rnams 'brel med don gzhan du 'gyur ba'i phyir ro
gru.english: And suppose that the the triggering is done without any contact between them at all; they are completely separate. In that case there wouldn't be anything about the thing that you asserted was the cause of the result that distinguished it from things that weren't the cause, as far as what did the triggering and what didn't do the triggering. And that's because things that exist through some nature of their own, and which are separate from one another, are different entitites which share no connection at all.

gru.acip: RGYU 'BRAS RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAR SMRA BA LA BSKYED BYA SKYED BYED LA PHRAD MA PHRAD KYI RTOG PA GNYIS PO 'DI DAG SPANGS NAS TE DE MA GTOGS PA'I RTOG PA GSUM PA GZHAN YANG YOD PAR 'GYUR BA MA YIN PAS RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA'I RGYUS 'BRAS BU MI SKYED PA KHO NA'O,,
gru.wylie: rgyu 'bras rang bzhin gyis grub par smra ba la bskyed bya skyed byed la phrad ma phrad kyi rtog pa gnyis po 'di dag spangs nas te de ma gtogs pa'i rtog pa gsum pa gzhan yang yod par 'gyur ba ma yin pas rang bzhin gyis grub pa'i rgyus 'bras bu mi skyed pa kho na'o
gru.english: Those who assert that causes and effects can exist through some nature of their own have given up these two ideas: that these—what is triggered and what does the triggering—could either make contact with each other, or never make contact with each other. And yet there is further no different, third idea—one other than those two—which could exist. Thus it can only be the case that a cause which existed through some nature of its own could never trigger a result.

gru.acip: DE'I PHYIR CI STE KHYOD KYI LTAR RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA'I RGYU YIS 'BRAS BU SKYED PAR MI BYED PA DE'I PHYIR 'BRAS BU ZHES BYA BA RANG BZHIN GYIS YOD PA MIN LA,
gru.wylie: de'i phyir ci ste khyod kyi ltar rang bzhin gyis grub pa'i rgyu yis 'bras bu skyed par mi byed pa de'i phyir 'bras bu zhes bya ba rang bzhin gyis yod pa min la
gru.english: As such, given that, this cause which according to you exists through some nature of its own could never act to trigger a result. And as such, we would have to say that there is no such thing as something you could refer to as a “result” which existed through some nature of its own.

gru.acip: RGOL BA GANG GI LTAR NA BSKYED BYA SKYED BYED GNYIS RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PAR 'DOD PA DE LA, RGYUS 'BRAS BU DANG PHRAD MA PHRAD KYI BRTAG PA BYAS NAS PHYOGS GNYIS KA LA SKYON DU 'GYUR BA YIN GYI,
gru.wylie: rgol ba gang gi ltar na bskyed bya skyed byed gnyis rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub par 'dod pa de la, rgyus 'bras bu dang phrad ma phrad kyi brtag pa byas nas phyogs gnyis ka la skyon du 'gyur ba yin gyi
gru.english: So suppose we have some debater here who asserts that these two—what is triggered, and what does the triggering—could exist by definition. When we proceed from here and examine whether the cause ever makes contact with the result or not, we get problems on both sides.

gru.acip: RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA MED KYANG RAB RIB CAN GYIS DMIGS PA'I SGRA {%SKRA} SHAD LA SOGS PA LTAR, THA SNYAD PA'I RNAM PAR RTOG PA TZAM GYIS 'JOG PA'I YUL DU 'GYUR BA LA NI, RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA'I RGYU 'BRAS KHAS LEN PA LA BKOD PA'I SKYON MTSUNGS PA BSAM DU MED PA NYID DO,,
gru.wylie: rang bzhin gyis grub pa med kyang rab rib can gyis dmigs pa'i sgra {%skra} shad la sogs pa ltar, tha snyad pa'i rnam par rtog pa tsam gyis 'jog pa'i yul du 'gyur ba la ni, rang bzhin gyis grub pa'i rgyu 'bras khas len pa la bkod pa'i skyon mtshungs pa bsam du med pa nyid do
gru.english: And so let's consider an object which is established only through concepts involving terms—something which is like the strand of hair that someone with cataracts perceives, even though it cannot exist through any nature of its own. It is not at all the case that we are thinking to posit here a problem which would be equivalent, for a person who accepted the idea that cause & effect could exist through some nature of its own.

gru.acip: DE YI PHYIR BDAG LA JI SKAD BSHAD PA'I PHRAD MA PHRAD KYI SKYON DU MI 'GYUR ZHING, 'JIG RTEN LA GRAGS PA YI DNGOS PO MA BRTAGS PAR GRUB PA RGYU 'BRAS DANG SHING RTA LA SOGS PA RNAMS KYANG YOD PAS THAMS CAD 'GRUB BO,,
gru.wylie: de yi phyir bdag la ji skad bshad pa'i phrad ma phrad kyi skyon du mi 'gyur zhing, 'jig rten la grags pa yi dngos po ma brtags par grub pa rgyu 'bras dang shing rta la sogs pa rnams kyang yod pas thams cad 'grub bo
gru.english: As such, the problem that has been raised—about these things making contact or not making contact—does not apply to me. All these things that are spoken of in the vernacular of the world, existing without being examined—cause & effect, and wagons, and all the like—do, further, exist. As such, everything is right there.

gru.acip: 'DIR 'GREL PAS DGAG BYA'I KHYAD PAR RANG BZHIN GYIS DANG RANG GI NGO BOS GRUB PA SOGS KYI RGYU 'BRAS LA GNOD PA BRJOD PA, RANG BZHIN GYIS MED PA SGYU MA LTAR SMRA BA LA TSUR LA BZLOG NA MI 'JUG CES SMRA DGOS PA YIN GYI,
gru.wylie: 'dir 'grel pas dgag bya'i khyad par rang bzhin gyis dang rang gi ngo bos grub pa sogs kyi rgyu 'bras la gnod pa brjod pa, rang bzhin gyis med pa sgyu ma ltar smra ba la tshur la bzlog na mi 'jug ces smra dgos pa yin gyi
gru.english: At this point in the autocommentary, problems are raised with cause & effect which are specified by applying a distinction of something being denied: “those that exist through some nature of their own,” or “those that exist through some essential nature.” That is, we need to mention phrases like “which do not exist through any nature of their own,” or “which resemble an illusion,” so that the same arguments cannot be turned back upon us.

gru.acip: RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA DANG YOD PA GNYIS KYI KHYAD PAR MA PHYED PA'I LAN LTAR SNANG 'BA' ZHIG 'DEBS PA MI BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: rang bzhin gyis grub pa dang yod pa gnyis kyi khyad par ma phyed pa'i lan ltar snang 'ba' zhig 'debs pa mi bya'o
gru.english: We should not here though fail to apply the distinction between existing through some nature of its own and existing in general; if we did make such replies, then they would only be mistaken ones. An argument that the problems are just the same

gru.acip: GSUM PA LA GNYIS, RGYU 'BRAS RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA 'GOG PA LA SKYON MTSUNGS PA'I RTZOD PA, RANG LA SKYON MI MTSUNGS PA'I LAN BSTAN PA'O,,
gru.wylie: gsum pa la gnyis, rgyu 'bras rang bzhin gyis grub pa 'gog pa la skyon mtshungs pa'i rtsod pa, rang la skyon mi mtshungs pa'i lan bstan pa'o
gru.english: This brings us to our third point from above—refuting any other argument on these points. This we will cover in two parts: argument that the problems are just the same with the denial that cause & effect could exist through any nature of its own; and presenting a response which shows that the problems are not the same with our position.

gru.acip: DANG PO NI, 'DIR RGYU 'BRAS RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA BKAG PA'I LAN DU, KHA CIG 'DI SKAD DU RGYUS 'BRAS BU SKYED PA LA PHRAD MA PHRAD KYI BRTAG PA BYED PA NI KHYED LA YANG MTSUNGS SO,,
gru.wylie: dang po ni, 'dir rgyu 'bras rang bzhin gyis grub pa bkag pa'i lan du, kha cig 'di skad du rgyus 'bras bu skyed pa la phrad ma phrad kyi brtag pa byed pa ni khyed la yang mtshungs so
gru.english: Someone comes now to respond to our denial that cause & effect could exist through some nature of its own. This person would say, “This approach of examining whether or not the cause makes contact with the result when it triggers that result applies to you, just the same.”

gru.acip: DE LTAR BYAS NA KHYOD KYI SUN 'BYIN PA LA SUN DBYUNG BYA SUN 'BYIN PA'I NUS PA MED PAS, KHYOD KYI SUN 'BYIN NYID SUN PHYUNG BA YIN PAS SHUGS KYIS NA RGYU 'BRAS KYI DNGOS PO YANG RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA NYID DO ZHES BRTAN PA'I {%both editions say brtan pa'i here} PHYIR SMRAS PA,
gru.wylie: de ltar byas na khyod kyi sun 'byin pa la sun dbyung bya sun 'byin pa'i nus pa med pas, khyod kyi sun 'byin nyid sun phyung ba yin pas shugs kyis na rgyu 'bras kyi dngos po yang rang bzhin gyis grub pa nyid do zhes brtan pa'i {%boTh eDiTioNS Say brTaN pa'i here} phyir smras pa
gru.english: As such, we can say that your attack has no power to attack any idea at all to be attacked. And that means that your attack is itself attacked. And as such, the implication is that entities of cause & effect are indeed quite precisely things that exist through some nature of their own; we can say it then ever more firmly.

gru.acip: GNYIS PA LA BZHI, RANG GI PHYOGS LA SUN 'BYIN DANG SGRUB PA 'THAD TSUL, GZHAN GYI THAL BA MI MTSUNGS PA'I RGYU MTSAN GSAL BAR BSHAD PA, RANG BZHIN MED PA BSGRUB NUS PA BZHIN DU GZHAN GYIS BZLOG STE BSGRUB MI NUS PA, 'DIR MA BSHAD PA'I SUN 'BYIN LHAG MA SHES PAR BYED TSUL LO,,
gru.wylie: gnyis pa la bzhi, rang gi phyogs la sun 'byin dang sgrub pa 'thad tshul, gzhan gyi thal ba mi mtshungs pa'i rgyu mtshan gsal bar bshad pa, rang bzhin med pa bsgrub nus pa bzhin du gzhan gyis bzlog ste bsgrub mi nus pa, 'dir ma bshad pa'i sun 'byin lhag ma shes par byed tshul lo
gru.english: This brings us to the second section from above, which is presenting a response which shows that the problems are not the same with our own position. Here we proceed in four parts: (1) demonstrating how the attack and the proof utilized in our own position are correct; (2) a clear explanation of the reason why our position is not equivalent to the statement of a necessary implication for the other party; (3) a demonstration of how—so long as we are able to establish that things have no nature of their own—the other party will be unable to prove any denial of our position; and (4) showing how we can understand additional attacks that have not been explained here so far.

gru.acip: DANG PO LA GNYIS, THA SNYAD DU GZHAN PHYOGS SUN 'BYIN PA KHAS LEN TSUL DANG, RANG GI PHYOGS SGRUB PA KHAS LEN TSUL LO, ,DANG PO NI,
gru.wylie: dang po la gnyis, tha snyad du gzhan phyogs sun 'byin pa khas len tshul dang, rang gi phyogs sgrub pa khas len tshul lo, ,dang po ni
gru.english: The first of these has two topics of its own: how it is that we accept, nominally, the attack of the opposing position; and how it is that we accept the proof of our own position. Here is the first.

gru.acip: 'DIR RGOL BA GANG LA PHYOGS YOD PA STE RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA'I DON DAM 'CHA' BA DE LA SKYON DU 'GYUR GYI,
gru.wylie: 'dir rgol ba gang la phyogs yod pa ste rang bzhin gyis grub pa'i don dam 'cha' ba de la skyon du 'gyur gyi
gru.english: Here a problem arises with that person who has a position; which is to say, with a person who is asserting that there is an object which could exist through some nature of its own.

gru.acip: BDAG LA RANG BZHIN KYIS GRUB PA'I DON DAM 'CHA' BA'I PHYOGS 'DI NI YOD PA MIN PAS, PHRAD MA PHRAD GNYIS KA LA SKYON BSTAN PA'I THAL BAR 'GYUR BA 'DI NI, BDAG LA SRID PA MA YIN TE, NGED KYI LTAR NA SUN 'BYUNG BYA DANG SUN 'BYIN PA GNYIS KA RANG BZHIN GYIS MA GRUB PAR KHAS LEN PA'I PHYIR RO,,
gru.wylie: bdag la rang bzhin kyis grub pa'i don dam 'cha' ba'i phyogs 'di ni yod pa min pas, phrad ma phrad gnyis ka la skyon bstan pa'i thal bar 'gyur ba 'di ni, bdag la srid pa ma yin te, nged kyi ltar na sun 'byung bya dang sun 'byin pa gnyis ka rang bzhin gyis ma grub par khas len pa'i phyir ro
gru.english: We though do not take any such position wherein we assert that there is any object which could exist through some nature of its own. As such, this statement of a necessary consequence presenting the problems of both making contact or not making contact is not something which is even possible for us. And that's because—according to us—one should accept the idea that neither the idea which is attacked nor the attacking itself is something that could exist through some nature of its own.

gru.acip: PHA ROL POS RGYU 'BRAS RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PAR KHAS BLANGS LA, RANG GIS RANG BZHIN GYIS MA GRUB PA'I SGYU MA BZHIN DU KHAS BLANGS PA BKOD DO,,
gru.wylie: pha rol pos rgyu 'bras rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub par khas blangs la, rang gis rang bzhin gyis ma grub pa'i sgyu ma bzhin du khas blangs pa bkod do
gru.english: And that is that when our opponent has accepted cause & effect that could exist by definition, we present to them our position, that these are things that cannot exist by themselves, through some kind of self-nature; but are, rather, similar to an illusion.

gru.acip: SKABS 'DIR YANG GZHAN LA 'PHANGS PA'I SKYON RANG LA MI 'ONG BA'I RGYU MTSAN DU RANG BZHIN GYIS MA GRUB PA'I PHYIR RO, ZHES GSUNGS PAS RANG LA MI MTSUNGS PA'I RGYU MTSAN NI, PHYOGS GNYIS RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA KHAS MI LEN PA YIN PAR GDON MI ZA BAR 'DOD PAR BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: skabs 'dir yang gzhan la 'phangs pa'i skyon rang la mi 'ong ba'i rgyu mtshan du rang bzhin gyis ma grub pa'i phyir ro, zhes gsungs pas rang la mi mtshungs pa'i rgyu mtshan ni, phyogs gnyis rang bzhin gyis grub pa khas mi len pa yin par gdon mi za bar 'dod par bya'o
gru.english: What's being said here is “the reason that the problems which are implied by the positions of the others do not apply to ourselves is that these things do not exist through any nature of their own.” That is, we would beyond any doubt have to say that the reason why these issues do not apply to ourselves in an equivalent way is that we would never accept the idea that either possibility existed through any nature of its own.

gru.acip: GNYIS SU DPYAD PA'I THOB BYA YANG RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA'I DNGOS PO MED PA LA MI RIGS PA'I PHYIR, MA BRTAGS PAR 'JIG RTEN GYI THA SNYAD DU THOB PAR KHAS BLANGS PA NI, 'THOB PA YANG YOD CES PA NAS GNYIS KYI TSUL GYIS NI MA YIN NO, ZHES PAS BSTAN TE, THOB PA ZHES PA NI THOB BYA THOB PA DANG MNGON PAR RTOGS PA LA BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: gnyis su dpyad pa'i thob bya yang rang bzhin gyis grub pa'i dngos po med pa la mi rigs pa'i phyir, ma brtags par 'jig rten gyi tha snyad du thob par khas blangs pa ni, 'thob pa yang yod ces pa nas gnyis kyi tshul gyis ni ma yin no, zhes pas bstan te, thob pa zhes pa ni thob bya thob pa dang mngon par rtogs pa la bya'o
gru.english: Now it would be illogical to say that something attained which we examined in the two different ways could not exist with an entity that existed through some nature of its own. As such, accepting the idea of an attainment without examination—in the vernacular of the world—is what's being indicated from the point of saying that there is an attainmnent, up through saying that it is not something that is there in either of the two ways. That is, when we speak of an “attainment,” we are referring to the attainment of an attainment, and a realization.

gru.acip: ,MI BDEN BZHIN DU'ANG RANG GI BYAD BZHIN MDZES PAR BSGRUB BYA'I PHYIR, ,DE NI YOD PA JI LTAR DE BZHIN 'DIR YANG SHES RAB GDOD {%GDONG}, ,SBYANG PAR BYA LA NUS PA MTHONG BAR 'GYUR BA'I GTAN TSIGS NI, ,'THAD PA DANG BRAL LAS KYANG BSGRUB BYA RTOGS ZHES SHES PAR BYA,
gru.wylie: mi bden bzhin du'ang rang gi byad bzhin mdzes par bsgrub bya'i phyir, ,de ni yod pa ji ltar de bzhin 'dir yang shes rab gdod {%gdong}, ,sbyang par bya la nus pa mthong bar 'gyur ba'i gtan tshigs ni, ,'thad pa dang bral las kyang bsgrub bya rtogs zhes shes par bya
gru.english: It may not be The real thing, But still it helps us To establish the beauty Of the original object Being reflected. As such, it does Possess that. Here, in the same way, We seek to clean The face of wisdom. And we should Understand that we Come to a realization Of the thesis that we Are undertaking To establish With reasonings too We would call Devoid of any Correctness: That we can see Have the force.

gru.acip: DES KYANG 'DOD PA'I DON NGES PA DANG GZUGS BRNYAN MI BDEN BZHIN DU'ANG, RANG GI BYAD BZHIN MDZES PAR BSGRUB PAR BYA BA'I PHYIR, GZUGS BRNYAN DE LA NI NUS PA YOD PA
gru.wylie: des kyang 'dod pa'i don nges pa dang gzugs brnyan mi bden bzhin du'ang, rang gi byad bzhin mdzes par bsgrub par bya ba'i phyir, gzugs brnyan de la ni nus pa yod pa
gru.english: Now the ascertainment of the object that we seek—and the reflection—may not be the real things; but still they help us to establish the beauty of the original object being reflected. As such, we can say that it—the reflection—does possess some force.

gru.acip: JI LTA BA DE BZHIN DU, 'DIR YANG GDONG PA DANG 'DRA BA'I SHES RAB KYI DRI MA MA RIG PA SBYANG BAR BYA BA LA, NUS PA MTHONG BAR 'GYUR BA'I GTAN TSIGS RTEN 'BREL DANG GCIG DU BRAL SOGS LAS BSGRUB BYA RANG BZHIN GYIS MED PA RTOGS PAR SHES PAR BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: ji lta ba de bzhin du, 'dir yang gdong pa dang 'dra ba'i shes rab kyi dri ma ma rig pa sbyang bar bya ba la, nus pa mthong bar 'gyur ba'i gtan tshigs rten 'brel dang gcig du bral sogs las bsgrub bya rang bzhin gyis med pa rtogs par shes par bya'o
gru.english: Here, in the same way as with that other case, we seek to clean the impurity of misunderstanding away from wisdom, which is similar to a person's face. And we should understand that we come to a realization that things do not exist through any nature of their own: which is the thesis that we are undertaking to establish with classical proofs such as that based on interdependence, and the lack of one or many. For these are reasonings that we can see have the force to remove that impurity marring the face.

gru.acip: DE YANG RANG BZHIN GYIS YOD PAR SGRUB PA'I 'THAD PA DANG BRAL BA'I GTAN TSIGS SO,,
gru.wylie: de yang rang bzhin gyis yod par sgrub pa'i 'thad pa dang bral ba'i gtan tshigs so
gru.english: These can also be referred to as types of reasoning which are “devoid of any correctness,” in the sense of it being correct to establish things as existing through some nature of their own.

gru.acip: KYANG GI SGRAS NI RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA'I 'THAD PA DANG BRAL BA'I SUN 'BYIN GYIS KYANG SUN DBYUNG BYA SUN 'BYIN NUS PA'I SHES PAR BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: kyang gi sgras ni rang bzhin gyis grub pa'i 'thad pa dang bral ba'i sun 'byin gyis kyang sun dbyung bya sun 'byin nus pa'i shes par bya'o
gru.english: When the root text says “too” here, we should understand it as referring to the force that an attack possesses to successfully attack what it attacks, in the absence of any correctness to the idea that things could exist through any nature of their own.

gru.acip: RTZA SHE LAS KYANG, ,STONG PA NYID KYIS BRTZAD BYAS TSE, ,GANG ZHIG LAN 'DEBS SMRA BYED PA, ,DE YIS THAMS CAD LAN BTAB MIN, ,BSGRUB PAR BYA DANG MTSUNGS PAR 'GYUR, ZHES GSUNGS SO,,
gru.wylie: rtsa she las kyang, ,stong pa nyid kyis brtsad byas tshe, ,gang zhig lan 'debs smra byed pa, ,de yis thams cad lan btab min, ,bsgrub par bya dang mtshungs par 'gyur, zhes gsungs so
gru.english: Wisdom says as well: When you examine things With emptiness, You find that those Who try to give an answer Have given none at all; And it's the same With attempting a proof.

gru.acip: GZHAN GYI GLAGS DANG BCAS PA STE SKYON BRJOD DANG BCAS PA'I LAN BRJOD NA, PHA ROL PO MI BZOD LA SKYED PAR BYED PA LA BDEN PA KHAS BLANGS NA SKYON 'JUG PA LTAR, GSAL BYED KYI RGYU LA'ANG RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA KHAS BLANGS NA SKYON YOD PA'I PHYIR RO,,
gru.wylie: gzhan gyi glags dang bcas pa ste skyon brjod dang bcas pa'i lan brjod na, pha rol po mi bzod la skyed par byed pa la bden pa khas blangs na skyon 'jug pa ltar, gsal byed kyi rgyu la'ang rang bzhin gyis grub pa khas blangs na skyon yod pa'i phyir ro
gru.english: And so suppose we were to give a reply with an “opening”; which is to say, where the other person could point out some logical fault. We know that certain problems would arise with accepting the idea that something which acted to trigger something else was real; just so, there would be problems with agreeing that a cause which acted to clarify some idea could exist through some nature of its own.

gru.acip: GZHAN YANG LEGS LDAN 'DIS DBU MA'I BSTAN BCOS SU RANG BZHIN MED PAR DAM BCAS PA'I DON SGRUB PA'I PHYIR DU BKOD BA'I SGRUB BYED LA, GZHAN GYIS SUN 'BYIN PA BKOD PA RNAMS KYI SKYON SPONG LA LTAG GCOD KYI LAN SMRA BAR BYED PAS,
gru.wylie: gzhan yang legs ldan 'dis dbu ma'i bstan bcos su rang bzhin med par dam bcas pa'i don sgrub pa'i phyir du bkod ba'i sgrub byed la, gzhan gyis sun 'byin pa bkod pa rnams kyi skyon spong la ltag gcod kyi lan smra bar byed pas
gru.english: Moreover, we can consider certain proofs that this same Master Bhavaviveka puts forth to establish the assertions, made in the classical commentary on the middle way, that things have no nature of their own. Here he does undertake to give definitive responses which serve to deny the problems that are raised by others in their attacks on this position.

gru.acip: 'DI NI GZHAN GYIS SUN DBYUNG BAR BYA BA KHO NA YIN PAS RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA KHAS BLANGS NA, SKYED BYED DANG GSAL BYED KYI RGYU GNYIS KA LA PHRAD MA PHRAD KYI SKYON MTSUNGS KYANG, DE KHAS MI LEN PA'I PHYIR SKYON MED DO ZHES PA KHO BO CAG GIS BTAB PA'I LAN KHO NA CHES MDZES SO,,
gru.wylie: 'di ni gzhan gyis sun dbyung bar bya ba kho na yin pas rang bzhin gyis grub pa khas blangs na, skyed byed dang gsal byed kyi rgyu gnyis ka la phrad ma phrad kyi skyon mtshungs kyang, de khas mi len pa'i phyir skyon med do zhes pa kho bo cag gis btab pa'i lan kho na ches mdzes so
gru.english: And so suppose we say that if something is only an idea that others seek to attack, we would assert that it existed through some nature of its own. The problems that arise with contact being made or not being made are equivalent, whether we're talking about causes that act to trigger something, or those which act to clarify something. Nonetheless, what we can do is to respond, “Well, since we accept no such thing, then we have no problem.” For us to do no more than make this kind of reply is perfectly elegant. Why our position is not equivalent

gru.acip: ,GAL TE RANG GI BSGRUB BYA GO BYED GTAN TSIGS DNGOS GRUB DANG, ,DNGOS SU GO BYA NYID 'GYUR BSGRUB BYA'I NGO BO'ANG YOD GYUR NA, ,PHRAD PA LA SOGS RIGS PA NYE BAR SBYOR BAR 'GYUR ZHIG NA, ,DE YANG YOD PA MIN PAS KHYED KYI YI CHAD 'BA' ZHIG YIN,
gru.wylie: gal te rang gi bsgrub bya go byed gtan tshigs dngos grub dang, ,dngos su go bya nyid 'gyur bsgrub bya'i ngo bo'ang yod gyur na, ,phrad pa la sogs rigs pa nye bar sbyor bar 'gyur zhig na, ,de yang yod pa min pas khyed kyi yi chad 'ba' zhig yin
gru.english: Suppose then It were the case That this entity Of what we refer to As a logical statement Meant to help others Comprehend what We are trying to prove— Along with the Essential nature of what We are trying to prove, That exact thing Which we hope will be Directly understood— Could exist. And suppose that We put together reasoning That they did make contact, Or anything of the like. This is further Something that Could never exist; As such, For you it is just Some exhausting Expenditure of effort.

gru.acip: GAL TE RANG GI BSGRUB BYA GO BYED GTAN TSIGS KYI DNGOS PO STE NGO BO DANG, DNGOS SU GO BAR BYA BA NYID DU 'GYUR BA BSGRUB BYA'I NGO BO RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA YOD PAR GYUR NA,
gru.wylie: gal te rang gi bsgrub bya go byed gtan tshigs kyi dngos po ste ngo bo dang, dngos su go bar bya ba nyid du 'gyur ba bsgrub bya'i ngo bo rang bzhin gyis grub pa yod par gyur na
gru.english: And so suppose then it were the case that this entity or essential nature of what we refer to as a logical statement meant to help others comprehend what we are trying to prove—along with the essential nature of what we are trying to prove, that exact thing which we hope will be directly understood—could exist in a way where they existed through some nature of their own.

gru.acip: BSGRUB BYA DANG SGRUB BYED PHRAD PA DANG, LA SOGS PAS MA PHRAD PAR SGRUB PA DANG SUN 'BYIN PA'I RIGS PA NYE BAR SBYOR BAR 'GYUR BA ZHIG NA,
gru.wylie: bsgrub bya dang sgrub byed phrad pa dang, la sogs pas ma phrad par sgrub pa dang sun 'byin pa'i rigs pa nye bar sbyor bar 'gyur ba zhig na
gru.english: And suppose then that we were to put together reasoning which was meant either to prove, or to attack, the idea that what was being proved and what did the proving did make contact, or “anything of the like”—referring to not making contact.

gru.acip: RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA DE YANG YOD PA MIN PAS MA DAG PA'I PHYOGS LA BKOD PA'I SKYON, DAG PA'I PHYOGS LA KHYED KYIS BKOD PA 'DI NI KHO BO CAG LA DON MED PAR YI CHAD PA STE YID 'BYUNG BA 'BA' ZHIG YIN PAR RTOGS TE,
gru.wylie: rang bzhin gyis grub pa de yang yod pa min pas ma dag pa'i phyogs la bkod pa'i skyon, dag pa'i phyogs la khyed kyis bkod pa 'di ni kho bo cag la don med par yi chad pa ste yid 'byung ba 'ba' zhig yin par rtogs te
gru.english: But the fact is further that the very fact of something existing through some nature of its own is something that could never exist; as such, we should understand that for those of you who are on the completely correct side of things to point out problems with those who are already on the completely incorrect side of things is just some kind of exhausting or hopeless expenditure of effort for all of us.

gru.acip: DE NYID KYI PHYIR GANG DAG MIG DANG KHAB LONG LA SOGS PAS MA PHRAD PAR RANG GI BYA BA BYED PAR RNAM PAR BZHAG PA'I DPE DE DAG KYANG BKAG PAR RIG PAR BYA STE, RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAR KHAS LEN NA DE DAG LA YANG PHRAD MA PHRAD KYI THAL BA MTSUNGS PA'I PHYIR RO,,
gru.wylie: de nyid kyi phyir gang dag mig dang khab long la sogs pas ma phrad par rang gi bya ba byed par rnam par bzhag pa'i dpe de dag kyang bkag par rig par bya ste, rang bzhin gyis grub par khas len na de dag la yang phrad ma phrad kyi thal ba mtshungs pa'i phyir ro
gru.english: For this reason, let's look at these examples where we use things like the eye or a magnet to describe how something can be established as performing its function even in the absence of contact. It would be logical then to deny these examples, since if we accept that a thing can exist through some nature of its own, the consequences of saying that it either made contact or did not make contact would be the same.

gru.acip: GZHAN YANG JI LTAR SGYU MA DANG RMI LAM LA SOGS PA PHYIR RGOL RANG GI PHYOGS LA'ANG GRUB PA'I DPE KHO NAS, PHYIR RGOL GYI 'JIG RTEN GYIS DNGOS PO RNAMS MTHA' DAG DBU MA PAS DNGOS PO STE RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA MED PAR RTOGS SU GZHUG PAR NUS PA NI, CHES SLA BA JI LTA BA
gru.wylie: gzhan yang ji ltar sgyu ma dang rmi lam la sogs pa phyir rgol rang gi phyogs la'ang grub pa'i dpe kho nas, phyir rgol gyi 'jig rten gyis dngos po rnams mtha' dag dbu ma pas dngos po ste rang bzhin gyis grub pa med par rtogs su gzhug par nus pa ni, ches sla ba ji lta ba
gru.english: Moreover, things like an illusion and a dream are nothing less than examples that can be accepted in the system of the person we are debating with. They are extremely simple ways that have the capacity to help these people on the other side—people of the normal world—come to the realization that all existing entitites are, as those of the middle way describe it, “those things,” meaning things that do not exist with any nature of their own.

gru.acip: DE LTAR PHA ROL PO LAS GZHAN DBU MA PA DAG LA DNGOS PO RNAMS RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAR KHONG DU CHUD PAR BDE BLAG TU NI NUS PA MA YIN TE, GNYIS KA LA BDEN PAR GRAGS PA'I DPE MED PA'I PHYIR RO,,
gru.wylie: de ltar pha rol po las gzhan dbu ma pa dag la dngos po rnams rang bzhin gyis grub par khong du chud par bde blag tu ni nus pa ma yin te, gnyis ka la bden par grags pa'i dpe med pa'i phyir ro
gru.english: It is not the case though that, in the same way, those other than the opponent here—meaning those who follow the middle way—would be enabled with this ease to comprehend that entities did exist through some nature of their own. And that's because there is no example that would be said to be true inside of both camps.

gru.acip: 'DIS NI BDEN MED SGRUB PA'I GTAN TSIGS RTEN 'BREL LTA BU LA, BDEN MED KYIS KHYAB PA MTHUN DPE'I STENG DU MA NGES PAR BDEN MED CHOS CAN GYI STENG DU TSAD MAS NGES PAR BYAR MED PAR GSUNGS SO,,
gru.wylie: 'dis ni bden med sgrub pa'i gtan tshigs rten 'brel lta bu la, bden med kyis khyab pa mthun dpe'i steng du ma nges par bden med chos can gyi steng du tshad mas nges par byar med par gsungs so
gru.english: What this is saying is that—with something like the concept of dependence, used as a rationale for proving that nothing exists in reality—there is no way that we can conclude, with an accurate perception, that the quality of not existing in reality applies to the subject under consideration, unless we have first confirmed—with reference to a concordant example—that if something is dependent it cannot exist in reality.

gru.acip: BDEN 'DZIN GYI RTZOD PA 'DI NI DOR BAR BYA DGOS TE, DNGOS PO GZUGS BRNYAN DANG 'DRA BA'I BRDZUN PA THAMS CAD LA, RANG DANG SPYI'I MTSAN NYID DANG MNGON SUM MAM RJES SU DPAG PA'AM RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA CI ZHIG YOD,,
gru.wylie: bden 'dzin gyi rtsod pa 'di ni dor bar bya dgos te, dngos po gzugs brnyan dang 'dra ba'i brdzun pa thams cad la, rang dang spyi'i mtshan nyid dang mngon sum mam rjes su dpag pa'am rang bzhin gyis grub pa ci zhig yod
gru.english: This argument where you grasp onto things as being real is something that now you really have to give up. Things are all fake, just like a reflection in a mirror. How then are you going to prove somehow that they exist through some nature of their own; that they possess some particular or more general characteristics of their own, which could be detected either through our direct senses, or through some kind of deduction?

gru.acip: CHOS RNAMS RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA MED PA'I BDAG MED 'DI NI, ,BCOM LDAN 'DAS KYIS GANG ZAG GI BDAG MED PA DANG, CHOS KYI BDAG MED PA'I DBYE BA RNAM PA GNYIS SU GSUNGS SO,,
gru.wylie: chos rnams rang bzhin gyis grub pa med pa'i bdag med 'di ni, ,bcom ldan 'das kyis gang zag gi bdag med pa dang, chos kyi bdag med pa'i dbye ba rnam pa gnyis su gsungs so
gru.english: Let's consider then this fact that there are no objects in the entire universe which possess some self-nature: which exist through any nature of their own. The Conqueror has stated that it has two great divisions: the lack of a self-nature to the person, and the lack of a self-nature to things.

gru.acip: DE GNYIS SU 'BYED TSUL DE YANG GZHI GANG ZAG DANG CHOS KYI STENG DU MED RGYU'I BDAG MI 'DRA BA GNYIS KYI SGO NAS PHYE BA MIN TE, MED RGYU'I BDAG NI RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA YIN PAS SO,,
gru.wylie: de gnyis su 'byed tshul de yang gzhi gang zag dang chos kyi steng du med rgyu'i bdag mi 'dra ba gnyis kyi sgo nas phye ba min te, med rgyu'i bdag ni rang bzhin gyis grub pa yin pas so
gru.english: It is not the case that the way in which we make this division into two is based upon two different types of a self which does not exist, starting off from the division of things into the person and things. That's because the self that is not there is one which exists through its own nature.

gru.acip: DE DAG LA GANG ZAG RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA'I GANG ZAG GI BDAG MED PA MA LUS PAR SGOM PA NI YOD PAR RNAM PAR GZHAG GO
gru.wylie: de dag la gang zag rang bzhin gyis grub pa'i gang zag gi bdag med pa ma lus par sgom pa ni yod par rnam par gzhag go
gru.english: We do make a presentation which shows that these individuals do possess a practice where they meditate upon all the forms of the lack of a self-nature to the person—of a person who could exist through some nature of their own.

gru.acip: ,GANG ZAG BDEN GRUB 'GOG PA'I RIGS PA'I RNAM GRANGS MTHA' YAS PA'I SHES RAB MI SKYED KYANG, NYON MONGS KYI SA BON GYI GNYEN PO RDZOGS PAR SGOM PA YOD LA, SHES BYA'I SGRIB PA'I GNYEN PO RDZOGS PAR SGOM PA NI MED DO,,
gru.wylie: gang zag bden grub 'gog pa'i rigs pa'i rnam grangs mtha' yas pa'i shes rab mi skyed kyang, nyon mongs kyi sa bon gyi gnyen po rdzogs par sgom pa yod la, shes bya'i sgrib pa'i gnyen po rdzogs par sgom pa ni med do
gru.english: It is not the case that these individuals are able to give rise to that wisdom where we used literally countless forms of reasoning to block the idea that the person could exist in some real way. Nonetheless, they do possess a practice where they are able to meditate, in full, upon the antidotes for the seeds of the negative emotions. At the same time, they do not possess a practice where they can meditate, in a complete way, upon the the antidotes to the obstacles to omniscience.

gru.acip: STONG PA NYID DAM STONG PA NYID MA YIN PA RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA NI CUNG ZAD KYANG YOD PA MA YIN TE, STONG PA NYID SO SO BA'I RNAM PA DE LTA BUS 'DUL BA KUN RDZOB TU YOD PAR BSNYAD PAR ZAD DO,,
gru.wylie: stong pa nyid dam stong pa nyid ma yin pa rang bzhin gyis grub pa ni cung zad kyang yod pa ma yin te, stong pa nyid so so ba'i rnam pa de lta bus 'dul ba kun rdzob tu yod par bsnyad par zad do
gru.english: Neither emptiness itself and everything which is not emptiness exists in the slightest way through some nature of their own. It is nothing more than the case that we are using all these different types of emptiness as names for what functions in a deceptive manner to tame disciples.

gru.acip: SNGA MA DAG GIS NI NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB PA'I PHYOGS SU MI BRJOD PA DANG, THA MAS NI GDAGS PA'I DON KUN RDZOB TU YOD PAR BRJOD PAR BYA BA'I DON NO,,
gru.wylie: snga ma dag gis ni ngo bo nyid kyis grub pa'i phyogs su mi brjod pa dang, tha mas ni gdags pa'i don kun rdzob tu yod par brjod par bya ba'i don no
gru.english: The point of the earlier lines is that we cannot speak of a position where we say that things exist through some essential nature of their own; the point of the later lines is to convey that we should speak of things as existing deceptively—as things that are labelled. The sixteen, beginning with emptiness on the inside

gru.acip: NANG GI CHOS MIG LA SOGS PA DRUG PO, RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA MED PA NYID GANG YIN PA DE NI NANG STONG PA NYID DU 'DOD DO,,
gru.wylie: nang gi chos mig la sogs pa drug po, rang bzhin gyis grub pa med pa nyid gang yin pa de ni nang stong pa nyid du 'dod do
gru.english: What we accept as being emptiness on the inside is the fact that the inner entities of the eye and the rest of the six do not exist in way where they are present through any nature of their own.

gru.acip: DE YANG MIG NI MIG RANG GI NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB PAS STONG STE, MIG DE'I RANG BZHIN NI RANG GI NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB PAS STONG PA DE YIN PA'I PHYIR RO,,
gru.wylie: de yang mig ni mig rang gi ngo bo nyid kyis grub pas stong ste, mig de'i rang bzhin ni rang gi ngo bo nyid kyis grub pas stong pa de yin pa'i phyir ro
gru.english: Which is to say, the eye is empty: it is not an eye that exists through any essential nature of its own. And that's because the nature of this eye is that it is empty of existing through any essential nature of its own.

gru.acip: 'GYUR 'PHYUGS PA YIN TE, DE LTA YIN NA BSGRUB BYA'I CHOS LOG PA LA RTAGS KYIS KHYAB DGOS PAR 'GYUR BA'I PHYIR RO,,
gru.wylie: 'gyur 'phyugs pa yin te, de lta yin na bsgrub bya'i chos log pa la rtags kyis khyab dgos par 'gyur ba'i phyir ro
gru.english: This is in fact an error in the translation, since if this were the case then what was given as the reason would have to subsume the opposite of the quality to be proven.

gru.acip: RAB TU BYUNG NAS KYANG CHOS NYID DE THOB PAR BYA BA'I PHYIR, SKRA 'AM GOS LA ME SHOR BA LTAR BRTZON 'GRUS RTZOM ZHING GNAS PA RNAM PAR 'JIG PA MED PA'O,,
gru.wylie: rab tu byung nas kyang chos nyid de thob par bya ba'i phyir, skra 'am gos la me shor ba ltar brtson 'grus rtsom zhing gnas pa rnam par 'jig pa med pa'o
gru.english: For the reason that they leave the home is to attain this real nature of things. They make efforts with the same urgency they would show if their hair or clothes were to catch on fire; this is how they live, and they have no fear of anything.

gru.acip: 'DIR SMRAS PA, KYE MA MA {%LA? both carvings say MA MA} LA GANG ZHIG DNGOS PO RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA CUNG ZAD KYANG MI 'DOD CING, GLO BUR DU BCOS MA MA YIN PA DANG, GZHAN LA LTOS PA MED PA'I RANG BZHIN YANG 'DOD PA KHYOD NI, PHAN TSUN 'GAL BA'I DON BRJOD PA ZHIG GO ZHE NA,
gru.wylie: 'dir smras pa, kye ma ma {%la? boTh carviNgS Say ma ma} la gang zhig dngos po rang bzhin gyis grub pa cung zad kyang mi 'dod cing, glo bur du bcos ma ma yin pa dang, gzhan la ltos pa med pa'i rang bzhin yang 'dod pa khyod ni, phan tshun 'gal ba'i don brjod pa zhig go zhe na
gru.english: And so we can say it this way. Suppose you burst out with something like— Oh my gosh! You are people who can accept not even the slightest version of something existing through any nature of its own; and yet at the same time you have no problem with agreeing that there is some nature to things which is not something that was ever created in some occurrence of the moment—a nature which has never relied upon anything else. And so you are expressing two ideas which simply contradict each other!

gru.acip: RANG BZHIN BKAG PA NI MIG SOGS GSHIS LUGS YIN PA BKAG PA YIN LA, RANG BZHIN KHAS BLANGS PA NI BKAG PA DE MIG SOGS KYI CHOS NYID CES PA'I RANG BZHIN DU 'DOD PA YIN PAS, DNGOS PO RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA BKAG PA DANG, DNGOS PO'I CHOS NYID KYI RANG BZHIN KHAS LEN PA LA 'GAL BA CUNG ZAD KYANG MED PA'I PHYIR RO,,
gru.wylie: rang bzhin bkag pa ni mig sogs gshis lugs yin pa bkag pa yin la, rang bzhin khas blangs pa ni bkag pa de mig sogs kyi chos nyid ces pa'i rang bzhin du 'dod pa yin pas, dngos po rang bzhin gyis grub pa bkag pa dang, dngos po'i chos nyid kyi rang bzhin khas len pa la 'gal ba cung zad kyang med pa'i phyir ro
gru.english: When we say that we are denying a nature, we are talking about denying a primordial way of being for the eye and so on. When we say that we accept a nature, we are agreeing to the idea that the denial just mentioned is the nature of the eye and the rest: what we call the true nature of these things. As such, there is not the slightest contradiction between denying that things could exist through some nature of their own, and agreeing to a nature in that sense of a true nature to things.

gru.acip: DE 'DRA BA'I CHOS NYID DE YANG BDAG GIS KUN RDZOB KYI BDEN PA STE THA SNYAD TZAM DU GRUB PA LA LTOS NAS, BCOS MA MIN PA DANG GZHAN LA MI LTOS PAR BRJOD DO,,
gru.wylie: de 'dra ba'i chos nyid de yang bdag gis kun rdzob kyi bden pa ste tha snyad tsam du grub pa la ltos nas, bcos ma min pa dang gzhan la mi ltos par brjod do
gru.english: This kind of a true nature to things is “what I am talking about when I speak of deceptive” reality; things that rely on existing only nominally—and it is something which is not artificial, or which does not depend upon something else.

gru.acip: GANG ZHIG BYIS PA'I SKYE BO RANG DGA' BAS BLTA PAR BYA BA MA YIN PA'I CHOS NYID DE NI RANG BZHIN DU RIGS LA, DE KUN RDZOB TU YOD PAR KHAS BLANGS PA DE TZAM GYIS DON DAM PAR DE DNGOS PO DANG DNGOS PO MED PAR RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA YANG MA YIN TE, DE NI RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA ZHI BA NYID YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: gang zhig byis pa'i skye bo rang dga' bas blta par bya ba ma yin pa'i chos nyid de ni rang bzhin du rigs la, de kun rdzob tu yod par khas blangs pa de tsam gyis don dam par de dngos po dang dngos po med par rang bzhin gyis grub pa yang ma yin te, de ni rang bzhin gyis grub pa zhi ba nyid yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: A kind of true nature to things that would not be something which could be viewed by just everyday infants would be fitting as this nature. And by the simple act of agreeing that this could exist in a deceptive way we can say that it is not something that could exist through some nature of its own—as an entity or a non-entity, in some ultimate way. This is what we refer to as a perfect state of peace, or the end of existing through some nature of its own.

gru.acip: RANG BZHIN CHOS NYID 'DI NI SLOB DPON 'PHAGS PAS ZHAL GYIS BZHES PA 'BA' ZHIG TU MA ZAD KYI, PHA ROL PO GZHAN YANG DON 'DI KHAS LEN DU GZHUG PAR NUS PAS, RANG BZHIN 'DI NI BRTZAD PA'I MTHAR RANG GZHAN GNYIS KA LA GRUB PA NYID DU YANG RNAM PAR BZHAG GO ,ZHES GSUNGS PA 'DI KHYAD PAR DU NGES PAR BYA DGOS SO,,
gru.wylie: rang bzhin chos nyid 'di ni slob dpon 'phags pas zhal gyis bzhes pa 'ba' zhig tu ma zad kyi, pha rol po gzhan yang don 'di khas len du gzhug par nus pas, rang bzhin 'di ni brtsad pa'i mthar rang gzhan gnyis ka la grub pa nyid du yang rnam par bzhag go ,zhes gsungs pa 'di khyad par du nges par bya dgos so
gru.english: Not only is this nature in the form of a true nature to things something that is accepted by our master, the Realized One; it is also possible for others of different positions to be guided into accepting this point. As such, we can say that “When you come to the end of this examination of a nature to things, you are establishing something quite perfectly for both yourself and for others.” We have to come to a special appreciation of this feature.

gru.acip: NAG TSO'I 'GYUR LAS, DE LA 'DI LTAR MCHOG TU 'DZIN PA NYID MED PA'I PHYIR DANG, KUN RDZOB TU DON JI LTA BA BZHIN DU BSGRUBS PA'I PHYIR RO,, ZHES 'BYUNG NGO,,
gru.wylie: nag tsho'i 'gyur las, de la 'di ltar mchog tu 'dzin pa nyid med pa'i phyir dang, kun rdzob tu don ji lta ba bzhin du bsgrubs pa'i phyir ro,, zhes 'byung ngo
gru.english: Naktso's translation has: “…because there is absolutely no considering something preeminent in that way, with it; and in a deceptive sense, it exists in the way it should.”

gru.acip: DE LA MIG SOGS RNAMS MIG SOGS KYIS STONG PAR GSUNGS PAS NI, MIG SOGS RNAMS RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAS STONG PA NYID GSAL BAR MDZAD PA YIN GYI, MIG NANG GI BYED PA'I BDAG DANG BRAL BA'I STONG PA'O ZHES NYAN THOS SDE PA 'DOD PA DANG,
gru.wylie: de la mig sogs rnams mig sogs kyis stong par gsungs pas ni, mig sogs rnams rang bzhin gyis grub pas stong pa nyid gsal bar mdzad pa yin gyi, mig nang gi byed pa'i bdag dang bral ba'i stong pa'o zhes nyan thos sde pa 'dod pa dang
gru.english: And so what does it mean, when we say that “the eye and the rest are empty of the eye and the rest”? This is merely a clarification of the fact that the eye and so on are empty of existing through any nature of their own; but it is not, first of all, as the listener groups would have it, when they refer to an emptiness in the form of the eye being devoid of some inner self-nature.

gru.acip: SEMS TZAM PAS MIG GZUNG 'DZIN RDZAS THA DAD PA TZAM GYIS STONG NGO ZHES MIG SOGS RANG GI NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB PAS MI STONG PA'I GCIG LA GCIG MED PA'I STONG PA NYID DU 'DOD PA LTAR NI MA YIN NO,,
gru.wylie: sems tsam pas mig gzung 'dzin rdzas tha dad pa tsam gyis stong ngo zhes mig sogs rang gi ngo bo nyid kyis grub pas mi stong pa'i gcig la gcig med pa'i stong pa nyid du 'dod pa ltar ni ma yin no
gru.english: Nor is it as the Mind Only school would have it, when they speak of an emptiness which is no more than the fact that the object and subject aspects of the eye are void of being essentially separate—an emptiness where the eye and so forth were not empty of existing through any essential nature of their own, but rather empty—each one—of being the other. Three more kinds of emptiness

gru.acip: RGYUD KYIS MA BSDUS PA'I GZUGS LA SOGS PA'I YUL DRUG RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAS STONG PA'I RANG BZHIN MED PA NYID NI, PHYI ROL GYI STONG PA NYID DU 'DOD DO,,
gru.wylie: rgyud kyis ma bsdus pa'i gzugs la sogs pa'i yul drug rang bzhin gyis grub pas stong pa'i rang bzhin med pa nyid ni, phyi rol gyi stong pa nyid du 'dod do
gru.english: Consider next then the fact of the lack of a nature to things like physical form and the rest which are not taken in by a person's mind stream; we are talking about the six objects, and the fact that they are empty of existing through any nature of their own. This then is what we say is “emptiness on the outside.”

gru.acip: PHYI'I GZUGS NI GZUGS KYI NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB PAS STONG PA NI, GANG GI PHYIR GZUGS DE'I RANG BZHIN NI DE YIN PA'I PHYIR RO,,
gru.wylie: phyi'i gzugs ni gzugs kyi ngo bo nyid kyis grub pas stong pa ni, gang gi phyir gzugs de'i rang bzhin ni de yin pa'i phyir ro
gru.english: Outer form then is empty of existing through some essential nature of being form; and that in turn is due to the fact that the very nature of form—of it—is that.

gru.acip: DE RANG GI NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB PA'I RANG BZHIN MED PA NYID NI, PHYI NANG GI STONG PA NYID DE LHAG MA SNGAR BZHIN NO,,
gru.wylie: de rang gi ngo bo nyid kyis grub pa'i rang bzhin med pa nyid ni, phyi nang gi stong pa nyid de lhag ma sngar bzhin no
gru.english: The lack of a nature to this container—the fact that it does not exist through any essential nature of its own—constitutes emptiness on the outside and the inside. And the rest follows as before. 4) Emptiness emptiness

gru.acip: PHYI NANG GI CHOS RNAMS SNGAR BSHAD PA LTAR RANG BZHIN KYIS GRUB PA MED PA NYID NI, DE KHO NA LA MKHAS PAS RANG BZHIN STONG PA NYID CES BSNYAD DO,,
gru.wylie: phyi nang gi chos rnams sngar bshad pa ltar rang bzhin kyis grub pa med pa nyid ni, de kho na la mkhas pas rang bzhin stong pa nyid ces bsnyad do
gru.english: Now the fact that both outside and inside entities, as previously explained, are without any existence that has come about through any nature of their own is what those who are masters of suchness refer to as the emptiness of any self-nature.

gru.acip: PHYI NANG GI CHOS KYI RANG BZHIN STONG PA NYID DE YANG STONG NYID KYI NGO BOS GRUB PA'AM BDEN PAS STONG PAR 'DOD PA YIN NO,,
gru.wylie: phyi nang gi chos kyi rang bzhin stong pa nyid de yang stong nyid kyi ngo bos grub pa'am bden pas stong par 'dod pa yin no
gru.english: That is, we assert that the very fact that outer and inner entities are empty of any nature of their own is in turn also empty of any reality, or existence through some essential nature of emptiness itself.

gru.acip: 'DI DAG GIS NI KHA CIG DON DAM PAR BDEN PA ZHES PA BDEN DNGOS RNAM PAR BCAD TZAM LA BYAS NAS DE BDEN GRUB TU SMRA BA DANG, GZHAN DAG DGAG BYA BCAD TZAM MIN PA'I SNGO SER LTAR SGRUB PAR RANG DBANG BA CHOS NYID DU BYAS NAS DE BDEN PAR 'DOD PA GNYIS KA YANG RGYAL BAS SHIN TU SMAD PAR GSUNGS SO,,
gru.wylie: 'di dag gis ni kha cig don dam par bden pa zhes pa bden dngos rnam par bcad tsam la byas nas de bden grub tu smra ba dang, gzhan dag dgag bya bcad tsam min pa'i sngo ser ltar sgrub par rang dbang ba chos nyid du byas nas de bden par 'dod pa gnyis ka yang rgyal bas shin tu smad par gsungs so
gru.english: What these lines are referring to is some people who take the expression “ultimate reality” as referring to the simple exclusion of entities that are real, and then say that that exists in truth. And there are others who point to things like the colors blue or yellow—positive entities which are not the simple exclusion of the thing that emptiness denies—and say that, in their independent form, these are the real nature of things; thus asserting, in effect, that these things are real. And what the lines are saying is that both these parties would be disparaged completely by the Victorious Buddhas. The four starting with great emptiness

gru.acip: SHAR LA SOGS PA 'DI DAG BCU CHAR PHYOGS RNAMS KYI NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB PAS STONG PA NYID NI GANG YIN PA DE NI CHEN PO STONG PA NYID YIN TE, PHYOGS RNAMS CHEN POR RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAR 'DZIN PA BZLOG PA'I PHYIR DU GSUNGS TE, PHYOGS LA PHYIN CI LOG TU 'DZIN PA NI MU STEGS BYE BRAG PAS PHYOGS RNAMS RTAG PA'I RDZAS NYID DU 'DZIN PA LTA BU'O,,
gru.wylie: shar la sogs pa 'di dag bcu char phyogs rnams kyi ngo bo nyid kyis grub pas stong pa nyid ni gang yin pa de ni chen po stong pa nyid yin te, phyogs rnams chen por rang bzhin gyis grub par 'dzin pa bzlog pa'i phyir du gsungs te, phyogs la phyin ci log tu 'dzin pa ni mu stegs bye brag pas phyogs rnams rtag pa'i rdzas nyid du 'dzin pa lta bu'o
gru.english: The fact that all ten directions of east and the rest are empty of existing through any essential nature of their own is “great emptiness.” And it was taught in order to stop people from holding that the directions are vast in a way that exists through some nature of its own. An example of taking the directions in a mistaken way would be where the River school called the Detailers holds that a direction represents some perfectly unchanging substance. 6) Ultimate emptiness

gru.acip: CHOS SKU DE NI DE YI RANG GI NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB PAS STONG PA NYID GANG YIN PA DE NI, DON DAM PA STONG PA NYID DE,
gru.wylie: chos sku de ni de yi rang gi ngo bo nyid kyis grub pas stong pa nyid gang yin pa de ni, don dam pa stong pa nyid de
gru.english: And so consider the emptiness represented by the fact that this body of all things is empty of existing through any essential nature of its own. This is what we refer to as “ultimate emptiness.”

gru.acip: KHAMS GSUM PO DE NI DE YI RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAS STONG PA NYID GANG YIN PA DE NI, 'DUS BYAS STONG PA NYID DU GSUNGS SO,,
gru.wylie: khams gsum po de ni de yi rang bzhin gyis grub pas stong pa nyid gang yin pa de ni, 'dus byas stong pa nyid du gsungs so
gru.english: And so then the emptiness of produced things was taught; which refers to the fact that these three realms are completely empty of any existing through some nature of their own. 8) The emptiness of things that exist but were not produced

gru.acip: DE NI DE YI RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAS STONG PA NYID GANG YIN PA DE NI 'DUS MA BYAS STONG PA NYID DU GSUNGS SO,,
gru.wylie: de ni de yi rang bzhin gyis grub pas stong pa nyid gang yin pa de ni 'dus ma byas stong pa nyid du gsungs so
gru.english: And the fact that this type of entity is empty of any existence through some nature of its own was taught as “the emptiness of things that exist but were not produced.” The four starting with emptiness beyond all extremes

gru.acip: MTHA' BRAL DE NI MTHA' BRAL DE'I RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA KHO NAS STONG PA NYID DE NI, MTHA' LAS 'DAS PA STONG PA NYID DU BSNYAD DO,,
gru.wylie: mtha' bral de ni mtha' bral de'i rang bzhin gyis grub pa kho nas stong pa nyid de ni, mtha' las 'das pa stong pa nyid du bsnyad do
gru.english: And what we call “free of extremes” refers to the emptiness of this freedom from extremes; the fact that it cannot be “simply that”—referring to existing through some nature of its own. We then use the expression here of “emptiness beyond all extremes.”

gru.acip: DPER NA SEMS TZAM PAS RANG GI LUGS KYI RTAG CHAD SOGS KYI MTHA' DANG BRAL BA'I DBUS SEMS BDEN GRUB TU 'DOD PA LTA BU'O,,
gru.wylie: dper na sems tsam pas rang gi lugs kyi rtag chad sogs kyi mtha' dang bral ba'i dbus sems bden grub tu 'dod pa lta bu'o
gru.english: This is similar for example to the case with the Mind Only school, where they hold as a middle view that the mind must exist in truth, once they have eliminated the two extremes of the mind either lasting forever or simply discontinuing. 10) The emptiness of no beginning or end

gru.acip: 'GRO 'ONG RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA DANG BRAL BA'I PHYIR RMI LAM LTA BU'I SRID PA 'DI, SRID PA DE YI RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAS DBEN PA NYID GANG YIN PA DE NI, THOG MA DANG THA MA MED PA'I STONG PA NYID DO ZHES BSTAN BCOS CHEN PO RGYAL BA'I YUM LAS NI NGES PAR BSNYAD DO,,
gru.wylie: 'gro 'ong rang bzhin gyis grub pa dang bral ba'i phyir rmi lam lta bu'i srid pa 'di, srid pa de yi rang bzhin gyis grub pas dben pa nyid gang yin pa de ni, thog ma dang tha ma med pa'i stong pa nyid do zhes bstan bcos chen po rgyal ba'i yum las ni nges par bsnyad do
gru.english: Coming and going are devoid of existing through any nature of their own; as such, our existence is similar to a dream. And the fact that this existence is perfectly devoid of existing through any nature of its own was referred to in the “great classical commentaries”—here referring to the sutras of the Mother of the Victors—with the description, “emptiness where there is no beginning, and no end.” 11) The emptiness that can never be given up

gru.acip: DOR BA MED PA NI DOR BA MED PA DE NYID KYI RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAS STONG PA DE NYID KYI STONG PA NYID GANG YIN PA DE NI, DOR BA MED PA STONG PA NYID CES BYA BAR BRJOD DE, STONG NYID DE DOR BA MED PA'I RANG BZHIN YIN PA DE'I PHYIR NA'O,,
gru.wylie: dor ba med pa ni dor ba med pa de nyid kyi rang bzhin gyis grub pas stong pa de nyid kyi stong pa nyid gang yin pa de ni, dor ba med pa stong pa nyid ces bya bar brjod de, stong nyid de dor ba med pa'i rang bzhin yin pa de'i phyir na'o
gru.english: This quality of never being given up is an essential never being given up which is empty of existing through any nature of its own. The fact of the emptiness of this particular object was then referred to as “the emptiness of never being given up”; and this is because this particular kind of emptiness has a nature of being something that we should never relinquish. 12) The emptiness of any nature

gru.acip: RANG BZHIN DE NYID DE NYID KYI NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB PAS STONG PA NYID GANG YIN PA DE NI RANG BZHIN STONG PA NYID DO,,
gru.wylie: rang bzhin de nyid de nyid kyi ngo bo nyid kyis grub pas stong pa nyid gang yin pa de ni rang bzhin stong pa nyid do
