gru.english: This very thing—this nature of things—is empty of existing in & of itself; which is to say, through some essential nature of its own. And this fact then is the emptiness of any nature.

gru.acip: BDEN MOD 'ON KYANG SKABS SNGA MAR NI PHYI NANG GI CHOS RNAMS KYI STONG NYID DE, DE KHO NA NYID 'JAL BA'I RIGS SHES KYIS GRUB PAS BDEN PAR GRUB BAM SNYAM PA BSAL BA'I PHYIR YIN LA,
gru.wylie: bden mod 'on kyang skabs snga mar ni phyi nang gi chos rnams kyi stong nyid de, de kho na nyid 'jal ba'i rigs shes kyis grub pas bden par grub bam snyam pa bsal ba'i phyir yin la
gru.english: That is indeed the case, but in that previous instance we were referring to the emptiness of inner and outer entities. And that was for the purpose of clarifying the question that might have come up, where someone asks, “Wouldn't it be the case that if something were established by a logical perception which were holding suchness under consideration, wouldn't that thing then exist in truth?”

gru.acip: 'DIR NI SUS KYANG MA BYAS PAR GSHIS SU GRUB PA'I RANG BZHIN YIN NA, BDEN PAR GRUB BAM SNYAM PA BSAL BA'I PHYIR GSUNGS PAS MI ZLOS SO,,
gru.wylie: 'dir ni sus kyang ma byas par gshis su grub pa'i rang bzhin yin na, bden par grub bam snyam pa bsal ba'i phyir gsungs pas mi zlos so
gru.english: Here though the kind of nature being considered is one in which there has been a natural existence, for all time—one which was never put together, by anyone at all. And the reason we were mentioning that here was to prevent the possibility that someone might wonder whether this sort of nature might exist in truth. As such, there is no redundancy here.

gru.acip: DOGS PA'I RGYU MTSAN 'DI GNYIS KA CHOS NYID LA YOD KYANG BDEN PAR GRUB PA 'GOG NUS PA MI 'GAL BA 'DI SHES NA, DON DAM BDEN PA BLO GANG GIS KYANG MI RTOGS PAR 'DZIN PA'I LOG PAR RTOG PA RNAMS LDOG PAR 'GYUR RO,,
gru.wylie: dogs pa'i rgyu mtshan 'di gnyis ka chos nyid la yod kyang bden par grub pa 'gog nus pa mi 'gal ba 'di shes na, don dam bden pa blo gang gis kyang mi rtogs par 'dzin pa'i log par rtog pa rnams ldog par 'gyur ro
gru.english: Both of the reasons why a person might hold some doubts here apply to a real nature of things; but there is no contradiction between them with reference to their ability to deny that things could exist in truth. Once you realize this point, you can stop the wrong idea which questions whether or not ultimate reality is something that any state of mind could ever realize. The emptiness of all things

gru.acip: CHOS DE DAG THAMS CAD NI DE DAG GI NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB PAS DBEN PA'I STONG PA NYID GANG YIN PA 'DI NI, CHOS THAMS CAD KYI STONG PA NYID DO,,
gru.wylie: chos de dag thams cad ni de dag gi ngo bo nyid kyis grub pas dben pa'i stong pa nyid gang yin pa 'di ni, chos thams cad kyi stong pa nyid do
gru.english: Now all of these various existing entities possess an emptiness where they are devoid of existing through any essential nature of their own. This then is the emptiness of all things. The emptiness of its own quality, in brief

gru.acip: GZUGS PHUNG GI MTSAN NYID NI GZUGS SU RUNG BA DANG LA SOGS PAS BSDUS PA RNAM MKHYEN GYI BAR GYI KUN BYANG GI CHOS RNAMS KYI RANG RANG GI MTSAN NYID DNGOS PO STE RANG GI NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB PA MED PA GANG YIN PA DE NI RANG GI MTSAN NYID STONG PA NYID DO,,
gru.wylie: gzugs phung gi mtshan nyid ni gzugs su rung ba dang la sogs pas bsdus pa rnam mkhyen gyi bar gyi kun byang gi chos rnams kyi rang rang gi mtshan nyid dngos po ste rang gi ngo bo nyid kyis grub pa med pa gang yin pa de ni rang gi mtshan nyid stong pa nyid do
gru.english: Here next we consider those things that can be pointed to as being form (which is in fact the definition of “form”), and “all the rest”—which includes all of those entities up to omniscience itself, whether they be on the negative side of things, or the enlightened side of things. These are all things which lack any quality of being “things” in the sense of possessing, each one, their own quality; which is to say, they have no quality of existing through some essential nature of their own. This then is the emptiness of a thing's own quality. Emptiness of own quality related to the original condition

gru.acip: ,GTONG BA SBYIN PA'I PHA ROL PHYIN, ,TSUL KHRIMS GDUNG MED MTSAN NYID BZOD, ,KHRO MED MTSAN NYID BRTZON 'GRUS KYI, ,KHA NA MA THO MED NYID DO,
gru.wylie: gtong ba sbyin pa'i pha rol phyin, ,tshul khrims gdung med mtshan nyid bzod, ,khro med mtshan nyid brtson 'grus kyi, ,kha na ma tho med nyid do
gru.english: The perfection of giving Is giving away. The own quality For the ethical life Is turning away From the torment. The own quality Of patience is An absence of anger; And for joyful effort It is that free Of disreputable actions.

gru.acip: BRTZON 'GRUS KYI MTSAN NYID NI, KHA NA MA THO BA MED PA'I DGE BA YONGS SU 'DZIN PA LA SPRO BA NYID DO,,
gru.wylie: brtson 'grus kyi mtshan nyid ni, kha na ma tho ba med pa'i dge ba yongs su 'dzin pa la spro ba nyid do
gru.english: The own quality of joyful effort is that perfect joy one feels about maintaining ones virtue, free of any disreputable actions.

gru.acip: ,SO SOR YANG DAG RIG RNAMS NI, ,SPOBS SOGS TSAD MED MTSAN NYID CAN, ,'GRO LA PHAN PA NYER SGRUB PA, ,BYAMS PA CHEN PO ZHES BYA'O,
gru.wylie: so sor yang dag rig rnams ni, ,spobs sogs tshad med mtshan nyid can, ,'gro la phan pa nyer sgrub pa, ,byams pa chen po zhes bya'o
gru.english: The perfect understandings Of details—confidence And so on—have an Own nature of being Without any extent; And what we call “Great love” accomplishes Help for living beings.

gru.acip: 'GRO BA RNAMS LA PHAN PA DANG BDE BA NYE BAR SGRUB PA NI, BYAMS PA CHEN PO ZHES BYA BA'I MTSAN NYID DANG, SDUG BSNGAL CAN GYI SEMS CAN RNAMS YONGS SU SKYOB PA NI, THUGS RJE CHEN PO'I MTSAN NYID DO,,
gru.wylie: 'gro ba rnams la phan pa dang bde ba nye bar sgrub pa ni, byams pa chen po zhes bya ba'i mtshan nyid dang, sdug bsngal can gyi sems can rnams yongs su skyob pa ni, thugs rje chen po'i mtshan nyid do
gru.english: And then the own nature of what we call “great love” is that it accomplishes help and happiness for all living beings. And the own nature of great compassion is that it acts to protect, entirely, each & every suffering being.

gru.acip: 'DUN PA DANG BRTZON 'GRUS DANG DRAN PA DANG TING NGE 'DZIN DANG, SHES RAB DANG RNAM PAR GROL BA NYAMS PA MI MNGA' BA NI GNYIS PA'O,,
gru.wylie: 'dun pa dang brtson 'grus dang dran pa dang ting nge 'dzin dang, shes rab dang rnam par grol ba nyams pa mi mnga' ba ni gnyis pa'o
gru.english: The second set of six consists of (7) aspiration, (8) effort, (9) recollection, (10) concentration, (11) wisdom, and (12) liberation which know no decline.

gru.acip: DE LTAR GZUGS NAS RNAM MKHYEN GYI BAR GYI MTSAN NYID RNAMS NI, DE RNAMS MTSON BYED KYI RANG GI NGO BO TZAM YIN PAS, RTAGS KYI DGAG BYA'I RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PA DANG KHYAD PAR SHIN TU CHE'O,,
gru.wylie: de ltar gzugs nas rnam mkhyen gyi bar gyi mtshan nyid rnams ni, de rnams mtshon byed kyi rang gi ngo bo tsam yin pas, rtags kyi dgag bya'i rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub pa dang khyad par shin tu che'o
gru.english: All of these examples of own qualities for things from physical form on up to omniscience itself serve to typify these objects, and give only their essential nature. As such there is a huge difference between these natures and the existence by nature or definition which is what we deny with our reasoning. A summary on emptiness of its own quality

gru.acip: GANG ZHIG 'DUS BYAS KYI CHOS RNAMS KYI MTSAN NYID DANG, 'DUS MA BYAS KYI CHOS RNAMS KYI RANG MTSON BYED KYI MTSAN NYID GANG YIN PA DE RNAMS, DE'I RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA DE KHO NAS STONG PA NYID DE NI RANG GI MTSAN NYID STONG PA NYID DO,,
gru.wylie: gang zhig 'dus byas kyi chos rnams kyi mtshan nyid dang, 'dus ma byas kyi chos rnams kyi rang mtshon byed kyi mtshan nyid gang yin pa de rnams, de'i rang bzhin gyis grub pa de kho nas stong pa nyid de ni rang gi mtshan nyid stong pa nyid do
gru.english: And then let's consider the own nature of those entities which are produced; and the own nature which typifies entities which exist but were not produced. Their emptiness of “that alone”—referring to existing through some nature of their own—is then their emptiness of some own nature. Emptiness of not seeing, and true nature

gru.acip: DE {%DA} LTAR BYUNG BA 'DI RANG GRUB PA'I DUS PHAN CHAD DU MI GNAS SHING, BYUNG ZIN 'DAS PA NI BYUNG BA DE ZHIG PA YIN PA DANG, 'BYUNG 'GYUR MA 'ONGS PA NI 'BYUNG 'GYUR DE DA LTAR MA SKYES PA'I PHYIR, GSUM PO DER YOD PA MA YIN NO,,
gru.wylie: de {%da} ltar byung ba 'di rang grub pa'i dus phan chad du mi gnas shing, byung zin 'das pa ni byung ba de zhig pa yin pa dang, 'byung 'gyur ma 'ongs pa ni 'byung 'gyur de da ltar ma skyes pa'i phyir, gsum po der yod pa ma yin no
gru.english: Now those things which have occurred in the present time do not remain beyond the point at which they have come into being. And things which have already occurred—those in the past time—have already stopped. Things which are yet to occur—those in the future—are still to come, and have not yet come to start in the present. As such, none of these three exist as those.

gru.acip: BYUNG ZIN DANG 'BYUNG 'GYUR DANG DA LTAR BA DE DAG RIM PA BZHIN DU ZHIG PA DANG MA SKYES PA'I DUS GNYIS DANG, RANG GRUB PA'I 'OG GANG DU MI DMIGS PA DE LA NI MI DMIGS PA ZHES BRJOD DO,,
gru.wylie: byung zin dang 'byung 'gyur dang da ltar ba de dag rim pa bzhin du zhig pa dang ma skyes pa'i dus gnyis dang, rang grub pa'i 'og gang du mi dmigs pa de la ni mi dmigs pa zhes brjod do
gru.english: Those things that have already occurred; and those that are yet to occur; and those in the present cannot be observed—respectively—in any of the two times of either what has already stopped or what is yet to start; nor subsequent to their having occurred. As such, we refer to them as “unseen.”

gru.acip: MI DMIGS PA DE RANG GI NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB PA DE YIS DBEN PA NYID GANG YIN PA DE NI, THER ZUG TU GNAS PA MIN PA DANG, 'JIG PA MIN PAS NA MI DMIGS PA ZHES BYA BA'I STONG PA NYID DO,
gru.wylie: mi dmigs pa de rang gi ngo bo nyid kyis grub pa de yis dben pa nyid gang yin pa de ni, ther zug tu gnas pa min pa dang, 'jig pa min pas na mi dmigs pa zhes bya ba'i stong pa nyid do
gru.english: Consider then this state of being unseen; the fact that it does not exist through any pure, essential nature of its own: the fact that it is entirely devoid of existing in that way. This is not something that can remain in some solid manner, nor is it something which stops. As such, it is the emptiness, we say, of “not seeing anything.” 16) The emptiness of true nature, beyond all things

gru.acip: RGYU DANG RKYEN LAS BYUNG BA'I PHYIR NA, DNGOS PO RNAMS LA 'DUS PA PA STE RGYU RKYEN 'DUS PA LAS BYUNG BA'I NGO BO RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA MED PAS, DE RNAMS LA DNGOS PO MED PA ZHES BYA LA,
gru.wylie: rgyu dang rkyen las byung ba'i phyir na, dngos po rnams la 'dus pa pa ste rgyu rkyen 'dus pa las byung ba'i ngo bo rang bzhin gyis grub pa med pas, de rnams la dngos po med pa zhes bya la
gru.english: We refer to functional entities as “brought together,” because they are something which occurs through causes & conditions. That is, they possess an essential nature of having occurred through the convening of causes & conditions. And since this essence has no existence as something that could exist through some nature of its own, we refer to these as “beyond all things.”

gru.acip: 'DUS PA LAS BYUNG BA DE NYID KYI NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB PAS STONG PA NYID NI, DNGOS PO MED PA'I NGO BO NYID KYI STONG PA NYID DO,,
gru.wylie: 'dus pa las byung ba de nyid kyi ngo bo nyid kyis grub pas stong pa nyid ni, dngos po med pa'i ngo bo nyid kyi stong pa nyid do
gru.english: And the fact that these same things which have occurred through that convening are empty of existing through any perfect, essential nature of their own is what we refer to as “the emptiness of any perfect essential nature, beyond all things.”

gru.acip: DE LTAR BCU DRUG TU BSHAD PA NI BDEN GRUB 'GOG PA'I RIGS PA MI 'DRA BA'I SGO NAS NI MIN TE, THAMS CAD LA YANG THER ZUG TU GNAS PA DANG 'JIG PA MED PA'I RIGS PAS BSGRUBS PA'I PHYIR RO,,
gru.wylie: de ltar bcu drug tu bshad pa ni bden grub 'gog pa'i rigs pa mi 'dra ba'i sgo nas ni min te, thams cad la yang ther zug tu gnas pa dang 'jig pa med pa'i rigs pas bsgrubs pa'i phyir ro
gru.english: The explanation that we make this way, into sixteen different types, is not something that is accomplished through different types of reasoning which denies that things could exist as real. And that's because every single one of them is proven through the logic which shows that things cannot stay in any solid way; nor can they stop.

gru.acip: GANG ZAG GCIG LA SPYIR BDEN MED DU SGRUB PA YANG MIN TE, GZHI MIG SOGS NANG GI CHOS RNAMS KYI STENG DU BDEN MED TSAD MAS GRUB NA GZHI GZHAN LA BLO KHA PHYOGS PA'I TSE, GZHAN GYIS SGRUB BYED BKOD PA LA MI LTOS PAR RANG GIS RTAGS LA BRTEN NAS THE TSOM CHOD PAR 'GYUR BA'I PHYIR RO,,
gru.wylie: gang zag gcig la spyir bden med du sgrub pa yang min te, gzhi mig sogs nang gi chos rnams kyi steng du bden med tshad mas grub na gzhi gzhan la blo kha phyogs pa'i tshe, gzhan gyis sgrub byed bkod pa la mi ltos par rang gis rtags la brten nas the tshom chod par 'gyur ba'i phyir ro
gru.english: Nor is it the case that with a single individual we can establish that—in general—things have no real existence. If we establish, with an accurate perception, the fact that nothing is real with regard to a particular locus—such as the inner entities of the eye and so on—then when we turn our minds to some other locus we are able to eliminate any doubts we may have had, based on the reason we used ourselves, and without relying upon any proof set forth by others.

gru.acip: PHUNG PO LNGA PO DE RNAMS DE YI RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAS STONG PA NYID GANG YIN PA DE NI, DNGOS PO STONG PA NYID DU MDOR BSHAD DO,,
gru.wylie: phung po lnga po de rnams de yi rang bzhin gyis grub pas stong pa nyid gang yin pa de ni, dngos po stong pa nyid du mdor bshad do
gru.english: And then that fact that these five parts to the person are empty of existing through any nature of their own is, in brief, what we refer to as “the emptiness of things.”

gru.acip: 'DUS MA BYAS DE NYID DNGOS POR MED PA DE'I RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAS STONG PA NYID NI, DNGOS PO MED PA STONG PA NYID DO ZHES BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: 'dus ma byas de nyid dngos por med pa de'i rang bzhin gyis grub pas stong pa nyid ni, dngos po med pa stong pa nyid do zhes bya'o
gru.english: And then when we speak of the fact that these same unproduced, existent phenomena—these absences of things—are empty of existing through any nature of their own, that is what we call “the emptiness of the lack of things.”

gru.acip: RANG BZHIN CHOS NYID DE RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA MED PA NI RANG BZHIN STONG PA NYID DO ZHES BYA BAR BSNYAD DO,,
gru.wylie: rang bzhin chos nyid de rang bzhin gyis grub pa med pa ni rang bzhin stong pa nyid do zhes bya bar bsnyad do
gru.english: This nature or way of all things is an absence of things existing through any nature of their own; as such, we give it the name of “the emptiness of any nature.”

gru.acip: BSHAD PA PHYI MA GNYIS RGYAS 'BRING GNYIS KA'I SKABS SU YANG YANG 'BYUNG BA NI, CHOS NYID DE DNGOS PO'I GSHIS YIN PA DANG, RTAG TU YOD PA DANG, MI RTOG YE SHES KYI GZHAL BYAR YOD PAR KHAS LEN NA BDEN PAR GRUB BO SNYAM PA'I DOGS PA GCAD PA'I DON YIN PAS DE RNAMS MI 'GAL BAR SHES PAR BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: bshad pa phyi ma gnyis rgyas 'bring gnyis ka'i skabs su yang yang 'byung ba ni, chos nyid de dngos po'i gshis yin pa dang, rtag tu yod pa dang, mi rtog ye shes kyi gzhal byar yod par khas len na bden par grub bo snyam pa'i dogs pa gcad pa'i don yin pas de rnams mi 'gal bar shes par bya'o
gru.english: Now why do the latter two explanations occur over & over again in the context of both the more extensive and the middling versions? This is because we accept that the true nature of things is their original nature; and that it exists for all time; and that it exists as that object which the wisdom beyond any mistaken perception holds under its consideration. As such, the intent here is to prevent any mistaken idea where people think that perhaps it exists in truth. You should understand then that we have no contradiction here.

gru.acip: THABS MKHAS KYI PHAR PHYIN DU 'JOG PA'I THABS LA MKHAS PA NI BYANG SA LAS, DRUG TSAN GNYIS GSUNGS PA'I DANG PO NANG GI SANGS RGYAS KYI CHOS 'GRUB PA LAS BRTZAMS PA'I THABS MKHAS PA DRUG NI,
gru.wylie: thabs mkhas kyi phar phyin du 'jog pa'i thabs la mkhas pa ni byang sa las, drug tshan gnyis gsungs pa'i dang po nang gi sangs rgyas kyi chos 'grub pa las brtsams pa'i thabs mkhas pa drug ni
gru.english: The kind of skillful means which we establish as the perfection of skillful means is described in Levels of the Bodhisattva. Here we find described two sets of six. The first set is composed of the six forms of skillful means which start off from ones inner practice of the teachings of the Buddha.

gru.acip: BYANG SEMS KYIS SEMS CAN THAMS CAD LA SNYING RJE DANG LDAN PAR LTA BA DANG, 'DU BYED THAMS CAD KYI RANG BZHIN YANG DAG PA JI LTA BA BZHIN DU SHES PA DANG, BLA NA MED PA'I BYANG CHUB KYI YE SHES 'DOD PA DANG, SEMS CAN LA LTA BA LA BRTEN NAS 'KHOR BA MI GTONG BA DANG, 'DU BYED JI LTA BA BZHIN SHES PA LA BRTEN NAS NYON MONGS PA CAN MA YIN PA'I SEMS KYIS 'KHOR BAR 'KHOR BA DANG, SANGS RGYAS 'DOD PA LA BRTEN NAS BRTZON 'GRUS 'BAR BA'O,,
gru.wylie: byang sems kyis sems can thams cad la snying rje dang ldan par lta ba dang, 'du byed thams cad kyi rang bzhin yang dag pa ji lta ba bzhin du shes pa dang, bla na med pa'i byang chub kyi ye shes 'dod pa dang, sems can la lta ba la brten nas 'khor ba mi gtong ba dang, 'du byed ji lta ba bzhin shes pa la brten nas nyon mongs pa can ma yin pa'i sems kyis 'khor bar 'khor ba dang, sangs rgyas 'dod pa la brten nas brtson 'grus 'bar ba'o
gru.english: Here we have— (1) The way that bodhisattvas view each and every living being with compassion; (2) The way in which they comprehend the nature of all factors as pure, exactly as it is; (3) The way in which they aspire to the wisdom of matchless enlightenment; (4) The way in which they refuse to abandon the circle of suffering, so far as how they look upon living beings; (5) The way in which they circle in the circle of suffering, with a mind that is free of negative emotions, all depending upon their understanding of the way that factors really are; and (6) The way in which they set on fire the efforts they make, all due to their yearning towards enlightenment.

gru.acip: BYANG SEMS RNAMS KYIS SEMS CAN GYI DGE BA'I RTZA BA CHUNG NGU RNAMS 'BRAS BU TSAD MED PAR SGYUR BAR BYED PA DANG, DE BZHIN DU TSOGS CHUNG NGUS DGE RTZA CHE BA DAG SGRUB PAR BYED PA DANG, BSTAN PA LA ZHE 'GRAS PA RNAMS KYI KHONG KHRO SEL BAR BYED PA DANG, BSTAN PA LA YID BAR MAR GNAS PA RNAMS DE LA 'DZUD PA DANG, ZHUGS PA RNAMS SMIN PAR BYED PA DANG, SMIN PA RNAMS GROL BAR BYED PA STE
gru.wylie: byang sems rnams kyis sems can gyi dge ba'i rtsa ba chung ngu rnams 'bras bu tshad med par sgyur bar byed pa dang, de bzhin du tshogs chung ngus dge rtsa che ba dag sgrub par byed pa dang, bstan pa la zhe 'gras pa rnams kyi khong khro sel bar byed pa dang, bstan pa la yid bar mar gnas pa rnams de la 'dzud pa dang, zhugs pa rnams smin par byed pa dang, smin pa rnams grol bar byed pa ste
gru.english: These six then are the following: (7) The way in which bodhisattvas take the more minor roots of virtue which living beings possess, and transform them into limitless results; and, just so, (8) The way they act to accomplish massive roots of virtue out of minor collections of goodness; (9) The way in which they manage to clear away the anger of those who feel some hatred towards the teachings; (10) The way they induce those who are feeling divided about the teachings to enter those teachings; (11) The way they act to ripen those who have already entered the teachings; and (12) They way they act to liberate those who are ripened.

gru.acip: SA BCU PA LAS, KYE RGYAL BA'I SRAS 'DI LTA STE, DPER NA RGYA MTSO CHEN POR 'GRO BA'I GRU BO CHE NI, RGYA MTSO CHEN PO LA MA THUG GI BAR DU CHED DU BSKYOD CING 'GRO BAR BYA BA YIN TE, GANG GI TSE RGYA MTSO CHEN PO LA PHYIN MA THAG TU RLUNG GI DKYIL 'KHOR GYIS BSKYOD NAS, CHED DU BSKYOD MI DGOS PAR 'GRO STE, DES RGYA MTSO CHEN PO LA NYIN GCIG CHOD PA DE NI SNGON CHED DU BSKYOD CING 'GRO BAS, LO BRGYAR YANG DE SRID DU TSAD MED PAR PHYIN PAR MI NUS SO,,
gru.wylie: sa bcu pa las, kye rgyal ba'i sras 'di lta ste, dper na rgya mtsho chen por 'gro ba'i gru bo che ni, rgya mtsho chen po la ma thug gi bar du ched du bskyod cing 'gro bar bya ba yin te, gang gi tshe rgya mtsho chen po la phyin ma thag tu rlung gi dkyil 'khor gyis bskyod nas, ched du bskyod mi dgos par 'gro ste, des rgya mtsho chen po la nyin gcig chod pa de ni sngon ched du bskyod cing 'gro bas, lo brgyar yang de srid du tshad med par phyin par mi nus so
gru.english: The Sutra on the Ten Levels puts it this way: O child of the Victors, this is the way it is. Think for example of a great ship bound for the great sea. It continues its journey with purpose, moving on until it reaches this massive body of water. And then suppose that, just after it has reached that greater sea, it is struck by a hurricane. No longer do the sailors have to make any conscious effort to advance the ship; it moves across the great sea making more progress in a single day than it had made in all their sailing up to that point. Not even in a hundred years would they have been able to move that far, beyond all limits.

whole_word_matches.context: ras 'di lta ste, dper na rgya mtsho chen por 'gro ba'i gru bo che ni, rgya mtsho chen po la ma thug gi bar du che

gru.acip: KYE RGYAL BA'I SRAS DE BZHIN DU BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA' DGE BA'I RTZA BA'I TSOGS SHIN TU BSAGS PA, THEG PA CHEN PO YANG DAG PAR BSGRUB PA YANG, BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA'I SPYOD PA'I RGYA MTSOR PHYIN NAS LHUN GYIS GRUB PA'I YE SHES KYIS YUD TZAM ZHIG LA, THAMS CAD MKHYEN PA'I YE SHES JI TZAM GNON PA DE NI, SNGON GYI CHED DU BYA BA'I LAS KYIS BSKAL PA 'BUM DU YANG, DE SNYED DU DPAG TU MED PA GNON PAR MI NUS SO, ZHES GSUNGS PA LTA BU'O,,
gru.wylie: kye rgyal ba'i sras de bzhin du byang chub sems dpa' dge ba'i rtsa ba'i tshogs shin tu bsags pa, theg pa chen po yang dag par bsgrub pa yang, byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa'i rgya mtshor phyin nas lhun gyis grub pa'i ye shes kyis yud tsam zhig la, thams cad mkhyen pa'i ye shes ji tsam gnon pa de ni, sngon gyi ched du bya ba'i las kyis bskal pa 'bum du yang, de snyed du dpag tu med pa gnon par mi nus so, zhes gsungs pa lta bu'o
gru.english: And it is the same, o monks, with those bodhisattvas who have made a massive collection of the roots of virtue, and who have practiced the greater way perfectly. Once they have come to the ocean of the deeds of the bodhisattvas, then spontaneous wisdom starts to have its effect on them, in even but a single moment, during which they are set upon by the wisdom of omniscience. And they reach a place that they had never arrived at, even after a hundred thousand eons of concerted effort. They could never have reached this place even with countless periods of trying, for that same amount of time.

gru.acip: SA BCU PA LAS, KYE RGYAL BA'I SRAS DAG DE LTAR BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA'I SA MI G-YO BA 'DI LA GNAS PA'I BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA' SNGON GYI SMON LAM GYI STOBS BSKYED PA DANG, CHOS KYI SGO'I RGYUN DE LA GNAS PA DE LA SANGS RGYAS BCOM LDAN 'DAS RNAMS DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA'I YE SHES NYE BAR SGRUB PAR MDZAD DE, DE LA 'DI SKAD CES KYANG BKA' STZAL TO,,
gru.wylie: sa bcu pa las, kye rgyal ba'i sras dag de ltar byang chub sems dpa'i sa mi g-yo ba 'di la gnas pa'i byang chub sems dpa' sngon gyi smon lam gyi stobs bskyed pa dang, chos kyi sgo'i rgyun de la gnas pa de la sangs rgyas bcom ldan 'das rnams de bzhin gshegs pa'i ye shes nye bar sgrub par mdzad de, de la 'di skad ces kyang bka' stsal to
gru.english: The Sutra on the Ten Levels puts it this way: Consider again, o children of the Victors, those bodhisattvas who are situated in this way, at the bodhisattva level known as “Unmoving.” They raise the force of the prayers they had made earlier, and remain there in the flow of the entrance of the Dharma. And then they go further and come to achieving the wisdom of the Buddhas, the Conquerors—those who have Gone That Way. And then they are spoken to, in the following high words.

gru.acip: 'ON KYANG RIGS KYI BU GANG NGED KYI STOBS BCU DANG, MI 'JIGS PA BZHI LA SOGS PA SANGS RGYAS KYI CHOS MA 'DRES PA PHUN SUM TSOGS PA DE KHYOD LA MED KYI, SANGS RGYAS KYI CHOS PHUN SUM TSOGS PA DE YONGS SU BTZAL BA'I PHYIR SBYOR BA BYOS SHIG ,BRTZON 'GRUS RTZOMS SHIG ,BZOD PA'I SGO 'DI NYID KYANG MA 'DOR CIG
gru.wylie: 'on kyang rigs kyi bu gang nged kyi stobs bcu dang, mi 'jigs pa bzhi la sogs pa sangs rgyas kyi chos ma 'dres pa phun sum tshogs pa de khyod la med kyi, sangs rgyas kyi chos phun sum tshogs pa de yongs su btsal ba'i phyir sbyor ba byos shig ,brtson 'grus rtsoms shig ,bzod pa'i sgo 'di nyid kyang ma 'dor cig
gru.english: And yet, o child of noble family, as yet you still do not possess the ten forces that I possess, and my four types of fearlessness, and all the other of the excellent, unadmixed qualities of a Buddha. As such, I urge you now to apply yourself in the pursuit of the totally excellent qualities of an Enlightened Being. Gird yourself in your efforts. And never abandon this particular doorway of forbearance.

gru.acip: GAL TE SANGS RGYAS BCOM LDAN 'DAS DE DAG GIS BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA' DE LA THAMS CAD MKHYEN PA'I YE SHES MNGON PAR SGRUB PA'I SGO RNAMS SU GZHUG PA MA MDZAD DU ZIN NA, DE DE NYID KYI TSE YONGS SU MYA NGAN LAS 'DA' BAR 'GYUR TE, SEMS CAN THAMS CAD KYI DON BYA BA YANG RGYUN CHAD PAR 'GYUR RO, ZHES GSUNGS SO,,
gru.wylie: gal te sangs rgyas bcom ldan 'das de dag gis byang chub sems dpa' de la thams cad mkhyen pa'i ye shes mngon par sgrub pa'i sgo rnams su gzhug pa ma mdzad du zin na, de de nyid kyi tshe yongs su mya ngan las 'da' bar 'gyur te, sems can thams cad kyi don bya ba yang rgyun chad par 'gyur ro, zhes gsungs so
gru.english: And then we have— If it were the case that the Buddhas, the Conquerors, were to fail to set the bodhisattva to entering the doorways where they could finally achieve the wisdom of omniscience, then at that very point they would instead pass into nirvana. And then the flow of their efforts to accomplish the needs of every living being would be cut off.

gru.acip: ,BCU PA'I SA LA DE YIS KUN NAS SANGS RGYAS RNAMS LAS DBANG BSKUR BA, ,DAM PA 'THOB CING YE SHES LHAG PAR MCHOG TU BYUNG BAR GYUR PA'ANG YIN, ,CHAR SPRIN RNAMS LAS CHU CHAR 'BAB PA JI LTAR DE BZHIN 'GRO RNAMS KYI, ,DGE BA'I LO TOG CHED DU RGYAL SRAS LAS KYANG LHUN GRUB CHOS CHAR 'BAB,
gru.wylie: bcu pa'i sa la de yis kun nas sangs rgyas rnams las dbang bskur ba, ,dam pa 'thob cing ye shes lhag par mchog tu byung bar gyur pa'ang yin, ,char sprin rnams las chu char 'bab pa ji ltar de bzhin 'gro rnams kyi, ,dge ba'i lo tog ched du rgyal sras las kyang lhun grub chos char 'bab
gru.english: At the tenth level, This one receives The highest investment Into power, From all the Buddhas Of every corner. High knowledge Also reaches Its highest expression. The rains Are sent down From the rainclouds; Just so, the Children of the Victors Also let the rain Fall, spontaneously, For the crops Of virtue among Living beings.

gru.acip: DE BZHIN DU, GDUL BYA'I 'GRO BA RNAMS KYI DGE BA'I LO TOG SPEL BA'I CHED DU, RGYAL SRAS SA BCU PA BA 'DI LAS KYANG LHUN GYIS GRUB PAR DAM PA'I CHOS KYI CHAR MNGON PAR 'BAB PA STE 'BEBS SO,,
gru.wylie: de bzhin du, gdul bya'i 'gro ba rnams kyi dge ba'i lo tog spel ba'i ched du, rgyal sras sa bcu pa ba 'di las kyang lhun gyis grub par dam pa'i chos kyi char mngon par 'bab pa ste 'bebs so
gru.english: Just so, the children of the Victors residing here at the tenth bodhisattva level also “let the rain fall”; they drop down, generously, and spontaneously, the rain of the holy Dharma. And this is all for the purpose of multiplying the crops of virtue among those living beings who are their disciples.

gru.acip: ,'DI DAG RNAMS LA BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA' YIS NI 'BUM PHRAG DANG, ,BYE BA PHRAG BRGYA 'THOB CING DE YIS BYE BA STONG 'GYUR 'THOB, ,DE NAS BYE BA BRGYA PHRAG STONG [216a] 'GYUR YANG 'THOB BYE BA PHRAG ,KHRAG KHRIG PHRAG BRGYAR RDZOGS PAR BSGRUB DANG SLAR YANG STONG PHRAG TU, ,YANG DAG PAR NI BSGYUR BA MTHA' DAG RAB TU 'THOB PAR 'GYUR,
gru.wylie: 'di dag rnams la byang chub sems dpa' yis ni 'bum phrag dang, ,bye ba phrag brgya 'thob cing de yis bye ba stong 'gyur 'thob, ,de nas bye ba brgya phrag stong [216a] 'gyur yang 'thob bye ba phrag ,khrag khrig phrag brgyar rdzogs par bsgrub dang slar yang stong phrag tu, ,yang dag par ni bsgyur ba mtha' dag rab tu 'thob par 'gyur
gru.english: At five different Levels, these come To be completed In groups attained of A hundred thousand; A billion; ten billion; A trillion; and a Hundred quintillion. And then once more Everything is multiplied, By another thousand, For a grand total [f. 216a].

gru.acip: DE BZHIN GSHEGS PAS GDUL BA'I SEMS CAN RNAMS LA BRGYA BYIN LA SOGS PA'I GZUGS BZUNG NAS LHUN GYIS GRUB PAR CHOS STON PAR NUS SO, ZHES BYA BA LA SOGS PA'I BAR GYI DON SDUD PA'O,,
gru.wylie: de bzhin gshegs pas gdul ba'i sems can rnams la brgya byin la sogs pa'i gzugs bzung nas lhun gyis grub par chos ston par nus so, zhes bya ba la sogs pa'i bar gyi don sdud pa'o
gru.english: The Ones Thus Gone are able to teach the Dharma spontaneously, by taking on for those living beings they seek to tame the form of Destroyer of the Hundred Cities, or whatever it might be.

gru.acip: GNYIS PA 'BRAS BU'I SA LA LNGA, DANG POR SANGS RGYAS PA'I TSUL, SKU DANG YON TAN GYI RNAM GZHAG ,SPRUL PA'I SKU BSTAN PA, THEG PA GCIG TU BSGRUB PA, MNGON PAR BYANG CHUB PA DANG BZHUGS PA'I DUS KYI BSHAD PA'O,,
gru.wylie: gnyis pa 'bras bu'i sa la lnga, dang por sangs rgyas pa'i tshul, sku dang yon tan gyi rnam gzhag ,sprul pa'i sku bstan pa, theg pa gcig tu bsgrub pa, mngon par byang chub pa dang bzhugs pa'i dus kyi bshad pa'o
gru.english: This brings us far back, to a second section promised, for a presentation on those levels which consist of the result. Here we proceed in five steps: (1) the way in which we first reach our enlightenment; (2) a description of the holy body, and the fine qualities, that we then achieve; (3) a presentation concerning our emanation body; (4) a proof that in the end it is all a single path; and (5) an explanation of the point at which we have become enlightened, and remain there.

gru.acip: DE DAG TU GTOGS PA DE RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA'I SKYE BA MED PA'I DE KHO NA NYID LA, DNGOS POS BYAS PA'I DBYE BA 'GA' YANG MED PA DE'I PHYIR DE KHO NA NYID NI RO MNYAM PA STE RO GCIG KHO NAR SHES PAR BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: de dag tu gtogs pa de rang bzhin gyis grub pa'i skye ba med pa'i de kho na nyid la, dngos pos byas pa'i dbye ba 'ga' yang med pa de'i phyir de kho na nyid ni ro mnyam pa ste ro gcig kho nar shes par bya'o
gru.english: If though we consider the suchness of these objects—the fact that they are devoid of anything included into them which could exist through any nature of its own—we can say that there are no distinctions at all here that were engendered by any functional entities. And thus it is that you should understand that, with suchness, everything “tastes the same,” meaning that it is all but a single song.

gru.acip: JI LTAR 'TSAM PAR SEMS CAN GYI DON SGRUB PA LHUR MDZAD CING, CHOS KYI DBYINGS LAS SKAD CIG KYANG MI BSKYOD LA, SEMS CAN GDUL BA'I DUS LAS KYANG MI 'DA' BA DE 'DRA BAR BDAG KYANG GYUR CIG ,CES PA'O,,
gru.wylie: ji ltar 'tsham par sems can gyi don sgrub pa lhur mdzad cing, chos kyi dbyings las skad cig kyang mi bskyod la, sems can gdul ba'i dus las kyang mi 'da' ba de 'dra bar bdag kyang gyur cig ,ces pa'o
gru.english: In these prayers, we have said to ourselves: There are those who are able, spontaneously, to serve the needs of all living beings, in just the right way. And at the same time, they never budge from the realm of all things, even for a moment. Moreover, they never shift out of that period during which they are working to tame living beings. May I too become like them!

gru.acip: DE LTAR RNAM PAR MI RTOG PA YIN YANG SEMS CAN GYI DON MDZAD PAR NUS PA GSAL BAR BYED PA NI, DPAG BSAM GYI SHING LTA BU DANG, YID BZHIN GYI NOR BU JI BZHIN DU RNAM PAR MI RTOG PAR GDUL BYA'I 'DOD PA'I DON SGRUB PA'I RGYU NYID DU 'GYUR RO,,
gru.wylie: de ltar rnam par mi rtog pa yin yang sems can gyi don mdzad par nus pa gsal bar byed pa ni, dpag bsam gyi shing lta bu dang, yid bzhin gyi nor bu ji bzhin du rnam par mi rtog par gdul bya'i 'dod pa'i don sgrub pa'i rgyu nyid du 'gyur ro
gru.english: This holy body never entertains any normal kinds of thoughts; but still we make it crystal-clear that it is still capable of working for the good of beings. What happens is that this body acts as a perfect cause for achieving all the goals that disciples may wish for, in a way that resembles a tree which grants our every wish; or which is comparable to a wish-giving jewel. Which is to say, there is no normal thinking process involved. [afterword.18b] Sanskrit unavailable

gru.acip: ,ME LONG SHIN TU DAG PA LA GZUGS BRNYAN LTAR DUS GCIG KHO NAR LHUN GYIS GRUB PAR STON PAR MDZAD DO,,
gru.wylie: me long shin tu dag pa la gzugs brnyan ltar dus gcig kho nar lhun gyis grub par ston par mdzad do
gru.english: And these forms are, moreover, displayed spontaneously, and all at the same time—like reflections in some perfectly clear mirror. [afterword.20] Sanskrit unavailable

gru.acip: DE BZHIN DU, TSUL KHRIMS DANG BZOD PA DANG, BRTZON 'GRUS DANG BSAM GTAN GYI TING NGE 'DZIN DANG, SHES RAB KYI PHAR PHYIN LA
gru.wylie: de bzhin du, tshul khrims dang bzod pa dang, brtson 'grus dang bsam gtan gyi ting nge 'dzin dang, shes rab kyi phar phyin la
gru.english: And then, in the very same way, they undertake to practice the perfection of an ethical lifestyle, and then the perfections of patience; joyful effort; single-pointed focus in the form of meditation; and wisdom.

gru.acip: DE LTAR BSHAD PA LAS BZLOG PA NI GNAS MIN PA ZHES BYA STE, DPER NA DGE BA LAS RNAM SMIN YID DU MI 'ONG BA 'BYUNG BA DANG, MTHONG LAM THOB PAS LAS DBANG GIS SRID PA BRGYAD PA 'GRUB PA NI GNAS MA YIN ZHING GO SKABS MED PA LTA BU'O,,
gru.wylie: de ltar bshad pa las bzlog pa ni gnas min pa zhes bya ste, dper na dge ba las rnam smin yid du mi 'ong ba 'byung ba dang, mthong lam thob pas las dbang gis srid pa brgyad pa 'grub pa ni gnas ma yin zhing go skabs med pa lta bu'o
gru.english: Anything that could happen in the opposite way from what we have described here then would be called what is “not actual.” For example, it would not be actual (there would be no chance of it) if a virtuous action led to an unpleasant ripening; or if an individual had attained the path of seeing and then—due to the power of karma—were to experience an eighth rebirth afterwards.

gru.acip: ,KUN TU RTOG SOGS CHES RNO NYID NI MCHOG BZHED LA, ,'BRING GNAS SKABS DANG RTUL NYID MCHOG MIN PAR BSHAD DANG, ,MIG LA SOGS DANG PHAN TSUN SGRUB NUS CHUD PA LA, ,RNAM PA THAMS CAD MKHYEN PA CHAGS MED STOBS SU GSUNGS,
gru.wylie: kun tu rtog sogs ches rno nyid ni mchog bzhed la, ,'bring gnas skabs dang rtul nyid mchog min par bshad dang, ,mig la sogs dang phan tshun sgrub nus chud pa la, ,rnam pa thams cad mkhyen pa chags med stobs su gsungs
gru.english: There is that State of imagination Which is not correct, And so on— What we assert To be supreme, In a particularly Sharp form. And then there are What we refer to As “not supreme”: Only middling, Or quite dull. There are the Eye and the rest, And the way these Inform, or have The power to Complete, each other. Omniscience has No density Towards them; This was spoken To be the force.

gru.acip: MIG LA SOGS PA'I DBANG PO NYER GNYIS DANG, DBANG PO RNAMS KYI PHAN TSUN 'BRAS BU CHUB PA STE SGRUB NUS PA'I RANG GI NGO BO RE RE LA RNAM PA THAMS CAD MKHYEN PA'I CHAGS PA STE THOGS PA MED PA DE NI, DBANG PO MCHOG DANG MCHOG MA YIN PA MKHYEN PA'I STOBS SU GSUNGS SO,,
gru.wylie: mig la sogs pa'i dbang po nyer gnyis dang, dbang po rnams kyi phan tshun 'bras bu chub pa ste sgrub nus pa'i rang gi ngo bo re re la rnam pa thams cad mkhyen pa'i chags pa ste thogs pa med pa de ni, dbang po mchog dang mchog ma yin pa mkhyen pa'i stobs su gsungs so
gru.english: And then consider the 22 powers of the eye and the rest; and then the way that these powers “inform” each other, or have the power to complete each other. Omniscience in the form of knowing the very essence of each of these has no “density” towards them here—meaning, it penetrates with the least obstruction. This then is what was spoken to be the force of knowing both those capacities which are supreme, and those which are not. The five beginning with knowing the paths

gru.acip: ,DE PHYIR BDAG 'DRAS KHYOD YON 'DI DAG CI, ,SHES PA DANG NI BRJOD PAR NUS 'GYUR RAM, ,'ON KYANG DE DAG 'PHAGS PA KLU SGRUB KYIS, ,BSHAD PHYIR DOGS SPANGS CUNG ZHIG TZAM ZHIG SMRAS,
gru.wylie: de phyir bdag 'dras khyod yon 'di dag ci, ,shes pa dang ni brjod par nus 'gyur ram, ,'on kyang de dag 'phags pa klu sgrub kyis, ,bshad phyir dogs spangs cung zhig tsam zhig smras
gru.english: Thus how could Someone like me Ever be able To understand, And then to express, These high qualities That you possess? Nonetheless, I have thrown aside Any doubts, And boldly offered Just the barest list, Because those Have been described By The Arya, Nagarjuna.

gru.acip: YON TAN DE DAG 'PHAGS PA KLU SGRUB KYIS BSHAD PA'I PHYIR TE DE LA BRTEN NAS YIN NO,,
gru.wylie: yon tan de dag 'phags pa klu sgrub kyis bshad pa'i phyir te de la brten nas yin no
gru.english: And I have been able to do so only because those qualities have been described by The Arya, Nagarjuna; and I have relied upon that description here. Benefits of understanding the qualities

gru.acip: DA NI SPRUL PA'I SKU NYAN RANG DANG BYANG SEMS RNAMS KYI DON DANG THABS THUN MONG BA 'BYUNG ZHING, SO SKYE RNAMS KYI DON YANG CI RIGS PAR 'BYUNG BA, BDE 'GRO LA SOGS PA'I SGRUB BYED DU GYUR PA'I DBANG DU BYAS NAS BSHAD PA,
gru.wylie: da ni sprul pa'i sku nyan rang dang byang sems rnams kyi don dang thabs thun mong ba 'byung zhing, so skye rnams kyi don yang ci rigs par 'byung ba, bde 'gro la sogs pa'i sgrub byed du gyur pa'i dbang du byas nas bshad pa
gru.english: That is, the next section here is meant to address the holy emanation body, from which are derived the goals of both the listeners & self-made buddhas, and the bodhisattvas—providing spiritual methods for both together. From here are derived the goals of the common beings as well; with this form aiding us in our quest for a higher rebirth, and the like. [afterword.44] Sanskrit unavailable

gru.acip: GANG GI PHYIR SNGON BYANG SEMS KYI DUS SU BDAG GIS SEMS CAN THAMS CAD DGROL BAR BYA'O ZHES KHYOD KYIS ZHAL GYIS BZHES PA DE NYID THABS KYI RNAM PA GZHAN GYIS NGES PAR BSGRUB DGOS SO,,
gru.wylie: gang gi phyir sngon byang sems kyi dus su bdag gis sems can thams cad dgrol bar bya'o zhes khyod kyis zhal gyis bzhes pa de nyid thabs kyi rnam pa gzhan gyis nges par bsgrub dgos so
gru.english: And further the fact is that—in times before, when you were simple bodhisattvas—you made a certain commitment: you said, “I will liberate each and every living being.” And then just such a commitment had to be accomplished by means of yet another kind. [afterword.47] Sanskrit unavailable

gru.acip: THEG PA GCIG TU SGRUB PA 'DI MDO KUN LAS BTUS PA LAS, THEG PA GCIG TU ZAD PAR NI MDO SDE DU MA LAS GSUNGS PA'I PHYIR RO, ZHES SOGS KYIS GSUNGS PA LAS SHES PAR BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: theg pa gcig tu sgrub pa 'di mdo kun las btus pa las, theg pa gcig tu zad par ni mdo sde du ma las gsungs pa'i phyir ro, zhes sogs kyis gsungs pa las shes par bya'o
gru.english: The fact that the ways can be proven as one is something that we can understand from sources such as the Compendium of the Sutras, where it says, “We can understand this from the fact that many different sutras describe how, in the end, there is indeed but a single way.” The point of enlightenment

gru.acip: GANG GIS SEMS CAN THAMS CAD KYI DON BSGRUB PAR BYA BA'I PHYIR DU MU MTHA' MED PAR SEMS CAN 'DI DAG GSO BAR BYED PA SANGS RGYAS RNAMS KYI THUGS RJE DE JI 'DRA BA ZHIG CE NA,
gru.wylie: gang gis sems can thams cad kyi don bsgrub par bya ba'i phyir du mu mtha' med par sems can 'di dag gso bar byed pa sangs rgyas rnams kyi thugs rje de ji 'dra ba zhig ce na
gru.english: One may come then with the following question: Can you describe the compassion of the Enlightened Ones, who—in order to bring about the goals of each & every living being—sustain these beings endlessly? [afterword.50] Sanskrit unavailable

gru.acip: MGON PO KLU SGRUB KYI DGONGS PA PHYIN CI MA LOG PAR 'GREL PA'I LUGS 'DI DGE SLONG DPAL LDAN ZLA GRAGS KYIS, DBU MA'I BSTAN BCOS RTZA BA SHES RAB SOGS LAS BTUS NAS,
gru.wylie: mgon po klu sgrub kyi dgongs pa phyin ci ma log par 'grel pa'i lugs 'di dge slong dpal ldan zla grags kyis, dbu ma'i bstan bcos rtsa ba shes rab sogs las btus nas
gru.english: And so this presentation, which comments unerringly upon the true intent of our Savior, Nagarjuna, has been related by a Buddhist monk known as the glorious Chandrakirti. My explanation has proceeded from the Root Text on Wisdom—that classical commentary of the middle way.

gru.acip: NGES DON GYI MDO SDE RNAMS LUNG JI LTA BA BZHIN DANG, 'PHAGS PA KLU SGRUB KYI MAN NGAG NI JI LTA BA BZHIN DU BRJOD PA YIN NO,,
gru.wylie: nges don gyi mdo sde rnams lung ji lta ba bzhin dang, 'phags pa klu sgrub kyi man ngag ni ji lta ba bzhin du brjod pa yin no
gru.english: My presentation is in complete accord with the traditional sources of the sutras which offer a literal presentation of reality; and in keeping as well with the personal advices of the Realized One himself: Nagarjuna. [colopon.2] Sanskrit unavailable

gru.acip: 'DIS NI RANG GIS THA SNYAD DU RNAM PAR BZHAG PA KHAS BLANGS PA THAMS CAD RANG MTSAN GYIS GRUB PA MED PA NYID LA 'JOG PAS, RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PA KHO NA'I STENG NAS RNAM GZHAG BYAS PA'I DON SMRA GNYIS LA SOGS PA'I GRUB MTHA' RNAMS RANG LUGS KYI DON DAM DU MA ZAD THA SNYAD DU YANG GRUB PA MED PAR 'DOD PA'I LUGS SO,,
gru.wylie: 'dis ni rang gis tha snyad du rnam par bzhag pa khas blangs pa thams cad rang mtshan gyis grub pa med pa nyid la 'jog pas, rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub pa kho na'i steng nas rnam gzhag byas pa'i don smra gnyis la sogs pa'i grub mtha' rnams rang lugs kyi don dam du ma zad tha snyad du yang grub pa med par 'dod pa'i lugs so
gru.english: All this is a reference to a system where we say the following. Once we accept the presentation of how things are established in terms, then what we are saying is that there is nothing at all which could exist “in actuality.” And so let's consider the beliefs expressed by the two Functionalist schools, and the like, who can only posit their own presentations with the assumption of things that could exist “in actuality.” The actual fact is that, according to our own system, it is not only the case that such objects could not exist in any ultimate way; neither could they exist even nominally.

gru.acip: DES NA RANG GI LUGS 'DI SEMS TZAM PA DANG YANG THUN MONG MA YIN PAR MA ZAD, MGON PO KLU SGRUB DANG 'PHAGS PA LHA'I DGONGS PA 'GREL BA'I DBU MA PA GZHAN GYI LUGS DANG YANG THUN MONG MA YIN PAR SHES PAR GYIS SHIG CES 'DOMS PA PO,,
gru.wylie: des na rang gi lugs 'di sems tsam pa dang yang thun mong ma yin par ma zad, mgon po klu sgrub dang 'phags pa lha'i dgongs pa 'grel ba'i dbu ma pa gzhan gyi lugs dang yang thun mong ma yin par shes par gyis shig ces 'doms pa po
gru.english: As such, what our author is actually advising us of here is the following— Not only should we say that the system that we ourselves are presenting here is nothing held in common even with those of the Mind Only. You must also understand the point that no one can say, either, that our beliefs are held in common with those of other systems of some thinkers of the Middle Way School who are attempting to comment upon the true intent of our Savior, Nagarjuna, and Aryadeva.

gru.acip: THA SNYAD DU YANG RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PA MED PA'I STENG NAS, BDEN GNYIS KYI RNAM GZHAG MDZAD PA 'DI LA BRTEN NAS RANG RGYUD KYI GRUB MTHA' DANG, KUN GZHI MI BZHED PA SOGS KYI BSHAD SROL THUN MONG MA YIN PA MANG DU YOD PA NI, DRANG NGES RNAM 'BYED LA SOGS PAR RGYAS PAR BSHAD PAS 'DIR MA SMOS SO,,
gru.wylie: tha snyad du yang rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub pa med pa'i steng nas, bden gnyis kyi rnam gzhag mdzad pa 'di la brten nas rang rgyud kyi grub mtha' dang, kun gzhi mi bzhed pa sogs kyi bshad srol thun mong ma yin pa mang du yod pa ni, drang nges rnam 'byed la sogs par rgyas par bshad pas 'dir ma smos so
gru.english: And so it is true that—even speaking nominally—there is nothing that could exist by definition. In addition, we have our presentation here of the two different types of reality. Based on this, there are many different, unique, systems of explanation—such as the school of the Independent Group, and those who do not accept the concept of a storehouse consciousness. I have explained all these at great length in works such as Distinguishing the Figurative from the Literal; as such, I will not go into them further here.

gru.acip: ,KLU SGRUB BLO MTSO SHIN TU RGYA CHE'I KHA DOG GIS 'JIGS PAS, ,SKYE BOS LUGS BZANG GANG DAG RGYANG RING SPANGS PAS DE YI TSIG ,LE'UR BYAS PA'I KHA 'BUS KU MU TA {%DA} KHA PHYE BA'I CHUS, ,DA LTA ZLA BA GRAGS PA RE RNAMS RAB TU SKONG BAR BYED,
gru.wylie: klu sgrub blo mtsho shin tu rgya che'i kha dog gis 'jigs pas, ,skye bos lugs bzang gang dag rgyang ring spangs pas de yi tshig ,le'ur byas pa'i kha 'bus ku mu ta {%da} kha phye ba'i chus, ,da lta zla ba grags pa re rnams rab tu skong bar byed
gru.english: They were frightened By the shade Of the expanse Of the ocean Of the mind Of Nagarjuna. And so individuals Took the beautiful system And discarded it off To a distance. But the flow Of pure water From that one Set in verse Opened the blooms Of a pure white Water lily, Whose buds had Been awaiting it. And with this Chandrakirti has now Fulfilled, perfectly, All the hopes.

gru.acip: DBU MA LA 'JUG PA 'DI SBYAR BA YIN NO ZHES BSHAD PA 'PHAGS PA KLU SGRUB KYI ZAB MO RTOGS PA'I BLO'I RGYA MTSO SHIN TU RGYA CHE LA GTING DPAG PAR DKA' BA'I NGAM GNAG PA'I KHA DOG GIS 'JIGS PAS,
gru.wylie: dbu ma la 'jug pa 'di sbyar ba yin no zhes bshad pa 'phags pa klu sgrub kyi zab mo rtogs pa'i blo'i rgya mtsho shin tu rgya che la gting dpag par dka' ba'i ngam gnag pa'i kha dog gis 'jigs pas
gru.english: The fact is that people became frightened when they heard someone say, “I will now compose Entering the Middle Way”—frightened simply when they saw the shade of the ebony abyss of depths so impossible to fathom, within the vast expanse of the ocean of that mind which could plumb the deeps of Arya Nagarjuna.

gru.acip: SEMS TZAM DU SMRA BA LA SOGS PA'I SKYO {%SKYE} BOS KLU SGRUB KYI LUGS BZANG PO GANG DAG RGYANG RING DU SPANGS MOD KYANG,
gru.wylie: sems tsam du smra ba la sogs pa'i skyo {%skye} bos klu sgrub kyi lugs bzang po gang dag rgyang ring du spangs mod kyang
gru.english: Now it is indeed the case that individuals like those who follow the Mind Only school have only rejected the beautiful system of Nagarjuna, discarding it off to a great distance.

gru.acip: JI LTAR GZHAN SDE SNGON SEMS RGYUD LA STONG NYID LA LHAG PAR MOS PA'I BAG CHAGS MA BZHAG PA RNAMS KYIS MNGON PA NAS BSHAD PA LTAR SRID RTZE MA GTOGS PA'I KHAMS GSUM GYI NYON MONGS MNGON GYUR RE ZHIG SPANGS SHING, GRUB PA'I MTHA' GZHAN NYE BAR SBYOR NUS PAR MTHONG YANG,
gru.wylie: ji ltar gzhan sde sngon sems rgyud la stong nyid la lhag par mos pa'i bag chags ma bzhag pa rnams kyis mngon pa nas bshad pa ltar srid rtse ma gtogs pa'i khams gsum gyi nyon mongs mngon gyur re zhig spangs shing, grub pa'i mtha' gzhan nye bar sbyor nus par mthong yang
gru.english: And so let's consider members of these other groups, who may not have—at some prior point in time—planted any deep seeds inside their mindstreams that would make them feel some strong aspiration towards emptiness. As explained in the texts on higher knowledge, they might still be able to eliminate—for a certain amount of time—different negative emotions for all three of the realms, except for that level known as the Peak of Existence. And we might observe them being able to apply themselves to other philosophical systems.

gru.acip: ,SLOB DPON KLU SGRUB LUGS BZANG BSNYAD LAS BDAG GIS BSOD RNAMS PHYOGS KYI MTHAR, ,KHYAB CING YID MKHA' NYON MONGS KYIS SNGOR STON KA'I RGYU SKAR STAR DKAR BA'AM, ,SEMS KYI SBRUL LA GDENGS KA'I NOR BU DANG 'DRA GANG ZHIG THOB PA DES, ,'JIG RTEN MA LUS DE NYID RTOGS NAS MYUR DU BDE GSHEGS SAR BGROD SHOG,
gru.wylie: slob dpon klu sgrub lugs bzang bsnyad las bdag gis bsod rnams phyogs kyi mthar, ,khyab cing yid mkha' nyon mongs kyis sngor ston ka'i rgyu skar star dkar ba'am, ,sems kyi sbrul la gdengs ka'i nor bu dang 'dra gang zhig thob pa des, ,'jig rten ma lus de nyid rtogs nas myur du bde gshegs sar bgrod shog
gru.english: Thus have I Enunciated that Beautiful system Of the Master, Nagarjuna. And by doing so, I have merit enough To stretch to the Very edges of Space itself. The sky of my mind Had been sent into The gloom of the Negative emotions. But now, In the midst, Has come a bright White light like A major star in The autumn heavens. Or else you could say That here is a mind Which resembles That fabulous jewel Which a cobra holds Embedded in their hood; And the acquisition of such Will allow the entire world To perceive suchness; And then may it happen That—with great speed— Every being completes Their journey to the level Of One Gone to Bliss.

gru.acip: SLOB DPON CHEN PO 'PHAGS PA KLU SGRUB KYI DBU MA'I LUGS BZANG PO LUNG DANG RIGS PA'I TSOGS SHIN TU GSAL BAS, BSNYAD PA STE BSHAD PA
gru.wylie: slob dpon chen po 'phags pa klu sgrub kyi dbu ma'i lugs bzang po lung dang rigs pa'i tshogs shin tu gsal bas, bsnyad pa ste bshad pa
gru.english: Thus then have I “enunciated”—which is to say, explained—that beautiful middle-way system of the great Master, The Arya, Nagarjuna; and I have done so by using perfectly clear examples of entire collections of both scriptural authority and logical reasoning.

gru.acip: ,NAG TSO'I 'GYUR LAS, KLU SGRUB LUGS MDZES PHYOGS SU GRAGS PA BRJOD LAS THOB PA'I BSOD NAMS GANG, ZHES 'BYUNG NGO,,
gru.wylie: nag tsho'i 'gyur las, klu sgrub lugs mdzes phyogs su grags pa brjod las thob pa'i bsod nams gang, zhes 'byung ngo
gru.english: Naktso's translation at this point includes the phrasing, “The merit that I have achieved, by proclaiming that lovely system of Nagarjuna throughout every corner of the world.” The master who composed the work

gru.acip: ,RGYAL BA'I GSUNG RAB KUN GYI SNYING PO MCHOG ,ZAB MO DBU MA MTHA' BRAL RTEN 'BYUNG LAM, ,MTHA' GNYIS SPANGS TE STON PAR LUNG BSTAN BZHIN, ,JI BZHIN 'GREL MDZAD 'PHAGS MCHOG KLU SGRUB ZHABS,
gru.wylie: rgyal ba'i gsung rab kun gyi snying po mchog ,zab mo dbu ma mtha' bral rten 'byung lam, ,mtha' gnyis spangs te ston par lung bstan bzhin, ,ji bzhin 'grel mdzad 'phags mchog klu sgrub zhabs
gru.english: It is the supreme heart Of all the high speech Of the Victors; It is the profound path Of the middle way, Occurrence in dependence, Free of all extremes. And there was one Who was prophesized To come and teach it, Free of the two extremes. I bow at the feet Of that highest of all The realized beings: Nagarjuna, Who explained this path As it really is.

gru.acip: ,GRUB PA'I DBANG PHYUG GSUM GYI BZHED PA'I SGO, ,GCIG TU DRIL NAS GNAD RNAMS MTHA' CHOD PAR, ,TSIG ZUR PHYIN PAR LEGS PAR BSHAD PA YIS, ,THAL 'GYUR LUGS MCHOG DRI MA MED PAR BYAS,
gru.wylie: grub pa'i dbang phyug gsum gyi bzhed pa'i sgo, ,gcig tu dril nas gnad rnams mtha' chod par, ,tshig zur phyin par legs par bshad pa yis, ,thal 'gyur lugs mchog dri ma med par byas
gru.english: The doorways of the positions Taken by these three lords Among the accomplished Were combined into one, Giving fine explanations Of the crucial points In a definitive way, Down to the last syllable. Thus then was the supreme System of the Consequence Group, Free of all impurity, created.

gru.acip: ,DER NGAL BA LAS BYUNG BA'I DGE BA YIS, ,'GRO KUN ZAB MO'I GNAD RNAMS KUN RTOGS NAS, ,NYIN MTSAN KUN TU SGRUB PA LHUR LEN PA, ,RTAG TU SRAS BCAS RGYAL BA MNYES BYED SHOG
gru.wylie: der ngal ba las byung ba'i dge ba yis, ,'gro kun zab mo'i gnad rnams kun rtogs nas, ,nyin mtshan kun tu sgrub pa lhur len pa, ,rtag tu sras bcas rgyal ba mnyes byed shog
gru.english: And I pray that by The virtue I've created In these exhausting efforts, Every living being May come to a perfect Realization of every Crucial point of the profound. May they throw themselves Into their practice Always, night & day, And ever come to please The Victors and their children.

gru.acip: c3) DE LTAR GSUNGS PAS GRUB PA'I DON BSHAD PA,
gru.wylie: c3) de ltar gsungs pas grub pa'i don bshad pa
gru.english: An explanation of the conclusion we can draw from statements to this effect.

gru.acip: b4) DE SGRUB PA'I KHUNGS BSTAN PA,
gru.wylie: b4) de sgrub pa'i khungs bstan pa
gru.english: A presentation of authentic sources which prove this point

gru.acip: a1) SA 'DIR BRTZON 'GRUS LHAG PAR BSTAN PA, [v. IV.1]
gru.wylie: a1) sa 'dir brtson 'grus lhag par bstan pa, [v. iv.1]
gru.english: A description of how, at this point, our practice of joyful effort becomes higher

gru.acip: a6) BDEN GRUB DANG BDEN 'DZIN NGOS GZUNG BA, [81b]
gru.wylie: a6) bden grub dang bden 'dzin ngos gzung ba, [81b]
gru.english: Their identification of “real existence,” and how we hold on to it

gru.acip: b2) LUNG GI DON DE RIGS PAS BSGRUB PA, [90b]
gru.wylie: b2) lung gi don de rigs pas bsgrub pa, [90b]
gru.english: Confirming the content of these scriptures through reasoning

gru.acip: a3) CHOS KYI BDAG MED RIGS PAS BSGRUB PA, [90b]
gru.wylie: a3) chos kyi bdag med rigs pas bsgrub pa, [90b]
gru.english: Using reasoning to prove that things have no self-nature

gru.acip: b5) DE RIGS PAS SGRUB PA'I SGRUB BYED BSTAN PA, [93b]
gru.wylie: b5) de rigs pas sgrub pa'i sgrub byed bstan pa, [93b]
gru.english: Presenting the proofs which establish this assertion through the use of logic * * *

gru.acip: a6) DE KHO NA NYID RTOGS PAR 'DOD PA'I GRUB MTHA' MKHAN GYI LUGS DGAG PA, [93b]
gru.wylie: a6) de kho na nyid rtogs par 'dod pa'i grub mtha' mkhan gyi lugs dgag pa, [93b]
gru.english: Denying the system of those who believe they have perceived some actual nature

gru.acip: b6) GRUB MTHAS BLO MA BSGYUR BA'I THA SNYAD DU YANG MED PAR BSTAN PA, [96b] [v. VI.12a]
gru.wylie: b6) grub mthas blo ma bsgyur ba'i tha snyad du yang med par bstan pa, [96b] [v. vi.12a]
gru.english: Demonstrating that things could not be said to grow from themselves even in the parlance of those who have not been influenced by any particular school of philosophy

gru.acip: a9) RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PA YOD PAR 'DOD PA DGAG PA, [130a]
gru.wylie: a9) rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub pa yod par 'dod pa dgag pa, [130a]
gru.english: Denying the belief that things could exist by definition

gru.acip: a10) RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA MI 'DOD PA LA KUN GZHI SOGS KHAS BLANG MI DGOS PAR BSTAN PA, [138b]
gru.wylie: a10) rang bzhin gyis grub pa mi 'dod pa la kun gzhi sogs khas blang mi dgos par bstan pa, [138b]
gru.english: A demonstration that it is not the case that if we deny that things could exist through any nature of their own, we must then accept things like foundations consciousness

gru.acip: a7) PHYI ROL MED PA'I SHES PA RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA DGAG
gru.wylie: a7) phyi rol med pa'i shes pa rang bzhin gyis grub pa dgag
gru.english: A denial that the understanding that there are no outer objects could ever exist through some nature of its own

gru.acip: a10) PHYI ROL MED PA'I SHES PA RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA'I DPE DGAG
gru.wylie: a10) phyi rol med pa'i shes pa rang bzhin gyis grub pa'i dpe dgag
gru.english: Denying a metaphor which is meant to show that awareness where there are no outer objects could exist through some nature of its own * * *

gru.acip: a12) RMI LAM GYI DPES SHES PA RANG BZHIN GYIS YOD PA MI 'GRUB PA, [vv. VI.48, VI.49]
gru.wylie: a12) rmi lam gyi dpes shes pa rang bzhin gyis yod pa mi 'grub pa, [vv. vi.48, vi.49]
gru.english: How it is that the metaphor of a dream fails to establish that awareness exists through some nature of its own

gru.acip: b12) RMI LAM GYI DPES SAD DUS SU PHYI ROL MED PA MI 'GRUB PA, [vv. VI.50, VI.51, VI.52a]
gru.wylie: b12) rmi lam gyi dpes sad dus su phyi rol med pa mi 'grub pa, [vv. vi.50, vi.51, vi.52a]
gru.english: How it is that the metaphor of a dream fails to establish the idea that, when we awake, there are no outer objects

gru.acip: c12) RMI LAM GYI DPES DNGOS PO THAMS CAD BRDZUN PAR 'GRUB PA, [v. VI.52b, v. VI.53]
gru.wylie: c12) rmi lam gyi dpes dngos po thams cad brdzun par 'grub pa, [v. vi.52b, v. vi.53]
gru.english: Establishing—through the metaphor of a dream—that all entities are deceptive

gru.acip: a13) DA LTAR BA LA NUS PA RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA
gru.wylie: a13) da ltar ba la nus pa rang bzhin gyis grub pa
gru.english: DGAG [f. 161a] [vv. VI.56b, VI.57a] A denial that the present could possess a potential that existed through some nature of its own

gru.acip: b13) MA 'ONGS PA'I NUS PA RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA DGAG [vv. VI.57b, VI.58]
gru.wylie: b13) ma 'ongs pa'i nus pa rang bzhin gyis grub pa dgag [vv. vi.57b, vi.58]
gru.english: A denial that the potential of the future could exist through some nature of its own

gru.acip: c13) 'DAS PA LA NUS PA RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA DGAG PA, [vv. VI.59, VI.60, VI.61]
gru.wylie: c13) 'das pa la nus pa rang bzhin gyis grub pa dgag pa, [vv. vi.59, vi.60, vi.61]
gru.english: A denial that the potential of the past could exist through some nature of its own

gru.acip: b7) GZHAN DBANG RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA'I SGRUB BYED TSAD MA DGAG
gru.wylie: b7) gzhan dbang rang bzhin gyis grub pa'i sgrub byed tshad ma dgag
gru.english: Denying the accurate perception which is supposed to prove that dominated things exist through some nature of their own

gru.acip: a8) GZHAN DBANG GI SGRUB BYED RANG RIG DGAG PA,
gru.wylie: a8) gzhan dbang gi sgrub byed rang rig dgag pa
gru.english: A denial of apperception, which is used to establish dominated entities

gru.acip: a9) GZHAN DBANG GI SGRUB BYED DRIS NAS DE MI 'THAD PAR BSTAN PA,
gru.wylie: a9) gzhan dbang gi sgrub byed dris nas de mi 'thad par bstan pa
gru.english: [vv. VI.72, VI.73a] A request for proof to substantiate the existence of dominated entities, and then a demonstration that the attempted proof is incorrect

gru.acip: c9) GZHAN DBANG RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA MO GSHAM KYI BU DANG MTSUNGS PAR BSTAN PA, [f. 183a, v. VI.77]
gru.wylie: c9) gzhan dbang rang bzhin gyis grub pa mo gsham kyi bu dang mtshungs par bstan pa, [f. 183a, v. vi.77]
gru.english: Establishing that dominated entities which existed through some nature of their own would be the equivalent of the child of a barren woman

gru.acip: c8) DES NA KLU SGRUB KYI LUGS KHO NA'I RJES SU 'BRANG BAR RIGS PA, [f. 184a, vv. VI.79, VI.80]
gru.wylie: c8) des na klu sgrub kyi lugs kho na'i rjes su 'brang bar rigs pa, [f. 184a, vv. vi.79, vi.80]
gru.english: A description of how—therefore—it is appropriate to follow the system of Arya Nagarjuna, exclusively

gru.acip: a9) TZAM GYI SGRAS PHYI ROL MI 'GOG PA SA BCU PA'I LUNG GIS BSGRUB PA, [f. 188b, v. VI.84]
gru.wylie: a9) tsam gyi sgras phyi rol mi 'gog pa sa bcu pa'i lung gis bsgrub pa, [f. 188b, v. vi.84]
gru.english: Showing how a citation from The Ten Levels supports the idea that the word “only” is not meant to deny outer objects

gru.acip: b9) DON DE NYID MDO GZHAN GYIS KYANG BSGRUB PA, [f. 189b, vv. VI.85, VI.86]
gru.wylie: b9) don de nyid mdo gzhan gyis kyang bsgrub pa, [f. 189b, vv. vi.85, vi.86]
gru.english: Demonstrating how this very same point is made in other sutras as well

gru.acip: c9) TZAM GYI SGRAS SEMS GTZO BO NYID DU BSGRUB PA, [f. 190b, vv. VI.87, VI.88, VI.89, VI.90]
gru.wylie: c9) tsam gyi sgras sems gtso bo nyid du bsgrub pa, [f. 190b, vv. vi.87, vi.88, vi.89, vi.90]
gru.english: Establishing that the intent of the word “only” is to say only that the mind is the primary thing

gru.acip: c5) MTHA' BZHI'I SKYE BA BKAG PAS GRUB PA'I DON, [f. 205b, v. VI.104a]
gru.wylie: c5) mtha' bzhi'i skye ba bkag pas grub pa'i don, [f. 205b, v. vi.104a]
gru.english: The point we arrive at, by denying that things could start in any of these four different ways

gru.acip: b3) GANG ZAG GI BDAG MED RIGS PAS BSGRUB PA
gru.wylie: b3) gang zag gi bdag med rigs pas bsgrub pa
gru.english: [f. 214b] Using reasoning to prove that the person has no self-nature

gru.acip: a4) THAR 'DOD KYIS THOG MAR BDAG RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA NYID DGAG DGOS PAR BSTAN PA, [f. 214b, v. VI.120]
gru.wylie: a4) thar 'dod kyis thog mar bdag rang bzhin gyis grub pa nyid dgag dgos par bstan pa, [f. 214b, v. vi.120]
gru.english: Showing how those who wish to achieve freedom need, before anything else, to deny that the self is something that could exist through any nature of its own

gru.acip: b4) BDAG DANG BDAG GI BA GNYIS RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA 'GOG PA'I TSUL,
gru.wylie: b4) bdag dang bdag gi ba gnyis rang bzhin gyis grub pa 'gog pa'i tshul
gru.english: How it is that we deny the idea that either me or mine could exist through any nature of their own

gru.acip: a5) BDAG RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA DGAG PA,
gru.wylie: a5) bdag rang bzhin gyis grub pa dgag pa
gru.english: Denying that the self could exist through any nature of its own * * *

gru.acip: b7) DE LTAR 'DOD PAR MI RIGS PA'I SGRUB BYED BSTAN PA, [f. 223a,
gru.wylie: b7) de ltar 'dod par mi rigs pa'i sgrub byed bstan pa, [f. 223a
gru.english: v. VI.129b] A presentation of support for saying that this kind of belief is incorrect

gru.acip: b9) SGRUB PHYOGS NAS YIN DU CHUG KYANG PHUNG PO BDAG TU STON PA MIN PA, [f. 226b, v. VI.134]
gru.wylie: b9) sgrub phyogs nas yin du chug kyang phung po bdag tu ston pa min pa, [f. 226b, v. vi.134]
gru.english: How this reference is not saying that the parts to the person are a self, even if we allow that the reference was meant in a positive sense

gru.acip: d7) MING GI THA SNYAD KYI DON GZHAN YANG GRUB PAR BSTAN PA, [f. 238a, v. VI.159]
gru.wylie: D7) ming gi tha snyad kyi don gzhan yang grub par bstan pa, [f. 238a, v. vi.159]
gru.english: A demonstration how there is another interpretation of the meaning of terms used as names

gru.acip: b5) BDAG GI BA RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA DGAG PA, [f. 241b, v. VI.165]
gru.wylie: b5) bdag gi ba rang bzhin gyis grub pa dgag pa, [f. 241b, v. vi.165]
gru.english: Denying that what belongs to the self could exist through any nature of its own

gru.acip: a6) RGYU 'BRAS RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA 'GOG PA LA SKYON MTSUNGS PA'I RTZOD PA, [f. 244b, vv. VI.171, VI.172]
gru.wylie: a6) rgyu 'bras rang bzhin gyis grub pa 'gog pa la skyon mtshungs pa'i rtsod pa, [f. 244b, vv. vi.171, vi.172]
gru.english: Argument that the problems are just the same with the denial that cause & effect could exist through any nature of its own

gru.acip: a7) RANG GI PHYOGS LA SUN 'BYIN DANG SGRUB PA 'THAD TSUL,
gru.wylie: a7) rang gi phyogs la sun 'byin dang sgrub pa 'thad tshul
gru.english: Demonstrating how the attack and the proof utilized in our own position are correct

gru.acip: b8) RANG GI PHYOGS SGRUB PA KHAS LEN TSUL, [f. 246b, vv. VI.174, VI. 175]
gru.wylie: b8) rang gi phyogs sgrub pa khas len tshul, [f. 246b, vv. vi.174, vi. 175]
gru.english: How it is that we accept the proof of our own position

gru.acip: c7) RANG BZHIN MED PA BSGRUB NUS PA BZHIN DU GZHAN GYIS BZLOG STE BSGRUB MI NUS PA, [f. 248a, v. VI.177]
gru.wylie: c7) rang bzhin med pa bsgrub nus pa bzhin du gzhan gyis bzlog ste bsgrub mi nus pa, [f. 248a, v. vi.177]
gru.english: A demonstration of how—so long as we are able to establish that things have no nature of their own—the other party will be unable to prove any denial of our position

gru.acip: c2) DES GRUB PA'I STONG NYID KYI RAB DBYE BSHAD PA,
gru.wylie: c2) des grub pa'i stong nyid kyi rab dbye bshad pa
gru.english: [f. 249b] An explanation of the divisions of emptiness thus confirmed

gru.acip: THA GRUR DPAG TSAD BRGYA STONG DU MA YOD PA, LAG MTHIL LTAR MNYAM PAR GYUR, NGAN SONG DANG, SDUG BSNGAL GYI SGRA MED PA, BUD MED KYI DNGOS PO MED PA,
gru.wylie: tha grur dpag tshad brgya stong du ma yod pa, lag mthil ltar mnyam par gyur, ngan song dang, sdug bsngal gyi sgra med pa, bud med kyi dngos po med pa
gru.english: It stretches for many hundreds and thousands of miles.  The surface of the ground there is as smooth as your palm, and you will never hear there a single sound of misery, or pain.  And there is no such thing there as one person who is treated less than another.

gru.acip: GANG GI TSE BDAG MA 'ONGS PA'I DUS NA BLA NA MED PA YANG DAG PAR RDZOGS PA'I BYANG CHUB MNGON PAR RDZOGS PAR SANGS RGYAS PA DE NA SEMS CAN GANG DAG CHU'I NANG DU SON TE, GRUR ZHUGS PA, GLING MED PAR PHYIN PA, SROG BSDO BA, CHU KLUNG DANG, RGYA MTSO'I NANG DU SON TE, SMRE SNGAGS SNA TSOGS 'DON PA DE DAG
gru.wylie: gang gi tshe bdag ma 'ongs pa'i dus na bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub mngon par rdzogs par sangs rgyas pa de na sems can gang dag chu'i nang du son te, grur zhugs pa, gling med par phyin pa, srog bsdo ba, chu klung dang, rgya mtsho'i nang du son te, smre sngags sna tshogs 'don pa de dag
gru.english: In future days, when I reach total enlightenment—when I reach my own matchless, perfect, and complete Buddhahood—there will be certain beings who sail the water.  They will board their ships at the risk of their very lives.  And there will come a time that they themselves fall into these waters, and cry out in every different way.

gru.acip: MNYAM PA, THA GRU CHE BA, YANGS PA, LAG MTHIL LTAR MNYAM PAR GYUR PA, LHA'I SPOS KYI SHING LJON PA RNAMS KYIS RAB TU BRGYAN PA, SPOS GTZANG ZHING SKYON MED PA DANG, LHA'I SPOS DANG ME TOG GIS RAB TU BRGYAN PA,
gru.wylie: mnyam pa, tha gru che ba, yangs pa, lag mthil ltar mnyam par gyur pa, lha'i spos kyi shing ljon pa rnams kyis rab tu brgyan pa, spos gtsang zhing skyon med pa dang, lha'i spos dang me tog gis rab tu brgyan pa
gru.english: The ground there is level, and vast in its extent, with a wide vista.  The surface of the ground is smooth as your palm, and adorned with the kind of trees from which the gods make their incense.  The incense is particularly pure and free from any defect; you can find it, and the flowers of the gods, spread everywhere.

whole_word_matches.context: mnyam pa, tha gru che ba, yangs pa, lag mthil ltar mnyam par gyur pa, lh

gru.acip: DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA DGRA BCOM PA YANG DAG PAR RDZOGS PA'I SANGS RGYAS GSER BZANG DRI MED RIN CHEN SNANG BRTUL ZHUGS GRUB PA ZHES BYA BA BZHUGS TE 'TSO ZHING GZHES LA CHOS KYANG STON CING,
gru.wylie: de bzhin gshegs pa dgra bcom pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas gser bzang dri med rin chen snang brtul zhugs grub pa zhes bya ba bzhugs te 'tsho zhing gzhes la chos kyang ston cing
gru.english: In this world lives One Who Has Gone Thus—a Defeater of the Foe, a Pure and Total Buddha—whose name is “Finest Gold, Free of All Impurity, Shining Jewel, Master of Spiritual Hardships.”  He spends his days happily, and also teaches the Dharma.

gru.acip: 'JAM DPAL, BCOM LDAN 'DAS DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA DGRA BCOM PA YANG DAG PAR RDZOGS PA'I SANGS RGYAS GSER BZANG DRI MED RIN CHEN SNANG BRTUL ZHUGS GRUB PA DE, SNGON BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA'I SPYAD PA SPYOD PA NA SMON LAM CHEN PO BZHI PO DE DAG BTAB BO,,
gru.wylie: 'jam dpal, bcom ldan 'das de bzhin gshegs pa dgra bcom pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas gser bzang dri med rin chen snang brtul zhugs grub pa de, sngon byang chub sems dpa'i spyad pa spyod pa na smon lam chen po bzhi po de dag btab bo
gru.english: And so these are the four great prayers, Gentle Voice, that the Conqueror, the One Gone Thus, the Defeater of the Foe, the Pure and Total Buddha by the name of “Finest Gold, Free of All Impurity, Shining Jewel, Master of Spiritual Hardships” made, during the time that he was perfecting the practices of a bodhisattva. The paradise of Finest Gold

gru.acip: 'JAM DPAL, BCOM LDAN 'DAS DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA DGRA BCOM PA YANG DAG PAR RDZOGS PA'I SANGS RGYAS GSER BZANG DRI MED RIN CHEN SNANG BRTUL ZHUGS GRUB PA DE'I SANGS RGYAS KYI ZHING DE NI
gru.wylie: 'jam dpal, bcom ldan 'das de bzhin gshegs pa dgra bcom pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas gser bzang dri med rin chen snang brtul zhugs grub pa de'i sangs rgyas kyi zhing de ni
gru.english: Gentle Voice, here are the wonders of the enlightened paradise of this Conqueror, this One Gone Thus, Defeater of the Foe, the Perfect and Total Buddha named “Finest Gold, Free of All Impurity, Shining Jewel, Master of Spiritual Hardships.”

gru.acip: MNYAM PA, YANGS PA, THA GRU CHE BA, TZANDAN SBRUL GYI SNYING PO'I DRI'I SHING LJON PAS MDZES PAR BYAS PA,
gru.wylie: mnyam pa, yangs pa, tha gru che ba, tsandan sbrul gyi snying po'i dri'i shing ljon pas mdzes par byas pa
gru.english: The surface of the earth here is level, with a wide vista, vast in its extent.  It is adorned everywhere with trees made of serpent's heart sandalwood.

whole_word_matches.context: mnyam pa, yangs pa, tha gru che ba, tsandan sbrul gyi snying po'i dri'i shing ljon

gru.acip: BCOM LDAN 'DAS DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA GSER BZANG DRI MED RIN CHEN SNANG BRTUL ZHUGS GRUB PA DE, BLA NA MED PA YANG DAG PAR RDZOGS PA'I BYANG CHUB MNGON PAR RDZOGS PAR SANGS RGYAS NAS SNGON GYI SMON LAM GYI STOBS KYIS BYANG CHUB KYI SHING DRUNG DU BZHUGS TE,
gru.wylie: bcom ldan 'das de bzhin gshegs pa gser bzang dri med rin chen snang brtul zhugs grub pa de, bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub mngon par rdzogs par sangs rgyas nas sngon gyi smon lam gyi stobs kyis byang chub kyi shing drung du bzhugs te
gru.english: This Conqueror, the One Gone Thus by the name of Finest Gold, Free of All Impurity, Shining Jewel, Master of Spiritual Hardships, did indeed attain his matchless, perfect, and total enlightenment.  And then, by the power of the prayers he had made prior to that, he took his seat at the foot of his own Bodhi Tree.

gru.acip: 'JAM DPAL, BCOM LDAN 'DAS DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA DGRA BCOM PA YANG DAG PAR RDZOGS PA'I SANGS RGYAS MYA NGAN MED MCHOG DPAL DE'I SANGS RGYAS KYI ZHING DE NI LAG MTHIL LTAR MNYAM PA, THA GRU CHE BA, YANGS PA,
gru.wylie: 'jam dpal, bcom ldan 'das de bzhin gshegs pa dgra bcom pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas mya ngan med mchog dpal de'i sangs rgyas kyi zhing de ni lag mthil ltar mnyam pa, tha gru che ba, yangs pa
gru.english: Gentle Voice, the enlightened paradise of this Conqueror, the Glorious One, Beyond All Sadness—Conqueror, Defeater of the Foe, Perfect and Total Buddha—has a ground which is as smooth as the palm of your hand; vast in extent, with a wide vista.

whole_word_matches.context: ngs rgyas kyi zhing de ni lag mthil ltar mnyam pa, tha gru che ba, yangs pa

gru.acip: SHIN TU YONGS SU DAG LA, MNYAM PA, DRI MA MED PA, 'OD GSAL PA, AAN DA RNYIL GYI RANG BZHIN CAN, RTZIG PA DANG, RA BA DANG, SKAR KHUNG DANG, RTA BABS DANG, DRA BA DANG, BA GAM NI SHEL LAS GRUB PA, SA GZHI LHA'I RIN PO CHE'I SHING LJON PAS MDZES PAR BYAS PA,
gru.wylie: shin tu yongs su dag la, mnyam pa, dri ma med pa, 'od gsal pa, aan da rnyil gyi rang bzhin can, rtsig pa dang, ra ba dang, skar khung dang, rta babs dang, dra ba dang, ba gam ni shel las grub pa, sa gzhi lha'i rin po che'i shing ljon pas mdzes par byas pa
gru.english: It is totally pure; and the surface is perfectly level.  Nothing here is unclean; light covers everywhere, and the ground is made of sapphire.  All the walls, and fences, and windowpanes, porches, ramparts, and domes are made of pure crystal.  The entire space is embellished with the jewel trees of the gods.

gru.acip: SEMS CAN DMYAL BA NA GNAS KYANG DER SANGS RGYAS KYI MTHUS DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA DE'I MTSAN MNGON DU 'GYUR TE, DE DAG DE NAS SHI 'PHOS NAS YANG MI'I 'JIG RTEN DU SKYE BAR 'GYUR, YANG DAG PA'I LTA BA CAN DANG, BRTZON 'GRUS DANG LDAN PA DANG, DGE BA'I BSAM PA CAN DU 'GYUR RO,,
gru.wylie: sems can dmyal ba na gnas kyang der sangs rgyas kyi mthus de bzhin gshegs pa de'i mtshan mngon du 'gyur te, de dag de nas shi 'phos nas yang mi'i 'jig rten du skye bar 'gyur, yang dag pa'i lta ba can dang, brtson 'grus dang ldan pa dang, dge ba'i bsam pa can du 'gyur ro
gru.english: The holy name of this Buddha Gone Thus, due to the Buddha's mystic power, comes to such people—even if they have already fallen into the realms of hell.  And because of this, they die and move on, taking a rebirth into the human realm.  Within this new realm, they become people with pure worldviews; great effort in their spiritual practice; and strong virtuous states of mind.

gru.acip: DGRA BO DE'I MING NAS BRJOD PA 'AM, GZUGS BYAS NAS, DER RIG SNGAGS DRAG PO SGRUB CING BYAD STEMS DANG, RO LANGS KYI SBYOR BAS SROG GI BAR CHAD BYA BA DANG, LUS RNAM PAR GZHIG PAR 'DOD PA LA,
gru.wylie: dgra bo de'i ming nas brjod pa 'am, gzugs byas nas, der rig sngags drag po sgrub cing byad stems dang, ro langs kyi sbyor bas srog gi bar chad bya ba dang, lus rnam par gzhig par 'dod pa la
gru.english: Then they call out the name of their enemies, or fashion an effigy of them.  They utter over these evil spells and curses, and then raise the dead—in hopes that this will create some disruption in the lives of their foes, or destroy their physical health completely.

gru.acip: RLUNG DANG, CHAR DUS SU LDANG ZHING LO THOG 'GRUB PAR 'GYUR, YUL DE NA GNAS PA'I SEMS CAN THAMS CAD KYANG NAD MED PA DANG, BDE BA DANG, MCHOG TU DGA' BA MANG BAR 'GYUR RO,,
gru.wylie: rlung dang, char dus su ldang zhing lo thog 'grub par 'gyur, yul de na gnas pa'i sems can thams cad kyang nad med pa dang, bde ba dang, mchog tu dga' ba mang bar 'gyur ro
gru.english: The seasonal winds will rise when they should; and so will the rains—which means that the harvests will be successful.  All the people living in this country will be free of disease; they will enjoy happiness, and great masses of highest joy.

gru.acip: BCOM LDAN 'DAS, GANG LA LA ZHIG DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA 'DI DAG GI MTSAN DANG, SNGON GYI SMON LAM GYI KHYAD PAR RGYAS PA DANG, CHOS KYI RNAM GRANGS 'DI 'CHANG BA DANG, KLOG PA DE'I RE BA THAMS CAD BDAG GIS YONGS SU BSKANG BAR BGYI, DON THAMS CAD KYANG BSGRUB PAR BGYI'O,,
gru.wylie: bcom ldan 'das, gang la la zhig de bzhin gshegs pa 'di dag gi mtshan dang, sngon gyi smon lam gyi khyad par rgyas pa dang, chos kyi rnam grangs 'di 'chang ba dang, klog pa de'i re ba thams cad bdag gis yongs su bskang bar bgyi, don thams cad kyang bsgrub par bgyi'o
gru.english: O Conquerors, I will personally fulfill all the hopes of any person who keeps and reads aloud the holy names of these Who Have Gone Thus; and the vast details of their ancient prayers; and this particular presentation of the teaching.  I will see to it that everything they want to achieve is achieved.

gru.acip: DGRA BO DE'I MING NAS BRJOD PA 'AM, GZUGS BYAS NAS DER RIG SNGAGS DRAG PO BSGRUB CING, BYAD STEMS DANG, RO LANGS KYI SBYOR BAS SROG GI BAR CHAD BYA BA DANG, LUS RNAM PAR GZHIG PAR 'DOD PA LA
gru.wylie: dgra bo de'i ming nas brjod pa 'am, gzugs byas nas der rig sngags drag po bsgrub cing, byad stems dang, ro langs kyi sbyor bas srog gi bar chad bya ba dang, lus rnam par gzhig par 'dod pa la
gru.english: Then they call out the names of their enemies, or fashion an effigy of them. They utter over these evil spells and curses, and then raise the dead—in hopes that this will create some disruption in the lives of their foes, or destroy their physical health completely. Yai shrutam bhavishyati tasya Bhagavato Bhaishajya Guru Vaidurya Prabhasya Tathagatasya namadheyam. Tesham na shakyam

gru.acip: RLUNG DANG, CHAR DUS SU LDANG ZHING LO TOG 'GRUB PAR 'GYUR RO, ,YUL DE NA GNAS PA'I SEMS CAN THAMS CAD KYANG NAD MED PA DANG, BDE BA DANG, MCHOG TU DGA' BA MANG BAR 'GYUR RO,,
gru.wylie: rlung dang, char dus su ldang zhing lo tog 'grub par 'gyur ro, ,yul de na gnas pa'i sems can thams cad kyang nad med pa dang, bde ba dang, mchog tu dga' ba mang bar 'gyur ro
gru.english: The seasonal winds will rise when they should; and so will the rains—which means that the harvests will be successful. All the people living in this country will be free of disease; they will enjoy happiness, and great masses of highest joy. Na cha tatra vishaye dushta yaksha rakshasa bhuta pishacha satvanam vihethayanti…

gru.acip: NA MO GU RU MANYDZU GHO sh'A YA, ZHES PAS STON LA, DON NI, RJE BLA MAS BSTOD TSIG RTZOM PA'I 'GOR, 'DOD DON BDE BLAG TU 'GRUB PA'I PHYIR, BLA MA 'JAM PA'I DBYANGS LA PHYAG 'TSAL LO, ,ZHES SGO GSUM DVANG BAS 'DUD PA'O,,
gru.wylie: na mo gu ru manydzu gho ShA ya, zhes pas ston la, don ni, rje bla mas bstod tshig rtsom pa'i 'gor, 'dod don bde blag tu 'grub pa'i phyir, bla ma 'jam pa'i dbyangs la phyag 'tshal lo, ,zhes sgo gsum dvang bas 'dud pa'o
gru.english: This opening section is indicated in the words, Namo Guru Manjughoshaya. The point of this line is as follows. Here our Lord Lama is bowing himself down-as he starts off on the composition of his work-because he seeks to reach his desired goal with ease. And so he bows himself down in crystal faith conveyed by all three doors of expression: with his body, in his speech, and through his thoughts. He offers this Sanskrit then which itself means, "I bow down to my Lama, the Soft Voice." The praise, in brief

gru.acip: DON NI, 'JIG RTEN NA CHAGS SOGS KYI RGUD PA JI SNYED YOD PA DE YI RTZA BA GANG ZAG DANG CHOS LA DMIGS NAS BDEN GRUB TU 'DZIN PA'I MA RIG PA STE,
gru.wylie: don ni, 'jig rten na chags sogs kyi rgud pa ji snyed yod pa de yi rtsa ba gang zag dang chos la dmigs nas bden grub tu 'dzin pa'i ma rig pa ste
gru.english: Here's how these lines are explained. Misunderstanding-where we focus on both the individual and on things, and hold them to exist in reality-is the very root of the total amount of trouble there is in this entire world. And we can describe this "trouble" as the feeling of attachment, and so on.

gru.acip: DANG PO LA GNYIS, BSTAN PA BLA NA MED PAR SGRUB PA DANG, STON PA BLA NA MED PAR SGRUB PA'O,,
gru.wylie: dang po la gnyis, bstan pa bla na med par sgrub pa dang, ston pa bla na med par sgrub pa'o
gru.english: The first of these parts comes in two sections: establishing that these teachings are the highest of all; and then establishing that their teacher is as well the highest.

gru.acip: DON NI, CHOS GANG DANG GANG RKYEN LA RAG LAS PA DE DANG DE RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAS STONG NGO ZHES GSUNG BA 'DI LAS YA MTSAN PA'I LEGS 'DOMS KYI TSUL NI CI ZHIG YOD DE MED DO ZHES PA'O,,
gru.wylie: don ni, chos gang dang gang rkyen la rag las pa de dang de rang bzhin gyis grub pas stong ngo zhes gsung ba 'di las ya mtshan pa'i legs 'doms kyi tshul ni ci zhig yod de med do zhes pa'o
gru.english: What these lines are referring to first is the statement that any thing there is which relies upon conditions is empty of existing through any nature of its own. And then it is asking the question, Where could you ever find a more amazing manner of fine instruction than this? For surely we could not. Things that work from their own side

gru.acip: DON NI, RTEN 'BREL YIN PA'I RGYU MTSAN GYIS BDEN GRUB GANG DU BZUNG BAS NA BYIS PA DNGOS SMRA BA RNAMS
gru.wylie: don ni, rten 'brel yin pa'i rgyu mtshan gyis bden grub gang du bzung bas na byis pa dngos smra ba rnams
gru.english: These lines are saying the following. "Infants" is a reference to those who say that working things must exist from their own side; we give them this name because they hold that things exist in truth, and offer as their reason that these things exist in dependence.
