gru.acip: GNYIS PA STON PA BLA NA MED PAR SGRUB PA LA GNYIS, RTEN 'BREL STON PA SMRA BA GZHAN LAS KHYAD ZHUGS TSUL DANG, DE LTA BU'I STON PA BLA NA MED PA LA PHYAG 'TSAL BA'O,,
gru.wylie: gnyis pa ston pa bla na med par sgrub pa la gnyis, rten 'brel ston pa smra ba gzhan las khyad zhugs tshul dang, de lta bu'i ston pa bla na med pa la phyag 'tshal ba'o
gru.english: We come then to our second section from above: establishing that the teacher who granted the highest teachings is as well the highest. This comes in two parts of its own: showing how the teacher who describes dependent events is superior to all other teachers; and then bowing down to just such a matchless teacher.

gru.acip: DANG PO LA GNYIS, STONG PA DANG RTEN 'BREL DON GCIG TU MI 'DOD PAS THUB PA'I BZHED PA MI RTOGS PAR BSTAN PA DANG, STONG PA DANG RTEN 'BREL DON GCIG PA THUB PA'I BZHED PA MCHOG TU SGRUB PA'O,,
gru.wylie: dang po la gnyis, stong pa dang rten 'brel don gcig tu mi 'dod pas thub pa'i bzhed pa mi rtogs par bstan pa dang, stong pa dang rten 'brel don gcig pa thub pa'i bzhed pa mchog tu sgrub pa'o
gru.english: The first of those steps itself covers two topics: (1) presenting the fact that-for as long as we disagree that emptiness and dependence amount to the same thing-we have still failed to grasp the position that the Able One takes; and (2) establishing the fact that the very highest position ever taken by the Able One is that emptiness and dependence amount to the same thing.

gru.acip: ,RTEN CING 'BREL PAR 'BYUNG BA'I TSUL, ,'GAL BA DANG NI MA GRUB PAR, ,MTHONG BA 'DI YIS KHYOD KYI LUGS, ,JI LTAR KHONG DU CHUD PAR NUS,
gru.wylie: rten cing 'brel par 'byung ba'i tshul, ,'gal ba dang ni ma grub par, ,mthong ba 'di yis khyod kyi lugs, ,ji ltar khong du chud par nus
gru.english: This is where Those who see it That the way in which Events occur in Dependence & connection Must be a contradiction, Or simply mistaken, Would never be able then To grasp your system.

gru.acip: RTEN CING 'BREL PAR 'BYUNG BA'I TSUL TE RTAGS YIN PA LA DNGOS SMRA BAS KHYAB PA 'GAL BA DANG NI, MU STEGS PAS RTAGS MA GRUB PAR MTHONG ZHING 'DOD PA 'DI YIS
gru.wylie: rten cing 'brel par 'byung ba'i tshul te rtags yin pa la dngos smra bas khyab pa 'gal ba dang ni, mu stegs pas rtags ma grub par mthong zhing 'dod pa 'di yis
gru.english: The way in which events occur in dependence & connection is given here as the reason we use to prove this emptiness. Those who assert that if things work then they have to be real would reply that it's a contradiction to say that if something exhibits dependence, then it must be empty. The way in which the River Schools would see it-the position they'd take-is that the reason given here, that things are dependent, was simply mistaken.

gru.acip: GNYIS PA LA GSUM, RANG BZHIN GYIS STONG PA LA BYA BYED 'THAD CING LDOG PHYOGS LA MI 'THAD PAR BZHED PA, CHOS THAMS CAD RTEN 'BREL YIN PA'I RGYU MTSAN GYIS RANG BZHIN GYIS STONG PAR GSUNGS TSUL, TSUL DES STON PA SMRA BA BLA NA MED PAR GRUB PA'O,,
gru.wylie: gnyis pa la gsum, rang bzhin gyis stong pa la bya byed 'thad cing ldog phyogs la mi 'thad par bzhed pa, chos thams cad rten 'brel yin pa'i rgyu mtshan gyis rang bzhin gyis stong par gsungs tshul, tshul des ston pa smra ba bla na med par grub pa'o
gru.english: Which brings us to that second topic: establishing the fact that the very highest position ever taken by the Able One is that emptiness and dependence amount to the same thing. Here we proceed through three points: (1) how we accept the position that all the normal workings of things are perfectly valid where everything is empty of any nature of its own, and invalid in the opposite case; (2) the way in which Lord Buddha stated that-for the reason that all the things there are occur in dependence-they must be empty of any nature of their own; and (3) how this situation then establishes that our Teacher is a matchless instructor.

gru.acip: GNYIS PA CHOS THAMS CAD RTEN 'BREL YIN PA'I RGYU MTSAN GYIS RANG BZHIN GYIS STONG PAR GSUNGS TSUL LA BZHI, CHOS THAMS CAD LTOS NAS GRUB PAS RTEN 'BREL DU BSTAN PA, RTEN 'BREL DU GRUB PAS RANG BZHIN GYIS STONG PAR BSTAN PA, RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB NA MYANG 'DAS SOGS MI RUNG PAR BSTAN PA, GSUNG DE RNAMS LA RGOL BA GZHAN GYIS GLAGS MI RNYED PAR BSTAN PA'O,,
gru.wylie: gnyis pa chos thams cad rten 'brel yin pa'i rgyu mtshan gyis rang bzhin gyis stong par gsungs tshul la bzhi, chos thams cad ltos nas grub pas rten 'brel du bstan pa, rten 'brel du grub pas rang bzhin gyis stong par bstan pa, rang bzhin gyis grub na myang 'das sogs mi rung par bstan pa, gsung de rnams la rgol ba gzhan gyis glags mi rnyed par bstan pa'o
gru.english: Which brings us to the second point from before: the way in which Lord Buddha stated that-for the reason that all the things there are occur in dependence-they must be empty of any nature of their own. Here we proceed in four steps: (1) demonstrating that everything in the universe is an event which occurs in dependence, since it exists in reliance; (2) demonstrating how things are empty of any nature of their own, since they exist in dependence; (3) demonstrating how things like nirvana and such would no longer be feasible, if they existed through some nature of their own; and (4) demonstrating how no one else could ever dispute, successfully, these statements.

gru.acip: ,LTOS MED NAM MKHA'I ME TOG BZHIN, ,DES NA MA BRTEN YOD MA YIN, ,NGO BOS GRUB NA DE 'GRUB PA, ,RGYU DANG RKYEN LA BLTOS PAR 'GAL,
gru.wylie: ltos med nam mkha'i me tog bzhin, ,des na ma brten yod ma yin, ,ngo bos grub na de 'grub pa, ,rgyu dang rkyen la bltos par 'gal
gru.english: Things that never relied Upon other things Are as likely as flowers That grow in thin air. Thus we can say That there exists nothing Which is not dependent. It would be a contradiction To say that something Which existed in and of itself Could ever come to exist Through relying on Its causes and conditions.

gru.acip: DON NI, BLTOS MED KYI CHOS NI NAM MKHA'I ME TOG BZHIN GZHI MA GRUB PA YIN LA
gru.wylie: don ni, bltos med kyi chos ni nam mkha'i me tog bzhin gzhi ma grub pa yin la
gru.english: What these lines are expressing is that, first of all, a thing which never relied upon other things is as likely as a flower that grew in mid-air; which is to say, there could be no such thing.

gru.acip: DES NA MA BRTEN PA'AM MA BLTOS PAR GRUB PA'I 'DUS BYAS DANG 'DUS MA BYAS KYI CHOS CUNG ZAD KYANG YOD PA MA YIN TE,
gru.wylie: des na ma brten pa'am ma bltos par grub pa'i 'dus byas dang 'dus ma byas kyi chos cung zad kyang yod pa ma yin te
gru.english: Thus we can say that there exists nothing-not the slightest thing, whether we are talking about something produced by causes & conditions, or an existing entity not so produced-which is not dependent, or which has come about without relying on something else.

gru.acip: CHOS THAMS CAD NGO BOS GRUB NA CHOS DE 'GRUB PA 'DUS BYAS RGYU DANG RKYEN TSOGS PA DANG, 'DUS MA BYAS CHA SHAS TSOGS PA LA BLTOS NAS GRUB DGOS PA 'GAL LO ZHES PA'O,,
gru.wylie: chos thams cad ngo bos grub na chos de 'grub pa 'dus byas rgyu dang rkyen tshogs pa dang, 'dus ma byas cha shas tshogs pa la bltos nas grub dgos pa 'gal lo zhes pa'o
gru.english: That is-if every existing entity existed in and of itself-then it would be a contradiction ever to say that this thing existed through relying upon the convening of its causes and conditions (in the case of a produced entity), or else through the joining together of its parts (in the case of an existing entity not brought about through causes & conditions). This is what the lines are saying. Those dependent are empty

gru.acip: DON NI, NGO BOS GRUB PA'I RANG BZHIN GZHAN DU LDOG PA MED PA'I PHYIR
gru.wylie: don ni, ngo bos grub pa'i rang bzhin gzhan du ldog pa med pa'i phyir
gru.english: Here's what this verse is saying. A nature to things where they existed through some essence of their own is something that could never be stopped-they could never turn to something else.

gru.acip: CHOS RNAMS LA NGO BOS GRUB PA'I RANG BZHIN 'GA' YOD NA MYA NGAN LAS 'DAS PA THOB PA MI RUNG ZHING MTHAR 'DZIN GYI SPROS PA KUN KYANG LDOG PA MED PAR GSUNGS SO ZHES PA'O,,
gru.wylie: chos rnams la ngo bos grub pa'i rang bzhin 'ga' yod na mya ngan las 'das pa thob pa mi rung zhing mthar 'dzin gyi spros pa kun kyang ldog pa med par gsungs so zhes pa'o
gru.english: As such, Lord Buddha has stated that-if there were any nature to things where they existed through some essence of their own-it would be wrong to say then that someone could attain nirvana: passing beyond grief. So too we could then never put a stop to the way we imagine things, as we grasp to the extremes. Beyond any dispute

gru.acip: DON NI, GONG GI RGYU MTSAN DE'I PHYIR STON PA KHYOD KYIS CHOS THAMS CAD LA NGO BOS GRUB PA'I RANG BZHIN RNAM PAR BRAL LO ZHES
gru.wylie: don ni, gong gi rgyu mtshan de'i phyir ston pa khyod kyis chos thams cad la ngo bos grub pa'i rang bzhin rnam par bral lo zhes
gru.english: What these lines are saying is the following. Thus-for the reasons just mentioned-you, our Teacher, have spoken well of how all existing things are devoid of any nature of their own, where they could exist through some self-essence.

gru.acip: GSUM PA TSUL DES STON PA SMRA BA BLA NA MED PAR GRUB PA NI, RANG BZHIN 'GA' YANG ZHES SOGS TSIGS BCAD GNYIS KYIS STON LA,
gru.wylie: gsum pa tshul des ston pa smra ba bla na med par grub pa ni, rang bzhin 'ga' yang zhes sogs tshigs bcad gnyis kyis ston la
gru.english: With this we have come to our third point from before: how this situation then establishes that our Teacher is a matchless instructor. This is expressed in the two verses of Je Tsongkapa's root text which include, "no real nature to things at all."

gru.acip: DON NI, CHOS GANG GI STENG DU 'ANG RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA 'GA' YANG MED PA DANG,
gru.wylie: don ni, chos gang gi steng du 'ang rang bzhin gyis grub pa 'ga' yang med pa dang
gru.english: Here's the point here. Let's start with two ideas. The first is that there is no nature to things at all where they exist as real; and this is true of every single entity in the universe.

gru.acip: DON NI PHYI NANG GI DNGOS PO 'DI DAG KUN THA SNYAD KYIS BTAGS PA TZAM MA GTOGS BTAGS DON NGO BOS GRUB PAS STONG PA DANG,
gru.wylie: don ni phyi nang gi dngos po 'di dag kun tha snyad kyis btags pa tsam ma gtogs btags don ngo bos grub pas stong pa dang
gru.english: Here's then what these two verses are saying. All of these inner and outer entities are nothing more than labeled with terms-the final labeled object that we come out with then is empty of existing through any essence of its own.

gru.acip: RTEN CING 'BREL 'BYUNG GI MING NYID KYIS NI DNGOS PO RNAMS RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA NYID DU 'DZIN PAR BYED NA DA KO STE DA NI DNGOS SMRA BA'I SKYE BO 'DI RNAMS
gru.wylie: rten cing 'brel 'byung gi ming nyid kyis ni dngos po rnams rang bzhin gyis grub pa nyid du 'dzin par byed na da ko ste da ni dngos smra ba'i skye bo 'di rnams
gru.english: And yet still there are people who use this same name-of "events that occur in dependence and connection"-to hang onto the idea, who persist in believing, that things could have some nature of their own. And these people are those who belong to that group which believes that-if something performs a function-then it must be real.

gru.acip: DON NI, RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA CHU'I TSA BA LTAR GSAR DU BCOS PA MIN PA, BRAN LTAR GZHAN LA BLTOS PA MED PA DANG,
gru.wylie: don ni, rang bzhin gyis grub pa chu'i tsha ba ltar gsar du bcos pa min pa, bran ltar gzhan la bltos pa med pa dang
gru.english: What these lines are saying is this: suppose, first of all, that things existed through some nature of their own, and that they were never something which was freshly concocted-in the way, for example, that water at a normal temperature is then heated up. Which is to say, suppose that things never relied upon each other, in the way that a servant might depend upon their master.

gru.acip: RTEN 'BREL BLTOS NAS GRUB PA DANG GSAR DU BCOS MA GNYIS PO JI LTA BUR NA GZHI GCIG LA MI 'GAL BAR GZHI MTHUN DU 'DU BA NYID DU 'GYUR TE MI 'GYUR RO ZHES PA'O,,
gru.wylie: rten 'brel bltos nas grub pa dang gsar du bcos ma gnyis po ji lta bur na gzhi gcig la mi 'gal bar gzhi mthun du 'du ba nyid du 'gyur te mi 'gyur ro zhes pa'o
gru.english: But suppose on the other hand that things do exist in reliance upon each other, as dependent events, entirely concocted, fresh creations. How could we ever say that these two things were not perfectly contradictory, and could both of them apply, to a single base of reference? Certainly we could not. The entire universe as an illusion

gru.acip: DON NI, RGYU MTSAN GONG GI DE'I PHYIR BRTEN NAS 'BYUNG BA'I CHOS GANG YIN PA THAMS CAD NGO BOS GRUB PA'I RANG BZHIN GYIS NI YE GDOD MA NAS RNAM PAR DBEN NAS MED KYANG
gru.wylie: don ni, rgyu mtshan gong gi de'i phyir brten nas 'byung ba'i chos gang yin pa thams cad ngo bos grub pa'i rang bzhin gyis ni ye gdod ma nas rnam par dben nas med kyang
gru.english: These lines are expressing the following idea. Thus-meaning, for the reason presented above-it is that all of these events which occur through a process of dependence are also things which have been, for time with no beginning, entirely devoid of any nature where any of them existed through some essential nature of its own.

gru.acip: RANG BZHIN DER GRUB PA LTAR SNANG BAS NA, RTEN 'BYUNG GI CHOS 'DI DAG KUN STON PA KHYOD KYIS SGYU MA JI LTA BA BZHIN DU GSUNGS SO ZHES PA'O,,
gru.wylie: rang bzhin der grub pa ltar snang bas na, rten 'byung gi chos 'di dag kun ston pa khyod kyis sgyu ma ji lta ba bzhin du gsungs so zhes pa'o
gru.english: And yet because these things did still appear as though they existed in nature, all of these events which occur in dependence were spoken by you, our Teacher, to be something that was similar to an illusion. A nature beyond all dispute

gru.acip: GNYIS PA RTEN 'BREL GSUNG TSUL GYI SGO NAS BYE BRAG TU BSTOD PA LA GSUM, RTEN 'BREL GSUNG TSUL DGOS PA DANG BCAS PA, THUB PAS NAN TAN GYIS BSGRUBS PA'I CHOS TSUL ZAB MO RTOGS PAR BZHED PA 'KHRUNGS TSUL, DE LA BRTEN NAS THUB PA'I DGONGS PA JI LTAR BTZAL BA'O,,
gru.wylie: gnyis pa rten 'brel gsung tshul gyi sgo nas bye brag tu bstod pa la gsum, rten 'brel gsung tshul dgos pa dang bcas pa, thub pas nan tan gyis bsgrubs pa'i chos tshul zab mo rtogs par bzhed pa 'khrungs tshul, de la brten nas thub pa'i dgongs pa ji ltar btsal ba'o
gru.english: Which brings us to our second more general section from above-a more particular praise for the way in which Lord Buddha describes dependent events. We proceed in three steps: a description of how he described these events, and the need for him to do so; how it is that the Able One gave birth to the manner in which he deigned to perceive the profound way of all things, making insistent efforts; and how-based on all this-we ourselves can seek out the true intent of the Able One.

gru.acip: GNYIS PA THUB PAS NAN TAN GYIS BSGRUBS PA'I CHOS TSUL ZAB MO RTOGS PAR BZHED LA 'KHRUNGS TSUL LA GNYIS, THUB PAS NAN TAN GYIS BSGRUBS TSUL DANG, DE RTOGS PAR BZHED PA 'KHRUNGS TSUL LO,,
gru.wylie: gnyis pa thub pas nan tan gyis bsgrubs pa'i chos tshul zab mo rtogs par bzhed la 'khrungs tshul la gnyis, thub pas nan tan gyis bsgrubs tshul dang, de rtogs par bzhed pa 'khrungs tshul lo
gru.english: Which brings us to our second step from above: How it is that the Able One gave birth to the manner in which he deigned to perceive the profound way of all things, making insistent efforts. Here there are two sections: how it was that the the Able One made his insistent efforts; and the exact way in which he deigned to perceive that particular object.

gru.acip: GRANGS MED PA'I BSKAL PA MANG POR YANG NAS YANG DU BTANG NAS BSGRUBS SO ZHES PA'O,,
gru.wylie: grangs med pa'i bskal pa mang por yang nas yang du btang nas bsgrubs so zhes pa'o
gru.english: And you gave all this away, again and again, for a great many countless eons of time. This then was how you accomplished your practice. Weak good fortune

gru.acip: ,KHYOD KYI BLA MED THEG PA'I TSUL, ,YOD DANG MED PA'I MTHA' SPANGS TE, ,JI BZHIN 'GREL PAR LUNG BSTAN PA, ,KLU SGRUB GZHUNG LUGS KUNDA'I TSAL,
gru.wylie: khyod kyi bla med theg pa'i tshul, ,yod dang med pa'i mtha' spangs te, ,ji bzhin 'grel par lung bstan pa, ,klu sgrub gzhung lugs kunda'i tshal
gru.english: Just how you interpreted The system of the way Which has no equal- Rejecting the extremes Of things existing Or not- Was indeed foretold. The paths of your classics, Our Arya Nagarjuna, Are a jasmine garden of wonder.

gru.acip: JI LTA BA BZHIN DGONGS PA 'GREL PAR LANG GSHEGS SU LUNG BSTAN PA'I 'PHAGS MCHOG KLU SGRUB KYI GZHUNG LUGS RTZA SHES LA SOGS PA'I KUN DA'I TSAL LTA BU DE,
gru.wylie: ji lta ba bzhin dgongs pa 'grel par lang gshegs su lung bstan pa'i 'phags mchog klu sgrub kyi gzhung lugs rtsa shes la sogs pa'i kun da'i tshal lta bu de
gru.english: And just how you, our Arya Nagarjuna-highest of realized beings-interpreted the true intent of this teaching is something which was indeed foretold you would do, in the sutra called A Journey to Langka. You did so in the paths of your classics-works such as The Root Text on Wisdom and so on-which are like a jasmine garden of wonder.

gru.acip: ,'DREN MCHOG DES DKA' BA DPAG MED KYIS, ,NAN TAN SNYING POR MDZAD NAS BSGRUB PA 'DI, ,THABS GANG ZHIG GIS 'PHEL BAR 'GYUR SNYAM PA'I, ,RNAM PAR DPYOD PAS NYIN MTSAN 'DA' BAR SHOG,
gru.wylie: 'dren mchog des dka' ba dpag med kyis, ,nan tan snying por mdzad nas bsgrub pa 'di, ,thabs gang zhig gis 'phel bar 'gyur snyam pa'i, ,rnam par dpyod pas nyin mtshan 'da' bar shog
gru.english: This then is the way Which the highest of guides Practiced himself, Undertaking infinite hardships To make it the very Heart of his path. May I as well Devote day and night, Considering, with my deepest insight, How I might Increase these teachings.

gru.acip: DON NI, 'DREN PA MCHOG SH'AKYA'I RGYAL PO DES DKA' BA BRGYA PHRAG DPAG MED KYI SGO NAS NAN TAN SNYING POR MDZAD NAS BSGRUBS PA'I BSTAN PA RIN PO CHE 'DI,
gru.wylie: don ni, 'dren pa mchog shAkya'i rgyal po des dka' ba brgya phrag dpag med kyi sgo nas nan tan snying por mdzad nas bsgrubs pa'i bstan pa rin po che 'di
gru.english: What this verse is saying is that this then is the way, the precious teaching, which the highest of guides-the King of the Shakya People-practiced himself, by undertaking infinite thousands of hardships to make it the very heart of his path.

gru.acip: ,RTEN CING 'BREL PAR 'BYUNG BA'I TSUL, ,'GAL BA DANG NI MA GRUB PAR, ,MTHONG BA 'DI YIS KHYOD KYI LUGS, ,JI LTAR KHONG DU CHUD PAR NUS,
gru.wylie: rten cing 'brel par 'byung ba'i tshul, ,'gal ba dang ni ma grub par, ,mthong ba 'di yis khyod kyi lugs, ,ji ltar khong du chud par nus
gru.english: This is where Those who see it That the way in which Events occur in Dependence & connection Must be a contradiction, Or simply mistaken, Would never be able then To grasp your system.

gru.acip: ,LTOS MED NAM MKHA'I ME TOG BZHIN, ,DES NA MA BRTEN YOD MA YIN, ,NGO BOS GRUB NA DE 'GRUB PA, ,RGYU DANG RKYEN LA BLTOS PAR 'GAL,
gru.wylie: ltos med nam mkha'i me tog bzhin, ,des na ma brten yod ma yin, ,ngo bos grub na de 'grub pa, ,rgyu dang rkyen la bltos par 'gal
gru.english: Things that never relied Upon other things Are as likely as flowers That grow in thin air. Thus we can say That there exists nothing Which is not dependent. It would be a contradiction To say that something Which existed in and of itself Could ever come to exist Through relying on Its causes and conditions.

gru.acip: ,KHYOD KYI BLA MED THEG PA'I TSUL, ,YOD DANG MED PA'I MTHA' SPANGS TE, ,JI BZHIN 'GREL PAR LUNG BSTAN PA, ,KLU SGRUB GZHUNG LUGS KUNDA'I TSAL,
gru.wylie: khyod kyi bla med theg pa'i tshul, ,yod dang med pa'i mtha' spangs te, ,ji bzhin 'grel par lung bstan pa, ,klu sgrub gzhung lugs kunda'i tshal
gru.english: Just how you interpreted The system of the way Which has no equal- Rejecting the extremes Of things existing Or not- Was indeed foretold. The paths of your classics, Our Arya Nagarjuna, Are a jasmine garden of wonder.

gru.acip: ,'DREN MCHOG DES DKA' BA DPAG MED KYIS, ,NAN TAN SNYING POR MDZAD NAS BSGRUB PA 'DI, ,THABS GANG ZHIG GIS 'PHEL BAR 'GYUR SNYAM PA'I, ,RNAM PAR DPYOD PAS NYIN MTSAN 'DA' BAR SHOG,
gru.wylie: 'dren mchog des dka' ba dpag med kyis, ,nan tan snying por mdzad nas bsgrub pa 'di, ,thabs gang zhig gis 'phel bar 'gyur snyam pa'i, ,rnam par dpyod pas nyin mtshan 'da' bar shog
gru.english: This then is the way Which the highest of guides Practiced himself, Undertaking infinite hardships To make it the very Heart of his path. May I as well Devote day and night, Considering, with my deepest insight, How I might Increase these teachings.

gru.acip: (1) BSTAN PA BLA NA MED PAR SGRUB PA,
gru.wylie: (1) bstan pa bla na med par sgrub pa
gru.english: Establishing that these teachings are the highest of all

gru.acip: (2) STON PA BLA NA MED PAR SGRUB PA,
gru.wylie: (2) ston pa bla na med par sgrub pa
gru.english: Establishing that their teacher is as well the highest

gru.acip: (b2) STONG PA DANG RTEN 'BREL DON GCIG PA THUB PA'I BZHED PA MCHOG TU SGRUB PA,
gru.wylie: (b2) stong pa dang rten 'brel don gcig pa thub pa'i bzhed pa mchog tu sgrub pa
gru.english: Establishing the fact that the very highest position ever taken by the Able One is that emptiness and dependence amount to the same thing

gru.acip: (a4) CHOS THAMS CAD LTOS NAS GRUB PAS RTEN 'BREL DU BSTAN PA,
gru.wylie: (a4) chos thams cad ltos nas grub pas rten 'brel du bstan pa
gru.english: Demonstrating that everything in the universe is an event which occurs in dependence, since it exists in reliance

gru.acip: (b4) RTEN 'BREL DU GRUB PAS RANG BZHIN GYIS STONG PAR BSTAN PA,
gru.wylie: (b4) rten 'brel du grub pas rang bzhin gyis stong par bstan pa
gru.english: Demonstrating how things are empty of any nature of their own, since they exist in dependence

gru.acip: (c4) RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB NA MYANG 'DAS SOGS MI RUNG PAR BSTAN PA,
gru.wylie: (c4) rang bzhin gyis grub na myang 'das sogs mi rung par bstan pa
gru.english: Demonstrating how things like nirvana and such would no longer be feasible, if they existed through some nature of their own

gru.acip: (c3) TSUL DES STON PA SMRA BA BLA NA MED PAR GRUB PA,
gru.wylie: (c3) tshul des ston pa smra ba bla na med par grub pa
gru.english: How this situation then establishes that our Teacher is a matchless instructor

gru.acip: (b) THUB PAS NAN TAN GYIS BSGRUBS PA'I CHOS TSUL ZAB MO RTOGS PAR BZHED PA 'KHRUNGS TSUL,
gru.wylie: (b) thub pas nan tan gyis bsgrubs pa'i chos tshul zab mo rtogs par bzhed pa 'khrungs tshul
gru.english: How it is that the Able One gave birth to the manner in which he deigned to perceive the profound way of all things, making insistent efforts

gru.acip: (1) THUB PAS NAN TAN GYIS BSGRUBS TSUL,
gru.wylie: (1) thub pas nan tan gyis bsgrubs tshul
gru.english: How it was that the the Able One made his insistent efforts

gru.acip: SKYABS 'GRO SEMS BSKYED, SANGS RGYAS CHOS DANG TSOGS KYI MCHOG RNAMS LA, BYANG CHUB BAR DU BDAG NI SKYABS SU MCHIS, BDAG GIS SBYIN SOGS BGYIS PA'I BSOD NAMS KYIS, 'GRO LA PHAN PHYIR SANGS RGYAS 'GRUB PAR SHOG
gru.wylie: skyabs 'gro sems bskyed, sangs rgyas chos dang tshogs kyi mchog rnams la, byang chub bar du bdag ni skyabs su mchis, bdag gis sbyin sogs bgyis pa'i bsod nams kyis, 'gro la phan phyir sangs rgyas 'grub par shog
gru.english: Refuge and The Wish I go for refuge To the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha Until I achieve enlightenment. By the power Of the goodness that I do In giving and the rest, May I reach Buddhahood For the sake Of every living being.

gru.acip: DE MIN 'DI NAS DON CHEN PO BSGRUB RGYU MA BYUNG BAR STONG LOG TU SHOR NA SEMS CAN, GYI DON BYED PA LTA BZHAG RANG GIS BDE 'GRO'I RTEN RNYED PA TZAM YANG DKA' BA YOD
gru.wylie: de min 'di nas don chen po bsgrub rgyu ma byung bar stong log tu shor na sems can, gyi don byed pa lta bzhag rang gis bde 'gro'i rten rnyed pa tsam yang dka' ba yod
gru.english: If now I cannot accomplish this great goal, if all I have gained is wasted, then there is little point in claiming to work for every living being: it is little likely that I myself will be able even to reach the higher realms of suffering life

gru.acip: DGE BSHES STON PA'I ZHAL NAS BSTAN PA THAMS CAD GRUB BZHI LAM GYIS 'KHYER SHES, PA NGA'I BLA MA'I KHYAD CHOS MIN PA LA MED
gru.wylie: dge bshes ston pa'i zhal nas bstan pa thams cad grub bzhi lam gyis 'khyer shes, pa nga'i bla ma'i khyad chos min pa la med
gru.english: As the spiritual friend Tonpa has spoken, The ability to wrap the totality of the teachings into one is a special skill of my Lama's—for the Father, nothing is not a

gru.acip: RGYAL MCHOG BSKAL BZANG RGYA MTSOS KYANG, RNAM THAR GTZANG MA DGA' LDAN BKA' BRGYUD PHYOGS RE 'DZIN PA'I GRUB MTHA' MIN NO MDO SNGAGS THAMS CAD GDAMS PAR SHAR BA'I BSHAD SGRUB BSTAN PA'I NYING KHU LAGS SO
gru.wylie: rgyal mchog bskal bzang rgya mtshos kyang, rnam thar gtsang ma dga' ldan bka' brgyud phyogs re 'dzin pa'i grub mtha' min no mdo sngags thams cad gdams par shar ba'i bshad sgrub bstan pa'i nying khu lags so
gru.english: That highest of Victors, Kelsang Gyatso, has said too: It is a pure tradition, The lineage of the Heaven of Bliss; It is no biased Or limited school of thought. It is the essential nectar, To learn and practice the Teaching So all the open and secret Word Seems personal instruction.

gru.acip: ZHES GSUNGS PA LTAR RANG RE RI PO DGA' LDAN PA'I BKA' SROL 'DI LA MDO SNGAGS, GANG GI THAD NAS KYANG GZHAN LA MED PA'I BSTAN PA CHA TSANG LA DRI MA DANG BRAL BA ZAB CING MYUR BA SOGS KHYAD CHOS 'GRAN ZLA MED PA MANG PO YOD PAS 'JAM MGON TZONG KHA PA CHEN POS SROL PHYE BAR MDZAD PA'I BYANG CHUB LAM RIM 'DI LA'ANG GRUB MTHA' GZHAN PHYOGS PA DANG BKA' GDAMS GONG MA RNAMS LA MED PA'I MAN NGAG MTHA' YAS PA LTA BU YOD LA
gru.wylie: zhes gsungs pa ltar rang re ri po dga' ldan pa'i bka' srol 'di la mdo sngags, gang gi thad nas kyang gzhan la med pa'i bstan pa cha tshang la dri ma dang bral ba zab cing myur ba sogs khyad chos 'gran zla med pa mang po yod pas 'jam mgon tsong kha pa chen pos srol phye bar mdzad pa'i byang chub lam rim 'di la'ang grub mtha' gzhan phyogs pa dang bka' gdams gong ma rnams la med pa'i man ngag mtha' yas pa lta bu yod la
gru.english: And that's just the way it is: our scriptural tradition, that of the Mount of the Heaven of Bliss, is one that is totally complete and spotless, on both sides—in the open and the secret Word. It is a kind of teaching that is found nowhere else. And it possesses a multitude of unique and unrivalled qualities: its depth, the speed with which it works, and so on. Thus it is that this teaching on the Steps of the Path to Buddhahood, as it was inaugurated by the Gentle Protector, Tsongkapa, looks to contain a nearly limitless number of spiritual advices found in none of the other schools, nor even among the older Keepers of the Word.

gru.acip: 'DI LA SA BCAD DU PHYE NA LAM GYI RTZA BA BSHES GNYEN BSTEN PA'I TSUL BSTEN NAS, BLO JI LTAR SBYANG BA'I TSUL LAM SGRUB PA'I MTHUN RKYEN 'GRUB PA DANG 'GAL RKYEN ZHI BAR GSOL BA 'DEBS PA SKYE BA THAMS CAD DU BLA MAS RJES SU GZUNG STE SA LAM GYI 'BRAS BU MNGON DU BYED NUS PAR SMON PA DANG BCAS TE BZHI YOD PA LAS
gru.wylie: 'di la sa bcad du phye na lam gyi rtsa ba bshes gnyen bsten pa'i tshul bsten nas, blo ji ltar sbyang ba'i tshul lam sgrub pa'i mthun rkyen 'grub pa dang 'gal rkyen zhi bar gsol ba 'debs pa skye ba thams cad du bla mas rjes su gzung ste sa lam gyi 'bras bu mngon du byed nus par smon pa dang bcas te bzhi yod pa las
gru.english: The text of the Source of All My Good may be divided into four different parts: 1) the very root of the path, which is how to take a Lama and serve himor her properly; 2) how to train your mind, once you have taken a Lama; 3) a request so that you can attain all the favorable conditions for succeeding in the path, and stop all the circumstances that might prevent you from doing so; and then finally 4) a prayer that in all your future lives you may be taken under the care of a Lama, and so gain the strength to reach the final end of the various levels and

gru.acip: CES GSUNGS PA LTAR RANG GIS SA LAM GYI YON TAN ZHIG 'THOB PAR 'DOD NA THOG, MAR DE BSGRUB TSUL STON PA'I BLA MA ZHIG NGES PAR BSTEN DGOS
gru.wylie: ces gsungs pa ltar rang gis sa lam gyi yon tan zhig 'thob par 'dod na thog, mar de bsgrub tshul ston pa'i bla ma zhig nges par bsten dgos
gru.english: All these lines are saying the same thing: if you have any hope of reaching up to the high spiritual qualities of the various levels and paths, then fromthe outset you must absolutely find and follow a Lama who can show you how to

gru.acip: DE 'DRA'I BLA MA'ANG GANG BYUNG BYUNG GI MING DU BTAGS PAS MI CHOG PAR MDO SDE RGYAN, LAS GSUNGS PA LTAR SGO GSUM DUL BA ZHI BA NYE BAR ZHI BA STE BSLAB GSUM DANG, LDAN PA SLOB MA LAS YON TAN LHAG PA BRTZON 'GRUS CHEN PO DANG LDAN PA LUNG GI, YON TAN PHUN SUM TSOGS PA MNGA' BA DE KHO NA NYID RTOGS PA CHOS SMRA BA LA MKHAS PA SLOB MA LA BRTZE BA CHEN PO YOD PA CHOS JI TZAM 'CHAD KYANG SKYO NGAL MED PA BCAS YON TAN BCU DANG LDAN PA ZHIG DANG
gru.wylie: de 'dra'i bla ma'ang gang byung byung gi ming du btags pas mi chog par mdo sde rgyan, las gsungs pa ltar sgo gsum dul ba zhi ba nye bar zhi ba ste bslab gsum dang, ldan pa slob ma las yon tan lhag pa brtson 'grus chen po dang ldan pa lung gi, yon tan phun sum tshogs pa mnga' ba de kho na nyid rtogs pa chos smra ba la mkhas pa slob ma la brtse ba chen po yod pa chos ji tsam 'chad kyang skyo ngal med pa bcas yon tan bcu dang ldan pa zhig dang
gru.english: And the Lama that we are describing here is not just any one you might happen to come across; it's not just anyone they call a "Lama." Rather, he must have in himthe ten high qualities described in the Jewel of the Sutras. He must first of all be subdued, at peace, and at high peace; that is to say, he must possess all three of the trainings. He must display fine spiritual qualities that exceed those of his student, and exhibit exceptional effort. He should have a total mastery of the Dharma in the form of scripture, and should have realized suchness. He should be highly skilled in teaching the Dharma, he must have a great love for his disciples, and he must never become tired or discouraged in his teaching, no matter how much or how often he is called upon to do so.

gru.acip: BLA MAS CHOS BSTAN PA RNAM LA SGRUB PA SNYING POR BYED PA SOGS SO SO'I BLO NUS DANG, BSTUN TE THABS SNA TSOGS KYIS BSTEN DGOS TSUL GSUNGS PA YIN LA
gru.wylie: bla mas chos bstan pa rnam la sgrub pa snying por byed pa sogs so so'i blo nus dang, bstun te thabs sna tshogs kyis bsten dgos tshul gsungs pa yin la
gru.english: The root text here then is saying that we must take ourselves to our Lama in a whole different number of ways, in keeping with our personal mental

gru.acip: DA DUNG KHUR DU MA SONG BAR RGYAN DU BZUNG STE BDAG SKAL BA RE BZANG SNYAM DU DAD CING, GUS PA CHEN PO'I SGO NAS BSAM SBYOR GNYIS KYIS TSUL BZHIN BSTEN TE BSGRUB PA DGOS
gru.wylie: da dung khur du ma song bar rgyan du bzung ste bdag skal ba re bzang snyam du dad cing, gus pa chen po'i sgo nas bsam sbyor gnyis kyis tshul bzhin bsten te bsgrub pa dgos
gru.english: And I amnot to view this service as if I were laboring for someone else; on the contrary, I should not even see it as a burden, but rather as a reward: it is my great good fortune to have the opportunity. And so I must succeed in serving himor her in both my thoughts and actions, with the deepest feelings of

gru.acip: DE LTAR BSHES GNYEN BSTEN TSUL 'DI BZANG PO BYUNG NA TSE RABS THAMS CAD DU BLA, MAS RJES SU 'DZIN PA DANG DA RES KYI LUS RTEN 'DI ANG KI DANG POR BRTZIS TE 'DI NAS BZUNG DAL BRGYAD 'BYOR BCU TSANG BA'I MI'I RTEN BZANG BAR MA CHAD PAR THOB NAS DAL 'BYOR GYI ANG KI MA 'KHRUGS PAR CHOS NYAMS SU BLANGS TE SANGS RGYAS KYI GO 'PHANG SGRUB THUB PA 'ONG
gru.wylie: de ltar bshes gnyen bsten tshul 'di bzang po byung na tshe rabs thams cad du bla, mas rjes su 'dzin pa dang da res kyi lus rten 'di ang ki dang por brtsis te 'di nas bzung dal brgyad 'byor bcu tshang ba'i mi'i rten bzang bar ma chad par thob nas dal 'byor gyi ang ki ma 'khrugs par chos nyams su blangs te sangs rgyas kyi go 'phang sgrub thub pa 'ong
gru.english: If our service of our Lama is good, then in all our future lives we will find ourselves taken under the care of Lamas. Then too we can count the life we have found now as the first in a long and unbroken series of lives in which we enjoy each of the eight spiritual leisures, and the ten fortunes. And there will never again be any mistake in this particular arithmetic: we will always enjoy the exact number of circumstances needed to follow our practice of the Dharma, and so finally reach the state of perfect enlightenment.

gru.acip: BZHI DGE SLONG 'CHAR KA LTA BU LA TSANG BA LAS MGON PO KLU SGRUB LA'ANG DNGOS, GNAS PA MTSANG LA RANG RES KYANG SANGS RGYAS DANG KHYAD MED PA'I BLA MA MJAL TE CHOS GSUNGS PA SOGS KYIS DE DAG DOD THUB SBYOR DU YOD PA LAS DNGOS GNAS MA TSANG YANG DAL BA BRGYAD DNGOS SU TSANG BA LA GTZO BOR DGONGS TE GSUNGS PA RED
gru.wylie: bzhi dge slong 'char ka lta bu la tshang ba las mgon po klu sgrub la'ang dngos, gnas pa mtshang la rang res kyang sangs rgyas dang khyad med pa'i bla ma mjal te chos gsungs pa sogs kyis de dag dod thub sbyor du yod pa las dngos gnas ma tshang yang dal ba brgyad dngos su tshang ba la gtso bor dgongs te gsungs pa red
gru.english: All four of the fortunes just explained have been possessed even by the likes of the monk Udayi, whereas the same cannot be said even for the Savior Nagarjuna, who lacked them in their literal form. We too have met our Lamas, who are no different froma Buddha, and they have spoken the Dharma and so on; these are a full substitute yes, but we cannot say that we have all those fortunes in their literal form. We do however enjoy all eight of the spiritual leisures; these then are our primary advantage, and it's with this fact in mind that the verse reads "life of leisure."

gru.acip: GZHAN PHYIR SNYING BRTZE ZHES PA SBYIN BDAG DANG BLA MA SOGS KYIS GANG ZAG GZHAN, RANG NYID KYI PHYIR DU SNYING BRTZE BAS CHOS KYI MTHUN RKYEN ZAS GOS SOGS STER BA'AM, CHOS STON PA SOGS TE RANG GIS CHOS SGRUB PA'I MTHUN RKYEN SBYIN MKHAN YOD PA LA BYA DGOS
gru.wylie: gzhan phyir snying brtse zhes pa sbyin bdag dang bla ma sogs kyis gang zag gzhan, rang nyid kyi phyir du snying brtse bas chos kyi mthun rkyen zas gos sogs ster ba'am, chos ston pa sogs te rang gis chos sgrub pa'i mthun rkyen sbyin mkhan yod pa la bya dgos
gru.english: What does it mean when the reference says, "There is compassion for the sake of others?" The "others" here refers to ourselves; our sponsors and Lamas and other such persons who act for our sake, motivated by compassion, to see that we are provided with all the conditions that will facilitate our practice of the Dharma: they give us food, or clothes, and other necessities; They teach us the Dharma; and so on. Therefore this phrase should be understood as describing the good fortune to have around us those who give us the things we need to

gru.acip: RANG CAG MI KHOM PA BRGYAD DANG BRAL NAS CHOS SGRUB TU YOD PA'I DUS 'DIR MI SGRUB, PAR TSE 'DI PA'I 'CHING THAG GIS BCINGS TE RNYED BKUR SNYAN GRAGS DANG 'JIG RTEN MTHUN 'JUG SGRUB PA SOGS DON MIN GYI LAS MANG PO BRTZAM STE BREL BA BYED PA 'DI MI KHOM PA DGU PA ZHIG CHED DU BTZAL BA YIN ZHING
gru.wylie: rang cag mi khom pa brgyad dang bral nas chos sgrub tu yod pa'i dus 'dir mi sgrub, par tshe 'di pa'i 'ching thag gis bcings te rnyed bkur snyan grags dang 'jig rten mthun 'jug sgrub pa sogs don min gyi las mang po brtsam ste brel ba byed pa 'di mi khom pa dgu pa zhig ched du btsal ba yin zhing
gru.english: So you and I are free of the eight ways in which a person can lack spiritual opportunity; and yet we fail to work here now, in the days when we do have a Dharma to practice. We find ourselves locked in the handcuffs of the present life; we throw ourselves into all sorts of meaningless activities aimed at gaining material things, or other people's approval, or a taste of fame; we want to fit into the world's way of life, and so on. These make us so busy that it's almost as if we have taken special care to invent a ninth way of lacking spiritual

gru.acip: RANG GIS SGRUB PAR BYED NA GNAS SKABS MNGON MTHO LHA MI'I RTEN BZANG NAS MTHAR, THUG RDO RJE 'CHANG GI GO 'PHANG MAN CHAD NGES PAR SGRUB NUS PA'I RTEN BZANG KHYAD PAR, CAN RNYED PA 'DI NYID DON CHEN PO DANG LDAN PAR SHES SHING NGO 'PHROD PAR GYUR NAS
gru.wylie: rang gis sgrub par byed na gnas skabs mngon mtho lha mi'i rten bzang nas mthar, thug rdo rje 'chang gi go 'phang man chad nges par sgrub nus pa'i rten bzang khyad par, can rnyed pa 'di nyid don chen po dang ldan par shes shing ngo 'phrod par gyur nas
gru.english: If I truly undertake to do so, it is certain that I can achieve everything from temporal goals, such as achieving a good and useful kind of birth in the higher forms of life—among humans or the beings of pleasure—on up to the ultimate goal of becoming the Keeper of the Diamond himself. All this can be achieved because of the extraordinary kind of life I have now gained; seek to understand this fact, try to truly recognize how significant the one chance is.

gru.acip: RNYED PAR DKA' ZHING RNYED NA DON CHE BA'I DAL 'BYOR TSANG BA'I RDO RJE'I LUS RTEN 'DI LTA, BUD RES THENGS GCIG TZAM RNYED PA'I SKABS 'DIR 'KHOR BA MTHA' MED KYI NGANG TSUL DANG SANGS RGYAS KYI GO 'PHANG BSKAL PA MANG POR SGRUB DGOS LUGS SOGS BSAMS NAS NYIN MTSAN BAR MA CHAD PAR GNAS SKABS KUN TU DON MED STONG LOG TU MA SHOR BAR SNYING PO LEN 'DOD KYI BLO RGYUN CHAD MED PAR SKYE BAR BYIN GYIS RLOBS SHIG CES GSOL BA BTAB PA YIN
gru.wylie: rnyed par dka' zhing rnyed na don che ba'i dal 'byor tshang ba'i rdo rje'i lus rten 'di lta, bud res thengs gcig tsam rnyed pa'i skabs 'dir 'khor ba mtha' med kyi ngang tshul dang sangs rgyas kyi go 'phang bskal pa mang por sgrub dgos lugs sogs bsams nas nyin mtshan bar ma chad par gnas skabs kun tu don med stong log tu ma shor bar snying po len 'dod kyi blo rgyun chad med par skye bar byin gyis rlobs shig ces gsol ba btab pa yin
gru.english: What we are requesting fromour Lama here is that he bless us to achieve this same level of obsession: bless me first to realize that the excellent life I've found, complete with every spiritual leisure, is hard to find and—once found—is ever so valuable. Now, in the one and only time I have ever managed to win this diamond body and life, let me think of how the circle of suffering has absolutely no beginning; how one must normally practice for many millions of years to reach the state of a Buddha; and other such truths. And grant me then to wish, and never stop to wish, that I could take this life's essence night and day: that I could at every given moment keep this precious time from being lost to actions which are pointless, devoid of any meaning. STEPS SHARED WITH THOSE OF LESSER CAPACITY IV. Steps Shared with Those of Lesser Capacity

gru.acip: TSE 'DI LONG MED MYUR DU 'CHI 'GYUR ZHING, GSOD SAR KHRID PA'I DUD 'GRO JI BZHIN DU, SKAD CIG RE RE BZHIN YANG 'CHI LA NYE DENG BYA SANG BYA'I BSAM PA MA RDZOGS PAR, BSAM PA BRGYA PHRAG MA BSAMS GCIG 'OG TSUD, GSHIN RJE 'JIGS RUNG NYAM PA'I MDUN BSUS NAS MAL GYI THA MAR DBUGS SDUD SROG CHAD TSE CHOS LAS GZHAN GYIS MI PHAN RIN CHEN GRUB
gru.wylie: tshe 'di long med myur du 'chi 'gyur zhing, gsod sar khrid pa'i dud 'gro ji bzhin du, skad cig re re bzhin yang 'chi la nye deng bya sang bya'i bsam pa ma rdzogs par, bsam pa brgya phrag ma bsams gcig 'og tshud, gshin rje 'jigs rung nyam pa'i mdun bsus nas mal gyi tha mar dbugs sdud srog chad tshe chos las gzhan gyis mi phan rin chen grub
gru.english: You are not long in this life Death comes quick; You step ever nearer to it With every moment that passes, Moving on like an animal Dragged to the slaughterhouse. Your plans for today Your plans for tomorrow Will never all be filled; Let go all your thousand plans, Devote yourself to one. You will be summoned into The awesome presence of Lord Death; The end is lying on your bed, The breathing stops, the life is gone. And on this day, My Rinchen Drup, Nothing but the Dharma Is any help to you.

gru.acip: CHAD LTA BA RNAMS LA THOG BABS PA DANG 'DRA BA YIN GZHAN YANG MKHAS GRUB MNGON, SHES CAN MANG POS GZIGS PAS KYANG RANG GZHAN YI BAR DO DANG SKE BA SNGA PHYI DRAN PA'I RNAM THAR SHIN TU MANG ZHING PHYI ROL BA'I DRANG SRONG MNGON SHES CAN RNAMS KYIS KYANG SKYE BA BRGYAD CU DRAN PA LA SOGS PA BYUNG BA YIN
gru.wylie: chad lta ba rnams la thog babs pa dang 'dra ba yin gzhan yang mkhas grub mngon, shes can mang pos gzigs pas kyang rang gzhan yi bar do dang ske ba snga phyi dran pa'i rnam thar shin tu mang zhing phyi rol ba'i drang srong mngon shes can rnams kyis kyang skye ba brgyad cu dran pa la sogs pa byung ba yin
gru.english: For those who deny that life goes on, hearing these lines is like being struck by a bolt of lightning. There are moreover quite numerous accounts of many wise and accomplished practitioners who have used clairvoyance to perceive the past and future lives, as well as the state between death and rebirth, which they and others have passed through. There are also cases like those of the non-Buddhist adepts who attain clairvoyance that allows themto recall eighty of their different lives.

gru.acip: ZHES GSUNGS PA LTAR 'CHI BA'I SKABS DANG PHYI MA'I SKYE BA LEN PA'I TSE CHOS MA, GTOGS GZHAN GANG GIS KYANG MI PHAN PAS NA TSE BLOS BTANG GIS PHYI MAR PHAN THABS KYI 'CHI CHOS GSHA' MA ZHIG NGES PAR SGRUB PA GAL CHE STE RANG RE RNAMS SHI BA'I RJES SU RIG PA RGYUN CHAD NAS MED DE MI 'GRO BAR SKYE BA RE MA BLANGS THABS MED LA DE LEN SA BDE 'GRO NGAN 'GRO GNYIS LAS MA 'DAS
gru.wylie: zhes gsungs pa ltar 'chi ba'i skabs dang phyi ma'i skye ba len pa'i tshe chos ma, gtogs gzhan gang gis kyang mi phan pas na tshe blos btang gis phyi mar phan thabs kyi 'chi chos gsha' ma zhig nges par sgrub pa gal che ste rang re rnams shi ba'i rjes su rig pa rgyun chad nas med de mi 'gro bar skye ba re ma blangs thabs med la de len sa bde 'gro ngan 'gro gnyis las ma 'das
gru.english: Since nothing else can help then, it is essential that we give up on life and be sure to devote ourselves to death, by practicing some pure form of the Dharma, as a way to assist our future self. It's not as if, after you and I have died, the streamof our mind just stops and we turn into nothing. Rather we have no choice but to take another birth. And there are no more than two places where we can take that birth: in the higher realms of happiness, or the lower realms of misery.

gru.acip: BCAS RKYANG TSUN CHOD LA MNANGS CHUNG MI BYED PAR TSUL BZHIN DU SRUNG DGOS PAS NA, DGE BSNYEN NAS DGE SLONG GI BAR GYI SO THAR RIS BRGYAD PO'I BSLAB SDOM GANG KHAS BLANGS PA RNAMS LA MKHAS PAR BSLAB CING SGRUB PA SNYING POR BYAS TE
gru.wylie: bcas rkyang tshun chod la mnangs chung mi byed par tshul bzhin du srung dgos pas na, dge bsnyen nas dge slong gi bar gyi so thar ris brgyad po'i bslab sdom gang khas blangs pa rnams la mkhas par bslab cing sgrub pa snying por byas te
gru.english: For this reason we must be sure never to think lightly of any transgression we might commit, even down to the minor vows; we must absolutely keep all our vows just so. And so you must become masters in understanding all the various vows and advices related to whichever one of the eight sets of the vows of freedomyou have assented to follow. And once you have learned themperfectly, well then you must make them the essence of your practice.

gru.acip: BOD KHA CIG LTAR YID BYED THAMS CAD BKAG STE NAG THOM ME BAR GNAS PA LA ZHI, GNAS DANG DE THOG NAS SEMS ZHES PA DE DBYIBS DANG KHA DOG GANG DU GRUB 'DUG BRTAGS NAS MA RNYED PA'I SEMS KYI KUN RDZOB PA'I NGO BO STONG SANG TZAM LA LHAG MTHONG DU BSHAD PA LTA BU MIN PAR
gru.wylie: bod kha cig ltar yid byed thams cad bkag ste nag thom me bar gnas pa la zhi, gnas dang de thog nas sems zhes pa de dbyibs dang kha dog gang du grub 'dug brtags nas ma rnyed pa'i sems kyi kun rdzob pa'i ngo bo stong sang tsam la lhag mthong du bshad pa lta bu min par
gru.english: There are Tibetan schools of the past too which have taught that meditative quietude consisted of not thinking about anything at all, just keeping the mind in some dark state of dullness. The high state of perfect insight then they explain as moving in this stupor to a realization of the pure and simple emptiness of the deceptive nature of the mind—except they describe this emptiness as what you come to when you analyze whether or not what we call the "mind" consists of any shape or color, and then fail to find that it's any

gru.acip: DNGOS GRUB RNAM PA GNYIS GANG LAS SGRUB PA'I GZHI'AM BRTEN SA LTA BU NI DBANG GI, DUS SU GANG KHAS BLANGS PA'I RTZA BA DANG YAN LAG GI DAM TSIG DANG SDOM PA MTHA' DAG RNAM PAR DAG PAR BSRUNG BA NYID YIN PAS
gru.wylie: dngos grub rnam pa gnyis gang las sgrub pa'i gzhi'am brten sa lta bu ni dbang gi, dus su gang khas blangs pa'i rtsa ba dang yan lag gi dam tshig dang sdom pa mtha' dag rnam par dag par bsrung ba nyid yin pas
gru.english: What then is it that can give you these attainments? Their cause or foundation, the very support that holds themall up, is one thing, and only one: to keep most pure every one of the root and secondary pledges and vows which you took upon yourself when you were granted the empowerments.

gru.acip: GANG LA BSGOM PA DANG LDAN ZHING, GAL TE DAM TSIG SDOM LA GNAS SKYE 'DIR LAS DBANG GIS MA 'GRUB SKYE BA GZHAN DU DNGOS GRUB THOB
gru.wylie: gang la bsgom pa dang ldan zhing, gal te dam tshig sdom la gnas skye 'dir las dbang gis ma 'grub skye ba gzhan du dngos grub thob
gru.english: But those who keep The meditation, And further maintain Their pledges and vows Will reach the goal Within this life or, Past deeds preventing, At least in the next.

gru.acip: CES DANG RNAM GROL ZLA BAS, MA BSGOM SGYUR KYANG LTUNG MED NA SKYE BA BCU DRUG DAG NA 'GRUB
gru.wylie: ces dang rnam grol zla bas, ma bsgom sgyur kyang ltung med na skye ba bcu drug dag na 'grub
gru.english: Vibhuti Chandra says as well, Even should he fail to meditate, A person will reach the goal Within the length of sixteen lives, So long as a downfall has not occurred.

gru.acip: CES PA DANG DAM TSIG LNGA PA LAS KYANG, GAL TE LTUNG BA MED GYUR NA SKYE BA BCU DRUG DAG NA 'GRUB
gru.wylie: ces pa dang dam tshig lnga pa las kyang, gal te ltung ba med gyur na skye ba bcu drug dag na 'grub
gru.english: The Book of the Five Pledges concurs: As long as there is no downfall, The goal is reached in sixteen lives.

gru.acip: CES SOGS GYUD DANG GRUB CHEN DU MAS LAN CIG MA YIN PAR GSUNGS PAS DE, 'DRA'I BKA' BSLU BA MED PA LA BCOS MA MIN PA'I NGES PA'AM YID CHES BRTAN PO GZHAN YIS BSGYUR DU MI BTUB PA'I GTING PHYIN PA RNYED PAR GUR NAS SROG DANG BSDOS
gru.wylie: ces sogs gyud dang grub chen du mas lan cig ma yin par gsungs pas de, 'dra'i bka' bslu ba med pa la bcos ma min pa'i nges pa'am yid ches brtan po gzhan yis bsgyur du mi btub pa'i gting phyin pa rnyed par gur nas srog dang bsdos
gru.english: You must come to know these facts with genuine certainty—that is, you must seek a kind of firmbelief in themthat is deeply rooted within you, so much that no one else could ever change your mind. And because of this knowledge you must then protect your commitments, "even if it costs your life."

gru.acip: MA ZHUGS PAR DAM PA ZHES PA NAM YANG MI SLU BA'I SKYES BU TSAD MA THUN PA, SANGS RGYAS BCOM LDAN 'DAS LA BYED PAS DE'I GSUNG RAB LAS BYUNG BA'I MAN NGAG JI LTA BA BZHIN DU SGRUB NUS PAR GSOL BA BTAB PA YIN GSUNGS
gru.wylie: ma zhugs par dam pa zhes pa nam yang mi slu ba'i skyes bu tshad ma thun pa, sangs rgyas bcom ldan 'das la byed pas de'i gsung rab las byung ba'i man ngag ji lta ba bzhin du sgrub nus par gsol ba btab pa yin gsungs
gru.english: What we are requesting of our Lama here, said our Lama, is that he or she grant us the power never to wander onto one of these paths. We are asking for the strength to practice, in exactly the proper way, the instructions found in the highest of spoken words. And these are the teachings of the "Holy One" mentioned in the verse. These words refer to a person who can never deceive us; a being who is incapable of lying; that ultimate meditator who keeps the practice of the times: they refer to the victorious, transcendent Buddha. THE CONCLUSION XIII. A Request for Good Circumstances

gru.acip: DE YANG LAM LA PHYIN CI MA LOG PA DANG LAM GOL BA DANG LAM NOR BAR SHOR BA, SOGS BZANG NGAN SNA TSOGS YOD CING RANG CAG GIS NYAMS SU BLANG BYA'I LAM DE LAM BZANG PO MA NOR MA 'KHRUL BA ZHIG LA MA ZHUGS NA 'KHRUL BA'I LAM PHYIN CI LOG CIG LA LO STONG DU SGRUB PA BYAS KYANG 'BRAS BU BZANG PO MA 'KHRUL BA 'BYUNG BA GTAN NAS MI SRID LA
gru.wylie: de yang lam la phyin ci ma log pa dang lam gol ba dang lam nor bar shor ba, sogs bzang ngan sna tshogs yod cing rang cag gis nyams su blang bya'i lam de lam bzang po ma nor ma 'khrul ba zhig la ma zhugs na 'khrul ba'i lam phyin ci log cig la lo stong du sgrub pa byas kyang 'bras bu bzang po ma 'khrul ba 'byung ba gtan nas mi srid la
gru.english: So there are these different sorts of spiritual paths, of widely varying quality: some are totally correct, some are totally wrong, some slide off from right to wrong, and on and on. You and I have access to a path which is pure, and unmistaken, and free of any error. We can either enter it now or go off on some wrong road that goes astray. If this second is our choice then we can try to follow such a way for a thousand years, but it is an absolute impossibility that we will derive fromit any good or certain result.

gru.acip: CHOS MDO SNGAGS BSHAD SGRUB ZUNG 'BREL GYI, LAM NGO BO GRANGS DANG GO RIM SOGS GNAD TSANG LA MA NOR YONGS RDZOGS LA DUS NYIN BZHIN BAG CHAGS CI THEBS KYIS
gru.wylie: chos mdo sngags bshad sgrub zung 'brel gyi, lam ngo bo grangs dang go rim sogs gnad tshang la ma nor yongs rdzogs la dus nyin bzhin bag chags ci thebs kyis
gru.english: Where every crucial point Is absolutely complete, and without any error The definitions, And divisions, and order, and all other details Of the path Where open and secret, teaching and practice combine.

gru.acip: BSHAR SGOM LA NYAMS LEN DNGOS GZHIR BYAS, DE'I SBYOR DANG MJUG GI RIM PA YANG, RJE BLA MA'I BKA' BZHIN LEGS BSGRUB STE, DAL 'BYOR LA SNYING PO LEN PAR 'TSAL
gru.wylie: bshar sgom la nyams len dngos gzhir byas, de'i sbyor dang mjug gi rim pa yang, rje bla ma'i bka' bzhin legs bsgrub ste, dal 'byor la snying po len par 'tshal
gru.english: For the main stage Follow review meditation on these, Every day that goes by It will plant many seeds in your mind. Follow as well For the stages of starting and ending Just what Our Lord Lama has taught us to do.

gru.acip: RANG LUGS KYI MKHAS GRUB DU MA'I GZHUNG MAN NGAG DANG BCAS PAR THOS BSAM SGOM, GSUM GYI SGO NAS LAM RIM LA RTZOL BCAS RTZOL MED KYI MYONG BA LEGS PAR BTON
gru.wylie: rang lugs kyi mkhas grub du ma'i gzhung man ngag dang bcas par thos bsam sgom, gsum gyi sgo nas lam rim la rtsol bcas rtsol med kyi myong ba legs par bton
gru.english: Rather take yourself through the great texts and special advices of the wise and accomplished masters of our own tradition, all in the proper order of learning, contemplation, and meditation. Get to a point where you are totally fluent in all the Steps of the path, first by making a conscious effort, and then later in

gru.acip: KLU SGRUB YAB SRAS THOGS MED MCHED LA SOGS, SNGON MED SHING RTA CHE LAS LEGS BRGYUD PA LHA GCIG PHUL BYUNG ZHABS DANG 'BROM STON RJE'I DRIN LAS GANGS CAN 'GRO BA'I DPAL DU THOB
gru.wylie: klu sgrub yab sras thogs med mched la sogs, sngon med shing rta che las legs brgyud pa lha gcig phul byung zhabs dang 'brom ston rje'i drin las gangs can 'gro ba'i dpal du thob
gru.english: It descended in a perfect stream Fromthe Father, Nagarjuna, and his Son; FromAsanga, the Brother, and others too, Unprecedented fromgreat innovators. Because of the kindness of one great God Along with the Lord named Dromton Je, Those of the Land of Snow had the glorious Fortune to obtain this teaching.

gru.acip: SNYIGS MA'I DUS 'DIR MANG THOS SGRUB LA BRTZON, CHOS BRGYAD SPANGS PAS DAL 'BYOR DON YOD BYED, MGON PO KHYOD KYI RLABS CHEN MDZAD PA LA, BDAG CAG BSAM PA THAG PAS YI RANG NGO
gru.wylie: snyigs ma'i dus 'dir mang thos sgrub la brtson, chos brgyad spangs pas dal 'byor don yod byed, mgon po khyod kyi rlabs chen mdzad pa la, bdag cag bsam pa thag pas yi rang ngo
gru.english: Here in the age Of degeneration You made every effort To gain great learning; You threw away The eight worldly thoughts And so made use Of Your leisure and fortune. Savior, we rejoice We are glad, happy deep inside, For what you have done, So good and powerful. ACI Daily Practice X A Thousand Angels of the Heaven of Bliss

gru.acip: DPAL LDAN RTZA BA'I BLA MA RIN PO CHE, BDAG GI SPYI BOR PAD ZLA'I STENG BZHUGS LA, BKA' DRIN CHEN PO'I SGO NAS RJES BZUNG STE, SKU GSUNG THUGS KYI DNGOS GRUB RTZOL DU GSOL
gru.wylie: dpal ldan rtsa ba'i bla ma rin po che, bdag gi spyi bor pad zla'i steng bzhugs la, bka' drin chen po'i sgo nas rjes bzung ste, sku gsung thugs kyi dngos grub rtsol du gsol
gru.english: Come I pray and sit My root Lama Shining and precious Upon the lotus Atop my head; Take me after You In great kindness, Grant that I attain Your body, speech and mind.

gru.acip: DNGOS GRUB KUN 'BYUNG THUB DBANG RDO RJE 'CHANG
gru.wylie: dngos grub kun 'byung thub dbang rdo rje 'chang
gru.english: I pray to the One who Holds the Diamond The source from where Every goal is found; ACI Daily Practice X A Thousand Angels of the Heaven of Bliss

gru.acip: DPAL LDAN RTZA BA'I BLA MA RIN PO CHE, BDAG GI SNYING KHAR PAD ZLA'I STENG BZHUGS LA, BKA' DRIN CHEN PO'I SGO NAS RJES BZUNG STE, SKU GSUNG THUGS KYI DNGOS GRUB RTZOL DU GSOL
gru.wylie: dpal ldan rtsa ba'i bla ma rin po che, bdag gi snying khar pad zla'i steng bzhugs la, bka' drin chen po'i sgo nas rjes bzung ste, sku gsung thugs kyi dngos grub rtsol du gsol
gru.english: Come I pray and sit My root Lama Shining and precious Upon the lotus In my heart; Take me after You In great kindness, Grant that I attain Your body, speech and mind. ACI Daily Practice X A Thousand Angels of the Heaven of Bliss

gru.acip: DPAL LDAN RTZA BA'I BLA MA RIN PO CHE, BDAG GI SNYING KHAR PAD ZLA'I STENG BZHUGS LA, BKA' DRIN CHEN PO'I SGO NAS RJES BZUNG STE, MCHOG DANG THUN MONG DNGOS GRUB RTZOL DU GSOL
gru.wylie: dpal ldan rtsa ba'i bla ma rin po che, bdag gi snying khar pad zla'i steng bzhugs la, bka' drin chen po'i sgo nas rjes bzung ste, mchog dang thun mong dngos grub rtsol du gsol
gru.english: Come I pray and sit My root Lama Shining and precious Upon the lotus In my heart; Take me after You In great kindness, Grant that I attain Both common and highest goals. ACI Daily Practice X A Thousand Angels of the Heaven of Bliss

gru.acip: LA GSUM BSAM PAS RKYEN NGAN LAM DU BSGYUR TSUL TSE GCIG GI NYAMS LEN DANG BLO, 'BYONGS PA'I TSAD SBYOR BAS RKYEN NGAN LAM DU BSGYUR TSUL DANG DAM TSIG BSLAB PA'O GNYIS PA SEMS BSKYED DNGOS LA SLOB TSUL LA GNYIS SMON SEMS BSKYED TSUL DANG 'JUG SDOM LEN TSUL LO GNYIS PA SEMS BSKYED NAS SPYOD PA LA SLOB TSUL LA DRUG SBYIN PA LA SLOB TSUL TSUL KHRIMS LA SLOB TSUL BZOD PA LA BRTZON 'GRUS LA BSAM GTAN LA SHES RAB LA SLOB TSUL LO DRUG PA LA GSUM MNYAM GZHAG NAM MKHA'I RNAL 'BYOR RJES THOB SGYU MA'I DBU MA'I LTA BA'I KHYAD CHOS SO GNYIS PA RDO RJE THEG PA'I LAM LA BLO SBYONG TSUL
gru.wylie: la gsum bsam pas rkyen ngan lam du bsgyur tshul tshe gcig gi nyams len dang blo, 'byongs pa'i tshad sbyor bas rkyen ngan lam du bsgyur tshul dang dam tshig bslab pa'o gnyis pa sems bskyed dngos la slob tshul la gnyis smon sems bskyed tshul dang 'jug sdom len tshul lo gnyis pa sems bskyed nas spyod pa la slob tshul la drug sbyin pa la slob tshul tshul khrims la slob tshul bzod pa la brtson 'grus la bsam gtan la shes rab la slob tshul lo drug pa la gsum mnyam gzhag nam mkha'i rnal 'byor rjes thob sgyu ma'i dbu ma'i lta ba'i khyad chos so gnyis pa rdo rje theg pa'i lam la blo sbyong tshul
gru.english: III. How to Train Ones Heart in the Path for Those of Greater Scope A. How to develop the Wish for enlightenment (bodhichitta) 1. How to train oneself in the things that cause the Wish a. How to develop the very root of the path: great b. How to meditate on the practice of seeing oneself and others as equal, and then exchanging each other i. How to meditate on seeing onself and others as ii. How to meditate on exchanging oneself and a) Problems that are caused by cherishing b) Benefits that come from cherishing others c) A summary of the problems and the d) The actualpractice of exchanging oneself and others iii. How to practice giving and taking Contemplation One c. A presentation of remaining points on the training of the mind i. How to use your attitude to transform bad circumstances into the path ii. How to turn this entire life into practice, and how to judge whether or not you've succeeded in training the mind iii. How to use your actions to transform bad circumstances into the path, and training oneself in the pledges 2. How to train oneself in the Wish itself a. How to develop the Wish in the form of a prayer b. How to take the vow to act out the Wish B. How to train oneself in the activities of a bodhisattva, once one has developed the Wish 1. How to train oneself in giving 2. How to train oneself in ethical living 3. How to train oneself in not getting angry 4. How to train oneself in joyful effort 5. How to train oneself in meditation 6. How to train oneself in wisdom a. The deep practice of empty space—the period in b. The deep practice of illusion—the period afterwards c. Features of the view of the middle way Followed by "How to Train Ones Heart in the Path of the Way of the Diamond..." We often see the practice of giving and taking placed within the context of the teachings on exchanging oneself and others, as for example in the outline to A Seven-Part Ritual including All the Essential Points for Collecting Goodness and Purifying Wrong, composed by the first Changkya Rinpoche, Ngawang Lobsang Chunden (1642-1714), a former life of Pabongka Rinpoche: Contemplation One

gru.acip: THEG PA CHEN POR 'JUG PA'I SGO SPYOD PA'I RTEN SEMS BSKYED TSUL LA RGYU 'BRAS MAN NGAG, BDUN GYI SGO NAS BSKYED TSUL BDAG GZHAN MNYAM BRJE'I SGO NAS BSKYED TSUL GNYIS RGYU 'BRAS MAN NGAG BDUN GYI SGO NAS SEMS BSKYED TSUL LA SEMS CAN THAMS CAD LA SEMS SNYOM PAR SGRUB PA GZHAN DON DON GNYER GYI BLO BSKYED PA SEMS BSKYED TSUL DNGOS GSUM GZHAN DON DON GNYER GYI BLO BSKYED PA LA MAR SHES DRIN DRAN DRIN BZO YID 'ONG GI BYAMS PA SNYING RJE CHEN PO LHAG BSAM RNAM DAG STE DRUGBDG GZHAN MNYAM BRJE'I SGO NAS SEMS BSKYED TSUL LA GTONG LEN SBYONG BA DANG SEMS BSKYED TSUL GNYIS
gru.wylie: theg pa chen por 'jug pa'i sgo spyod pa'i rten sems bskyed tshul la rgyu 'bras man ngag, bdun gyi sgo nas bskyed tshul bdag gzhan mnyam brje'i sgo nas bskyed tshul gnyis rgyu 'bras man ngag bdun gyi sgo nas sems bskyed tshul la sems can thams cad la sems snyom par sgrub pa gzhan don don gnyer gyi blo bskyed pa sems bskyed tshul dngos gsum gzhan don don gnyer gyi blo bskyed pa la mar shes drin dran drin bzo yid 'ong gi byams pa snying rje chen po lhag bsam rnam dag ste drugbdg gzhan mnyam brje'i sgo nas sems bskyed tshul la gtong len sbyong ba dang sems bskyed tshul gnyis
gru.english: A. How to develop the Wish for enlightenment, which is the door for entering the greater way, and the basis for engaging in the deeds of the 1. Developing the Wish through the seven-step, cause-and-effect method a. Reaching a state of equal-mindedness towards all living beings b. Developing the state of mind wherein one strives to achieve the goals of others i. Recognizing them as your mother ii. Recalling their kindness iii. Repaying their kindness iv. The "beautiful" form of love v. Great compassion vi. Personalresponsibility c. How the Wish is actually developed 2. Developing the Wish through the practice of exchanging oneself and a. The practice of giving and taking b. How the Wish is developed Contemplation One The following section describing an extraordinary combination of the two methods of reaching the Wish for Enlightenment comes from A Detailed Outline of the "Dissection" Instruction for the Steps of the Path to Buddhahood. A copy of this text was found in the personal library of Kyabje Trijang Rinpoche, tutor of His Holiness, the present Dalai Lama.

gru.acip: BDAG BDE GZHAN GYI SDUG BSNGAL DAG, YANG DAG BRJE BAR MA BYAS NA SANGS RGYAS NYID DU MI GRUB CING 'KHOR BA NA YANG BDE BA MED
gru.wylie: bdag bde gzhan gyi sdug bsngal dag, yang dag brje bar ma byas na sangs rgyas nyid du mi grub cing 'khor ba na yang bde ba med
gru.english: Suppose you failto exchange perfectly Your happiness and the pain of others; You'll never achieve then enlightenment, Nor find any happiness here in life.

gru.acip: MA DAG SKYE 'CHI YI 'PHRUL 'KHOR, RTOG PAS BTAGS TZAM LAS GZHAN PA'I GRUB RGYU RDUL TZAM YANG MED PAS MA 'JIGS CHOS NYID NGANG SKYUR ZHOG
gru.wylie: ma dag skye 'chi yi 'phrul 'khor, rtog pas btags tsam las gzhan pa'i grub rgyu rdul tsam yang med pas ma 'jigs chos nyid ngang skyur zhog
gru.english: This huge machine that runs our birth and death as impure things Is something that's created by our projections, and nothing more: It has in it not a single atom of existing some other way— Throw yourself then into the realm of the real, pure fearlessness. Contemplation Two He also gives compassion as a reason to practice giving and taking:

gru.acip: GTONG LAN LA NYAMS LEN SNYING POR BYED NA RJE BTZUN NGAG DBANG RDO RJE'I PHYAG BZHES LTAR, THOG MAR SKYABS 'GRO SEMS BSKYED BYA DE NAS GTONG LEN SGOM LA BDAG GI BSAM PA'I STOBS DAG DANG ZHES SOGS KYIS BDEN STOBS BRJOD DE NAS BSGOM BYA SGOM BYED LA SOGS PA'I CHOS THAMS CAD RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA MED PA'I NGES SHES DRANGS NAS
gru.wylie: gtong lan la nyams len snying por byed na rje btsun ngag dbang rdo rje'i phyag bzhes ltar, thog mar skyabs 'gro sems bskyed bya de nas gtong len sgom la bdag gi bsam pa'i stobs dag dang zhes sogs kyis bden stobs brjod de nas bsgom bya sgom byed la sogs pa'i chos thams cad rang bzhin gyis grub pa med pa'i nges shes drangs nas
gru.english: Contemplation Six If you plan to make the meditation on giving and taking the central point of your practice, you can follow the custom of the venerable Ngawang Dorje. First go through the process of going for refuge and bringing up the Wish for enlightenment. After that, do the meditation on giving and taking. Next make the prayer that your meditation actually come true, by the power of truth, with the lines that include, "By the pureness of the power of my intentions..." [The full prayer here reads: By the pureness of the power of my intentions, By the power of the blessings of Those Gone Thus, By the powers of the realm of emptiness, May all the goals that I may have, And all my wishes, whatever they be, Come true, with perfect ease.] After this, bring up in your mind the clear conviction that no object in the universe has any nature of its own: not the object being meditated upon, nor the person meditating upon it, nor anything else at all. And then [continue with certain special practices, followed by a final dedication and prayer]. Contemplation Seven: An explanation of the practice of giving and taking in the second reference from the Offering to Lamas Later in his same commentary, Ngulchu Dharma Bhadra discusses the second reference to the practice of giving and taking from the Offering to Lamas:

gru.acip: DE NAS 'DI LTAR 'GRUB PA SKAL BA BZANG SNYAM DU DGA' BA BSKYED PA'I MTHAR BDE STONG LA, MNYAM PAR BZHAG DE LAS LDANG BA NA DE NI RANG GI SEMS KYIS BCOS PA TZAM YIN PAS SEMS CAN THAMS CAD SDUG BSNGAL DANG BRAL ZHING BDE BA DANG LDAN PA ZHIG NGAS BYA'O SNYAM PA'I LHAG BSAM BSKYED SLAR YANG RANG LA DE LTA BU'I NUS PA YOD MED BRTAGS PA NA GZHAN DON LTA BZHAG RANG DON YANG MTHAR MA PHYIN PAS DA LTA NUS PA MED
gru.wylie: de nas 'di ltar 'grub pa skal ba bzang snyam du dga' ba bskyed pa'i mthar bde stong la, mnyam par bzhag de las ldang ba na de ni rang gi sems kyis bcos pa tsam yin pas sems can thams cad sdug bsngal dang bral zhing bde ba dang ldan pa zhig ngas bya'o snyam pa'i lhag bsam bskyed slar yang rang la de lta bu'i nus pa yod med brtags pa na gzhan don lta bzhag rang don yang mthar ma phyin pas da lta nus pa med
gru.english: Contemplation Seven Bring up in your heart then a feeling of joy, thinking how very fortunate you are to have undertaken this practice. Finally then enter into deep meditation on detong. When you come out of this meditation, bring up in your heart that state of personal responsibility where you say to yourself, "Every living being must be freed from every form of suffering, and must come to have every form of happiness. I myself will assure that they do." Realize too that this is possible because everything here is only a construction of your own mind. Next go back and examine yourself, to see whether or not you presently possess any capacity to actually bring about this goal. You will soon realize that for the present you have failed to realize even your own goals, much less achieve the capacity to help others achieve theirs.

gru.acip: 'DI NI SNGAGS KYI SKABS NAS BSHAD PA'I RDO RJE'I BZLAS PA DANG CHA 'DRA ZHING MKHAS GRUB, RJES RJE BLA MAR MGON PO KHYOD KYI ZHAL GYI DBUGS TZAM YANG MTHA' DAG 'GRO LA SMAN PA'I RGYUR 'GYUR NA ZHES SOGS BSTOD PA MDZAD PA'ANG 'DI LA DGONGS PA RED 'DI DAG LA MAN NGAG GZHAN YANG YOD MOD RGYUN DU CHAGS MED MI BYED PA'I RIGS LA 'CHAD DU MI RUNG GSUNGS
gru.wylie: 'di ni sngags kyi skabs nas bshad pa'i rdo rje'i bzlas pa dang cha 'dra zhing mkhas grub, rjes rje bla mar mgon po khyod kyi zhal gyi dbugs tsam yang mtha' dag 'gro la sman pa'i rgyur 'gyur na zhes sogs bstod pa mdzad pa'ang 'di la dgongs pa red 'di dag la man ngag gzhan yang yod mod rgyun du chags med mi byed pa'i rigs la 'chad du mi rung gsungs
gru.english: This meditation, by the way, has some parallels in the practice of the "recitation of diamond," which is part of the secret teachings. This is also the point that the great Kedrup has in mind in his famed lines of praise, addressed to our Lord Lama [Je Tsongkapa]: A single puff of breath from Your holy lips, O Savior, Brings soothing benefit to limitless beings. There are many books of instruction on these points, but it would be improper for me to explain them to an audience that was not following the practice of desirelessness on a regular basis. Some indication of the ultimate power of the practice is imparted in a very special praise of Pabongka Rinpoche himself, written by his devoted disciple, Kyabje Trijang Rinpoche—tutor to His Holiness the XIVth Dalai Lama, and Root Lama of our own Root Lama, Khen Rinpoche Geshe Lobsang Tharchin:

gru.acip: DA HRIL TE DRIL NA SNA BUG GI RLUNG PHAR LA 'GRO TSE RANG RGYUD KYI CHOS BDE DGE THAMS, CAD 'GRO DRUG GI MA SEMS CAN KUN LA GTONG BA DANG RLUNG NANG DU RGYU TSE 'GRO KUN GYI SDIG SDUG BSNGAL THAMS CAD RANG LA BLANGS TSUL DE LTA'I GTONG LEN RNAL 'BYOR GYIS SEMS BYANG CHUB MCHOG LA GZHOL BAR BYA DUS GNAS SKABS JI LTAR GYUR KYANG RUNG SKYABS BLA MA MCHOG GSUM SNYING LA BSAM THABS GTONG LEN GNYIS PO NYAMS SU BLANGS CHOS 'DI 'DRAR 'PHRAD PA SKAL BA BZANG DON JI LTAR BSAM BZHIN LEGS 'GRUB PAR SKYABS MCHOG GSUM DAM PAS BYIN GYIS RLOBS
gru.wylie: da hril te dril na sna bug gi rlung phar la 'gro tshe rang rgyud kyi chos bde dge thams, cad 'gro drug gi ma sems can kun la gtong ba dang rlung nang du rgyu tshe 'gro kun gyi sdig sdug bsngal thams cad rang la blangs tshul de lta'i gtong len rnal 'byor gyis sems byang chub mchog la gzhol bar bya dus gnas skabs ji ltar gyur kyang rung skyabs bla ma mchog gsum snying la bsam thabs gtong len gnyis po nyams su blangs chos 'di 'drar 'phrad pa skal ba bzang don ji ltar bsam bzhin legs 'grub par skyabs mchog gsum dam pas byin gyis rlobs
gru.english: Now I'll put it all together for you; See Your breath as it passes out, Give With it Dharma: happiness, good, To Every mother in six realms. Then When you breathe in take from every Being All their bad deeds and their pain. Go Thus deep, give and also take, Lose Your heart to this supreme Wish. When And wherever you may be Run To your Lama and Three Jewels. Live In this way, both give and take; Luck Amazing that I found this Dharma. Contemplation Eight Grant Me your blessing holy Jewels, Let Every Dharma wish come true. The first Changkya Rinpoche describes the role of breath in the meditation of giving and taking as well in a work entitled, "Entertainment for those of the Higher Way," being an Explanation of the Letter of Instruction known as the "Eight Verses," a Work of Advice on Practicing the Wish for Enlightenment composed by the Great Bodhisattva, Dorje Senge of Langri Tang:

gru.acip: BYAMS PA'I DMIGS PA RTZAL DU BTON NAS GTONG BA NI SEMS CAN RNAMS DON SGRUB PA'I, PHYIR YID BZHIN GYI NI LUS SU BSGYUR ZHES DANG SDONG BKOD DANG RDO RJE RGYAL MTSAN GYI MDO SOGS LAS KYANG LUS LONGS SPYOD SOGS GTONG BAR GSUNGS PA BZHIN RANG GI LUS GANG 'DOD KYI DNGOS PAR SPRUL NAS SNOD DANG BCUD LA BTANG BAS
gru.wylie: byams pa'i dmigs pa rtsal du bton nas gtong ba ni sems can rnams don sgrub pa'i, phyir yid bzhin gyi ni lus su bsgyur zhes dang sdong bkod dang rdo rje rgyal mtshan gyi mdo sogs las kyang lus longs spyod sogs gtong bar gsungs pa bzhin rang gi lus gang 'dod kyi dngos par sprul nas snod dang bcud la btang bas
gru.english: Here is how to do the practice of giving, by focusing upon the category of love. Remember the text that says, In order to accomplish the goals of every living being, Turn your body into the form of a wish-fulfilling jewel. Sutras such as Stalks in Array and the Victory Banner of Diamond also state that we should learn to give away our body and our possessions. Here you turn your body into anything and everything that someone might want to have, and then send it out to the world, and to the people living in the world.

gru.acip: DE'I MJUG TU DE LTAR BDAG GIS GTONG LEN BYAS PA BZHIN DE LTAR GYUR 'DUG GAM MI, 'DUG BRTAG PA'I TSE RANG GI MOS PA TZAM LAS DA LTA DNGOS GNAS PAR PHAN BDE DNGOS SU SGRUB PA DE LTAR GYUR MI 'DUG PAR MTHONG NAS DA NI DE LTAR DNGOS SU 'ONG BA ZHIG BYED SNYAM DU RANG GI NGOS NAS KHUR DU KHYER BA'I LHAG BSAM BSKYED
gru.wylie: de'i mjug tu de ltar bdag gis gtong len byas pa bzhin de ltar gyur 'dug gam mi, 'dug brtag pa'i tshe rang gi mos pa tsam las da lta dngos gnas par phan bde dngos su sgrub pa de ltar gyur mi 'dug par mthong nas da ni de ltar dngos su 'ong ba zhig byed snyam du rang gi ngos nas khur du khyer ba'i lhag bsam bskyed
gru.english: Now at the very end you should look into yourself and see whether things really happened the way you pictured they should when you did the giving and taking. And what you will find is that it was all only a wish: that in actuality there was no help or happiness which came about at present. This should lead you to think to yourself, "Well then, I will have to see to it that this actually does happen." Try to bring up in your heart therefore the feeling of personal responsibility, where you decide that you would be willing to carry the load all on your own. Contemplation Thirteen: On making the meditation on giving and taking an all-day practice Pabongka Rinpoche, in his masterpiece on the steps of the path, includes the following section on how to make an all-day practice from the meditation on giving and taking.

gru.acip: 'DI RNAMS SDUG BSNGAL CHUNG RIM NAS NYAMS SU BLANGS NA SDUG BSNGAL CHEN PO LA 'BYONGS, PAR GSUNGS PAS DE LTAR DGONGS PAR ZHU ZHES PA 'DI NI LUNG DANG RIGS PA'I BDAG NYID GNYAL STON PA RIN CHEN BSAM GRUB KYIS RGYUD NAS BSKUL TE BLO BZANG GRAGS PA'I DPAL GYIS BKOD PA'O
gru.wylie: 'di rnams sdug bsngal chung rim nas nyams su blangs na sdug bsngal chen po la 'byongs, par gsungs pas de ltar dgongs par zhu zhes pa 'di ni lung dang rigs pa'i bdag nyid gnyal ston pa rin chen bsam grub kyis rgyud nas bskul te blo bzang grags pa'i dpal gyis bkod pa'o
gru.english: The Holy Ones have stated that—if you are able to follow these practices and work on problems while they are still in their lesser stages—then you will be able to remove the karma that would have brought you more serious problems. I therefore ask that you live your lives this way. This brief explanation has been put down on paper by the glorious Lobsang Drakpa [Je Tsongkapa] in response to a request received, through other parties, from the embodiment of all scripture and reasoning: Rinchen Samdrup, the Teacher from Nyel. The eminent Pabongka Rinpoche, in his Gift of Liberation, further links the concept of giving and taking with that of transforming problems into siritual opportunities:

gru.acip: DER MA ZAD NGAS SNGON GTONG LEN BYAS TE SEMS CAN GYI SDIG SDUG BDAG LA BLANGS PA, YIN PAS DA DON GRUB SONG SNYAM DU DGA' BA BSKYED NAS SLAR SDUG BSNGAL GYI LHAG MA RNAMS KYANG SMIN PAR SNON NAS SEMS CAN RNAMS KYIS SDUG BSNGAL MYONG 'GYUR TSANG MA DES GO CHOD PAR BSGOM ZHING
gru.wylie: der ma zad ngas sngon gtong len byas te sems can gyi sdig sdug bdag la blangs pa, yin pas da don grub song snyam du dga' ba bskyed nas slar sdug bsngal gyi lhag ma rnams kyang smin par snon nas sems can rnams kyis sdug bsngal myong 'gyur tshang ma des go chod par bsgom zhing
gru.english: And that's not all. You should beyond that feel great joy, thinking to yourself, "In the past I did the practice of giving and taking, trying to take on myself all the bad deeds and obstacles of every living being. And now I see my wishes have been accomplished." And then continue your meditation, with the hope that whatever suffering might remain should also come and ripen upon you, that it should be added atop what has come already, and that it should compensate, in full, for the entire quantity of suffering that living kind is going to experience ever again in the future.

gru.acip: BLO SBYONG LA LEGS PAR GOMS PA DES CHOS SRUNG SOGS LA'ANG NA TSA SOGS BYUNG BA'I TSE, SEMS CAN THAMS CAD KYI SDUG BSNGAL BDAG LA SMIN PA 'DI NGAS GTONG LEN BYAS PA'I DGOS PA GRUB PA YIN PAS SLAR YANG DA LTA'I NAD 'DI LAS DA DUNG JE THUR THONGS SHIG CES PHRIN LAS BCOL
gru.wylie: blo sbyong la legs par goms pa des chos srung sogs la'ang na tsha sogs byung ba'i tshe, sems can thams cad kyi sdug bsngal bdag la smin pa 'di ngas gtong len byas pa'i dgos pa grub pa yin pas slar yang da lta'i nad 'di las da dung je thur thongs shig ces phrin las bcol
gru.english: Think about people who have gotten really good at training their minds this way. They might get sick or such even in the act of undertaking to save the Dharma, or something of the like. But they can think to themselves, Now I've succeeded in accomplishing the goals I was trying to reach when I undertook the practice of giving and taking: now I've been able to get all the sufferings of every living being to And they can also call on these beings to do their great and holy deeds: Now come again, and send me more sickness, but please let it be even more terrible than the last!

gru.acip: BLO CHER MA 'BYONGS PA DAG GIS DE LTAR MI NUS SHING 'JIGS NA NA TSA SOGS MI 'BYUNG, BA'I GROGS BCOL BA SOGS SPYI LTAR BYED SDUG BSNGAL BYUNG TSE RANG SDOD SAR CHU SHOR BA NA RTZA BA RTZAD GCOD BYAS NAS 'GOG PA LTAR SDUG BSNGAL GYI RGYU SDIG PA SPONG ZHING BDE BA'I RGYU TSOGS GSOG DGE BA SGRUB
gru.wylie: blo cher ma 'byongs pa dag gis de ltar mi nus shing 'jigs na na tsha sogs mi 'byung, ba'i grogs bcol ba sogs spyi ltar byed sdug bsngal byung tshe rang sdod sar chu shor ba na rtsa ba rtsad gcod byas nas 'gog pa ltar sdug bsngal gyi rgyu sdig pa spong zhing bde ba'i rgyu tshogs gsog dge ba sgrub
gru.english: Perhaps there are those among you who haven't learned to think in such a radical way yet, and who may find yourselves unable to practice this way—you may even be afraid to try it. In that case you can just follow the normal course of action: call on the spirits and ask them to help you avoid the sickness, or whatever it may be. In any case, you have to consider where it's all coming from when any kind of trouble begins in your life. Be like a person who finds a pool of water on the floor of their house, and runs around looking for where it's coming from, so they can stop it. Get rid of the realcause of your suffering—your own bad deeds—and go about bringing together the real causes of happiness: your own good deeds. Our next selection is taken from The Rays of the Sun (S0185), a text on training oneself in the Wish for enlightenment, by Hortun Namka Pel:

gru.acip: BLO SBYANGS PAS 'DOD THOG TU GRUB PA'I TSE BLO 'BYONGS PAR STON PA NI YID BDE 'BA' ZHIG, RGYUN DU BSTEN ZHES GSUNGS TE BSGOMS PAS CHOS KYI RO MYONG BAR BYAS NAS SDUG BSNGAL DANG GRAGS MIN SOGS RKYEN NGAN PA CI BYUNG YANG GTONG LEN GYI SGO NAS BLO SBYONG NYAMS SU BLANGS PA'I DON BYUNG SNYAM NAS DGA' MGU RANGS PA MA GTOGS YID MI BDE SOGS KYI RKYEN DU MI 'GRO BAR GOMS THUB PA'I TSE GNYEN PO'I THOG MA'I TSAD DU PHYIN PA YIN
gru.wylie: blo sbyangs pas 'dod thog tu grub pa'i tshe blo 'byongs par ston pa ni yid bde 'ba' zhig, rgyun du bsten zhes gsungs te bsgoms pas chos kyi ro myong bar byas nas sdug bsngal dang grags min sogs rkyen ngan pa ci byung yang gtong len gyi sgo nas blo sbyong nyams su blangs pa'i don byung snyam nas dga' mgu rangs pa ma gtogs yid mi bde sogs kyi rkyen du mi 'gro bar goms thub pa'i tshe gnyen po'i thog ma'i tshad du phyin pa yin
gru.english: Next is a line that speaks of how we know when we have actually succeeded in training our minds: when this training has reached the point we hoped for. The line goes: You are able to stay in a state of happiness alone, in a constant stream. Contemplation Fourteen The point is that, once you have practiced it, you start to get a feeling for the sweet taste of the Dharma; then no matter what kind of problem comes to you—whether it be some kind of pain, or a bad name, or anything of the like—you learn to think to yourself that the goal of your practice of giving and taking, your training in the Wish for enlightenment, has been attained. Then these problems stop turning into something that brings you any kind of unhappiness; rather, they cause you nothing but sheer joy. When you are able to meditate this way, then we can say that you've reached the first point of the

gru.acip: DE'I GNYEN PO YID LA MA BYAS PAR DE LTA BU'I BLO, DES BSGRIBS NA TSE 'DIR SDOD PA'I BLO SKYES NAS DE'I RING LA 'DI DANG 'DI DGOS SO ZHES TSE 'DI TZAM GYI BDE BA BSGRUB PA DANG SDUG BSNGAL SEL BA'I THABS 'BA' ZHIG LA SEMS SEMS NAS
gru.wylie: de'i gnyen po yid la ma byas par de lta bu'i blo, des bsgribs na tshe 'dir sdod pa'i blo skyes nas de'i ring la 'di dang 'di dgos so zhes tshe 'di tsam gyi bde ba bsgrub pa dang sdug bsngal sel ba'i thabs 'ba' zhig la sems sems nas
gru.english: Suppose you let this kind of attitude go on, suppose you fail to apply the spiritual antidotes that would stop these sorts of thoughts. The thoughts then create a kind of spiritual blindness: you begin to get the idea that you are going to be able to stay here in this life, and then you start to obsess on this life. All you can concentrate on then is how to get what you want, and how to escape what you don't want, in this life. Your life becomes, “Today I need this, and this, and next this.”

gru.acip: GAL TE 'JIG RTEN PHYI MA LA DMIGS NAS BSGRUB, TU CHUG KYANG PHYIS NAS RIM GYIS BSGRUB BO SNYAM PA'I PHYI BSHOL GYI LE LO 'GOG MI NUS SHING GNYID RMUGS DANG BRE MO'I GTAM DANG BZA' BTUNG LA SOGS PA'I RNAM G.YENG GIS DUS 'DA' BAS BRTZON PA CHEN POS TSUL BZHIN DU BSGRUB PA MI 'ONG NGO
