Well then, you must be suggesting that the system of the Buddha is all the same as the system of every non-Buddhist belief, that there is no difference in their correctness at all. And you must be saying too that we could never state

gru.acip: ZLA BA LAS 'ONGS LEGS BSHAD 'OD DKAR GYIS, BLO MIG KUN TA'I TSAL RAB PHYE BA'I TSE SANGS RGYAS BSKYANGS KYIS BSTAN PA'I LAM MTHONG NAS KLU SGRUB LUGS BZANG GTZO BOR MI 'DZIN SU ZHES KHO BO CAG NI DE SKAD DU SMRA'O
gru.wylie: zla ba las 'ongs legs bshad 'od dkar gyis, blo mig kun ta'i tshal rab phye ba'i tshe sangs rgyas bskyangs kyis bstan pa'i lam mthong nas klu sgrub lugs bzang gtso bor mi 'dzin su zhes kho bo cag ni de skad du smra'o
gru.english: And when this pure white light of the Moon,* this Has opened wide the night-blooming lotus, the eyes of the And we finally see that path set before us by Buddhapalita, Who then would fail to hold as their core Nagarjuna's excellent way? [*Translator's note: The "Moon" here (chandra in Sanskrit) is an allusion to Master Chandrakirti.]

gru.acip: ,RGYAL BA KUN GYI THUGS RJE GCIG BSDUS NAS, ,RGYAL SRAS GZHON NU'I GAR GYIS SRID GSUM 'DIR, ,RGYAL BA'I MDZAD PA MTHA' DAG SGRUB BRTZON PA, ,RGYAL SRAS THU BO SPYAN RAS GZIGS LA 'DUD,
gru.wylie: rgyal ba kun gyi thugs rje gcig bsdus nas, ,rgyal sras gzhon nu'i gar gyis srid gsum 'dir, ,rgyal ba'i mdzad pa mtha' dag sgrub brtson pa, ,rgyal sras thu bo spyan ras gzigs la 'dud
gru.english: Compassion of all the Victors, rolled into one; Playing the dance of the young bodhisattva Through all three worlds there are; Striving to accomplish the Victors' every deed— I bow to Loving Eyes, prince of bodhisattvas.

gru.acip: ,SHES RAB CHEN PO'I MCHOG GYUR SH'A RI'I BU, ,ZAB DON 'GREL MDZAD KLU SGRUB ZLA BA GRAGS, ,RGYAL BA GNYIS PA YAB SRAS LA BTUD NAS, ,SHER PHYIN SNYING PO'I RNAM BSHAD BRI BAR BYA,
gru.wylie: shes rab chen po'i mchog gyur shA ri'i bu, ,zab don 'grel mdzad klu sgrub zla ba grags, ,rgyal ba gnyis pa yab sras la btud nas, ,sher phyin snying po'i rnam bshad bri bar bya
gru.english: I bow to Shariputra, Wisdom vast and supreme; To Nagarjuna and Chandrakirti, Who clarified that deepest idea— To the father, the Victor returned to earth, And to his spiritual son. And now I will explain for you The Heart of Perfect Wisdom. Why we need emptiness

gru.acip: KLU SGRUB KYIS KYANG, ,GANG DAG STONG NYID MI SHES PA, ,DE DAG THAR PA BSTEN {%RTEN} MA YIN, ,'GRO DRUG SRID PA'I BRTZON RAR NI, ,RMONGS PA DE DAG 'KHOR BAR 'GYUR, ,ZHES GSUNGS PA'I PHYIR RO,,
gru.wylie: klu sgrub kyis kyang, ,gang dag stong nyid mi shes pa, ,de dag thar pa bsten {%rten} ma yin, ,'gro drug srid pa'i brtson rar ni, ,rmongs pa de dag 'khor bar 'gyur, ,zhes gsungs pa'i phyir ro
gru.english: Nagarjuna too has stated: Freedom is a complete impossibility For anyone who does not understand emptiness. Those who are blind will continue to circle Here in the prison of six different births.

gru.acip: DE'I GNAD KYANG, BDAG DANG BDAG GIR RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAR BZUNG NA 'KHOR BAR 'KHOR ZHING, DE RANG BZHIN GYIS MED PAR RTOGS NA 'KHOR BA LAS GROL BAR 'GYUR BA'I RGYU MTSAN GYIS YIN TE,
gru.wylie: de'i gnad kyang, bdag dang bdag gir rang bzhin gyis grub par bzung na 'khor bar 'khor zhing, de rang bzhin gyis med par rtogs na 'khor ba las grol bar 'gyur ba'i rgyu mtshan gyis yin te
gru.english: Here's how we can express just why this point is so crucial: If you hold on to the belief that “me” and “mine” exist through some nature of their own, then you will continue to wander through the cycle of pain. And if you finally realize that neither of these exists through any such nature, then this will act as the cause which liberates you from the cycle.

gru.acip: MDO LUNG SNGA MA SA {%MAS} KYANG 'GRUB PA'I PHYIR RO,,
gru.wylie: mdo lung snga ma sa {%mas} kyang 'grub pa'i phyir ro
gru.english: The same point is established by the citations from sutra that we gave before.

gru.acip: PHYI MA'I DBANG DU BYAS NA, SAm BHU tI LAS, ,DBANG PHYUG DANG NI GZUGS BZANG DANG, ,DPAL DANG GRAGS DANG YE SHES DANG, ,BRTZON 'GRUS PHUN SUM TSOGS PA STE, ,DRUG PO DE LA SKAL ZHES BYA, ,ZHES GSUNGS PA LTAR TE,
gru.wylie: phyi ma'i dbang du byas na, saM bhu Ti las, ,dbang phyug dang ni gzugs bzang dang, ,dpal dang grags dang ye shes dang, ,brtson 'grus phun sum tshogs pa ste, ,drug po de la skal zhes bya, ,zhes gsungs pa ltar te
gru.english: The second sense of the word “Conqueror” is as we see it in this verse, from The Kiss: When we say “share of goodness,” It can refer to six different things: Lord of power; exquisite form; Glory; fame; wisdom; And excellent effort.

gru.acip: CHEN PO PHYI MA NI DON BDUN LA 'JUG STE, MDO SDE RGYAN LAS, DMIGS PA CHE BA DANG, SGRUB PA GNYIS DANG, YE SHES DANG, BRTZON 'GRUS DANG, THABS MKHAS DANG, SGRUB PA DANG, 'PHRIN LAS CHEN PO STE BDUN LA 'JUG PAR BSHAD PA LTAR RO,,
gru.wylie: chen po phyi ma ni don bdun la 'jug ste, mdo sde rgyan las, dmigs pa che ba dang, sgrub pa gnyis dang, ye shes dang, brtson 'grus dang, thabs mkhas dang, sgrub pa dang, 'phrin las chen po ste bdun la 'jug par bshad pa ltar ro
gru.english: The second use of “great” has seven different connotations. As the Jewel of the Sutras puts it, the word “great” refers to a great focus and greatness of the two accomplishments; of wisdom; effort; skillful means; practice; and deeds.

gru.acip: SHES RAB KYI PHA ROL TU PHYIN PA ZAB MO'I SPYOD PA LA BRTZON PAS SPYAD PA STE BSGRUB PAR 'DOD PA'I GANG ZAG DES TSOGS SBYOR DANG MTHONG SGOM GYI LAM RNAMS SU TSUL JI LTAR BSLAB PAR BYA ZHES DRIS SO,,
gru.wylie: shes rab kyi pha rol tu phyin pa zab mo'i spyod pa la brtson pas spyad pa ste bsgrub par 'dod pa'i gang zag des tshogs sbyor dang mthong sgom gyi lam rnams su tshul ji ltar bslab par bya zhes dris so
gru.english: The question being asked here in the sutra boils down to: Suppose a person hoped to follow—that is, hoped to devote themselves to accomplishing—the deep practice of the perfection of wisdom. What would they have to do; how should they practice the paths of accumulation and preparation, and the paths of seeing and habituation?

gru.acip: BTAGS DON BTZAL NA RIG SHES KYI DPYAD BZOD DU MA GRUB PAS, GZUGS SOGS KYI PHUNG PO RE RER MA ZAD, PHUNG PO LNGA PO DE DAG THAMS CAD KYANG RANG BZHIN GYIS STONG PAR RNAM PAR YANG DAG PAR TE PHYIN CI MA LOG PAR GNAS TSUL JI LTA BA BZHIN RJES SU BLTA BAR BYA'O ZHES STONG NYID ZAB MO LA BLTA TSUL MDOR BSDUS TE BSTAN PA YIN LA,
gru.wylie: btags don btsal na rig shes kyi dpyad bzod du ma grub pas, gzugs sogs kyi phung po re rer ma zad, phung po lnga po de dag thams cad kyang rang bzhin gyis stong par rnam par yang dag par te phyin ci ma log par gnas tshul ji lta ba bzhin rjes su blta bar bya'o zhes stong nyid zab mo la blta tshul mdor bsdus te bstan pa yin la
gru.english: When we do seek out the creation of our projections, though, it cannot bear up under the examination of our logical mind. As such, we should see first that all five heaps—all five parts to a person, and not just each of them, such as the heap of form, individually—are empty of any nature of their own. When we say “see” here what we mean is that we should see this thing purely: meaning unmistakenly, just as it really is. The lines here constitute a brief summary of how it is that we should come to see profound emptiness.

gru.acip: GANG ZAG GI GZUGS PHUNG NI MA BRTAGS MA DPYAD PA'I THA SNYAN {%SNYAD} PA'I SHES NGOR SNANG BA TZAM MA GTOGS, DON DAM DPYOD BYED KYI RIGS PAS RNAM PAR BRTAGS SHING DPYAD PA NA BTAGS DON MI RNYED PAS RANG NGOS NAS SAM RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAS STONG PA'O,,
gru.wylie: gang zag gi gzugs phung ni ma brtags ma dpyad pa'i tha snyan {%snyad} pa'i shes ngor snang ba tsam ma gtogs, don dam dpyod byed kyi rigs pas rnam par brtags shing dpyad pa na btags don mi rnyed pas rang ngos nas sam rang bzhin gyis grub pas stong pa'o
gru.english: A person's physical body is something that exists only by appearing to the mind as it operates in a nominal mode, without examining or exploring what's really there. And when we do undertake an examination or exploration using logic which operates in the realm of the ultimate, we lose the thing that we were projecting. At that point we can say that this thing is empty of coming from its own side: that it is empty of existing through any nature of its own.

gru.acip: DPER NA, CHU NANG GI ZLA BA DANG ME LONG GI GZUGS BRNYAN DANG SMIG RGYU'I CHU DANG RMI LAM GYI MI DANG SGYU MA'I RTA GLANG SOGS THA SNYAD PA'I SHES NGOR SNANG BA TZAM MA GTOGS, SNANG TZAM NYID NAS ZLA BA SOGS SU MA GRUB PA BZHIN NO,,
gru.wylie: dper na, chu nang gi zla ba dang me long gi gzugs brnyan dang smig rgyu'i chu dang rmi lam gyi mi dang sgyu ma'i rta glang sogs tha snyad pa'i shes ngor snang ba tsam ma gtogs, snang tsam nyid nas zla ba sogs su ma grub pa bzhin no
gru.english: This is like, for example, the way in which other things exist only as they appear to a nominal state of mind: things like a moon reflected in the water; or someone's reflection in a mirror; or a mirage of water appearing in a desert; people we meet in a dream; or an illusory horse or elephant conjured up by a magician. These exist only in appearance; they do not exist as the moon itself, and so on.

gru.acip: GAL TE RANG BZHIN GYIS MA GRUB NA MED PAR MI 'GYUR RAM SNYAM NA,
gru.wylie: gal te rang bzhin gyis ma grub na med par mi 'gyur ram snyam na
gru.english: Now you might think to yourself: When you say that something “cannot exist through any nature of its own,” are you saying that it cannot exist at all?

gru.acip: DPER NA, ZLA BA'I GZUGS BRNYAN NI ZLA BA YIN PAR MA GRUB KYANG ZLA BAR SNANG BA TZAM MI 'GAL BA LTAR RO,,
gru.wylie: dper na, zla ba'i gzugs brnyan ni zla ba yin par ma grub kyang zla bar snang ba tsam mi 'gal ba ltar ro
gru.english: It is, for example, no contradiction that a reflection of the moon on the surface of a lake can simply appear as though it were the moon, even though it is not in fact the moon itself. The moon on a lake

gru.acip: 'O NA, ZLA BA'I GZUGS BRNYAN ZLA BAR MA GRUB PA DE BZHIN DU, GZUGS NYID KYANG GZUGS SUM {%SU MA} GRUB PA YIN NAM, GZHAN DU DE'I DPER JI LTAR RIGS ZHE NA,
gru.wylie: 'o na, zla ba'i gzugs brnyan zla bar ma grub pa de bzhin du, gzugs nyid kyang gzugs sum {%su ma} grub pa yin nam, gzhan du de'i dper ji ltar rigs zhe na
gru.english: One may then ask this question: And so a reflection of the moon is not the moon. Are you saying that, in the same way, form itself is not form? Otherwise it doesn't make any sense to use this as an example for your point.

gru.acip: CUNG ZAD BRJOD NA, DPE DON DE LTAR SBYOR BA NI GZUGS BRNYAN BYAD BZHIN DU MA GRUB PA DE BZHIN DU, GZUGS NI GZUGS SU RANG BZHIN GYIS MA GRUB CES GO BAR BYED PA YIN ZHING,
gru.wylie: cung zad brjod na, dpe don de ltar sbyor ba ni gzugs brnyan byad bzhin du ma grub pa de bzhin du, gzugs ni gzugs su rang bzhin gyis ma grub ces go bar byed pa yin zhing
gru.english: Perhaps though I could say just a bit about it here. Let's look at how the metaphor, and what it refers to, relate to one another. The reflection of a thing is not the thing being reflected itself; just so, what the metaphor is meant to help us understand is that physical form is not something which exists, through any nature of its own, as physical form.

gru.acip: DE YANG ME LONG GI GZUGS BRNYAN LTA BU NI 'JIG RTEN PA'I RGAN PO BRDA BYANG RNAMS KYIS BYAD BZHIN DU MA GRUB PAR RTOGS NUS PAS, GZUGS BRNYAN DE 'JIG RTEN NA BRDZUN PAR GRAGS LA,
gru.wylie: de yang me long gi gzugs brnyan lta bu ni 'jig rten pa'i rgan po brda byang rnams kyis byad bzhin du ma grub par rtogs nus pas, gzugs brnyan de 'jig rten na brdzun par grags la
gru.english: Now something like a reflection in the mirror is something that even old fogies in the everyday world—anybody who knows what the words “reflection in the mirror” mean—are capable of understanding is not the thing itself: the thing which is being reflected in the mirror. As such, just normal people in the world might say that “a reflection is false: not what it appears to be.”

gru.acip: GZUGS RANG BZHIN GYIS MA GRUB KYANG DER MA GRUB PAR 'JIG RTEN RANG GA BAS RTOGS MI NUS PAS, GZUGS DE NI 'JIG RTEN RANG GA BA'I SHES NGOR BDEN PAR SNANG ZHING DE'I NGOR BDEN YANG,
gru.wylie: gzugs rang bzhin gyis ma grub kyang der ma grub par 'jig rten rang ga bas rtogs mi nus pas, gzugs de ni 'jig rten rang ga ba'i shes ngor bden par snang zhing de'i ngor bden yang
gru.english: The fact that physical form does not exist through any nature of its own though is not something that your average person in the world would be able to figure out on their own. As such, physical form is something which appears to exist—at least, to the mind of the average person—as something that exists really; we can even say that, to their perceptions, it does exist really.

gru.acip: DBU MA'I RIGS PAS SNANG BA LTAR MA GRUB PAR RTOGS NUS PAS DBU MA PA LA GRAGS PA'I BRDZUN PA YIN NO,,
gru.wylie: dbu ma'i rigs pas snang ba ltar ma grub par rtogs nus pas dbu ma pa la grags pa'i brdzun pa yin no
gru.english: Nonetheless, it is possible—by using the reasoning presented by the middle way—to come to a realization that this same physical form cannot in fact exist the way it seems to exist. And thus it would be unreal, in the sense that this word is understood by followers of the middle way.

gru.acip: DE'I PHYIR 'JIG RTEN NA GRAGS PA'I BRDZUN PA ZHIG DPER BZUNG NAS, DE LA BRDZUN PAR MA GRAGS PA'I GZUGS SOGS RANG GI NGO BOS GRUB PAR SNANG YANG, DER MA RUB PAR {%RUNG BAR} SGRUB PAR BYED PA YIN NO,,
gru.wylie: de'i phyir 'jig rten na grags pa'i brdzun pa zhig dper bzung nas, de la brdzun par ma grags pa'i gzugs sogs rang gi ngo bos grub par snang yang, der ma rub par {%rung bar} sgrub par byed pa yin no
gru.english: Thus we have started here with the metaphor of something which is understood, by average people of the world, to be unreal. And then we move on to something which is not commonly thought, by these same people, to be unreal: physical form and the rest. And what we do is to prove that—even though these things appear to exist through some essence of their own—it would be wrong to say that they actually did.

gru.acip: DES NA GZUGS BRNYAN BYAD BZHIN DU MA GRUB KYANG GZUGS BRNYAN DU GRUB PA LTAR, GZUGS RANG BZHIN GYIS MA GRUB KYANG GZUGS SU GRUB PAR THA SNYAD PA'I TSAD MAS 'JOG NUS TE, DE 'DRA BA GZHAN LA'ANG SBYAR RO,,
gru.wylie: des na gzugs brnyan byad bzhin du ma grub kyang gzugs brnyan du grub pa ltar, gzugs rang bzhin gyis ma grub kyang gzugs su grub par tha snyad pa'i tshad mas 'jog nus te, de 'dra ba gzhan la'ang sbyar ro
gru.english: A reflection in a mirror is not the thing which is being reflected in the mirror—but it is a reflection. In the same way, we can say that—even though physical form does not exist through any nature of its own—it can be established by an accurate, nominal type of perception as being physical form. And this same idea can be applied to everything else as well.

gru.acip: DPER NA GZUGS BRNYAN ZLA BAR SNANG BA DANG DE ZLA BAR MA GRUB PA GNYIS NGO BO GCIG CING THA DAD MA YIN PA LTAR RO,,
gru.wylie: dper na gzugs brnyan zla bar snang ba dang de zla bar ma grub pa gnyis ngo bo gcig cing tha dad ma yin pa ltar ro
gru.english: For example, the fact that the reflection of the moon on a lake is appearing as though it were the moon itself is essentially the same as the reflection's not actually being the moon; essentially, they are no different things.

gru.acip: DE YANG GZUGS BRNYAN ZLA BAR SNANG BA DANG GZUGS BRNYAN ZLA BAR MA GRUB PA GNYIS GZHI GCIG LA DUS GCIG TU TSOGS PA 'JIG RTEN PA'I THA SNYAD PA'I TSAD MAS NGES PA MNGON SUM GYIS GRUB PA YIN LA,
gru.wylie: de yang gzugs brnyan zla bar snang ba dang gzugs brnyan zla bar ma grub pa gnyis gzhi gcig la dus gcig tu tshogs pa 'jig rten pa'i tha snyad pa'i tshad mas nges pa mngon sum gyis grub pa yin la
gru.english: Moreover, the fact that the reflection appears to be the moon and the fact that it is not actually the moon are two things which can be established directly—through the perceptions of a nominal form of accurate perception in the mind of your average person—to exist in tandem, and at the same moment, with regard to a single shared object.

gru.acip: DE LTAR YANG, MGON PO KLU SGURB {%SGRUB} KYIS BYANG CHUB SEMS 'GREL LAS, ,KUN RDZOB LAS NI THA DAD PAR, ,DE NYID DMIGS PA MA YIN TE, ,KUN RDZOB STONG PA NYID DU BSHAD, ,STONG NYID KHO NA KUN RDZOB YIN, ,MED NA MI 'BYUNG NGES PA'I PHYIR, ,BYAS DANG MI RTAG JI BZHIN NO,, ZHES GSUNGS SO,,
gru.wylie: de ltar yang, mgon po klu sgurb {%sgrub} kyis byang chub sems 'grel las, ,kun rdzob las ni tha dad par, ,de nyid dmigs pa ma yin te, ,kun rdzob stong pa nyid du bshad, ,stong nyid kho na kun rdzob yin, ,med na mi 'byung nges pa'i phyir, ,byas dang mi rtag ji bzhin no,, zhes gsungs so
gru.english: Our protector, Nagarjuna, has expressed this as follows in his Commentary on the Wish for Enlightenment: Suchness is not something You can ever see Separate from the deceptive, For deceptive things Have been described As nothing other than emptiness. If you cancel one of the two, The other always disappears— Just the same as things that are made And things that constantly change.

gru.acip: DE BZHIN DU TSOR BA DANG, 'DU SHES RANG {%DANG}, 'DU BYED DANG, RNAM PAR SHES PA RNAMS STONG PA'O, ,ZHES PA STE, GZUGS PHUNG LA BSHAD PA'I DPE DON DE BZHIN DU, TSOR BA SOGS BZHI PO RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA {%PAS} STONG PA'O,,
gru.wylie: de bzhin du tshor ba dang, 'du shes rang {%dang}, 'du byed dang, rnam par shes pa rnams stong pa'o, ,zhes pa ste, gzugs phung la bshad pa'i dpe don de bzhin du, tshor ba sogs bzhi po rang bzhin gyis grub pa {%pas} stong pa'o
gru.english: The corresponding sutra lines here go: “The same is true of your feelings, and your ability to discriminate between things, and the other factors that make you up, and all the different kinds of awareness that you possess: all of them are empty.” What these are saying is that the other four heaps—feelings and the rest—are empty of existing through any nature of their own; that is, we can take the same metaphor, and its meaning, from the explanation of the heap of the body, physical form, and apply it to these four.

gru.acip: CHOS THAMS CAD RANG GI MTSAN NYID GZUGS SU RUNG BA LA SOGS PA DANG, SPYI'I MTSAN NYID MI RTAG PA DANG BDAG MED PA LA SOGS PA RNAMS KYANG RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PA MED PA DANG,
gru.wylie: chos thams cad rang gi mtshan nyid gzugs su rung ba la sogs pa dang, spyi'i mtshan nyid mi rtag pa dang bdag med pa la sogs pa rnams kyang rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub pa med pa dang
gru.english: Further, nothing in the universe has any characteristic of its own which defines it as itself—a characteristic like being something we can point to as being physical form, and which at the same time exists by definition. Nor does anything possess any more general characteristic—such as being a changing thing, or something with no self-nature—which could exist by definition.

gru.acip: KLU SGRUB KYIS KYANG RIGS PA DRUG CU PA LAS, ,BRTEN NAS SKYES PAR MA SKYES PAR, ,DE NYID MKHYEN PA MCHOG GIS GSUNGS, ,ZHES DANG,
gru.wylie: klu sgrub kyis kyang rigs pa drug cu pa las, ,brten nas skyes par ma skyes par, ,de nyid mkhyen pa mchog gis gsungs, ,zhes dang
gru.english: Arya Nagarjuna has also stated, in his Sixty Verses on Reasoning: Things that start In dependence Never start— This is the very thing That the One with Highest Knowledge Has spoken.

gru.acip: KLU SGRUB KYIS RTZA SHE LAS, ,GANG GIS RTEN CING 'BREL BAR 'BYUNG, ,'GAG PA MED PA SKYE MED PA, ,ZHES SOGS DANG,
gru.wylie: klu sgrub kyis rtsa she las, ,gang gis rten cing 'brel bar 'byung, ,'gag pa med pa skye med pa, ,zhes sogs dang
gru.english: And Arya Nagarjuna, in his Root Text on Wisdom, says: To those who have taught That things occur In dependence on one another— Where there is no stopping, And there is no starting…

gru.acip: DON DAM PA'I CHOS RNAMS NI DGAG BYA BDEN GRUB SOGS GNYIS SNANG GI SPROS PA RNAM PAR BCAD PA'I TSUL GYIS SNANG TSUL DANG GNAS TSUL MTHUN PAR GNAS SHING, GNAS PA LTAR GZIGS PA YIN LA, KUN RDZOB PA'I CHOS RNAMS NI GNYIS SNANG GI SPROS PA DU MA DANG BCAS TE SNANG TSUL DANG GNAS TSUL MI MTHUN PAR GZIGS PA'I PHYIR RO,,
gru.wylie: don dam pa'i chos rnams ni dgag bya bden grub sogs gnyis snang gi spros pa rnam par bcad pa'i tshul gyis snang tshul dang gnas tshul mthun par gnas shing, gnas pa ltar gzigs pa yin la, kun rdzob pa'i chos rnams ni gnyis snang gi spros pa du ma dang bcas te snang tshul dang gnas tshul mi mthun par gzigs pa'i phyir ro
gru.english: Things belonging to ultimate reality reside in a state where the way things appear and the way they actually exist are in accord with each other: they preclude any false constructions of the things that emptiness denies—things that could exist in truth—and all of their discrepancy between appearances and reality.

gru.acip: SPYIR GNYIS SNANG GI SPROS PA LA SGRA RTOG DANG, YUL YUL CAN THA DAD PA'I SNANG BA DANG, BDEN GRUB DANG DER SNANG BA DANG, KUN RDZOB KYI GNYIS SNANG SOGS MANG YANG 'DIR SHES NA DE RNAMS GANG DANG SBYAR KYANG MI 'GAL LO,,
gru.wylie: spyir gnyis snang gi spros pa la sgra rtog dang, yul yul can tha dad pa'i snang ba dang, bden grub dang der snang ba dang, kun rdzob kyi gnyis snang sogs mang yang 'dir shes na de rnams gang dang sbyar kyang mi 'gal lo
gru.english: Generally speaking, there are many forms that these “false constructions of the discrepancy” can take: false concepts based on words; or when object and subject appear to be separate; the idea that things could exist in truth, and the appearance that they do; or discrepancy in the sense of deceptive appearances; and so on. If you know what you're doing, these can all be applied to almost any context of the concept without any contradiction.

gru.acip: RTAGS YANG DAG GI DGAG BYA MTHAR THUG NI, RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA, RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PA, RANG NGOS NAS GRUB PA, BDEN PAR GRUB PA, DON DAM PAR GRUB PA, YANG DAG PAR GRUB PA, RANG DBANG DU GRUB PA RNAMS TE, RANG BZHIN GYIS STONG PA 'AM, RANG BZHIN GYIS MED CES SBYOR RUNG BA THAMS CAD LA NI DE THAMS CAD KYIS STONG BA DANG MED CES SBYOR RUNG STE, DE RNAMS DON GCIG MING GI RNAM GRANGS TZAM YIN PA'I PHYIR RO,,
gru.wylie: rtags yang dag gi dgag bya mthar thug ni, rang bzhin gyis grub pa, rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub pa, rang ngos nas grub pa, bden par grub pa, don dam par grub pa, yang dag par grub pa, rang dbang du grub pa rnams te, rang bzhin gyis stong pa 'am, rang bzhin gyis med ces sbyor rung ba thams cad la ni de thams cad kyis stong ba dang med ces sbyor rung ste, de rnams don gcig ming gi rnam grangs tsam yin pa'i phyir ro
gru.english: But as for the ultimate form of what we deny with a correct reason, there are many ways to express it: a thing that exists through some nature of its own a thing that exists by definition a thing that exists from its own side a thing that exists in truth a thing that exists in some ultimate way a thing that exists in essence a thing that exists on its own power. These are all different expressions that could properly be applied here in the sutra where you see phrases like “empty of any nature of its own” or “not something which exists through some nature of its own.” That is, they are all simply synonymous. How practice brings enlightenment

gru.acip: SH'A RI'I BU ZHES BOS NAS, TSOGS SBYOR GNYIS DANG MTHONG SGOM GYI LAM GNYIS TE BZHI LA SLOB TSUL GONG DU BSTAN PA'I TSUL DE LTA BAS NA, GANG ZAG BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA' SEMS DPA' CHEN PO RNAMS KYI MNYAM GZHAG YE SHES KYI GZIGS NGO NA GZUGS MED PA NAS, THA MA'I THOB PA DANG MA THOB PA'I BAR GANG YANG RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA MED PA'I PHYIR
gru.wylie: shA ri'i bu zhes bos nas, tshogs sbyor gnyis dang mthong sgom gyi lam gnyis te bzhi la slob tshul gong du bstan pa'i tshul de lta bas na, gang zag byang chub sems dpa' sems dpa' chen po rnams kyi mnyam gzhag ye shes kyi gzigs ngo na gzugs med pa nas, tha ma'i thob pa dang ma thob pa'i bar gang yang rang bzhin gyis grub pa med pa'i phyir
gru.english: This begins with Lord Buddha addressing Shariputra, one more time. And what the sutra is saying here is: There we have it; with the sections just finished, we have shown you how to practice these four paths: the pair of the paths of accumulation and preparation; and the pair of the paths of seeing and habituation. And we have been considering how thus it is that something like physical form cannot be present to the perceptions of these people—these great warrior saints—while they are experiencing the wisdom which is meditating deeply on emptiness. And we have continued in this vein from physical form up to the last part about “something to reach, and something not to reach”; we have been learning how it is that there is nothing in the universe that exists through any nature of its own.

gru.acip: SANGS RGYAS THOB PA LA STONG NYID RTOGS DGOS PAR MA ZAD, THEG PA GSUM PO GANG GI'ANG THAR PA THOB PA LA NI STONG NYID NGES PAR RTOGS DGOS TE, STONG NYID RTOGS PA'I LTA BA NI ZHI SGO GNYIS SU MED PAR BSHAD PA'I DGOS PA DE YIN ZHING, TING NGE 'DZIN RGYAL PO'I LUNG SNGAR DRANGS PA LTAR DANG 'PHAGS PA KLU SGRUB KYIS KYANG,
gru.wylie: sangs rgyas thob pa la stong nyid rtogs dgos par ma zad, theg pa gsum po gang gi'ang thar pa thob pa la ni stong nyid nges par rtogs dgos te, stong nyid rtogs pa'i lta ba ni zhi sgo gnyis su med par bshad pa'i dgos pa de yin zhing, ting nge 'dzin rgyal po'i lung sngar drangs pa ltar dang 'phags pa klu sgrub kyis kyang
gru.english: If we hope to attain enlightenment, we must definitely see emptiness. Not only that, but to attain freedom using any of the three different tracks, we must without question see emptiness. This is the whole purpose of why the view in which we realize emptiness has been described as “a door to peace which has no second.” We can refer back to the citation we gave above, from the King of Concentration; while the Realized One, Nagarjuna, has also said:

gru.acip: 'DIR THAL 'GYUR BA'I LUGS GZHIR BZHAG NAS 'CHAD PA YIN ZHING, 'DI LA RIGS PA'I RNAM GRANGS MANG YANG CHOS THAMS CAD RTOG PAS BTAGS TZAM DU 'JOG LUGS SHES NA RANG BZHIN GYIS MA GRUB PA'I TSUL SHES SLA BAS,
gru.wylie: 'dir thal 'gyur ba'i lugs gzhir bzhag nas 'chad pa yin zhing, 'di la rigs pa'i rnam grangs mang yang chos thams cad rtog pas btags tsam du 'jog lugs shes na rang bzhin gyis ma grub pa'i tshul shes sla bas
gru.english: I will give my presentation here based on the position of the highest school: the Consequence Branch. Now there are many different, and equivalent, types of reasoning that you could use here; but if you understand how everything in the world is established through nothing more than a process of laying concepts on things, then it will be a simple matter for you to grasp how it is that these things cannot exist through any nature of their own.

gru.acip: RIGS PA DES CHOS THAMS CAD RTOG PAS BTAGS TZAM DU GRUB PAS, RTOG PAS BTAGS TZAM MIN PAR RANG DBANG GIS GRUB PAR 'DZIN PA NI BDEN 'DZIN DANG, DES BZUNG BA LTAR GRUB NA RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA DANG BDEN PAR GRUB PA SOGS SU 'GYUR RO,,
gru.wylie: rigs pa des chos thams cad rtog pas btags tsam du grub pas, rtog pas btags tsam min par rang dbang gis grub par 'dzin pa ni bden 'dzin dang, des bzung ba ltar grub na rang bzhin gyis grub pa dang bden par grub pa sogs su 'gyur ro
gru.english: The logic we have outlined here establishes that everything in the universe is nothing but a product of our conceptualization. Thus, when we take something to be otherwise—when we take it as not being a product of our concepts, but rather something that can exist through its own power—that's what we call “believing that something is real, or true.” If things actually existed in the way this state of mind thinks they do, then they would have to be things that existed through some nature of their own; or in truth; or in the other wording we've used above. Not parts, not wholes

gru.acip: DGAG BYA DE 'GOG PA'I REGS {%RIGS} PA NI MGON PO KLU SGRUB KYI RTZA BA SHES RAB LAS RGYAS PAR GSUNGS SHING, RIN CHEN 'PHRENG BA LAS,
gru.wylie: dgag bya de 'gog pa'i regs {%rigs} pa ni mgon po klu sgrub kyi rtsa ba shes rab las rgyas par gsungs shing, rin chen 'phreng ba las
gru.english: The logic we use to disprove the thing that emptiness denies here is described at great length by our protector, Nagarjuna, in his Root Verses on Wisdom. He also states the following, in his String of Precious Jewels:

gru.acip: ,ZHES PHUNG PO'I STENG DU NGA RTOG PAS BTAGS PA TZAM MA GTOGS, NGA RANG NGOS NAS MA GRUB PAR BSTAN TO, ,DE YANG SKYES BU NI NGA'AM GANG ZAG GO
gru.wylie: zhes phung po'i steng du nga rtog pas btags pa tsam ma gtogs, nga rang ngos nas ma grub par bstan to, ,de yang skyes bu ni nga'am gang zag go
gru.english: The point here is that “me” is just a concept applied to the parts of the person; there is no “me” which exists from its own side. When it says “the person” here, what that means is “me,” or the individual.

gru.acip: ,SKYES BU KHAMS DRUG 'DUS PA'I PHYIR, ,ZHES PAS, NGA DE KHAMS DRUG 'DUS PA'I STENG NAS BZHAG PAR BSTAN CING, RGYU MTSAN DE NYID KYIS SKYE BU'AM NGA RANG BZHIN GYIS MA GRUB PA NI, YANG DAG MIN ZHES PAS BSTAN TO,,
gru.wylie: skyes bu khams drug 'dus pa'i phyir, ,zhes pas, nga de khams drug 'dus pa'i steng nas bzhag par bstan cing, rgyu mtshan de nyid kyis skye bu'am nga rang bzhin gyis ma grub pa ni, yang dag min zhes pas bstan to
gru.english: And then “The person is a composite of six different elements” is meant to indicate that “me” is an idea laid upon the six elements considered altogether. For this very reason then, the person—or “me”—cannot be something which exists through any nature of its own; and this is the point of the phrase, “cannot exist in essence.”

gru.acip: DPE DE BZHIN DU KHAMS RE RE YANG RANG RANG GI CHA SHAS TSOGS PA LA BRTEN NAS BZHAG PAS YANG DAG PAR RAM BDEN PAR GRUB PA MED CES STON PA NI, JI LTA BAR, ,DE BZHIN KHAMS NI RE RE YANG, ,'DUS PHYIR YANG DAG NYID DU MIN, ,ZHES GSUNGS SO,,
gru.wylie: dpe de bzhin du khams re re yang rang rang gi cha shas tshogs pa la brten nas bzhag pas yang dag par ram bden par grub pa med ces ston pa ni, ji lta bar, ,de bzhin khams ni re re yang, ,'dus phyir yang dag nyid du min, ,zhes gsungs so
gru.english: As we've seen with this example, the same applies to each of the elements taken individually: each one is established on the basis of the composite of its own parts. As such, they cannot themselves exist “in essence,” or “in truth.” That is the message of the lines: And each of these elements, In turn, is a composite; So could never exist In essence either.

gru.acip: DE'I PHYIR CHOS THAMS CAD KYANG MING BRDAS BZHAG TZAM DANG RTOG PAS BTAGS TZAM DU GRUB BO,,
gru.wylie: de'i phyir chos thams cad kyang ming brdas bzhag tsam dang rtog pas btags tsam du grub bo
gru.english: Thus it is that we determine that everything in the world too is just established through names and terms—it's all just a creation of our concepts.

gru.acip: ,ZHES PA'I RKANG PA DANG POS CHOS THAMS CAD NI, RNAM PA KUN TU STE GTAN NAS MED PA MIN PA DANG, RANG BZHIN GYIS NI YOD PAS MIN, ,ZHES PAS RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA MIN PAR BSTAN TE,
gru.wylie: zhes pa'i rkang pa dang pos chos thams cad ni, rnam pa kun tu ste gtan nas med pa min pa dang, rang bzhin gyis ni yod pas min, ,zhes pas rang bzhin gyis grub pa min par bstan te
gru.english: What the first section of these lines is saying is that it's not the case that things don't exist “at all”; which is to say, in no way at all. Then when it continues with “nor do they exist through a nature of their own,” what it's saying is that nothing ever came to be through a self-nature.

gru.acip: GTAN NAS MED PA MIN ZHES PAS THA SNYAD DU YOD PA DANG, RANG BZHIN GYIS YOD PA MIN ZHES PAS BDEN PAR GRUB PA MIN ZHES STON PAS
gru.wylie: gtan nas med pa min zhes pas tha snyad du yod pa dang, rang bzhin gyis yod pa min zhes pas bden par grub pa min zhes ston pas
gru.english: When we say that it's not the case that things don't exist at all, what we're saying is that things do exist in a nominal way; and when we say it's not the case that things exist through some nature of their own, what we're saying is that things don't exist in truth. Learning to avoid the two extremes

gru.acip: BRTEN NAS BYUNG BA'AM BZHAG PA'I YOD PAR GO BA'I TSE, GTAN NAS MED PA'I CHAD MTHA' DNGOS SU 'GOG NUS PA'I TSUL GYIS RTAG MTHA' YANG 'GOG PA YIN TE, BRTEN NAS BYUNG BA'AM BZHAG GI ,RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA MIN ZHES GO BA NA RTAG MTHA' LEGS PAR 'GOG NUS PA'I PHYIR RO,,
gru.wylie: brten nas byung ba'am bzhag pa'i yod par go ba'i tshe, gtan nas med pa'i chad mtha' dngos su 'gog nus pa'i tshul gyis rtag mtha' yang 'gog pa yin te, brten nas byung ba'am bzhag gi ,rang bzhin gyis grub pa min zhes go ba na rtag mtha' legs par 'gog nus pa'i phyir ro
gru.english: And when we realize that things do exist through a process of occurring in dependence—through being established because of their dependence—then in the same way that this idea has the power to block, directly, the extreme that things could have stopped, it also serves to block as well the idea that things could go on without ever changing. And that's because once we understand how things occur in dependence—how they are established because of their dependence—then we also understand that they cannot have come about through some nature of their own. This concept has the perfect capacity to block the extreme idea that things could go on without ever changing.

gru.acip: DE YANG RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAR BZUNG BA'I BLO YOD PA TZAM GYIS RTAG MTHAR LHUNG BAR MI 'JOG STE, RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAR 'DZIN PA'I BLO NI THEG CHEN 'PHAGS PA LA YANG YOD PA'I PHYIR RO,,
gru.wylie: de yang rang bzhin gyis grub par bzung ba'i blo yod pa tsam gyis rtag mthar lhung bar mi 'jog ste, rang bzhin gyis grub par 'dzin pa'i blo ni theg chen 'phags pa la yang yod pa'i phyir ro
gru.english: Now we don't say that just because someone is entertaining a state of mind where they hold that things exist through some nature of their own, they can be said to have fallen into the extreme view that things must go on without changing. And that's because the state of mind where we believe that things are existing through their own nature can even be found in a realized being who is on the bodhisattva track, of the higher way.

gru.acip: BCINGS PA'I DON NI BDEN 'DZIN YOD PA TZAM MIN GYI, CHOS GANG LA YANG BDEN PAR GRUB BAM MA GRUB SNYAM DU SEMS PA NA, DE NYID BDEN PAR GRUB PAR 'DZIN PA'I BDEN ZHEN LAS MI 'DA' ZHING 'DA' MI NUS NA NI, DES BCINGS PAR 'JOG GO
gru.wylie: bcings pa'i don ni bden 'dzin yod pa tsam min gyi, chos gang la yang bden par grub bam ma grub snyam du sems pa na, de nyid bden par grub par 'dzin pa'i bden zhen las mi 'da' zhing 'da' mi nus na ni, des bcings par 'jog go
gru.english: And what does it mean when we say that someone is “chained” like this? It doesn't just refer to the fact that they possess the tendency to believe that things are real. Rather, it means that—when the person who is chained considers the question of whether things exist in a real way or not—they can never go beyond an attachment to thinking that these things are real: they can never go beyond believing that things are, in fact, real. When they cannot go beyond this, then that's what we call being “chained.”

gru.acip: RANG 'DZIN RTOG PA 'GA' ZHIG GI NGO BOR YOD NA SPYIR YOD MI DGOS TE, BUM PA BDEN GRUB DE DE 'DZIN PA'I RTOG PA'I NGO BO {%BOR} YOD KYANG SPYIR MED LA,
gru.wylie: rang 'dzin rtog pa 'ga' zhig gi ngo bor yod na spyir yod mi dgos te, bum pa bden grub de de 'dzin pa'i rtog pa'i ngo bo {%bor} yod kyang spyir med la
gru.english: Just because something exists to the perceptions of certain persons who hold that something is there doesn't necessarily mean that, in general, it has to actually be there. The “fact” that a water pitcher exists in truth exists to the perceptions of a person who believes this to be the case; and yet in general this “fact” doesn't exist at all.

gru.acip: 'JIG RTEN PAS YOD PAR KHAS LEN NA YOD PA DANG, MED PAR KHAS LEN NA MED PAS MA KHYAB KYANG, YOD MED NI 'JIGS RTEN GYI THA SNYAD DANG GRAGS PA DON MTHUN LA BLTOS NAS 'JOG PA YIN TE, MGON PO KLU SGRUB KYIS,
gru.wylie: 'jig rten pas yod par khas len na yod pa dang, med par khas len na med pas ma khyab kyang, yod med ni 'jigs rten gyi tha snyad dang grags pa don mthun la bltos nas 'jog pa yin te, mgon po klu sgrub kyis
gru.english: Now it is not the case that everything that the world agrees exists exists, nor that everything that the world agrees does not exist does not exist; nonetheless, deciding whether something exists or not is something that we do depending on the verbiage and convention accepted in the world. As our protector, Nagarjuna, has said it:

gru.acip: PHUNG PO RE BA DANG TSOGS PA SOGS NGA MIN KYANG, DE DAG LA BRTEN NAS NGA KUN RDZOB TU 'THAD PA'ANG RIGS PAS 'GRUB CING,
gru.wylie: phung po re ba dang tshogs pa sogs nga min kyang, de dag la brten nas nga kun rdzob tu 'thad pa'ang rigs pas 'grub cing
gru.english: Just so, none of the parts of the person, nor the sum of these parts or the like, is “me.” But based on these things it is still correct—that is, logically defensible—to say “me,” albeit only in an apparent way.

gru.acip: LE'U GNYIS PA'I BYANG CHUB SEMS 'GREL LAS MGON PO KLU SGRUB KYIS, ,CHOS RNAM {%RNAMS} STONG PA 'DI SHES NAS, ,LAS DANG 'BRAS BU BSTEN PA GANG, ,NGO MTSAR BAS KYANG 'DI NGO MTSAR, ,RMAD BYUNG BAS KYANG 'DI RMAD BYUNG, ,ZHES DANG,
gru.wylie: le'u gnyis pa'i byang chub sems 'grel las mgon po klu sgrub kyis, ,chos rnam {%rnams} stong pa 'di shes nas, ,las dang 'bras bu bsten pa gang, ,ngo mtshar bas kyang 'di ngo mtshar, ,rmad byung bas kyang 'di rmad byung, ,zhes dang
gru.english: Our protector, Nagarjuna, said too in his Commentary on the Wish for Enlightenment for the second chapter: Someone who grasps That all these things Are empty, And then goes on To devote themselves To karma and its consequences Is more amazing than amazing; More wondrous than the wondrous.

gru.acip: ,DE YANG 'PHAGS PA KLU SGRUB KYI, ,LUGS BZANG JI BZHIN 'DZIN MDZAD PA, ,BLO BZANG RGYAL BA GNYIS PA YI, ,DGONGS PA'I DON GYI GNAD BSDUS BSHAD,
gru.wylie: de yang 'phags pa klu sgrub kyi, ,lugs bzang ji bzhin 'dzin mdzad pa, ,blo bzang rgyal ba gnyis pa yi, ,dgongs pa'i don gyi gnad bsdus bshad
gru.english: My explanation begins By upholding the grand tradition Of Nagarjuna, who saw emptiness; And then it summarizes The crucial points In the true thinking of Lobsang— The Buddha returned to earth.

gru.acip: ,CES PA 'DI NI, DAD DANG RNAM DPYOD LDAN PA'I GNAS BRTAN GRAGS PA DPAL 'BYOR GYIS NAN CHER BSKUL BA LA BRTEN NAS, CO NE'I MDO SNGAGS ZUNG 'BREL GYI BLA MA'I GO SAR GNAS PA'I SH'AKYA'I DGE SLONG RIGS PA SMRA BA DON GYI DBU MA BAR {%PAR} RLOM PA GRAGS PA BSHAD SGRUB KYI BSKUL BA PO'I NGO DANG PHAN YON LA BSAMS TE LCAGS PHAG GI LOR GZIMS KHANG NYID NAS SBYAR BA'O,,
gru.wylie: ces pa 'di ni, dad dang rnam dpyod ldan pa'i gnas brtan grags pa dpal 'byor gyis nan cher bskul ba la brten nas, co ne'i mdo sngags zung 'brel gyi bla ma'i go sar gnas pa'i shAkya'i dge slong rigs pa smra ba don gyi dbu ma bar {%par} rlom pa grags pa bshad sgrub kyi bskul ba po'i ngo dang phan yon la bsams te lcags phag gi lor gzims khang nyid nas sbyar ba'o
gru.english: Here is how this commentary happened. I was approached by the elder Drakpa Peljor, a monk of great faith and intelligence, who insisted vehemently that I should write such a work—and so I did. My name is Drakpa Shedrup, and I am a monk of the order of Shakyamuni who fancies himself a true philosopher of the Middle Way; and who holds the position of the senior teacher at both the college for the study of the open teachings and at that for the study of the secret, here in Choney Monastery. Thinking to honor the one who urged me to write the text, and of the benefit it might bring to others, I have composed it quietly in my personal quarters, in the Iron Pig year.

gru.acip: ZHUS TSUL DNGOS NI BCOM LDAN 'DAS BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA'I THEG PA LA YANG DAG PAR ZHUGS PAS JI LTAR GNAS PAR BGYI, JI LTAR BSGRUB PAR BGYI, JI LTAR SEMS RAB TU GZUNG BAR BGYI ZHES DON TSAN GSUM ZHUS SO, ,GNYIS PA LAN LA,
gru.wylie: zhus tshul dngos ni bcom ldan 'das byang chub sems dpa'i theg pa la yang dag par zhugs pas ji ltar gnas par bgyi, ji ltar bsgrub par bgyi, ji ltar sems rab tu gzung bar bgyi zhes don tshan gsum zhus so, ,gnyis pa lan la
gru.english: This brings us to the actual way in which the sutra was requested. Subhuti asks the Conqueror, “What of those who have entered well into the way of the bodhisattva?” He phrases his question in three different sections: “How shall they live? How shall they practice? How should they keep their thoughts?” Here secondly we explain the Buddha's reply.

gru.acip: DE BZHIN DU PHUNG PO 'DI LA BRTEN NAS NGA'O SNYAM DU 'BYUNG YANG, PHUNG PO'I TSOGS PA DANG RGYUN DANG CHA SHAS GANG YANG NGA'I MTSAN GZHIR 'JOG RGYU MED CING, PHUNG PO LAS NGO BO THA DAD PA GZHAN ZHIG KYANG NGA'I MTSAN GZHIR BZUNG MED PAS, NGA DE NI PHUNG PO LA BRTEN NAS BTAGS PA TZAM YIN GYI, RANG GI NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB PA MED DO,,
gru.wylie: de bzhin du phung po 'di la brten nas nga'o snyam du 'byung yang, phung po'i tshogs pa dang rgyun dang cha shas gang yang nga'i mtshan gzhir 'jog rgyu med cing, phung po las ngo bo tha dad pa gzhan zhig kyang nga'i mtshan gzhir bzung med pas, nga de ni phung po la brten nas btags pa tsam yin gyi, rang gi ngo bo nyid kyis grub pa med do
gru.english: In the same way, the heaps of parts that make us up serve as a basis for us to get the impression “This is me.” There is nothing at all about these heaps as a whole, nor their continuation over time, nor their separate components, that we could establish as being an actual representation of “me.” At the same time though there is nothing else, nothing essentially separate from these heaps of parts to ourselves, that we could consider an actual representation of “me” either. As such, this “me” is merely something labeled upon the heaps of parts that make us up; there is nothing which exists by its own essence.

gru.acip: 'O NA SKYES BU STE GANG ZAG JI LTAR 'JOG PA YANG DE NYID LAS, ,SKYES BU KHAMS DRUG 'DUS PA'I PHYIR, ,YANG DAG MA YIN JI LTA BAR, ,DE BZHIN KHAMS NI RE RE YANG, ,'DUS PHYIR YANG DAG NYID DU MIN, ,ZHES GSUNGS TE, RGYU MTSAN DES NA SKYES BU NI RANG GI KHAMS DRUG 'DUS PA'I STENG DU BTAGS PA TZAM MA GTOGS, YANG DAG PAR MA GRUB BO,,
gru.wylie: 'o na skyes bu ste gang zag ji ltar 'jog pa yang de nyid las, ,skyes bu khams drug 'dus pa'i phyir, ,yang dag ma yin ji lta bar, ,de bzhin khams ni re re yang, ,'dus phyir yang dag nyid du min, ,zhes gsungs te, rgyu mtshan des na skyes bu ni rang gi khams drug 'dus pa'i steng du btags pa tsam ma gtogs, yang dag par ma grub bo
gru.english: How then do we establish the existence of the persona (which in this case simply means “person”)? The same work says: Because the persona includes all six elements, It's nothing that purely exists; Just so, because they include their parts, None of these elements purely exist. Given the reason stated above, the persona is nothing more than something labeled upon the six elements that make them up—it does not though purely exist.

gru.acip: DE JI LTA BA BZHIN DU KHAMS RNAMS KYANG RANG RANG GI CHA SHAS 'DUS PA LA BRTEN NAS BTAGS PA YIN PA'I PHYIR YANG DAG PAR MA GRUB ZHES BSTAN TO, ,DE BZHIN DU PHUNG SOGS KYI CHOS THAMS CAD KYANG RANG RANG GI CHA SHAS DANG TSOGS PA LA BRTEN NAS BTAGS PA YIN PA'I PHYIR RANG DBANG DU GRUB PA MED CES SBYOR RO,,
gru.wylie: de ji lta ba bzhin du khams rnams kyang rang rang gi cha shas 'dus pa la brten nas btags pa yin pa'i phyir yang dag par ma grub zhes bstan to, ,de bzhin du phung sogs kyi chos thams cad kyang rang rang gi cha shas dang tshogs pa la brten nas btags pa yin pa'i phyir rang dbang du grub pa med ces sbyor ro
gru.english: Just so, none of these elements themselves exist purely, for they too are simply labeled upon the parts that they include. This same reasoning can be applied to the heaps of parts that make up a person, and all other objects as well: you can say about all of them that, because they are labeled on their parts and their whole, they do not exist independently.

gru.acip: GONG GI PHRO NI, BDEN PAR GRUB PA'I SEMS CAN GANG YANG MYANG 'DAS THOB PA MED PAR SEMS BSKYED DGOS PA'I RGYU MTSAN LA DE CI'I PHYIR ZHE NA, RAB 'BYOR ZHES BOS NAS GAL TE BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA' GANG SEMS CAN LA SEMS CAN DU BDEN PAR GRUB PA'I 'DU SHES 'JUG NA, BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA' DE BDAG MED RTOGS PA'I BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA' ZHES MI BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: gong gi phro ni, bden par grub pa'i sems can gang yang myang 'das thob pa med par sems bskyed dgos pa'i rgyu mtshan la de ci'i phyir zhe na, rab 'byor zhes bos nas gal te byang chub sems dpa' gang sems can la sems can du bden par grub pa'i 'du shes 'jug na, byang chub sems dpa' de bdag med rtogs pa'i byang chub sems dpa' zhes mi bya'o
gru.english: Here we return to where we left off in the root text. One may ask, “Why is it so? What reason is there for saying that we should develop a Wish for enlightenment, while still understanding that there is no truly existing being at all who ever achieves this nirvana?” Lord Buddha first calls Subhuti by name, and then explains that we could never call any particular bodhisattva a “bodhisattva who had realized the meaning of no-self-nature” if this bodhisattva were to slip into conceiving of any living being as a living being who existed truly.

gru.acip: SBYIN PA SBYIN PA LA BRTZON PA LTA BU NI JI LTAR GNAS PAR BYA ZHES PA'I DON DANG, DE'I 'KHOR GSUM LA BDEN PAR MI ZHEN PA NI JI LTAR BSGRUB PAR BYA ZHES PA'I DON DANG, BDEN MED DU RTOGS PA'I BLO LA SEMS RTZE GCIG TU BYED PA NI SEMS RAB TU GZUNG BAR BYA ZHES PA'I DON DU BSHAD DE, PHAR PHYIN GZHAN LA'ANG SBYAR BAR BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: sbyin pa sbyin pa la brtson pa lta bu ni ji ltar gnas par bya zhes pa'i don dang, de'i 'khor gsum la bden par mi zhen pa ni ji ltar bsgrub par bya zhes pa'i don dang, bden med du rtogs pa'i blo la sems rtse gcig tu byed pa ni sems rab tu gzung bar bya zhes pa'i don du bshad de, phar phyin gzhan la'ang sbyar bar bya'o
gru.english: There are a number of expressions here. One is that “We should stay in our giving just as those who are striving in their giving.” Another is “We should try to practice in a way where we have no belief that the three spheres of this act are real.” And they are both to be explained as meaning “Maintain, perfectly, a state of mind where you are single-pointedly absorbed in the understanding that nothing is true.”

gru.acip: RAB 'BYOR CHOS THAMS CAD THA SNYAD BTAGS PA TZAM DU YOD PA MA GTOGS, RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA RDUL TZAM YANG MED PA'I PHYIR RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAR 'DZIN PA NI PHYIN CI LOG TU ZHEN PA YIN PAS,
gru.wylie: rab 'byor chos thams cad tha snyad btags pa tsam du yod pa ma gtogs, rang bzhin gyis grub pa rdul tsam yang med pa'i phyir rang bzhin gyis grub par 'dzin pa ni phyin ci log tu zhen pa yin pas
gru.english: And what Lord Buddha is saying then is: “O Subhuti, every single object in the universe exists only through our projections; they have not a single atom of any other kind of existence—any natural existence. As such, anyone who holds that things could exist through any nature of their own is entertaining a belief which is completely mistaken.

gru.acip: CI NAS KYANG RANG BZHIN KYIS GRUB PAR ZHEN PA'I MTSAN MAR 'DZIN PA'I 'DU SHES LA BYANG CHUB SEMS DPAS GNAS PAR MI BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: ci nas kyang rang bzhin kyis grub par zhen pa'i mtshan mar 'dzin pa'i 'du shes la byang chub sems dpas gnas par mi bya'o
gru.english: “And bodhisattvas never stay in any kind of conception where they hold to the signs of things: where they believe in any way at all that things could exist through any nature of their own.”

gru.acip: SBYIN SOGS BSOD NAMS KYI TSOGS LAS SANGS RGYAS KYI GZUGS SKU 'GRUB PAR 'GYUR ZHING, GZUGS KYI SKU NI MTSAN DPES BRGYAN PA'O, ,RAB 'BYOR 'DI JI SNYAM DU SEMS ZHES PA NI, RAB 'BYOR KHYOD KYIS DON 'DI LA JI LTAR YIN SNYAM DU SEMS PA STE BSAM,
gru.wylie: sbyin sogs bsod nams kyi tshogs las sangs rgyas kyi gzugs sku 'grub par 'gyur zhing, gzugs kyi sku ni mtshan dpes brgyan pa'o, ,rab 'byor 'di ji snyam du sems zhes pa ni, rab 'byor khyod kyis don 'di la ji ltar yin snyam du sems pa ste bsam
gru.english: The merit of acts such as giving and the rest bring us the physical body of a Buddha, and this physical body is adorned with various major signs and minor marks. The words “Now Subhuti, what do you think?” mean “Subhuti, turn your mind to this subject, and think about how it could be—contemplate upon it.”

gru.acip: 'O NA MI BRDZUN PA GANG ZHE NA, JI TZAM DU MTSAN DPE PHUN SUM TSOGS PA RNAMS BDEN BAR MED PA DE TZAM NI MI BRDZUN ZHING BDEN TE, DE LTAR DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA LA BDEN PAR GRUB PA'I MTSAN DANG MTSAN MA MED PAR BLTA BAR BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: 'o na mi brdzun pa gang zhe na, ji tsam du mtshan dpe phun sum tshogs pa rnams bden bar med pa de tsam ni mi brdzun zhing bden te, de ltar de bzhin gshegs pa la bden par grub pa'i mtshan dang mtshan ma med par blta bar bya'o
gru.english: “Well then what,” you may ask, “is meant by the following words: 'the signs are not deceptive'?” The totally exquisite signs and marks on a Buddha's body are also not deceptive, and are true, but only insofar as they do not exist truly. And so you should see the One Thus Gone as having no signs, no signs to indicate his nature, at all.

gru.acip: RGYU MTSAN DE BAS NA DE BZHIN GSHEGS PAS TSUL DE LA DGONGS NAS LUNG GI CHOS KYI RNAM GRANGS 'DI GRU GZINGS LTA BU STE GRU GZING NI CHU'I PHA ROL TU PHYIN PA NA MI DGOS PAR SHES PA LTA BU MTHAR PHYIN PA'I 'PHAGS PA RNAMS KYIS NI, 'BRAS BU THOB BYED KYI THABS LUNG GI TSOGS LTA BU'I CHOS RNAMS KYANG 'BRAS BU THOB PA'I TSE 'DOR ZHING SPANG BAR BYA NA, DAM PA'I CHOS MA YIN PA RNAMS 'DOR BA GZHIR BCAS TE LTA CI SMOS SO ZHES GSUNGS SO,,
gru.wylie: rgyu mtshan de bas na de bzhin gshegs pas tshul de la dgongs nas lung gi chos kyi rnam grangs 'di gru gzings lta bu ste gru gzing ni chu'i pha rol tu phyin pa na mi dgos par shes pa lta bu mthar phyin pa'i 'phags pa rnams kyis ni, 'bras bu thob byed kyi thabs lung gi tshogs lta bu'i chos rnams kyang 'bras bu thob pa'i tshe 'dor zhing spang bar bya na, dam pa'i chos ma yin pa rnams 'dor ba gzhir bcas te lta ci smos so zhes gsungs so
gru.english: This then is why—this then is what the One Thus Gone meant when he said that—this presentation of the Dharma is like a ship. We understand that, once we have crossed over a body of water in a ship to the far shore, then we no longer have any need of the ship itself. Realized beings who have reached the final goal are the same. Once they reach this goal, then they abandon or leave behind even these teachings of the Dharma—even those collections of physical Dharma which are the means for us to reach the goal. What need then is there to mention—given then what we just said, the sutra is saying—what these beings do with that which is not the Dharma?

whole_word_matches.context: shul de la dgongs nas lung gi chos kyi rnam grangs 'di gru gzings lta bu ste gru gzing ni chu'i pha rol tu phyin
lung gi chos kyi rnam grangs 'di gru gzings lta bu ste gru gzing ni chu'i pha rol tu phyin pa na mi dgos par shes

gru.acip: MGON PO KLU SGRUB KYIS RTZA BA SHES RAB KYI RAB BYED NYER GNYIS PA LAS,
gru.wylie: mgon po klu sgrub kyis rtsa ba shes rab kyi rab byed nyer gnyis pa las
gru.english: It's just the way that our savior, Nagarjuna, has described it in the 22nd chapter of his Root Text on Wisdom—

gru.acip: LAN DU RAB 'BYOR GYIS BSOD NAMS KYI PHUNG PO MANG BAR ZHUS SHING BSOD NAMS KYI PHUNG PO DE YANG RMI LAM DANG SGYU MA LTA BUR THA SNYAD TZAM DU YOD PAR 'JOG LAGS KYI, BSOD NAMS KYI PHUNG PO DE NYID DON DAM PAR PHUNG POR GRUB PA MA MCHIS SHING, THA SNYAD DU DE BZHIN GSHEGS PAS DE LA BSOD NAMS KYI PHUNG PO, ,BSOD NAMS KYI PHUNG PO ZHES THA SNYAD MDZAD CING GSUNGS SO ZHES GSOL,
gru.wylie: lan du rab 'byor gyis bsod nams kyi phung po mang bar zhus shing bsod nams kyi phung po de yang rmi lam dang sgyu ma lta bur tha snyad tsam du yod par 'jog lags kyi, bsod nams kyi phung po de nyid don dam par phung por grub pa ma mchis shing, tha snyad du de bzhin gshegs pas de la bsod nams kyi phung po, ,bsod nams kyi phung po zhes tha snyad mdzad cing gsungs so zhes gsol
gru.english: In response, Subhuti replies: It would be many great mountains of merit—and these same great mountains of merit are mountains of merit that we could establish as existing only in name, only in the way that a dream or an illusion exists: these same great mountains of merit though could never exist as mountains that existed ultimately. The Ones Thus Gone as well speak in a nominal sense of “great mountains of merit, great mountains of merit”—applying the name to them.

gru.acip: BCOM LDAN 'DAS KYIS BKA' STZAL PA, RAB 'BYOR, BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA' GANG LA LA ZHIG 'DI SKAD DU, BDAG GIS ZHING BKOD PA RNAMS BSGRUB PAR BYA'O, ,ZHES ZER NA, DE NI, MI BDEN PAR SMRA BA'O,,
gru.wylie: bcom ldan 'das kyis bka' stsal pa, rab 'byor, byang chub sems dpa' gang la la zhig 'di skad du, bdag gis zhing bkod pa rnams bsgrub par bya'o, ,zhes zer na, de ni, mi bden par smra ba'o
gru.english: Then the Conqueror spoke once more, Suppose, o Subhuti, that some bodhisattva were to say, “I am working to bring about my paradise.” This would not be spoken true.

gru.acip: DE LTA BAS NA BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA' ZHING GI BKOD PA BSGRUB PAR BYA BA NA 'DI LTAR BDEN ZHEN GYIS MI GNAS PAR SEMS BSKYED PAR BYA'O, ,DON DAM PAR CI LA YANG MI GNAS SHING GZUGS SGRA SOGS KYI CHOS GANG LA BDEN ZHEN GYIS MI GNAS PAR SEMS BSKYED PAR BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: de lta bas na byang chub sems dpa' zhing gi bkod pa bsgrub par bya ba na 'di ltar bden zhen gyis mi gnas par sems bskyed par bya'o, ,don dam par ci la yang mi gnas shing gzugs sgra sogs kyi chos gang la bden zhen gyis mi gnas par sems bskyed par bya'o
gru.english: Since this is so, says Lord Buddha, those bodhisattvas who are working to bring about their paradise should develop their Wish for enlightenment without staying in any such state where they hold a belief in some true existence. They should develop their Wish without staying in any state where they believe in the ultimate existence of anything at all. They should develop their Wish without staying in any state where they hold a belief in some true existence of any object at all: in anything you can see, or in sounds, or in any of the rest. The emptiness of my body

gru.acip: LAN DU LUS DE CHE BAR ZHUS SHING, LUS DE NYID CHA DU MA TSOGS PA'I PHUNG PO THA SNYAD TZAM DU YOD KYI, CHA LA MA BLTOS PA'I DNGOS PO STE NGO BOR MED PAR DE BZHIN GSHEGS PAS GSUNGS TE, 'JIG RTEN GYI THA SNYAD DU LUS DE LA CHE'O ZHES BYA'O, ,DES NA DON DAM PAR LUS SU GRUB PA MA MCHIS PA'I KUN RDZOB PA'I LUS DE LA LUS ZHES BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: lan du lus de che bar zhus shing, lus de nyid cha du ma tshogs pa'i phung po tha snyad tsam du yod kyi, cha la ma bltos pa'i dngos po ste ngo bor med par de bzhin gshegs pas gsungs te, 'jig rten gyi tha snyad du lus de la che'o zhes bya'o, ,des na don dam par lus su grub pa ma mchis pa'i kun rdzob pa'i lus de la lus zhes bya'o
gru.english: And Subhuti respectfully replies, “Such a body would be large.” Those Who Have Gone Thus though have stated that this same body exists only as a term applied to the heaps, to some collection of a great many parts. It could never be a thing at all which existed in essence; that is, it could never be something which did not depend on its parts, say they. And this is precisely why we can call such a body “large,” in the sense that words are used in the everyday world. And so what we call “the body” is the body which exists in a deceptive sense: one that could never exist as a body in any ultimate sense.

gru.acip: DE BZHIN GSHEGS PAS SHES RAB KYI PHA ROL TU PHYIN PA ZHES GANG GSUNGS PA DE NYID DON DAM PAR PHA ROL TU PHYIN PAR GRUB PA MED CING, DES NA THA SNYAD DU SHES RAB KYI PHA ROL TU PHYIN PA ZHES 'DOGS SO,,
gru.wylie: de bzhin gshegs pas shes rab kyi pha rol tu phyin pa zhes gang gsungs pa de nyid don dam par pha rol tu phyin par grub pa med cing, des na tha snyad du shes rab kyi pha rol tu phyin pa zhes 'dogs so
gru.english: That same perfection of wisdom spoken by the Ones Thus Gone to be the “perfection of wisdom” is a perfection of wisdom that doesn't even exist as a perfection of wisdom in an ultimate sense. And this is precisely why we can, in a nominal sense, label it the “perfection of wisdom.”

gru.acip: LAN DU DE MANG NGO ZHES ZHUS SHING, SA'I RDUL PHRA RAB GANG YIN PA DE RNAMS NI DON DAM PAR RDUL DU GRUB PA MA MCHIS PAR DE BZHIN GSHEGS PAS GSUNGS TE, DON DAM PAR MED CING THA SNYAD DU YOD PA DES NA SA'I RDUL ZHES BGYI'O,,
gru.wylie: lan du de mang ngo zhes zhus shing, sa'i rdul phra rab gang yin pa de rnams ni don dam par rdul du grub pa ma mchis par de bzhin gshegs pas gsungs te, don dam par med cing tha snyad du yod pa des na sa'i rdul zhes bgyi'o
gru.english: And then Subhuti respectfully replies, “It would indeed be a great many.” He goes on to say that the Ones Gone Thus have stated that these same atoms of dust could never exist as atoms, in an ultimate sense. And it is precisely because these atoms do not exist ultimately—but do exist nominally—that we can even speak of them as “atoms of dust.”

gru.acip: DES NA RDUL PHRA RAB GCIG NI YAN GAR DU GNAS MI NUS PAS GZHAN DANG TSOGS SHING 'DUS PA LA LTOS DGOS PAS RDUL PHRA RAB RANG DBANG GIS MA GRUB CING, DE MA GRUB PAS DE BSAGS PA'I RDUL RAGS PA'ANG RANG DBANG GIS MA GRUB CES BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: des na rdul phra rab gcig ni yan gar du gnas mi nus pas gzhan dang tshogs shing 'dus pa la ltos dgos pas rdul phra rab rang dbang gis ma grub cing, de ma grub pas de bsags pa'i rdul rags pa'ang rang dbang gis ma grub ces bya'o
gru.english: Neither then could a single atom ever exist independently: it would have then to exist only in conjunction with, as a composite part of, other pieces of matter. In such case, no single atom would possess any independent existence; and then neither could any more gross physical object which was composed of such atoms.

gru.acip: DE NAS 'JIG RTEN GYI KHAMS SU MA ZAD, SANGS RGYAS KYI GZUGS SKU DANG DE'I MTSAN DPE YANG DON DAM PAR MA GRUB CES PA NI,
gru.wylie: de nas 'jig rten gyi khams su ma zad, sangs rgyas kyi gzugs sku dang de'i mtshan dpe yang don dam par ma grub ces pa ni
gru.english: Lord Buddha next wants to express to us how not only are the various worlds something that cannot exist in an ultimate way, but this is true as well of the body of form of a Buddha, and the signs and marks upon this body.

gru.acip: TSUL 'DI NGO MTSAR CHE STE, MGON PO KLU SGRUB ZHABS KYIS, ,CHOS RNAMS STONG PA 'DI SHES NAS, ,LAS DANG 'BRAS BU BSTAN PA GANG, ,NGO MTSAR BAS KYANG 'DI NGO MTSAR, ,RMAD BYUNG BAS KYANG 'DI RMAD BYUNG, ,ZHES GSUNGS PA LTAR RO,,
gru.wylie: tshul 'di ngo mtshar che ste, mgon po klu sgrub zhabs kyis, ,chos rnams stong pa 'di shes nas, ,las dang 'bras bu bstan pa gang, ,ngo mtshar bas kyang 'di ngo mtshar, ,rmad byung bas kyang 'di rmad byung, ,zhes gsungs pa ltar ro
gru.english: And indeed this is a wondrous thing, for as our Protector, Nagarjuna, also puts it— When I think of someone Who comprehends that things Are empty, and who Goes on to teach about Action and consequence, Then truly I feel It is more wondrous than wondrous More miraculous than miraculous.

gru.acip: RGYU MTSAN NI GZUGS SGRA SOGS LA ZHEN CING GNAS PA'I YUL GZUGS SOGS GANG YIN PA DE NYID DON DAM PAR MI GNAS PA STE MA GRUB PA'I PHYIR RO ZHES SO,,
gru.wylie: rgyu mtshan ni gzugs sgra sogs la zhen cing gnas pa'i yul gzugs sogs gang yin pa de nyid don dam par mi gnas pa ste ma grub pa'i phyir ro zhes so
gru.english: The Teacher then concludes by saying, And for what reason is it so? Because none of these things to see or sounds or the rest—none of these very things to see that we believe in, or stay in—ever stay in any ultimate way themselves, never exist in any ultimate way themselves.

gru.acip: RAB 'BYOR DE BZHIN GSHEGS PAS THOB BYA'I CHOS GANG YANG SANGS RGYAS PA'AM BSTAN PA DE RNAMS LA BDEN PA DON DAM PA'I CHOS RNAMS BDEN PAR GRUB PA YANG MED CING, RDZUN PA KUN RDZOB PA'I CHOS RNAMS KYANG BDEN PAR GRUB PA MED DO ZHES SO,,
gru.wylie: rab 'byor de bzhin gshegs pas thob bya'i chos gang yang sangs rgyas pa'am bstan pa de rnams la bden pa don dam pa'i chos rnams bden par grub pa yang med cing, rdzun pa kun rdzob pa'i chos rnams kyang bden par grub pa med do zhes so
gru.english: And I speak to you, o Subhuti, of that thing where Those Gone Thus reach some enlightenment; and of that thing which is the Dharma that They teach. These have no truth, a truth where ultimately existing things exist in reality. Neither do they have any deception, where deceptively existing things exist in reality.

gru.acip: 'DIR NI MTHONG LAM THOB PA LA NYE BA DANG DE THOB PA'I SKABS NAS DE LTAR BYED PA LA DGONGS NAS GSUNGS TE DON NI SNGAR BSHAD ZIN PA LTAR RO, ,BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA'I THEG PA LA ZHUGS PA'I CHOS DE GANG YANG BDEN PAR GRUB PA MED DO ZHES MJUG BSDUS SO,,
gru.wylie: 'dir ni mthong lam thob pa la nye ba dang de thob pa'i skabs nas de ltar byed pa la dgongs nas gsungs te don ni sngar bshad zin pa ltar ro, ,byang chub sems dpa'i theg pa la zhugs pa'i chos de gang yang bden par grub pa med do zhes mjug bsdus so
gru.english: Here though repeating the same wording is intended to fit the context of being either close to attaining the path of seeing or having already attained this path. The meaning of the section is the same as we explained previously; here it is like a summary for describing how nothing related to entering the way of the bodhisattva could ever exist in truth. No teacher was taught

gru.acip: GAL TE DE 'DRA BA'I CHOS 'GA' ZHIG YOD PAR GYUR NA NI, DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA MAR ME MDZAD KYIS NGA LA BRAM ZE'I KHYE'U KHYOD MA 'ONGS PA'I DUS 'DI TZAM NAS SANGS RGYAS SH'AKYA THUB PA ZHES BYA BAR 'GYUR RO ZHES LUNG MI STON PA ZHIG NA, MNGON PAR RDZOGS PAR SANGS RGYAS PA'I CHOS GANG YANG BDEN PAR GRUB PA MED PA'I PHYIR NA, DE'I TSE DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA MAR ME MDZAD KYIS NGA LA DE LTAR BYANG CHUB TU LUNG BSTAN TO,,
gru.wylie: gal te de 'dra ba'i chos 'ga' zhig yod par gyur na ni, de bzhin gshegs pa mar me mdzad kyis nga la bram ze'i khye'u khyod ma 'ongs pa'i dus 'di tsam nas sangs rgyas shAkya thub pa zhes bya bar 'gyur ro zhes lung mi ston pa zhig na, mngon par rdzogs par sangs rgyas pa'i chos gang yang bden par grub pa med pa'i phyir na, de'i tshe de bzhin gshegs pa mar me mdzad kyis nga la de ltar byang chub tu lung bstan to
gru.english: If there had been any such thing, anything of the sort, then the One Gone Thus, “Maker of Light,” could never have granted the Buddha his final prediction, saying “O child of Brahman family, in so and so many days to come you will become the Buddha called 'Able One of the Shakya Clan'.” But the fact is that—since there's nothing about a fully enlightened Buddha which does exist in truth—then the One Thus Gone named “Maker of Light” did in fact at that time “grant this final prediction of my enlightenment to me.”

gru.acip: DE YANG GANG GIS GANG ZHIG GANG DU LUNG BSTAN PA'I CHOS RNAMS NI THA SNYAD BTAGS YOD MING RKYANG TZAM YIN GYI, DON DAM PAR GRUB PA MED PA'I TSUL GONG DU BRJOD ZIN TO,,
gru.wylie: de yang gang gis gang zhig gang du lung bstan pa'i chos rnams ni tha snyad btags yod ming rkyang tsam yin gyi, don dam par grub pa med pa'i tshul gong du brjod zin to
gru.english: Now the person who makes such a prediction, and who they make the prediction about, and the prediction they make for them are things that exist only in name: only as a projection. As we've already explained above, they have no ultimate kind of existence.

gru.acip: THOB BYA THOB BYED KYI CHOS LA BDEN PAR ZHEN NAS BDEN 'DZIN GYIS BCINGS PA RNAMS NI DNGOS LUNG BSTAN PA'I SNOD DU MI RUNG BA'I PHYIR TE, BDEN GRUB KYI CHOS BSGYUR DU MI NUS PAS THOB BYED SOGS GANG YANG 'JOG TU MI RUNG BAR SNGAR BSHAD ZIN PA'I PHYIR RO,,
gru.wylie: thob bya thob byed kyi chos la bden par zhen nas bden 'dzin gyis bcings pa rnams ni dngos lung bstan pa'i snod du mi rung ba'i phyir te, bden grub kyi chos bsgyur du mi nus pas thob byed sogs gang yang 'jog tu mi rung bar sngar bshad zin pa'i phyir ro
gru.english: And that's because a person who was still locked in the chains of believing that these particular things were real—something to be reached, and something that helped them reach it—would be no proper vessel to receive a precise prediction. This in turn (as we've already covered) is due to the fact that any object which existed in reality could never change—which would mean that they couldn't be something that helped us reach a goal, or anything of the like. Why they have gone thus

gru.acip: DE BZHIN GSHEGS PAS CHOS GANG SANGS RGYAS PA'AM BSTAN PA DE LA RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA'I DON DAM PA'I CHOS BDEN PA YANG MED CING, DER GRUB PA'I KUN RDZOB PA'I CHOS BRDZUN PA YANG MED DO,,
gru.wylie: de bzhin gshegs pas chos gang sangs rgyas pa'am bstan pa de la rang bzhin gyis grub pa'i don dam pa'i chos bden pa yang med cing, der grub pa'i kun rdzob pa'i chos brdzun pa yang med do
gru.english: This thing where the One Gone Thus reaches their enlightenment—here meaning an ultimate thing, a thing about this teaching that could exist through some nature of its own—could never be real. Neither though could it be false, in the sense of being some object within deceptive reality which existed with the same kind of nature.

gru.acip: DE NAS RAB 'BYOR GYIS DE LA BU'I DPE'I LUS DE DON DAM PAR LUS SU MA GRUB KYANG, THA SNYAD DU DE LTAR 'JOG GO ZHES ZHUS PA NA BCOM LDAN 'DAS KYIS DE DE BZHIN NO ZHES SOGS GNANG NGO,,
gru.wylie: de nas rab 'byor gyis de la bu'i dpe'i lus de don dam par lus su ma grub kyang, tha snyad du de ltar 'jog go zhes zhus pa na bcom ldan 'das kyis de de bzhin no zhes sogs gnang ngo
gru.english: Subhuti then respectfully addresses the Buddha by noting, on this point, that the body in the example of the child's growth may not exist in any ultimate way, but can still be established as existing nominally. The Conqueror then concurs with this position, in the words that include “This is how it is.”

gru.acip: BCOM LDAN 'DAS KYIS RAB 'BYOR LA DE MED PA'I RGYU MTSAN DE BAS NA DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA KUN BYANG GI CHOS THAMS CAD GANG ZAG GI BDAG TU GRUB PA'I SEMS CAN MED PA, SROG MED PA, GANG ZAG MED PA'O ZHES GSUNGS SO,,
gru.wylie: bcom ldan 'das kyis rab 'byor la de med pa'i rgyu mtshan de bas na de bzhin gshegs pa kun byang gi chos thams cad gang zag gi bdag tu grub pa'i sems can med pa, srog med pa, gang zag med pa'o zhes gsungs so
gru.english: And the Conqueror then says to Subhuti, “This is why—it is because no such thing could ever be—the One Thus Gone says that all existing things, whether they be part of the negative side of things or the enlightened, are such that no living being exists, and nothing that lives exists, and no person exists, who possesses some 'self' of the person.”

gru.acip: BSDU NA BDAG NI THOB PAR BYED PA'O, ,'DI NI THOB PAR BYA BA'I CHOS SO SNYAM DU BDEN ZHEN GYIS 'JUG NA MED PA LA YOD PAR RLOM PA MNGON PA'I NGA RGYAL CAN DU BSHAD PAS MI RUNG ZHES PA STE BDEN PAR GRUB NA BSGYUR DU MI RUNG BA'I PHYIR CHOS GANG LA'ANG THOB BYA THOB BYED SOGS BZHAG TU MI RUNG NGO ZHES GONG DU BSHAD ZIN TO,,
gru.wylie: bsdu na bdag ni thob par byed pa'o, ,'di ni thob par bya ba'i chos so snyam du bden zhen gyis 'jug na med pa la yod par rlom pa mngon pa'i nga rgyal can du bshad pas mi rung zhes pa ste bden par grub na bsgyur du mi rung ba'i phyir chos gang la'ang thob bya thob byed sogs bzhag tu mi rung ngo zhes gong du bshad zin to
gru.english: To sum then, let's take the case of someone who, with a belief that things are real, thinks to themselves that “I am going to achieve this or that,” or “This is the thing that I'm going to achieve.” What's being said in the text is that they would then be a person who had some extreme kind of delusion of grandeur—a delusion where they thought something existed, when in truth it didn't exist at all. This then would be “wrong,” the text is saying—because if things existed in truth then it would be wrong for them ever to exhibit change. Then further it would be wrong to say about any object at all that it could either be achieved or cause us to achieve anything. This point has already been explained previously.

gru.acip: 'DI DAG GIS NI JI LTAR BSGRUB PAR BYA ZHES PA'I DON BDAG MED BSGOM TSUL BSTAN TO,,
gru.wylie: 'di dag gis ni ji ltar bsgrub par bya zhes pa'i don bdag med bsgom tshul bstan to
gru.english: All of these sections have been addressing the question at the beginning of the sutra of “How should they practice?” That is, they have instructed us in how we are to meditate upon the lack of a self.

gru.acip: RAB 'BYOR, BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA' GANG ZHIG 'DI SKAD DU, BDAG GIS ZHING BKOD PA RNAMS BSGRUB BO, ,ZHES ZER NA, DE YANG DE BZHIN DU BRJOD PAR BYA'O,, DE CI'I PHYIR ZHE NA, RAB 'BYOR ZHING BKOD PA RNAMS ZHING BKOD PA RNAMS ZHES BYA BA DE NI, DE DAG BKOD PA MED PAR DE BZHIN GSHEGS PAS GSUNGS PA'I PHYIR TE, DES NA ZHING BKOD PA RNAMS ZHES BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: rab 'byor, byang chub sems dpa' gang zhig 'di skad du, bdag gis zhing bkod pa rnams bsgrub bo, ,zhes zer na, de yang de bzhin du brjod par bya'o,, de ci'i phyir zhe na, rab 'byor zhing bkod pa rnams zhing bkod pa rnams zhes bya ba de ni, de dag bkod pa med par de bzhin gshegs pas gsungs pa'i phyir te, des na zhing bkod pa rnams zhes bya'o
gru.english: And suppose, o Subhuti, that some bodhisattva were to say, “I am working to bring about my paradise.” That would not be spoken rightly. Why is it so? Because, o Subhuti, the paradise that you are working to bring about when you say “I am working to bring about my paradise” is something that the One Thus Gone has said that you could never bring about. And this is precisely why we can even speak of these as “paradises to bring about.”

gru.acip: RAB 'BYOR BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA' GANG ZHIG 'DI SNYAM DU, BDAG GIS GANG DU 'TSANG RGYA BA'I GNAS KYI ZHING GI BKOD PA PHUN SUM TSOGS PA RNAM PAR DON DAM PAR BSGRUB PAR BYA'O ZHES ZHEN CING TSIG GIS ZER NA, DE YANG DE BZHIN DU BRJOD CING ZHEN PAR BYAR MI RUNG NGO,,
gru.wylie: rab 'byor byang chub sems dpa' gang zhig 'di snyam du, bdag gis gang du 'tshang rgya ba'i gnas kyi zhing gi bkod pa phun sum tshogs pa rnam par don dam par bsgrub par bya'o zhes zhen cing tshig gis zer na, de yang de bzhin du brjod cing zhen par byar mi rung ngo
gru.english: And suppose, o Subhuti, that some bodhisattva were to think to themselves, “I am working to bring about a perfect paradise, the place where I will become enlightened, in a way which is ultimately real.” That is, suppose they were to entertain this kind of belief, and express it in their words. That too would not be spoken rightly; it would not be a right sort of belief.

gru.acip: RGYU MTSAN LA ZHING GI BKOD PA DE DAG NI, KUN RDZOB TU TSOGS SHING 'DUS PA SGYU MA LTAR YOD PA LAS GZHAN BDEN PAR GRUB PA'I BKOD PA MED PAR DE BZHIN GSHEGS PAS GSUNGS PA'I PHYIR TE, DES NA THA SNYAD DU ZHING BKOD PA RNAMS ZHES BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: rgyu mtshan la zhing gi bkod pa de dag ni, kun rdzob tu tshogs shing 'dus pa sgyu ma ltar yod pa las gzhan bden par grub pa'i bkod pa med par de bzhin gshegs pas gsungs pa'i phyir te, des na tha snyad du zhing bkod pa rnams zhes bya'o
gru.english: Why, for what reason, would that be the case? It's because the One Thus Gone has said that there is no such creating of a paradise—of paradises that were brought about in a way which was real, rather than existing, in a deceptive way, as a collection or a gathering of other things; as something that resembled an illusion. And this is precisely why we can even speak of paradises which are brought about in a nominal way. What we call “a bodhisattva”

gru.acip: DE LTAR YIN KYANG SEMS CAN GYI SEMS KYI RGYUN NI DON DAM PAR RGYUN ZHES BYA BAR GRUB PA MED PAR NGAS BSHAD DE, DON DAM PAR MED PA DES NA THA SNYAD DU SEMS KYI RGYUN ZHES BYA BAR BRJOD DO,,
gru.wylie: de ltar yin kyang sems can gyi sems kyi rgyun ni don dam par rgyun zhes bya bar grub pa med par ngas bshad de, don dam par med pa des na tha snyad du sems kyi rgyun zhes bya bar brjod do
gru.english: “And even though that is the case,” continues the Buddha, “I say that none of the mindstreams of these living beings could ever exist as a stream in any ultimate sense. And it is precisely because of this—that they cannot exist in any ultimate sense—that we can call them a “mindstream.”

gru.acip: 'DIS SPYAN LNGA DANG SPYAN LNGA'I YUL RNAMS KYANG THA SNYAD TZAM DU 'JOG GI ,DON DAM PAR MA GRUB CES BSTAN TO,,
gru.wylie: 'dis spyan lnga dang spyan lnga'i yul rnams kyang tha snyad tsam du 'jog gi ,don dam par ma grub ces bstan to
gru.english: This last section then is meant to demonstrate to us how the five different kinds of eyes, and the objects of these five kinds of eyes, are established only nominally: how they cannot though exist in any ultimate sense. The emptiness of the mind, in time

gru.acip: DES NA TSOR BA BDEN PAR MA GRUB PAR STON PA'I RIGS PA MANG YANG RTZA BA NI, ,ZHI BA LHAS, ,GANG TSE TSOR BO 'GA' MED NA, ,TSOR BA 'GA' YANG YOD MIN TE, ,ZHES GSUNGS PA 'DI LTA BU YIN LA,
gru.wylie: des na tshor ba bden par ma grub par ston pa'i rigs pa mang yang rtsa ba ni, ,zhi ba lhas, ,gang tshe tshor bo 'ga' med na, ,tshor ba 'ga' yang yod min te, ,zhes gsungs pa 'di lta bu yin la
gru.english: There are then many different forms of reasoning used to demonstrate that feelings do not exist in and of themselves; the principal one though is the following. As Master Shantideva has put it, If it's the case that there is No one at all who feels, Then neither can there be Any feeling that they feel.

gru.acip: MDOR NA TSOR BA LA SOGS PA'I SHES PA KUN KYANG DMIGS PA LA BRTEN NAS MAR ME'I 'OD BZHIN DU THA SNYAD TZAM DU SKYE'I, DE LTA BU LA MA BRTEN PAR RANG DBANG GIS MI SKYE BAS RANG BZHIN GYIS MA GRUB BO,,
gru.wylie: mdor na tshor ba la sogs pa'i shes pa kun kyang dmigs pa la brten nas mar me'i 'od bzhin du tha snyad tsam du skye'i, de lta bu la ma brten par rang dbang gis mi skye bas rang bzhin gyis ma grub bo
gru.english: We can summarize then by saying that all states of mind involved with feeling and the like depend upon the object towards which they are focused; they thus arise only nominally, in the way that light emanates from a butter lamp. They cannot though arise on their own, without depending on something like this object of focus—and thus they do not exist through some nature of their own.

gru.acip: RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA, BDEN PAR GRUB PA, DON DAM PAR GRUB PA, RANG GI NGO BOS GRUB PA, RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PA, RANG DBANG GIS GRUB PA, YANG DAG PAR GRUB PA, BLTOS MED DU GRUB PA RNAMS NI DON GCIG MING GI RNAM GRANGS TZAM MO, ,'DIS SEMS JI LTAR GZUNG BAR BYA BA'I TSUL BSTAN TO,,
gru.wylie: rang bzhin gyis grub pa, bden par grub pa, don dam par grub pa, rang gi ngo bos grub pa, rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub pa, rang dbang gis grub pa, yang dag par grub pa, bltos med du grub pa rnams ni don gcig ming gi rnam grangs tsam mo, ,'dis sems ji ltar gzung bar bya ba'i tshul bstan to
gru.english: The following expressions all have the same meaning—they are all simply different ways of saying the same thing: existing through some nature of its own; existing in truth; existing ultimately; existing through its own essence; existing by definition; existing in and of itself; existing absolutely; and existing without relying on anything else. The preceding section then is meant to answer the original question of how we should keep our thoughts.

gru.acip: BSOD NAMS KYI PHUNG PO DE DAG NI THA SNYAD DU SGYU MA LTAR TSOGS PA LAS BYUNG BA YIN GYI, DE LTA BU LA MA BLTOS PAR GAL TE RANG GI NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB NA BSOD NAMS KYI PHUNG PO ZHES DE BZHIN GSHEGS PAS MI GSUNG NGO,,
gru.wylie: bsod nams kyi phung po de dag ni tha snyad du sgyu ma ltar tshogs pa las byung ba yin gyi, de lta bu la ma bltos par gal te rang gi ngo bo nyid kyis grub na bsod nams kyi phung po zhes de bzhin gshegs pas mi gsung ngo
gru.english: The great mountains of merit thus created are, in a nominal sense, produced by a combination of things, in the same way that an illusion is. Yet if they were produced without depending on this sort of thing—that is, if they existed through some essential nature of their own—then the One Thus Gone would never refer to them as “great mountains of merit.”

gru.acip: RGYU MTSAN NI BSOD NAMS KYI PHUNG PO ZHES PA'I PHUNG PO'I DON NI TSOGS PA'I DON YIN LA, RANG DBANG GIS GRUB NA TSOGS PA LA MA BLTOS PAR GRUB PAR 'GYUR RO ZHES DGONGS SO,,
gru.wylie: rgyu mtshan ni bsod nams kyi phung po zhes pa'i phung po'i don ni tshogs pa'i don yin la, rang dbang gis grub na tshogs pa la ma bltos par grub par 'gyur ro zhes dgongs so
gru.english: The reason here is that—when we speak of a “great mountain of merit”—the “mountain” implies a combination or collection of things. The point that Lord Buddha is making is that—if things existed in and of themselves—then they would exist without depending upon any such collection of things.

gru.acip: RAB 'BYOR, 'DI JI SNYAM DU SEMS, GZUGS KYI SKU YONGS SU GRUB PAS DE BZHIN GSHEGS PAR BLTA'AM,
gru.wylie: rab 'byor, 'di ji snyam du sems, gzugs kyi sku yongs su grub pas de bzhin gshegs par blta'am
gru.english: O Subhuti, what do you think? Should we ever consider someone One Gone Thus simply because they have attained the physical form of an Enlightened Being?

gru.acip: GZUGS KYI SKU YONGS SU GRUB PA 'DI LA DON DAM PAR DE BZHIN GSHEGS PAR BLTA BA STE BZUNG ZHING 'DOD PAR BYA SNYAM 'AM ZHES DRIS PA NA,
gru.wylie: gzugs kyi sku yongs su grub pa 'di la don dam par de bzhin gshegs par blta ba ste bzung zhing 'dod par bya snyam 'am zhes dris pa na
gru.english: Lord Buddha asks then, “What do you think? Should we ever consider” (meaning 'hold' or 'believe') “that someone is”—in an ultimate way—”One Gone Thus simply because they have attained the physical form of an Enlightened Being?”

gru.acip: RGYU MTSAN NI GZUGS KYI SKU YANG RGYU RKYEN TSOGS PA LAS GRUB KYI, DON DAM PAR GRUB PA MA MCHIS PA BSOD NAMS KYI PHUNG PO DANG 'DRA STE, THA SNYAD DU GZUGS KYI SKUR GRUB PA ZHES BRJOD DO,,
gru.wylie: rgyu mtshan ni gzugs kyi sku yang rgyu rkyen tshogs pa las grub kyi, don dam par grub pa ma mchis pa bsod nams kyi phung po dang 'dra ste, tha snyad du gzugs kyi skur grub pa zhes brjod do
gru.english: The reason is that the physical form of an Enlightened Being is also something that is produced, attained, by the combining of its causes and factors; it is not however something that could exist in some ultimate way. In this sense it is similar to those great mountains of merit: that is, we can—just nominally—refer to the “attainment of the physical form of an Enlightened Being.”

gru.acip: GAL TE GZUGS KYI SKU ZHIG YOD NA DE'I MTSAN DPE RNAMS BDEN GRUB TU YOD SNYAM NA DE MED CES STON PA NI,
gru.wylie: gal te gzugs kyi sku zhig yod na de'i mtshan dpe rnams bden grub tu yod snyam na de med ces ston pa ni
gru.english: Another issue could be posed now: “If the physical form of an Enlightened Being does exist, then there must also exist—in a real way—the signs and marks of an Enlightened Being upon this form.” No signs upon the form

gru.acip: DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA'I SKU LA MTSAN DPE PHUN SUM TSOGS PA BDEN GRUB TU YOD PA'I SGO NAS DE BZHIN GSHEGS PAR BDEN ZHEN GYIS MI BLTA STE,
gru.wylie: de bzhin gshegs pa'i sku la mtshan dpe phun sum tshogs pa bden grub tu yod pa'i sgo nas de bzhin gshegs par bden zhen gyis mi blta ste
gru.english: The idea here is that we should never consider someone to be One Gone Thus through any kind of belief that they are real: through any belief that the exquisite signs and marks exist upon the physical form of One Gone Thus in some real way.
