gru.acip: MTSAN DPE PHUN SUM TSOGS PA DE DAG NI TSOGS SHING 'DUS PA'I DNGOS PO SGYU MA LTAR GRUB PAS DON DAM PAR MTSAN DPE PHUN SUM TSOGS PAR GRUB PA MA MCHIS KYANG, THA SNYAD DU DE SKAD CES BRJOD DO,,
gru.wylie: mtshan dpe phun sum tshogs pa de dag ni tshogs shing 'dus pa'i dngos po sgyu ma ltar grub pas don dam par mtshan dpe phun sum tshogs par grub pa ma mchis kyang, tha snyad du de skad ces brjod do
gru.english: These exquisite signs and marks are things which exist in the way of an illusion: which have been produced by the combination or assembling of other things. As such, they could never exist, in an ultimate way, as exquisite signs and marks; nonetheless, we can call them—in a nominal sense—what we do.

gru.acip: RGYU MTSAN NI CHOS DANG CHOS BSTAN PA ZHES BYA BA NI THA SNYAD TZAM MA GTOGS GANG YANG DON DAM PAR MA GRUB PA'I PHYIR RO ZHES PA'I DON NI SNGAR BSHAD ZIN CING,
gru.wylie: rgyu mtshan ni chos dang chos bstan pa zhes bya ba ni tha snyad tsam ma gtogs gang yang don dam par ma grub pa'i phyir ro zhes pa'i don ni sngar bshad zin cing
gru.english: The reason for saying this—as we've explained it already earlier—is because the Dharma itself, and the teaching of this Dharma, are “things that exist only nominally; they are not something that could exist at all in an ultimate sense.”

gru.acip: DE DAG NI RANG RANG GI MING GI THA SNYAD 'JUG PA'I GZHIR RANG DBANG GIS MA GRUB CING, SGRA DE DANG DE'I BRJOD BYA'I RANG LDOG RNAMS NI BDEN PAR MA GRUB CES STON PA'O,,
gru.wylie: de dag ni rang rang gi ming gi tha snyad 'jug pa'i gzhir rang dbang gis ma grub cing, sgra de dang de'i brjod bya'i rang ldog rnams ni bden par ma grub ces ston pa'o
gru.english: What's being expressed by the sutra at this point is the following. None of these things is, in any natural or automatic way, the thing which the name we use for it refers to. The fact of a word and the thing it is used to refer to is, again, something not something which exists in some real way.

gru.acip: DER GRUB NA NI GNOD BYED CI YOD ZHE NA, YOD DE, 'PHAGS PA THOGS MED KYIS THEG BSDUS LAS,
gru.wylie: der grub na ni gnod byed ci yod zhe na, yod de, 'phags pa thogs med kyis theg bsdus las
gru.english: “But if it were to exist in some real way,” you may ask, “what would be the problem?” The realized being Asanga has given us an answer on this, in his Abbreviated Presentation of the Greater Way—

gru.acip: ,MING GI SNGA ROL BLO MED PHYIR, ,MANG BA'I PHYIR DANG MA 'DRES PHYIR, ,DE YI BDAG NYID BDAG MANG DANG, ,BDAG 'DRES 'GAL BAS 'GRUB PAR 'GYUR,
gru.wylie: ming gi snga rol blo med phyir, ,mang ba'i phyir dang ma 'dres phyir, ,de yi bdag nyid bdag mang dang, ,bdag 'dres 'gal bas 'grub par 'gyur
gru.english: Before it is given the name, There is no idea of it; It would be many, And they never mix. There would be many itselfs, Or it would be themselves; And so our point is proven By these inconsistencies.

gru.acip: BCOM LDAN 'DAS KYIS KYANG DE'I LAN SONG ZIN PA LA DGONGS NAS, SEMS CAN DE DAG NI SEMS CAN DU DON DAM PAR GRUB PA YANG MA YIN, THA SNYAD DU SEMS CAN MED PA YANG MA YIN NO,,
gru.wylie: bcom ldan 'das kyis kyang de'i lan song zin pa la dgongs nas, sems can de dag ni sems can du don dam par grub pa yang ma yin, tha snyad du sems can med pa yang ma yin no
gru.english: The Conqueror too is bearing in mind that he has already responded to this question, and so now he begins the part about how such beings will not be, in an ultimate sense, living beings; nor will they not, nominally, be a living being.

gru.acip: YANG RAB 'BYOR CHOS GANG YIN PA DE THAMS CAD NI BDEN PAR MA GRUB PAR MTSUNGS SHING MNYAM PA STE, DE LTA BU'I MNYAM PA DE'I DBANG DU BYAS PA LA MI MNYAM PA'I CHOS GANG YANG MED PAS SO,,
gru.wylie: yang rab 'byor chos gang yin pa de thams cad ni bden par ma grub par mtshungs shing mnyam pa ste, de lta bu'i mnyam pa de'i dbang du byas pa la mi mnyam pa'i chos gang yang med pas so
gru.english: The Buddha says now, “I say to you further, o Subhuti, that none of the things that exist exist in any real way; and in this they are equivalent, they are equal. And this is because—relative to this way in which things are equal—there is nothing at all which is not equal.

gru.acip: MNYAM PA DE YANG SEMS CAN MED PA, SROG MED PA, GANG ZAG GI BDAG MED PAR MNYAM PA STE, DON DAM PAR CHOS SU GRUB PA MED KYANG THA SNYAD DU SBYIN SOGS DGE BA'I CHOS DE DAG THAMS CAD KYIS DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA SANGS RGYAS SHING, SANGS RGYAS KYI THUGS RGYUD KYI DGE BA'I CHOS RNAMS LA'ANG SANGS RGYAS ZHES BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: mnyam pa de yang sems can med pa, srog med pa, gang zag gi bdag med par mnyam pa ste, don dam par chos su grub pa med kyang tha snyad du sbyin sogs dge ba'i chos de dag thams cad kyis de bzhin gshegs pa sangs rgyas shing, sangs rgyas kyi thugs rgyud kyi dge ba'i chos rnams la'ang sangs rgyas zhes bya'o
gru.english: This kind of equal is equal in the sense that it is without any self to a living being; it is without any self to something that lives; and is without any self to a person. Ultimately speaking, there is nothing at all that exists as a thing; nonetheless, in a nominal sense, every single thing which is virtue leads to the total enlightenment of One Gone Thus, of a Buddha. And we can as well refer to all the virtuous things within the holy heart of a Buddha as “a Buddha.”

gru.acip: DON DAM PAR CHOS RNAMS MA GRUB NA 'ANG THA SNYAD DU SEMS CAN GANG LA LA ZHIG GIS STONG GSUM GYI STONG CHEN PO'I 'JIG RTEN GYI KHAMS NA RI'I RGYAL PO RI RAB JI SNYED PA DE LTA BU'I TSAD KYI GSER LA SOGS PA'I RIN PO CHE SNA BDUN GYI PHUNG PO RNAMS BSDUS TE SBYIN PA BYIN PA BAS KYANG,
gru.wylie: don dam par chos rnams ma grub na 'ang tha snyad du sems can gang la la zhig gis stong gsum gyi stong chen po'i 'jig rten gyi khams na ri'i rgyal po ri rab ji snyed pa de lta bu'i tshad kyi gser la sogs pa'i rin po che sna bdun gyi phung po rnams bsdus te sbyin pa byin pa bas kyang
gru.english: Now even though there is nothing in the universe that exists in any ultimate sense, nonetheless certain people could indeed pile together great heaps of the seven different precious things—gold and the rest—that were the same size as the universal mountains that existed on all of the planets in planets of this great world system: a system with a thousand of a thousand of a thousand planets. And they could offer this as a gift to someone.

gru.acip: RAB 'BYOR BYIS PA SO SO'I SKYE BO RNAMS ZHES BYA BA NI DE DAG DON DAM PAR SKYE BO NYID DU GRUB PA MED PAR DE BZHIN GSHEGS PAS GSUNGS TE, THA SNYAD DU MING GIS DE SKAD CES BRJOD DO,,
gru.wylie: rab 'byor byis pa so so'i skye bo rnams zhes bya ba ni de dag don dam par skye bo nyid du grub pa med par de bzhin gshegs pas gsungs te, tha snyad du ming gis de skad ces brjod do
gru.english: And these same people who are referred to as “children” or “common beings,” o Subhuti, are beings that the One Gone Thus has said never existed at all—in an ultimate sense—as living creatures; they are only called by this name, in a nominal sense.

gru.acip: DE LA CHAD LTA 'GOG PA NI, RAB 'BYOR KHYOD 'DI SNYAM DU BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA'I THEG PA LA YANG DAG PAR ZHUGS PA RNAMS KYIS GZUGS SOGS KYI CHOS GANG LA LA ZHIG DON DAM PAR MA GRUB PAR RTOGS PA NA,
gru.wylie: de la chad lta 'gog pa ni, rab 'byor khyod 'di snyam du byang chub sems dpa'i theg pa la yang dag par zhugs pa rnams kyis gzugs sogs kyi chos gang la la zhig don dam par ma grub par rtogs pa na
gru.english: Now then we will need to go on to avoiding the extreme which says that everything has simply stopped. Lord Buddha says, “O Subhuti, suppose you were to think of those who have entered well into the way of the bodhisattva, and who perceived that any particular thing—whether it be something that we can see or anything else of the like—could never exist in any ultimate way.”

gru.acip: DES NA THA SNYAD DU BSOD NAMS YONGS SU GZUNG BA ZHES BYA'O ZHES GSUNGS TE, 'DI'I GZUNG BAR MI BYA'O ZHES PAS BSOD NAMS KYI PHUNG PO LA BDEN GRUB TU ZHEN PA'I RTAG LTA DANG, YONGS SU GZUNG MOD KYIS ZHES CHAD PAR LTA BA SEL LO,,
gru.wylie: des na tha snyad du bsod nams yongs su gzung ba zhes bya'o zhes gsungs te, 'di'i gzung bar mi bya'o zhes pas bsod nams kyi phung po la bden grub tu zhen pa'i rtag lta dang, yongs su gzung mod kyis zhes chad par lta ba sel lo
gru.english: And this is precisely why, Lord Buddha says, that—nominally speaking—we can call it “gathering the merit in.” When the sutra says here that we are “not to gather,” it is helping us to avoid the view that things are unchanging—where we believe that the mountains of merit exist in truth. When it says that we “should, of course, gather,” then it is helping us to avoid the view that things have simply stopped. The Buddha neither comes nor goes

gru.acip: DE RNAMS DON DAM PAR MED PA'I RANG BZHIN RDUL PHRA RAB KYI TSOGS ZHES GANG GSUNGS PA DE NI, DE RNAMS DON DAM PAR TSOGS SU GRUB PA MA MCHIS PAR DE BZHIN GSHEGS PAS MKHYEN NAS GSUNGS PA'I SLAD DU STE, DES NA THA SNYAD DU RDUL PHRA RAB KYI TSOGS ZHES BGYI'O,,
gru.wylie: de rnams don dam par med pa'i rang bzhin rdul phra rab kyi tshogs zhes gang gsungs pa de ni, de rnams don dam par tshogs su grub pa ma mchis par de bzhin gshegs pas mkhyen nas gsungs pa'i slad du ste, des na tha snyad du rdul phra rab kyi tshogs zhes bgyi'o
gru.english: And just why do they have a nature of not existing in an ultimate way? Think about the “piles of tiny particles” which were described. All this is because the One Thus Gone has seen that these are piles that could never exist in any ultimate way; and then he has said that they cannot. And this is precisely why we can call them, in a nominal sense, “piles of tiny particles.”

gru.acip: CHA BCAS KYANG 'DI LA PHYOGS BZHI DANG STENG 'OG TU RDUL DRUG GIS BSKOR NAS GNAS PAS 'GRUB LA, MED NA DE LA RIGS PA'I GNOD BYED STON TSUL MTSON TZAM SNGAR BSHAD ZIN TO,,
gru.wylie: cha bcas kyang 'di la phyogs bzhi dang steng 'og tu rdul drug gis bskor nas gnas pas 'grub la, med na de la rigs pa'i gnod byed ston tshul mtshon tsam sngar bshad zin to
gru.english: And once we say that these particles do have parts, then we would have to say that they exist as atoms which are wrapped in six other particles—ones which are positioned to the four directions, as well as above and below. If we said that they didn't have these other particles as part of them, then we would incur the same logical fallacies which we have already briefly mentioned.

gru.acip: GAL TE DON DAM PAR SNOD BCUD KYI 'JIG RTEN GYI KHAMS DE LTA BU ZHIG MCHIS PAR GYUR NA NI, DE NYID TSOGS SHING 'DUS PA LA MA BLTOS PAR RAGS PA RIL PO GCIG TU GRUB CING 'DZIN DGOS PAR 'GYUR BA'I SLAD DU STE, DE LTAR GRUB NA DE BZHIN GSHEGS PAS KYANG GZIGS DGOS PAR 'GYUR RO,,
gru.wylie: gal te don dam par snod bcud kyi 'jig rten gyi khams de lta bu zhig mchis par gyur na ni, de nyid tshogs shing 'dus pa la ma bltos par rags pa ril po gcig tu grub cing 'dzin dgos par 'gyur ba'i slad du ste, de ltar grub na de bzhin gshegs pas kyang gzigs dgos par 'gyur ro
gru.english: And why is it so? Because if there were, in an ultimate sense, any such thing as a planet or world, both the place and the beings inhabiting it, then one would have to be grasping it as one whole solid and solitary thing whose existence did not rely upon its composite parts, on some collection of parts. And if it actually did exist in that way, then the One Thus Gone would also have to see it as being so.

gru.acip: 'JIG RTEN NA RIL POR RAGS PA LING PO CHA MED GCIG TU GRUB PAR 'DZIN PA GANG GSUNGS PA'I 'DZIN PA DE YANG DON DAM PAR 'DZIN PAR GRUB PAR MA MCHIS SO ZHES PA'I SNGA MAS GZUNG BYA DANG, 'DIS 'DZIN PA YANG DON DAM PAR GRUB PAR STON PAR BSHAD DO,,
gru.wylie: 'jig rten na ril por rags pa ling po cha med gcig tu grub par 'dzin pa gang gsungs pa'i 'dzin pa de yang don dam par 'dzin par grub par ma mchis so zhes pa'i snga mas gzung bya dang, 'dis 'dzin pa yang don dam par grub par ston par bshad do
gru.english: And thus it is that the One Thus Gone has said that even the “tendency to grasp things as one whole solid thing”—as gross, discrete entities that are singular things not made of parts—described by the One Thus Gone is a kind of grasping that could never exist anyway. The first part above then is meant to demonstrate that what is grasped to could never exist in any ultimate sense, while this last part is to demonstrate that what does the grasping could never exist in this sense either.

gru.acip: CI NAS KYANG CHOS SU 'DU SHES ZHES PA NI CHOS GANG LA YANG BDEN PAR GRUB SNYAM PA'I 'DU SHES BDEN 'DZIN MI SKYE ZHING, BDEN PA'I 'DU SHES LA MI GNAS PAR BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: ci nas kyang chos su 'du shes zhes pa ni chos gang la yang bden par grub snyam pa'i 'du shes bden 'dzin mi skye zhing, bden pa'i 'du shes la mi gnas par bya'o
gru.english: The line about “never…conceiving of anything as an object of all” means that the bodhisattva should never allow any tendency to think of things as being real to arise—no tendency of thinking to oneself that anything at all could exist as a real object. Neither should they ever live in a way where they continue to think of things as real. The power of clear thinking

gru.acip: BSOD NAMS ZHES PA NI BSOD NAMS DANG YE SHES KYI TSOGS GNYIS GA MTSON ZHING, SBYIN PA TSUL KHRIMS BZOD PA GSUM LAS NI GTZO BOR BSOD NAMS KYI TSOGS GSOG LA, BSAM GTAN SHES RAB GNYIS KYIS NI GTZO BOR YE SHES KYI TSOGS GSOG CING, BRTZON 'GRUS LAS NI DE GNYIS KA 'BYUNG NGO, ,DES NA SHER PHYIN LA THOS BSAM SOGS BYED PA NI YE SHES KYI TSOGS GSOG PA GTZO CHE'O,,
gru.wylie: bsod nams zhes pa ni bsod nams dang ye shes kyi tshogs gnyis ga mtshon zhing, sbyin pa tshul khrims bzod pa gsum las ni gtso bor bsod nams kyi tshogs gsog la, bsam gtan shes rab gnyis kyis ni gtso bor ye shes kyi tshogs gsog cing, brtson 'grus las ni de gnyis ka 'byung ngo, ,des na sher phyin la thos bsam sogs byed pa ni ye shes kyi tshogs gsog pa gtso che'o
gru.english: When we say “merit” here, it really applies to both the collection of merit and the collection of wisdom. Following the three perfections of giving, an ethical way of life, and patience are—primarily—amassing the collection of merit. Following the two perfections of meditation and wisdom are primarily amassing the collection of wisdom. And both of these collections are produced by the perfection of joyful effort. We can say then that learning and contemplating upon the perfection of wisdom—and other similar practices—are primarily amassing the collection of wisdom.

gru.acip: DE DAG NI 'DUS BYAS RNAMS LA THUN MONG DU SBYAR NAS BSHAD PA STE, MDO LAS NI, ,GZUGS NI DBU BA BRDOS PA 'DRA, ,TSOR BA CHU YI CHU BUR BZHIN, ,'DU SHES SMIG RGYU LTA BU STE, ,'DU BYED RNAMS NI CHU SHING BZHIN, ,RNAM PAR SHES PA SGYU MA LTAR, ,NYI MA'I GNYEN GYIS BKA' STZAL TO,, ZHES BSHAD CES MGON PO KLU SGRUB GSUNG NGO, ,
gru.wylie: de dag ni 'dus byas rnams la thun mong du sbyar nas bshad pa ste, mdo las ni, ,gzugs ni dbu ba brdos pa 'dra, ,tshor ba chu yi chu bur bzhin, ,'du shes smig rgyu lta bu ste, ,'du byed rnams ni chu shing bzhin, ,rnam par shes pa sgyu ma ltar, ,nyi ma'i gnyen gyis bka' stsal to,, zhes bshad ces mgon po klu sgrub gsung ngo,
gru.english: The explanation given here applies to things brought about by causes as an entire group. A more restricted application is quoted from sutra by Master Nagarjuna: The physical form is like a bubble that forms, And the feelings resemble the froth of a wave; Discrimination is just a mirage, And the other factors like empty cane; Awareness is similar to an illusion— Thus did the Cousin of the Sun speak.

gru.acip: ,SHIN TU DPAG PAR DKA' BA RGYAL BA'I YUM, ,JI BZHIN DGONGS PA 'GREL MDZAD 'DZAM GLING RGYAN, ,KLU SGRUB THOGS MED CES NI SA GSUM NA, ,YONGS SU GRAGS PA'I ZHABS LA BDAG PHYAG 'TSAL,
gru.wylie: shin tu dpag par dka' ba rgyal ba'i yum, ,ji bzhin dgongs pa 'grel mdzad 'dzam gling rgyan, ,klu sgrub thogs med ces ni sa gsum na, ,yongs su grags pa'i zhabs la bdag phyag 'tshal
gru.english: I prostrate At the holy feet Of those known As Nagarjuna & Asanga, So widely famed Through the three realms. You are true jewels Of our world Who undertook To comment, In a perfectly Accurate way, Upon the true thought Of the Mother Sutras Of the Victors, So extremely difficult To fathom.

gru.acip: MTSON LA MGON PO KLU SGRUB DANG 'PHAGS PA THOGS MED CES NI SA 'OG SA STENG SA BLA STE SA GSUM NA YONGS SU GRAGS PA'I ZHABS LA'O,,
gru.wylie: mtshon la mgon po klu sgrub dang 'phags pa thogs med ces ni sa 'og sa steng sa bla ste sa gsum na yongs su grags pa'i zhabs la'o
gru.english: To represent the entire group of these jewels, we have here "those known as Nagarjuna & Arya Asanga." And then our author is prostrating at the holy feet of these sages, so widely famed through the entire world of the three realms-which here refers to below the surface of the earth; upon it; and above it.

gru.acip: GANG LA NA, SHING RTA CHEN PO KLU SGRUB DANG THOGS MED RNAM PA GNYIS LAS LEGS PAR BRGYUD PA'I ZAB MO LTA BA DANG, RGYA CHEN SPYOD PA'I LAM GYI RIM PA TSANG LA MA NOR BAR YONGS SU RDZOGS PA'I GNAD BSDUS PA'I GDAMS PA'I MDZOD 'DZIN PA DPAL MAR ME MDZAD LA'O,,
gru.wylie: gang la na, shing rta chen po klu sgrub dang thogs med rnam pa gnyis las legs par brgyud pa'i zab mo lta ba dang, rgya chen spyod pa'i lam gyi rim pa tshang la ma nor bar yongs su rdzogs pa'i gnad bsdus pa'i gdams pa'i mdzod 'dzin pa dpal mar me mdzad la'o
gru.english: Who then does our author bow to, in these lines? It is Dipankara, "Maker of Lamps," which is the glorious Lord Atisha. This is because he is a holder of a great treasure of advices which incorporate each & every one of the essential points of the steps of the way-completely, and unerringly. And these are the paths of the profound view, and widespread activities, which have descended so perfectly from the two great innovators: Arya Nagarjuna, and Arya Asanga.

gru.acip: DE YANG JO BO CHEN POS BLA MA GSER GLING PA BSTEN NAS BYAMS PA DANG THOGS MED NAS BRGYUD PA'I GDAMS PA GSAN LA, RIGS {%RIG} PA'I KHU BYUG BSTEN NAS 'JAM DBYANGS DANG KLU SGRUB NAS BRGYUD PA'I GANG SA DUD {%BRGYUD PA'I GDAMS PA} MA LUS PA GSAN NAS GDAMS PA'I CHU BO GNYIS ZUNG DU 'BREL BAR MDZAD DO,,
gru.wylie: de yang jo bo chen pos bla ma gser gling pa bsten nas byams pa dang thogs med nas brgyud pa'i gdams pa gsan la, rigs pa'i khu byug bsten nas 'jam dbyangs dang klu sgrub nas brgyud pa'i gang sa dud ma lus pa gsan nas gdams pa'i chu bo gnyis zung du 'brel bar mdzad do
gru.english: Now the Great Lord learned the advices that came down through Loving One and Asanga by studying with the Lama of the Golden Isle. And he learned all the advices that descended through Gentle Voice and Arya Nagarjuna by studying with the master Vidya Kokila. And then he undertook to combine the flows of these two teaching traditions. Bowing to spiritual friends

gru.acip: ,'DZAM GLING MKHAS PA YONGS KYI GTZUG GI RGYAN, ,SNYAN PA'I BA DAN 'GRO NA LHANG NGE BA, ,KLU SGRUB THOGS MED GNYIS LAS RIM BZHIN DU, ,LEGS BRGYUD BYANG CHUB LAM GYI RIM PA NI,
gru.wylie: 'dzam gling mkhas pa yongs kyi gtsug gi rgyan, ,snyan pa'i ba dan 'gro na lhang nge ba, ,klu sgrub thogs med gnyis las rim bzhin du, ,legs brgyud byang chub lam gyi rim pa ni
gru.english: The steps on the path To enlightenment, Passed down With such excellence, In their own stages, Through the two Of Nagarjuna and Asanga, Are a jewel on the topknot Of each & every master Upon this planet; A victory banner Of great renown, Glorious here Among beings.

gru.acip: 'DZAM GLING 'DIR BYON PA'I MKHAS PA YONGS KYI GTZUG GI RGYAN DU GYUR CING, MKHAS PA'I SNYAN PA PHYOGS KUN DU GRAGS PA'I BA DAN 'GRO BA'I GNAS 'DI NA NYI MA LTAR LHANG NGER GSAL BA KLU SGRUB DANG THOGS MED GNYIS LAS RIM PA BZHIN DU LEGS PAR BRGYUD PA'I BYANG CHUB LAM GYI RIM PA'I GZHUNG NYID 'CHAD PAR BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: 'dzam gling 'dir byon pa'i mkhas pa yongs kyi gtsug gi rgyan du gyur cing, mkhas pa'i snyan pa phyogs kun du grags pa'i ba dan 'gro ba'i gnas 'di na nyi ma ltar lhang nger gsal ba klu sgrub dang thogs med gnyis las rim pa bzhin du legs par brgyud pa'i byang chub lam gyi rim pa'i gzhung nyid 'chad par bya'o
gru.english: The steps on the path to enlightenment-as they have been passed down with such excellence, in their own stages, through the two of Nagarjuna and Asanga-are like the jewel on the topknot upon the heads of each & every master who has ever come to this planet. They shine in glory here in the world of beings like the sun itself, upon the peak where we see flying the victory banner of the great renown of these masters, waving proudly in fame that reaches every direction. And it is a classic work upon these steps that "I will now explain to you."

gru.acip: 'DOD PA'I DON SKANG TSUL NI, 'DI'I DON NYAMS SU BLANGS PA LAS MNGON MTHO DANG NGES LEGS 'GRUB PA DANG,
gru.wylie: 'dod pa'i don skang tshul ni, 'di'i don nyams su blangs pa las mngon mtho dang nges legs 'grub pa dang
gru.english: And how is it that the steps fulfil wishes? If we put into actual practice the ideas that the steps teach us, then we achieve higher rebirths, and definite good.

gru.acip: ,MTHONG NAS SROG GI PHYIR YANG MI GTONG BAR, ,BKA' BZHIN SGRUB PA'I MCHOD PAS MNYES PAR BYED, ,RNAL 'BYOR NGAS KYANG NYAMS LEN DE LTAR BGYIS, ,THAR 'DOD KHYED KYANG DE BZHIN BSKYANG 'TSAL LO,
gru.wylie: mthong nas srog gi phyir yang mi gtong bar, ,bka' bzhin sgrub pa'i mchod pas mnyes par byed, ,rnal 'byor ngas kyang nyams len de ltar bgyis, ,thar 'dod khyed kyang de bzhin bskyang 'tshal lo
gru.english: Seeing this, We see that we must Please them with the offering Of accomplishing everything They have commanded us to do, Without ever giving it up, Even at the cost of our life. I, the deep practitioner, Have accomplished my practice This way; And you who hope for freedom Should do your practice The same.

gru.acip: BLA MA MNYES PA SGO MTHA' DAG NAS BSGRUB CING MA MNYES PA NAM YANG MI BSGRUB PA DANG, LUS KYIS BKUR ZHING NGAG GIS BSTOD PA SOGS DANG, CI GSUNG BKA' BZHIN DU SGRUB PA'I SGO NAS SBYOR BAS TSUL BZHIN DU BSTEN PA RU STE
gru.wylie: bla ma mnyes pa sgo mtha' dag nas bsgrub cing ma mnyes pa nam yang mi bsgrub pa dang, lus kyis bkur zhing ngag gis bstod pa sogs dang, ci gsung bka' bzhin du sgrub pa'i sgo nas sbyor bas tshul bzhin du bsten pa ru ste
gru.english: With this we begin our study with this Lama, relying upon them properly in our actual actions. This involves undertaking everything we can that pleases them, and never doing anything which does not please them. We honor them for example with the actions we undertake, and speak well of them in our words. We rely upon them by carrying out everything they have asked us to do, just as they have asked us to do it.

gru.acip: BSTEN PA LA RAG YAS {%LAS} PAR MTHONG NAS RKYEN CUNG ZAD TZAM DU MA ZAD, SROG GI PHYIR YANG MI GTONG BAR BKA' BZHIN DU SGRUB PA'I MCHOD PAS MNYES PAR BYED DGOS SO,,
gru.wylie: bsten pa la rag yas par mthong nas rkyen cung zad tsam du ma zad, srog gi phyir yang mi gtong bar bka' bzhin du sgrub pa'i mchod pas mnyes par byed dgos so
gru.english: We see that all our goals depend upon relying upon our Teacher in this way; then we see that we must absolutely please them with the offering of accomplishing everything they have commanded us to do. And we continue this behavior without ever giving it up, not just for some small reason, but even at the cost of our life.

gru.acip: DAL BRGYAD 'BYOR BCU LDAN PA'I SGO NAS CHOS SGRUB PA LA KHOS {%KHOM} PAS NA DAL BA'I RTEN KHYAD PAR CAN 'DI NI,
gru.wylie: dal brgyad 'byor bcu ldan pa'i sgo nas chos sgrub pa la khos pas na dal ba'i rten khyad par can 'di ni
gru.english: Now we possess a body & mind of exceptional "leisure" in that we possess the time & opportunity to practice the Dharma, given that we have available to us the eight classical forms of leisure, and the ten classical forms of fortune.

gru.acip: RTEN 'DI LA BRTEN NAS MNGON MTHO TZAM DU MA ZAD, NGES LEGS THAR PA DANG THAMS CAD MKHYEN PA BSGRUBS NA'ANG THOB NUS PAR GSUNGS PA'I PHYIR NA LHAG GO
gru.wylie: rten 'di la brten nas mngon mtho tsam du ma zad, nges legs thar pa dang thams cad mkhyen pa bsgrubs na'ang thob nus par gsungs pa'i phyir na lhag go
gru.english: These leisures & fortunes though are even more precious, because-as it has been stated in the teachings-by relying on this current body & mind that we possess, we can not only reach a higher rebirth, but are even able to attain "definite good": which is to say, freedom & omniscience.

gru.acip: THAMS CAD MKHYEN PA SGRUB PA LAS BRTZAMS TE GSUNGS PA THAMS CAD SKYES BU CHEN PO'I CHOS SKOR DU 'DU BA YIN NO,,
gru.wylie: thams cad mkhyen pa sgrub pa las brtsams te gsungs pa thams cad skyes bu chen po'i chos skor du 'du ba yin no
gru.english: Those teachings that were given primarily in the context of achieving omniscience are all grouped into the collection of instructions for people of great capacity.

gru.acip: SDIG SPONG DGE BA SGRUB PA'I SGO NAS MNGON MTHO DON GNYER GYI BLO DE, SKYES BU CHUNG NGU DANG THUN MONG BA'I LAM DANG, 'KHOR BA LAS GROL 'DOD KYI SGO NAS THAR PA DON GNYER GYI BLO DE SKYES BU 'BRING DANG THUN MONG BA'I LAM YIN TE, DE GNYIS KA'ANG BYANG SEMS KYI RGYUD LA YOD CING, DES NYAMS SU LEN DGOS PA'I PHYIR RO,,
gru.wylie: sdig spong dge ba sgrub pa'i sgo nas mngon mtho don gnyer gyi blo de, skyes bu chung ngu dang thun mong ba'i lam dang, 'khor ba las grol 'dod kyi sgo nas thar pa don gnyer gyi blo de skyes bu 'bring dang thun mong ba'i lam yin te, de gnyis ka'ang byang sems kyi rgyud la yod cing, des nyams su len dgos pa'i phyir ro
gru.english: That state of mind where we aspire to higher rebirths by means of giving up bad deeds, and accomplishing good deeds, constitutes the path which is shared with people of lesser capacity. And that state of mind where we aspire to freedom because we want to be liberated from the cycle of pain constitutes the path which is shared with people of medium capacity. Both of these states of mind are present in the mind stream of a bodhisattva; and both of them must be practiced by a bodhisattva.

gru.acip: BDAG GIS NI BDE SKYO {%SKYE} 'GROR SKYE BA'I RGYU CHER MA BSGRUBS LA, NGAN 'GROR SKYE BA'I NI MANG DU BSAGS SO,,
gru.wylie: bdag gis ni bde skyo 'gror skye ba'i rgyu cher ma bsgrubs la, ngan 'gror skye ba'i ni mang du bsags so
gru.english: Now it's not that I have managed in this life to accomplish a great many deeds that would cause me to be born into the realms of greater happiness; in fact, I have accumulated a great many causes to be born into the realms of misery.

gru.acip: GNYIS PA PHYI MA'I BDE THABS LA GSUM, SKYABS 'GRO BSLAB BYA DANG BCAS PA DANG, DE LA LAS GNYIS KYI BLANG DOR LA 'JUG DGOS PA DANG, RNAM MKHYEN SGRUB PA'I RTEN BSHAD PA'O,,
gru.wylie: gnyis pa phyi ma'i bde thabs la gsum, skyabs 'gro bslab bya dang bcas pa dang, de la las gnyis kyi blang dor la 'jug dgos pa dang, rnam mkhyen sgrub pa'i rten bshad pa'o
gru.english: Which brings us to our second part from before: how to engage in methods that will bring us happiness after the death ahead of us. This comes in the following three sections: an explanation of how to go for shelter, along with the traditional advices for this practice; an explanation of how, in this regard, we will need to learn to take up and give up, respectively, the two kinds of karma; and then a presentation on the foundation that we need to lay, in order to achieve the state of omniscience.

gru.acip: ,DE YANG DKAR NAG LAS 'BRAS LEGS BSAMS NAS, ,BLANG DOR TSUL BZHIN SGRUB LA RAG LAS SO, ,RNAL 'BYOR NGAS KYANG NYAMS LEN DE LTAR BGYIS, ,THAR 'DOD KHYED KYANG DE BZHIN BSKYANG 'TSAL LO,
gru.wylie: de yang dkar nag las 'bras legs bsams nas, ,blang dor tshul bzhin sgrub la rag las so, ,rnal 'byor ngas kyang nyams len de ltar bgyis, ,thar 'dod khyed kyang de bzhin bskyang 'tshal lo
gru.english: And now we have to Consider, carefully, White & black karma, And its consequences. We have to rely On a practice that Relates in a correct way To what we take up And what we give up. I, the deep practitioner, Have accomplished my practice This way; And you who hope for freedom Should do your practice The same.

gru.acip: DKON MCHOG GIS SKYOB PA DE YANG LAS 'BRAS LA BLANG DOR PHYIN CI LOG TU BSGRUBS NA MI 'BYUNG BAS,
gru.wylie: dkon mchog gis skyob pa de yang las 'bras la blang dor phyin ci log tu bsgrubs na mi 'byung bas
gru.english: Succeeding in having the Three Jewels protect us is not something that can happen if we carry out our practice in a way where we have mixed up the question of what we should take up and what we should give up, as far as karma and its consequences.

gru.acip: DKAR PO DGE BA DANG NAG PO MI DGE BA'I LAS 'BRAS BU DANG BCAS PA JI LTAR YIN LEGS PAR BSAMS NAS DGE BA 'BRAS BU DANG BCAS PA LA BLANG BYA DANG, MI DGE 'BRAS BU DANG BCAS LA DOR BYAR BYED PA'I SGO NAS TSUL BZHIN DU SGRUB PA LA RAG LAS SO,,
gru.wylie: dkar po dge ba dang nag po mi dge ba'i las 'bras bu dang bcas pa ji ltar yin legs par bsams nas dge ba 'bras bu dang bcas pa la blang bya dang, mi dge 'bras bu dang bcas la dor byar byed pa'i sgo nas tshul bzhin du sgrub pa la rag las so
gru.english: As such, we have to consider very carefully how it is that karma, along with its consequences, work both for "white deeds" (referring to good deeds) and "black deeds" (referring to bad deeds). What we take up with our practice then is good deeds, along with their results; and what we give up is bad deeds, along with their results. Accomplishing successful sheltering then is something that relies upon a practice that relates to this pair in the correct way.

gru.acip: DANG PO NI, LAM MCHOG SGRUB LA SOGS TE,
gru.wylie: dang po ni, lam mchog sgrub la sogs te
gru.english: The first of these is expressed in the lines which include "to achieve that supreme path":

gru.acip: ,LAM MCHOG SGRUB LA MTSAN NYID TSANG BA'I RTEN, ,MA RNYED BAR DU SA PHYOD {%CHOD} MI 'ONG BAS, ,DE YI MA TSANG MED PA'I RGYU LA BSLAB,
gru.wylie: lam mchog sgrub la mtshan nyid tshang ba'i rten, ,ma rnyed bar du sa phyod mi 'ong bas, ,de yi ma tshang med pa'i rgyu la bslab
gru.english: If we hope to achieve That supreme path, Then we need to find A body & mind Which possesses the Requisite qualities, All complete. Until we do, We won't be able to take Great bounds forward. And so we need To train ourselves In the necessary causes, In no way incomplete.

gru.acip: KHYAD PAR DU LAM MCHOG RNAM MKHYEN SGRUB PA LA TSE RING BA KHA DOG BZANG BA SOGS RNAM SMIN GYI RGYU BRGYAD SOGS MTSAN NYID TSANG BA'I RTEN CI RIGS PA MA RNYID {%RNYED} KYI BAR DU
gru.wylie: khyad par du lam mchog rnam mkhyen sgrub pa la tshe ring ba kha dog bzang ba sogs rnam smin gyi rgyu brgyad sogs mtshan nyid tshang ba'i rten ci rigs pa ma rnyid kyi bar du
gru.english: More particularly, if we hope to achieve that supreme path of omniscience, then we need to find a form of body & mind which possesses the requisite qualities, all complete. This would include for example the eight causes that will ripen into things like a long life, and a beautiful complexion.

gru.acip: LAM SGRUB KYANG SA CHOD MI 'ONG BAS, DE 'ONG BA'I CHED DU RTEN MTSAN NYID TSANG BA DE YI MA TSANG MED PA'I RGYU SGRUB PA LA BSLAB PAR BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: lam sgrub kyang sa chod mi 'ong bas, de 'ong ba'i ched du rten mtshan nyid tshang ba de yi ma tshang med pa'i rgyu sgrub pa la bslab par bya'o
gru.english: Until we do find these, we won't be able to take great bounds forward in our practice of the path. And so in order to get to this point, we need to train ourselves in carrying out all the necessary causes that will allow us to achieve a body & mind which is complete in every respect here-and in no way incomplete.

gru.acip: GNYIS PA SPYOD PA LA BSLAB TSUL LA DRUG ,SBYIN PA, TSUL KHRIMS, BZOD PA, BRTZON 'GRUS, BSAM GTAN, SHES RAB PO,,
gru.wylie: gnyis pa spyod pa la bslab tshul la drug ,sbyin pa, tshul khrims, bzod pa, brtson 'grus, bsam gtan, shes rab po
gru.english: Which brings us to our second part from above: instructions for training ourselves in these activities. Here we have six divisions: giving, the ethical life, patience, joyful effort, meditation, and wisdom.

gru.acip: BZHI PA LA GNYIS LAS, DANG PO NI, BRTZON 'GRUS LA GSUM LAS, DANG PO NI, MI BZLOG BRTAN PA'I SOGS BZHI STE,
gru.wylie: bzhi pa la gnyis las, dang po ni, brtson 'grus la gsum las, dang po ni, mi bzlog brtan pa'i sogs bzhi ste
gru.english: This brings us to our fourth perfection, which again has those same two points. The first of these is described in the words "steadfast…never turning back," which are describing the first of the three different types of joyful effort.

gru.acip: ,MI LDOG BRTAN PA'I BRTZON 'GRUS GO BGOS NA, ,LUNG RTOGS YON TAN YAR NGO'I ZLA BZHIN 'PHEL, ,SPYOD LAM THAMS CAD DON DANG LDAN PAR 'GYUR, ,GANG BRTZAMS LAS KYI MTHA' RNAMS YID BZHIN 'GRUB,
gru.wylie: mi ldog brtan pa'i brtson 'grus go bgos na, ,lung rtogs yon tan yar ngo'i zla bzhin 'phel, ,spyod lam thams cad don dang ldan par 'gyur, ,gang brtsams las kyi mtha' rnams yid bzhin 'grub
gru.english: Suppose we are able To don the strong armor Of steadfast, joyful effort, Never turning back. Our fine qualities- In both scriptural study And inner realizations- Will multiply, Like a waxing moon. Any project we undertake Will end up having A meaningful result; And any undertaking We ever initiate Will come to its Successful conclusion, Just as we intended.

gru.acip: GTZO BOR GO CHA'I BRTZON 'GRUS KYI DBANG DU BYAS NA, PHYIR MI BZLOG CING BRTAN PA'I BRTZON 'GRUS KYI GO CHA BGOS NA, LUNG DANG RTOGS PA'I YON TAN THAMS CAD YAR DO'I {%NGO'I} ZLA BA BZHIN GONG DU 'PHEL LA,
gru.wylie: gtso bor go cha'i brtson 'grus kyi dbang du byas na, phyir mi bzlog cing brtan pa'i brtson 'grus kyi go cha bgos na, lung dang rtogs pa'i yon tan thams cad yar do'i zla ba bzhin gong du 'phel la
gru.english: Focusing then primarily on the type of joyful effort called "armor-like," suppose that we are able to don the strong armor of steadfast, joyful effort: a kind of effort where we never turn back. In this case, all of our fine qualities-in both scriptural study and inner realizations-will multiply ever more strongly, much like a waxing moon.

gru.acip: RANG GIS BYA BA GANG BRTZAMS PA'I LAS KYI MTHA' RNAMS YID LA BSAMS PA BZHIN DU 'GRUB PAR 'GYUR RO,,
gru.wylie: rang gis bya ba gang brtsams pa'i las kyi mtha' rnams yid la bsams pa bzhin du 'grub par 'gyur ro
gru.english: And, finally, any undertaking that we ever initiate will come to its intended, successful conclusion-just as we originally hoped it would. How to undertake joyful effort

gru.acip: ,DE LTAR SHES NAS LE LO KUN SEL BA'I, ,RLABS CHEN BRTZON 'GRUS RGYAL SRAS RNAMS KYIS BRTZAMS, ,RNAL 'BYOR NGAS KYANG NYAMS LEN DE LTAR BGYIS, ,THAR 'DOD KHYED KYANG DE BZHIN BSKYANG 'TSAL LO,
gru.wylie: de ltar shes nas le lo kun sel ba'i, ,rlabs chen brtson 'grus rgyal sras rnams kyis brtsams, ,rnal 'byor ngas kyang nyams len de ltar bgyis, ,thar 'dod khyed kyang de bzhin bskyang 'tshal lo
gru.english: Children of the Victors Understood perfectly These points, And so they were Able to undertake Joyful effort which was Hugely effective, To clear away Every trace Of laziness. I, the deep practitioner, Have accomplished my practice This way; And you who hope for freedom Should do your practice The same.

gru.acip: JI SKAD BSHAD PA DE LTAR SHES NAS BYI {%PHYI} BSHOL GYI LE LO KUN SEL BAR BYED PA'I RLABS CHEN GYI BRTZON 'GRUS SNGON RGYAL SRAS RNAMS KYIS BRTZAMS PAR BYAS PA LTAR 'JUG GO
gru.wylie: ji skad bshad pa de ltar shes nas byi bshol gyi le lo kun sel bar byed pa'i rlabs chen gyi brtson 'grus sngon rgyal sras rnams kyis brtsams par byas pa ltar 'jug go
gru.english: Children of the Victors who lived in days gone by understood perfectly the points being made here, and so they were able to undertake just this kind of joyful effort: one which was hugely effective, and which functioned to clear away every trace of the kind of laziness where we tend to procrastinate about things we're supposed to get done. We too then must do the same. The fine qualities of meditation

gru.acip: RTAG PA DANG CHAD PA'I MTHAR 'DZIN PA'I MTHAR 'DZIN GYI DMIGS PA'I GTAD SO BDEN GRUB TU BZUNG BA LTAR
gru.wylie: rtag pa dang chad pa'i mthar 'dzin pa'i mthar 'dzin gyi dmigs pa'i gtad so bden grub tu bzung ba ltar
gru.english: Which is to say, we all have a tendency to hold things as existing in a real sense: a habit of holding to things in an extreme way, which means that at bottom we think that things could either never change, or simply disappear.

gru.acip: ,RTZE GCIG GOMS PAS TING 'DZIN 'GRUB PA NI, ,SMOS PAR CI 'TSAL TSUL BZHIN DPYOD PA YI, ,SO SOR RTOG PA YIS KYANG YIN LUGS LA, ,G-YO MED SHIN TU BRTAN PAR GNAS PA YI,
gru.wylie: rtse gcig goms pas ting 'dzin 'grub pa ni, ,smos par ci 'tshal tshul bzhin dpyod pa yi, ,so sor rtog pa yis kyang yin lugs la, ,g-yo med shin tu brtan par gnas pa yi
gru.english: What need to mention Accustoming ourselves To remaining single-pointed, And reaching One-point concentration? We then move into Specific individual understandings, Through accurate analysis. Through this, we see That we can give birth To a fixed concentration That can remain, Very solidly And without shifting, On the way things Really are.

gru.acip: ,TING 'DZIN BSKYED PAR MTHONG NAS ZHE {%ZHI} LHAG GNYIS, ,ZUNG 'BREL SGRUB LA BRTZON RNAMS YA MTSAN NO, ,RNAL 'BYOR NGAS KYANG NYAMS LEN DE LTAR BGYIS, ,THAR 'DOD KHYED KYANG DE BZHIN BSKYANG 'TSAL LO,
gru.wylie: ting 'dzin bskyed par mthong nas zhe lhag gnyis, ,zung 'brel sgrub la brtson rnams ya mtshan no, ,rnal 'byor ngas kyang nyams len de ltar bgyis, ,thar 'dod khyed kyang de bzhin bskyang 'tshal lo
gru.english: Those who make intense efforts Towards achieving the two Of quietude & special insight In combination Are truly wondrous. I, the deep practitioner, Have accomplished my practice This way; And you who hope for freedom Should do your practice The same.

gru.acip: RANG GI DMIGS PA GANG RUNG CIG LA DMIGS NAS MI DPYOD PAR RTZE GCIG TU GNAS PA GOMS PAS TING NGE 'DZIN 'GRUB PAR 'GYUR BA NI GZHIR BCAS SHING
gru.wylie: rang gi dmigs pa gang rung cig la dmigs nas mi dpyod par rtse gcig tu gnas pa goms pas ting nge 'dzin 'grub par 'gyur ba ni gzhir bcas shing
gru.english: And so let us consider that state of wisdom where we have accustomed ourselves to remaining single-pointed upon any one particular object of focus, without engaging in some particular analysis-that is, where we have reached one-point concentration, and taken this as our starting point.

gru.acip: ZHI LHAG GNYIS LAS PHYOGS RE TZAM MA YIN PAR ZUNG 'BREL SGRUB PAR BYED PA LA BRTZON PA RNAMS YA MTSAN NO STE NGO MTSAR CHE'O,,
gru.wylie: zhi lhag gnyis las phyogs re tsam ma yin par zung 'brel sgrub par byed pa la brtson pa rnams ya mtshan no ste ngo mtshar che'o
gru.english: And so those who make intense efforts towards achieving the two of quietude & special insight in combination-without just one side or the other-are truly wondrous, truly amazing.

gru.acip: RANG GI DMIGS PA LA GTOD DE RTZE GCIG TU GNAS PA GOMS KYANG ZHI GNAS 'GRUB MOD
gru.wylie: rang gi dmigs pa la gtod de rtse gcig tu gnas pa goms kyang zhi gnas 'grub mod
gru.english: Now it is admittedly the case that-if we become accustomed to directing our mind towards its particular object, and remaining there single-pointedly-we can achieve quietude.

gru.acip: LHAG MTHONG 'GRUB PA LA NI, DE TZAM GYIS MCHOG {%MA CHOG} PAR RTZE GCIG TU GNAS BZHIN PA'I DAD {%NGANG} NAS DPYAD STOBS KYIS SHIN SBYANGS KYI BDE BA 'DREN NUS PA DANG DGOS PA'I DON NO,,
gru.wylie: lhag mthong 'grub pa la ni, de tsam gyis mchog par rtse gcig tu gnas bzhin pa'i dad nas dpyad stobs kyis shin sbyangs kyi bde ba 'dren nus pa dang dgos pa'i don no
gru.english: But this alone is not enough, if we hope to go on to attain special insight. The point here then is that we have to be able to-and in fact we must-reach a state of single-pointed focus, and then staying in that focus use our powers of examination to bring on the bliss of physical & mental litheness. Conducting a session in two periods

gru.acip: DE KHO NA NYID KYI DON LA MNYAM PAR BZHAG PA'I MNYAM GZHAG DGAG BYA BDEN GRUB BKAG PA'I NAM MKHA' LTA BU'I STONG NYID SGOM PA DANG,
gru.wylie: de kho na nyid kyi don la mnyam par bzhag pa'i mnyam gzhag dgag bya bden grub bkag pa'i nam mkha' lta bu'i stong nyid sgom pa dang
gru.english: Now first here we are meditating upon an emptiness which is like empty space: this is a balanced meditation where we are sitting in balance on the object of suchness, and where we have succeeded in putting a stop to that thing which the concept of emptiness denies; that is, a state where things could exist in truth.

gru.acip: DE LAS YANGS {%LANGS} NAS RJES THOB TU BDEN PAR SNANG YANG DER MA GRUB PA'I SGYU MA LTA BU'I STONG PA NYID
gru.wylie: de las yangs nas rjes thob tu bden par snang yang der ma grub pa'i sgyu ma lta bu'i stong pa nyid
gru.english: And then at some point we come out of this meditation; and in this aftermath, things still appear to us as though they existed in truth. But we know that they do not, and so here is a second kind of emptiness where things are like an illusion.

gru.acip: DAD DANG RNAM DPYOD ZUNG DU 'BREL BA'I KHYA'O LUNG DGA' {%BKA'} BCU PA BLO BZANG BSAM 'GRUB KYIS BSKUL BA'I NGOR,
gru.wylie: dad dang rnam dpyod zung du 'brel ba'i khya'o lung dga' bcu pa blo bzang bsam 'grub kyis bskul ba'i ngor
gru.english: It was composed at the urgent behest of that Master of the Ten Classics, Lobsang Samdrup of the Land of Kyao, who combines within him both great faith and intellectual acumen.

gru.acip: SH'AKYA'I DGE SLONG BSHAD SGRUB MING CAN GYIS 'PHRAL DU MGYOGS LAS SU BRIS PA STE, PHYIS BAR {%PAR} DU BRKO BA'I TSE YI GE BA'ANG BSKUL BA PO NYID DO,,
gru.wylie: shAkya'i dge slong bshad sgrub ming can gyis 'phral du mgyogs las su bris pa ste, phyis bar du brko ba'i tshe yi ge ba'ang bskul ba po nyid do
gru.english: The text was written by myself-a Buddhist monk who holds the name of "Shedrup"-working as fast as I could, with only little time to do so. Later, when it came time to carve the piece onto blocks, the scribal work was performed by that same monk who made the original request.

gru.acip: ,SHIN TU DPAG PAR DKA' BA RGYAL BA'I YUM, ,JI BZHIN DGONGS PA 'GREL MDZAD 'DZAM GLING RGYAN, ,KLU SGRUB THOGS MED CES NI SA GSUM NA, ,YONGS SU GRAGS PA'I ZHABS LA BDAG PHYAG 'TSAL,
gru.wylie: shin tu dpag par dka' ba rgyal ba'i yum, ,ji bzhin dgongs pa 'grel mdzad 'dzam gling rgyan, ,klu sgrub thogs med ces ni sa gsum na, ,yongs su grags pa'i zhabs la bdag phyag 'tshal
gru.english: I prostrate At the holy feet Of those known As Nagarjuna & Asanga, So widely famed Through the three realms. You are true jewels Of our world Who undertook To comment, In a perfectly Accurate way, Upon the true thought Of the Mother Sutras Of the Victors, So extremely difficult To fathom.

gru.acip: ,'DZAM GLING MKHAS PA YONGS KYI GTZUG GI RGYAN, ,SNYAN PA'I BA DAN 'GRO NA LHANG NGE BA, ,KLU SGRUB THOGS MED GNYIS LAS RIM BZHIN DU, ,LEGS BRGYUD BYANG CHUB LAM GYI RIM PA NI,
gru.wylie: 'dzam gling mkhas pa yongs kyi gtsug gi rgyan, ,snyan pa'i ba dan 'gro na lhang nge ba, ,klu sgrub thogs med gnyis las rim bzhin du, ,legs brgyud byang chub lam gyi rim pa ni
gru.english: The steps on the path To enlightenment, Passed down With such excellence, In their own stages, Through the two Of Nagarjuna and Asanga, Are a jewel on the topknot Of each & every master Upon this planet; A victory banner Of great renown, Glorious here Among beings.

gru.acip: ,MTHONG NAS SROG GI PHYIR YANG MI GTONG BAR, ,BKA' BZHIN SGRUB PA'I MCHOD PAS MNYES PAR BYED, ,RNAL 'BYOR NGAS KYANG NYAMS LEN DE LTAR BGYIS, ,THAR 'DOD KHYED KYANG DE BZHIN BSKYANG 'TSAL LO,
gru.wylie: mthong nas srog gi phyir yang mi gtong bar, ,bka' bzhin sgrub pa'i mchod pas mnyes par byed, ,rnal 'byor ngas kyang nyams len de ltar bgyis, ,thar 'dod khyed kyang de bzhin bskyang 'tshal lo
gru.english: Seeing this, We see that we must Please them with the offering Of accomplishing everything They have commanded us to do, Without ever giving it up, Even at the cost of our life. I, the deep practitioner, Have accomplished my practice This way; And you who hope for freedom Should do your practice The same.

gru.acip: ,DE YANG DKAR NAG LAS 'BRAS LEGS BSAMS NAS, ,BLANG DOR TSUL BZHIN SGRUB LA RAG LAS SO, ,RNAL 'BYOR NGAS KYANG NYAMS LEN DE LTAR BGYIS, ,THAR 'DOD KHYED KYANG DE BZHIN BSKYANG 'TSAL LO,
gru.wylie: de yang dkar nag las 'bras legs bsams nas, ,blang dor tshul bzhin sgrub la rag las so, ,rnal 'byor ngas kyang nyams len de ltar bgyis, ,thar 'dod khyed kyang de bzhin bskyang 'tshal lo
gru.english: And now we have to Consider, carefully, White & black karma, And its consequences. We have to rely On a practice that Relates in a correct way To what we take up And what we give up. I, the deep practitioner, Have accomplished my practice This way; And you who hope for freedom Should do your practice The same.

gru.acip: ,LAM MCHOG SGRUB LA MTSAN NYID TSANG BA'I RTEN, ,MA RNYED BAR DU SA PHYOD {%CHOD} MI 'ONG BAS, ,DE YI MA TSANG MED PA'I RGYU LA BSLAB, ,SGO GSUM SDIG LTUNG DRI MAS SPAGS [*SBAGS] PA 'DI,
gru.wylie: lam mchog sgrub la mtshan nyid tshang ba'i rten, ,ma rnyed bar du sa phyod mi 'ong bas, ,de yi ma tshang med pa'i rgyu la bslab, ,sgo gsum sdig ltung dri mas spags [*sbags] pa 'di
gru.english: If we hope to achieve That supreme path, Then we need to find A body & mind Which possesses the Requisite qualities, All complete. Until we do, We won't be able to take Great bounds forward. And so we need To train ourselves In the necessary causes, In no way incomplete. The fact is that We have been dirtied By the stain Of negative actions And downfalls Committed through The three doors of Our actions, words, and thoughts.

gru.acip: ,MI LDOG {%BZLOG} BRTAN PA'I BRTZON 'GRUS GO BGOS NA, ,LUNG RTOGS YON TAN YAR NGO'I ZLA BZHIN 'PHEL, ,SPYOD LAM THAMS CAD DON DANG LDAN PAR 'GYUR, ,GANG BRTZAMS LAS KYI MTHA' RNAMS YID BZHIN 'GRUB,
gru.wylie: mi ldog brtan pa'i brtson 'grus go bgos na, ,lung rtogs yon tan yar ngo'i zla bzhin 'phel, ,spyod lam thams cad don dang ldan par 'gyur, ,gang brtsams las kyi mtha' rnams yid bzhin 'grub
gru.english: Suppose we are able To don the strong armor Of steadfast, joyful effort, Never turning back. Our fine qualities- In both scriptural study And inner realizations- Will multiply, Like a waxing moon. Any project we undertake Will end up having A meaningful result; And any undertaking We ever initiate Will come to its Successful conclusion, Just as we intended.

gru.acip: ,DE LTAR SHES NAS LE LO KUN SEL BA'I, ,RLABS CHEN BRTZON 'GRUS RGYAL SRAS RNAMS KYIS BRTZAMS, ,RNAL 'BYOR NGAS KYANG NYAMS LEN DE LTAR BGYIS, ,THAR 'DOD KHYED KYANG DE BZHIN BSKYANG 'TSAL LO,
gru.wylie: de ltar shes nas le lo kun sel ba'i, ,rlabs chen brtson 'grus rgyal sras rnams kyis brtsams, ,rnal 'byor ngas kyang nyams len de ltar bgyis, ,thar 'dod khyed kyang de bzhin bskyang 'tshal lo
gru.english: Children of the Victors Understood perfectly These points, And so they were Able to undertake Joyful effort which was Hugely effective, To clear away Every trace Of laziness. I, the deep practitioner, Have accomplished my practice This way; And you who hope for freedom Should do your practice The same.

gru.acip: ,RTZE GCIG GOMS PAS TING 'DZIN 'GRUB PA NI, ,SMOS PAR CI 'TSAL TSUL BZHIN DPYOD PA YI, ,SO SOR RTOG PA YIS KYANG YIN LUGS LA, ,G-YO MED SHIN TU BRTAN PAR GNAS PA YI,
gru.wylie: rtse gcig goms pas ting 'dzin 'grub pa ni, ,smos par ci 'tshal tshul bzhin dpyod pa yi, ,so sor rtog pa yis kyang yin lugs la, ,g-yo med shin tu brtan par gnas pa yi
gru.english: What need to mention Accustoming ourselves To remaining single-pointed, And reaching One-point concentration? We then move into Specific individual understandings, Through accurate analysis. Through this, we see That we can give birth To a fixed concentration That can remain, Very solidly And without shifting, On the way things Really are.

gru.acip: ,TING 'DZIN BSKYED PAR MTHONG NAS ZHE {%ZHI} LHAG GNYIS, ,ZUNG 'BREL SGRUB LA BRTZON RNAMS YA MTSAN NO, ,RNAL 'BYOR NGAS KYANG NYAMS LEN DE LTAR BGYIS, ,THAR 'DOD KHYED KYANG DE BZHIN BSKYANG 'TSAL LO,
gru.wylie: ting 'dzin bskyed par mthong nas zhe lhag gnyis, ,zung 'brel sgrub la brtson rnams ya mtshan no, ,rnal 'byor ngas kyang nyams len de ltar bgyis, ,thar 'dod khyed kyang de bzhin bskyang 'tshal lo
gru.english: Those who make intense efforts Towards achieving the two Of quietude & special insight In combination Are truly wondrous. I, the deep practitioner, Have accomplished my practice This way; And you who hope for freedom Should do your practice The same.

gru.acip: c4) RNAM MKHYEN SGRUB PA'I RTEN BSHAD PA,
gru.wylie: c4) rnam mkhyen sgrub pa'i rten bshad pa
gru.english: A presentation on the foundation that we need to lay, in order to achieve the state of omniscience

gru.acip: d4) BRTZON 'GRUS,
gru.wylie: D4) brtson 'grus
gru.english: Joyful effort

gru.english: Methods For Reaching The Holy Being

gru.wylie: tshe sgrub
gru.english: Methods Of Attaining Long Life

gru.wylie: blo bzang don grub
gru.english: Lobsang Dundrup

gru.acip: MKHAS GRUB RJE DGE LEGS DPAL BZANG PO
gru.wylie: mkhas grub rje dge legs dpal bzang po
gru.english: Kedrup Je Gelek Pel Sangpo

gru.acip: DBEN SA PA BLO BZANG DON GRUB
gru.wylie: dben sa pa blo bzang don grub
gru.english: Wensapa Lobsang Dundrup

gru.acip: MKHAS GRUB BSTAN 'DZIN
gru.wylie: mkhas grub bstan 'dzin
gru.english: Kedrup Tendzin

gru.wylie: gter sgrub
gru.english: Practices For Prosperity

gru.acip: DNGOS GRUB BRGYAD
gru.wylie: dngos grub brgyad
gru.english: Instructions For The Practice Of The Eight Attainments

gru.acip: ,GANG ZHIG SKAD CIG YID LA DRAN TZAM GYIS, ,RTAG CHAD MTHAR LTA'I RI BO RNAM 'JOMS LA, ,BLA MED THEG MCHOG LAM LA BKRI BYED PA, ,MGON PO KLU SGRUB ZHABS LA PHYAG 'TSAL LO,
gru.wylie: gang zhig skad cig yid la dran tsam gyis, ,rtag chad mthar lta'i ri bo rnam 'joms la, ,bla med theg mchog lam la bkri byed pa, ,mgon po klu sgrub zhabs la phyag 'tshal lo
gru.english: When you think of this person For even but a moment, Then the mountain of extreme views- The ideas that things could exist forever Or might not exist at all- Crumbles and falls to the ground. I bow to the one who leads me Along the matchless path Of the highest way; I bow down to the feet Of my protector, Nagarjuna.

gru.acip: ,DE LA 'DIR BDAG NYID CHEN PO 'PHAGS PA KLU SGRUB KYIS MDZAD PA'I RIGS PA DRUG CU PA NI GANG BSHAD PAR BYA BA'I CHOS SO,,
gru.wylie: de la 'dir bdag nyid chen po 'phags pa klu sgrub kyis mdzad pa'i rigs pa drug cu pa ni gang bshad par bya ba'i chos so
gru.english: The work that I will be commenting upon in this text is the Sixty Verses on Reasoning, composed by that great being, the Realized One, Nagarjuna.

gru.acip: DE YANG SPYIR BKA' THAMS CAD KYI DGONGS PA MTHAR THUG DBU MA CHEN PO'I DON CAN DU BSTAN PAR BYA BA'I PHYIR, KHYAD PAR NYAN THOS SDE PA SKYE 'JIG RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAR 'DOD PA DAG GI LOG RTOG DGAG PAR BYA BA'I PHYIR DE DAG LA YANG GRAGS PA'I NYAN THOS KYI SDE SNOD KYI LUNG DON RIGS PAS GTAN LA 'BEBS PAR BYED PA YIN NO,,
gru.wylie: de yang spyir bka' thams cad kyi dgongs pa mthar thug dbu ma chen po'i don can du bstan par bya ba'i phyir, khyad par nyan thos sde pa skye 'jig rang bzhin gyis grub par 'dod pa dag gi log rtog dgag par bya ba'i phyir de dag la yang grags pa'i nyan thos kyi sde snod kyi lung don rigs pas gtan la 'bebs par byed pa yin no
gru.english: Our first, general goal is to demonstrate that the ultimate intent of everything which Lord Buddha ever taught was to express the ideas of the magnificent Middle Way. More specifically, we will use logic to establish the meaning of the scriptures of the listener group-something that even they recognize-in order to refute their mistaken position that things could start or stop on their own.

gru.acip: GSUM PA'ANG MI RIGS TE, MNYAM GZHAG TU BCOM PA'I PHYIR ZER NA, KHYAB PA MA NGES SHING, RJES THOB TU BCOM PA MI 'GRUB STE, BLANG BYA LEN ZHING DOR BYA 'DOR BA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: gsum pa'ang mi rigs te, mnyam gzhag tu bcom pa'i phyir zer na, khyab pa ma nges shing, rjes thob tu bcom pa mi 'grub ste, blang bya len zhing dor bya 'dor ba'i phyir
gru.english: The third idea is also mistaken. If Jangchub Yeshe is saying that it's during a state of deep meditation that one has destroyed all appearances, and thus Nagarjuna has no goal in mind, then we would say that it's not necessarily the case. If he's saying that these appearances have been destroyed during the aftermath period, following such a meditation, then we would say he is simply wrong-since we do at this point undertake certain actions and avoid others.

gru.acip: DE LTA NA THUB DBANG DU 'GRUB PA RTEN 'BYUNG GSUNG BA NGES PA LA BLTOS, DE YANG THUB DBANG DU NGES PA LA BLTOS PAS PHAN TSUN BLTOS PA'I PHYIR, GNYIS KA MI 'GRUB BO ZHE NA,
gru.wylie: de lta na thub dbang du 'grub pa rten 'byung gsung ba nges pa la bltos, de yang thub dbang du nges pa la bltos pas phan tshun bltos pa'i phyir, gnyis ka mi 'grub bo zhe na
gru.english: Someone may come and raise the following objection- Based on what you've said, deciding whether or not someone is a Lord of the Able Ones depends on determining whether or not they are teaching dependence. But that in itself depends on determining whether or not they are indeed a Lord of the Able Ones. Since proving one depends upon proving the other, neither can be proved!

gru.acip: PHAN TSUN BLTOS PAS NGO BO NYID KYIS MI 'GRUB PA 'DOD LA, SPYIR MI 'GRUB PAR THAL NA NI KHYAB PA MED DO,,
gru.wylie: phan tshun bltos pas ngo bo nyid kyis mi 'grub pa 'dod la, spyir mi 'grub par thal na ni khyab pa med do
gru.english: We can agree that the two depend upon each other, and so neither is proven in and by itself. To say though that it is therefore the case that they cannot, in general, be proven is not a necessary conclusion.

gru.acip: GNYIS PA BRTZAMS PAR BYA BA'I GZHUNG DNGOS LA, RTEN 'BREL MTHA' BRAL DU BSTAN PA DANG, PHUNG SOGS GSUNGS PA DRANG DON DU BSGRUB PA DANG, PHUNG POR ZHEN PA'I NYES DMIGS DANG, THAR PA'I PHAN YON NO,,
gru.wylie: gnyis pa brtsams par bya ba'i gzhung dngos la, rten 'brel mtha' bral du bstan pa dang, phung sogs gsungs pa drang don du bsgrub pa dang, phung por zhen pa'i nyes dmigs dang, thar pa'i phan yon no
gru.english: Secondly, I will cover the following topics in the actual text to be composed: demonstrating that dependence is freedom from extreme positions; establishing that statements about the parts of a person and so on were figurative; problems of attachment to the parts of a person; and the benefits of freedom. Demonstrating that dependence is freedom from the two extremes

gru.acip: DANG PO LA, YOD MTHA' DGAG ,MTHA' GNYIS KYI SGRUB BYED DGAG ,MTHA' GNYIS KYI NGO BO DGAG PA'O,,
gru.wylie: dang po la, yod mtha' dgag ,mtha' gnyis kyi sgrub byed dgag ,mtha' gnyis kyi ngo bo dgag pa'o
gru.english: The first topic has three parts: refuting the extreme view that things exist; refuting arguments in favor of the two extreme views; and refuting the substance of the two extreme views. Refuting the extreme view that things exist

gru.acip: ,BLO TZAM LA GNYIS SNANG GI KHYAB PA GANG DU YANG SGRUB MI NUS TE, 'BREL PA MED PA'I PHYIR RO,,
gru.wylie: blo tsam la gnyis snang gi khyab pa gang du yang sgrub mi nus te, 'brel pa med pa'i phyir ro
gru.english: There is no way you can say that just because someone has a mind, then that mind has to be involved in this discrepancy; there's no connection.

gru.acip: MIG SHES KYI NGOR SGRA MED PAS SGRA MED PAR MI 'GRUB PA BZHIN, MNYAM GZHAG DANG DON DAM BDEN PA YUL YUL CAN DANG RTOGS BYA RTOGS BYED DU SLOB DPON YAB SRAS KYIS GSUNGS SHING, DE LTAR THA SNYAD PA'I TSAD MAS GZHAL BA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: mig shes kyi ngor sgra med pas sgra med par mi 'grub pa bzhin, mnyam gzhag dang don dam bden pa yul yul can dang rtogs bya rtogs byed du slob dpon yab sras kyis gsungs shing, de ltar tha snyad pa'i tshad mas gzhal ba'i phyir
gru.english: The fact that sound doesn't appear to the consciousness of the eye doesn't prove that sound doesn't exist. And so the masters-Father & Son-have said that the state of meditation of a realized being is the subject which is doing the perceiving; while ultimate reality is the object which is being perceived. Moreover, this fact can be confirmed by a conventional type of accurate perception.

gru.acip: SPANG GNYEN DON LA GRUB PA 'GOG PA YIN GYI, SA BON SPONG BA LA BDAG MED MNGON SUM DU MTHONG DGOS PAR 'JUG 'GREL SOGS KUN TU GSUNGS PA'I PHYIR DANG BDEN PA MNGON PAR RTOGS PA SKAD CIG MA GCIG TU GSUNGS PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: spang gnyen don la grub pa 'gog pa yin gyi, sa bon spong ba la bdag med mngon sum du mthong dgos par 'jug 'grel sogs kun tu gsungs pa'i phyir dang bden pa mngon par rtogs pa skad cig ma gcig tu gsungs pa'i phyir
gru.english: We deny that problems and their antidotes could exist in reality. But the great books-such as Entering the Middle Way, and its various commentaries-all agree that to eliminate negative seeds we need to see, directly, the fact that nothing is itself. And they agree that the realization of this reality is something that changes from instant to instant.

gru.acip: DANG PO NI, RANG SDE NA RE, CHOS THAMS CAD STONG NYID DU MI 'THAD DE, SGRUB BYED MED CING GNOD BYED YOD PAS SO,,
gru.wylie: dang po ni, rang sde na re, chos thams cad stong nyid du mi 'thad de, sgrub byed med cing gnod byed yod pas so
gru.english: Here is the first. Now there are certain of our own Buddhist schools which say that it cannot be correct to assert that every existing thing in the universe is empty. They would say that-first of all-there is no way to prove that this idea is correct; and secondly, there are ways to prove that it is wrong.

gru.acip: DANG PO NI, STONG NYID DU SGRUB PA'I 'THAD PA MI SRID PA'I PHYIR DANG,
gru.wylie: dang po ni, stong nyid du sgrub pa'i 'thad pa mi srid pa'i phyir dang
gru.english: About there being no proofs for this idea, they would say that it's in fact impossible to prove anything as correct, if it's the case that everything is empty.

gru.acip: DE LTAR THAL BA LAS, BYIS PAS THAR PA MA THOB PA'I PHYIR, SNANG BA 'DI DAG MI BDEN PAS, YOD PA'I MTHAR MA GRUB BO,,
gru.wylie: de ltar thal ba las, byis pas thar pa ma thob pa'i phyir, snang ba 'di dag mi bden pas, yod pa'i mthar ma grub bo
gru.english: And yet rather than things being the way this absurd statement proposes, the fact is that these infants have not achieved freedom. The way that things appear to them is not real; and thus we can say that, in being the extreme of existence, the things that appear to them don't even exist.

gru.acip: RANG LUGS MI SGRUB PAR GZHAN GYI PHYOGS 'GOG PA TZAM DU KHAS LEN MI LEN DANG,
gru.wylie: rang lugs mi sgrub par gzhan gyi phyogs 'gog pa tsam du khas len mi len dang
gru.english: (7) Do they or do they not accept the idea of simply refuting an opponent's position, without establishing ones own?

gru.acip: SLOB DPON CHEN PO LEGS LDAN 'BYED KYIS, GZUGS KYI SKYE BA MED DO SNYAM DU DPYOD NA SHER PHYIN LA SPYOD KYI, GZUGS KYI SKYE BA MED PA YOD DO SNYAM NA SHER PHYIN LA MI SPYOD DE, RIGS {%RIG} NGOR SKYE BA 'GOG PA YIN GYI, SKYE MED MI SGRUB PAR GSUNGS PA'I PHYIR, DES NA 'THAD PHYOGS NI DANG PO LTAR YIN LA,
gru.wylie: slob dpon chen po legs ldan 'byed kyis, gzugs kyi skye ba med do snyam du dpyod na sher phyin la spyod kyi, gzugs kyi skye ba med pa yod do snyam na sher phyin la mi spyod de, rigs ngor skye ba 'gog pa yin gyi, skye med mi sgrub par gsungs pa'i phyir, des na 'thad phyogs ni dang po ltar yin la
gru.english: According to the great master Bhavaviveka, the mind is exploring the perfection of wisdom when we examine the concept that physical form never starts; whereas the mind is not exploring this perfection when we examine the concept that an absence of starting to physical form is something that itself exists. This is because he has stated that-although this kind of starting is denied within the mind at this point-the absence of such starting is not itself established. Therefore the position we would say is correct here would relate to the former.

gru.acip: DE YANG CHOS CAN LA MTHUN SNANG YOD MED YIN TE, RANG RGYUD KYI RTAGS YOD MED NI, MTHAR RGOL PHYI RGOL GYI MTHUN SNANG DU GZHI CHOS CAN GRUB MA GRUB LA RAG LAS PA'I PHYIR RO,,
gru.wylie: de yang chos can la mthun snang yod med yin te, rang rgyud kyi rtags yod med ni, mthar rgol phyi rgol gyi mthun snang du gzhi chos can grub ma grub la rag las pa'i phyir ro
gru.english: And as far as the question of whether the person who initiates an argument, and their opponent, can ever be perceiving the object under consideration in the same way, we would point out that-in the final analysis-the entire question of whether an "independent" proof exists or not itself depends on this question: of whether there even exists a basis of the argument-an object under consideration-which can appear in the same way to both the proponent and the opponent.

gru.acip: TSIG GSAL GYI STONG THUN DU 'DIR SKYE BA BKAG PA BSGRUB BYA'I CHOS SU 'DOD PA'I TSE DE KHO NAR RTEN CHOS CAN PHYIN CI LOG TZAM GYI BDAG GI DNGOS PO RNYED PA NYAMS PAR 'GYUR BAR RTOG GE PA 'DIS RANG NYID KYIS KHAS BLANGS PA YIN NO ZHES GSUNGS SO,,
gru.wylie: tshig gsal gyi stong thun du 'dir skye ba bkag pa bsgrub bya'i chos su 'dod pa'i tshe de kho nar rten chos can phyin ci log tsam gyi bdag gi dngos po rnyed pa nyams par 'gyur bar rtog ge pa 'dis rang nyid kyis khas blangs pa yin no zhes gsungs so
gru.english: He expresses this point in his interlude on emptiness known as A Clarification of the Verses: When we take the position here that denying the growth of things is the quality we seek to prove, then this logician has-on his own accord-accepted precisely, with nothing more than this, that the idea that the basis of the quality (the subject under consideration) can be perceived to be a self-existing entity, and thus simply mistaken, has been compromised.

gru.acip: MDO SDE PA DANG GRANGS CAN RTZOD PA NA, RTAG MI RTAG GANG GIS KYANG KHYAD PAR MA BYAS PA'I SGRA LA MTHUN SNANG YOD PA BZHIN DU, DBU MA PA DANG DNGOS POR SMRA BA LA YANG BDEN STONG GANG GIS KYANG KHYAD PAR MA BYAS PA'I SNANG TZAM LA MTHUN SNANG YOD PAS MTHUN SNANG MED PAR MA GRUB BO ZHE NA,
gru.wylie: mdo sde pa dang grangs can rtsod pa na, rtag mi rtag gang gis kyang khyad par ma byas pa'i sgra la mthun snang yod pa bzhin du, dbu ma pa dang dngos por smra ba la yang bden stong gang gis kyang khyad par ma byas pa'i snang tsam la mthun snang yod pas mthun snang med par ma grub bo zhe na
gru.english: One may return with the following argument: When a member of the Sutrist School debates a follower of the Numerist School, they both see the subject under consideration-sound-in the same way, without qualifying it in different ways, as being permanent or impermanent. Similarly, when a member of the Middle Way School debates someone belonging to the Functionalist group, they see the subject under consideration in the same way-without qualifying it as existing in truth, or as being empty of true existence. You are wrong, thus, when you say that the two parties cannot see such things in the same way.

gru.acip: SLOB DPON ZLA BA GRAGS PA DANG PHYOGS GLANG GNYIS KA RANG RGYUD KYI GTAN TSIGS YIN NA TSUL SGRUB BYED KYI TSAD MA'I RTZA BA BLOS SGRO MA BTAGS PAR YOD PA'I DE KHO NA NYID 'DZIN PA LA RAG LAS PAR BZHED PA GNYIS KA MTHUN KYANG, ZLA BA GRAGS PAS DE LTA BU MI SRID PA'I PHYIR, RANG RGYUD KYI GTAN TSIGS MI BZHED PA YIN NO,,
gru.wylie: slob dpon zla ba grags pa dang phyogs glang gnyis ka rang rgyud kyi gtan tshigs yin na tshul sgrub byed kyi tshad ma'i rtsa ba blos sgro ma btags par yod pa'i de kho na nyid 'dzin pa la rag las par bzhed pa gnyis ka mthun kyang, zla ba grags pas de lta bu mi srid pa'i phyir, rang rgyud kyi gtan tshigs mi bzhed pa yin no
gru.english: Master Chandrakirti and Master Dignaga are the same in asserting that-if something were an independently effective syllogism-then the very root of the accurate perception which confirmed its three necessary elements is that it would have to depend on a perception of suchness that existed without any false elaboration by the mind. Chandrakirti though would say that such a thing was impossible; and for this reason would deny the idea of an independently effective syllogism.

gru.acip: DE MA GRUB CES ZER NA DE YANG MA GRUB BO, ,DNGOS PO RIGS PAS GRUB PAR KHAS BLANGS PA'I PHYIR CE NA,
gru.wylie: de ma grub ces zer na de yang ma grub bo, ,dngos po rigs pas grub par khas blangs pa'i phyir ce na
gru.english: The debater might come back with: So if you say my point isn't proven for that first reason, here's another! What's that? They can't be followers of the Middle Way, because they accept the idea of logic that can engender an accurate perception by the very nature of an entity.

gru.acip: GRUB MTHA' SMRA BA THAMS CAD 'CHOL BAR 'GYUR TE, DON SMRA GNYIS KYIS KYANG BYAS PA THAMS CAD BDEN MED SGYU MA LTA BUR KHAS BLANGS PAR 'GYUR TE, RTEN 'BREL DU KHAS BLANGS PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: grub mtha' smra ba thams cad 'chol bar 'gyur te, don smra gnyis kyis kyang byas pa thams cad bden med sgyu ma lta bur khas blangs par 'gyur te, rten 'brel du khas blangs pa'i phyir
gru.english: And if you continue with this line of thinking, then you're going to make a jumble of all the schools of philosophy there are. We'd have to say, for example, that the two schools which accept the existence of outer objects also accept that nothing in the world which is made could exist in truth-that they also accept that all made things exist in the manner of an illusion; all because they already accept the concept of dependence. Incidental points about how things don't exist the way they appear

gru.acip: DNGOS MED LA MA BRTEN PAR DNGOS PO MI 'GRUB STE, DNGOS MIN MA BKAG PAR DNGOS PO MI 'GRUB PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: dngos med la ma brten par dngos po mi 'grub ste, dngos min ma bkag par dngos po mi 'grub pa'i phyir
gru.english: And it's not that when we say "people should not rely upon the absence of things" that things come to exist. Because you cannot say a thing exists without blocking the possibility that it was something that couldn't exist.

gru.acip: GNYIS PA LA, MTHA' GNYIS KYI SGRUB BYED DGAG PA LA LUNG GI SGRUB BYED MI 'THAD PA DANG, DE DAG LA MYANG 'DAS MI 'THAD PA'O,,
gru.wylie: gnyis pa la, mtha' gnyis kyi sgrub byed dgag pa la lung gi sgrub byed mi 'thad pa dang, de dag la myang 'das mi 'thad pa'o
gru.english: This brings us to our second major topic from above-refuting arguments in favor of the two extreme views. We'll proceed in two steps: demonstrating how it is incorrect to say that there are scriptural references which support these two views; and then showing how nirvana could never be correct if these two views are. Denying the support of scriptural reference

gru.acip: DANG PO LA, BYIS PA LA MA NGES PA DANG, 'PHAGS PA LA BSTAN PA MA GRUB PA'O,,
gru.wylie: dang po la, byis pa la ma nges pa dang, 'phags pa la bstan pa ma grub pa'o
gru.english: As far as the first step, we will again cover the point in two parts: showing that these arguments lead to indefinite conclusions when presented to an infant, and then showing that they fail altogether when presented to a realized being. Denying scriptural references presented to an infant

gru.acip: DANG PO NI, DNGOS PO DANG DNGOS MED YOD DE, 'KHOR BA DANG MYANG 'DAS YOD PA'I PHYIR, KHYAB PA YOD DE, NYE BAR LEN PA'I PHUNG PO LNGA'I DNGOS PO 'KHOR BA YIN LA, DE RGYUN CHAD PA'I DNGOS MED MYA NGAN LAS 'DAS PA YIN PAS 'KHOR 'DAS MED PAR YANG MA GRUB STE, DE MED NA BLANG DOR BYA BA'I PHYIR STON PAR MI RIGS PA LA, BCOM LDAN 'DAS KYIS GSUNGS PA'I PHYIR CE NA,
gru.wylie: dang po ni, dngos po dang dngos med yod de, 'khor ba dang myang 'das yod pa'i phyir, khyab pa yod de, nye bar len pa'i phung po lnga'i dngos po 'khor ba yin la, de rgyun chad pa'i dngos med mya ngan las 'das pa yin pas 'khor 'das med par yang ma grub ste, de med na blang dor bya ba'i phyir ston par mi rigs pa la, bcom ldan 'das kyis gsungs pa'i phyir ce na
gru.english: Here is the first. Now someone may come and make the following argument: Things and the absence of things do indeed exist, Because the cycle of pain, and nirvana, do exist. And the one does follow from the other, Because "things"-as represented by the five parts to a person that we've taken on-are the cycle of pain; whereas "the absence of things"-as represented by the discontinuation of these parts-is nirvana. And as such, you cannot say that neither the cycle, nor nirvana, exists. For if they did not exist, then it would be incorrect to teach about them, in order that disciples could reach the one and abandon the other-whereas Lord Buddha did describe them.

gru.acip: 'PHAGS PA LA BSTAN PA'I PHYIR ZER NA MA GRUB STE,
gru.wylie: 'phags pa la bstan pa'i phyir zer na ma grub ste
gru.english: Now suppose you continue this argument with: Because he described them to realized beings. In that case, we would have to say, "We disagree."

gru.acip: 'PHAGS PAR MA GYUR PA 'PHAGS PAR 'GYUR BAR BYA BA'I PHYIR TU DE GNYIS BSTAN DGOS, DE GNYIS STON PA LA DE'I GONG DU 'PHAGS PA DGOS PAS PHAN TSUN BRTAN PA'I PHYIR RANG BZHIN MED PAR GRUB PO,,
gru.wylie: 'phags par ma gyur pa 'phags par 'gyur bar bya ba'i phyir tu de gnyis bstan dgos, de gnyis ston pa la de'i gong du 'phags pa dgos pas phan tshun brtan pa'i phyir rang bzhin med par grub po
gru.english: And that's because Lord Buddha would have had to teach about these two in order to make realized beings out of people who were not realized beings. And to teach the two, there would have had to be realized beings before he taught them. These two prerequisites being interdependent in fact proves that these things can have no nature of their own.

gru.acip: DE LTA MA YIN PAR 'PHAGS PA KHO NA LA GRUB NA 'PHAGS PA'I THA SNYAD BRGYAD KYANG MI RIGS PAR 'GYUR LA, 'JIG RTEN NA YANG JI LTAR BSTAN PA LTAR GNAS PA LA 'PHAGS PA'I THA SNYAD DU GRAGS SO,,
gru.wylie: de lta ma yin par 'phags pa kho na la grub na 'phags pa'i tha snyad brgyad kyang mi rigs par 'gyur la, 'jig rten na yang ji ltar bstan pa ltar gnas pa la 'phags pa'i tha snyad du grags so
gru.english: If this were not the case-and if something were spoken of as "higher" only if it had been seen to be true by these higher, realized beings-then there would be no such thing as the eight higher expressions; and the expression "high words" would never be used in the everyday world to refer to words which described things in the way they truly were.

gru.acip: 'KHOR BA DANG MYA NGAN LAS 'DAS PA RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB NA 'PHAGS PA'I MNYAM GZHAG GIS GZIGS PAR RIGS NA YANG SRID PA DANG MYA NGAN LAS 'DAS PA GNYIS PO 'DI NI RANG BZHIN GYIS YOD PA MA YIN PA'I PHYIR GZUGS BRNYAN BZHIN DE RANG BZHIN GYIS YOD PA MA YIN PA GZIGS PA NI DE KHO NA GZIGS PA MA YIN TE, RAB RIB CAN LA SOGS PAS KYANG DE KHO NA NYID MTHONG BAR 'GYUR BA'I PHYIR RO,,
gru.wylie: 'khor ba dang mya ngan las 'das pa rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub na 'phags pa'i mnyam gzhag gis gzigs par rigs na yang srid pa dang mya ngan las 'das pa gnyis po 'di ni rang bzhin gyis yod pa ma yin pa'i phyir gzugs brnyan bzhin de rang bzhin gyis yod pa ma yin pa gzigs pa ni de kho na gzigs pa ma yin te, rab rib can la sogs pas kyang de kho na nyid mthong bar 'gyur ba'i phyir ro
gru.english: Now even suppose that it was correct to say that-if the cycle of pain, and the nirvana where we escape this cycle, existed in & of themselves-then they could be perceived by a realized being during that deep meditation upon ultimate reality. The fact though is that these two-the life of suffering and the nirvana where we go beyond it-are not things that could exist through any nature of their own. As such, they are similar to the reflection of something that we see in a mirror. To see then that they are not things which exist through any nature of their own is not to see that they exist in & of themselves. And that's true because a person who thought they saw something there-but only because they had a serious problem with cataracts-would then have to be a person who was seeing the way things really are. How we explain nirvana

gru.acip: SRID PA RANG BZHIN MED PAR MNGON SUM DU YONGS SU SHES PA NYID LA MYA NGAN LAS 'DAS PA THOB CES BYA BAR BRJOD PA YIN PAS THA SNYAD DU MED PA MA GRUB CING DON DAM DU KHYAB PA MA GRUB BO,,
gru.wylie: srid pa rang bzhin med par mngon sum du yongs su shes pa nyid la mya ngan las 'das pa thob ces bya bar brjod pa yin pas tha snyad du med pa ma grub cing don dam du khyab pa ma grub bo
gru.english: When we have understood, completely (or directly) that the cycle of existence has no nature of its own-then that itself is what we call achieving nirvana, or going beyond all grief. As such, we can say that nirvana is something that cannot be established as not existing in a nominal sense; and then neither is it something that must then exist in an ultimate sense. Detail on nirvana

gru.acip: DNGOS PO MI RTAG PA NI RANG GI NGO BOS GRUB PA MED KYI, DNGOS PO SNGAR BYUNG ZHING SKYES PA BZHIG PA LA JI LTAR 'GOG PA STE MI RTAG PAR RNAM PAR BRTAGS PA
gru.wylie: dngos po mi rtag pa ni rang gi ngo bos grub pa med kyi, dngos po sngar byung zhing skyes pa bzhig pa la ji ltar 'gog pa ste mi rtag par rnam par brtags pa
gru.english: The fact that functional things are changing is not something that exists in & of itself; rather, the way in which a functional entity occurred in the past-started-and then later ends, or comes to a stop, is an event that we label a "changing nature."

gru.acip: BZHIN DU MYA NGAN LAS 'DAS KYANG RANG GI NGO BOS GRUB PA MED KYI, 'KHOR BA RANG BZHIN MED PA MYANG 'DAS YIN PAS DE BLO YUL DU 'CHAR BA 'KHOR BA BLO YUL DU 'CHAR BA LA BLTOS PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: bzhin du mya ngan las 'das kyang rang gi ngo bos grub pa med kyi, 'khor ba rang bzhin med pa myang 'das yin pas de blo yul du 'char ba 'khor ba blo yul du 'char ba la bltos pa'i phyir
gru.english: In the same way, achieving nirvana-going beyond grief-is not something that could exist in & of itself; rather, that fact that the cycle of pain has no nature of its own is itself nirvana. As such, forming a mental image of nirvana is something that relies upon forming a mental image of the cycle.

gru.acip: DES NA GRUB MTHA' 'DZIN PA'I NYAN THOS RNAM PAR MI MKHAS PA DE DAG CHOS CAN,
gru.wylie: des na grub mtha' 'dzin pa'i nyan thos rnam par mi mkhas pa de dag chos can
gru.english: As such, let us consider those who truly have no wisdom: those listeners who hold to that particular school of thought.

gru.acip: KLU SGRUB YAB SRAS KYI DGONGS PA DPAL LDAN ZLA BA GRAGS PAS BKRAL BA'I GZHUNG RNAMS SU DE DAG RGYUD SMIN BYED KYI LAM TZAM DU GSUNGS KYI, GROL LAM DU GANG DU YANG MA GSUNGS PAS
gru.wylie: klu sgrub yab sras kyi dgongs pa dpal ldan zla ba grags pas bkral ba'i gzhung rnams su de dag rgyud smin byed kyi lam tsam du gsungs kyi, grol lam du gang du yang ma gsungs pas
gru.english: As for the thinking of Arya Nagarjuna and his spiritual son, the great books in which the glorious Chandrakirti makes his commentary refer to those sixteen only as paths which function to ripen our mental stream; he says nothing about them being paths of liberation.

gru.acip: MI MKHAS PA GANG DAG GIS NI SNANG TZAM GYIS 'DUS BYAS LA RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS SKYE BA DANG 'JIG PA RNAM PAR BRTAGS PA DE DAG GIS NI RTEN CING 'BREL PAR 'BYUNG BA THOG MA DANG DBUS DANG THA MA DANG BRAL BA 'KHOR LO LTA BU'I 'GRO BA STE 'JUG TSUL RNAM PAR MI SHES SHING MI RTOGS TE, RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PA LA SKYE BA DANG 'JIG PA MI SRID PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: mi mkhas pa gang dag gis ni snang tsam gyis 'dus byas la rang gi mtshan nyid kyis skye ba dang 'jig pa rnam par brtags pa de dag gis ni rten cing 'brel par 'byung ba thog ma dang dbus dang tha ma dang bral ba 'khor lo lta bu'i 'gro ba ste 'jug tshul rnam par mi shes shing mi rtogs te, rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub pa la skye ba dang 'jig pa mi srid pa'i phyir
gru.english: Those who have no nature of being wise imagine-simply because of the way things appear-that produced things have a starting and an ending, through some definition of their own. People like this have no understanding at all of the workings of all those entities which occur in a dependent relationship: of how they operate. They cannot grasp how much like a wheel these things are, devoid of any kind of starting point, or middle point, or ending point. And all this because they cannot see how-with things that exist in & of themselves-the very events of starting & stopping are impossible. The two realities, defined

gru.acip: PHUNG PO LA GTZANG BDE RTAG BDAG BZHI NI KUN RDZOB TU YANG TSAD MA'I GZHAL BYA MA YIN PAS GZHI MA GRUB PA KHO NA'O,,
gru.wylie: phung po la gtsang bde rtag bdag bzhi ni kun rdzob tu yang tshad ma'i gzhal bya ma yin pas gzhi ma grub pa kho na'o
gru.english: The perception that the parts to us could be clean; pleasure; lasting; or possessed of any kind of self-nature is-even in terms of deceptive reality-something that could never be considered by any form of accurate perception. As such, parts like that simply could never exist.

gru.acip: 'PHAGS PA RNAMS KYIS KYANG BDEN GNYIS KYI RNAM DBYE BYED PA NA DE DAG KUN RDZOB BDEN PAR KHAS LEN PA YIN TE, KLU SGRUB BZHIN,
gru.wylie: 'phags pa rnams kyis kyang bden gnyis kyi rnam dbye byed pa na de dag kun rdzob bden par khas len pa yin te, klu sgrub bzhin
gru.english: Realized beings then do accept the division of things into two realities; and thus they do accept the concept of a deceptive reality-just the same way that Arya Nagarjuna does.

gru.acip: THA SNYAD PA'I TSAD MA BZHI'I GZHAL BYA YANG BYIS PA RNAMS KYIS BDEN PAR ZHEN YANG BDEN GNYIS KYI RNAM DBYE LA MKHAS PA'I SO SO SKYE BO DANG, 'PHAGS PA RNAMS KYIS RDZUN PAR GZIGS PAS RDZUN PAR GNAS PA'I PHYIR GZHI MA GRUB PA'I SKYON MED LA,
gru.wylie: tha snyad pa'i tshad ma bzhi'i gzhal bya yang byis pa rnams kyis bden par zhen yang bden gnyis kyi rnam dbye la mkhas pa'i so so skye bo dang, 'phags pa rnams kyis rdzun par gzigs pas rdzun par gnas pa'i phyir gzhi ma grub pa'i skyon med la
gru.english: When we speak of the objects which are held under consideration by the four forms of the conventional type of accurate perception, these are things that infants grasp to as real; whereas both people who have yet to see emptiness directly-but who are well versed in the division into two realities-and realized beings see that these objects are deceptive. And because they do exist, as deceptive, then we avoid the problem of saying that they have no existence at all.

gru.acip: GANG DAG DBU MA PA LA KHAS LEN YE MED PA'I SHES BYED DU KLU SGRUB KYIS DE LTAR SGRUB BO ZHES SMRA BA RNAMS KYIS GRUB MTHA'I RNAM DBYE MA BYAS NA MDZES SO,,
gru.wylie: gang dag dbu ma pa la khas len ye med pa'i shes byed du klu sgrub kyis de ltar sgrub bo zhes smra ba rnams kyis grub mtha'i rnam dbye ma byas na mdzes so
gru.english: Yes there are those who point to statements such as where Arya Nagarjuna says "that's the way they are" and take them as evidence that those of the Middle Way take no position at all. In my opinion though it would be better if such people stayed out of the business of trying to distinguish between the different schools of Buddhism.

gru.acip: DE LA RTEN 'BREL RTOGS PA'I BLO RANG BZHIN MED PAR RTOGS PA'I THABS SU 'GYUR BA YIN TE, BSGRUB BYA RTOGS PA'I BLO RTAGS RTOGS PA LAS SKYE DGOS PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: de la rten 'brel rtogs pa'i blo rang bzhin med par rtogs pa'i thabs su 'gyur ba yin te, bsgrub bya rtogs pa'i blo rtags rtogs pa las skye dgos pa'i phyir
gru.english: This argument serves as a method for the state of mind which realizes the fact of dependent relationship to go further and realize how things have no nature of their own.
