gru.english: In the same way, the heaps of parts that make us up serve as a basis for us to get the impression "This is me." There is nothing at all about these heaps as a whole, nor their continuation over time, nor their separate components, that we could establish as being an actual representation of "me." At the same time though there is nothing else, nothing essentially separate from these heaps of parts to ourselves, that we could consider an actual representation of "me" either. As such, this "me" is merely something labeled upon the heaps of parts that make us up; there is nothing which exists by its own essence.

gru.acip: 'O NA SKYES BU STE GANG ZAG JI LTAR 'JOG PA YANG DE NYID LAS, ,SKYES BU KHAMS DRUG 'DUS PA'I PHYIR, ,YANG DAG MA YIN JI LTA BAR, ,DE BZHIN KHAMS NI RE RE YANG, ,'DUS PHYIR YANG DAG NYID DU MIN, ,ZHES GSUNGS TE, RGYU MTSAN DES NA SKYES BU NI RANG GI KHAMS DRUG 'DUS PA'I STENG DU BTAGS PA TZAM MA GTOGS, YANG DAG PAR MA GRUB BO,,
gru.wylie: 'o na skyes bu ste gang zag ji ltar 'jog pa yang de nyid las, ,skyes bu khams drug 'dus pa'i phyir, ,yang dag ma yin ji lta bar, ,de bzhin khams ni re re yang, ,'dus phyir yang dag nyid du min, ,zhes gsungs te, rgyu mtshan des na skyes bu ni rang gi khams drug 'dus pa'i steng du btags pa tsam ma gtogs, yang dag par ma grub bo
gru.english: How then do we establish the existence of the persona (which in this case simply means "person")? The same work says: Because the persona includes all six elements, It's nothing that purely exists; Just so, because they include their parts, None of these elements purely exist.[54] Given the reason stated above, the persona is nothing more than something labeled upon the six elements that make them up—it does not though purely exist.

gru.acip: DE JI LTA BA BZHIN DU KHAMS RNAMS KYANG RANG RANG GI CHA SHAS 'DUS PA LA BRTEN NAS BTAGS PA YIN PA'I PHYIR YANG DAG PAR MA GRUB ZHES BSTAN TO, ,DE BZHIN DU PHUNG SOGS KYI CHOS THAMS CAD KYANG RANG RANG GI CHA SHAS DANG TSOGS PA LA BRTEN NAS BTAGS PA YIN PA'I PHYIR RANG DBANG DU
gru.wylie: de ji lta ba bzhin du khams rnams kyang rang rang gi cha shas 'dus pa la brten nas btags pa yin pa'i phyir yang dag par ma grub zhes bstan to, ,de bzhin du phung sogs kyi chos thams cad kyang rang rang gi cha shas dang tshogs pa la brten nas btags pa yin pa'i phyir rang dbang du
gru.english: GRUB PA MED CES SBYOR RO,, Just so, none of these elements themselves exist purely, for they too are simply labeled upon the parts that they include. This same reasoning can be applied to the heaps of parts that make up a person, and all other objects as well: you can say about all of them that, because they are labeled on their parts and their whole, they do not exist independently.

gru.acip: MGON PO KLU SGRUB KYIS, ,GANG DAG STONG NYID MI SHES PA, ,DE DAG THAR PA BSTEN MA YIN, ,'GRO DRUG SRID PA'I BTZON RAR NI, ,RMONGS PA DE DAG 'KHOR BAR 'GYUR, ,ZHES GSUNGS SHING,
gru.wylie: mgon po klu sgrub kyis, ,gang dag stong nyid mi shes pa, ,de dag thar pa bsten ma yin, ,'gro drug srid pa'i btson rar ni, ,rmongs pa de dag 'khor bar 'gyur, ,zhes gsungs shing
gru.english: This is supported by the words of the savior Nagarjuna: Freedom is a complete impossibility For anyone who does not understand emptiness. Those who are blind will continue to circle Here in the prison of six different births.[59]

gru.acip: GONG GI PHRO NI, BDEN PAR GRUB PA'I SEMS CAN GANG YANG MYANG 'DAS THOB PA MED PAR SEMS BSKYED DGOS PA'I RGYU MTSAN LA DE CI'I PHYIR ZHE NA, RAB 'BYOR ZHES BOS NAS GAL TE BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA' GANG SEMS CAN LA SEMS CAN DU BDEN PAR GRUB PA'I 'DU SHES 'JUG NA, BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA' DE BDAG MED RTOGS PA'I BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA' ZHES MI BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: gong gi phro ni, bden par grub pa'i sems can gang yang myang 'das thob pa med par sems bskyed dgos pa'i rgyu mtshan la de ci'i phyir zhe na, rab 'byor zhes bos nas gal te byang chub sems dpa' gang sems can la sems can du bden par grub pa'i 'du shes 'jug na, byang chub sems dpa' de bdag med rtogs pa'i byang chub sems dpa' zhes mi bya'o
gru.english: Here we return to where we left off in the root text. One may ask, "Why is it so? What reason is there for saying that we should develop a Wish for enlightenment, while still understanding that there is no truly existing being at all who ever achieves this nirvana?" Lord Buddha first calls Subhuti by name, and then explains that we could never call any particular bodhisattva a "bodhisattva who had realized the meaning of no-self-nature" if this bodhisattva were to slip into conceiving of any living being as a living being who existed truly.

gru.acip: SBYIN PA SBYIN PA LA BRTZON PA LTA BU NI JI LTAR GNAS PAR BYA ZHES PA'I DON DANG, DE'I 'KHOR GSUM LA BDEN PAR MI ZHEN PA NI JI LTAR BSGRUB PAR BYA ZHES PA'I DON DANG, BDEN MED DU RTOGS PA'I BLO LA SEMS RTZE GCIG TU BYED PA NI SEMS RAB TU GZUNG BAR BYA ZHES PA'I DON DU BSHAD DE, PHAR PHYIN GZHAN LA'ANG SBYAR BAR BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: sbyin pa sbyin pa la brtson pa lta bu ni ji ltar gnas par bya zhes pa'i don dang, de'i 'khor gsum la bden par mi zhen pa ni ji ltar bsgrub par bya zhes pa'i don dang, bden med du rtogs pa'i blo la sems rtse gcig tu byed pa ni sems rab tu gzung bar bya zhes pa'i don du bshad de, phar phyin gzhan la'ang sbyar bar bya'o
gru.english: There are a number of expressions here. One is that "We should stay in our giving just as those who are striving in their giving." Another is "We should try to practice in a way where we have no belief that the three spheres of this act are real." And they are both to be explained as meaning "Maintain, perfectly, a state of mind where you are single-pointedly absorbed in the understanding that nothing is true."

gru.acip: RAB 'BYOR CHOS THAMS CAD THA SNYAD BTAGS PA TZAM DU YOD PA MA GTOGS, RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA RDUL TZAM YANG MED PA'I PHYIR RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAR 'DZIN PA NI PHYIN CI LOG TU ZHEN PA YIN PAS,
gru.wylie: rab 'byor chos thams cad tha snyad btags pa tsam du yod pa ma gtogs, rang bzhin gyis grub pa rdul tsam yang med pa'i phyir rang bzhin gyis grub par 'dzin pa ni phyin ci log tu zhen pa yin pas
gru.english: And what Lord Buddha is saying then is: "O Subhuti, every single object in the universe exists only through our projections; they have not a single atom of any other kind of existence—any natural existence. As such, anyone who holds that things could exist through any nature of their own is entertaining a belief which is completely mistaken.

gru.acip: CI NAS KYANG RANG BZHIN KYIS GRUB PAR ZHEN PA'I MTSAN MAR 'DZIN PA'I 'DU SHES LA BYANG CHUB SEMS DPAS GNAS PAR MI BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: ci nas kyang rang bzhin kyis grub par zhen pa'i mtshan mar 'dzin pa'i 'du shes la byang chub sems dpas gnas par mi bya'o
gru.english: "And bodhisattvas never stay in any kind of conception where they hold to the signs of things: where they believe in any way at all that things could exist through any nature of their own."

gru.acip: BDEN 'DZIN GYIS BCINGS PA'I SBYIN SOGS LAS BSOD NAMS CHEN PO 'BYUNG MOD, BDEN 'DZIN GYIS BCINGS PA DANG BRAL BA'I SGO NAS SBYIN SOGS BSGRUB PA NA BSOD NAMS LHAG PAR CHE BAR NGES ZHES STON PA NI, DE CI'I PHYIR ZHE NA, RAB 'BYOR BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA' GANG MI GNAS PAR SBYIN PA SBYIN PA DE'I BSOD NAMS KYI PHUNG PO CHE BA'I MTHA' TSAD NI GZHAN GYIS GZUNG BAR SLA
gru.wylie: bden 'dzin gyis bcings pa'i sbyin sogs las bsod nams chen po 'byung mod, bden 'dzin gyis bcings pa dang bral ba'i sgo nas sbyin sogs bsgrub pa na bsod nams lhag par che bar nges zhes ston pa ni, de ci'i phyir zhe na, rab 'byor byang chub sems dpa' gang mi gnas par sbyin pa sbyin pa de'i bsod nams kyi phung po che ba'i mtha' tshad ni gzhan gyis gzung bar sla
gru.english: BA MIN TE DKA' BA'I PHYIR RO,,One would have to admit that a person locked in the chains of grasping to some true existence can collect a great amount of merit through acts of giving and the like. But suppose a person is able to practice giving and the rest after he has freed himself from these same chains. Their merit then is certain to be ever much greater. And it is to emphasize this point that the Buddha says, Why is it so? Think, o Subhuti, of the mountains of merit collected by any bodhisattva who performs the act of giving without staying. This merit is not something whose limit you could easily ever measure; in fact, it would be quite difficult to measure.

gru.acip: SBYIN SOGS BSOD NAMS KYI TSOGS LAS SANGS RGYAS KYI GZUGS SKU 'GRUB PAR 'GYUR ZHING, GZUGS KYI SKU NI MTSAN DPES BRGYAN PA'O, ,RAB 'BYOR 'DI JI SNYAM DU SEMS ZHES PA NI, RAB 'BYOR KHYOD KYIS DON 'DI LA JI LTAR YIN SNYAM DU SEMS PA STE BSAM,
gru.wylie: sbyin sogs bsod nams kyi tshogs las sangs rgyas kyi gzugs sku 'grub par 'gyur zhing, gzugs kyi sku ni mtshan dpes brgyan pa'o, ,rab 'byor 'di ji snyam du sems zhes pa ni, rab 'byor khyod kyis don 'di la ji ltar yin snyam du sems pa ste bsam
gru.english: The merit of acts such as giving and the rest bring us the physical body of a Buddha, and this physical body is adorned with various major signs and minor marks. The words "Now Subhuti, what do you think?" mean "Subhuti, turn your mind to this subject, and think about how it could be—contemplate upon it."

gru.acip: 'O NA MI BRDZUN PA GANG ZHE NA, JI TZAM DU MTSAN DPE PHUN SUM TSOGS PA RNAMS BDEN BAR MED PA DE TZAM NI MI BRDZUN ZHING BDEN TE, DE LTAR DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA LA BDEN PAR GRUB PA'I MTSAN DANG MTSAN MA MED PAR BLTA BAR BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: 'o na mi brdzun pa gang zhe na, ji tsam du mtshan dpe phun sum tshogs pa rnams bden bar med pa de tsam ni mi brdzun zhing bden te, de ltar de bzhin gshegs pa la bden par grub pa'i mtshan dang mtshan ma med par blta bar bya'o
gru.english: "Well then what," you may ask, "is meant by the following words: 'the signs are not deceptive'?" The totally exquisite signs and marks on a Buddha's body are also not deceptive, and are true, but only insofar as they do not exist truly. And so you should see the One Thus Gone as having no signs, no signs to indicate his nature, at all.

gru.acip: BDEN GRUB KYI MTSAN DANG MTSAN MA MED PAR BSTAN PAS SGRO 'DOGS KYI MTHA' SEL BA'I PHYIR RO, ,DE'I SNGA MAS GZUGS SKU DANG PHYI MAS CHOS KYI SKU BSTAN TE NGO BO NYID SKU GTZO CHE'O,,
gru.wylie: bden grub kyi mtshan dang mtshan ma med par bstan pas sgro 'dogs kyi mtha' sel ba'i phyir ro, ,de'i snga mas gzugs sku dang phyi mas chos kyi sku bstan te ngo bo nyid sku gtso che'o
gru.english: The text though also states that there exist no signs, and no signs that would indicate any nature, which also exist truly. This fact keeps us from the extreme of asserting the existence of something which actually does not exist. The former of these two is referring to the physical body of a Buddha. The latter is referring to the reality body, and chiefly to the essence body. Bodhisattvas of the last 500 years [K25b]

gru.acip: MI 'GAL BA'I TSUL NI 'GA' ZHIG 'BRAS BU DANG SGRUB PA'I DUS DANG 'GA' ZHIG NI LUNG GI DUS LA DGONGS SHING, LA LA NI 'PHAGS YUL GYI DBANG DU MDZAD PAR MNGON NO,,
gru.wylie: mi 'gal ba'i tshul ni 'ga' zhig 'bras bu dang sgrub pa'i dus dang 'ga' zhig ni lung gi dus la dgongs shing, la la ni 'phags yul gyi dbang du mdzad par mngon no
gru.english: The reason for their lack of contradiction is that some of these works are meant to refer to the length of time that people will still be achieving goals, or still be practicing. Still others refer to the length of time that the physical records of these teachings remain in our world. Some, finally, appear to be referring to the Land of the Realized.[69]

gru.acip: RGYU MTSAN DE BAS NA DE BZHIN GSHEGS PAS TSUL DE LA DGONGS NAS LUNG GI CHOS KYI RNAM GRANGS 'DI GRU GZINGS LTA BU STE GRU GZING NI CHU'I PHA ROL TU PHYIN PA NA MI DGOS PAR SHES PA LTA BU MTHAR PHYIN PA'I 'PHAGS PA RNAMS KYIS NI, 'BRAS BU THOB BYED KYI THABS LUNG GI TSOGS LTA BU'I CHOS RNAMS KYANG 'BRAS BU THOB PA'I TSE 'DOR ZHING SPANG BAR BYA NA, DAM PA'I CHOS MA YIN PA RNAMS 'DOR BA GZHIR BCAS TE LTA CI SMOS SO
gru.wylie: rgyu mtshan de bas na de bzhin gshegs pas tshul de la dgongs nas lung gi chos kyi rnam grangs 'di gru gzings lta bu ste gru gzing ni chu'i pha rol tu phyin pa na mi dgos par shes pa lta bu mthar phyin pa'i 'phags pa rnams kyis ni, 'bras bu thob byed kyi thabs lung gi tshogs lta bu'i chos rnams kyang 'bras bu thob pa'i tshe 'dor zhing spang bar bya na, dam pa'i chos ma yin pa rnams 'dor ba gzhir bcas te lta ci smos so
gru.english: ZHES GSUNGS SO,,This then is why—this then is what the One Thus Gone meant when he said that—this presentation of the Dharma is like a ship. We understand that, once we have crossed over a body of water in a ship to the far shore, then we no longer have any need of the ship itself. Realized beings who have reached the final goal are the same. Once they reach this goal, then they abandon or leave behind even these teachings of the Dharma—even those collections of physical Dharma which are the means for us to reach the goal. What need then is there to mention—given then what we just said, the sutra is saying—what these beings do with that which is not the Dharma?

whole_word_matches.context: shul de la dgongs nas lung gi chos kyi rnam grangs 'di gru gzings lta bu ste gru gzing ni chu'i pha rol tu phyin
lung gi chos kyi rnam grangs 'di gru gzings lta bu ste gru gzing ni chu'i pha rol tu phyin pa na mi dgos par shes

gru.acip: DE NI 'BRAS BU THOB PA'I TSE DGOS PA GRUB ZIN PAS LUNG DE LTA BU RANG DON DU DGOS PA MED PA DANG, DE LA RAG MA LAS PA'I DON NO,,
gru.wylie: de ni 'bras bu thob pa'i tshe dgos pa grub zin pas lung de lta bu rang don du dgos pa med pa dang, de la rag ma las pa'i don no
gru.english: The point here is that—once we have achieved the goal—then the purpose for physical Dharma like this has already been accomplished; and it is no longer of any need, at least, for reaching one's own goals: one will no longer need to depend upon it. The emptiness of the Dharma

gru.acip: MGON PO KLU SGRUB KYIS RTZA BA SHES RAB KYI RAB BYED NYER GNYIS PA LAS,
gru.wylie: mgon po klu sgrub kyis rtsa ba shes rab kyi rab byed nyer gnyis pa las
gru.english: It's just the way that our savior, Nagarjuna, has described it in the 22^(nd) chapter of his Root Text on Wisdom—

gru.acip: LAN DU RAB 'BYOR GYIS BSOD NAMS KYI PHUNG PO MANG BAR ZHUS SHING BSOD NAMS KYI PHUNG PO DE YANG RMI LAM DANG SGYU MA LTA BUR THA SNYAD TZAM DU YOD PAR 'JOG LAGS KYI, BSOD NAMS KYI PHUNG PO DE NYID DON DAM PAR PHUNG POR GRUB PA MA MCHIS SHING, THA SNYAD DU DE BZHIN GSHEGS PAS DE LA BSOD NAMS KYI PHUNG PO, ,BSOD NAMS KYI PHUNG PO ZHES THA SNYAD MDZAD CING
gru.wylie: lan du rab 'byor gyis bsod nams kyi phung po mang bar zhus shing bsod nams kyi phung po de yang rmi lam dang sgyu ma lta bur tha snyad tsam du yod par 'jog lags kyi, bsod nams kyi phung po de nyid don dam par phung por grub pa ma mchis shing, tha snyad du de bzhin gshegs pas de la bsod nams kyi phung po, ,bsod nams kyi phung po zhes tha snyad mdzad cing
gru.english: GSUNGS SO ZHES GSOL, In response, Subhuti replies: It would be many great mountains of merit—and these same great mountains of merit are mountains of merit that we could establish as existing only in name, only in the way that a dream or an illusion exists: these same great mountains of merit though could never exist as mountains that existed ultimately. The Ones Thus Gone as well speak in a nominal sense of "great mountains of merit, great mountains of merit"—applying the name to them.

gru.acip: JI SRID GZHI GANG LA BDEN PAR GRUB BAM MA GRUB SNYAM DU SPYOD PA ZHUGS PA NA BDEN ZHEN LAS 'DA' MI NUS PA'I BAR DE SRID DU BDEN 'DZIN GYI ZHEN YUL SUN 'BYIN MI NUS PAS BDEN 'DZIN GYIS BCINGS PAR 'JOG GO ,
gru.wylie: ji srid gzhi gang la bden par grub bam ma grub snyam du spyod pa zhugs pa na bden zhen las 'da' mi nus pa'i bar de srid du bden 'dzin gyi zhen yul sun 'byin mi nus pas bden 'dzin gyis bcings par 'jog go
gru.english: As long as a person is still relating to any particular thing with uncertainty in their mind as to whether it exists in truth or not—so long as they are still unable to transcend their belief in things as real—then they remain unable to debunk the existence of the object that our tendency to see things as real thinks is there. And on this basis then we would say they are still chained by the fetters of holding that things are real.

gru.acip: DON DAM PAR GNAS BYA DANG GNAS BYED DANG GNAS PA PO GANG YANG MA GRUB PA'I PHYIR RO ZHES BSHAD DE,
gru.wylie: don dam par gnas bya dang gnas byed dang gnas pa po gang yang ma grub pa'i phyir ro zhes bshad de
gru.english: This is because, ultimately speaking, there does not even exist any place to stay, no thing to make one stay there, nor even anyone who stays there.

gru.acip: MI SKYE BA'I CHOS LA BZOD PA THOB PAS CHOS THAMS CAD BDEN MED DU MNGON SUM DU GZIGS SHING GANG LUNG BSTAN PA DANG THOB PAR BYA BA DANG 'TSANG RGYA BAR 'GYUR BA THAMS CAD KYANG RANG BZHIN GYIS STONG PAR GZIGS PAS, MAR ME MDZAD LAS BDEN GRUB KYI CHOS GANG YANG BLANGS SNYAM DU ZHEN PA MED DO,,
gru.wylie: mi skye ba'i chos la bzod pa thob pas chos thams cad bden med du mngon sum du gzigs shing gang lung bstan pa dang thob par bya ba dang 'tshang rgya bar 'gyur ba thams cad kyang rang bzhin gyis stong par gzigs pas, mar me mdzad las bden grub kyi chos gang yang blangs snyam du zhen pa med do
gru.english: When one reaches the stage of the great mastery of things that never grow, one directly perceives that no object at all has any true existence. One perceives that what was predicted to finally happen, and the thing one is to achieve, and becoming enlightened—all of them—are empty of any natural existence. As such the Buddha had no belief that he was taking up any truly existing Dharma at all from the Buddha, Light Maker.

gru.acip: DE LTA BU LA DGONGS NAS, MA DROS PAS ZHUS PA'I MDO LAS, ,GANG ZHIG RKYEN LAS SKYES PA DE MA SKYES, ,DE LA SKYE BA'I RANG BZHIN YOD MA YIN, ,RKYEN LA RAG LAS GANG DE STONG PAR BSHAD, ,GANG ZHIG STONG NYID SHES DE BAG YOD YIN, ,ZHES GSUNGS SHING, SNGAR BSHAD PA'I BDEN MED SGRUB PA'I RIGS PA RNAMS KYANG 'DIR YANG SBYAR RO,,
gru.wylie: de lta bu la dgongs nas, ma dros pas zhus pa'i mdo las, ,gang zhig rkyen las skyes pa de ma skyes, ,de la skye ba'i rang bzhin yod ma yin, ,rkyen la rag las gang de stong par bshad, ,gang zhig stong nyid shes de bag yod yin, ,zhes gsungs shing, sngar bshad pa'i bden med sgrub pa'i rigs pa rnams kyang 'dir yang sbyar ro
gru.english: This is exactly the idea expressed in the Sutra Requested by Anavatapta, where it says: Nothing which is born from conditions Is ever born at all; It has no nature of being born. Anything that depends on conditions Is said to be empty; Those who understand emptiness Truly have awareness.[91] You can also apply at this point all the reasonings presented earlier for demonstrating how things have no true existence.

gru.acip: BCOM LDAN 'DAS KYIS BKA' STZAL PA, RAB 'BYOR, BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA' GANG LA LA ZHIG 'DI SKAD DU, BDAG GIS ZHING BKOD PA RNAMS BSGRUB PAR BYA'O, ,ZHES ZER NA, DE NI, MI BDEN PAR SMRA BA'O,,
gru.wylie: bcom ldan 'das kyis bka' stsal pa, rab 'byor, byang chub sems dpa' gang la la zhig 'di skad du, bdag gis zhing bkod pa rnams bsgrub par bya'o, ,zhes zer na, de ni, mi bden par smra ba'o
gru.english: Then the Conqueror spoke once more, Suppose, o Subhuti, that some bodhisattva were to say, "I am working to bring about my paradise." This would not be spoken true.

gru.acip: DE LTAR 'TSANG RGYA BA LA GANG DU 'TSANG RGYA BA'I ZHING DAG BSGRUB DGOS PAR STON PA NI, BCOM LDAN 'DAS KYIS RAB 'BYOR LA BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA' GANG LA LA ZHIG BDAG GIS ZHING BKOD PA RNAMS BDEN ZHEN GYIS DON DAM PAR BSGRUB BAR BYA'O SNYAM ZHES ZER NA, TSIG DE NI MI BDEN PAR SMRA BA'O,,
gru.wylie: de ltar 'tshang rgya ba la gang du 'tshang rgya ba'i zhing dag bsgrub dgos par ston pa ni, bcom ldan 'das kyis rab 'byor la byang chub sems dpa' gang la la zhig bdag gis zhing bkod pa rnams bden zhen gyis don dam par bsgrub bar bya'o snyam zhes zer na, tshig de ni mi bden par smra ba'o
gru.english: Lord Buddha wishes to indicate that, in order for a person to reach the enlightenment described above, he or she must first bring about a paradise in which to achieve the enlightenment. Therefore the Conqueror says to Subhuti, Suppose some bodhisattva were to say or think to themselves—while holding a belief in true existence, and referring to ultimate existence—"I am working to bring about paradises." This statement would not be spoken true.

gru.acip: DE LTA BAS NA BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA' ZHING GI BKOD PA BSGRUB PAR BYA BA NA 'DI LTAR BDEN ZHEN GYIS MI GNAS PAR SEMS BSKYED PAR BYA'O, ,DON DAM PAR CI LA YANG MI GNAS SHING GZUGS SGRA SOGS KYI CHOS GANG LA BDEN ZHEN GYIS
gru.wylie: de lta bas na byang chub sems dpa' zhing gi bkod pa bsgrub par bya ba na 'di ltar bden zhen gyis mi gnas par sems bskyed par bya'o, ,don dam par ci la yang mi gnas shing gzugs sgra sogs kyi chos gang la bden zhen gyis
gru.english: MI GNAS PAR SEMS BSKYED PAR BYA'O,,Since this is so, says Lord Buddha, those bodhisattvas who are working to bring about their paradise should develop their Wish for enlightenment without staying in any such state where they hold a belief in some true existence. They should develop their Wish without staying in any state where they believe in the ultimate existence of anything at all. They should develop their Wish without staying in any state where they hold a belief in some true existence of any object at all: in anything you can see, or in sounds, or in any of the rest. The emptiness of my body

gru.acip: PHYI'I ZHING GI BKOD PA LTA BUR MA ZAD, BCUD KYI GANG ZAG GI LUS KYI BKOD PA YANG RKYEN TSOGS PA TZAM LAS DON DAM PAR GRUB PA MED DO ZHES STON PA NI, ,RAB 'BYOR DPER NA SKYES BU ZHIG LUS RI'I RGYAL PO RI RAB TZAM DU GYUR NA LUS DE CHE BA YIN SNYAM MAM ZHES DRIS PA NA,,
gru.wylie: phyi'i zhing gi bkod pa lta bur ma zad, bcud kyi gang zag gi lus kyi bkod pa yang rkyen tshogs pa tsam las don dam par grub pa med do zhes ston pa ni, ,rab 'byor dper na skyes bu zhig lus ri'i rgyal po ri rab tsam du gyur na lus de che ba yin snyam mam zhes dris pa na
gru.english: Lord Buddha wishes to show that the above applies not only to outer things such as paradises, but also to the beings who inhabit this world: to objects such as the body of a person. He wishes to show that they too exist only because conditions have come together, and not in an ultimate way. Therefore he asks Subhuti, "Suppose someone's body were to grow as large as the king of all mountains, Mt. Sumeru. What do you think? Would that person's body

gru.acip: LAN DU LUS DE CHE BAR ZHUS SHING, LUS DE NYID CHA DU MA TSOGS PA'I PHUNG PO THA SNYAD TZAM DU YOD KYI, CHA LA MA BLTOS PA'I DNGOS PO STE NGO BOR MED PAR DE BZHIN GSHEGS PAS GSUNGS TE, 'JIG RTEN GYI THA SNYAD DU LUS DE LA CHE'O ZHES BYA'O, ,DES NA DON DAM PAR LUS SU GRUB PA MA MCHIS PA'I KUN RDZOB PA'I LUS DE LA LUS ZHES BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: lan du lus de che bar zhus shing, lus de nyid cha du ma tshogs pa'i phung po tha snyad tsam du yod kyi, cha la ma bltos pa'i dngos po ste ngo bor med par de bzhin gshegs pas gsungs te, 'jig rten gyi tha snyad du lus de la che'o zhes bya'o, ,des na don dam par lus su grub pa ma mchis pa'i kun rdzob pa'i lus de la lus zhes bya'o
gru.english: And Subhuti respectfully replies, "Such a body would be large." Those Who Have Gone Thus though have stated that this same body exists only as a term applied to the heaps, to some collection of a great many parts. It could never be a thing at all which existed in essence; that is, it could never be something which did not depend on its parts, say they. And this is precisely why we can call such a body "large," in the sense that words are used in the everyday world. And so what we call "the body" is the body which exists in a deceptive sense: one that could never exist as a body in any ultimate sense.

gru.acip: DE BZHIN GSHEGS PAS SHES RAB KYI PHA ROL TU PHYIN PA ZHES GANG GSUNGS PA DE NYID DON DAM PAR PHA ROL TU PHYIN PAR GRUB PA MED CING, DES NA THA SNYAD DU SHES RAB KYI PHA ROL TU PHYIN PA ZHES 'DOGS SO,,
gru.wylie: de bzhin gshegs pas shes rab kyi pha rol tu phyin pa zhes gang gsungs pa de nyid don dam par pha rol tu phyin par grub pa med cing, des na tha snyad du shes rab kyi pha rol tu phyin pa zhes 'dogs so
gru.english: That same perfection of wisdom spoken by the Ones Thus Gone to be the "perfection of wisdom" is a perfection of wisdom that doesn't even exist as a perfection of wisdom in an ultimate sense. And this is precisely why we can, in a nominal sense, label it the "perfection of wisdom."

gru.acip: DE NAS YANG DE RDUL PHRA RAB DANG RDUL PHRA RAB BSAGS PA'I 'JIG RTEN GYI KHAMS DON DAM PAR MA GRUB ZHES STON PA NI, BCOM LDAN 'DAS KYIS RAB 'BYOR LA STONG GSUM 'JIG RTEN GYI KHAMS NA SA'I RDUL JI SNYED YOD PA DE MANG NGAM ZHES DRIS PAR,
gru.wylie: de nas yang de rdul phra rab dang rdul phra rab bsags pa'i 'jig rten gyi khams don dam par ma grub zhes ston pa ni, bcom ldan 'das kyis rab 'byor la stong gsum 'jig rten gyi khams na sa'i rdul ji snyed yod pa de mang ngam zhes dris par
gru.english: Now further Lord Buddha wishes to show us how neither atoms nor the very planets which are composed of these atoms can exist in an ultimate way. First the Conqueror asks Subhuti whether the total number of atoms of dust in all the planets within the great world system—a system with a thousand of a thousand of a thousand planets—would be a great many atoms of dust. The emptiness of atoms Subhūtir āha. Bahu Bhagavan bahu Sugata pṛthivī rajo bhavet.

gru.acip: LAN DU DE MANG NGO ZHES ZHUS SHING, SA'I RDUL PHRA RAB GANG YIN PA DE RNAMS NI DON DAM PAR RDUL DU GRUB PA MA MCHIS PAR DE BZHIN GSHEGS PAS GSUNGS TE, DON DAM PAR MED CING THA SNYAD DU YOD PA DES NA SA'I RDUL ZHES BGYI'O,,
gru.wylie: lan du de mang ngo zhes zhus shing, sa'i rdul phra rab gang yin pa de rnams ni don dam par rdul du grub pa ma mchis par de bzhin gshegs pas gsungs te, don dam par med cing tha snyad du yod pa des na sa'i rdul zhes bgyi'o
gru.english: And then Subhuti respectfully replies, "It would indeed be a great many." He goes on to say that the Ones Gone Thus have stated that these same atoms of dust could never exist as atoms, in an ultimate sense. And it is precisely because these atoms do not exist ultimately—but do exist nominally—that we can even speak of them as "atoms of dust."

gru.acip: DES NA RDUL PHRA RAB BSAGS PA'I 'JIG RTEN GYI KHAMS GANG YIN PA DE YANG DON DAM PAR 'JIG RTEN GYI KHAMS SU GRUB PA MA MCHIS PAR DE BZHIN GSHEGS PAS GSUNGS PA'I SLAD DU STE, DES NA THA SNYAD DU 'JIG RTEN GYI KHAMS ZHES BGYI'O,,
gru.wylie: des na rdul phra rab bsags pa'i 'jig rten gyi khams gang yin pa de yang don dam par 'jig rten gyi khams su grub pa ma mchis par de bzhin gshegs pas gsungs pa'i slad du ste, des na tha snyad du 'jig rten gyi khams zhes bgyi'o
gru.english: This in turn explains why whatever planets there may be which are composed of conglomerations of these particles of dust could never themselves exist as planets, in an ultimate sense. The Ones Gone Thus have said this of them; and this is precisely why—this is the reason that—they are in a nominal sense spoken of as "planets."

gru.acip: DE DAG DON DAM PAR GRUB PA MED PA'I RIGS PA PHYOGS TZAM NI, RDUL PHRA RAB BSAGS PA'I 'JIG RTEN GYI KHAMS RNAMS KYANG RDUL PHRA RAB 'DUS PA'I STENG DU BTAGS PA TZAM YIN GYI, RDUL PHRA RAB RE RE BA DANG TSOGS PA DANG DE LAS DON GZHAN NA 'JIG RTEN GYI KHAMS ZHES PA ZHIG LOGS SU MED DE, DPER NA BUM PA'I MCHU ZHABS LTO BA SOGS TSOGS PA LA BUM PAR BTAGS PA BZHIN NO,,
gru.wylie: de dag don dam par grub pa med pa'i rigs pa phyogs tsam ni, rdul phra rab bsags pa'i 'jig rten gyi khams rnams kyang rdul phra rab 'dus pa'i steng du btags pa tsam yin gyi, rdul phra rab re re ba dang tshogs pa dang de las don gzhan na 'jig rten gyi khams zhes pa zhig logs su med de, dper na bum pa'i mchu zhabs lto ba sogs tshogs pa la bum par btags pa bzhin no
gru.english: We might pause here and give just a partial presentation of the logic which is used to prove that these planets do not in fact exist in an ultimate sense. Planets composed of conglomerations of atoms are nothing more than a projection applied to these atoms. And there is in fact no other, separate thing called a "planet" which is either any of the atoms considered individually; nor the sum of these atoms alone; nor something unrelated to these two. It's similar to the idea that a "vase" is no more than an object projected onto the sum of its parts—things like the lip of the vase, its base, and its belly.

gru.acip: DES NA RDUL PHRA RAB GCIG NI YAN GAR DU GNAS MI NUS PAS GZHAN DANG TSOGS SHING 'DUS PA LA LTOS DGOS PAS RDUL PHRA RAB RANG DBANG GIS MA GRUB CING, DE MA GRUB PAS DE BSAGS PA'I RDUL RAGS PA'ANG RANG DBANG GIS MA GRUB CES BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: des na rdul phra rab gcig ni yan gar du gnas mi nus pas gzhan dang tshogs shing 'dus pa la ltos dgos pas rdul phra rab rang dbang gis ma grub cing, de ma grub pas de bsags pa'i rdul rags pa'ang rang dbang gis ma grub ces bya'o
gru.english: Neither then could a single atom ever exist independently: it would have then to exist only in conjunction with, as a composite part of, other pieces of matter. In such case, no single atom would possess any independent existence; and then neither could any more gross physical object which was composed of such atoms.

gru.acip: MDOR NA RDUL PHRA RAB NI GCIG GI RANG BZHIN DU BDEN PAR MED CING, 'JIG RTEN GYI KHAMS NI DU MA TSOGS PA'I RANG BZHIN DU BDEN PAR MA GRUB CES STONG NYID BSGOM PAR BSHAD PA'O,,
gru.wylie: mdor na rdul phra rab ni gcig gi rang bzhin du bden par med cing, 'jig rten gyi khams ni du ma tshogs pa'i rang bzhin du bden par ma grub ces stong nyid bsgom par bshad pa'o
gru.english: To put it in a nutshell, the fact is that no atom can have any nature, any true nature, of being one thing. Neither can any planet have a nature, any true nature, of being composed of a conglomerate of many such atoms. This is the meditation on emptiness that we are being asked to do.

gru.acip: DE NAS 'JIG RTEN GYI KHAMS SU MA ZAD, SANGS RGYAS KYI GZUGS SKU DANG DE'I MTSAN DPE YANG DON DAM PAR MA GRUB CES PA NI, Lord Buddha next
gru.wylie: de nas 'jig rten gyi khams su ma zad, sangs rgyas kyi gzugs sku dang de'i mtshan dpe yang don dam par ma grub ces pa ni, lorD buDDha NexT
gru.english: wants to express to us how not only are the various worlds something that cannot exist in an ultimate way, but this is true as well of the body of form of a Buddha, and the signs and marks upon this body.

gru.acip: SKABS 'DIR BDEN 'DZIN NI MA RIG PAR 'DOD DGOS PAS, MA RIG PAS KUN NAS BSLANGS TE DGE BA'I LAS BSAGS NA 'KHOR BAS BSDUS PA'I MNGON MTHO DANG, MI DGE BA'I LAS BSAGS NA NI NGAN 'GRO'I LUS 'GRUB PAS GZHUNG DU MA LAS BSHAD DO,,
gru.wylie: skabs 'dir bden 'dzin ni ma rig par 'dod dgos pas, ma rig pas kun nas bslangs te dge ba'i las bsags na 'khor bas bsdus pa'i mngon mtho dang, mi dge ba'i las bsags na ni ngan 'gro'i lus 'grub pas gzhung du ma las bshad do
gru.english: We'd have to say that, in the context we have here, the belief in reality mentioned refers to a kind of ignorance. And there are many major scriptures which state that—if we collect good karma, but we are motivated to do so by ignorance—then all we achieve is a higher rebirth, still within the cycle of pain. If—motivated by the same ignorance—we collect bad karma, then all we achieve is the body of one living in the lower realms.[284]

gru.acip: TSUL 'DI NGO MTSAR CHE STE, MGON PO KLU SGRUB ZHABS KYIS, ,CHOS RNAMS STONG PA 'DI SHES NAS, ,LAS DANG 'BRAS BU BSTAN PA GANG, ,NGO MTSAR BAS KYANG 'DI NGO MTSAR, ,RMAD BYUNG BAS KYANG 'DI RMAD BYUNG, ,ZHES GSUNGS PA LTAR RO,,
gru.wylie: tshul 'di ngo mtshar che ste, mgon po klu sgrub zhabs kyis, ,chos rnams stong pa 'di shes nas, ,las dang 'bras bu bstan pa gang, ,ngo mtshar bas kyang 'di ngo mtshar, ,rmad byung bas kyang 'di rmad byung, ,zhes gsungs pa ltar ro
gru.english: And indeed this is a wondrous thing, for as our Protector, Nagarjuna, also puts it— When I think of someone Who comprehends that things Are empty, and who Goes on to teach about Action and consequence, Then truly I feel It is more wondrous than wondrous More miraculous than miraculous.[101]

gru.acip: GZHUNG 'DI DAG GIS NI JI LTAR GNAS PA DANG BSGRUBS PA DANG GZUNG BAR BYA BA'I TSUL BSTAN TO,,
gru.wylie: gzhung 'di dag gis ni ji ltar gnas pa dang bsgrubs pa dang gzung bar bya ba'i tshul bstan to
gru.english: All the sections of the sutra up to this point have described then the answer to the question of how we are to live; how we are to practice; and how we are to keep our thoughts.

gru.acip: RGYU MTSAN NI DE LTA BU'I BDAG TU 'DU SHES PA SOGS NI ZHEN YUL LA PHYIN CI LOG TU ZHUGS PA YIN PAS, DE NYID YANG DAG PA'I 'DU SHES THAMS CAD DANG BRAL BA'I PHYIR RAM, 'DU SHES DAG DON DAM PAR 'DU SHES SU GRUB PA DANG BRAL BA'I PHYIR ZHES PA'O ZHUS PA NA,
gru.wylie: rgyu mtshan ni de lta bu'i bdag tu 'du shes pa sogs ni zhen yul la phyin ci log tu zhugs pa yin pas, de nyid yang dag pa'i 'du shes thams cad dang bral ba'i phyir ram, 'du shes dag don dam par 'du shes su grub pa dang bral ba'i phyir zhes pa'o zhus pa na
gru.english: The reason for this is that conceiving of oneself as oneself and so on in the way described is to be completely mistaken about the object that one thinks one sees. And someone like this then would have lost every correct way of thinking. You could also say that they would lose any correct way of thinking—be free of every kind of this conception—if all these ways of thinking were thought to exist as thinking in some ultimate way.[103] Beyond all fear

gru.acip: BDEN PAR GRUB NA BSGYUR DU MI RUNG BAS LAS 'BRAS LA SOGS PA'I BYA BYED THAMS CAD BZHAG TU MI RUNG ZHING MI 'THAD LA, BDEN PAR MED PA'AM RANG BZHIN GYIS MA GRUB PA LA BYA BYED THAMS CAD DANG MYANG 'DAS SOGS
gru.wylie: bden par grub na bsgyur du mi rung bas las 'bras la sogs pa'i bya byed thams cad bzhag tu mi rung zhing mi 'thad la, bden par med pa'am rang bzhin gyis ma grub pa la bya byed thams cad dang myang 'das sogs
gru.english: If things did exist in a true way, then it would be improper to say that they ever changed. And then it would be improper, it would never be right, to describe all the workings of things like karma and its consequences. The way in which all things work, and nirvana itself, and everything else are all quite proper. And none of these objects has any true existence, none of them has any nature of their own.

gru.acip: NGO MTSAR CHE BA'I RGYU MTSAN NI, CHOS KUN RANG BZHIN GYIS MA GRUB PAR STON PA'I GZHUNG PHA ROL TU PHYIN PA DAM PA MCHOG 'DI NI DA LTA DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA NGAS GSUNGS TE, SNGON SANGS RGYAS BCOM LDAN 'DAS DPAG TU MED PA RNAMS KYIS GSUNGS PA'I PHYIR RO,,
gru.wylie: ngo mtshar che ba'i rgyu mtshan ni, chos kun rang bzhin gyis ma grub par ston pa'i gzhung pha rol tu phyin pa dam pa mchog 'di ni da lta de bzhin gshegs pa ngas gsungs te, sngon sangs rgyas bcom ldan 'das dpag tu med pa rnams kyis gsungs pa'i phyir ro
gru.english: Here is the reason why it will be so wondrous. The holy, or highest, perfection—a work which teaches how no object exists through any nature of its own—is now being spoken to you by myself, by the One Thus Gone. And this is the same perfection which has been spoken in the past by Conquering Buddhas who are beyond any number to count.

gru.acip: RGYU MTSAN NI GZUGS SGRA SOGS LA ZHEN CING GNAS PA'I YUL GZUGS SOGS GANG YIN PA DE NYID DON DAM PAR MI GNAS PA STE MA GRUB PA'I PHYIR RO ZHES
gru.wylie: rgyu mtshan ni gzugs sgra sogs la zhen cing gnas pa'i yul gzugs sogs gang yin pa de nyid don dam par mi gnas pa ste ma grub pa'i phyir ro zhes
gru.english: SO,,The Teacher then concludes by saying, And for what reason is it so? Because none of these things to see or sounds or the rest—none of these very things to see that we believe in, or stay in—ever stay in any ultimate way themselves, never exist in any ultimate way themselves.

gru.acip: RAB 'BYOR DE BZHIN GSHEGS PAS THOB BYA'I CHOS GANG YANG SANGS RGYAS PA'AM BSTAN PA DE RNAMS LA BDEN PA DON DAM PA'I CHOS RNAMS BDEN PAR GRUB PA YANG MED CING, RDZUN PA KUN RDZOB PA'I CHOS RNAMS KYANG BDEN PAR GRUB
gru.wylie: rab 'byor de bzhin gshegs pas thob bya'i chos gang yang sangs rgyas pa'am bstan pa de rnams la bden pa don dam pa'i chos rnams bden par grub pa yang med cing, rdzun pa kun rdzob pa'i chos rnams kyang bden par grub
gru.english: PA MED DO ZHES SO,,And I speak to you, o Subhuti, of that thing where Those Gone Thus reach some enlightenment; and of that thing which is the Dharma that They teach. These have no truth, a truth where ultimately existing things exist in reality. Neither do they have any deception, where deceptively existing things exist in reality.[340]

gru.acip: BCOM LDAN 'DAS, BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA'I THEG PA LA YANG DAG PAR ZHUGS PAS JI LTAR GNAS PAR BGYI, JI LTAR BSGRUB PAR BGYI, JI LTAR SEMS RAB TU GZUNG BAR BGYI,
gru.wylie: bcom ldan 'das, byang chub sems dpa'i theg pa la yang dag par zhugs pas ji ltar gnas par bgyi, ji ltar bsgrub par bgyi, ji ltar sems rab tu gzung bar bgyi
gru.english: O Conquering One, what of those who have entered well into the way of the bodhisattva? How shall they live? How shall they practice? How should they

gru.acip: GAL TE DE 'DRA BA'I CHOS 'GA' ZHIG YOD PAR GYUR NA NI, DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA MAR ME MDZAD KYIS NGA LA BRAM ZE'I KHYE'U KHYOD MA 'ONGS PA'I DUS 'DI TZAM NAS SANGS RGYAS SH'AKYA THUB PA ZHES BYA BAR 'GYUR RO ZHES LUNG MI STON PA ZHIG NA, MNGON PAR RDZOGS PAR SANGS RGYAS PA'I CHOS GANG YANG BDEN PAR GRUB PA MED PA'I PHYIR NA, DE'I TSE DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA MAR ME MDZAD KYIS NGA LA DE LTAR BYANG CHUB TU LUNG BSTAN TO,,If there had been
gru.wylie: gal te de 'dra ba'i chos 'ga' zhig yod par gyur na ni, de bzhin gshegs pa mar me mdzad kyis nga la bram ze'i khye'u khyod ma 'ongs pa'i dus 'di tsam nas sangs rgyas shAkya thub pa zhes bya bar 'gyur ro zhes lung mi ston pa zhig na, mngon par rdzogs par sangs rgyas pa'i chos gang yang bden par grub pa med pa'i phyir na, de'i tshe de bzhin gshegs pa mar me mdzad kyis nga la de ltar byang chub tu lung bstan to,,if There haD beeN
gru.english: any such thing, anything of the sort, then the One Gone Thus, "Maker of Light," could never have granted the Buddha his final prediction, saying "O child of Brahman family, in so and so many days to come you will become the Buddha called 'Able One of the Shakya Clan'." But the fact is that—since there's nothing about a fully enlightened Buddha which does exist in truth—then the One Thus Gone named "Maker of Light" did in fact at that time "grant this final prediction of my enlightenment to me."

gru.acip: DE YANG GANG GIS GANG ZHIG GANG DU LUNG BSTAN PA'I CHOS RNAMS NI THA SNYAD BTAGS YOD MING RKYANG TZAM YIN GYI, DON DAM PAR GRUB PA MED
gru.wylie: de yang gang gis gang zhig gang du lung bstan pa'i chos rnams ni tha snyad btags yod ming rkyang tsam yin gyi, don dam par grub pa med
gru.english: PA'I TSUL GONG DU BRJOD ZIN TO,,Now the person who makes such a prediction, and who they make the prediction about, and the prediction they make for them are things that exist only in name: only as a projection. As we've already explained above, they have no ultimate kind of existence.[405]

gru.acip: THOB BYA THOB BYED KYI CHOS LA BDEN PAR ZHEN NAS BDEN 'DZIN GYIS BCINGS PA RNAMS NI DNGOS LUNG BSTAN PA'I SNOD DU MI RUNG BA'I PHYIR TE, BDEN GRUB KYI CHOS BSGYUR DU MI NUS PAS THOB BYED SOGS GANG YANG 'JOG TU MI
gru.wylie: thob bya thob byed kyi chos la bden par zhen nas bden 'dzin gyis bcings pa rnams ni dngos lung bstan pa'i snod du mi rung ba'i phyir te, bden grub kyi chos bsgyur du mi nus pas thob byed sogs gang yang 'jog tu mi
gru.english: RUNG BAR SNGAR BSHAD ZIN PA'I PHYIR RO,,And that's because a person who was still locked in the chains of believing that these particular things were real—something to be reached, and something that helped them reach it—would be no proper vessel to receive a precise prediction. This in turn (as we've already covered) is due to the fact that any object which existed in reality could never change—which would mean that they couldn't be something that helped us reach a goal, or anything of the like. Why they have gone

gru.acip: DE BZHIN GSHEGS PAS CHOS GANG SANGS RGYAS PA'AM BSTAN PA DE LA RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA'I DON DAM PA'I CHOS BDEN PA YANG MED CING, DER GRUB PA'I KUN RDZOB PA'I CHOS BRDZUN PA YANG MED DO,,This thing where the One
gru.wylie: de bzhin gshegs pas chos gang sangs rgyas pa'am bstan pa de la rang bzhin gyis grub pa'i don dam pa'i chos bden pa yang med cing, der grub pa'i kun rdzob pa'i chos brdzun pa yang med do,,thiS ThiNg where The oNe
gru.english: Gone Thus reaches their enlightenment—here meaning an ultimate thing, a thing about this teaching that could exist through some nature of its own—could never be real. Neither though could it be false, in the sense of being some object within deceptive reality which existed with the same kind of nature.

gru.acip: DE NAS RAB 'BYOR GYIS DE LA BU'I DPE'I LUS DE DON DAM PAR LUS SU MA GRUB KYANG, THA SNYAD DU DE LTAR 'JOG GO ZHES ZHUS PA NA BCOM LDAN 'DAS KYIS
gru.wylie: de nas rab 'byor gyis de la bu'i dpe'i lus de don dam par lus su ma grub kyang, tha snyad du de ltar 'jog go zhes zhus pa na bcom ldan 'das kyis
gru.english: DE DE BZHIN NO ZHES SOGS GNANG NGO,,Subhuti then respectfully addresses the Buddha by noting, on this point, that the body in the example of the child's growth may not exist in any ultimate way, but can still be established as existing nominally. The Conqueror then concurs with this position, in the words that include "This is how it is."

gru.acip: BCOM LDAN 'DAS KYIS RAB 'BYOR LA DE MED PA'I RGYU MTSAN DE BAS NA DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA KUN BYANG GI CHOS THAMS CAD GANG ZAG GI BDAG TU GRUB PA'I SEMS CAN MED PA, SROG MED PA, GANG ZAG MED PA'O ZHES GSUNGS SO,,And
gru.wylie: bcom ldan 'das kyis rab 'byor la de med pa'i rgyu mtshan de bas na de bzhin gshegs pa kun byang gi chos thams cad gang zag gi bdag tu grub pa'i sems can med pa, srog med pa, gang zag med pa'o zhes gsungs so,,aND
gru.english: the Conqueror then says to Subhuti, "This is why—it is because no such thing could ever be—the One Thus Gone says that all existing things, whether they be part of the negative side of things or the enlightened, are such that no living being exists, and nothing that lives exists, and no person exists, who possesses some 'self' of the person."[438]

gru.acip: BSDU NA BDAG NI THOB PAR BYED PA'O, ,'DI NI THOB PAR BYA BA'I CHOS SO SNYAM DU BDEN ZHEN GYIS 'JUG NA MED PA LA YOD PAR RLOM PA MNGON PA'I NGA RGYAL CAN DU BSHAD PAS MI RUNG ZHES PA STE BDEN PAR GRUB NA BSGYUR DU MI RUNG BA'I PHYIR CHOS GANG LA'ANG THOB BYA THOB BYED SOGS BZHAG TU MI RUNG NGO ZHES GONG DU BSHAD ZIN TO,,To sum then, let's take
gru.wylie: bsdu na bdag ni thob par byed pa'o, ,'di ni thob par bya ba'i chos so snyam du bden zhen gyis 'jug na med pa la yod par rlom pa mngon pa'i nga rgyal can du bshad pas mi rung zhes pa ste bden par grub na bsgyur du mi rung ba'i phyir chos gang la'ang thob bya thob byed sogs bzhag tu mi rung ngo zhes gong du bshad zin to,,to SuM TheN, leT'S Take
gru.english: the case of someone who, with a belief that things are real, thinks to themselves that "I am going to achieve this or that," or "This is the thing that I'm going to achieve." What's being said in the text is that they would then be a person who had some extreme kind of delusion of grandeur—a delusion where they thought something existed, when in truth it didn't exist at all. This then would be "wrong," the text is saying—because if things existed in truth then it would be wrong for them ever to exhibit change. Then further it would be wrong to say about any object at all that it could either be achieved or cause us to achieve anything. This point has already been explained previously.[439]

gru.acip: 'DI DAG GIS NI JI LTAR BSGRUB PAR BYA ZHES PA'I DON BDAG MED BSGOM TSUL
gru.wylie: 'di dag gis ni ji ltar bsgrub par bya zhes pa'i don bdag med bsgom tshul
gru.english: BSTAN TO,,All of these sections have been addressing the question at the beginning of the sutra of "How should they practice?" That is, they have instructed us in how we are to meditate upon the lack of a self.[440]

gru.acip: RAB 'BYOR, BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA' GANG ZHIG 'DI SKAD DU, BDAG GIS ZHING BKOD PA RNAMS BSGRUB BO, ,ZHES ZER NA, DE YANG DE BZHIN DU BRJOD PAR BYA'O,, DE CI'I PHYIR ZHE NA, RAB 'BYOR ZHING BKOD PA RNAMS ZHING BKOD PA RNAMS ZHES BYA BA DE NI, DE DAG BKOD PA MED PAR DE BZHIN GSHEGS PAS GSUNGS PA'I PHYIR TE, DES NA ZHING BKOD PA RNAMS ZHES BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: rab 'byor, byang chub sems dpa' gang zhig 'di skad du, bdag gis zhing bkod pa rnams bsgrub bo, ,zhes zer na, de yang de bzhin du brjod par bya'o,, de ci'i phyir zhe na, rab 'byor zhing bkod pa rnams zhing bkod pa rnams zhes bya ba de ni, de dag bkod pa med par de bzhin gshegs pas gsungs pa'i phyir te, des na zhing bkod pa rnams zhes bya'o
gru.english: And suppose, o Subhuti, that some bodhisattva were to say, "I am working to bring about my paradise." That would not be spoken rightly.[123] Why is it so? Because, o Subhuti, the paradise that you are working to bring about when you say "I am working to bring about my paradise" is something that the One Thus Gone has said that you could never bring about. And this is precisely why we can even speak of these as "paradises to bring about."

gru.acip: RAB 'BYOR BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA' GANG ZHIG 'DI SNYAM DU, BDAG GIS GANG DU 'TSANG RGYA BA'I GNAS KYI ZHING GI BKOD PA PHUN SUM TSOGS PA RNAM PAR DON DAM PAR BSGRUB PAR BYA'O ZHES ZHEN CING TSIG GIS ZER NA, DE YANG DE BZHIN DU BRJOD CING ZHEN PAR BYAR MI RUNG NGO,,And suppose, o Subhuti,
gru.wylie: rab 'byor byang chub sems dpa' gang zhig 'di snyam du, bdag gis gang du 'tshang rgya ba'i gnas kyi zhing gi bkod pa phun sum tshogs pa rnam par don dam par bsgrub par bya'o zhes zhen cing tshig gis zer na, de yang de bzhin du brjod cing zhen par byar mi rung ngo,,aND SuppoSe, o subhuTi
gru.english: that some bodhisattva were to think to themselves, "I am working to bring about a perfect paradise, the place where I will become enlightened, in a way which is ultimately real." That is, suppose they were to entertain this kind of belief, and express it in their words. That too would not be spoken rightly; it would not be a right sort of belief.[443]

gru.acip: RGYU MTSAN LA ZHING GI BKOD PA DE DAG NI, KUN RDZOB TU TSOGS SHING 'DUS PA SGYU MA LTAR YOD PA LAS GZHAN BDEN PAR GRUB PA'I BKOD PA MED PAR DE BZHIN GSHEGS PAS GSUNGS PA'I PHYIR TE, DES NA THA SNYAD DU ZHING BKOD PA
gru.wylie: rgyu mtshan la zhing gi bkod pa de dag ni, kun rdzob tu tshogs shing 'dus pa sgyu ma ltar yod pa las gzhan bden par grub pa'i bkod pa med par de bzhin gshegs pas gsungs pa'i phyir te, des na tha snyad du zhing bkod pa
gru.english: RNAMS ZHES BYA'O,,Why, for what reason, would that be the case? It's because the One Thus Gone has said that there is no such creating of a paradise—of paradises that were brought about in a way which was real, rather than existing, in a deceptive way, as a collection or a gathering of other things; as something that resembled an illusion. And this is precisely why we can even speak of paradises which are brought about in a nominal way. What we call "a bodhisattva"

gru.acip: DE LTAR YIN KYANG SEMS CAN GYI SEMS KYI RGYUN NI DON DAM PAR RGYUN ZHES BYA BAR GRUB PA MED PAR NGAS BSHAD DE, DON DAM PAR MED PA DES NA THA SNYAD DU SEMS KYI RGYUN ZHES BYA BAR BRJOD DO,,"And even though that is
gru.wylie: de ltar yin kyang sems can gyi sems kyi rgyun ni don dam par rgyun zhes bya bar grub pa med par ngas bshad de, don dam par med pa des na tha snyad du sems kyi rgyun zhes bya bar brjod do,,"aND eveN Though ThaT iS
gru.english: the case," continues the Buddha, "I say that none of the mindstreams of these living beings could ever exist as a stream in any ultimate sense. And it is precisely because of this—that they cannot exist in any ultimate sense—that we can call them a "mindstream."[464]

gru.acip: DES NA TSOR BA BDEN PAR MA GRUB PAR STON PA'I RIGS PA MANG YANG RTZA BA NI, ,ZHI BA LHAS, ,GANG TSE TSOR BO 'GA' MED NA, ,TSOR BA 'GA' YANG YOD MIN TE,
gru.wylie: des na tshor ba bden par ma grub par ston pa'i rigs pa mang yang rtsa ba ni, ,zhi ba lhas, ,gang tshe tshor bo 'ga' med na, ,tshor ba 'ga' yang yod min te
gru.english: ,ZHES GSUNGS PA 'DI LTA BU YIN LA,There are then many different forms of reasoning used to demonstrate that feelings do not exist in and of themselves; the principal one though is the following. As Master Shantideva has put it, If it's the case that there isNo one at all who feels,Then neither can there beAny feeling that they feel.[128]

gru.acip: MDOR NA TSOR BA LA SOGS PA'I SHES PA KUN KYANG DMIGS PA LA BRTEN NAS MAR ME'I 'OD BZHIN DU THA SNYAD TZAM DU SKYE'I, DE LTA BU LA MA BRTEN PAR RANG DBANG GIS MI SKYE BAS RANG BZHIN GYIS MA GRUB BO,,We can summarize
gru.wylie: mdor na tshor ba la sogs pa'i shes pa kun kyang dmigs pa la brten nas mar me'i 'od bzhin du tha snyad tsam du skye'i, de lta bu la ma brten par rang dbang gis mi skye bas rang bzhin gyis ma grub bo,,we caN SuMMarize
gru.english: then by saying that all states of mind involved with feeling and the like depend upon the object towards which they are focused; they thus arise only nominally, in the way that light emanates from a butter lamp. They cannot though arise on their own, without depending on something like this object of focus—and thus they do not exist through some nature of their own.[473]

gru.acip: RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA, BDEN PAR GRUB PA, DON DAM PAR GRUB PA, RANG GI NGO BOS GRUB PA, RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PA, RANG DBANG GIS GRUB PA, YANG DAG PAR GRUB PA, BLTOS MED DU GRUB PA RNAMS NI DON GCIG MING GI RNAM GRANGS TZAM MO, ,'DIS SEMS JI LTAR GZUNG BAR BYA BA'I
gru.wylie: rang bzhin gyis grub pa, bden par grub pa, don dam par grub pa, rang gi ngo bos grub pa, rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub pa, rang dbang gis grub pa, yang dag par grub pa, bltos med du grub pa rnams ni don gcig ming gi rnam grangs tsam mo, ,'dis sems ji ltar gzung bar bya ba'i
gru.english: TSUL BSTAN TO,,The following expressions all have the same meaning—they are all simply different ways of saying the same thing: existing through some nature of its own; existing in truth; existing ultimately; existing through its own essence; existing by definition; existing in and of itself; existing absolutely; and existing without relying on anything else.The preceding section then is meant to answer the original question of how we should keep our thoughts.

gru.acip: BSOD NAMS KYI PHUNG PO DE DAG NI THA SNYAD DU SGYU MA LTAR TSOGS PA LAS BYUNG BA YIN GYI, DE LTA BU LA MA BLTOS PAR GAL TE RANG GI NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB NA BSOD NAMS KYI PHUNG PO ZHES DE BZHIN GSHEGS PAS MI GSUNG
gru.wylie: bsod nams kyi phung po de dag ni tha snyad du sgyu ma ltar tshogs pa las byung ba yin gyi, de lta bu la ma bltos par gal te rang gi ngo bo nyid kyis grub na bsod nams kyi phung po zhes de bzhin gshegs pas mi gsung
gru.english: NGO,,The great mountains of merit thus created are, in a nominal sense, produced by a combination of things, in the same way that an illusion is. Yet if they were produced without depending on this sort of thing—that is, if they existed through some essential nature of their own—then the One Thus Gone would never refer to them as "great mountains of merit."[480]

gru.acip: RGYU MTSAN NI BSOD NAMS KYI PHUNG PO ZHES PA'I PHUNG PO'I DON NI TSOGS PA'I DON YIN LA, RANG DBANG GIS GRUB NA TSOGS PA LA MA BLTOS PAR GRUB
gru.wylie: rgyu mtshan ni bsod nams kyi phung po zhes pa'i phung po'i don ni tshogs pa'i don yin la, rang dbang gis grub na tshogs pa la ma bltos par grub
gru.english: PAR 'GYUR RO ZHES DGONGS SO,,The reason here is that—when we speak of a "great mountain of merit"—the "mountain" implies a combination or collection of things. The point that Lord Buddha is making is that—if things existed in and of themselves—then they would exist without depending upon any such collection of things.[481]

gru.acip: RAB 'BYOR, 'DI JI SNYAM DU SEMS, GZUGS KYI SKU YONGS SU GRUB PAS DE BZHIN GSHEGS PAR BLTA'AM,
gru.wylie: rab 'byor, 'di ji snyam du sems, gzugs kyi sku yongs su grub pas de bzhin gshegs par blta'am
gru.english: O Subhuti, what do you think? Should we ever consider someone One Gone Thus simply because they have attained the physical form of an Enlightened Being?

gru.acip: RAB 'BYOR GYIS GSOL PA, BCOM LDAN 'DAS, DE NI, MA LAGS TE, GZUGS KYI SKU YONGS SU GRUB PAS DE BZHIN GSHEGS PAR MI BLTA'O, ,DE CI'I SLAD DU ZHE NA, BCOM LDAN 'DAS, GZUGS KYI SKU YONGS SU GRUB PA, GZUGS KYI SKU YONGS SU RDZOGS PA ZHES BGYI BA NI, DE YONGS SU GRUB PA MA MCHIS PAR DE BZHIN GSHEGS PAS GSUNGS PA'I SLAD DU STE, DES NA, GZUGS KYI SKU YONGS SU GRUB PA ZHES BGYI'O,,
gru.wylie: rab 'byor gyis gsol pa, bcom ldan 'das, de ni, ma lags te, gzugs kyi sku yongs su grub pas de bzhin gshegs par mi blta'o, ,de ci'i slad du zhe na, bcom ldan 'das, gzugs kyi sku yongs su grub pa, gzugs kyi sku yongs su rdzogs pa zhes bgyi ba ni, de yongs su grub pa ma mchis par de bzhin gshegs pas gsungs pa'i slad du ste, des na, gzugs kyi sku yongs su grub pa zhes bgyi'o
gru.english: And Subhuti respectfully replied, O Conqueror, it is not so: we should never consider someone One Gone Thus simply because they have attained the physical form of an Enlightened Being. And why is it so? Because, o Conqueror, the attainment of the physical form of an Enlightened Being—this thing we call the "attainment of the physical form of an Enlightened Being"—is an attainment that the One Thus Gone has said could never exist. And this is precisely why we can even call it the "attainment of the physical form of an Enlightened Being."

gru.acip: GZUGS KYI SKU YONGS SU GRUB PA 'DI LA DON DAM PAR DE BZHIN GSHEGS PAR BLTA BA STE BZUNG ZHING 'DOD PAR BYA SNYAM 'AM ZHES DRIS PA NA,
gru.wylie: gzugs kyi sku yongs su grub pa 'di la don dam par de bzhin gshegs par blta ba ste bzung zhing 'dod par bya snyam 'am zhes dris pa na
gru.english: Lord Buddha asks then, "What do you think? Should we ever consider" (meaning 'hold' or 'believe') "that someone is"—in an ultimate way—"One Gone Thus simply because they have attained the physical form of an Enlightened Being?"[484]

gru.acip: RGYU MTSAN NI GZUGS KYI SKU YANG RGYU RKYEN TSOGS PA LAS GRUB KYI, DON DAM PAR GRUB PA MA MCHIS PA BSOD NAMS KYI PHUNG PO DANG 'DRA STE, THA SNYAD DU GZUGS KYI SKUR GRUB PA ZHES BRJOD DO,,The reason is that the
gru.wylie: rgyu mtshan ni gzugs kyi sku yang rgyu rkyen tshogs pa las grub kyi, don dam par grub pa ma mchis pa bsod nams kyi phung po dang 'dra ste, tha snyad du gzugs kyi skur grub pa zhes brjod do,,the reaSoN iS ThaT The
gru.english: physical form of an Enlightened Being is also something that is produced, attained, by the combining of its causes and factors; it is not however something that could exist in some ultimate way. In this sense it is similar to those great mountains of merit: that is, we can—just nominally—refer to the "attainment of the physical form of an Enlightened Being."[486]

gru.acip: GAL TE GZUGS KYI SKU ZHIG YOD NA DE'I MTSAN DPE RNAMS BDEN GRUB TU YOD
gru.wylie: gal te gzugs kyi sku zhig yod na de'i mtshan dpe rnams bden grub tu yod
gru.english: SNYAM NA DE MED CES STON PA NI,Another issue could be posed now: "If the physical form of an Enlightened Being does exist, then there must also exist—in a real way—the signs and marks of an Enlightened Being upon this form." No signs upon the form

gru.acip: DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA'I SKU LA MTSAN DPE PHUN SUM TSOGS PA BDEN GRUB TU YOD PA'I SGO NAS DE BZHIN GSHEGS PAR BDEN ZHEN GYIS MI BLTA STE, The idea
gru.wylie: de bzhin gshegs pa'i sku la mtshan dpe phun sum tshogs pa bden grub tu yod pa'i sgo nas de bzhin gshegs par bden zhen gyis mi blta ste, the iDea
gru.english: here is that we should never consider someone to be One Gone Thus through any kind of belief that they are real: through any belief that the exquisite signs and marks exist upon the physical form of One Gone Thus in some real way.[490]

gru.acip: MTSAN DPE PHUN SUM TSOGS PA DE DAG NI TSOGS SHING 'DUS PA'I DNGOS PO SGYU MA LTAR GRUB PAS DON DAM PAR MTSAN DPE PHUN SUM TSOGS PAR GRUB PA MA MCHIS KYANG, THA SNYAD DU DE SKAD CES BRJOD DO,,These exquisite signs
gru.wylie: mtshan dpe phun sum tshogs pa de dag ni tshogs shing 'dus pa'i dngos po sgyu ma ltar grub pas don dam par mtshan dpe phun sum tshogs par grub pa ma mchis kyang, tha snyad du de skad ces brjod do,,theSe exquiSiTe SigNS
gru.english: and marks are things which exist in the way of an illusion: which have been produced by the combination or assembling of other things. As such, they could never exist, in an ultimate way, as exquisite signs and marks; nonetheless, we can call them—in a nominal sense—what we do.[491]

gru.acip: RGYU MTSAN NI CHOS DANG CHOS BSTAN PA ZHES BYA BA NI THA SNYAD TZAM MA GTOGS GANG YANG DON DAM PAR MA GRUB PA'I PHYIR RO ZHES PA'I DON NI SNGAR
gru.wylie: rgyu mtshan ni chos dang chos bstan pa zhes bya ba ni tha snyad tsam ma gtogs gang yang don dam par ma grub pa'i phyir ro zhes pa'i don ni sngar
gru.english: BSHAD ZIN CING,The reason for saying this—as we've explained it already earlier—is because the Dharma itself, and the teaching of this Dharma, are "things that exist only nominally; they are not something that could exist at all in an ultimate sense."

gru.acip: DE DAG NI RANG RANG GI MING GI THA SNYAD 'JUG PA'I GZHIR RANG DBANG GIS MA GRUB CING, SGRA DE DANG DE'I BRJOD BYA'I RANG LDOG RNAMS NI BDEN PAR
gru.wylie: de dag ni rang rang gi ming gi tha snyad 'jug pa'i gzhir rang dbang gis ma grub cing, sgra de dang de'i brjod bya'i rang ldog rnams ni bden par
gru.english: MA GRUB CES STON PA'O,,What's being expressed by the sutra at this point is the following. None of these things is, in any natural or automatic way, the thing which the name we use for it refers to. The fact of a word and the thing it is used to refer to is, again, something not something which exists in some real way.[501]

gru.acip: DER GRUB NA NI GNOD BYED CI YOD ZHE NA, YOD DE, 'PHAGS PA THOGS MED KYIS
gru.wylie: der grub na ni gnod byed ci yod zhe na, yod de, 'phags pa thogs med kyis
gru.english: THEG BSDUS LAS,"But if it were to exist in some real way," you may ask, "what would be the problem?" The realized being Asanga has given us an answer on this, in his Abbreviated Presentation of the Greater Way—

gru.acip: ,MING GI SNGA ROL BLO MED PHYIR,,MANG BA'I PHYIR DANG MA 'DRES PHYIR,,DE YI BDAG NYID BDAG MANG DANG,,BDAG 'DRES 'GAL BAS 'GRUB PAR 'GYUR,
gru.wylie: ming gi snga rol blo med phyir,,mang ba'i phyir dang ma 'dres phyir,,de yi bdag nyid bdag mang dang,,bdag 'dres 'gal bas 'grub par 'gyur
gru.english: Before it is given the name,There is no idea of it;It would be many,And they never mix. There would be many itselfs,Or it would be themselves;And so our point is provenBy these inconsistencies.[132]

gru.acip: BCOM LDAN 'DAS KYIS KYANG DE'I LAN SONG ZIN PA LA DGONGS NAS, SEMS CAN DE DAG NI SEMS CAN DU DON DAM PAR GRUB PA YANG MA YIN, THA SNYAD DU SEMS
gru.wylie: bcom ldan 'das kyis kyang de'i lan song zin pa la dgongs nas, sems can de dag ni sems can du don dam par grub pa yang ma yin, tha snyad du sems
gru.english: CAN MED PA YANG MA YIN NO,,The Conqueror too is bearing in mind that he has already responded to this question, and so now he begins the part about how such beings will not be, in an ultimate sense, living beings; nor will they not, nominally, be a living being.

gru.acip: YANG RAB 'BYOR CHOS GANG YIN PA DE THAMS CAD NI BDEN PAR MA GRUB PAR MTSUNGS SHING MNYAM PA STE, DE LTA BU'I MNYAM PA DE'I DBANG DU BYAS PA LA MI MNYAM PA'I CHOS GANG YANG MED PAS SO,,The Buddha says now, "I say
gru.wylie: yang rab 'byor chos gang yin pa de thams cad ni bden par ma grub par mtshungs shing mnyam pa ste, de lta bu'i mnyam pa de'i dbang du byas pa la mi mnyam pa'i chos gang yang med pas so,,the buDDha SayS Now, "i Say
gru.english: to you further, o Subhuti, that none of the things that exist exist in any real way; and in this they are equivalent, they are equal. And this is because—relative to this way in which things are equal—there is nothing at all which is not equal.[516]

gru.acip: MNYAM PA DE YANG SEMS CAN MED PA, SROG MED PA, GANG ZAG GI BDAG MED PAR MNYAM PA STE, DON DAM PAR CHOS SU GRUB PA MED KYANG THA SNYAD DU SBYIN SOGS DGE BA'I CHOS DE DAG THAMS CAD KYIS DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA SANGS RGYAS SHING, SANGS RGYAS KYI THUGS RGYUD KYI DGE BA'I CHOS RNAMS LA'ANG SANGS
gru.wylie: mnyam pa de yang sems can med pa, srog med pa, gang zag gi bdag med par mnyam pa ste, don dam par chos su grub pa med kyang tha snyad du sbyin sogs dge ba'i chos de dag thams cad kyis de bzhin gshegs pa sangs rgyas shing, sangs rgyas kyi thugs rgyud kyi dge ba'i chos rnams la'ang sangs
gru.english: RGYAS ZHES BYA'O,,This kind of equal is equal in the sense that it is without any self to a living being; it is without any self to something that lives; and is without any self to a person. Ultimately speaking, there is nothing at all that exists as a thing; nonetheless, in a nominal sense, every single thing which is virtue leads to the total enlightenment of One Gone Thus, of a Buddha. And we can as well refer to all the virtuous things within the holy heart of a Buddha as "a Buddha."[517]

gru.acip: DON DAM PAR CHOS RNAMS MA GRUB NA 'ANG THA SNYAD DU SEMS CAN GANG LA LA ZHIG GIS STONG GSUM GYI STONG CHEN PO'I 'JIG RTEN GYI KHAMS NA RI'I RGYAL PO RI RAB JI SNYED PA DE LTA BU'I TSAD KYI GSER LA SOGS PA'I RIN PO CHE SNA BDUN GYI PHUNG PO RNAMS BSDUS TE SBYIN PA BYIN PA BAS
gru.wylie: don dam par chos rnams ma grub na 'ang tha snyad du sems can gang la la zhig gis stong gsum gyi stong chen po'i 'jig rten gyi khams na ri'i rgyal po ri rab ji snyed pa de lta bu'i tshad kyi gser la sogs pa'i rin po che sna bdun gyi phung po rnams bsdus te sbyin pa byin pa bas
gru.english: KYANG,Now even though there is nothing in the universe that exists in any ultimate sense, nonetheless certain people could indeed pile together great heaps of the seven different precious things—gold and the rest—that were the same size as the universal mountains[134] that existed on all of the planets in planets of this great world system: a system with a thousand of a thousand of a thousand planets. And they could offer this as a gift to someone.[520]

gru.acip: RAB 'BYOR BYIS PA SO SO'I SKYE BO RNAMS ZHES BYA BA NI DE DAG DON DAM PAR SKYE BO NYID DU GRUB PA MED PAR DE BZHIN GSHEGS PAS GSUNGS TE, THA
gru.wylie: rab 'byor byis pa so so'i skye bo rnams zhes bya ba ni de dag don dam par skye bo nyid du grub pa med par de bzhin gshegs pas gsungs te, tha
gru.english: SNYAD DU MING GIS DE SKAD CES BRJOD DO,,And these same people who are referred to as "children" or "common beings," o Subhuti, are beings that the One Gone Thus has said never existed at all—in an ultimate sense—as living creatures; they are only called by this name, in a nominal sense.[535]

gru.acip: DE LA CHAD LTA 'GOG PA NI, RAB 'BYOR KHYOD 'DI SNYAM DU BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA'I THEG PA LA YANG DAG PAR ZHUGS PA RNAMS KYIS GZUGS SOGS KYI CHOS GANG LA LA ZHIG DON DAM PAR MA GRUB PAR RTOGS PA NA,Now then we will
gru.wylie: de la chad lta 'gog pa ni, rab 'byor khyod 'di snyam du byang chub sems dpa'i theg pa la yang dag par zhugs pa rnams kyis gzugs sogs kyi chos gang la la zhig don dam par ma grub par rtogs pa na,now TheN we will
gru.english: need to go on to avoiding the extreme which says that everything has simply stopped. Lord Buddha says, "O Subhuti, suppose you were to think of those who have entered well into the way of the bodhisattva, and who perceived that any particular thing—whether it be something that we can see or anything else of the like—could never exist in any ultimate way."

gru.acip: DES NA THA SNYAD DU BSOD NAMS YONGS SU GZUNG BA ZHES BYA'O ZHES GSUNGS TE, 'DI'I GZUNG BAR MI BYA'O ZHES PAS BSOD NAMS KYI PHUNG PO LA BDEN GRUB TU ZHEN PA'I RTAG LTA DANG, YONGS SU GZUNG MOD KYIS ZHES CHAD PAR
gru.wylie: des na tha snyad du bsod nams yongs su gzung ba zhes bya'o zhes gsungs te, 'di'i gzung bar mi bya'o zhes pas bsod nams kyi phung po la bden grub tu zhen pa'i rtag lta dang, yongs su gzung mod kyis zhes chad par
gru.english: LTA BA SEL LO,,And this is precisely why, Lord Buddha says, that—nominally speaking—we can call it "gathering the merit in." When the sutra says here that we are "not to gather," it is helping us to avoid the view that things are unchanging—where we believe that the mountains of merit exist in truth. When it says that we "should, of course, gather," then it is helping us to avoid the view that things have simply stopped. The Buddha neither comes nor goes

gru.acip: DE RNAMS DON DAM PAR MED PA'I RANG BZHIN RDUL PHRA RAB KYI TSOGS ZHES GANG GSUNGS PA DE NI, DE RNAMS DON DAM PAR TSOGS SU GRUB PA MA MCHIS PAR DE BZHIN GSHEGS PAS MKHYEN NAS GSUNGS PA'I SLAD DU STE, DES NA THA SNYAD DU RDUL PHRA RAB KYI TSOGS ZHES BGYI'O,,And just why do they have a
gru.wylie: de rnams don dam par med pa'i rang bzhin rdul phra rab kyi tshogs zhes gang gsungs pa de ni, de rnams don dam par tshogs su grub pa ma mchis par de bzhin gshegs pas mkhyen nas gsungs pa'i slad du ste, des na tha snyad du rdul phra rab kyi tshogs zhes bgyi'o,,aND juST why Do They have a
gru.english: nature of not existing in an ultimate way? Think about the "piles of tiny particles" which were described. All this is because the One Thus Gone has seen that these are piles that could never exist in any ultimate way; and then he has said that they cannot. And this is precisely why we can call them, in a nominal sense, "piles of tiny particles."[595]

gru.acip: CHA BCAS KYANG 'DI LA PHYOGS BZHI DANG STENG 'OG TU RDUL DRUG GIS BSKOR NAS GNAS PAS 'GRUB LA, MED NA DE LA RIGS PA'I GNOD BYED STON TSUL MTSON
gru.wylie: cha bcas kyang 'di la phyogs bzhi dang steng 'og tu rdul drug gis bskor nas gnas pas 'grub la, med na de la rigs pa'i gnod byed ston tshul mtshon
gru.english: TZAM SNGAR BSHAD ZIN TO,,And once we say that these particles do have parts, then we would have to say that they exist as atoms which are wrapped in six other particles—ones which are positioned to the four directions, as well as above and below. If we said that they didn't have these other particles as part of them, then we would incur the same logical fallacies which we have already briefly mentioned.

gru.acip: RDUL PHRA RAB RANG BZHIN GYIS MA GRUB PAR BSHAD NAS DE BSAGS PA'I RAGS PA YANG RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA MED DO ZHES STON PA NI,
gru.wylie: rdul phra rab rang bzhin gyis ma grub par bshad nas de bsags pa'i rags pa yang rang bzhin gyis grub pa med do zhes ston pa ni
gru.english: Now that we've heard it explained how no tiny particle could ever exist through any nature of its own, we go on to a part of the text where it is described how none of the grosser composites of these particles could ever exist through any nature of their own.

gru.acip: STONG GSUM GYI STONG CHEN PO'I 'JIG RTEN GYI KHAMS DE YANG DON DAM PAR KHAMS SU GRUB PA MED PAR DE BZHIN GSHEGS PAS GSUNGS TE, DES NA THA SNYAD TZAM DU MING GIS STONG GSUM GYI STONG CHEN PO'I 'JIG RTEN GYI KHAMS ZHES BYA'O, ,'DIS SNOD BCUD GNYIS KA MTSON NO,,
gru.wylie: stong gsum gyi stong chen po'i 'jig rten gyi khams de yang don dam par khams su grub pa med par de bzhin gshegs pas gsungs te, des na tha snyad tsam du ming gis stong gsum gyi stong chen po'i 'jig rten gyi khams zhes bya'o, ,'dis snod bcud gnyis ka mtshon no
gru.english: That is, the One Thus Gone has also said that these planets of a great world system—a system of a thousand of a thousand of a thousand planets—are planets that could never exist in any ultimate sense. And this is precisely why, in a nominal sense, we can call them—we can give them the names of—"planets of a great world system, a system of a thousand of a thousand of a thousand planets." This description is meant to apply both to the planets, and to the people and things found upon them. Atoms are not what they seem

gru.acip: GAL TE DON DAM PAR SNOD BCUD KYI 'JIG RTEN GYI KHAMS DE LTA BU ZHIG MCHIS PAR GYUR NA NI, DE NYID TSOGS SHING 'DUS PA LA MA BLTOS PAR RAGS PA RIL PO GCIG TU GRUB CING 'DZIN DGOS PAR 'GYUR BA'I SLAD DU STE, DE LTAR GRUB NA DE BZHIN GSHEGS PAS KYANG GZIGS DGOS PAR 'GYUR RO,,
gru.wylie: gal te don dam par snod bcud kyi 'jig rten gyi khams de lta bu zhig mchis par gyur na ni, de nyid tshogs shing 'dus pa la ma bltos par rags pa ril po gcig tu grub cing 'dzin dgos par 'gyur ba'i slad du ste, de ltar grub na de bzhin gshegs pas kyang gzigs dgos par 'gyur ro
gru.english: And why is it so? Because if there were, in an ultimate sense, any such thing as a planet or world, both the place and the beings inhabiting it, then one would have to be grasping it as one whole solid and solitary thing whose existence did not rely upon its composite parts, on some collection of parts. And if it actually did exist in that way, then the One Thus Gone would also have to see it as being so.

gru.acip: DE BZHIN GSHEGS PAS DE LTA BU'I SNOD BCUD KYI 'JIG RTEN RNAMS TSOGS SHING MA 'DUS PA'I RIL PO RAGS PA CHA MED GCIG TU GRUB PAR MA GZIGS PAS,
gru.wylie: de bzhin gshegs pas de lta bu'i snod bcud kyi 'jig rten rnams tshogs shing ma 'dus pa'i ril po rags pa cha med gcig tu grub par ma gzigs pas
gru.english: But the fact is that the One Thus Gone has not seen such worlds—worlds of both places and the beings who inhabit them—as being things which existed each as a solitary one, without parts; as a gross and singular object which was not a composite, and which did not depend on the collection of its parts.

gru.acip: 'JIG RTEN NA RIL POR RAGS PA LING PO CHA MED GCIG TU GRUB PAR 'DZIN PA GANG GSUNGS PA'I 'DZIN PA DE YANG DON DAM PAR 'DZIN PAR GRUB PAR MA MCHIS SO ZHES PA'I SNGA MAS GZUNG BYA DANG, 'DIS 'DZIN PA YANG DON DAM PAR GRUB PAR STON PAR BSHAD DO,,
gru.wylie: 'jig rten na ril por rags pa ling po cha med gcig tu grub par 'dzin pa gang gsungs pa'i 'dzin pa de yang don dam par 'dzin par grub par ma mchis so zhes pa'i snga mas gzung bya dang, 'dis 'dzin pa yang don dam par grub par ston par bshad do
gru.english: And thus it is that the One Thus Gone has said that even the "tendency to grasp things as one whole solid thing"—as gross, discrete entities that are singular things not made of parts—described by the One Thus Gone is a kind of grasping that could never exist anyway. The first part above then is meant to demonstrate that what is grasped to could never exist in any ultimate sense, while this last part is to demonstrate that what does the grasping could never exist in this sense either.

gru.acip: CI NAS KYANG CHOS SU 'DU SHES ZHES PA NI CHOS GANG LA YANG BDEN PAR GRUB SNYAM PA'I 'DU SHES BDEN 'DZIN MI SKYE ZHING, BDEN PA'I 'DU SHES LA MI GNAS PAR BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: ci nas kyang chos su 'du shes zhes pa ni chos gang la yang bden par grub snyam pa'i 'du shes bden 'dzin mi skye zhing, bden pa'i 'du shes la mi gnas par bya'o
gru.english: The line about "never…conceiving of anything as an object of all" means that the bodhisattva should never allow any tendency to think of things as being real to arise—no tendency of thinking to oneself that anything at all could exist as a real object. Neither should they ever live in a way where they continue to think of things as real. The power of clear thinking

gru.acip: BSOD NAMS ZHES PA NI BSOD NAMS DANG YE SHES KYI TSOGS GNYIS GA MTSON ZHING, SBYIN PA TSUL KHRIMS BZOD PA GSUM LAS NI GTZO BOR BSOD NAMS KYI TSOGS GSOG LA, BSAM GTAN SHES RAB GNYIS KYIS NI GTZO BOR YE SHES KYI TSOGS GSOG CING, BRTZON 'GRUS LAS NI DE GNYIS KA 'BYUNG NGO, ,DES NA SHER PHYIN LA THOS BSAM SOGS BYED PA NI YE SHES KYI TSOGS GSOG PA GTZO CHE'O,,
gru.wylie: bsod nams zhes pa ni bsod nams dang ye shes kyi tshogs gnyis ga mtshon zhing, sbyin pa tshul khrims bzod pa gsum las ni gtso bor bsod nams kyi tshogs gsog la, bsam gtan shes rab gnyis kyis ni gtso bor ye shes kyi tshogs gsog cing, brtson 'grus las ni de gnyis ka 'byung ngo, ,des na sher phyin la thos bsam sogs byed pa ni ye shes kyi tshogs gsog pa gtso che'o
gru.english: When we say "merit" here, it really applies to both the collection of merit and the collection of wisdom. Following the three perfections of giving, an ethical way of life, and patience are—primarily—amassing the collection of merit. Following the two perfections of meditation and wisdom are primarily amassing the collection of wisdom. And both of these collections are produced by the perfection of joyful effort. We can say then that learning and contemplating upon the perfection of wisdom—and other similar practices—are primarily amassing the collection of wisdom.

gru.acip: DE DAG NI 'DUS BYAS RNAMS LA THUN MONG DU SBYAR NAS BSHAD PA STE, MDO LAS NI, ,GZUGS NI DBU BA BRDOS PA 'DRA, ,TSOR BA CHU YI CHU BUR BZHIN, ,'DU SHES SMIG RGYU LTA BU STE, ,'DU BYED RNAMS NI CHU SHING BZHIN, ,RNAM PAR SHES PA SGYU MA LTAR, ,NYI MA'I GNYEN GYIS BKA' STZAL TO,, ZHES BSHAD CES MGON PO KLU SGRUB GSUNG NGO, ,
gru.wylie: de dag ni 'dus byas rnams la thun mong du sbyar nas bshad pa ste, mdo las ni, ,gzugs ni dbu ba brdos pa 'dra, ,tshor ba chu yi chu bur bzhin, ,'du shes smig rgyu lta bu ste, ,'du byed rnams ni chu shing bzhin, ,rnam par shes pa sgyu ma ltar, ,nyi ma'i gnyen gyis bka' stsal to,, zhes bshad ces mgon po klu sgrub gsung ngo,
gru.english: The explanation given here applies to things brought about by causes as an entire group. A more restricted application is quoted from sutra by Master Nagarjuna: The physical form is like a bubble that forms, And the feelings resemble the froth of a wave; Discrimination is just a mirage, And the other factors like empty cane; Awareness is similar to an illusion— Thus did the Cousin of the Sun speak.[153]

gru.acip: ,CHES ZAB ZAB MO'I MDO DON BKRAL BA'I DGES, ,GZHUNG MANG MANG DU THOS PA'I BLO LDAN BDAG ,SKYE KUN KUN MKHYEN LAM SGRUB RTEN RNYED TSOGS, ,RAB RDZOGS RDZOGS PA'I SANGS RGYAS MYUR THOB SHOG ,
gru.wylie: ches zab zab mo'i mdo don bkral ba'i dges, ,gzhung mang mang du thos pa'i blo ldan bdag ,skye kun kun mkhyen lam sgrub rten rnyed tshogs, ,rab rdzogs rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas myur thob shog
gru.english: Thus then I have done some virtue In clarifying the meaning Of that deepest truth of a sutra deep; And I pray that I, who try to think With clarity, and study many things In the many scriptures there are, Have collected sufficient goodness to find A body and mind in which I can practice, In all my lives, the path to knowing all. May I complete the total goodness needed To quickly reach the state Of a totally enlightened Being. How the teaching came to us

gru.acip: CES RDOR GCOD KYI 'GREL PA THAR PAR BGROD PA'I LAM BZANG ZAB DON SNANG BA'I NYI MA ZHES BYA BA 'DI NI, SH'AKYA'I DGE SLONG GRAGS PA BSHAD SGRUB CES BYA BAS RANG LO BCU PHRAG BDUN PA RAB BYUNG BCU GNYIS PA'I SHING BYI LOR DAD PAS CO NE'I DGON NYID DU SBYAR BA'I YI GE PA NI T'A YI LA LUNG BLO BZANG DON GRUB BO,,
gru.wylie: ces rdor gcod kyi 'grel pa thar par bgrod pa'i lam bzang zab don snang ba'i nyi ma zhes bya ba 'di ni, shAkya'i dge slong grags pa bshad sgrub ces bya bas rang lo bcu phrag bdun pa rab byung bcu gnyis pa'i shing byi lor dad pas co ne'i dgon nyid du sbyar ba'i yi ge pa ni tA yi la lung blo bzang don grub bo
gru.english: This brings us to the conclusion of our commentary upon The Diamond Cutter entitled The Sun which Illuminates that Most Profound of Things—An Excellent Path for Travelling to Freedom. It has been composed by the Shakya monk named Drakpa Shedrup, in the seventh decade of my life; that is, in the wooden rat year of the twelfth cycle [1744]. I wrote the book with feelings of great devotion here at Chone Monastery; the scribe who helped me was Lobsang Dundrup of Tayi Lalung.

gru.acip: BCOM LDAN 'DAS, BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA'I THEG PA LA YANG DAG PAR ZHUGS PAS JI LTAR GNAS PAR BGYI, JI LTAR BSGRUB PAR BGYI, JI LTAR SEMS RAB TU GZUNG BAR BGYI,
gru.wylie: bcom ldan 'das, byang chub sems dpa'i theg pa la yang dag par zhugs pas ji ltar gnas par bgyi, ji ltar bsgrub par bgyi, ji ltar sems rab tu gzung bar bgyi
gru.english: And now, o Conquering One, what of those who have entered well into the way of the bodhisattva? How shall they live? How shall they practice? How should they keep their thoughts?

gru.acip: RAB 'BYOR, DE'I PHYIR NYON LA LEGS PAR RAB TU YID LA ZUNGS SHIG DANG, BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA'I THEG PA LA YANG DAG PAR ZHUGS PAS JI LTAR GNAS PAR BYA BA DANG, JI LTAR BSGRUB PAR BYA BA DANG, JI LTAR SEMS RAB DU GZUNG BAR BYA BA NGAS KHYOD LA BSHAD DO,,
gru.wylie: rab 'byor, de'i phyir nyon la legs par rab tu yid la zungs shig dang, byang chub sems dpa'i theg pa la yang dag par zhugs pas ji ltar gnas par bya ba dang, ji ltar bsgrub par bya ba dang, ji ltar sems rab du gzung bar bya ba ngas khyod la bshad do
gru.english: And since it is so, o Subhuti, listen now to what I speak, and be sure that it stays firmly in your heart, for I shall reveal to you how it is that those who have entered well into the way of the bodhisattva should live, and how they should practice, and how they should keep their thoughts.

gru.acip: BCOM LDAN 'DAS KYIS BKA' STZAL PA, RAB 'BYOR, BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA' GANG LA LA ZHIG 'DI SKAD DU, BDAG GIS ZHING BKOD PA RNAMS BSGRUB PAR BYA'O, ,ZHES ZER NA, DE NI, MI BDEN PAR SMRA BA'O,,
gru.wylie: bcom ldan 'das kyis bka' stsal pa, rab 'byor, byang chub sems dpa' gang la la zhig 'di skad du, bdag gis zhing bkod pa rnams bsgrub par bya'o, ,zhes zer na, de ni, mi bden par smra ba'o
gru.english: Then the Conqueror spoke once more, Suppose, o Subhuti, that some bodhisattva were to say, "I am working to bring about my paradise." This would not be spoken true.

gru.acip: BCOM LDAN 'DAS, BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA'I THEG PA LA YANG DAG PAR ZHUGS PAS JI LTAR GNAS PAR BGYI, JI LTAR BSGRUB PAR BGYI, JI LTAR SEMS RAB TU GZUNG BAR BGYI,
gru.wylie: bcom ldan 'das, byang chub sems dpa'i theg pa la yang dag par zhugs pas ji ltar gnas par bgyi, ji ltar bsgrub par bgyi, ji ltar sems rab tu gzung bar bgyi
gru.english: O Conquering One, what of those who have entered well into the way of the bodhisattva? How shall they live? How shall they practice? How should they

gru.acip: RAB 'BYOR, BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA' GANG ZHIG 'DI SKAD DU, BDAG GIS ZHING BKOD PA RNAMS BSGRUB BO, ,ZHES ZER NA, DE YANG DE BZHIN DU BRJOD PAR BYA'O,, DE CI'I PHYIR ZHE NA, RAB 'BYOR ZHING BKOD PA RNAMS ZHING BKOD PA RNAMS ZHES BYA BA DE NI, DE DAG BKOD PA MED PAR DE BZHIN GSHEGS PAS GSUNGS PA'I PHYIR TE, DES NA ZHING BKOD PA RNAMS ZHES BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: rab 'byor, byang chub sems dpa' gang zhig 'di skad du, bdag gis zhing bkod pa rnams bsgrub bo, ,zhes zer na, de yang de bzhin du brjod par bya'o,, de ci'i phyir zhe na, rab 'byor zhing bkod pa rnams zhing bkod pa rnams zhes bya ba de ni, de dag bkod pa med par de bzhin gshegs pas gsungs pa'i phyir te, des na zhing bkod pa rnams zhes bya'o
gru.english: And suppose, o Subhuti, that some bodhisattva were to say, "I am working to bring about my paradise." That would not be spoken rightly. Why is it so? Because, o Subhuti, the paradise that you are working to bring about when you say "I am working to bring about my paradise" is something that the One Thus Gone has said that you could never bring about. And this is precisely why we can even speak of these as "paradises to bring about."

gru.acip: RAB 'BYOR, 'DI JI SNYAM DU SEMS, GZUGS KYI SKU YONGS SU GRUB PAS DE BZHIN GSHEGS PAR BLTA'AM,
gru.wylie: rab 'byor, 'di ji snyam du sems, gzugs kyi sku yongs su grub pas de bzhin gshegs par blta'am
gru.english: O Subhuti, what do you think? Should we ever consider someone One Gone Thus simply because they have attained the physical form of an Enlightened Being?
