gru.acip: RAB 'BYOR GYIS GSOL PA, BCOM LDAN 'DAS, DE NI, MA LAGS TE, GZUGS KYI SKU YONGS SU GRUB PAS DE BZHIN GSHEGS PAR MI BLTA'O, ,DE CI'I SLAD DU ZHE NA, BCOM LDAN 'DAS, GZUGS KYI SKU YONGS SU GRUB PA, GZUGS KYI SKU YONGS SU RDZOGS PA ZHES BGYI BA NI, DE YONGS SU GRUB PA MA MCHIS PAR DE BZHIN GSHEGS PAS GSUNGS PA'I SLAD DU STE, DES NA, GZUGS KYI SKU YONGS SU GRUB PA ZHES BGYI'O,,
gru.wylie: rab 'byor gyis gsol pa, bcom ldan 'das, de ni, ma lags te, gzugs kyi sku yongs su grub pas de bzhin gshegs par mi blta'o, ,de ci'i slad du zhe na, bcom ldan 'das, gzugs kyi sku yongs su grub pa, gzugs kyi sku yongs su rdzogs pa zhes bgyi ba ni, de yongs su grub pa ma mchis par de bzhin gshegs pas gsungs pa'i slad du ste, des na, gzugs kyi sku yongs su grub pa zhes bgyi'o
gru.english: And Subhuti respectfully replied, O Conqueror, it is not so: we should never consider someone One Gone Thus simply because they have attained the physical form of an Enlightened Being. And why is it so? Because, o Conqueror, the attainment of the physical form of an Enlightened Being—this thing we call the "attainment of the physical form of an Enlightened Being"—is an attainment that the One Thus Gone has said could never exist. And this is precisely why we can even call it the "attainment of the physical form of an Enlightened Being."

gru.acip: DE'I RJES SU GRUB PA'I MTHA' SO SO'I CHOS BSTAN PAR BYA STE,
gru.wylie: de'i rjes su grub pa'i mtha' so so'i chos bstan par bya ste
gru.english: Take them through the beliefs of each one of the different schools of the teachings.

gru.acip: GRUB PA'I MTHA' THAMS CAD BSTAN NAS, DE'I RJES SU KYE'I RDO RJER BCUG PAR GYUR NA NGES PAR 'GRUB PO ZHES PA'I DON TO,,
gru.wylie: grub pa'i mtha' thams cad bstan nas, de'i rjes su kye'i rdo rjer bcug par gyur na nges par 'grub po zhes pa'i don to
gru.english: What these lines by Lord Buddha are saying then is that--if first you do this, teaching them all the different schools of Buddhism--then afterwards you may bring them into the practice of Lo Diamond, and they will surely attain their goals.]

gru.acip: DES NA CHOS RJE PHAG MO GRU PA SOGS 'GA' ZHIG GI ,CHOS DRUG GI KHRID YIG NA LAM THUN MONG BA'I KHRID TSUL MI SNANG BA NI, TSOGS KHRID LAM RIM BZHIN DU KHRID PA'I RJES SU GDAMS NGAG 'DI STER BA'I LUGS SU SNANG BAS, YANG DGON PA'I KHRID YIG NA 'DUG PA BZHIN, LAM THUN MONG BA LA SNGON DU 'KHRID PA SHIN TU GNAD CHE BAR ZUNGSSHIG ,
gru.wylie: des na chos rje phag mo gru pa sogs 'ga' zhig gi ,chos drug gi khrid yig na lam thun mong ba'i khrid tshul mi snang ba ni, tshogs khrid lam rim bzhin du khrid pa'i rjes su gdams ngag 'di ster ba'i lugs su snang bas, yang dgon pa'i khrid yig na 'dug pa bzhin, lam thun mong ba la sngon du 'khrid pa shin tu gnad che bar zungsshig
gru.english: Therefore we can say that the fact that--in the books of instruction on the six practices written by the Dharma Lord Pakmo Drupa and some others--we find no sections on guiding the student along the path that is shared, appears to reflect a system of teaching where these advices were granted only after a more public teaching on something like the steps of the path.  You should therefore consider it an extremely crucial point that the student should first be guided along the path which is shared, just as we see it in the book of instructions by Yang Gunpa.

whole_word_matches.context: des na chos rje phag mo gru pa sogs 'ga' zhig gi ,chos drug gi khrid yig na lam th

gru.acip: ,ZLA BA DE'I TSES BRGYAD LA MKHAS GRUB CHEN PO SANGS RGYAS YE SHES LA DBYANGS CAN MA DKAR MO'I RJES GNANG ZHUS TE
gru.wylie: zla ba de'i tshes brgyad la mkhas grub chen po sangs rgyas ye shes la dbyangs can ma dkar mo'i rjes gnang zhus te
gru.english: On the eighth day of that same month, he came to that wise and accomplished master, Kedrup Sangye Yeshe, and had the good fortune to be granted the rite of permission into the secret world of the Lady of Song (Sarasvati, or Yangchenma), in her form of purest white.

gru.acip: KHYAD PAR DBYANGS CAN MA DE'I THUGS KA NAS LHA MO DBYANGS CAN MA LNGON MO PHYAG GNYIS RIN PO CHE'I YOL GO DNGOS GRUB GZUGS CAN LTA BU'I SHING THOG GSAR PAS BKANG BA 'DZIN PA ZHIG 'THON TE SNOD BCUD DANG BCAS PA TZO MO LA PHUL BA,
gru.wylie: khyad par dbyangs can ma de'i thugs ka nas lha mo dbyangs can ma lngon mo phyag gnyis rin po che'i yol go dngos grub gzugs can lta bu'i shing thog gsar pas bkang ba 'dzin pa zhig 'thon te snod bcud dang bcas pa tso mo la phul ba
gru.english: Here is what he saw.  Out of the heart of the Lady of Song comes another goddess, another Lady of Song--this one with a body of sea-blue green.  In her two hands she bears forth a priceless bowl of jewel, filled with fresh fruit that are, in reality, high spiritual attainments in a physical form.  This Lady of the Sky turns, and offers the bowl and its fruit to the first Lady. Sarasvati, the Lady of Song

gru.acip: ZHES PA 'DI PHYAG BRIS SU MDZAD DO, ,BSTOD PA 'DI NI DBYANGS CAN MA'I SKU JI LTAR GZIGS PA LTAR DU BSTOD PA MDZAD PA YIN PAS 'DI LA DBYANGS CAN MA'I BSTOD PA GZIGS SNANG MA ZHES RJE BTZUN BLO BZANG CHOS KYI RGYAL MTSAN GYI THUGS SRAS GRUB CHEN RNAMS MTHUN PAR GSUNG GO,
gru.wylie: zhes pa 'di phyag bris su mdzad do, ,bstod pa 'di ni dbyangs can ma'i sku ji ltar gzigs pa ltar du bstod pa mdzad pa yin pas 'di la dbyangs can ma'i bstod pa gzigs snang ma zhes rje btsun blo bzang chos kyi rgyal mtshan gyi thugs sras grub chen rnams mthun par gsung go
gru.english: This poem was found as a handwritten manuscript. [Translator's note: The author of the biography, Master Tsechok Ling, notes that much of the poetry found in the biography--and we will translate numerous poems as we go through the course--is not found in the First Panchen's Lamas collected works; but has rather been taken from a secret tradition of chanting his poems at the tantric college connected to His Holiness' main monastery, Trashi Hlunpo.] Since it sings the praises of the Lady of Song according to someone who is describing what they actually saw, the great masters who are spiritual sons of the venerable Lobsang Chukyi Gyeltsen speak as one in referring to it as The Praise of the Lady of Song, Who Came to Me. The Asian Classics Institute ____________________________________________________________________________ Diamond Mountain University Tantric Series Course I The Path to Bliss, Part One Reading, Class Two: The Buddha Before Me The Buddha Before Me We begin the path which is shared now, first with the actual text of The Path to Bliss (ACIP digital text 5944), by His Holiness the First Panchen Lama, Lobsang Chukyi Gyeltsen (1570-1662).

gru.acip: ,DE NAS MKHAS GRUB SANGS RGYAS YE SHES KYI BKA' BZHIN LAM RIM CHUNG BA BZUNG NAS ZHAG BCU SKOR SONG BA'I MTSAMS LAM RIM CHE BA LA GZIGS PAS THUGS SHIN TU 'GRO BA ZHIG BYUNG STE 'DZIN PAR RTZOM PA NA
gru.wylie: de nas mkhas grub sangs rgyas ye shes kyi bka' bzhin lam rim chung ba bzung nas zhag bcu skor song ba'i mtshams lam rim che ba la gzigs pas thugs shin tu 'gro ba zhig byung ste 'dzin par rtsom pa na
gru.english: The accomplished one, the master Sangye Yeshe, then asked him to memorize the text of Je Tsongkapa's Short Book on the Steps of the Path [about 10 pages long].  He did as his teacher had asked, and then about ten days later happened to see a copy of The Great Book on the Steps of the Path [also by Je Tsongkapa, and over 1,000 pages long]. Je Tsongkapa He was immediately attracted to it, and set about memorizing this work as well.

gru.acip: DE LA BSKOR BA LAN MANG DU BYAS TE GSOL BA BTAB PAS BYIN GYIS BRLABS TE LAM RIM CHEN MO YONGS SU RDZOGS PA THOGS PA MED PAR ZIN TE MKHAS GRUB SANGS RGYAS YE SHES LA RGYUGS PHUL,
gru.wylie: de la bskor ba lan mang du byas te gsol ba btab pas byin gyis brlabs te lam rim chen mo yongs su rdzogs pa thogs pa med par zin te mkhas grub sangs rgyas ye shes la rgyugs phul
gru.english: He began to walk sacred circles, over and over, around the Buddha.  He begged Him for His blessing, and then suddenly he was able to memorize the entire Great Book, with almost no effort at all.  And then he went to his teacher, Kedrup Sangye Yeshe--who examined him and found he had memorized both works perfectly. The Asian Classics Institute ____________________________________________________________________________ Diamond Mountain University Tantric Series Course I The Path to Bliss, Part One Reading, Class Three: The Lama before Me * * * The Lama before Me We continue with His Holiness the First Panchen Lama's Path to Bliss:

gru.acip: DA NI DBANG LUNG GDAMS NGAG PHAL CHER YANG ZHUS ZIN, MDO SNGAGS KYI LAM GYI RIM PA RNAMS LA YANG GO BA RAGS PA TZAM CHAGS, ,LHAG PA'I LHA MANG PO'I BSNYEN SGRUB SOGS KYANG DGA' RAB BYUNG,
gru.wylie: da ni dbang lung gdams ngag phal cher yang zhus zin, mdo sngags kyi lam gyi rim pa rnams la yang go ba rags pa tsam chags, ,lhag pa'i lha mang po'i bsnyen sgrub sogs kyang dga' rab byung
gru.english: He thought to himself, "Now I have been granted almost all the various empowerments, and oral transmissions, and personal advices.  I also possess a fairly good understanding of all the various steps of the path, for both the open and secret teachings.  Moreover, I've had some good success in retreats and the like relating to a great many high deities.

gru.acip: DA NI BKRA SHIS LHUN POR PHYIN NAS SHING RTA CHEN PO'I GZHUNG YONGS RDZOGS LA BSLAB SBYONG MTHAR PHYIN PA ZHIG MYUR BAR BYA'O SNYAM DU DGONGS NAS MKHAS GRUB SANGS RGYAS YE SHES LA DE BZHIN ZHUS PA NA,
gru.wylie: da ni bkra shis lhun por phyin nas shing rta chen po'i gzhung yongs rdzogs la bslab sbyong mthar phyin pa zhig myur bar bya'o snyam du dgongs nas mkhas grub sangs rgyas ye shes la de bzhin zhus pa na
gru.english: "And so now I should travel to Trashi Hlunpo, with all possible speed, and undertake the entire course of study in the major texts of those Great Ones Who Brought the Horse of Wood." He then respectfully informed his Master, Kedrup Sangye Yeshe, of these thoughts.

gru.acip: MA ZAD, MKHAS GRUB SANGS RGYAS YE SHES KYI ZHABS DRUNG DU MDO SNGAGS KYI LAM GYI DKA' GNAS THAMS CAD GSAN TE THUGS NYAMS SU BZHES PAR MDZAD PAS,
gru.wylie: ma zad, mkhas grub sangs rgyas ye shes kyi zhabs drung du mdo sngags kyi lam gyi dka' gnas thams cad gsan te thugs nyams su bzhes par mdzad pas
gru.english: Not only that--he had also already sat at the feet of the wise and accomplished Sangye Yeshe, and listened to every difficult point in both the open and secret teachings, and grasped them thoroughly.

gru.acip: GNYIS PA SBYOR BAS BSTEN TSUL NI, DGE BA'I BSHES GNYEN RNAMS MDUN DU GSAL BZHIN PA'I NGANG NAS BDAG GIS SANGS RGYAS DNGOS KYI DGE BA'I BSHES GNYEN 'DI RNAMS KYI PHYIR DU, LUS SROG LONGS SPYOD LA SOGS PA LTOS PA MED PAR GTONG ZHING, KHYAD PAR BKA' BZHIN BSGRUB PA'I MCHOD PAS MNYES PAR BYA'O, ,DE LTAR BYED NUS PAR BLA MA LHAS BYIN GYIS BRLAB TU GSOL, ZHES GSOL BA BTAB PAS,
gru.wylie: gnyis pa sbyor bas bsten tshul ni, dge ba'i bshes gnyen rnams mdun du gsal bzhin pa'i ngang nas bdag gis sangs rgyas dngos kyi dge ba'i bshes gnyen 'di rnams kyi phyir du, lus srog longs spyod la sogs pa ltos pa med par gtong zhing, khyad par bka' bzhin bsgrub pa'i mchod pas mnyes par bya'o, ,de ltar byed nus par bla ma lhas byin gyis brlab tu gsol, zhes gsol ba btab pas
gru.english: Here next is the second part from before: learning to rely upon our spiritual Guide in our actions.  Again focus clearly on the spiritual Guides before you; keep this vision in mind as you make the following supplication: "I swear that I will give away my body, my life, and all the things I own--everything there is--for these my spiritual Guides.  Most especially I will please them with the offering of carrying out what they ask me to do.  I beg you, my Lama, my Angel, to grant me the ability to do all this."

gru.acip: ,RNAM DKAR BYE BA LAS GRUB RTZIBS STONG CAN, ,'KHOR LO'I MTSAN MNGA' NGANG PA'I DRA BA LTAR, ,RAB MDZES NOR BU'I 'OD 'BAR ZHABS SEN GYIS, ,REG PAS BDAG SNYING ZE'U 'GRU SKAL BZANG MDZOD,
gru.wylie: rnam dkar bye ba las grub rtsibs stong can, ,'khor lo'i mtshan mnga' ngang pa'i dra ba ltar, ,rab mdzes nor bu'i 'od 'bar zhabs sen gyis, ,reg pas bdag snying ze'u 'gru skal bzang mdzod
gru.english: I see the marks, the wheel of a thousand spokes, born from ten million deeds of purest white; and the webbing between the toes like that of a snow-white goose; and nails of the toes blazing in lovely jewel light. Let them touch me-- let golden fortune touch the inner threads of my heart. [Translator's note: The sign of a thousand-spoked Dharma wheel on the palms of the hands and soles of the feet; extra webbing connecting the fingers and toes; and a gilded look to the fingernails and toenails are some of the signs on the body of an enlightened being.]

whole_word_matches.context: 'i 'od 'bar zhabs sen gyis, ,reg pas bdag snying ze'u 'gru skal bzang mdzod

gru.acip: SPYI BOR BLA MA LHA BSGOM BZHIN PA'I NGANG NAS 'DI LTAR BSAM STE DAM PA'I CHOS BSGRUB PA LA KHOM PAS DAL BA DANG, CHOS BSGRUB PA'I PHYI NANG GI CHA RKYEN TSANG BAS 'BYOR PA ZHES BYA,
gru.wylie: spyi bor bla ma lha bsgom bzhin pa'i ngang nas 'di ltar bsam ste dam pa'i chos bsgrub pa la khom pas dal ba dang, chos bsgrub pa'i phyi nang gi cha rkyen tshang bas 'byor pa zhes bya
gru.english: Maintain the meditative vision of your Lama, the Angel, atop your head, and then take your mind through the following train of thought. "I possess both spiritual opportunity--in that I have the time to practice the holy Dharma; and spiritual resources--since I enjoy all the outer and inner conditions needed for this practice.

gru.acip: MDOR NA RANG CAG RNAMS KYIS THOB PA'I DAL 'BYOR GYI RTEN 'DI DON SHIN TU CHE STE 'DI LA BRTEN NAS MNGON MTHO'I LUS LONGS SPYOD PHUN SUM TSOGS PA'I RGYU SBYIN PA, TSUL KHRIMS BZOD PA SOGS KYANG SGRUB NUS LA,
gru.wylie: mdor na rang cag rnams kyis thob pa'i dal 'byor gyi rten 'di don shin tu che ste 'di la brten nas mngon mtho'i lus longs spyod phun sum tshogs pa'i rgyu sbyin pa, tshul khrims bzod pa sogs kyang sgrub nus la
gru.english: "To put it briefly, the body and mind that all of here possess--endowed as they are with these spiritual opportunities and resources--is something of extraordinary importance.  Using this body and mind, we can practice the perfection of giving, which then brings to us the exquisite physical form and material possessions of the higher realms.  So too we can practice the ethical life; and patience; and all the other perfections.

gru.acip: KHYAD PAR RTEN 'DI LA SDOM PA GSUM GA SKYE ZHING, SNYIGS DUS KYI TSE THUNG GCIG LA SANGS RGYAS KYI GO 'PHANG YANG BDE BLAG TU SGRUB NUS PAS SO,,
gru.wylie: khyad par rten 'di la sdom pa gsum ga skye zhing, snyigs dus kyi tshe thung gcig la sangs rgyas kyi go 'phang yang bde blag tu sgrub nus pas so
gru.english: "Most especially, the various vows can grow with this particular body and mind; and so we can even attain, with ease, the high state of an enlightened Being--in but a single, brief life here in the age of degeneration."

gru.acip: KHYAD PAR DAL 'BYOR TSANG BA'I RTEN RNAM PAR DAG PA THOB PA LA TSUL KHRIMS RNAM PAR DAG PAS GZHI BZUNG, SBYIN SOGS KYIS GROGS BYAS, SMON LAM DRI MA MED PAS MTSAMS SBYAR BA SOGS DGOS NA RGYU DE LTA BU BSGRUB PA YANG SHIN TU NYUNG BA DANG,
gru.wylie: khyad par dal 'byor tshang ba'i rten rnam par dag pa thob pa la tshul khrims rnam par dag pas gzhi bzung, sbyin sogs kyis grogs byas, smon lam dri ma med pas mtshams sbyar ba sogs dgos na rgyu de lta bu bsgrub pa yang shin tu nyung ba dang
gru.english: More particularly, there are certain things needed in order to attain this perfect kind of mind and body, complete as it is with the various spiritual opportunities and resources.  First we must observe a perfectly ethical life, as a foundation.  This must be accompanied then by the perfections of giving and the rest.  And finally we must make the passage between death and rebirth with the purest of prayers.  People who manage to attain these and the other necessary causes for a body and mind like the ones we have now are in themselves extremely few.

gru.acip: 'DI SNGON NAS BRIS ZIN TE DA BAR RAB TU GNAS PA MA GRUB PAS, DA LAM KHYOD KYIS ZHAL PHYE LA RAB GNAS SHIG GYIS GSUNGS,
gru.wylie: 'di sngon nas bris zin te da bar rab tu gnas pa ma grub pas, da lam khyod kyis zhal phye la rab gnas shig gyis gsungs
gru.english: "I wrote this book some time ago," said the monk, "but so far I haven't had a chance to perform the ceremony of consecration over it.  And so today you should open it, and perform the consecration."

gru.acip: DA BDAG DANG MA SEMS CAN THAMS CAD KYI RGYUD LA 'CHI BA MI RTAG PA DRAN PA DANG, NGAN 'GRO'I SDUG BSNGAL GYIS 'JIGS NAS DKON MCHOG GSUM LA SNYING NAS SKYABS SU 'GRO ZHING LAS 'BRAS LA YID CHES KYI DAD PA SKYES NAS SDIG SPONG DGE BA TSUL BZHIN SGRUB NUS PAR BLA MA LHAS BYIN GYIS BRLAB TU GSOL, ZHES GSOL BA BTAB PAS,
gru.wylie: da bdag dang ma sems can thams cad kyi rgyud la 'chi ba mi rtag pa dran pa dang, ngan 'gro'i sdug bsngal gyis 'jigs nas dkon mchog gsum la snying nas skyabs su 'gro zhing las 'bras la yid ches kyi dad pa skyes nas sdig spong dge ba tshul bzhin sgrub nus par bla ma lhas byin gyis brlab tu gsol, zhes gsol ba btab pas
gru.english: And so now I make the following supplication: "I beg you, my Lama, my Angel, to give me your blessing, so that I and every other living being--all of them my own mother--may remain mindful of our impermanence, our coming death; and so we may feel real fear for the sufferings of the three lower realms, and thus come for shelter, from our hearts, to the Three Jewels; and so we may find an intelligent sense of belief in the laws of karma and its consequences, thus stopping all the negative deeds we do, while practicing--in the proper way--every virtuous deed."

gru.acip: ,LO DE LA STONG 'KHOR SPRUL SKU 'JAM DBYANGS RGYA MTSO DANG, SKYID SHOD ZHABS DRUNG BSTAN 'DZIN BLO BZANG RGYA MTSO SOGS BLA CHEN MANG POS GTZOS BSNYEN RDOGS GSAR SGRUB BRGYA PHRAG MANG PO'I DON MDZAD,
gru.wylie: lo de la stong 'khor sprul sku 'jam dbyangs rgya mtsho dang, skyid shod zhabs drung bstan 'dzin blo bzang rgya mtsho sogs bla chen mang pos gtsos bsnyen rdogs gsar sgrub brgya phrag mang po'i don mdzad
gru.english: In that same year [1615], he was able to accomplish the ordination of many hundreds of people into the vows of a full monk.  These groups were headed by such illustrious high reincarnated Lamas as Tunkor Trulku Jamyang Gyatso and Kyishu Shabdrung Tendzin Lobsang Gyatso.

gru.acip: ,DUS GSUM SANGS RGYAS KYI NGO BO, ,BKA' DRIN GSUM LDAN GYI BLA MA, ,'BRAL MED SPYI GTZUG TU BZHUGS LA, ,BYIN RLABS DNGOS GRUB KYI CHAR PHOBS,
gru.wylie: dus gsum sangs rgyas kyi ngo bo, ,bka' drin gsum ldan gyi bla ma, ,'bral med spyi gtsug tu bzhugs la, ,byin rlabs dngos grub kyi char phobs
gru.english: O Lama who has paid me the three kinds of kindness, essence of the Buddhas of the past and present and future; I beg that you never leave me, stay here seated on the top of my head, spill down upon me a shower of blessings and attainments.

gru.acip: ,NGAL BA BRGYA PHRAG GIS BSGRUBS PA, ,SRID PA'I PHUN TSOGS KYI DGA' STON, ,LHO PHYOGS DRI BZHON GYIS BSKYOD PA'I, ,PADMO'I 'DAB STONG GI ZIL BA,
gru.wylie: ngal ba brgya phrag gis bsgrubs pa, ,srid pa'i phun tshogs kyi dga' ston, ,lho phyogs dri bzhon gyis bskyod pa'i, ,padmo'i 'dab stong gi zil ba
gru.english: Hundreds of days exhausted we worked to arrange this party of worldly goods-- the thousand fragile petals of a lotus stirred by the deathwind from the south.

gru.acip: DGE BA BCU LA SOGS PA'I DGE BA PHRA MO NAS SGRUB CING, MI DGE BA BCU LA SOGS PA'I MI DGE BA PHRA MOS KYANG SGO GSUM LA MA GOS PA'I BLANG DOR LA 'BAD PAR BYA'O, ,DE LTAR BYED NUS PAR BLA MA LHAS BYIN GYIS BRLAB TU GSOL, ZHES GSOL BA BTAB PAS,
gru.wylie: dge ba bcu la sogs pa'i dge ba phra mo nas sgrub cing, mi dge ba bcu la sogs pa'i mi dge ba phra mos kyang sgo gsum la ma gos pa'i blang dor la 'bad par bya'o, ,de ltar byed nus par bla ma lhas byin gyis brlab tu gsol, zhes gsol ba btab pas
gru.english: Make fierce efforts to do what is right, and to avoid what is wrong.  Seek to carry out even the very slightest form of good deed, whether it be one of the ten positive actions or anything of the like.  Seek too to avoid sullying your actions or words or thoughts with even the most insignificant form of bad deed--with any of the ten negative actions, or anything of that kind. Make then the following supplication too: "I beg you, my Lama, my Angel, to give me your blessing, so I may be able to keep this too."

gru.acip: GNYIS PA DNGOS GZHI NI, SPYI BOR BLA MA LHA BSGOM BZHIN PA'I NGANG NAS 'DI LTAR BSAM STE, SHES PA KHO RANG GI NGOS NAS LUNG MA BSTAN YIN PA LA, DANG POR BDAG DANG BDAG GI BA LA DMIGS NAS RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAR 'DZIN PA'I BLO SKYE,
gru.wylie: gnyis pa dngos gzhi ni, spyi bor bla ma lha bsgom bzhin pa'i ngang nas 'di ltar bsam ste, shes pa kho rang gi ngos nas lung ma bstan yin pa la, dang por bdag dang bdag gi ba la dmigs nas rang bzhin gyis grub par 'dzin pa'i blo skye
gru.english: Now the actual meditation here goes like this.  Maintain a continual awareness of your Angel Lama atop your head, and then take yourself through the following train of thought. In and of itself, the mind is simply neutral.  But then it begins to go through a certain process: first it looks upon either me or what is mine, and an idea develops that these exist through some nature of their own.

gru.acip: SNGON DU SEMS CAN THAMS CAD LA SEMS SNYOMS PA SGRUBS TE, MAR SHES NAS BYANG CHUB KYI SEMS KYI BAR BSGOM PA YIN PAS 'DI LA GNYIS, THUN GYI NGO BO LA JI LTAR BYA BA DANG , THUN MTSAMS SU JI LTAR BYA BA'I TSUL LO, ,DANG PO LA SBYOR DNGOS MJUG GSUM LAS, DANG PO SBYOR BA NI,
gru.wylie: sngon du sems can thams cad la sems snyoms pa sgrubs te, mar shes nas byang chub kyi sems kyi bar bsgom pa yin pas 'di la gnyis, thun gyi ngo bo la ji ltar bya ba dang , thun mtshams su ji ltar bya ba'i tshul lo, ,dang po la sbyor dngos mjug gsum las, dang po sbyor ba ni
gru.english: In the first of these two methods, before anything we try to develop a sense of equanimity towards every living being.  And then after that we take ourselves through the various steps, from recognizing that all beings are our mother up to the Wish for enlightenment itself. And so now we proceed in two parts:  what to do during our meditation sessions, and then what to do inbetween these sessions.  The first of these is divided into the  preparation, the actual session, and then the conclusion.  We begin now with the preparation.

gru.acip: DUS DE'I TSE LUNG BSTAN MKHAN PO MANG PO ZHIG GIS SKU TSE'I BAR CHAD CHE BAS TSE SGRUB MDZAD DGOS SO ZHES BSKUL BA NA CHOS BRGYAD 'GO SNYOMS KYI GSUNG 'DI LTAR BYON TE,
gru.wylie: dus de'i tshe lung bstan mkhan po mang po zhig gis sku tshe'i bar chad che bas tshe sgrub mdzad dgos so zhes bskul ba na chos brgyad 'go snyoms kyi gsung 'di ltar byon te
gru.english: In those days a great many seers came forth and warned him that powerful forces were at work which could cut short his time on this earth.  They implored him, saying that the traditional rituals for assuring the long and healthy life of a Lama must quickly be performed.  He replied to them with the following poem, about gaining a sense of equanimity in the face of the Eight Worldly Thoughts.

gru.acip: ,TSE RING DU GNAS NA RNAM DKAR GYI, ,LAM BZANG PO SGRUB PO SHI YANG BDE, ,LAS BAG CHAGS BZANG PO'I NGANG DU 'CHI, ,AA LA LA GSON SHI SEMS LA SNYOMS, ,TSE SGRUB KUN JI LTAR DGYES DGYES MDZOD,
gru.wylie: tshe ring du gnas na rnam dkar gyi, ,lam bzang po sgrub po shi yang bde, ,las bag chags bzang po'i ngang du 'chi, ,aa la la gson shi sems la snyoms, ,tshe sgrub kun ji ltar dgyes dgyes mdzod
gru.english: It's good To live a long life--because then You can practice For year after year that excellent path Of shining White deeds, and then die happily: Die, With your mind crammed full of excellent karmic seeds. A-la-la! Because then its all the same, to live or to die! So go ahead, Do all the long--life prayers you like!

gru.acip: ,DPAL PHUN TSOGS 'BYOR NA MCHOD SBYIN GYIS, ,TSOGS GSOG GO DBUL POR GYUR KYANG SLA, ,CHUD ZOS DOGS SER SNA'I SDUG BSNGAL MED, ,AA LA LA 'BYOR RGUD SEMS LA SNYOMS, ,NOR SGRUB KUN JI LTAR DGYES DGYES MDZOD,
gru.wylie: dpal phun tshogs 'byor na mchod sbyin gyis, ,tshogs gsog go dbul por gyur kyang sla, ,chud zos dogs ser sna'i sdug bsngal med, ,aa la la 'byor rgud sems la snyoms, ,nor sgrub kun ji ltar dgyes dgyes mdzod
gru.english: It's good To have lots of money and things, Because then You can make more offerings, and do charity; And then Be quite as happy, when you're poor again, Because then You're freed from that special pain Of refusing To share what you have with others, And the worry That you'll one day lose what you have. A-la-la! Because then it's all the same if you're rich or poor! So go ahead, Do all the rituals for wealth that you want!

gru.acip: ,DUS MA RUNGS SNYIGS MA LNGA BDO BAS, ,BDUD NAG PO'I RIGS RNAMS STOBS LDAN ZHING , ,LHA DKAR PO'I PHYOGS RNAMS SGRUB THAG RING , ,MI PHAL CHER MI DGE SDIG LA RNGAMS,
gru.wylie: dus ma rungs snyigs ma lnga bdo bas, ,bdud nag po'i rigs rnams stobs ldan zhing , ,lha dkar po'i phyogs rnams sgrub thag ring , ,mi phal cher mi dge sdig la rngams
gru.english: Evil times, These are, as the five degenerations spread. Hosts of demons, Forces of the dark, grow ever more powerful. Few can reach The forces of light, the holy angels. And the vast majority Of humankind thirsts only for wrongness. [Translator's note: The five degenerations are a shortening of the average life span; an increase in the length and force of mental afflictions in people's minds; a degeneration in the personalities of people, becoming more and more difficult to turn to a spiritual life; the coming of an era of violence; and a worsening of people's wordview.]

gru.acip: ,DON 'DO MED BYA BAS MI G-YENG BAR, ,DUS GTAN GYI MDUN MA SGRUB RE RAN, ,DA RAN PAR MA ZAD 'PHYIS PA TZAM,
gru.wylie: don 'do med bya bas mi g-yeng bar, ,dus gtan gyi mdun ma sgrub re ran, ,da ran par ma zad 'phyis pa tsam
gru.english: Keep yourself now, From being distracted by things of no real benefit; The time has come To accomplish your ultimate dreams-- No, not That the time has come, but almost too late already.

gru.acip: ,RJE 'DREN MCHOG RGYAL PO BLA MA'I ZHABS, ,'DI 'BRAL MED SPYI BO'I RGYAN BZUNG LA, ,BKA' MDO RGYUD RGYA MTSO'I BCUD BSDUS PA, ,LAM THABS SHES ZAB MO'I NYAMS LEN GYIS, ,DPAL SKU GSUM BDE BA CHEN PO DE, ,TSE 'DI LA BSGRUBS NA MI LEGS SAM, ,ZHES SOGS NYAMS MGUR MANG DU MDZAD DO,
gru.wylie: rje 'dren mchog rgyal po bla ma'i zhabs, ,'di 'bral med spyi bo'i rgyan bzung la, ,bka' mdo rgyud rgya mtsho'i bcud bsdus pa, ,lam thabs shes zab mo'i nyams len gyis, ,dpal sku gsum bde ba chen po de, ,tshe 'di la bsgrubs na mi legs sam, ,zhes sogs nyams mgur mang du mdzad do
gru.english: Come, offer your forehead To your Lord, your Lama, Highest Guide and King; Let it be a jewel That they wear upon their feet, and never remove. Throw your entire life Into practicing that profound path Which combines Both method and wisdom; The very cream Churned from the infinite ocean Of the Word of the Buddhas, Both open and secret. Wouldn't it be better if in this very life You and I could attain the unending bliss Of the three glorious bodies of an Angel? What think you? * * * Never to Leave the Highest Path We continue now with our review of the foundation commitments, in preparation for taking the vows of the secret way.  We have reached the second part of the more serious transgressions of the bodhisattva vows:

gru.acip: MA RANG SROG LA BABS PA LTA BU'I SDUG BSNGAL BYUNG BA LAS, BDAG CUNG ZAD NA PA LA SDUG BSNGAL CHE BAR BYAS, SDIG SDUG GTAM NGAN RANG SROG LA'ANG MA BLTAS PAR SHA THANG THANG DU BSGRUBS PA'I ZAS NOR THAMS CAD BDAG LA BRTZE BAS PHOG ,
gru.wylie: ma rang srog la babs pa lta bu'i sdug bsngal byung ba las, bdag cung zad na pa la sdug bsngal che bar byas, sdig sdug gtam ngan rang srog la'ang ma bltas par sha thang thang du bsgrubs pa'i zas nor thams cad bdag la brtse bas phog
gru.english: If it looked as though I might be falling even the least bit ill, this hurt my mother even more than something that might threaten her very life.  She went about obtaining, and then giving over for me, whatever money it took to assure that I would grow up healthy and strong.  And she did whatever she had to to get the money--even if it was immoral, or it physically hurt her, or damaged her reputation, or even endangered her own life.

gru.acip: MA RANG GI KHYER 'KHOS DANG BSTUN PA'I PHAN PA DANG BDE BA TSAD MED PA BSGRUBS, GNOD PA DANG SDUG BSNGAL TSAD MED PA LAS BSKYABS PAS DRIN SHIN TU CHE SNYAM DU BSAM,
gru.wylie: ma rang gi khyer 'khos dang bstun pa'i phan pa dang bde ba tshad med pa bsgrubs, gnod pa dang sdug bsngal tshad med pa las bskyabs pas drin shin tu che snyam du bsam
gru.english: In short, my mother did everything within her personal capacity to assure me limitless forms of help and happiness, and to protect me from limitless forms of suffering. Think thus how very kind your mother has been to you.

gru.acip: MA NAM BYAS PA'I TSE, PHAN PA DANG BDE BA TSAD MED PA BSGRUBS, GNOD PA DANG SDUG BSNGAL TSAD MED PA LAS BSKYABS, KHYAD PAR BDAG GIS 'DI MED NA CUNG ZAD KYANG SDOD MI TSUGS PA DANG , 'DIS KYANG BDAG MED NA CUNG ZAD KYANG SDOD MI TSUGS PA LTA BU'I YID GCUGS PA BGRANG LAS 'DAS PA BYAS,
gru.wylie: ma nam byas pa'i tshe, phan pa dang bde ba tshad med pa bsgrubs, gnod pa dang sdug bsngal tshad med pa las bskyabs, khyad par bdag gis 'di med na cung zad kyang sdod mi tshugs pa dang , 'dis kyang bdag med na cung zad kyang sdod mi tshugs pa lta bu'i yid gcugs pa bgrang las 'das pa byas
gru.english: �And during each of those lives as my mother, they worked to acquire for me unlimited forms of help and happiness.  They protected me from unlimited forms of harm and suffering.  We were in a position where, without them, I simply never would have made it--and the same could be said for them without me.  We have counted on each other for lifetimes beyond number.

gru.acip: DE NAS RE SHIG SKU MTSAMS MDZAD DE DPAL GSANG BA 'DUS PA'I ZAB LAM RIM PA LNGA LA NYAMS BZHES RTZE GCIG TU MDZAD PAS RIM LNGA'I RTOGS PA MNGON DU GYUR TE PHYI RABS KYI GDUL BYA RNAMS LA 'JAM MGON BLA MA'I RJES SU SLOB PAR 'DOD PA RNAMS KYIS RANG NGOS NAS NYAMS LEN BYUNG PHYIN RJE'I BSTAN PA 'DI LA TSE GCIG NYID LA ZUNG 'JUG BSGRUB PA'I NYE LAM 'DI LTA BU YOD DO ZHES RDO RJE'I SGRA DBYANGS SGROGS PAR MDZAD PA NI,
gru.wylie: de nas re shig sku mtshams mdzad de dpal gsang ba 'dus pa'i zab lam rim pa lnga la nyams bzhes rtse gcig tu mdzad pas rim lnga'i rtogs pa mngon du gyur te phyi rabs kyi gdul bya rnams la 'jam mgon bla ma'i rjes su slob par 'dod pa rnams kyis rang ngos nas nyams len byung phyin rje'i bstan pa 'di la tshe gcig nyid la zung 'jug bsgrub pa'i nye lam 'di lta bu yod do zhes rdo rje'i sgra dbyangs sgrogs par mdzad pa ni
gru.english: Following this he went into a personal retreat for some time, devoting himself single-mindedly to the practice of the Five Stages, a profound path within the teachings of the glorious Secret Collection.  As a result, he gained high realizations into these stages. He then burst forth with the following Song of the Diamond.  It is meant to declare the fact that there really does exist, here in the teachings of Lord Tsongkapa, a shortcut for achieving the Combination of the Two--tantric Buddhahood--in but this one brief life. The song tells the story of how he himself succeeded in actually using this shortcut; and he writes it specifically for future generations of disciples who hope to practice in the footsteps of our Lama, the Gentle Protector, Je Tsongkapa.

gru.acip: ,YANG CHOS 'KHOR PAD+MO'I LTE BA LA, ,DPAL YE SHES RDO RJE'I RANG BZHIN GYI, ,NOR BEEd'URA DKAR PO'I PI Wm NI, ,RGYUD 'OD ZER LNGA YI RI MO CAN, ,GDANGS MI SHIG RDO RJE GSUM GYI DBYANGS, ,DPAL MKHA' SPYOD GRUB PA'I GTAM SNYAN 'DIS, ,DBYE DKA' BA MA RIG MDUD PA 'BYED, ,'DI BSAMS SHING RJE BTZUN BLA MA'I DRIN, ,DRIN CHE BAR NGES SO BLA MA RJE,
gru.wylie: yang chos 'khor pad+mo'i lte ba la, ,dpal ye shes rdo rje'i rang bzhin gyi, ,nor beeDUra dkar po'i pi wM ni, ,rgyud 'od zer lnga yi ri mo can, ,gdangs mi shig rdo rje gsum gyi dbyangs, ,dpal mkha' spyod grub pa'i gtam snyan 'dis, ,dbye dka' ba ma rig mdud pa 'byed, ,'di bsams shing rje btsun bla ma'i drin, ,drin che bar nges so bla ma rje
gru.english: So too In the center of the lotus Of the chakra Of every existing thing I took up the lute Made of clearest crystal, Whose very nature Was the diamond of shining wisdom. I struck the strings, Light beams of five different hues, And played the song, A melody of the three Diamonds That can never be destroyed. With these glorious lines Of the victory, in attaining The glory Of the true Angel's heaven, I burst asunder The knot of ignorance, A bond So nearly beyond all breaking. When I think of this, I think of my Lama's kindness-- And oh how kind you have been to me, My Lama and my Lord.

gru.acip: ,PHA KHYOD ZHABS BSTEN CING MCHOD PA DANG , ,YID RTZE GCIG GDUNG BAS GSOL 'DEBS NA, ,MCHOG THUN MONGS DNGOS GRUB MA LUS KUN, ,DUS MYUR DU STZOL MDZAD AA TI SHA
gru.wylie: pha khyod zhabs bsten cing mchod pa dang , ,yid rtse gcig gdung bas gsol 'debs na, ,mchog thun mongs dngos grub ma lus kun, ,dus myur du stsol mdzad aa ti sha
gru.english: If a person, o Father, Kneels at your feet, And makes gifts to you, And with single-pointed Thoughts of devotion Begs you for your help, Then you grant them Each and every spiritual goal: Both the highest attainments, And those which are shared. And you grant them with speed, my Atisha,

gru.acip: ,TSE MI RTAG DGUN NYI LTA BU 'DI, ,DGRA CHOS BRGYAD RKYEN GYIS MI G-YENG BAR, ,DA RTZE GCIG DAM CHOS BSGRUB PA RU, ,RGYUD BYIN GYIS RLOBS SHIG 'BROM STON RJE,
gru.wylie: tshe mi rtag dgun nyi lta bu 'di, ,dgra chos brgyad rkyen gyis mi g-yeng bar, ,da rtse gcig dam chos bsgrub pa ru, ,rgyud byin gyis rlobs shig 'brom ston rje
gru.english: This life is fleeting, Brief as a winter's day; So the time has come For me to devote myself With a single mind To the holy Dharma. I can no longer Allow myself to wander off, Distracted by the enemy Of all these eight worldly thoughts. Bless my mind to do so, Dromtun you my Lord.

gru.acip: ,CHAGS SDANG GI TSA GRANG NAD MANG 'KHRUGS, ,LAS NGAN GYI 'KHRU SKYUGS KHRAG TU 'BAB, ,DGE LEGS KYI TSE SROG YANG YANG 'GAG ,YANG SRID DU SDUG BSNGAL PHUNG CHEN GRUB,
gru.wylie: chags sdang gi tsha grang nad mang 'khrugs, ,las ngan gyi 'khru skyugs khrag tu 'bab, ,dge legs kyi tshe srog yang yang 'gag ,yang srid du sdug bsngal phung chen grub
gru.english: And so then Their bodies are wracked By every Different kind of illness, The disorders Of heat or of cold-- Of liking Or disliking things, ignorantly. And then They collect bad karma: The poisons Of diarrhea and vomit Seep into The veins, and the life Of goodness Is stolen away, So that again They assure that a mountain of suffering Awaits them anew In the cycle of pain.

gru.acip: ,DE NAS BKRA SHIS LHUN PO'I DBYEN BSDUM MCHOD RTEN GSAR BZHENGS MDZAD DE RAB GNAS KYI SKABS GRUB CHEN SA RA HA DANG , GRUB CHEN CHOS RDO RJE GNYIS DNGOS SU BYON PA SOGS DAG PA'I GZIGS SNANG NGO MTSAR RMAD DU BYUNG BA MTHA' YAS PA BYUNG SNANG NGO ,
gru.wylie: de nas bkra shis lhun po'i dbyen bsdum mchod rten gsar bzhengs mdzad de rab gnas kyi skabs grub chen sa ra ha dang , grub chen chos rdo rje gnyis dngos su byon pa sogs dag pa'i gzigs snang ngo mtshar rmad du byung ba mtha' yas pa byung snang ngo
gru.english: He then made his way to Trashi Hlunpo, where he directed the construction of a new offering shrine dedicated to the cause of harmony among the monastic community.  During the ritual of consecration for this stupa, a countless number of amazing signs occurred, signs of the purity of his heart and the pureness of the world as he experienced it; signs for example like having the high secret masters Saraha and Chu Dorje actually appear in person at the ceremony. [Translator's note:  The high master Saraha was Arya Nagarjuna's tantric teacher; and Chu Dorje was a high Tibetan Lama who lived in the late 1400's.] * * * The Worst Deed of All is Simply a View The next section in our review of the root bodhisattva vows includes perhaps the most serious misdeed we can ever commit--which is simply a wrong way of viewing the world: something which then triggers every other mistake we can every make.

gru.acip: DE NAS RIM GYIS SPA GRO THIM BU DAR DKAR GYI BAR DU PHEBS, SPYIR LHO MON DE RANG RANG GI GRUB MTHA' DANG BLA MA SO SO'I PHYOGS 'DZIN GZHAN LAS CHE YANG RJE 'DI LA NI RANG NYID LA GRUB MTHA'I PHYOGS 'DZIN MED PAR KUN LA DAG SNANG MDZAD PA'I MTHUS THAMS CAD KYIS BSNYEN BKUR 'BUL BA ZHABS TOG TSAD MED PA BYUNG ZHING ,
gru.wylie: de nas rim gyis spa gro thim bu dar dkar gyi bar du phebs, spyir lho mon de rang rang gi grub mtha' dang bla ma so so'i phyogs 'dzin gzhan las che yang rje 'di la ni rang nyid la grub mtha'i phyogs 'dzin med par kun la dag snang mdzad pa'i mthus thams cad kyis bsnyen bkur 'bul ba zhabs tog tshad med pa byung zhing
gru.english: Gradually then he reached all the way to the Bhutanese areas of Padro, Timbu, and Darkar.  The southerners who lived here--the people called the Mun--had an even greater tendency than other people to stick with their own local religious beliefs and Lamas. Our Lord though had spent his whole life without any feelings of religious prejudice:  he had always tried to see the divine in the beliefs of all peoples.  And because of this karma, all those that he visited paid homage to him:  the respect and support he received were immeasurable.

gru.acip: KHYAD PAR THAMS CAD MKHYEN PA BSOD NAMS RGYA MTSO'I DNGUL GDUNG GI SGO RGYAN THAMS CAD BZHIG NAS MA RUNGS PAR BYAS PA, RJE 'DI PAS BSTAN RGYUN DANG RTEN 'BREL LA DGONGS TE GSER G-YU SOGS RIN PO CHE'I PHUNG PO LAS GSAR BSGRUBS MDZAD DE, THAMS CAD MKHYEN PA'I PHYAG RDZAS DAR LA BAB PA'I DUS SU BSGRUBS PA'I SGO RGYAN ZIL GYIS GNON PA LTA BU BZO BAR MDZAD DO,
gru.wylie: khyad par thams cad mkhyen pa bsod nams rgya mtsho'i dngul gdung gi sgo rgyan thams cad bzhig nas ma rungs par byas pa, rje 'di pas bstan rgyun dang rten 'brel la dgongs te gser g-yu sogs rin po che'i phung po las gsar bsgrubs mdzad de, thams cad mkhyen pa'i phyag rdzas dar la bab pa'i dus su bsgrubs pa'i sgo rgyan zil gyis gnon pa lta bu bzo bar mdzad do
gru.english: One thing especially he undertook.  There was a silver-plated tomb in which the remains of the Omniscient One, Sunam Gyatso, were interred.  [This was His Holiness the 3rd Dalai Lama, 1543-1588.] The ornamentation around the entrance to the tomb had all broken apart, and everything was in a state of disrepair.  Thinking that it would set in motion auspicious forces, and also help keep the teachings healthy in the world, the Lord set about having the entire tomb renovated, using great quantities of precious material like gold and turquoise.  He also ordered the preparation of exquisite, personal ritual instruments of the same material as the entrance way, for use by the Omniscient One when he had grown again to maturity.

gru.acip: 'PHRIN LAS 'BAD MED LHUN GYIS GRUB CING , SKU GSUNG THUGS KYI 'OD ZER RE RE TZAM SPROS PAS KYANG SEMS CAN DPAG TU MED PA THAMS CAD MKHYEN PA'I GO 'PHANG LA 'GOD NUS PA LA SOGS PA,
gru.wylie: 'phrin las 'bad med lhun gyis grub cing , sku gsung thugs kyi 'od zer re re tsam spros pas kyang sems can dpag tu med pa thams cad mkhyen pa'i go 'phang la 'god nus pa la sogs pa
gru.english: �Their holy deeds occur across the universe in every instant with complete spontaneity, simply by the very nature of things.  Every time they send forth a single ray of light, every time they do or speak or think a single thing at all, then this single beam of light has the capacity to bring an inconceivable number of suffering living beings to the same state of omniscience.  And these are only some of the high powers which they enjoy.

gru.acip: BRTZON 'GRUS KYI NYAMS LEN,
gru.wylie: brtson 'grus kyi nyams len
gru.english: d2. The practice of joyful effort (25a)

gru.acip: GZHAN YANG RANG NYID PHUN SUM TSOGS PA CIG BYED PAR 'DOD NAS 'KHOR BA THOG MA MED PA NAS, RANG GCES PAR BZUNG BAS RANG GZHAN GYI DON GANG YANG MA GRUB PAR MA ZAD, SDUG BSNGAL SNA TSOGS ZHIG MYONG BAR 'DUG
gru.wylie: gzhan yang rang nyid phun sum tshogs pa cig byed par 'dod nas 'khor ba thog ma med pa nas, rang gces par bzung bas rang gzhan gyi don gang yang ma grub par ma zad, sdug bsngal sna tshogs zhig myong bar 'dug
gru.english: And that's not all.  For time with no beginning here in the cycle of pain, I have cherished only myself, seeking the best of things only for myself.  But doing so hasn't accomplished anything for me or for others.  On the contrary; it has forced us to undergo an endless variety of sufferings.

gru.acip: ,BYANG CHUB MCHOG GI SEMS GCIG SKYE 'GYUR LA, ,DE 'DRA'I RNAM PAS TSOGS GZHAN RE RE ZHING , ,SGRUB DGOS GYUR KYANG SNYING RJES SKYO BA MED, ,BYANG CHUB DAM PA SGYID LUG MED PAR SGRUB,
gru.wylie: byang chub mchog gi sems gcig skye 'gyur la, ,de 'dra'i rnam pas tshogs gzhan re re zhing , ,sgrub dgos gyur kyang snying rjes skyo ba med, ,byang chub dam pa sgyid lug med par sgrub
gru.english: Suppose that it takes this long To reach a single moment Of the Wish for highest Buddhahood; Or to accumulate any one of the deeds We need to reach this state. Still you must use your compassion: Use it to stop any hesitation, Stop any trace of feeling discouraged. Reach your enlightenment.

gru.acip: DE NAS NA TSOD LDAN ZHES PA SHING MO PHAG GI LO 'TSUB LHONGS CHE ZHING PHYI NANG GI MTSAN LTAS KYANG 'TSUB 'GYUR CHE BA BYUNG NAS BKRA SHIS LHUN PO'I BLA MA RNAMS KYIS GTZOS RJE NYID KYI SLOB MA GTZO CHE BA MANG POS SKU TSE TSE SGRUB MDZAD DGOS ZHES GSOL BA BTAB CING RKYEN BZLOG DGOS TSUL NAN GYIS ZHUS KYANG
gru.wylie: de nas na tshod ldan zhes pa shing mo phag gi lo 'tshub lhongs che zhing phyi nang gi mtshan ltas kyang 'tshub 'gyur che ba byung nas bkra shis lhun po'i bla ma rnams kyis gtsos rje nyid kyi slob ma gtso che ba mang pos sku tshe tshe sgrub mdzad dgos zhes gsol ba btab cing rkyen bzlog dgos tshul nan gyis zhus kyang
gru.english: In the year of Youth then--which would be the female wood pig year [1635]--there were terrible signs of impending doom: great inner and outer portents of upheaval.  Many of the Lord's major disciples, headed by the lamas of Trashi Hlunpo, came to him, begging him, saying that a ceremony for his long life must be conducted, imploring him to allow that rituals be held to prevent any obstacles to his health.

gru.acip: RJE NYID NI SNGON GYI GRUB CHEN RNAMS KYI RNAM THAR LTAR 'JIG RTEN CHOS BRGYAD 'GO SNYOMS ZHING , RKYEN BZANG NGAN GANG BYUNG YANG LAM DU 'KHYER BA LAS RKYEN BZLOG SOGS MA MDZAD CING , CHOS BRGYAD 'GO SNYOMS PA'I GSUNG YANG 'DI LTAR BYON TE,
gru.wylie: rje nyid ni sngon gyi grub chen rnams kyi rnam thar ltar 'jig rten chos brgyad 'go snyoms zhing , rkyen bzang ngan gang byung yang lam du 'khyer ba las rkyen bzlog sogs ma mdzad cing , chos brgyad 'go snyoms pa'i gsung yang 'di ltar byon te
gru.english: The Lord though refused to have any such ceremonies undertaken.  He persisted in following in the footsteps of the great adepts of the past: he simply continued on in tasks like smashing and flattening the Eight Worldly Thoughts in his own mind; and working to turn everything that happened--good or bad--into a path to something higher.  At this point he also came out with the following words on smashing those same eight thoughts:

gru.acip: ,GANG LA BRTEN NA BSLU BA MED PA'I, ,DKON MCHOG GSUM DANG RJE BTZUN BLA MA, ,DBYER MED SNYING GA'I PAD+MORA BZHUGS LA, ,MCHOG DANG THUN MONG DNGOS GRUB KUN STZOL,
gru.wylie: gang la brten na bslu ba med pa'i, ,dkon mchog gsum dang rje btsun bla ma, ,dbyer med snying ga'i pad+mora bzhugs la, ,mchog dang thun mong dngos grub kun stsol
gru.english: I beseech you, my holy Lama-- You who are indivisible From those who can never Lead us wrong, the Jewels-- To come and seat yourself Upon the lotus within my heart; Granting then all attainments, Both the highest, and the shared.

gru.acip: ,DE BAS NAM MKHA' GNAS PA DE SRID, ,SKYE RGA NA 'CHI MED PA'I PHUN TSOGS, ,BSGRUBS NA 'GRUB CING SGRUB DBANG YOD DUS, ,SGRUB PAR MI BYED BYIS PA'I SPYOD PA,
gru.wylie: de bas nam mkha' gnas pa de srid, ,skye rga na 'chi med pa'i phun tshogs, ,bsgrubs na 'grub cing sgrub dbang yod dus, ,sgrub par mi byed byis pa'i spyod pa
gru.english: But there is something different-- A perfect place Beyond being born Once more like this; Beyond getting old; Beyond all sickness; Beyond death itself: A place which instead Stays as long as the sky. Reach out, and you will reach it; Reach out, while you still have the strength; And if you miss the chance to reach You are nothing if not A foolish child.

gru.acip: ,SDIG SDUG GTAM NGAN KHYAD DU BSAD NAS, ,SKYID KYANG MI 'TSENGS SDUG MI PHUNG BA'I, ,TSE 'DI'I PHUN TSOGS SGRUB RNAMS MTHONG TSE,
gru.wylie: sdig sdug gtam ngan khyad du bsad nas, ,skyid kyang mi 'tshengs sdug mi phung ba'i, ,tshe 'di'i phun tshogs sgrub rnams mthong tshe
gru.english: Look at all of you, Reaching for all those Supposedly good things Of this life; Things that make you feel good But never satisfy you-- Pleasure that ruins, Hard-won at the cost Of ignoring what might hurt others, The pain, and others' disdain.

gru.acip: ,'JIG RTEN 'DI YI BDE SKYID SGRUB DANG , ,GRUB RNAMS BRTAN DANG RGYAS PA'I DON DU, ,BZLAS BRJOD RIM GRO MCHOD SBYIN LA SOGS, ,BRTZON PA CHEN POS LEGS PAR BSGRUBS KYANG ,
gru.wylie: 'jig rten 'di yi bde skyid sgrub dang , ,grub rnams brtan dang rgyas pa'i don du, ,bzlas brjod rim gro mchod sbyin la sogs, ,brtson pa chen pos legs par bsgrubs kyang
gru.english: Oh you've put your heart into it; You've read the prayers for the families, Paid your respects, made your offerings, And you got what you wanted: Some kind of pleasure, here in the world-- Consolidating, investing, multiplying All the money you made.

gru.acip: ,RANG DON KHO NAR NOR DANG TSE SGRUB, ,DBANG SDUD DRAG PO'I MNGON SPYOD LA SOGS, ,NGAN SONG SGRUB PA'I MYUR LAM YIN ZHES, ,MDO RGYUD KUN LAS GSUNGS PA YIN NAM,
gru.wylie: rang don kho nar nor dang tshe sgrub, ,dbang sdud drag po'i mngon spyod la sogs, ,ngan song sgrub pa'i myur lam yin zhes, ,mdo rgyud kun las gsungs pa yin nam
gru.english: Don't you recall That thing they said In all the open and secret books? If you want the very quickest path To reach the realms of misery, Then throw yourself into secret rites To reach money, to reach long life, To gain power, to destroy your enemies-- All for nobody but yourself.

gru.acip: ,CHOS BRGYAD 'CHING BA'I LCAGS SGROG SPANGS NAS, ,BDAG NYID PHYIR DU BRGYA PHRAG DKA' BAS, ,'DI SNANG BDE SKYID 'BA' ZHIG SGRUB PHYIR, ,BZLAS BRJOD DKA' THUB RNAM DKAR DGE TSOGS, ,BRTZON PA'I 'BRAS BU JI LTAR 'GYUR ZHES, ,SHES LDAN RNAMS LA DAL BUS GLENG NGO, ,ZHES,
gru.wylie: chos brgyad 'ching ba'i lcags sgrog spangs nas, ,bdag nyid phyir du brgya phrag dka' bas, ,'di snang bde skyid 'ba' zhig sgrub phyir, ,bzlas brjod dka' thub rnam dkar dge tshogs, ,brtson pa'i 'bras bu ji ltar 'gyur zhes, ,shes ldan rnams la dal bus gleng ngo, ,zhes
gru.english: All this is just a little relaxing talk Between me and those of you Who have a good mind; And all I have to say to you is, "Throw off now the iron fetters Of the eight worldly thoughts. Stop and think, think carefully, About what result will come to you If you give yourself up to holy practices Of reciting the sacred scriptures And undertaking spiritual hardships, Making a thousand devoted efforts To get some worldly gain for yourself, All of it only--for yourself. " * * * Deeds of Lesser Benefit We continue with the secondary offenses against the vows of the bodhisattva, from Geshe Tsewang Samdrup's String of Shining Jewels:

gru.acip: ,GZHON NU DANG LANG TSO DAR BA'I DUS, ,SDIG GROGS DANG DUG GSUM SHUGS DRAG GIS, ,BSLAD NAS KYANG NGAN 'GRO'I SDUG BSNGAL RGYU, ,BAG MED DU SGRUB NA CI RANG DRAG ,
gru.wylie: gzhon nu dang lang tsho dar ba'i dus, ,sdig grogs dang dug gsum shugs drag gis, ,bslad nas kyang ngan 'gro'i sdug bsngal rgyu, ,bag med du sgrub na ci rang drag
gru.english: One more time then Through growing up One more time through Being grown up-- Mixing one more time With the wrong people, Infected by the power Of their triple poison-- Getting things ready One more time For a trip to the pain Of the lower realms Despite myself-- I'm not really sure now What . . . to do . . .

gru.acip: BYANG SEMS RNAMS MYANG 'DAS LA DGA' BAR MI BYA ZHING , DE LA RGYAB KYI PHYOGS PAR BYA, NYON MONGS PA 'JIGS PAR MI BYA ZHING , DE DAG LAS SEMS SHIN TU DBEN PAR MI BYA STE, BSKAL PA GRANGS MED GSUM DU 'KHOR BAR 'KHOR ZHING , BYANG CHUB BSGRUB DGOS PA BLTA ZHING , DE SKAD SMRA NA 'KHOR BAR GCIG BU 'GROD PAR SEMS PA'I NYES BYAS 14,
gru.wylie: byang sems rnams myang 'das la dga' bar mi bya zhing , de la rgyab kyi phyogs par bya, nyon mongs pa 'jigs par mi bya zhing , de dag las sems shin tu dben par mi bya ste, bskal pa grangs med gsum du 'khor bar 'khor zhing , byang chub bsgrub dgos pa blta zhing , de skad smra na 'khor bar gcig bu 'grod par sems pa'i nyes byas 14
gru.english: (14) The secondary offense of thinking that you only have to travel through the circle of suffering life You commit this when you think to yourself, and also say to others, the following: "Bodhisattvas don't like to reach nirvana; in fact, they work for the opposite. They have no fear of the mental afflictions, and they do not try to keep their minds totally away from these thoughts. They only want to achieve Buddhahood, and they wander around in the circle of suffering life for three 'countless' eons."

gru.acip: DE'I PHYIR DU SEMS CAN THAMS CAD DGRAR LANGS KYANG KHRO BA'I SEMS SKAD CIG KYANG MI BSKYED PAR GNOD LAN DU PHAN PA BSGRUBS TE, RANG GZHAN GYI RGYUD LA BZOD PA'I PHAR PHYIN LA SOGS PA'I SANGS RGYAS KYI CHOS RNAMS YONGS SU RDZOGS PAR BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: de'i phyir du sems can thams cad dgrar langs kyang khro ba'i sems skad cig kyang mi bskyed par gnod lan du phan pa bsgrubs te, rang gzhan gyi rgyud la bzod pa'i phar phyin la sogs pa'i sangs rgyas kyi chos rnams yongs su rdzogs par bya'o
gru.english: In order to do so, I will complete within myself, and within every other living being, all the high qualities of a Buddha: those of perfection of patience and all the rest.  To attain this patience, I will never allow myself a single moment of anger at others--even if every living being that there is should suddenly rise up against me, as my enemy.  For every harm they do to me, I will return some helpful good to them.

gru.acip: DE NAS BRTZON 'GRUS KYI NYAMS LEN NI, SPYI BOR BLA MA LHA BSGOM BZHIN PA'I NGANG x MA SEMS CAN THAMS CAD KYI DON DU MYUR DU YANG DAG PAR RDZOGS PA'I SANGS RGYAS KYI GO 'PHANG THOB PAR BYA,
gru.wylie: de nas brtson 'grus kyi nyams len ni, spyi bor bla ma lha bsgom bzhin pa'i ngang x ma sems can thams cad kyi don du myur du yang dag par rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas kyi go 'phang thob par bya
gru.english: This brings us to the practice of joyful effort.  Picture your Lama Angel at the tip of your head, as before, and take yourself through the following train of thought: For the sake of every living being--every one of them my own mother--I will now attain the state of a fully enlightened Buddha, as quickly as possible.

gru.acip: DE'I PHYIR DU MTSAN DPE LA SOGS PA SANGS RGYAS KYI CHOS RE RE BSGRUB PA DANG , SBYIN PA LA SOGS PA BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA'I CHOS RE RE BSGRUB PA'I PHYIR DU BSKAL PA 'BUM PHRAG RE RER MNAR MED DU GNAS NAS SANGS RGYAS KYI GO 'PHANG BSGRUB DGOS NA'ANG BRTZON PA MI 'DOR ZHING SPRO BA BSKYED NAS,
gru.wylie: de'i phyir du mtshan dpe la sogs pa sangs rgyas kyi chos re re bsgrub pa dang , sbyin pa la sogs pa byang chub sems dpa'i chos re re bsgrub pa'i phyir du bskal pa 'bum phrag re rer mnar med du gnas nas sangs rgyas kyi go 'phang bsgrub dgos na'ang brtson pa mi 'dor zhing spro ba bskyed nas
gru.english: And I will take joy in this task--I will never for a moment relinquish in my effort--even if reaching the state of enlightenment requires that I remain in the lowest of all the hell realms for billions upon billions of years, in order to acquire any single one of qualities of a Buddha, like the marks and signs of their holy body; or to succeed in any one of the deeds of a bodhisattva, such as the perfection of giving.

gru.acip: DGE 'DUN STONG RVA CAN BRGAL BA LO GRANGS DE SNYED DU THAMS CAD MKHYEN PA BSGRUB PA LA RTZE GCIG TU THUGS BRTUN NAS 'DUN PA RMAD DU BYUNG BA'I RNAM THAR LA 'GOD PAR BYAS PA'I PHYIR DANG , JI SKAD DU,
gru.wylie: dge 'dun stong rva can brgal ba lo grangs de snyed du thams cad mkhyen pa bsgrub pa la rtse gcig tu thugs brtun nas 'dun pa rmad du byung ba'i rnam thar la 'god par byas pa'i phyir dang , ji skad du
gru.english: The point is that this one monk, in a certain number of years, would surpass thousands upon thousands of other monks--he would set his single-pointed attention fiercely upon attaining the state of omniscience, and in this extraordinary aspiration his single life would embody the efforts of thousands of other people's lives.  As we also hear [in The Prayer of Samantabhadra]--

gru.acip: 'DI YAN NYES BYAS GSUM NI BRTZON 'GRUS KYI MI MTHUN PHYOGS SO,
gru.wylie: 'di yan nyes byas gsum ni brtson 'grus kyi mi mthun phyogs so
gru.english: The three secondary offenses just listed all work against the practice of effort. The Asian Classics Institute ____________________________________________________________________________ Diamond Mountain University Tantric Series Course III The Path to Bliss, Part Three Reading Five: A Perfect Beginner's Meditation * * * The Light of a Rainbow One of the great strengths of His Holiness the First Panchen Lama's presentation of the steps of the path to enlightenment is the amount of help he gives us in developing the last two perfections--meditation and wisdom: the foundation of worldview.  We go turn to them now, in the Path to Bliss.

gru.acip: STAN BDE BA LA LUS DRANG POR BSRANG , RKANG PA RDO RJE SKYIL KRUNG DANG , LAG PA GNYIS MNYAM GZHAG GI PHYAG RGYA BCAS RLUNG CHAM LA 'BEBS PA SOGS ZHI GNAS BSGRUB PA'I RGYU TSOGS BSTEN PA SNGON DU BTANG NAS,
gru.wylie: stan bde ba la lus drang por bsrang , rkang pa rdo rje skyil krung dang , lag pa gnyis mnyam gzhag gi phyag rgya bcas rlung cham la 'bebs pa sogs zhi gnas bsgrub pa'i rgyu tshogs bsten pa sngon du btang nas
gru.english: Find yourself a comfortable meditation seat.  Sit upon it with a straight back, and with your legs folded in the lotus posture.  Place your hands in the meditation gesture.  Do all the practices that help bring on stillness: things like bringing your breath down.  All of these are preliminary to the actual practice of meditation.

gru.acip: DNGOS GZHI LA ZHI GNAS BSGRUB PA'I DMIGS RTEN DU MA ZHIG GSUNGS KYANG GTZO BOR SANGS RGYAS RJES SU DRAN PA'I MCHOG TU 'GYUR BA DANG , SNGAGS KYI LHA'I RNAL 'BYOR SGOM PA'I SNOD RUNG DU 'GYUR BA SOGS DGOS PA DU MA YOD PAS LHA'I SKU LA DMIGS PA LEGS LA,
gru.wylie: dngos gzhi la zhi gnas bsgrub pa'i dmigs rten du ma zhig gsungs kyang gtso bor sangs rgyas rjes su dran pa'i mchog tu 'gyur ba dang , sngags kyi lha'i rnal 'byor sgom pa'i snod rung du 'gyur ba sogs dgos pa du ma yod pas lha'i sku la dmigs pa legs la
gru.english: Now as for the actual session, a great many meditation objects for developing stillness are described in the teachings.  For the most part though the practice of bringing to mind the Buddha is the highest.  It also has many other purposes, such as helping you become a worthy vessel for the Yoga of the Angel in the secret way.  As such, it is best to focus your meditation upon the holy form of a divine being.

gru.acip: SEMS DMIGS RTEN LA RTZE GCIG TU GTANG BA DE NYID BLO'I YUL DU MA BRJED PAR NGAN TZAM DRAN TZAM BYAS NAS, BLO DE'I RGYUN SKYONG BA NI LAS DANG PO PAS SEMS GNAS SGRUB PA'I THABS DAM PA'O,,
gru.wylie: sems dmigs rten la rtse gcig tu gtang ba de nyid blo'i yul du ma brjed par ngan tsam dran tsam byas nas, blo de'i rgyun skyong ba ni las dang po pas sems gnas sgrub pa'i thabs dam pa'o
gru.english: Continue then with the mind placed single-pointedly upon the object of your meditation.  Try just to get to where you are not losing this object completely--where you can keep it in mind even in some cursory way, and maintain some continuity of the visualization.  All this is a perfect method for a beginner to get themselves up to one of the nine levels of meditation.

gru.acip: MDOR NA TING NGE 'DZIN RNAM PAR DAG PA CIG SGOM NA, NYES PA LNGA SPONG 'DU BYED BRGYAD, ,BSTEN PA'I RGYU LAS BYUNG BA'O, ZHES GSUNGS PA LTAR, NYES PA LNGA SPONG BA'I GNYEN PO 'DU BYED BRGYAD BSTEN PA'I SGO NAS SGRUB DGOS TE,
gru.wylie: mdor na ting nge 'dzin rnam par dag pa cig sgom na, nyes pa lnga spong 'du byed brgyad, ,bsten pa'i rgyu las byung ba'o, zhes gsungs pa ltar, nyes pa lnga spong ba'i gnyen po 'du byed brgyad bsten pa'i sgo nas sgrub dgos te
gru.english: To put it briefly, anyone who hopes to reach some genuine state of concentration in their meditation would do well to follow the advice expressed in the lines [from Lord Maitreya's Distinguishing between the Middle and the Extremes]: It comes from a certain cause: Eliminating the five problems of meditation, And applying the eight different actions. The point here is of course that real meditation can only be attained if we know how to apply the eight different actions as antidotes to the five typical problems that come up during meditation.

gru.acip: DE YANG TING NGE 'DZIN LA SBYOR BA'I TSE LE LO NYES PA YIN PAS, DE'I GNYEN PO BZHI STE, TING NGE 'DZIN GYI YON TAN MTHONG BA'I DAD PA DANG , TING NGE 'DZIN LA DON GNYER GYI 'DUN PA DANG , TING NGE 'DZIN LA RTZOL BA'I BRTZON 'GRUS DANG , RTZOL BA'I 'BRAS BU SHIN SBYANGS,
gru.wylie: de yang ting nge 'dzin la sbyor ba'i tshe le lo nyes pa yin pas, de'i gnyen po bzhi ste, ting nge 'dzin gyi yon tan mthong ba'i dad pa dang , ting nge 'dzin la don gnyer gyi 'dun pa dang , ting nge 'dzin la rtsol ba'i brtson 'grus dang , rtsol ba'i 'bras bu shin sbyangs
gru.english: Now when we first try to sit ourselves down to meditate, the problem of not feeling like meditating comes up.  There are four corrections to this problem.  The first is faith--an ability to see the great benefits of getting good at deep meditation. The second is really wanting to meditate: a strong desire to master it.  The third is being willing to make great effort--to do the hard work that mastering meditation requires.  The fourth correction here is actually getting good at meditation, which is the result of the hard work.

gru.acip: DE SKABS DBEN PA'I GNAS SU SGRUB PA SNYING POR MDZAD PA LA THUGS SMON PA'I GSUNG DBYANGS 'DI LTAR MDZAD DE,
gru.wylie: de skabs dben pa'i gnas su sgrub pa snying por mdzad pa la thugs smon pa'i gsung dbyangs 'di ltar mdzad de
gru.english: At this point he composed the following song, as a heart-prayer that he would be able to take himself to some isolated place, and devote his entire attention to his practice.

gru.acip: ,RJE SANGS RGYAS KUN GYI YE SHES NYID, ,PHA 'GRAN ZLA MED PA'I BLO BZANG GRAGS, ,MI BDAG SNYING PAD+MO'I DBUS BZHUGS LA, ,MCHOG THUN MONG DNGOS GRUB STZAL DU GSOL,
gru.wylie: rje sangs rgyas kun gyi ye shes nyid, ,pha 'gran zla med pa'i blo bzang grags, ,mi bdag snying pad+mo'i dbus bzhugs la, ,mchog thun mong dngos grub stsal du gsol
gru.english: You are the Lord, The very essence of the wisdom Of every enlightened being there is. You are my father, Lobsang Drakpa, A father that none can compare with. Come, o Lord of Living Kind, And seat yourself here in the midst Of the lotus at this one man's heart. Grant me all the goals-- Both those of the world, And those beyond it.

gru.acip: ,LAM THABS SHES ZAB MO'I NYAMS LEN GYIS, ,DGRA SKYE RGA NA 'CHI RTZAD BCAD NAS, ,DUS RTAG TU 'DU 'BRAL MI BYED PA'I, ,LUS LONGS SPYOD GROGS SOGS SGRUB PAR SMON,
gru.wylie: lam thabs shes zab mo'i nyams len gyis, ,dgra skye rga na 'chi rtsad bcad nas, ,dus rtag tu 'du 'bral mi byed pa'i, ,lus longs spyod grogs sogs sgrub par smon
gru.english: Use the deep practice, The path that combines method and wisdom, To rip out the hearts Of your enemies: that birth, that aging, the sickness and death. In every moment of your life Pray for a body and things and friends that no longer come and go.

gru.acip: ,TSUL 'DI LTAR RE BA'I DON PO RNAMS, ,SKYABS BSLU MED BLA MA DKON MCHOG GIS, ,YUN MI RING MYUR DU 'GRUB PA YI, ,GEGS ZHI ZHING MTHUN RKYEN 'GRUB PAR MDZOD, ,CES SO,
gru.wylie: tshul 'di ltar re ba'i don po rnams, ,skyabs bslu med bla ma dkon mchog gis, ,yun mi ring myur du 'grub pa yi, ,gegs zhi zhing mthun rkyen 'grub par mdzod, ,ces so
gru.english: By the power Of my Lama and the Triple Gem, which cannot ever fail, May we quickly attain All the deep goals we hope for--all those expressed in these lines. May every obstacle That might keep them from coming true soon be stopped, And every Helpful condition that might give them birth soon appear. * * * Promising not to Meditate Poorly We continue with the explanation of the secondary offenses against the vows of the bodhisattva, from Geshe Tsewang Samdrup.  Meditating seriously is a theme.

gru.acip: DE GNYIS RE MOS SU BYAS NAS BSKYANGS PAS TING NGE 'DZIN SKYON MED 'GRUB KYI, NGES SHES KYI 'DZIN STANGS NGAR LDAN DU BYAS PA'I GSAL CHA MED PA'I DNGAS PA TZAM LA YID BRTAN MI BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: de gnyis re mos su byas nas bskyangs pas ting nge 'dzin skyon med 'grub kyi, nges shes kyi 'dzin stangs ngar ldan du byas pa'i gsal cha med pa'i dngas pa tsam la yid brtan mi bya'o
gru.english: If you can maintain your meditation, alternating between these two steps, then you will attain deep meditation which is flawless.  Be careful not to trust a simple feeling of brightness that lacks though a state of clarity where you have a firm hold on the object, with intensity.

gru.acip: DE LTA BU'I TSUL GYIS LEGS PAR BSKYANGS PAS SEMS GNAS PA DGU RIM GYIS THOB NAS LUS SEMS SHIN SBYANGS DANG BCAS PA'I ZHI GNAS 'GRUB PAR 'GYUR RO,,
gru.wylie: de lta bu'i tshul gyis legs par bskyangs pas sems gnas pa dgu rim gyis thob nas lus sems shin sbyangs dang bcas pa'i zhi gnas 'grub par 'gyur ro
gru.english: If you are able to maintain the above procedure properly, then you will pass--one by one--through the nine levels of meditation, and thus achieve stillness, along with the practiced ease of body and mind that accompanies it.

gru.acip: ,KHONG GZHAN TSO LTA KHRID DANG PHYAG CHEN SGOM, ,MI KHO BO LA BSGOM BYA SGOM BYED DANG , ,DON 'DI BSGOM GYI MTSAN MA RDUL TZAM MED, ,SGOM SGRUB KUN JI LTAR DGYES DGYES MDZOD,
gru.wylie: khong gzhan tsho lta khrid dang phyag chen sgom, ,mi kho bo la bsgom bya sgom byed dang , ,don 'di bsgom gyi mtshan ma rdul tsam med, ,sgom sgrub kun ji ltar dgyes dgyes mdzod
gru.english: He gets others To meditate on the teachings of emptiness, and the great seal-- But he himself Never meditates, and there's nothing he meditates on-- There's not the slightest Sign that he's meditated on a single atom of this truth-- Go ahead, Meditate all you want, practice all you want . . .

gru.acip: PHUNG PO LNGA TSOGS TZAM PA'AM LUS SEMS GNYIS TSOGS TZAM PA'I BAM ME BA DE'I STENG DU RTOG PAS BTAGS PA TZAM MA YIN PAR, DANG PO NAS TSUGS THUB TU GRUB PA'I NGA ZHIG YOD PAR 'DZIN PA NI, NGAR 'DZIN LHAN SKYES KYIS NGA'I 'DZIN TSUL YIN LA,
gru.wylie: phung po lnga tshogs tsam pa'am lus sems gnyis tshogs tsam pa'i bam me ba de'i steng du rtog pas btags pa tsam ma yin par, dang po nas tshugs thub tu grub pa'i nga zhig yod par 'dzin pa ni, ngar 'dzin lhan skyes kyis nga'i 'dzin tshul yin la
gru.english: But neither does "me " seem to me to be just an idea applied to the whole package of the five parts of me, or two the two of my body and my mind taken together.  I grasp, rather, to some solid "me " that has existed on its own, since the very beginning.  That's then how the inborn grasping to a "me " holds on to its "me. "

gru.acip: ,LAS DGE SDIG 'BRAS BU MA DMIGS SHING , ,LAM SPANG GNYEN DGAG BSGRUB DANG YANG BRAL, ,YID 'BAD PAS BSGRUBS PA'I 'BRAS BUS DBEN, ,DBYINGS 'DI 'DRA RGYAL BA'I DGONGS PA SNYAM,
gru.wylie: las dge sdig 'bras bu ma dmigs shing , ,lam spang gnyen dgag bsgrub dang yang bral, ,yid 'bad pas bsgrubs pa'i 'bras bus dben, ,dbyings 'di 'dra rgyal ba'i dgongs pa snyam
gru.english: Karma-- The fruits of good and evil deeds Never existed at all. The path-- Things to stop, things to stop them, Reaching, avoiding, never happened. The mind-- Is completely void of all those goals You worked so hard to attain. This . . . place-- It seems to me Is what the Victors wanted to teach us.

gru.acip: GZHAN YANG DE LTAR BZUNG BA LTAR GYI NGA DE PHUNG PO LNGA DANG GCIG TU GRUB NA PHUNG PO LNGA SKYE 'JIG BYED PA BZHIN DU BLO NGES BZUNG BA LTAR GYI TSUGS THUB TU GRUB PA'I NGA DE YANG SKYE 'JIG BYED PAR 'GYUR LA,
gru.wylie: gzhan yang de ltar bzung ba ltar gyi nga de phung po lnga dang gcig tu grub na phung po lnga skye 'jig byed pa bzhin du blo nges bzung ba ltar gyi tshugs thub tu grub pa'i nga de yang skye 'jig byed par 'gyur la
gru.english: Suppose still that the "me " I hold on to the way we spoke of before were one with my five different parts--the five heaps.  This "me " that exists the way I so strongly hold it to be--this very solid, self-standing "me "--would then have to be something that was in a continual state of growing and decaying, just as the five parts themselves are in this same state.

gru.acip: DE LTAR NA SKYE 'JIG BYED PA'I NGA DE'I SKAD CIG SNGA PHYI RNAMS GCIG TU GRUB BAM THA DAD DU GRUB,
gru.wylie: de ltar na skye 'jig byed pa'i nga de'i skad cig snga phyi rnams gcig tu grub bam tha dad du grub
gru.english: And if "me " were in this same state, then I'd have to ask myself a question: "Let me think about the successive instants of this 'me'--this me that is in a continual state of growing and decaying.  Do these instants amount to one thing, or to separate things? "

gru.acip: GCIG TU GRUB NA TSE SNGA PHYI'I NGA DANG TSE 'DI'I NGA GSUM CHA MED GCIG TU 'GYUR LA,
gru.wylie: gcig tu grub na tshe snga phyi'i nga dang tshe 'di'i nga gsum cha med gcig tu 'gyur la
gru.english: If they amount to one thing, then the me of my last life, and the me of my next life, and the me in this life right now--these three--are all a single, indivisible thing.

gru.acip: THA DAD DU GRUB NA, SPYIR THA DAD TZAM LA 'BREL MED THA DAD YIN MI DGOS KYANG , RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA'I THA DAD YIN NA 'BREL PA GTAN NAS MED PA'I THA DAD YIN DGOS PAS,
gru.wylie: tha dad du grub na, spyir tha dad tsam la 'brel med tha dad yin mi dgos kyang , rang bzhin gyis grub pa'i tha dad yin na 'brel pa gtan nas med pa'i tha dad yin dgos pas
gru.english: And suppose those successive instants amounted to separate things.  Now in general, it's not the case that if things are simply separate from each other then they are necessarily separate from, and totally unrelated to, each other.  It is the case though that--if anything were separate from another thing and also existed through some nature of its own--then the two things would have to be separate in a way that could never allow for any relationship between them at all.

gru.acip: DES NA BLO DES BZUNG BA LTAR GYI NGA DE PHUNG PO LNGA DANG GCIG TU MA GRUB BO SNYAM DU BSAM,
gru.wylie: des na blo des bzung ba ltar gyi nga de phung po lnga dang gcig tu ma grub bo snyam du bsam
gru.english: Decide then to yourself that no "me " which exists in the way that the tendency we've described above holds that it does could ever be one with the five parts of yourself.

gru.acip: GZHAN YANG DE LTAR BZUNG BA'I NGA DE PHUNG PO LNGA DANG GCIG TU GRUB NA, BDEN PAR GRUB PA'I GCIG YIN PAS CHA THAMS CAD NAS THAMS CAD DU GCIG TU 'GYUR LA,
gru.wylie: gzhan yang de ltar bzung ba'i nga de phung po lnga dang gcig tu grub na, bden par grub pa'i gcig yin pas cha thams cad nas thams cad du gcig tu 'gyur la
gru.english: And suppose once more that the "me " which we hold on to that way were one with the five parts to yourself.  It would then have to be a single thing which existed in reality.  And then it would have to be one from every possible point of view.

gru.acip: DE LTAR NA NGA'AM BDAG PHUNG PO LNGA NYE BAR LEN PA PO DANG , PHUNG PO LNGA NGA'AM BDAG GIS NYE BAR BLANG BYA MA YIN PA SOGS KYI NYES PA DU MA YOD PAS, DE LTAR BZUNG BA'I NGA DE PHUNG PO LNGA DANG GCIG TU MA GRUB PAR BSAM MO,,
gru.wylie: de ltar na nga'am bdag phung po lnga nye bar len pa po dang , phung po lnga nga'am bdag gis nye bar blang bya ma yin pa sogs kyi nyes pa du ma yod pas, de ltar bzung ba'i nga de phung po lnga dang gcig tu ma grub par bsam mo
gru.english: But in this case, still more problems would arise.  For example, "me " or "myself " could never then be the one that took on these five parts at birth; nor could the same five parts be what "me " or "myself " took on at birth.  Decide to yourself once more, therefore, that the "me " which we hold on to as described above could never be one with the five parts to ourselves.

gru.acip: BZHI PA BDEN PA'I DU BRAL NGES PA'I GNAD NI, DE LTAR BZUNG BA'I NGA DE PHUNG PO LNGA'I STENG DU GCIG TU MA GRUB KYANG , PHUNG PO LNGA'I STENG DU THA DAD DU GRUB BO SNYAM NA,
gru.wylie: bzhi pa bden pa'i du bral nges pa'i gnad ni, de ltar bzung ba'i nga de phung po lnga'i steng du gcig tu ma grub kyang , phung po lnga'i steng du tha dad du grub bo snyam na
gru.english: Here finally is the fourth of the crucial points: coming to a definite understanding that the object is not multiple "real " things. Suppose that you think to yourself, "Now even though the 'me' which I hold on to that way doesn't exist as a single thing within the five parts to me, it does exist within these same five parts as separate things. "

gru.acip: GZUGS PHUNG SOGS RE RE NAS BSAL BA'I 'OG TU DE LTAR BZUNG BA'I NGA DE 'DI'O, ,ZHES THA DAD DU NGOS 'DZIN RGYU DGOS PA LAS DE LTAR MI 'DUG PAS, DE LTAR BZUNG BA'I NGA DE PHUNG PO LNGA DANG THA DAD DU MA GRUB SNYAM DU BSAM,
gru.wylie: gzugs phung sogs re re nas bsal ba'i 'og tu de ltar bzung ba'i nga de 'di'o, ,zhes tha dad du ngos 'dzin rgyu dgos pa las de ltar mi 'dug pas, de ltar bzung ba'i nga de phung po lnga dang tha dad du ma grub snyam du bsam
gru.english: If things were as we've said, then after you broke the various heaps of form and the rest out individually, you'd have to be able to identify them separately, in wording like "this heap is what that 'me' is. "  But in fact we don't do this.  As such, you must decide to yourself that the "me " which we hold on to as described before cannot be something which is separate from the five parts to yourself.

gru.acip: BLO MTHO BA RNAMS KYIS NI NGAR 'DZIN LHAN SKYES LA NGA JI LTAR SNANG BA LTAR GRUB MA GRUB DPYAD PA BYAS PA LA BRTEN NAS, GNAD BZHI'I DPYAD PA BYAS PA DANG 'DRA BAR BDEN MED KYI NGES SHES 'DREN PAS,
gru.wylie: blo mtho ba rnams kyis ni ngar 'dzin lhan skyes la nga ji ltar snang ba ltar grub ma grub dpyad pa byas pa la brten nas, gnad bzhi'i dpyad pa byas pa dang 'dra bar bden med kyi nges shes 'dren pas
gru.english: Those of you who have reached some higher level though can go straight to looking into whether "me " actually exists or not in the way that it seems to exist to our inborn tendency to hold to "me. "  This examination serves, in the same way as the analysis involving the four crucial points, to bring back that same state of certainty.

gru.acip: DE'I TSE NGES NGOR NGA RANG BZHIN MED PAR NGES PA'I NGES SHES DAM SBRING NGE BA DANG , SNANG NGOR DGAG BYA BDEN GRUB BKAG TZAM GYI STONG SANG NGE BA'I KHYAD PAR GNYIS LDAN DU BYAS NAS RTZE GCIG TU SKYOB PA NI MNYAM GZHAG NAM MKHA' LTA BU'I SKYONG TSUL LO,,
gru.wylie: de'i tshe nges ngor nga rang bzhin med par nges pa'i nges shes dam sbring nge ba dang , snang ngor dgag bya bden grub bkag tsam gyi stong sang nge ba'i khyad par gnyis ldan du byas nas rtse gcig tu skyob pa ni mnyam gzhag nam mkha' lta bu'i skyong tshul lo
gru.english: At this point you need to learn to maintain your single-pointed meditation with two different qualities.  First you have a very strong and sure perception that what you are seeing is the fact that "me " is something which doesn't have any nature of its own.  Secondly there appears to your mind some kind of sheer emptiness: the simple absence of the thing that we deny--the simple absence of anything that is "real. "  This then is how to carry out the meditation we know as "The Empty Sky. "

gru.acip: DANG PO LA BEM SHES LDAN MIN 'DU BYED GSUM LAS, DANG PO LUS LTA BU LA MTSON NA DE YANG SHA RUS RDOS BCAS KYI YAN LAG LNGA TSOGS TZAM GYI LUS 'DI'I STENG DU, RTOG PAS BTAGS PA TZAM MA YIN PAR TSUGS THUB TU GRUB PA'I LUS YO RE BA ZHIG YOD PAR RANG CAG RNAMS LA BSNYON MED DU 'CHAR BA NI DGAG BYA'I SNANG TSUL YIN LA,
gru.wylie: dang po la bem shes ldan min 'du byed gsum las, dang po lus lta bu la mtshon na de yang sha rus rdos bcas kyi yan lag lnga tshogs tsam gyi lus 'di'i steng du, rtog pas btags pa tsam ma yin par tshugs thub tu grub pa'i lus yo re ba zhig yod par rang cag rnams la bsnyon med du 'char ba ni dgag bya'i snang tshul yin la
gru.english: For the first of these, we cover three different types of caused things: material things, mental things, and then changing things which are neither material nor mental.  To represent material things, we can take something like our own body. In actuality this body is nothing more than a collection of the five components [four limbs and a head]--nothing but flesh and bone in a certain configuration.  In actuality it's nothing more than a projection; but to us it appears as though it were, indisputably, some whole, discrete, and self-standing body. This is how the thing we deny appears to us.

gru.acip: DE LTA BU'I LUS DE SHA RUS RDOS BCAS KYI YAN LAG LNGA TSOGS TZAM GYI LUS 'DI'I STENG DU YOD NA, SHA RUS RDOS BCAS KYI YAN LAG LNGA TSOGS TZAM GYI LUS 'DI DANG GCIG TU GRUB BAM THA DAD DU GRUB,
gru.wylie: de lta bu'i lus de sha rus rdos bcas kyi yan lag lnga tshogs tsam gyi lus 'di'i steng du yod na, sha rus rdos bcas kyi yan lag lnga tshogs tsam gyi lus 'di dang gcig tu grub bam tha dad du grub
gru.english: Now suppose there really were a body like that within this other body, the one which is nothing more than a collection of the five components--nothing but flesh and bone in a certain configuration.  The question then would be whether it was one with, or distinct from, the body of the mere collection of components, the flesh-and-blood configuration.

gru.acip: GCIG TU GRUB NA SHA RUS RDOS BCAS KYI YAN LAG LNGA TSOGS TZAM GYI LUS 'DI PHA MA'I KHU KHRAG LAS GRUB PA YIN PAS,
gru.wylie: gcig tu grub na sha rus rdos bcas kyi yan lag lnga tshogs tsam gyi lus 'di pha ma'i khu khrag las grub pa yin pas
gru.english: Let's say it was one with it.  The fact is that the body which is nothing more than the five components pasted together--the flesh-and-blood lump--is something that's made from the semen and blood of your parents.

gru.acip: THA DAD DU GRUB NA MGO LA SOGS PA'I YAN LAG RE RE NAS BSAL BA'I RJES SU, LUS DE 'DI'O ZHES BSTAN RGYU DGOS PA LAS DE LTAR MI 'DUG PAS, DE LTA BU'I LUS GTAN NAS MED SNYAM DU NGES SHES DRANGS NAS BSKYANG BAR BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: tha dad du grub na mgo la sogs pa'i yan lag re re nas bsal ba'i rjes su, lus de 'di'o zhes bstan rgyu dgos pa las de ltar mi 'dug pas, de lta bu'i lus gtan nas med snyam du nges shes drangs nas bskyang bar bya'o
gru.english: Now suppose instead that that self-standing body from before were something distinct from the body of the mere collection of components, the flesh-and-blood configuration.  In that case we'd have to be able to separate out each different component--the head or whatever--and then point to it and say, "That's the body. " But of course this is not the way it is; and so you must reach a state of certainty where you think to yourself, "No such self-standing body even exists at all. "  And once you reach that state, you must be able to maintain it.

gru.acip: GNYIS PA DE RING GI SHES PA LTA BU LA MTSON NA, DE RING GI SNGA DRO'I SHES PA DANG DE RING GI PHYI DRO'I SHES PA GNYIS KYI STENG DU RTOG PAS BTAGS PA TZAM MA YIN PAR RANG NGOS NAS GRUB PA'I DE RING GI SHES PA ZHIG YOD NA,
gru.wylie: gnyis pa de ring gi shes pa lta bu la mtshon na, de ring gi snga dro'i shes pa dang de ring gi phyi dro'i shes pa gnyis kyi steng du rtog pas btags pa tsam ma yin par rang ngos nas grub pa'i de ring gi shes pa zhig yod na
gru.english: Let's go on then, secondly, to things that are mental: we can use our own mind, today's mind, to represent this category.  Now let's suppose that what we call "my mind today " were not simply a projection imposed upon the combination of my mind during the first half of the day and my mind during the second half of the day--suppose there existed some "my mind today " that existed from its own side.

gru.acip: DE RING GI SNGA DRO'I SHES PA DANG DE RING GI PHYI DRO'I SHES PA GNYIS GCIG TU GRUB BAM THA DAD DU GRUB,
gru.wylie: de ring gi snga dro'i shes pa dang de ring gi phyi dro'i shes pa gnyis gcig tu grub bam tha dad du grub
gru.english: We'd have to see then, again, whether this "my mind today " were something that was either one with, or distinct from, the pair of my mind during the first half of the day and my mind during the second half of the day.

gru.acip: GCIG TU GRUB NA DE RING GI SNGA DRO'I SHES PA'I STENG DU DE RING GI PHYI DRO'I SHES PA YOD PAR 'GYUR LA,
gru.wylie: gcig tu grub na de ring gi snga dro'i shes pa'i steng du de ring gi phyi dro'i shes pa yod par 'gyur la
gru.english: Suppose first that it were one with them.  In this case, there would have to be a mind of mine during the second half of the day that existed within the mind of mine during the first half of the day.

gru.acip: THA DAD DU GRUB NA DE RING GI SNGA DRO'I SHES PA DANG , DE RING GI PHYI DRO'I SHES PA GNYIS RE RE NAS BSAL BA'I RJES SU, DE RING GI SHES PA DE 'DI'O ZHES BSTAN RGYU DGOS PA LAS DE LTAR MI 'DUG PAS, DE LTA BU'I SHES PA GTAN NAS MED SNYAM DU NGES SHES DRANGS NAS SNGAR LTAR SGOM PAR BYED DO,,
gru.wylie: tha dad du grub na de ring gi snga dro'i shes pa dang , de ring gi phyi dro'i shes pa gnyis re re nas bsal ba'i rjes su, de ring gi shes pa de 'di'o zhes bstan rgyu dgos pa las de ltar mi 'dug pas, de lta bu'i shes pa gtan nas med snyam du nges shes drangs nas sngar ltar sgom par byed do
gru.english: Suppose instead that that particular "mind of mine today " were something distinct from those two.  In that case we'd have to be able to isolate out the two of "my mind during the first part of the day " and "my mind during the second part of the day, " and then point to either one and say "that one's the mind I had all day today. " Again though that's not the way it is--and so again you have to come to a sense of certainty that there is no such mind.  And then, as before, you need to keep up a continual meditation on this.

gru.acip: GSUM PA DUS LO GCIG LTA BU LA MTSON NA, LO'I GDAGS GZHI ZLA BA BCU GNYIS PO'I STENG DU RTOG PAS BTAGS PA TZAM MA YIN PAR, RANG NGOS NAS GRUB PA'I LO ZHIG YOD NA ZLA BA BCU GNYIS PO DANG GCIG TU GRUB BAM THA DAD DU GRUB,
gru.wylie: gsum pa dus lo gcig lta bu la mtshon na, lo'i gdags gzhi zla ba bcu gnyis po'i steng du rtog pas btags pa tsam ma yin par, rang ngos nas grub pa'i lo zhig yod na zla ba bcu gnyis po dang gcig tu grub bam tha dad du grub
gru.english: As something to represent the third type of thing above--a thing which is changing but which is neither material or mental--let's take something like time: a single year.  Now a "year " is simply a projection that we impose upon the basis for the projection: a group of twelve months. But suppose it weren't that way, and that there were such a thing as a year that existed from its own side.
