gru.wylie: dri ma med pa'i dbang bskur bas rdo rje theg pa'i lam gyi snod du byas pa'i sgrub pa po rdo rje theg pa'i lam nas 'gro bar 'dod pa rnams kyis ni, thog mar dngos grub gnyis kyi rtsa ba dam tshig dang sdom pa rnam par dag par bya ba la 'bad dgos
gru.english: Now first one must be made into a practitioner who is a worthy vessel for the path of the diamond way; this is achieved through receiving an immaculate form of empowerment.  If one then has any hope of actually traveling this path of the diamond way, then the very first thing they must do after that is to devote all their energy to seeing that their various vows and pledges are purely kept; for these are the very root of every spiritual attainment.

gru.acip: DPAL SANGS RGYAS THAMS CAD DANG MNYAM PAR SBYOR BA MKHA' 'GRO MA SGYU MA BDE MCHOG GI BRTAG PA BDUN PA LAS KYANG , ,DKYIL 'KHOR DU NI MA ZHUGS SHING , ,DAM TSIG RNAMS NI SPANGS PA DANG , ,GSANG BA YANG DAG MI SHES PAS, ,BSGRUBS KYANG CI YANG MI 'GRUB BO,
gru.wylie: dpal sangs rgyas thams cad dang mnyam par sbyor ba mkha' 'gro ma sgyu ma bde mchog gi brtag pa bdun pa las kyang , ,dkyil 'khor du ni ma zhugs shing , ,dam tshig rnams ni spangs pa dang , ,gsang ba yang dag mi shes pas, ,bsgrubs kyang ci yang mi 'grub bo
gru.english: This is also described in the seventh section of the glorious text of Highest Bliss known as The Lady of Illusion, The Angel, Who Joins with Each and Every Buddha: If you have not entered the secret world; If you give up on your secret pledges; And if you have no perfect understanding Of the teachings of the secret way, Then you can practice all you want But you'll attain no goals at all.

gru.acip: KHYAD PAR DU RANG LA DBANG BSKUR BA, RGYUD BSHAD PA, MAN NGAG GNANG BA GANG YANG RUNG BA'I BLA MA DE DNGOS GRUB KUN GYI GZHI RNAM PAR MTHONG NAS,
gru.wylie: khyad par du rang la dbang bskur ba, rgyud bshad pa, man ngag gnang ba gang yang rung ba'i bla ma de dngos grub kun gyi gzhi rnam par mthong nas
gru.english: The most important thing of all is that we come to see that the very source of all high spiritual qualities is our Lama: meaning any Lama who has granted us empowerment; or explained to us the secret teachings; or given us personal advices on the practice.

gru.acip: RDO RJE SLOB DPON NI DNGOS GRUB KYI RTZA BA YIN PAS RGYUD SDE DU MA NAS MTSAN NYID MANG DU GSUNGS PAS MTSAN NYID KYI CHOS RNAMS SHES PAR BYAS LA SLOB MA BSTAN PAR 'DOD PA RNAMS KYIS YON TAN DE DAG DANG LDAN PA LA 'BAD CING BLA MA BSTEN 'DOD PA RNAMS KYIS KYANG DE 'DRA BA 'TSAL BA LA 'BAD LA MA RNYED NA'ANG DE 'DRA BA'I MTSAN NYID CAN GYIS RJES SU 'DZIN PA'I RGYUR TSOGS GSOG PA DANG SMON LAM LA BRTZAN DGOS PAS BLA MA'I MTSAN NYID DE DAG SHES PAR BYA BA NI SHIN TU GAL CHE'O,
gru.wylie: rdo rje slob dpon ni dngos grub kyi rtsa ba yin pas rgyud sde du ma nas mtshan nyid mang du gsungs pas mtshan nyid kyi chos rnams shes par byas la slob ma bstan par 'dod pa rnams kyis yon tan de dag dang ldan pa la 'bad cing bla ma bsten 'dod pa rnams kyis kyang de 'dra ba 'tshal ba la 'bad la ma rnyed na'ang de 'dra ba'i mtshan nyid can gyis rjes su 'dzin pa'i rgyur tshogs gsog pa dang smon lam la brtsan dgos pas bla ma'i mtshan nyid de dag shes par bya ba ni shin tu gal che'o
gru.english: Our Diamond Master is the very root of every spiritual attainment we could ever hope to gain; as such, we must take the time to acquaint ourselves with the great number of requisite qualities for such a Master described in a broad range of secret texts. Those who hope to teach disciples of their own should exert themselves in gaining these qualities; while those who hope to find a Lama to take themselves to should make the same efforts in seeking someone with these qualities. If they fail to find one, then they should undertake to collect the necessary good karma which would cause them to be taken into the care of a Lama so qualified; they should make great efforts in all the prayers too needed to bring these Lamas.  All this then demonstrates the crucial importance of learning exactly what the necessary qualities of a Diamond Master are. ***

gru.acip: DE LA RTZA BA'I ZHES KHYAD PAR SBYAR BA NI LTUNG BA GANG GIS GOS NA SDOM PA GCOD PA STE LTUNG BA'I MTHAR THUG SHOS YIN GYI, BSRUNGS NA DNGOS GRUB DANG MA BSRUNGS NA SDUG BSNGAL GYI RTZA BA ZHES MI BYA,
gru.wylie: de la rtsa ba'i zhes khyad par sbyar ba ni ltung ba gang gis gos na sdom pa gcod pa ste ltung ba'i mthar thug shos yin gyi, bsrungs na dngos grub dang ma bsrungs na sdug bsngal gyi rtsa ba zhes mi bya
gru.english: Specifying that these downfalls are "root" downfalls means that these are downfalls which, should they infect our practice, sever our vows.  And so they are "root" downfalls in the sense that they are the very most serious of all downfalls.  The word "root" here is not to be explained as meaning that these are the downfalls which--if you keep yourself from committing them--are the root of attainments, and which act as the root of suffering if we do not keep ourselves from committing them. *** Beginning here with Geshe Tsewang Samdrup's explanation of the first root downfall, from His String of Shining Jewels:

gru.acip: BRNYAS SMOD BYAS TSUL NI DPAL MCHOG 'GREL CHEN LAS, GANG GIS RNAL 'BYOR PA DKYIL 'KHOR DU 'JUG PAR BYED PA'I SLOB DPON DE LA KHYOD TSUL KHRIMS 'CHAL BA DANG BRTZON 'GRUS ZHAN PA DANG , RMONGS PA YIN NO ZHES SMU PAR MI BYA'O, ,ZHES GSUNGS PA LTAR TSUL 'CHAL ZHES SOGS KYIS SMOD PA DANG BRNYAS PA'O,
gru.wylie: brnyas smod byas tshul ni dpal mchog 'grel chen las, gang gis rnal 'byor pa dkyil 'khor du 'jug par byed pa'i slob dpon de la khyod tshul khrims 'chal ba dang brtson 'grus zhan pa dang , rmongs pa yin no zhes smu par mi bya'o, ,zhes gsungs pa ltar tshul 'chal zhes sogs kyis smod pa dang brnyas pa'o
gru.english: The way in which one disparages or criticizes the Lama in this downfall is described as follows in the Great Commentary to Supreme Glory: Suppose there is a Master who has granted a yogi or yogini entrance into the secret world.  This disciple then must never speak badly of their Master, saying to them: "You are acting in an immoral way," or "You have so little joyful effort," or "You don't know what you're doing." Thus what it means to "disparage" or "criticize" our Master is to say things like "you are immoral" or the like. ***

gru.acip: 'DUS PA'I LE'U LNGA PA LAS KYANG , ,SEMS CAN MTSAMS MED LA SOGS PA, ,SDIG PA CHEN PO BYED PA YANG , ,RDO RJE THEG PA RGYA MTSO CHE, ,THEG PA MCHOG NI 'DI LA 'GRUB, ,SNYING NAS SLOB DPON SMOD PA DAG ,BSGRUBS KYANG 'GRUB PAR YONG MI 'GYUR,
gru.wylie: 'dus pa'i le'u lnga pa las kyang , ,sems can mtshams med la sogs pa, ,sdig pa chen po byed pa yang , ,rdo rje theg pa rgya mtsho che, ,theg pa mchog ni 'di la 'grub, ,snying nas slob dpon smod pa dag ,bsgrubs kyang 'grub par yong mi 'gyur
gru.english: The fifth chapter of the Collection says as well: Even those who have committed The greatest mistakes of all-- Deeds like the immediate sins-- Can attain their goal here, In the Way of the Diamond: In the ultimate ocean, the highest path. But those who have disparaged Their master from their heart Will never reach the goal, No matter how hard they try. ***

gru.acip: DANG POR SLOB DPON LA BSNYEN BKUR BYAS TE THOS BSAM GYIS DE KHO NA NYID RTOGS NAS DA NI 'DIS CI ZHIG BYA ZHES BLA MA LA BRNYAS PAR BYED PA NI, SNYING NAS SLOB DPON SMOD PA STE DE DANG LHAN CIG TU ZANG ZING GI LONGS SPYOD KYIS DGA' BAR BYED PAS KYANG MI 'GRUB NA DES MI 'GRUB PA SMOS CI DGOS, ZHES CHOS SPONG DANG MTSAMS MED LAS KYANG SDIG CHE BAR GSUNGS SO,
gru.wylie: dang por slob dpon la bsnyen bkur byas te thos bsam gyis de kho na nyid rtogs nas da ni 'dis ci zhig bya zhes bla ma la brnyas par byed pa ni, snying nas slob dpon smod pa ste de dang lhan cig tu zang zing gi longs spyod kyis dga' bar byed pas kyang mi 'grub na des mi 'grub pa smos ci dgos, zhes chos spong dang mtshams med las kyang sdig che bar gsungs so
gru.english: What does it mean here to "disparage your Master from the bottom of your heart"?  As the texts say, this is where you disparage your Lama in the following way:  At first you pay Them proper respect.  You study with Them, and contemplate what you've studied, and you come to understand suchness.  And then you say to yourself, "So what do I need them for anymore?" If a person who has committed those other actions can no longer reach attainments, the texts say, even by pleasing their Lama by sharing their material possessions with them; then what need is there to say that a person like this could never reach any attainments? The point of this last part is to say that the act of disparaging ones Master is more serious even than actions such as giving up the Dharma, or committing one of the "immediate" misdeeds. ***

gru.acip: DES NA NYES SPYOD DE DAG NI DNGOS GRUB THAMS CAD 'PHROG CING NGAN 'GRO SHIN TU NYAM NGA BA'I SDUG BSNGAL GYI RTZA BAR RGYUD SDE LAS YANG YANG NAN CHE BAR GSUNGS PAS GNAS 'DI LA NI SHIN TU GZAB PAR BYA'O,
gru.wylie: des na nyes spyod de dag ni dngos grub thams cad 'phrog cing ngan 'gro shin tu nyam nga ba'i sdug bsngal gyi rtsa bar rgyud sde las yang yang nan che bar gsungs pas gnas 'di la ni shin tu gzab par bya'o
gru.english: The secret teachings thus emphasize, over and over again, how these kinds of negative behavior--disparaging your Master--steal away from us every possible spiritual attainment, and act as the very root of unbearable misery in the lower realms.  As such we must exercise extreme caution in this particular point. ***

gru.acip: RDO RJE SNYING PO RGYAN GYI LE'U BCU BZHI PA LAS, ,GANG GIS SLOB DPON YANG DAG SMAD, ,DE YIS RGYUD KUN SGRUB PA'I MCHOG ,GNYID DANG 'DU 'DZI RNAM SPANGS TE, ,BSKAL PA STONG DU LEGS BSGRUBS KYANG , ,DMYAL SOGS SGRUB PAR BYED PA'O,
gru.wylie: rdo rje snying po rgyan gyi le'u bcu bzhi pa las, ,gang gis slob dpon yang dag smad, ,de yis rgyud kun sgrub pa'i mchog ,gnyid dang 'du 'dzi rnam spangs te, ,bskal pa stong du legs bsgrubs kyang , ,dmyal sogs sgrub par byed pa'o
gru.english: The 14th chapter of the Jewel of the Essence of the Diamond says as well, Suppose as such that a person Truly disparages their Master. They can become then The highest practitioner of the secret ways-- They can work perfectly For a thousand eons, Refusing to sleep, avoiding the crowds, And yet the only achievement That they will ever see Is the realms of hell, and such. ***

gru.acip: BDE MCHOG RTZA RGYUD KYI LE'U DANG PO LAS KYANG , ,SHIN TU MNYAM BZHAG SGRUB PA POS, ,RTAG TU DAM TSIG BSKYANG BAR BYA, ,DAM TSIG NYAMS PAS DKYIL 'KHOR DU, ,DBANG SKUR DNGOS GRUB THOB MI 'GYUR,
gru.wylie: bde mchog rtsa rgyud kyi le'u dang po las kyang , ,shin tu mnyam bzhag sgrub pa pos, ,rtag tu dam tshig bskyang bar bya, ,dam tshig nyams pas dkyil 'khor du, ,dbang skur dngos grub thob mi 'gyur
gru.english: The first chapter of the root tantra of Highest Bliss also states: Those who hope to practice, Those who live in meditation, Must always maintain their pledges. A person who has received empowerment Into the world of secrets But whose pledges have been broken Can never reach any attainment at all. ***

gru.acip: DE LTAR RANG GI SLOB DPON LA MI SMOD PA TZAM DU MA ZAD GZHAN SMOD PA GROGS SU BYAS NA'ANG SNGAR BSHAD PA LTAR RANG GI DNGOS GRUB KYI GEGS CHEN POR 'GYUR BAS RNAM PA THAMS CAD DU SPANG BAR BYA,
gru.wylie: de ltar rang gi slob dpon la mi smod pa tsam du ma zad gzhan smod pa grogs su byas na'ang sngar bshad pa ltar rang gi dngos grub kyi gegs chen por 'gyur bas rnam pa thams cad du spang bar bya
gru.english: And we're not just talking about disparaging your own Master.  Even if we contribute to disparaging someone else's Master, then this acts as a tremendous obstacle to our own practice, just as described before.  As such we must strictly avoid this as well. ***

gru.acip: SU LA ZHE NA, BRTZON 'GRUS DANG RTZOL BA SHIN TU 'BAR BA DANG LDAN PA'I GDUL BYA MCHOG RNAMS LA STER BAR BYED DE BRTZON PA MED PAS BYANG CHUB PAR MA GYUR PA NI SLOB MA NYID KYI NYES PA'O,
gru.wylie: su la zhe na, brtson 'grus dang rtsol ba shin tu 'bar ba dang ldan pa'i gdul bya mchog rnams la ster bar byed de brtson pa med pas byang chub par ma gyur pa ni slob ma nyid kyi nyes pa'o
gru.english: And just who is it that they grant this attainment to?  They grant it to those who are absolutely on fire with effort and hard work: to the very highest kind of disciple.  If someone lacks this kind of commitment and fails to reach enlightenment in this life, well that's their own fault. *** We turn next to relevant material on this first downfall from Je Tsongkapa's Golden Harvest:

gru.acip: GANG PHYIR RDO RJE 'DZIN PA YIS, ,DNGOS GRUB SLOB DPON RJES 'BRANG GSUNGS, ,DE BAS DE LA BRNYAS PA NI, ,RTZA BA'I LTUNG BA DANG POR BSHAD,
gru.wylie: gang phyir rdo rje 'dzin pa yis, ,dngos grub slob dpon rjes 'brang gsungs, ,de bas de la brnyas pa ni, ,rtsa ba'i ltung ba dang por bshad
gru.english: The One Who Holds the Diamond Has said that every attainment there is Follows from our Master. As such, it is taught That the very first Among all the root downfalls Is to criticize our Master. ***

gru.acip: ,SNYING NAS SLOB DPON SMOD PA DAG ,BSGRUBS KYANG 'GRUB PAR YONG MI 'GYUR, ,ZHES BYA BA LA GANG GI THAD NAS DE NI GDAMS NGAG LA SOGS PA THOB PAS CI ZHIG DGOS ZHES PA NI SNYING NAS SLOB DPON SMOD PA'O, ,ZHES BSHAD PA LTA BU'O,
gru.wylie: snying nas slob dpon smod pa dag ,bsgrubs kyang 'grub par yong mi 'gyur, ,zhes bya ba la gang gi thad nas de ni gdams ngag la sogs pa thob pas ci zhig dgos zhes pa ni snying nas slob dpon smod pa'o, ,zhes bshad pa lta bu'o
gru.english: Those who have disparaged Their Master from their heart Will never reach the goal, Now matter how hard they try. It's just as these lines describe it.  "Disparaging your Master from your heart" means to say or think to yourself about someone from whom you have received these private advices and so on: "Since I've already got what I wanted, then what do I need them for now?"

gru.acip: LTUNG BAR 'GYUR BA'I RGYU MTSAN NI DE LTAR SMAD PAS LTUNG BAR 'GYUR BA'I RGYU MTSAN GANG GI PHYIR NA SLOB MA'I RGYUD LA DNGOS GRUB GNYIS GANG 'GRUB PA NI RDO RJE SLOB DPON MNYES PAR BYAS PA KHO NA'I RJES SU 'BRANG BAR RDO RJE 'DZIN PA RDO RJE 'CHANG GIS GSUNGS PA DE BAS NA'O,
gru.wylie: ltung bar 'gyur ba'i rgyu mtshan ni de ltar smad pas ltung bar 'gyur ba'i rgyu mtshan gang gi phyir na slob ma'i rgyud la dngos grub gnyis gang 'grub pa ni rdo rje slob dpon mnyes par byas pa kho na'i rjes su 'brang bar rdo rje 'dzin pa rdo rje 'chang gis gsungs pa de bas na'o
gru.english: Here then is the reason why disparaging ones Master is a downfall: "Just why is it a downfall for one to disparage ones Master?  It is because the Keeper of the Diamond--the Holder of the Diamond--has Himself stated that any attainments that the disciple may hope to gain within their heart, both types of attainments, follow from one action, and from one action only: from pleasing their Diamond Master." ***

gru.acip: MTSAMS MED DANG DAM CHOS SPONG BAS KYANG RDO RJE THEG PA'I SGOR ZHUGS NAS BSGRUBS NA DNGOS GRUB MCHOG 'GRUB PA YOD KYANG SNGAR BSTAN PA LTAR GYI SLOB DPON SNYING NAS SMOD PAS NI BSGRUBS KYANG MI 'GRUB PAS MTSAMS MED SOGS LAS NYES DMIGS CHE BAR GSANG 'DUS LAS GSUNGS PAS RTZA LTUNG RNAMS KYI NANG NAS KYANG 'DIS MA GOS PA LA 'BAD DO, ,'DI YANG SLAR GSO BA'I THABS KYIS PHYIR BCOS TSUL BZHIN DU BYAS NA NGAN 'GROR 'GRO BA DGAG NUS KYANG DNGOS GRUB THOB PA LA CHES RING DU SONG BA'O,
gru.wylie: mtshams med dang dam chos spong bas kyang rdo rje theg pa'i sgor zhugs nas bsgrubs na dngos grub mchog 'grub pa yod kyang sngar bstan pa ltar gyi slob dpon snying nas smod pas ni bsgrubs kyang mi 'grub pas mtshams med sogs las nyes dmigs che bar gsang 'dus las gsungs pas rtsa ltung rnams kyi nang nas kyang 'dis ma gos pa la 'bad do, ,'di yang slar gso ba'i thabs kyis phyir bcos tshul bzhin du byas na ngan 'gror 'gro ba dgag nus kyang dngos grub thob pa la ches ring du song ba'o
gru.english: Suppose you have committed even an action such as one of the "immediate" misdeeds, or the sin of giving up the holy Dharma.  If you then enter the gates of the diamond way and practice sincerely, you can still reach the highest attainment of all. If however you disparage your Master from the depths of your heart, as we described earlier, then no matter how much you try to practice you will not be able to reach attainments.  Thus it is, says the teaching of the Secret Collection, that this particular bad deed is more serious that even actions such as the immediate misdeeds. Given this fact, we must make intense efforts to avoid, even among all the root downfalls, this particular one.  We might follow, properly, the various methods for restoring our vows after committing this one, and try to repair the damage.  And it's true that we will thereby be able to stop the karma that would have sent us to the lower realms.  But still we have delayed any spiritual attainments we might have gained, for an infinitely long length of time.

gru.acip: GUS SHING BSTOD PA, BLA MA'I THUGS DGONGS BZHIN SGRUB PA, YID DU 'ONG BA'I YO BYAD PHUL BA,
gru.wylie: gus shing bstod pa, bla ma'i thugs dgongs bzhin sgrub pa, yid du 'ong ba'i yo byad phul ba
gru.english: We must respect our Lama, and speak highly of Them.  We must carry out every wish of Their precious heart.  We must present Them with lovely offerings.

gru.acip: DE LTAR BYAS PA'I PHAN YON NI BLA MA DE LA RTAG TU BYIN PAS NI SANGS RGYAS THAMS CAD LA RTAG TU BYIN PA DANG 'DRA BA'I BSOD NAMS KYI TSOGS RDZOGS PAR 'GYUR LA TSOGS MANG DU BSAGS PA DE LAS NI DNGOS GRUB KYI MCHOG SANGS RGYAS MYUR DU 'THOB NA DNGOS GRUB GZHAN LTA CI SMOS,
gru.wylie: de ltar byas pa'i phan yon ni bla ma de la rtag tu byin pas ni sangs rgyas thams cad la rtag tu byin pa dang 'dra ba'i bsod nams kyi tshogs rdzogs par 'gyur la tshogs mang du bsags pa de las ni dngos grub kyi mchog sangs rgyas myur du 'thob na dngos grub gzhan lta ci smos
gru.english: What are the benefits of doing all this?  A person who constantly makes offerings to their Lama is collecting the massive amounts of good karma that they would by making the same gifts all the time to each and every Buddha that there is.  From this then they will quickly reach the highest of all attainments--Buddhahood itself; and needless to say every other form of spiritual goal. ***

gru.acip: SANGS RGYAS DANG DBYER MED PAR LTA BA'I DGOS PA NI RDO RJE 'CHANG DANG BLA MA LA DAD PA MNYAM PAR BYA BA DANG RDO RJE 'CHANG GI NGA RGYAL BRTAN PAR BYA BA DANG TSEGS CHUNG NGUS TSOGS BSAGS PAS MYUR DU 'GRUB PA'I DON DU YIN PAR SH'AN+TI PAS GSANG 'DUS KYI 'GREL PAR GSUNGS SO,
gru.wylie: sangs rgyas dang dbyer med par lta ba'i dgos pa ni rdo rje 'chang dang bla ma la dad pa mnyam par bya ba dang rdo rje 'chang gi nga rgyal brtan par bya ba dang tshegs chung ngus tshogs bsags pas myur du 'grub pa'i don du yin par shAn+ti pas gsang 'dus kyi 'grel par gsungs so
gru.english: Exactly why is it that we must view our Master as being indivisible from the Buddha?  The point is that we thus come to feel an equal amount of faith for both the Keeper of the Diamond and our Lama. It further helps us become firm in our own practice of identifying ourselves with the Keeper of the Diamond, and enables us to speedily collect great amounts of good karma, without any trouble at all.   These are the benefits which Shantipa describes in his commentary to the Secret Collection. ***

gru.acip: YON TAN GANG YOD KYI NGOS NAS BRTAGS NA RANG LA DNGOS GRUB RGYAS PA'I RGYU BYED LA SKYON CUNG ZAD RE YOD PA'I NGOS NAS BRTAGS NA GDON MI ZA BAR DNGOS GRUB KYI GEGS SU 'GYUR BA'I PHYIR RO,
gru.wylie: yon tan gang yod kyi ngos nas brtags na rang la dngos grub rgyas pa'i rgyu byed la skyon cung zad re yod pa'i ngos nas brtags na gdon mi za bar dngos grub kyi gegs su 'gyur ba'i phyir ro
gru.english: However much we watch our Lama to see what good spiritual qualities they possess, it acts to increase our own spiritual attainments.  And however much we watch Them to see what minor faults They may happen to posses, it acts beyond any shadow of a doubt to prevent us from any attainments. ***

gru.acip: SEMS CAN RNAMS ZHES MANG TSIG TU 'BYUNG YANG SEMS CAN GANG YANG RUNG BA GCIG GO ,DE LA BYA BA CI ZHIG BYAS PAS LTUNG BAR 'GYUR BA NI, THEG CHEN PAS SEMS CAN THAMS CAD LA BU GCIG PA BZHIN DU BSAM ZHING DUS THAMS CAD DU GTANG BAR MI BYA STE SEMS CAN GYI ZHING DANG BRAL BA'I THEG CHEN PA NI SRIN BU ME KHYER LA NYI 'OD DANG LDAN PAR BTAGS PA DANG 'DRA BAR MING TZAM PA'O, ,ZHAS NAG PO PAS BSHAD PA DANG , BYAMS PA'I SEMS NI SEMS CAN LA BLA NA MED PA'I PHAN BDE BSGRUB PAR 'DOD PA STE DE NAM YANG DOR BAR MI BYA'O ZHES SH'AN+TI PAS BSHAD PA GNYIS DON 'DRA BAS DE'I BZLOG PHYOGS NI BYAMS PA'I SEMS SPONG BA'O,
gru.wylie: sems can rnams zhes mang tshig tu 'byung yang sems can gang yang rung ba gcig go ,de la bya ba ci zhig byas pas ltung bar 'gyur ba ni, theg chen pas sems can thams cad la bu gcig pa bzhin du bsam zhing dus thams cad du gtang bar mi bya ste sems can gyi zhing dang bral ba'i theg chen pa ni srin bu me khyer la nyi 'od dang ldan par btags pa dang 'dra bar ming tsam pa'o, ,zhas nag po pas bshad pa dang , byams pa'i sems ni sems can la bla na med pa'i phan bde bsgrub par 'dod pa ste de nam yang dor bar mi bya'o zhes shAn+ti pas bshad pa gnyis don 'dra bas de'i bzlog phyogs ni byams pa'i sems spong ba'o
gru.english: The wording of this particular vow says that we have committed it when we have lost our love "for living beings," using the plural.  You should understand though that we break it whenever we have lost our love for any one living being. Now exactly what is it that we have to do to commit this particular downfall?  Krishnapada explains it as follows: Those who follow the greater way must feel towards every living being the same way they would towards their only child.  They must never, for even a single instant, give up on any one of these beings.  A follower of the greater way who has divorced themselves from this powerful karmic object of a single living being no longer even deserves the name of a "follower of the greater way."  It would be like calling  a firefly "the sun." Shantipa puts it this way: The state of "love" is where we have a true desire to assure that each and every living being reaches a state of unsurpassed help and happiness: where we never, ever, give up on one of them. These two explanations of the vow amount to the same thing, and so we can say that acting in a way opposite to what is described in them as "love" would constitute the act of giving up our love. ***

gru.acip: BDAG GIS SEMS CAN THAMS CAD KYI DON DU BYANG CHUB BSGRUB PA GA LA NUS SNYAM PA'I BSAM PAS SMON SEMS BTANG NA BYANG SEMS BTANG PA'I RTZA LTUNG ,
gru.wylie: bdag gis sems can thams cad kyi don du byang chub bsgrub pa ga la nus snyam pa'i bsam pas smon sems btang na byang sems btang pa'i rtsa ltung
gru.english: Suppose we give up the Wish for enlightenment in the form of a prayer, by thinking to ourselves, "How could someone like me ever be able to reach enlightenment to help every living being?"  In so doing we have then committed the root downfall we call [5] "Giving up the Wish for Enlightenment." *** Je Rinpoche comments:

gru.acip: DE LA BYA BA CI ZHIG BYAS PAS LTUNG BAR 'GYUR BA NI, BDAG GIS SEMS CAN MTHA' YAS PA'I DON DU BYANG CHUB SGRUB PAR MI NUS SNYAM NAS SMON SEMS DE SPONG BA NA RTZA LTUNG LNGA PA YIN NO,
gru.wylie: de la bya ba ci zhig byas pas ltung bar 'gyur ba ni, bdag gis sems can mtha' yas pa'i don du byang chub sgrub par mi nus snyam nas smon sems de spong ba na rtsa ltung lnga pa yin no
gru.english: What action do we have to do in order to commit this particular downfall?  The fifth root downfall is committed whenever we give up the Wish for enlightenment in the form of a prayer, by thinking to ourselves, "I simply don't have the capacity to become an Enlightened Being for the sake of an infinite number of living creatures." *** On to the sixth downfall, from Geshe Tsewang Samdrup:

gru.acip: THEG PA GSUM GANG RUNG DU GTOGS PA'I RGYAL BA'I BKA' GANG YANG RUNG BA LA 'DI SANGS RGYAS KYI GSUNGS PA'I CHOS MA YIN NO, ZHES SKUR PA ZHE NAS BTAB NA RANG GZHAN GRUB MTHA' LA SMOD PA'I RTZA LTUNG ,
gru.wylie: theg pa gsum gang rung du gtogs pa'i rgyal ba'i bka' gang yang rung ba la 'di sangs rgyas kyi gsungs pa'i chos ma yin no, zhes skur pa zhe nas btab na rang gzhan grub mtha' la smod pa'i rtsa ltung
gru.english: Suppose that we discount what is actually the Word of the Buddha, by saying "This is not something that Lord Buddha taught" about any part of the Words of the Victorious Ones, included into any of the three ways.  We have then committed the root downfall called [6] "Disparaging the beliefs of any system, whether our own or others." *** Je Tsongkapa's comments:

gru.acip: NAG PO PAS RANG NI SANGS RGYAS PA DANG GZHAN NI MU STEGS CAN DANG CHOS NI MNGON PAR MTHO BA'I LAM LA BYAS NAS, MU STEGS CAN LA SMAD BYAS NA, ,RNAM PAR SNANG MDZAD RING BA'I RGYU, ,ZHES 'DREN NO, ,'ON KYANG MU STEGS LA SKYON GDAGS 'DOD KYIS SMAD NA NYES PA 'BYUNG YANG 'DIR RTZA LTUNG GI YUL STON PAS MI BDE'O, ,DES NA RTZA LTUNG BKA' 'GREL LAS, RANG GI GRUB PA'I MTHA' GSANG SNGAGS DANG GZHAN GYI GRUB PA'I MTHA' PHA ROL TU PHYIN PA'I THEG PA LA BSHAD PA LTAR BYA'O,
gru.wylie: nag po pas rang ni sangs rgyas pa dang gzhan ni mu stegs can dang chos ni mngon par mtho ba'i lam la byas nas, mu stegs can la smad byas na, ,rnam par snang mdzad ring ba'i rgyu, ,zhes 'dren no, ,'on kyang mu stegs la skyon gdags 'dod kyis smad na nyes pa 'byung yang 'dir rtsa ltung gi yul ston pas mi bde'o, ,des na rtsa ltung bka' 'grel las, rang gi grub pa'i mtha' gsang sngags dang gzhan gyi grub pa'i mtha' pha rol tu phyin pa'i theg pa la bshad pa ltar bya'o
gru.english: Krishnapada takes "Dharma of our own school" here to refer to the teachings of Buddhism, and "Dharma of other schools" to refer to the teachings of non-Buddhists.  He takes "Dharma" itself to refer to any path that leads to the higher births.  To back this up he quotes [the Total Purification of Appearances]: Disparaging the teachings of non-Buddhists Takes us farther from the Angel, Appearances. While it is a negative deed if we criticize non-Buddhist schools out of a motivation to say something badly of them, it doesn't quite fit to say that these schools constitute the object towards which we commit the root downfall we're discussing here.  As such we should follow the clarification found in A Commentary on Difficult@ Points in the Root Downfalls, where it says that "the beliefs of our own school" refers to the teachings of the secret word; while "the beliefs of other schools" refers to the open Buddhist teachings, those of the way of the perfection of wisdom. ***

gru.acip: ,'O NA SH'AN+TI PAS DGRA NAG 'GREL PAR, SMAD MI BYA ZHES BYA BA NI RTZOD PAS SUN DBYUNG BAR MI BYA STE 'GRO BA DAG NI RANG RANG GI 'DUN PA'I THEG PA TZAM LAS RIM GYIS 'JUS SHING BYANG CHUB PAR 'GYUR GYI BTZAN THABS SU 'DUN PA BZLOG PA NI SDANG BA 'PHEL BA'I RGYU TZAM YIN PAS BZHAG STE, ZHES GRUB MTHA' 'DZIN PA SUN 'BYIN PA LA SMOD PAR GSUNGS PA JI LTAR YIN SNYAM NA, SNGAGS SAM MTSAN NYID KYI THEG PA LA SKYON BKAL NAS BKA' MA YIN NO, ,ZHES SUN PHYUNG BA NA DE DAG GI GRUB MTHA' 'DZIN PA'I YANG 'DUN PA LDOG PA LA BSHAD PAS SKYON MED DO,
gru.wylie: 'o na shAn+ti pas dgra nag 'grel par, smad mi bya zhes bya ba ni rtsod pas sun dbyung bar mi bya ste 'gro ba dag ni rang rang gi 'dun pa'i theg pa tsam las rim gyis 'jus shing byang chub par 'gyur gyi btsan thabs su 'dun pa bzlog pa ni sdang ba 'phel ba'i rgyu tsam yin pas bzhag ste, zhes grub mtha' 'dzin pa sun 'byin pa la smod par gsungs pa ji ltar yin snyam na, sngags sam mtshan nyid kyi theg pa la skyon bkal nas bka' ma yin no, ,zhes sun phyung ba na de dag gi grub mtha' 'dzin pa'i yang 'dun pa ldog pa la bshad pas skyon med do
gru.english: "Well then," you may ask.  "How does it fit in here when Shantipa, in his commentary to the Ebony Enemy, describes the act of disparaging here as overthrowing the belief of a particular school?  He says, When the wording of the vow here says that we should "never disparage their beliefs," what it means is that we should not seek to overthrow others" beliefs through argument.  The point is that beings reach enlightenment by being taken up gradually, without overextending themselves past the particular way which they find comfortable at any given time.  If instead we undertake some drastic step to try to change their minds, it only causes hard feelings--and so for the time being we should let it be." And yet there's no problem here.  What Shantipa is referring to here is where we say something negative about either the secret or open ways of Buddhism, overthrowing it in the sense of saying "This is not the Word of the Buddha," and thus changing the person's mind: causing them to give up their desire to learn a particular school of Buddhism.

gru.acip: RDO RJE SEMS DPA' DENG KHYOD KYI, ,SNYING LA YANG DAG ZHUGS PAR GYUR, ,GAL TE TSUL 'DI SMRAS NA NI, ,DE MA THAG TU DRAL TE GSHEGS, ,ZHES STON MKHAN GYI DAM TSIG NYAMS PA DANG SNYING LA RDO RJE SEMS DPA' SNGAR ZHUGS PA MI BZHUGS PAR 'BYON PA SOGS KYI SGO NAS GZHUNG DU MAR GSANG BA MI BSGRAG PA LA NAN TAN CHE BAR GSUNGS SHING SAR MNYAM SBYOR GYI LUNG DRANGS PA LTAR DKYIL 'KHOR DU MA ZHUGS PAS BSGRUBS KYANG CI YANG MI 'GRUB PAR GSUNGS PAS SLOB MA DES BSGRUBS KYANG DNGOS GRUB KHYAD PAR CAN GTAN MI 'THOB PAS DGOS PA MED PA'I PHYIR RO,
gru.wylie: rdo rje sems dpa' deng khyod kyi, ,snying la yang dag zhugs par gyur, ,gal te tshul 'di smras na ni, ,de ma thag tu dral te gshegs, ,zhes ston mkhan gyi dam tshig nyams pa dang snying la rdo rje sems dpa' sngar zhugs pa mi bzhugs par 'byon pa sogs kyi sgo nas gzhung du mar gsang ba mi bsgrag pa la nan tan che bar gsungs shing sar mnyam sbyor gyi lung drangs pa ltar dkyil 'khor du ma zhugs pas bsgrubs kyang ci yang mi 'grub par gsungs pas slob ma des bsgrubs kyang dngos grub khyad par can gtan mi 'thob pas dgos pa med pa'i phyir ro
gru.english: The empowerment includes the following wording: Today the Warrior of Diamond himself Has taken His seat within your heart. If you ever speak of these things, Then your heart will rip apart, And He will take His leave. The point here is that the pledges of the person who reveals the secrets deteriorate; and whereas the Warrior of the Diamond up to that point had resided within their heart, he is now no longer there.  In these and other descriptions, a great many major texts exhort us insistently never to reveal these secrets. Moreover, as we noted earlier in the quotation from The Book of Union, a person who has not yet been granted entrance into the secret world may engage in secret practices as much as they want, but they won't be able to reach any attainments at all by doing so.  As such, there is simply no purpose served by revealing secrets to such people: even if they try to put them into practice, there is absolutely no chance that they will reach any meaningful attainments this way.

gru.acip: ,SANGS RGYAS THOD PA'I LE'U GSUM PA LAS KYANG , DPER NA BU TSA MED PA'I KHYIM, ,SHI BA TZAM GYIS STONG PA NYID, ,DE BZHIN DBANG DANG BRAL NA NI, ,YE SHES KUN GYIS STONG PA NYID, ,DPER NA PI WAm SBYOR KUN TSOGS, ,RGYUD DANG BRAL NA BRDUNG MI RUNG , ,DE BZHIN DBANG DANG BRAL NA NI, ,SNGAGS DANG BSAM GTAN 'GRUB MI 'GYUR, ZHES GSUNGS LA STON MKHAN DANG NYAN MKHAN LA YANG NYES SMIdA SHIN TU CHE STE DE NYID LAS, RMONGS PA GANG ZHIG DBANG MED PAR, ,BDAG NI DBANG BSKUR ZHES SMRA BA, ,JI SRID SANGS RGYAS BZHUGS KYI BAR, ,SLOB MAR BCAS TE DMYAL BAR 'GRO, ,ZHES GSUNGS,
gru.wylie: sangs rgyas thod pa'i le'u gsum pa las kyang , dper na bu tsha med pa'i khyim, ,shi ba tsam gyis stong pa nyid, ,de bzhin dbang dang bral na ni, ,ye shes kun gyis stong pa nyid, ,dper na pi waM sbyor kun tshogs, ,rgyud dang bral na brdung mi rung , ,de bzhin dbang dang bral na ni, ,sngags dang bsam gtan 'grub mi 'gyur, zhes gsungs la ston mkhan dang nyan mkhan la yang nyes smiDa shin tu che ste de nyid las, rmongs pa gang zhig dbang med par, ,bdag ni dbang bskur zhes smra ba, ,ji srid sangs rgyas bzhugs kyi bar, ,slob mar bcas te dmyal bar 'gro, ,zhes gsungs
gru.english: The third chapter of The Skull of the Buddha too says, When a householder without issue Dies, their house is automatically empty; When a person lacks empowerment, They are empty of any kind of wisdom. The most beautiful lute you could ever own Cannot be played if it has no strings. A person who has no empowerment Can never make their mantras work, Or attain any deep meditation. The damage to the person who reveals the secrets, and to the person who hears them as well, is extremely serious.  As the same work states, Suppose some ignorant fool Who lacks a proper empowerment Says, "Oh I can empower you." They pass then to the realms of hell, Together with their disciple, And remain there for as long As the Buddhas themselves exist. ***

gru.acip: PHYAG CHEN THIG LE'I LE'U GNYIS PA LAS, GANG ZHIG RGYUD LUNG NGA RGYAL GYIS, ,DBANG BSKUR MED LA 'CHAD BYED PA, ,SLOB DPON SLOB MA SHI MA THAG ,DNGOS GRUB THOB KYANG DMYAL BAR 'GRO, ZHES THUN MONG GI DNGOS GRUB 'GA' ZHIG THOB KYANG DPON SLOB GNYIS KA DMYAL BAR SKYE BAR GSUNGS SO,
gru.wylie: phyag chen thig le'i le'u gnyis pa las, gang zhig rgyud lung nga rgyal gyis, ,dbang bskur med la 'chad byed pa, ,slob dpon slob ma shi ma thag ,dngos grub thob kyang dmyal bar 'gro, zhes thun mong gi dngos grub 'ga' zhig thob kyang dpon slob gnyis ka dmyal bar skye bar gsungs so
gru.english: The second chapter of A Drop of the Great Seal states, Suppose a prideful person Decides to explain the words Of the secret teachings to someone Who lacks the proper empowerment. They might perhaps then reach Some minor kind of attainment, But the moment after their deaths The master and teacher both Will pass to the realms of hell. What this text is saying is that the master and disciple may thereby reach one of the worldly attainments, but will both then take a rebirth into the realms of hell. ***

gru.acip: BRNYAS SMOD BYED LUGS NI NAG PO PAS PHUNG PO SANGS RGYAS KYI RANG BZHIN DU GNAS PA DANG SANGS RGYAS SU SKYED PA LA SOGS PA'I BYIN GYIS BRLABS PA'I MTHUS RNAM SNANG LA SOGS PAR BYAS PA LA NANG GI SBYIN SREG GIS MCHOD CING BDE BAS BDE BA BSGRUB PAR BYA RGYU LA, 'GOG PA DANG G-YANG SAR MCHONG BA DANG DMAN PA'I BRTUL ZHUGS DANG GNAS MIN GYI BZOD PA DANG YAN LAG NYING LAG GCOD PA DANG SMYUNG BAR GNAS PA DANG DKA' THUB DANG DKA' SPYAD SOGS BYED PA BRNYAS PA'I DON DU BSHAD DO,
gru.wylie: brnyas smod byed lugs ni nag po pas phung po sangs rgyas kyi rang bzhin du gnas pa dang sangs rgyas su skyed pa la sogs pa'i byin gyis brlabs pa'i mthus rnam snang la sogs par byas pa la nang gi sbyin sreg gis mchod cing bde bas bde ba bsgrub par bya rgyu la, 'gog pa dang g-yang sar mchong ba dang dman pa'i brtul zhugs dang gnas min gyi bzod pa dang yan lag nying lag gcod pa dang smyung bar gnas pa dang dka' thub dang dka' spyad sogs byed pa brnyas pa'i don du bshad do
gru.english: How exactly is it that we hurt the parts to ourself?  Krishnapada explains it as follows.  The very nature of our five heaps is that they are these Enlightened Beings.  Among other things, they also turn into these Enlightened Beings.  Given that they are blessed with this tremendous power, we should be making offerings to our heaps, performing the act of eating as an inner offering of fire: we should be doing all that we can to find pleasant ways of making sure that our heaps feel good. If instead we undertake an action such as hanging ourselves; jumping off of a cliff; engaging in some destructive form of spiritual hardship; trying some kind of meaningless physical test; cutting off larger or smaller appendages of our body; starving ourselves; or any sort of supposedly spiritual but actually harmful, hurtful activity--well then this is what it means, he says, to hurt the parts to ourself. ***

gru.acip: BKA' BZHIN SGRUB PA, MI NUS PA SHAD SBYANG 'OS PA LA SHAD SBYANG BYA BA,
gru.wylie: bka' bzhin sgrub pa, mi nus pa shad sbyang 'os pa la shad sbyang bya ba
gru.english: We must always carry out what our Lama directs us to do.  There may be cases we are simply unable to do what They have told us to; these cases deserve though an explanation of why we were unable, and we must be sure to go to them and make this explanation. *** Some notes on this guideline from Je Tsongkapa's commentary to the Fifty Verses:

gru.acip: BLO GROS CHEN PO STE SHES RAB CHE BA'I SLOB MAS RANG GI BLA MA'I BKA' STE BSGO BA NI 'BAD PA CHEN PO BYAS TE MNYAN CING BSGRUB PAR BYA'O, DE YANG MI 'DOD BZHIN DU MA YIN PAR SHIN TU DGA' ZHING RANGS PA'I SEMS KYIS BYA'O,
gru.wylie: blo gros chen po ste shes rab che ba'i slob mas rang gi bla ma'i bka' ste bsgo ba ni 'bad pa chen po byas te mnyan cing bsgrub par bya'o, de yang mi 'dod bzhin du ma yin par shin tu dga' zhing rangs pa'i sems kyis bya'o
gru.english: What this text is saying is that disciples "who posses high intellect "--which means disciples of great wisdom--must make great efforts to "obey," to carry out, their Lama's "commands": meaning the things They ask us to do.  And we must never do so unwillingly, but rather "with joy," meaning that we derive high pleasure in doing so. ***

gru.acip: 'O NA BLA MAS BSGO BA THAMS CAD SGRUB DGOS SAM SNYAM NA, CHOS DANG LDAN PA'I BSGO BA YIN YANG RANG GIS JI LTAR BYAS KYANG MI NUS PA YIN NA MI NUS PA'I BSGO BA DE LA MI NUS PA'I RGYU MTSAN LEGS PAR BRDA SPROD PA'I TSIG GIS SHAD SBYANG BYAS NAS MA BSGRUBS KYANG NYES PA MED DO, GAL TE BYA BA DE RIGS PA DANG LDAN PA'I SGO NAS BSGRUB PAR NUS PA MIN PAR MI RIGS PA CHOS MI LDAN GYI BSGO BA YIN NA'ANG SNGAR LTAR SHAD SBYANG BYAS LA 'JUG PAR MI BYA
gru.wylie: 'o na bla mas bsgo ba thams cad sgrub dgos sam snyam na, chos dang ldan pa'i bsgo ba yin yang rang gis ji ltar byas kyang mi nus pa yin na mi nus pa'i bsgo ba de la mi nus pa'i rgyu mtshan legs par brda sprod pa'i tshig gis shad sbyang byas nas ma bsgrubs kyang nyes pa med do, gal te bya ba de rigs pa dang ldan pa'i sgo nas bsgrub par nus pa min par mi rigs pa chos mi ldan gyi bsgo ba yin na'ang sngar ltar shad sbyang byas la 'jug par mi bya
gru.english: Now the following question might arise.  "When it says that we must "obey our Lama's commands," does it mean that we should do whatever They ask us to do?" If the order is one which is in keeping with the Dharma, but there is absolutely no way that we would be capable of performing the task required, then we must go to our Master and in respectful terms inform Them that we are unable to fulfill Their directive, for the reason that we are simply personally incapable of doing so.  If we then fail to carry out the task, we have done no bad deed. Suppose though that the task that They direct us to carry out is not something which can be done and still be proper; that is, suppose They order us to do something which is wrong: something which is not in keeping with the Dharma.   In this case we must go before Them, as described above, and explain why we cannot perform the action requested--for we should not perform this action. ***

gru.acip: DE 'DRA BA MA YIN PA'I BLA MA'I CHOS LDAN GYI BKA' BSGO BA THAMS CAD LAS 'DA' BAR MI BYA BA LA 'BAD BA CI YOD THAMS CAD KYIS 'BAD DE DNGOS GRUB MCHOG THUN MONG GNYIS DANG MTHO RIS LHA MI'I RTEN DANG DE LA NYE BAR MKHO BA'I BDE BA THAMS CAD BLA MA LAS 'THOB LA DE YANG BLA MA'I GSUNG NYID SLOB MA LA BYIN RLABS 'JUG PA'I SGO'I GTZO BO YIN PA DE BAS NA GNAS DE LAS 'GAL BAR MI BYA'O,
gru.wylie: de 'dra ba ma yin pa'i bla ma'i chos ldan gyi bka' bsgo ba thams cad las 'da' bar mi bya ba la 'bad ba ci yod thams cad kyis 'bad de dngos grub mchog thun mong gnyis dang mtho ris lha mi'i rten dang de la nye bar mkho ba'i bde ba thams cad bla ma las 'thob la de yang bla ma'i gsung nyid slob ma la byin rlabs 'jug pa'i sgo'i gtso bo yin pa de bas na gnas de las 'gal bar mi bya'o
gru.english: Aside from cases like the one just mentioned, we must make every effort that we are humanly capable of to carry out whatever our Lama orders us to do which is in keeping with the Dharma: we must never fail to carry out a single such directive. And this is because everything that we could ever hope for is achieved through our Lama's grace: every attainment, both the ultimate goal and the shared goals; achieving a rebirth in the higher realms, the body of a human or a pleasure being; and every form of happiness that we could ever need. The words that pass to us from the holy lips of our Lama are, simply put, the single highest from of blessing that we disciples could ever receive.  As such, we must never fail to do exactly what these words tell us to do. ***

gru.acip: GAL TE 'DI NI KHYAD GSOD YIN PAS DE'I LTUNG BA NI RTZA LTUNG GNYIS PA YIN GYI BCU GSUM PA MIN NO ZHE NA, SKYON MED DE RTZA LTUNG GNYIS PA NI 'DI TZAM LAS 'DAS KYANG NYES PA CIR YANG MI 'GYUR ZHES BCAS PA KHYAD DU GSAD NAS BCAS MTSAMS LAS 'DAS PA YIN LA, 'DI NI SNGAR DPAL MCHOG 'GREL PA'I LUNG DRANGS PA LTAR YID KYIS RNAL 'BYOR SGOM PA YOD NA DE TZAM GYIS RDOR DRIL SOGS KYI DGOS PA 'GRUB PAS DE DAG MI DGOS SO, ,ZHES DAM TSIG BSTEN PA DOR BA YIN PAS KHYAD PAR CHE BA'I PHYIR RO,
gru.wylie: gal te 'di ni khyad gsod yin pas de'i ltung ba ni rtsa ltung gnyis pa yin gyi bcu gsum pa min no zhe na, skyon med de rtsa ltung gnyis pa ni 'di tsam las 'das kyang nyes pa cir yang mi 'gyur zhes bcas pa khyad du gsad nas bcas mtshams las 'das pa yin la, 'di ni sngar dpal mchog 'grel pa'i lung drangs pa ltar yid kyis rnal 'byor sgom pa yod na de tsam gyis rdor dril sogs kyi dgos pa 'grub pas de dag mi dgos so, ,zhes dam tshig bsten pa dor ba yin pas khyad par che ba'i phyir ro
gru.english: One may ask the following question: "If we commit this particular root downfall through an act of disregarding or discounting something, then wouldn't we be committing the second root downfall, and not the thirteenth?" And yet there's no such problem.  In the second root downfall, we are disregarding a rule set down for us by saying, "I don't see where there'd be any problem at all if I went beyond this particular rule," and then we do actually transgress the rule. Here in this root downfall though we act as described earlier in the citation from the commentary on Highest Glory: we are rejecting the practice of using these instruments of pledge by saying, "If I can perform this particular yogic practice mentally, then that in itself fulfills the need for a diamond, a bell, and the like; as such, the actual objects are of no use for me." We can say thus that there's quite a big difference between the acts of disregarding something in these two downfalls. *** Geshe Tsewang Samdrup now on the last of the fourteen root downfalls:

gru.acip: SAM PU tA'I BRTAG PA DGU PA'I RAB BYED GSUM PA LAS, GLEGS BAM DANG NI BRIS SKU NYID, ,GAL TE SKAL BA MED MTHONG NA, ,SKYE BA 'DIR NI 'GRUB MI 'GYUR, ,'JIG RTEN PHA ROL SPYOD YUL MIN,
gru.wylie: sam pu Ta'i brtag pa dgu pa'i rab byed gsum pa las, glegs bam dang ni bris sku nyid, ,gal te skal ba med mthong na, ,skye ba 'dir ni 'grub mi 'gyur, ,'jig rten pha rol spyod yul min
gru.english: As the third chapter of the ninth section of the secret book called Samputa says, If a person without sufficient goodness Lays eyes on your secret books or images, You will not reach your goal in the present life, Nor ever see yourself these things In the lives you have to come. ***

gru.acip: BOD KYI MKHAS PA KHA CIG NA RE, RDOR DRIL GYIS NI KHYAB PAR SNANG BAS SGRUB PAR MI NUS PAS NA DAM TSIG RDOR DRIL ZUR PA MI STON PA ZHIG BCANG GSUNG STE LEGS PA 'DRA'O,
gru.wylie: bod kyi mkhas pa kha cig na re, rdor dril gyis ni khyab par snang bas sgrub par mi nus pas na dam tshig rdor dril zur pa mi ston pa zhig bcang gsung ste legs pa 'dra'o
gru.english: Certain Tibetan sages have said then that--given the fact that [during public rituals] our diamond and bell can be seen all over the place--we will then fail to reach the goal; and that therefore we should keep a separate diamond and bell of pledge: one which we do not show.  This seems to me an excellent idea. *** Back to the String of Shining Jewels:

gru.acip: LHA DANG SNGAGS KYI DE NYID MI SHES KYANG , LHA'I SGRUB THABS GCIG TZAM MAM, BSKYED RDZOGS SU MING BTAGS PA'I DMIGS PA THUN RE TZAM BSGOM PA LA BRTEN NAS NGA RNAL 'BYOR PA'O ZHES 'DZIN NA BRDZUN GYI RNAL 'BYOR NGA RGYAL BYED PA'I SBOM PO,
gru.wylie: lha dang sngags kyi de nyid mi shes kyang , lha'i sgrub thabs gcig tsam mam, bskyed rdzogs su ming btags pa'i dmigs pa thun re tsam bsgom pa la brten nas nga rnal 'byor pa'o zhes 'dzin na brdzun gyi rnal 'byor nga rgyal byed pa'i sbom po
gru.english: Suppose we are the kind of person who doesn't know the real truth about Angels and the teachings of the Secret Word.  But we are engaged in a single small practice for reaching an Angel, or else we are meditating once in a while on some object that's supposedly related to the stage of creation or the stage of completion.  And so because of this we feel some kind of pride, considering ourselves to be a master practitioner.  With this then we have committed the serious offense known as [7] "Having delusions about being a master practitioner." *** Je Tsongkapa comments simply--

gru.acip: DUS RTAG TU BLA MA DE'I BSNYEN BKUR BA'I BYA BA LA LDANG MKHAS TE LDANG BA YANG PA DANG DE DAG SGRUB PA LA MKHAS PA PHUN SUM TSOGS PAR BYA'O,
gru.wylie: dus rtag tu bla ma de'i bsnyen bkur ba'i bya ba la ldang mkhas te ldang ba yang pa dang de dag sgrub pa la mkhas pa phun sum tshogs par bya'o
gru.english: We must become, as the text says, constant masters at rising from our seat in order to honor our Lama.  What this means is that we become experts in the practice of rising gracefully and lightly from our seat as They themselves stand or sit. *** Back to Geshe Samdrup:

gru.acip: PHYAG RGYA'I DE KHO NA NYID 'DZIN PA NI RIGS GANG GI SGRUB PA PO GANG YIN PAS RNAM SNANG LA SOGS PA'I SKUR BSKYED NAS SEMS CAN GYI KHAMS SBYONG ZHING BZLAS SGOM BYED PA,
gru.wylie: phyag rgya'i de kho na nyid 'dzin pa ni rigs gang gi sgrub pa po gang yin pas rnam snang la sogs pa'i skur bskyed nas sems can gyi khams sbyong zhing bzlas sgom byed pa
gru.english: "Holding the suchness of the accoutrement" here means that we rise up in the divine form of the Angel of Appearances, or whichever Angel it is that we are following.  In this form then we work to purify the nature of every living being, and to perform the practices of recitation and meditation. ***

gru.acip: RIN CHEN NI MNYAM NYID YE SHES YIN LA, RIGS NI DE LAS BYUNG BAS NA RIN CHEN 'BYUNG LDAN NO, RNAL 'BYOR NI DE'I RNAM PAR SEMS RTZE GCIG GIS YANG DANG YANG DU SBYOR BA RIN 'BYUNG GI RIGS KYI SGRUB PA PO STE DE'I 'DA' BAR MI BYA BAR NYAMS SU BLANG BAR BYA BA'I DAM TSIG NI SBYIN PA LA DGA' BA RNAMS DE LA SBYOR BAS DE DAG DGA' BAR BYED PA'I PHYIR YID DU 'ONG BA DE LA'O,
gru.wylie: rin chen ni mnyam nyid ye shes yin la, rigs ni de las byung bas na rin chen 'byung ldan no, rnal 'byor ni de'i rnam par sems rtse gcig gis yang dang yang du sbyor ba rin 'byung gi rigs kyi sgrub pa po ste de'i 'da' bar mi bya bar nyams su blang bar bya ba'i dam tshig ni sbyin pa la dga' ba rnams de la sbyor bas de dag dga' bar byed pa'i phyir yid du 'ong ba de la'o
gru.english: The "jewel" in the name of the Angel called "Source of Jewels" is the wisdom referred to as "equivalent wisdom."  Because the family here is produced by this wisdom, the Angel is named "Source of Jewels."  The yoga of this Angel is where we unite ourselves, over and over, with this Angel, single-pointedly.  And this is what makes someone a practitioner of this particular family. The pledge that we take upon ourselves here--the action which we cannot transgress--is to delight in the various forms of giving. And when we "join" or apply ourselves to this act of giving, it brings us delight: thus it is that giving is described as "wonderful." ***

gru.acip: NYIN RE LA SBYIN PA BYED LUGS NI ZANG ZING DANG CHOS LA DNGOS SU BYED PA MA BYUNG BA'I TSE, RANG GI LUS DANG LONGS SPYOD GZHAN LA GTONG BA'I BSAM PA DANG RANG GI DGE BA'I CHOS GZHAN LA BSNGO BA'I BSAM PA SBYANGS TE, GTONG SEMS SPEL BA NYID SBYIN PA LA SLOB PA'I GTZO BO YIN PA'I PHYIR RO, ,BTANG SNYOMS DANG BYAMS PA BSGOMS NAS KYANG MI 'JIGS PA DANG BYAMS PA'I SBYIN PA BYA'O, ,DE BZHIN DU DAM CHOS 'DZIN PA DANG MCHOD PA LA YANG DNGOS DE CHOS DANG YID KYI SGO NAS BSGRUB PAR BYA STE RIGS GZHAN GNYIS KYI NI GO SLA'O,
gru.wylie: nyin re la sbyin pa byed lugs ni zang zing dang chos la dngos su byed pa ma byung ba'i tshe, rang gi lus dang longs spyod gzhan la gtong ba'i bsam pa dang rang gi dge ba'i chos gzhan la bsngo ba'i bsam pa sbyangs te, gtong sems spel ba nyid sbyin pa la slob pa'i gtso bo yin pa'i phyir ro, ,btang snyoms dang byams pa bsgoms nas kyang mi 'jigs pa dang byams pa'i sbyin pa bya'o, ,de bzhin du dam chos 'dzin pa dang mchod pa la yang dngos de chos dang yid kyi sgo nas bsgrub par bya ste rigs gzhan gnyis kyi ni go sla'o
gru.english: Now as for how we perform these acts of giving, there may be days when we're not actually able to present someone else with a material object, or with the Dharma.  In cases like this we should do the practice mentally, reflecting on how we can give our body or our things away to others, and dedicating to others the good deeds we have already done. This makes sense because the main point of the practice of giving is to increase our inner capacity for generosity.  And the very emotions of equanimity and love are giving protection from fear, and giving love.  It's easily grasped then how we can practice in the other two families the actions of both keeping the Dharma and making offerings, both actually and mentally. *** Returning now to Geshe Tsewang Samdrup, for the pledges of the next family:

gru.acip: PHYI NANG GSANG BA DE KHO NA NYID KYI MCHOD PA SOGS THAMS CAD LA RANG GI STOBS CI YOD KYIS 'BAD PA KHAS LEN PA DANG , NYIN MTSAN DUS DRUG TU MCHOD PA BYED PA STE GNYIS, DON GRUB KYI RIGS KYI DAM TSIG STE BSDOM NA BCU DGU'O,
gru.wylie: phyi nang gsang ba de kho na nyid kyi mchod pa sogs thams cad la rang gi stobs ci yod kyis 'bad pa khas len pa dang , nyin mtshan dus drug tu mchod pa byed pa ste gnyis, don grub kyi rigs kyi dam tshig ste bsdom na bcu dgu'o
gru.english: There are, finally, two pledges for the Family of Attainment, or Amoghasiddhi.  The first is [18] the promise to exert ourselves, to the very best of offering; for example in performing the outer offerings, the inner offerings, the secret offering, and the offering of suchness. The second pledge here is [19] to actually perform these offerings six times in every 24-hour period. This then brings us to a total of 19 different individual pledges for the five Families. *** Je Tsongkapa explains:

gru.acip: LNGA PA DON GRUB KYI SDOM GZUNG NI, ME TOG SOGS PHYI'I MCHOD PA, NANG MCHOD BYIN GYIS RLABS NAS 'BUL BA NANG GI MCHOD PA, PHYAG RGYA DANG SBYAR BA'I BDE BAS DKYIL 'KHOR BA'I LHA RNAMS TSIM PAR BYED PA GSANG BA'I MCHOD PA, BDE BA DES STONG NYID RTOGS PA DE KHO NA NYID KYI MCHOD PA STE SNGAR BZHIN SLOB PA'O,
gru.wylie: lnga pa don grub kyi sdom gzung ni, me tog sogs phyi'i mchod pa, nang mchod byin gyis rlabs nas 'bul ba nang gi mchod pa, phyag rgya dang sbyar ba'i bde bas dkyil 'khor ba'i lha rnams tshim par byed pa gsang ba'i mchod pa, bde ba des stong nyid rtogs pa de kho na nyid kyi mchod pa ste sngar bzhin slob pa'o
gru.english: Here as our fifth point is a description of the vow taken for the Angel of Attainment.  Offering flowers and the like constitutes an outer offering.  The inner offering is where we perform the ceremony of blessing the inner offering, and then present it.  It is the secret offering to satiate the Angels of the secret world with the bliss that comes through union with a sacred partner.  And the offering of suchness is to use this bliss to perceive emptiness.  We must train ourselves in these offerings, as mentioned before. ***

gru.acip: TSANGS PA BZHI NI TSANGS PA'I GNAS BZHI RU GRAGS PA'I TSAD MED BZHI STE DON GRUB BYA SGRUB YE SHES YIN LA SEMS CAN GYI DON GYI BYA BA SGRUB PA'I THABS DAM PA NI TSAD MED BZHI YIN PAS DE NYIN DANG MTSAN DU SGOM PA LA NANG TSAN GYI BYA BA YIN NAM DPYAD PAR BYA'O,
gru.wylie: tshangs pa bzhi ni tshangs pa'i gnas bzhi ru grags pa'i tshad med bzhi ste don grub bya sgrub ye shes yin la sems can gyi don gyi bya ba sgrub pa'i thabs dam pa ni tshad med bzhi yin pas de nyin dang mtshan du sgom pa la nang tshan gyi bya ba yin nam dpyad par bya'o
gru.english: The mention here of the "Four of the Pure One" is a reference to the Four Immeasurable Thoughts, which are sometimes spoken of as the Four Practices of the Pure One.  The point here is that the Angel named Attainment is the wisdom of attainment, and the very highest method of attaining or achieving the benefit of all other beings is this practice of the Four Immeasurable Thoughts.  As such it would be worth looking into this particular pledge to see if the practice of meditating upon these four during specific periods of the night and day should be considered one of its component parts. *** This next section is an explanation of the wording used to take the vows of the secret word, which begins: I call upon every Buddha And bodhisattva there is; Listen now please to me. My name is (say your name), And from this moment Until the day that I reach The inner heart of enlightenment, I give birth to the supreme Wish for enlightenment, A Wish with nothing higher, Just as the Protectors Of the past and present and future Committed themselves first To becoming an Enlightened Being.]

gru.acip: DAM TSIG DE RNAMS THAMS CAD RIGS SO SO'I SGRUB PA PO THAMS CAD KYIS BSRUNG DGOS MOD KYANG RANG GI RIGS GANG YIN PA'I DAM TSIG LA LHAG PAR NAN TAN BYED DGOS PAR SANGS RGYAS GSANG BAS GSUNGS,
gru.wylie: dam tshig de rnams thams cad rigs so so'i sgrub pa po thams cad kyis bsrung dgos mod kyang rang gi rigs gang yin pa'i dam tshig la lhag par nan tan byed dgos par sangs rgyas gsang bas gsungs
gru.english: Now it is admittedly true that all of the pledges of the Five Families are to be honored by practitioners, despite their being connected to any one of the families; nonetheless, the teachings of the tantra called the "secret Buddha" explain that each of us should pay special attention to honoring the pledges of the particular family to which we belong. ***

gru.acip: DPER NA MI BSKYOD PA'AM DE'I RIGS LA ME TOG PHOG PA'I SGRUB PA PO YIN NA DAM TSIG GSUM DANG SLOB DPON GZUNG BA LA NAN TAN DU BYA DGOS PA LTA BU'O,
gru.wylie: dper na mi bskyod pa'am de'i rigs la me tog phog pa'i sgrub pa po yin na dam tshig gsum dang slob dpon gzung ba la nan tan du bya dgos pa lta bu'o
gru.english: Suppose, for example, that we are a practitioner whose flower petal during the empowerment fell into the section of the mandala dedicated to the Angel named Unshakable.  In this case we are meant to pay special attention to the three pledges of this Angel, and to maintaining our relationship with our Master. ***

gru.acip: SROG GCOD PA NAS RDZUN GYI BAR SPONG BA BZHI'I STENG DU CHANG 'THUNG BA SPONG BA'I BSLAB PA'I GZHI LNGA NI DNGOS GRUB 'GRUB PA'I GZHIR BSRUNG DGOS TE,
gru.wylie: srog gcod pa nas rdzun gyi bar spong ba bzhi'i steng du chang 'thung ba spong ba'i bslab pa'i gzhi lnga ni dngos grub 'grub pa'i gzhir bsrung dgos te
gru.english: This five-part foundation of giving up the four negative deeds from killing up to lying, and the one of intoxicants on top of them, should be honored as the basis of reaching every spiritual attainment there is. ***

gru.acip: BZA' BA'I DAM TSIG SHA LNGA DANG BDUD RTZI LNGA BSTEN DGOS PAR RNAL 'BYOR BLA MED KYI SKABS SU GSUNGS PA RNAMS LA GRUB NA LAS DANG PO PAS RI LU BYAS NAS NYI MA RE RE ZHING BSTEN PAR GSUNGS PA LTAR BYA LA, MA GRUB NA BZA' BTUNG LA DE DAG BSAM GTAN TZAM GYIS BSKYED NAS LONGS SPYOD PAR BYAS PAS KYANG 'GRUB,
gru.wylie: bza' ba'i dam tshig sha lnga dang bdud rtsi lnga bsten dgos par rnal 'byor bla med kyi skabs su gsungs pa rnams la grub na las dang po pas ri lu byas nas nyi ma re re zhing bsten par gsungs pa ltar bya la, ma grub na bza' btung la de dag bsam gtan tsam gyis bskyed nas longs spyod par byas pas kyang 'grub
gru.english: We also have a pledge which relates to eating; that is, it is spoken in the secret teachings of the unsurpassed class that we are required to partake of the five types of flesh and the five types of nectar.  If it is possible, those who are just starting out should follow the advice in scripture about partaking, each day, of these substances in the form of a sacred pill.  In a case where it is not possible, we can also perform this practice by transforming our regular food and drink with our concentration into these substances, and then partaking of them. ***

gru.acip: ,GANG ZHIG MCHOG DANG THUN MONG DNGOS GRUB KYI, ,RTZA BAR RAB BSNGAGS DAM TSIG RGYA MTSO LAS, ,BDE MCHOG RTZA BA'I RGYUD LAS GSUNGS PA YI, ,DAM TSIG BRGYAD KYI RNAM BZHAG CUNG ZAD 'BRI,
gru.wylie: gang zhig mchog dang thun mong dngos grub kyi, ,rtsa bar rab bsngags dam tshig rgya mtsho las, ,bde mchog rtsa ba'i rgyud las gsungs pa yi, ,dam tshig brgyad kyi rnam bzhag cung zad 'bri
gru.english: There is something which is praised as being The very root of all attainments: The highest, and the ones which are shared as well. This is the eight pledges, of all that vast sea Of pledges there are--the ones spoken In the root tantra of Highest Bliss. And here I will make Just the slightest presentation of them.

gru.acip: ,SHR'I HE RU KA RNAL 'BYOR MCHOG ,SLOB DPON RNAL 'BYOR MA NYID YIN, ,RGYUD 'DI RU NI SGRUB PA PO, ,LEGS PAR GYUR PA NYID YIN TE, ,BRNYAS MI BYA ZHING SPANG MI BYA, ,NUS PA YIS NI MCHOD PAR BYA,
gru.wylie: shrI he ru ka rnal 'byor mchog ,slob dpon rnal 'byor ma nyid yin, ,rgyud 'di ru ni sgrub pa po, ,legs par gyur pa nyid yin te, ,brnyas mi bya zhing spang mi bya, ,nus pa yis ni mchod par bya
gru.english: Glorious Heruka is the highest of deep practices, and the Master Is nothing less than your mother. Those who follow this secret practice Are nothing less than excellent; And so you should never berate them, And never abandon them. You should make to them offerings As much as you are able.

gru.acip: BDE MCHOG GI RGYUD 'DI RU NI DBANG BSKUR BA'I RNAL 'BYOR PA SGRUB PA PO NI LEGS PA STE MCHOG TU GYUR PA YIN TE, DES NA DE DAG LA BRNYAS PA STE KHYAD DU GSOD PA DANG , MI SPANG BA STE MI SMAD PAR GUS PAS CI NUS PA YIS MCHOD PAR BYA'O,, ZHES PA'O,,
gru.wylie: bde mchog gi rgyud 'di ru ni dbang bskur ba'i rnal 'byor pa sgrub pa po ni legs pa ste mchog tu gyur pa yin te, des na de dag la brnyas pa ste khyad du gsod pa dang , mi spang ba ste mi smad par gus pas ci nus pa yis mchod par bya'o,, zhes pa'o
gru.english: Those who follow this secret practice of Highest Bliss--that is, those deep practitioners who have gained initiation into it--are nothing less than excellent, meaning nothing less than the highest of practitioners.  And so you should never berate them, never discount them.  Nor should you ever abandon them, meaning put them down; but rather you should make to them offerings, as much as you are able. ************

gru.acip: ,K'A K'A GDONG SOGS BRGYAD PO NI, ,MOS DANG DAD PA 'PHEL BYED PA, ,RTAG PAR DNGOS GRUB RNAMS KYI RGYU, ,DAM TSIG RNAMS KYANG SKYONG BAR BYED,
gru.wylie: kA kA gdong sogs brgyad po ni, ,mos dang dad pa 'phel byed pa, ,rtag par dngos grub rnams kyi rgyu, ,dam tshig rnams kyang skyong bar byed
gru.english: With Crowface and the rest of the eight, belief and devotion come to increase. They are always the cause of every attainment; keep then all these commitments.

gru.acip: K'A K'A ZHES SOGS RKANG PA GNYIS KYI DON NI, KH'A GDONG MA LA SOGS PA SGO MTSAMS MA BRGYAD MCHOD PA DE BZHIN DU SGRUB PA POS BDE MCHOG GI RNAL 'BYOR PA RNAMS LA DAD CING GUS PAS MCHOD NA YID BYIN GYIS RLOB PA YIN ZHES PA'I DON DU GSUNG ZHING ,
gru.wylie: kA kA zhes sogs rkang pa gnyis kyi don ni, khA gdong ma la sogs pa sgo mtshams ma brgyad mchod pa de bzhin du sgrub pa pos bde mchog gi rnal 'byor pa rnams la dad cing gus pas mchod na yid byin gyis rlob pa yin zhes pa'i don du gsung zhing
gru.english: Here is the meaning of the two lines [in the Tibetan, three in the English] that include the words, "Crowface and the rest."  We make offerings to the eight woman Guardians of the Gates: to Crowface and the rest.  Just so, a follower of this secret practice should make offerings, with great devotion and respect, to deep practitioners of the teachings of Highest Bliss.  If they do so, say the lines, then their minds will receive great blessings.

gru.acip: YANG NA KH'A GDONG MA LA SOGS PA BRGYAD PO 'DI GUS PA DANG DAD PA 'PHEL BAR BYED PA YIN LA, DE YANG DNGOS GRUB RNAMS KYI RGYU YIN NO ZHES PA STE, DE YANG SNGAR BSHAD PA LTAR BLA MA DANG 'DI YI RNAL 'BYOR PA LA RTAG PAR TE RGYUN DU GUS PA NI DNGOS GRUB RNAMS KYI RGYU YIN LA, GUS PA DANG DAD PA GONG NAS GONG DU 'PHEL BAR BYED PA LA, ,BAR DU GCOD PA'I BGEGS NI SGO MTSAMS MAS BZLOG PA YIN PAS, SGO MTSAMS MA RNAMS DE DAG 'PHEL BA'I RGYU YIN NO,, ZHES PA'O,,
gru.wylie: yang na khA gdong ma la sogs pa brgyad po 'di gus pa dang dad pa 'phel bar byed pa yin la, de yang dngos grub rnams kyi rgyu yin no zhes pa ste, de yang sngar bshad pa ltar bla ma dang 'di yi rnal 'byor pa la rtag par te rgyun du gus pa ni dngos grub rnams kyi rgyu yin la, gus pa dang dad pa gong nas gong du 'phel bar byed pa la, ,bar du gcod pa'i bgegs ni sgo mtshams mas bzlog pa yin pas, sgo mtshams ma rnams de dag 'phel ba'i rgyu yin no,, zhes pa'o
gru.english: You can also read the lines as saying that Crowface and the rest of the eight Guardians cause your respect and devotion to come to increase; and that these emotions are the cause of every spiritual attainment.  The point here is that, as we noted before, the cause of every spiritual attainment is to always (meaning continually) feel respect for one's Lama and for deep practitioners who follow this secret teaching.  And the Guardians of the Gates can help us stop any hindrances which might prevent this respect and faith from growing ever higher; as such, they are causes that help these emotions increase.

gru.acip: K'A K'A SOGS KYI DON 'CHAD TSUL PHYI MA LTAR NA RTAG PAR DNGOS GRUB RNAMS KYI RGYU ZHES PA DNGOS GRUB RNAMS KYI RGYUR GYUR PA'I DAM TSIG RNAMS ZHES 'OG MA DANG 'BREL DGOS SO,,
gru.wylie: kA kA sogs kyi don 'chad tshul phyi ma ltar na rtag par dngos grub rnams kyi rgyu zhes pa dngos grub rnams kyi rgyur gyur pa'i dam tshig rnams zhes 'og ma dang 'brel dgos so
gru.english: If we read the part about the Crowface one and so on the latter way, then the line that says "They are always the cause of every attainment" has to be connected to the following lines, so that together they mean that these commitments are the cause of every spiritual attainment. ************

gru.acip: THOGS MED PA ZHES PA NI, GANG GIS KYANG GZHOM DU MI NUS PA'I DON DU BSHAD PAS, SNGAGS KYI THUN MONG MA YIN PA'I GRUB MTHA' LAS GZHAN DU BKRI MI NUS PA DANG ,
gru.wylie: thogs med pa zhes pa ni, gang gis kyang gzhom du mi nus pa'i don du bshad pas, sngags kyi thun mong ma yin pa'i grub mtha' las gzhan du bkri mi nus pa dang
gru.english: The word "untouchable" is often explained as referring to someone who cannot be overcome by another.  The expression here means that one should reach the point where they could never be led off into any system of belief other than the unique way of the secret word.

gru.acip: ,'DI BRGYAD DAM TSIG KUN SPYOD YIN, ,SGRUB PA LA NI GNAS PA YI, ,SGRUB PA POS NI RTAG SHES BYA,
gru.wylie: 'di brgyad dam tshig kun spyod yin, ,sgrub pa la ni gnas pa yi, ,sgrub pa pos ni rtag shes bya
gru.english: This then is the way Of life of the eight pledges; Practitioners who live a life Trying to carry them out Must always be aware.

gru.acip: 'DI BRGYAD DAM TSIG CES SOGS RKANG PA GSUM NI, DE YANG SNGA MA RNAMS KYI DON MDOR HRIL GYIS SGRIL NA, SNGAR BSHAD PA LTAR GYI G-YON PA'I KUN SPYOD THAMS CAD BYED PA DANG , RGYUD 'DIR DBANG BSKUR BA'I SGRUB PA PO DANG SLOB DPON LA MI BRNYAS SHING CI NUS KYIS MCHOD PA RNAMS NI DAM TSIG DANG PO DANG ,
gru.wylie: 'di brgyad dam tshig ces sogs rkang pa gsum ni, de yang snga ma rnams kyi don mdor hril gyis sgril na, sngar bshad pa ltar gyi g-yon pa'i kun spyod thams cad byed pa dang , rgyud 'dir dbang bskur ba'i sgrub pa po dang slob dpon la mi brnyas shing ci nus kyis mchod pa rnams ni dam tshig dang po dang
gru.english: We turn next to the three lines [in the Tibetan] that include "This...the eight pledges."  Now we could summarize the points given above in the following way.  The first pledge is that we should, as explained earlier on, observe all the various forms of leftways behavior.  We should never berate those practitioners who have been empowered to follow this secret teachings, nor our Master, and we should further make offerings to them, to the best of our ability.

gru.acip: DE DAG SHES PA TZAM LA MI 'JOG PAR TSUL BZHIN DU SGRUB PA LA GNAS PA'I SGRUB PA PO RNAMS KYIS RTAG TU STE YANG DANG YANG DU DRAN SHES BAG YOD DANG LDAN PAR BYAS TE BSRUNG BAR BYA YI, BRJED CING YAL BAR 'DOR BAR BYA BA MA YIN NO,, ZHES PA'O,,
gru.wylie: de dag shes pa tsam la mi 'jog par tshul bzhin du sgrub pa la gnas pa'i sgrub pa po rnams kyis rtag tu ste yang dang yang du dran shes bag yod dang ldan par byas te bsrung bar bya yi, brjed cing yal bar 'dor bar bya ba ma yin no,, zhes pa'o
gru.english: Those practitioners who seek to live a life where they are trying to carry out these pledges in the proper way, rather than just being satisfied with learning about them, must always (meaning over and over again) use mindfulness, awareness, and great care to keep their pledges.  These are not something that one should allow to slip one's mind, nor ever simply ignore. ************

gru.acip: DE YANG RTZA RGYUD LAS, ,SHIN TU MNYAM BZHAG SGRUB PA POS, ,DAM TSIG RTAG TU BSKYANG BAR BYA,
gru.wylie: de yang rtsa rgyud las, ,shin tu mnyam bzhag sgrub pa pos, ,dam tshig rtag tu bskyang bar bya
gru.english: Now the root secret teaching also says, Practitioners should stay In deep concentration And always keep their pledges.

gru.acip: ZHES GSUNGS PA LTAR, LAM 'DI'I SGRUB PA POS SHIN TU MNYAM PAR BZHAG PA STE SGO GSUM MA YENGS PAR BYAS NAS, BSRUNG BAR BYA BA RTZA BA DANG YAN LAG GI DAM TSIG RGYUD GZHAN NAS GSUNGS PA DANG , RGYUD 'DIR GSUNGS PA'I DAM TSIG RNAMS RTAG TU STE RGYUN DU MA NYAMS PAR BSKYANG BAR BYA DGOS SO,,
gru.wylie: zhes gsungs pa ltar, lam 'di'i sgrub pa pos shin tu mnyam par bzhag pa ste sgo gsum ma yengs par byas nas, bsrung bar bya ba rtsa ba dang yan lag gi dam tshig rgyud gzhan nas gsungs pa dang , rgyud 'dir gsungs pa'i dam tshig rnams rtag tu ste rgyun du ma nyams par bskyang bar bya dgos so
gru.english: Practitioners of this path should stay in deep concentration--which means that they should keep from ever being distracted, in their actions, words, or thoughts--and always (meaning continually) keep their pledges, refusing to let them be broken.  The pledges that they should keep are the primary and secondary pledges spoken in other secret teachings, as well as those spoken in this one.

gru.acip: DAM TSIG DE DAG MA BSRUNG NA RTZA RGYUD KYI LE'U DANG PO LAS, ,DAM TSIG NYAMS PAS DKYIL 'KHOR DU, ,DBANG BSKUR DNGOS GRUB THOB MI 'GYUR,
gru.wylie: dam tshig de dag ma bsrung na rtsa rgyud kyi le'u dang po las, ,dam tshig nyams pas dkyil 'khor du, ,dbang bskur dngos grub thob mi 'gyur
gru.english: The first chapter of the root secret teaching describes what will happen if you fail to keep your pledges: Those who break their pledges Will never reach the attainments Of empowerment in the secret world.

gru.acip: ZHES GSUNGS PA LTAR, RTZA BA'I DAM TSIG LA SOGS PA NYAMS PAS NI SNGAR DKYIL 'KHOR DU DBANG BSKUR BA THOB PAR MI 'GYUR BA STE NUS PA NYAMS PAR 'GYUR LA, SNGAGS BZLAS PA SOGS KYIS KYANG DNGOS GRUB THOB PAR MI 'GYUR BA DANG , DER MA ZAD TSE 'DIR NAD GDON DU MAS GTZE BA DANG , PHYI MAR NGAN 'GROR 'GRO BA SOGS KYI NYES DMIGS SHIN TU CHE BA DANG ,
gru.wylie: zhes gsungs pa ltar, rtsa ba'i dam tshig la sogs pa nyams pas ni sngar dkyil 'khor du dbang bskur ba thob par mi 'gyur ba ste nus pa nyams par 'gyur la, sngags bzlas pa sogs kyis kyang dngos grub thob par mi 'gyur ba dang , der ma zad tshe 'dir nad gdon du mas gtse ba dang , phyi mar ngan 'gror 'gro ba sogs kyi nyes dmigs shin tu che ba dang
gru.english: The point of these lines is that those who break their primary pledges or the like will "never reach" their previous empowerment into the secret world--meaning that the energy of the empowerment will be lost.  And then even if they undertake practices such as reciting the secret words they will never reach any spiritual attainments.  Not only that; they will further be harmed by a great many spirits of sickness, and also have obstacles in their future lives, such as having to take birth in the lower realms.  The problems then of breaking your pledges are extremely serious.

gru.acip: ZHES SOGS KYIS DAM TSIG BSRUNG BA'I SGRUB PA PO DE LA DPA' BO DANG DPA' MO RNAMS KYIS RTAG TU DGYES PAS DGONGS PAR 'GYUR ZHING , DPAL HE RU KAS MCHOG DANG THUN MONG GI DNGOS GRUB THAMS CAD STZOL BAR 'GYUR BA SOGS PHAN YON DPAG TU MED PAR GSUNGS SO,,
gru.wylie: zhes sogs kyis dam tshig bsrung ba'i sgrub pa po de la dpa' bo dang dpa' mo rnams kyis rtag tu dgyes pas dgongs par 'gyur zhing , dpal he ru kas mchog dang thun mong gi dngos grub thams cad stsol bar 'gyur ba sogs phan yon dpag tu med par gsungs so
gru.english: The point is that all the man and woman warriors look with pleasure upon those practitioners who keep their pledges.  The glorious Heruka too comes and grants them every attainment, both the highest and those that are shared.  The benefits of keeping ones pledges are thus spoken to be infinite.

gru.acip: RANG GI KUN SPYOD TSUL DANG MTHUN PA LA BRTZON PAS, RANG GI RDO RJE SPUN RANG GI KUN SPYOD DE LAS 'DAS PA NA, DGA' BA'I BSAM PAS THABS KYIS BZLOG PA BYA BA SOGS BLA MA BSTEN TSUL 'DI GNAD CHE ZHING , DNGOS GRUB MA LUS PA'I 'BYUNG GNAS YIN PA LA,
gru.wylie: rang gi kun spyod tshul dang mthun pa la brtson pas, rang gi rdo rje spun rang gi kun spyod de las 'das pa na, dga' ba'i bsam pas thabs kyis bzlog pa bya ba sogs bla ma bsten tshul 'di gnad che zhing , dngos grub ma lus pa'i 'byung gnas yin pa la
gru.english: Now suppose that we observe one of our diamond sisters or brothers transgressing this code of behavior in some way.  Assuming that we ourselves are making sincere efforts in this same code, and that our motivation is a joyful one, we must find some skillful means to try to dissuade them from doing what they are doing. *** Je Tsongkapa expands, in His commentary upon the Fifty Verses:

gru.acip: ,'DIR MANG SMRA BA CI ZHIG DGOS, ,BLA MA DGYES BYED GANG YIN BYA, ,MI MNYES BYED KUN SPANG BA NI, ,DE DANG DE LA 'BAD DE BYA, ,DNGOS GRUB SLOB DPON RJES 'BRANG ZHES, ,RDO RJE 'DZIN PA NYID GSUNG BAR, ,SHES NAS DNGOS PO THAMS CAD KYIS, ,BLA MA YONGS SU MNYES PAR BYA,
gru.wylie: 'dir mang smra ba ci zhig dgos, ,bla ma dgyes byed gang yin bya, ,mi mnyes byed kun spang ba ni, ,de dang de la 'bad de bya, ,dngos grub slob dpon rjes 'brang zhes, ,rdo rje 'dzin pa nyid gsung bar, ,shes nas dngos po thams cad kyis, ,bla ma yongs su mnyes par bya
gru.english: The Fifty Verses says, What need is there to say much? Work with every effort you have To do those things which please your Lama And avoid those things which don't. The Keeper of the Diamond himself Has said that all attainments Follow from our Master. Once you grasp this fact, Then devote yourself to pleasing your Lama. With every possible thing you posses. ***

gru.acip: DE NI BLA MA DGYES BYED GANG YIN PA DE SHES PAR BYAS NAS SGRUB PA DE DANG MI MNYES PA'I RGYU GANG YIN PA DE SHES PAR BYAS NAS SPONG BA DE LA NI 'BAD DE BYED PA YIN NO, ,DE LTAR BYED PA YANG DNGOS GRUB THAMS CAD RDO RJE SLOB DPON MNYES PAR BYAS PA'I RJES SU 'BRANG BA STE RJES SU 'GRO LDOG BYED DO ZHES RDO RJE 'DZIN PA NYID KYIS GSUNGS PAS DE SHES NAS SGO GSUM GYI DNGOS PO THAMS CAD KYIS BLA MA RDO RJE SLOB DPON MNYES PAR BYA'O,
gru.wylie: de ni bla ma dgyes byed gang yin pa de shes par byas nas sgrub pa de dang mi mnyes pa'i rgyu gang yin pa de shes par byas nas spong ba de la ni 'bad de byed pa yin no, ,de ltar byed pa yang dngos grub thams cad rdo rje slob dpon mnyes par byas pa'i rjes su 'brang ba ste rjes su 'gro ldog byed do zhes rdo rje 'dzin pa nyid kyis gsungs pas de shes nas sgo gsum gyi dngos po thams cad kyis bla ma rdo rje slob dpon mnyes par bya'o
gru.english: What these lines are saying is that we should study, and learn, what it is which pleases our Lama. And then we must do it. We should as well acquaint ourselves with what it is that displeases our Lama, and avoid ever doing it.  And this is how we should devote our every effort. The reason for doing so has been described by the Holder of the Diamond himself: Each and every spiritual attainment "follows" from pleasing our Diamond Master; which is to say, the attainments come if we do please Them, and don't if we don't.  Once we grasp this fact, we must seek to please our Lama, our Diamond Master, with "every possible thing we posses": a reference to our actions, our words, and our thoughts. ***

gru.acip: DE LTAR NA SPYIR THEG PA GANG GI SGOR 'JUG KYANG THOG MAR BLA MA'I BSTEN TSUL GAL CHE BAR MANG DU GSUNGS LA KHYAD PAR DU RDO RJE THEG PA PA RNAMS KYI DNGOS GRUB THAMS CAD NI BLA MA'I RJES SU BYED PAR RGYUD DU MA LAS NAN TAN SHIN TU CHE BAR GSUNGS PAS LAM GYI RTZA BA NI RDO RJE SLOB DPON LA BSTEN TSUL YIN LA DE YANG DMIGS PA THUN RE TZAM GYI BLA MA'I RNAL 'BYOR GYIS NI BSLAB BYA 'DI RNAMS MI SHES PAS GZHUNG 'DI'I DON LEGS PAR SHES PA LA 'BAD PA CHEN PO BYA'O,
gru.wylie: de ltar na spyir theg pa gang gi sgor 'jug kyang thog mar bla ma'i bsten tshul gal che bar mang du gsungs la khyad par du rdo rje theg pa pa rnams kyi dngos grub thams cad ni bla ma'i rjes su byed par rgyud du ma las nan tan shin tu che bar gsungs pas lam gyi rtsa ba ni rdo rje slob dpon la bsten tshul yin la de yang dmigs pa thun re tsam gyi bla ma'i rnal 'byor gyis ni bslab bya 'di rnams mi shes pas gzhung 'di'i don legs par shes pa la 'bad pa chen po bya'o
gru.english: As a general note, this teaching on hope to take ourselves properly to our Lama has been described in a great many scriptures as being of vital importance, right at the outset, regardless of which of the different ways we hope to enter. More especially, there are a great mass of secret texts which absolutely insist that--for those of the diamond way--each and every spiritual attainment we could ever hope for comes directly through our Lama. As such, the very root of the path is the way in which we take ourselves to our Lama.  And it's not enough that we just reflect on the details of this Lama practice now and again in some formal meditation sessions; we won't be able to learn the guidelines this way.  Rather we must make powerful efforts to study the Fifty Verses.

gru.acip: 'DIR NI RJE BLA MAS RTZA RGYUD KYI 'GREL PA SBAS DON KUN GSAL DANG SGRUB THABS KYI RGYA CHER BSHAD PA 'DOD 'JO GNYIS SU PAn+dI TA GSUM GYI DGONGS PA GUNG SGRIGS NAS GSUNGS PA NYID GO BDE BAR BSHAD PA YIN PAS YID CHES PA'I GNAS SU GZUNG RIGS PA YIN NO,
gru.wylie: 'dir ni rje bla mas rtsa rgyud kyi 'grel pa sbas don kun gsal dang sgrub thabs kyi rgya cher bshad pa 'dod 'jo gnyis su paN+Di ta gsum gyi dgongs pa gung sgrigs nas gsungs pa nyid go bde bar bshad pa yin pas yid ches pa'i gnas su gzung rigs pa yin no
gru.english: The presentation I have given here is nothing less than a compilation of the true intent of the three masters, as found in two works by our Lord and Lama, Je Tsongkapa: the Illumination of Every Secret Point, a commentary to the root secret teaching; and the Wish-Giving Cow, an expanded explanation of the ritual for reaching the Angel.  As such you may rightly consider this presentation an authentic one.

gru.acip: DE YANG RGYUD 'DI'I SGRUB PA POS DNGOS GRUB 'GRUB PA LA G-YON PA'I KUN SPYOD MCHOG TU BSNGAGS TE, HE RU KA MNGON 'BYUNG LAS, G-YON PA'I KUN SPYOD MANG DU GSUNGS PA'I MTHAR,
gru.wylie: de yang rgyud 'di'i sgrub pa pos dngos grub 'grub pa la g-yon pa'i kun spyod mchog tu bsngags te, he ru ka mngon 'byung las, g-yon pa'i kun spyod mang du gsungs pa'i mthar
gru.english: The practice of leftways behavior is highly recommended by holy beings as the highest practice for followers of this particular secret teaching.  The practice of realization for Heruka first describes many different forms of leftwards behavior, and then says,

gru.acip: ,CUNG ZAD GSUNGS DANG MA GSUNGS PA, ,DPAL LDAN KHRAG 'THUNG G-YON PAS SPYOD, ,SGRUB BO SA STENG SA 'OG NA, ,BZLAS DANG BRTUL ZHUGS BRAL BAS KYANG , ,G-YON PAS DNGOS GRUB 'GYUR BA YIN,
gru.wylie: cung zad gsungs dang ma gsungs pa, ,dpal ldan khrag 'thung g-yon pas spyod, ,sgrub bo sa steng sa 'og na, ,bzlas dang brtul zhugs bral bas kyang , ,g-yon pas dngos grub 'gyur ba yin
gru.english: It is spoken of little, or not at all; The glorious drinker of blood acts left, And reaches the goals.  Even without Any prayers or hardships, those on the earth Or below reach attainments acting left.

gru.acip: ZHES G-YAS G-YON GNYIS LAS G-YON PA SHES RAB TU GSUNGS SHING , DE LA 'DIR SHES RAB NI, CHOS THAMS CAD RANG GI NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB PAS STONG PA'I DE KHO NA NYID DE SHES RAB KYI DMIGS PA LA DER BYAS PA DANG , DON DE RTOGS PA'I SHES RAB GNYIS SO,,
gru.wylie: zhes g-yas g-yon gnyis las g-yon pa shes rab tu gsungs shing , de la 'dir shes rab ni, chos thams cad rang gi ngo bo nyid kyis grub pas stong pa'i de kho na nyid de shes rab kyi dmigs pa la der byas pa dang , don de rtogs pa'i shes rab gnyis so
gru.english: The point here is that it is spoken that--of the right and the left--the left represents wisdom.  The word "wisdom" here refers to two different things.  The first is that object which wisdom focuses upon'the suchness which is the fact that all existing things are devoid of any nature of existing in and of themselves.  The second is that state of wisdom which realizes this fact.

gru.acip: DE'I DANG PO'I DBANG DU BYAS NA, SNOD BCUD KYI BYA BYED THAMS CAD 'JOG PA NI, CHOS KUN RANG BZHIN GYIS MA GRUB PA'I RGYU MTSAN GYIS 'JOG STE, RANG GI NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB PA LA NI, RTZA SHES LAS,
gru.wylie: de'i dang po'i dbang du byas na, snod bcud kyi bya byed thams cad 'jog pa ni, chos kun rang bzhin gyis ma grub pa'i rgyu mtshan gyis 'jog ste, rang gi ngo bo nyid kyis grub pa la ni, rtsa shes las
gru.english: Relative to the first of these, the fact that we can establish all the workings of the world around us, and of the beings in this world, is all due to the fact that no object at all exists through any nature of its own.  Suppose something were to exist through some essence of its own.  Remember the words from the Root Text on Wisdom, where it says:

gru.acip: ZHES GSUNGS PA BZHIN DU, BYA BYED GANG YANG MI RUNG BA'I PHYIR DANG , CHOS RNAMS RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PAS STONG PA LA NI,
gru.wylie: zhes gsungs pa bzhin du, bya byed gang yang mi rung ba'i phyir dang , chos rnams rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub pas stong pa la ni
gru.english: None of the workings of the thing then would be right; and this is the point.  Suppose on the other hand that everything that exists was devoid of existing by definition.  They all then would be like the other lines, the ones that say:

gru.acip: DE LTAR BYAS NA G-YON PAS MTSON PA'I SHES RAB NI DNGOS GRUB THAMS CAD KYI SGRUB BYED YIN PAS, LAM 'DI'I RTOGS PA KHYAD PAR CAN SKYE BA'I RTEN 'BREL DA LTA NAS SGRIG PA'I PHYIR DU G-YON PA'I KUN SPYOD RNAMS BYED DO,,
gru.wylie: de ltar byas na g-yon pas mtshon pa'i shes rab ni dngos grub thams cad kyi sgrub byed yin pas, lam 'di'i rtogs pa khyad par can skye ba'i rten 'brel da lta nas sgrig pa'i phyir du g-yon pa'i kun spyod rnams byed do
