gru.wylie: yang kha cig ,ma dag pa'i sgyu lus thob pa la sems dben sngon du song bas khyab par thal, gsal sgron las, de 'dra ba'i sgyu ma'i sku gang las sgrub pa'i gzhi'i rlung dang sems ni, zhes pa nas, sems dben gyi ye shes gsum bskyed pa'i sems dang , de'i bzhon pa'i rlung yin pas sgyu lus kyi sngon du sems dben 'gro dgos so, ,zhes gsungs pa'i phyir na ma khyab ste
gru.english: Someone may come then and make this other argument-- But isn't it always the case that a person first attains transcendent mind before reaching the impure body of illusion?  Because isn't there that section from The Lantern which begins with "The foundation wind and state of mind from which this kind of illusory body is made..." and goes up to "--because it is the state of mind which gives rise to the three kinds of wisdom in transcendent mind, and also the wind upon which this rides, then transcendent mind must come before the body of illusion"? To this we answer, "It doesn't necessarily follow."

gru.acip: RDZOGS RIM PAS RDOR BZLAS BYED PA'I SKABS GSUM YOD DE, DES ZHI RGYAS DBANG DRAG GI LAS SGRUB PA'I DON DU RDOR BZLAS BYED PA NA, RTZA BA'I RLUNG BZHI LA BYED LA,
gru.wylie: rdzogs rim pas rdor bzlas byed pa'i skabs gsum yod de, des zhi rgyas dbang drag gi las sgrub pa'i don du rdor bzlas byed pa na, rtsa ba'i rlung bzhi la byed la
gru.english: There are three occasions upon which a practitioner of the stage of completion engages in the practice of the recitation of the diamonds.  When they are using this practice to attain the four different modes of peace, prosperity, power, and ferocity, then they utilize the four principal winds.

gru.acip: DES MIG DANG , RNA BA DANG , SNA DANG , LCE DANG , LUS KYI MNGON SHES LNGA SGRUB PA'I DON DU RDOR BZLAS BYED PA NA, RIM BZHIN RGYU BA SOGS YAN LAG GI RLUNG LNGA LA BYED CING ,
gru.wylie: des mig dang , rna ba dang , sna dang , lce dang , lus kyi mngon shes lnga sgrub pa'i don du rdor bzlas byed pa na, rim bzhin rgyu ba sogs yan lag gi rlung lnga la byed cing
gru.english: When they are using the practice of reciting the diamonds to reach the five different types of clairvoyance--those of the eyes, ears, nose, tongue, and body--then they utilize, respectively, the five secondary winds of Running and the rest.

gru.acip: RTAGS MA GRUB STE, DE NYID LAS, SNYING GA'I MI SHIGS PA DNGOS LA RLUNG THIM PA LA NI DE'I RTZA MDUD LHOD PAR SONG BA DGOS PAS, DE'I SNGON DU SNYING GAR SDUD PA'I THABS KYIS BSDUS TE DH'U T'IR THIM PA NI DE DANG NYE BA'I DH'U T'IR THIM PA YIN GYI DER THIM PA MIN NO,,
gru.wylie: rtags ma grub ste, de nyid las, snying ga'i mi shigs pa dngos la rlung thim pa la ni de'i rtsa mdud lhod par song ba dgos pas, de'i sngon du snying gar sdud pa'i thabs kyis bsdus te dhU tIr thim pa ni de dang nye ba'i dhU tIr thim pa yin gyi der thim pa min no
gru.english: But this last is not true, for the same work states-- It is necessary that the knot in the channels of the heart must be loosened before the winds can dissolve into the indestructible drop itself, at the heart.  When prior to this then we use certain methods to gather the winds at the heart and indeed succeed in gathering them there, so that they dissolve into the channel of dance, the fact is that they dissolve into the channel of dance at a point close to this drop.  It is not though that they actually dissolve into the drop.

gru.acip: DANG PO GRUB STE, LE'U GSUM PAR, RIN CHEN BRTAN PAR GYUR NAS SPRO, ,BRTAN PAR MA GYUR YONGS MI SPRO, ,ZHES PA'I GZHUNG GI MTHAR THUG GI DON BSHAD PA'I SKABS KYI SGRON GSAL LAS DE LTAR GSUNGS PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: dang po grub ste, le'u gsum par, rin chen brtan par gyur nas spro, ,brtan par ma gyur yongs mi spro, ,zhes pa'i gzhung gi mthar thug gi don bshad pa'i skabs kyi sgron gsal las de ltar gsungs pa'i phyir
gru.english: The first point here is true because this is what the Lantern says at the point where it explains the ultimate meaning of the third chapter of the root tantra where it states, When the vision is stable the jewel glows; When it's not yet stable, it can never glow.

gru.acip: GNYIS PA GRUB STE, LUS DBEN GYI SKABS SU SNYING GAR GNAD DU BSNUN PA LAS BYUNG BA'I STONG PA BZHI'I YE SHES MED PA'I PHYIR, SPROS PAS CHOG GO ,
gru.wylie: gnyis pa grub ste, lus dben gyi skabs su snying gar gnad du bsnun pa las byung ba'i stong pa bzhi'i ye shes med pa'i phyir, spros pas chog go
gru.english: The second point from above is true because at the stage of transcendent body there is no wisdom of the four forms of emptiness which has come about through working at crucial points in the heart.  One could go on at length on these points.

gru.acip: MKHAS GRUB RJE'I GSUNG ZIN BRIS LAS, SROG RTZOL GSUM DANG KHYAD PAR DU RDOR BZLAS TE NANG GI RKYEN GSUM DANG , PHYI'I RKYEN NI RIM LNGA LAS, SGYU MA DAG NI THAMS CAD LAS, ,ZHES PA NAS, GSAL BAR 'DI LAS MTSON PAR NUS, ,ZHES GSUNGS PA LTAR, PHYAG RGYA SROG RTZOL DU SONG BA STE PHYI NANG GI RKYEN DE DAG LA BRTEN NAS SEMS DBEN GYI YE SHES BSKYED NUS KYI, ZHES DANG ,
gru.wylie: mkhas grub rje'i gsung zin bris las, srog rtsol gsum dang khyad par du rdor bzlas te nang gi rkyen gsum dang , phyi'i rkyen ni rim lnga las, sgyu ma dag ni thams cad las, ,zhes pa nas, gsal bar 'di las mtshon par nus, ,zhes gsungs pa ltar, phyag rgya srog rtsol du song ba ste phyi nang gi rkyen de dag la brten nas sems dben gyi ye shes bskyed nus kyi, zhes dang
gru.english: This is true because Kedrup Je's Notes further says, One is capable of giving rise to the wisdom of transcendent mind by relying upon the outer and inner factors.  The inner factors are three, with the three different practices for mastering the life-wind, and most especially the recitation of the diamonds.  The outer factors are using practice with a partner as a practice for mastering the life-wind, as expressed in the lines from The Five Stages which begin with "Of all the various types of illusion..." and continue up to "...All appear clearly through Her."

gru.acip: 'DI LA MKHAS PA KHA CIG NA RE, SEMS DBEN MTHAR THUG GI YE SHES GSUM SKYED PA LA LAS RGYA BRTEN DGOS PA NI RIM LNGA'I GZHUNG 'DI'I DGONGS PA YIN GYI SEMS DBEN TZAM LA MIN TE, GSAL SGRON LAS, SGYU LUS KYI SGRUB GZHI'I SEMS DBEN GYI YE SHES GSUM RDZOGS PAR SKYED PA LA PHYI'I PHYAG RGYA DGOS SO, ,ZHES DANG ,
gru.wylie: 'di la mkhas pa kha cig na re, sems dben mthar thug gi ye shes gsum skyed pa la las rgya brten dgos pa ni rim lnga'i gzhung 'di'i dgongs pa yin gyi sems dben tsam la min te, gsal sgron las, sgyu lus kyi sgrub gzhi'i sems dben gyi ye shes gsum rdzogs par skyed pa la phyi'i phyag rgya dgos so, ,zhes dang
gru.english: On this, some sages express the following opinion-- The actual intent of these lines from the Five Stages is to say that we need to practice with a partner of the rite in order to give birth to the three wisdoms of the ultimate form of transcendent mind.  The text is not though saying this about reaching the stage of transcendent mind as a whole.  This is reflected in the following statement from the Lantern: In order to give rise, completely, to the three different forms of the wisdom of transcendent mind which act as the material from which the body of illusion is made, one needs an outer partner.

gru.acip: 'DI LA KHA CIG NA RE, TSE 'DIR 'TSANG RGYA BA LA LAS RGYA NGES PAR BSTEN DGOS PA'I MA MTHA' SA MTSAMS NI SEMS DBEN THOB PA NAS YIN TE, YE SHES RDO RJE KUN LAS BTUS PA'I t'I KA LAS, 'DIR PHYAG RGYA DANG STONG PA GSUM RJES SU 'GRO LDOG NGES PAR GSUNGS PA NI, SGYU MA'I SKU SGRUB NUS PA'I SEMS DBEN GYI STONG PA GSUM RDZOGS PAR SKYE BA PHYAG RGYA LA NGES PAR LTOS PA LA DGONGS PA YIN TE,
gru.wylie: 'di la kha cig na re, tshe 'dir 'tshang rgya ba la las rgya nges par bsten dgos pa'i ma mtha' sa mtshams ni sems dben thob pa nas yin te, ye shes rdo rje kun las btus pa'i TI ka las, 'dir phyag rgya dang stong pa gsum rjes su 'gro ldog nges par gsungs pa ni, sgyu ma'i sku sgrub nus pa'i sems dben gyi stong pa gsum rdzogs par skye ba phyag rgya la nges par ltos pa la dgongs pa yin te
gru.english: Others express the following opinion: The point at which it does finally become absolutely necessary to practice with a partner of the rite is once one has attained transcendent mind.  This is true because the commentary entitled The Complete Compendium of the Diamond of Wisdom states: The statement here that a partner and the three forms of emptiness are such that where one is there, the other comes; and where one is missing, the other cannot come; is made with the intention of saying that--if we hope to see the three forms of emptiness within transcendent mind arise, the form of transcendent mind that has the power to bring about the body of illusion--then we must necessarily practice with a partner.

gru.acip: YANG KHA CIG NA RE, LAS RGYA BSTEN DGOS PA'I MTSAMS SEMS DBEN THOB PA NAS YIN ZER BA MI 'THAD DE, GANG ZAG MTSAN NYID TSANG BA LA RIM GNYIS SGOM PA'I SNGON DU DBANG GSUM PA DNGOS DBANG DU BSKUR BA YOD PA GANG ZHIG ,GSANG BA GRUB PA LAS, LAS DANG PO BAS PHYI'I PHYAG RGYA'I THABS SPANGS NA THABS GZHAN GYIS DGA' BZHI'I LHAN SKYES MTSON DU MED PAR GSUNGS PA'I PHYIR NA MA KHYAB STE,
gru.wylie: yang kha cig na re, las rgya bsten dgos pa'i mtshams sems dben thob pa nas yin zer ba mi 'thad de, gang zag mtshan nyid tshang ba la rim gnyis sgom pa'i sngon du dbang gsum pa dngos dbang du bskur ba yod pa gang zhig ,gsang ba grub pa las, las dang po bas phyi'i phyag rgya'i thabs spangs na thabs gzhan gyis dga' bzhi'i lhan skyes mtshon du med par gsungs pa'i phyir na ma khyab ste
gru.english: Someone might come and make the following argument: It's incorrect to say that the point at which one must practice with a partner of the rite begins from when one has attained transcendent mind.  This is true because (1) there do exist cases where one can impart the third empowerment in its actual form to persons who possess the necessary qualities, even before they begin their practice of the two stages of the secret teachings; and (2) the text of Reaching the Secret says that beginners who give up on the method of practicing with an outer partner cannot bring about the simultaneous wisdom of the four forms of bliss with any other method. Our reply to this is that--although the latter two points are true--they don't necessarily imply the former.

gru.acip: MKHAS GRUB RJE'I GSUNG ZIN BRIS LAS, LUS DBEN SOGS KYI SKABS SU DE DAG BYUNG BA NI STONG PA BZHI MTSAN NYID PA YIN YANG SEMS DBEN GYI STONG PA BZHI MIN GSUNGS,
gru.wylie: mkhas grub rje'i gsung zin bris las, lus dben sogs kyi skabs su de dag byung ba ni stong pa bzhi mtshan nyid pa yin yang sems dben gyi stong pa bzhi min gsungs
gru.english: Kedrup Je's Notes says that--when these occur during stages such as the transcendent body--then they are definitive forms of the four kinds of emptiness, but not the four kinds of emptiness that belong to the stage of transcendent mind.

gru.acip: RDZOGS RIM DNGOS GRUB SNYE MA LAS, LUGS LDOG GI SNANG MCHED THOB GSUM 'OD GSAL GYI YE SHES SU MI RUNG YANG , LUGS LDOG GI DGA' BA GZHAN GSUM LHAN SKYES SU 'JOG PA GCIG BSHAD LA, DE BZHIN DU LUGS MTHUN GYI SNANG MCHED THOB GSUM DANG DE GSUM DGA' BA GSUM DU BZHAG PA LHAN SKYES KYI DGA' BAR MI 'JOG KYANG , LUGS MTHUN YAS BABS KYI DGA' BA GSUM LHAN SKYES KYI DGA' BAR 'JOG PA'I SKABS GCIG KYANG YOD PAR MNGON NO, ,ZHES GSUNGS PA TZAM LAS GSAL BAR BSHAD PA MI SNANG LA,
gru.wylie: rdzogs rim dngos grub snye ma las, lugs ldog gi snang mched thob gsum 'od gsal gyi ye shes su mi rung yang , lugs ldog gi dga' ba gzhan gsum lhan skyes su 'jog pa gcig bshad la, de bzhin du lugs mthun gyi snang mched thob gsum dang de gsum dga' ba gsum du bzhag pa lhan skyes kyi dga' bar mi 'jog kyang , lugs mthun yas babs kyi dga' ba gsum lhan skyes kyi dga' bar 'jog pa'i skabs gcig kyang yod par mngon no, ,zhes gsungs pa tsam las gsal bar bshad pa mi snang la
gru.english: Here the text on the stage of completion entitled The Golden Harvest of Attainments says, It would be incorrect to say that the three stages of light, proliferation, and attainment as the process reverses itself constitute the wisdom of the clear light.  Nonetheless, there is an explanation that the other three forms of bliss during this reversal of the process are the simultaneous form.  We do see, in the same way, the three of light, proliferation, and attainment spoken of as the process moves in its forward progression--and we see these three spoken of as being three of the forms of bliss, even though they are not said to be simultaneous bliss.  It does appear though that there is another point where the three forms of bliss during the forward progression are said to be simultaneous bliss. We don't find any more specific reference on this point than what is here.

gru.acip: DANG PO NI, SEMS DBEN MTHAR THUG GI DPE'I 'OD GSAL LAS RLUNG CUNG ZAD G-YOS TE LUGS LDOG GI NYER THOB GRUB PA DANG DUS MNYAM DU, SEMS DBEN MTHAR THUG GI DPE'I 'OD GSAL GYIS LHAN CIG BYED RKYEN DANG DE'I BZHON PAR GYUR PA'I GNYUG RLUNG GIS NYER LEN BYAS NAS MTSAN DPES SPRAS PA'I LHA'I SKU DNGOS GNAS LA GRUB PA NAS BZUNG STE, DON GYI 'OD GSAL GYI THABS NYE BA'I RGYU RNAMS MA SKYES TSUN CHAD KYI RDZOGS RIM NI, SGYU LUS KYI RIM PA'I NGO BO'O,,
gru.wylie: dang po ni, sems dben mthar thug gi dpe'i 'od gsal las rlung cung zad g-yos te lugs ldog gi nyer thob grub pa dang dus mnyam du, sems dben mthar thug gi dpe'i 'od gsal gyis lhan cig byed rkyen dang de'i bzhon par gyur pa'i gnyug rlung gis nyer len byas nas mtshan dpes spras pa'i lha'i sku dngos gnas la grub pa nas bzung ste, don gyi 'od gsal gyi thabs nye ba'i rgyu rnams ma skyes tshun chad kyi rdzogs rim ni, sgyu lus kyi rim pa'i ngo bo'o
gru.english: Here is the essential nature then of the stage called "the illusory body": The illusory body is the stage of completion which begins with the following.  At the same point that one reaches the approximate clear light of the final end of the stage of transcendent mind--and the winds have then shifted slightly, which allows one to reach the stage of attainment during the reversal of the process--something else happens.  This is where the approximate clear light of the final end of the stage of transcendent mind provides a contributing factor, and the primordial wind upon which it rides provides a material cause, and then one attains the actual body of an Angel, embellished with all the various signs and marks of an enlightened being.  The stage of the illusory body continues from this point on up to where one is able to give rise to the immediate causes which provide the means for attaining the actual clear light.

gru.acip: SGYU LUS 'GRUB PA LA SNGON DU LUS PHRA RAGS GNYIS SO SOR 'BYED NUS PA CIG DGOS LA, BSGOMS STOBS KYIS LUS PHRA RAGS GNYIS SO SOR 'BYED PA DANG , LAS NYON GYIS LUS PHRA RAGS GNYIS SO SOR 'BYED PA GNYIS LAS,
gru.wylie: sgyu lus 'grub pa la sngon du lus phra rags gnyis so sor 'byed nus pa cig dgos la, bsgoms stobs kyis lus phra rags gnyis so sor 'byed pa dang , las nyon gyis lus phra rags gnyis so sor 'byed pa gnyis las
gru.english: Before a person can attain the body of illusion, they must first be able to separate the two bodies--subtle and gross--from each other.  Here there are two types: the separation of the subtle and gross bodies through the power of meditation, and the separation of these two through karma and mental afflictions.

gru.acip: DE LA NI SPYOD PA MI DGOS KYANG SEMS DBEN GYI TING NGE 'DZIN LA GOMS PAR BYAS PAS TSE 'DIR LUS GNYIS SO SOR 'BYED PA DANG , PHYE BA'I LUS DE SGYU LUS RDO RJE 'CHANG GI SKUR DNGOS GNAS PAR LDANG BA NI SHIN TU BSGRUB BKA' BAS SNGON DU SPYOD PA GSUM GANG RUNG NGES PAR BYA DGOS PAR GSUNGS SO,,
gru.wylie: de la ni spyod pa mi dgos kyang sems dben gyi ting nge 'dzin la goms par byas pas tshe 'dir lus gnyis so sor 'byed pa dang , phye ba'i lus de sgyu lus rdo rje 'chang gi skur dngos gnas par ldang ba ni shin tu bsgrub bka' bas sngon du spyod pa gsum gang rung nges par bya dgos par gsungs so
gru.english: Even though none of the activities is necessary here, it is nonetheless extremely difficult to use continued practice in the one-point concentration of transcendent mind to separate the two bodies from each other here in this life; and to rise up in the actual illusory body: in the body of the Keeper of the Diamond himself.  As such, it is stated that we must absolutely engage in one or more of the three activities.

gru.acip: DON DE LTAR MKHAS GRUB RJE'I GSUNG ZIN BRIS LAS GSUNGS TE, RTZOD TSE GZHAL BYA MED PA'I SHES PA 'JOG DKA' BAS DPYAD DGOS SO,,
gru.wylie: don de ltar mkhas grub rje'i gsung zin bris las gsungs te, rtsod tshe gzhal bya med pa'i shes pa 'jog dka' bas dpyad dgos so
gru.english: This is how Kedrup Je's Notes explains the point.  But in a debate you'd have a difficult time positing an instance of mind that didn't have anything it was considering; and so this bears some further examination.

gru.acip: KHA CIG ,TSE 'DIR GRUB PA'I MA DAG PA'I SGYU LUS NI NANG LDANG KHO NA YIN TE, DE SNYING GA'I DH'U T'I'I NANG KHO NAR GNAS PA'I PHYIR TE, ZIN BRIS DE NYID LAS, TSE 'DIR GRUB PA'I MA DAG PA'I SGYU LUS DE LUS RAGS PA LAS SO SOR PHYE BA YIN KYANG GO SA SO SOR PHYE BA NI MA YIN TE, DE'I NUS PA MED PA'I PHYIR RO, ,ZHES DANG ,
gru.wylie: kha cig ,tshe 'dir grub pa'i ma dag pa'i sgyu lus ni nang ldang kho na yin te, de snying ga'i dhU tI'i nang kho nar gnas pa'i phyir te, zin bris de nyid las, tshe 'dir grub pa'i ma dag pa'i sgyu lus de lus rags pa las so sor phye ba yin kyang go sa so sor phye ba ni ma yin te, de'i nus pa med pa'i phyir ro, ,zhes dang
gru.english: Now someone may come and make the following claim-- Whenever a person attains the impure body of illusion in this same lifetime, it can only be something which rises within them.  This is the case because that same text, the Notes, says: Even though--when one attains the impure body of illusion in this same lifetime--this body is separated from the gross body, it is not the case that they are separated out in a way that they then occupy two different spaces.  This is true because it has no such power.

gru.acip: KHA CIG ,SGYU LUS THOG MAR 'GRUB PA'I TSE LUS RAGS PA LAS PHYI ROL DU LDANG DGOS TE, GSAL SGRON LAS, ZUNG 'JUG GI SKU 'DI THOG MAR 'GRUB NA LUS SNGA MA LAS GO SA LOGS SU GNAS PA'I TSUL GYIS 'GRUB LA, ZHES DANG ,
gru.wylie: kha cig ,sgyu lus thog mar 'grub pa'i tshe lus rags pa las phyi rol du ldang dgos te, gsal sgron las, zung 'jug gi sku 'di thog mar 'grub na lus snga ma las go sa logs su gnas pa'i tshul gyis 'grub la, zhes dang
gru.english: Someone else might make the following claim: It must be the case that--when we first attain the body of illusion--it rises outside of the gross body.  This is true because the Lantern states, When we first attain the precious body of the combination of the two, we achieve it in a way where it occupies a space which is discrete from that of the previous body.

gru.acip: LONGS SKU LUS SNGA MA LAS GO SA LOGS SU DANG POR 'GRUB PA DANG , DE NAS LUS SNGA MA LA ZHUGS PA'I SPRUL SKU 'DZIN TSUL YANG SNGAR BSHAD PA BZHIN DU SHES PAR BYA STE, ZHES GSUNGS PA'I PHYIR DANG , DAG MA DAG GI SGYU LUS 'GRUB TSUL 'DRA BAR BSHAD PA'I PHYIR ZHES ZER,
gru.wylie: longs sku lus snga ma las go sa logs su dang por 'grub pa dang , de nas lus snga ma la zhugs pa'i sprul sku 'dzin tshul yang sngar bshad pa bzhin du shes par bya ste, zhes gsungs pa'i phyir dang , dag ma dag gi sgyu lus 'grub tshul 'dra bar bshad pa'i phyir zhes zer
gru.english: It also says-- The paradise body is at first attained in a place which is discrete from that of the previous body.  It should be understood that--as we described above--we then go on to re-enter this previous body, in the way that someone would take on a body of emanation. And after all, it is stated that the ways in which we attain the pure body of illusion and the impure body of illusion are the same.

gru.acip: KHA CIG ,SGYU LUS THOG MAR 'GRUB PA'I DUS SU NANG LDANG PHYI LDANG GNYIS KA YOD DE, RNAL 'BYOR PA DES LUS KYI PHYI ROL LAM NANG GANG DU LDANG BAR BZHED PA LTAR 'GRUB PA'I PHYIR TE, DE NYID LAS, SEMS DBEN GYI RLUNG SEMS KYI GNYUG MA'I LUS LAS SGYU MA'I SKU 'GRUB PA'I DUS SU, LUS RAGS PA LAS LOGS SU PHYE NAS LUS KYI PHYI ROL LAM NANG GANG DU 'DOD PA DER 'GRO BA'I DON NO, ,ZHES GSUNGS PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: kha cig ,sgyu lus thog mar 'grub pa'i dus su nang ldang phyi ldang gnyis ka yod de, rnal 'byor pa des lus kyi phyi rol lam nang gang du ldang bar bzhed pa ltar 'grub pa'i phyir te, de nyid las, sems dben gyi rlung sems kyi gnyug ma'i lus las sgyu ma'i sku 'grub pa'i dus su, lus rags pa las logs su phye nas lus kyi phyi rol lam nang gang du 'dod pa der 'gro ba'i don no, ,zhes gsungs pa'i phyir
gru.english: Still others make another claim-- Both possibilities exist: where when a person first attains the body of illusion, this body rises either within the gross body or outside of it.  This is the case because wherever this kind of deep practitioner decides that it should rise--on the outside or the inside of the body--is where it will rise.  As the same text says, Consider that point--the point at which this precious body of illusion is attained, out of the primordial body of the winds and thoughts of the stage of transcendent mind.  It comes out whichever way one wishes it: either the body is attained in a location which is discrete from that of the gross body--that is to say, outside of it--or inside of it.

gru.acip: KHYAB STE, SEMS DBEN GYI RLUNG LAS 'GRUB PAR GSUNGS PAS MA DAG PA'I SGYU LUS KYI DBANG DU BYAS PAR GSAL ZHING , GRUB PA'I DUS SU ZHES MA GSUNGS PAR 'GRUB PA'I DUS SU ZHES GSUNGS 'DUG PAS GRUB ZIN GNAS PA'I DBANG DU BYAS PA MIN PAR GSAL BA'I PHYIR ZHES ZER,
gru.wylie: khyab ste, sems dben gyi rlung las 'grub par gsungs pas ma dag pa'i sgyu lus kyi dbang du byas par gsal zhing , grub pa'i dus su zhes ma gsungs par 'grub pa'i dus su zhes gsungs 'dug pas grub zin gnas pa'i dbang du byas pa min par gsal ba'i phyir zhes zer
gru.english: And the citation does necessarily prove our assertion.  Since it talks about the body of illusion which is attained "out of the winds of the stage of transcendent mind," it is clearly referring to the impure body of illusion.  And since it says "when this body is attained," and not "when this body has already been attained," it is clearly not referring to a body of illusion which is staying there well after it has already been attained.

gru.acip: DE LTAR BZHED PA GSUM LAS RJE'I DGONGS PAR GANG SONG DPYAD PAR BYA'O, ,GANG LTAR YANG TSE 'DIR THOB PA'I MA DAG PA'I SGYU LUS LUS RAGS PA LAS GO SA LOGS SU GNAS MI THUB PAR BSHAD PA LTAR KHAS LEN MI RUNG STE, DRANGS MA THAG PA'I GSAL SGRON GYI GZHUNG DANG 'GAL BA'I PHYIR DANG , MKHAS GRUB RJE'I DGONGS PA DE LTAR MA YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: de ltar bzhed pa gsum las rje'i dgongs par gang song dpyad par bya'o, ,gang ltar yang tshe 'dir thob pa'i ma dag pa'i sgyu lus lus rags pa las go sa logs su gnas mi thub par bshad pa ltar khas len mi rung ste, drangs ma thag pa'i gsal sgron gyi gzhung dang 'gal ba'i phyir dang , mkhas grub rje'i dgongs pa de ltar ma yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: It is something that bears further examination to decide which of these three positions reflects the thinking of the Lord himself.  At any rate, it would be incorrect to agree to the explanation that an impure body of illusion attained in this same lifetime could never occupy a space which was discrete from that occupied by the gross body.  This is because such a position would contradict the section of the Lantern just quoted, and further because this is not what Kedrup Je thinks on this point.

gru.acip: RTAGS GNYIS PA GRUB STE, DUS 'KHOR t'IKA CHEN LAS, GNYUG MA'I LUS MA DAG PA'I SGYU LUS KYI SKUR LANGS PA'ANG JI SRID RAGS PA DANG GNYUG MA'I LUS KYI RTEN DANG BRTEN PA'I 'BREL BA MA TSAD KYI RING LA DUS THAMS CAD DU RAGS PA'I LUS SPANGS NAS GNAS MI NUS KYANG ,
gru.wylie: rtags gnyis pa grub ste, dus 'khor TIka chen las, gnyug ma'i lus ma dag pa'i sgyu lus kyi skur langs pa'ang ji srid rags pa dang gnyug ma'i lus kyi rten dang brten pa'i 'brel ba ma tshad kyi ring la dus thams cad du rags pa'i lus spangs nas gnas mi nus kyang
gru.english: This latter reason we've given to prove what we said is true because of the following quotation from the Great Commentary to the Wheel of Time, [written by Kedrup Je himself]: The primordial body does assuredly rise up into the impure body of illusion; but until such time as the relationship of something which provides the basis and something which rests upon this basis is exhausted between the gross body and the primordial body, then there is absolutely no point at which the primordial body could abandon the gross body and be able to continue.

gru.acip: DON GYI 'OD GSAL SKYE BA'I TSE MA DAG PA'I SGYU LUS THIM PAR 'GYUR BA'I RGYU MTSAN CI YIN ZHE NA, MKHAS GRUB RJE'I GSUNG ZIN BRIS LAS, DON GYI 'OD GSAL THOG MAR SHAR BA'I TSE DPE'I 'OD GSAL GYI YE SHES KYI BZHON PAR 'GYUR BA'I RLUNG DE CHES PHRA BAR SONG BA'I STOBS KYIS MA DAG PA'I SGYU LUS KYI SKU'I RNAM PA YANG 'OD GSAL DU BSDUS NAS THIM PAR 'GYUR, ZHES GSUNGS KYANG ,
gru.wylie: don gyi 'od gsal skye ba'i tshe ma dag pa'i sgyu lus thim par 'gyur ba'i rgyu mtshan ci yin zhe na, mkhas grub rje'i gsung zin bris las, don gyi 'od gsal thog mar shar ba'i tshe dpe'i 'od gsal gyi ye shes kyi bzhon par 'gyur ba'i rlung de ches phra bar song ba'i stobs kyis ma dag pa'i sgyu lus kyi sku'i rnam pa yang 'od gsal du bsdus nas thim par 'gyur, zhes gsungs kyang
gru.english: One might ask why it is that--when the actual clear light arises--then the impure body of illusion dissolves.  We see the following in Kedrup Je's Notes: When the actual clear light first makes its appearance, the wind which is serving as the vehicle for the wisdom of the approximate clear light becomes ever more subtle; due to this, the bodily form of the impure body of illusion too withdraws into the clear light and dissolves.

gru.acip: SHA RUS LA SOGS PA DANG BRAL BAS MIG YOR TE MI'I GRIB MA'I LUS LTA BU'O, ,SKAD CIG GIS G-YO BAS SMIG RGYU LTA BU'O, ,RLUNG SEMS TZAM LAS GRUB PA'I LUS YIN PA NI RMI LAM DU LUS RAGS PA LAS ZUR DU PHYE BA'I RMI LAM GYI LUS LTA BU'O, ,RNAM SMIN GYI LUS DANG RGYUD GCIG TU GTOGS KYANG GZHAN DU SNANG BA NI BRAG CHA LTA BU'O,,
gru.wylie: sha rus la sogs pa dang bral bas mig yor te mi'i grib ma'i lus lta bu'o, ,skad cig gis g-yo bas smig rgyu lta bu'o, ,rlung sems tsam las grub pa'i lus yin pa ni rmi lam du lus rags pa las zur du phye ba'i rmi lam gyi lus lta bu'o, ,rnam smin gyi lus dang rgyud gcig tu gtogs kyang gzhan du snang ba ni brag cha lta bu'o
gru.english: Because we lack any flesh or bone or the like, we are like (3) a scarecrow; that is, like a body that is no more than the shadow outline of a real person.  Since we are shifting from instant to instant, we resemble (4) a mirage.  This thing of a body which is made of nothing more than wind and mind is as well like (5) one's body seen in a dream, existing in the dream as something discrete from our gross body.  Even though this body is something subsumed, along with the body which has ripened from karma, within a single person, it appears as something other--and so it is like (6) an echo.

gru.acip: SNGAR BSHAD PA LTAR RDO RJE'I SKU GANG LAS SGRUB PA'I GZHI GNYUG MA'I LUS RLUNG SEMS TZAM DU ZAD PA'I TSUL LA NGES PA BRTAN PO RNYED NAS, STONG PA RNAMS KYI RLUNG SEMS TZAM LAS SGYU MA'I SKU 'GRUB PA'I TSUL LA YANG DANG YANG DU SHIN TU NGO MTSAR BA'I BSAM PAS MOS PA BRTAN POS BSKYED PAR BYA'O, ,ZHES GDAMS SHING ,
gru.wylie: sngar bshad pa ltar rdo rje'i sku gang las sgrub pa'i gzhi gnyug ma'i lus rlung sems tsam du zad pa'i tshul la nges pa brtan po rnyed nas, stong pa rnams kyi rlung sems tsam las sgyu ma'i sku 'grub pa'i tshul la yang dang yang du shin tu ngo mtshar ba'i bsam pas mos pa brtan pos bskyed par bya'o, ,zhes gdams shing
gru.english: The foundation for attaining the diamond body is, as we've said before, this primordial body, which itself is made of simple wind and mind, and nothing more.  Come to a firm realization that this is so, and think over and over about how incredible it is that we can achieve the precious body of illusion using nothing more than the winds and mind of the different forms of emptiness.  And then make it happen, with the hope--the unwavering hope--that these thoughts bring within you.

gru.acip: BDAG BYIN RLABS PA'I BSHAD PA LAS, YID LA BYED TSUL GTAM TZAM YANG RNYED DKA' BA'I DON DE SGYU LUS MA GRUB KYANG 'DI'I GDAMS NGAG PHYIN CI MA LOG PA RNYED NA DA LTA NAS GOMS PAS NAM ZHIG NA SGYU MA'I SKU 'JA' LUS RDO RJE SEMS DPA'I GO 'PHANG 'GRUB PA'I BAG CHAGS THUN MONG MA YIN PA 'JOG BYED DU SNANG BAS SHIN TU NGO MTSAR BA'I GNAS SO,,
gru.wylie: bdag byin rlabs pa'i bshad pa las, yid la byed tshul gtam tsam yang rnyed dka' ba'i don de sgyu lus ma grub kyang 'di'i gdams ngag phyin ci ma log pa rnyed na da lta nas goms pas nam zhig na sgyu ma'i sku 'ja' lus rdo rje sems dpa'i go 'phang 'grub pa'i bag chags thun mong ma yin pa 'jog byed du snang bas shin tu ngo mtshar ba'i gnas so
gru.english: This is also described in the treatise called The Blessing of Oneself, where our Lord grants us the following holy words-- Here's the point of saying that it's a difficult thing to come across even a discussion that gets you thinking about these things.  Suppose that--even if you are unable right now to attain the body of illusion--you do come across some unmistaken instructions for doing so.  If right now you begin to habituate yourself to these teachings, then you will see that it acts to plant a unique type of mental seed which will allow you, at a certain point in the future, to actually reach the body of illusion: the rainbow body, the state of the Warrior of Diamond himself.  This is an incredible thing.

gru.acip: RDZOGS RIM DNGOS GRUB SNYE MA LAS, RTZA MDUD LEGS PAR GROL NAS SGYU LUS DNGOS SU BSKYED MI NUS TSUN CHAD NI SEMS DBEN DU BSDU'O,,
gru.wylie: rdzogs rim dngos grub snye ma las, rtsa mdud legs par grol nas sgyu lus dngos su bskyed mi nus tshun chad ni sems dben du bsdu'o
gru.english: And that's because what we're describing here is similar to what the text on the stage of completion entitled The Golden Harvest of Attainments describes in the following lines: Everything from the point where you release, perfectly, the knots in the channels up to the last point where you are still unable to actually give birth to the body of illusion is included into the stage of transcendent mind.

gru.acip: BSHAD TSUL 'DI NI DBYANGS CAN DGA' BLO'I SA LAM RNAM GZHAG LAS GSUNGS TE, SHES BYED NI GSAL SGRON LAS, MTSAN PHYED NA BLA MAS LAS RGYA LA BRTEN PA'I DNGOS DBANG BSKUR TE 'OD GSAL MTSON PAR BYED PA'O, ,DE NAS THO RANGS 'OD GSAL SGOM TSUL DANG , DE'I 'OG TU ZUNG ('JU)GA SGRUB LUGS KYI GDAMS NGAG PHOG PAS DON GYI 'OD GSAL 'THOB CING , DE'I 'OG TU ZUNG 'JUG 'GRUB BO, ,ZHES GSUNGS PA 'DI YIN NO, ,'ON KYANG GZHUNG 'DI NI DANG PO NAS BLA MED KYI LAM DU RIGS NGES PA'I LAM BGROD TSUL BSHAD PA'I GZHUNG YIN PAS DPYAD BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: bshad tshul 'di ni dbyangs can dga' blo'i sa lam rnam gzhag las gsungs te, shes byed ni gsal sgron las, mtshan phyed na bla mas las rgya la brten pa'i dngos dbang bskur te 'od gsal mtshon par byed pa'o, ,de nas tho rangs 'od gsal sgom tshul dang , de'i 'og tu zung ('ju)ga sgrub lugs kyi gdams ngag phog pas don gyi 'od gsal 'thob cing , de'i 'og tu zung 'jug 'grub bo, ,zhes gsungs pa 'di yin no, ,'on kyang gzhung 'di ni dang po nas bla med kyi lam du rigs nges pa'i lam bgrod tshul bshad pa'i gzhung yin pas dpyad bya'o
gru.english: This way of explaining comes from Yangchen Gaway Lodru's presentation on the levels and paths, where the following section from the Lantern is quoted as authority-- In the midnight hour, the Lama grants the actual form of the empowerment where one practices with a partner of the rite; this brings on an experience of the clear light.  The Lama then grants instructions on how to meditate upon the clear light of daybreak, and after that the instructions on how the combination of the two is achieved. These points though bear some further examination, since the section of text quoted here is one which is describing how a person who always has and always will be on the path of the unsurpassed teachings travels the path.

gru.acip: BSHAD TSUL 'DI DANG MI MTHUN PAR MKHAS GRUB RJE'I BRTAG GNYIS RNAM BSHAD LAS, BYANG SEMS SRID PA THA MA PA DE LA DBANG GSUM PA DNGOS DBANG DU BSKUR BA'I TSE, PHYAG RGYA LA BRTEN NAS BDE CHEN MTSAN NYID TSANG BA BSKYED PAR NUS LA, STONG NYID MNGON SUM DU RTOGS ZIN MA NYAMS PA SNGAR NAS YOD PAS,
gru.wylie: bshad tshul 'di dang mi mthun par mkhas grub rje'i brtag gnyis rnam bshad las, byang sems srid pa tha ma pa de la dbang gsum pa dngos dbang du bskur ba'i tshe, phyag rgya la brten nas bde chen mtshan nyid tshang ba bskyed par nus la, stong nyid mngon sum du rtogs zin ma nyams pa sngar nas yod pas
gru.english: There is a part in Kedrup Je's Treatise on the Secret Teaching in Two Sections which presents this is a way which conflicts with the explanation above.  It says, Suppose now that the third of the empowerments is given in its actual form to a bodhisattva who is in his or her final rebirth.  This bodhisattva, through practice with their partner, is able to give birth to a form of ecstasy which is complete in every aspect.  They are though still maintaining--they have still not lost--their direct perception of emptiness from before.

gru.acip: YE SHES DE NI DON GYI 'OD GSAL YIN LA, DBANG BSKUR PA'I TSE DON GYI 'OD GSAL GYI SNGON DU 'PHEN PA GTONG BA SOGS KYI GDAMS NGAG PHOG PAS, 'PHEN PA SOGS KYI DBANG GIS DBANG DUS KYI 'OD GSAL DE LAS LUGS LDOG TU LDANG BA NA, SHIN TU PHRA BA'I RLUNG SEMS LAS GRUB PA'I KHA SBYOR GYI LUS MTSAN DPES BRGYAN PA'I RNAM PA CAN DU LDANG BA YIN NO, ,ZHES DBANG DUS KYI 'OD GSAL NI DON GYI 'OD GSAL DANG DE LAS ZUNG 'JUG GI SKUR LDANG BAR BSHAD DO,,
gru.wylie: ye shes de ni don gyi 'od gsal yin la, dbang bskur pa'i tshe don gyi 'od gsal gyi sngon du 'phen pa gtong ba sogs kyi gdams ngag phog pas, 'phen pa sogs kyi dbang gis dbang dus kyi 'od gsal de las lugs ldog tu ldang ba na, shin tu phra ba'i rlung sems las grub pa'i kha sbyor gyi lus mtshan dpes brgyan pa'i rnam pa can du ldang ba yin no, ,zhes dbang dus kyi 'od gsal ni don gyi 'od gsal dang de las zung 'jug gi skur ldang bar bshad do
gru.english: This wisdom is itself the actual clear light.  At the point of their empowerment, they have been granted instructions on practices such as setting a goal for themselves prior to the actual clear light.  Suppose next that--due to these intentions and so forth--they rise forth from the clear light of the time of the empowerment, in a reverse way.  In this case then they rise forth in the form of a body embellished with all the signs and marks of an Enlightened Being--the body of the capsule, made of extremely subtle winds and the mind. What this text is saying then is that the clear light at the point of the empowerment is the actual clear light, and that we rise out of this clear light in the holy body of the combination of the two.

gru.acip: YANG 'DI LA KHA CIG NA RE, DE GNYIS LA BAR CHAD MED LAM DANG RNAM GROL LAM GYI THA SNYAD SBYOR DGOS SHING SBYAR DU RUNG BA YIN TE, MKHAS GRUB RJE'I ZIN BRIS LAS, DE NI PHYOGS GZHAN NAS BAR CHAD MED LAM DANG RNAM GROL LAM GYI THA SNYAD BSHAD PA LTAR 'DIR YANG SBYAR NA, 'OD GSAL DE YUN THUNG THUNG KHEM PA GCIG LAS MI 'ONG BA MA YIN PAS, DES BAR CHAD MED LAM BYAS, LUGS LDOG GI NYER THOB SHAR BA NA RNAM GROL LAM THOB PAR BZHAG KYANG 'GAL BA MED DO, ,ZHES GSUNGS PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: yang 'di la kha cig na re, de gnyis la bar chad med lam dang rnam grol lam gyi tha snyad sbyor dgos shing sbyar du rung ba yin te, mkhas grub rje'i zin bris las, de ni phyogs gzhan nas bar chad med lam dang rnam grol lam gyi tha snyad bshad pa ltar 'dir yang sbyar na, 'od gsal de yun thung thung khem pa gcig las mi 'ong ba ma yin pas, des bar chad med lam byas, lugs ldog gi nyer thob shar ba na rnam grol lam thob par bzhag kyang 'gal ba med do, ,zhes gsungs pa'i phyir
gru.english: On this same point, some make another claim: We must refer to these two with the terms "uninterrupted path" and "path of liberation," and it is quite right to do so.  This is because the Notes of Kedrup Je say, In other contexts, we see the terms "uninterrupted path" and "path of liberation" utilized.  Suppose that we try to correlate these terms here to our discussion.  Since it's not the case that this clear light would last no longer than a short time, a single moment, then we can make it the uninterrupted path.  There is also no contradiction if we say that someone has achieved the path of liberation at the point that the stage of attainment in the reverse progression has made its appearance.

gru.acip: DE BZHI NI RIM BZHIN DGA' BA BZHI'I DBANG DU BYAS PA'I RDZOGS RIM YIN LA, DANG PO GNYIS KYIS THIG LE'I RNAL 'BYOR SBYONG BA DANG , GSUM PA NI RDOR BZLAS YIN LA, DES RLUNG GI RNAL 'BYOR SBYANGS NAS RLUNG DANG THIG LE LAS RUNG BYAS PA'I DBANG GIS 'OD GSAL DU LUGS 'BYUNG GIS SDUD PA DANG LUGS LDOG TU LDANG BA YANG YANG GOMS PAS ZAB GSAL GNYIS MED KYI DAG PA'I YE SHES KYI SKU BSGRUBS TE, DE'I RIGS 'DRA NYID KYIS 'BRAS BU LA NYE BAR SBYOR BAR GSUNGS SO,
gru.wylie: de bzhi ni rim bzhin dga' ba bzhi'i dbang du byas pa'i rdzogs rim yin la, dang po gnyis kyis thig le'i rnal 'byor sbyong ba dang , gsum pa ni rdor bzlas yin la, des rlung gi rnal 'byor sbyangs nas rlung dang thig le las rung byas pa'i dbang gis 'od gsal du lugs 'byung gis sdud pa dang lugs ldog tu ldang ba yang yang goms pas zab gsal gnyis med kyi dag pa'i ye shes kyi sku bsgrubs te, de'i rigs 'dra nyid kyis 'bras bu la nye bar sbyor bar gsungs so
gru.english: These four, respectively, represent steps in the stage of completion that relate to the four forms of bliss.  With the first two, we engage in the deep practice of the drops.  The third is the recitation of the diamonds; with this we engage in the deep practice of the winds, and then with reference to making the winds and drops suitable for their work we practice, over and over again, using the forward progression to withdraw things into the clear light, and then the reverse progression to rise out of it.  In this way we attain the precious body of pure wisdom, where the profound and the clear are indivisible.  And it is with nothing more than the continuation of this same thing, it is stated, that we arrive at the final goal.

gru.acip: RIM PA DANG PO BZHIS RTZA RLUNG THIG LE RNAMS SHIN TU DUL BAR BYAS NAS, BSAM GYIS MI KHYAB PA'I RIM PA'I SKABS SU SNOD BCUD RIM GYIS 'OD GSAL DU SDUD PA DANG , DE LAS LDANG BA'I RNAL 'BYOR MANG DU BYAS PA'I MTHUS GNYIS SU MED PA'I YE SHES KYI SKU 'GRUB CING DE'I RGYUN NYID KYIS 'BRAS BU LA NYE BAR SBYOR BAR GSUNGS SO,,
gru.wylie: rim pa dang po bzhis rtsa rlung thig le rnams shin tu dul bar byas nas, bsam gyis mi khyab pa'i rim pa'i skabs su snod bcud rim gyis 'od gsal du sdud pa dang , de las ldang ba'i rnal 'byor mang du byas pa'i mthus gnyis su med pa'i ye shes kyi sku 'grub cing de'i rgyun nyid kyis 'bras bu la nye bar sbyor bar gsungs so
gru.english: It is stated that the first four stages function to bring the channels, winds, and drops under a high degree of control.  At the point of the stage of the inconceivable then we gradually withdraw both the world and its inhabitants into clear light.  After we rise out of this clear light, then we undertake a great many different deep practices.  Due to these practices, we are able to attain the holy body of wisdom; and with nothing more than the continuation of this same thing we arrive at the final goal.

gru.acip: 'DI DAG NI L'U AI PA'I LUGS KYI RDZOGS RIM GYI RNAM BSHAD DNGOS GRUB SNYE MA DANG , DRIL BU RIM LNGA'I RNAM BSHAD SBAS DON LTA BA'I MIG 'BYED GNYIS LAS SHES PAR BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: 'di dag ni lU ai pa'i lugs kyi rdzogs rim gyi rnam bshad dngos grub snye ma dang , dril bu rim lnga'i rnam bshad sbas don lta ba'i mig 'byed gnyis las shes par bya'o
gru.english: You can learn all these points from the Golden Harvest of Attainments, an explanation of the stage of completion according to the system of Luipa; and from Opening the Eyes to See the Hidden Meaning, which is an explanation of the five stages in the system of Ghantapada.

gru.acip: DER MA BYUNG BA GRUB CHEN BIR WA PA'I GDAMS PA NAS BSHAD PA'I KYEE RDOR GYI RDZOGS RIM DBANG GSUM GYI LAM DU BSDUS NAS NYAMS SU LEN TSUL DANG , GRUB CHEN dOm BI PA DANG MI THUB ZLA BAS BSHAD PA'I DPYID KYI THIG LE DANG KHA DOG BSHIGS PA'I RIM PA SOGS GRUB CHEN TSAD LDAN GYIS BSHAD PA'I RDZOGS RIM MANG YANG ,
gru.wylie: der ma byung ba grub chen bir wa pa'i gdams pa nas bshad pa'i kyee rdor gyi rdzogs rim dbang gsum gyi lam du bsdus nas nyams su len tshul dang , grub chen DoM bi pa dang mi thub zla bas bshad pa'i dpyid kyi thig le dang kha dog bshigs pa'i rim pa sogs grub chen tshad ldan gyis bshad pa'i rdzogs rim mang yang
gru.english: There are a great many practices of the stage of completion which have been taught by authentic and accomplished masters which are not included in this list.  Among them is the practice of the stage of completion in the secret teachings of Lo Diamond, as explained by the accomplished master Virupa--where there is a way that we practice this stage all contained in the path of the three empowerments.  Another example would be the practices--described by the accomplished masters Dombipada and Durjaya Chandra--of the drop of spring, and the stages in the dissolution of the colors.

gru.acip: DUS 'KHOR GYI RDZOGS RIM MA GTOGS PA BLA MED SPYI'I RDZOGS RIM TSAD LDAN GYIS BSHAD PA THAMS CAD BSKYED RIM BRTAN PAR BYAS RJES SU, RTZA RLUNG THIG LE LAS RUNG DU BSGRUBS NAS BSAM GTAN GNYIS GANG RUNG GIS SNOD BCUD 'OD GSAL DU BSDUS NAS 'JUG LDANG YANG YANG BYED PA'I RIM PAS ZUNG 'JUG GI YE SHES KYI SKU BSGRUBS TE, DE'I RIGS 'DRA NYID KYIS 'BRAS BU LA NYE BAR SBYOR BA NI 'DRA BAR GSUNGS SO,,
gru.wylie: dus 'khor gyi rdzogs rim ma gtogs pa bla med spyi'i rdzogs rim tshad ldan gyis bshad pa thams cad bskyed rim brtan par byas rjes su, rtsa rlung thig le las rung du bsgrubs nas bsam gtan gnyis gang rung gis snod bcud 'od gsal du bsdus nas 'jug ldang yang yang byed pa'i rim pas zung 'jug gi ye shes kyi sku bsgrubs te, de'i rigs 'dra nyid kyis 'bras bu la nye bar sbyor ba ni 'dra bar gsungs so
gru.english: Nonetheless, all of the authoritative practices of the stage of completion in the teachings of the unsurpassed class (with the exception of the stage of completion for the Wheel of Time) describe the same general process.  We first establish ourselves firmly in the stage of creation, and then undertake practices to make the channels, winds, and drops more ready for higher work.  Using then either one of the two forms of meditative concentration, we withdraw the world and all its inhabitants into the clear light.  We practice, over and over again, the process of going into this state and then rising out of it.  Gradually thus we attain the holy body of the wisdom of the combination of the two.  And with nothing more than the continuation of this same thing, we arrive at the final goal.

gru.acip: 'ON KYANG RLUNG DANG THIG LE LAS RUNG DU SGRUB LUGS LA SGO MANG PO YOD PAS DE DAG SO SO'I RGYUD RNAMS NAS GSUNGS PA LTAR DU TSAD LDAN RNAMS KYIS KYANG SO SOR BKRAL BA YIN NO,,
gru.wylie: 'on kyang rlung dang thig le las rung du sgrub lugs la sgo mang po yod pas de dag so so'i rgyud rnams nas gsungs pa ltar du tshad ldan rnams kyis kyang so sor bkral ba yin no
gru.english: There are however a great many methods for making the winds and drops more ready for higher work; and these have been further clarified by authoritative masters, based on what has been stated in the original texts for each different secret teaching.

gru.acip: DE LTAR RLUNG DANG THIG LE LAS RUNG DU SGRUB LUGS LA SGO MI 'DRA BA MANG PO YOD KYANG THABS DES RLUNG DBU MAR ZHUGS GNAS THIM GSUM BYAS PA LAS GTUM MO SBAR NAS BYANG SEMS BZHUS PA LAS BYUNG BA'I 'BRAS BU DGA' BA BZHI 'AM STONG PA BZHI'I YE SHES BSKYED NAS,
gru.wylie: de ltar rlung dang thig le las rung du sgrub lugs la sgo mi 'dra ba mang po yod kyang thabs des rlung dbu mar zhugs gnas thim gsum byas pa las gtum mo sbar nas byang sems bzhus pa las byung ba'i 'bras bu dga' ba bzhi 'am stong pa bzhi'i ye shes bskyed nas
gru.english: And even given all these many different descriptions of methods to be used for making the winds and drops more ready for higher work, one should understand that the way these methods work is basically the same.  We use this practice to take the inner winds through the three-fold process of entering, staying, and dissolving in the central channel, thus bringing the inner fire to blaze.  This causes the element of enlightenment to melt down, which gives birth to the result of the wisdom of the four forms of bliss--the four forms of emptiness.

gru.acip: LHAN SKYES KYI DGA' BA'AM 'OD GSAL GYI YE SHES KYI RGYUN SKYONG BAR BYED PAS CHOS SKU'I NYER LEN DANG , RDZOGS RIM GYI LAM RNAMS SKYE 'CHI BAR DO GSUM JI LTA BA BZHIN DU BSKYED NAS, 'CHI BA'I RIM PA JI BZHIN PA'I 'OD GSAL GYI RLUNG SEMS LAS BAR DO JI BZHIN PA'I SGYU MA'I SKU BSGRUBS TE, DE NYID KYIS GZUGS SKU'I NYER LEN BYAS NAS 'TSANG RGYA BA NI 'DRA BAR SHES NA,
gru.wylie: lhan skyes kyi dga' ba'am 'od gsal gyi ye shes kyi rgyun skyong bar byed pas chos sku'i nyer len dang , rdzogs rim gyi lam rnams skye 'chi bar do gsum ji lta ba bzhin du bskyed nas, 'chi ba'i rim pa ji bzhin pa'i 'od gsal gyi rlung sems las bar do ji bzhin pa'i sgyu ma'i sku bsgrubs te, de nyid kyis gzugs sku'i nyer len byas nas 'tshang rgya ba ni 'dra bar shes na
gru.english: Maintaining the flow of the wisdom of simultaneous bliss--of the clear light--provides the thing which turns into the truth body.  We use the different paths of the stage of completion then to replicate the three steps of rebirth, death, and the inbetween state.  We bring about the precious body of illusion, which is comparable to the way that the inbetween being comes about through the winds and thoughts of the clear light during the various stages of the death process.  This in itself provides the thing which turns into the body of form.  And thus we achieve enlightenment.

gru.acip: THOB ZIN BOGS 'BYIN GYI SPYOD PA BYED PA'I SKABS BZHI LAS LHAG MED DE, BSKYED RIM MTHAR PHYIN NAS THUN MONG GI DNGOS GRUB 'GRUB PA'I DON DU SPYOD PA BYED PA DANG , SEMS DBEN THOB NAS SGYU LUS 'GRUB PA'I DON DU SPYOD PA BYED PA DANG , SGYU LUS THOB NAS 'OD GSAL GYIS SBYANGS PA'I YE SHES KYI SKU THOB PA'I DON DU SPYOD PA BYED PA DANG , SLOB PA'I ZUNG 'JUG THOB NAS MI SLOB PA'I ZUNG 'JUG THOB PA'I DON DU SPYOD PA BYED PA STE BZHI LAS MED PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: thob zin bogs 'byin gyi spyod pa byed pa'i skabs bzhi las lhag med de, bskyed rim mthar phyin nas thun mong gi dngos grub 'grub pa'i don du spyod pa byed pa dang , sems dben thob nas sgyu lus 'grub pa'i don du spyod pa byed pa dang , sgyu lus thob nas 'od gsal gyis sbyangs pa'i ye shes kyi sku thob pa'i don du spyod pa byed pa dang , slob pa'i zung 'jug thob nas mi slob pa'i zung 'jug thob pa'i don du spyod pa byed pa ste bzhi las med pa'i phyir
gru.english: There are though no more than four different points at which we undertake the activities that set fire to paths that we have already attained.  These are (1) the activities that we undertake, once we have reached the final end of the stage of creation, in order to reach the shared attainments; (2) activities that we undertake, once we have reached transcendent mind, in order to attain the body of illusion; (3) activities that we undertake, once we have reached the illusory body, in order to attain the holy body of wisdom which has been purified by the clear light; and (4) activities that we undertake, once we have reached the combination of the two for someone who is still learning, in order to reach the combination of the two for someone who needs to learn nothing more.

gru.acip: BSKYED RIM PAS SPYOD PA MA BYAS PAR THUN MONG GI DNGOS GRUB MANG PO 'GRUB PA YOD KYANG , THUN MONG GI DNGOS GRUB KYI MTHAR THUG PA RNAMS DANG , GZHAN MANG PO YANG DUS THUNG NGUR BDE BLAG TU 'GRUB PA'I THABS SU SPYOD PA BYED PA YIN NO,,
gru.wylie: bskyed rim pas spyod pa ma byas par thun mong gi dngos grub mang po 'grub pa yod kyang , thun mong gi dngos grub kyi mthar thug pa rnams dang , gzhan mang po yang dus thung ngur bde blag tu 'grub pa'i thabs su spyod pa byed pa yin no
gru.english: Now it is possible for a person on the stage of creation to reach a great many different shared attainments even without undertaking these activities; but they go on to engage in the activities as a method to reach the ultimate ones among the shared attainments, and many other attainments as well--in a relatively short period of time, and relatively easily.

gru.acip: RIM PA GNYIS KAS DE LTAR SPYOD PA BYAS KYANG RANG RANG GI SKABS KYI 'BRAS BU MYUR DU MA GRUB NA, RIM GYIS SO SO'I SNYING PO BSKUL TSUL NI LE'U BCU PA'I RGYUD 'GREL DANG N'A RO PA'I RGYUD PHYI MA'I 'GREL PA LAS SHES PAR BYA'O, ,ZHES GSAL SGRON LAS GSUNGS SO,,
gru.wylie: rim pa gnyis kas de ltar spyod pa byas kyang rang rang gi skabs kyi 'bras bu myur du ma grub na, rim gyis so so'i snying po bskul tshul ni le'u bcu pa'i rgyud 'grel dang nA ro pa'i rgyud phyi ma'i 'grel pa las shes par bya'o, ,zhes gsal sgron las gsungs so
gru.english: The Lantern goes on to state that-- If in either one of the stages you undertake these particular activities, but fail to quickly reach the goals of whatever practice it may happen to be at the time, then you should undertake special methods of forcing the essence of the particular practice, in certain steps.  These methods you can learn from the commentary to the tantra for the tenth chapter, or else from the commentary to the latter tantra of Naropa.

gru.acip: BZHI PA 'BRAS BU MNGON DU BYED TSUL NI, LAM 'DI DAG GI 'BRAS BU NI RNAM PA GSUM STE, SANGS RGYAS NI RAB, GRUB PA CHEN PO BRGYAD NI 'BRING , ZHI RGYAS DBANG DRAG GI 'PHRIN LAS NI THA MA'O,,
gru.wylie: bzhi pa 'bras bu mngon du byed tshul ni, lam 'di dag gi 'bras bu ni rnam pa gsum ste, sangs rgyas ni rab, grub pa chen po brgyad ni 'bring , zhi rgyas dbang drag gi 'phrin las ni tha ma'o
gru.english: This brings us to the fourth section in our presentation of the unsurpassed class as a whole: how we manifest the results of our practice.  The spiritual results of these various paths are of three different types: in the highest case, we attain enlightenment; a medium result is that we reach the eight great attainments; and as the least of results we gain the ability for the four modes of holy action: peace, generosity, power, and ferocity.

gru.acip: PHYI MA GNYIS NI THUN MONG GI DNGOS GRUB YIN PAS, BSDU NA MCHOG DANG THUN MONG GI DNGOS GRUB GNYIS SO,,
gru.wylie: phyi ma gnyis ni thun mong gi dngos grub yin pas, bsdu na mchog dang thun mong gi dngos grub gnyis so
gru.english: The latter two of these three are shared attainments; as such, the goals can simply be divided into two types: supreme and shared attainments.

gru.acip: GANG BSKUR BA'I DBANG LA, BYIS PA LTAR 'JUG PA'I DBANG BDUN NI, BYIS PA BTZAS PA NA MAS BKRU PA DANG , DE NAS RNA BA 'BUGS SHING RGYAN 'DOGS, TZUG PHUD 'JOG CING RGOD PA SOGS DANG , CHOS MTHUN PA YIN LA, DE YANG DUS KYI 'KHOR LO'I BYANG PHYOGS SKU'I ZHAL LA MNGON DU PHYOGS PAR SLOB MA SKU RDO RJER BSKYED PA LA BSGRUBS PA'I DKYIL 'KHOR GYI NANG GI YUM BZHIS CHU DBANG DANG , DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA LNGAS COD PAnA GYI DBANG BSKUR,
gru.wylie: gang bskur ba'i dbang la, byis pa ltar 'jug pa'i dbang bdun ni, byis pa btsas pa na mas bkru pa dang , de nas rna ba 'bugs shing rgyan 'dogs, tsug phud 'jog cing rgod pa sogs dang , chos mthun pa yin la, de yang dus kyi 'khor lo'i byang phyogs sku'i zhal la mngon du phyogs par slob ma sku rdo rjer bskyed pa la bsgrubs pa'i dkyil 'khor gyi nang gi yum bzhis chu dbang dang , de bzhin gshegs pa lngas cod paNa gyi dbang bskur
gru.english: And what are the empowerments which are given?  The seven empowerments where one enters like a child are analogous to (1) an infant coming out of the womb being washed by the mother; and then (3) piercing the child's ears, and placing ornaments in them; (2) tying their hair up in a knot; (4) the child laughing, and the like [which are explained as (5) the child learning to utilize objects, or partaking of things, day and night; (6) the granting of the child's name; and (7) the parents constantly granting the child lessons, in things such as learning to read]. Now the disciple faces the head of the Angel of the Wheel of Time which is on the northern side--the head of the holy body--and turns themselves into the diamond of the holy body.  Standing then inside the secret world which was created, they are granted (1) the empowerment of the sacred water by the four queens, and (2) the empowerment of the crown by the five Buddhas who have Gone That Way.

gru.acip: RAL GRI'I RIGS LA, DKON MCHOG SOGS MCHOD PA DANG , RGYAL BA SKYED MDZAD RDO RJE GCIG PA'I RIGS LA, STONG NYID SNYING RJE'I BDAG NYID CAN GYI PHYAG CHEN GYI DNGOS GRUB SKYED PAR GSUNGS PA RNAMS SO,,
gru.wylie: ral gri'i rigs la, dkon mchog sogs mchod pa dang , rgyal ba skyed mdzad rdo rje gcig pa'i rigs la, stong nyid snying rje'i bdag nyid can gyi phyag chen gyi dngos grub skyed par gsungs pa rnams so
gru.english: In the Family of the Sword [Attainment, Amoghasiddhi], we make offerings to the Jewels, and the like.  In the Family of the One Diamond, the Source of Victors [presumably Vajradhara], we seek to reach the attainments of the great seal--a combination of emptiness and compassion.

gru.acip: DPA' BO GCIG PA DANG LHAN SKYES LTA BU NI LHA'I RNAL 'BYOR MTHAR PHYIN NAS ZHI SOGS KYI LAS SNA TSOGS SGRUB PA'I THABS SU GSUNGS KYI, RDZOGS RIM YONGS RDZOGS SKYE BA'I SMIN BYED TSANG BA MIN NO,,
gru.wylie: dpa' bo gcig pa dang lhan skyes lta bu ni lha'i rnal 'byor mthar phyin nas zhi sogs kyi las sna tshogs sgrub pa'i thabs su gsungs kyi, rdzogs rim yongs rdzogs skye ba'i smin byed tshang ba min no
gru.english: It is said that if one comes to the final end of a deep practice of something like either the solitary warrior or the couple, then it can serve as a means of attaining a variety of attainments such as the modes of peace and so on; but this would not have within itself all the required elements needed for a practice which would ripen ones mind to give rise to the stage of completion in its entirety.

gru.acip: DE'I BSKYED RIM GYI 'CHINGS NI, SKU RDO RJE BSNYEN PA, GSUNG RDO RJE NYER SGRUB, THUGS RDO RJE SGRUB PA, YE SHES RDO RJE SGRUB CHEN TE BSNYEN SGRUB YAN LAG BZHI'AM,
gru.wylie: de'i bskyed rim gyi 'chings ni, sku rdo rje bsnyen pa, gsung rdo rje nyer sgrub, thugs rdo rje sgrub pa, ye shes rdo rje sgrub chen te bsnyen sgrub yan lag bzhi'am
gru.english: The root sources for the stage of creation here are called the "four components of practice"--the retreat for the diamond of the holy body; the close practice for the diamond of holy speech; the practice for the diamond of holy mind; and the great practice for the diamond of wisdom.

gru.acip: GNYIS PA NI, SOR BSAM LA SOGS PA'I YAN LAG DRUG GO ,CI'I PHYIR RDZOGS RIM LA YAN LAG DRUG TU BZHAG CE NA, THOB BYA SANGS RGYAS LA SKU GSUNG THUGS GSUM YOD PAS DE SGRUB BYED KYI RDZOGS RIM YANG YAN LAG DRUG TU NGES TE,
gru.wylie: gnyis pa ni, sor bsam la sogs pa'i yan lag drug go ,ci'i phyir rdzogs rim la yan lag drug tu bzhag ce na, thob bya sangs rgyas la sku gsung thugs gsum yod pas de sgrub byed kyi rdzogs rim yang yan lag drug tu nges te
gru.english: This brings us to the second point in our explanation of the stage of completion in the Wheel of Time: the six-part practice of the inner winds, which is what we use to work at the critical points of the inner body.  One may ask why the stage of completion in this system is referred to as the "six-part practice."  The things that we hope to achieve here are three in number: the holy body, speech, and mind of an Enlightened Being.  As such, the stage of completion that we use for attaining these three has exactly six different parts.

gru.acip: SOR BSAM GNYIS KYIS STONG GZUGS SNGAR MA GRUB PA SGRUB CING GRUB ZIN BRTAN PAR BYAS PA'I SGO NAS RGYAL BA'I SKU SGRUB LA, SROG 'DZIN GNYIS KYIS NGAG GI RTZA BA RLUNG LA DBANG THOB PAR BYAS NAS RGYAL BA'I GSUNG SGRUB CING , RJES DRAN NI MI 'GYUR BA'I BDE BA'I NYE RGYU DANG , TING NGE 'DZIN NI MI 'GYUR BA'I BDE BA'I NGO BO YIN PAS RGYAL BA'I THUGS SGRUB BYED YIN PA'I PHYIR RO,,
gru.wylie: sor bsam gnyis kyis stong gzugs sngar ma grub pa sgrub cing grub zin brtan par byas pa'i sgo nas rgyal ba'i sku sgrub la, srog 'dzin gnyis kyis ngag gi rtsa ba rlung la dbang thob par byas nas rgyal ba'i gsung sgrub cing , rjes dran ni mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba'i nye rgyu dang , ting nge 'dzin ni mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba'i ngo bo yin pas rgyal ba'i thugs sgrub byed yin pa'i phyir ro
gru.english: This in turn is true because the two steps of withdrawal and concentration act to bring about the holy body of a Victor, by allowing one to attain an empty form that they have not attained before; and by making one which has already been attained more stable.  The two steps of mastering the winds and retention allow one to attain power over the wind which is the root of speech, thus acting to bring about the holy speech of a Victor.  The step of recollection acts as an immediate cause for immutable bliss, while one-point meditation--since its essence is immutable bliss--allows one to attain the holy mind of a Victor.

gru.acip: DE 'DRA BA'I BDE STONG ZUNG 'JUG NI, RANG DANG RJES SU MTHUN PA'I RGYUS SGRUB DGOS LA, DE YANG RANG NYID STONG GZUGS KYI 'DOD LHA YAB YUM DU SNANG BA'I YUM LA RJES SU CHAGS PA LAS RANG GI SEMS DE KHO NA NYID LA ZHUGS PA'I MI 'GYUR BA'I BDE BA THOB PA GNYIS ZUNG DU SBREL NUS PA'I TING NGE 'DZIN GYI YAN LAG YIN TE, DE LTAR SNGAGS RIM LAS GSUNGS PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: de 'dra ba'i bde stong zung 'jug ni, rang dang rjes su mthun pa'i rgyus sgrub dgos la, de yang rang nyid stong gzugs kyi 'dod lha yab yum du snang ba'i yum la rjes su chags pa las rang gi sems de kho na nyid la zhugs pa'i mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba thob pa gnyis zung du sbrel nus pa'i ting nge 'dzin gyi yan lag yin te, de ltar sngags rim las gsungs pa'i phyir
gru.english: This combination of the two--of bliss and voidness--is something which must be attained through the corresponding causes.  That is, we appear in the form of the Angels of Desire, Man and Woman, in our empty forms.  Because of our desire for the Woman, our own mind attains a state of immutable bliss, itself engaged in suchness as its object.  We work to keep these two together.  And it is the step of one-point meditation which gives us the power to do so.  This is case because this is how the Steps on the Way of the Secret Word describes it.

gru.acip: SNGAGS RIM LAS, DBU MA SBYANGS PA'I GO BA NI, SOR SDUD KYIS RTAGS BCU GCIG PO BSGRUBS PA BSAM GTAN GYIS BRTAN PAR BYAS PAS RLUNG CUNG ZAD LAS SU RUNG NAS G-YAS G-YON GYI RLUNG RANG SHUGS KYIS DBU MAR 'GRO BA RTZOM PA YIN LA, MTSAMS DE NAS G-YAS G-YON GYI RGYU BA 'GOG PA'I SBYOR BA BYAS NA GNAD DU 'GRO'O, ,DE'I GONG DU BYAS KYANG MI 'GRO BAS, YAN LAG DANG PO GNYIS NI SREG RTZOL SGOM PA'I TSAD 'DZIN NO, ,ZHES GSUNGS PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: sngags rim las, dbu ma sbyangs pa'i go ba ni, sor sdud kyis rtags bcu gcig po bsgrubs pa bsam gtan gyis brtan par byas pas rlung cung zad las su rung nas g-yas g-yon gyi rlung rang shugs kyis dbu mar 'gro ba rtsom pa yin la, mtshams de nas g-yas g-yon gyi rgyu ba 'gog pa'i sbyor ba byas na gnad du 'gro'o, ,de'i gong du byas kyang mi 'gro bas, yan lag dang po gnyis ni sreg rtsol sgom pa'i tshad 'dzin no, ,zhes gsungs pa'i phyir
gru.english: The Steps on the Way of the Secret Word puts it like this-- Here's what we mean when we talk about "training the central channel."  We attain the eleven different signs by using the step of withdrawal.  We then use the step of concentration to make these stable.  Because of this, the inner winds become somewhat ready for higher work.  And with this, the winds on the right and the left begin to pass into the central channel, all on their own.  If at this point we undertake methods to stop the running of the right and left winds, it will have the desired effect.  If we attempt to do this prior to this point though, it will not.  As such, the first two steps of the six are considered the point past which we can begin our practice of mastering the inner winds.

gru.acip: DE DAG GI DON BSDU NA, SOR BSAM GNYIS KYIS RDO RJE'I SKU'I RGYU GZUGS BSGRUBS PA'I SGO NAS DBU MA SBYANGS, SROG RTZOL GYIS SBYANGS PA'I DBU MA'I NANG DU RO RKYANG GI RLUNG GNYIS 'JUG ,'DZIN PAS BCUG PA DE DER PHYI NANG DU 'BYUNG 'JUG MI BYED PAR BZUNG , RJES DRAN GYIS BZUNG BA DE LA BRTEN NAS PHYAG RGYA GSUM GANG RUNG BSGOMS PAS BYANG SEMS BZHUS NAS PHAB PA PHYIR MA 'PHOS PAR BZUNG BAS 'GYUR MED KYI BDE BA BSGRUBS,
gru.wylie: de dag gi don bsdu na, sor bsam gnyis kyis rdo rje'i sku'i rgyu gzugs bsgrubs pa'i sgo nas dbu ma sbyangs, srog rtsol gyis sbyangs pa'i dbu ma'i nang du ro rkyang gi rlung gnyis 'jug ,'dzin pas bcug pa de der phyi nang du 'byung 'jug mi byed par bzung , rjes dran gyis bzung ba de la brten nas phyag rgya gsum gang rung bsgoms pas byang sems bzhus nas phab pa phyir ma 'phos par bzung bas 'gyur med kyi bde ba bsgrubs
gru.english: Let us then summarize these points.  The two steps of withdrawal and concentration serve to prepare the central channel, by bringing about the form which acts as a cause for the diamond body.  The step of mastering the life-wind serves to bring two winds--the winds of the channel of taste and of the solitary channel--into the central channel which has thus been prepared.  The stage of retention acts to retain the winds that have been pushed into this channel--preventing them from being expelled or re-admitted, out or in.  The step of recollection utilizes a practice with any one or more of the three kinds of partners, taking the winds thus retained as their basis, to get the element of enlightenment to melt down; it allows it to descend, but holds it back from passing outside, thus bringing about immutable bliss.

gru.acip: TING NGE 'DZIN GYIS SOR BSAM GYIS BSGRUBS PA'I GZUGS DE LAS RANG 'DOD LHA YAB YUM GYI STONG GZUGS KYI SKUR BYAS TE PHYAG CHEN LA RJES SU CHAGS NAS, MI 'GYUR BA'I BDE BA THOB PA DE GONG NAS GONG DU SPEL BA'I MTHAR BEM PO'I PHUNG SOGS THAMS CAD ZAD DE, LUS STONG GZUGS RDO RJE'I SKU DANG THUGS DNGOS PO'I DE KHO NA NYID LA DUS KUN TU MNYAM PAR BZHAG PA'I MI 'GYUR BA'I BDE BA GNYIS ZUNG DU 'JUG PA'I SKU THOB PA 'DI SEMS 'GREL SKOR GSUM GYI GNAD BSDUS PA'I SNYING PO YIN PAR SNGAGS RIM LAS GSUNGS SO,,
gru.wylie: ting nge 'dzin gyis sor bsam gyis bsgrubs pa'i gzugs de las rang 'dod lha yab yum gyi stong gzugs kyi skur byas te phyag chen la rjes su chags nas, mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba thob pa de gong nas gong du spel ba'i mthar bem po'i phung sogs thams cad zad de, lus stong gzugs rdo rje'i sku dang thugs dngos po'i de kho na nyid la dus kun tu mnyam par bzhag pa'i mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba gnyis zung du 'jug pa'i sku thob pa 'di sems 'grel skor gsum gyi gnad bsdus pa'i snying po yin par sngags rim las gsungs so
gru.english: The step of single-point meditation acts to take the form that was brought about by the steps of withdrawal and concentration, and turn it into ourselves, appearing in the empty form of a Man and Woman Angel.  This creates an intense form of desire towards the great seal, through which we attain immutable bliss.  This increases ever and ever more high, until at the end the heap of material form and so on, all of it, simply comes to an end.  And then we attain the combination of the two: a body which is the diamond body of empty form; and a holy mind which consists of immutable bliss, forever engaged in every moment within a deep meditation upon the suchness to all objects.  This, says the Steps on the Way of the Secret Word, is the very essence that includes all the essential points of the "three great books that comment upon the mind" [three great tantric scriptures from the Tengyur].

gru.acip: NGES PA LNGA NI, DUS NGES PA RTAGS BCU RDZOGS PA'I MTHAR, GNAS NGES PA DBU MA'I NANG DU, NGO BO NGES PA RDUL BSAGS PA MIN PAR RANG SEMS KYI SNANG BA TZAM DU GRUB LA, SKU NGES PA RDO RJE SEMS DPA'I SKU, RNAM PA NGES PA YAB YUM ZHAL SBYOR GYI RNAM PA CAN DU MTHONG BAR 'GYUR RO,,
gru.wylie: nges pa lnga ni, dus nges pa rtags bcu rdzogs pa'i mthar, gnas nges pa dbu ma'i nang du, ngo bo nges pa rdul bsags pa min par rang sems kyi snang ba tsam du grub la, sku nges pa rdo rje sems dpa'i sku, rnam pa nges pa yab yum zhal sbyor gyi rnam pa can du mthong bar 'gyur ro
gru.english: Here are the five fixed features.  The time is fixed, in that these forms come at the end--when all ten signs have already appeared.  The place is fixed, in that this all occurs within the central channel.  The nature is fixed, in that this is all composed only of images within ones own mind: these things are not something made up of molecules of physical matter.  The holy form is fixed, in that the bodies that appear are those of the Warrior of Diamond, Man and Woman.  And the aspect is fixed, in that what we see is in the aspect of the Angel Man and Woman, joined in a kiss.

gru.acip: DE LTAR SOR SDUD KYIS RTAGS BCU GCIG PO BSGRUBS PA DE BSAM GTAN GYI YAN LAG GIS BRTAN PAR BYAS PAS RLUNG CUNG ZAD LAS SU RUNG NAS G-YAS G-YON GYI RLUNG RANG SHUGS KYIS DBU MAR 'GRO BA RTZOM PA ZHIG BYUNG NA SOR BSAM GYI NUS PA DES RDZOGS PAS, MTSAMS DE NAS SROG RTZOL BSGOM DGOS TE,
gru.wylie: de ltar sor sdud kyis rtags bcu gcig po bsgrubs pa de bsam gtan gyi yan lag gis brtan par byas pas rlung cung zad las su rung nas g-yas g-yon gyi rlung rang shugs kyis dbu mar 'gro ba rtsom pa zhig byung na sor bsam gyi nus pa des rdzogs pas, mtshams de nas srog rtsol bsgom dgos te
gru.english: The component known as "concentration" then takes the eleven signs which have been brought about in this way by the step of withdrawal, and makes them more stable.  With this, the inner winds are brought to some small measure of readiness for higher work, and so the right and left winds begin to move, on their own accord, into the central channel.  The power of the steps of withdrawal and concentration is expended through this, and so at this juncture we must begin our practice of mastering the life-wind.

gru.acip: DBU MAR TSUD PA BRTAN PA ZHIG BYUNG NA SROG RTZOL GYI NUS PA DES RDZOGS PAS, DE NAS 'DZIN PA BSGOM DGOS TE, DBU MA'I NANG DU BRTAN PAR GNAS PA NI SROG RTZOL GYI LAG RJES MIN GYI 'DZIN PAS BSGRUB DGOS PA'I PHYIR RO,,
gru.wylie: dbu mar tshud pa brtan pa zhig byung na srog rtsol gyi nus pa des rdzogs pas, de nas 'dzin pa bsgom dgos te, dbu ma'i nang du brtan par gnas pa ni srog rtsol gyi lag rjes min gyi 'dzin pas bsgrub dgos pa'i phyir ro
gru.english: If we are able to attain a point where these winds have been injected into the central channel in a stable way, then the step of mastering the winds is thereby exhausted, and we must begin practicing the step of retention.  This is because the fact that the winds can remain firmly within the central channel is not an aftereffect of the step of mastering the winds, but rather something which must be brought about by the step of retention.

gru.acip: DE NAS RLUNG DBU MAR TSUD PA DANG BTZUD PA DER GNAS PA BYUNG BA NA RJES DRAN GYI GTUM MO'I RNAL 'BYOR GYI MTHUS GTUM MO 'BAR NAS KHAMS ZHU BA RDO RJE'I RTZE MO'I BAR DU 'ONGS NAS PHYIR MA 'PHOS PA NA LHAN SKYES MI 'GYUR BA'I BDE BA 'GRUB PAR GSUNGS SO,,
gru.wylie: de nas rlung dbu mar tshud pa dang btsud pa der gnas pa byung ba na rjes dran gyi gtum mo'i rnal 'byor gyi mthus gtum mo 'bar nas khams zhu ba rdo rje'i rtse mo'i bar du 'ongs nas phyir ma 'phos pa na lhan skyes mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba 'grub par gsungs so
gru.english: Once we have pushed the winds into the central channel--and once the winds that we have pushed into this channel are staying there--then we use recollection, the power of the deep practice of inner fire, to bring this fire to blaze, and melt down the element.  The element then comes down as far as the tip of the diamond.  If we are then able to prevent it from moving out, it is said, then we achieve simultaneous and immutable bliss.

gru.acip: GNYIS PA LTAR NA, LAS DANG YE RGYA LA BRTEN NAS LHAN SKYES KYI BDE BA MTSAN NYID TSANG BA THOB KYANG , DE TZAM GYIS MI CHOG PAR STONG GZUGS KYI PHYAG RGYA LA BRTEN NAS MI 'GYUR BA'I BDE BA SGRUB PA LA 'BREL CI YOD, CES SOGS DOGS PA BSLANGS PAR MDZAD PA LA,
gru.wylie: gnyis pa ltar na, las dang ye rgya la brten nas lhan skyes kyi bde ba mtshan nyid tshang ba thob kyang , de tsam gyis mi chog par stong gzugs kyi phyag rgya la brten nas mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba sgrub pa la 'brel ci yod, ces sogs dogs pa bslangs par mdzad pa la
gru.english: If on the other hand the latter is the case, then what's the point of first gaining simultaneous bliss which is complete in every respect through practicing with an actual or imagined partner, and then--since that in itself isn't enough--going on to work for immutable bliss with a partner of empty form?

gru.acip: GNYIS PA LTAR NA, STONG GZUGS KYI SKU GNYUG RLUNG LAS SGRUB PAR 'DOD DGOS NA, DE LTAR TSAD LDAN SUS KYANG MA BSHAD PA'I PHYIR DANG , STONG GZUGS KYI SKU'I BSGRUB GZHI NI SOR SDUD KYI SKABS SU SHAR BA'I DUS 'KHOR YAB YUM GYI SNANG BA DE LA, YAN LAG PHYI MA RNAMS KYIS RJE BZANG DU GYUR PA LAS BSGRUB PAR GSUNGS PAS,
gru.wylie: gnyis pa ltar na, stong gzugs kyi sku gnyug rlung las sgrub par 'dod dgos na, de ltar tshad ldan sus kyang ma bshad pa'i phyir dang , stong gzugs kyi sku'i bsgrub gzhi ni sor sdud kyi skabs su shar ba'i dus 'khor yab yum gyi snang ba de la, yan lag phyi ma rnams kyis rje bzang du gyur pa las bsgrub par gsungs pas
gru.english: But if the two aren't different, then we would have to take the position that the holy body of the empty form is created from the primordial wind; whereas no one of authority at all has ever said that this was the case.  The basis for the creation of the holy body of the empty form is, rather, stated to be the appearance of the Angel Man and Woman of the Wheel of Time, which comes during the step of withdrawal.  The latter steps then serve to make this appearance increasingly more perfect, until the empty form is created.

gru.acip: SOR SDUD KYI SKABS KYI DE YANG GNYUG RLUNG LAS BSGRUBS PA'AM, YANG NA DANG POR BSGRUBS PA MIN YANG LAM GYI SKABS 'DI 'DRA ZHIG NAS BSGRUBS PA DANG KHYAD MED DU SONG BA YIN ZHES PA'I GSAL KHA SHES BYED DANG BCAS PA SGRON DGOS SO ZHES DOGS PA BSLANGS PAR MDZAD DO,,
gru.wylie: sor sdud kyi skabs kyi de yang gnyug rlung las bsgrubs pa'am, yang na dang por bsgrubs pa min yang lam gyi skabs 'di 'dra zhig nas bsgrubs pa dang khyad med du song ba yin zhes pa'i gsal kha shes byed dang bcas pa sgron dgos so zhes dogs pa bslangs par mdzad do
gru.english: And so now you'd have to be able to give us some clear scriptural evidence that said either that this appearance during the step of withdrawal is also something which is created by the primordial wind, or which said that--even though it is not created this way at the beginning--it is still created at some similar point in the path, making the two then no different.

gru.acip: DES NA SKU DE 'GRUB PA LA RDUL PHRA RAB TSOGS PA'I LUS NYAMS PAR BYA DGOS PAS, DE NI GSER 'GYUR GYI RTZIS LCAGS GSER DU BSGYUR BA BZHIN DU LUS LA BYANG CHUB KYI SEMS 'DZAG MED DU BCINGS PAS BEMS PO'I KHAMS RNAMS ZAD PAR BYED DE,
gru.wylie: des na sku de 'grub pa la rdul phra rab tshogs pa'i lus nyams par bya dgos pas, de ni gser 'gyur gyi rtsis lcags gser du bsgyur ba bzhin du lus la byang chub kyi sems 'dzag med du bcings pas bems po'i khams rnams zad par byed de
gru.english: It is though true that--in order to reach this holy body--the body which is composed of aggregates of atoms must be made to disappear.  As such, we must lock the element of enlightenment within the body, preventing it from oozing out.  This then can act like the alchemical elixir which turns iron into gold.  It brings all the various material parts of us to an end.

gru.acip: ZHES STONG GZUGS KYI SKU DNGOS GNAS PA 'GRUB PA LA BEMS PO'I KHAMS ZAD DGOS PAR GSUNGS PA GNYIS MI 'GAL TSUL JI LTAR YIN, STONG GZUGS KYI LHA SKU DNGOS GNAS LA 'GRUB PA'I MTSAMS GANG NAS YIN,
gru.wylie: zhes stong gzugs kyi sku dngos gnas pa 'grub pa la bems po'i khams zad dgos par gsungs pa gnyis mi 'gal tshul ji ltar yin, stong gzugs kyi lha sku dngos gnas la 'grub pa'i mtshams gang nas yin
gru.english: What this last is saying then is that, in order to attain the actual form of the holy body of empty form, we must bring all the various material parts of us to an end.  How then is it that these two presentations aren't in contradiction with each other?  And at which point is it, exactly, that we do attain the actual form of the Angel's holy body of empty form?

gru.acip: BLA MED KYI LAM GYIS SANGS RGYAS 'GRUB TSUL LA BSHAD SROL MI 'DRA BA GNYIS YOD DE, RNAM SMIN GYI PHUNG PO ZAD PAR MA BYAS PAR DE'I NANG NAS SANGS RGYAS 'GRUB PA NI BLA MED SPYI'I LUGS SROL DANG , RNAM SMIN GYI PHUNG PO THABS MKHAS KYIS ZAD PAR BYAS TE SANGS RGYAS 'GRUB PA NI DUS 'KHOR BA'I LUGS SROL YIN LA,
gru.wylie: bla med kyi lam gyis sangs rgyas 'grub tshul la bshad srol mi 'dra ba gnyis yod de, rnam smin gyi phung po zad par ma byas par de'i nang nas sangs rgyas 'grub pa ni bla med spyi'i lugs srol dang , rnam smin gyi phung po thabs mkhas kyis zad par byas te sangs rgyas 'grub pa ni dus 'khor ba'i lugs srol yin la
gru.english: Now there are two different ways of explaining how, through the path of the unsurpassed class, we attain enlightenment.  The general way of explaining it in the overall teachings of the unsurpassed way is that we attain enlightenment within the heaps that result from our past karma--we don't put an end to them.  The system of the Wheel of Time though is that we use unexpected means to put and end to the heaps that have resulted from our past karma, and then attain enlightenment.

gru.acip: MKHAS SHING GRUB PA BRNYES PA'I BLA MA DU MA'I ZHABS RDUL SPYI BOS NOD PA, MANG THOS RIG PA 'DZIN PA'I GZUGS BRNYAN 7-SPRANGA BTZUN NGAG DBANG DPAL LDAN GYIS SBYAR BA 'DIS KYANG BSTAN 'GRO LA PHAN THOGS PAR GYUR CIG ,,
gru.wylie: mkhas shing grub pa brnyes pa'i bla ma du ma'i zhabs rdul spyi bos nod pa, mang thos rig pa 'dzin pa'i gzugs brnyan 7-spranga btsun ngag dbang dpal ldan gyis sbyar ba 'dis kyang bstan 'gro la phan thogs par gyur cig
gru.english: This work then has been completed by myself, Ngawang Pelden, who has in his life gone and thrown himself down in the dust at the feet of a great many wise and accomplished Lamas, pressing his head to their toes.  This Ngawang Pelden is an imposter posing as one who keeps the knowledge, as one of great learning--but after all he is just an old beggar of a monk.  At any rate, he prays that this effort will be of benefit, both to the teachings and to living beings.

gru.acip: ,NGAG DBANG NGAG LA ROL PA'I RNAM DPYOD LAS, ,DPAL LDAN RGYUD GZHUNG GSAL BYED MCHOG 'DI GRUB, ,CHOS KYI SPYAN LDAN RGYUD DON TSOL 'DOD RNAMS, ,YAB RJE'I GZHUNG RGYA 'BYED PA'I LDE MIG STE,
gru.wylie: ngag dbang ngag la rol pa'i rnam dpyod las, ,dpal ldan rgyud gzhung gsal byed mchog 'di grub, ,chos kyi spyan ldan rgyud don tshol 'dod rnams, ,yab rje'i gzhung rgya 'byed pa'i lde mig ste
gru.english: This then is a light supreme Which illuminates the glorious [pelden] classics That belong to the secret way. The text was composed by Ngawang, The one who sports in the spoken word, The one of fine discrimination. For those who possess the eyes of Dharma And who seek the meaning of the secret word, It's a key they can use for opening The vast classics of the Father, the Lord [Je Tsongkapa].

gru.acip: ,DE PHYIR SER BYES TRE HOR RAB 'BYAMS PA, ,BYAMS PA MKHAS GRUB CES PA'I MING CAN GYIS, ,GANG GI ZHABS SKYES THUGS RJE BSKUL BA LAS, ,SKYES MCHOG MKHAR RDO MCHOG GIS PAR 'DI BSKRUN,
gru.wylie: de phyir ser byes tre hor rab 'byams pa, ,byams pa mkhas grub ces pa'i ming can gyis, ,gang gi zhabs skyes thugs rje bskul ba las, ,skyes mchog mkhar rdo mchog gis par 'di bskrun
gru.english: As such, this book's been printed By the great one, Kyechok Kardo, After requests for this kindness from the one Who is his servant: the one they call Jampa Kedrup, a geshe Of the rabjampa class who hails From the Trehor College of Sera Je.

gru.acip: ,,RJE BTZUN RDO RJE RNAL 'BYOR MA N'A RO MKHA' SPYOD KYI SIN+D+HU RA'I DKYIL 'KHOR SGRUB MCHOD DANG DBANG GI CHO GA BDE CHEN GSAL SGRON ZHES BYA BA BZHUGS SO,,
gru.wylie: rje btsun rdo rje rnal 'byor ma nA ro mkha' spyod kyi sin+d+hu ra'i dkyil 'khor sgrub mchod dang dbang gi cho ga bde chen gsal sgron zhes bya ba bzhugs so
gru.english: Herein lies A Light for Finding Ecstasy, a ritual for reaching, making offerings to, and then taking empowerment into the secret world of sindhura: the practice of the Heaven of the Angel, granted to Naropa for reaching the holy Angel of the Diamond.

gru.acip: ,BRJOD BRAL LHAN CIG SKYES PA'I BDE STONG GAR, ,SMIN LEGS BYU RU'I E-GA MOR BSGYUR BA'I ZHABS, ,BDE CHEN 'KHOR LOR BSTEN NAS DE NYID KYI, ,SGRUB DKYIL CHO GA MDOR BSDUS GSAL BAR BRI,
gru.wylie: brjod bral lhan cig skyes pa'i bde stong gar, ,smin legs byu ru'i e-ga mor bsgyur ba'i zhabs, ,bde chen 'khor lor bsten nas de nyid kyi, ,sgrub dkyil cho ga mdor bsdus gsal bar bri
gru.english: You are the dance Of that which cannot be spoken: Bliss and voidness, Simultaneous. You came to us In the form Of a Lady posing lovely, A visage of coral hue. And so first I rest my head Upon the wheel of ecstasy, At Your feet. And then I swear to compose, In the clearest words I can, But the briefest ritual text On the mandala for reaching You.

gru.acip: DE LA 'DIR BDE DGYES SOGS BLA MED KYI DBANG DANG RJE BTZUN MA'I BYIN RLABS THOB PA'I RNAL 'BYOR PAS, TSES BCU RNAM GNYIS SOGS DUS TSES BZANG POR DKYIL 'KHOR SGRUB MCHOD DANG DBANG BLANG BA LA DRUG ,YO BYAD BSHAM PA, BDAG BSKYED BAO-MA PA, BUM PA BSGRUB PA, MDUN BSKYED SGRUB MCHOD, DBANG BLANG BA, MJUG BSDU BA'O,,
gru.wylie: de la 'dir bde dgyes sogs bla med kyi dbang dang rje btsun ma'i byin rlabs thob pa'i rnal 'byor pas, tshes bcu rnam gnyis sogs dus tshes bzang por dkyil 'khor sgrub mchod dang dbang blang ba la drug ,yo byad bsham pa, bdag bskyed bao-ma pa, bum pa bsgrub pa, mdun bskyed sgrub mchod, dbang blang ba, mjug bsdu ba'o
gru.english: (The ceremony you find herein is meant for yogis who have already received empowerment into one of the secret teachings of the unsurpassed classthe secret instructions of the Pleasure of Diamond, or one such as thatand who have also been granted the blessing of the Holy Lady.  It is meant to be performed on special days such as one of the two tenth days in the waxing and waning of the moon, as a method for reaching, making offerings to, and taking empowerment within Her secret world. The ceremony proceeds in six parts: (1) preparing the articles of ritual; (2) the practice of becoming the Angel; (3) bringing the sacred vase into being; (4) reaching the Angel outside of us, and making offerings to Her; (5) taking the empowerment; and (6) the conclusion of the ritual.) A. Preparing the Articles of Ritual A. Preparing the Articles of Ritual

gru.acip: G-YAS d'A MA RU 'KHROL ZHING G-YON THOD PA BDUD RTZIS GANG BA THUGS KAR 'DZIN PA, GRU MO G-YON NA KHA t+V'Am GA BSNAMS PA, ZHABS RDO RJE'I SKYIL KRUNG GIS BZHUGS PA, RUS PA'I RGYAN DRUG GIS BRGYAN PA, SKYABS GNAS THAMS CAD 'DUS PA'I NGO BOR GYUR,
gru.wylie: g-yas DA ma ru 'khrol zhing g-yon thod pa bdud rtsis gang ba thugs kar 'dzin pa, gru mo g-yon na kha T+vAM ga bsnams pa, zhabs rdo rje'i skyil krung gis bzhugs pa, rus pa'i rgyan drug gis brgyan pa, skyabs gnas thams cad 'dus pa'i ngo bor gyur
gru.english: With His right hand, He beats a damaru drum, And in His left He holds a skullcup Filled with the nectar Of deathlessness.
