To be someone who is fit to practice this liberating path, the blessing of the Sow alone is not something that could substitute for the requirements stated.  This is because a person must be made a proper vessel for the stage of creation through the Empowerment of the Vase, and a proper vessel for the stage of completion through the higher three empowerments.  A person who has not first received the empowerments that will ripen their being is not a proper vessel for the other things, such as the blessing or the permission.

gru.acip: LHAG PAR DNGOS GRUB 'GRUB PA'I RGYU BZHI STE, DAD PAS PHYIR MI LDOG PA, SHES RAB KYIS THE TSOM MI ZA BA, YID RTZE GCIG PA, SHIN TU GSANG BA BCAS BZHI PO DANG LDAN PA DGOS, YID RTZE GCIG PA NI YI DAM GCIG LA CHIG DRIL BYED PA'I DON YIN GSUNGS,
gru.wylie: lhag par dngos grub 'grub pa'i rgyu bzhi ste, dad pas phyir mi ldog pa, shes rab kyis the tshom mi za ba, yid rtse gcig pa, shin tu gsang ba bcas bzhi po dang ldan pa dgos, yid rtse gcig pa ni yi dam gcig la chig dril byed pa'i don yin gsungs
gru.english: Most especially, this person must have the four qualities that will allow them to achieve the high attainments.  They must have faith so strong that they become unstoppable.  They must have wisdom so strong that they do not doubt.  They must have a one-pointed mind, and they must keep completely secret.  Our Lama explained that "one-pointed mind" refers to concentrating on one Angel only; the one that was close to one's heart.

gru.acip: DBANG BZHI THOB PA NI SMIN LAM DU 'JUG ZIN PAS NA 'JUG RUNG DU MI 'GRO BA'I PHYIR DE LTAR BZHAG PA MI 'THAD PAR STAG PHU BSTAN PA'I RGYAL MTSAN SOGS RANG PHYOGS KYI MKHAS GRUB TSAD LDAN MANG POS GSUNGS PAS, 'DIR RANG LUGS GONG DU BSHAD PA LTAR SMIN LAM 'JUG RUNG DBANG BZHI MA THOB BA NYID LA 'JOG DGOS,
gru.wylie: dbang bzhi thob pa ni smin lam du 'jug zin pas na 'jug rung du mi 'gro ba'i phyir de ltar bzhag pa mi 'thad par stag phu bstan pa'i rgyal mtshan sogs rang phyogs kyi mkhas grub tshad ldan mang pos gsungs pas, 'dir rang lugs gong du bshad pa ltar smin lam 'jug rung dbang bzhi ma thob ba nyid la 'jog dgos
gru.english: The fact is though that, once one receives the four empowerments, they have already entered the path that ripens us, so you can't say that they have made them fit to enter it.  Asserting that they do is incorrect, as many unerring and accomplished masters of our own school, such as Tenpay Gyeltsen of Takpu and others, have stated.  Therefore on this question we must adhere to the position we stated above, and establish a person as being fit to enter the path that ripens only if they have not received the four empowerments.

gru.acip: PAn CHEN N'A RO PAS KYANG DE DAG KHUNGS SU MDZAD DE YI DAM RDO RJE RNAL 'BYOR MA DNGOS KYI MAN NGAG LA BRTEN NAS SROL PHYES, DE DAG KYANG TSIG GI BRGYUD PA TZAM MIN PAR RANG NYID KYIS SA LAM GYI RTOGS PA JI LTAR NYAMS SU MYONG BA BZHIN BSTAN PAS BSTAN PA GZHAN LAS KHYAD PAR DU 'PHAGS SHING, DER MA ZAD RJE BLA MAS, RGYA GAR GRUB CHEN RNAMS KYIS KYANG RGYUD DON DE NYID BCU BZHI'I CHINGS DANG SBYAR BA'I STENG NAS BKRAL BAS RGYUD KYI MAN NGAG RNYED SLA BAR GSUNGS SHING,
gru.wylie: paN chen nA ro pas kyang de dag khungs su mdzad de yi dam rdo rje rnal 'byor ma dngos kyi man ngag la brten nas srol phyes, de dag kyang tshig gi brgyud pa tsam min par rang nyid kyis sa lam gyi rtogs pa ji ltar nyams su myong ba bzhin bstan pas bstan pa gzhan las khyad par du 'phags shing, der ma zad rje bla mas, rgya gar grub chen rnams kyis kyang rgyud don de nyid bcu bzhi'i chings dang sbyar ba'i steng nas bkral bas rgyud kyi man ngag rnyed sla bar gsungs shing
gru.english: These essential practices are what Panchen Naropa used as his authoritative source when he founded his system based on the advices he had received directly from the Angel of Diamond.  They were not just passed on as mere words; rather they relate the actual realizations of the path as Naropa himself experienced them.  This makes them far superior to other teachings; even Je Lama said: "The great realized saints of India also gave their explanations utilizing the root sources of the Fourteen Essential Practices, and this has made the advices of this secret teaching easy to find."

gru.acip: 'GRO BA CHAGS PAS MYOS SHING, DE LA ZHEN PA RNAMS 'DUL BA'I SLAD DU RNAL 'BYOR MA MI MO'I RNAM PAS BUD MED KYI KHROD DU BYON TE RGYUD BYIN GYIS RLOB PA SOGS KYIS DNGOS GRUB LHAG PAR MYUR BA'I KHYAD CHOS TE KHYAD CHOS GSUM DANG,
gru.wylie: 'gro ba chags pas myos shing, de la zhen pa rnams 'dul ba'i slad du rnal 'byor ma mi mo'i rnam pas bud med kyi khrod du byon te rgyud byin gyis rlob pa sogs kyis dngos grub lhag par myur ba'i khyad chos te khyad chos gsum dang
gru.english: Finally, these are times when beings are crazed with desire; and because She wants to tame those who have a craving for that sort of thing, the Angel comes to us in the form of a human female, mixing with the women of the world, so She can give Her blessings to our being.  Things like this give our path its third unique quality: that it brings the attainments with incredible speed.

gru.acip: YANG YAB YUM GNYI GAR SKYE BDUN GYI SHA LA BRTEN PA SOGS KYIS MKHA' SPYOD BSGRUB TSUL YOD PA 'DRA NA'ANG, LUS MA SPANGS PAR MKHA' SPYOD DU BGROD THABS KYI GTZO BO NI YUM BKA' 'DI NYID YIN PAR MTSAN GYI STENG NAS KYANG SHES TSUL SOGS PHAN YON RGYAS PAR STZAL,
gru.wylie: yang yab yum gnyi gar skye bdun gyi sha la brten pa sogs kyis mkha' spyod bsgrub tshul yod pa 'dra na'ang, lus ma spangs par mkha' spyod du bgrod thabs kyi gtso bo ni yum bka' 'di nyid yin par mtshan gyi steng nas kyang shes tshul sogs phan yon rgyas par stsal
gru.english: And although both the Man and Wife traditions are similar in that we work to reach the Heaven of the Angel by following practices such as using the flesh of a person who has only seven lives left to go, the principal method for traveling to Her Heaven without leaving this very body is only the Word of the Wife.  The truth of this, related our Lama, I have also learned from visions.  And so with these and other words He described, in great detail, the benefits of the path we were to learn.

gru.acip: GSUM PA JI LTAR NYAMS SU LEN PA'I TSUL LA GNYIS, PHYI'I MKHA' SPYOD GTZO BOR SGRUB PA BSKYED RIM GYI RNAL 'BYOR DANG, NANG GI MKHA' SPYOD GTZO BOR SGRUB PA RDZOGS RIM GYI RNAL 'BYOR RO,
gru.wylie: gsum pa ji ltar nyams su len pa'i tshul la gnyis, phyi'i mkha' spyod gtso bor sgrub pa bskyed rim gyi rnal 'byor dang, nang gi mkha' spyod gtso bor sgrub pa rdzogs rim gyi rnal 'byor ro
gru.english: This brings us to the part of the teaching on how it is that on should carry out the authentic Dharma he has found.  Here there are two divisions: the practice of the stage of creation, which is mainly to help us achieve the outer Heaven; and the practice of the stage of completion, which is mainly to help us achieve the inner Heaven. *  *  *  *  * The Secret Treasure of the Angels

gru.acip: DMIGS RKANG DANG PO, GNAS KHANG 'DI YANG THA MAL PA'I RNAM PA CAN MA YIN PAR RJE BTZUN RDO RJE RNAL 'BYOR MA'I YE SHES RANG SNANG LAS GRUB PA'I CHOS 'BYUNG NYIS BRTZEGS CAN, BLA MA DANG RANG NYID GROGS RNAMS KYANG RJE BTZUN MA DNGOS YIN SNYAM PA DANG, THAMS CAD 'OD KYI RNAM PA CAN DU BSAM LA,
gru.wylie: dmigs rkang dang po, gnas khang 'di yang tha mal pa'i rnam pa can ma yin par rje btsun rdo rje rnal 'byor ma'i ye shes rang snang las grub pa'i chos 'byung nyis brtsegs can, bla ma dang rang nyid grogs rnams kyang rje btsun ma dngos yin snyam pa dang, thams cad 'od kyi rnam pa can du bsam la
gru.english: Here is the first of the visualizations which Master Quicksilver presented.  The place where you are sitting now is no ordinary place.  It is the star palace of the holy Angel of Diamond, a spontaneous emanation of Her wisdom.  Your teacher, and you yourself, and everyone around you here right now is the Holy Angel Herself.  Everything is made of light.

gru.acip: JI LTAR YANG DAM TSIG DANG SDOM PA MIG 'BRAS LTAR BSRUNG BA NI DNGOS GRUB KUN GYI RTZA BA YIN PAS SHIN TU GAL CHE'O,,
gru.wylie: ji ltar yang dam tshig dang sdom pa mig 'bras ltar bsrung ba ni dngos grub kun gyi rtsa ba yin pas shin tu gal che'o
gru.english: In any case, keeping the commitments and vows which you pledged yourself to during your empowerment--and doing so with all the care that you take to shield your eyes from something that would harm them--is the very root of every spiritual attainment.  And so this point is absolutely indispensable.

gru.acip: GNYIS PA GANG NYAMS SU BLANG BA'I CHOS NI, RNAL 'BYOR GSANG MTHA'I RGYUD KYI BCUD PHYUNG BA BOD LJONGS BSTAN PA'I MNGA' BDAG DPAL LDAN SA SKYA'I LCAGS RI MI 'DA' BA'I GSER CHOS BCU GSUM KYI NANG TSAN MCHOG BSGRUBS PAS THUN MONG ZHAR LA 'GRUB PA DMAR MO SKOR GSUM DU GRAGS PA'I SNYING PO'AM MCHOG TU GYUR PA,
gru.wylie: gnyis pa gang nyams su blang ba'i chos ni, rnal 'byor gsang mtha'i rgyud kyi bcud phyung ba bod ljongs bstan pa'i mnga' bdag dpal ldan sa skya'i lcags ri mi 'da' ba'i gser chos bcu gsum kyi nang tshan mchog bsgrubs pas thun mong zhar la 'grub pa dmar mo skor gsum du grags pa'i snying po'am mchog tu gyur pa
gru.english: Here secondly is our explanation of the teaching it is which we put into practice.  The teaching we present here is the very heart, the very pinnacle, of the instructions known as the Three Collections of the Crimson Queen.  These themselves form an integral part of the Thirteen Teachings of Gold, and are a method of attaining the ultimate goal and thereby automatically reaching all the shared goals of the world as well. The Thirteen Teachings were never to be allowed beyond the walls of Sakya Monastery, and were the purview of the glorious tradition of the Sakyas, who are themselves the absolute lords of the Word of the Buddha here in the Land of Snows.  The Thirteen Teachings are the distilled essence of all the tantras of the yoga of the ultimate secret.

gru.acip: RDO RJE RNAL 'BYOR MAS GRUB CHEN N'A RO TA PA LA DNGOS SU GNANG BA TSE 'DI LA LUS MA SPANGS PAR MKHA' SPYOD DU BGROD PAR BYED PA N'A RO MKHA' SPYOD KYI GDAMS PA SNYAN RGYUD TSAD MA BZHI LDAN ZHES BYA BA BLA MA LUNG BSTAN BCOS NYAMS MYONG TSAD MA STE,
gru.wylie: rdo rje rnal 'byor mas grub chen nA ro ta pa la dngos su gnang ba tshe 'di la lus ma spangs par mkha' spyod du bgrod par byed pa nA ro mkha' spyod kyi gdams pa snyan rgyud tshad ma bzhi ldan zhes bya ba bla ma lung bstan bcos nyams myong tshad ma ste
gru.english: And what exactly is the teaching we present here?  It is the advices on the Heaven of Naropa: instructions which enable us to travel to the Heaven of the Sky in this life, before we die.  These advices were granted directly to the accomplished saint Narotapa by the Angel of Daimond. These are instructions possess the four qualities of an authentic oral tradition.  That is, they possess an authentic Lama, an authentic Word, an authentic commentarial tradition, and authentic experience.

gru.acip: NYAL BA'I RNAL 'BYOR THOG MAR 'BYUNG BA 'DI GNAD SHIN TU CHE STE, GRUB CHEN L'U AI PAS, ,NYIN MO BCOM LDAN RDO RJE CAN, ,RNAL 'BYOR MA NI MTSAN MOR BSHAD, ,CES GSUNGS PA LTAR DUS KYI DBANG DU MDZAD PA RED,
gru.wylie: nyal ba'i rnal 'byor thog mar 'byung ba 'di gnad shin tu che ste, grub chen lU ai pas, ,nyin mo bcom ldan rdo rje can, ,rnal 'byor ma ni mtshan mor bshad, ,ces gsungs pa ltar dus kyi dbang du mdzad pa red
gru.english: There is a very great significance to the fact that the sleeping practice comes before all the others; it relates to the time of day, as the great accomplished saint Luyipa has spoken in the lines, The day they say is the Conqueror with the Diamond; And the Angel of Heaven, She is then the night.

gru.acip: DE YANG YUM BKA' RNAL 'BYOR MA 'DI THABS SHES KYI RGYUD GNYIS LA SHES RAB KYI RGYUD DANG, PHA RGYUD MA RGYUD GNYIS LAS MA RGYUD, SNANG STONG GNYIS LAS STONG PHYOGS YIN ZHING, MA RGYUD KYI 'CHAD BYA'I GTZO BO YANG STONG PHYOGS SHES RAB KYI CHA 'OD GSAL BSGRUB TSUL YIN LA,
gru.wylie: de yang yum bka' rnal 'byor ma 'di thabs shes kyi rgyud gnyis la shes rab kyi rgyud dang, pha rgyud ma rgyud gnyis las ma rgyud, snang stong gnyis las stong phyogs yin zhing, ma rgyud kyi 'chad bya'i gtso bo yang stong phyogs shes rab kyi cha 'od gsal bsgrub tshul yin la
gru.english: To explain further, there are two types of secret teachings: those of method and those of wisdom.  Of these two, the practice of the Angel, part of the Word of the Wife, represents a secret teaching of wisdom.  And when we consider the secret teachings as divided into Man or Wife, it is a teaching of the Wife. If we separate all objects into appearances and emptiness, then this practice relates to the emptiness side of things.  Moreover, the main subject explained in the secret teachings of the Wife is how to achieve the clear light, which is a kind of wisdom, and included in the emptiness side of things.

gru.acip: DPER NA 'JIG RTEN NA LAS KA'I 'GO BRTZAM TSE TSES GRANGS BLTA BA DANG, ZLA BA DANG PO'I TSES GCIG LA LO SAR GYI RTEN 'BREL BYED PA, TSE SGRUB KYI 'GO SNGA DROR BRTZAMS PA TSUN CHAD RTEN 'BREL GYI GNAD DU BYA DGOS PA LTAR 'DIR YANG DUS KYI RTEN 'BREL GYI GNAD CHE ZHING,
gru.wylie: dper na 'jig rten na las ka'i 'go brtsam tshe tshes grangs blta ba dang, zla ba dang po'i tshes gcig la lo sar gyi rten 'brel byed pa, tshe sgrub kyi 'go snga dror brtsams pa tshun chad rten 'brel gyi gnad du bya dgos pa ltar 'dir yang dus kyi rten 'brel gyi gnad che zhing
gru.english: In the everyday world, for example, we look to find an auspicious day for starting any important task.  We consider the first day of the first month, New Year's Day, significant in getting off to a good start for the whole year.  When we perform one of those rituals for a long life, we always start in the morning; all the way up to more important things, we consider the time important in making a good beginning.  Here also the time for a good beginning is a very crucial matter.

gru.acip: DER MA ZAD RDO RJE MKHA' 'GRO LAS, ,YUL 'DI RNAMS KYI BU MO GANG, ,SGRUB PA PO LA DNGOS GRUB STER, ,RTAG TU MTSAN MO 'PHYAN PA DANG, ,RTAG TU MTSAN MO 'DU BAR BYED, ,MKHA' SPYOD SHIN TU RNYED DKA' BA'I, ,DNGOS GRUB CHEN PO STER BAR 'GYUR,
gru.wylie: der ma zad rdo rje mkha' 'gro las, ,yul 'di rnams kyi bu mo gang, ,sgrub pa po la dngos grub ster, ,rtag tu mtshan mo 'phyan pa dang, ,rtag tu mtshan mo 'du bar byed, ,mkha' spyod shin tu rnyed dka' ba'i, ,dngos grub chen po ster bar 'gyur
gru.english: Moreover there are those lines from the Angel of Diamond: The young girls of this land Give attainments to practitioners; They always make their rounds at night, It is at night they always gather, Giving us the great attainment, The Angel's Heaven, so hard to find.

gru.acip: ZHES GSUNGS PA LTAR PHYI ROL GYI MKHA' 'GRO MA THAMS CAD LHAG PAR RGYU ZHING 'DU BA'I DUS KYANG MTSAN MO YIN PAS YUL NYER BZHI'I MKHA' 'GRO MA RNAMS RGYU BA DANG 'PHYAN PA'I DUS DER NYAMS LEN GYI 'GO BRTZAMS NA DE DAG GIS RJES SU GZUNG BA DANG, BYIN GYIS BRLAB PA, RTOGS PA MYUR DU SKYE BA, MKHA' SPYOD KYI DNGOS GRUB 'GRUB SLA BA SOGS KYI RTEN 'BREL DANG DGOS PA KHYAD PAR CAN YOD CING,
gru.wylie: zhes gsungs pa ltar phyi rol gyi mkha' 'gro ma thams cad lhag par rgyu zhing 'du ba'i dus kyang mtshan mo yin pas yul nyer bzhi'i mkha' 'gro ma rnams rgyu ba dang 'phyan pa'i dus der nyams len gyi 'go brtsams na de dag gis rjes su gzung ba dang, byin gyis brlab pa, rtogs pa myur du skye ba, mkha' spyod kyi dngos grub 'grub sla ba sogs kyi rten 'brel dang dgos pa khyad par can yod cing
gru.english: As spoken here, night is the time when all the outer Angels are especially active, traveling around, meeting with one another.  If we start our practice off at this particular time, when all the Angels of the twenty-four sacred places are making their rounds far and wide, then They will take us into their care; They will bless our being; our realizations will come quickly, and we will reach our goal of the Heaven of the Angel with speed.  The timing of this practice therefore helps us get off to a good start towards these and our other goals; it is of vital significance.

gru.acip: THA MAL GYI SNANG ZHEN BKAG STE SNANG LA RANG BZHIN MED PAR BDE STONG GI RNAM ROL DU SHAR BA'I GNAS KHANG CHOS 'BYUNG GRU GSUM NYIS BRTZEGS KYI NANG DU SENG KHRI, DE'I STENG DU PADMA 'DAB BZHI'AM SNA TSOGS PADMA 'DAB BRGYAD KYI LTE BAR NYI GDAN DMAR KHYIL LE BA,
gru.wylie: tha mal gyi snang zhen bkag ste snang la rang bzhin med par bde stong gi rnam rol du shar ba'i gnas khang chos 'byung gru gsum nyis brtsegs kyi nang du seng khri, de'i steng du padma 'dab bzhi'am sna tshogs padma 'dab brgyad kyi lte bar nyi gdan dmar khyil le ba
gru.english: First you must consciously stop looking at things as everyday.  See your bedroom as empty of any nature of its own, as appearing through the play of bliss and emptiness: see it as a dharma star, made of the two triangular sections stacked together.  In the middle of the star is a lion throne, and atop this throne is a lotus; this can either be the four-petal kind, or the multicolor lotus with eight petals.  In the center of the lotus there is a sundisk cushion glowing with a vibrant crimson color.

whole_word_matches.context: stong gi rnam rol du shar ba'i gnas khang chos 'byung gru gsum nyis brtsegs kyi nang du seng khri, de'i steng du

gru.acip: NYAL BA'I RNAL 'BYOR NYAMS SU BLANGS BA'I DGOS PA YANG GNYID DANG 'OD GSAL BSRE BA'I DGE RTZA SMIN BYED DU 'GRO ZHING, CHOS SKU 'GRUB PA'I RGYUR BYED PA YIN GSUNGS,
gru.wylie: nyal ba'i rnal 'byor nyams su blangs ba'i dgos pa yang gnyid dang 'od gsal bsre ba'i dge rtsa smin byed du 'gro zhing, chos sku 'grub pa'i rgyur byed pa yin gsungs
gru.english: The purpose for doing this practice of sleeping, said our Lama, is that it ripens the virtuous power in you that will make you able to mix your sleep with the clear light; the practice also serves as a cause that will help you achieve the Dharma body. Second: The Practice of Waking

gru.acip: LDANG BA'I RNAL 'BYOR BYED PA'I DGOS PA RMI LAM LONGS SKU DANG, SAD PA SPRUL SKUR BSRE BA LA PHAN ZHING, LAM GYI LONGS SKU 'GRUB PA'I RGYUR 'GRO BAR GSUNGS,
gru.wylie: ldang ba'i rnal 'byor byed pa'i dgos pa rmi lam longs sku dang, sad pa sprul skur bsre ba la phan zhing, lam gyi longs sku 'grub pa'i rgyur 'gro bar gsungs
gru.english: The purpose for doing the practice of waking, said our Lama, is that it helps your ability to mix your dreams with the body of enjoyment, and your waking with the body of emanation.  It helps you as well to attain the paradise body of this path. Third: The Practice of Partaking of the Nectar

gru.acip: RNAL 'BYOR MA 'DI SA LUGS DANG 'BREL CHE BAS SA LUGS KYI BDUD RTZI RIL BU RNYED NA NGES PAR RUNG LA, DE MIN RANG LUGS PAn CHEN RIN PO CHE NAS BRGYUD PA BZANG BAR GSUNGS PAS PAn CHEN CHOS RGYAN SOGS KYIS SGRUB CHOG MDZAD PA'I BKRA SHIS LHUN PO'I BDUD RTZI RIL BU ME 'BAR BKA' RGYA MA ZHES YOD PA RNYED NA DE LTA BU RANG LUGS DAM PA TSAD LDAN GYI PHYAG NAS BYUNG BA'I BDUD RTZI RIL BU DNGOS SAM, DE'I PHAB RGYUN NGES PAR BSRES PA'I SEL MED KYI BDUD RTZI RIL BU
gru.wylie: rnal 'byor ma 'di sa lugs dang 'brel che bas sa lugs kyi bdud rtsi ril bu rnyed na nges par rung la, de min rang lugs paN chen rin po che nas brgyud pa bzang bar gsungs pas paN chen chos rgyan sogs kyis sgrub chog mdzad pa'i bkra shis lhun po'i bdud rtsi ril bu me 'bar bka' rgya ma zhes yod pa rnyed na de lta bu rang lugs dam pa tshad ldan gyi phyag nas byung ba'i bdud rtsi ril bu dngos sam, de'i phab rgyun nges par bsres pa'i sel med kyi bdud rtsi ril bu
gru.english: Because this practice of the Angel is closely tied to the Sakya tradition, it is definitely appropriate if you can get some of their nectar pills to use.  Aside from these, in our own tradition, it has been spoken that the nectar pills that have come down through the Panchen Rinpoches are especially good. There are the pills of Tashi Hlunpo known as "those that blaze fire, that are kept under seal"; they were made by the Panchen Chugyen and other Panchen Rinpoches using the ritual of creation. So if you can find them then use pills like these, either ones that have come directly from the hands of one of the authentic holy masters of our own tradition, or else pills that have come down from them, by having bits of the original pills mixed into them, without any adulteration.

gru.acip: BSGRUBS PA'I NANG MCHOD LAS LAG GA YON PA'I MTHEB SRIN GYIS BLANGS TE 'BRU GSUM BRJOD PA DANG SBRAGS LAG GA YAS PA'I MTHIL DU AOm RANG GI MDUN TSUR NGOS DANG, A'A: GA YAS, H'Um GA YON DU GNAS PAR BSAMS TE RTZE MO RANG LA BSTAN PA'I CHOS 'BYUNG GA YON SKOR DU BRIS PA'I DBUS NAS BDE STONG GNYIS SU MED PA'I YE SHES BDUD RTZI'I RNAM PAR SHAR BA'I SNYING PO BLANG BAR MOS NAS RANG LHAR GSAL BA'I LCER MYANG BA BAm YIG LA THIM PAS SNYIGS MA BSREGS, DVANGS MAS TSIMS NAS LUS THAMS CAD BDE BA CHEN PO'I YE SHES KYI BDUD RTZIS GANG ZHING, SDIG SGRIB NYES LTUNG THAMS CAD DAG PAR MOS SHING,
gru.wylie: bsgrubs pa'i nang mchod las lag ga yon pa'i mtheb srin gyis blangs te 'bru gsum brjod pa dang sbrags lag ga yas pa'i mthil du aoM rang gi mdun tshur ngos dang, a'a: ga yas, hUM ga yon du gnas par bsams te rtse mo rang la bstan pa'i chos 'byung ga yon skor du bris pa'i dbus nas bde stong gnyis su med pa'i ye shes bdud rtsi'i rnam par shar ba'i snying po blang bar mos nas rang lhar gsal ba'i lcer myang ba baM yig la thim pas snyigs ma bsregs, dvangs mas tshims nas lus thams cad bde ba chen po'i ye shes kyi bdud rtsis gang zhing, sdig sgrib nyes ltung thams cad dag par mos shing
gru.english: Hold this now in your right hand, and take out some of the liquid with the thumb and ring finger of your left hand.  As you say the three holy letters, draw a dharma star on the palm of your right hand, going around to the left as you make the lines.  The top corner of the star should be facing you, and imagine that the letter om is on the corner towards you; the ah is to the right; and the hung is to the left. Now pick up the liquid from the center of the star, with a strong feeling that you are taking up the very essence of wisdom which is made of bliss and emptiness inseparably combined, appearing in the form of nectar.  See yourself as the Angel, and touch the nectar to Your tongue. The nectar comes down and melts into the vam letter.  It burns away all the dregs inside, and fills you with refined essence.  Try to feel strongly that you are satiated with nectar of the wisdom of great bliss, and that all your bad deeds and obscurations, all the wrongful acts and downfalls you have committed against your vows and pledges, are completely cleaned away.

gru.acip: NANG MCHOD KYI SGRUB GZHI SOGS MED NA LAG GA YAS PA'I MTHIL DU DE LTAR BRIS PA'I DBUS NAS BDUD RTZI'I SNYING PO BLANGS TE MYANG BAR BSAM DGOS,
gru.wylie: nang mchod kyi sgrub gzhi sogs med na lag ga yas pa'i mthil du de ltar bris pa'i dbus nas bdud rtsi'i snying po blangs te myang bar bsam dgos
gru.english: If you don't have the necessary ingredients or whatever to make the inner offering, then you should draw the figure in the palm of your right hand as described above.  Imagine that you are taking up the essence of the nectar from the center, and partake of it.

gru.acip: 'OD DANG BDUD RTZI'I DANGS MA RNAMS SNYING GA'I BAm YIG LA THIM PAS BYIN GYIS BRLABS TE SNGAR BAS KYANG 'OD DANG GZI BRJID CHE BAR GYUR PAS BDE STONG SKYES PAR BSAM LA, RGYAN LDAN PHYAG MTSAN MED PA'I RNAM PAR LANGS PAR MOS PA NI SPRUL SKU 'GRUB PA'I SMIN BYED DO,
gru.wylie: 'od dang bdud rtsi'i dangs ma rnams snying ga'i baM yig la thim pas byin gyis brlabs te sngar bas kyang 'od dang gzi brjid che bar gyur pas bde stong skyes par bsam la, rgyan ldan phyag mtshan med pa'i rnam par langs par mos pa ni sprul sku 'grub pa'i smin byed do
gru.english: Picture then that the light, carrying with it the very essence of nectar, sinks into the vam letter at your heart, blessing your being.  The light then blazes up more glorious than before, triggering within you bliss and voidness.  As you get out of bed then, see yourself rising in Her form, complete with Her ornaments, but without Her instruments. All of this is meant to act as a seed that ripens into your reaching the enlightened body of emanation. Yoga Three: The Practice of Taking the Nectar

gru.acip: NYAL LUGS PHYI MA LTAR BYED NA STONG NYID KYI NGANG LA NYAL BA THUGS KYI DAG PA STE 'CHI BA SBYONG, LHA SKUR LDANG BA SKU DAG PA STE SKYE BA SBYONG, BDUD RTZI MYANG BA 'OD DPAG MED GSUNG GI DAG PA STE LONGS SKU 'GRUB PA'I SMIN BYED DANG, 'DI'I DAG PA SBYOR TSUL SHIN TU LEGS TE 'OD GSAL DE LAS GZUGS SKUR BZHENGS TE, BZLAS BRJOD SOGS BYED PAS SO,,
gru.wylie: nyal lugs phyi ma ltar byed na stong nyid kyi ngang la nyal ba thugs kyi dag pa ste 'chi ba sbyong, lha skur ldang ba sku dag pa ste skye ba sbyong, bdud rtsi myang ba 'od dpag med gsung gi dag pa ste longs sku 'grub pa'i smin byed dang, 'di'i dag pa sbyor tshul shin tu legs te 'od gsal de las gzugs skur bzhengs te, bzlas brjod sogs byed pas so
gru.english: Sleeping in the latter of the two ways--that is, dropping off to sleep within the void--is also the purity of Her holy mind, and acts to transform the state of death.  Getting out of bed in Her sacred form is the purity of Her holy body, and functions to transform the state of rebirth. Partaking of the nectar is the purity of the sacred speech of Limitless Light, and serves to ripen our minds for achieving the body of paradise.  This way of explaining what the three purities refer to is a very fine one, since we should be getting up out of a state of the clear light, rising in the holy body of an enlightened form, and then undertaking our various practices, such as recitation. The Categories of Practice

gru.acip: DE'I DON TSAR CHEN GYIS, DAL 'BYOR GRU CHEN SOGS SHO LO KA GCIG GSUNGS TE,
gru.wylie: de'i don tshar chen gyis, dal 'byor gru chen sogs sho lo ka gcig gsungs te
gru.english: The gist of these steps of the path is expressed by Tsarchen the Great in the single Tibetan verse which mentions "The good ship of leisure and fortune . . ." [Translators' note: The complete verse goes like this--

whole_word_matches.context: de'i don tshar chen gyis, dal 'byor gru chen sogs sho lo ka gcig gsungs te

gru.acip: ,DAL 'BYOR GRU CHEN MI RTAG DRAN PA YI, ,BA DAN DKAR PO BSKYOD PA LAS 'BRAS KYI, ,BLANG DOR MTHUN PA'I RLUNG GIS RAB BSKUL NAS, ,'JIGS RUNG 'KHOR BA'I MTSO LAS SGROL BAR SHOG,
gru.wylie: dal 'byor gru chen mi rtag dran pa yi, ,ba dan dkar po bskyod pa las 'bras kyi, ,blang dor mthun pa'i rlung gis rab bskul nas, ,'jigs rung 'khor ba'i mtsho las sgrol bar shog
gru.english: And by the power Of this deed May I board the good ship Of spiritual leisure and fortune; May I set the white sails Of constantly remembering My own impermanence, And thus see the ship stir forth; May the fair winds Of my careful observation Of the laws of karma And its consequences Then fill the sails And drive us all Across the terror of this sea, The cycle of pain we live in.]

whole_word_matches.context: dal 'byor gru chen mi rtag dran pa yi, ,ba dan dkar po bskyod pa las

gru.acip: DAL 'BYOR GYI LUS RTEN RNYED DKA' BA RGYA MTSO'I GRU CHEN PO LTA BU 'DI MI RTAG PAR MYUR DU 'JIG PA NA, DGE BA'I PHYOGS KYI BA DAN DKAR PO DE LAS 'BRAS BLANG DOR MTHUN PHYOGS KYI RLUNG GIS RAB TU BSKUL NAS 'JIGS RUNG RGYA MTSO LTA BU'I 'KHOR BA NYES DMIGS CAN 'DI LAS SGROL BAR SHOG CIG
gru.wylie: dal 'byor gyi lus rten rnyed dka' ba rgya mtsho'i gru chen po lta bu 'di mi rtag par myur du 'jig pa na, dge ba'i phyogs kyi ba dan dkar po de las 'bras blang dor mthun phyogs kyi rlung gis rab tu bskul nas 'jigs rung rgya mtsho lta bu'i 'khor ba nyes dmigs can 'di las sgrol bar shog cig
gru.english: A body and mind of leisure and fortune are difficult to find; they are like a great ship upon the sea.  This ship is impermanent, and will quickly be destroyed.  And so we must see that the fair winds of our careful observation of the laws of karma and its consequences fill the white sails we have set--the sails of goodness--and thus drive us all across the terror of the cycle of pain we live in, which is so much like a vast sea: a cycle of life with all these many problems.

whole_word_matches.context: dal 'byor gyi lus rten rnyed dka' ba rgya mtsho'i gru chen po lta bu 'di mi rtag par myur du 'jig pa na, dge

gru.acip: RANG GZHAN SEMS CAN THAMS CAD KYIS KHA TZAM TSIG TZAM MA YIN PAR SNYING KHONG RUS PA'I GTING NAS SKYABS SU 'GRO DGOS TE BLO RTZE GNYIS KYIS DON MI 'GRUB PA DANG, RKANG PA YAR MAR BOR BA DANG RTA GNYIS LA ZHON NAS 'DOD SAR MI PHYIN PA'I BLO LING SKYUR GYIS MGRIN GCIG TU,
gru.wylie: rang gzhan sems can thams cad kyis kha tsam tshig tsam ma yin par snying khong rus pa'i gting nas skyabs su 'gro dgos te blo rtse gnyis kyis don mi 'grub pa dang, rkang pa yar mar bor ba dang rta gnyis la zhon nas 'dod sar mi phyin pa'i blo ling skyur gyis mgrin gcig tu
gru.english: We ourselves, and all these other living beings, go for shelter then; not just in our words, but from the very core of our hearts.  If our minds are beset by doubts about what we should do, we will never be able to achieve our goals.  We can never reach our destination if we just stand in one place shuffling around our feet, or if we try to ride on the backs of two horses at once.

gru.acip: MDUN DANG GA-YAS KYI SANGS RGYAS RNAMS KYIS SKYABS STON PA MDZAD DU GSOL SNYAM DU RDZOGS PA'I ZHES SOGS BRJOD, RGYAB DANG SKYABS YUL RNAMS KYI THUGS RGYUD LA MNGA' BA'I RTOGS PA'I CHOS RNAMS KYIS SKYABS DNGOS MDZAD DU GSOL SNYAM DU DAM PA'I ZHES SOGS BRJOD, GA-YON DANG MTHA' SKOR DU BZHUGS PA'I DGE 'DUN DKON MCHOG RNAMS KYIS SKYABS SGRUB PA'I GROGS MDZAD DU GSOL SNYAM DU, 'PHAGS PA'I ZHES SOGS BRJOD,
gru.wylie: mdun dang ga-yas kyi sangs rgyas rnams kyis skyabs ston pa mdzad du gsol snyam du rdzogs pa'i zhes sogs brjod, rgyab dang skyabs yul rnams kyi thugs rgyud la mnga' ba'i rtogs pa'i chos rnams kyis skyabs dngos mdzad du gsol snyam du dam pa'i zhes sogs brjod, ga-yon dang mtha' skor du bzhugs pa'i dge 'dun dkon mchog rnams kyis skyabs sgrub pa'i grogs mdzad du gsol snyam du, 'phags pa'i zhes sogs brjod
gru.english: As you recite the lines that include the word "full" enlightenment, think that you are asking the Buddhas on the front petal, and on the one to your Lama's right, to please teach you about protection. As you recite the lines that include "holy" Dharma, think that you are asking for actual protection from the books on the back petal, as well as from the Dharma realizations in the hearts of all the places of refuge. And when you recite the lines that include "persons who are realized," think that you are asking the Jewel of the Community on the left petal, as well as all the other Community surrounding the flower, to please assist you in your search for protection.

gru.acip: GRUB NA BDUD RTZI 'BEBS SBYANGS LAM RIM LTAR BYAS LA SPANG GNYEN RO GCIG TU MA GYUR GYI BAR DU SKYABS SU 'GRO BA'O,
gru.wylie: grub na bdud rtsi 'bebs sbyangs lam rim ltar byas la spang gnyen ro gcig tu ma gyur gyi bar du skyabs su 'gro ba'o
gru.english: If you are able, then at this point you should do the practice of descent of nectar as taught in the books on the steps of the path.  You should keep up this practice of seeking shelter until the point where, for you, the bad qualities you need to eliminate and the antidotes that enable you to eliminate them combine in a single song. The Wish for Enlightenment

gru.acip: RANG SEMS LA BDE BA SKYES BDE BAS STONG PA NGES PA'I BDE STONG DBYER MED KYI NGANG LA CUNG ZAD MNYAM PAR 'JOG PA NI DON DAM PA'I SKYABS 'GRO YIN NO, DE LTAR STONG PAS CHOS SKU BDE BAS LONGS SKU, DE'I NGANG LAS SNANG YUL RANG LHAR GSAL BAS SPRUL SKU 'GRUB PA'I RGYUR ZHING, STONG NYID BSGOM PAS DON DAM SEMS BSKYED KYANG TSANG NGO,
gru.wylie: rang sems la bde ba skyes bde bas stong pa nges pa'i bde stong dbyer med kyi ngang la cung zad mnyam par 'jog pa ni don dam pa'i skyabs 'gro yin no, de ltar stong pas chos sku bde bas longs sku, de'i ngang las snang yul rang lhar gsal bas sprul sku 'grub pa'i rgyur zhing, stong nyid bsgom pas don dam sems bskyed kyang tshang ngo
gru.english: Bliss is triggered in your mind; stay here in meditation for a bit, in the realm of indivisible bliss and void, focused on emptiness itself.  This is what we call the "ultimate way of going for shelter." The emptiness here acts as a cause for achieving my dharma body; the bliss acts as a cause for attaining my enjoyment body; and seeing what appears to us in this state as the Angel, as myself, provides a cause for reaching my body of emanation.  And because we are meditating upon emptiness, the ultimate form of the Wish for enlightenment is also complete here.

gru.acip: 'DIR SGRUB THABS BSGOM PA'I SNGON 'GRO LA SKYABS 'GRO 'BYUNG BA NI, LAM LOG PA MU STEGS PA LAS KHYAD PAR DU BYED PA SKYABS 'GRO'I KHRID DU GSUNGS PAS 'DI PHYI NANG GI KHYAD PAR SKYABS 'GROS 'BYED PA'I LUGS YIN,
gru.wylie: 'dir sgrub thabs bsgom pa'i sngon 'gro la skyabs 'gro 'byung ba ni, lam log pa mu stegs pa las khyad par du byed pa skyabs 'gro'i khrid du gsungs pas 'di phyi nang gi khyad par skyabs 'gros 'byed pa'i lugs yin
gru.english: Why does taking refuge appear here as a preliminary, before you perform the rest of the ritual for reaching the Angel?  In the texts which explain the refuge practice, it is stated that this is what distinguishes this way from mistaken paths of non-Buddhist traditions.  Therefore refuge comes first in order to express the fact that it is this which separates a Buddhist from a non-Buddhist.

gru.acip: THAR PA'I PHAN YON LA SEMS 'DZIN PA'I DMIGS RNAM GOMS NAS NGES 'BYUNG LA MYONG BA MA BTON PAR SBYIN PA, TSUL KHRIMS, BZOD PA, BRTZON 'GRUS, BSAM GTAN GYI DGE RTZA GANG GOMS KYANG THAR PA'I RGYUR GTAN NAS MI 'GRO BAS THAR 'DOD KYIS THOG MAR GDAMS NGAG GANG ZAB ZER BA GZHAN THAMS CAD BZHAG NAS NGES 'BYUNG LA RTOG BSGOM BYA DGOS,
gru.wylie: thar pa'i phan yon la sems 'dzin pa'i dmigs rnam goms nas nges 'byung la myong ba ma bton par sbyin pa, tshul khrims, bzod pa, brtson 'grus, bsam gtan gyi dge rtsa gang goms kyang thar pa'i rgyur gtan nas mi 'gro bas thar 'dod kyis thog mar gdams ngag gang zab zer ba gzhan thams cad bzhag nas nges 'byung la rtog bsgom bya dgos
gru.english: If we fail to do this first, we can meditate on any great virtue at all--giving, morality, patience, effort, or meditative concentration--but there is no way at all that it will act as a cause for freedom. Therefore those who hope to reach freedom must first set aside all those other instructions, no matter how profound they are supposed to be, and do thinking meditation on renunciation.

gru.acip: THEG CHEN SGRUB PA POS RANG DON YID BYED KYI SKYON DANG, GZHAN DON GYI PHAN YON LA DRAN SHES THUN RE BSTEN NAS SEMS BSKYED LA MYONG BA 'DON PA'I DMIGS RNAM NAS GOMS PAR MA BYAS NA GZHAN GANG BYAS KYANG LAM DU MI 'GYUR TE, GZHAN DU NA DGE RTZA RNAMS RANG DON YID BYED KYIS DBANG BYAS NAS DMAN PA'I BYANG CHUB KYI RGYU 'BA' ZHIG TU 'GYUR BA'I PHYIR TE,
gru.wylie: theg chen sgrub pa pos rang don yid byed kyi skyon dang, gzhan don gyi phan yon la dran shes thun re bsten nas sems bskyed la myong ba 'don pa'i dmigs rnam nas goms par ma byas na gzhan gang byas kyang lam du mi 'gyur te, gzhan du na dge rtsa rnams rang don yid byed kyis dbang byas nas dman pa'i byang chub kyi rgyu 'ba' zhig tu 'gyur ba'i phyir te
gru.english: Persons who are trying to practice the greater way should bring to mind again and again that state of recollection in which we remember all the problems of paying attention to our own needs, and all the benefits of paying attention to the needs of others.  They should habituate themselves to these ideas, which will bring out in them a fluency in the Wish. If we fail to do this first, then it doesn't matter which of the other things we do, it won't become a path.  This is because if we act the other way, if we let all our virtues fall under the influence of paying attention to our own needs, then any good we do can only act as a cause for a lower enlightenment.

gru.acip: DES NA NANG PA SANGS RGYAS PA'I SANGS RGYAS NI SKYABS STON PA PO SMAN PA MKHAS PA DANG 'DRA, DES BSTAN PA'I CHOS NI SKYABS DNGOS SMAN DANG 'DRA, DGE 'DUN NI SKYABS DE SGRUB PA'I GROGS NAD GA YOG DANG 'DRA, RANG NYID NI CHAGS SOGS NYON MONGS PA'I NAD KYIS ZIN PA'I NAD PA DANG 'DRA BAS,
gru.wylie: des na nang pa sangs rgyas pa'i sangs rgyas ni skyabs ston pa po sman pa mkhas pa dang 'dra, des bstan pa'i chos ni skyabs dngos sman dang 'dra, dge 'dun ni skyabs de sgrub pa'i grogs nad ga yog dang 'dra, rang nyid ni chags sogs nyon mongs pa'i nad kyis zin pa'i nad pa dang 'dra bas
gru.english: And so the Buddha of the Buddhist faith is a Teacher of refuge, which makes Him like a master physician.  The Dharma that He teaches is the actual refuge, and so resembles the medicine.  The community of monks help us reach this refuge, and they are similar then to nurses.  I have caught the disease of attachment and the other mental afflictions, so I am like the patient.

gru.acip: ('DI SGRUB THABS SOGS DANG MI MTHUN KYANG ZIN THOR GZHI MED KYI NOR BA CHE BA 'OD DON MED CING RANG BZO YANG MED PAS MAN NGAG GI GNAD JI YIN DPYAD MDZOD,)
gru.wylie: ('di sgrub thabs sogs dang mi mthun kyang zin thor gzhi med kyi nor ba che ba 'od don med cing rang bzo yang med pas man ngag gi gnad ji yin dpyad mdzod,)
gru.english: (Note by the editor of the original Tibetan text: This description doesn't match the ones found in the ritual of reaching the Angel or the other texts, but it doesn't mean that there is some fatal flaw in these notes, nor have I myself just made it up.  It must represent some deep point in the instructions of our Lama, and I leave it to you to figure out what that is.)

gru.acip: PADMA'I MTHAR DUR BDAG GIS GTZOS PA'I BKA' SDOD RNAMS KYIS BSKOR BA BSAM, RGYAS PA 'DI DMIGS PA 'CHAR BDE ZHING, SGRUB THABS 'DI'I CHO GA'I GZHUNG DU GSAL BA'ANG RGYAS PA'I LUGS YIN,
gru.wylie: padma'i mthar dur bdag gis gtsos pa'i bka' sdod rnams kyis bskor ba bsam, rgyas pa 'di dmigs pa 'char bde zhing, sgrub thabs 'di'i cho ga'i gzhung du gsal ba'ang rgyas pa'i lugs yin
gru.english: At the outer edges of the lotus, picture the Protectors of the Word, with the Lord of the Burial Ground at their head.  This version of the extensive visualization is easy to see in your mind; the visualization that appears in the recitation text for this ritual of reaching the Angel also represents the extensive one.

gru.acip: DE LAS THAR BA'I THABS DA LTA RANG NYID KYIS BSGRUB PA BYAR YOD PAS SEMS CAN THAMS CAD BDE BA THAMS CAD DANG LDAN, SDUG BSNGAL THAMS CAD LAS THAR BA ZHIG NGA RANG GCIG PUS BYED DGOS PA 'DUG ,'ON KYANG DA LTA RANG YANG 'KHOR BA'I SDUG BSNGAL GYIS MNAR BZHIN PA 'DI 'DRAS SEMS CAN GYI DON BYED MI NUS PA 'DUG PAS SHA GZUG RANG ZA'I TSUL GYIS SNGON DU BDAG GIS SANGS RGYAS KYI GO 'PHANG DUS MYUR BA NYID DU THOB PA ZHIG CI NAS KYANG BYA'O,
gru.wylie: de las thar ba'i thabs da lta rang nyid kyis bsgrub pa byar yod pas sems can thams cad bde ba thams cad dang ldan, sdug bsngal thams cad las thar ba zhig nga rang gcig pus byed dgos pa 'dug ,'on kyang da lta rang yang 'khor ba'i sdug bsngal gyis mnar bzhin pa 'di 'dras sems can gyi don byed mi nus pa 'dug pas sha gzug rang za'i tshul gyis sngon du bdag gis sangs rgyas kyi go 'phang dus myur ba nyid du thob pa zhig ci nas kyang bya'o
gru.english: The way to free them is something I have in my hands now, to achieve.  Seeing that every living being has every kind of happiness, and that they escape every kind of pain, is something that I have to do, and I have to do it by myself. But right now the fact is that I don't have any power to help all these beings; I'm being tormented by all the sufferings of cyclic life the same way they are.  So I have do like the story of the quarter of meat; I have to eat it myself, I have to achieve the state of a Buddha first myself, immediately, no matter what.

gru.acip: RDZOGS PA'I BYANG CHUB KYI BDE BA LA 'GOD PAR BYA ZHES BAS BDE BA DANG LDAN 'DOD KYI BYAMS PA TSAD MED, SEMS CAN THAMS CAD SANGS RGYAS KYI GO 'PHANG THOB NA RANG GI 'DOD DON MTHAR THUG GRUB PAS DGA' BA TSAD MED YIN, TSAD MED BZHI BSGOM PA SPYI LTAR BTON KYANG CHOG ,
gru.wylie: rdzogs pa'i byang chub kyi bde ba la 'god par bya zhes bas bde ba dang ldan 'dod kyi byams pa tshad med, sems can thams cad sangs rgyas kyi go 'phang thob na rang gi 'dod don mthar thug grub pas dga' ba tshad med yin, tshad med bzhi bsgom pa spyi ltar bton kyang chog
gru.english: The words "lead them finally to the bliss of total enlightenment" stand for the limitless prayer of love, the kind of love that wants beings to get every kind of happiness.  If every living being actually did reach the state of Buddhahood, then our own ultimate hope would be achieved, and this is the limitless prayer of joy.  It's also all right at this point if you do your meditation on these four attitudes by reciting the limitless prayers the way we usually do them in our other rituals.

gru.acip: DE LA BDUD RTZI MYANG BA ZIN NAS MDUN GYI NAM MKHAR SKYABS YUL GSAL BTAB LA, SKYABS 'GRO'I SKABS 'DIR DE'I RGYU GNYIS TSANG BA'I SGO NAS SKYABS 'GRO GANG 'GRUB 'DON, GZHAN RNAMS LA SEMS 'DZIN GYIS SKYABS SEMS BYED PA LA NAN TAN DU 'BAD DGOS TSUL SOGS SEMS 'DZIN SKOR MDOR BSDUS GSUNGS,
gru.wylie: de la bdud rtsi myang ba zin nas mdun gyi nam mkhar skyabs yul gsal btab la, skyabs 'gro'i skabs 'dir de'i rgyu gnyis tshang ba'i sgo nas skyabs 'gro gang 'grub 'don, gzhan rnams la sems 'dzin gyis skyabs sems byed pa la nan tan du 'bad dgos tshul sogs sems 'dzin skor mdor bsdus gsungs
gru.english: Now it is true that from the time you did the practice of partaking the nectar you have been visualizing the places of refuge; the difference here at the point of taking refuge is that you recite a full complement of the refuge practice, complete with the two reasons for doing it. Our Lama then spoke a bit about the practice of holding the mind, and other topics; describing how even at the other points in the recitation we had to use holding the mind to make persistent efforts at keeping up this prayer of going for refuge and developing the Wish.

gru.acip: NGES NGOR CHOS THAMS CAD RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA RDUL TZAM YANG MED BA'I LTA BA GANG SHES BSGOM PA YUL STONG PA NYID DANG,
gru.wylie: nges ngor chos thams cad rang bzhin gyis grub pa rdul tsam yang med ba'i lta ba gang shes bsgom pa yul stong pa nyid dang
gru.english: The object that your perceptions grasp is emptiness, the fact that no thing in the universe has a single atom of natural existence: the object of correct view as you meditate on it at this point, which is only to the extent that you understand it so far.

gru.acip: NANG SKYES BU'I RGYUD KYIS BSDUS PA'I RDZAS BDUD RTZI LNGA SOGS LA SGRUB GZHI BYAS NAS PHUL BAS NA NANG MCHOD CES ZER, NANG MCHOD LA SGRUB GZHI NGES PAR DGOS PA GRUB MTHA' GZHAN PHYOGS PA PHAL CHER GYIS CHANG DANG AA RAG LA BYED KYANG RANG LUGS RJE'I BKA' SROL 'DIR 'DUL BA'I BCAS KHRIMS LA DGONGS TE SGRUB GZHI CHANG RAG MIN BAR JA KHU LA MDZAD PAS DE LTAR BYA DGOS,
gru.wylie: nang skyes bu'i rgyud kyis bsdus pa'i rdzas bdud rtsi lnga sogs la sgrub gzhi byas nas phul bas na nang mchod ces zer, nang mchod la sgrub gzhi nges par dgos pa grub mtha' gzhan phyogs pa phal cher gyis chang dang aa rag la byed kyang rang lugs rje'i bka' srol 'dir 'dul ba'i bcas khrims la dgongs te sgrub gzhi chang rag min bar ja khu la mdzad pas de ltar bya dgos
gru.english: The name "inner offering" comes from the fact that you offer something you have created using substances, such as the five nectars, that are inner; that is, part of a person's body.  You need some ingredients to turn into the inner offering, and most other schools use beer or wine.  Our own position though, which follows the tradition of Je Rinpoche, takes into consideration the established rules of the teachings on vowed morality, and says to use concentrate of tea, rather than beer or wine.  This then is the way you should do it.

gru.acip: SGRUB GZHI MA 'DZOMS KYANG MOS PA NAN TAN BYA DGOS,
gru.wylie: sgrub gzhi ma 'dzoms kyang mos pa nan tan bya dgos
gru.english: Even if you can't get together the ingredients needed to turn into the inner offering, you must at least imagine strongly that they are all there.

gru.acip: DE YANG RANG GI SNYING KHAR CHOS 'BYUNG NYIS BRTZEGS NANG ZLA DKYIL DBUS SU BAm YIG DANG MTHA' SKOR DU KHAndA RO HI'I SNGAGS PHRENG DMAR POS BSKOR BA'I BAm YIG GI N'A DA LAS KHAndA RO HE'AM DU MA SKYES MA PHYAG GA YAS GNYIS GRI GUG DANG d'A MA RU, GA YON GNYIS THOD PA DANG KHA tVAm GA 'DZIN PA DPAG MED SPROS TE NANG MCHOD KYI SGRUB GZHI LA GNAS PA'I BGEGS RNAMS BSKRAD SONG SNYAM PA'I MOS PA DANG BCAS KHAndA RO HI'I SNGAGS BRJOD DE NANG MCHOD KYI KHEBS BSAL, NANG MCHOD BYIN RLABS DANG PO 'DI'I SKABS BRDA MTSON TZAM DU KHA CHOD PHYE BA TZAM LAS 'THOR BA MI DGOS,
gru.wylie: de yang rang gi snying khar chos 'byung nyis brtsegs nang zla dkyil dbus su baM yig dang mtha' skor du khaNDa ro hi'i sngags phreng dmar pos bskor ba'i baM yig gi nA da las khaNDa ro he'am du ma skyes ma phyag ga yas gnyis gri gug dang DA ma ru, ga yon gnyis thod pa dang kha TvaM ga 'dzin pa dpag med spros te nang mchod kyi sgrub gzhi la gnas pa'i bgegs rnams bskrad song snyam pa'i mos pa dang bcas khaNDa ro hi'i sngags brjod de nang mchod kyi khebs bsal, nang mchod byin rlabs dang po 'di'i skabs brda mtshon tsam du kha chod phye ba tsam las 'thor ba mi dgos
gru.english: So now picture the dharma star, made of two triangular sections stacked together, at your heart.  Inside it is a moondisk, and in the center of that is the letter bam, surrounded by a string of red letters, the secret words of Kendarohi.  Imagine that from the crook on the bam letter you send forth an uncountable number of this Angel Kendarohi, otherwise known as the Lady of Pieces.  In Their two right hands They hold a chopknife and a damaru hand-drum; in Their two left hands, a skullcup and kadamga staff. Try to get a strong feeling that now They have really driven away all the hindrances that were staying around the ingredients for creating the inner offering.  Keep this feeling and recite the secret words of Kendarohi, as you open the top to the inner offering.  At this point, when you first bless the inner offering, opening the top is just symbolic, and you needn't spray the liquid; just crack open the lid.

gru.acip: DE LA SBYANG BYA MA DAG PA THA MAL GYI SNANG ZHEN DANG, BDEN GRUB TU SNANG BA'I SNANG ZHEN GNYIS YOD PAS DE GNYIS KA SBYANG,
gru.wylie: de la sbyang bya ma dag pa tha mal gyi snang zhen dang, bden grub tu snang ba'i snang zhen gnyis yod pas de gnyis ka sbyang
gru.english: Here there are two things that the offering could be made pure of, and you have to purify it of both.  They are the tendency to see things as everyday, and the tendency to see things as existing truly.

gru.acip: 'DI'I SKABS NGA RGYAL 'JOG LUGS SNANG NGOR NANG MCHOD KYI SGRUB GZHI SNOD DANG BCAS PA STONG PAR SBYANGS,
gru.wylie: 'di'i skabs nga rgyal 'jog lugs snang ngor nang mchod kyi sgrub gzhi snod dang bcas pa stong par sbyangs
gru.english: The way of directing your supreme confidence here is as follows.  What appears to your perceptions is the ingredients that will become the inner offering, along with the vessel that holds them, all purified into emptiness.

gru.acip: NGES NGOR CHOS THAMS CAD RANG BZHIN MED PA'I STONG NYID KYI LTA BA DRAN PAR BYAS NAS RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAS STONG PA'I YUL STONG SANG DE DANG, YUL STONG PA NYID RTOGS PA'I BLO YUL CAN BDE BA CHEN PO GNYIS LA NGA RGYAL BZHAG PA YIN,
gru.wylie: nges ngor chos thams cad rang bzhin med pa'i stong nyid kyi lta ba dran par byas nas rang bzhin gyis grub pas stong pa'i yul stong sang de dang, yul stong pa nyid rtogs pa'i blo yul can bde ba chen po gnyis la nga rgyal bzhag pa yin
gru.english: What your perceptions grasp is sheer emptiness, as an object of the mind, and which is empty of any natural existence.  It has come from your recollecting the view which sees that no existing thing has any nature of its own. And it is two things towards which you direct your supreme confidence, which you hold to be yourself: these are (1) mind as a subject, that is, the state of mind which perceives the object emptiness; and (2) great bliss.

gru.acip: SNANG NGOR STONG SANG BSGOM PA TZAM GYIS THA MAL GYI SNANG ZHEN SBYONG NUS KYANG BDEN ZHEN SBYONG MI NUS, SGRUB GZHI NANG MCHOD SOGS CHOS THAMS CAD NGES NGOR RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA RDUL TZAM YANG MED PA'I STONG NYID KYI LTA BA DRAN PAR BYAS NA BDEN ZHEN YANG SBYONG NUS,
gru.wylie: snang ngor stong sang bsgom pa tsam gyis tha mal gyi snang zhen sbyong nus kyang bden zhen sbyong mi nus, sgrub gzhi nang mchod sogs chos thams cad nges ngor rang bzhin gyis grub pa rdul tsam yang med pa'i stong nyid kyi lta ba dran par byas na bden zhen yang sbyong nus
gru.english: Just meditating on sheer emptiness as it appears to your perceptions is enough to purify yourself of the tendency to see things as everyday, but it is not enough to purify you of the tendency to see things as being true.  But if you can recollect the view which sees emptiness--if what your perceptions grasp is that the ingredients to become the inner offering, and every other existing entity, lack even a single atom of natural existence--then you can purify yourself of the tendency to see things as true as well.

gru.acip: KLU SGRUB KYIS, ,DGE BA 'DI YIS SKYE BO KUN, ,BSOD NAMS YE SHES TSOGS BSAGS SHING, ,BSOD NAMS YE SHES LAS BYUNG BA'I, ,DAM PA SKU GNYIS, ZHES DANG,
gru.wylie: klu sgrub kyis, ,dge ba 'di yis skye bo kun, ,bsod nams ye shes tshogs bsags shing, ,bsod nams ye shes las byung ba'i, ,dam pa sku gnyis, zhes dang
gru.english: Master Nagarjuna too has said, By this virtue may all beings Gather the masses of merit and wisdom. May they achieve the ultimate two That the merit and the wisdom produce.

gru.acip: GSUM PA BSKYED PA NI, STONG PA'I NGANG LAS NANG MCHOD KYI SGRUB GZHI 'OG MA RLUNG DKYIL GYI GO SAR, BDE STONG GI YE SHES LAS GRUB PA'I YI GE YAm NYAL STABS KHA RANG LA BSTAN PA LAS RLUNG DKYIL ZLA GAM GZHU BKANG BA'I DBYIBS LTA BU BCAD KHA'AM GZHU RGYUD RANG LA BSTAN PA, ZUR GA YAS GA YON GNYIS SU SNE MOR SROG CHAGS GSUM GYI MTSAN MAS MDZES PA'I RGYAL MTSAN DAR LCE GSUM PAS MTSAN PA,
gru.wylie: gsum pa bskyed pa ni, stong pa'i ngang las nang mchod kyi sgrub gzhi 'og ma rlung dkyil gyi go sar, bde stong gi ye shes las grub pa'i yi ge yaM nyal stabs kha rang la bstan pa las rlung dkyil zla gam gzhu bkang ba'i dbyibs lta bu bcad kha'am gzhu rgyud rang la bstan pa, zur ga yas ga yon gnyis su sne mor srog chags gsum gyi mtshan mas mdzes pa'i rgyal mtshan dar lce gsum pas mtshan pa
gru.english: We have now reached the third step in the practice of the inner offering, which is producing it.  Picture that, out of a state of emptiness, a disk of wind appears below the ingredients to be made into the inner offering.  In the place where the disk is then comes a letter yam, which consists of the wisdom of bliss and emptiness. The letter is horizontal, with its head facing you.  It then takes the shape of a half moon, or a bow which is strung and bent.  The side of the moon that is cut off, which would correspond to the straight bowstring, again has its face to you.  On the corners to the right and left--at the two tips of the half moon--stand victory banners; they are adorned by insignia of three different animals, and consist of three pennants each.

gru.acip: DE STENG RAm DMAR PO NYAL STABS MGO RANG LA BSTAN PA YONGS SU GYUR PA LAS MED KYIL 'BAR BZHIN BA GRU GSUM DMAR PO ZUR GCIG RANG LA BSTAN PA GZHU RGYUD YOD SA'I BCAD KHA DANG KHAD CHAD PA, ZUR GNYIS PHYIR BSTAN PA RLUNG DKYIL GYI ZLUM SKOR DANG KHAD CHAD PA,
gru.wylie: de steng raM dmar po nyal stabs mgo rang la bstan pa yongs su gyur pa las med kyil 'bar bzhin ba gru gsum dmar po zur gcig rang la bstan pa gzhu rgyud yod sa'i bcad kha dang khad chad pa, zur gnyis phyir bstan pa rlung dkyil gyi zlum skor dang khad chad pa
gru.english: Above all this picture a red letter ram; it lies horizontally with its head facing you.  This letter transforms into a flat mass of fire, blazing in flame, and red.  The fire is triangular, and one corner points towards you, breaking the line of the straight edge of the bow shape.  The two outside corners of the triangle break the line of the curved part of the flat mass of wind.

whole_word_matches.context: a bstan pa yongs su gyur pa las med kyil 'bar bzhin ba gru gsum dmar po zur gcig rang la bstan pa gzhu rgyud yod

gru.acip: DE BZHIN THOD PA'I RNA LTAG GA YON PHYOGS BYANG DU BYA GRUB YE SHES KYI NGO BO DON YONG GRUB PA'I SA BON KHAm LJANG GU LAS SHA CHEN DKAR PO KHAm GIS MTSAN PA,
gru.wylie: de bzhin thod pa'i rna ltag ga yon phyogs byang du bya grub ye shes kyi ngo bo don yong grub pa'i sa bon khaM ljang gu las sha chen dkar po khaM gis mtshan pa
gru.english: In the same way now picture a green letter kham.  This is the seed syllable for Attaining, and its essence is the wisdom that accomplishes.  It is positioned to the skull's left, on its north side, at the side where one ear used to be.  From this letter comes the nectar of great flesh; it is white, and marked with a kham letter.

gru.acip: MCHOD PA DANG, TSOGS 'KHOR, GSER SKYEMS SOGS THAMS CAD LA BYIN RLABS 'DI BZHIN BYA DGOS, RGYAS PAR NA GRUB RGYAL LUGS KYI TSE YAR BA 'GUGS PA, NYAMS PA GSO BA SOGS TSE 'GUGS BSTIM GYI DMIGS PA THAMS CAD NANG MCHOD BYIN RLABS 'DI LA SBYAR CHOG PA BLA MA'I GSUNG RGYUN YIN,
gru.wylie: mchod pa dang, tshogs 'khor, gser skyems sogs thams cad la byin rlabs 'di bzhin bya dgos, rgyas par na grub rgyal lugs kyi tshe yar ba 'gugs pa, nyams pa gso ba sogs tshe 'gugs bstim gyi dmigs pa thams cad nang mchod byin rlabs 'di la sbyar chog pa bla ma'i gsung rgyun yin
gru.english: You should perform the rite of blessing this way whenever you make offerings, or when you perform the gathering for offering, the ritual of the golden drink, and so on.  If you wish to perform an even more extensive blessing rite, it is the oral tradition of the Lamas of our lineage that you may add to this version all the details of bringing in extra life that are found in the system of Drupgyal, or else those of bringing in and adding life that are found in rituals such as restoration.

gru.acip: RDO RJE 'CHANG GIS RGYUD NAS GSUNGS PA'I BCUD LEN KYANG 'DI NYID YIN ZHING, BDUD RTZI RIL BU SGRUB BYED KYANG, 'BRU GSUM GYI BZLAS GRANGS GSOG PA LAS GZHAN DMIGS PA DANG CHO GA NANG MCHOD BYIN RLABS 'DI LAS LOGS SU MED PAS 'DI'I RNAM GZHAG LA LEGS PAR BYANG PA BYED BA GNAD CHE,
gru.wylie: rdo rje 'chang gis rgyud nas gsungs pa'i bcud len kyang 'di nyid yin zhing, bdud rtsi ril bu sgrub byed kyang, 'bru gsum gyi bzlas grangs gsog pa las gzhan dmigs pa dang cho ga nang mchod byin rlabs 'di las logs su med pas 'di'i rnam gzhag la legs par byang pa byed ba gnad che
gru.english: The practice of taking essence which has come down through the Holder of the Diamond is this very rite.  And when you perform the creation of the nectar pills, there is no other visualization or ritual (except for the part about accumulating recitations of the three holy letters) apart from this rite of blessing.  Therefore it is of critical importance that you become well versed in the entire subject of this rite.

gru.acip: RDZAS BCUS SGRUB PA PO'I PHUNG KHAMS SKYE MCHED SBYANGS NAS DPE DON GYI 'OD GSAL DU ZHUGS PA MTSON, NYI MA 'CHAR KA'I MDOG LTAR DMAR SER DANG REG BYA TSA BAR GYUR PAS PHUNG KHAMS SKYE MCHED DPE DON GYI 'OD GSAL DU BCUG NAS SBYANGS PA MTSON,
gru.wylie: rdzas bcus sgrub pa po'i phung khams skye mched sbyangs nas dpe don gyi 'od gsal du zhugs pa mtshon, nyi ma 'char ka'i mdog ltar dmar ser dang reg bya tsha bar gyur pas phung khams skye mched dpe don gyi 'od gsal du bcug nas sbyangs pa mtshon
gru.english: The ten substances in the cup symbolize the secret practitioner's purifying their heaps, categories, and gateways, and then entering the approximate and actual clear lights.  Being golden red like the sky just before the sun comes up, and being hot to the touch, represent the purification of one's own heaps, categories, and gateways after we have entered the approximate and actual clear lights.

gru.acip: DE NAS BSANG SBYANG SNGAR LTAR LA, MCHOD PA'I SGRUB GZHI SNOD BCAS STONG PAR SBYANGS, SGRUB GZHI RGYAB LTA BUR YOD KYANG BSANG SBYANG SKABS SGRUB GZHI YOD SA DER DMIGS, BSKYED PA NA RANG GI MDUN DU BSKYED DGOS,
gru.wylie: de nas bsang sbyang sngar ltar la, mchod pa'i sgrub gzhi snod bcas stong par sbyangs, sgrub gzhi rgyab lta bur yod kyang bsang sbyang skabs sgrub gzhi yod sa der dmigs, bskyed pa na rang gi mdun du bskyed dgos
gru.english: Now do the clearing and purifying as before; this time what is purified into emptiness is the materials to be made into the offering, along with the containers holding them.  When you do the actual clearing and purifying, you should focus to wherever these materials are--even if, for example, they should be in back of you.  When you do the production of the offering, you should do so in front of you.

gru.acip: MING YIG DANG POS MING TZAM BRDA TZAM, RTOG PAS PHAR BTAGS TZAM GYI SNANG BA RTEN 'BYUNG DANG, THIG LES NI RANG BZHIN GYIS MA GRUB PA'I STONG PA MTSON PA RTZIS KYI SKABS STONG PA'I GNAS SU THIG CES THIG LE BRI BA DANG 'DRA,
gru.wylie: ming yig dang pos ming tsam brda tsam, rtog pas phar btags tsam gyi snang ba rten 'byung dang, thig les ni rang bzhin gyis ma grub pa'i stong pa mtshon pa rtsis kyi skabs stong pa'i gnas su thig ces thig le bri ba dang 'dra
gru.english: Using the first letter of the word signifies interdependence, or what we call "appearances": the fact that things are just names, just words, just labeled with our ideas.  The dot represents emptiness, the fact that nothing exists naturally; it's like in astrological calculations, where it says "a dot for nothing," meaning that you should write a dot for zero.

gru.acip: DE'I STENG GI DKYIL DU RAm RIG DMAR PO ZHIG BYUNG BA 'OD DU ZHU BA LAS ME DKYIL DMAR PO GRU GSUM PA ZUR CIG RANG LA BSTAN PA MTHA' KUN TU ME LHAB LHAB 'BAR BZHIN PA, DE'I ZUR RER RANG GI MDUN NAS BRTZAMS TE GA-YON SKOR GYIS A'A: DKAR DMAR MTHING GSUM LAS MI MGO BCAD MA THAG PA SKRA SBAD LING CAN SO SKYA TSIG GE BA DKAR DMAR MTHING GSUM GYI LTAG PA NANG BSTAN,
gru.wylie: de'i steng gi dkyil du raM rig dmar po zhig byung ba 'od du zhu ba las me dkyil dmar po gru gsum pa zur cig rang la bstan pa mtha' kun tu me lhab lhab 'bar bzhin pa, de'i zur rer rang gi mdun nas brtsams te ga-yon skor gyis a'a: dkar dmar mthing gsum las mi mgo bcad ma thag pa skra sbad ling can so skya tshig ge ba dkar dmar mthing gsum gyi ltag pa nang bstan
gru.english: On top of the wind disk, in its center, a red ram syllable appears.  It melts into light and becomes a flat mass of fire, shaped like a triangle, with one point facing towards you.  It is sending out a torrent of blazing flames on all sides.  At each of the triangle's points, beginning with the point in front of you to the left, are three ah letters, colored white, red, and blue.  Each letter turns into a freshly-severed human head (also colored white, red, and blue) with disshelved hair, and baring teeth, with their faces pointing out.

whole_word_matches.context: ar po zhig byung ba 'od du zhu ba las me dkyil dmar po gru gsum pa zur cig rang la bstan pa mtha' kun tu me lhab

gru.acip: THOD PA'I SKAD DOD KA P'A LA ZHES 'BYUNG LA, DE'I MING YIG DANG PO THIG LES BRGYAN PA NI MCHOD RDZAS SOGS, MING DANG BRDA DANG RTOG PAS BTAGS TZAM LAS DON DAM PAR GRUB PA MED PA MTSON,
gru.wylie: thod pa'i skad dod ka pA la zhes 'byung la, de'i ming yig dang po thig les brgyan pa ni mchod rdzas sogs, ming dang brda dang rtog pas btags tsam las don dam par grub pa med pa mtshon
gru.english: The Sanskrit word for skullcup here is kapala; so if you take the first letter of this word and add to it the dot which stands for "m", it symbolizes that--ultimately speaking--the offering substances do not exist, but are just labeled by our own names and terms and mental images.

gru.acip: SARBA SIDDHI MME PRA YATZTSA DNGOS GRUB THAMS CAD BDAG LA RAB TU STZOL CIG ,SARBA KARMA SU TZA ME BDAG LA LAS THAMS CAD STZAL DU GSOL, TZITTAm SHR'I YAm KU RU SEMS KYI DPAL DU MDZOD CIG
gru.wylie: sarba siddhi mme pra yatstsha dngos grub thams cad bdag la rab tu stsol cig ,sarba karma su tsa me bdag la las thams cad stsal du gsol, tsittaM shrI yaM ku ru sems kyi dpal du mdzod cig
gru.english: Sarva siddhim me prayacha means "May You grant me freely every attainment."  Sarva karmasu cha me is "I ask You to grant me every activity."  Chittam shriyam kuru means "Make my mind shining."

gru.acip: 'BROM GYIS JO BO LA, NGED BOD 'DIR SGOM SGRUB BYED BA MANG PO YOD PA LA, YON TAN KHYAD PAR CAN BRNYES PA MI BDOG ZHUS PAR, JO BOS, THEG PA CHEN PO'I YON TAN CHE SKYES CHUNG SKYES THAMS CAD BLA MA LA BRTEN NAS SKYE BA LA, KHYED BOD BLA MA LA THA MAL PA'I 'DU SHES LAS MED, GA NA SKYE GSUNGS PA DANG,
gru.wylie: 'brom gyis jo bo la, nged bod 'dir sgom sgrub byed ba mang po yod pa la, yon tan khyad par can brnyes pa mi bdog zhus par, jo bos, theg pa chen po'i yon tan che skyes chung skyes thams cad bla ma la brten nas skye ba la, khyed bod bla ma la tha mal pa'i 'du shes las med, ga na skye gsungs pa dang
gru.english: Remember also the conversation between Dromton Je and Lord Atisha: And Drom said respectfully to the Lord, "Here in Tibet there are many who are trying to meditate and practice, but there are none who have attained any really  exceptional good qualities." The Lord replied, "In the greater way, the good qualities  a person might be able to develop--whether they are great or small--all come from their Lama.  The only way you Tibetans ever think about your Lamas is that they are  normal, everyday people.  So how could you ever develop high qualities?"

gru.acip: DBEN SA PAS, ,MDOR NA NYAMS RTOGS CHE CHUNG GANG SKYES KYANG, ,DAD PA CHE CHUNG BSGOMS PA'I MTHU YIN PAS, ,DNGOS GRUB RTZA BA DRIN CAN BLA MA YI, ,YON TAN BSAM ZHING SKYON NAS MI BLTA BA'I, ,GDAMS PA 'DI NYID MTHIL DU 'DZIN PAR SHOG ,DAM BCA' 'DI 'DRA GEGS MED MTHAR PHYIN SHOG CES GSUNGS,
gru.wylie: dben sa pas, ,mdor na nyams rtogs che chung gang skyes kyang, ,dad pa che chung bsgoms pa'i mthu yin pas, ,dngos grub rtsa ba drin can bla ma yi, ,yon tan bsam zhing skyon nas mi blta ba'i, ,gdams pa 'di nyid mthil du 'dzin par shog ,dam bca' 'di 'dra gegs med mthar phyin shog ces gsungs
gru.english: Master Wensapa described it as follows: In short, whether we develop greater or lesser Spiritual practice and realizations Depends on the force with which we meditate On faith that itself is greater or lesser. Think therefore on the good qualities Of your Lama of kindness, the root Of all attainments, and do not look For faults in Them. May I keep this one advice The center of my practice; May I bring this resolve Unhindered to its final end. [Translator's note: The Tibetan editor notes that the Tibetan for the next to the last line is not precisely the original form, which we find elsewhere as MTHIL DU 'DZIN PA DANG,.]

gru.acip: BLA MA LA SANGS RGYAS DNGOS SU MA BLTAS NA LEGS SKAR GYIS SANGS RGYAS LA MTHONG BA LTAR SKYON 'BA' ZHIG LAS MI MTHONG BAS RANG LA YON TAN 'BYUNG BA'I SKABS MED, DES NA RIGS PA YANG DAG GI SGO NAS BLA MA SANGS RGYAS SU BSGRUB DGOS,
gru.wylie: bla ma la sangs rgyas dngos su ma bltas na legs skar gyis sangs rgyas la mthong ba ltar skyon 'ba' zhig las mi mthong bas rang la yon tan 'byung ba'i skabs med, des na rigs pa yang dag gi sgo nas bla ma sangs rgyas su bsgrub dgos
gru.english: If you fail to look on your Lama as being the Buddha himself, you will end up seeing nothing in Them but faults, the way that Sunakshatra saw the Buddha.  This will totally disallow you from ever developing any high qualities.  Therefore you must use good logic and prove to yourself that your Lama is the Buddha.

gru.acip: DE SGRUB BYED LAM RIM GYI KHRID LAS BYUNG BA LTAR YANG YANG BSAMS TE MYONG BA 'DON PA GAL CHE,
gru.wylie: de sgrub byed lam rim gyi khrid las byung ba ltar yang yang bsams te myong ba 'don pa gal che
gru.english: The proofs for this are found in the teachings on the steps of the path to enlightenment, and it is vital that you contemplate these again and again, until you achieve some fluency in this thinking.

gru.acip: GRUB CHEN NAG PO SPYOD PA DANG, DGE TSUL TSEM BU PAS RDO RJE PHAG MO MDZE MOR MTHOR, GANGG'A'I GLING NAS RJE BTZUN KU S'A LI, ZHES SOGS LTAR DGE TSUL TSEM BU BA MKHA' SPYOD DU KHRID TSUL,
gru.wylie: grub chen nag po spyod pa dang, dge tshul tshem bu pas rdo rje phag mo mdze mor mthor, ganggA'i gling nas rje btsun ku sA li, zhes sogs ltar dge tshul tshem bu ba mkha' spyod du khrid tshul
gru.english: Our Lama related the story of the accomplished saint Krishna Acharya and the novice monk Tsembupa*, who saw the Diamond Sow as a woman leper.  The lines of the prayer say, "You came Yourself down to the land of the Ganges River, and led the venered Kusali."  And so She did; She actually took the novice Tsembupa off to Her heaven. [*Translator's note: This is the Tibetan for his name; the original Sanskrit is uncertain.]

gru.acip: DPAL MGON KLU SGRUB KYIS, ,MCHOD PA THAMS CAD RNAM SPANGS NAS, ,BLA MA LA MCHOD YANG DAG BRTZAMS, ,DE MNYES PAS NI KUN MKHYEN PA'I, ,YE SHES MCHOG ZHI THOB PAR 'GYUR, ,CES GSUNGS,
gru.wylie: dpal mgon klu sgrub kyis, ,mchod pa thams cad rnam spangs nas, ,bla ma la mchod yang dag brtsams, ,de mnyes pas ni kun mkhyen pa'i, ,ye shes mchog zhi thob par 'gyur, ,ces gsungs
gru.english: The glorious savior Nagarjuna has spoken as well, Give up all your other offerings; Make pure offerings to your Lama. If you please Them you will achieve The highest wisdom, omniscience, peace.

gru.acip: 'BROM GYIS JO BO LA, NGED BOD 'DIR SGOM SGRUB BYED BA MANG PO YOD PA LA, YON TAN KHYAD PAR CAN BRNYES PA MI BDOG ZHUS PAR, JO BOS, THEG PA CHEN PO'I YON TAN CHE SKYES CHUNG SKYES THAMS CAD BLA MA LA BRTEN NAS SKYE BA LA, KHYED BOD BLA MA LA THA MAL PA'I 'DU SHES LAS MED, GA NA SKYE GSUNGS PA DANG,
gru.wylie: 'brom gyis jo bo la, nged bod 'dir sgom sgrub byed ba mang po yod pa la, yon tan khyad par can brnyes pa mi bdog zhus par, jo bos, theg pa chen po'i yon tan che skyes chung skyes thams cad bla ma la brten nas skye ba la, khyed bod bla ma la tha mal pa'i 'du shes las med, ga na skye gsungs pa dang
gru.english: Remember also the conversation between Dromton Je and Lord Atisha: And Drom said respectfully to the Lord, "Here in Tibet there are many who are trying to meditate and practice, but there are none who have attained any really  exceptional good qualities." The Lord replied, "In the greater way, the good qualities a person might be able to develop--whether they are great or small--all come from their Lama.  The only way you Tibetans ever think about your Lamas is that they are normal, everyday people.  So how could you ever develop high qualities?"

gru.acip: DBEN SA PAS, ,MDOR NA NYAMS RTOGS CHE CHUNG GANG SKYES KYANG, ,DAD PA CHE CHUNG BSGOMS PA'I MTHU YIN PAS, ,DNGOS GRUB RTZA BA DRIN CAN BLA MA YI, ,YON TAN BSAM ZHING SKYON NAS MI BLTA BA'I, ,GDAMS PA 'DI NYID MTHIL DU 'DZIN PAR SHOG ,DAM BCA' 'DI 'DRA GEGS MED MTHAR PHYIN SHOG ,CES GSUNGS,
gru.wylie: dben sa pas, ,mdor na nyams rtogs che chung gang skyes kyang, ,dad pa che chung bsgoms pa'i mthu yin pas, ,dngos grub rtsa ba drin can bla ma yi, ,yon tan bsam zhing skyon nas mi blta ba'i, ,gdams pa 'di nyid mthil du 'dzin par shog ,dam bca' 'di 'dra gegs med mthar phyin shog ,ces gsungs
gru.english: Master Wensapa described it as follows: In short, whether we develop greater or lesser Spiritual practice and realizations Depends on the force with which we meditate On faith that itself is greater or lesser. Think therefore on the good qualities Of your Lama of kindness, the root Of all attainments, and do not look For faults in Them. May I keep this one advice The center of my practice; May I bring this resolve Unhindered to its final end. [Translator's note: The Tibetan editor notes that the Tibetan for the next to the last line is not precisely the original form, which we find elsewhere as MTHIL DU 'DZIN PA DANG,.]

gru.acip: BLA MA LA SANGS RGYAS DNGOS SU MA BLTAS NA LEGS SKAR GYIS SANGS RGYAS LA MTHONG BA LTAR SKYON 'BA' ZHIG LAS MI MTHONG BAS RANG LA YON TAN 'BYUNG BA'I SKABS MED, DES NA RIGS PA YANG DAG GI SGO NAS BLA MA SANGS RGYAS SU BSGRUB DGOS,
gru.wylie: bla ma la sangs rgyas dngos su ma bltas na legs skar gyis sangs rgyas la mthong ba ltar skyon 'ba' zhig las mi mthong bas rang la yon tan 'byung ba'i skabs med, des na rigs pa yang dag gi sgo nas bla ma sangs rgyas su bsgrub dgos
gru.english: If you fail to look on your Lama as being the Buddha himself, you will end up seeing nothing in Them but faults, the way that Sunakshatra saw the Buddha.  This will totally disallow you from ever developing any high qualities.  Therefore you must use good logic and prove to yourself that your Lama is the Buddha.

gru.acip: DE SGRUB BYED LAM RIM GYI KHRID LAS BYUNG BA LTAR YANG YANG BSAMS TE MYONG BA 'DON PA GAL CHE,
gru.wylie: de sgrub byed lam rim gyi khrid las byung ba ltar yang yang bsams te myong ba 'don pa gal che
gru.english: The proofs for this are found in the teachings on the steps of the path to enlightenment, and it is vital that you contemplate these again and again, until you achieve some fluency in this thinking.

gru.wylie: grub chen nag po spyod pa dang, dge tshul tshem bu pas rdo rje phag mo mdze mor mthong, ganggA'i gling nas rje btsun ku sA li, zhes sogs ltar dge tshul tshem bu ba mkha' spyod du khrid tshul
gru.english: Our Lama related the story of the accomplished saint Krishna Acharya and the novice monk Tsembupa*, who saw the Diamond Sow as a woman leper.  The lines of the prayer say, "You came Yourself down to the land of the Ganges River, and led the venered Kusali."  And so She did; She actually took the novice Tsembupa off to Her heaven. [*Translator's note: This is the Tibetan for his name; the original Sanskrit is uncertain.]

gru.wylie: dpal mgon klu sgrub kyis, ,mchod pa thams cad rnam spangs nas, ,bla ma la mchod yang dag brtsams, ,de mnyes pas ni kun mkhyen pa'i, ,ye shes mchog zhi thob par 'gyur, ,ces gsungs
gru.english: The glorious savior Nagarjuna has spoken as well, Give up all your other offerings; Make pure offerings to your Lama. If you please Them you will achieve The highest wisdom, omniscience, peace.

gru.acip: DANG PO BLA MA BSKYED PA'I ZHAL SHES NI, LCANG SKYA DANG THU'U BKVAN GYI GSUNG RGYUN LTAR, BLA MA DPA' BO RDO RJE CHOS SU BSKYED PA PHYI, SANGS RGYAS RDO RJE CHOS SU BSKYED PA NANG, DE YUM BCAS SU BSKYED PA GSANG SGRUB,
gru.wylie: dang po bla ma bskyed pa'i zhal shes ni, lcang skya dang thu'u bkvan gyi gsung rgyun ltar, bla ma dpa' bo rdo rje chos su bskyed pa phyi, sangs rgyas rdo rje chos su bskyed pa nang, de yum bcas su bskyed pa gsang sgrub
gru.english: The first of these private instructions is that of how to produce the Lama.  According to the teaching traditions of Changkya and Tuken, producing our Lama as Dharma of Diamond the Warrior is a practice for reaching the outer Angel.  Producing Her or Him as Dharma of Diamond the Buddha is for reaching the inner Angel, and producing Him or Her together with Their partner is for reaching the secret Angel.

gru.acip: SA LUGS LA BLA RNAL THUN MONG BA MA GTOGS THUN MONG MIN PA SNYAN BRGYUD KHO NAR MDZAD PAS DNGUL CHU'I SGRUB THABS SU THUN MONG BA MDZAD, DE'ANG BLA MA DPA' BO RDO RJE CHOS SU BSKYED PA THUN MONG BA, SANGS RGYAS RDO RJE CHOS SU BSKYED PA THUN MONG MA YIN PA YIN, DE GNYIS NGO BO GCIG CING, BLA MA LA SANGS RGYAS DNGOS KYI 'DU SHES YOD NA RNAM PA SANGS RGYAS SU BSGOM MA BSGOMS LA KHYAD MED KYANG,
gru.wylie: sa lugs la bla rnal thun mong ba ma gtogs thun mong min pa snyan brgyud kho nar mdzad pas dngul chu'i sgrub thabs su thun mong ba mdzad, de'ang bla ma dpa' bo rdo rje chos su bskyed pa thun mong ba, sangs rgyas rdo rje chos su bskyed pa thun mong ma yin pa yin, de gnyis ngo bo gcig cing, bla ma la sangs rgyas dngos kyi 'du shes yod na rnam pa sangs rgyas su bsgom ma bsgoms la khyad med kyang
gru.english: According to the Sakya tradition the unique practice of the Lama, as opposed to the shared one, can only be passed down orally, and so in Ngulchu's ritual for reaching the Angel he has used the shared one.  Now producing your Lama as Dharma of Diamond the Warrior is the shared practice, and producing Her or Him as Dharma of Diamond the Buddha is the unique practice.  In fact these two beings have one and the same nature; and if you see your Lama as the Buddha himself, it makes no difference whether you meditate on Him in the form of the Buddha or not.

gru.acip: SKU'I RNAM 'GYUR GYI KHYAD PAR LA RTEN 'BREL GYI GNAD YOD PAS, KHO BOS NYE LAM 'DIR THUN MONG MIN PA'I LUGS LTAR BKOD PA GRUB MCHOG 'JAM DBYANGS BDE RDOR DANG STAG PHU BSTAN PA'I RGYAL MTSAN SOGS KYI DGONGS PA YIN,
gru.wylie: sku'i rnam 'gyur gyi khyad par la rten 'brel gyi gnad yod pas, kho bos nye lam 'dir thun mong min pa'i lugs ltar bkod pa grub mchog 'jam dbyangs bde rdor dang stag phu bstan pa'i rgyal mtshan sogs kyi dgongs pa yin
gru.english: There is though a crucial, auspicious point in how you decide to visualize your Lama's outer form.  Therefore, said our Lama, I followed the unique system when I composed this section in the Short Path, the ritual text we are using here.  In so doing I have adhered to the intent of Lamas such as those supreme realized saints--Jamyang Dedor; Tenpay Gyeltsen from Takpu; and others.

gru.acip: DES NA RANG GI MDUN GYI NAM MKHAR ZHVA KHRID LTAR YE SHES RANG SNANG LAS GRUB PA'I THAR PA CHEN PO'I GZHAL YAS KHANG GRU BZHI SGO BZHI RTA BABS BZHI DANG LDAN PA, MTHO ZHING YANGS LA RGYA CHE LTA NA SDUG PA, DRVA BA DRVA PHYED SOGS RIN PO CHE'I RGYAN DU MAS MDZES SHING, GSER GYI RGYA PHIBS LA NOR BU'I TOG GIS SPRAS PA,
gru.wylie: des na rang gi mdun gyi nam mkhar zhva khrid ltar ye shes rang snang las grub pa'i thar pa chen po'i gzhal yas khang gru bzhi sgo bzhi rta babs bzhi dang ldan pa, mtho zhing yangs la rgya che lta na sdug pa, drva ba drva phyed sogs rin po che'i rgyan du mas mdzes shing, gser gyi rgya phibs la nor bu'i tog gis spras pa
gru.english: So now in the air in front of you, following the treatise of Shalu, picture the Palace of the Great Liberation; it is an expression of wisdom, four-sided, with four gates and four stepways.  The palace is lofty and vast, lovely to look upon.  Its walls are studded with a multitude of adornments made of different precious materials: full aprons of gold, half aprons, and so on.  Atop the palace are domes with tips made of jewels.

whole_word_matches.context: snang las grub pa'i thar pa chen po'i gzhal yas khang gru bzhi sgo bzhi rta babs bzhi dang ldan pa, mtho zhing y

gru.acip: YANG NA GDUL BYA'I RGYUD LA 'PHRIN LAS 'JUG THABS KYI GTZO BO NI CHOS GSUNGS PA YIN PAS BLA MA'I GSUNG GI 'PHRIN LAS SLOB MA'I RGYUD LA 'JUG PA'I PHYIR GSUNG RDO RJE'I NGO BO SANGS RGYAS RDO RJE CHOS TE 'OD DPAG MED KYI SKU MDOG LTA BU, RGYAS PA'I LAS 'GRUB CING THUGS NYE BA'I RNAM PAS ZHAL 'DZUM ZHING SGEG PA,
gru.wylie: yang na gdul bya'i rgyud la 'phrin las 'jug thabs kyi gtso bo ni chos gsungs pa yin pas bla ma'i gsung gi 'phrin las slob ma'i rgyud la 'jug pa'i phyir gsung rdo rje'i ngo bo sangs rgyas rdo rje chos te 'od dpag med kyi sku mdog lta bu, rgyas pa'i las 'grub cing thugs nye ba'i rnam pas zhal 'dzum zhing sgeg pa
gru.english: You can also explain the color of His holy body in another way.  The principal way in which the high activities of the Buddhas can affect disciples is through the teaching of the Dharma.  Here our Lama wants His or Her own high activity of speech to affect the beings of Their disciples, so They take on the form of Dharma of Diamond the Buddha, whose essence is the diamond of speech, and whose color is like that of the Angel named Immeasurable Light.  Our Lama's holy face is pleasant and smiling, reflecting the activity of prosperity and Their intimate love for us.

gru.acip: LANG TSO DAR LA BABS PA'I MTHAR THUG NI LO BCU DRUG LA 'BYUNG BAS SKU LUS LA KHENGS KHUM SOGS MED PA MDZES SHING 'DZUM PAS RGYAS PA'I LAS DANG, MCHOG MTHUN MONG GI DNGOS GRUB 'GRUB PA MTSON NO,
gru.wylie: lang tsho dar la babs pa'i mthar thug ni lo bcu drug la 'byung bas sku lus la khengs khum sogs med pa mdzes shing 'dzum pas rgyas pa'i las dang, mchog mthun mong gi dngos grub 'grub pa mtshon no
gru.english: The very pinnacle of youthful strength comes when we are sixteen; and thus here our Lama is sixteen years old.  The fact that their holy body is so beautiful--free of any excess or deficiency of flesh, or any other fault--and that They are smiling represents one of the four modes: that of generosity.  It represents as well the fact that They will help us achieve both the ultimate and common attainments.

gru.acip: CHOS DBYINGS RDO RJE MAS RNAM THAR SGO GSUM DANG, CHOS SKU 'GYUR BA MED PA MTSON PA'I CHOS 'BYUNG GRU GSUM MTHING NAG PHUL BA SPYAN GYIS GZIGS PA TZAM GYIS CHOS THAMS CAD RANG BZHIN GYIS MED PAR RTOGS PA'I BDE STONG DBYER MED KYI YE SHES KHYAD PAR CAN THUGS RGYUD LA 'KHRUNGS PAS MNYES BAR BSAMS PA NI PHYI BUM DBANG DANG 'BREL BA'I MCHOD PA,
gru.wylie: chos dbyings rdo rje mas rnam thar sgo gsum dang, chos sku 'gyur ba med pa mtshon pa'i chos 'byung gru gsum mthing nag phul ba spyan gyis gzigs pa tsam gyis chos thams cad rang bzhin gyis med par rtogs pa'i bde stong dbyer med kyi ye shes khyad par can thugs rgyud la 'khrungs pas mnyes bar bsams pa ni phyi bum dbang dang 'brel ba'i mchod pa
gru.english: The Lady of the Sphere of the Dharma offers a dharma star with three points; it is dark blue and represents both the three doors to total freedom, and the immutable Dharma Body.  Just seeing the star causes an extraordinary form of wisdom to rise up in the hearts of the Beings to whom we offer it.  This is the wisdom of indivisible bliss and emptiness, the wisdom which realizes that no object in the universe has any natural existence.  Think to yourself that They are pleased with your gift; this then is the outer offering, the one that relates to the empowerment of the vase.

whole_word_matches.context: dang, chos sku 'gyur ba med pa mtshon pa'i chos 'byung gru gsum mthing nag phul ba spyan gyis gzigs pa tsam gyis

gru.acip: PHYI MCHOD KUN GYIS KYANG BDE STONG SKYED PAS NA, MKHAS GRUB SANGS RGYAS YE SHES KYIS KYANG, MCHOD PA THAMS CAD LA DE KHO NA NYID KYI MCHOD PA YOD DE, MCHOD PA DE DANG DE LAS THUGS RGYUD LA BDE STONG 'KHRUNGS PA'I PHYIR, ZHES GSUNGS,
gru.wylie: phyi mchod kun gyis kyang bde stong skyed pas na, mkhas grub sangs rgyas ye shes kyis kyang, mchod pa thams cad la de kho na nyid kyi mchod pa yod de, mchod pa de dang de las thugs rgyud la bde stong 'khrungs pa'i phyir, zhes gsungs
gru.english: Since even the outer offerings, all of them, have this nature of giving bliss and emptiness, the learned and accomplished Sangye Yeshe has stated that There is an offering of thusness In every one of the offerings, For each and every separate offering Makes bliss and emptiness rise in Their hearts.

gru.acip: DE NAS MCHOD PA THAMS CAD KYI MCHOG SGRUB PA'I MCHOD PA 'BUL BA NI, DKON MCHOG GSUM LA BDAG SKYABS MCHI, ,ZHES SOGS TE, RANG SRID ZHI'I 'JIGS PAS MNAR BA LA MI BZOD PA'I NGES 'BYUNG, GZHAN DE LTAR MNAR BA LA MI BZOD PA'I SNYING RJE, 'JIGS BDE LAS SKYOB PA'I SKYABS BSLU BA MED PA MDUN GYI TSOGS ZHING RNAMS YIN SNYAM PA'I YID CHES KYIS BLO LINGS 'GEL BYED PA THEG CHEN THUN MONG MIN PA'I SKYABS 'GRO BYA,
gru.wylie: de nas mchod pa thams cad kyi mchog sgrub pa'i mchod pa 'bul ba ni, dkon mchog gsum la bdag skyabs mchi, ,zhes sogs te, rang srid zhi'i 'jigs pas mnar ba la mi bzod pa'i nges 'byung, gzhan de ltar mnar ba la mi bzod pa'i snying rje, 'jigs bde las skyob pa'i skyabs bslu ba med pa mdun gyi tshogs zhing rnams yin snyam pa'i yid ches kyis blo lings 'gel byed pa theg chen thun mong min pa'i skyabs 'gro bya
