gru.english: Next we offer the highest of all offerings, which is the offering of our own practice.  This begins with the words, "I go for refuge to the Three Jewels."  Here we take refuge, in the way which is unique to the greater way.  This first includes renunciation, where we can no longer bear the way we ourselves are tortured by the various terrors of the circle of life and lower peace.  Second is compassion, where we can no longer bear the way other beings are tortured by the same things.  And finally there is the state of mind where we put our complete and total trust in the Beings before us, the Beings with whom we hope to amass virtue; we have the intelligent belief that They are a shelter which can protect us from these fears; They are a refuge which can never fail.

gru.acip: DE LTA BU'I BDUN RNAM DAG BYED PA NI SGRUB PA'I MCHOD PA YIN GSUNGS,
gru.wylie: de lta bu'i bdun rnam dag byed pa ni sgrub pa'i mchod pa yin gsungs
gru.english: Our Lama said then that this "Pure Prayer of the Seven," as He had just described it, was an offering of our practice. *  *  *  *  * We turn now to the commentary by Lama Quicksilver: Presenting the Outer and Inner Offerings

gru.acip: DHARME CHOS TE SKU MDOG DKAR MO CHOS 'BYUNG MTHING NAG CHOS SKU 'GYUR MED GRU GSUM GYI RNAM THAR SGO GSUM NI, STONG PA NYID DANG, SMON PA MED PA, MTSAN MA MED PA MTSON PA 'DZIN PA DANG,
gru.wylie: dharme chos te sku mdog dkar mo chos 'byung mthing nag chos sku 'gyur med gru gsum gyi rnam thar sgo gsum ni, stong pa nyid dang, smon pa med pa, mtshan ma med pa mtshon pa 'dzin pa dang
gru.english: Dharme is for the Lady of Dharma, and Her holy body is white.  She holds a bluish-black dharma star, symbolizing the immutable Dharma Body.  Its three corners represent the three doors of freedom: those of emptiness; of no aspirations; and of no signs.  [The three doors of freedom refer to the general emptiness of things, the emptiness of things as causes, and the emptiness of things as results.  They are the understanding that things are empty, that they have always been empty, and that they will forever continue to be so.]

whole_word_matches.context: mdog dkar mo chos 'byung mthing nag chos sku 'gyur med gru gsum gyi rnam thar sgo gsum ni, stong pa nyid dang, sm

gru.acip: KU S'A LI'I TSOGS GSOG SKABS, KU S'A LI ZHES PA DGE BA CAN LA 'JUG PAS NANG GI YON TAN SBAS NAS MKHAS NYAMS GRUB NYAMS GANG YANG MED PAR PHYI'I KUN SPYOD PHAL PA LTAR STON CING, MNGON MTSAN CHUNG NGU'I THOG NAS DGE SBYOR KHO NAR 'BAD PA LA NANG GI YON TAN GI SGO NAS BTAGS PA DANG,
gru.wylie: ku sA li'i tshogs gsog skabs, ku sA li zhes pa dge ba can la 'jug pas nang gi yon tan sbas nas mkhas nyams grub nyams gang yang med par phyi'i kun spyod phal pa ltar ston cing, mngon mtshan chung ngu'i thog nas dge sbyor kho nar 'bad pa la nang gi yon tan gi sgo nas btags pa dang
gru.english: Next we gather the great goodness of Kusali.  The word kusali means goodness, and it refers to a person who conceals the high spiritual qualities she or he has within them.  In their outer actions they seem to be just a regular person; they make no show of being a sage or saint.  But in truth they give their entire strength to one thing, and one thing only: to the practice of virtue, with few signs to others of what they are doing.  And so the word kusali is applied to describe their inner spiritual qualities.

gru.acip: DON DU 'DIS PHYI TSUL MKHAS PA DANG GRUB PA, PHYAG MCHOD BYED PA SOGS GANG YANG MI STON PAR YAR MAR GYI MGRON LA SBYIN GTONG MI MNGON PA'I TSUL GYIS TSOGS RLABS PO CHE GSOG PA ZHIG YIN,
gru.wylie: don du 'dis phyi tshul mkhas pa dang grub pa, phyag mchod byed pa sogs gang yang mi ston par yar mar gyi mgron la sbyin gtong mi mngon pa'i tshul gyis tshogs rlabs po che gsog pa zhig yin
gru.english: The point is, to put it briefly, that we are able to amass a great amount of virtue in a very effective way: on the outside there is no sign of who we might be, a sage or a saint, nor any activity such as making prostrations or offerings to the Holy Ones; but in a way that no one else can see we are performing a great act of giving to the guests we have invited, those both high and low.

gru.acip: GA YAS SU RJE BTZUN 'JAM DBYANGS LA BSTAN 'GRO'I 'GAL RKYEN SEL ZHING MTHUN RKYEN SGRUB PA LA MGON SKYOB MDZAD NUS PA'I MGON PO YON TAN GYI MGRON GNAS GSUM GYI DPA' BO MKHA' 'GRO CHOS SRUNG YONGS GRAGS RNAMS DANG, GTZANG RIS KYI MGON PO BDUN CU RTZA LNGA LA SOGS PA, DRANG SRONG MCHOG BRGYAD SOGS LHA MI'I DRANG SRONG BDEN TSIG GRUB PA, DZAMBHA LA DANG NOR RGYUN MA SOGS GNOD SBYIN NOR LHA'I TSOGS,
gru.wylie: ga yas su rje btsun 'jam dbyangs la bstan 'gro'i 'gal rkyen sel zhing mthun rkyen sgrub pa la mgon skyob mdzad nus pa'i mgon po yon tan gyi mgron gnas gsum gyi dpa' bo mkha' 'gro chos srung yongs grags rnams dang, gtsang ris kyi mgon po bdun cu rtsa lnga la sogs pa, drang srong mchog brgyad sogs lha mi'i drang srong bden tshig grub pa, dzambha la dang nor rgyun ma sogs gnod sbyin nor lha'i tshogs
gru.english: To the Lamas' own right is holy Gentle Voice, surrounded by the ones we know as the "Guests of Holy Quality," for these are the Protectors who have the power to defend the Teachings and all living beings, who can clear away all that works against us and gather together all that works for us. These guests are all the Warriors and their Angels, along with the more familiar Protectors of the Dharma.  Here too are each of the angels and gods who succor and preserve us, starting with the group that includes the 75 Keepers of the Pure Realms; as well as the highly realized saints of men and gods, those who have attained the Word of Truth: the Eight Great Saints and others.  Along with them are the Gods of Wealth: the sprites known as Jambhala, the Lady of Riches, and the rest.

gru.acip: SGRUB THABS GZHUNG GI TSIG RNAMS MGRON BZHI DANG GSAL BAR MI MTHUN YANG THU'U BKVAN GSUNG SOR BZHAG YIN,
gru.wylie: sgrub thabs gzhung gi tshig rnams mgron bzhi dang gsal bar mi mthun yang thu'u bkvan gsung sor bzhag yin
gru.english: The lines at this point in the ritual for reaching the Angel don't explicitly match this explanation of the four groups of guests, but my goal here was to maintain the wording of Tuken.

gru.acip: NGED KYIS SGRUB THABS 'DIR BKOD PA'I BLA MA'I RNAL 'BYOR DANG, KU S'A LI'I TSOGS GSOG ,'OG NAS 'BYUNG BA'I LUS DKYIL RNAMS DNGUL CHU'I GZHUNG DANG MI 'GRIGS KYANG, 'KHRID YIG BEE d'URA ZHUN MA'I THEM SKAS DANG THU'U BKVAN RIN PO CHE'I DGONGS PA YIN PAS SKYON MED PA'I STENG DU LEGS CHA GZHAN LAS CHE BA YOD GSUNGS,
gru.wylie: nged kyis sgrub thabs 'dir bkod pa'i bla ma'i rnal 'byor dang, ku sA li'i tshogs gsog ,'og nas 'byung ba'i lus dkyil rnams dngul chu'i gzhung dang mi 'grigs kyang, 'khrid yig bee DUra zhun ma'i them skas dang thu'u bkvan rin po che'i dgongs pa yin pas skyon med pa'i steng du legs cha gzhan las che ba yod gsungs
gru.english: In the ritual text, said our Lama, there are a number of sections where what I have written is at some variance with the treatise of Ngulchu.  These are the Practice of the Lama; the Ritual of Kusali, for amassing the power of goodness; and the Secret World of the Body.  Nevertheless they reflect the intent of the instruction known as the Staircase of Lapis Made Pure, as well as that of Tuken Rinpoche.  So not only are these sections not wrong, they have distinct advantages over other versions.

gru.acip: BDUD RTZI'I RDUL PHRA RAB TSUN CHAD AOm DU GYUR PA RANG GI DPRAL BAR THIM, LUS KYI SDIG SGRIB DAG ,BUM DBANG THOB, BLA MA'I SKU'I BYIN RLABS LUS LA ZHUGS, LAM BSKYED RIM BSGOM PA LA DBANG BAR BYAS, 'BRAS BU SPRUL SKU 'GRUB PA'I NUS PA BZHAG ,
gru.wylie: bdud rtsi'i rdul phra rab tshun chad aoM du gyur pa rang gi dpral bar thim, lus kyi sdig sgrib dag ,bum dbang thob, bla ma'i sku'i byin rlabs lus la zhugs, lam bskyed rim bsgom pa la dbang bar byas, 'bras bu sprul sku 'grub pa'i nus pa bzhag
gru.english: Every part of the nectar, down to the atoms it is made of, turns to the same letter, om.  This ray of light dissolves into my forehead.  The bad deeds and obstacles of my body are made pure.  I receive the Empowerment of the Vase, and the blessings of the Lamas' holy bodies enter my own actions.  I am empowered to practice the path of the stage of creation; and the ability to reach one of the final results, the Body of Emanation, is planted within me.

gru.acip: YANG GNAS GSUM KA LAS 'OD DANG, 'BRU GSUM PHRENG SGRIG ,BDUD RTZI BCAS DKAR DMAR MTHING GSUM CIG CAR BYUNG BA RANG GI GNAS GSUM DU CIG CAR THIM, SGO GSUM GYI SDIG SGRIB, TSIG DBANG, GSANG GSUM GYI BYIN RLABS, BSAM MI KHYAB, NGO BO NYID SKU 'GRUB PA'I NUS PA BZHAG PAR MOS PA'I BAR RIM BZHIN SBYOR,
gru.wylie: yang gnas gsum ka las 'od dang, 'bru gsum phreng sgrig ,bdud rtsi bcas dkar dmar mthing gsum cig car byung ba rang gi gnas gsum du cig car thim, sgo gsum gyi sdig sgrib, tshig dbang, gsang gsum gyi byin rlabs, bsam mi khyab, ngo bo nyid sku 'grub pa'i nus pa bzhag par mos pa'i bar rim bzhin sbyor
gru.english: The light comes once more; this time from all three places, with strings of the three letters in a line, complete with nectar.  They all fly out at once, in the same colors of white, red, and blue, and dissolve at once into the same three places on me.  They purify the bad deeds and obstacles of all three of the doorways through which I express myself; I receive the Empowerment of the Word, and the blessings of the Lamas' three secrets; I am empowered to practice the Inconceivable; and receive the ability to reach the Body of Pure Essence.

gru.acip: SGRUB THABS SU BKOD PA 'DI DBANG BZHI THUN MONG BA LEN TSUL BSDUS PA LA DMIGS PA 'CHAR BDE PHYIR TSIG CUNG ZAD RGYAS SU BTANG BA YIN,
gru.wylie: sgrub thabs su bkod pa 'di dbang bzhi thun mong ba len tshul bsdus pa la dmigs pa 'char bde phyir tshig cung zad rgyas su btang ba yin
gru.english: What I have written into the ritual text at this point is a brief version of the regular practice of accepting the four empowerments.  Nonetheless I expanded the wording a bit so that it would be easier for you to visualize.

gru.acip: DBYANGS CAN GRUB PA'I RDO RJE RANG GI SLOB MA DNGUL CHU BLO BZANG 'JIGS MED DBANG PO DANG, TRE BO KHANG GSAR SKYABS MGON GNYIS LA THIM, DE GNYIS RTZA BA'I BLA MA LA THIM, RTZA BA'I BLA MA YANG SNYING DU GCES PA'I BU GCIG PU'I MAS BU LA BRTZE GDUNG JI LTAR YOD PA LAS KYANG BRGYA 'GYUR STONG 'GYUR GYIS 'GRAN DU MED PA LTA BU'I RANG LA THUGS SHIN TU MNYES SHING RJES SU CHAGS PAS RANG LA MAR THIM LA KHAD DANG,
gru.wylie: dbyangs can grub pa'i rdo rje rang gi slob ma dngul chu blo bzang 'jigs med dbang po dang, tre bo khang gsar skyabs mgon gnyis la thim, de gnyis rtsa ba'i bla ma la thim, rtsa ba'i bla ma yang snying du gces pa'i bu gcig pu'i mas bu la brtse gdung ji ltar yod pa las kyang brgya 'gyur stong 'gyur gyis 'gran du med pa lta bu'i rang la thugs shin tu mnyes shing rjes su chags pas rang la mar thim la khad dang
gru.english: This continues on up to the present day [of Master Dechen Nyingpo's time], so that Yangchen Druppay Dorje melts into His two disciples, Ngulchu Lobsang Jigme and Trehor Kangsar Kyabgon.*  These two then melt into the Root Lama.  In joy, my Root Lama is on the verge of coming down and melting into me.  Her joy is a great pleasure with me; the burning love of a mother for her one and only son could never compare, were it magnified a hundred, or even a thousand times. [*In October of 1993, Khen Rinpoche Geshe Lobsang Tharchin said that we were allowed to add to the text here that these two melt down into Dechen Nyingpo himself; he into Kyabje Trijang Rinpoche; and he into Khen Rinpoche.]

gru.acip: PHYI'I SNANG TSUL MKHAS PA DANG, GRUB PA SOGS KYI TSUL MED PAR NYAL NAS SDOD PA LTA BU'I SPYOD LAM DE'I NGANG NAS BDE STONG GNYIS SU MED PA'I YE SHES LA RTZE GCIG TU MNYAM PAR BZHAG BZHIN PA'I NGANG NAS LUS YAR MGRON LA MCHOD PA, MAR MGRON LA SBYIN PA GTONG BA STE, MI MNGON PA'I TSOGS RLABS CHEN GSOG CING,
gru.wylie: phyi'i snang tshul mkhas pa dang, grub pa sogs kyi tshul med par nyal nas sdod pa lta bu'i spyod lam de'i ngang nas bde stong gnyis su med pa'i ye shes la rtse gcig tu mnyam par bzhag bzhin pa'i ngang nas lus yar mgron la mchod pa, mar mgron la sbyin pa gtong ba ste, mi mngon pa'i tshogs rlabs chen gsog cing
gru.english: One who is doing this practice may not look like a learned master or a great practitioner to others, on the outside.  Rather they might appear to simply be lying around sleeping.  However, even as they engage in this activity, the person is actually in a state of single-pointed meditation on the wisdom of indivisible bliss and voidness, making high offerings to guests of the offering who are above, and performing great acts of charity to the guests who are below.  This is an extremely effective way of gathering together virtue in an inconspicuous way.

gru.acip: GA-YAS PA GRI GUG GIS DPRAL LTAG SOGS SU NYUG TZAM RE BYAS NAS THOD PA BKOGS PA, PHYI DKAR LA NANG DMAR BA DE YAm LAS RLUNG DKYIL RAm LAS ME DKYIL GYI STENG MI MGO'I SGYED BU RI RAB TZAM GSUM GRUB PA'I STENG DU DPRAL BA TSOGS ZHING LA BSTAN NAS BSKYON PA'I KHYED DE KHYED DE RGYA STONG GSUM LTAR SHIN TU CHE BAR GYUR PA'I NANG DU,
gru.wylie: ga-yas pa gri gug gis dpral ltag sogs su nyug tsam re byas nas thod pa bkogs pa, phyi dkar la nang dmar ba de yaM las rlung dkyil raM las me dkyil gyi steng mi mgo'i sgyed bu ri rab tsam gsum grub pa'i steng du dpral ba tshogs zhing la bstan nas bskyon pa'i khyed de khyed de rgya stong gsum ltar shin tu che bar gyur pa'i nang du
gru.english: With a touch from the chopknife in your right hand--at the front, back and sides of the head--it slices open, and you pop out the skull.  The outside of the skull is white, and the inside red.  From yam comes a disk of wind, and from ram comes a disk of fire.  Atop of the fire come three firestones made of human heads the size of Mount Meru.  The skull sits on top of these, with the forehead facing the garden of virtue to whom you are making the offering.  Then the skull begins to expand and expand until its breadth is very very wide, a big as an entire galaxy.

gru.acip: ZHES THUN RER CIG 'GRUB BAM NYER BDUN NYUNG MTHAR 'BUL, DE RJES TSOM BU NYER GSUM MA TSAR GCIG, RGYUN PAR 'JUG PA BDE BAR BYED 'DOD NA TSIGS BCAD GCIG GIS 'BUL TSUL BLO LHAN SKYES KYI BDE BA'I NGO BOR MOS PA NI GSANG BA'I MAndAL DANG, DES STONG NYID LA NGES SHES CI YOD BSKYED PA NI DE KHO NA NYID KYI MAndAL DANG, DE GNYIS KYIS LHAN CIG BYED PA'I RKYEN LAS SKYES PA'I YE SHES DE NYID KYIS GZUNG BYA'I YUL RNAMS PHUNG KHAMS SKYE MCHED KYI RGYU LAS BYUNG BA NI NANG GI MAndAL DANG, RI RAB GLING BZHI GLING PHRAN BRGYAD, RIN CHEN NI, RGYAL SRID SNA BDUN, GTER CHEN PO'I BUM PA, NYI MA DANG ZLA BAR BCAS PA STE TSOM BU NYER GSUM MA'I RNAM PAR SHAR BA PHYI'I MAndAL TE,
gru.wylie: zhes thun rer cig 'grub bam nyer bdun nyung mthar 'bul, de rjes tshom bu nyer gsum ma tshar gcig, rgyun par 'jug pa bde bar byed 'dod na tshigs bcad gcig gis 'bul tshul blo lhan skyes kyi bde ba'i ngo bor mos pa ni gsang ba'i maNDal dang, des stong nyid la nges shes ci yod bskyed pa ni de kho na nyid kyi maNDal dang, de gnyis kyis lhan cig byed pa'i rkyen las skyes pa'i ye shes de nyid kyis gzung bya'i yul rnams phung khams skye mched kyi rgyu las byung ba ni nang gi maNDal dang, ri rab gling bzhi gling phran brgyad, rin chen ni, rgyal srid sna bdun, gter chen po'i bum pa, nyi ma dang zla bar bcas pa ste tshom bu nyer gsum ma'i rnam par shar ba phyi'i maNDal te
gru.english: We should do all this at least once in each of our sessions; or at the very least offer the mandala in 27 piles of grain.  Then offer the mandala with 23 piles a single time.  If you wish to do this more easily on a regular basis, you can use [the following] briefer lines: [Here is a world Of mountains and continents, The precious ones And the goldmine vase, The sun and moon as well. All of them come From the heaps and parts And gateways that are me, Held by the mind of wisdom: Simultaneous bliss and emptiness. I offer this world to You, My Savior and Protector, Treasure of Compassion.] Herein you offer [1] the mountain known as Mount Meru, as well as [2-5] the four continents and [6-13] their eight sub-continents.  You also offer [14-20] the precious ones, meaning the seven riches of a king, [21] the great goldmine vase, and [22-23] the sun and moon as well.  These 23 objects represent the outer mandala. The inner mandala is the fact that all of these things come from the heaps and parts and gateways that make up the person: "me".  These objects are held onto by the mind of wisdom which is brought about by the two simultaneous factors of bliss and emptiness.  The secret mandala is imagining the mandala as being of the very essence of the mind of simultaneous bliss; and the mandala of thusness is when because of this bliss the Lamas develop various degrees of a true perception of emptiness.

gru.acip: BLA MA'I SPYI BO'I AOm LAS BDUD RTZI DKAR PO'I RGYUN BABS RANG GI SPYI BOR THIM, BUM PA'I DBANG THOB, LUS KYI SGRIB PA DAG ,LAM BSKYED RIM BSGOM PA LA DBANG, 'BRAS BU SPRUL SKU 'GRUB PA'I NUS PA BZHAG
gru.wylie: bla ma'i spyi bo'i aoM las bdud rtsi dkar po'i rgyun babs rang gi spyi bor thim, bum pa'i dbang thob, lus kyi sgrib pa dag ,lam bskyed rim bsgom pa la dbang, 'bras bu sprul sku 'grub pa'i nus pa bzhag
gru.english: From the letter om at the tips of the Lamas' heads comes forth a stream of white nectar.  It dissolves into the tip of your own head.  You receive the empowerment of the vase, and you are purified of all your physical obstacles.  You are empowered to practice the path of the stage of creation, and the ability to achieve one of your goals--the Emanation Body--is planted within you.

gru.acip: ,MGRIN PA'I A'A: LAS BDUD RTZI DMAR PO'I RGYUN BABS RANG GI MGRIN PAR THIM, GSANG BA'I DBANG THOB, NGAG GI DRI MA DAG ,LAM RDZOGS RIM BSGOM PA LA DBANG, 'BRAS BU LONGS SPYOD RDZOGS SKU 'GRUB PA'I NUS PA BZHAG
gru.wylie: mgrin pa'i a'a: las bdud rtsi dmar po'i rgyun babs rang gi mgrin par thim, gsang ba'i dbang thob, ngag gi dri ma dag ,lam rdzogs rim bsgom pa la dbang, 'bras bu longs spyod rdzogs sku 'grub pa'i nus pa bzhag
gru.english: From the letter ah at the Lamas' throats comes a stream of crimson nectar.  It dissolves into your own throat.  You receive the empowerment of the secret, and you are purified of the bad deeds of your speech.  You are empowered to practice the path of the stage of completion, and the ability to achieve the goal of the Body of Complete Enjoyment is planted within you.

gru.acip: THUGS KA'I H'Um LAS BDUD RTZI SNGON PO'I RGYUN BABS RANG GI SNYING GAR THIM, SHES RAB YE SHES KYI DBANG THOB, YID KYI DRI MA DAG ,LAM PHO NYA BSTEN PA LA DBANG, 'BRAS BU CHOS SKU 'GRUB PA'I NUS PA BZHAG
gru.wylie: thugs ka'i hUM las bdud rtsi sngon po'i rgyun babs rang gi snying gar thim, shes rab ye shes kyi dbang thob, yid kyi dri ma dag ,lam pho nya bsten pa la dbang, 'bras bu chos sku 'grub pa'i nus pa bzhag
gru.english: From the letter hung at the Lamas' hearts comes a stream of blue nectar.  It dissolves into your own heart.  You receive the empowerment of the knowledge and wisdom, and you are purified of all your mental bad deeds.  You are empowered to use the path of a messenger, and the ability to achieve the goal of the Dharma Body is planted within you.

gru.acip: ,GNAS GSUM NAS CIG CAR DU BDUD RTZI'I RGYUN BABS RANG GI GNAS GSUM DU THIM PAS TSIG DBANG RIN PO CHE THOB, SGO GSUM GYI BAG CHAGS DAG ,LAM BSAM GYIS MI KHYAB+ LA DBANG, 'BRAS BU NGO BO NYID SKU 'GRUB PA'I NUS PA BZHAG
gru.wylie: gnas gsum nas cig car du bdud rtsi'i rgyun babs rang gi gnas gsum du thim pas tshig dbang rin po che thob, sgo gsum gyi bag chags dag ,lam bsam gyis mi khyab+ la dbang, 'bras bu ngo bo nyid sku 'grub pa'i nus pa bzhag
gru.english: From all three places on the Lamas come streams of nectar, all together.  They dissolve into the same three places on you.  You receive the precious empowerment of the word, and you are purified of the bad seeds of your actions, words, and thoughts.  You are empowered to practice the path of the inconceivable, and the ability to achieve the goal of the Essence Body is planted within you.

gru.acip: RDZA BUM GYI RGYU 'JIM PA DANG MTSUNGS PA 'KHOR BA SGRUB BYED KYI THA MAL PA'I GZHI'I SKYE SHI BAR DO GSUM PO, RDZA BUM MA BZOS PA DANG 'DRA BAR SKYE SHI BAR DO RANG DGAR MA BTANG BAR, 'JIM PAS LHA SKU BZOS PA DANG 'DRA BAR SKU GSUM LAM 'KHYER GYIS 'BRAS BU SKU GSUM DU BSGYUR BA NI SBYONG TSUL DNGOS YIN,
gru.wylie: rdza bum gyi rgyu 'jim pa dang mtshungs pa 'khor ba sgrub byed kyi tha mal pa'i gzhi'i skye shi bar do gsum po, rdza bum ma bzos pa dang 'dra bar skye shi bar do rang dgar ma btang bar, 'jim pas lha sku bzos pa dang 'dra bar sku gsum lam 'khyer gyis 'bras bu sku gsum du bsgyur ba ni sbyong tshul dngos yin
gru.english: The hunk of clay that was meant to be made into a jar represents the three normal processes of every regular life: the birth, death, and state between birth and death that make up our experience of the great circle.  Deciding not to slap together the jar stands for not just letting birth, death, and the state between these two to happen the way they would have.  Using the clay instead for the exquisite form of an Angel means using those three normal events as a path to the three bodies, and changing them into the three Bodies of a Buddha.  This is the real way that we purify the three.

gru.acip: DES NA GZHI DUS KYI 'CHI BA SBYONG ZHING, LAM DUS KYI 'OD GSAL GYI RGYUD SMIN BYED DU BYED LA, 'BRAS DUS KYI SANGS RGYAS KYI CHOS SKU 'GRUB PAR BYED PA'I BTAGS PA'I RNAL 'BYOR NI 'CHI BA CHOS SKU'I LAM 'KHYER DANG,
gru.wylie: des na gzhi dus kyi 'chi ba sbyong zhing, lam dus kyi 'od gsal gyi rgyud smin byed du byed la, 'bras dus kyi sangs rgyas kyi chos sku 'grub par byed pa'i btags pa'i rnal 'byor ni 'chi ba chos sku'i lam 'khyer dang
gru.english: Thus we can describe the practice of using death as a path to the Dharma Body in the following way.  It is a practice where we use our imagination, to purify ourselves of death as it normally occurs.  It utilizes the clear light of the path to ripen our mind stream.  And it functions to bring us, at the point of the final result, the Dharma Body of a Buddha.

gru.acip: GZHI DUS KYI BAR DO SBYONG ZHING LAM DUS KYI SGYU LUS KYI RGYUD SMIN PAR BYED LA, 'BRAS DUS KYI SANGS RGYAS KYI LONGS SKU 'GRUB PAR BYED PA BAR DO LONGS SKU'I LAM 'KHYER,
gru.wylie: gzhi dus kyi bar do sbyong zhing lam dus kyi sgyu lus kyi rgyud smin par byed la, 'bras dus kyi sangs rgyas kyi longs sku 'grub par byed pa bar do longs sku'i lam 'khyer
gru.english: The practice of using the state between death and birth as a path to the Body of Enjoyment then is meant to purify ourselves of this same state as it normally occurs.  It utilizes the body of illusion, at the point of the path, to ripen our mind stream.  And it functions to bring us, at the point of the final result, the Enjoyment Body of a Buddha.

gru.acip: GZHI DUS KYI SKYE BA SBYONG ZHING LAM DUS KYI ZUNG 'JUG GI RGYUD SMIN BAR BYED LA, 'BRAS DUS KYI SANGS RGYAS KYI SPRUL SKU 'GRUB BYED SKYE BA SPRUL SKU'I LAM 'KHYER YIN,
gru.wylie: gzhi dus kyi skye ba sbyong zhing lam dus kyi zung 'jug gi rgyud smin bar byed la, 'bras dus kyi sangs rgyas kyi sprul sku 'grub byed skye ba sprul sku'i lam 'khyer yin
gru.english: So too the practice of using birth as a path to the Body of Emanation is aimed at purifying ourselves of birth as it normally occurs.  It utilizes the union, at the point of the path, to ripen our mind stream.  And it functions to bring us, at the point of the final result, the Emanation Body of a Buddha. *  *  *  *  * Here begins the continuation of Master Quicksilver's commentary--

gru.acip: DES PHYI NANG GI RTEN 'BREL LA BRTEN NAS LTE BAR DBU MAR RO RKYANG GIS 'KHYUD PAS NANG GI DBYIBS GRU GSUM AE DANG, DE'I NANG DU KHAMS DMAR PO BAm YIG GI RNAM PAR YOD PA NI NANG GI RNAL 'BYOR MA STE AE BAm MNYAM PAR SBYOR BA,
gru.wylie: des phyi nang gi rten 'brel la brten nas lte bar dbu mar ro rkyang gis 'khyud pas nang gi dbyibs gru gsum ae dang, de'i nang du khams dmar po baM yig gi rnam par yod pa ni nang gi rnal 'byor ma ste ae baM mnyam par sbyor ba
gru.english: The inner Angel can be explained in the following way.  Through this then, based upon a whole network of inner and outer conditions, your channel of taste  and solitary channel twist around the central channel at your navel.  This creates, on the inside, a triangular shaped eh [the shape of this Sanskrit vowel is triangular], and inside of that is the red element in the form of a vam syllable. This union of eh and vam is the inner Angel.

whole_word_matches.context: te bar dbu mar ro rkyang gis 'khyud pas nang gi dbyibs gru gsum ae dang, de'i nang du khams dmar po baM yig gi rn

gru.acip: SA LUGS PHAL CHER LA BAm YIG SOGS BAR DO'I LAM KHYER SKABS 'DIR MI 'BYUNG BAR 'OG TU 'BYUNG YANG, SBYANG GZHI 'CHI BA 'OD GSAL MNGON DU GYUR PA'I TSE 'CHI BA 'OD GSAL 'GAG PA DANG BAR DO GRUB PA GNYIS SRANG MDA'I MTHO DMA' LTAR DUS GCIG TU 'BYUNG BAR GSUNGS KYI, 'CHI BA 'OD GSAL 'GAG NAS RE ZHIG NAS BAR DO GRUB PA'I BAR CHOD PA MA GSUNGS PAS NA DE SBYONG BYED BAR DO LONGS SKU'I LAM KHYER YANG SKABS 'DIR BYED PA ` RJE TZONG KHA PA RJES 'BRANG DANG BCAS PA BZHED PA LTAR BAm YIG BAR DO LONGS SKU'I LAM KHYER NAM MKHAR 'JOG PA RJE LCANG SKYAS BZHED PAR MA ZAD GRUB CHEN N'A RO PA RANG GIS MDZAD PA'I RGYA GZHUNG DU'ANG YOD PAS DE BZHIN NGES PAR DGOS SO,
gru.wylie: sa lugs phal cher la baM yig sogs bar do'i lam khyer skabs 'dir mi 'byung bar 'og tu 'byung yang, sbyang gzhi 'chi ba 'od gsal mngon du gyur pa'i tshe 'chi ba 'od gsal 'gag pa dang bar do grub pa gnyis srang mda'i mtho dma' ltar dus gcig tu 'byung bar gsungs kyi, 'chi ba 'od gsal 'gag nas re zhig nas bar do grub pa'i bar chod pa ma gsungs pas na de sbyong byed bar do longs sku'i lam khyer yang skabs 'dir byed pa ` rje tsong kha pa rjes 'brang dang bcas pa bzhed pa ltar baM yig bar do longs sku'i lam khyer nam mkhar 'jog pa rje lcang skyas bzhed par ma zad grub chen nA ro pa rang gis mdzad pa'i rgya gzhung du'ang yod pas de bzhin nges par dgos so
gru.english: For the most part the Sakyas don't put this part about the vam letter--using the intermediate state as a path--at this point; rather, for them it comes later.  However it has been stated in scripture that during the appearance of the clear light of death (the thing which you must purify), the end of this clear light and the beginning of the intermediate state occur simultaneously, moving like the two plates of a scale.  Nowhere in scripture does it say that there is any kind of gap between the clear light of death and the beginning of the intermediate state. Therefore, it is at this point in the practice where you must transform the intermediate state into a path to the Enjoyment Body, in order to purify this experience.  That this is where we set out the vam letter in empty space--and perform the practice of using the intermediate state as a path to the Body of Enjoyment--is the position of Lord Tsongkapa, and all those who have followed Him.  And not only is the instruction given by the great Lord and Master Changkya, it is also found in the original Sanskrit treatises of the secret practitioner Naropa.  So it is certain that you must practice in this way.

gru.acip: MA THOB PA THOB BO SNYAM PA'I NGA RGYAL DU 'GYUR DOGS NI MED DE, DPER NA DGE SLONG LA DON GYI DGE SLONG DGRA BCOM PA DANG, GSOL BZHI'I DGE SLONG CHO GA'I SGO NAS SGRUB PA DANG, RTAGS TZAM 'DZIN PA'I DGE SLONG DANG, KHAS 'CHE BA'I DGE SLONG RNAMS SU YOD PA LAS,
gru.wylie: ma thob pa thob bo snyam pa'i nga rgyal du 'gyur dogs ni med de, dper na dge slong la don gyi dge slong dgra bcom pa dang, gsol bzhi'i dge slong cho ga'i sgo nas sgrub pa dang, rtags tsam 'dzin pa'i dge slong dang, khas 'che ba'i dge slong rnams su yod pa las
gru.english: You don't have to worry that this practice is going to become the kind of pride that thinks you have achieved a certain spiritual level when you have not.  There are, for example, different kinds of fully-ordained monks.  "Ultimate" monks are anyone who is an enemy-destroyer.  A "monk of the statement and the three responses" [first by abbot, followed by three repetitions of these words, where one is ordained in a proper ritual] is one who has become a monk by means of ritual.  Then there are those who only maintain the appearance of a monk, and those who are monks by their own admission [those who took the vows for wrong reasons, and think they are monks but are not].

gru.acip: DE YANG NGA LA SOGS PA'I CHOS THAMS CAD RANG BZHIN GYIS MA GRUB PA'AM, BDAG MED PAR BSGOM PA LA MED RGYU'I BDAG DE NGES PAR BYA DGOS PAS, RANG RER CHOS DANG GANG ZAG GANG SNANG BA THAMS CAD DE DANG DE ZHES KHO RANG GI NGOS NAS TSUR GRUB PA LTA BU TSUGS THUB LING NGE BA ZHIG RANG SHUGS KYIS SHAR 'ONG BA DE DGAG BYA YIN,
gru.wylie: de yang nga la sogs pa'i chos thams cad rang bzhin gyis ma grub pa'am, bdag med par bsgom pa la med rgyu'i bdag de nges par bya dgos pas, rang rer chos dang gang zag gang snang ba thams cad de dang de zhes kho rang gi ngos nas tshur grub pa lta bu tshugs thub ling nge ba zhig rang shugs kyis shar 'ong ba de dgag bya yin
gru.english: Here we are meditating on the fact that no existing object in the universe, whether it be "me" or anything else, has any nature of its own; we are meditating on the truth that nothing has any self-nature.  To do this though we must be able to see what self-nature it is that nothing has. Things tend to appear to you and I as if they existed all on their own.  Whenever we talk about this or that, about any object that appears in our world (whether it be part of us or anything else), we get a very vivid and automatic impression that it exists from its own side.  That it could really be this way is what we seek to deny; this is what we seek to see does not exist.

gru.acip: DE GZUGS PHUNG SOGS GANG DU 'DUG BRTAGS NA, NGA'I GZUGS KYI PHUNG PO SOGS ZER BA'I SKABS LTA BU'I NGA RANG BZHIN GYIS YOD PA ZHIG GTAN NAS RNYED DU MED, DE BZHIN DU CHOS THAMS CAD RANG RANG GI NGOS NAS GRUB PA RDUL TZAM YANG MED PAR NGES PA'I NGES SHES BSKYED,
gru.wylie: de gzugs phung sogs gang du 'dug brtags na, nga'i gzugs kyi phung po sogs zer ba'i skabs lta bu'i nga rang bzhin gyis yod pa zhig gtan nas rnyed du med, de bzhin du chos thams cad rang rang gi ngos nas grub pa rdul tsam yang med par nges pa'i nges shes bskyed
gru.english: We are made up of various heaps, of different piles of parts, and we can examine each of these--such as our physical body--to see if any "me" who could exist this way is there.  But when we speak of "my" body, or any of the other parts, it is totally impossible for us to locate there any "me" who exists by nature.  The same is true for every single object in the universe: not one of them has one single atom of natural existence, of existing from its own side.  We must reach the point where we actually perceive this fact.

gru.acip: DE'I RTZI MA YAL BA'I THOG ,CHOS THAMS CAD RANG BZHIN GYIS MA GRUB PA'I DON BSAMS NAS YUL STONG PA NYID DANG YUL CAN BDE BA CHEN PO GNYIS GNYIS SU MED PA'I YE SHES LA GDAGS GZHIR BYAS TE,
gru.wylie: de'i rtsi ma yal ba'i thog ,chos thams cad rang bzhin gyis ma grub pa'i don bsams nas yul stong pa nyid dang yul can bde ba chen po gnyis gnyis su med pa'i ye shes la gdags gzhir byas te
gru.english: Try to maintain this feeling, this atmosphere, and then begin contemplating on the fact that no object in the universe has any nature of its own.  This combination--the object of emptiness, and the subject which is great bliss--is the undivided wisdom; and now it is going to get a new identity.

gru.acip: DES NA SNGON DU BSOD NAMS KYI TSOGS GSOG PA NI DPER NA RANG NYID RGYA NAG GONG MA LTA BUR SKYE BA LEN PAR 'DOD NA TSE 'DIR BSGYUR DU MED PA DE'I RGYU GSOG DGOS PAS MTHONG CHOS LA MYONG 'GYUR DANG, SKYES NAS MYONG 'GYUR DANG, LAN GRANGS GZHAN LA MYONG 'GYUR GYI LAS GSOG TSUL YOD PA LAS SKYES NAS MYONG 'GYUR GYI LAS BSAGS TE DE'I RJES SU 'CHI BA 'OD GSAL MNGON DU GYUR NAS GONG MAR SKYE 'GYUR LTA BU'I BAR DO GRUB NAS SLAR GONG MAR SKYE BA LEN PA LTAR,
gru.wylie: des na sngon du bsod nams kyi tshogs gsog pa ni dper na rang nyid rgya nag gong ma lta bur skye ba len par 'dod na tshe 'dir bsgyur du med pa de'i rgyu gsog dgos pas mthong chos la myong 'gyur dang, skyes nas myong 'gyur dang, lan grangs gzhan la myong 'gyur gyi las gsog tshul yod pa las skyes nas myong 'gyur gyi las bsags te de'i rjes su 'chi ba 'od gsal mngon du gyur nas gong mar skye 'gyur lta bu'i bar do grub nas slar gong mar skye ba len pa ltar
gru.english: First you must gather together a great collection of good energy. Suppose, for example, that you want to be born as someone like the emperor of China.  You are not going to simply transform into him in this life: you are going to have to create the appropriate causes.  Of the three kinds of deeds--those whose results occur in this same lifetime, those whose results occur in the very next lifetime, and those whose results occur in lifetimes after that--you are going to have to do the kinds of deeds that will ripen in your very next life. And after you have done that, you go through the experience of the clear light of death, and take on a body in the intermediate state which looks like the one you're going to have when you take birth as the Emperor.  And then you actually go and take this birth.

gru.acip: DE'I RJES SU CHOS SKU 'GRUB PA'I RGYUR YE SHES KYI TSOGS GSOG PA 'CHI BA CHOS SKU BSGOM PA NI LAS BSAGS NAS 'CHI BA DANG CHOS MTHUN, BAm YIG NAM MKHAR 'JOG PA BAR DO LONGS SKU'I LAM 'KHYER NI, GONG MAR SKYE 'GYUR GYI BAR DO GRUB PA DANG CHOS MTHUN,
gru.wylie: de'i rjes su chos sku 'grub pa'i rgyur ye shes kyi tshogs gsog pa 'chi ba chos sku bsgom pa ni las bsags nas 'chi ba dang chos mthun, baM yig nam mkhar 'jog pa bar do longs sku'i lam 'khyer ni, gong mar skye 'gyur gyi bar do grub pa dang chos mthun
gru.english: After this we must amass what is called the "collection of wisdom," which acts as the cause for us to achieve the Dharma Body.  We do this with the practice of using death as a path to the Dharma Body, which is analogous to collecting karma and then dying. When we place the vam letter in empty space and perform the practice of using the inbetween state as a path to the Body of Enjoyment, we do something which is analogous to reaching the body of the inbetween state for a person who is going to take rebirth as the Emperor of China just after that.

gru.acip: ZLA BA BAm YIG SNGAGS 'PHRENG LAS 'OD ZER SPRO BSDU BYED PA NI MNGAL NANG DU RIM GYIS LUS DBYIBS GRUB PA DANG CHOS MTHUN, RANG RDO RJE RNAL 'BYOR MAR GYUR PA NI MNGAL NAS PHYI ROL DU BTZAS PA DANG CHOS MTHUN NO,
gru.wylie: zla ba baM yig sngags 'phreng las 'od zer spro bsdu byed pa ni mngal nang du rim gyis lus dbyibs grub pa dang chos mthun, rang rdo rje rnal 'byor mar gyur pa ni mngal nas phyi rol du btsas pa dang chos mthun no
gru.english: Light comes out of the moon and the vam and the string of secret words, and then dissolves back in.  This is analogous to the stages in the development of the outer shape of our body within the womb.  And eventually becoming the Diamond Angel is analogous to the Chinese emperor actually coming out of the womb.

gru.acip: BAm YIG GIS BAR DO'I LUS NGAG YID GSUM MTSON TSUL AE WAm SGRA SGRUB KYI SGO NAS BSAMS NA NGES PA RNYED SLA BAR GSUNGS PAS,
gru.wylie: baM yig gis bar do'i lus ngag yid gsum mtshon tshul ae waM sgra sgrub kyi sgo nas bsams na nges pa rnyed sla bar gsungs pas
gru.english: We will next describe how the letter vam symbolizes the three body, speech, and mind of a being in the state between death and birth.  It is said that one can understand this point clearly by considering closely the linguistic composition of the word evam; so here we will cover that.

gru.acip: THOG MAR RNAM BCAD DANG, DE NAS AA DANG THIG LE RNAMS BZHAG ,KA L'A PA LAS, AA YIG DAG GI BAR DU AU'OS RNAM BCAD AU AA'I YI GER BSGYUR, AU WA GSAL BYED DBYANGS KYIS DMAN PA PHA ROL TU NYE BAR SBYAR BAR BYA'OS, AA SROG WAR DRANGS PA WA SROG LDAN DU GYUR, THIG LE STE KLAD KOR NGA ROR, 'JIG RTEN PA'I NYE BAR SPYOD PA LAS 'DZIN PA GRUB BO ZHES PAS BSGRUBS PAS WAm GRUB,
gru.wylie: thog mar rnam bcad dang, de nas aa dang thig le rnams bzhag ,ka lA pa las, aa yig dag gi bar du au'os rnam bcad au aa'i yi ger bsgyur, au wa gsal byed dbyangs kyis dman pa pha rol tu nye bar sbyar bar bya'os, aa srog war drangs pa wa srog ldan du gyur, thig le ste klad kor nga ror, 'jig rten pa'i nye bar spyod pa las 'dzin pa grub bo zhes pas bsgrubs pas waM grub
gru.english: So let us start with the contraction, and then the a and the dot.  Now the Kalapa mentions that "Between two a letters, a short u is contracted: the u and and a are transformed.  The u becomes a consonant v; and the following a, being lesser, is pulled into it.  That is to say, the a vowel is pulled up to make a va, complete with its vowel.  'The dot is the zero, the intonation; the works of the world work and it comes out'; which is to say, combine it, and come to vam."

gru.acip: 'O NA DNGUL KHRID DU AE SGRUB PA CI ZHE NA, GONG GI RNAM BCAD LUS BSGYUR BA'I AA DE LUS PAS ZHAR LA SGRUB PA YIN GYI, NGO MA WAm SGRUB PAS CHOG GSUNGS,
gru.wylie: 'o na dngul khrid du ae sgrub pa ci zhe na, gong gi rnam bcad lus bsgyur ba'i aa de lus pas zhar la sgrub pa yin gyi, ngo ma waM sgrub pas chog gsungs
gru.english: "Then why is it," one may ask, "that in the treatise of Ngulchu they present the composition of the e?"  Up above, the body of the contraction was transformed, which left behind the a.  This incidentally is converted into e; but the main point here, said our Lama, is satisfied by showing how the vam is derived.

gru.acip: MDOR NA BAm YIG NI GZHI LAM 'BRAS GSUM GYI GNAS SKABS KYI SGRUB GZHI SHIN TU PHRA BA'I RLUNG SEMS DANG MTHUN,
gru.wylie: mdor na baM yig ni gzhi lam 'bras gsum gyi gnas skabs kyi sgrub gzhi shin tu phra ba'i rlung sems dang mthun
gru.english: In short, the letter vam is comparable to the very subtle inner wind and mind that are the basic material at all three steps: our original state, the path, and the ultimate result.

gru.acip: DE YONGS SU GYUR PA LAS RTEN DANG BRTEN PA YONGS SU RDZOGS PA'I RNAL 'BYOR MAR SKAD CIG NYID LA DUS GCIG TU GRUB PAR BSAM STE, 'DI LA MNGON BYANG LNGA BSKYED KYI SKYE BA SPRUL SKU'I LAM 'KHYER ZER,
gru.wylie: de yongs su gyur pa las rten dang brten pa yongs su rdzogs pa'i rnal 'byor mar skad cig nyid la dus gcig tu grub par bsam ste, 'di la mngon byang lnga bskyed kyi skye ba sprul sku'i lam 'khyer zer
gru.english: Think then that this ball is transformed; that it becomes, in a single instant, all at once, the Holy Angel Her world in its entirety, with all its beings and the places where they stay.  This process is also known as "the practice of using birth as a path to the Body of Emanation, where you produce the five total enlightenments."

gru.acip: DE LA ZLA BA'I KHA DOG DKAR BAS ME LONG YE SHES LAS BYANG CHUB PA, DE BZHIN DU AOm GSUM MA'I YIG 'BRU DMAR BAS MNYAM NYID, BAm YIG ZHUGS PA SOR RTOG ,'OD ZER SPRO BSDU BYA GRUB,
gru.wylie: de la zla ba'i kha dog dkar bas me long ye shes las byang chub pa, de bzhin du aoM gsum ma'i yig 'bru dmar bas mnyam nyid, baM yig zhugs pa sor rtog ,'od zer spro bsdu bya grub
gru.english: This means that from the moon disk, since its color is white, comes the enlightenment produced by mirror wisdom.  By the same token, the various letters of the secret words of the triple om relate to equivalent wisdom, for they are red.  The letter vam, coming down as it does, stands for analytical wisdom.  The shining forth of the light, and its subsequent withdrawal, is connected to performance wisdom.

gru.acip: GZHAN YANG RGYAL PO AINDRA BH'U TI'I PHAG MO ZHAL GNYIS MA'I SGRUB THABS DANG, SNGAGS BTU'I SKABS KYANG GA YON SKOR MTHAR CHAGS SU 'BAB PA LAS, GA YON SKOR BYED TSUL SA LUGS LTAR GYI NYIS LDAB LOG PA DE 'DRAR GTAN NAS MI 'BAB LA,
gru.wylie: gzhan yang rgyal po aindra bhU ti'i phag mo zhal gnyis ma'i sgrub thabs dang, sngags btu'i skabs kyang ga yon skor mthar chags su 'bab pa las, ga yon skor byed tshul sa lugs ltar gyi nyis ldab log pa de 'drar gtan nas mi 'bab la
gru.english: We can refer also to the Ritual for Achieving the Sow, the Angel of Two Faces, composed by King Indrabhuti; as well as to the ritual for the brief secret words.  Both put forth the order as it normally appears, circling to the left.  None of these explain in any way or form the letters as going around to the left the way the Sakyas do, with the reversed pairs of syllables.

gru.acip: LNGA PA CHEN PO'I DGONGS PA DANG YANG MI MTHUN PAS, 'DI DAG RGYUD DANG PAn GRUB TSAD LDAN MANG PO'I GZHUNG MAN NGAG DANG BCAS PA'I DGONGS PA DANG BSTUN DGOS,
gru.wylie: lnga pa chen po'i dgongs pa dang yang mi mthun pas, 'di dag rgyud dang paN grub tshad ldan mang po'i gzhung man ngag dang bcas pa'i dgongs pa dang bstun dgos
gru.english: The Sakya presentation is moreover inconsistent with the thought of the Great Fifth, whereas any such explanation should properly reflect the thinking of a great number of accomplished and authoritative masters, as expressed in the classics they have written, and the traditional advices that accompany these works.

gru.acip: ,ZHES GSUNGS PA LTAR GANG ZAG LA MI RTON CHOS LA RTON PA ZHIG DGOS PAS DNGUL CHU BA'I GSUNG ZIN DANG DBYANGS CAN GRUB RDOR GYI GSUNG SMON 'GREL LHA'I RNGA DBYANGS SOGS SU LUNG RIGS KYI LAM LAS DRANGS PA'I DGAG GZHAG RGYAS PAR GSUNGS YOD PAS DE DAG LA YID RTON BYED DGOS,
gru.wylie: zhes gsungs pa ltar gang zag la mi rton chos la rton pa zhig dgos pas dngul chu ba'i gsung zin dang dbyangs can grub rdor gyi gsung smon 'grel lha'i rnga dbyangs sogs su lung rigs kyi lam las drangs pa'i dgag gzhag rgyas par gsungs yod pas de dag la yid rton byed dgos
gru.english: The Buddha here is telling us, "You must rely not on the personality of the teacher, but rather on the teaching itself."  You and I have at our disposal the Notes spoken by Ngulchu, as well as the prayer commentary, Drumsong of the Gods, which are words of Yangchen Drupdor; and many other works too are there.  These are writings that use the paths of scriptural reference and logical reasoning to arrive at very detailed refutations of incorrect positions, and presentations of what is actually right.  These then are what you should rely upon.

gru.acip: 'ON KYANG JO BO N'A RO TA PA NAS BZUNG SA CHEN GONG RIM BRGYUD PA DANG BCAS PA NAS DA LTA'I BAR BRGYUD THAG HA CANG RING BA'I STABS KYIS GDAMS NGAG LA 'KHYOR ZHUGS PA DAG THER MA THON PA LAS DE LTAR GSUNGS MKHAN RNAMS MKHAS ZHING GRUB PA BRNYES PA SHA STAG YIN PAS
gru.wylie: 'on kyang jo bo nA ro ta pa nas bzung sa chen gong rim brgyud pa dang bcas pa nas da lta'i bar brgyud thag ha cang ring ba'i stabs kyis gdams ngag la 'khyor zhugs pa dag ther ma thon pa las de ltar gsungs mkhan rnams mkhas zhing grub pa brnyes pa sha stag yin pas
gru.english: We must realize though as well that these teachings have come down to us in a lineage that spans an immense number of years, from the Lord Narotapa on to the line of the great Sakya masters of old, and then on down to the present day.  The very length of this lineage has inevitably caused a number of corruptions to creep undetected into the instructions.  This is not to say that those who have spoken these instructions were not learned and accomplished; they most certainly were, all of them.

gru.acip: 'DZIN STANGS CHOS THAMS CAD RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA RDUL TZAM YANG MED PA'I STONG NYID KYI LTA BA DBU MA THAL 'GYUR BA, DE LTAR RTOGS MKHAN GYI BLO YANG 'BRAS DUS KYI YE SHES CHOS SKU DNGOS YIN SNYAM PA'I NGA RGYAL TE CHOS SKU'I NGA RGYAL 'JOG PA'I RGYU BZHI TSANG BA DGOS SO,
gru.wylie: 'dzin stangs chos thams cad rang bzhin gyis grub pa rdul tsam yang med pa'i stong nyid kyi lta ba dbu ma thal 'gyur ba, de ltar rtogs mkhan gyi blo yang 'bras dus kyi ye shes chos sku dngos yin snyam pa'i nga rgyal te chos sku'i nga rgyal 'jog pa'i rgyu bzhi tshang ba dgos so
gru.english: How do we interpret these things?  We are maintaining (3) the viewpoint of the Consequence group of the Middle-Way School: the idea of emptiness itself, where there does not exist even a single thing in the universe which possesses a single atom its own nature. Finally we maintain (4) a certain sense of divine pride, where we think to ourselves that this state of mind, this state of realization, is the actual Wisdom Dharma Body of a person at the point of the final goal.  All four of these features must be present.

gru.acip: 'DIS LAM DUS SU DPE DANG DON GYI 'OD GSAL 'CHAR BA'I SMIN BYED DU 'GYUR ZHING, DPE'I 'OD GSAL LA GNYIS SNANG PHRA MO YOD LA GNYIS SNANG PHRA MO'ANG NUB PA NI DON GYI 'OD GSAL YIN ZHING, 'BRAS DUS SU CHOS SKU 'GRUB PA'I RGYUR 'GYUR PA DANG, GZHI LA 'CHI BA SBYONG BAS NA 'CHI BA CHOS SKU'I LAM 'KHYER ZHES BYA,
gru.wylie: 'dis lam dus su dpe dang don gyi 'od gsal 'char ba'i smin byed du 'gyur zhing, dpe'i 'od gsal la gnyis snang phra mo yod la gnyis snang phra mo'ang nub pa ni don gyi 'od gsal yin zhing, 'bras dus su chos sku 'grub pa'i rgyur 'gyur pa dang, gzhi la 'chi ba sbyong bas na 'chi ba chos sku'i lam 'khyer zhes bya
gru.english: The practice of thinking this way will ripen your mind to the point where--at the time of the path--you will be able to reach the stages called "approximate" and "actual" clear light. Approximate clear light is where there is still some perception of things as self-existent, some subtle discrepancy between what you see and what you think you see.  But when this discrepancy has dissipated, that is real clear light. At the stage of the result, this will act as a cause for you to achieve the Dharma Body.  And because this is the purification of your death during the stage of the original condition, we call this practice "using death as a path to the Dharma Body."

gru.acip: DES PHRA BA BAR DO'I LUS MTSON PA STE GZHI DUS SU BAR SRID SBYONG BAS NA BAR DO LONGS SKU'I LAM 'KHYER ZHES BYA, LAM DUS SU DAG MA DAG GI SGYU LUS DANG, 'BRAS DUS SU 'OG MIN DU LONGS SKU 'GRUB PA'I RGYUR 'GYUR RO,
gru.wylie: des phra ba bar do'i lus mtshon pa ste gzhi dus su bar srid sbyong bas na bar do longs sku'i lam 'khyer zhes bya, lam dus su dag ma dag gi sgyu lus dang, 'bras dus su 'og min du longs sku 'grub pa'i rgyur 'gyur ro
gru.english: The fact that the vam syllable is so tiny represents the subtle body of an intermediate being.  And so with reference to the original state you are trying to transform your life in the intermediate state, and this is why we call this practice "using the intermediate state as a path to the Enjoyment Body."  This practice acts as a cause for attaining your impure rainbow body and your totally pure rainbow body at the stage of the path.  With reference to the final result, it acts as a cause to achieving the state of the Enjoyment Body in the Paradise Below No Other.

gru.acip: THIG LES GOR GOR PO, N'A DAS 'KHRANG 'GYUR SOGS LUS KYI CHA RIM GYIS RDZOGS PA STE AE BAm GZUGS SGRUB KYI SKABS SU AA THUNG DANG YA RA LA WA'I YI GE BZHI 'GOD LUGS KYIS BAm YIG GRUB PAS DE LA YI GE DE RNAMS TSANG ZHING DE RNAMS LHA MO BZHI'I SA BON YIN LA,
gru.wylie: thig les gor gor po, nA das 'khrang 'gyur sogs lus kyi cha rim gyis rdzogs pa ste ae baM gzugs sgrub kyi skabs su aa thung dang ya ra la wa'i yi ge bzhi 'god lugs kyis baM yig grub pas de la yi ge de rnams tshang zhing de rnams lha mo bzhi'i sa bon yin la
gru.english: The dot represents the fourth stage: the embryo as a tiny ball shape.  The crook represents the solidification of the embryo, and jutting out of limbs, during the fifth week of development.  This gradual completion of the different parts of the bodily form is similar to where we deconstruct the shape of the word evam: complete within it are the short a slash, and the four syllables of ya, ra, la, and wa.  Together these then make up the letter vam itself, and so within it are all these complete: the four seed syllables for the four goddesses.

gru.acip: SNGAGS PHRENG GIS MNYAM NYID YE SHES, SA BON DU MA ZAD PHYAG MTSAN YANG YIN TE, AE WAm GZUGS GRUB KYI SKABS SU DBUS SU AA THUNG GRI GUG GI RNAM PA BZHAG , CES BYA BAS SOR RTOG YE SHES, ZLA BAS ME LONG YE SHES, 'OD ZER SPRO BSDU BYED PA BYA SGRUB YE SHES,
gru.wylie: sngags phreng gis mnyam nyid ye shes, sa bon du ma zad phyag mtshan yang yin te, ae waM gzugs grub kyi skabs su dbus su aa thung gri gug gi rnam pa bzhag , ces bya bas sor rtog ye shes, zla bas me long ye shes, 'od zer spro bsdu byed pa bya sgrub ye shes
gru.english: Thus the string of secret words represents equivalent wisdom.  Not only is the letter a seed syllable, but it is also an accoutrement: as they say, "When you deconstruct the form of the evam, place a short a vowel in the center, in the form of a chopknife."  And so this refers to the wisdom of individual analysis, [which cuts things up to understand them].  The moon symbolizes mirror-like wisdom, and then the sending out and return of the rays of light is the wisdom of accomplishment.

gru.acip: DE DAG NI SKYE BA SPRUL SKU'I LAM KHYER TE DE GZHI DUS SU SKYE SRID SBYONG BA DANG, LAM DUS SU DAG MA DAG GI RAGS PA'I LUS 'GRUB PA'I SMIN BYED DANG, 'BRAS DUS SU GZUGS SKU'I RGYUR 'GYUR PA'O, 'DI LA PHRA BA LONGS SKU DANG RAGS PA SPRUL SKU GNYIS LAS PHYI MA'O,
gru.wylie: de dag ni skye ba sprul sku'i lam khyer te de gzhi dus su skye srid sbyong ba dang, lam dus su dag ma dag gi rags pa'i lus 'grub pa'i smin byed dang, 'bras dus su gzugs sku'i rgyur 'gyur pa'o, 'di la phra ba longs sku dang rags pa sprul sku gnyis las phyi ma'o
gru.english: All of these represent using birth as a path to the Body of Enjoyment.  Relative to our original condition, they are the purification of the person at the point of rebirth.  Relative to the path, they ripen us for achieving the pure and impure forms of the grosser form of the body [of illusion].  At the point of the final result, they act as a cause for the Form Body of a Buddha.  This body has two aspects: the more subtle, which is the Body of Enjoyment; and the more gross, the Body of Emanation.  Here we're referring to the latter. *  *  *  *  * The following is an addendum to Reading Six; it was written in 1991: What a Buddhist Should Do When a Person is Dying by Khen Rinpoche Geshe Lobsang Tharchin, Abbot of Sera Mey Tibetan Monastery In the spring of 1991, the director of an American hospital which often treats Mongolian and Tibetan patients requested advice on any special steps to be taken with followers of the Buddhist religion as they die.  Khen Rinpoche Geshe Lobsang Tharchin, who has recently been appointed by His Holiness the XIVth Dalai lama as the abbot of Sera Mey, one of the largest Budddhist monasteries in the world, gave the following brief advice. How should family, friends, and hospital staff handle a Buddhist who is dying? As a person is dying, it is extremely important not to disturb or upset them in any way.  Family, friends, and staff should not show any excitement near the deathbed, and should speak softly, in restrained tones.  It is best at this time

gru.acip: BDE MCHOG LA RDO RJE'I RVA GUR GRU BZHI YIN YANG, 'DI'I RVA GUR ZLUM POR GSUNGS, 'OG GI RDO RJE'I ZLUM SKOR GYI GRANGS DANG, STENG GI ZLUM SKOR GRANGS MANG NYUNG 'DRA,
gru.wylie: bde mchog la rdo rje'i rva gur gru bzhi yin yang, 'di'i rva gur zlum por gsungs, 'og gi rdo rje'i zlum skor gyi grangs dang, steng gi zlum skor grangs mang nyung 'dra
gru.english: In the teachings of Highest Bliss, said our Lama, the diamond canopy is rectangular; here though it is round.  The number of diamond bolts in these top circular sections matches the number in the sections below.

whole_word_matches.context: bde mchog la rdo rje'i rva gur gru bzhi yin yang, 'di'i rva gur zlum por gsungs, 'og gi r

gru.acip: YE SHES KYI ME BRGYAD NI RI'I RTZA BAR YOD, GRUB THOB DANG 'OL BA PHO MO SOGS DANG, DUR KHROD BRGYAD RE RE LA'ANG SHING DANG PHYOGS SKYONG SOGS KHYAD CHOS BRGYAD BRGYAD YOD PA BDE MCHOG LUS DKYIL GYI SKABS LTAR YIN,
gru.wylie: ye shes kyi me brgyad ni ri'i rtsa bar yod, grub thob dang 'ol ba pho mo sogs dang, dur khrod brgyad re re la'ang shing dang phyogs skyong sogs khyad chos brgyad brgyad yod pa bde mchog lus dkyil gyi skabs ltar yin
gru.english: The eight fires of knowledge are found at the base of the mountains.  The burial grounds have great adepts staying in them, as well as male and female eagles.  Each one of the eight burial grounds has as well eight specific features, such as a particular tree, local spirit protector, and so on; these details are similar to the secret world of your body as taught in the practice of Highest Bliss.

gru.acip: DE YANG DUR KHROD KYIS NGES 'BYUNG DANG LTA BA, ME RIS BYANG SEMS MTSON ZHING, SRUNG 'KHOR GCIG PUS KYANG NGES 'BYUNG BYANG SEMS YANG DAG PA'I LTA BA GSUM GA MTSON PA STE, MDOR NA 'DI'I SGRUB PA PO LAM THUN MONG BAS RGYUD SBYANGS PA ZHIG DGOS PAR MTSON,
gru.wylie: de yang dur khrod kyis nges 'byung dang lta ba, me ris byang sems mtshon zhing, srung 'khor gcig pus kyang nges 'byung byang sems yang dag pa'i lta ba gsum ga mtshon pa ste, mdor na 'di'i sgrub pa po lam thun mong bas rgyud sbyangs pa zhig dgos par mtshon
gru.english: Now the burial ground stands for renunciation and the ultimate view; the mountain of fire is the wish to achieve enlightenment for all living beings.  You can also say that any one of the circles of protection symbolizes all three of these paths: renunciation, the wish for enlightenment, and the correct view of reality.  To put it briefly, they all represent the fact that a person who hopes to practice this teaching of the Angel must be one who is well versed in the path that is shared by both the open and secret ways.

gru.acip: YANG NA, CHOS 'BYUNG GCIG LA DKAR DMAR GNYIS KA TSANG BAS KYANG BDE STONG DBYER MED MTSON PA DANG, GRU GSUM GYIS RNAM THAR SGO GSUM MTSON,
gru.wylie: yang na, chos 'byung gcig la dkar dmar gnyis ka tshang bas kyang bde stong dbyer med mtshon pa dang, gru gsum gyis rnam thar sgo gsum mtshon
gru.english: The white and red are complete in each one of the triangles individually, and so you can say as well that each one symbolizes inseparable bliss and emptiness.  The three points of the triangle then stand for the three doors to total freedom.

whole_word_matches.context: a tshang bas kyang bde stong dbyer med mtshon pa dang, gru gsum gyis rnam thar sgo gsum mtshon

gru.acip: SPYAN NAM MKHAR GZIGS PAS RJE BTZUN MA RANG NYID PHYI NANG GI MKHA' SPYOD LA MNGA' BRNYES PA DANG, DE YANG MKHA' SPYOD DU GZIGS PAS RANG GI SGRUB PA PO MKHA' SPYOD DU MYUR DU 'KHRID PA'I BRDA STE, DPER NA 'BRAS SPUNGS MDA' NAS 'BRAS SPUNGS SU 'GRO'AM ZHES 'DRI TSE 'BRAS SPUNGS LA YANG BLTA BA BZHIN DANG,
gru.wylie: spyan nam mkhar gzigs pas rje btsun ma rang nyid phyi nang gi mkha' spyod la mnga' brnyes pa dang, de yang mkha' spyod du gzigs pas rang gi sgrub pa po mkha' spyod du myur du 'khrid pa'i brda ste, dper na 'bras spungs mda' nas 'bras spungs su 'gro'am zhes 'dri tshe 'bras spungs la yang blta ba bzhin dang
gru.english: The Holy Angel is looking upwards, which is means that She has Herself already gained the inner and outer Paradise.  When She looks to Her Paradise it is also meant as a sign for us, that She will quickly lead those who follow Her practice to Her Paradise.  It's like if you've walked from Lhasa out to the flats below Drepung Monastery, and somebody asks you if you're going to the Monastery, and you say "Yes" just by looking up at it.

gru.acip: ZHAL NAS KHRAG 'DZAG PA 'GRO KUN SNYING RJE CHEN POS YONGS SU MI GTONG BA DANG, NU 'BUR RAB TU RGYAS PAS RJE BTZUN MA RANG NYID 'DOD CHAGS RGYAS PA'I TSUL DANG, SGRUB PA PO'I RGYUD KYI 'DOD CHAGS SPONG BA MTSON, BHA GA NAS KHRAG RGYUN 'DZAG PA GTUM MO'I RTZA SAD PAR MTSON,
gru.wylie: zhal nas khrag 'dzag pa 'gro kun snying rje chen pos yongs su mi gtong ba dang, nu 'bur rab tu rgyas pas rje btsun ma rang nyid 'dod chags rgyas pa'i tshul dang, sgrub pa po'i rgyud kyi 'dod chags spong ba mtshon, bha ga nas khrag rgyun 'dzag pa gtum mo'i rtsa sad par mtshon
gru.english: Blood is dripping from the Holy Angel's mouth, and this is to show Her great compassion for all living kind, a compassion that will never allow Her to give up any one of us.  The nipples on Her breasts are full, and completely erect, which symbolizes Her own show of passion, and the final elimination of ignorant desire in the minds of those who follow Her practice.  Blood is oozing as well from the Angel's bhaga; this represents that the core of Her inner heat has been awakened.

gru.acip: ZHA KHRID DU ZANGS KYI GRI GUG GSUNGS KYANG, RANG LUGS LA DUS MTSAN MA'I GRI GUG ZANGS DANG, RNAL 'BYOR MA'I GRI GUG GNAM LCAGS LAS GRUB PA BYA DGOS,
gru.wylie: zha khrid du zangs kyi gri gug gsungs kyang, rang lugs la dus mtshan ma'i gri gug zangs dang, rnal 'byor ma'i gri gug gnam lcags las grub pa bya dgos
gru.english: It is stated in the treatise of Shalu that the chopknife is made of brass, but our own position is that the chopknife which the demoness Lady of the Night holds should be brass, and the Angel's of lightning-steel.

gru.acip: KHYAD PAR DGE LUGS PA ZAB GSAL GNYIS MED KYI RNAL 'BYOR ZHES BYA LA, RNAM PA LHA'I RNAM PAR GSAL BAS RGYA CHE BA GZUGS SKU SGRUB BYED, 'DZIN STANGS RANG BZHIN MED PAR STONG NYID BSGOM PAS ZAB PA STE CHOS SKU SGRUB BYED YIN LA,
gru.wylie: khyad par dge lugs pa zab gsal gnyis med kyi rnal 'byor zhes bya la, rnam pa lha'i rnam par gsal bas rgya che ba gzugs sku sgrub byed, 'dzin stangs rang bzhin med par stong nyid bsgom pas zab pa ste chos sku sgrub byed yin la
gru.english: And more especially, in the Way of the Pure, we have the deep practice of inseparable depth and clarity.  Picturing yourself clearly in the form of an Angel acts as a cause for you to achieve the ultimate result of widespread activities [first 3 1/2 perfections]--which is the physical body of the Buddha.  Thinking of Her as having no quality of Her own is a meditation on emptiness, which acts as a cause for achieving goal of the deep side of things--which is the Dharma Body.

gru.acip: DUS CIG TU GRUB PA L'U AI PA DANG DRIL BU PAR GSAL KHA MED KYANG DER NYE ZHING, NAG PO PAR RIM GYIS BSKYED PAR GSUNGS PA'I LUGS GNYIS LAS DANG PO LTAR YIN LA,
gru.wylie: dus cig tu grub pa lU ai pa dang dril bu par gsal kha med kyang der nye zhing, nag po par rim gyis bskyed par gsungs pa'i lugs gnyis las dang po ltar yin la
gru.english: This system of bringing up the secret world all in one flash is not something which is described very overtly in the teachings of Luipa and Ghantapada, but it is quite close to what they do.  There is a different system, where you bring up the visualization step by step, described by Kirshnapada.  Here we are following the former of these two.

gru.acip: PHYAG GA-YAS GSER GYI RDO RJE PHYED PA'I YU BA BYAS PAS GNAM LCAGS LAS GRUB PA'I GRI GUG YU BA DANG BCAS PA LA SOR BCU GNYIS TZAM SO GNYIS YOD PA 'OG 'KHOR BA'I PHYOGS SU BSTAN NAS 'DZIN PAS SEMS CAN RNAMS KYI 'DOD CHAGS KHONG KHRO, NGA RGYAL, MA RIG ,THE TSOM, LOG LTA STE RTZA NYON DRUG SOGS GCOD PA +
gru.wylie: phyag ga-yas gser gyi rdo rje phyed pa'i yu ba byas pas gnam lcags las grub pa'i gri gug yu ba dang bcas pa la sor bcu gnyis tsam so gnyis yod pa 'og 'khor ba'i phyogs su bstan nas 'dzin pas sems can rnams kyi 'dod chags khong khro, nga rgyal, ma rig ,the tshom, log lta ste rtsa nyon drug sogs gcod pa +
gru.english: In Her right hand She holds a handle of half a golden diamond, and a chopknife of sky-steel.  Along with the handle, it is about 12 sors [fingerwidths] long.  It has two points, and She is holding it downwards towards the circle of suffering.  This represents that She is cutting the six root mental afflictions from the mind of every living being.  These six are ignorant liking, ignorant disliking, pride, ignorance itself, doubts, and wrong views. Translator's note: The special mark in the Tibetan here at the end of line, and elsewhere, represents that the word "symbolizes" or "represents" is being repeated throughout this section.

gru.acip: KHA tV'Am GA LA GNYIS LAS, SLOB DPON PADMAS BSNAMS PA RTZE GSUM GYIS MTSAN PA NI PHA RGYUD KYI YIN PAS SBA MI DGOS KYANG, 'DI'I SKABS KYI RTZE MOR RDO RJES MTSAN PA'I KHA tV'Am GA NI MA RGYUD KYI YIN PAS RGYA GAR GYI PAn GRUB TSOS KYANG SHIN TU GSANG ZHING SBED PAR MDZAD,
gru.wylie: kha TvAM ga la gnyis las, slob dpon padmas bsnams pa rtse gsum gyis mtshan pa ni pha rgyud kyi yin pas sba mi dgos kyang, 'di'i skabs kyi rtse mor rdo rjes mtshan pa'i kha TvAM ga ni ma rgyud kyi yin pas rgya gar gyi paN grub tshos kyang shin tu gsang zhing sbed par mdzad
gru.english: Now there are two types of khatvanga staffs.  The one that Master Padma wields, which is tipped with a trident, belongs to the secret teachings of the Man and so need not be kept from the sight of others.  The khatvanga at this point in the ritual though, the one set with a diamond, is part of the secret way of the Wife, and so even in the days of the wise and accomplished saints of India was kept well hidden, in the strictest secrecy.

gru.acip: TSANGS SKUD LA, 'KHOR LO RTZIBS BRGYAD PA PHYI DBYIBS GRU BZHI PA'I ZUR BZHI LAS THON PA'I ZHES PA'I ZUR BZHI NI, 'KHOR LO'I PHYOGS BZHIR NOR BU BZHI YOD PAS, ZUR BZHI THON PA LTA BU,
gru.wylie: tshangs skud la, 'khor lo rtsibs brgyad pa phyi dbyibs gru bzhi pa'i zur bzhi las thon pa'i zhes pa'i zur bzhi ni, 'khor lo'i phyogs bzhir nor bu bzhi yod pas, zur bzhi thon pa lta bu
gru.english: The "cord of Brahma" here is described as "a wheel with eight spokes, with the appearance of having been drawn through a square positioned at the four corners."  Here the "four corners" refer to four jewels positioned on the wheel in the four cardinal directions.  Thus the circle looks as if it were drawn around these four corners.

whole_word_matches.context: tshangs skud la, 'khor lo rtsibs brgyad pa phyi dbyibs gru bzhi pa'i zur bzhi las thon pa'i zhes pa'i zur bzhi ni

gru.acip: 'DI YOD SA'I BSTOD PA DNGOS GRUB MYUR DU 'GUGS PA'I LCAGS KYU ZHES PAR YANG RNAL 'BYOR MA'I RTEN BRTEN PA'I DAG PA DANG, MTSON DON SHIN TU LEGS PA MANG PO GSUNGS TSUL, RUS RGYAN PHYIN DRUG DANG SBYOR BA'ANG RJE RIN PO CHE'I DGONGS PA YIN TSUL DNGUL KHRID LTAR GSUNGS,
gru.wylie: 'di yod sa'i bstod pa dngos grub myur du 'gugs pa'i lcags kyu zhes par yang rnal 'byor ma'i rten brten pa'i dag pa dang, mtshon don shin tu legs pa mang po gsungs tshul, rus rgyan phyin drug dang sbyor ba'ang rje rin po che'i dgongs pa yin tshul dngul khrid ltar gsungs
gru.english: These lines are found in a eulogy called A Hook for Snaring and Swiftly Pulling In Every High Attainment.  The Lama spoke further of this work, of its wonderful descriptions of the absolute purity of the place and the people of the Angel's world, and more too of its exquisite explanations of the symbolism.  Then He utilized the treatise of Ngulchu to show how the concept of relating the ornaments of bone to the six perfections was something that the Precious Lord Tsongkapa had also accepted.

gru.acip: RNAL 'BYOR MA 'DIR CHO GA MDOR BSDUS TE GSUNGS PA LAS GZHAN SGRUB THABS BSGOM TSUL RGYAS PAR BYAS NA BDE MCHOG GI SGRUB THABS DANG GNAD GCIG TU 'BAB PA YOD, DBANG BSKUR RGYAS GDAB MI BYED NA MTSAMS 'DIR RIGS BDAG RANG CHAS SU BSGOM PA YIN YANG, 'DIR DBANG BSKUR RGYAS GDAB BYED PA'I LUGS LTAR 'OG TU 'BYUNG GSUNG,
gru.wylie: rnal 'byor ma 'dir cho ga mdor bsdus te gsungs pa las gzhan sgrub thabs bsgom tshul rgyas par byas na bde mchog gi sgrub thabs dang gnad gcig tu 'bab pa yod, dbang bskur rgyas gdab mi byed na mtshams 'dir rigs bdag rang chas su bsgom pa yin yang, 'dir dbang bskur rgyas gdab byed pa'i lugs ltar 'og tu 'byung gsung
gru.english: The ritual for the Angel here, said our Lama, has been granted in a relatively brief form; and yet if one practices a more extensive ritual for reaching Her, in the end it is essentially the same as the method for reaching the Angel of Highest Bliss.  If you are not performing the Empowerment of Marking, then at this point you visualize yourself as the Lord of Enlightened Kind, complete in all His normal attire.  The version here though is one of the kind in which this empowerment is performed, and this will be covered further on. *  *  *  *  * We turn now to Lama Quicksilver--

gru.acip: MDOR NA BDE MCHOG LHA DRUG CU RE GNYIS RTEN DANG BRTEN PAR BCAS PA KHA tV'Am GA LA TSANG ZHING, DE THAMS CAD KYANG GTZO BO LAS RGYUD THA DAD PA MA YIN GYI GTZO BO'I YE SHES KHO NA'I CHA SHAS LAS GRUB PAS DE'I RNAM 'GYUR YIN PAS NA YAB MTSON ZHING SBAS PA'I TSUL GYIS 'DZIN PA'O, ,
gru.wylie: mdor na bde mchog lha drug cu re gnyis rten dang brten par bcas pa kha TvAM ga la tshang zhing, de thams cad kyang gtso bo las rgyud tha dad pa ma yin gyi gtso bo'i ye shes kho na'i cha shas las grub pas de'i rnam 'gyur yin pas na yab mtshon zhing sbas pa'i tshul gyis 'dzin pa'o,
gru.english: To put it briefly, the entire secret world of Highest Bliss--the 62 beings and the places where they stay--are all complete in this khatvanga.  None of these beings is a separate person from the central figure, but rather they are literally made of nothing more than a piece of His wisdom--and are thus His expression.  And so the staff represents the Man, and She holds Him in a way which is hidden from others.

gru.acip: YUL GRU MTHA' YAS PA'I SA NAS RTZVA SHING SOGS MER BSREGS PA'I THAL BA RGYA MTSOR BTAB PA LO BRGYAR DKRUGS TE GZIGS PHUL RUNG RDUL PHRA MO RE RE NAS 'DI LUNG PA 'DI DANG, PHU MDA' 'DI DANG 'DI'I SA RDO DANG RTZVA SHING GI RTZVA RTZE SOGS 'DI DANG 'DI'I RDUL YIN ZHES MA NOR BAR GSAL BAR 'BYED NUS PA,
gru.wylie: yul gru mtha' yas pa'i sa nas rtsva shing sogs mer bsregs pa'i thal ba rgya mtshor btab pa lo brgyar dkrugs te gzigs phul rung rdul phra mo re re nas 'di lung pa 'di dang, phu mda' 'di dang 'di'i sa rdo dang rtsva shing gi rtsva rtse sogs 'di dang 'di'i rdul yin zhes ma nor bar gsal bar 'byed nus pa
gru.english: If you went to every nook and cranny of an area and took little bushes from each place, and burned them all in a fire, and then took the ashes and threw them in the ocean and let them be churned around in the waves there for a hundred years, and then offered a drop of this water up to the sight of the Buddha, He could tell you from which state, valley, and pebble--and even the tip of which leaf--each of the particles in the drop came from: He can distinguish all this clearly, without any error at all.

whole_word_matches.context: yul gru mtha' yas pa'i sa nas rtsva shing sogs mer bsregs pa'i

gru.acip: SNYING GA'I THAD KYI MDUN RGYAB TU, 'KHOR LO'I DBUS SU RDO RJE RTZE GSUM PAS MTSAN PA, RUS PA GRU BZHI PA'I GRAR BZHI NAS RUS PA'I PHRENG BA NYIS GSHIBS SAM GSUM GSHIBS, PHRAG GONG GNYIS DANG MCHAN 'OG GNYIS SU RGYA GRAM DU BTANG BA, 'KHOR LO'I RTZIBS BRGYAD KYIS SNYING GA'I RTZA 'DAB BRGYAD MTSON PA DANG, 'KHOR LO'I MAS PHYOGS KYI RTZIBS DBUS MA NAS DRA PHYED 'PHYANG BA,
gru.wylie: snying ga'i thad kyi mdun rgyab tu, 'khor lo'i dbus su rdo rje rtse gsum pas mtshan pa, rus pa gru bzhi pa'i grar bzhi nas rus pa'i phreng ba nyis gshibs sam gsum gshibs, phrag gong gnyis dang mchan 'og gnyis su rgya gram du btang ba, 'khor lo'i rtsibs brgyad kyis snying ga'i rtsa 'dab brgyad mtshon pa dang, 'khor lo'i mas phyogs kyi rtsibs dbus ma nas dra phyed 'phyang ba
gru.english: At Her front and back, at the level of Her heart, is a circle marked in its center with a three-pointed diamond.  From four points around the bone circle come double or triple strands of interwoven beads, which are connected together by crossed strings which go over the two upper parts of Her shoulders and underneath Her arms.  The eight spokes of the central wheel of the breastplate represent the eight channel petals of the heart chakra.  Dangles of bone beads hang down from the lower middle spoke of the circle.

whole_word_matches.context: r lo'i dbus su rdo rje rtse gsum pas mtshan pa, rus pa gru bzhi pa'i grar bzhi nas rus pa'i phreng ba nyis gshibs

gru.acip: THIG LE BYA BA MI RO BSREGS PA'I THAL BA LUS LA BYUGS NA SNGO SKYA 'BYUNG BA DANG, DE'I STENG SKYES PA'I RUS PA MER MA SHOR BA ZHIB PAR BYAS PA SOR MO LNGA 'DZOM GYIS NYUG NAS DPRAL BA SOGS SU TSOM BU BYA BAR GSUNGS LA, RUS PA NI PA'I KHU BA LAS GRUB PA YIN PAS LHA YAB LA NANG DU KHU BA YOD CES MTSON PHYIR BYUGS PA DANG, YUM LA MED PAS MI DGOS PAR GSUNGS SO, ,
gru.wylie: thig le bya ba mi ro bsregs pa'i thal ba lus la byugs na sngo skya 'byung ba dang, de'i steng skyes pa'i rus pa mer ma shor ba zhib par byas pa sor mo lnga 'dzom gyis nyug nas dpral ba sogs su tshom bu bya bar gsungs la, rus pa ni pa'i khu ba las grub pa yin pas lha yab la nang du khu ba yod ces mtshon phyir byugs pa dang, yum la med pas mi dgos par gsungs so,
gru.english: In sacred texts it is stated that you should sprinkle water upon the ashes of a human corpse and smear them all over your body.  This gives your skin a pale blue color.  On top of that you should then take a male's bones which were not completely burned in the cremation fire, crush them into a powder, and with all five fingers smear this powder upon your forehead and such, making a dot in the center. The bones of a human body are something which is formed from the father's semen.  Male angels have this semen within Them, and thus place the ash upon their bodies to indicate this.  The sacred texts state that because women angels do not have this semen, they have no need to wear the ash.

gru.acip: RUS RGYAN LHA'I DAG PA DANG SBYAR NA, SPYI BO'I 'KHOR LOS MI BSKYOD PA, RNA RGYAN 'OD DPAG MED, MGUL RGYAN RIN 'BYUNG, GDU BU RNAM PAR SNANG MDZAD, SKA RAGS DON YOD GRUB DAG PA'O, ,
gru.wylie: rus rgyan lha'i dag pa dang sbyar na, spyi bo'i 'khor los mi bskyod pa, rna rgyan 'od dpag med, mgul rgyan rin 'byung, gdu bu rnam par snang mdzad, ska rags don yod grub dag pa'o,
gru.english: Each of these various bone ornaments is related to one of the ultimate purities of an enlightened being.  The circular headdress represents the purity of the Angel Unshakable (Akshobya); the earrings represent the purity of Limitless Light (Amitabha); the throat ornament represents the purity of Jewels (Ratnakara); the bracelets represent the purity of Appearances (Vairochana); and the belt represents the purity of Attainment (Amoghasiddha).

gru.acip: PHAR PHYIN DRUG DANG SBYOR TSUL, RJE RIN PO CHE, BU STON RIN PO CHE, SA CHEN BCAS KYI BSHAD PA MI 'DRA BA YOD PA LAS SA CHEN LTAR NA, GDU BUS SBYIN PA, 'OG PAG GIS TSUL KHRIMS, RNA RGYAN GYIS BZOD PA, MGUL RGYAN GYIS BRTZON 'GRUS, DBU RGYAN GYIS BSAM GTAN, TSANGS SKUD KYIS SHES RAB PHAR PHYIN MTSON,
gru.wylie: phar phyin drug dang sbyor tshul, rje rin po che, bu ston rin po che, sa chen bcas kyi bshad pa mi 'dra ba yod pa las sa chen ltar na, gdu bus sbyin pa, 'og pag gis tshul khrims, rna rgyan gyis bzod pa, mgul rgyan gyis brtson 'grus, dbu rgyan gyis bsam gtan, tshangs skud kyis shes rab phar phyin mtshon
gru.english: Here is how the six bone ornaments relate to the six perfections.  Je Tsongkapa, Buton Rinpoche, and Sachen explain the correlation in different ways.  Of these different explanations, Sachen says that the bracelets and anklets represent the perfection of giving; the skirt represents the perfection of an ethical life; the earrings the perfection of patience; the necklace the perfection of effort; the headdress the perfection of meditation; and the breastplate the perfection of wisdom.

gru.acip: RANG LUGS RJE TZONG KHA PA LTAR MGUL RGYAN SBYIN PA, GDU BU TSUL KHRIMS, RNA RGYAN BZOD PA, SPYI BO'I NOR BU BRTZON 'GRUS, MCHOD PHYIR THOGS BSAM GTAN, SKED RGYAN SHES RAB RNAMS MTSON,
gru.wylie: rang lugs rje tsong kha pa ltar mgul rgyan sbyin pa, gdu bu tshul khrims, rna rgyan bzod pa, spyi bo'i nor bu brtson 'grus, mchod phyir thogs bsam gtan, sked rgyan shes rab rnams mtshon
gru.english: Our own system, the system of Je Tsongkapa, says that the necklace represents giving; the bracelets and anklets the ethical way of life; the earrings patience; the jewel at the top of the head effort; the breastplate meditation; and the waist ornament wisdom.

gru.acip: RJE RIN PO CHES KYANG, SDIG SGRIB SBYONG BA DANG, BGEGS 'JOMS PA DANG, THA MAL GYI SNANG ZHEN 'GAG PA DANG, ZHI RGYAS DBANG DRAG GI DNGOS GRUB 'GRUB PA SOGS DGOS PA DU MA GSUNGS PAS GAL CHE BAS RAB DBANG BZHI YONGS RDZOGS DE MIN BUM DBANG GI NGO BO CHU DBANG GI BYED PA NGAG 'DON DU BKOD PA LTAR DANG,
gru.wylie: rje rin po ches kyang, sdig sgrib sbyong ba dang, bgegs 'joms pa dang, tha mal gyi snang zhen 'gag pa dang, zhi rgyas dbang drag gi dngos grub 'grub pa sogs dgos pa du ma gsungs pas gal che bas rab dbang bzhi yongs rdzogs de min bum dbang gi ngo bo chu dbang gi byed pa ngag 'don du bkod pa ltar dang
gru.english: Out precious Lord, Je Tsongkapa, has said that there are many reasons why you should visualize yourself as the head of the secret world, or His consort.  He says that if you visualize yourself in this way you will reach many goals, including purifying yourself of bad deeds and obstacles; destroying all obstructing forces; stopping the habit of seeing things as normal; and attaining the four modes: learning to be peaceful, generous, powerful, and fierce.  Therefore it is important to do the visualization in this way. Ideally you should try to get visualize all four initiations in their entirety.  However, if this is not possible, you should get the essence of the vase initiation, which is the water empowerment.  This is how I have composed my own recitation text.

gru.acip: GZHAN YANG BSNYEN BSGRUB YAN LAG BZHI ZHES PA, DAM TSIG BSKYED PA BSNYEN PA'I YAN LAG ,SKU BYIN GYIS RLOB PA NYE SGYUB KYI YAN LAG ,YE SHES PA SPYAN 'DREN PA SGRUB PA'I YAN LAG ,DBANG BSKUR RGYAS BDEBS BYED PA SGRUB CHEN GYI YAN LAG STE DE BZHI TSANG BAR 'GYUR BA'O,,
gru.wylie: gzhan yang bsnyen bsgrub yan lag bzhi zhes pa, dam tshig bskyed pa bsnyen pa'i yan lag ,sku byin gyis rlob pa nye sgyub kyi yan lag ,ye shes pa spyan 'dren pa sgrub pa'i yan lag ,dbang bskur rgyas bdebs byed pa sgrub chen gyi yan lag ste de bzhi tshang bar 'gyur ba'o
gru.english: In addition, you should try here to accomplish all four of the components of the practice for getting close.  These four are the components of getting close in which you create the beings of pledge; the component of getting close in which you receive the blessing of Their holy bodies; the component of actual accomplishment, in which you invite the Wisdom Beings to come; and the component of great achievement, where They confer and consummate the initiation.

gru.acip: BUM SGRUB KYI BSZLAS PA 'DI'I NYE SNYING GI BYED PA SA LUGS LA YOD PA 'DRA BAS DGE LUGS LA MI BZHED CING, BYIN RLABS DRUG SKOR BYA BA, RANG SNGAGS KYI BYIN RLABS, SANGS RGYAS MKHA' 'GRO MA'I SNGAGS, SGOM BZHI'I SNGAGS, A'A LI K'A LI, YI GE BRGYA BA'I BYIN RLABS TE SA DGE THAMS CAD BZHED PA DE DAG GIS BDAG GI GZHI BSGYUR BA'O, ,
gru.wylie: bum sgrub kyi bszlas pa 'di'i nye snying gi byed pa sa lugs la yod pa 'dra bas dge lugs la mi bzhed cing, byin rlabs drug skor bya ba, rang sngags kyi byin rlabs, sangs rgyas mkha' 'gro ma'i sngags, sgom bzhi'i sngags, a'a li kA li, yi ge brgya ba'i byin rlabs te sa dge thams cad bzhed pa de dag gis bdag gi gzhi bsgyur ba'o,
gru.english: It seems that, in the Sakya tradition, the words that we recite during the creation of the vase are considered an essence mantra for this Angel of Diamond.  This though is not accepted in the Way of the Pure.  However, the following prayers and practices are accepted by everyone in the Sakya tradition and the Way of the Pure, and you can use all of them as we transform the very foundation of ourselves: 1) The group of the six prayers of blessing; 2) The mantra blessing of oneself; 3) The mantra of the Angel of the Buddhas; 4) The mantra of the four meditations; 5) The words of Ali and Kali; and 6) The Mantra of the Hundred Syllables.

gru.acip: DE LA BRTEN NAS LTE BA'I RTZA MDUD GRU GSUM YOD PA AE DANG, DE DBUS BYANG SEMS DMAR PO YOD PA BAm GYI NGO BOR GNAS PA NANG GI RNAL 'BYOR MA MJAL BAR SHOG CES PA DANG, LTE BA'I BAm YIG STONG PA NYID DANG DBYER MED PA'I RNAL 'BYOR MA'I NGO BO DANG, SPYI BO'I BYANG SEMS DKAR PO BDE BA CHEN PO HE RU KA'I NGO BOR GNAS PA LA PHYI'I RKYEN LAS RGYA DANG MNYAM PAR SBYAR BA LA BRTEN NAS PHYAG RGYA MA'I BHA GA NAS RLUNG SPOS RENG GI DUD PA LTA BU BYUNG BAS RANG GI THUR SEL GYI RLUNG GYEN DU LDOG NAS LTE BA'I GTUM MO'I ME SBAR, SPYI BO'I BYANG SEMS BABS PA'I 'DU 'PHROD BYED PA NANG DANG,
gru.wylie: de la brten nas lte ba'i rtsa mdud gru gsum yod pa ae dang, de dbus byang sems dmar po yod pa baM gyi ngo bor gnas pa nang gi rnal 'byor ma mjal bar shog ces pa dang, lte ba'i baM yig stong pa nyid dang dbyer med pa'i rnal 'byor ma'i ngo bo dang, spyi bo'i byang sems dkar po bde ba chen po he ru ka'i ngo bor gnas pa la phyi'i rkyen las rgya dang mnyam par sbyar ba la brten nas phyag rgya ma'i bha ga nas rlung spos reng gi dud pa lta bu byung bas rang gi thur sel gyi rlung gyen du ldog nas lte ba'i gtum mo'i me sbar, spyi bo'i byang sems babs pa'i 'du 'phrod byed pa nang dang
gru.english: And He is praying that He might then meet the inner Angel of Diamond: the one who resides at the navel in the nature of the e letter of the triangular knot in the channels there; combined with vam letter of the red element of enlightenment found at the middle of this knot. The essence of the Diamond Angel is indivisible from the emptiness of the vam syllable at the navel; and the essence of Heruka is the great bliss of the white element at the center tip of the head.  We then use an outer factor to affect these elements: we go into union with our physical consort. Due to this, inner wind comes from our consort's bhaga, like smoke from a stick of incense.  This wind pushes up our downward-clearing wind, reversing it--which causes the fire of the inner hear to blaze.  The white element falls down from the center tip of the head and starts to wrestle with the red element.  This is the inner Diamond Queen.

whole_word_matches.context: de la brten nas lte ba'i rtsa mdud gru gsum yod pa ae dang, de dbus byang sems dmar po yod pa

gru.acip: 'KHOR BSGYUR RTZIBS KYI MU KHYUD KYI SMON LAM GYI DBANG GIS BDE BA CAN GYI ZHING BSGRUBS PA SOGS LTAR PHAR PHYIN THEG PAR YANG DE LTAR YOD NA, GSANG SNGAGS KYI SKABS DE BAS CHES MYUR LA ZAB PA 'BYUNG STE, SNGAGS KYI KUN SLONG KHYAD PAR BA'I RTZIS ZIN PA'I SGO NAS 'DI LTAR BSGOM NA BSKAL CHEN GRANGS MED MANG PO'I TSOGS SKAD CIG SKAD CIG LA RDZOGS PA 'ONG LA,
gru.wylie: 'khor bsgyur rtsibs kyi mu khyud kyi smon lam gyi dbang gis bde ba can gyi zhing bsgrubs pa sogs ltar phar phyin theg par yang de ltar yod na, gsang sngags kyi skabs de bas ches myur la zab pa 'byung ste, sngags kyi kun slong khyad par ba'i rtsis zin pa'i sgo nas 'di ltar bsgom na bskal chen grangs med mang po'i tshogs skad cig skad cig la rdzogs pa 'ong la
gru.english: Even in the way of the perfections there are prayers like the Circle of Spokes for Emperors of the World, which is so powerful that it can bring one to the Heaven of Joy.  In the teachings of the secret word then there are practices which are even more swift and deep; if one's meditation here is immersed in the exceptional motivation of the secret way, then you can gather in every single instant of the practice the amount of goodness that it would take many "countless" greater eons to complete otherwise.

gru.acip: RTZA LTUNG DANG PO DANG GNYIS PA GNYIS DNGOS GRUB 'PHROG PA'I GEGS CHE SHOS YIN TE, BSNYEN BKUR BYAS PAS NUS MTHU CHE, ,GSANG STE SPYOD PA BAR CHAD NYUNG, ,ZHES GSUNGS PA LTAR,
gru.wylie: rtsa ltung dang po dang gnyis pa gnyis dngos grub 'phrog pa'i gegs che shos yin te, bsnyen bkur byas pas nus mthu che, ,gsang ste spyod pa bar chad nyung, ,zhes gsungs pa ltar
gru.english: Moreover, the first and second of the secret root downfalls are the greatest obstacles that could steal away your spiritual attainments.
