gru.acip: GNYIS PA BSKYED RIM GYI 'BRAS BU 'GRUB PAR SMON PA LA GNYIS, BSKYED RIM GYI 'BRAS BU 'GRUB PAR SMON PA DNGOS DANG, BSKYED RIM GYI 'BRAS BU 'GRUB PA'I THABS KHYAD PAR CAN LA SMON PA'O, ,DANG PO LA GNYIS, LUS MA SPANGS PAR MKHA' SPYOD 'GRUB PAR SMON PA DANG, BAR DO DANG SKYE BA GZHAN DU RJES SU 'DZIN PAR SMON PA'O,,
gru.wylie: gnyis pa bskyed rim gyi 'bras bu 'grub par smon pa la gnyis, bskyed rim gyi 'bras bu 'grub par smon pa dngos dang, bskyed rim gyi 'bras bu 'grub pa'i thabs khyad par can la smon pa'o, ,dang po la gnyis, lus ma spangs par mkha' spyod 'grub par smon pa dang, bar do dang skye ba gzhan du rjes su 'dzin par smon pa'o
gru.english: The second step--praying that we achieve the goals of the stage of creation--can be divided into two parts: the actual prayer to achieve the goals of the creation stage, and a prayer for special methods which achieve these goals.  And the first of these parts we can further divide into two groups: praying to reach Her heaven without giving up ones body, and praying to be taken by Her either in the in-between state or in later lives.

gru.acip: RDO RJE PHAG MO'I BSKYED RIM NGAG BZLAS DANG BCAS PA 'DI MKHA' SPYOD SGRUB PA'I THABS MCHOG TU GYUR PA YIN ZHING RDZOGS RIM LA NGES PAR LTOS MI DGOS PAS BSKYED RIM PHAG MO MKHA' SPYOD CES GSUNGS KYANG DON DU 'DI NYID BSKYED RDZOGS ZUNG 'BREL GYI NYAMS LEN YIN PAS BSKYED RIM GZHAN LAS KHYAD PAR DU 'PHAGS SO,,
gru.wylie: rdo rje phag mo'i bskyed rim ngag bzlas dang bcas pa 'di mkha' spyod sgrub pa'i thabs mchog tu gyur pa yin zhing rdzogs rim la nges par ltos mi dgos pas bskyed rim phag mo mkha' spyod ces gsungs kyang don du 'di nyid bskyed rdzogs zung 'brel gyi nyams len yin pas bskyed rim gzhan las khyad par du 'phags so
gru.english: As Master Tsarchen is saying here, this creation-stage practice of the Diamond Sow, along with the practice of verbal recitation, is actually the highest method for reaching Her heaven; as such it is not completely necessary to delve into the practices of the completion stage.  It is for this reason that this practice of the creation stage has been given the name "Heaven of the Sow."  And since the purpose of this particular practice is to unite the creation and completion stages together, it is considered to be on a completely higher level than other creation-stage practices.

gru.acip: RDZOGS RIM GYI SKABS SU RTZA GSUM 'KHOR LO LNGA'I DBUS SU KHAMS DKAR DMAR GYI 'DU 'PHROD DANG, RLUNG ZHUGS GNAS THIM PA SOGS KYIS RTZA RLUNG THIG LE LAS RUNG DU SGRUB PA'I THABS LAS RANG NYID SNANG MCHED THOB GSUM GYI YE SHES MNGON DU BYAS PA'I RLUNG SEMS TZAM LAS GRUB PA'I SGYU MA'I SKUR DNGOS GNAS LA RDZOGS PA NI KUN RDZOB SGYU MA'I RDZOGS RIM DNGOS DANG, RDZOGS RIM DE'I LAM THAMS CAD KYANG SNYING GA'I SNGAGS 'KHOR GYIS MTSON PA STE,
gru.wylie: rdzogs rim gyi skabs su rtsa gsum 'khor lo lnga'i dbus su khams dkar dmar gyi 'du 'phrod dang, rlung zhugs gnas thim pa sogs kyis rtsa rlung thig le las rung du sgrub pa'i thabs las rang nyid snang mched thob gsum gyi ye shes mngon du byas pa'i rlung sems tsam las grub pa'i sgyu ma'i skur dngos gnas la rdzogs pa ni kun rdzob sgyu ma'i rdzogs rim dngos dang, rdzogs rim de'i lam thams cad kyang snying ga'i sngags 'khor gyis mtshon pa ste
gru.english: At the point when you are practicing the stage of completion, there is a gathering of red and white elements in the center of the five chakras formed by the three channels, winds, and drops.  We use this method to bring on an experience of the three wisdoms: appearance, spread, and attainment, thus completing in concrete reality the transformation into our illusory body--that which is made of winds and mind alone.  And that in fact is the real stage of completion--the part that relates to deceptive reality, or our illusory body.  The entire path of the completion stage as well is encoded within the circle of secret words at the heart.

gru.acip: PHYI NANG GI THABS KYIS RTZA RLUNG THIG LE LAS RUNG DU SGRUB PA'I THABS JE BZANG LAS BDE BA CHEN PO'I YE SHES DANG, YE SHES DES STONG NYID MNGON SUM DU BYAS PA'I NGES DON GYI RDO RJE RNAL 'BYOR MA DON GYI LHAN SKYES BSKYED PA NI DON DAM 'OD GSAL GYI RDZOGS RIM DNGOS DANG,
gru.wylie: phyi nang gi thabs kyis rtsa rlung thig le las rung du sgrub pa'i thabs je bzang las bde ba chen po'i ye shes dang, ye shes des stong nyid mngon sum du byas pa'i nges don gyi rdo rje rnal 'byor ma don gyi lhan skyes bskyed pa ni don dam 'od gsal gyi rdzogs rim dngos dang
gru.english: Then we use inner and outer methods to hone our channels, winds, and drops.  And through this process of purification comes the wisdom of great bliss--that wisdom we then use to bring about the direct perception of emptiness.  This induces the actual simultaneous state--the real Angel of Diamond.  And that in fact is the real stage of completion--the part that relates to ultimate reality, or bringing on the clear light.

gru.acip: RDZOGS RIM DE'I LAM THAMS CAD ZHAR BYUNG RDZOGS RIM GNYIS KYIS MTSON TE, STENG MKHA' SPYOD KYI DGA' 'KHYIL DKAR PO LA BRTEN NAS STONG PA MI RTOG PA BSGRUBS, 'OG RLUNG GI DKYIL 'KHOR DGA' 'KHYIL DMAR PO LA BRTEN NAS BDE BA BSGRUBS, BAR SNYING GA'I SNGAGS 'KHOR SPYI DANG KHYAD PAR BAm YIG GI N'A DA ME 'BAR LA KHAD PA LA BRTEN NAS DROD BSGRUBS,
gru.wylie: rdzogs rim de'i lam thams cad zhar byung rdzogs rim gnyis kyis mtshon te, steng mkha' spyod kyi dga' 'khyil dkar po la brten nas stong pa mi rtog pa bsgrubs, 'og rlung gi dkyil 'khor dga' 'khyil dmar po la brten nas bde ba bsgrubs, bar snying ga'i sngags 'khor spyi dang khyad par baM yig gi nA da me 'bar la khad pa la brten nas drod bsgrubs
gru.english: The entire path of this completion stage is encoded within the two incidental completion stage practices.  The attainment of a non-conceptual perception of emptiness is associated with the white bliss swirl of the upper heaven.  The attainment of bliss is associated with the red bliss swirl at the sphere of the lower wind.  The attainment of inner heat is associated in general with the circle of secret words at the heart, and more specifically with that point when the nada and the vam is about to burst into flame.

gru.acip: RJE BTZUN MA'I SPRUL PA YIN PAR NGES SHES 'DRONGS TE GSOL BA BTAB PAS RDZAS SNGAGS SOGS LA BRTEN NAS NAM MKHA' LA 'GRO NUS PA TZAM GYI MKHA' SPYOD DANG ,NYAMS SNANG DANG RMI LAM LTA BU MA YIN PAR MNGON SUM NYID DU RTEN DE RANG LA MCHOG GI DNGOS GRUB THOB NGES PA'I MKHA' SPYOD RIG PA 'DZIN PA'I GRONG KHYER DU LAG PA'I 'KHRIG MA NAS BZUNG STE 'KHRID PAR SHOG CIG ,CES SMON PA'O,
gru.wylie: rje btsun ma'i sprul pa yin par nges shes 'drongs te gsol ba btab pas rdzas sngags sogs la brten nas nam mkha' la 'gro nus pa tsam gyi mkha' spyod dang ,nyams snang dang rmi lam lta bu ma yin par mngon sum nyid du rten de rang la mchog gi dngos grub thob nges pa'i mkha' spyod rig pa 'dzin pa'i grong khyer du lag pa'i 'khrig ma nas bzung ste 'khrid par shog cig ,ces smon pa'o
gru.english: ...May it quickly dawn on me that she really is an emanation of the Holy Angel. And after I have begged Her, may She then grab me by the wrist and lead me away to Her heaven, that city of women of sacred knowledge--not just the heaven of being able to fly in the sky after using some magic potion or incantation; not just in a vision or a dream; but Her true paradise, that actual place where I then reach the highest goal. Wandering

gru.acip: ,SINDHUR LANGGA LI YI SDONG BUR BCAS, ,RO LDAN GNAS SU BSGRUBS SHING YUL KUN TU, ,MYUL BA'I GANG GI MDZOD SPUR 'KHYIL RIS CAN, ,'PHOS PA'I MDZES MAS MKHA' SPYOD 'KHRID PAR SHOG , CES PA STE,
gru.wylie: sindhur langga li yi sdong bur bcas, ,ro ldan gnas su bsgrubs shing yul kun tu, ,myul ba'i gang gi mdzod spur 'khyil ris can, ,'phos pa'i mdzes mas mkha' spyod 'khrid par shog , ces pa ste
gru.english: And by this power May I use the sindhura And the trunk of Langali To practice in The home of the dead And then go wandering off To places far and near; And when I meet the one Where the drawing of the swirl Moves off to the spot In between Her brows, May the Lovely One Lead me off To the Heaven of the Angel.

gru.acip: DE YANG GONG DU BSHAD PA LTAR GYI DBANG PO RAB BZLAS BSGOM TZAM GYIS GROL BA'I RE BA CHE BA MED TSE 'BRING SINDHU RA'I BSGRUB PA BYA DGOS PAS
gru.wylie: de yang gong du bshad pa ltar gyi dbang po rab bzlas bsgom tsam gyis grol ba'i re ba che ba med tshe 'bring sindhu ra'i bsgrub pa bya dgos pas
gru.english: Then as I explained earlier, those of highest capacity can use simply meditation and recitation to reach freedom; but those who do not think this very likely to happen are practitioners of medium capacity, and so if they want to reach freedom in this life, they need to do the practice of sindhura.

gru.acip: 'DI LA BSNYEN PA DANG, BSGRUB PA DANG, LAS SBYOR GSUM YOD PA NYAMS SU LEN TSUL ZIN BRIS LTAR LA,
gru.wylie: 'di la bsnyen pa dang, bsgrub pa dang, las sbyor gsum yod pa nyams su len tshul zin bris ltar la
gru.english: In order to go about this, there are three steps: first, you must do a close retreat; next, you must perform certain special rituals; and finally, you must live out and apply these holy activities.  You should follow the method for practicing those as it has been describe in the Notes.

gru.acip: BSGRUB PA'I SKABS SU SINDHU RA'I DKYIL 'KHOR DA LTA'I PAR 'DEBS RGYU'I PHYAG LEN 'DI RANG GIS THUS SHIG ,BZLAS BA'I TSE MDUN BSKYED KYI THUGS KAR CHOS 'BYUNG DMAR PO GRU GSUM NYIS BRTZEGS KYI NANG DU ZHES SOGS BRJOD NAS BZLAS DMIGS SPYI DANG,
gru.wylie: bsgrub pa'i skabs su sindhu ra'i dkyil 'khor da lta'i par 'debs rgyu'i phyag len 'di rang gis thus shig ,bzlas ba'i tshe mdun bskyed kyi thugs kar chos 'byung dmar po gru gsum nyis brtsegs kyi nang du zhes sogs brjod nas bzlas dmigs spyi dang
gru.english: When you reach the point of the second step, where you are performing the special rituals, then you should be collecting together now, from the sindhura mandala, the powder that you will be using to mark yourself.  Then as you do your recitation, use in general the usual recitation visualization where you picture a red dharma star made of two triangular sections stacked together at the holy heart of the Being in front of you, and so forth.

whole_word_matches.context: a'i tshe mdun bskyed kyi thugs kar chos 'byung dmar po gru gsum nyis brtsegs kyi nang du zhes sogs brjod nas bzla

gru.acip: GROGS KYIS 'CHANG DGOS PA'I RNAL 'BYOR PA'I DBYUG PA'I RING THUNG 'DOM PHYED DANG, LAG PA GNYIS KYI SOR MO SNYING GAR RTZE SPRAD PA'I GRU MO PHAN TSUN GYI MTHA'I TSAD DON 'DRA LA, DBYIBS NI RGYU SBA YIN STABS BZLUM POR NGES SHING, SBOM PHRA BSHAD PA MED KYANG TSAD GANG TZAM GYIS CHOG PAR MNGON NO,,
gru.wylie: grogs kyis 'chang dgos pa'i rnal 'byor pa'i dbyug pa'i ring thung 'dom phyed dang, lag pa gnyis kyi sor mo snying gar rtse sprad pa'i gru mo phan tshun gyi mtha'i tshad don 'dra la, dbyibs ni rgyu sba yin stabs bzlum por nges shing, sbom phra bshad pa med kyang tshad gang tsam gyis chog par mngon no
gru.english: Now for the yogi's staff which a friend must hold for you: it should be a half dom (armspan) in length.  This is about the same as the measurement you get when you place the tips of your fingers at your heart and spread your elbows out to the sides, from the tip of one elbow to the tip of the other.  Since it needs to be kept hidden, the tree you take if from should have a smooth cylindrical shape.  Its thickness has not been clarified, but it would appear that whatever it happens to be is allowable.

whole_word_matches.context: ng, lag pa gnyis kyi sor mo snying gar rtse sprad pa'i gru mo phan tshun gyi mtha'i tshad don 'dra la, dbyibs ni

gru.acip: SINDHU RGYA SKAD DANG, BOD SKAD LI KHRI, DE DANG LANGGA LI'I SHING SOGS YO BYAD DANG PHYAG LEN MA 'DZOL BA'I SGO NAS, RO LDAN TE DUR 'KHROD KYI GNAS SU BSGRUBS SHING YUL PHYOGS THAMS CAD DU MYUL BA STE 'KHYAMS PAS
gru.wylie: sindhu rgya skad dang, bod skad li khri, de dang langga li'i shing sogs yo byad dang phyag len ma 'dzol ba'i sgo nas, ro ldan te dur 'khrod kyi gnas su bsgrubs shing yul phyogs thams cad du myul ba ste 'khyams pas
gru.english: Once all this completed, then take all the essentials--such as the Sindhura powder (as it is called in Sanskrit, or Litri in Tibetan); and a Langali trunk; and your own spiritual observances free of any errors--and practice in the home of the dead (meaning in a burial ground, surrounded by corpses).  And then go wandering off--journey at random--in every direction, to places both far away and nearby.

gru.acip: GONG DU BSHAD PA LTAR GYI BZLAS SGOM DANG, SINDHU RA'I SGRUB PA SOGS BYAS KYANG MA GRUB PA'AM, DE LTA BU LAG TU MA LON PAS TSE 'DIR LUS MA SPANGS PAR MKHA' SPYOD DU BGROD MI NUS NA DBANG PO THA MA STE,
gru.wylie: gong du bshad pa ltar gyi bzlas sgom dang, sindhu ra'i sgrub pa sogs byas kyang ma grub pa'am, de lta bu lag tu ma lon pas tshe 'dir lus ma spangs par mkha' spyod du bgrod mi nus na dbang po tha ma ste
gru.english: This verse is talking about someone who either carried out the recitation and meditation and the practice of sindhura as I have described above, but still didn't reach Her; or, someone who did not actually truly carry out these practices fully.  In either case, if someone finds that they cannot travel to Her Heaven without giving up their present body, then they are a practitioner of lowest capacity.

gru.acip: GAL TE DE LTA BU YANG LE LO SOGS KYIS MA GRUB NA DBANG PO THA MA'I YANG THA MA STE, DES KYANG DBANG DANG BYIN RLABS MTSAN NYID TSANG BA LEGS PAR THOB NAS DAM SDOM MA NYAMS PA'AM, NYAMS KYANG 'CHI KHA TSUN CHAD LA BSHAGS BSDAMS SNGON DU 'GRO BAS DBANG ZHU BA DANG, BDAG 'JUG LEN PA CI RIGS KYI SGO NAS SNGAGS SDOM SOR CHUD DE RTZA LTUNG GIS MA GOS NA, SKYE BA GSUM MAM, LNGA'AM, BDUN NAM, MA THA BCU DRUG TSUN LA MCHOG GI DNGOS GRUB THOB PAR GSUNGS SO,,
gru.wylie: gal te de lta bu yang le lo sogs kyis ma grub na dbang po tha ma'i yang tha ma ste, des kyang dbang dang byin rlabs mtshan nyid tshang ba legs par thob nas dam sdom ma nyams pa'am, nyams kyang 'chi kha tshun chad la bshags bsdams sngon du 'gro bas dbang zhu ba dang, bdag 'jug len pa ci rigs kyi sgo nas sngags sdom sor chud de rtsa ltung gis ma gos na, skye ba gsum mam, lnga'am, bdun nam, ma tha bcu drug tshun la mchog gi dngos grub thob par gsungs so
gru.english: Those of us who are too lazy to accomplish even this much are categorized as the very lowest of the low.  But even this kind of person has received a proper empowerment and blessing, complete in all of their necessary components.  And it has been stated that once that has transpired, then if they have not broken their pledges and vows; or if they have broken them, but at some point before the time of their death they restore their secret vows--first by confessing and swearing and then by either requesting empowerment or taking self-initiation; then unless this person has been sullied by a new root downfall, they will reach their highest goals either in three lifetimes, or five, or seven, or at the very most within sixteen lifetimes.

gru.acip: DES NA GAL TE ZHES PA BRTAG PA THA ZUNG GI DON TE, RGYA GAL TE BSGOM BZLAS SOGS LA 'BAD KYANG TSE 'DIR MKHA' SPYOD DU BGROD NAS RTEN DE LA GROL BAR NGES PA'I NUS PA THOB PAR MA GYUR KYANG, DA DUNG LE LO DANG THE TSOM MED PAR RTZE GCIG TU 'BAD PA'I MTHU LA BRTEN NAS, BAR DO'I GNAS NAS DPA' BO MKHA' 'GROS MKHA' SPYOD DU BSU BA'AM, DE YANG MA GRUB NA RING POR MI THOGS PA MA THA SKYE BA BCU DRUG TSUN LA, DAG PA MKHA' SPYOD KYI DGA' MA RJE BTZUN RDO RJE RNAL 'BYOR MAS RJES SU 'DZIN PAR SHOG CIG, CES SMON PA'O,,
gru.wylie: des na gal te zhes pa brtag pa tha zung gi don te, rgya gal te bsgom bzlas sogs la 'bad kyang tshe 'dir mkha' spyod du bgrod nas rten de la grol bar nges pa'i nus pa thob par ma gyur kyang, da dung le lo dang the tshom med par rtse gcig tu 'bad pa'i mthu la brten nas, bar do'i gnas nas dpa' bo mkha' 'gros mkha' spyod du bsu ba'am, de yang ma grub na ring por mi thogs pa ma tha skye ba bcu drug tshun la, dag pa mkha' spyod kyi dga' ma rje btsun rdo rje rnal 'byor mas rjes su 'dzin par shog cig, ces smon pa'o
gru.english: Thus the expression in the verse--in case it comes--is stating some theoretical possibility: "if by some wild chance" I make efforts in practices such as meditation and recitation but it doesn't happen that I travel to the Heaven of the Angel before I die, and with that body and mind attain the power that makes it certain that I will become liberated, then at least now may I give up all laziness.  May I give up all doubt, and throw myself into one-pointed efforts in my practice; and by this force may it come--we are praying--that the warriors and their angels come to greet me during the state between death and rebirth.  But even if that doesn't happen, still before very long--that is, within the length of 16 lifetimes--may I be led away by the lover from Heaven, by the Diamond Queen. The Door of the Pure One

gru.acip: GNYIS PA BSKYED RIM GYI 'BRAS BU 'GRUB PA'I THABS KHYAD PAR CAN LA SMON PA LA GNYIS, MYUR LAM 'PHO BA'I RNAL 'BYOR LA SOMON PA DANG, BSAM MI KHYAB MTHUN MONG MA YING PA LA SMON PA'O, ,DANG PO NI,
gru.wylie: gnyis pa bskyed rim gyi 'bras bu 'grub pa'i thabs khyad par can la smon pa la gnyis, myur lam 'pho ba'i rnal 'byor la somon pa dang, bsam mi khyab mthun mong ma ying pa la smon pa'o, ,dang po ni
gru.english: We are now on the second half of praying to achieve the goals of the stage of creation -- praying for special methods which achieve these goals.  There are two prayers for this: the prayer for the quick path -- the deep practice of transferring our consciousness; and the prayer for the unique practice of the inconceivable.  Here is the first:

gru.acip: YANG GZUGS MED KHAMS SU SKYE NA MA GTOGS BAR DO YOD PAR GSUNGS LA, DBANG PO THA MA BAR DOR DPA' BO MKHA' 'GROS BSU YANG BAR DO GRUB DGOS PAS DE'I 'JIGS SKRAG SOGS MYONG MI DGOS PA'I PHYIR GSUNGS PAR BZHED PA SOGS YOD KYANG
gru.wylie: yang gzugs med khams su skye na ma gtogs bar do yod par gsungs la, dbang po tha ma bar dor dpa' bo mkha' 'gros bsu yang bar do grub dgos pas de'i 'jigs skrag sogs myong mi dgos pa'i phyir gsungs par bzhed pa sogs yod kyang
gru.english: Now unless one has been in the formless realm, the texts state that you will have an in-between state birth.  And it is there that those practioners of lowest capacity are escorted to heaven by Warriors and their Angels.  But the whole experience of getting there is terrifying.  And so there are some who have expressed the opinion that this practice was designed for those lowest capacity practioners, so that they could avoid all fear and anxiety associated with the in-between state.

gru.acip: SGRUB KHANG DANG RANG GI LUS LA 'JA' ZUG PA DANG, SINDHU RA DANG ME TOG GI CHAR 'BAB PA DANG, RGYU MED PAR DRI ZHIM PO LDANG BA DANG, SPYI BO SKRANGS PA DANG, RANG KHRAG 'DZAG PA SOGS MKHA' SPYOD 'GRUB PA'I RTAGS KHYAD PAR CAN MA BYUNG GI BAR DU SBYONG ZHING, DE NAS MA BRJED TZAM BYED PA LAS SBYONG KHA THAL NA 'PHO RAB TSE THUNG ZHES TSE LA GNOD PAR GSUNGS SO,,
gru.wylie: sgrub khang dang rang gi lus la 'ja' zug pa dang, sindhu ra dang me tog gi char 'bab pa dang, rgyu med par dri zhim po ldang ba dang, spyi bo skrangs pa dang, rang khrag 'dzag pa sogs mkha' spyod 'grub pa'i rtags khyad par can ma byung gi bar du sbyong zhing, de nas ma brjed tsam byed pa las sbyong kha thal na 'pho rab tshe thung zhes tshe la gnod par gsungs so
gru.english: Then at the end a rainbow comes down and pierces through your meditation hut and your body.  A rain of flowers and sindhura falls.  A sweet scent rises up out of nowhere, and the crown of your head starts to swell.  Your own blood drips down.  Keep practicing until these kind of special signs come that you are reaching Her heaven.  Right now, we should only practice this until we're sure we won't forget how to do it.  Otherwise, if we practice it too much, it has been stated that it will hurt our life-energy, for as they say: "The better the sending, the shorter the life."

gru.acip: RGYUD THAMS CAD KYI DON GYI BCUD KHYUNG BA SLOB DPON NAG PO PAS BKRAL BA RGYAS PA DANG, GRUB CHEN DRIL BU PAS RJE BTZUN RDO RJE RNAL 'BYOR MA LA DNGOS SU MNOS PA DRIL BU RIM LNGA 'BRING PO, GRUB CHEN L'U AI PAS SLOB DPON SHA WA RI PA STE BOD SKAD DU RI KHROD DBANG PHYUG LA NOS PA RDZOGS RIM BSDU BA GSUM PA SOGS BZHUGS KYANG DE THAMS CAD LAS ZAB CING CHES KHYAD PAR 'PHAGS PA NI ZAB DON DRIL BU'I SKOR RDO RJE RNAL 'BYOR MAS DRIL BU PAR GNANG BA DANG, YANG ZAB N'A RO'I SKOR, N'A RO PA LA RNAL 'BYOR MAS GNANG BA STE
gru.wylie: rgyud thams cad kyi don gyi bcud khyung ba slob dpon nag po pas bkral ba rgyas pa dang, grub chen dril bu pas rje btsun rdo rje rnal 'byor ma la dngos su mnos pa dril bu rim lnga 'bring po, grub chen lU ai pas slob dpon sha wa ri pa ste bod skad du ri khrod dbang phyug la nos pa rdzogs rim bsdu ba gsum pa sogs bzhugs kyang de thams cad las zab cing ches khyad par 'phags pa ni zab don dril bu'i skor rdo rje rnal 'byor mas dril bu par gnang ba dang, yang zab nA ro'i skor, nA ro pa la rnal 'byor mas gnang ba ste
gru.english: What did come to us though are treatments of the ancient tantras which extract for us the very cream of all these secret teachings.  We have the expanded commentary on the stage of completion left to us by Master Krishnapada.  And then there is the medium-length treatment of this same stage in the Five Stages of Ghantapada, a teaching that famed adept Ghantapada was granted directly at the feet of the Holy Angel of Diamond.  So too there is the abbreviated presentation of the completion stage which the famed adept Luipa was granted at the feet of Master Shavari, whose name we translate into Tibetan as Ritrupa, or The Hermit.  But most profound of all these profound presentations is the collection of teachings concerning the Angel who took Naropa to Her Heaven: teachings which were granted to Naropa by the Diamond Angel.

gru.acip: ,SHIN TU ZAB PA'I RGYUD SDE'I GNAD BSDUS PA, ,GRUB PA'I DBANG PHYUG TE LO N'A RO NAS, ,RIM BZHIN BRGYUD PA N'A RO CHOS DRUG CES, ,SNYAN PA'I GRAGS PAS PHYOGS KUN RAB KHYAB PA'I, ,LAM 'DIR 'BAD LAS SKAL LDAN MTHA' YAS KYI, ,RNAM PAR 'DREN PA'I GO 'PHANG MTHOR GSHEGS PA'I, ,GDUNG RABS 'DZIN PA'I GSUNG GIS NAN TAN DU, ,YANG YANG BSKUL PHYIR LAM DE 'DIR BSHAD BYA,
gru.wylie: shin tu zab pa'i rgyud sde'i gnad bsdus pa, ,grub pa'i dbang phyug te lo nA ro nas, ,rim bzhin brgyud pa nA ro chos drug ces, ,snyan pa'i grags pas phyogs kun rab khyab pa'i, ,lam 'dir 'bad las skal ldan mtha' yas kyi, ,rnam par 'dren pa'i go 'phang mthor gshegs pa'i, ,gdung rabs 'dzin pa'i gsung gis nan tan du, ,yang yang bskul phyir lam de 'dir bshad bya
gru.english: Its fame has spread to every land; The "Six Practices of Naropa," Handed down from those two lords Of spiritual accomplishment, From Telopa and Naropa, A teaching that incorporates Every crucial point Of the deepest of secret teachings. There have come to me great holders Of the lineage of our forefathers, Persons who've attained the heights Of that great Guide of living kind, Countless ones of the fortune That comes from doing good, Ones who have devoted themselves To the path of Naropa's way; And they have spoken to me urgently, And entreated me to give them Explanation of this teaching-- For them then I begin.

gru.acip: GRUB PA'I DBANG PHYUG JO BO N'A RO TA PAS RGYUD SDE RGYA MTSO'I SNYING PO'I BCUD PHYUNG BA'I GDAMS PA ZAB MO N'A RO CHOS DRUG TU GRAGS PA'I BSHAD KHRID, LUS SBYONG N'A RO DRUG SKOR 'BEBS KYI SKOR SOGS DANG, LAG KHRID BCAS RJE BDAG NYID CHEN PO'I GSUNG KHRID YIG YID CHES GSUM LDAN GYI STENG NAS NYAMS KHRID BZHI BSHAD KYI TSUL DU LEGS PAR THOB PA'I BRGYUD PA NI,
gru.wylie: grub pa'i dbang phyug jo bo nA ro ta pas rgyud sde rgya mtsho'i snying po'i bcud phyung ba'i gdams pa zab mo nA ro chos drug tu grags pa'i bshad khrid, lus sbyong nA ro drug skor 'bebs kyi skor sogs dang, lag khrid bcas rje bdag nyid chen po'i gsung khrid yig yid ches gsum ldan gyi steng nas nyams khrid bzhi bshad kyi tshul du legs par thob pa'i brgyud pa ni
gru.english: Here is the complete lineage for instructions I have received, in four different ways, upon what are known as the "Six Practices of Naropa"--advices that represent the inner essence drawn from the ocean of the various groups of secret teachings by that absolute lord of all accomplished saints, the Lord, Narotapa.  I have received commentarial teachings; instructions on the various practices of the body among the six, on how substances descend and so forth; teachings through private demonstrations; and experiential teachings based on the presentation by the Lord, the Great Being Tsongkapa, entitled The Book of Three Beliefs.

gru.acip: BCOM LDAN 'DAS DPAL 'KHOR LO SDOM PA, TEE LO SHES RAB BZANG PO, N'A RO TA PA 'JIGS MED GRAGS PA, MAR STON CHOS KYI BLO GROS, MID LA BZHAD PA'I RDO RJE, MNYAM MED DVAGS PO LHA RJE, 'GRO MGON PHAG MO GRUB, 'BRI GUNG 'JIG RTEN GSUM MGON, SPYAN SNGA RIN CHEN MGON PO, KUN LDAN RAS PA,
gru.wylie: bcom ldan 'das dpal 'khor lo sdom pa, tee lo shes rab bzang po, nA ro ta pa 'jigs med grags pa, mar ston chos kyi blo gros, mid la bzhad pa'i rdo rje, mnyam med dvags po lha rje, 'gro mgon phag mo grub, 'bri gung 'jig rten gsum mgon, spyan snga rin chen mgon po, kun ldan ras pa
gru.english: 1) The Conqueror, the Glorious Union of the Spheres (Chakra Samvara) 2) Telopa Sherab Sangpo (10th century) 3) Narotapa Jikme Drakpa (d. 1027) 4) Martun Chukyi Lodru (1012-1097) 5) Mila Shepay Dorje (1040-1123) 6) The matchless Dakpo Hlaje (1079-1153) 7) Drogun Pakmo Drup (1110-1170) 8) Drigung Jikten Sumgun Rinchen Pel (1143-1217) 9) Chennga Rinchen Gunpo 10) Kunden Repa (1148-1217)

gru.acip: SGRA BSGYUR BYAMS PA DPAL BA, RJE BSOD NAMS DBANG PHYUG, RGYAL SRAS BSOD NAMS SENG GE, RJE YANG RTZE BA, CHOS RJE BU STON RIN PO CHE, DPAL LDAN BLA MA DAM PA BSOD NAMS RGYAL MTSAN, SPYAN SNGA RIN PO CHE GRAGS PA BYANG CHUB, RJE BTZUN BLA MA TZONG KHA PA CHEN PO, MKHAS GRUB DGE LEGS DPAL BZANG, BA SO CHOS KYI RGYAL MTSAN,
gru.wylie: sgra bsgyur byams pa dpal ba, rje bsod nams dbang phyug, rgyal sras bsod nams seng ge, rje yang rtse ba, chos rje bu ston rin po che, dpal ldan bla ma dam pa bsod nams rgyal mtshan, spyan snga rin po che grags pa byang chub, rje btsun bla ma tsong kha pa chen po, mkhas grub dge legs dpal bzang, ba so chos kyi rgyal mtshan
gru.english: 11) The translator Jampa Pelwa (1173-1225) 12) The Lord Sunam Wangchuk 13) The bodhisattva Sunam Sengge 14) The Lord Yangtsewa 15) The Dharma Lord Buton Rinpoche (1290-1364) 16) The good and glorious Lama Sunam Gyeltsen (1312-1376) 17) Chengga Rinpoche Drakpa Jangchub (b. 1356) 18) The holy lama, Tsongkapa the Great (1357-1419) 19) Kedrup Gelek Pelsang (1385-1438) 20) Baso Chukyi Gyeltsen (1402-1473)

gru.acip: GRUB CHEN CHOS RDO RJE, RGYAL BA BLO BZANG DON GRUB, MKHAS GRUB SANGS RGYAS YE SHES, PAn CHEN THAMS CAD MKHYEN PA BLO BZANG CHOS KYI RGYAL MTSAN, KUN SPANGS RTA PHUG PA DAM CHOS RGYAL MTSAN, GRUB THOB SMAN KHANG PA NGAG DBANG CHOS 'PHEL, MKHAN CHEN DPAL 'BYOR GRAGS PA, KLONG RDOL BLA MA NGAG DBANG BLO BZANG, 'JOG RI NGAG DBANG BSTAN 'DZIN, LHA RTZE YE SHES BSTAN 'DZIN,
gru.wylie: grub chen chos rdo rje, rgyal ba blo bzang don grub, mkhas grub sangs rgyas ye shes, paN chen thams cad mkhyen pa blo bzang chos kyi rgyal mtshan, kun spangs rta phug pa dam chos rgyal mtshan, grub thob sman khang pa ngag dbang chos 'phel, mkhan chen dpal 'byor grags pa, klong rdol bla ma ngag dbang blo bzang, 'jog ri ngag dbang bstan 'dzin, lha rtse ye shes bstan 'dzin
gru.english: 21) The great and accomplished Chu Dorje 22) The Victor, (Wensapa) Lobsang Dundrup (1505-1566) 23) Kedrup Sanggye Yeshe (1525-1591) 24) The All-Knowing Panchen, Lobsang Chukyi Gyeltsen (1565-1662) 25) Kunpang Tapukpa Damchu Gyeltsen (1595-1607) 26) The accomplished saint, Menkangpa Ngawang Chupel (1635-1707) 27) Kenchen Peljor Drakpa 28) Longdol Lama Ngawang Lobsang (1719-1795) 29) Jokri Ngawang Tendzin (b. 1748) 30) Hlatse Yeshe Tendzin

gru.acip: 7YANG NA, SMAN KHANG PA NAS, PHUR LCOG NGAG DBANG BYAMS PA, YONGS 'DZIN YE SHES RGYAL MTSAN, RJE NGAG DBANG BSTAN DAR, BSHES GNYEN YE SHES BSTAN 'DZIN, RJE 'JAM DPAL TSUL KHRIMS, YONGS 'DZIN BYAMS PA KUN KHYAB, RGYAL SRAS BSKAL BZANG BSTAN 'DZIN, RDO RJE 'CHANG SKAL BZANG MKHAS GRUB BAM, CHOS KYI RDO RJE, KHYAB BDAG 'KHOR LO'I MGON PO YAB RJE PADMA BADZRA DPAL BZANG PO, DES BDAG LA DGYES BZHIN DU STZAL,
gru.wylie: 7yang na, sman khang pa nas, phur lcog ngag dbang byams pa, yongs 'dzin ye shes rgyal mtshan, rje ngag dbang bstan dar, bshes gnyen ye shes bstan 'dzin, rje 'jam dpal tshul khrims, yongs 'dzin byams pa kun khyab, rgyal sras bskal bzang bstan 'dzin, rdo rje 'chang skal bzang mkhas grub bam, chos kyi rdo rje, khyab bdag 'khor lo'i mgon po yab rje padma badzra dpal bzang po, des bdag la dgyes bzhin du stsal
gru.english: The lineage also splits like this: 26) Menkangpa (1635-1707) 27) Purchok Ngawang Jampa (1682-1762) 28) The Tutor, Yeshe Gyeltsen (1713-1793) 29) The Lord, Ngawang Tendar (Alaksha Ngawang Tendar) (b. 1759) 30) The Great Spiritual Friend, Yeshe Tendzin 31) The Lord, Jampel Tsultrim 32) The Tutor, Jampa Kunkyab 33) The Bodhisattva Prince, Kelsang Tendzin 34) The Keeper of the Diamond, Kelsang Kedrup, also known as Chukyi Dorje 35) The Good and Glorious Padma Vajra, Lord Over a Secret World, Savior of the Retinue, and Our Spiritual Father (1876-1941 [?]) 36) and from him, to myself, granted joyfully.

gru.acip: 7YANG ZAB LAM N'A RO CHOS DRUG GI KHRID YIG, DGA' LDAN NAG TSANG BLO BZANG BSTAN PA DAR RGYAS KYIS MDZAD PA'I YIG CHA'I STENG NAS NYAMS KHRID ZAB MO LUS SBYONG N'A RO DRUG SKOR GYI LAG KHRID DANG BCAS PA LEGS PAR NOS PA'I BRGYUD PA NI, NAG TSANG RDO RJE 'CHANG BSTAN PA DAR RGYAS, TRE HOR KHANG GSAR SKYABS MGON BLO BZANG TSUL KHRIMS BSTAN PA'I RGYAL MTSAN, NAGS SHOD STAG PHU RDO RJE 'CHANG NGAG DBANG BLO BZANG DPAL BZANG LDAN 'JAM DPAL BSTAN PA'I DNGOS GRUB DPAL BZANG PO'I ZHAL SNGA NAS, BDAG LA DGYES BZHIN DU STZAL TO,,
gru.wylie: 7yang zab lam nA ro chos drug gi khrid yig, dga' ldan nag tshang blo bzang bstan pa dar rgyas kyis mdzad pa'i yig cha'i steng nas nyams khrid zab mo lus sbyong nA ro drug skor gyi lag khrid dang bcas pa legs par nos pa'i brgyud pa ni, nag tshang rdo rje 'chang bstan pa dar rgyas, tre hor khang gsar skyabs mgon blo bzang tshul khrims bstan pa'i rgyal mtshan, nags shod stag phu rdo rje 'chang ngag dbang blo bzang dpal bzang ldan 'jam dpal bstan pa'i dngos grub dpal bzang po'i zhal snga nas, bdag la dgyes bzhin du stsal to
gru.english: There is also the lineage through which the book of instructions on the deep path of the Six Practices of Naropa--along with the profound teachings of personal experience based on the text composed by Lobsang Tenpa Dargye of the Naktsang College of Ganden, and the private instructions on the practices of the body known as the six topics of Naropa--has been imparted so well: 1) The Keeper of the Diamond from Naktsang, Tenpa Dargye 2) Lobsang Tsultrim Tenpay Gyeltsen, our Refuge and Protector, from the New House of Trehor College (aka Drupkangpa, 1848-?) 3) The Good and Glorious Ngawang Lobsang of Takpu, Keeper of the Diamond, from Nakshu College; the Good and Glorious Jampel Tenpay Ngudrup 4) And from his holy lips, granted joyfully to myself.]

gru.acip: DES NA CHOS RJE PHAG MO GRU PA SOGS 'GA' ZHIG GI ,CHOS DRUG GI KHRID YIG NA LAM THUN MONG BA'I KHRID TSUL MI SNANG BA NI, TSOGS KHRID LAM RIM BZHIN DU KHRID PA'I RJES SU GDAMS NGAG 'DI STER BA'I LUGS SU SNANG BAS, YANG DGON PA'I KHRID YIG NA 'DUG PA BZHIN, LAM THUN MONG BA LA SNGON DU 'KHRID PA SHIN TU GNAD CHE BAR ZUNGS SHIG ,
gru.wylie: des na chos rje phag mo gru pa sogs 'ga' zhig gi ,chos drug gi khrid yig na lam thun mong ba'i khrid tshul mi snang ba ni, tshogs khrid lam rim bzhin du khrid pa'i rjes su gdams ngag 'di ster ba'i lugs su snang bas, yang dgon pa'i khrid yig na 'dug pa bzhin, lam thun mong ba la sngon du 'khrid pa shin tu gnad che bar zungs shig
gru.english: Therefore we can say that the fact that--in the books of instruction on the six practices written by the Dharma Lord Pakmo Drupa and some others--we find no sections on guiding the student along the path that is shared, appears to reflect a system of teaching where these advices were granted only after a more public teaching on something like the steps of the path.  You should therefore consider it an extremely crucial point that the student should first be guided along the path which is shared, just as we see it in the book of instructions by Yang Gunpa. [Translator's note: The victorious Yang Gunpa Gyeltsen Pel (1213-1258) was a master of the Drukpa Kagyu tradition.  He seems to fit into the lineage as follows: he was a student of Chen-nga Drakpa Jungne, who was a student of Drikung Jikten Sumgun, who was a student of Pakmo Drupa, who was a student of Gampopa Dakpo Hlaje, who was a student of Jetsun Milarepa.]

whole_word_matches.context: des na chos rje phag mo gru pa sogs 'ga' zhig gi ,chos drug gi khrid yig na lam th

gru.acip: 'DI NI RJE BTZUN BYAMS PA NAS THOGS MED DANG, RJE BTZUN 'JAM DBYANGS NAS KLU SGRUB DANG, ZHI BA LHA LA BRGYUD PA'I CHU BO GSUM 'DRES KYI, GDAMS PA RDO RJE THEG PA DANG, PHAR PHYIN THEG PA GANG GI SGOR 'JUG KYANG BYA DGOS PAR JO BO CHEN PO BZHED DO,,
gru.wylie: 'di ni rje btsun byams pa nas thogs med dang, rje btsun 'jam dbyangs nas klu sgrub dang, zhi ba lha la brgyud pa'i chu bo gsum 'dres kyi, gdams pa rdo rje theg pa dang, phar phyin theg pa gang gi sgor 'jug kyang bya dgos par jo bo chen po bzhed do
gru.english: On this same point, Lord Atisha expressed the position that these advices, which combine three great currents of teaching--those passed down to Master Asanga from the holy Maitreya, those come to the realized being Nagarjuna from the holy Manjushri, and those descended through Master Shantideva--are an absolute necessity, whether one hopes to enter the gateway of the diamond way, or that of the way of the perfections.

gru.acip: STONG RA LA RTOG BZO GZHAN MANG PO 'DUG NA'ANG, DPAL PHAG MO GRU PA'I KHRID YIG LAS DE TZAM ZHIG LAS MI 'BYUNG STE, DE GAS CHOG GO ,STONG RA LUS SBYONG 'DI DAG RGYA GZHUNG KHUNGS THUB CHE BA LAS MI 'BYUNG YANG, BLA MA RNAMS KYI MAN NGAG GIS MDZAD 'DUG LA, DE YANG RTZA RLUNG SGOM PA LA 'JAM SBYOR GYIS TING NGE 'DZIN SKYE DKA' BAR BYUNG NA, DRAG SBYOR GYIS BYED PA LA 'DI DAG SBYANGS NA GEGS CHUNG BA LA BSAMS SO,,
gru.wylie: stong ra la rtog bzo gzhan mang po 'dug na'ang, dpal phag mo gru pa'i khrid yig las de tsam zhig las mi 'byung ste, de gas chog go ,stong ra lus sbyong 'di dag rgya gzhung khungs thub che ba las mi 'byung yang, bla ma rnams kyi man ngag gis mdzad 'dug la, de yang rtsa rlung sgom pa la 'jam sbyor gyis ting nge 'dzin skye dka' bar byung na, drag sbyor gyis byed pa la 'di dag sbyangs na gegs chung ba la bsams so
gru.english: There are many other details of the practice of the empty form that have just been made up by people; what you actually find in the treatise of the glorious Pakmo Druppa though is no more than what I've put here, and it's enough. These practices of the empty form and the physical exercises do not appear in any very authoritative scripture of classical Indian Buddhism; nonetheless, they do represent oral advices of the Lamas of the lineage.  Their intended use, again, is in a case where you are utilizing drastic methods to work with your channels and winds because you have found it difficult to reach the required level of concentration by employing more gentle methods.  The idea is that, if you train yourself in these first, you will encounter fewer obstacles.

whole_word_matches.context: ra la rtog bzo gzhan mang po 'dug na'ang, dpal phag mo gru pa'i khrid yig las de tsam zhig las mi 'byung ste, de

gru.acip: DPAL PHAG MO GRU PAS MDZAD PA NA YANG, SNGON DU DBANG BZHI RDZOGS PAR BSKUR BA'I LUGS MDZAD 'DUG PAS, MAR LUGS LA'ANG RGYUD KYI GZHUNG DANG GDAMS NGAG 'DZIN PA'I BLA MA SNGA MA CHEN PO RNAMS KYI BZHED PAS, DBANG BZHI YONGS SU RDZOGS PAR THOB PA CIG NGES PAR DGOS SO,,
gru.wylie: dpal phag mo gru pas mdzad pa na yang, sngon du dbang bzhi rdzogs par bskur ba'i lugs mdzad 'dug pas, mar lugs la'ang rgyud kyi gzhung dang gdams ngag 'dzin pa'i bla ma snga ma chen po rnams kyi bzhed pas, dbang bzhi yongs su rdzogs par thob pa cig nges par dgos so
gru.english: In the works of the glorious Pakmo Drupa also the proper system is to first grant the disciple an initiation complete with all four empowerments.  Thus we can say that, in the system of Marpa as well, the great Lamas of the past--those who have held both the secret books and the private instructions--believed that it was necessary to be granted an initiation complete with all four empowerments; and so it is absolutely certain that one should do so.

whole_word_matches.context: dpal phag mo gru pas mdzad pa na yang, sngon du dbang bzhi rdzogs par b

gru.acip: ,DBANG MED NA NI DNGOS GRUB MED, ,BYE MA BTZIR LA MAR MED LTAR, ,GANG ZHIG RGYUD LUNG NGA RGYAL GYIS, ,DBANG BSKUR MED PAR 'CHAD BYED PA, ,SLOB DPON SLOB MA SHI MA THAG , ,DNGOS GRUB THOB KYANG DMYAL BAR 'GRO, ,DE BAS 'BAD PA THAMS CAD KYIS, ,BLA MA LAS NI DBANG DON ZHU,
gru.wylie: dbang med na ni dngos grub med, ,bye ma btsir la mar med ltar, ,gang zhig rgyud lung nga rgyal gyis, ,dbang bskur med par 'chad byed pa, ,slob dpon slob ma shi ma thag , ,dngos grub thob kyang dmyal bar 'gro, ,de bas 'bad pa thams cad kyis, ,bla ma las ni dbang don zhu
gru.english: Those without an initiation can never achieve the goals; It's like squeezing sand to produce some butter. Anytime someone has the arrogance To teach the secret books without an initiation, Then both the master and the disciple Will drop to the hells, though the may have achieved The power to perform miracles. Thus must you seek the initiations From a Lama, with every effort you can.

gru.acip: ,DBANG BSKUR BA NI GTZO BO STE, ,DNGOS GRUB THAMS CAD RTAG TU GNAS, ,NGA YIS JI BZHIN DON BSHAD KYIS, ,DE PHYIR THOG MAR YANG DAG NYON,
gru.wylie: dbang bskur ba ni gtso bo ste, ,dngos grub thams cad rtag tu gnas, ,nga yis ji bzhin don bshad kyis, ,de phyir thog mar yang dag nyon
gru.english: Receiving initiation is the most important part; All the goals will stay with you then. I'll explain how it works, so now At the outset listen well.

gru.acip: ,YANG DAG DBANG BSKUR GYIS DBEN NA, ,SGRUB POS RGYUD KYI DON SHES KYANG, ,SLOB DPON SLOB MA MTSUNGS PAR NI, ,MI BZAD DMYAL BA CHEN POR 'GRO,
gru.wylie: yang dag dbang bskur gyis dben na, ,sgrub pos rgyud kyi don shes kyang, ,slob dpon slob ma mtshungs par ni, ,mi bzad dmyal ba chen por 'gro
gru.english: Suppose though they lack pure initiation; Then master and disciple, equally, Will drop to great and unbearable hells, Even if they're accomplished, And learn what the secret books say.

gru.acip: ZHES GSUNGS PAS GSANG CHEN BSHAD PA DANG SGOM PA'I SNOD DU RUNG BA DBANG RNAM DAG THOB PA LA RAG LAS PAS, DBANG NI DNGOS GRUB KYI RTZA BA YIN TE, DE MED NA RGYUD DON SHES NAS LAM LA CI TZAM 'BAD KYANG DNGOS GRUB KHYAD PAR CAN THOB MI SRID LA, DE MA THOB PA'I NYES DMIGS TZAM DU MA ZAD DNGOS GRUB PHRA MO THOB KYANG DPON SLOB GNYIS KA DMYAL BAR 'GRO'O,,
gru.wylie: zhes gsungs pas gsang chen bshad pa dang sgom pa'i snod du rung ba dbang rnam dag thob pa la rag las pas, dbang ni dngos grub kyi rtsa ba yin te, de med na rgyud don shes nas lam la ci tsam 'bad kyang dngos grub khyad par can thob mi srid la, de ma thob pa'i nyes dmigs tsam du ma zad dngos grub phra mo thob kyang dpon slob gnyis ka dmyal bar 'gro'o
gru.english: Given what these works state, then becoming a suitable vessel for learning and meditating upon the way of the great secret all depends upon being granted initiation, in a pure form.  This empowerment then is the very root of all attainments; without it, one can make whatever efforts you may in learning what the secret books say and in practicing this path, but it is completely impossible that you will attain any very extraordinary attainments.  And failing to achieve these attainments is not the only problem; even if they manage to accomplish some minor goals, both master and disciple will drop to the hells.

gru.acip: MI RUNG BA MED KYANG DANG PO DBANG RNAM DAG GZHAN SNGON DU MA SONG NA, DE TZAM GYIS DBANG GI GO MI CHOD PAS DBANG RDZOGS PA, RGYUD SDE RNAM DAG NAS GSUNGS PA, PAn GRUB KYIS KYANG LEGS PAR BSHAD PA, BLA MA DAM PA RNAMS LAS RIM PA BZHIN DU RGYUD SNOD DU RUNG BAR BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: mi rung ba med kyang dang po dbang rnam dag gzhan sngon du ma song na, de tsam gyis dbang gi go mi chod pas dbang rdzogs pa, rgyud sde rnam dag nas gsungs pa, paN grub kyis kyang legs par bshad pa, bla ma dam pa rnams las rim pa bzhin du rgyud snod du rung bar bya'o
gru.english: Although there is nothing wrong with this particular custom, it cannot by itself substitute for a proper initiation if one has not previously received another initiation in its pure form.  As such one must seek a full empowerment: one which is taught from an authentic, traditional secret teaching; one which has been commented upon by learned masters of the past, and practiced by accomplished saints.  One must prepare one's heart, making it a suitable vessel for the secret teachings, all in the proper steps, at the feet of great and holy Lamas.

gru.acip: DE 'DRA BA'I DBANG RNAM DAG THOB PA'I DUS SU BLA MA DANG RGYAL BA SRAS BCAS DBANG DU BZHAG NAS, JI SKAD GSUNGS PA BZHIN SGRUB PAR KHAS BLANGS PA'I DAM TSIG DANG, SDOM PA RNAMS KYI BSRUNG MTSAMS LEGS PAR SHES PAR BYAS NAS, TSUL BZHIN DU SRUNG DGOS PA YIN TE,
gru.wylie: de 'dra ba'i dbang rnam dag thob pa'i dus su bla ma dang rgyal ba sras bcas dbang du bzhag nas, ji skad gsungs pa bzhin sgrub par khas blangs pa'i dam tshig dang, sdom pa rnams kyi bsrung mtshams legs par shes par byas nas, tshul bzhin du srung dgos pa yin te
gru.english: During the pure form of an initiation as described above, your Lama--and the victorious Buddhas, along with their sons and daughters--place you in a state of power; which is to say, you receive commitments and vows which you pledge to keep, just as they were taught to you.  You must then study, carefully, all these various guidelines, and honor them properly.

gru.acip: BDE MCHOG RTZA RGYUD LAS, ,SHIN TU MNYAM GZHAG SGRUB PA POS, ,DAM TSIG RTAG TU BSKYANG BAR BYA, ,DAM TSIG NYAMS PAS DKYIL 'KHOR DU, ,DBANG BSKUR DNGOS GRUB THOB MI 'GYUR, ,ZHES DANG,
gru.wylie: bde mchog rtsa rgyud las, ,shin tu mnyam gzhag sgrub pa pos, ,dam tshig rtag tu bskyang bar bya, ,dam tshig nyams pas dkyil 'khor du, ,dbang bskur dngos grub thob mi 'gyur, ,zhes dang
gru.english: This fact is supported by The Root Tantra of Highest Bliss, which says: Practitioners living in deep meditation Must always honor all their commitments; One who's received empowerment in A secret world, but broken their pledges, Can never attain their goals.

gru.acip: MNYAM SBYOR LAS, ,DKYIL 'KHOR DU NI MA ZHUGS SHING, ,DAM TSIG RNAMS NI SPANGS PA DANG, ,GSANG BA'I DE NYID MI SHES PAS, ,BSGRUBS KYANG CI YANG MI 'GRUB PO,
gru.wylie: mnyam sbyor las, ,dkyil 'khor du ni ma zhugs shing, ,dam tshig rnams ni spangs pa dang, ,gsang ba'i de nyid mi shes pas, ,bsgrubs kyang ci yang mi 'grub po
gru.english: As Practicing Together states, Those who have never entered the secret world, Those who have failed to keep their commitments, And those who know not the essence of the secrets May try to achieve as best they can, but can't.

gru.acip: ,ZHES DKYIL 'KHOR DU BZHUG PA SNGON DU 'GRO BA'I DBANG MA THOB PA DANG, BSRUNG BYA'I DAM TSIG RNAMS YAL BAR DOR BA DANG, RIM GNYIS KYI GSANG BA'I GNAD RNAMS LEGS PAR MI SHES PAS, RING DU BSGRUBS KYANG 'DOD PA'I DNGOS GRUB CI YANG MI 'GRUB PAR GSUNGS PAS,
gru.wylie: zhes dkyil 'khor du bzhug pa sngon du 'gro ba'i dbang ma thob pa dang, bsrung bya'i dam tshig rnams yal bar dor ba dang, rim gnyis kyi gsang ba'i gnad rnams legs par mi shes pas, ring du bsgrubs kyang 'dod pa'i dngos grub ci yang mi 'grub par gsungs pas
gru.english: What this text is saying is that those who have failed to obtain the proper empowerment required before entering a secret world; and those who disregard the pledges that they are supposed to honor; and those who have no clear understanding of the crucial, secret points of the two stages may attempt to practice over a very long period of time, and yet still will achieve not even a single one of the attainments that they hope for.

gru.acip: RNAL 'BYOR BLA MED PA'I SGRUB PA POR KHAS BLANGS NAS, LUGS DE LA RTZA LTUNG GI GRANGS DU YOD KYANG MI SHES NA MI 'ONG BAS, RTZA BA DANG YAN LAG GI DAM TSIG BSRUNG MTSAMS LEGS PAR SHES PAR BYAS NAS SRUNG BA GAL CHE'O,,
gru.wylie: rnal 'byor bla med pa'i sgrub pa por khas blangs nas, lugs de la rtsa ltung gi grangs du yod kyang mi shes na mi 'ong bas, rtsa ba dang yan lag gi dam tshig bsrung mtshams legs par shes par byas nas srung ba gal che'o
gru.english: It's never going to come out right if--once you have committed to become a practitioner of the unsurpassable secret teachings--you don't even how many root vows there are for you to keep in this system.  As such it is extremely important that you learn, and learn well, the parameters of the root and secondary pledges, and then honor them strictly.

gru.acip: RANG NYID SRID MTSOR LTUNG BA BZHIN DU SEMS CAN RNAMS KYANG DE DANG 'DRA BAR BLTA ZHING, DE RNAMS KYANG RANG GI MA YIN PA DANG, MA BYAS RES KYIS PHAN PA BSGRUBS SHING, GNOD PA BSAL BA'I DRIN CHE BA DANG, DE LA LAN DU PHAN 'DOGS PA'I DRIN GZO'I BLO BRTAN PO BSKYED NAS,
gru.wylie: rang nyid srid mtshor ltung ba bzhin du sems can rnams kyang de dang 'dra bar blta zhing, de rnams kyang rang gi ma yin pa dang, ma byas res kyis phan pa bsgrubs shing, gnod pa bsal ba'i drin che ba dang, de la lan du phan 'dogs pa'i drin gzo'i blo brtan po bskyed nas
gru.english: Every living being has slipped and fallen, just like I have, into this ocean of suffering life.  And each one of them has been my own mother.  As they served me as my mother, they paid me great kindness: they did all they could to bring me every goodness, and all they could to save me from every kind of harm.  We must try to reach a very steady state of mind where we hope to repay their kindness, by rendering them some great help in return.

gru.acip: DE NAS DON DE GNYIS RDZOGS PAR SGRUB PA NI, SANGS RGYAS NYAG GCIG TU MTHONG NAS, DE RNAMS KYI DON DU SANGS RGYAS THOB 'DOD KYI BLO'I 'GYUR BA DRAG PO'I SGO NAS BYANG CHUB TU SEMS BSKYED,
gru.wylie: de nas don de gnyis rdzogs par sgrub pa ni, sangs rgyas nyag gcig tu mthong nas, de rnams kyi don du sangs rgyas thob 'dod kyi blo'i 'gyur ba drag po'i sgo nas byang chub tu sems bskyed
gru.english: Let me come to see that the total ability to achieve these two goals is possessed only by an Enlightened Being, and by no one else.  And let me in this way reach the Wish for enlightenment--fierce feelings in my heart that I want to reach Buddhahood for the sake of all these beings.

gru.acip: ,GRUB PA MCHOG RNAMS KYIS BSHAD PAS, ,THUN MTSAMS SU NI SPYAD PAR BYA, ,'BUM PHRAG TU NI BZLAS GYUR NA, ,RNAM PAR DAG PA'I BDAG NYID 'GYUR,
gru.wylie: grub pa mchog rnams kyis bshad pas, ,thun mtshams su ni spyad par bya, ,'bum phrag tu ni bzlas gyur na, ,rnam par dag pa'i bdag nyid 'gyur
gru.english: Thus have the highest masters spoken, So follow this in between your sessions; For if you recite a hundred thousand, You become a being of purity.

gru.acip: ,ZHES THUN MTSAMS SU RDOR SEMS BSGOMS NAS, YIG BRGYA NYER GCIG RE MA CHAG PAR BZLAS NA LTUNG BA MI 'PHEL BA DANG, 'BUM PHRAG GCIG BZLAS NA NYES PA RNAMS 'DAG PAR GRUB PA MCHOG BRNYES PA RNAMS KYIS GSUNGS PAS DE LTAR BYA'O, ,ZHES GSUNGS PA BZHIN DU DGOS PA DE NYID KYI PHYIR DU RDOR SEMS KYI BSGOM BZLAS BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: zhes thun mtshams su rdor sems bsgoms nas, yig brgya nyer gcig re ma chag par bzlas na ltung ba mi 'phel ba dang, 'bum phrag gcig bzlas na nyes pa rnams 'dag par grub pa mchog brnyes pa rnams kyis gsungs pas de ltar bya'o, ,zhes gsungs pa bzhin du dgos pa de nyid kyi phyir du rdor sems kyi bsgom bzlas bya'o
gru.english: The point here is that, [as Je Tsongkapa stated]-- If you stop between sessions to do the practice of the Warrior of Diamond, and recite the mantra of a hundred syllables 21 times on each occasion, without breaking it--then the negative power of your broken vows will never increase.  And if you recite a hundred thousand of these mantras, then you will purify yourself of all your negative deeds.  All this, the verses are saying, has been taught by beings who attained the ultimate goal; and thus you must follow it. We should, therefore, undertake the practice of meditation and recitation centered upon the Warrior of Diamond, to attain the goals mentioned here.

gru.acip: ZHAL LUNG LAS, ,'DI YI DON LDAN 'GA' ZHIG LA, ,NGA NI DE YI LUS GNAS TE, ,SGRUB PO GZHAN LA MCHOD PA LEN, ,DE YIS DE MNYES RANG GI RGYUD, ,LAS KYI SGRIB PA DAG BYED DO,
gru.wylie: zhal lung las, ,'di yi don ldan 'ga' zhig la, ,nga ni de yi lus gnas te, ,sgrub po gzhan la mchod pa len, ,de yis de mnyes rang gi rgyud, ,las kyi sgrib pa dag byed do
gru.english: The Word of the Glorious Gentle Voice too says, I come and stay within the bodies Of a few who have the meaning, And bring attainments.  I take Where others are offering. This is then what pleases, And works to purify them Of the obstacles of past deeds.

gru.acip: SKYON GYI NGOS NAS BRTAGS NA DNGOS GRUB KYI GEGS BYED LA, YON TAN GYI NGOS NAS BRTAGS NA DNGOS GRUB MYUR DU 'GRUB PA'I PHYIR RO, ,DE LTA BU LA SOGS PA'I TSUL GYIS BLA MA DE NYID LA DMIGS PA'I DAD PA DANG, BKA' DRIN RJES SU DRAN TE GUS PA CHEN PO MANG DU SBYANG NGO,,
gru.wylie: skyon gyi ngos nas brtags na dngos grub kyi gegs byed la, yon tan gyi ngos nas brtags na dngos grub myur du 'grub pa'i phyir ro, ,de lta bu la sogs pa'i tshul gyis bla ma de nyid la dmigs pa'i dad pa dang, bka' drin rjes su dran te gus pa chen po mang du sbyang ngo
gru.english: The reason for doing this is that--if you tend to examine your Lama from the point of view of faults that you see--it acts as a great hinderance to reaching your own spiritual attainments.  If on the other hand you examine Them from the point of view of Their high qualities, then you will be able to each your goals with speed.  Use these and other such methods to work then, over and over, to develop great faith focussed upon your Lama, remembering as well His or Her great kindness towards you.  In short, work constantly to develop intense devotion towards Them.

gru.acip: DE NAS GUS PA CHEN POS THUN MONG DANG, THUN MONG MA YIN PA'I LAM RNAMS MYUR DU RGYUD LA SKYE BA DANG, DE DAG GI 'GAL RKYEN ZHI ZHING MTHUN RKYEN YID BZHIN DU 'GRUB PA'I GSOL BA BTAB PAS, DGYES TE BLA MA'I GNAS GSUM GYI YI GE LAS 'OD ZER DKAR DMAR MTHING GSUM 'PHROS PA,
gru.wylie: de nas gus pa chen pos thun mong dang, thun mong ma yin pa'i lam rnams myur du rgyud la skye ba dang, de dag gi 'gal rkyen zhi zhing mthun rkyen yid bzhin du 'grub pa'i gsol ba btab pas, dgyes te bla ma'i gnas gsum gyi yi ge las 'od zer dkar dmar mthing gsum 'phros pa
gru.english: With deep feelings of devotion then beg your Lama to assist you in reaching within you both the shared and the unique paths, with all possible speed.  Ask Them to help put an end to anything that might prevent you from reaching these paths, and to help you attain everything that might help you do so, just as your heart desires.  Imagine then that your Lama is filled with pleasure over your request, and that light rays of three colors--white, red, and dark blue--fly out from the sacred syllables at the three places on Her or His body.

gru.acip: RANG GI GNAS GSUM DU RIM PA BZHIN DU ZHUGS PAS, LUS KYI NANG THAMS CAD 'OD ZER GSUM GYIS RIM PA BZHIN DU KHENGS, SGO GSUM GYI DRI MA SBYANGS, BUM PA DANG GSANG BA DANG SHES RAB YE SHES KYI DBANG RIM PA BZHIN THOB, SKU RDO RJE SOGS GSUM GYI DNGOS GRUB RIM PA BZHIN THOB PAR BSAM,
gru.wylie: rang gi gnas gsum du rim pa bzhin du zhugs pas, lus kyi nang thams cad 'od zer gsum gyis rim pa bzhin du khengs, sgo gsum gyi dri ma sbyangs, bum pa dang gsang ba dang shes rab ye shes kyi dbang rim pa bzhin thob, sku rdo rje sogs gsum gyi dngos grub rim pa bzhin thob par bsam
gru.english: Each of these rays of light melts into the corresponding spot on your own body, and the entire inside of your body comes to be filled with the three lights, one by one.  The lights purify you of every impurity that you have ever committed through any of the gates of expression: in your actions, words, or thoughts.  You receive, one after the other, the empowerments of the vase, of the secret, and of wisdom knowledge.  Imagine that they cause you to attain, one after the other, the spiritual goals of the three diamonds: enlightened action and the rest.

gru.acip: DE NAS SKU'I GNAS THAMS CAD LAS 'OD ZER SNA TSOGS 'PHROS, RANG GI LUS KYI SGO THAMS CAD NAS ZHUGS SGO GSUM GYI SGRIB PA PHRA BA SBYANGS DBANG BZHI PA THOB, RDO RJE GSUM DBYER MI PHYED PA'I DNGOS GRUB THOB PAR BSAM MO,,
gru.wylie: de nas sku'i gnas thams cad las 'od zer sna tshogs 'phros, rang gi lus kyi sgo thams cad nas zhugs sgo gsum gyi sgrib pa phra ba sbyangs dbang bzhi pa thob, rdo rje gsum dbyer mi phyed pa'i dngos grub thob par bsam mo
gru.english: Light rays of a variety of colors fly out then from each of the places on your Lama's holy body; they sink into each of the gateways of your body and purify you of even the most subtle obstacles of body, speech, and mind--you achieve the fourth empowerment.  Imagine then that you have reached the attainment of three diamonds indivisible, one from the other.

gru.acip: SPYI BOR THOD PA'I 'OG KLAD RGYA'I STENG DU DBU MAR RO RKYANG GIS MDUD PA RE RE BCINGS PA'I MDUD MTSAMS NAS PHYOGS KYI RTZA BZHI THON, DE RE RE LAS GNYIS GNYIS GYES PA'I BRGYAD, DE RE RE LAS GNYIS GNYIS GYES PA'I BCU DRUG ,DE RE RE LAS GNYIS GNYIS GYES PA'I SUM CU SO GNYIS, KHA DOG KHRA CHOL LE BA GDUGS KHA PHUB PA LTA BU DBYIBS GRU GSUM,
gru.wylie: spyi bor thod pa'i 'og klad rgya'i steng du dbu mar ro rkyang gis mdud pa re re bcings pa'i mdud mtshams nas phyogs kyi rtsa bzhi thon, de re re las gnyis gnyis gyes pa'i brgyad, de re re las gnyis gnyis gyes pa'i bcu drug ,de re re las gnyis gnyis gyes pa'i sum cu so gnyis, kha dog khra chol le ba gdugs kha phub pa lta bu dbyibs gru gsum
gru.english: The first chakra is located at the tip of your head, underneath the skull and above the brain.  At this point the central channel of taste and the solitary channel both twist around the central channel and form a knot.  From this knot come four major channels.  From the branches of each of those four channels come two more channels, making a total of eight.  From each of these split off another two channels, making sixteen, and then two more branch off from each of the sixteen making a total of 32.  The color of this chakra is that of a black and white pattern [although some teachings traditions say to visualize it as white]; its shape is triangular and it is curved slightly downward, like an umbrella facing down.

whole_word_matches.context: ha dog khra chol le ba gdugs kha phub pa lta bu dbyibs gru gsum

gru.acip: DE RE RE LAS BZHI BZHI GYES PA'I RE BZHI'AM YANG NA DE RE RE LAS GNYIS GNYIS GYES PA'I SUM CU SO GNYIS, DE RE RE LAS GNYIS GNYIS GYES PA'I RE BZHI, GDUGS KHA BSLANGS PA LTA BU KHA DOG DMAR PO DBYIBS GRU GSUM RTZA 'DAB SBUBS STONG RTZE MO GRO SOG GRIS BCAD PA LTA BU SBOM PHRA 'JAG MA TZAM 'JAM ZHING MNYEN PA,
gru.wylie: de re re las bzhi bzhi gyes pa'i re bzhi'am yang na de re re las gnyis gnyis gyes pa'i sum cu so gnyis, de re re las gnyis gnyis gyes pa'i re bzhi, gdugs kha bslangs pa lta bu kha dog dmar po dbyibs gru gsum rtsa 'dab sbubs stong rtse mo gro sog gris bcad pa lta bu sbom phra 'jag ma tsam 'jam zhing mnyen pa
gru.english: Then you can either visualize that each of these sixteen branches off into four making a total of 64 channels; or alternately the sixteen each split into two, making 32, and then these 32 each split into two, making 64.  The chakra is colored red, has a triangular shape, and curves upward slightly like an umbrella turned upside-down.  The channels are hollow and about the width of a segment of wheat stalk at their outer tips.  They are soft and flexible like the flesh of your tongue.

whole_word_matches.context: hi, gdugs kha bslangs pa lta bu kha dog dmar po dbyibs gru gsum rtsa 'dab sbubs stong rtse mo gro sog gris bcad p

gru.acip: BSKYED RIM BSGOM PA NI 'JIG RTEN PA'I DNGOS GRUB SGRUB PA LA DGOS KYI, MCHOG SGRUB PA LA MI DGOS SO ZHES PA'I LOG RTOG BOD NA LUGS 'GA' ZHIG LA SNANG YANG, BLA MA MAR PA NAS BRGYUD PA'I MES LUGS DANG, MTSUR DANG RNGOG GSUM GA'I LUGS LA SNGON DU BSKYED RIM LA 'KHRID PA SNANG ZHING,
gru.wylie: bskyed rim bsgom pa ni 'jig rten pa'i dngos grub sgrub pa la dgos kyi, mchog sgrub pa la mi dgos so zhes pa'i log rtog bod na lugs 'ga' zhig la snang yang, bla ma mar pa nas brgyud pa'i mes lugs dang, mtshur dang rngog gsum ga'i lugs la sngon du bskyed rim la 'khrid pa snang zhing
gru.english: We do see, here in Tibet, a number of systems which have expressed the following completely wrong idea: The practice of the creation stage is something that you need to achieve worldly goals, but is not something which is necessary for reaching ultimate goals. There does appear though in all three of the systems come down from Lama Marpa--those of Me, Tsur, and Ngok--the custom of training the student in the stage of completion. [Translator's note: As mentioned at the beginning of the work, the "Four Great Pillars" or important disciples of Marpa the Translator, consisted of Chuku Dorje of Ngok; Wanggi Dorje, the Teacher from Tsur; Tsunpo, the Teacher from Me; and Milarepa.].

gru.acip: MGON PO KLU SGRUB KYIS KYANG, ,BSKYED PA'I RIM LA LEGS GNAS SHING, ,RDZOGS PA'I RIM PA 'DOD RNAMS LA, ,THABS 'DI RDZOGS PA'I SANGS RGYAS KYIS, ,SKAS KYI RIM PA LTA BUR GSUNGS,
gru.wylie: mgon po klu sgrub kyis kyang, ,bskyed pa'i rim la legs gnas shing, ,rdzogs pa'i rim pa 'dod rnams la, ,thabs 'di rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas kyis, ,skas kyi rim pa lta bur gsungs
gru.english: Our Savior, Nagarjuna, has said as well: Follow the stage of creation In the proper way; Those who hope to come to The next stage, of completion, Must utilize this method: The completely Enlightened Ones Have said, "It's like a ladder."

gru.acip: 'DI YI MAN NGAG LA GTZO BOR MDZAD PA'I BLA MA GONG MA RNAMS, BDE MCHOG LA MDZAD PA MANG STE, SGAM PO PAS NI ZANGS DKAR GYI SLOB MA MAR YUL BLO LDAN LA BRTEN NAS, ZANGS DKAR GYI LUGS KYI BDE MCHOG DANG, DPAL PHAG MO GRU PAS NI, LO CHUNG NAS BRGYUD PA MAR LUGS KYI BDE MCHOG DANG, CHOS RJE 'BRI GUNG PAS NI, MAR DO NAS BRGYUD PA'I COG RO LUGS KYI BDE MCHOG LA MDZAD SNANG STE, DE GSUM GA YANG DPAL L'U AI PA'I LUGS KYI BDE MCHOG DRUG CU RTZA GNYIS PA'I DKYIL 'KHOR LA BRTEN PA'O,,
gru.wylie: 'di yi man ngag la gtso bor mdzad pa'i bla ma gong ma rnams, bde mchog la mdzad pa mang ste, sgam po pas ni zangs dkar gyi slob ma mar yul blo ldan la brten nas, zangs dkar gyi lugs kyi bde mchog dang, dpal phag mo gru pas ni, lo chung nas brgyud pa mar lugs kyi bde mchog dang, chos rje 'bri gung pas ni, mar do nas brgyud pa'i cog ro lugs kyi bde mchog la mdzad snang ste, de gsum ga yang dpal lU ai pa'i lugs kyi bde mchog drug cu rtsa gnyis pa'i dkyil 'khor la brten pa'o
gru.english: Among the Lamas of the past who made the advices on this practice their principal practice, there were many that followed the way of Highest Bliss.  Gampopa sat at the feet of Maryul Londen, a disciple of Sangkar, and learned the secret teachings of Highest Bliss according to the system of Sangkar.  The glorious Pakmo Drupa practiced the teachings of Highest Bliss according to the system of Marpa, as it was passed down from Lochung.  And the Dharma lord Drigungpa also followed the way of Highest Bliss, according to the system of Chokro, as passed down from Mardo.  All three of these Lamas also kept the practice of the secret world of the 62 Angels of Highest Bliss, in keeping with the system of the glorious Luipa. [Translator's note: The places of Marpa (Mardo), Gampopa, and Pakmo Drupa in the lineage of the Six Practices have been discussed above.  Maryul Londen and Sangkar have also appeared before.  Chokro Chukyi Gyeltsen (1108-1176)  is described in A Treasury of the Names of the Wise and Accomplished Beings Who Appeared Over the Years in the Snowy Land as having studied the teachings of Highest Bliss with Namka Uw, the spiritual son of Marpa.  Lochung Lekpay Sherab (fl. 1050), whose first name means "Younger Translator," was the assistant of the "Great Translator" Rinchen Sangpo (958-1055).]

gru.acip: NGO BO NYID MED TSUL NI, NGO BOS MED CES PAS STON TE, GANG ZAG DANG GZUGS LA SOGS PA'I CHOS LA NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB PA'I RANG BZHIN MED CES PA'O, ,BSHAD PA DE DAG NI GRUB CHEN MTSO SKYES KYI 'GREL PA'I DGONGS PA'O, ,'DI NI RANG BZHIN GYIS DANG RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS MED CES GSUNG RAB LAS MANG DU 'BYUNG BA RNAMS KYI DON NO,,
gru.wylie: ngo bo nyid med tshul ni, ngo bos med ces pas ston te, gang zag dang gzugs la sogs pa'i chos la ngo bo nyid kyis grub pa'i rang bzhin med ces pa'o, ,bshad pa de dag ni grub chen mtsho skyes kyi 'grel pa'i dgongs pa'o, ,'di ni rang bzhin gyis dang rang gi mtshan nyid kyis med ces gsung rab las mang du 'byung ba rnams kyi don no
gru.english: The way in which these things lack any essence of their own is indicated in the words "nothing which exists in its very essence."  That is to say, "No objects--neither the person nor the things that make up a person (such as their physical form)--have any kind of nature where they exist through some very essence of their own."  The explanation of the lines we have given here represents the ideas expressed by the great and accomplished master Saroruha in his commentary.  The same point is being made many times throughout the teachings of the highest word when they say that "nothing has any nature of its own," or "nothing exists by definition."

gru.acip: DE 'DRA BA'I RANG BZHIN NAM NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB PA MED PA DANG, RANG BZHIN GYIS MA SKYES PA DE YANG SNGAR MI STONG BA CIG GSAR DU LUNG RIGS KYIS BSGRUBS PA MIN GYI, YE GDOD MA NAS DE LTAR YIN PA LA YIN PAR NGO SHES PAR BYED PA NI, GDOD NAS ZHES PAS STON NO,,
gru.wylie: de 'dra ba'i rang bzhin nam ngo bo nyid kyis grub pa med pa dang, rang bzhin gyis ma skyes pa de yang sngar mi stong ba cig gsar du lung rigs kyis bsgrubs pa min gyi, ye gdod ma nas de ltar yin pa la yin par ngo shes par byed pa ni, gdod nas zhes pas ston no
gru.english: Now let's consider the same thing: the fact that nothing exists through any nature or essence of its own; and the fact that nothing is born through some nature of its own.  It's not as if, up to this moment, things were somehow not empty of any such nature, and then from now on they are going to be empty because we've managed to prove that they are, through the use of scriptural references and reasoning.  Rather, they have been this way for an infinite length of time; and to be sure we recognize this fact, the text says that "they have been ever since before there was a beginning."

gru.acip: DE LTAR DES NI DBU MA PA 'PHAGS PA KLU SGRUB DANG 'PHAGS PA LHA DANG ZLA BA GRAGS PA LA SOGS PA'I BZHED PA RTEN CING 'BREL PAR 'BYUNG BA'I MTSAN NYID DE BZHIN NYID SHES PAR 'DOD PAS YIN PAR 'GYUR RO, ,ZHES DE GSUM GYI LUGS BLANG BYA YIN NO, ,ZHES BSHAD LA,
gru.wylie: de ltar des ni dbu ma pa 'phags pa klu sgrub dang 'phags pa lha dang zla ba grags pa la sogs pa'i bzhed pa rten cing 'brel par 'byung ba'i mtshan nyid de bzhin nyid shes par 'dod pas yin par 'gyur ro, ,zhes de gsum gyi lugs blang bya yin no, ,zhes bshad la
gru.english: As such, they should seek rather to understand the position of those of the Middle Way--of the realized being Nagarjuna, and of Aryadeva, Chandrakirti, and the rest; that is, a kind of real nature whose distinguishing mark is the teachings on dependent origination.  Then it will come. And so it is the system of these three that one should follow.

gru.acip: MGON PO KLU SGRUB DANG 'PHAGS PA LHA GNYIS NI GZHUNG PHYI MO'I DBU MA PA YIN PAS, 'DI GNYIS KYI RJES SU DBU MA'I GRUB MTHA' SMRA BA GZHAN RNAMS KYANG 'BRANG MOD KYANG, DE GNYIS KYI LUGS 'DZIN PA MI 'DRA BA MANG DU YOD PA LA MNGA' BDAG MEE TRI PA, DPAL LDAN ZLA BA GRAGS PA'I RJES SU 'BRANG BAR BSHAD LA, YANG DE KHO NA NYID BCU PA LAS,
gru.wylie: mgon po klu sgrub dang 'phags pa lha gnyis ni gzhung phyi mo'i dbu ma pa yin pas, 'di gnyis kyi rjes su dbu ma'i grub mtha' smra ba gzhan rnams kyang 'brang mod kyang, de gnyis kyi lugs 'dzin pa mi 'dra ba mang du yod pa la mnga' bdag mee tri pa, dpal ldan zla ba grags pa'i rjes su 'brang bar bshad la, yang de kho na nyid bcu pa las
gru.english: Now two of these three--the savior Nagarjuna, and Aryadeva--are what we call "those of the Middle-Way who wrote the later treatises."  It is admittedly true that there were many others who followed after these two and professed the middle Way; but of all of the many different sages who continued this tradition on, that absolute lord of the Dharma--Maitripa--is one who is said to have followed in the footsteps of the glorious Chandrakirti.  As The Ten Kinds of Suchness itself says,

gru.acip: SHES RAB CAN GANG DAG GANG ZAG DANG CHOS KYI NGO BO RNAMS, RANG RANG GI RGYU DANG RKYEN LA BRTEN NAS 'BYUNG BA DANG, BRTEN NAS BTAGS PA YIN PA'I PHYIR NA, BDEN PA DANG YANG DAG PAR MED DO, ,ZHES 'DI DAG LA RANG GI NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB PA'I RANG BZHIN CUNG ZAD KYANG MED DE,
gru.wylie: shes rab can gang dag gang zag dang chos kyi ngo bo rnams, rang rang gi rgyu dang rkyen la brten nas 'byung ba dang, brten nas btags pa yin pa'i phyir na, bden pa dang yang dag par med do, ,zhes 'di dag la rang gi ngo bo nyid kyis grub pa'i rang bzhin cung zad kyang med de
gru.english: What this is saying is that those of wisdom grasp the following.  The very essence of all things--whether they relate to the person or to the things that make up a person--is that they occur through dependence on their particular causes and conditions: they are projections based on something else.  As such they do not exist as something which is real or "pure."  They possess not even the slightest bit of any nature which could ever exist in and of itself.

gru.acip: DE LTAR MTSAN MAR 'DZIN PA BDEN 'DZIN GYI DMIGS GTAD RDUL TZAM YANG MA GRUB KYANG, LAS 'BRAS LA SOGS PA'I RGYU 'BRAS KYI 'KHOR 'DAS KYI BYA BYED THAMS CAD NYAMS PA MED PA SGYU MA DANG, RMI LAM DANG GZUGS BRNYAN GYI BYA BYED BZHIN DU 'CHAR BA YOD DO,,
gru.wylie: de ltar mtshan mar 'dzin pa bden 'dzin gyi dmigs gtad rdul tsam yang ma grub kyang, las 'bras la sogs pa'i rgyu 'bras kyi 'khor 'das kyi bya byed thams cad nyams pa med pa sgyu ma dang, rmi lam dang gzugs brnyan gyi bya byed bzhin du 'char ba yod do
gru.english: Now although it is true to say thus that there exists not even an atom of what our tendency to see things as real (our tendency to take the indications as the object) centers itself upon, this is not to imply at all that all the workings of things, whether they be in the circle of suffering or beyond it--that is, cause and effect itself, as expressed in phenomena such as deeds and their consequences--is in any way diminished.  There is something that appears as if it were the workings of things, albeit in the way of a magic trick, or a dream, or a reflection in a mirror.

gru.acip: BDEN GNYIS KYI RNAM GZHAG DE 'DRA CIG DGOS PAR LAM 'DI'I RNAL 'BYOR PA CHEN PO MID LAS KYANG, ,KHYED BLO DMAN RNAMS KYIS BSAM NGO DANG, ,BSTUN NAS SANGS RGYAS KUN MKHYEN GYIS, ,THAMS CAD YOD CES GSUNGS PA YIN, ,DON DAM BDEN PA'I DBANG DU NI, ,BGEGS LAS SANGS RGYAS NYID KYANG MED, ,SGOM PA PO MED SGOM BYA MED, ,BGROD BYA SA DANG LAM RTAGS MED, ,'BRAS BU SKU DANG YE SHES MED, ,DE PHYIR MYA NGAN 'DAS PA MED, ,MING DANG TSIG GIS BTAGS PA TZAM, ,KHAMS GSUM BRTAN DANG GA YO BAR BCAS, ,GDOD NAS MA GRUB SKYE BA MED, ,GZHI MED LHAN CIG SKYES PA MED, ,LAS DANG LAS KYI RNAM SMIN MED, ,DE PHYIR 'KHOR BA'I MING YANG MED, ,MTHAR THUG DON LA DE LTAR GDA',
gru.wylie: bden gnyis kyi rnam gzhag de 'dra cig dgos par lam 'di'i rnal 'byor pa chen po mid las kyang, ,khyed blo dman rnams kyis bsam ngo dang, ,bstun nas sangs rgyas kun mkhyen gyis, ,thams cad yod ces gsungs pa yin, ,don dam bden pa'i dbang du ni, ,bgegs las sangs rgyas nyid kyang med, ,sgom pa po med sgom bya med, ,bgrod bya sa dang lam rtags med, ,'bras bu sku dang ye shes med, ,de phyir mya ngan 'das pa med, ,ming dang tshig gis btags pa tsam, ,khams gsum brtan dang ga yo bar bcas, ,gdod nas ma grub skye ba med, ,gzhi med lhan cig skyes pa med, ,las dang las kyi rnam smin med, ,de phyir 'khor ba'i ming yang med, ,mthar thug don la de ltar gda'
gru.english: The fact that we need to set forth the two realities in this way is described as follows by that great practitioner of this path, Milarepa: The omniscient Buddha did proclaim That all of this existed, But that was only to fit the minds Of those of you whose intellect Was not enough developed. In an ultimate sense He denied them: The Buddha himself does not exist. There is no one who meditates, And nothing to meditate upon. There is no destination, And no sign of the path. There is no goal you can attain, No body and no wisdom. And so the state of nirvana itself Is something non-existent. Everything is but a projection Created by names and words. And all three realms, their solid ground, And those who cross its face Have never existed, from before the beginning, And never started either. There's no orginal way it was, Nor what comes simultaneous. There's no such thing as karma, And nothing that ripens from it. And so then even the name Of the "cycle of suffering" Is nothing that exists. In the ultimate sense of things This is the way it is.

gru.acip: ,ZHES DON DAM PAR 'KHOR 'DAS KYI CHOS GANG YANG RDUL TZAM YANG MA GRUB PAR GSUNGS NAS, ,AE MA SEMS CAN MED GYUR NA, ,DUS GSUM SANGS RGYAS CI LAS BYUNG, ,RGYU MED 'BRAS BU MI SRID PAS, ,KUN RDZOB BDEN PA'I DBANG DU NI, ,'KHOR BA DANG NI MYA NGAN 'DAS, ,THAMS CAD YOD CES THUB PAS GSUNGS, ,YOD PA DNGOS POR SNANG BA DANG, ,MED PA STONG PA'I CHOS NYID GNYIS, ,NGO BO DBYER MED RO GCIG PAS, ,RANG RIG GZHAN RIG YOD MIN TE, ,THAMS CAD ZUNG 'JUG YANGS PA YIN, ,DE LTAR RTOGS PA'I MKHAS PA YIS, ,RNAM SHES MA MTHONG YE SHES MTHONG, ,SEMS CAN MA MTHONG SANGS RGYAS MTHONG, ,CHOS CAN MA MTHONG CHOS NYID MTHONG,
gru.wylie: zhes don dam par 'khor 'das kyi chos gang yang rdul tsam yang ma grub par gsungs nas, ,ae ma sems can med gyur na, ,dus gsum sangs rgyas ci las byung, ,rgyu med 'bras bu mi srid pas, ,kun rdzob bden pa'i dbang du ni, ,'khor ba dang ni mya ngan 'das, ,thams cad yod ces thub pas gsungs, ,yod pa dngos por snang ba dang, ,med pa stong pa'i chos nyid gnyis, ,ngo bo dbyer med ro gcig pas, ,rang rig gzhan rig yod min te, ,thams cad zung 'jug yangs pa yin, ,de ltar rtogs pa'i mkhas pa yis, ,rnam shes ma mthong ye shes mthong, ,sems can ma mthong sangs rgyas mthong, ,chos can ma mthong chos nyid mthong
gru.english: What Lord Milarepa is saying here is that, from an ultimate point of view, there exists not even a single atom of anything, whether we're talking about the cycle of pain or that which is beyond it.  Then he continues: What now?  If there are no living beings, Then where do Buddhas past, And present and future come from? Because it's impossible for a result To occur without a cause, The Able Ones have stated That--with regard to the deceptive Form of reality-- Everything in the cycle of suffering And within nirvana as well Really does exist. Consider these two things: The existing side, where things appear, And the side that doesn't exist, The side of emptiness. Because their very essence Is indivisible Within a single song, You neither know your mind Nor does it know itself: Everything is that vast expanse Of the union of enlightenment. The wise who realize these things See no state of consciousness, But rather the state of wisdom; See no living being, But rather an Enlightened One; See not the things that are empty, But rather their emptiness.

gru.acip: ,ZHES DON DAM PAR 'KHOR 'DAS KYI CHOS RNAMS KYI MING TZAM YANG MA GRUB PA DANG, DE LTAR YIN KYANG KUN RDZOB TU NI, SEMS CAN GYIS SANGS RGYAS THOB PA LA SOGS PA 'KHOR 'DAS KYI RNAM GZHAG KUN YOD PA DANG,
gru.wylie: zhes don dam par 'khor 'das kyi chos rnams kyi ming tsam yang ma grub pa dang, de ltar yin kyang kun rdzob tu ni, sems can gyis sangs rgyas thob pa la sogs pa 'khor 'das kyi rnam gzhag kun yod pa dang
gru.english: The point here is, first of all, that none of the objects relating either to the cycle of suffering or to the state beyond it has any existence in an ultimate sense; not even in name.  Despite this fact, the whole structure of this cycle of pain and passing beyond it really does, in a deceptive way, exist: living beings can attain enlightenment, and all the rest.

gru.acip: DE YANG MING DANG TSIG GIS BTAGS PA TZAM LA 'JOG PA DANG, DNGOS POR SNANG BA'I RTEN 'BREL DANG, RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA MED PA'I STONG PA GNYIS, NGO BO GCIG TU GNAS PAS SNANG STONG, GCIG GIS GCIG MA DOR BAR GSUNGS PA NI, LUGS 'DI'I BLA MA GONG MA'I KHYAD CHOS CIG TU SNANG BAS,
gru.wylie: de yang ming dang tshig gis btags pa tsam la 'jog pa dang, dngos por snang ba'i rten 'brel dang, rang bzhin gyis grub pa med pa'i stong pa gnyis, ngo bo gcig tu gnas pas snang stong, gcig gis gcig ma dor bar gsungs pa ni, lugs 'di'i bla ma gong ma'i khyad chos cig tu snang bas
gru.english: And all of this is established only through names and words.  The fact of dependent origination, which appears to us as different things, and the fact of emptiness, where nothing has any nature of its own, exist as a single essence: the appearance of things and emptiness.  The teachings which say that neither of these two obviates the other are an extraordinary feature among the Lamas of this system in days gone by.

gru.acip: DE NAS 'KHRUL 'KHOR LA MANG NYUNG DANG BYED LUGS MI 'DRA BA MANG DU SNANG NA'ANG, 'DIR DPAL PHAG MO GRU PAS MDZAD PA'I THABS LAM TSIGS BCAD MA'I LHAN THABS LAS,
gru.wylie: de nas 'khrul 'khor la mang nyung dang byed lugs mi 'dra ba mang du snang na'ang, 'dir dpal phag mo gru pas mdzad pa'i thabs lam tshigs bcad ma'i lhan thabs las
gru.english: Now we see a great number of different systems on just how many elements there are to the practice of the machine of the body, and many different versions of how to carry it out as well.  Nonetheless we will follow here the system found in the appendix by the glorious Pakmo Drupa entitled "Verses on the Path of Skilful Means."

gru.english: Next is our description of "bending the body like a hook."  First close your two hands in what we call "fists of diamond," and then thrust them forward from heart straight out to the front, lined up with each other, and with considerable force. Then stretch both your arms out to the left of you.  Starting with your right arm, slowly and with force bend your arms back as far as your shoulder, and beat your elbow against your side.

gru.wylie: stong ra la rtog bzo gzhan mang po 'dug na'ang, dpal phag mo gru pa'i khrid yig las de tsam zhig las mi 'byung ste, de gas chog go
gru.english: There are many other details of the practice of the empty form that have just been made up by people; what you actually find in the treatise of the glorious Pakmo Druppa though is no more than what I've put here, and it's enough.

gru.acip: DE LA SPYIR RNAL 'BYOR BLA MED KYI RDZOGS RIM RNAMS LA SNGON DU, RO RKYANG GI RLUNG DBU MAR 'DZUD PA'I THABS KHYAD PAR CAN CIG MED MI RUNG YIN LA, DE LA YANG RGYUD SDE SO SO LA BRTEN PA'I GRUB CHEN GYI LUGS MI 'DRA BA MANG DU YOD KYANG, 'DIR NI LTE BA SPRUL PA'I 'KHOR LO LA BRTEN PA'I GTUM MO, AA THUNG GI SROG RTZOL GYI SGO NAS, SROG DH'U T'IR SDUD PA YIN NO,,
gru.wylie: de la spyir rnal 'byor bla med kyi rdzogs rim rnams la sngon du, ro rkyang gi rlung dbu mar 'dzud pa'i thabs khyad par can cig med mi rung yin la, de la yang rgyud sde so so la brten pa'i grub chen gyi lugs mi 'dra ba mang du yod kyang, 'dir ni lte ba sprul pa'i 'khor lo la brten pa'i gtum mo, aa thung gi srog rtsol gyi sgo nas, srog dhU tIr sdud pa yin no
gru.english: Now, generally speaking, it would not be right to have a completion-stage practice of the class of unsurpassed practice in the secret teachings which lacked some extraordinary method of getting the winds to enter into the central channel.  In this regard, there are a great number of different systems established by the great and accomplished practitioners, based on each of the different groups of secret teachings.  In the present system though we use a practice of inner fire, based at the chakra of emanation at the navel--working with the life-wind of the short ah--to gather the life wind into the channel of the dance.

gru.acip: DE'I TSUL NI NGAG BZLAS ZIN NAS ZHAR BYUNG RDZOGS RIM DANG PO'I 'GOR LUS GNAD CHOS BDUN LDAN DU BYAS LA, RLUNG RO DGU PHRUGS SU BSAL TSUL N'A RO'I CHOS DRUG GI SKABS LTAR GYI RGYAS PAR MI DGOS PAR TSE SGRUB GYI SKABS BZHIN
gru.wylie: de'i tshul ni ngag bzlas zin nas zhar byung rdzogs rim dang po'i 'gor lus gnad chos bdun ldan du byas la, rlung ro dgu phrugs su bsal tshul nA ro'i chos drug gi skabs ltar gyi rgyas par mi dgos par tshe sgrub gyi skabs bzhin
gru.english: This is how to proceed.  After you have finished your verbal recitation, then move on to the first of the incidental practices of the stage of completion.  As you begin this, put your body into the seven point posture.  Then clear the channels with the practice of the nine fold wind.  It's not necessary that you do this in the extensive version found in the Six Practices of Naropa; rather you can follow the method that we use in the ritual for attaining long life.

gru.acip: DE NAS 'KHOR LO BZHI GSAL 'DEBS PA NI, LTE BA SPRUL PA'I 'KHOR LO PHYI DBYIBS AE GRU GSUM GYI RNAM PA CAN, RTZA 'DAB KYI GRANGS RE BZHI PA, KHA DOG DMAR PO, ,KHA GYEN DU PHYOGS PA'I RNAM PA CAN DU BSGOM MO, ,'DI DAG LA 'DAB PA'I GRANGS RAGS PA RNAMS SMOS NAS, ZHIB PAR MA SMOS 'DUG PA BZHIN 'DIR CHOG PAR SNANG BSAM BSHAD DO,,
gru.wylie: de nas 'khor lo bzhi gsal 'debs pa ni, lte ba sprul pa'i 'khor lo phyi dbyibs ae gru gsum gyi rnam pa can, rtsa 'dab kyi grangs re bzhi pa, kha dog dmar po, ,kha gyen du phyogs pa'i rnam pa can du bsgom mo, ,'di dag la 'dab pa'i grangs rags pa rnams smos nas, zhib par ma smos 'dug pa bzhin 'dir chog par snang bsam bshad do
gru.english: Here next is how you visualize the four chakras.  The outer appearance of the chakra of emanation, at the navel, is that of the letter eh, which is triangular [in Sansksrit].  The chakra has 64 petals, and is red.  One should picture it as facing upwards.  Only a rough number for the petals on all these chakras is mentioned; the more detailed numbers are not given.  I am giving them this way too since it will in my opinion suffice for the present practice.

whole_word_matches.context: 'debs pa ni, lte ba sprul pa'i 'khor lo phyi dbyibs ae gru gsum gyi rnam pa can, rtsa 'dab kyi grangs re bzhi pa,

gru.acip: SPYI BO BDE CHEN GYI 'KHOR LO PHYI DBYIBS AE GRU GSUM GYI RNAM PA CAN, RTZA 'DAB KYI GRANGS SO GNYIS PA, KHA DOG SNA TSOGS PA, KHA 'OG TU PHYOGS PA'I RNAM PA CAN DU BSGOM STE, 'KHOR LO ZUNG RE RE THABS SHES ZUNG RE'I TSUL DU SGOM PA YIN NO,,
gru.wylie: spyi bo bde chen gyi 'khor lo phyi dbyibs ae gru gsum gyi rnam pa can, rtsa 'dab kyi grangs so gnyis pa, kha dog sna tshogs pa, kha 'og tu phyogs pa'i rnam pa can du bsgom ste, 'khor lo zung re re thabs shes zung re'i tshul du sgom pa yin no
gru.english: At the tip of the head is the chakra of great bliss; its outer appearance is that of a triangular eh syllable.  It has 32 petals, and is multi-colored.  See it as facing downwards: the point is that you visualize the various chakras in pairs, each as a member of a method/wisdom combination.

whole_word_matches.context: spyi bo bde chen gyi 'khor lo phyi dbyibs ae gru gsum gyi rnam pa can, rtsa 'dab kyi grangs so gnyis pa
