gru.acip: DE YANG THOG MAR RTZA GSUM GSAL GDAB LA, DE GSAL BA DANG DE LA SEMS BZUNG GIN RTZA'I GSAL SNANG DANG DE LA SEMS GNAS PA GNYIS TSOGS BSGRUB STE, SEMS 'DZIN PA NI RTZA GSUM 'DUS PA'I DH'U T'I'I NANG DU GZUNG BA GNAD CHE'O,,
gru.wylie: de yang thog mar rtsa gsum gsal gdab la, de gsal ba dang de la sems bzung gin rtsa'i gsal snang dang de la sems gnas pa gnyis tshogs bsgrub ste, sems 'dzin pa ni rtsa gsum 'dus pa'i dhU tI'i nang du gzung ba gnad che'o
gru.english: Now the first thing you should do is to visualize the three channels; if you maintain a careful focus on them while you try to picture them quickly, then you'll be able to achieve both a clarity of the vision and an ability to hold your mind on it together.  A key point in the focus here is that you try to concentrate on the point within the channel of the dance where the three channels converge.

gru.acip: LUGS 'DI LA RTZA'I GSAL GI GNAS CHA BRTAN PO RING DU SGRUB PA DANG, MI SGRUB PA GNYIS SNANG NA'ANG, SNGA MA LTAR BYAS NA LEGS PA YIN TE, GRUB CHEN LVA BA PA'I GZHUNG LAS, RTZA'I GSAL SNANG SGRUB PAR BSHAD DO,,
gru.wylie: lugs 'di la rtsa'i gsal gi gnas cha brtan po ring du sgrub pa dang, mi sgrub pa gnyis snang na'ang, snga ma ltar byas na legs pa yin te, grub chen lva ba pa'i gzhung las, rtsa'i gsal snang sgrub par bshad do
gru.english: Now it seems that, as this system has been passed down, you can either invest some time in assuring that your vision of the channels, and your ability to maintain this vision, is strong; or you can go on without reaching this point.  It's better though if you do it the former way; the great and accomplished saint, Kambala, is making this same point in his text when He says that one must reach a point of clarity in the vision of the channels.

gru.acip: DE NAS ZHAR BYUNG RDZOGS RIM GNYIS PAS STENG MKHA' SPYOD KYI DGA' 'KHYIL DKAR PO LA BRTEN NAS BDE BA SGRUB, 'OG SA SPYOD KYI DGA' 'KHYIL DMAR PO LA BRTEN NAS STONG PA SGRUB,
gru.wylie: de nas zhar byung rdzogs rim gnyis pas steng mkha' spyod kyi dga' 'khyil dkar po la brten nas bde ba sgrub, 'og sa spyod kyi dga' 'khyil dmar po la brten nas stong pa sgrub
gru.english: After this perform the second of the completion stage practices, using the white swirl of bliss--the one that acts in the heaven--to reach bliss, and using the red swirl of bliss--the one that acts on the ground below--to reach emptiness.

gru.acip: DE LA GSANG CHEN BLA NA MED PA'I LAM GYIS MCHOG SGRUB PAR 'DOD PA DAG GIS, JI SKAD DU RDO RJE 'PHRENG BA LAS, RTZA YI RIM MED NGES PAR NI, ,PHUNG PO LA SOGS MI 'BYUNG ZHING , PHUNG PO MED NA YE SHES CHE, RNAL 'BYOR PA YIS 'THOB MI 'GYUR, ZHES DANG , DE PHYIR 'BAD PA THAMS CAD KYIS, ,RTZA YI 'KHOR LO SHES PAR BYA, ZHES GSUNGS PA LTAR RTZA'I RNAM BZHAG SHES DGOS,
gru.wylie: de la gsang chen bla na med pa'i lam gyis mchog sgrub par 'dod pa dag gis, ji skad du rdo rje 'phreng ba las, rtsa yi rim med nges par ni, ,phung po la sogs mi 'byung zhing , phung po med na ye shes che, rnal 'byor pa yis 'thob mi 'gyur, zhes dang , de phyir 'bad pa thams cad kyis, ,rtsa yi 'khor lo shes par bya, zhes gsungs pa ltar rtsa'i rnam bzhag shes dgos
gru.english: Anyone who has any hope of reaching the ultimate goal by traveling the path of the unsurpassed teachings of the Great Secret must first gain an understanding of how the inner channels work.  As the String of Diamonds puts it, If the various stages Of the inner channels Did not themselves exist, Then surely the heaps And other parts of ourselves Could never happen in the first place. And if there were no heaps, Then yogis and yoginis Could never reach great wisdom. And it goes on to say-- With every effort then That you can make, Strive to understand The chakras of the channels. The following translation is an excerpt from Master Chone Drakpa Shedrup--his explanation on the practice of the completion stage according to the system of the great yogi Luipa, entitled: Lamp that Illuminates the Very Heart of All the Essential Points in the "Golden Harvest of Attainments".  This excerpt can be found in the ACIP database, text S0259, folios 17B-20A, 20B-21A. ************** Our Inner Channels

gru.acip: SKU GSUNG THUGS KYI RTZA'I NANG NA SGO MTSAMS MA BRGYAD DANG SBYOR RGYU MED PAR BSHAD KYANG SPYIR RTZA DANG SBYOR RUNG BAR SEMS TE, LCE'I RTZA BAR GNAS PA'I RTZA SOGS LAS DE RNAMS BSKYED PA DANG SBYOR BA'I PHYIR DANG GNAS NYER BZHI'I RTZA NANG GI KHAMS RNAMS DPA' BO RNAMS DANG SBYOR BAR GSUNGS PAS KYANG 'GRUB PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: sku gsung thugs kyi rtsa'i nang na sgo mtshams ma brgyad dang sbyor rgyu med par bshad kyang spyir rtsa dang sbyor rung bar sems te, lce'i rtsa bar gnas pa'i rtsa sogs las de rnams bskyed pa dang sbyor ba'i phyir dang gnas nyer bzhi'i rtsa nang gi khams rnams dpa' bo rnams dang sbyor bar gsungs pas kyang 'grub pa'i phyir
gru.english: Now it has been taught that there are not any channels among those of enlightened body, speech, and mind which relate to the eight guardian goddesses at the gates of the cardinal and ordinal directions.  Nonetheless, it seems to me perfectly appropriate, in general, to relate these goddesses to the channels.  This is because they do relate to the channels in the sense, for example, of springing forth from the channel at the root of the tongue.   Our point is further established by the fact that it is stated in scripture that the elements contained in the channels of the 24 places relate to the various warriors.

gru.acip: RO RKYANG DBU MA GSUM LUS KYI NANG G-YAS G-YON GSUM NA YOD PAR BSHAD PA NI, DE GSUM DANG POR 'CHAGS PA'I TSE DE LTAR GNAS KYANG , LUS RIM GYIS GRUB PA'I TSE LTE 'OG NAS G-YAS G-YON DU 'KHYOG NAS GNAS PA YIN TE, DE YANG RKYANG MA NI LTE 'OG NAS DBUS SU 'KHYOG STE RTAGS KYI RTZER SONG NAS PHO MO GNYIS KA LA DRI CHU 'PHEN 'DZIN GYI BYA BA BYED CING KHYAD PAR SKYES PA LA KHU BA 'PHEN 'DZIN BYED,
gru.wylie: ro rkyang dbu ma gsum lus kyi nang g-yas g-yon gsum na yod par bshad pa ni, de gsum dang por 'chags pa'i tshe de ltar gnas kyang , lus rim gyis grub pa'i tshe lte 'og nas g-yas g-yon du 'khyog nas gnas pa yin te, de yang rkyang ma ni lte 'og nas dbus su 'khyog ste rtags kyi rtser song nas pho mo gnyis ka la dri chu 'phen 'dzin gyi bya ba byed cing khyad par skyes pa la khu ba 'phen 'dzin byed
gru.english: Now when we say that the trio of the channel of taste, the solitary channel, and the central channel are situated on the inside or right or left of the body, this is with reference to how they are laid out when they first form in the body. As the body though goes through its various stages of development, these three channels start to curve right or left in the area below the navel.  That is--below the navel--the solitary channel curves in towards the center and extends to the tip of the sexual organ.  Here, in both males and females, it performs the function of releasing or retaining urine.  And in males in particular, it also performs this function for the semen.

gru.acip: RGYUD RDOR 'PHRENG LAS, ,DE NAS RLUNG GI DE NYID MCHOG ,DON DAM PA NI BSHAD KYIS NYON, ,RNAL 'BYOR BAS NI RLUNG BSGOMS NA, ,MYUR DU DNGOS GRUB 'THOB PAR 'GYUR, ,ZHES GSUNGS PAS RLUNG GI BSHAD SHES DGOS,
gru.wylie: rgyud rdor 'phreng las, ,de nas rlung gi de nyid mchog ,don dam pa ni bshad kyis nyon, ,rnal 'byor bas ni rlung bsgoms na, ,myur du dngos grub 'thob par 'gyur, ,zhes gsungs pas rlung gi bshad shes dgos
gru.english: So too the tantra called The String of Diamonds says, Now then I shall explain to you That highest thing of all: The true nature of the winds, The ultimate. Listen well, For any yogi who truly learns To practice the inner winds Will quickly reach their goal. In short, you must absolutely learn this explanation of the winds. The following is also an excerpt from the first Changkya Rinpoche's Presentation of the Channels, Winds and Drops. Work Then with the Winds

gru.acip: SNGAR BSHAD PA LTAR RTZA BA'I RLUNG LNGA NI RIM PA BZHIN MGON PO LNGA'I RLUNG DU 'JOG TSUL YOD DE, MI BSKYOD PA, RIN 'BYUNG, DON GRUB, 'OD DPAG MED, RNAM SNANG GI RLUNG DU 'JOG PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: sngar bshad pa ltar rtsa ba'i rlung lnga ni rim pa bzhin mgon po lnga'i rlung du 'jog tshul yod de, mi bskyod pa, rin 'byung, don grub, 'od dpag med, rnam snang gi rlung du 'jog pa'i phyir
gru.english: Now there is a way of describing the five primary winds we mentioned above as the "protector winds," relating them respectively to the Angels named Unshakable; Source of Jewels; Attainment; Limitless Light; and Appearances.

gru.acip: GNYIS PA YAN LAG GI RLUNG LA RGYU BA LA SOGS PA'I LNGA PO DE MGON PO LNGA'I RLUNG DU 'JOG TSUL YOD DE, RGYU BA RNAM SNANG, RNAM PAR RGYU BA RIN 'BYUNG, YANG DAG PAR RGYU BA 'OD DPAG MED, RAB TU RGYU BA DON GRUB, NGES PAR RGYU BA MI BSKYOD PA'I RLUNG YIN PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: gnyis pa yan lag gi rlung la rgyu ba la sogs pa'i lnga po de mgon po lnga'i rlung du 'jog tshul yod de, rgyu ba rnam snang, rnam par rgyu ba rin 'byung, yang dag par rgyu ba 'od dpag med, rab tu rgyu ba don grub, nges par rgyu ba mi bskyod pa'i rlung yin pa'i phyir
gru.english: This brings us to the second part of our presentation: the part on the secondary winds. There is a way in which these secondary winds--the five that start with the one called the "flowing" wind--are as well said to be the winds of the Five Protectors. The flowing wind is the wind of the Angel named Appearances; the running wind is the wind of the Source of Jewels; the coursing wind is the wind of Limitless Light; the surging wind is the wind of Attainment; and the racing wind is the wind of Unshakable.

gru.acip: GNYIS PA YI GE GSAL BTAB NAS SGOM PA NI, GTUM MO'I SKABS SU RTZA 'KHOR BZHI GSAL BTAB NAS SGOM PA LA, RTZA GSUM DANG 'KHOR LO BZHI DANG DE DAG LA YI GE BKOD NAS SGOM PA NI, RTZA RGYUD KYE RDO RJE DANG, BSHAD RGYUD SAM BHU tA SOGS KYI DGONGS PA YIN LA, NAG PO SPYOD PA SOGS GRUB CHEN MANG POS KYANG GSUNGS SO,,
gru.wylie: gnyis pa yi ge gsal btab nas sgom pa ni, gtum mo'i skabs su rtsa 'khor bzhi gsal btab nas sgom pa la, rtsa gsum dang 'khor lo bzhi dang de dag la yi ge bkod nas sgom pa ni, rtsa rgyud kye rdo rje dang, bshad rgyud sam bhu Ta sogs kyi dgongs pa yin la, nag po spyod pa sogs grub chen mang pos kyang gsungs so
gru.english: Here now is the second point, on how to meditate through visualizing the sacred syllables.  When you reach the part where you practice inner heat, then you do so by picturing the four main chakras.  This practice where you visualize the three channels and the four petals, and then lay out sacred syllables within them, is something that the root tantra on Lo Diamond, as well as the explanatory tantra named Samputa, and other texts, intend for us to do.  There are a great number of high and accomplished saints, such as Kirshnacharya, who have as well stated that we should do so.

gru.acip: YI GE 'GOD PA LA RGYAS BSDUS GNYIS KYI LUGS YOD DE, RGYAS PA NI 'KHOR LO'I LTE BA DANG 'DAB MA GNYIS KA LA YI GE SGOM PA YIN KYANG, LUGS 'DI'I MAN NGAG NA MI GSAL LO, ,BSDUS PA NI 'KHOR LO BZHI'I LTE BAR YI GE BZHI SGOM PA YIN TE, BSHAD RGYUD LAS GSAL ZHING GRUB CHEN DU MA'I GZHUNG LAS KYANG 'BYUNG NGO,,
gru.wylie: yi ge 'god pa la rgyas bsdus gnyis kyi lugs yod de, rgyas pa ni 'khor lo'i lte ba dang 'dab ma gnyis ka la yi ge sgom pa yin kyang, lugs 'di'i man ngag na mi gsal lo, ,bsdus pa ni 'khor lo bzhi'i lte bar yi ge bzhi sgom pa yin te, bshad rgyud las gsal zhing grub chen du ma'i gzhung las kyang 'byung ngo
gru.english: There are two different ways of laying out the sacred syllables: the extensive, and the abbreviated.  For the more extensive way we picture syllables both in the centers of the chakras and on their petals as well.  How to actually do this though is not very clear in the advices of this system. In the briefer system we picture four different syllables in the center of the four chakras; this is a practice which is described clearly in the explanatory tantras, and is found as well in the major works of a great many high and accomplished saints.

gru.acip: GNYIS PA RDZOGS RIM GYI RTOGS PA SKYE BAR SMON PA LA GNYIS, RDZOGS RIM GYI LAM RGYUD LA SKYE BAR SMON PA DANG, RDZOGS RIM GYI 'BRAS BU 'GRUB PAR SMON PA'O,,
gru.wylie: gnyis pa rdzogs rim gyi rtogs pa skye bar smon pa la gnyis, rdzogs rim gyi lam rgyud la skye bar smon pa dang, rdzogs rim gyi 'bras bu 'grub par smon pa'o
gru.english: At this point we have reached the second division: praying for realizations of the stage of completion to develop in our minds.  It has two parts: praying to develop in our minds the path of the completion stage, and praying to achieve the results of the completion stage.

gru.acip: DE YANG NANG GI MKHA' SPYOD GTZO BOR SGRUB PA RDZOGS RIM LA DBU MA CHE CHUNG ZHES GSUNGS PA NI, KHA SBYOR LAS, ,GANG GI BSKAL PA GRANGS MED PAS, ,JI SRID SANGS RGYAS GANG THOB PA, ,GANG GI DAM PA'I BDE KHYOD KYIS, ,SKYE BA 'DIR NI THOB PAR 'GYUR, ,ZHES GSUNGS PA LTAR,
gru.wylie: de yang nang gi mkha' spyod gtso bor sgrub pa rdzogs rim la dbu ma che chung zhes gsungs pa ni, kha sbyor las, ,gang gi bskal pa grangs med pas, ,ji srid sangs rgyas gang thob pa, ,gang gi dam pa'i bde khyod kyis, ,skye ba 'dir ni thob par 'gyur, ,zhes gsungs pa ltar
gru.english: Here in the stage of completion, which is primarily undertaken in order to reach the inner Heaven of the Angel, we find two methods: the so-called greater method, and the so-called lesser method, of the central channel.  As it says in the work Samputa, or The Kiss: That which would take you Countless eons--reaching Buddhahood-- Is something which, with holy bliss, You can attain in this same life.

gru.acip: YE SHES DE SKYE BA YANG BDE MCHOG RTZA RGYUD LAS, PHO NYA LHAN CIG SKYES GRUB PA, ,MCHOG DANG 'BRING DANG THA MA STE, ,ZHES GSUNGS PA LTAR,
gru.wylie: ye shes de skye ba yang bde mchog rtsa rgyud las, pho nya lhan cig skyes grub pa, ,mchog dang 'bring dang tha ma ste, ,zhes gsungs pa ltar
gru.english: Regarding the means of developing this wisdom, the Sambara Root Tantra states: The messengers born of the simultaneous Are of three kinds: Highest, medium, and lowest.

gru.acip: GNYIS PA NANG GI MKHA' SPYOD GTZO BOR SGRUB PA RDZOGS RIM RTZA DBU MA LA BSLAB PA LA,
gru.wylie: gnyis pa nang gi mkha' spyod gtso bor sgrub pa rdzogs rim rtsa dbu ma la bslab pa la
gru.english: This brings us to the second great division to the instructions on how to carry out an authentic Dharma once you have succeeded in locating it.  Here we cover how to train oneself in the stage of completion--that is, in the practice of the central channel, which is mainly to help us achieve the inner Heaven of the Angel.

gru.acip: BSKYED RIM LA BRTEN NAS PHYI'I MKHA' SPYOD BSGRUB STE MKHA' SPYOD KYI RTEN DE LA DON GYI 'OD GSAL MNGON DU BYED, RDZOGS RIM GYIS NI TSE 'DIR LUS LA GNAD DU BSNUN NAS DON GYI 'OD GSAL 'THOB PAR BYED PA YIN,
gru.wylie: bskyed rim la brten nas phyi'i mkha' spyod bsgrub ste mkha' spyod kyi rten de la don gyi 'od gsal mngon du byed, rdzogs rim gyis ni tshe 'dir lus la gnad du bsnun nas don gyi 'od gsal 'thob par byed pa yin
gru.english: A person can use the stage of creation to reach the outer Heaven and then, with the life and body they have found there, succeed in bringing about the actual clear light.  The practice of the stage of completion, on the other hand, is used in this present life to bring us to achieve this same clear light through the process of targeting critical points of the body.

gru.acip: DES NA, BSKYED RIM GYIS PHYI'I MKHA' SPYOD GRUB STE ZHING DER SKYES TSE, BLA MA HE RU KA: YAB YUM GYIS DNGOS SU DBANG BSKUR, KHRID MAN NGAG SOGS GNANG NAS RTEN DE LA DON GYI 'OD GSAL 'THOB STE, DAG PA MKHA' SPYOD KYI LUS RTEN YIN NA RTEN DER 'TSANG RGYA BAS KHYAB,
gru.wylie: des na, bskyed rim gyis phyi'i mkha' spyod grub ste zhing der skyes tshe, bla ma he ru ka: yab yum gyis dngos su dbang bskur, khrid man ngag sogs gnang nas rten de la don gyi 'od gsal 'thob ste, dag pa mkha' spyod kyi lus rten yin na rten der 'tshang rgya bas khyab
gru.english: And so when you use the stage of creation to reach the Angel's outer Heaven and then take birth there, you meet your Lama, the Heruka Man and Wife.  They grant you the empowerments directly, and impart to you the various teachings, special instructions, and so on.  There in that body and life then you achieve the actual clear light, for it is an axiom that once you have reached the body and life of a being in the Heaven of Purity, then you will without fail become enlightened in that same body and life.

gru.acip: TSE 'DI LA DON GYI 'OD GSAL 'THOB PAR 'DOD NA, PHYI'I MKHA' SPYOD SGRUB BYED BSKYED RIM BSGOM DGOS PAR MA ZAD, RDZOGS RIM YANG NGES PAR BSGOM DGOS,
gru.wylie: tshe 'di la don gyi 'od gsal 'thob par 'dod na, phyi'i mkha' spyod sgrub byed bskyed rim bsgom dgos par ma zad, rdzogs rim yang nges par bsgom dgos
gru.english: If you hope to attain the actual clear light here in this present life, then you must practice the stage of creation so that you reach the outer Heaven of the Angel.  Not only that, you must absolutely go on to practice the stage of completion.

gru.acip: NANG RDO RJE'I LUS LA GNAD DU BSNUN TE BSGRUB NA RDZOGS RIM GYI RTOGS PA MYUR DU RGYUD LA SKYE YI, DE MIN ZHI GNAS BSGOM PA, SEMS NGO BSKYANG PA, RDZOGS RIM DANG MA 'BREL BA'I BSKYED RIM BSGOM PA, SNGAGS BZLA BA SOGS KHA PHYIR BLTAS KYI THOS BSAM SGOM PA GANG BYAS KYANG BDE STONG NGAM RDZOGS RIM GYI RTOGS PA RGYUD LA MI SKYE,
gru.wylie: nang rdo rje'i lus la gnad du bsnun te bsgrub na rdzogs rim gyi rtogs pa myur du rgyud la skye yi, de min zhi gnas bsgom pa, sems ngo bskyang pa, rdzogs rim dang ma 'brel ba'i bskyed rim bsgom pa, sngags bzla ba sogs kha phyir bltas kyi thos bsam sgom pa gang byas kyang bde stong ngam rdzogs rim gyi rtogs pa rgyud la mi skye
gru.english: If you use the practice of targeting the critical points of your inner body, the body of diamond, then the various realizations of the stage of completion will grow speedily in the stream of your mind.  You can try other things: developing meditative quietude, trying to realize the nature of the mind, practicing any steps of the stage of creation which are not related directly to the stage of completion, reciting the secret words, or anything else.  But no matter what learning or contemplation or meditation you undertake which is directed towards your outside, it will never produce in your mind the realizations of the stage of completion--bliss and voidness.

gru.acip: DE LTAR LUS KYI RTZA JI SNYED KUN GYI MCHOG NI DBU MA YIN ZHING, DE LA'ANG BDE MCHOG RTZA RGYUD LAS, PHO NYA LHAN CIG SKYES GRUB PA, ,MCHOG DANG 'BRING DANG THA MA STE, ,
gru.wylie: de ltar lus kyi rtsa ji snyed kun gyi mchog ni dbu ma yin zhing, de la'ang bde mchog rtsa rgyud las, pho nya lhan cig skyes grub pa, ,mchog dang 'bring dang tha ma ste,
gru.english: Of all these many channels of the body, the highest of all is the central channel.  Of this the secret root text of Highest Bliss says, The messengers born of the simultaneous Are supreme, and medium, and also least.

gru.acip: GSANG BA'I PHO NYA THA MA NI, SNGAGS LAM LA ZHUGS PA RNAMS KYIS SGRUB PA'I GROGS MDZAD PA LA BRTEN NAS, GSANG BA'I PHO NYA THA MA SNYING GA'I RTZA MDUD MA YIN PA'I RTZA MDUD GZHAN RNAMS GROL TE RLUNG DBU MAR ZHUGS GNAS THIM GSUM BYAS PA'I GNYUG SEMS BDE CHEN GYI NGO BOR SONG BAS STONG NYID RTOGS PA,
gru.wylie: gsang ba'i pho nya tha ma ni, sngags lam la zhugs pa rnams kyis sgrub pa'i grogs mdzad pa la brten nas, gsang ba'i pho nya tha ma snying ga'i rtsa mdud ma yin pa'i rtsa mdud gzhan rnams grol te rlung dbu mar zhugs gnas thim gsum byas pa'i gnyug sems bde chen gyi ngo bor song bas stong nyid rtogs pa
gru.english: The least of the secret messengers is involved when the primal state of mind takes on the nature of great bliss and perceives emptiness.  This occurs through the following process.  Due to the fact that persons who have entered the path of the secret word provide us assistance in our practice, the least of the secret messengers appears--which is the unraveling of the knots in the channels (not all the knots, that is, but those other than the one in the channels at the heart).  The winds then go through the three steps of entering in, staying within, and dissolving into the the central channel.  This creates the primal state of mind that perceives the emptiness. [*Translator's note: The Tibetan editor notes a possible error in this section.]

gru.acip: DBU MA'I YAR SNA ZUG SA SMIN MTSAMS KYI SGO NI BYIN RLABS 'JUG PA'I SGO YIN LA, DPRAL BA'I GSHED DU BRKOS PA ZLOG ,GSUNGS PA LTAR BAR CHAD KYANG DE NAS 'JUG PAS, TSE SGRUB KYI SKABS SU, SMIN MTSAMS RTZA YI SGO 'PHAR DU, ,ZHES SOGS LTAR SMIN MTSAMS KYI RTZA SGO DGAG DGOS PA'I GNAD KYANG DES YIN,
gru.wylie: dbu ma'i yar sna zug sa smin mtshams kyi sgo ni byin rlabs 'jug pa'i sgo yin la, dpral ba'i gshed du brkos pa zlog ,gsungs pa ltar bar chad kyang de nas 'jug pas, tshe sgrub kyi skabs su, smin mtshams rtsa yi sgo 'phar du, ,zhes sogs ltar smin mtshams kyi rtsa sgo dgag dgos pa'i gnad kyang des yin
gru.english: The place that the upper tip of the central channel penetrates to is the door at the spot above and between the eyebrows; this is the door where blessings enter.  It is also stated that we should "stop the drill to the forehead flesh," which is to say that this is where obstacles make their way in as well.  This is the key point too that makes it necessary for us to block the door to the channel at this place on the forehead when we perform a ritual to prolong life.  This fact is reflected in verses such as the one with the line, "In the mirror on the door of the forehead channel..."

gru.acip: GRUB CHEN NAG PO SPYOD PA DANG LVA BA PA DANG, MTSO SKYES SOGS KYI GZHUNG MANG POR YANG DE BZHIN DU BSHAD LA, KHYAD PAR DU RGYUD KYI RDZOGS RIM GYI GDAMS NGAG GAL CHE BA RNAMS TSANG BAR BKOD PA'I MAN NGAG SNYE MAR YANG, SKABS DER RLUNG BUM PA CAN SGOM PA MA BSHAD DO,,
gru.wylie: grub chen nag po spyod pa dang lva ba pa dang, mtsho skyes sogs kyi gzhung mang por yang de bzhin du bshad la, khyad par du rgyud kyi rdzogs rim gyi gdams ngag gal che ba rnams tshang bar bkod pa'i man ngag snye mar yang, skabs der rlung bum pa can sgom pa ma bshad do
gru.english: A great number of other works--those of the accomplished saint Kirshna Acharya, of Kambala, and of Tsokye and others, give their explanation the same way.  Most significantly, the Advices of the Golden Harvest--that one work in which all the most important instructions on the stage of completion are contained in their entirety--makes no mention of undertaking the practice of the capsule of wind at this juncture either.

gru.acip: RLUNG SBYOR SGOM PA'I LUS GNAD SOGS NI SNGAR DANG 'DRA LA, SGOM PA'I DUS NI DPAL PHAG MO GRUB PA'I KHRID YIG LAS, BLA MA RNAMS KYIS RLUNG MNYAM RGYU'I DUS SU SGOM PAR BSHAD KYANG, NYAMS LEN LA NYIN MTSAN KUN TU SGOM PA YIN GSUNGS TE,
gru.wylie: rlung sbyor sgom pa'i lus gnad sogs ni sngar dang 'dra la, sgom pa'i dus ni dpal phag mo grub pa'i khrid yig las, bla ma rnams kyis rlung mnyam rgyu'i dus su sgom par bshad kyang, nyams len la nyin mtshan kun tu sgom pa yin gsungs te
gru.english: When you undertake the practice of the capsule of wind, the important details of your bodily posture and so on are the same as before.  As for the time of day when you should do the practice, Pakmo Druppa's book of instructions says, Certain Lamas have said that one should do the practice at times of the day when the winds run equally by nature; but when you are really trying to carry this out in a practical way you should meditate all the time, night and day.

gru.acip: 'DI LA DPAL PHAG MO GRU PA'I KHRID YIG TSIGS BCAD MAR, RO RKYANG GI RTZA GNYIS NAS DBU MAR CHUD PAR SGOM PA DGANG BA'I SBYOR BA DANG, THUB TSAD BZUNG NAS MI THUB PA NA SE GOL CIG GI YUN TZAM ZHIG PHYIR BTANG NAS LHAG MA SDOM PA GZHIL BA'I RLUNG SBYOR DU BYAS LA,
gru.wylie: 'di la dpal phag mo gru pa'i khrid yig tshigs bcad mar, ro rkyang gi rtsa gnyis nas dbu mar chud par sgom pa dgang ba'i sbyor ba dang, thub tshad bzung nas mi thub pa na se gol cig gi yun tsam zhig phyir btang nas lhag ma sdom pa gzhil ba'i rlung sbyor du byas la
gru.english: The versed book of instructions by Pakmo Drupa says on this that the step of "filling up" refers to imagining that the wind has been injected into the central channel from the other two--the channel of taste and the solitary channel.  The step in the capsule of "ejecting" then refers to holding the wind as long as you can and, when you feel you can't any longer, releasing and exhaling the breath for the length of a single fingersnap, then retaining whatever is left.

whole_word_matches.context: 'di la dpal phag mo gru pa'i khrid yig tshigs bcad mar, ro rkyang gi rtsa gnyi

gru.acip: RLUNG 'GOG LUGS DANG YUN CI TZAM ZHIG NAS PHYIR GTONG BA NI, DPAL PHAG MO GRU PA'I GDAMS NGAG LAS, DANG POR RTZA SBYONG BA MIN PAS RLUNG MI THUB BZHIN DU MI GNON PAR, DBUGS KYIS THUB TSAD MI DRAG TZAM DU MNAN LA, PHYI NAS JE DRAG JE DRAG TU GNON PA YIN NO,,
gru.wylie: rlung 'gog lugs dang yun ci tsam zhig nas phyir gtong ba ni, dpal phag mo gru pa'i gdams ngag las, dang por rtsa sbyong ba min pas rlung mi thub bzhin du mi gnon par, dbugs kyis thub tshad mi drag tsam du mnan la, phyi nas je drag je drag tu gnon pa yin no
gru.english: How do we block the wind, and how long are we supposed to hold it before we let it out?  The instructions by the glorious Pakmo Drupa say that-- Since at first our channels are not yet cleared, we should not try to hold the wind longer than is comfortable: hold the breath in as long as you can without any force.  Later on you will be able to keep it there with more and more force.

whole_word_matches.context: g yun ci tsam zhig nas phyir gtong ba ni, dpal phag mo gru pa'i gdams ngag las, dang por rtsa sbyong ba min pas r

gru.acip: DPER NA SEMS 'DZIN GSAR DU SGRUB PA LA, YUD CIG GI RING LA SEMS RTZOL BAS PHAR LA BZHAG PA TZAM MIN PAR, RANG SHUGS KYIS GNAS PA MI 'ONG YANG, MTSAMS SHIG NAS RANG SHUGS KYIS GNAS PA 'ONG BA BZHIN DU RLUNG 'KHOR LO'I LTE BAR 'DZIN PA LA YANG, RE ZHIG GI RING LA RANG GI RTZOL BAS DER 'DZIN PA TZAM MIN PAR, GNAS DER RANG SHUGS KYIS GNAS PA MI 'ONG NGO,,
gru.wylie: dper na sems 'dzin gsar du sgrub pa la, yud cig gi ring la sems rtsol bas phar la bzhag pa tsam min par, rang shugs kyis gnas pa mi 'ong yang, mtshams shig nas rang shugs kyis gnas pa 'ong ba bzhin du rlung 'khor lo'i lte bar 'dzin pa la yang, re zhig gi ring la rang gi rtsol bas der 'dzin pa tsam min par, gnas der rang shugs kyis gnas pa mi 'ong ngo
gru.english: When you are first learning to hold your mind on a certain visualization, for example, it doesn't happen that your mind stays just stays there automatically, without taking a moment of effort to place it there.  In time though, if you practice, it does become completely instinctive.  It's the same thing here with holding the winds in the hub of the chakra; if for the time being you don't make some conscious effort to hold them there, you won't be able to reach a point where they stay there automatically.

gru.acip: DANG PO NI, LTE BA'I RTZA 'KHOR GYI DBUS SU DMIGS NAS SROG DBU MAR 'JUG PA 'DI LA, RTAGS 'CHAR TSUL NI, GRUB CHEN LVA BA PAS, ,DANG PO RI DVAGS SRED BZHIN SNANG BA STE, ,MTSAN MA GNYIS PA DUD KHA'I RNAM PA CAN, ,GSUM PA SRIN BU ME KHYER DANG 'DRA BA, ,BZHI PA SGRON ME 'BAR BA LTA BUR GSAL, ,MTSAN MA LNGA PA RNAM PAR MA BRTAGS PAR, ,SPRIN BRAL NAM MKHA' LTA BUR SNANG BA YIN, ,ZHES GSUNGS SO,,
gru.wylie: dang po ni, lte ba'i rtsa 'khor gyi dbus su dmigs nas srog dbu mar 'jug pa 'di la, rtags 'char tshul ni, grub chen lva ba pas, ,dang po ri dvags sred bzhin snang ba ste, ,mtshan ma gnyis pa dud kha'i rnam pa can, ,gsum pa srin bu me khyer dang 'dra ba, ,bzhi pa sgron me 'bar ba lta bur gsal, ,mtshan ma lnga pa rnam par ma brtags par, ,sprin bral nam mkha' lta bur snang ba yin, ,zhes gsungs so
gru.english: Here first are how the signs come to you when you have gotten the wind to enter the central channel through focusing upon the center of the chakra at the navel.  The great one, the accomplished Kambala, has described them as follows: First you get a vision like The temptation of a forest creature. The second sign is something like A vision of some smoke. The third is something similar to A flight of fireflies, And the fourth is something clear, Like the burning of a lamp. With the fifth of the signs a vision comes Unawares, of something like The sky devoid of clouds.

gru.acip: DE TZAM GYI GO BAS NI YAS BABS DANG, MAS BRTAN GYI DGA' BZHI SPYI DANG, KHYAD PAR DU LHAN SKYES KYI BDE CHEN LEGS POR NGOS MI ZIN PAR MTHONG NAS, RGYUD SDE NAS 'BYUNG BA'I DGA' BA BZHI TSAN GNYIS, GRUB CHEN GYI GZHUNG DANG MTHUN PAR BSHAD DO,,
gru.wylie: de tsam gyi go bas ni yas babs dang, mas brtan gyi dga' bzhi spyi dang, khyad par du lhan skyes kyi bde chen legs por ngos mi zin par mthong nas, rgyud sde nas 'byung ba'i dga' ba bzhi tshan gnyis, grub chen gyi gzhung dang mthun par bshad do
gru.english: I've come to the realization though that--if you understand no more than this about the process--then you will find yourself unable, in a more general sense, to recognize properly the four types of bliss which occur as the element moves down, and as it moves up.  More particularly, you will be unable to recognize the great, simultaneous bliss.  This then is why I've presented for you the two sets of the four kinds of bliss, as they are found in the canon of secret teachings, and in keeping with the way they've been explained in the works of the great sages.

gru.acip: SEMS DBEN GYI YE SHES MTSAN NYID RDZOGS PA SKYES PA'I RLUNG SEMS TZAM LAS, SGYU LUS MTSAN NYID PA SGRUB PA YIN ZHING, MAR LUGS KYI GSANG 'DUS KYI GDAMS NGAG RNAMS DANG, MAR LUGS KYI RIM LNGA'I RTZA TSIG RIM LNGA BSDUS PA GSAL BA LAS KYANG, MAN NGAG 'DI LAS GSAL BAR 'BYUNG LA, DE BZHIN DU 'DIR YANG 'ONG RGYUR SNANG BA MA BYUNG BA NI, 'DUS PA 'PHAGS SKOR LA BRTEN NAS LEGS PAR SHES DGOS PAR SNANG NGO,,
gru.wylie: sems dben gyi ye shes mtshan nyid rdzogs pa skyes pa'i rlung sems tsam las, sgyu lus mtshan nyid pa sgrub pa yin zhing, mar lugs kyi gsang 'dus kyi gdams ngag rnams dang, mar lugs kyi rim lnga'i rtsa tshig rim lnga bsdus pa gsal ba las kyang, man ngag 'di las gsal bar 'byung la, de bzhin du 'dir yang 'ong rgyur snang ba ma byung ba ni, 'dus pa 'phags skor la brten nas legs par shes dgos par snang ngo
gru.english: Now an authentic illusory body comes from nothing other than the wind and mind that occur when one has succeeded in developing the wisdom of transcendent mind which is complete in every aspect.  The various books of advice on the Secret Collection in the tradition of Marpa, as well as The Brief Illumination of the Five Levels, the root text in this same tradition for the practice of the five levels, are more clear on this subject than are the books of advice written specifically on the six practices.  It further seems to me that--since there is no mention in the works on these six of the various visions that come to you--then to learn them well you have to turn as well to the teachings of the Collection in the tradition of the Realized Being.

gru.acip: KHYAD PAR CAN GYI RLUNG SEMS TZAM LAS SGYU MA'I SKU SGRUB LUGS DANG,
gru.wylie: khyad par can gyi rlung sems tsam las sgyu ma'i sku sgrub lugs dang
gru.english: ? Exactly how it is that the body of illusion comes about through nothing more than a very special state of wind and mind;

gru.acip: SKU DE GRUB PA'I STENG NAS DON GYI 'OD GSAL DU 'JUG PA LA, SNANG MCHED LA SOGS PA'I STONG PA BZHI 'CHAR TSUL DANG,
gru.wylie: sku de grub pa'i steng nas don gyi 'od gsal du 'jug pa la, snang mched la sogs pa'i stong pa bzhi 'char tshul dang
gru.english: ? How it is that one enters into the actual clear light on top of attaining this body, and just how the four kinds of emptiness--those that relate to radiance, proliferation, and the rest--appear to one;

gru.acip: DON GYI 'OD GSAL GRUB NAS SLOB PA'I ZUNG 'JUG SGRUB TSUL DANG,
gru.wylie: don gyi 'od gsal grub nas slob pa'i zung 'jug sgrub tshul dang
gru.english: ? How it is that one reaches the union of the two where one still has more to learn, subsequent to attaining the actual clear light;

gru.acip: DE LA BRTEN NAS MI SLOB PA'I ZUNG 'JUG SGRUB TSUL DANG,
gru.wylie: de la brten nas mi slob pa'i zung 'jug sgrub tshul dang
gru.english: ? How it is that, due to all this, one then attains the union of the two where there is nothing left to learn;

gru.acip: BSKYANGS NA, LHA'I SKU MDUN GYI ME LONG LA SHAR BA LA BLTAS NAS DE BLOS BTON TE, RANG LA BSTIMS NAS RANG LHA SKU SGYU MA BZHIN DU SGOM PA NI, SNGA MA'I ZHAR LA GRUB ZIN CING, SNGA MA STOBS CHE BAS PHYI MA CHA CHUNG,
gru.wylie: bskyangs na, lha'i sku mdun gyi me long la shar ba la bltas nas de blos bton te, rang la bstims nas rang lha sku sgyu ma bzhin du sgom pa ni, snga ma'i zhar la grub zin cing, snga ma stobs che bas phyi ma cha chung
gru.english: If you can continue to maintain this kind of practice, then you can easily give up mentally on that idea of staring at the reflection of some picture of an Angel in a mirror. This is because the whole point of having this reflection melt into you, and meditating upon how you now have the body of an Angel which is like an illusion, has again already been accomplished with the practice you have completed before; and since this previous practice is so much more powerful, the latter is of little use.

gru.acip: BSKYED RIM GSAL BAR BYED PA LA KHANG PA KHYAD PAR CAN BSGRUBS PA'I NANG DU, RDZAS SNA GZHAN MANG PO YANG TSOGS PAR BYAS NAS, BRIS SKU SOGS ME LONG GI NANG DU SHAR BA LA BLTAS KYIN SGOM PA CIG , MAR 'GOS GNYIS KA'I LUGS LA 'JUG PA DANG 'DRES PA'I RNAM GZHAG CIG 'BYUNG 'DUG GO,
gru.wylie: bskyed rim gsal bar byed pa la khang pa khyad par can bsgrubs pa'i nang du, rdzas sna gzhan mang po yang tshogs par byas nas, bris sku sogs me long gi nang du shar ba la bltas kyin sgom pa cig , mar 'gos gnyis ka'i lugs la 'jug pa dang 'dres pa'i rnam gzhag cig 'byung 'dug go
gru.english: We also find descriptions where, in order to clarify certain points on the stage of creation, one sets up a special room. Inside this room you set up a whole variety of objects, including paintings of holy beings and the like, which you get to reflect in mirrors. And then you teach the student to stare at the mirror and meditate that way. This is all some kind of mixed-up version of teachings that can be found in the systems of Lord Marpa and Gu.

gru.acip: CHOS THAMS CAD SGYU MA DANG RMI LAM BZHIN DU GSUNGS PA'I SGYU MA LTA BU'I DON NI GNYIS TE, DON DAM BDEN PA SGYU MA LTA BUR GSUNGS PA LTA BU YOD TZAM DU GRUB KYANG BDEN PA KHEGS PA LA BYAS PA DANG, STONG BZHIN DU SNANG BA'I SNANG BA SGYU MA LTA BU GNYIS LAS, 'DIR NI PHYI MA'O,,
gru.wylie: chos thams cad sgyu ma dang rmi lam bzhin du gsungs pa'i sgyu ma lta bu'i don ni gnyis te, don dam bden pa sgyu ma lta bur gsungs pa lta bu yod tsam du grub kyang bden pa khegs pa la byas pa dang, stong bzhin du snang ba'i snang ba sgyu ma lta bu gnyis las, 'dir ni phyi ma'o
gru.english: Now when we say that all existing things are "like an illusion" or a "dream"--that is, when we say things are "illusory"--we can mean one of two different things. When we speak of ultimate reality as being illusory, what we mean is that--apart from the fact that it exists--it is the cancellation of any "true" existence. And then there is a second "illusory" that refers to something appearing in a certain way of which it is, in reality, devoid. In our present context we are dealing with the latter sense of "illusory."

gru.acip: GANG ZAG LA SOGS PA'I CHOS RNAMS KYANG YUL STENG NAS, RANG GIS NGO BOS GRUB PA'I RANG BZHIN GYIS GDOD MA NAS STONG YANG DER GRUB PAR SNANG BA LA BSNYON MI NUS PAR SHES PA'O,,
gru.wylie: gang zag la sogs pa'i chos rnams kyang yul steng nas, rang gis ngo bos grub pa'i rang bzhin gyis gdod ma nas stong yang der grub par snang ba la bsnyon mi nus par shes pa'o
gru.english: It's just the same for the person, and for every other existing thing. The object--from its own side--has been, from the very beginning, devoid of having any nature of its own. We understand though that no one can deny that it appears to have such a nature.

gru.acip: DE LTAR LHA DANG MI LA SOGS PAR SNANG BA NI GANG ZAG DANG, GZUGS SGRA SOGS SU SNANG BA NI CHOS SU 'JOG PAS, GANG ZAG DANG CHOS RNAMS LA RANG GI NGO BOS GRUB PA'I RANG BZHIN RDUL TZAM YANG MED KYANG, LAS SOG PA PO SOGS DANG, BLTA BA DANG MNYAN PAR BYA BA SOGS RTEN 'BREL GYI BYA BYED THAMS CAD KYANG 'THAD DO,,
gru.wylie: de ltar lha dang mi la sogs par snang ba ni gang zag dang, gzugs sgra sogs su snang ba ni chos su 'jog pas, gang zag dang chos rnams la rang gi ngo bos grub pa'i rang bzhin rdul tsam yang med kyang, las sog pa po sogs dang, blta ba dang mnyan par bya ba sogs rten 'brel gyi bya byed thams cad kyang 'thad do
gru.english: And so when something appears to be an Angel or a human or anything of the like, we can say that there's a person there. And when something appears to be something we can see or something we can hear, or anything of the like, then we can say that the parts of a person are there. And so even though people and the parts of people lack even so much as a single atom of existing through some automatic nature of their own, we can say that all the workings of things--the fact that things happen from other things--is all perfectly proper: there do exist things like beings to collect karma; and there do exist things like those we see and those that we hear.

gru.acip: MDOR NA NGA'O SNYAM DU 'DZIN PA'I GZHI GANG ZAG LA, PHUNG PO DANG RANG BZHIN CIG THA DAD GANG DU GRUB SNYAM DU BRTAGS PA'I SGO NAS, GANG ZAG LA RANG BZHIN CUNG ZAD KYANG MED DO SNYAM PA'I NGES PA BRTAN PO BYA STE, STONG PHYOGS LA DE 'DRA BA MANG DU SBYANG,
gru.wylie: mdor na nga'o snyam du 'dzin pa'i gzhi gang zag la, phung po dang rang bzhin cig tha dad gang du grub snyam du brtags pa'i sgo nas, gang zag la rang bzhin cung zad kyang med do snyam pa'i nges pa brtan po bya ste, stong phyogs la de 'dra ba mang du sbyang
gru.english: In short, you must take this thing you are focusing on when you think "me"--you must take this person--and do an analysis, thinking to yourself whether it could be one and the same as its parts, the heaps, or whether it could be divorced from them. In this way you will come to a very firm understanding wherein you think to yourself, "This 'person' doesn't have even the very slightest nature of its own." Practice thinking this way, about the emptiness side of things, over and over.

gru.acip: 'DUN PA'I STOBS KYIS 'DZIN TSUL BSHAD NA, SPYIR LAM SGOM PA LA MI LTOS PAR GZHI DUS NAS KYANG, RMI LAM GSAL BA 'GA' ZHIG LA, RMI LAM ZIN PA MANG PO 'ONG BAS RMI LAM ZIN PA TZAM ZHIG LAM BSGOMS NAS SGRUB MI DGOS LA,
gru.wylie: 'dun pa'i stobs kyis 'dzin tshul bshad na, spyir lam sgom pa la mi ltos par gzhi dus nas kyang, rmi lam gsal ba 'ga' zhig la, rmi lam zin pa mang po 'ong bas rmi lam zin pa tsam zhig lam bsgoms nas sgrub mi dgos la
gru.english: We might say a bit here about maintaining recognition in your dreams by force of your will power. Generally speaking, there do exist individuals whose dreams are very clear even though they are still at what we could call the "original condition" of their lives--at a point where they have not yet undertaken a spiritual path. And among these there are many who can maintain recognition during their dreams; as such, simply having some recognition during your dreams is not something that can only be achieved through spiritual practice.

gru.acip: DE'I PHYIR NYIN BAR GYI DRAN 'DUN DRAG POS GZHAG PA'I BAG CHAGS RMI LAM DU SAD THUB PA LA NI, RMI LAM GYI SHES PA SHIN TU GSAL BA GCIG DGOS PAS, DE'I THABS KYANG NYIN MO BSGRUB DGOS SO,,
gru.wylie: de'i phyir nyin bar gyi dran 'dun drag pos gzhag pa'i bag chags rmi lam du sad thub pa la ni, rmi lam gyi shes pa shin tu gsal ba gcig dgos pas, de'i thabs kyang nyin mo bsgrub dgos so
gru.english: The point then is that--if you hope to be one of those who can plant a seed in their minds through very strong recollection and will power during the day, and then get this seed to reawaken during their dreams--then you're going to have to have to be one of those people whose perception of their dreams is already extremely vivid. And this means that during the day you're also going to have to undertake various means of becoming one of these latter types of people.

gru.acip: 'JIG RTEN LAS 'DAS PA'I RNAM THAR LA SBYONG BA NI, BDE BA CAN DANG, MNGON DGA' DANG, 'OG MIN SOGS SANGS RGYAS KYI ZHING DAG PA DANG, DER BZHUGS PA'I SANGS RGYAS BYANG SEMS BLTA BA DANG, MCHOD PA DANG CHOS NYAN PA SOGS KYI 'PHEN PA BTANG NAS, DE RNAMS SGRUB PA'O,,
gru.wylie: 'jig rten las 'das pa'i rnam thar la sbyong ba ni, bde ba can dang, mngon dga' dang, 'og min sogs sangs rgyas kyi zhing dag pa dang, der bzhugs pa'i sangs rgyas byang sems blta ba dang, mchod pa dang chos nyan pa sogs kyi 'phen pa btang nas, de rnams sgrub pa'o
gru.english: The second way is called "skill in transcendent episodes." Here you decide, before sleeping, that you will try to go to the Heaven of Happiness, or to Total Bliss, or Below None, or any other Buddha paradise.  And there, you decide, you will go and meet the Buddhas and bodhisattvas who live in those places, and make offerings to them, and listen to the Dharma from them, and other such things.  Then in your dreams all this really happens.

gru.acip: DES NA RMI LAM LA RMI LAM DU MA SHES PAR 'KHRUL BA NI, BYIS PA CHUNG NGUS BYAD BZHIN GYI GZUGS BRNYAN LA BYAD BZHIN DNGOS YIN PAR 'DZIN PA DANG 'DRA, RMI LAM LA RMI LAM DU SHES PA NI RGAN PO BRDA LA BYANG BAS, BYAD BZHIN DU SNANG YANG BYAD BZHIN GYIS STONG PAR SHES PA DANG 'DRA, BYAD BZHIN GYI GZUGS BRNYAN BYAD BZHIN GYIS STONG PA DPER BYAS NAS, CHOS GZHAN RNAMS KYANG DE BZHIN DU RANG GI NGO BOS GRUB PA'I RANG BZHIN MED PAR SHES PAR BYED PA BZHIN DU,
gru.wylie: des na rmi lam la rmi lam du ma shes par 'khrul ba ni, byis pa chung ngus byad bzhin gyi gzugs brnyan la byad bzhin dngos yin par 'dzin pa dang 'dra, rmi lam la rmi lam du shes pa ni rgan po brda la byang bas, byad bzhin du snang yang byad bzhin gyis stong par shes pa dang 'dra, byad bzhin gyi gzugs brnyan byad bzhin gyis stong pa dper byas nas, chos gzhan rnams kyang de bzhin du rang gi ngo bos grub pa'i rang bzhin med par shes par byed pa bzhin du
gru.english: As such, making the error of failing to recognize a dream as a dream is like when--as an infant--you grasp to the reflection of an object as being the object itself.  And then knowing your dreams to be dreams is like an older person, one who is already acquainted with the way the thing works; who understands that, even though the reflection may appear as though it were the object, it is devoid of being this object.  Now you can use this as an example--the fact that the reflection of an object is devoid of being that object--which helps you understand how no other existing object either has any nature where it could exist in and of itself.

gru.acip: RMI LAM LA RMI LAM DU SHES PA DE DPE LA BLANGS NAS, CHOS GZHAN THAMS CAD KYANG DE DANG 'DRA BAR BDEN PAR GRUB PA CUNG ZAD KYANG MED DO SNYAM DU NGES PAR BYA STE, BDEN 'DZIN GYIS JI LTAR BZUNG BA LEGS PAR SHES NAS DES BZUNG BA LTAR MED PA'I RGYU MTSAN YANG DAG RNAMS SHES DGOS SO,,
gru.wylie: rmi lam la rmi lam du shes pa de dpe la blangs nas, chos gzhan thams cad kyang de dang 'dra bar bden par grub pa cung zad kyang med do snyam du nges par bya ste, bden 'dzin gyis ji ltar bzung ba legs par shes nas des bzung ba ltar med pa'i rgyu mtshan yang dag rnams shes dgos so
gru.english: You must come to a point where you can take the example of recognizing a dream as a dream and reach a current understanding of things, where you say to yourself, "Every single other thing that exists is the same way: just like the things in dreams, they are devoid of a single shred of true existence."  In short, you have to become very familiar with how our tendency to hold things as real grasps on to what it thinks it sees, and then you have to study well all the true reasons why things cannot be as it thinks they are.

gru.acip: DE LTAR SHES NAS RMI LAM GYI SNOD BCUD THAMS CAD DKYIL 'KHOR GNYIS KYI RNAM PAR 'CHAR BA LA BSLAB CING, DE LTAR SHAR BA DE DAG KYANG RANG GI NGO BOS GRUB PAS STONG BZHIN DU DER SNANG BA'I SGYU MAR 'CHAR BA LA BSLAB STE, DE DAG THAMS CAD KYANG BDE STONG GNYIS KYI RNAM ROL DU BLTA BA SAD DUS BZHIN BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: de ltar shes nas rmi lam gyi snod bcud thams cad dkyil 'khor gnyis kyi rnam par 'char ba la bslab cing, de ltar shar ba de dag kyang rang gi ngo bos grub pas stong bzhin du der snang ba'i sgyu mar 'char ba la bslab ste, de dag thams cad kyang bde stong gnyis kyi rnam rol du blta ba sad dus bzhin bya'o
gru.english: Once you have learned all this you can first practice getting all the places and beings that you see in your dreams to appear as the two halves of a divine and secret world.  After that you have to practice learning to see them as illusory: as things that are devoid of existing in and of themselves, despite the fact that they appear to.  Then go on, as you would in your waking hours, to try to see them all as the divine play of the divine couple of bliss and voidness.

gru.acip: SHI BA'I DUS KYI 'CHI SRID 'GAGS PA DANG, BAR DOR GRUB PA GNYIS SRANG MDA'I MTHO DMAN BZHIN 'ONG NGO,,
gru.wylie: shi ba'i dus kyi 'chi srid 'gags pa dang, bar dor grub pa gnyis srang mda'i mtho dman bzhin 'ong ngo
gru.english: Now when a person dies, the ending of the being at death slides into the beginning of the intermediate being in just the way that a scale gradually tips from one side to another.

gru.acip: GZUGS KHAMS PA'I BAR DO NI DKAR POR MNGAL 'JUG LAS GSUNGS LA, GZUGS MED NAS KHAMS 'OG MA GNYIS SU SKYE NA BAR DO YOD LA, DE GNYIS NAS GZUGS MED DU SKYE NA GANG DU SHI BA DER GZUGS MED KYI PHUNG PO 'GRUB KYI BAR DO MED DO,,
gru.wylie: gzugs khams pa'i bar do ni dkar por mngal 'jug las gsungs la, gzugs med nas khams 'og ma gnyis su skye na bar do yod la, de gnyis nas gzugs med du skye na gang du shi ba der gzugs med kyi phung po 'grub kyi bar do med do
gru.english: And finally those to take birth in the form realm, says Entering the Womb, look white.  There is an intermediate state for those who move from the formless realm to a birth in one of the two lower realms, but a being who moves from one of these two to take birth in the formless realm simply takes on the various heaps of this type of being wherever it is that they happen to die, and so there is no intermediate state for them.

gru.acip: ZHAG SNGA MA PHYED DANG BZHI SONG BA'I MTSAMS NAS, RANG SHI BA DANG BAR DOR GNAS PA SHES PA YIN ZHES ZER MOD KYANG, KHUNGS RNAM DAG YE MI SNANG ZHING, SGRUB BYED RNAM DAG GZHAN YANG MI 'DUG PAS RTOG BTAGS SO,,
gru.wylie: zhag snga ma phyed dang bzhi song ba'i mtshams nas, rang shi ba dang bar dor gnas pa shes pa yin zhes zer mod kyang, khungs rnam dag ye mi snang zhing, sgrub byed rnam dag gzhan yang mi 'dug pas rtog btags so
gru.english: They also claim that, when you reach the juncture represented by the end of the first 3� days, you realize that you have died, and that you are living in the intermediate state.  There doesn't appear though to be any authoritative source at all for this idea, and no other compelling evidence for it either, and so it is a simple fabrication.

gru.acip: 'DI LA GSANG 'DUS 'PHAGS SKOR DU STONG PA BZHI'I RIM GYIS 'OD GSAL MNGON DU BYED PA DE, 'CHI RIM BZHIN DU BYED, SGYU MA'I LONGS SKU SGRUB PA DE BAR DO JI BZHIN DU BYED,
gru.wylie: 'di la gsang 'dus 'phags skor du stong pa bzhi'i rim gyis 'od gsal mngon du byed pa de, 'chi rim bzhin du byed, sgyu ma'i longs sku sgrub pa de bar do ji bzhin du byed
gru.english: This all comes from the teachings on the Secret Collection in the tradition of the Realized One, where going one by one through the four types of emptiness and thus bringing about the clear light is compared to the various steps in the process of death.  And then achieving an illusory paradise body is compared to the process of the intermediate state.

gru.acip: DE LTAR NA DA LTA SAD DUS SU SGYU LUS SGRUB PA BAR DO BZHIN DU SGRUB PAS, GNAS SKABS 'DIR YANG BAR DO'I MING GIS BTAGS PA ZHIG MDZAD DO,,
gru.wylie: de ltar na da lta sad dus su sgyu lus sgrub pa bar do bzhin du sgrub pas, gnas skabs 'dir yang bar do'i ming gis btags pa zhig mdzad do
gru.english: And thus it is that--since reaching the illusory body now, during our waking hours, is like reaching the intermediate state--then this same phrase, "intermediate state," has been applied to this one other circumstance as well.

gru.acip: DE BZHIN DU GNYID KYI 'OD GSAL GYI MJUG TU, RMI LAM GYI SGYU LUS BAR DO JI BZHIN DU SGRUB PA CIG YOD PAS, RMI LAM LA YANG BAR DO'I MING GIS BTAGS SHING, GANG ZAG KHYAD PAR CAN GYIS 'CHI BA'I 'OD GSAL GYI MTHAR, GZHAN LA BAR DOR 'ONG RGYU DE LONGS SKUR SKYED PA CIG YOD PAS, DE LA BSAMS NAS BAR DOR BSHAD DO,,
gru.wylie: de bzhin du gnyid kyi 'od gsal gyi mjug tu, rmi lam gyi sgyu lus bar do ji bzhin du sgrub pa cig yod pas, rmi lam la yang bar do'i ming gis btags shing, gang zag khyad par can gyis 'chi ba'i 'od gsal gyi mthar, gzhan la bar dor 'ong rgyu de longs skur skyed pa cig yod pas, de la bsams nas bar dor bshad do
gru.english: So too, there is the other circumstance--following the clear light of sleep--when we reach an illusory body in our dreams, much the same way as we reach the intermediate state.  And so it is that the expression "intermediate state" is applied to our dream state as well. Finally there are those special individuals who, at the end of the clear light of death, can take what comes to others as an intermediate-state experience and use it to create their paradise body.  This then is the intent behind calling what they do too an "intermediate state."

gru.acip: DE LTAR SAD DUS KYI SGYU LUS DANG, RMI LAM GYI SGYU LUS DANG, BAR DO 'ONG BA'I DOD LA SGRUB PA'I SGYU LUS GSUM, GZHI'I BAR DO JI BZHIN DU SGRUB SHES NA, SAD DUS SU GTUM MO BSGOMS PAS SROG DBU MAR ZHUGS GNAS THIM GSUM BYUNG BA'I STOBS KYIS, STONG PA BZHI 'AM DGA' BA BZHI'I RIM GYIS 'OD GSAL MNGON DU BYED PA DE, 'CHI BA'I DUS SU RLUNG SEMS RIM GYIS DBU MAR ZHUGS NAS, 'CHI BA'I 'OD GSAL MNGON DU BYED PA JI BZHIN DU, SAD DUS KYI 'OD GSAL DANG, GNYID DUS KYI 'OD GSAL DANG, 'CHI KA'I 'OD GSAL BSGOM TSUL GSUM GA YANG, GZHI'I 'CHI RIM LA RLUNG SEMS DBU MAR SDUD PA'I RIM PAS, STONG PA BZHI 'CHAR BA JI BZHIN DU BYA DGOS PAR SHES DGOS SO,,
gru.wylie: de ltar sad dus kyi sgyu lus dang, rmi lam gyi sgyu lus dang, bar do 'ong ba'i dod la sgrub pa'i sgyu lus gsum, gzhi'i bar do ji bzhin du sgrub shes na, sad dus su gtum mo bsgoms pas srog dbu mar zhugs gnas thim gsum byung ba'i stobs kyis, stong pa bzhi 'am dga' ba bzhi'i rim gyis 'od gsal mngon du byed pa de, 'chi ba'i dus su rlung sems rim gyis dbu mar zhugs nas, 'chi ba'i 'od gsal mngon du byed pa ji bzhin du, sad dus kyi 'od gsal dang, gnyid dus kyi 'od gsal dang, 'chi ka'i 'od gsal bsgom tshul gsum ga yang, gzhi'i 'chi rim la rlung sems dbu mar sdud pa'i rim pas, stong pa bzhi 'char ba ji bzhin du bya dgos par shes dgos so
gru.english: This then shows how the illusory body of the waking state and the illusory body of dreams, and the illusory body that you achieve in place of the normal intermediate state that would come to you--these three--relate to the intermediate state in its original form.  Once you understand this, you must go on to understand the process with the state of death as well.  This begins with your undertaking the practice of inner fire, thus inducing the life winds to enter, stay, and dissolve into the central channel.  Due to this, you are able to bring about the four kinds of emptiness--the four kinds of bliss--one by one, and thus reach the clear light. Now when a person dies, the winds and the mind gradually enter the central channel, which brings about the clear-light experience of death.  You are going to have to learn then how to get three events to come about in a similar way; that is, how to practice the clear light of your waking hours, and the clear light of your sleeping hours, and the clear light of the hour of death on the pattern of the way in which--during the different stages of death in its original form--the four types of emptiness come to you due to the gradual gathering of the winds and the mind into the central channel.

gru.acip: YANG GAL CHE BA SHI BA'I 'OD GSAL GYI MTHAR BAR DO JI BZHIN DU SGYU LUS SGRUB PA'I BSRE BA YANG STONG BAR 'GYUR BA DANG,
gru.wylie: yang gal che ba shi ba'i 'od gsal gyi mthar bar do ji bzhin du sgyu lus sgrub pa'i bsre ba yang stong bar 'gyur ba dang
gru.english: You've obliterated as well that crucial concept of blending in the sense of coming to the end of the clear light of death and achieving an illusory body in the way you would have an intermediate being's body.

gru.acip: DANG PO NI, BAR DO 'DZIN PA 'DI LA GANG ZAG RNAM PA GSUM YOD DE, ,RAB NI ZHAL LUNG DANG SPYOD BSDUS DANG SGRON GSAL LAS GSUNGS PA LTAR, 'CHI BA'I MTHAR BAR DO 'ONG BA'I DOD LA SGYU MA'I LONGS SKU GRUB NAS, RTEN DE LA 'TSANG RGYA BA CIG STE,
gru.wylie: dang po ni, bar do 'dzin pa 'di la gang zag rnam pa gsum yod de, ,rab ni zhal lung dang spyod bsdus dang sgron gsal las gsungs pa ltar, 'chi ba'i mthar bar do 'ong ba'i dod la sgyu ma'i longs sku grub nas, rten de la 'tshang rgya ba cig ste
gru.english: Here is the first.  There are three different types of individuals who have recognition during the intermediate state.  The most advanced, as described in the Word from the Lips, the briefer Activities, and the Lamp of Illumination, reaches the end of the death process and then, in place of an intermediate state, reaches the illusory paradise body--achieving enlightenment then in that body.

gru.acip: 'DI LA TSE 'DIR LAM GYI RTOGS PA JI TZAM ZHIG THOB PA DGOS SNYAM NA, RIM PA DANG PO'I RTOGS PA MTHAR PHYUNG, DE NAS SROG DH'U T'IR ZHUGS GNAS THIM GSUM BYAS PA LA BRTEN NAS DGA' BA BZHI DANG, STONG PA BZHI'I YE SHES RIM GYIS BSKYED DE SGYU MA'I SKU DNGOS 'GRUB PA LA NYE BA CIG DGOS SO,,
gru.wylie: 'di la tshe 'dir lam gyi rtogs pa ji tsam zhig thob pa dgos snyam na, rim pa dang po'i rtogs pa mthar phyung, de nas srog dhU tIr zhugs gnas thim gsum byas pa la brten nas dga' ba bzhi dang, stong pa bzhi'i ye shes rim gyis bskyed de sgyu ma'i sku dngos 'grub pa la nye ba cig dgos so
gru.english: One may ask just which realizations of the path a person should have reached in this life in order to reach enlightenment in this way.  He or she must first of all come to the final end of the realizations of the first of the two stages.  They must also have attained, step by step, the wisdom of the four kinds of bliss and the four types of emptiness--through the process of bringing the life winds to enter, stay, and dissolve into the channel of dance.  And they must therefore be someone who is quite close to reaching the actual body of illusion.

gru.acip: RDZOGS RIM BSGOM PA CIG GIS, 'CHI BA'I DUS SU SA CHU LA THIM PA'I RTAGS NAS 'CHI BA'I 'OD GSAL, DNGOS GZHI 'CHAR BA'I RIM PA DANG, DE LAS LANGS MA THAG TU BAR DO 'GRUB PA'I RIM PA LEGS PAR SHES NAS, DA LTA NAS DE'I GDAMS NGAG RNAMS MANG DU SBYONG BA YIN TE, 'DI NI RMI LAM 'DUN PAS 'DZIN PA DANG 'DRA STE, 'CHI BA'I 'OD GSAL RLUNG STOBS KYIS MI ZIN KYANG, DE'I GDAMS NGAG LA GOMS PA'I STOBS KYIS 'JUG PA'I PHYIR RO,,
gru.wylie: rdzogs rim bsgom pa cig gis, 'chi ba'i dus su sa chu la thim pa'i rtags nas 'chi ba'i 'od gsal, dngos gzhi 'char ba'i rim pa dang, de las langs ma thag tu bar do 'grub pa'i rim pa legs par shes nas, da lta nas de'i gdams ngag rnams mang du sbyong ba yin te, 'di ni rmi lam 'dun pas 'dzin pa dang 'dra ste, 'chi ba'i 'od gsal rlung stobs kyis mi zin kyang, de'i gdams ngag la goms pa'i stobs kyis 'jug pa'i phyir ro
gru.english: And if, further, they are someone who has been practicing the stage of completion, they must have a good understanding of the various signs that occur at death, from the dissolution of the element of earth into that of water, on up to the clear light of death.  They must know, well, the order in which they appear to the mind during the actual state of death; and they must be well acquainted with the stages by which one--just after they have come out of these experiences--reaches the state of an intermediate being.  Finally they must be someone who, in this present life, has been practicing their meditations over and over.  This third type of person is similar to the type we described above who undertakes to gain recognition in their dreams by force of will power previous to that, during their working hours.  This is because, even though they are not able to have recognition of the clear light of death by power of their winds, they do engage in the practice by force of the high degree of familiarity they have gained with the pertinent instructions.

gru.acip: 'DI LA 'CHI BA'I 'OD GSAL ZIN NA DUS DER 'TSANG RGYA BAR 'DOD CING, DE YANG BAR DO DANG POR SANGS RGYAS PA ZHES ZER BA NI, SHIN TU MI RIGS TE, 'CHI SRID MA 'GAGS PAR BAR DO GRUB PA GZHUNG TSAD LDAN RNAMS DANG 'GAL BA'I PHYIR DANG, 'CHI SRID TSE 'DI DANG BAR DO GNYIS KYI NANG NAS, TSE 'DI NYID DU GZHAG DGOS PA'I PHYIR DANG, DER 'CHI BA'I 'OD GSAL ZIN NA SKABS DER SANGS RGYAS PA GZHUNG TSAD LDAN GANG NAS KYANG MA BSHAD CING, MI 'THAD PA'I PHYIR RO,,
gru.wylie: 'di la 'chi ba'i 'od gsal zin na dus der 'tshang rgya bar 'dod cing, de yang bar do dang por sangs rgyas pa zhes zer ba ni, shin tu mi rigs te, 'chi srid ma 'gags par bar do grub pa gzhung tshad ldan rnams dang 'gal ba'i phyir dang, 'chi srid tshe 'di dang bar do gnyis kyi nang nas, tshe 'di nyid du gzhag dgos pa'i phyir dang, der 'chi ba'i 'od gsal zin na skabs der sangs rgyas pa gzhung tshad ldan gang nas kyang ma bshad cing, mi 'thad pa'i phyir ro
gru.english: What we say is that this person then goes on to achieve recognition of the clear light of death, and becomes enlightened at that point.  The claim that, rather, this individual could reach enlightenment at the point where they have first entered the intermediate state is completely incorrect.  This is because saying that one could enter the intermediate state prior to such time as the being of death had come to an end would contradict authoritative scriptures--and if you had to position the being of death either in this life or in the intermediate state, you'd have to say it belonged to this life.  And there is not a single authoritative scripture at all which says that the person reaches enlightenment at that point, as they maintain recognition of the clear light of death--and it would be incorrect to say so.

gru.acip: DE BZHIN DU SHI BA'I 'OD GSAL GYI MTHAR BAR DO MTSAN NYID PA'I LUS LEN DGOS NA, BAR DO ZIN NAS LAM SBYANGS KYANG RTEN DE NYID LA MCHOG MI 'GRUB PAS,
gru.wylie: de bzhin du shi ba'i 'od gsal gyi mthar bar do mtshan nyid pa'i lus len dgos na, bar do zin nas lam sbyangs kyang rten de nyid la mchog mi 'grub pas
gru.english: The case is the same at the end of the clear light of death: if one at that point had to take on the body of an actual inbetween being, then even if one were to reach recognition during this intermediate state and undertake some practice of the path, they would still never reach the highest goal in such a body and mind.

gru.acip: GANG ZAG DANG PO LA GZHAN LA BAR DO 'ONG BA'I DOD LA, ,KHONG LA RLUNG SEMS LAS LAM GYI LONGS SKU 'GRUB PA CIG DGOS PA YIN TE, 'DI DAG GI SGRUB BYED RNAMS KYANG GZHAN DU BSHAD ZIN TO,,
gru.wylie: gang zag dang po la gzhan la bar do 'ong ba'i dod la, ,khong la rlung sems las lam gyi longs sku 'grub pa cig dgos pa yin te, 'di dag gi sgrub byed rnams kyang gzhan du bshad zin to
gru.english: And so the simple fact is that the first of the three individuals must necessarily be someone who achieves--in the face of what comes to other people as turning into an intermediate being--a paradise body of the path stage, produced by his or her winds and thoughts.  I have, further, set forth all the evidence of these points at great length, in other writings.

gru.acip: {@CHECK THIS TIBETAN IN MS MESSED UP?}DE LTAR BAR DO NGOS ZIN NAS BAR DO'I LUS MTSAN NYID PA LEN DGOS PAR BYUNG BA 'DIS, RTEN DE LA MCHOG MI 'GRUB KYANG, RANG NYID YI DAM GYI LHAR SGOM PA DANG, DE KHO NA NYID KYI LTA BA SKYONG BA DANG, GANG SNANG GI SNOD BCUD THAMS CAD LA SNGAR SNANG BA SGYU MA DANG, RMI LAM SGYU MAR BSHAD PA BZHIN DU BSGOMS NA KHYAD PAR CHE BAS DE RNAMS KYI GDAMS NGAG NAS BAR DO'I SKABS YIN PAR BSAMS KYIN BSGOM PAR BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: {@check this tibetan in ms messed up?}de ltar bar do ngos zin nas bar do'i lus mtshan nyid pa len dgos par byung ba 'dis, rten de la mchog mi 'grub kyang, rang nyid yi dam gyi lhar sgom pa dang, de kho na nyid kyi lta ba skyong ba dang, gang snang gi snod bcud thams cad la sngar snang ba sgyu ma dang, rmi lam sgyu mar bshad pa bzhin du bsgoms na khyad par che bas de rnams kyi gdams ngag nas bar do'i skabs yin par bsams kyin bsgom par bya'o
gru.english: And so thus you can recognize the intermediate state for what it is; and while a person who has had to take on the actual body of an intermediate being cannot achieve the highest goal with that configuration of body and mind, it can make an immense difference if you can undertake to see yourself as a close Angel; try to maintain the correct view of suchness; and meditate on how what appears to you is illusory, and illusory as a dream is--all in the sense that we explained before.  As such you will have to be practicing at this point, constantly reminding yourself how what is now coming to you is the period of the intermediate state, as it was described in the instructions received.

gru.acip: DE LA GOMS PA MANG DU BYAS PA LA BRTEN NAS, SGYU MA'I SKU SGRUB DGOS PAS, 'DIR 'OD GSAL SNGA MA DE LAS KHYAD PAR DU GYUR PA CIG SPYOD DGOS SO, ,DE YANG SGYU MA'I LUS DNGOS SAM RJES MTHUN PA'I RTEN CIG LA BRTEN NAS 'OD GSAL DU 'JUG PA CIG YIN NO,,
gru.wylie: de la goms pa mang du byas pa la brten nas, sgyu ma'i sku sgrub dgos pas, 'dir 'od gsal snga ma de las khyad par du gyur pa cig spyod dgos so, ,de yang sgyu ma'i lus dngos sam rjes mthun pa'i rten cig la brten nas 'od gsal du 'jug pa cig yin no
gru.english: And since it is the case that one must master this kind of clear light through constant practice if one hopes to attain the illusory body, then one must obviously be practicing a clear light which is far more extraordinary than the kinds we've just described.  There is moreover a practice where one enters into clear light based on a mental and physical configuration involving either an actual or an approximate illusory body.

gru.acip: ZHES GSUNGS PA 'DIR SNANG LA, GRUB CHEN GYI GZHUNG KHUNGS THUB NAS GNYID KYI STONG PA BZHI BSHAD NAS 'OD GSAL 'DZIN TSUL 'DI 'DRA BA GZHAN GANG NAS KYANG MI 'BYUNG BAS, 'DI NAS BSHAD PA BZHIN SHES DGOS SO,,
gru.wylie: zhes gsungs pa 'dir snang la, grub chen gyi gzhung khungs thub nas gnyid kyi stong pa bzhi bshad nas 'od gsal 'dzin tshul 'di 'dra ba gzhan gang nas kyang mi 'byung bas, 'di nas bshad pa bzhin shes dgos so
gru.english: So we do see this reference; and we would have to say that there appears no comparable explanation at all, in any authoritative treatise by the great masters, of the four types of emptiness of sleep, and how to achieve recognition of the clear light of sleep.  And so you should understand these points as we have explained them here.

gru.acip: ,ZHES BDE SDUG GI GNAS LUS KYI MTHA' STE, SNGAR GTUM MO BSGOMS PAS DAG PAR MA BYAS PAR 'PHOS NA, NGAL BA DON MED DU BH'A BA BHA DRAS BSHAD PAS, SNGAR GYI GTUM MO SGOM PA 'PHO BA KHYAD PAR CAN SGRUB PA'I RGYU CIG YIN NO,,
gru.wylie: zhes bde sdug gi gnas lus kyi mtha' ste, sngar gtum mo bsgoms pas dag par ma byas par 'phos na, ngal ba don med du bhA ba bha dras bshad pas, sngar gyi gtum mo sgom pa 'pho ba khyad par can sgrub pa'i rgyu cig yin no
gru.english: The "place" for pleasure and pain is the "end" of the body.  Suppose we undertake to send on our consciousness without having first undertaken the practice of inner fire, and thus purified this body.  Master Bhavabhadra has described this as nothing more than meaningless trouble for ourselves.  And so we can say that one of the causes for accomplishing a truly amazing practice of sending our mind on is to meditate first upon the inner fire.

gru.acip: 'DIR 'PHO BA SBYONG BA'I RTEN DU LHA GANG SGOM SNYAM NA, BLA MA RNAMS RANG GI YI DAM GANG YIN SGOM PAR BZHED, KHA SBYOR DANG GDAN BZHI LAS 'DI LA SGOS KYI LHA SGOM TSUL CIG GSUNGS PAS GRUB NA DE BZHIN DU BYED RGYU YIN YANG, 'DIR TSIG MANGS SU DOGS NAS MA BRIS SO,,
gru.wylie: 'dir 'pho ba sbyong ba'i rten du lha gang sgom snyam na, bla ma rnams rang gi yi dam gang yin sgom par bzhed, kha sbyor dang gdan bzhi las 'di la sgos kyi lha sgom tshul cig gsungs pas grub na de bzhin du byed rgyu yin yang, 'dir tshig mangs su dogs nas ma bris so
gru.english: To begin with, you might wonder to yourself which Angel we should use as the foundation for our practice of sending on the mind.  The Lamas have said that we should do the practice using our own Close Angel.  The Kiss and the Four Seats talk about a specific way of doing this practice with our personal Angel guide; and it is certainly true that this is the way we should do it as we proceed.  Fearing though that this presentation would go on too long if I included those particular instructions here, I will leave it at that.

gru.acip: DE NAS LTE BA'I AA DANG, SNYING KHA'I H'Um DANG, SPYI GTZUG GI KshA GSAL BTAB NAS, 'OG RLUNG DRAG TU THEN PAS AA DE NYID, RTZA DBU MA'I NANG NAS YAR LA KHYU RU RU BYUNG NAS, SNYING KHA'I H'Um LA THIM PAR BSAM ZHING, AA HI KA CI TZAM GRUB PA CIG BZLOS SO,,
gru.wylie: de nas lte ba'i aa dang, snying kha'i hUM dang, spyi gtsug gi kSha gsal btab nas, 'og rlung drag tu then pas aa de nyid, rtsa dbu ma'i nang nas yar la khyu ru ru byung nas, snying kha'i hUM la thim par bsam zhing, aa hi ka ci tsam grub pa cig bzlos so
gru.english: Focus now upon the ah at the navel, the hung at the heart, and the ksha at the tip of the head.  Draw the lower wind up forcefully and see that this same ah letter wends its way up inside the central channel, melting then into the hung at the heart.  Now repeat the expression ah hi ka as many times as you can.

gru.acip: GRONG 'JUG BYED PA'I DGOS PA NI, RIGS DMA' BAS GZHAN DON CHEN PO MI 'GRUB PAS RIGS MTHO BA'I RTEN 'DZIN PA DANG, NAD BU CAN GYIS RANG GZHAN GYI DON MI 'GRUB PAR MTHONG NAS, NAD MED PA'I LUS RTEN 'DZIN PA DANG, NA SO RGAS PAS GZHON PA'I LUS RTEN 'DZIN PA SOGS KYI DON DU GRONG 'JUG BYED DO,,
gru.wylie: grong 'jug byed pa'i dgos pa ni, rigs dma' bas gzhan don chen po mi 'grub pas rigs mtho ba'i rten 'dzin pa dang, nad bu can gyis rang gzhan gyi don mi 'grub par mthong nas, nad med pa'i lus rten 'dzin pa dang, na so rgas pas gzhon pa'i lus rten 'dzin pa sogs kyi don du grong 'jug byed do
gru.english: Just why do we undertake the practice of entering the city?  Perhaps we were born into a very low social status--one with which [in ancient India] it would be difficult to accomplish any great good for others.  And so we take possession of the body of someone of a higher station.  Or else we have contracted some very serious illness, and we see that it would be difficult for us then to be of help either to ourselves or to others--and then we take on a body free of any illness.  Perhaps too we have simply gotten too old, and we seek a younger body.  It is for these and similar purposes that we enter the city.

gru.acip: JI LTAR BYED PA'I TSUL LA 'DI PA'I BLA MA RNAMS GSUM DU BYED PA'I DANG PO SKYANG BA NI, RLUNG SEMS GNYIS LA DBANG THOB, TSE 'DIR GZHAN DON 'GRUB PAR MTHONG ZHING, SEMS CAN LA SNYING RJE TSAD MED DANG LDAN PA'I GANG ZAG GIS GRONG DU 'JUG PA'I MAN NGAG NYAMS SU BLANG BAR BYA STE,
gru.wylie: ji ltar byed pa'i tshul la 'di pa'i bla ma rnams gsum du byed pa'i dang po skyang ba ni, rlung sems gnyis la dbang thob, tshe 'dir gzhan don 'grub par mthong zhing, sems can la snying rje tshad med dang ldan pa'i gang zag gis grong du 'jug pa'i man ngag nyams su blang bar bya ste
gru.english: As for the method that we use to carry out this practice, the Lamas have outlined three different steps.  The first of these is called "extending."  For this, we must first of all be someone who has attained mastery over their winds and mind.  We must as well perceive that if we do undertake the practice in this present life then it will be of benefit to others.  And finally we must be possessed of limitless compassion for all living beings.  This is the kind of person who can carry out the instructions for entering the city.

gru.acip: GNYIS PA LAM LA BOGS 'BYIN PA'I THABS SPYOD PA NI, TSE 'DIR MCHOG 'GRUB PA LA SPYOD PA DGOS LA, 'DI LA YANG BSKYED RIM PA'I SPYOD PA DANG, RDZOGS RIM PA'I SPYOD PA GNYIS DANG, DE RE RE LA YANG SPROS BCAS DANG, SPROS MED DANG, SHIN TU SPROS MED KYI SPYOD PA GSUM BYED PAR SGRON GSAL LAS GSUNGS SO,,
gru.wylie: gnyis pa lam la bogs 'byin pa'i thabs spyod pa ni, tshe 'dir mchog 'grub pa la spyod pa dgos la, 'di la yang bskyed rim pa'i spyod pa dang, rdzogs rim pa'i spyod pa gnyis dang, de re re la yang spros bcas dang, spros med dang, shin tu spros med kyi spyod pa gsum byed par sgron gsal las gsungs so
gru.english: Here now is our second major section, on "enjoyment" as a method for advancing your practice drastically. There are two types of this enjoyment: that for a person following the stage of creation, and that for one who is following the stage of completion. The Lamp of Illumination further states that each of these may be divided into enjoyment with elaboration; without elaboration; and completely free of elaboration.

gru.acip: BYED PA'I DUS NI SGYU LUS SGRUB PA'I MGO RTZOM PA'I DUS DANG, SGYU LUS GRUB NAS 'OD GSAL SBYONG BA'I DUS DANG, SLOB PA'I ZUNG 'JUG THOB NAS, MI SLOB PA'I ZUNG 'JUG THOB PA'I PHYIR DU BYED PA'I DUS GSUM MO, ,'DI RNAMS 'DIR SMOS PA NI MAN NGAG GI GNAD TSANG BA LA 'DI RNAMS KYANG DGOS SO,, ZHES KHA BSKANG PA DANG, DE DAG GI BAG CHAGS BZHAG PA'I PHYIR BYAS KYI, RGYA CHER NI TSIG MANGS SU DOGS PAS MA BRIS TE, SHES PAR 'DOD NA 'DUS PA'I MAN NGAG LAS BTZAL BAR BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: byed pa'i dus ni sgyu lus sgrub pa'i mgo rtsom pa'i dus dang, sgyu lus grub nas 'od gsal sbyong ba'i dus dang, slob pa'i zung 'jug thob nas, mi slob pa'i zung 'jug thob pa'i phyir du byed pa'i dus gsum mo, ,'di rnams 'dir smos pa ni man ngag gi gnad tshang ba la 'di rnams kyang dgos so,, zhes kha bskang pa dang, de dag gi bag chags bzhag pa'i phyir byas kyi, rgya cher ni tshig mangs su dogs pas ma bris te, shes par 'dod na 'dus pa'i man ngag las btsal bar bya'o
gru.english: When does one partake of these enjoyments? There are three different periods: 1) when one has just got to the point of producing one's illusory body; 2) when one has already produced their illusory body, and is practicing to reach proficiency in clear light; and 3) as a means for attaining the union of the two beyond all further learning. The reason I have mentioned these practices here is as a sort of addendum, to tell you that "if you really want all the crucial points of these advices in a comprehensive way, you're going to need these as well." I also wanted to plant a seed in you to practice them in the future. I have not written any very detailed description of them here because of a concern that this treatise would become too lengthy. If you would like to know more on this subject, you can seek it in the advices on the Secret Collection. Bringing about the Final Result

gru.acip: DE'I RTEN GZUGS KYI SKU RLUNG SEMS TZAM LAS GRUB PA NI LONGS SKU YIN LA, SKU DE GNYIS NGO BO GCIG LA LDOG PA THA DAD TZAM YIN ZHING, GZUGS SKU DE LA GNYIS SU MED PA'I YE SHES KYI SKU ZHES LAN DU MAR GSUNGS PAS, GZUGS SKU SANGS RGYAS KYI SAS MA BSDUS PAR GDUL BYA'I RGYUD KYIS BSDUS PA DANG, SHES PA LAS NGO BO THA DAD PA'I BEMS POR 'DOD PA DANG, 'BRAS BU'I SKABS SU YE SHES MED PA SOGS SU SMRAS PA NI, LEGS PAR SMRAS PA MIN PAR SHES PAR BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: de'i rten gzugs kyi sku rlung sems tsam las grub pa ni longs sku yin la, sku de gnyis ngo bo gcig la ldog pa tha dad tsam yin zhing, gzugs sku de la gnyis su med pa'i ye shes kyi sku zhes lan du mar gsungs pas, gzugs sku sangs rgyas kyi sas ma bsdus par gdul bya'i rgyud kyis bsdus pa dang, shes pa las ngo bo tha dad pa'i bems por 'dod pa dang, 'bras bu'i skabs su ye shes med pa sogs su smras pa ni, legs par smras pa min par shes par bya'o
gru.english: The physical body which serves as the basis of this last body is the enjoyment body, and it is made of nothing but the winds and mind. And so these two bodies are merely separate expressions of a single essence; because of this and the fact that this physical body is on a multitude of occasions spoken of as the "body of indivisible wisdom," one should be aware that statements such as the following are not ones which are good: --that the physical body of an enlightened being is not subsumed by the level of a Buddha, but rather something subsumed within the being of the disciple; --the belief that this same body consists of particles of matter which are not types of mental stuff; and --that at the point of the final result one no longer has any wisdom.

gru.acip: ,GRUB CHEN TE LO N'A RO'I GDAMS PA MCHOG , ,DPAL LDAN N'A RO CHOS DRUG CES GRAGS PA, ,GANGS RI'I KHROD 'DIR SKAL LDAN MTHA' YAS LA, ,ZAB MO RDO RJE THEG PA'I DGA' STON MCHOG ,
gru.wylie: grub chen te lo nA ro'i gdams pa mchog , ,dpal ldan nA ro chos drug ces grags pa, ,gangs ri'i khrod 'dir skal ldan mtha' yas la, ,zab mo rdo rje theg pa'i dga' ston mchog
gru.english: This then has been The Six Yogas of the glorious Naropa, Those highest advices Of those accomplished masters, Telopa and Naropa. It is the highest feast Of the profound way of the diamond For infinite numbers Of fortunate ones, here in the Land of Snow.

gru.acip: , ,DPAL LDAN DMAG ZOR RGYAL MO LAS BZHI LHA MOS BSKOR BA DANG YANG GSANG DRAG MO DANG 'CHI MED TSE'I LHA MO DANG BCAS PA'I DBANG DANG RIGS GTAD ZAB MO BSKUR TSUL BKLAGS PAS DON GRUB CES BYA BA BZHUGS SO,,
gru.wylie: ,dpal ldan dmag zor rgyal mo las bzhi lha mos bskor ba dang yang gsang drag mo dang 'chi med tshe'i lha mo dang bcas pa'i dbang dang rigs gtad zab mo bskur tshul bklags pas don grub ces bya ba bzhugs so
gru.english: Recite It, and Your Goals are Achieved: Instructions for Granting Empowerment and Entrance to the Family for the Glorious Queen of the End of War, surrounded by the Goddesses of the Four Modes, along with the Ferocious Woman of the Ultimate Secret, and the Goddess of Deathless Life.

gru.acip: DPAL LDAN DMAG ZOR RGYAL MO LAS BZHI LHA MOS BSKOR BA DANG YANG GSANG DRAG MO DANG 'CHI MED TSE'I LHA MO DANG BCAS PA'I DBANG DANG RIGS GTAD ZAB MO SGRUB PAR BYA BA LA,
gru.wylie: dpal ldan dmag zor rgyal mo las bzhi lha mos bskor ba dang yang gsang drag mo dang 'chi med tshe'i lha mo dang bcas pa'i dbang dang rigs gtad zab mo sgrub par bya ba la
gru.english: Among these you will find the instructions for granting empowerment and entrance to the family for the glorious Queen of the End of War, surrounded by the Goddesses of the Four Modes, along with the Ferocious Woman of the Ultimate Secret, and the Goddess of Deathless Life.  Here then is how you undertake this empowerment and entrance.

gru.acip: GNAS DBEN PAR YI DAM GYI RTEN DANG MCHOD GTOR LEGS PAR BSHAMS PA'I MDUN THAD DU STEGS CHUNG DMA' BAR THIG BTAB STE, DBUS SU GRU GSUM MTHING NAG THOD RAS BSKOR BA,
gru.wylie: gnas dben par yi dam gyi rten dang mchod gtor legs par bshams pa'i mdun thad du stegs chung dma' bar thig btab ste, dbus su gru gsum mthing nag thod ras bskor ba
gru.english: Find a place quiet and far away; place there with beauty an image of the close Angel, and offering cakes to be presented.  Below and to the front of this altar there should be a small platform, on which you will draw out a mandala.  At its center is a triangle of midnight blue, surrounded by a line of skulls.

whole_word_matches.context: un thad du stegs chung dma' bar thig btab ste, dbus su gru gsum mthing nag thod ras bskor ba

gru.acip: SA BON SNGAGS 'KHOR DANG BCAS PA 'OD DU ZHU NAS BUM CHU LA THIM PA(R BSAM STE BSANG CHU BSGRUB,)
gru.wylie: sa bon sngags 'khor dang bcas pa 'od du zhu nas bum chu la thim pa(r bsam ste bsang chu bsgrub,)
gru.english: The seed syllable, Along with the words Of the mantra which surround it, All melt down into light, And sink into the water Within the vase. With this, you have brought into being the holy water which will be used to clear away negativities. Invoking the Goddesses

gru.acip: GTZO MO'I RGYAB KYI DRAG PO LHA MO'I MDUN DU BAM RO GAN RGYAL BSKYEL BA'I STENG DU BHYO: MTHING NAG YONGS SU GYUR PA LAS, LHA MO RE MA TI GSANG SGRUB ZHAL GCIG PHYAG GNYIS MA SHIN TU KHRO SHIN TU KHRO SHING GTUM PA SPYAN GSUM DMAR LA ZLUM ZHING, SMIN MA DANG SMA RA 'BAD PA RAL PA KHAM NAG THUR DU NYIL BA RTING BAR 'PHYANG BA,
gru.wylie: gtso mo'i rgyab kyi drag po lha mo'i mdun du bam ro gan rgyal bskyel ba'i steng du bhyo: mthing nag yongs su gyur pa las, lha mo re ma ti gsang sgrub zhal gcig phyag gnyis ma shin tu khro shin tu khro shing gtum pa spyan gsum dmar la zlum zhing, smin ma dang sma ra 'bad pa ral pa kham nag thur du nyil ba rting bar 'phyang ba
gru.english: There on the ground In front of the Goddess of Ferocity Who rides behind the central Angel Is a human corpse, lying face up. Above it appears a bhyoh of midnight blue, Which turns into the goddess Named Remati--the one Who is practiced in secret. She has one head, And two arms; She rages, She rages, With a temper of fire. She has three eyes, Bloodshot and bulging, With bushy eyebrows And hair on Her face; Her dusty yellow hair Is tied up in locks That stretch down to Her heels.

gru.acip: BHYO: ,DPAL LDAN NYAN GYI RE MA TI, ,LAS BZHI LHA MO GSANG SGRUB SOGS, ,'KHOR DANG BCAS PA MA LUS PA, ,SNGON GYI DAM TSIG GNYER DGONGS NAS, ,GNAS 'DIR MYUR DU GSHEGS SU GSOL,
gru.wylie: bhyo: ,dpal ldan nyan gyi re ma ti, ,las bzhi lha mo gsang sgrub sogs, ,'khor dang bcas pa ma lus pa, ,sngon gyi dam tshig gnyer dgongs nas, ,gnas 'dir myur du gshegs su gsol
gru.english: Bhyoh! O Glorious Remati, Woman of Wrath; O Goddesses of the Four Modes, The Lady of Secret Practice, and such; Along with each and every Angel Counted in Your retinue; Think back now to The pledge You took In the days of old, And come we beg You To this place with speed.

gru.acip: ,ZHI RGYAS DBANG DRAG LHA MO'I THUGS DAM BSKANGS, ,GSANG SGRUB YANG GSANG DRAG MO'I THUGS DAM BSKANGS, ,THUGS DAM BSKONG SHING NYAMS CHAGS GSOS GYUR NAS, ,BAR CHAD SEL ZHING DNGOS GRUB STZAL DU GSOL, (,ZHES BSKANG RDZAS DANG,)
gru.wylie: zhi rgyas dbang drag lha mo'i thugs dam bskangs, ,gsang sgrub yang gsang drag mo'i thugs dam bskangs, ,thugs dam bskong shing nyams chags gsos gyur nas, ,bar chad sel zhing dngos grub stsal du gsol, (,zhes bskang rdzas dang,)
gru.english: O Goddesses of Peace, of Prosperity, Of Power, of Ferocity, May it please Your precious heart. O Lady of Secret Practice, Secret more than secret, Woman of ferocity, May it please Your precious heart. And now that Your holy hearts are pleased, Now that I've restored the pledges I broke, Then come and clear my obstacles, And grant all my attainments. With these lines, you have offered the things which please Their hearts.

gru.acip: ,DPON SLOB DGON GNAS BCAS PA LA, ,DGOS PA'I YO BYAD CI BYUNG YANG, ,DPAL LDAN LHA MO'I 'PHRIN LAS KYIS, ,'BAD MED LHUN GYIS 'GRUB PAR MDZOD, (,CES 'PHRIN LAS BCOL,)
gru.wylie: dpon slob dgon gnas bcas pa la, ,dgos pa'i yo byad ci byung yang, ,dpal ldan lha mo'i 'phrin las kyis, ,'bad med lhun gyis 'grub par mdzod, (,ces 'phrin las bcol,)
