gru.wylie: bshad tshul 'di dang mi mthun par mkhas grub rje'i brtag gnyis rnam bshad las, byang sems srid pa tha ma pa de la dbang gsum pa dngos dbang du bskur ba'i tshe, phyag rgya la brten nas bde chen mtshan nyid tshang ba bskyed par nus la, stong nyid mngon sum du rtogs zin ma nyams pa sngar nas yod pas
gru.english: There is a part in Kedrup Je's Treatise on the Secret Teaching in Two Sections which presents this in a way which conflicts with the explanation above.  It says, Suppose now that the third of the empowerments is given in its actual form to a bodhisattva who is in his or her final rebirth.  This bodhisattva, through practice with their partner, is able to give birth to a form of ecstasy which is complete in every aspect.  They are though still maintaining--they have still not lost--their direct perception of emptiness from before.

gru.acip: YE SHES DE NI DON GYI 'OD GSAL YIN LA, DBANG BSKUR PA'I TSE DON GYI 'OD GSAL GYI SNGON DU 'PHEN PA GTONG BA SOGS KYI GDAMS NGAG PHOG PAS, 'PHEN PA SOGS KYI DBANG GIS DBANG DUS KYI 'OD GSAL DE LAS LUGS LDOG TU LDANG BA NA, SHIN TU PHRA BA'I RLUNG SEMS LAS GRUB PA'I KHA SBYOR GYI LUS MTSAN DPES BRGYAN PA'I RNAM PA CAN DU LDANG BA YIN NO, ,ZHES DBANG DUS KYI 'OD GSAL NI DON GYI 'OD GSAL DANG DE LAS ZUNG 'JUG GI SKUR LDANG BAR BSHAD DO,,
gru.wylie: ye shes de ni don gyi 'od gsal yin la, dbang bskur pa'i tshe don gyi 'od gsal gyi sngon du 'phen pa gtong ba sogs kyi gdams ngag phog pas, 'phen pa sogs kyi dbang gis dbang dus kyi 'od gsal de las lugs ldog tu ldang ba na, shin tu phra ba'i rlung sems las grub pa'i kha sbyor gyi lus mtshan dpes brgyan pa'i rnam pa can du ldang ba yin no, ,zhes dbang dus kyi 'od gsal ni don gyi 'od gsal dang de las zung 'jug gi skur ldang bar bshad do
gru.english: This wisdom is itself the actual clear light.  At the point of their empowerment, they have been granted instructions on practices such as setting a goal for themselves prior to the actual clear light.  Suppose next that--due to these intentions and so forth--they rise forth from the clear light of the time of the empowerment, in a reverse way.  In this case then they rise forth in the form of a body embellished with all the signs and marks of an Enlightened Being--the body of the capsule, made of extremely subtle winds and the mind. What this text is saying then is that the clear light at the point of the empowerment is the actual clear light, and that we rise out of this clear light in the holy body of the Combination of the Two. * * * Je Tsongkapa, in His famed Lamp that Illuminates, Totally, the Teaching on the Five Steps (ACIP digital text S05302, f. 256b), also refers to this account of how Lord Buddha was enlightened--

gru.acip: DE NAS THIG LE MCHOG MA'I SGRUB THABS BSHAD PA, TZANDAN DANG, 'O MA'I ZAS LA KHRI BZLAS NAS NYI MA BDUN NA MCHOD PA RGYAS PAR BYAS TE YAR GYI NGO'I TSES BRGYAD LA RI'I RTZE MOR SONG LA MTSAN THOG THAG BZLAS NA THO RANGS NGES PAR 'ONGS TE CUNG ZAD RGOD PAS CHAGS PA BYAS NAS MDUN DU SDOD DO,,
gru.wylie: de nas thig le mchog ma'i sgrub thabs bshad pa, tsandan dang, 'o ma'i zas la khri bzlas nas nyi ma bdun na mchod pa rgyas par byas te yar gyi ngo'i tshes brgyad la ri'i rtse mor song la mtshan thog thag bzlas na tho rangs nges par 'ongs te cung zad rgod pas chags pa byas nas mdun du sdod do
gru.english: Next we explain a ritual for reaching the Lady of the Ultimate Drop, Tilottama.  Set out a small torma cake which has mixed in it both sandalwood and milk.  For the length of seven days, make extensive offerings, and then on the eighth day of the waxing moon climb a high mountain peak.  Spend the whole night there reciting mantas, and at daybreak She will without doubt come to you.  She acts a little wild, and will stand in front of you in a pose of passion.

gru.acip: 'KHYUD PA DANG 'O BYAS SHING DGA' BAS CHAGS PAR BYAS NA 'DI LTAR 'GRUB PAR 'GYUR TE, GANG 'DOD PA DE STER ZHING, RGYAB TU ZHON NA MTHO RIS SU YANG 'KHYER BAR BYED DO, ,GZHAN YANG RGYAL SRID STER BAR BYED DO,,
gru.wylie: 'khyud pa dang 'o byas shing dga' bas chags par byas na 'di ltar 'grub par 'gyur te, gang 'dod pa de ster zhing, rgyab tu zhon na mtho ris su yang 'khyer bar byed do, ,gzhan yang rgyal srid ster bar byed do
gru.english: If you embrace Her, and kiss her, and take your pleasure with Her joyfully, then She will grant you certain attainments--She will give you anything you seek, and can take you on Her back to one of the higher rebirths.  She also has the power to gift you an entire kingdom. * * * An ancient text by Master Ratna Rakshita repeats the need for a physical partner, one like the Lady who served as Lord Buddha's own; this from The One with the Lotus: A Commentary upon Difficult Points in the Great King of Secret Books, the Glorious "Source of Vows" (ACIP digital text TD01420, ff. 17a-17b)--

gru.acip: BCOM LDAN 'DAS DON GRUB BYANG CHUB SHING GI RTZA BAR 'DUG PA LA NAM MKHAR BZHUGS PA'I YANG DAG PAR RDZOGS PA'I SANGS RGYAS RNAMS KYIS MI G-YO BA'I TING NGE 'DZIN 'DUS BYAS PA BSAL NAS MTSAN PHYED NA BLA NA MED PA'I SHES RAB GTAD DE, SHES RAB DANG DBANG BZHI PA DAG BYIN NO ZHES SO,,
gru.wylie: bcom ldan 'das don grub byang chub shing gi rtsa bar 'dug pa la nam mkhar bzhugs pa'i yang dag par rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas rnams kyis mi g-yo ba'i ting nge 'dzin 'dus byas pa bsal nas mtshan phyed na bla na med pa'i shes rab gtad de, shes rab dang dbang bzhi pa dag byin no zhes so
gru.english: The Conqueror, Siddhartha, sat at the base of the Bodhi Tree; the Buddhas of total enlightenment stood in the sky above, and stirred him from the unmoving, single-pointed meditation which he had gathered around him.  At the midnight hour, They granted him this unsurpassed Lady of Wisdom--as the holy books say, "They gave him the empowerment of wisdom, and the fourth empowerment." * Je Tsongkapa's Partner Practice The story of how Je Tsongkapa, the founder of the Gelukpa order of the Dalai Lamas, met and practiced with His spiritual partner is described in many works, some of which we will turn to here.  The late Dzeme Rinpoche Lobsang Pelnden Tendzin Yargye (1927-1996), one of the closest disciples of Kyabje Trijang Rinpoche, tutor to His Holiness the present Dalai Lama, begins our discussion simply in His Entertainment of a Million Wonders: Notes on the Glorious Sphere of Highest Bliss (Chakra Sanvara) (ACIP digital text S12108, f. 242b)--

gru.acip: /132 NRA/ DE NAS DGA' LDAN DU PHEBS BDE MCHOG GI BSKYED RIM 'DOD 'JO DANG, RDZOGS RIM CHE CHUNG SGRUB THABS RNAMS DANG, SGRON GSAL DAG THER DANG MCHAN CAN, BSDUS DON, LE'U SO SO'I MTHA' DPYOD RNAMS DANG, RGYUD SDE BZHI DANG 'BREL BA'I BSHAD PA MTHA' DAG DANG GDAMS PA RGYUN MA CHAD PAR GSUNGS, MDO SNGAGS KYI BSTAN PA NYIN MO LTAR GSAL BA'I THUGS RJE CHEN PO MDZAD DO,,
gru.wylie: /132 nra/ de nas dga' ldan du phebs bde mchog gi bskyed rim 'dod 'jo dang, rdzogs rim che chung sgrub thabs rnams dang, sgron gsal dag ther dang mchan can, bsdus don, le'u so so'i mtha' dpyod rnams dang, rgyud sde bzhi dang 'brel ba'i bshad pa mtha' dag dang gdams pa rgyun ma chad par gsungs, mdo sngags kyi bstan pa nyin mo ltar gsal ba'i thugs rje chen po mdzad do
gru.english: [Instructions for painting scene number] 132A: Je Rinpoche then makes his way to Ganden, where he teaches constantly, covering the Cow that Grants All Wishes, on the stage of creation in the secret teachings of Highest Bliss; the practices for reaching the Angel which involve both the greater and lesser forms of the stage of completion; the final, corrected version of the Lantern, as well as the version with interlinear notes; a summary of the work; a dialectical analysis of each of the different chapters; and an explanation related to the four different classes of tantra--along with personal advices on each.  In short, He grants the great kindness of illuminating the open and secret teachings, as if He were the sun itself.

gru.acip: DE DUS SNYUN DVANGS SKABS 'JAM DBYANGS GZI BRJID RMAD DU BYUNG BA GCIG GI ZHAL NAS DA PHYIN CHAD BSKYED RDZOGS KYI THUGS NYAMS SU BZHES PA LA 'GRUS PAR MDZAD NA SNGAGS BLA MED KYI RTOGS PA KHYAD PAR CAN MYUR DU 'KHRUNGS SHING, SLOB MA SKAL LDAN BDUN LA YANG LAM GYI RTOGS PA KHYAD PAR CAN RE SKYE BAR 'GYUR GSUNGS,
gru.wylie: de dus snyun dvangs skabs 'jam dbyangs gzi brjid rmad du byung ba gcig gi zhal nas da phyin chad bskyed rdzogs kyi thugs nyams su bzhes pa la 'grus par mdzad na sngags bla med kyi rtogs pa khyad par can myur du 'khrungs shing, slob ma skal ldan bdun la yang lam gyi rtogs pa khyad par can re skye bar 'gyur gsungs
gru.english: [Scene number] 132B: During this time--at a point where he is recovering from his illness--a majestic form of Gentle Voice appears to Je Rinpoche.  He tells the Lord, "From this point on, you must throw yourself into practicing the stages of creation and completion.  If you do so, then you will quickly give birth to high realizations of the unsurpassed teachings of the secret word.  Seven of your disciples--those with the fortune that comes from good deeds--will as well achieve extraordinary realizations of the path."

gru.acip: DA PHYIN CHAD GTZO BOR BSKYED RDZOGS KYI RNAL 'BYOR THUGS NYAMS SU BZHES PA LA 'GRUS PAR MDZAD NA, SNGAGS BLA MED KYI SGO NAS RTOGS PA KHYAD PAR CAN MYUR DU RGYUD LA 'KHRUNGS SHING, SLOB MA SKAL LDAN BDUN LA YANG, LAM GYI RTOGS PA KHYAD PAR CAN RE SKYE BAR 'GYUR RO, ,ZHES LUNG BSTAN PAR MDZAD PA LA,
gru.wylie: da phyin chad gtso bor bskyed rdzogs kyi rnal 'byor thugs nyams su bzhes pa la 'grus par mdzad na, sngags bla med kyi sgo nas rtogs pa khyad par can myur du rgyud la 'khrungs shing, slob ma skal ldan bdun la yang, lam gyi rtogs pa khyad par can re skye bar 'gyur ro, ,zhes lung bstan par mdzad pa la
gru.english: From now on I want you to concentrate your efforts primarily on undertaking the practices of the creation and completion stages.  If you utilize the practices of the unsurpassed teachings of the way of the secret word, then extraordinary realizations will come to you, and quickly.  Seven of your disciples, those with the most goodness in them, will as well each achieve extraordinary realizations of the path.

gru.acip: RJE'I ZHAL SNGA NAS RANG GIS GTZO BOR SKU MTSAMS KYI NGANG NAS SGRUB PA LHUR MDZAD NA, RJE'I ZHAL SNGA NAS RANG GI THUGS RGYUD LA LAM DE MYUR DU 'KHRUNG PA'I NANG GI RGYU BDE STONG GI YE SHES KHYAD PAR CAN LA SOGS PA SNGAR THUGS RGYUD LA 'KHRUNGS TSAR ZHING, PHYI'I RKYEN ZHING SKYES KYI PHO NYA MO RNAMS KYIS GROGS MDZAD PA LA SOGS PA KHYAD PAR CAN MYUR DU 'ONG,
gru.wylie: rje'i zhal snga nas rang gis gtso bor sku mtshams kyi ngang nas sgrub pa lhur mdzad na, rje'i zhal snga nas rang gi thugs rgyud la lam de myur du 'khrung pa'i nang gi rgyu bde stong gi ye shes khyad par can la sogs pa sngar thugs rgyud la 'khrungs tshar zhing, phyi'i rkyen zhing skyes kyi pho nya mo rnams kyis grogs mdzad pa la sogs pa khyad par can myur du 'ong
gru.english: "The Lord himself, for His part, should as well focus His efforts mainly upon doing retreat.  The inner causes that bring on this particular path with speed are things like the extraordinary wisdom of bliss and voidness--and the Lord has long since given birth to these within His holy heart.  Now He will have extraordinary experiences brought on by the outer aids: by Messengers born of paradise, for example, who will help Him in His quest.

gru.acip: SKABS 'DIR RJE RTOGS LDAN PAR MNAL LTAS BYUNG TSUL SKOR, MKHAS GRUB THAMS CAD MKHYEN PAS MDZAD PA'I GSANG RNAM SOGS SU GONG DU BKOD PA LTAR BYUNG ZHING, RJE BLO GROS LEGS BZANG GIS MDZAD PA'I GSANG RNAM DU 'KHOR GYI MNAL LTAS GONG GI DE DAG DANG CUNG ZAD MI 'DRA BA 'DI LTAR BYUNG STE,
gru.wylie: skabs 'dir rje rtogs ldan par mnal ltas byung tshul skor, mkhas grub thams cad mkhyen pas mdzad pa'i gsang rnam sogs su gong du bkod pa ltar byung zhing, rje blo gros legs bzang gis mdzad pa'i gsang rnam du 'khor gyi mnal ltas gong gi de dag dang cung zad mi 'dra ba 'di ltar byung ste
gru.english: Concerning the visions that Lord Tokdenpa experienced in his dreams at this point, works like the Secret Biography of the omniscient Kedrup Je give the account as we've presented it above.  We see though in the secret biography of Lord Lodru Leksang a slightly different version of the dream visions that Je Tsongkapa's disciples were experiencing during this period.

gru.acip: RJE'I ZHAL SNGA NAS RANG GIS GTZO BOR SKU MTSAMS KYI NGANG NAS SGRUB PA LHUR MDZAD NA, RJE'I ZHAL SNGA NAS RANG GI THUGS RGYUD LA LAM DE MYUR DU 'KHRUNGS PA'I NANG GI RGYU BDE STONG GI YE SHES KHYAD PAR CAN LA SOGS PA SNGAR THUGS RGYUD LA 'KHRUNGS TSAR ZHING PHYI'I RKYEN ZHING SKYES KYI PHO NYA MO RNAMS KYIS GROGS MDZAD PA LA SOGS PA KHYAD PA CAN MYUR DU 'ONG,
gru.wylie: rje'i zhal snga nas rang gis gtso bor sku mtshams kyi ngang nas sgrub pa lhur mdzad na, rje'i zhal snga nas rang gi thugs rgyud la lam de myur du 'khrungs pa'i nang gi rgyu bde stong gi ye shes khyad par can la sogs pa sngar thugs rgyud la 'khrungs tshar zhing phyi'i rkyen zhing skyes kyi pho nya mo rnams kyis grogs mdzad pa la sogs pa khyad pa can myur du 'ong
gru.english: And then Je Tsongkapa said, "The Holy One has told me that I should be making great efforts now in doing retreat."  He continued by saying, "This Being has told me that I have already given birth, in my heart, to the inner causes that would make this path come quickly to me: causes such as an extraordinary form of the wisdom of bliss and voidness.  And He says that there will quickly come to me an extraordinary form of the outer aids to realization: aids like Messenger ladies born of paradise, who will come and be my companions in my quest.

gru.acip: SGRUB MCHOD SOGS 'DU KHANG DU BYAS NA DBANG MA THOB PAS DKYIL 'KHOR MTHONG BA'I DGAG BYA CHE BAS SNGAGS KYI SGRUB KHANG 'GOL BA GCIG DGOS GSUNGS NAS, LUG LOR YANGS PA CAN GYI RMANG BTINGS,
gru.wylie: sgrub mchod sogs 'du khang du byas na dbang ma thob pas dkyil 'khor mthong ba'i dgag bya che bas sngags kyi sgrub khang 'gol ba gcig dgos gsungs nas, lug lor yangs pa can gyi rmang btings
gru.english: At this point, Je Tsongkapa said to his disciples: "If we continue activities like our tantric ceremonies and offerings in the monastery temple, then there is the major problem that people who have not yet received empowerment into these practices will be able to see our secret world.  We need to build a separate building where we can do these special practices."  And so in the Year of the Sheep [1415], the foundation for Yangpachen Temple was laid. And here is the latter part, from the same text; we can see that Geshe Chahar has excerpted directly from it.  The songs that are mentioned include a number of sections that concern practice with our spiritual partner; we'll be getting familiar with them later on in the course--

gru.acip: ,CES 'DZAM GLING 'DI KHO NAR YANG RGYA GAR RGYA NAG BAL YUL SOGS DANG, ,NANG TSAN BOD YUL 'DIR DBUS GTZANG MDO KHAMS SOGS KUN TU MKHAS DANG GRUB PA'I RNAM ROL MTHA' KLAS PAS 'GRO BA'I DON MDZAD DANG MDZAD PAR 'GYUR
gru.wylie: ces 'dzam gling 'di kho nar yang rgya gar rgya nag bal yul sogs dang, ,nang tshan bod yul 'dir dbus gtsang mdo khams sogs kun tu mkhas dang grub pa'i rnam rol mtha' klas pas 'gro ba'i don mdzad dang mdzad par 'gyur
gru.english: What these lines are telling us is that Je Tsongkapa--in just this one world, not to mention others--came and acted out the part of a wise and accomplished saint countless times in foreign lands such as India, China, Nepal, and others; here in Tibet, He did so in the provinces of U-Tsang, Amdo, Kham, and all the rest.  And He will continue to do so in the future. * * * Je Tsongkapa was of course the teacher of His Holiness the First Dalai Lama, Gendun Drup (1391-1474).  The Dalai Lamas and the Panchen Lamas share the distinction of being the greatest lines of reincarnated Lamas in the history of Tibet, and the first of the Panchen Lamas--Lobsang Chukyi Gyeltsen (1565-1662)--was the greatest of His line. His own relationship to Sarasvati is expressed in the following poem, which we add here first of all since our course in the Diamond Way began with this Lama's Path to Bliss, and secondly because the lines give us a rare insight into the intensity of a partnership with a divine Being. The selection is taken from A Brief Biography of His Holiness the First Panchen Lama, Lobsang Chukyi Gyeltsen, which is found in The Biographies of the Lamas of the Teachings on the Steps of the Path to Enlightenment (ACIP digital text S05985, see pp. 493-495), written by Tsechok Ling, Yongdzin Yeshe Gyeltsen (1713-1793), Tutor to His Holiness the Eighth Dalai Lama.  His Holiness, like Je Tsongkapa, has these experiences of Sarasvati just as He is reaching manhood.

gru.acip: ZLA BA DE'I TSES BRGYAD LA MKHAS GRUB CHEN PO SANGS RGYAS YE SHES LA DBYANGS CAN MA DKAR MO'I RJES GNANG ZHUS TE
gru.wylie: zla ba de'i tshes brgyad la mkhas grub chen po sangs rgyas ye shes la dbyangs can ma dkar mo'i rjes gnang zhus te
gru.english: On the eighth day of that same month, He came to that wise and accomplished master, Kedrup Sangye Yeshe, and had the good fortune to be granted the rite of permission into the secret world of the Lady of Song (Sarasvati, or Yangchenma), in Her form of purest white.

gru.acip: KHYAD PAR DBYANGS CAN MA DE'I THUGS KA NAS LHA MO DBYANGS CAN MA SNGON MO PHYAG GNYIS RIN PO CHE'I YOL GO DNGOS GRUB GZUGS CAN LTA BU'I SHING THOG GSAR PAS BKANG BA 'DZIN PA ZHIG 'THON TE SNOD BCUD DANG BCAS PA GTZO MO LA PHUL BA,
gru.wylie: khyad par dbyangs can ma de'i thugs ka nas lha mo dbyangs can ma sngon mo phyag gnyis rin po che'i yol go dngos grub gzugs can lta bu'i shing thog gsar pas bkang ba 'dzin pa zhig 'thon te snod bcud dang bcas pa gtso mo la phul ba
gru.english: Here is what He saw.  Out of the heart of the Lady of Song comes another goddess, another Lady of Song--this one with a body of sea-blue green.  In Her two hands She bears forth a priceless bowl of jewel, filled with fresh fruit that are, in reality, high spiritual attainments in a physical form.  This Lady of the Sky turns, and offers the bowl and its fruit to the first Lady.

gru.acip: ZHES PA 'DI PHYAG BRIS SU MDZAD DO, ,BSTOD PA 'DI NI DBYANGS CAN MA'I SKU JI LTAR GZIGS PA LTAR DU BSTOD PA MDZAD PA YIN PAS 'DI LA DBYANGS CAN MA'I BSTOD PA GZIGS SNANG MA ZHES RJE BTZUN BLO BZANG CHOS KYI RGYAL MTSAN GYI THUGS SRAS GRUB CHEN RNAMS MTHUN PAR GSUNG GO,
gru.wylie: zhes pa 'di phyag bris su mdzad do, ,bstod pa 'di ni dbyangs can ma'i sku ji ltar gzigs pa ltar du bstod pa mdzad pa yin pas 'di la dbyangs can ma'i bstod pa gzigs snang ma zhes rje btsun blo bzang chos kyi rgyal mtshan gyi thugs sras grub chen rnams mthun par gsung go
gru.english: This poem was found as a handwritten manuscript.* Since it sings the praises of the Lady of Song according to someone who is describing what they actually saw, the great masters who are spiritual sons of the venerable Lobsang Chukyi Gyeltsen speak as one in referring to it as The Praise of the Lady of Song, Who Came to Me. *Translator's note: The author of the biography, Master Tsechok Ling, notes that much of the poetry found in the biography is not found in the First Panchen's Lamas collected works; but has rather been taken from a secret tradition of chanting his poems at the tantric college connected to His Holiness' main monastery, Trashi Hlunpo. * * * * The Partner Practice of Master Naropa, Lady Niguma, and Their Immediate Lineage One of the earliest, and perhaps the greatest, histories of Buddhism in India and Tibet--for the period up to Je Tsongkapa--is the Blue Annals of Gu Lotsawa Shunnu Pel (1392-1481).  We'll use it to begin our exploration of the partner practice shared by Master Naropa (1012-1100) and Lady Niguma (c. 1000).  The entire chapter on the life of Lady Niguma is found in Course 8 of the Tantric Series; here is just the opening section, which states Her relationship to Master Naropa (f. 2b of the section on Kodrakpa and Niguma, ACIP uncataloged data file reference DNGOA).

gru.acip: LUGS DE'I LEN PA PO NI GRUB THOB KHYUNG PO RNAL 'BYOR TE, DE NI GDUNG RUS KHYUNG PO, YAB STAG SKYES, YUM BKRA SHIS SKYID GNYIS KYI SRAS SU STAG GI LO LA SNYE MO RA MANGS SU 'KHRUNGS,
gru.wylie: lugs de'i len pa po ni grub thob khyung po rnal 'byor te, de ni gdung rus khyung po, yab stag skyes, yum bkra shis skyid gnyis kyi sras su stag gi lo la snye mo ra mangs su 'khrungs
gru.english: The one who first received this method of practice was the accomplished yogi Kyungpo Neljor.  He was born among the Kyungpo people, Born of the Tiger, and His holy mother was Trashi Kyi, Joy of Goodness.  Their excellent son came into this world in the Year of the Tiger [probably the one in 1014 AD or close to it], at Ramang in the province of Nyemo. * * * The six practices of Niguma are listed as follows in His Holiness the First Panchen Lama's Lamp for Making Things Even More Clear: An Expanded Explanation of the Root Text for the Great Seal (Mahamudra) according to the System of the Precious Tradition of the Virtuous Ones (The Gelukpa) (ACIP digital text S05940, f. 11a):

gru.acip: ,,LHA DKON MCHOG GSUM LA PHYAG 'TSAL LO, ,DKON MCHOG GSUM GYIS THUGS RJES BZUNG,, ,'GRO DRUG PHA MA'I RANG BZHIN LA, ,GCIG GNYIS PHA MAR MA SHES KYANG, ,BKA' BZHIN SGRUB PO 'DI 'DRA 'TSAL, ,RTOG MED GTZANG SBRA LA GNAS SHING, ,MU STEGS DRI MED THEG CHEN RIGS, ,RNYED NA BDAG LA BKA' STZOL GCIG, ,CES BUD MED 'DI LTA BU ZHIG BYUNG NA YAB YUM GYI BKA' MI BCAG GSUNG,
gru.wylie: lha dkon mchog gsum la phyag 'tshal lo, ,dkon mchog gsum gyis thugs rjes bzung,, ,'gro drug pha ma'i rang bzhin la, ,gcig gnyis pha mar ma shes kyang, ,bka' bzhin sgrub po 'di 'dra 'tshal, ,rtog med gtsang sbra la gnas shing, ,mu stegs dri med theg chen rigs, ,rnyed na bdag la bka' stsol gcig, ,ces bud med 'di lta bu zhig byung na yab yum gyi bka' mi bcag gsung
gru.english: I bow down to my Angel, and to the Jewels. In kindness the Triple Gem Has taken me into Their care; And although every single being Of the six realms of existence Is by their very nature Our father and our mother, We do not know one another. Nonetheless, I agree to honor The wishes you've expressed; But to do so you must seek for me A maiden who's like this. She must be free of imagining That things come from their side, And she must be a person Of absolute cleanliness. She must be a pure Hindu, And at the same time must belong To a family of the greater way. If you can find this maiden, Your wish is my command. "That is," he said, "I will be able to avoid breaking your command, Father and Mother, if you can find me a maiden like this."

gru.acip: RIGS BRAM ZE YIN, GRUB MTHA' PHYI ROL PA YIN ZER NAS, RE ZHIG BU MO DE MIG CES RE LTA 'DUG, BLON PO'I BSAM PA LA 'DI NYID KYI MING DANG RIGS DANG MDZAD SPYOD LA BRTAGS PAS, RGYAL PO JI LTAR GSUNG BA'I YON TAN RNAMS BU MO 'DI LA 'TSANG 'DUG PA, SPRO MI SPRO LTA DGOS SNYAM NAS, KHYED KYIS RGYAL PO ZHI BA'I GO CHA'I SRAS KUN TU BZANG PO BYA BA, PAntI TA CHEN PO'I MTSAN THOS SAM,
gru.wylie: rigs bram ze yin, grub mtha' phyi rol pa yin zer nas, re zhig bu mo de mig ces re lta 'dug, blon po'i bsam pa la 'di nyid kyi ming dang rigs dang mdzad spyod la brtags pas, rgyal po ji ltar gsung ba'i yon tan rnams bu mo 'di la 'tshang 'dug pa, spro mi spro lta dgos snyam nas, khyed kyis rgyal po zhi ba'i go cha'i sras kun tu bzang po bya ba, paNTi ta chen po'i mtshan thos sam
gru.english: And the Maiden simply stands there, silent, gazing steadily into the minister's eyes.  The minister thinks to himself, "Judging from the maiden's name, and her family, and the way she acts, she possesses all the qualities which the King has described.  Now we have to see whether she will like the plan." And so he says to Her, "Have you by any chance ever heard mention of the name of Total Goodness, who is the son of the king Armor of Peace, and is furthermore a great and learned man?"

gru.acip: ,GNAS NGO MTSAR MKHA' 'GROS LUNG BSTAN PA, ,BYANG PHYOGS PHU LA HA RIR PHYIN, ,DNGOS GRUB CAN GYI DGON PA RU, ,SGO SRUNG N'A RO PAn CHEN LA,
gru.wylie: gnas ngo mtshar mkha' 'gros lung bstan pa, ,byang phyogs phu la ha rir phyin, ,dngos grub can gyi dgon pa ru, ,sgo srung nA ro paN chen la
gru.english: And then one day I made my way To a wondrous land foretold By the Angels of the Sky-- To Pulahari, in the north. Here I met the great sage Naropa, Gatekeeper of the monastery Of those with spiritual attainment.

gru.acip: LO KY'A DUN DU RNAL 'BYOR GYI DBANG PHYUG CHEN PO PHAM MTHING PA LAS RGYA LA BRTEN NAS MCHOG GI DNGOS GRUB BRNYES PA YAB YUM GNYIS KA'I SKU MA NYAMS PAR BZHUGS PA LA BDE MCHOG RANG BYON DU GRAGS PA DE'I MDUN DU
gru.wylie: lo kyA dun du rnal 'byor gyi dbang phyug chen po pham mthing pa las rgya la brten nas mchog gi dngos grub brnyes pa yab yum gnyis ka'i sku ma nyams par bzhugs pa la bde mchog rang byon du grags pa de'i mdun du
gru.english: He then continued to Lokya Dun, to the place they call the "Image of the Angel of Highest Bliss, which Occurred All on its Own."  This is where that great Lord among Yogis, Pamtingpa, attained the highest goal by practicing with His actual, physical partner.  The physical bodies of both this Lama and his Lady are entombed here, and the flesh has never decayed.

gru.acip: RDO RJE GDAN GYI SHAR BHRI KA MA LA SH'I LA'I SHAR LHO AOO dE BI SHA ZHES PA'I YUL PHYOGS KYI NAGS KHROD DBEN PA ZHIG TU SGRUB PA SNYING POR MDZAD DE BZHUGS PA'I SKABS,
gru.wylie: rdo rje gdan gyi shar bhri ka ma la shI la'i shar lho aoo De bi sha zhes pa'i yul phyogs kyi nags khrod dben pa zhig tu sgrub pa snying por mdzad de bzhugs pa'i skabs
gru.english: There was a point when He was staying in a very isolated place in the forest called Oddivisha, in the forest east of the Seat of the Diamond [present-day Bodhgaya], and east as well of Vikramalashila Monastery.  Here He had thrown himself into His spiritual practice.

gru.acip: YUL DE'I RGYAL PO NYID DPYID KA'I DUS SU SKYO BSANG GI CHED DANG, RI DVAGS LA 'PHONG BSLAB PA'I DON DU GRUB CHEN DRIL BU PA BZHUGS PA'I NAGS GSEB MTHUG PO DER PHYIN PA NA, RGYAL PO DES SLOB DPON MTHONG STE
gru.wylie: yul de'i rgyal po nyid dpyid ka'i dus su skyo bsang gi ched dang, ri dvags la 'phong bslab pa'i don du grub chen dril bu pa bzhugs pa'i nags gseb mthug po der phyin pa na, rgyal po des slob dpon mthong ste
gru.english: Now the king of this land--with the intention of lifting his spirits with the onset of spring, and also in order to practice hunting wild animals with his bow--happened to ride into that thick part of the woods were this saint, Ghantapada, was staying.  And so he caught sight of the yogi.

gru.acip: SLOB DPON NI RIM PA LNGA LA SBYANGS PAS RIM PA GSUM PA'I DAM TSIG GI PHYAG RGYA YAN CHAD MNGON DU MDZAD ZIN NAS, LAS KYI PHYAG RGYA BSGRUB PA'I SKABS SU PHEBS TE, MNGON PAR SHES PAS GZIGS PA NA LAS KYI PHYAG RGYA BSGRUB PA'I RTEN 'BREL NI 'DIS 'GRUB PA SNYAM DU DGONGS TE,
gru.wylie: slob dpon ni rim pa lnga la sbyangs pas rim pa gsum pa'i dam tshig gi phyag rgya yan chad mngon du mdzad zin nas, las kyi phyag rgya bsgrub pa'i skabs su phebs te, mngon par shes pas gzigs pa na las kyi phyag rgya bsgrub pa'i rten 'brel ni 'dis 'grub pa snyam du dgongs te
gru.english: The Master though had been engaged in a practice of the Five Stages; he had already gone through all the practices up through the point in the third stage where we work with a partner of pledge, and the time had come for Him to start practicing with an actual partner.  He used His powers of clairvoyance to gaze into the future, and thought to Himself, "This is how I'm going to set in motion the conditions that will allow me to have an actual partner, and practice with Her."

gru.acip: RIM GYIS DE LA DBANG DANG DAM TSIG THAMS CAD KYI SNOD DU RUNG BAR MDZAD DE, LAS KYI PHYAG RGYAR BZHES NAS, RIM LNGA'I RIM PA LNGA PA MTHAR PHYIN PA'I BAR DU LO BCU GNYIS SU SGRUB PA YUN BSRINGS TE ZUNG 'JUG PHYAG RGYA CHEN PO'I MCHOG GI DNGOS GRUB MNGON DU MDZAD,
gru.wylie: rim gyis de la dbang dang dam tshig thams cad kyi snod du rung bar mdzad de, las kyi phyag rgyar bzhes nas, rim lnga'i rim pa lnga pa mthar phyin pa'i bar du lo bcu gnyis su sgrub pa yun bsrings te zung 'jug phyag rgya chen po'i mchog gi dngos grub mngon du mdzad
gru.english: And then very gradually the monk went about making her into a worthy vessel for secret empowerment, and secret vows.  Then He took her as his physical partner.  They practiced together for a long time--for 12 years, going all the way to the completion of the fifth stage.  He attained then the highest spiritual goal of all: the Great Seal of the Union of the Two.

gru.acip: DE NAS KUN TU BZANG PO'I SPYOD PAS SLOB DPON RANG NYID LA MI MOS PA'I 'GRO BA RNAMS KYI MA DAD PA BZLOG PAR BYA BA'I CHED DANG, MA 'ONGS PA'I SEMS CAN DMAN PA RNAMS KYI DON DU THUGS RJE CHEN PO'I SPRUL PA SPYAN DRANGS PA'I DGOS PA YONGS SU BSGRUB PA'I SLAD DANG, AOO dE BI SHA'I YUL NA GNAS PA'I SKYE BO RNAMS RDO RJE THEG PA LA GZUD PAR DGONGS PA BCAS KYI DON DU GRONG KHYER DU 'BYON PAR BZHED DE SPRUL PA'I BU DANG PU MO GNYIS SHIG KYANG SPRUL TO,,
gru.wylie: de nas kun tu bzang po'i spyod pas slob dpon rang nyid la mi mos pa'i 'gro ba rnams kyi ma dad pa bzlog par bya ba'i ched dang, ma 'ongs pa'i sems can dman pa rnams kyi don du thugs rje chen po'i sprul pa spyan drangs pa'i dgos pa yongs su bsgrub pa'i slad dang, aoo De bi sha'i yul na gnas pa'i skye bo rnams rdo rje theg pa la gzud par dgongs pa bcas kyi don du grong khyer du 'byon par bzhed de sprul pa'i bu dang pu mo gnyis shig kyang sprul to
gru.english: And then the Master decided to return to the city, for three reasons.  First of all, He wanted to put a stop to the lack of faith that people were feeling towards Him, by showing them the pureness of His actions.  He further wanted to accomplish the purpose for which the emanation of the Compassionate One had been invited, in order to help lower kinds of living beings in the future.  And then thirdly He had the idea that He could get the people of the country of Oddivisha to enter the diamond way.  He set off then for the city, bringing along with him a little boy and a little girl that He had emanated.

gru.acip: SLOB DPON GYIS GONG DU BSHAD PA'I DGOS PA GSUM BSGRUB PA'I SLAD DANG, RANG GI NUS PA BSTAN PA'I DON DU RVA'I BSHOR SA LA BRDABS PAS SA 'OG RIM PA BDUN PHUG STE SA 'OG NAS CHU CHEN PO GYEN DU PHYUNG,
gru.wylie: slob dpon gyis gong du bshad pa'i dgos pa gsum bsgrub pa'i slad dang, rang gi nus pa bstan pa'i don du rva'i bshor sa la brdabs pas sa 'og rim pa bdun phug ste sa 'og nas chu chen po gyen du phyung
gru.english: The Master--for the three reasons we mentioned above, and to demonstrate His true power--took the drinking horn from His mouth and threw it down to the ground.  It pierced the earth seven whole levels underground, and a geyser of water shot forth from the surface.

gru.acip: CHU RNAMS GA-YAS PHYOGS SU 'BAB STE SKU DE LA BSKOR BA LAN BDUN BYAS NAS SA 'OG TU SONG ZHING, THUGS RJE CHEN PO'I SKU RANG BYUNG DE DUS DA LTA'I SKABS SU'ANG BYIN RLABS CHE ZHING YUL DE'I SKYE 'GRO THAMS CAD KYI MGON SKYABS SU GYUR TE BZHUGS LA, AOO dI BI SHA PA KUN KYANG RDO RJE'I THEG PA LA ZHUGS NAS DNGOS GRUB THOB PA'ANG MANG DU BYUNG BAR GSUNGS SO,,
gru.wylie: chu rnams ga-yas phyogs su 'bab ste sku de la bskor ba lan bdun byas nas sa 'og tu song zhing, thugs rje chen po'i sku rang byung de dus da lta'i skabs su'ang byin rlabs che zhing yul de'i skye 'gro thams cad kyi mgon skyabs su gyur te bzhugs la, aoo Di bi sha pa kun kyang rdo rje'i theg pa la zhugs nas dngos grub thob pa'ang mang du byung bar gsungs so
gru.english: The waters gathered started swirling in a clockwise direction, and circled the sacred image seven times.  Then they sank back down into the earth.  The statue of the Compassionate One stands there to this day, imparting tremendous blessings.  It has become the guardian of every single person in the entire surrounding land.  And as a result, concluded our Lama, many of the inhabitants of Oddivisha have entered the diamond way, and gained high spiritual attainments.

gru.acip: YE SHES GSUM NI SNANG MCHED THOB GSUM GYI YE SHES YIN PAS DE BSKYED PA PHYAG RGYA LA LTOS DGOS SHING, SEMS DBEN DPE'I 'OD GSAL 'GRUB PA LA DE'I SNGON DU RLUNG PHRA RAGS THAMS CAD SNYING GA'I DBU MAR SDUD DGOS LA,
gru.wylie: ye shes gsum ni snang mched thob gsum gyi ye shes yin pas de bskyed pa phyag rgya la ltos dgos shing, sems dben dpe'i 'od gsal 'grub pa la de'i sngon du rlung phra rags thams cad snying ga'i dbu mar sdud dgos la
gru.english: The "three different divisions of wisdom" mentioned here are the wisdoms of radiance, proliferation, and near-attainment--and this is why we need to rely upon a spiritual partner, in order to bring them on.  And in order to develop the approximate clear light of the stage of transcendent mind, we must first gather all the different inner winds--both the subtle and the more gross--into the heart.

gru.acip: DE LA SGRUB DGOS PA NI, SEMS CAN THAMS CAD BDE BA 'DOD PA DANG SDUG BSNGAL MI 'DOD PA KHO NA YIN LA BDE BA SGRUB PA DANG SDUG BSNGAL SEL BA YANG DAM PA'I CHOS KHO NA LA RAG LAS PA'I PHYIR RO,,
gru.wylie: de la sgrub dgos pa ni, sems can thams cad bde ba 'dod pa dang sdug bsngal mi 'dod pa kho na yin la bde ba sgrub pa dang sdug bsngal sel ba yang dam pa'i chos kho na la rag las pa'i phyir ro
gru.english: One is the need to accomplish this goal.  And that is the fact, first of all, that every single living creature there is wants to have happiness, and doesn't want to have any suffering--that's all.  Secondly, the attainment of happiness, and the prevention of suffering, is something that depends upon the holy Dharma--that's all.

gru.acip: SGRUB NUS PA NI, PHYI'I RKYEN BSHES GNYEN DANG NANG GI RKYEN DAL 'BYOR DANG LDAN PA'I PHYIR RO,,
gru.wylie: sgrub nus pa ni, phyi'i rkyen bshes gnyen dang nang gi rkyen dal 'byor dang ldan pa'i phyir ro
gru.english: Another is the fact that we do have the capacity to accomplish the goal.  And that's because we do possess the outer aid of a spiritual guide, and the inner aid of our spiritual leisure and fortune. * * * Here is how an "outer aid" is described with reference to keeping our various vows.  From The String of Shining Jewels--An Explanation of the Rules contained in the Three Types of Vows: Those of Individual Freedom, Those of the Bodhisattva, and Those of the Secret Word (ACIP digital text S00201, f. 1b), by Geshe Tsewang Samdrup (fl. 1835).

gru.acip: DPE'I SGO NAS KYANG RNYED DKA' BAS, DA RES CHOS SGRUB PAR KHOM ZHING, PHYI'I RKYEN BLA MA DGE BA'I BSHES GNYEN SANGS RGYAS DNGOS LTA BU DANG PHRAD, NANG GI RKYEN SHES PA LA SKYON MA ZHUGS SHING THOS BSAM SGOM GSUM BYAR RUNG BA'I SHES RAB DANG LDAN,
gru.wylie: dpe'i sgo nas kyang rnyed dka' bas, da res chos sgrub par khom zhing, phyi'i rkyen bla ma dge ba'i bshes gnyen sangs rgyas dngos lta bu dang phrad, nang gi rkyen shes pa la skyon ma zhugs shing thos bsam sgom gsum byar rung ba'i shes rab dang ldan
gru.english: In terms of a metaphor then a life like this is difficult to attain.  And so this time we do have the time to practice the Dharma, and we have met with the outer aid of a spiritual guide, who is like an actual Buddha for us.  We possess as well wisdom: the inner factor of a mind which is in no way defective, and to which we can apply the three-step process of learning, contemplating, and meditating.

gru.acip: RANG GIS SGRUB PAR BYED NA GNAS SKABS MNGON MTHO LHA MI'I RTEN BZANG NAS MTHAR THUG RDO RJE 'CHANG GI GO 'PHANG MAN CHAD NGES PAR SGRUB NUS PA'I RTEN BZANG KHYAD PAR CAN RNYED PA 'DI NYID DON CHEN PO DANG LDAN PAR SHES SHING NGO 'PHROD PAR GYUR,
gru.wylie: rang gis sgrub par byed na gnas skabs mngon mtho lha mi'i rten bzang nas mthar thug rdo rje 'chang gi go 'phang man chad nges par sgrub nus pa'i rten bzang khyad par can rnyed pa 'di nyid don chen po dang ldan par shes shing ngo 'phrod par gyur
gru.english: We have found then an extraordinary combination of an excellent body and mind, with which we can without question attain--if we make efforts from our side--everything from the short-term goal of a rebirth as a man or worldly god, up to the ultimate goal of the state of the Keeper of the Diamond himself.  We must try to grasp how incredibly important this is, and try to recognize what has happened to us. * * * Here's a final combination of the two from The Rays of the Sun: Instructions for Developing the Good Heart (ACIP digital text S00185, f. 48a), by the Mongol sage, Hortun Namka Pel (c. 1650)--

gru.acip: SGYU MA'I SKU DE PHUNG PO SNYING PA DAM TSIG SEMS DPAR BLTAS PA'I THUGS KHAR YE SHES SEMS DPA'I TSUL GYI ZHUGS NAS MNYAM RJES KYI NYAMS LEN RNAMS BYAS PAS RNAM DAG YE SHES KYI RNAL 'BYOR 'GRUB TU NYE BA'I MTSAN MA MTHONG BA NA,
gru.wylie: sgyu ma'i sku de phung po snying pa dam tshig sems dpar bltas pa'i thugs khar ye shes sems dpa'i tshul gyi zhugs nas mnyam rjes kyi nyams len rnams byas pas rnam dag ye shes kyi rnal 'byor 'grub tu nye ba'i mtshan ma mthong ba na
gru.english: This body of illusion enters into the the holy heart of our old heaps--which we are viewing as a pledge being--in the way that a wisdom being would.  We then go through the periods of the main meditation and the aftermath, with which we begin to see signs that we are close to attaining the deep practice of pure wisdom.

gru.acip: PHYAG RGYAR MA ZAD SGRUB PA PO YANG JI SKAD BSHAD PA'I MTSAN NYID DANG LDAN PA DGOS KYI, DE LTA MIN NA NYES PA SHIN TU CHE STE,
gru.wylie: phyag rgyar ma zad sgrub pa po yang ji skad bshad pa'i mtshan nyid dang ldan pa dgos kyi, de lta min na nyes pa shin tu che ste
gru.english: Not only must the partner possess the required qualifications, but the practitioner who hopes to practice with this partner must possess them as well.  If they do not, then it is a very serious problem.

gru.acip: DES NA YUL RTEN GNYIS KA MTSAN NYID DANG MI LDAN PA'I RNAL 'BYOR PAS NI YE RGYA LA BRTEN DGOS TE, RDOR SEMS KYI SGRUB THABS LAS, YANG NA SNYING GNAS YE SHES KYI PHYAG RGYA MNGON PAR SPRUL TE, ZHES SOGS GSUNGS SHING,
gru.wylie: des na yul rten gnyis ka mtshan nyid dang mi ldan pa'i rnal 'byor pas ni ye rgya la brten dgos te, rdor sems kyi sgrub thabs las, yang na snying gnas ye shes kyi phyag rgya mngon par sprul te, zhes sogs gsungs shing
gru.english: As such, a deep practitioner who finds themselves in a situation where they cannot find a qualified partner, and where they themselves are not yet qualified, should utilize instead an imaginary partner--a partner of wisdom.  As we see in references like the Ritual for Reaching the Warrior of Diamond, "Alternately, you can emanate an imaginary partner, who dwells within your heart."

gru.acip: DE YANG MI BSKYOD PA'I SGRUB PA POS THOG MAR SME SHA CAN NAM GDOL PA'I BU MO'I RNAM PAR SNYING GNAS 'BYIN DGOS TE, RNAM GZHAG RIM PA LAS, BSAM PAS RANG GI RIGS KYI BU MO SPRO BA'AM YANG NA PHYI ROL GYI BU MO BLANGS LA, ZHES GSUNGS PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: de yang mi bskyod pa'i sgrub pa pos thog mar sme sha can nam gdol pa'i bu mo'i rnam par snying gnas 'byin dgos te, rnam gzhag rim pa las, bsam pas rang gi rigs kyi bu mo spro ba'am yang na phyi rol gyi bu mo blangs la, zhes gsungs pa'i phyir
gru.english: And if you happen to be a practitioner who belongs to the Family of Unshakeable, you should at the beginning bring up in your heart the corresponding type of Lady; in this case, that would be an imagined partner in the form either of the daughter of a leper, or the daughter of a butcher.  As the Steps of the Presentation puts it, Either send forth, with your imagination, a daughter of your own family, or else go and take an actual maiden as your partner. * * * Choney Lama repeats the need for an actual partner in his Golden Harvest of Attainments: An Explication of the Two Stages in the Practice of the Glorious Diamond Lord of Terror (Bhairava, or Yamantaka) (ACIP digital text S00257, f. 20a).

gru.acip: DE YANG YUL RTEN GNYIS KA RGYUD NAS BSHAD PA LTAR MTSAN NYID TSANG DGOS KYI, GANG BYUNG GIS MI CHOG GO ,'ON KYANG MKHAS GRUB NOR BZANG PAS NI YE RGYA TZAM LA BRTEN NAS SEMS DBEN DPE'I 'OD GSAL MTHAR THUG BSKYED NUS PA ZHIG KYANG BZHED DE DPYAD PAR BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: de yang yul rten gnyis ka rgyud nas bshad pa ltar mtshan nyid tshang dgos kyi, gang byung gis mi chog go ,'on kyang mkhas grub nor bzang pas ni ye rgya tsam la brten nas sems dben dpe'i 'od gsal mthar thug bskyed nus pa zhig kyang bzhed de dpyad par bya'o
gru.english: Keep in mind though that both the practitioner and the partner that they seek to practice with must both possess all the necessary qualifications, as they are described in the secret books--you can't just take anybody as your partner.  We should note here though that the wise and accomplished Norsang [a Lama introduced already above] takes the position that it is possible to reach the ultimate form of transcendent mind, the approximate clear light, practicing with only an imaginary partner.  This claim needs to be investigated further. * * * Je Tsongkapa refers to a point at which an imagined partner is to be preferred in His Book on the Stages of Dissolution (ACIP digital text S05309, ff. 9b-10a):

gru.acip: DE'I STONG PA NI SNGAR BSHAD PA LTAR RANG GI NGO BOS GRUB PAS STONG PA DE YIN LA, DE'I BDE BA NI, SROG DH'U T'IR GZHUGS GNAS THIM GSUM BYAS PA LAS BYUNG BA'I LHAN CIG SKYES PA'I BDE BA CHEN PO STE, DE GNYIS YUL DANG YUL CAN DU SBYOR BA'O,,
gru.wylie: de'i stong pa ni sngar bshad pa ltar rang gi ngo bos grub pas stong pa de yin la, de'i bde ba ni, srog dhU tIr gzhugs gnas thim gsum byas pa las byung ba'i lhan cig skyes pa'i bde ba chen po ste, de gnyis yul dang yul can du sbyor ba'o
gru.english: When we speak of "voidness" here, what we're referring to is where, as we explained before, something is void of existing in and of itself.  When we speak of "bliss," what we're referring to is the great, simultaneous ecstasy which is produced as the inner winds go through the three-step process of entering, staying, and dissolving within the channel of the dance.  These two are joined "in union" in the sense that one is the object perceived, and one is the state of mind which perceives it.

gru.acip: 'DI LA DPAL GSANG BA 'DUS PA LA SOGS PA'I RGYUD GZHAN LAS LHAN CIG SKYES PA'I BDE CHEN 'DREN NUS NA DE NYID DANG STONG PA NYID KYI LTA BA GNYIS NGO BO DBYER MED DU SBYAR NAS BSGOM PA DANG RLUNG SEMS CAN LAS GRUB PA'I SGYU LUS BSGOM PA NYID KYI CHOG GI
gru.wylie: 'di la dpal gsang ba 'dus pa la sogs pa'i rgyud gzhan las lhan cig skyes pa'i bde chen 'dren nus na de nyid dang stong pa nyid kyi lta ba gnyis ngo bo dbyer med du sbyar nas bsgom pa dang rlung sems can las grub pa'i sgyu lus bsgom pa nyid kyi chog gi
gru.english: On this subject, in other systems of the secret teachings--such as the Secret Collection--we try to reach a point where we are capable of bringing on simultaneous, great bliss; and then we create an indivisible union of the two: a view which combines this bliss and emptiness, in essence one.  And then all we do is meditate upon a body of illusion which is a product of both wind and mind; in those systems, this is all we need.

gru.acip: GAL TE SGRUB PA PO DANG RJES SU 'THUN PA'I PHYAG RGYA MA MA RNYED NA DE'I TSE JI LTAR BYA ZHE NA,
gru.wylie: gal te sgrub pa po dang rjes su 'thun pa'i phyag rgya ma ma rnyed na de'i tshe ji ltar bya zhe na
gru.english: One may ask the following question: "What should a secret practitioner do, if they are not able to find a partner who fits them?"

gru.acip: (LUNG 'DI'I KHUNGS 'DIR MI GSAL YANG, RDO RJE SEMS DPA'I SGRUB THABS LAS THAMS CAD GSANG BA'I RGYUD LAS GSUNGS PAR BSHAD DO,,) CES GSUNGS (LA, DE YANG SANGS RGYAS KYI GTZO BO'I YUM YIN) PAS SO,
gru.wylie: (lung 'di'i khungs 'dir mi gsal yang, rdo rje sems dpa'i sgrub thabs las thams cad gsang ba'i rgyud las gsungs par bshad do,,) ces gsungs (la, de yang sangs rgyas kyi gtso bo'i yum yin) pas so
gru.english: (Although the source of these lines is not clarified here in this text, it is explained in the Ritual for Reaching the Warrior of Diamond that they are spoken in The Secret Book of a World of Secrets.  The verse then is  a reference to the main or principal Mother or Wife of the Buddhas.) * * * Je Rinpoche continues in the same text with the following (ff. 435a-435b):

gru.acip: (GZI CHE BA'AM) 'OD CHEN PO NI BRTZON 'GRUS KYI BRTUN PA CAN NO,,
gru.wylie: (gzi che ba'am) 'od chen po ni brtson 'grus kyi brtun pa can no
gru.english: They will come to have "great light" (meaning an aura of majesty); that is, they will possess the splendid force of effort.

gru.acip: SKU GSUM NI RDO RJE 'CHANG CHEN PO STE DE'I DNGOS GRUB 'THOB PAR 'GYUR PA'O,,
gru.wylie: sku gsum ni rdo rje 'chang chen po ste de'i dngos grub 'thob par 'gyur pa'o
gru.english: They will then "achieve the three holy bodies," the great state of the Holder of the Diamond--meaning they will attain this spiritual goal.

gru.acip: (DES NA 'GYUR GSAR GNYIS KA 'THUN PAR 'BYUNG BA LTAR BYA'O, ,YE RGYA DANG SNYOMS PAR 'JUG PA LA SEMS BRTAN PA NI YE RGYA LA BRTEN NA, PHYI ROL GYI PHYAG RGYA LA MI LTOS PAR DE'I DGOS PA SGRUB NUS PA'I RIGS CAN GCIG YOD PAS, DES SHIN TU SPROS MED KYI SPYOD PA BYED PA YIN NO,,) PA THOB PAS PHYI ROL GYI PHYAG RGYA DANG SNYOMS PAR ZHUGS NAS, MCHOG TU BDE BA NYAMS SU MYONG BAR BYA'O ZHES BSTAN PAR BYA BA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: (des na 'gyur gsar gnyis ka 'thun par 'byung ba ltar bya'o, ,ye rgya dang snyoms par 'jug pa la sems brtan pa ni ye rgya la brten na, phyi rol gyi phyag rgya la mi ltos par de'i dgos pa sgrub nus pa'i rigs can gcig yod pas, des shin tu spros med kyi spyod pa byed pa yin no,,) pa thob pas phyi rol gyi phyag rgya dang snyoms par zhugs nas, mchog tu bde ba nyams su myong bar bya'o zhes bstan par bya ba'i phyir
gru.english: (We can say then that both the newer translations work out to the same thing.  What it means to "have a firm understanding" of union with an imaginary partner is that there does exist a certain class of person who--if they practice with an imaginary partner--will be able to attain the goal of partner practice without having to rely upon an outer partner.  They are engaged in what we call the "activity which is very much free of elaboration.") * * * Here is one final note by Je Rinpoche from the same work; it clarifies the meaning of "wisdom" in "wisdom partner," or "imaginary partner" (f. 462b)--

gru.acip: LAS KYI PHYAG RGYA DANG SGRUB PA PO MTSAN NYID TSANG DKA' BAS, YE SHES KYI PHYAG RGYA'I DBANG DU BYAS NA,
gru.wylie: las kyi phyag rgya dang sgrub pa po mtshan nyid tshang dka' bas, ye shes kyi phyag rgya'i dbang du byas na
gru.english: It's a difficult thing though to find someone who possesses all the required qualities of an actual partner, and difficult as well to find a practitioner who has all the qualifications to join with this partner.  Here then we'll describe how to proceed with an imaginary partner.

gru.acip: STONG PA'I NGANG LAS KHAm SNGON PO ZHIG BYUNG, DE ZHU BA LAS RDO RJE KHAm GYIS MTSAN PA DANG, DE YONGS SU GYUR BA LAS REG BYA RDO RJE MAR SGRUB THABS LTAR BSKYED DE GNAS RNAMS SU RIGS LNGA SOGS SO SOR 'GOD, GANG DU JI LTAR BZHUGS PA NI GONG GI DES SHES,
gru.wylie: stong pa'i ngang las khaM sngon po zhig byung, de zhu ba las rdo rje khaM gyis mtshan pa dang, de yongs su gyur ba las reg bya rdo rje mar sgrub thabs ltar bskyed de gnas rnams su rigs lnga sogs so sor 'god, gang du ji ltar bzhugs pa ni gong gi des shes
gru.english: Out of this state of emptiness then emerges a blue kham letter.  It melts down and becomes a diamond marked with a letter kham.  This then transforms: we create out of it the Diamond Lady of Touch, just as we usually do it in the ritual for reaching the Angel.  We then place the Angels of the Five Families at each of Their individual places of the body.  Where we place Them, and how They stay there, can be understood from our previous description.

gru.acip: 'ON KYANG RAL GCIG MA NI YUM GYI BYA ROG GDONG GI BU GA'I NANG TZAM RTZA 'KHOR YOD PA DER 'GOD, YUM DNGOS MIN PAR BSGOM PA TZAM LA LUS DKYIL MTSAN NYID PA MI 'ONG STE, LUS KYI CHA DE DANG DER 'GYUR BA'I SGRUB GZHI MED PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: 'on kyang ral gcig ma ni yum gyi bya rog gdong gi bu ga'i nang tsam rtsa 'khor yod pa der 'god, yum dngos min par bsgom pa tsam la lus dkyil mtshan nyid pa mi 'ong ste, lus kyi cha de dang der 'gyur ba'i sgrub gzhi med pa'i phyir
gru.english: The Lady of the Single Lock though you position just inside the opening of the "crow's face" [vagina] of the Wife, where the chakra is.  She does not consist of the Wife herself, but only as a visualization, and so we wouldn't classify this as a full secret world of the body.  This is because, in this particular case, there is no particular part of the body which becomes each one of the Angels. * * * We are given a picture of how one partner might lead to the next (we'll see this go both ways) in Je Tsongkapa's Lamp that Illuminates, Totally, the Teaching on the Five Steps (ACIP digital text S05302, f. 21b)

gru.acip: BSKYED RIM PA SPYOD PA BYED PA LA BYANG CHUB KYI SEMS MTSAN NYID TSANG BA YOD PAS, SPYIR SANGS RGYAS THOB 'DOD YOD MOD KYANG, BSKYED RIM MTHAR PHYIN PA'I 'OG TU RDZOGS RIM GYI LAM RNAMS MI BSKYED PAR THUN MONG GI DNGOS GRUB KYIS YID DRANGS NAS SPYOD PA BYED PA YIN PAS, BSAM PA GNYIS PA MA GTOGS PA GSUM NI RDZOGS RIM PA LA SBYAR RO,,
gru.wylie: bskyed rim pa spyod pa byed pa la byang chub kyi sems mtshan nyid tshang ba yod pas, spyir sangs rgyas thob 'dod yod mod kyang, bskyed rim mthar phyin pa'i 'og tu rdzogs rim gyi lam rnams mi bskyed par thun mong gi dngos grub kyis yid drangs nas spyod pa byed pa yin pas, bsam pa gnyis pa ma gtogs pa gsum ni rdzogs rim pa la sbyar ro
gru.english: A practitioner on the stage of creation who is practicing what we call "the activities" does possess the Wish for enlightenment, complete in every respect; and so admittedly we would have to say, generally speaking, that they do possess the wish to attain Buddhahood.  What happens though is that they reach the end of their practice of the stage of creation, and fail subsequent to that to start working on the paths of the stage of completion.  Their mind is drawn away by the pursuit of the common attainments.  And so we would say that three of the intentions--all except the second--apply to the stage of completion.

gru.acip: LE'U LNGA PA'I SGRON GSAL LAS, DNGOS KYI PHYAG RGYA MA RNYED NA, SANGS RGYAS KYI YUM SHER PHYIN RANG GI SNYING LA GNAS PA PHYUNG NAS, DE DANG LHAN CIG SNYOMS 'JUG BYED PA SHES BYED DANG BCAS PAS BSGRUBS LA,
gru.wylie: le'u lnga pa'i sgron gsal las, dngos kyi phyag rgya ma rnyed na, sangs rgyas kyi yum sher phyin rang gi snying la gnas pa phyung nas, de dang lhan cig snyoms 'jug byed pa shes byed dang bcas pas bsgrubs la
gru.english: The Lamp that Illuminates says, when discussing the fifth chapter, that if we cannot find an actual spiritual partner then we should bring forth the perfection of wisdom which is the Wife of the Buddhas, and then go into union with Her.  It demonstrates this point using scriptural support.

gru.acip: RDZOGS RIM GYI SKABS GSUM DU NI SGRUB THABS KYI CHO GA'I RIM PA CI RIGS PA LA BRTEN NAS YE RGYA DANG SNYOMS PAR ZHUGS PA NA NANG GI RLUNG GI RNAL 'BYOR MTHAR SON PAS GROGS BYAS PA'I MTHUS, GNYIS SNANG GI SPROS PA MANG PO BCAD NAS STONG PA BZHI KHYAD PAR CAN MNGON DU BYED DO,,
gru.wylie: rdzogs rim gyi skabs gsum du ni sgrub thabs kyi cho ga'i rim pa ci rigs pa la brten nas ye rgya dang snyoms par zhugs pa na nang gi rlung gi rnal 'byor mthar son pas grogs byas pa'i mthus, gnyis snang gi spros pa mang po bcad nas stong pa bzhi khyad par can mngon du byed do
gru.english: In the three different contexts of the practice of the stage of completion then you would take some step of the ritual that involved going into union with an imaginary partner.  You thus perfect a deep practice of working with the inner winds which then lends you support in the task of eliminating a great many forms of elaboration, in the sense of perceiving things in duality.  And then you would manifest an extraordinary form of the four forms of emptiness.

gru.acip: 'DI NI BRTZON 'GRUS SHIN TU DRAG LA SPROS PA LA MI DGA' BAS LHAN SKYES SGOM PA LA SHIN TU DAD PA CHE BA'I SGO NAS SNGAR LTAR SPYOD PAS, BHU SU KU'I SPYOD PA ZHES GSUNGS TE, ZA NYAL 'CHAG PA'I SPYOD PA CAN YIN PA'I PHYIR RO,,
gru.wylie: 'di ni brtson 'grus shin tu drag la spros pa la mi dga' bas lhan skyes sgom pa la shin tu dad pa che ba'i sgo nas sngar ltar spyod pas, bhu su ku'i spyod pa zhes gsungs te, za nyal 'chag pa'i spyod pa can yin pa'i phyir ro
gru.english: When a person who has a fierce degree of effort--and who is not attracted to elaboration, but has great faith in meditating upon the simultaneous--engages in activity as we described it above, we call them someone who is following the "activities of a bhusuku."  This is because they would be engaging in activities in the form of "eating, sleeping, and going."

gru.acip: BDAG MED MA'I RNAM PA CAN GYIS BYA DGOS PA SNGAR BDAG MED MA'I RNAL 'BYOR GYIS 'GRUB PAR GSUNGS PAS SHES SHING, 'ON KYANG LHA PHO'I RNAM PA CAN DU BSGOMS PA LA HE RU KA ZHES THA SNYAD BYAS PA'O, ,BH'A WA'I 'GREL PAR SKYES BUR 'GYUR GYI DOD LA 'GRUB PAR 'GYUR, ZHES 'BYUNG BA LEGS TE, PHO'I RNAM PAR BSGYUR BA NI SKYES BU NYID KYIS BSTAN ZIN PA'I PHYIR RO, ,ZHES MKHAS GRUB RJE'I BRTAG GNYIS PHYI MA'I LE'U GNYIS PA'I RNAM BSHAD LAS GSUNGS PA LTAR 'DIR SBYOR SHES PA DGOS TSUL,
gru.wylie: bdag med ma'i rnam pa can gyis bya dgos pa sngar bdag med ma'i rnal 'byor gyis 'grub par gsungs pas shes shing, 'on kyang lha pho'i rnam pa can du bsgoms pa la he ru ka zhes tha snyad byas pa'o, ,bhA wa'i 'grel par skyes bur 'gyur gyi dod la 'grub par 'gyur, zhes 'byung ba legs te, pho'i rnam par bsgyur ba ni skyes bu nyid kyis bstan zin pa'i phyir ro, ,zhes mkhas grub rje'i brtag gnyis phyi ma'i le'u gnyis pa'i rnam bshad las gsungs pa ltar 'dir sbyor shes pa dgos tshul
gru.english: Our Lama noted that we had to understand how to apply these lines in keeping with the following statement from Kedrup Je's explanation of the second chapter of the latter Text of Two Sections: The fact that you must do it with the form of the Lady of No-Self-Nature can be understood from the earlier statement that you "attain the goal through the practice of the Lady of No-Self-Nature."  You do though just call yourself "Heruka," and meditate on yourself as having the form of a male Angel.  	The statement in Bhava's commentary that "You attain the goal as the surrogate, as one who's become a man" is quite good, because transforming oneself into the form of a male has already been indicated in the phrase "only a man."

gru.acip: LAS RGYA ZHES BYA'O, ,DE LA YANG LAS BYED TSUL GYI SGO NAS SAM, MI BSKYOD PA SOGS RIGS LNGA'I SGRUB PA PO SO SOS GTZO BOR BSTEN BYA'I SGO NAS DBYE NA SME SHA CAN, BTZO BLAG MKHAN, PHRENG RGYUD MKHAN, GAR MKHAN, BZO BYED MKHAN GYI BU MO DANG LNGA YOD,
gru.wylie: las rgya zhes bya'o, ,de la yang las byed tshul gyi sgo nas sam, mi bskyod pa sogs rigs lnga'i sgrub pa po so sos gtso bor bsten bya'i sgo nas dbye na sme sha can, btso blag mkhan, phreng rgyud mkhan, gar mkhan, bzo byed mkhan gyi bu mo dang lnga yod
gru.english: This then is what we call an actual partner.  This type of partner can be divided out into different kinds, either by how they perform their function, or according to the main type of partner that practitioners of each of the Five Families--those of Unshakable and all the rest--do their practice with.  Dividing it this way, there are five different kinds of actual partners: the type which is the daughter of a leper; that which is the daughter of a dyer of clothes; of one who makes rosaries; of a dancer; and of an artist.

gru.acip: ,BDE BA'I YE SHES SKYES PA DE, ,CHOS KYI PHYAG RGYA ZHES BYA'O, ,CHAGS PA MED PA DAM TSIG STE, ,LHUN GRUB PHYAG RGYA CHEN PO YIN, ,CES GSUNGS PA LTAR RO,,
gru.wylie: bde ba'i ye shes skyes pa de, ,chos kyi phyag rgya zhes bya'o, ,chags pa med pa dam tshig ste, ,lhun grub phyag rgya chen po yin, ,ces gsungs pa ltar ro
gru.english: Bringing on the wisdom of bliss Is what we call the partner of the Dharma; To have no attachment is the partner of pledge, And the spontaneous is the Great Seal.

gru.acip: 'GOS LO CHEN PO GZHON NU DPAL NI, STONG NYID NGES PA'I RNAM PAR MI RTOG PA'I YE SHES DE NYID PHYAG RGYA CHEN POR BZHED DE, DEB SNGON GYI PHYAG CHEN LO RGYUS THOG MAR, DA NI SANGS RGYAS KYI BSTAN PA GZHI SO SO THAR PA NAS DPAL GSANG BA 'DUS PA'I BAR GYI SGRUB PA DANG NYAMS LEN THAMS CAD LA RGYAS 'DEBS PAR BYED PA PHYAG RGYA CHEN PO'I GTAM BRJOD PAR BYA STE, ZHES BSHAD PAS SO,,
gru.wylie: 'gos lo chen po gzhon nu dpal ni, stong nyid nges pa'i rnam par mi rtog pa'i ye shes de nyid phyag rgya chen por bzhed de, deb sngon gyi phyag chen lo rgyus thog mar, da ni sangs rgyas kyi bstan pa gzhi so so thar pa nas dpal gsang ba 'dus pa'i bar gyi sgrub pa dang nyams len thams cad la rgyas 'debs par byed pa phyag rgya chen po'i gtam brjod par bya ste, zhes bshad pas so
gru.english: The great Gu Lotsawa, Shunnu Pel, takes the position that the Great Seal is nothing other than that non-conceptual wisdom with which we perceive emptiness.  In the opening section of the account of the tradition of the Great Seal found in His Blue Annals, He says-- And now we will turn to the subject of the story of the Great Seal, which acts to seal or mark all these spiritual endeavors and practices--everything from the foundation of all these practices, the teachings on discipline, or individual freedom, up to the secret teachings of the glorious Secret Collection.

gru.acip: BZHI PA NI, 'DIR RNAL 'BYOR MA'I RGYUD RNAMS SHES RAB KYI PHYOGS BDE STONG DBYER MED GTZO BOR STON LA, STONG PA DE KHO NA NYID KYI LTA BA NI MGON PO KLU SGRUB KYIS RGYAS PAR GTAN LA PHAB PA LAS LHAG PA CIG BSHAD RGYU MED PA LA DGONGS NAS RGYUD RNAMS SU MDOR BSDUS TE GSUNGS SO,,
gru.wylie: bzhi pa ni, 'dir rnal 'byor ma'i rgyud rnams shes rab kyi phyogs bde stong dbyer med gtso bor ston la, stong pa de kho na nyid kyi lta ba ni mgon po klu sgrub kyis rgyas par gtan la phab pa las lhag pa cig bshad rgyu med pa la dgongs nas rgyud rnams su mdor bsdus te gsungs so
gru.english: Here then is our fourth point.  The secret books on the practice of the Lady Angel in this system are devoted primarily to a presentation of indivisible bliss and emptiness.  Emptiness though--the worldview of suchness--is only treated in these secret texts in a very brief way; the reason behind this is that the writers of these works considered the Protector, Nagarjuna, to have presented this subject in such perfect detail that there wasn't much need to say anything much more.

gru.acip: 'DI LA 'JIG PA MED PA'I PHYAG RGYA ZHES PA, 'GYUR BA MED PA ZHES BSGYUR BA BDE BAS, DAM TSIG GI PHYAG RGYA 'GYUR BA MED PA'I BDE CHEN TE, 'DI BSGRUB BYA YIN LA, PHYAG RGYA SNGA MA GSUM NI SGRUB BYED YIN NO,,
gru.wylie: 'di la 'jig pa med pa'i phyag rgya zhes pa, 'gyur ba med pa zhes bsgyur ba bde bas, dam tshig gi phyag rgya 'gyur ba med pa'i bde chen te, 'di bsgrub bya yin la, phyag rgya snga ma gsum ni sgrub byed yin no
gru.english: This type of partner is spoken of as an "indestructible" partner, but the word would be better translated from the Sanskrit as an "immutable" partner.  As such, the partner of pledge is themselves immutable bliss--the thing which we seek to achieve.  And then the former three types of partners are the means which we use to achieve this one.

gru.acip: DE'ANG DBANG PO RAB PHYAG CHEN, 'BRING YE RGYA, THA MA LAS RGYA LA BRTEN NAS SGRUB PO,,
gru.wylie: de'ang dbang po rab phyag chen, 'bring ye rgya, tha ma las rgya la brten nas sgrub po
gru.english: Understand further that [in the system of the Kalachakra] a person of highest faculties practices with a Great Seal; one of medium capacity with an imagined partner; and one of lowest capacity with an actual partner. * * *

gru.acip: ,ZHES BYA BAS YE SHES KYI PHYAG RGYA 'DU BYAS NAS 'DOD YON LA LONGS SPYOD PA'I TSUL GYIS DNGOS GRUB THAMS CAD BSGRUB PAR BYA'O ZHES GO BAR BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: zhes bya bas ye shes kyi phyag rgya 'du byas nas 'dod yon la longs spyod pa'i tshul gyis dngos grub thams cad bsgrub par bya'o zhes go bar bya'o
gru.english: You should understand that what these lines are saying is that we reach each and every spiritual attainment by gathering to us a wisdom partner, and by enjoying the objects of the senses with them. * * * Kenchen Lobsang Tendzin Gyeltsen (b. 1639) includes these same lines in a rite of empowerment, as we see in A Ceremony for Bringing Oneself into the Secret World of the Five Angels of Highest Bliss (Sanvara), along with the Concluding Verses of Auspiciousness; from the Collected Works of that King of the Dharma, Kenchen (ACIP digital text S12271, ff. 10b-11a):

gru.acip: ,YE SHES PHYAG RGYAR BYIN BRLABS NAS, ,'DOD PA THAMS CAD LONGS SPYOD DE, ,DNGOS GRUB THAMS CAD BSGRUB PAR GYIS,,
gru.wylie: ye shes phyag rgyar byin brlabs nas, ,'dod pa thams cad longs spyod de, ,dngos grub thams cad bsgrub par gyis
gru.english: First bless them as a partner of wisdom, And then go and partake of every pleasure; Go and attain every goal there is.

gru.acip: RANG GI LUS LHA'I SKU PHYAG RGYA CHEN POR BSGOM PA NI 'DOR MI RUNG BA'I PHYAG RGYA'I DAM TSIG YIN LA, DE DANG YE SHES KYI PHYAG RGYA GNYIS MNYAM PAR SBYAR TE DNGOS GRUB THAMS CAD BSGRUB DGOS SO,,
gru.wylie: rang gi lus lha'i sku phyag rgya chen por bsgom pa ni 'dor mi rung ba'i phyag rgya'i dam tshig yin la, de dang ye shes kyi phyag rgya gnyis mnyam par sbyar te dngos grub thams cad bsgrub dgos so
gru.english: Seeing our own body as the holy form of an Angel, as the Great Seal, is the pledge of the spiritual partner, that which should never be given up.  This body you must then join in union with the imagined partner, and thus reach every attainment there is. * Mudras to Fit Varying Capacities It might be useful at this juncture to begin examining how these different kinds of partners are meant for practitioners at different levels of spiritual attainment.  The following is from Je Tsongkapa's Book of Three Beliefs, on the teachings of the Six Yogas of Naropa (ACIP digital text S05317, ff. 31a-31b):

gru.acip: SNGAGS KYI GDUL BYA'I DBANG PO RAB RIN PO CHE LTA BU'I GANG ZAG GIS RIM GNYIS BOGS 'BYIN GYI SPYOD PA GSUM CI RIGS LA BSLABS PAS TSE GCIG GIS SANGS RGYAS 'GRUB PAR GSUNGS PA DANG 'GAL BA'I SKYON DU 'GYUR BA'I PHYIR RO,,
gru.wylie: sngags kyi gdul bya'i dbang po rab rin po che lta bu'i gang zag gis rim gnyis bogs 'byin gyi spyod pa gsum ci rigs la bslabs pas tshe gcig gis sangs rgyas 'grub par gsungs pa dang 'gal ba'i skyon du 'gyur ba'i phyir ro
gru.english: It is stated in scripture that disciples of the way of the secret word who possess the highest faculties--those people who are truly like jewels in this world--train themselves in one or more of the three activities used to take ones practice of the two stages to a whole new level, and thus attain enlightenment in a single lifetime.  The idea above of course runs into problems, since it contradicts these statements.

gru.acip: ,ZHES PA KHUNGS SU DRANGS NAS 'DOD YON LA LONGS SPYOD PA DANG, BDE BA CHEN PO SGRUB BYED DANG BCAS PA MDO SNGAGS GNYIS KA'I THUN MONG BAR BZHED LA,
gru.wylie: zhes pa khungs su drangs nas 'dod yon la longs spyod pa dang, bde ba chen po sgrub byed dang bcas pa mdo sngags gnyis ka'i thun mong bar bzhed la
gru.english: These are authoritative sources which we can cite to show that partaking of objects of pleasure--and great bliss, along with the means for attaining it--are accepted jointly by both the open and secret teachings of Buddhism.

gru.acip: 'OD GSAL ZUNG 'JUG RGYUD LDAN LHAN SKYES KYI PHO NYA STE PHO NYA ZHES PA 'DOD DON MYUR DU SGRUB PA'I MI LA PHO NYA'I BANG CHEN ZHES PA LTAR LHAN SKYES KYI BDE STONG MYUR DU BSKYED PA'I PHYIR PHO NYA'O,,
gru.wylie: 'od gsal zung 'jug rgyud ldan lhan skyes kyi pho nya ste pho nya zhes pa 'dod don myur du sgrub pa'i mi la pho nya'i bang chen zhes pa ltar lhan skyes kyi bde stong myur du bskyed pa'i phyir pho nya'o
gru.english: Here we are referring to a Messenger of the simultaneous: one who possesses, within them, the clear light, and the Union of the Two.  The expression "messenger" means a messenger in the sense of an envoy--a person who goes and quickly procures whatever thing it is you wish.  Here the Lady is called a "messenger" because She quickly produces in you simultaneous bliss and voidness. * * * Je Rinpoche goes deeply, as usual, into the subject of the Messenger in His Illumination of Every Secret Point (ACIP digital text S05316, ff. 130a-131a):

gru.acip: THAMS CAD DU GNYIS SU MED PA'I DGA' BA'I RANG BZHIN TE DGA' BA 'BYUNG BA'I TSUL GYIS YANG DAG PA STE LEGS PAR GNAS NAS, 'OG STE SA 'OG LA SOGS PA NA GANG CI YOD PA'I 'JIG RTEN PA'I DNGOS GRUB DANG, STENG GI STE PHYAG RGYA CHEN PO'I DNGOS GRUB STER BA'O ZHES 'CHAD DO,,
gru.wylie: thams cad du gnyis su med pa'i dga' ba'i rang bzhin te dga' ba 'byung ba'i tshul gyis yang dag pa ste legs par gnas nas, 'og ste sa 'og la sogs pa na gang ci yod pa'i 'jig rten pa'i dngos grub dang, steng gi ste phyag rgya chen po'i dngos grub ster ba'o zhes 'chad do
gru.english: They are, "at every point, of the nature of indivisible pleasure," meaning that they remain "purely," or very well, in the mode of producing pleasure.  They deliver to us all the worldly kinds of attainments that there are--referred to here with the word "below," a reference to powers such as the one called "underground," or the ability to travel through solid earth.  And they also deliver to us the "above," meaning the spiritual achievement of the Great Seal.

gru.acip: DE LTAR 'OG TU GNAS PA STENG DU STE SNGON LA BKOD NAS BSGOMS NA DNGOS GRUB STER ZHES 'CHAD DO,,
gru.wylie: de ltar 'og tu gnas pa steng du ste sngon la bkod nas bsgoms na dngos grub ster zhes 'chad do
gru.english: And what the text is saying is that if we visualize those positioned below as "above"--meaning that we position them first--then it brings to us our spiritual attainments.

gru.acip: DE YANG SKAL BA DANG LDAN PA'I SEMS CAN GYI DON BSGRUB PA'I PHYIR DANG, 'O BYA BA DANG 'KHYUD PA LA SOGS PA THAMS CAD DU STER BA'I TSUL GYIS GNAS KUN TU 'GRO BA'O,,
gru.wylie: de yang skal ba dang ldan pa'i sems can gyi don bsgrub pa'i phyir dang, 'o bya ba dang 'khyud pa la sogs pa thams cad du ster ba'i tshul gyis gnas kun tu 'gro ba'o
gru.english: This Messenger "goes everywhere," in order to accomplish the goals of all those living beings who possess the necessary goodness, and by granting, everywhere, practices like kissing, and embracing.

gru.acip: DE 'DRA BA'I PHO NYA MO DE NI MIG GIS MTHONG BA DANG LUS KYIS REG PA DANG THOS PAS KYANG DNGOS GRUB KUN STER NA, RGYUN DU TSUL BZHIN DU BSGRUBS PAS DNGOS GRUB STER BA LTA CI SMOS, ZHES PA PAndI TA GSUM GYIS BSHAD DO,,
gru.wylie: de 'dra ba'i pho nya mo de ni mig gis mthong ba dang lus kyis reg pa dang thos pas kyang dngos grub kun ster na, rgyun du tshul bzhin du bsgrubs pas dngos grub ster ba lta ci smos, zhes pa paNDi ta gsum gyis bshad do
gru.english: The three pandits put it this way: A Messenger like this will deliver you your attainments even if all you do is lay your eyes upon Them, or touch them, or simply hear Them.  What need then to speak of how They deliver you attainments if on a regular basis you engage in practices to reach Them?

gru.acip: PHO NYA MO MTHONG BA SOGS KYIS DNGOS GRUB STER LUGS NI BDE BA CHEN PO BSKYED PA'I SGO NAS YIN TE, RDO RJE GUR LAS,
gru.wylie: pho nya mo mthong ba sogs kyis dngos grub ster lugs ni bde ba chen po bskyed pa'i sgo nas yin te, rdo rje gur las
gru.english: How do these Messengers grant us attainments simply as we gaze upon them, and the rest?  They do so by bringing on in us great bliss.  As the Canopy of Diamond puts it,

gru.acip: RNAL 'BYOR JI SNYED PA 'DOD PA'I BSTAN BCOS LAS BSHAD PA'I KA RA NA'I TSOGS, RDO RJE SEMS DPAS GSUNGS PA DE SNYED SHES PAR BYAS NAS DE DANG MTHUN PAR ROL BAR BYED PA NI, DNGOS GRUB THAMS CAD SBYIN PAR BYED PAR BSHAD DO,,
gru.wylie: rnal 'byor ji snyed pa 'dod pa'i bstan bcos las bshad pa'i ka ra na'i tshogs, rdo rje sems dpas gsungs pa de snyed shes par byas nas de dang mthun par rol bar byed pa ni, dngos grub thams cad sbyin par byed par bshad do
gru.english: Master then the total number of deep practices--the entire collection of acts described in the classical commentary on the arts of pleasure: the entire number of these described by the Warrior of Diamond.  And then follow them in your play.  This, it is said, will bring you each and every attainment.

gru.acip: 'GREL PA GZHAN LAS NI GNAS DANG NYE BA'I GNAS LA SOGS PA RNAL 'BYOR GYI GNAS LA GNAS PA'I PHO NYA MOS NI, DNGOS GRUB THAMS CAD STER TE TZUMBA NA DANG 'KHYUD PA 'DOD PA'I BSTAN BCOS LAS BSHAD PA'I RIM PAS BSTEN NA DNGOS GRUB TU 'GYUR RO ZHES 'CHAD DO,,
gru.wylie: 'grel pa gzhan las ni gnas dang nye ba'i gnas la sogs pa rnal 'byor gyi gnas la gnas pa'i pho nya mos ni, dngos grub thams cad ster te tsumba na dang 'khyud pa 'dod pa'i bstan bcos las bshad pa'i rim pas bsten na dngos grub tu 'gyur ro zhes 'chad do
gru.english: Other commentaries explain this section as saying that our Messenger lady comes and stays in the places of deep practice: at the main spots, and at the secondary spots, thus granting us every attainment.  We come to reach all our spiritual goals through a practice which proceeds through the steps described in the classical commentary upon the arts of pleasure--through kissing, and then embracing.

gru.acip: 'DI LA SKAL LDAN GYIS, PHO NYA GSUM YOD PA LAS, LHAN CIG SKYES DNGOS GRUB CES PA NI MTSON PA TZAM MO,,
gru.wylie: 'di la skal ldan gyis, pho nya gsum yod pa las, lhan cig skyes dngos grub ces pa ni mtshon pa tsam mo
gru.english: On this point, Master Kelnden* states that there are three different types of Messengers, and that the reference to "attainments with the one born of the simultaneous" is but one example. *Original Sanskrit uncertain.

gru.acip: 'DI DAG GRUB PAS DGOS PA CI YOD CE NA, YID NI NANG DU CHUD PA YIS MNGON PAR 'DOD PA'I DNGOS GRUB BSGRUB PAR BYA'O ZHES 'CHAD DO,,
gru.wylie: 'di dag grub pas dgos pa ci yod ce na, yid ni nang du chud pa yis mngon par 'dod pa'i dngos grub bsgrub par bya'o zhes 'chad do
gru.english: "And for what purpose," you may ask, "do we practice with such as these?"  The scripture is saying that it is so that They might take us into Their hearts, and then help us attain all the goals we hope for.

gru.acip: BLA MA RNAMS LHAN CIG SKYES DNGOS KYIS LHAN SKYES MA BSTAN LA, GRUB CES PAS ZHING GI BDAG NYID CHEN PO LAS RNAL 'BYOR MAR GRUB PA DANG, BSAM GTAN DANG BZLAS PA SOGS LAS RNAL 'BYOR MAR GRUB PA BSTAN TO,,
gru.wylie: bla ma rnams lhan cig skyes dngos kyis lhan skyes ma bstan la, grub ces pas zhing gi bdag nyid chen po las rnal 'byor mar grub pa dang, bsam gtan dang bzlas pa sogs las rnal 'byor mar grub pa bstan to
gru.english: Some Lamas have said that the words "what is actually born of the simultaneous" refer to the feminine in the form of simultaneous or ultimate reality; that the word "create" is a reference to the creation of an Angel by the great beings of holy places; and that the other refers to an Angel brought into being through things like concentration and the recitation of mantra.

gru.acip: DANG PO NI MCHOG STE DNGOS GRUB GNYIS KA STER BAS SO, ,GNYIS PA NI 'BRING STE 'JIG RTEN PA'I DNGOS GRUB STER BAS SO, ,GSUM PA NI THA MA STE DNGOS GRUB GNYIS STER MI NUS KYANG DE GNYIS SGRUB PA'I GROGS BYED PAS SO, ,ZHES GSUNG NGO,,
gru.wylie: dang po ni mchog ste dngos grub gnyis ka ster bas so, ,gnyis pa ni 'bring ste 'jig rten pa'i dngos grub ster bas so, ,gsum pa ni tha ma ste dngos grub gnyis ster mi nus kyang de gnyis sgrub pa'i grogs byed pas so, ,zhes gsung ngo
gru.english: The first of these is "supreme," in the sense that they grant us both of the attainments.  The second is "medium," in that they give us worldly attainments.  The third is "least" in that--even though they are not capable of giving us both attainments--they serve as our companions, helping us to reach both.

gru.acip: YID NI NANG DU CHUD PA YIS TE DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA THAMS CAD KYI SKYED MA MO'I SHES RAB MA DANG SBYOR TSUL JI LTAR GSUNGS PA BZHIN DU MNYAM PAR SBYOR BA DANG LDAN PAS YID GZHAN DU MI GA-YENG BAR TSIM PAR BYAS PA LA, MNGON PAR 'DOD PA'I DNGOS GRUB BSGRUB PAR BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: yid ni nang du chud pa yis te de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi skyed ma mo'i shes rab ma dang sbyor tshul ji ltar gsungs pa bzhin du mnyam par sbyor ba dang ldan pas yid gzhan du mi ga-yeng bar tshim par byas pa la, mngon par 'dod pa'i dngos grub bsgrub par bya'o
gru.english: And then They take us into Their hearts--meaning that we begin to practice union, in the way it is described in the scriptures, with one of these Ladies who "gives birth to each and every One Gone Thus," meaning a Woman of Wisdom.  And if we then satiate Them, without every allowing our mind to wander, then we will come to achieve every goal that we ever hoped for.

gru.acip: SKAL MED LA BYIN YANG SBAS DON ZAB MO RNYED PAR MI 'GYUR ZHING YID CHES PAR MI 'GYUR LA, SKAL BA DMAN PAS BSGRUBS KYANG 'GRUB PAR MI 'GYUR TE, DMUS LONG GI LAG TU NOR BU'I MCHOG BZHAG PA BZHIN DU, CHO GA KHYAD PAR CAN 'DI YANG SKAL BA DMAN PAS MI MTHONG NGO,,
gru.wylie: skal med la byin yang sbas don zab mo rnyed par mi 'gyur zhing yid ches par mi 'gyur la, skal ba dman pas bsgrubs kyang 'grub par mi 'gyur te, dmus long gi lag tu nor bu'i mchog bzhag pa bzhin du, cho ga khyad par can 'di yang skal ba dman pas mi mthong ngo
gru.english: You can share these things with a person who lacks sufficient goodness, but they will never be able to find the deep and hidden meanings; nor will they believe in the practice.  Those of insufficient goodness may attempt the practice, but they will not succeed in the practice.  It would be like placing a supremely precious jewel into the hands of a blind person; those of insufficient goodness cannot even see this extraordinary rite.

gru.acip: SKAL BA MI DMAN NA NI SNGON GYI BSOD NAMS BSAGS PA CHUNG BA STE HA CANG MI CHE BA'I SGRUB PA POS KYANG, NGA STE HE RU KA DANG THA MI DAD PA'I BLA MA MNYES PAR BYAS PAS, RGYUD DU SBAS PA'I ZAB MO'I DON RNAMS RNYED PA STE KHONG DU CHUD PAR 'GYUR ZHING, BSGRUBS PAS KYANG 'GRUB PAR 'GYUR RO,,
gru.wylie: skal ba mi dman na ni sngon gyi bsod nams bsags pa chung ba ste ha cang mi che ba'i sgrub pa pos kyang, nga ste he ru ka dang tha mi dad pa'i bla ma mnyes par byas pas, rgyud du sbas pa'i zab mo'i don rnams rnyed pa ste khong du chud par 'gyur zhing, bsgrubs pas kyang 'grub par 'gyur ro
gru.english: Suppose though that a deep practitioner's goodness is not insufficient; and suppose then that they work to please their Lama--someone who is not separate from the "me" mentioned in the text; from Heruka himself.  Even if their store of merit is relatively "small"--that is, not huge--then they will find the deep and hidden meanings; meaning that they will grasp their import.  And then you can attempt the practice, and you will succeed in the practice. * * * Khalkha Damtsik Dorje, in His Shining Glory of Great Bliss (ACIP uncataloged data), describes the need for secrecy in the context of the eight pledges, many of which relate to practice with a partner:

gru.acip: BHA BAS RANG GI GA-YON DU SKYES PA'AM BUD MED BZHAG NAS 'GRO BA'I SKYES PA'AM BUD MED NI, BDE MCHOG GI RNAL 'BYOR PA'AM RNAL 'BYOR MAR SHES PAR BYA'O, ,DE'I PHYIR YANG 'DOD PA'I DNGOS GRUB TU 'GYUR RO,,
gru.wylie: bha bas rang gi ga-yon du skyes pa'am bud med bzhag nas 'gro ba'i skyes pa'am bud med ni, bde mchog gi rnal 'byor pa'am rnal 'byor mar shes par bya'o, ,de'i phyir yang 'dod pa'i dngos grub tu 'gyur ro
gru.english: Master Bhava states that--any time we see a man or woman who positions themselves such that they move with some other man or woman to their left--then we can understand that the former is a man or woman who is a deep practitioner of the secret teachings of Highest Bliss.  And for this same reason they will attain the goals that their heart desires.

gru.acip: YANG DE NYID LAS, ,RTAG TU G-YON PA YIS NI BYA, ,BUD MED RNAMS LA MTHUN PAR BYA, ,DE YIS NGES PAR RTAG PAR 'BYUNG, ,RKANG PA G-YON PA'I MTHE BONG GIS, ,SA YANG RKO ZHING RI MO 'DRI, ,LAG PA G-YON PAS RANG PHYOGS KYI, ,SPYI BO LA NI 'PHRUG PAR BYED, ,RANG LUS LAG PA G-YON PAS STON, ,DE YIS RANG GI RIGS NI DRAN, ,SGRUB PO'I LUS LA GNAS PA YIN, This same text says,
gru.wylie: yang de nyid las, ,rtag tu g-yon pa yis ni bya, ,bud med rnams la mthun par bya, ,de yis nges par rtag par 'byung, ,rkang pa g-yon pa'i mthe bong gis, ,sa yang rko zhing ri mo 'dri, ,lag pa g-yon pas rang phyogs kyi, ,spyi bo la ni 'phrug par byed, ,rang lus lag pa g-yon pas ston, ,de yis rang gi rigs ni dran, ,sgrub po'i lus la gnas pa yin, thiS SaMe TexT SayS
gru.english: Always perform every act Using the left-hand one; Act in harmony With all of womankind; By doing so you'll always Achieve your goals, with certainty. Use the big toe of your left foot To dig or draw upon the earth; Use your left hand too To shake the center tip of your head. Point to your own body Using the left one of your hands. These will help you to recall The family you belong to; You will be living then In the body of a practitioner.

gru.acip: ,BRDA NI LNGA PO BSTAN PA DAG ,SGRUB PA PO YIS LAG G-YON GYIS, ,'DI NI DPA' BO'I GNAS YIN TE, ,BRDA RNAMS LA NI RAB 'JUG PA'O, ,ZHES DANG,
gru.wylie: brda ni lnga po bstan pa dag ,sgrub pa po yis lag g-yon gyis, ,'di ni dpa' bo'i gnas yin te, ,brda rnams la ni rab 'jug pa'o, ,zhes dang
gru.english: For making the sign, For showing the five, Practitioners always use The left of their two hands. This is the way Of those who are great warriors; Always then follow the practice Of making these special signs.

gru.acip: SDOM 'BYUNG LAS KYANG, DE NAS LAG G-YON GYI NI BRDA, ,MDOR BSDUS 'DI LA BSHAD PAR BYA, ,ZHES GSUNGS PAS DE 'DRA BA'I 'DU BA BSGRUB PA'I PHYIR DU DA LTA NAS LAG PA G-YON PA LA MCHOD PAR BYED DE DGOS PA GZHAN YANG YOD DO,, The Source of Vows too says,
gru.wylie: sdom 'byung las kyang, de nas lag g-yon gyi ni brda, ,mdor bsdus 'di la bshad par bya, ,zhes gsungs pas de 'dra ba'i 'du ba bsgrub pa'i phyir du da lta nas lag pa g-yon pa la mchod par byed de dgos pa gzhan yang yod do,, the source of vowS Too SayS
gru.english: Now next I will explain In brief the practice of making The sign here in this teaching, With the left of your hands. Given all this, one should learn to make offerings with their left hand from now, in order to undertake this type of union later.  There are other reasons as well why you should make the offering of the hand.

gru.acip: SPYIR GNAS GANG DU LHA GANG BSGOMS NAS MCHOD KYANG PHAN YON CHE MOD KYI, KHYAD PAR LAG PA G-YON PA'I RTZA KHAMS LA 'KHOR LO BDE MCHOG GI LHA TSOGS DGYES PAS BYON TE MCHOD PA LEN PAR MDZAD PA'I GNAD KHYAD PAR CAN YOD PAS, PHYI ROL MCHOD PA'AM, LUS DKYIL LAM, PHYI DKYIL YONGS RDZOGS MCHOD PA TZAM GYI PHAN YON ZHIG LAG MCHOD 'BA' ZHIG LA YANG YOD DE, 'DI RNAMS KYI RGYU MTSAN NI HE RU KA'I BKA' NYID KYIS GRUB PA YIN NO,, ZHES KYANG DAM PA 'GA' ZHIG GSUNG,
gru.wylie: spyir gnas gang du lha gang bsgoms nas mchod kyang phan yon che mod kyi, khyad par lag pa g-yon pa'i rtsa khams la 'khor lo bde mchog gi lha tshogs dgyes pas byon te mchod pa len par mdzad pa'i gnad khyad par can yod pas, phyi rol mchod pa'am, lus dkyil lam, phyi dkyil yongs rdzogs mchod pa tsam gyi phan yon zhig lag mchod 'ba' zhig la yang yod de, 'di rnams kyi rgyu mtshan ni he ru ka'i bka' nyid kyis grub pa yin no,, zhes kyang dam pa 'ga' zhig gsung
gru.english: A number of holy ones of the past have said as well that:  One must admit that, generally speaking, it is of great benefit to visualize Angels anywhere, and then make offerings to them.
