There is though a very special point to the practice where the entire assembly of the Angels of the secret teachings of the Sphere of Great Bliss come, with great pleasure, into the channels and elements of your left hand and take your offerings.  As such, the benefits of a number of different forms of offering are all complete within the one practice of the offering of the hand: the benefits of making outer offerings; those of the secret world of the body; and those of the outer secret world.  The reasons why this is true are established in the word of none other than Heruka himself.

gru.acip: (SNGAR THEG PA 'DIR MCHOG MYUR DU 'GRUB PAR GSUNGS PA'I MYUR KHYAD NI, BDE BA CHEN PAS STONG NYID SGOM PA YIN LA, DE'I BDE BA 'DREN PA'I THABS GNYIS LAS, NANG GI THABS NI SNGAR BSHAD ZIN PAS 'DIR PHYAG RGYA LA BRTEN PA'I THABS NI,)
gru.wylie: (sngar theg pa 'dir mchog myur du 'grub par gsungs pa'i myur khyad ni, bde ba chen pas stong nyid sgom pa yin la, de'i bde ba 'dren pa'i thabs gnyis las, nang gi thabs ni sngar bshad zin pas 'dir phyag rgya la brten pa'i thabs ni,)
gru.english: (The one single feature, one which has been described earlier, which makes this particular path so quick is that we meditate upon emptiness by using the state of great bliss.  There are two ways of bringing on this bliss; the first we have already finished describing, and so here we move on to describing the method of practice with a spiritual partner.)

gru.acip: MA DANG SRING MO ZHES BYA BA LA SOGS PA LA, MA ZHES BYA BA NI MA DANG 'DRA BAR (SGRUB PA PO DANG SEMS SHIN TU) RJES SU 'THUN PA'I PHYAG RGYA MA'O,,
gru.wylie: ma dang sring mo zhes bya ba la sogs pa la, ma zhes bya ba ni ma dang 'dra bar (sgrub pa po dang sems shin tu) rjes su 'thun pa'i phyag rgya ma'o
gru.english: We see references to a "mother" and a "sister" and so on; the point here is that our spiritual partner is someone who is as close to us as our own Mother.  (That is, our hearts are extremely close.)

gru.acip: 'DI RNAMS LAS GANG YANG RUNG BA'I RNAL 'BYOR PAR RANG RANG GI RIGS KYI BUD MED (MI BSKYOD PA'I RIGS LA SME SHA CAN DANG, RNAM SNANG GI RIGS LA GTZO BLAG MKHAN LA SOGS PA) BLANGS LA BSGRUB PA'I THABS MDOR BYAS LAS BSHAD PA'I RIM PAS
gru.wylie: 'di rnams las gang yang rung ba'i rnal 'byor par rang rang gi rigs kyi bud med (mi bskyod pa'i rigs la sme sha can dang, rnam snang gi rigs la gtso blag mkhan la sogs pa) blangs la bsgrub pa'i thabs mdor byas las bshad pa'i rim pas
gru.english: Any of the deep practitioners described here then takes on a woman who belongs to the same family as them (the family of the Angel Unshakeable relates to a leper; that of the Angel Appearances relates to a dyer; and so on), and follows the steps as described in the Brief Presentation for reaching the Angel as described in the briefer scriptures.

gru.acip: SPYI BO LA SOGS PAR RIGS LNGA DGOD PA BYAS LA SGRUB PA PO GANG GIS ('DOD PA SPYOD PAS NI) MNYES PAR BYAS NA THABS DES DE(S) DNGOS GRUB RGYA CHEN PO 'THOB PAR 'GYUR:- (^RDZOGS RIM KHYAD PAR CAN THOB PA RNAMS LA NI RIGS SO SO'I NGES PA MED DO, ,) -:TE,
gru.wylie: spyi bo la sogs par rigs lnga dgod pa byas la sgrub pa po gang gis ('dod pa spyod pas ni) mnyes par byas na thabs des de(s) dngos grub rgya chen po 'thob par 'gyur:- (^rdzogs rim khyad par can thob pa rnams la ni rigs so so'i nges pa med do, ,) -:te
gru.english: They place the Angels of the Five Families at the tip of their head and so on.  Any practitioner then who manages to please their partner (with the activities of sexual desire) will, through these methods, attain extensive spiritual goals.  (Note that those who have reached a high level aren't necessarily bound to one or another of the Families.)

gru.acip: THEG PA CHEN PO ZHES BYA BA MCHOG GI CHOS (GANG LA YOD PA) GANG YIN PA DE NI, THEG CHEN MCHOG GI CHOS NYID TE DE'I NANG DU DNGOS GRUB RGYA CHE ZHING STE MCHOG TU GYUR PA (SGRUB PA PO) DES 'THOB PAR 'GYUR GYI,
gru.wylie: theg pa chen po zhes bya ba mchog gi chos (gang la yod pa) gang yin pa de ni, theg chen mchog gi chos nyid te de'i nang du dngos grub rgya che zhing ste mchog tu gyur pa (sgrub pa po) des 'thob par 'gyur gyi
gru.english: The reference to the "greater way" here is meant to say that wherever there is this highest spiritual practice (meaning, for whomever follows it) then there are extensive attainments of the spiritual goals--the ultimate point of this greater way; attainments reached by this "highest one" (referring to the practitioner).

gru.acip: (SGRUB PA PO DANG,) RJES SU MI MTHUN PA'I (SEMS DANG LDAN PA'I) PHYAG RGYA (MA) DANG MNYAM PAR SBYOR BAS NI NGES PAR (TE GDON MI ZA BAR) SEMS (RNAM RTOG GI DBANG DU 'GRO BA'I) GA-YENG BA SKYE BAR 'GYUR (BAS, PHYAG RGYAR MI BYA'O, DES NA SEMS SHIN TU BRTZE BA'I PHYAG RGYA DGOS LA) RO,,
gru.wylie: (sgrub pa po dang,) rjes su mi mthun pa'i (sems dang ldan pa'i) phyag rgya (ma) dang mnyam par sbyor bas ni nges par (te gdon mi za bar) sems (rnam rtog gi dbang du 'gro ba'i) ga-yeng ba skye bar 'gyur (bas, phyag rgyar mi bya'o, des na sems shin tu brtse ba'i phyag rgya dgos la) ro
gru.english: If however they (the practitioner) undertakes the practice of union with a (woman) partner who does not have a feeling of (an attitude of) deep affection for them, then with certainty (meaning without any doubt) their mind will come to be distracted (in that they will fall under the sway of mistaken perceptions).  (And, as such, they should not take this person as their partner.  We can say then that a person should find a spiritual partner who holds them deep within their heart, in love.)

gru.acip: MDOR BYAS LA, ,SME SHA CAN GYI BDAG NYID CHE, ,BU MO AUTPAL MTHING KHA'I MDOG , ,MIG YANGS DAM PA RNYED NAS NI, ,MNYAM PAR BZHAG CING LEGS PAR BSLABS, ,SGRUB PA PO LA SHIN TU MOS, ZHES GSUNG PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: mdor byas la, ,sme sha can gyi bdag nyid che, ,bu mo autpal mthing kha'i mdog , ,mig yangs dam pa rnyed nas ni, ,mnyam par bzhag cing legs par bslabs, ,sgrub pa po la shin tu mos, zhes gsung pa'i phyir
gru.english: As the Brief Presentation puts it, She is a supreme being of the leper family, A girl with the color of a sapphire lotus-- She must have gained the highest of eyes, Wide open, and be perfectly trained In the meditation on union, along with Complete love for the practitioner.

gru.acip: DNGOS GRUB THAMS CAD 'DOD PA DE DAG NI RMONGS PAS DNGOS GRUB MED CING BDE BA MED DE, RGYAL SRID SHOR BA BZHIN LAM MCHOG LA DAD PA DANG BRAL BA'I PHYIR RO ZHES 'CHAD DO,,
gru.wylie: dngos grub thams cad 'dod pa de dag ni rmongs pas dngos grub med cing bde ba med de, rgyal srid shor ba bzhin lam mchog la dad pa dang bral ba'i phyir ro zhes 'chad do
gru.english: People who act this way--even though they do hope for each and every high spiritual goal--are acting out of blindness; they will never achieve these goals, and they will never be happy.  They will be like kings who have lost their kingdoms, for they have no faith in the highest path of all.

gru.acip: DE 'DRA BA DE LA BSHUNG ZHING DMAN PA'I SEMS KYIS DKA' THUB BYED NA, PHUN SUM TSOGS PA THAMS CAD NGES PAR ZAD PAR 'GYUR LA, DKYIL 'KHOR GYI 'KHOR LO BSGOMS PA LA BRTEN NAS GRUB PA STE DGE BA BSAGS PA RNAMS KYANG, SNGAR BSHAD PA DE BZHIN DU ZAD PAR 'GYUR RO, ,'KHOR LO GRUB PA'ANG DE BZHIN DU'O, ,ZHES LHA SBAS KYI 'GREL PAR 'BYUNG BA 'GYUR LEGS SO,,
gru.wylie: de 'dra ba de la bshung zhing dman pa'i sems kyis dka' thub byed na, phun sum tshogs pa thams cad nges par zad par 'gyur la, dkyil 'khor gyi 'khor lo bsgoms pa la brten nas grub pa ste dge ba bsags pa rnams kyang, sngar bshad pa de bzhin du zad par 'gyur ro, ,'khor lo grub pa'ang de bzhin du'o, ,zhes lha sbas kyi 'grel par 'byung ba 'gyur legs so
gru.english: If rather we say bad things about Them behind Their back, or undertake our difficult practices with some kind of lower thoughts, then it will definitely wipe out all the excellent things we have done before.  All the attainments--meaning all the good karma that we have collected earlier by meditating upon the circles of beings within the secret world--will, as we said it before, be wiped out.  And so the translation as we see it in a line from the commentary of Deva Rakshita is a good one when it says here, "The same will happen with the circles of beings You have reached."

gru.acip: DE LTA BUS DAM TSIG NYAMS NA, DE LAS LDANG BA'I THABS DAM TSIG GSO BA'I SGRUB THABS DANG, BZLAS PA LVA BA PA DANG LHA SBAS KYI 'GREL PAR BSHAD DO,,
gru.wylie: de lta bus dam tshig nyams na, de las ldang ba'i thabs dam tshig gso ba'i sgrub thabs dang, bzlas pa lva ba pa dang lha sbas kyi 'grel par bshad do
gru.english: The commentaries of Master Kambala and Master Deva Rakshita say at this point that--in the case that our pledges are broken in this way--then we should undertake means of recovering ourselves, through rituals for reaching Angels that include a section on restoring the pledges, or else through the recitation of mantras.

gru.acip: BRTAN PAR GYUR PAS KUN RDZOB PA'I RANG BZHIN GYI BYANG CHUB KYI SEMS LAS RANG GI SEMS DON DAM PA'I RANG BZHIN RNAM PAR MI RTOG PA'I NGO BO NYID DU GYUR PA NA, SGRUB PA PO RDO RJE 'CHANG NYID DU 'GRUB PAR BYED PA'O,,
gru.wylie: brtan par gyur pas kun rdzob pa'i rang bzhin gyi byang chub kyi sems las rang gi sems don dam pa'i rang bzhin rnam par mi rtog pa'i ngo bo nyid du gyur pa na, sgrub pa po rdo rje 'chang nyid du 'grub par byed pa'o
gru.english: When we become firm in this practice, then out of the Wish for enlightenment which has a deceptive nature is born the state of mind that has the nature of the ultimate: where its very nature is that we no longer have any mistaken perceptions.  And then the practitioner can truly take themselves to the state of nothing less than the Holder of the Diamond himself. * * * Je Rinpoche provides us with a list of qualifications for partner practice in His Book of Three Beliefs, on the teachings of the Six Yogas of Naropa (ACIP digital text S05317, ff. 30b-31a):

gru.acip: RTZA BA DANG YAN LAG GI DAM TSIG LA MKHAS SHING, JI LTA BA BZHIN DU SRUNG BA, DKYIL 'KHOR GYI 'KHOR LO'I SGRUB THABS LA MKHAS SHING, THUN BZHIR BSGOMS PAS LEGS PAR BYANG BA,
gru.wylie: rtsa ba dang yan lag gi dam tshig la mkhas shing, ji lta ba bzhin du srung ba, dkyil 'khor gyi 'khor lo'i sgrub thabs la mkhas shing, thun bzhir bsgoms pas legs par byang ba
gru.english: We must both be well versed in the root and secondary pledges, and be observing them well.  We must further be masters of the ritual for reaching the circles of Angels in the secret world, and should have become adept in the practice of the four sessions of meditation.

gru.acip: RGYUD SDE DANG, GRUB CHEN GYI GZHUNG KHUNGS MA NAS BSHAD PA'I MTSAN NYID TSANG BA CIG GIS BYED PA YIN PA LA, DE LTAR BSHAD PA'I BRDA CHAD RAGS PA TZAM YANG MA CHAGS PAR, ZAB MO YIN ZER BA'I MAN NGAG LTAR SNANG RE LA NGES PA DRANGS NAS,
gru.wylie: rgyud sde dang, grub chen gyi gzhung khungs ma nas bshad pa'i mtshan nyid tshang ba cig gis byed pa yin pa la, de ltar bshad pa'i brda chad rags pa tsam yang ma chags par, zab mo yin zer ba'i man ngag ltar snang re la nges pa drangs nas
gru.english: In short, partner practice is something which must be done by a person who possesses these and all the other qualifications that are described in the various groups of the secret teachings, and in the authoritative classics of great practitioners of the past.  We shouldn't be one of those people who has not even the slightest acquaintance with the topics treated in these works, and gets drawn off by some bogus presentation that's supposed to be oh so deep. * * * In His Lamp that Illuminates, Totally, the Teaching on the Five Steps (ACIP digital text S05302, f. 201a-201b), Je Rinpoche reminds us that an understanding of emptiness alone is not enough for partner practice:

gru.acip: LAM DUS KYI SNANG MCHED THOB GSUM 'OD GSAL DANG BCAS PA 'BYUNG TSUL NI, 'DIR RDZOGS RIM GYI DMIGS PA PHAL CHER RLUNG DBU MAR ZHUGS GNAS THIM GSUM BYAS PA LA BRTEN NAS SNANG MCHED THOB GSUM 'OD GSAL DANG BCAS PA BSKYED PA DANG, DE LA BRTEN NAS SGYU LUS DANG, SKABS GZHAN DU STONG GZUGS KYI SKU BSGRUB PA'I PHYIR YIN LA,
gru.wylie: lam dus kyi snang mched thob gsum 'od gsal dang bcas pa 'byung tshul ni, 'dir rdzogs rim gyi dmigs pa phal cher rlung dbu mar zhugs gnas thim gsum byas pa la brten nas snang mched thob gsum 'od gsal dang bcas pa bskyed pa dang, de la brten nas sgyu lus dang, skabs gzhan du stong gzugs kyi sku bsgrub pa'i phyir yin la
gru.english: Here is how, at the point where we are still practicing the path, the steps of radiance, proliferation, and near-attainment--along with the clear light--make their appearance.  In this system, the majority of the topics within the stage of completion are meant to bring on these three steps, together with the clear light, through the three-fold process of getting the winds to enter, stay, and dissolve into the central channel.  Due to this then we reach the body of illusion, and at the other point reach the holy body of the empty form.

gru.acip: DES NA BDE STONG DBYER MED KYI BDE BA'I CHA SGRUB TSUL YANG JI LTA BA RJE BLA MA'I BKA' DRIN GYIS SHES DGOS LA, KHYAD PAR DU BDE BA DE LA RGYAS 'DEBS BYED DANG, GANG LA MNYAM PAR 'JOG PA'I YUL GYI STONG PA NYID RTAG CHAD GOL BA'I MTHA' LAS 'DAS PA'I JI LTA BA NYID NI RJE BLA MA NYAG GCIG GIS GSAL BAR MDZAD PA YIN NO,,
gru.wylie: des na bde stong dbyer med kyi bde ba'i cha sgrub tshul yang ji lta ba rje bla ma'i bka' drin gyis shes dgos la, khyad par du bde ba de la rgyas 'debs byed dang, gang la mnyam par 'jog pa'i yul gyi stong pa nyid rtag chad gol ba'i mtha' las 'das pa'i ji lta ba nyid ni rje bla ma nyag gcig gis gsal bar mdzad pa yin no
gru.english: We can say then that coming to an accurate understanding of how we reach the bliss part in the indivisible pair of bliss and voidness is something we can only do by relying upon the kindness of Je Rinpoche.  We must especially acquaint ourselves with the way in which we set the seal upon this bliss, and with exactly how it is that we come in our practice of union to reach, as our object, a kind of emptiness which transcends the two erroneous extremes of thinking that things are unchanging, or have stopped altogether.  It is Je Tsongkapa, and only Je Tsongkapa, who has clarified exactly how we do so.

gru.acip: RJE BLA MAS RJE BTZUN RAN MDA' BAR PHUL PA'I GDAMS PA LAS, MTSAN NYID KYI THEG PA'I GNAD GSUM GONG DU BSTAN PA RNAMS KYANG SHES, SNGAGS KYI THABS LAM GYI GDAMS NGAG KYANG YOD PA KLU SGRUB DANG ZLA GRAGS 'DRA BA DE MTSAN NYID THEG PA RKYANG PA'I GDUL BYA LAS MYUR PA DANG CHES KHYAD PAR DU 'PHAGS PA YIN GYI, MTSAN NYID KYI LAM GYI GNAD MED PA'I SNGAGS KYI THUN MONG MA YIN PA'I GDUL BYA DE MTSAN NYID KYI GDUL BYA LAS DMAN,
gru.wylie: rje bla mas rje btsun ran mda' bar phul pa'i gdams pa las, mtshan nyid kyi theg pa'i gnad gsum gong du bstan pa rnams kyang shes, sngags kyi thabs lam gyi gdams ngag kyang yod pa klu sgrub dang zla grags 'dra ba de mtshan nyid theg pa rkyang pa'i gdul bya las myur pa dang ches khyad par du 'phags pa yin gyi, mtshan nyid kyi lam gyi gnad med pa'i sngags kyi thun mong ma yin pa'i gdul bya de mtshan nyid kyi gdul bya las dman
gru.english: We see the following words of advice that Je Rinpoche offered to the holy Lama Rendawa: Suppose then we come across a person who first of all understands the three crucial points of the open path of the rational, as we have described them above.  And on top of this they also possess the advices of the special methods of the path of the secret way.  Such a disciple is then similar to Arya Nagarjuna, and Master Chandrakirti, and is vastly superior to a student who knows only of the open path of the rational--they move along the path much more quickly. We should point out as well though that a disciple of this unique path of the secret word who lacks the crucial points of the teachings of this path of the rational is worse than a disciple who is limited to the rational.

gru.acip: DRAN RGYU'I LTA BA NI GCIG DANG DU BRAL SOGS GTAN TSIGS GANG RUNG ZHIG GIS LEGS PAR GTAN LA 'BEBS NUS PA ZHIG DGOS SO, ,DE LTAR YIN NA LAG TU BLANG DU YOD DO, ,'DI RJES DRAN SGRUB BYED DU GSUNGS PAS DE LTAR YANG SHES DGOS SO,,
gru.wylie: dran rgyu'i lta ba ni gcig dang du bral sogs gtan tshigs gang rung zhig gis legs par gtan la 'bebs nus pa zhig dgos so, ,de ltar yin na lag tu blang du yod do, ,'di rjes dran sgrub byed du gsungs pas de ltar yang shes dgos so
gru.english: As for the view that we do bring to mind, the partner must be a person who has been able to establish, clearly, the meaning of emptiness by utilizing any one of the logical arguments for it: proofs such as the fact that things are neither one nor many.  If we find a person such as this, only then can we take them up in our arms.  It has been stated that we use this recollection to establish the emptiness to ourselves; and so they should know how to do that as well.

gru.acip: ,ZA ZHING 'THUNG LA GNYIS SPROD KYIS DGA' ZHING, ,RTAG TU YANG DANG YANG DU 'KHOR LO 'GENG, ,CHOS 'DI LTA BUS 'JIG RTEN PHA ROL 'GRUB 'GYUR TE, ,RMONGS PA'I 'JIG RTEN MGO BOR RDOG PAS MNAN NAS SONG,
gru.wylie: za zhing 'thung la gnyis sprod kyis dga' zhing, ,rtag tu yang dang yang du 'khor lo 'geng, ,chos 'di lta bus 'jig rten pha rol 'grub 'gyur te, ,rmongs pa'i 'jig rten mgo bor rdog pas mnan nas song
gru.english: Eat, drink, enjoy the touch between the two; Spend all your time filling the wheel, again and again. This is the teaching that will take you across this world; You will walk across on the heads of the world's blind.

gru.acip: RIN PO CHE'I MAndAL DANG BCAS TE, GSOL BA BTAB PA LAS DGYES BZHIN DU GNANG BA LA, SNGAGS KYI TSUL LA NYAMS SU LEN PA'I TSUL GYIS NAN TAN YUN RING DU 'GRUS PAR BYAS LA,
gru.wylie: rin po che'i maNDal dang bcas te, gsol ba btab pa las dgyes bzhin du gnang ba la, sngags kyi tshul la nyams su len pa'i tshul gyis nan tan yun ring du 'grus par byas la
gru.english: We then presented as well a mandala of precious substances, and made our heartfelt request for the teaching.  And in response our Lama granted it quite happily.  We then went and made great efforts, over a long period of time, to devote ourselves in the manner of practice that belongs to the secret word.

gru.acip: DGOS PA GANG GI DON DU NA, RNAL 'BYOR PA GANG GIS PHO NYA'I MTSAN NYID YANG DAG PA SHES PAR 'GYUR BA'I CHED YIN LA, DE LTAR SHES NA MKHA' 'GRO MA RNAMS DAM TSIG LAS MI 'DA' BAR SGRUB PA PO RNAMS LA PHAN PA'I PHYIR DU GNAS PAR 'GYUR RO,,
gru.wylie: dgos pa gang gi don du na, rnal 'byor pa gang gis pho nya'i mtshan nyid yang dag pa shes par 'gyur ba'i ched yin la, de ltar shes na mkha' 'gro ma rnams dam tshig las mi 'da' bar sgrub pa po rnams la phan pa'i phyir du gnas par 'gyur ro
gru.english: And for what purpose do we do so?  It is so that every deep practitioner can come to a clear understanding of just what the characteristics of a proper Messenger are.  Because if they do know these characteristics, then the Angels of the Sky will be able to come to these practitioners and assist them, without violating the pledge that They have made.

gru.acip: GNYIS PA NI, ,MIG DMAR BA SHAS CHE ZHING SER BA DANG, ,DE BZHIN RKANG PA LAG PA'ANG DMAR, ,MALLI KA YI DRI 'BYUNG ZHING, ,BDER GSHEGS 'DUS PA NYID DGA' BA'I, ,BUD MED DNGOS GRUB STER BAR BYED,
gru.wylie: gnyis pa ni, ,mig dmar ba shas che zhing ser ba dang, ,de bzhin rkang pa lag pa'ang dmar, ,malli ka yi dri 'byung zhing, ,bder gshegs 'dus pa nyid dga' ba'i, ,bud med dngos grub ster bar byed
gru.english: Here then is the second: Her eyes are a russet color, Gold with crimson predominate; Her legs and arms as well Possess a rosy tint. She gives off the jasmine fragrance Of a mallika bloom, She includes within Herself All Those Gone to Bliss-- She is a Woman of Pleasure Who grants you all your goals.

gru.acip: PHYAG RGYA DE RNAMS NI GROL BA'I DNGOS GRUB GYI DON DU, DGE BA'I BSHES GNYEN TE RNAL 'BYOR PA THAMS CAD KYI THUN MONG DU RJES SU 'GRO BA MA'O,,
gru.wylie: phyag rgya de rnams ni grol ba'i dngos grub gyi don du, dge ba'i bshes gnyen te rnal 'byor pa thams cad kyi thun mong du rjes su 'gro ba ma'o
gru.english: For all those "spiritual friends"--meaning secret practitioners--who seek the goal of liberation, the types of partners mentioned above are all women that they can come to.

gru.acip: PHYAG RGYA LA BRTEN PA DANG BRAL NA MI 'GRUB PAR RTZA RGYUD LAS GSUNGS PA DE NYID BSHAD RGYUD SAMPU tA LAS KYANG GSAL BAR GSUNGS TE, THABS DANG SHES RAB MA GTOGS PAR SANGS RGYAS NYID MNGON DU THOB PAR MI 'GYUR RO,,
gru.wylie: phyag rgya la brten pa dang bral na mi 'grub par rtsa rgyud las gsungs pa de nyid bshad rgyud sampu Ta las kyang gsal bar gsungs te, thabs dang shes rab ma gtogs par sangs rgyas nyid mngon du thob par mi 'gyur ro
gru.english: The root tantra states that--if we fail to practice with a spiritual partner--then we cannot achieve our goals; and The Kiss, which is the explanatory tantra, clearly states the same thing as well: "Without the union of method [the male partner] and wisdom [the female partner], there is no way of achieving that singular state of enlightenment."

gru.acip: DE'I PHYIR SHES RAB MA DNGOS SU YANG DAG PAR RDZOGS PA'I BYANG CHUB SBYIN PAR BYED PA BZANG MO SPANG BAR MI BYA STE, PHYAG RGYA RE RE DANG LDAN PA 'DI MA GTOGS PAR DNGOS GRUB STER BAR MI 'GYUR RO ZHES SO,,
gru.wylie: de'i phyir shes rab ma dngos su yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub sbyin par byed pa bzang mo spang bar mi bya ste, phyag rgya re re dang ldan pa 'di ma gtogs par dngos grub ster bar mi 'gyur ro zhes so
gru.english: As such we should never give up our Lady of Excellence: the Woman of Wisdom who grants us, directly, the state of perfect and complete enlightenment.  Because unless we are possessed of some one of these different partners, we will never be granted our goals.

gru.acip: ,'DI DAG MDOR BSDUS MGON PO KLU SGRUB KYIS, ,BSHES SPRINGS LAS GSUNGS YA RABS BUD MED NI, ,SRING MO LTA BUR RJES MTHUN GANG YIN DANG, ,MDZA' MO BZHIN DU SNYING LA BABS PA DANG, ,MA BZHIN PHAN PAR 'DOD DANG BRAN MO BZHIN, ,DBANG GYUR GANG YIN RIGS KYI LHA BZHIN BKUR,
gru.wylie: 'di dag mdor bsdus mgon po klu sgrub kyis, ,bshes springs las gsungs ya rabs bud med ni, ,sring mo lta bur rjes mthun gang yin dang, ,mdza' mo bzhin du snying la babs pa dang, ,ma bzhin phan par 'dod dang bran mo bzhin, ,dbang gyur gang yin rigs kyi lha bzhin bkur
gru.english: To summarize all these, bring to mind The description that our protector, Nagarjuna, Gives in his Letter to a Friend for a woman Who is one of high integrity. She should be as dear to our heart As a sister, and as pleasing as a good female friend. She should have the same desire to help us As our very own Mother possesses; And should be as self-controlled as a servant. A woman like this, He says, should be Honored like the goddess your family worships. * * * His Holiness the First Panchen Lama, Lobsang Chukyi Gyeltsen, discusses the best configuration of mind and body for partner practice in His Essence of the Ocean of Attainments: An Explanation of the Creation Stage of the Glorious Secret Collection (Guhya Samaja), King of All the Secret Teachings (ACIP digital text S00265, ff. 41b-42b):

gru.acip: YANG BHA GA DANG LING GA YANG DAG PAR SBYOR MI NUS PA DES NI BDE BA CHEN PO'I TING NGE 'DZIN MI RNYED DO, ZHES DBANG PO GNYIS SBYOR BA MED PAR 'DOD YON LAM BYED KYI BDE BA CHEN PO LA BRTEN NAS SGYU MA'I SKU TSE DE LA MI 'GRUB PAR GSUNGS PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: yang bha ga dang ling ga yang dag par sbyor mi nus pa des ni bde ba chen po'i ting nge 'dzin mi rnyed do, zhes dbang po gnyis sbyor ba med par 'dod yon lam byed kyi bde ba chen po la brten nas sgyu ma'i sku tshe de la mi 'grub par gsungs pa'i phyir
gru.english: We also see the statement that "If a person is unable to join the bhaga and the linga together in perfect union, then they will never find the single-point mind of greatest bliss."  What this says is that--without a union of the two sexual organs--we will never be able to utilize great bliss, where we use the objects of desire as a path, to reach our illusory body in this one life.

gru.acip: DANG PO GRUB STE, DBANG PO GNYIS SBYOR LA BRTEN PA'I KHAMS DKAR DMAR GYI 'DU 'PHROD MED PA'I PHYIR, GNYIS PA GRUB STE, DE NA PHO MO'I DBANG PO TZAM YANG MED PA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: dang po grub ste, dbang po gnyis sbyor la brten pa'i khams dkar dmar gyi 'du 'phrod med pa'i phyir, gnyis pa grub ste, de na pho mo'i dbang po tsam yang med pa'i phyir
gru.english: The first of these statements holds true because pleasure beings of this type lack the meeting of the white and red elements that comes with the joining of the two sexual organs.  The second is true because beings in the higher two realms don't even have the male and female organs.

gru.acip: GSUM PA GRUB STE, GLING DE GSUM NA KHAMS KYI 'DU 'PHROD YOD KYANG BDE CHEN LAM DU BYED NUS PA'I DBANG PO RNO PA MED CING, TSE STOD LA BSAGS PA'I LAS TSE SMAD LA SMIN NUS PA MED PA'I PHYIR TE, DE RNAMS LONGS SPYOD KYI SA PA YIN GYI LAS KYI SA PA MA YIN PA'I PHYIR TE,
gru.wylie: gsum pa grub ste, gling de gsum na khams kyi 'du 'phrod yod kyang bde chen lam du byed nus pa'i dbang po rno pa med cing, tshe stod la bsags pa'i las tshe smad la smin nus pa med pa'i phyir te, de rnams longs spyod kyi sa pa yin gyi las kyi sa pa ma yin pa'i phyir te
gru.english: The third statement is true because--even though beings on these three continents do possess the meeting of the elements--they lack the sharp intellectual faculties that enable them to use bliss as a spiritual path.  They also lack the ability to collect karma in the earlier part of their life that will ripen in the later part.  This is because they are what we call "inhabitants of realms of enjoyment" and not "inhabitants of a realm of karma."

gru.acip: BZHI PA GRUB STE, DE DAG LAM SGOM PA'I RTEN DU MI RUNG BA'I PHYIR,
gru.wylie: bzhi pa grub ste, de dag lam sgom pa'i rten du mi rung ba'i phyir
gru.english: The fourth statement above is accurate because the body and mind of a being in the lower realm is simply not a usable configuration for practicing the path.

gru.acip: DES NA SNGAGS BLA MED KYI GDUL BYA'I GTZO BO DE DZAMBU GLING PA'I MI'I RTEN CAN YIN PA LA DGONGS NAS, YUL NYI SHU RTZA BZHI'I DPA' BO DANG RNAL 'BYOR MA RNAMS DZAMBU GLING KHO NAR BZHUGS NAS SGRUB PA PO'I RGYUD BYIN GYIS RLOB PA DANG, LAM SGRUB PA'I GROGS MDZAD PAR RDO RJE MKHA' 'GRO'I 'GREL PAR GSUNGS SO,,
gru.wylie: des na sngags bla med kyi gdul bya'i gtso bo de dzambu gling pa'i mi'i rten can yin pa la dgongs nas, yul nyi shu rtsa bzhi'i dpa' bo dang rnal 'byor ma rnams dzambu gling kho nar bzhugs nas sgrub pa po'i rgyud byin gyis rlob pa dang, lam sgrub pa'i grogs mdzad par rdo rje mkha' 'gro'i 'grel par gsungs so
gru.english: And so we can say that the principal type of disciple for the practice of the unsurpassed teachings of the way of the secret word is one who possesses a human body and mind, here on the continent of Jambu.  This in fact is what they have in mind, states the commentary to the Diamond Angel of the Sky, when the Warriors and Angels of the 24 holy places choose to reside only here on the Jambu continent, working Their blessings upon secret practitioners who reside here, assisting them in their practice of the path. * * * Lama Quicksilver gives us more detail on these distinctions in His Secret Treasure of the Angels (ACIP digital text S00202, ff. 45b-46b):

gru.acip: PHYI NANG GSANG BA DE KHO NA NYID KYI MCHOD PA SOGS THAMS CAD LA RANG GI STOBS CI YOD KYIS 'BAD PA KHAS LEN PA DANG, NYIN MTSAN DUS DRUG TU MCHOD PA BYED PA STE GNYIS, DON GRUB KYI RIGS KYI DAM TSIG STE BSDOM NA BCU DGU'O,
gru.wylie: phyi nang gsang ba de kho na nyid kyi mchod pa sogs thams cad la rang gi stobs ci yod kyis 'bad pa khas len pa dang, nyin mtshan dus drug tu mchod pa byed pa ste gnyis, don grub kyi rigs kyi dam tshig ste bsdom na bcu dgu'o
gru.english: There are, finally, two pledges for the Family of Attainment, or Amogha Siddhi.  The first is the promise to exert ourselves, to the very best of offering; for example in performing the outer offerings, the inner offerings, the secret offering, and the offering of suchness. The second pledge here is to actually perform these offerings six times in every 24-hour period.  This then brings us to a total of 19 different individual pledges for the five Families. * * * Je Tsongkapa explains, again from His own Golden Harvest (ACIP digital text S05270, f. 19a):

gru.acip: LNGA PA DON GRUB KYI SDOM GZUNG NI, ME TOG SOGS PHYI'I MCHOD PA, NANG MCHOD BYIN GYIS RLABS NAS 'BUL BA NANG GI MCHOD PA, PHYAG RGYA DANG SBYAR BA'I BDE BAS DKYIL 'KHOR BA'I LHA RNAMS TSIM PAR BYED PA GSANG BA'I MCHOD PA, BDE BA DES STONG NYID RTOGS PA DE KHO NA NYID KYI MCHOD PA STE SNGAR BZHIN SLOB PA'O,
gru.wylie: lnga pa don grub kyi sdom gzung ni, me tog sogs phyi'i mchod pa, nang mchod byin gyis rlabs nas 'bul ba nang gi mchod pa, phyag rgya dang sbyar ba'i bde bas dkyil 'khor ba'i lha rnams tshim par byed pa gsang ba'i mchod pa, bde ba des stong nyid rtogs pa de kho na nyid kyi mchod pa ste sngar bzhin slob pa'o
gru.english: Here as our fifth point is a description of the vow taken for the Angel of Attainment.  Offering flowers and the like constitutes an outer offering.  The inner offering is where we perform the ceremony of blessing the inner offering, and then present it.  It is the secret offering to satiate the Angels of the secret world with the bliss that comes through union with a sacred partner.  And the offering of suchness is to use this bliss to perceive emptiness.  We must train ourselves in these offerings, as mentioned before. * * * Of all the secret commitments, the Eight Mother Vows--an important element in many different traditions of the Diamond Way, such as that of the Angel of Diamond (Vajra Yogini)-- are of course the ones which relate most to practice with a spiritual partner.  And one of the best commentaries on these vows is that of Master Damtsik Dorje: The Shining Glory of Great Bliss, a Presentation of the Eight Pledges Spoken in the Root Tantra of Highest Bliss (ACIP uncataloged data).  Here are selections on the vows, from this work.

gru.acip: THOGS MED PA ZHES PA NI, GANG GIS KYANG GZHOM DU MI NUS PA'I DON DU BSHAD PAS, SNGAGS KYI THUN MONG MA YIN PA'I GRUB MTHA' LAS GZHAN DU BKRI MI NUS PA DANG,
gru.wylie: thogs med pa zhes pa ni, gang gis kyang gzhom du mi nus pa'i don du bshad pas, sngags kyi thun mong ma yin pa'i grub mtha' las gzhan du bkri mi nus pa dang
gru.english: The word "untouchable" is often explained as referring to someone who cannot be overcome by another.  The expression here means that one should reach the point where they could never be led off into any system of belief other than the unique way of the secret word.

gru.acip: ,'DI BRGYAD DAM TSIG KUN SPYOD YIN, ,SGRUB PA LA NI GNAS PA YI, ,SGRUB PA POS NI RTAG SHES BYA,
gru.wylie: 'di brgyad dam tshig kun spyod yin, ,sgrub pa la ni gnas pa yi, ,sgrub pa pos ni rtag shes bya
gru.english: This then is the way Of life of the eight pledges; Practitioners who live a life Trying to carry them out Must always be aware.

gru.acip: 'DI BRGYAD DAM TSIG CES SOGS RKANG PA GSUM NI, DE YANG SNGA MA RNAMS KYI DON MDOR HRIL GYIS SGRIL NA, SNGAR BSHAD PA LTAR GYI G-YON PA'I KUN SPYOD THAMS CAD BYED PA DANG, RGYUD 'DIR DBANG BSKUR BA'I SGRUB PA PO DANG SLOB DPON LA MI BRNYAS SHING CI NUS KYIS MCHOD PA RNAMS NI DAM TSIG DANG PO DANG,
gru.wylie: 'di brgyad dam tshig ces sogs rkang pa gsum ni, de yang snga ma rnams kyi don mdor hril gyis sgril na, sngar bshad pa ltar gyi g-yon pa'i kun spyod thams cad byed pa dang, rgyud 'dir dbang bskur ba'i sgrub pa po dang slob dpon la mi brnyas shing ci nus kyis mchod pa rnams ni dam tshig dang po dang
gru.english: We turn next to the three lines [in the Tibetan] that include "This...the eight pledges."  Now we could summarize the points given above in the following way.  The first pledge is that we should, as explained earlier on, observe all the various forms of leftways behavior.  We should never berate those practitioners who have been empowered to follow this secret teachings, nor our Master, and we should further make offerings to them, to the best of our ability.

gru.acip: DE DAG SHES PA TZAM LA MI 'JOG PAR TSUL BZHIN DU SGRUB PA LA GNAS PA'I SGRUB PA PO RNAMS KYIS RTAG TU STE YANG DANG YANG DU DRAN SHES BAG YOD DANG LDAN PAR BYAS TE BSRUNG BAR BYA YI, BRJED CING YAL BAR 'DOR BAR BYA BA MA YIN NO,, ZHES PA'O,,
gru.wylie: de dag shes pa tsam la mi 'jog par tshul bzhin du sgrub pa la gnas pa'i sgrub pa po rnams kyis rtag tu ste yang dang yang du dran shes bag yod dang ldan par byas te bsrung bar bya yi, brjed cing yal bar 'dor bar bya ba ma yin no,, zhes pa'o
gru.english: Those practitioners who seek to live a life where they are trying to carry out these pledges in the proper way, rather than just being satisfied with learning about them, must always (meaning over and over again) use mindfulness, awareness, and great care to keep their pledges.  These are not something that one should allow to slip one's mind, nor ever simply ignore. * * * Je Tsongkapa describes the essential role of practice with an imaginary partner during the creation stage in His Cow that Produces Every Wish, on the teachings of the Sphere of Highest Bliss (Chakra Sanvara) (ACIP digital text S05320, ff. 174a-175b).  Je Rinpoche has a very similar presentation of these vows in His Illumination of Every Secret Point (ACIP digital text S05316), at ff. 131b-134a, and serious students may want to read that as well.

gru.acip: DNGOS GRUB KYI RGYU'I DAM TSIG BRGYAD KYI DANG PO NI, SNGAR BSHAD PA'I GA-YON PA'I KUN SPYOD DANG, MI BRNYAS SHING MCHOD PA NI DAM TSIG DANG PO'O,,
gru.wylie: dngos grub kyi rgyu'i dam tshig brgyad kyi dang po ni, sngar bshad pa'i ga-yon pa'i kun spyod dang, mi brnyas shing mchod pa ni dam tshig dang po'o
gru.english: There are eight different pledges which are the very cause of all attainments; here is the first.  We describe this first pledge as being the leftways behavior that we described before, along with a commitment never to disparage high beings, and always to make Them offerings.

gru.acip: ,'O NA PHO NYA MO BSTEN PAR DKA' 'AM SLA SNYAM NA, PHO NYA MO NI RAL GRI'I SO DANG 'DRA STE, RAL GRI'I SO LA BRTEN PA NA 'JIGS SHING YID MA YENGS PA DGOS PA DE BZHIN DU PHO NYA MO DANG 'GROGS PA LEGS NA SDIG PA DAG PAR BYED CING, BSOD NAMS 'PHEL BAR BYED PAS SGRUB PA POS NI DNGOS GRUB 'THOB LA,
gru.wylie: 'o na pho nya mo bsten par dka' 'am sla snyam na, pho nya mo ni ral gri'i so dang 'dra ste, ral gri'i so la brten pa na 'jigs shing yid ma yengs pa dgos pa de bzhin du pho nya mo dang 'grogs pa legs na sdig pa dag par byed cing, bsod nams 'phel bar byed pas sgrub pa pos ni dngos grub 'thob la
gru.english: "Well now," you may ask yourself, "is this practicing with a Messenger lady something which is easy, or hard, to do?"  A Messenger lady is very much like the edge of a razor blade: when you use a razor, you have to have some healthy fear of it, and never allow your mind to wander.  If you do a good job of making a Messenger lady your companion, then all of your bad deeds will be cleaned away and--because She helps them increase their good deeds--the deep practitioner comes to reach their spiritual goals.

gru.acip: GNYIS PA PHYI'I RKYEN LAS RGYA LA BRTEN NAS BSGOM PA NI, RGYUD SDE DANG GRUB CHEN GYI GZHUNG KHUNGS MA NAS BSHAD PA'I MTSAN NYID TSANG BA ZHIG MA GTOGS GZHAN GYIS BYAS NA NGAN 'GRO'I SGO 'BYED PAS RE ZHIG LA BZHAG GO,
gru.wylie: gnyis pa phyi'i rkyen las rgya la brten nas bsgom pa ni, rgyud sde dang grub chen gyi gzhung khungs ma nas bshad pa'i mtshan nyid tshang ba zhig ma gtogs gzhan gyis byas na ngan 'gro'i sgo 'byed pas re zhig la bzhag go
gru.english: The second part concerns practice with the outer aid of an actual partner.  This practice can only be done by someone who possesses each and every one of the requisite qualifications outlined in the original tantras, and in those authoritative works composed by the great sages.  Anyone else who attempts it is simply working to open the gates to the lower realms.  As such, I will forego for the time being any presentation of it here. * * * Shaluwa Rinchen Lobsang Kyenrab, a famed master in the lineage of the teachings of the Angel of Diamond (Vajra Yogini), echoes Je Rinpoche's approach in His Easy Road for the Virtuous to Travel to the Heaven of the Sky," being Instructions for Undertaking the Deep Practice of the Two Stages of the Secret Teachings of the Holy Queen of the Heaven of Naropa (Vajrayogini) (ACIP digital text S00064, f. 76b)

gru.acip: DE NI SANGS RGYAS ZHES BYA BA LA SOGS PA GSUNGS TE, SGRUB PA PO DE NI BLO (NI 'DIR SHES RAB YIN LA DE YANG SKABS KYIS SHES RAB MA) STE LEGS PAR BSLABS PA'I PHYAG RGYA GANG LA YOD PA DE NI BLO CAN TE,
gru.wylie: de ni sangs rgyas zhes bya ba la sogs pa gsungs te, sgrub pa po de ni blo (ni 'dir shes rab yin la de yang skabs kyis shes rab ma) ste legs par bslabs pa'i phyag rgya gang la yod pa de ni blo can te
gru.english: This is expressed in the lines that talk about "Buddhas" and so on: this kind of deep practitioner is "possessed of intellect," in the sense that they possess a well-trained spiritual partner, here called "intellect" (meaning here, "wisdom" and, given the context, a Woman of Wisdom).

gru.acip: RNAM PAR MI RTOG PA (STE, CHOS RNAMS KYI YIN LUGS KYI) 'I NGO BO NYID SHES PA (DES MTSAN 'DZIN GYI RTOG PA 'JOMS PAS NI), SANGS RGYAS NYID DE RDO RJE 'CHANG CHEN PO NYID 'GRUB PAR 'GYUR ZHING (STE, GO 'PHANG DER), BDAG NYID RDZOGS PAR 'GYUR BA STE, DRANG BA'I DON TO,,
gru.wylie: rnam par mi rtog pa (ste, chos rnams kyi yin lugs kyi) 'i ngo bo nyid shes pa (des mtshan 'dzin gyi rtog pa 'joms pas ni), sangs rgyas nyid de rdo rje 'chang chen po nyid 'grub par 'gyur zhing (ste, go 'phang der), bdag nyid rdzogs par 'gyur ba ste, drang ba'i don to
gru.english: A practitioner like this, who no longer misperceives things, understands the very essence of things--(which is to say, the true nature of these things).  (And with this understanding, they are able to destroy their tendency to misperceive things, seeing them as existing in their indications.)  And then they will attain no less than Buddhahood: the state of the great Keeper of the Diamond.  And (in this state) they will come to the perfection of their very being--itself a term which is figurative. * Partner Practice and the Ordained Are ordained people allowed to engage in practice with an actual, physical partner?  For an answer, we turn first to Choney Lama's Cloud of Offerings to Please the Great Lord Atisha: Brief Words of Clarity in Explanation of the 'Lamp on the Path to Enlightenment' (ACIP uncataloged data, ff. 19b-20b).  The Lama is discussing the propriety of partner practice with reference to the tantric empowerment of the ordained (here referred to as "those who follow the path of celibacy").

gru.acip: ,BRTUL ZHUGS CAN DE PHAM PA YI, ,LTUNG BA DAG NI 'BYUNG 'GYUR ZHING, ,DE NI NGAN SONG DES LTUNG PAS, ,GRUB PA NAM YANG YOD MA YIN, ,ZHES SO,
gru.wylie: brtul zhugs can de pham pa yi, ,ltung ba dag ni 'byung 'gyur zhing, ,de ni ngan song des ltung pas, ,grub pa nam yang yod ma yin, ,zhes so
gru.english: Those who are keeping this discipline Would come to commit thereby infractions Of the kind that we call a "defeat." This then would send them down To the realms of misery, and then never Would they reach their spiritual goals.

gru.acip: TSUL KHRIMS KYI BRTUL ZHUGS CAN DE LA NI PHAM PA YI RTZA BA'I LTUNG BA DAG 'BYUNG BAR 'GYUR ZHING GANG ZAG DE NI NGAN SONG DU NGES PAR LTUNG BAR 'GYUR BAS GRUB PA THOB BA NAM YANG YOD PA MA YIN TE, RGYU MTSAN NI DES SANGS RGYAS KYIS NAN CHER BKAG PA DE SPYAD PAR GYUR PA'I PHYIR RO,,
gru.wylie: tshul khrims kyi brtul zhugs can de la ni pham pa yi rtsa ba'i ltung ba dag 'byung bar 'gyur zhing gang zag de ni ngan song du nges par ltung bar 'gyur bas grub pa thob ba nam yang yod pa ma yin te, rgyu mtshan ni des sangs rgyas kyis nan cher bkag pa de spyad par gyur pa'i phyir ro
gru.english: Those who are keeping this ethical discipline would come to commit root infractions, what we call "defeats."  This then would send them down, without a shadow of a doubt, to the realms of misery.  And then neither would they ever reach their spiritual goals.  The reason for this is that they would be engaging in something which was vehemently prohibited by the Buddha.

gru.acip: TING NGE 'DZIN GYI TSOGS BSDUS PA TSUL KHRIMS YIN, DES NA TSUL KHRIMS LAS TING 'DZIN, DE LAS SHES RAB RNAMS 'BREL MAR SGRUB PA'I RGYU 'BRAS YIN PAS RGYU DGE LUGS PAS BYAS, 'BRAS BU GZHAN LA GRUB PA LTA BU YIN ZHES GUNG THANG GI RJE'I BSTOD 'GREL NA GSUNGS,
gru.wylie: ting nge 'dzin gyi tshogs bsdus pa tshul khrims yin, des na tshul khrims las ting 'dzin, de las shes rab rnams 'brel mar sgrub pa'i rgyu 'bras yin pas rgyu dge lugs pas byas, 'bras bu gzhan la grub pa lta bu yin zhes gung thang gi rje'i bstod 'grel na gsungs
gru.english: That thing which allows us to gather together masses of intense concentration is in fact our capacity for ethical behavior.  And so we can say that leading an ethical life leads to concentration, and that leads to wisdom--all in a logical progression.  As such, we read in the commentary to the praise of Je Tsongkapa by Gungtang, the statement above is like saying that the Gelukpas go and create the necessary causes, and then the result comes to those others.

gru.acip: BHU KTA ZHES PA LAS 'PHROS NAS, RGYAL SRAS ZHI BA LHA DE 'DRA YIN TSOD, KLU SGRUB KYIS GSER 'GYUR MDZAD PA KHYOD KYIS MI MANG PO BSLUS PA RED CES BTZAN PHUD BYAS, ZLA GRAGS RI MOR BRIS PA'I BA LAS 'O MA BZHOS PAS KHYOD PHYI ROL BA'I RIG SNGAGS MKHAN ZHIG RED CES BTZAN PHUD BYAS, ZHI BA LHA GANG YANG MI SHES ZER NAS BTZAN PHUD BYAS, DE THAMS CAD PHRAG DOG RED,
gru.wylie: bhu kta zhes pa las 'phros nas, rgyal sras zhi ba lha de 'dra yin tshod, klu sgrub kyis gser 'gyur mdzad pa khyod kyis mi mang po bslus pa red ces btsan phud byas, zla grags ri mor bris pa'i ba las 'o ma bzhos pas khyod phyi rol ba'i rig sngags mkhan zhig red ces btsan phud byas, zhi ba lha gang yang mi shes zer nas btsan phud byas, de thams cad phrag dog red
gru.english: In a discussion that led off from the reference to the word "Bhukta," our Lama spoke of how the great bodhisattva Shantideva was considered no more than this by others.  Arya Nagarjuna turned iron into gold to help His monastery, and then all they could say in return was that He had thereby deceived a lot of people--and they expelled Him from the place.  Master Chandrakirti drew a picture of a cow and then went and milked real milk from it--and all they could do was accuse him of being a non-Buddhist magician, and throw him out of his monastery too.  In fact they threw out Master Shantideva too, saying He didn't know anything.  Every one of these incidents was no more than simple envy. * * * Je Rinpoche, in His Lamp that Illuminates, Totally, the Teaching on the Five Steps makes a distinction between ordained people who would and would not be able to follow the practice of a spiritual partner (ACIP digital text S05302, ff. 277b-280a):

gru.acip: DE BAS NA 'BRAS BU KHYAD PAR CAN NI RGYU KHYAD PAR CAN LAS 'BYUNG BAS, 'BRAS BU'I SKABS KYI BDE BA CHEN PO YANG, RGYU'I SKABS SU 'DOD PA'I YON TAN LA SPYAD PA'I BDE BA KHYAD PAR CAN LAS 'GRUB PA DE LAS GZHAN DU SPYOD PA BYA DKA' BA RNAMS KYIS NI BDE BA CHEN PO'I SEMS RTZE GCIG PA MI 'THOB STE,
gru.wylie: de bas na 'bras bu khyad par can ni rgyu khyad par can las 'byung bas, 'bras bu'i skabs kyi bde ba chen po yang, rgyu'i skabs su 'dod pa'i yon tan la spyad pa'i bde ba khyad par can las 'grub pa de las gzhan du spyod pa bya dka' ba rnams kyis ni bde ba chen po'i sems rtse gcig pa mi 'thob ste
gru.english: We can say then that if you are looking for an extraordinary result you need to find an extraordinary cause.  If you're talking about great bliss being the result you'd like to reach, then to produce it you're going to need--as a cause--that exceptional bliss which you derive from activities which center on the objects of the senses.  If instead though you focus your activities on something else, engaging really in difficult activities, you can never reach the single-pointed state of mind of great bliss.

gru.acip: ,'BRAS BU DON GNYER RGYU BSGRUBS NA, ,DER NI LHA MO SU ZHIG 'GOG , ,DE BAS 'BAD PA THAMS CAD KYIS, ,KUN TU 'GRO BA MCHOD PAR BYA,
gru.wylie: 'bras bu don gnyer rgyu bsgrubs na, ,der ni lha mo su zhig 'gog , ,de bas 'bad pa thams cad kyis, ,kun tu 'gro ba mchod par bya
gru.english: If you seek the result, you must create the cause; And so then would deny the Goddess? Exert then every effort you can In the offering of coming everywhere.

gru.acip: ,DKA' THUB SDOM PA MI BZAD PAS, ,LUS NI SKAMS SHING SDUG BSNGAL 'GYUR, ,SDUG BSNGAL GYIS NI SEMS GA-YENGS NA, ,GA-YENGS PAS DNGOS GRUB GZHAN DU 'GYUR,
gru.wylie: dka' thub sdom pa mi bzad pas, ,lus ni skams shing sdug bsngal 'gyur, ,sdug bsngal gyis ni sems ga-yengs na, ,ga-yengs pas dngos grub gzhan du 'gyur
gru.english: Spiritual hardships, extreme vows, And unbearable practices only Emaciate and torture you. If your mind is distracted by pain, Then your path wanders too, To some other goal.

gru.acip: RTZA BA'I RGYUD LAS KYANG, .DKA' THUB SDOM PA MI BZAD PA, ,BSTEN PAS 'GRUB PAR MI 'GYUR GYI, ,'DOD PA KUN LA LONGS SPYOD PAS, ,BSTEN NA MYUR DU 'GRUB PAR 'GYUR, ,ZHES GSUNGS SO,,
gru.wylie: rtsa ba'i rgyud las kyang, .dka' thub sdom pa mi bzad pa, ,bsten pas 'grub par mi 'gyur gyi, ,'dod pa kun la longs spyod pas, ,bsten na myur du 'grub par 'gyur, ,zhes gsungs so
gru.english: The root tantra as well says, You can follow some austerities, Extreme vows, unbearable practices, But it will never bring you your goals. Follow instead a kind of practice Where you enjoy every pleasure there is; With this you quickly come to your goals.

gru.acip: DKA' THUB NI LUS NGAL ZHING DUB PA'I SBYOR BAS GTZUG LAG KHANG LA SOGS PA SGRUB PA DANG SDOM PA NI SHING DRUNG PA LA SOGS PA SBYANGS PA'I YON TAN BCU GNYIS DANG, MI BZAD PA NI RI LA 'PHYONG ZHING MER 'JUG PA SOGS TE,
gru.wylie: dka' thub ni lus ngal zhing dub pa'i sbyor bas gtsug lag khang la sogs pa sgrub pa dang sdom pa ni shing drung pa la sogs pa sbyangs pa'i yon tan bcu gnyis dang, mi bzad pa ni ri la 'phyong zhing mer 'jug pa sogs te
gru.english: When they mention "austerities" or "spiritual hardships" here, what they're talking about is things like throwing yourself into the construction of a temple where you exhaust and hurt your body.  When they speak of "extreme vows" they're referring to the twelve forms of the training--things like making your home outside in the weather at the base of a tree.  When they mention "unbearable practices," what they're talking about is actions like jumping off a cliff, or throwing oneself into a fire, as a supposed spiritual practice.

gru.acip: DE RNAMS BSTEN PA'I GDUNGS BZHIN PAS BYANG CHUB MI 'GRUB PA NI, DE RNAMS KYIS LUS SKAMS PA STE RGUD PAS SDUG BSNGAL BAR 'GYUR LA, DES NI KUN DA LTA BU'I BYANG CHUB KYI SEMS NYAMS PAS, BDE BA CHEN PO'I TING NGE 'DZIN LAS GZHAN DU GA-YENGS PAS NA, TSE 'DIR DNGOS GRUB MCHOG MI 'GRUB BO,,
gru.wylie: de rnams bsten pa'i gdungs bzhin pas byang chub mi 'grub pa ni, de rnams kyis lus skams pa ste rgud pas sdug bsngal bar 'gyur la, des ni kun da lta bu'i byang chub kyi sems nyams pas, bde ba chen po'i ting nge 'dzin las gzhan du ga-yengs pas na, tshe 'dir dngos grub mchog mi 'grub bo
gru.english: You can torture yourself with practices like these, but they will never bring you to enlightenment.  Rather, they only emaciate and hurt your body, bringing you pain.  This then causes the element of enlightenment within you--the one which resembles semen--to decline.  Due to this, in turn, you become distracted and wander off to something other than the single-point mind of great bliss.  And because of this you fail to reach the ultimate goal here in this life.

gru.acip: DE'I PHYIR 'DOD YON GYI SGO NAS SGO GSUM BDE BAR MI GNAS NA, SEMS RTZE GCIG PA MI 'THOB PA DANG, YID MNYAM PAR 'JOG PAR MI 'GYUR BAS, DE'I DON DU BDE BA'I SPYOD PA SPYAD DGOS PAR GSUNGS PA NI, SEMS RTZE GCIG PA'I MNYAM GZHAG BRTAN PA TZAM ZHIG BSGRUB PA LA MIN GYI, LHAN SKYES KYI BDE BA CHEN PO'I TING NGE 'DZIN BSGRUB PA'I PHYIR YIN NO,,
gru.wylie: de'i phyir 'dod yon gyi sgo nas sgo gsum bde bar mi gnas na, sems rtse gcig pa mi 'thob pa dang, yid mnyam par 'jog par mi 'gyur bas, de'i don du bde ba'i spyod pa spyad dgos par gsungs pa ni, sems rtse gcig pa'i mnyam gzhag brtan pa tsam zhig bsgrub pa la min gyi, lhan skyes kyi bde ba chen po'i ting nge 'dzin bsgrub pa'i phyir yin no
gru.english: As such, we can say that, if we were to fail to remain in a state of "comfort" with regard to our three doors of expression--meaning, as far as our engagement in the objects of the senses--then we would be unable to reach a single-point state of mind, and we would be unable to put our mind into a deep state of meditation.  And what we are being advised to do here then is to undertake activities of pleasure so that we can put the mind in this state.  This by the way is not just for the purpose of reaching a firm state of deep meditation, where the mind is single-point.  Rather, it is all for the purpose of reaching a single-point state of mind filled with great bliss. * The Lama's Role in Granting Permission for Partner Practice In the end, the decision of whether we should undertake practice with a partner is made--as are all such decisions--by our Heart Lama.  We hear first from the Expanded Commentary upon the Briefer Presentation of the Secret Teachings of Lo Diamond (Hevajra), composed by the Indian master Vajra Garbha (ACIP digital text TD01180, f. 81b):

gru.acip: ,BYIS PA GZUD PA'I DUS SU, ,RTAG TU GOMS PA'I RNAL 'BYOR GYIS, ,MNYAM PAR GZHAG PAS DNGOS GRUB THOB,,
gru.wylie: byis pa gzud pa'i dus su, ,rtag tu goms pa'i rnal 'byor gyis, ,mnyam par gzhag pas dngos grub thob
gru.english: When the child is entering, A yogi devoted to practice Attains their goals by engaging In the meditation on union. * * * We see the same advice reflected in the opening lines of A Book on the Stages of Dissolution, Crucial Points Taught Only by Word of Mouth, by Je Rinpoche (S05309, f. 10b):

gru.acip: BLA MA DANG YI DAM MKHA' 'GRO CHOS SKYONG RNAMS KYIS GNANG BA MDZAD NAS BDE CHEN MCHOG GI DNGOS GRUB STZAL DU GSOL,
gru.wylie: bla ma dang yi dam mkha' 'gro chos skyong rnams kyis gnang ba mdzad nas bde chen mchog gi dngos grub stsal du gsol
gru.english: And I pray, abave all, that my Lama--and the Close Angels, and Angels of the Sky, and Protectors of the Dharma--might grant me Their permission to engage in this practice, and thus bestow upon me the attainment of the highest form of ecstasy. * * * Choney Lama, in His Lamp which Illuminates the Very Heart of All the Essential Points in the "Harvest of Attainments," is treating the subject of practice with a partner when He states the following (ACIP digital text S00259, f. 36a):

gru.acip: SGYU LUS SGRUB TSUL SOGS NI BLA MA BRGYUD PA'I MAN NGAG LAS SHES DGOS KYI, GZHAN DU MA YIN TE, BDAG BYIN RLABS LAS,
gru.wylie: sgyu lus sgrub tshul sogs ni bla ma brgyud pa'i man ngag las shes dgos kyi, gzhan du ma yin te, bdag byin rlabs las
gru.english: The method for attaining the body of illusion, and other such practices, can only be learned through the oral advices of the Lamas of the lineage; there is no other way.  As the Instructions for Blessing Oneself put it,

gru.acip: DE YANG DPER NA, SLOB DPON 'PHAGS PA KLU SGRUB KYI GRUB PA'I DNGUL CHU'I DPE DANG 'DRA'O,, DE YANG DNGUL CHU'I THIGS PA GCIG LA, GSER DANG, MU MEN DANG, MU TIG DANG, GLA RTZI DANG, BYANG SEMS DANG, RANG BYUNG DANG, DRI CHEN DANG, DRI CHU DANG, SHA CHEN DANG, MU ZI DANG, RDO CHU STE BCU GCIG PO BLUGS NAS 'GYUR,
gru.wylie: de yang dper na, slob dpon 'phags pa klu sgrub kyi grub pa'i dngul chu'i dpe dang 'dra'o,, de yang dngul chu'i thigs pa gcig la, gser dang, mu men dang, mu tig dang, gla rtsi dang, byang sems dang, rang byung dang, dri chen dang, dri chu dang, sha chen dang, mu zi dang, rdo chu ste bcu gcig po blugs nas 'gyur
gru.english: This is similar for example to the realized being Nagarjuna's metaphor of the quicksilver.  Suppose you take a single drop of quicksilver and add to it the following eleven substances: gold, the deep-blue mumen stone, pearl, musk, semen, menstrual blood, feces, urine, human flesh, sulphur, and limestone water.

gru.acip: DE LA PHYI MA BRGYUD DE STON PA LTAR DU BRJOD NA, DE LA GSUM, SKAL BA DANG BSOD NAMS RAB TSE 'DI LA 'GRUB PA DANG, 'BRING BAR DOR MAN NGAG GI RGYUN GYIS 'GRUB PA DANG, THA MA 'CHI KA MA'I GDAMS NGAG GIS RKYEN BYAS NAS MTHO RIS KYI LUS LA BRTEN NAS SKYE BA PHA ROL DU 'GRUB PAR 'GYUR BA'O,,
gru.wylie: de la phyi ma brgyud de ston pa ltar du brjod na, de la gsum, skal ba dang bsod nams rab tshe 'di la 'grub pa dang, 'bring bar dor man ngag gi rgyun gyis 'grub pa dang, tha ma 'chi ka ma'i gdams ngag gis rkyen byas nas mtho ris kyi lus la brten nas skye ba pha rol du 'grub par 'gyur ba'o
gru.english: Here we will describe the latter method of instruction: where you go through a process.  Here there are three different parts.  Those of highest inner good, who possess the greatest amount of merit, reach the goal in this very life.  Those of middling good achieve it in the state between death and rebirth, through the continued influence of the advices received before.  And those of least inner good come to the goal in their future life, through using a higher-realm body, one that has come to them through the influence of practicing the advices at the moment of their death.

gru.acip: DE YANG THOG MAR PHA MA'I RTEN 'BREL DANG, RANG GI SEMS LA LAS KYI BAG CHAGS BSGOS PA'I MTHUS, MI LUS GRUB PA'I DUS SU DANG POR LTE BAR KUN 'DAR GYI CHA SHAS PHRA BRENG BA CIG CHAGS TE, DE LA AA NA HA DA ZHES BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: de yang thog mar pha ma'i rten 'brel dang, rang gi sems la las kyi bag chags bsgos pa'i mthus, mi lus grub pa'i dus su dang por lte bar kun 'dar gyi cha shas phra breng ba cig chags te, de la aa na ha da zhes bya'o
gru.english: Now at the beginning, as a human body first forms, something grows at the navel, due to the interaction of the parents and the power of karmic seeds infused previously in the mind.  This is a very fine, elongated section of the trembling channel, and it is given the name of anahada,

gru.acip: DA NI GNYIS PA LAM BSGOM PA RNAL 'BYOR GYI GNAD LA GNYIS, DE KHO NA NYID RIM GYIS STON PA DANG, DNGOS SU STON PA'O,, DANG PO LA GSUM, RAB TSE 'DI LA 'GRUB PA DANG, 'BRING BAR DO DANG, THA MA MTHO RIS KYI GNAD KYIS SO,,
gru.wylie: da ni gnyis pa lam bsgom pa rnal 'byor gyi gnad la gnyis, de kho na nyid rim gyis ston pa dang, dngos su ston pa'o,, dang po la gsum, rab tshe 'di la 'grub pa dang, 'bring bar do dang, tha ma mtho ris kyi gnad kyis so
gru.english: Now we will cover the second major section, which is the crucial point of deep practice--meditation upon the path.   We proceed in two stages: teaching suchness in steps, and teaching it directly.   The first of these has three parts of its own: the way of highest practitioners, who use the crucial opportunity of this life to achieve the goal; the way of medium practitioners, who use the crucial opportunity of the inbetween state to achieve the goal; and the way of lesser practitioners, who use the crucial opportunity of a higher rebirth to achieve the goal.

gru.acip: RNAL 'BYOR PA BRTZON 'GRUS RAB KYIS TSE 'DI LA DBU MA KHA 'BYED PA'I GDAMS NGAG BSGOMS PAS RLUNG DBU MAR 'DUS PAS PHYAG RGYA CHEN PO RTOGS PAR 'GYUR RO,,
gru.wylie: rnal 'byor pa brtson 'grus rab kyis tshe 'di la dbu ma kha 'byed pa'i gdams ngag bsgoms pas rlung dbu mar 'dus pas phyag rgya chen po rtogs par 'gyur ro
gru.english: A deep practitioner of highest effort can--in this very life--meditate on these instructions for opening the central channel, and thus bring the winds into this same channel; this then brings them to realize the great seal.

gru.acip: THA MA DROD TZAM SKYES SHING DU BA LA SOGS PA'I RTAGS MA MTHONG YANG TING NGE 'DZIN DANG MA BRAL NA, MTHO RIS KYI GNAD LA BRTEN NAS RKYEN BYAS NAS SKYE GNAS SU LUS 'GRUB PA'I DUS SU RLUNG 'DUS PAS BDAG PO'I RKYEN BYAS, SKYE GNAS PHYAG RGYA CHEN PO THOB PAR 'GYUR BA YIN NO,, RANG LHAG PAR GNAS PA'I DMIGS PA'I RIM PA'O,,
gru.wylie: tha ma drod tsam skyes shing du ba la sogs pa'i rtags ma mthong yang ting nge 'dzin dang ma bral na, mtho ris kyi gnad la brten nas rkyen byas nas skye gnas su lus 'grub pa'i dus su rlung 'dus pas bdag po'i rkyen byas, skye gnas phyag rgya chen po thob par 'gyur ba yin no,, rang lhag par gnas pa'i dmigs pa'i rim pa'o
gru.english: Those of lowest effort are able only to achieve inner warmth.  And even though they are unable to see the various signs of smoke and the rest, they do have the following experiences, if they are able to avoid losing their ability to concentrate single-pointedly: they take their next birth in one of the higher realms, and due to this crucial point--due to the way in which this acts as a special factor for them--they are able to bring the winds in at this particular stage, where they have managed to achieve a body in a new realm.  This then acts as an internal factor allowing them to achieve, in this new life, the realization of the great seal. This concludes the section on the stages by which you consecrate yourself.

gru.acip: DE NAS RANG GYI SNYING GA'I H'Um LAS 'OD ZER LCAGS KYU LTA BU KHA DOG DMAR NAG DBUGS PHYIR GTONG PA'I DUS SU, RANG GI KHA NAS HA SGRA DANG BCAS PA PHYIR BTANG ZHING, MU DR'A LA TZUM PA SBYIN SHES RAB KYIS SIB KYI SGRA DANG BCAS PAS, DBUGS NANG DU DRANGS PAS SHES RAB KYI LTE BA'I RDO RJE RTZE GSUM PA'I LTE BA NA PHAt SER PO, DBUGS LCAGS KYU'I RNAM PAS GYEN LA DRANGS PAS SHES RAB KYIS HA'I SGRA DANG BCAS PAS DBUGS PHYIR BTANG PA'I DUS SU, PHAt PHYUNG LA SGRUB PA POS SIB KYI SGRA DANG BCAS PA KHA'I NANG NAS BCUG STE,
gru.wylie: de nas rang gyi snying ga'i hUM las 'od zer lcags kyu lta bu kha dog dmar nag dbugs phyir gtong pa'i dus su, rang gi kha nas ha sgra dang bcas pa phyir btang zhing, mu drA la tsum pa sbyin shes rab kyis sib kyi sgra dang bcas pas, dbugs nang du drangs pas shes rab kyi lte ba'i rdo rje rtse gsum pa'i lte ba na phaT ser po, dbugs lcags kyu'i rnam pas gyen la drangs pas shes rab kyis ha'i sgra dang bcas pas dbugs phyir btang pa'i dus su, phaT phyung la sgrub pa pos sib kyi sgra dang bcas pa kha'i nang nas bcug ste
gru.english: Then as you exhale see a ray of light, colored dark crimson and shaped like a hook, coming out with your breath.  As you send it out make a ha sound as well. Then kiss your partner; the Woman of Wisdom draws the breath in with a sip sound.  See a yellow phet at the juncture of the diamond at Her navel, and pull it upwards with the hook-shaped breath.  When the Woman of Wisdom exhales with the sound of ha, the phet comes out of Her mouth, and the meditator pushes it into his own, with the sound of sip.

gru.acip: 'DA' KA MA'I GNAS 'DIS NI MTHO RIS ZHES BYA BA THAR PA'I GROGS SU 'GRO BA LAS, THAR PA KHO NA 'GRUB PA NI MA YIN ZHES GSUNGS NGO, ,TSE 'DI LA DBU MA CUNG ZAD KHA BYE BA RNAMS BAR DO NYID DU PHYAG RGYA CHEN PO 'GRUB PAR 'GYUR BA YIN NO, GNAD KYI MAN NGAG LA BRTEN NAS RIM GYIS CHOS KYI DBYINGS RTOGS PA'I THABS BSTAN ZIN TO,,
gru.wylie: 'da' ka ma'i gnas 'dis ni mtho ris zhes bya ba thar pa'i grogs su 'gro ba las, thar pa kho na 'grub pa ni ma yin zhes gsungs ngo, ,tshe 'di la dbu ma cung zad kha bye ba rnams bar do nyid du phyag rgya chen po 'grub par 'gyur ba yin no, gnad kyi man ngag la brten nas rim gyis chos kyi dbyings rtogs pa'i thabs bstan zin to
gru.english: This crucial point, to be practiced at the moment of death, is said to refer to "higher births"; the idea being that it functions to aid you in reaching freedom, rather than leading itself to this goal.  Those who are able to open the central channel just a bit in this life achieve the realization of the great seal only during the inbetween state. This concludes our presentation of the method for perceiving ultimate reality through a successive process, by utilizing the advices on the crucial points.

gru.acip: DPER NA DU BA NI ME'I SNGON ROL NAS GRUB PA'ANG MA YIN TE, ME LAS MA GTOGS PA GZHAN 'ONGS PA'ANG MA YIN LA, MI 'GAG PAR GNAS P'ANG MA YIN KYANG, DU BA NI ME LAS BYUNG BZHIN DER 'GAGS PAS, DU BA RTAG TU ME DANG 'BREL BAS SO,,
gru.wylie: dper na du ba ni me'i sngon rol nas grub pa'ang ma yin te, me las ma gtogs pa gzhan 'ongs pa'ang ma yin la, mi 'gag par gnas pAng ma yin kyang, du ba ni me las byung bzhin der 'gags pas, du ba rtag tu me dang 'brel bas so
gru.english: Smoke, for example, is not something that occurs before the fire does.  It neither arises from something other than fire, nor does it stay without ever stopping.  Smoke comes from fire and stops with it, and so smoke is always related to fire.

gru.acip: DE BZHIN DU DKAR PO LA SOGS PA'I RTOG PA YANG SKYE MED LAS, SNGON ROL DU GRUB PA YANG MA YIN LA, MI 'GAG PAR GNAS PA'ANG MA YIN LA, 'ON KYANG SKYE MED LAS BYUNG ZHING DER THIM PAS, SKYE MED DANG RGYUN DU 'BREL BA YIN NO,
gru.wylie: de bzhin du dkar po la sogs pa'i rtog pa yang skye med las, sngon rol du grub pa yang ma yin la, mi 'gag par gnas pa'ang ma yin la, 'on kyang skye med las byung zhing der thim pas, skye med dang rgyun du 'brel ba yin no
gru.english: The thought of whiteness and such is the same.  It is not something that has arisen before, from something other than the state where nothing starts; nor is it something which stays without ever stopping.  Rather, it occurs out of the state where nothing starts, and dissolves back into this state.  As such, it is constantly related to the state where nothing starts.

gru.acip: PHYI ROL GYI SDE TSAN DRUG GYUR PA LAS THIG LE DRUG TU 'GYUR TE, SDE TSAN RE RE THIG LE RE RE 'GYUR RO,, DE DAG GI THIG LE GNYIS GNYIS LAS, AE'I LOGS RE RE GRUB PAS, AE GRU GSUM SHES RAB GYI RANG BZHIN GRUB STE, DE'I NANG NA WAm GNYIS MED KYI TSUL DU GNAS SO,, [ALL WAMS HERE S/H CRESCENT]
gru.wylie: phyi rol gyi sde tshan drug gyur pa las thig le drug tu 'gyur te, sde tshan re re thig le re re 'gyur ro,, de dag gi thig le gnyis gnyis las, ae'i logs re re grub pas, ae gru gsum shes rab gyi rang bzhin grub ste, de'i nang na waM gnyis med kyi tshul du gnas so,, [all wams here s/h crescent]
gru.english: The six groups of the outside rows then transform into six drops, each group becoming a drop.  Each pair of the six becomes an angle of the e syllable.  The e with its three angles then becomes the nature of wisdom; the wam resides within it, indivisible.

whole_word_matches.context: thig le gnyis gnyis las, ae'i logs re re grub pas, ae gru gsum shes rab gyi rang bzhin grub ste, de'i nang na wa

gru.acip: DE LTAR PHYI NANG GI RIM PA GNYIS KYI AE WAm SO SOR 'GRUB LA GZHAN SDE TSAN BRGYAD THIG LE BCU A'A LI BCU GNYIS TE, RIM PA GNYIS KYI AE WAm GNYIS KA THUN MONG DU 'GRUB GSUNG,
gru.wylie: de ltar phyi nang gi rim pa gnyis kyi ae waM so sor 'grub la gzhan sde tshan brgyad thig le bcu a'a li bcu gnyis te, rim pa gnyis kyi ae waM gnyis ka thun mong du 'grub gsung
gru.english: Thus there are two evam's that form, individually, from the inner and outer rows.  Thus it is that others say that the eight groups, and the ten small circles, and the twelve vowels turn to a common syllable, to the two evam's of the two rows.

gru.acip: DE NYID LA , AE YI CHA BYAD BZANG PO GANG, ,DBUS SU WA GYES RNAM PAR BRGYAN, ,ZHES SO, DE YANG RKYANG MA'I NUS PAS AE 'GRUB LA, ,RO MA'I NUS PAS WAm 'GRUB STE RTZA GNYIS KYANG GNYIS MED DU 'GYUR TE, RDO RJE'I SKYIL KRUNG RDZOGS SANGS RGYAS, ,ZHES GSUNGS SO,,
gru.wylie: de nyid la , ae yi cha byad bzang po gang, ,dbus su wa gyes rnam par brgyan, ,zhes so, de yang rkyang ma'i nus pas ae 'grub la, ,ro ma'i nus pas waM 'grub ste rtsa gnyis kyang gnyis med du 'gyur te, rdo rje'i skyil krung rdzogs sangs rgyas, ,zhes gsungs so
gru.english: It is to the same point that they say, This excellent part of the e Is bedecked in the center with vam. The e incidentally comes about through the power of the solitary channel, while the warn comes about through the power of the channel of taste.  These two channels then are also indivisible, and thus the line that goes "The diamond posture is total enlightenment."

gru.acip: DE LTAR GYUR PA DANG, GDOD NAS DANGS SHING THOGS PA MED PA'I RTZA GRUB NAS DES PRA SE NA LTA BU'I SO DANG SEN MO LA SOGS PA SKYED PAR BYED GSUNG NGO, ,DE DAG GIS 'BRAS BU MYA NGAN LAS 'DAS PA'I GNAD BSTAN ZIN TO,
gru.wylie: de ltar gyur pa dang, gdod nas dangs shing thogs pa med pa'i rtsa grub nas des pra se na lta bu'i so dang sen mo la sogs pa skyed par byed gsung ngo, ,de dag gis 'bras bu mya ngan las 'das pa'i gnad bstan zin to
gru.english: You become like that; and it's said as well that--because you have attained those channels which have been pure essence and ineffable since before time--then you begin to grow crystalline teeth, and fingernails, and all the rest. With this we have completed the crucial point of the ultimate goal, or nirvana.

gru.acip: DE LA BTUD CING BRTEN PAS YON TAN CI ZHIG 'BYUNG BA NI, RDO RJE 'CHANG DANG MTSUNGS PA'I BLA MA (GANG) YIN PA DE (LA) BTUD CING (BRTEN NA,) GANG ZAG KHYAD PAR CAN GYI SLOB MA LA CHOS SKU, LONGS SKU, SPRUL SKU STE (SKU GSUM BDE BA BA CHE)N PO DE NYID, GRUB PA BRGYAD DANG, ZHI RGYAS SOGS (THUN MONG) GI (DNGOS GRUB DANG BCAS) PA DUS (SKAD CIG) STE SNYIGS MA'I TSE THUNG GCIG (LA STZOL) BAR (MDZAD) PA YIN NO,,
gru.wylie: de la btud cing brten pas yon tan ci zhig 'byung ba ni, rdo rje 'chang dang mtshungs pa'i bla ma (gang) yin pa de (la) btud cing (brten na,) gang zag khyad par can gyi slob ma la chos sku, longs sku, sprul sku ste (sku gsum bde ba ba che)n po de nyid, grub pa brgyad dang, zhi rgyas sogs (thun mong) gi (dngos grub dang bcas) pa dus (skad cig) ste snyigs ma'i tshe thung gcig (la stsol) bar (mdzad) pa yin no
gru.english: And what good qualities are born in us when we do bow to our Lama in this way?  Suppose that I do bow and surrender myself to You, meaning to that Lama of mine who is equal to the Keeper of the Diamond.  Then I know that, if I prove to be a disciple who is a truly exceptional person, I shall be granted--in but a single moment of time (meaning, in but one of those brief human lifetimes here in the days of darkness)--that single ecstasy of the three holy forms: the holy body of the Dharma; the holy body of enjoyment; and the holy body of emanation.  And along with this I shall be granted all the goals that are shared as well, including things like the eight attainments, as well as the capacity to act in the modes of peace, prosperity, and the rest.

gru.acip: STZOL TSUL NI, (YID BZHIN) GYI (NOR) BU LA GSOL BA BTABS PAS DGOS 'DOD 'BYUNG BA DE BZHIN DU, DE DANG 'DRA BA'I BLA MA YANG BSTEN CING MCHOD NA, YID LA ('DOD DGU'I MCHOG STZOL) BA STE CI 'DOD PA'I DNGOS GRUB STER RO, ,DGU NI MANG TSIG GO
gru.wylie: stsol tshul ni, (yid bzhin) gyi (nor) bu la gsol ba btabs pas dgos 'dod 'byung ba de bzhin du, de dang 'dra ba'i bla ma yang bsten cing mchod na, yid la ('dod dgu'i mchog stsol) ba ste ci 'dod pa'i dngos grub ster ro, ,dgu ni mang tshig go
gru.english: Just how are these goals granted?  When you make supplication to a gem which fulfills your wishes, then it grants you all your dreams.  If I take myself to a Lama who resembles such a jewel, and make offerings to Them, then They grant the highest of all the many dreams that I may have in my heart--meaning that They provide me with whatever spiritual goals I may aspire to.  The Tibetan word gu literally means nine, but it is used here in the verse to mean many.

gru.acip: 'O NA SLOB MA RNAMS KYI RGYAN DU JI LTAR 'GRO ZHE NA, CHOS KYI (SKAL) BA (BZANG) PO DANG LDAN PA'I (SLOB MA) RNAMS KYI GNAS SKABS (PHAN) PA DANG MTHAR THUG (BDE BA MA LUS BSGRUB) PAR BYED (NUS PA'I THABS) KYI (MCHOG) DE DANG 'DRA BA GZHAN MED PAS NA, (GNYIS PA DANG BRAL BA) STE DE NYID KYIS SO,,
gru.wylie: 'o na slob ma rnams kyi rgyan du ji ltar 'gro zhe na, chos kyi (skal) ba (bzang) po dang ldan pa'i (slob ma) rnams kyi gnas skabs (phan) pa dang mthar thug (bde ba ma lus bsgrub) par byed (nus pa'i thabs) kyi (mchog) de dang 'dra ba gzhan med pas na, (gnyis pa dang bral ba) ste de nyid kyis so
gru.english: "Well then," you may ask, "just how does this work function as an ornament for disciples?"  The fact is that there is nothing else like this particular method, this highest means of all, for disciples who are possessed of good fortune, or capacity for the teachings of the Dharma.  It is a way for them to reach all that is good in the immediate sense, and all forms of ultimate happiness as well.  Given the very fact that it is the highest means, we can say that there is nothing which can compare with it.

gru.acip: DE YANG RANG BLOS SBYAR BA TZAM MA YIN TE, RGYAL BAS GSUNGS PA'I (MDO) DANG, (RGYUD) SDE RNAMS DANG, 'PHAGS BOD KYI MKHAS GRUB DU MA'I (MAN NGAG) SNA TSOGS KYI (PAD TSAL LAS 'ONGS PA,) STE DE DAG LA BRTEN NAS RTZOM PA'I PHYIR ZHES SO,,
gru.wylie: de yang rang blos sbyar ba tsam ma yin te, rgyal bas gsungs pa'i (mdo) dang, (rgyud) sde rnams dang, 'phags bod kyi mkhas grub du ma'i (man ngag) sna tshogs kyi (pad tshal las 'ongs pa,) ste de dag la brten nas rtsom pa'i phyir zhes so
gru.english: And this instruction is in no way something that the author has just made up by themselves.  Rather, says the text, it has come from the lotus garden of the open and secret teachings spoken by the victorious Buddha, and from the various advices written by a great number of wise and accomplished masters from the Land of the Realized, India, and from Tibet as well.  The work has "come" from these sources in the sense that it was composed by someone relying upon these sources. Why We Need to Take Ourselves to a Lama

gru.acip: GNYIS PA BSHAD PA NYID NYE BAR DGOD PA LA GNYIS, BLA MA BSTEN DGOS PA'I RGYU MTSAN LUNG GIS BSGRUBS PA DANG, BSTEN THABS KYI CHO GA'I KHYAD PAR BSHAD PA'O,,
gru.wylie: gnyis pa bshad pa nyid nye bar dgod pa la gnyis, bla ma bsten dgos pa'i rgyu mtshan lung gis bsgrubs pa dang, bsten thabs kyi cho ga'i khyad par bshad pa'o
gru.english: Here secondly is our presentation of the explanation itself, which proceeds in two steps.  First we use scriptural authority to demonstrate why it is necessary to take ourselves to a Lama.  And then we explain the details of the ritual one can actually use to take oneself to the Lama.

gru.acip: DANG PO NI, BLA MA BSTEN DGOS PA'I (RGYU MTSAN) LUNG GIS 'GRUB PA (DE LTAR NA,) MDO SNGAGS KYI (LAM GYI GNAD TSANG BA'I BLA MA'I RNAL 'BYOR) TE SGRUB THABS (BSGOM PA NI, DAL 'BYOR LA SNYING PO LEN PA'I THABS MCHOG TU GYUR BA YIN PAS) 'OG TU 'CHAD PA'I CHO GA ('DI LTAR NYAMS SU BLANG BAR BYA'O,) ,ZHES SO,,
gru.wylie: dang po ni, bla ma bsten dgos pa'i (rgyu mtshan) lung gis 'grub pa (de ltar na,) mdo sngags kyi (lam gyi gnad tshang ba'i bla ma'i rnal 'byor) te sgrub thabs (bsgom pa ni, dal 'byor la snying po len pa'i thabs mchog tu gyur ba yin pas) 'og tu 'chad pa'i cho ga ('di ltar nyams su blang bar bya'o,) ,zhes so
gru.english: Here is the first.  Thus we have described, proving our point through scriptural authority, why--the reason why--we must take ourselves to our Lama.  Thus, undertaking a ritual for reaching our Angel, a deep practice of the Lama--a version of this practice which includes all the crucial points of the path of both the open and secret teachings--is the highest way of getting the very essence out of the leisure and opportunity we have found in this life.  As such, says the text, we should do this practice--that is, the ritual which we shall describe in the sections to come--as follows. Preparing our Motivation

gru.acip: GDONG DNGOS DANG SBAR MO BZHIS 'DZIN PA SOGS GDONG GI BYA BA BYED NUS PAS NA, (GDONG LNGA) PA STE SENGGE BRGYAD KYIS BTEGS CING, GZI 'OD ('BAR BA'I RIN CHEN) TE RIN PO CHE LAS GRUB PA'I (KHRI) PHUN SUM TSOGS PA'I (STENG) DU, (CHU SKYES) TE PADMA DANG,
gru.wylie: gdong dngos dang sbar mo bzhis 'dzin pa sogs gdong gi bya ba byed nus pas na, (gdong lnga) pa ste sengge brgyad kyis btegs cing, gzi 'od ('bar ba'i rin chen) te rin po che las grub pa'i (khri) phun sum tshogs pa'i (steng) du, (chu skyes) te padma dang
gru.english: Atop the tree is an excellent throne of magnificent, sparkling jewels; that is, a throne carved itself out of gemstone.  The throne is held aloft by eight lions--which are referred to in the original Tibetan with the poetic name of "beasts of the five faces."  The point here is that they are supporting the throne for example both with their head and with their four paws, which are thus performing the same function as the head.  This throne is set with cushions, beginning with one made of a lotus, which in the original Tibetan is again referred to with a poeticism: the child of the lake.

gru.acip: SPYI BOR RNAM PAR SNANG MDZAD CES SOGS 'BYUNG BA LTAR RNAM SNANG SPYI BOR 'GOD PA SOGS BYAS TE, GZUGS PHUNG RNAM SNANG, DE BZHIN DU TSOR PHUNG RIN 'BYUNG, 'DU SHES 'OD DPAG MED, 'DU BYED DON GRUB, RNAM SHES KYI PHUNG PO MI BSKYOD PA STE
gru.wylie: spyi bor rnam par snang mdzad ces sogs 'byung ba ltar rnam snang spyi bor 'god pa sogs byas te, gzugs phung rnam snang, de bzhin du tshor phung rin 'byung, 'du shes 'od dpag med, 'du byed don grub, rnam shes kyi phung po mi bskyod pa ste
gru.english: We see for example references that mention how "the Angel of Various Appearances is at the tip of Their head"; following these, we for example place the Angel of Appearances at the tip of the head, and so on.  Our Lama's heap of form then is the Angel of Appearances; Their heap of feelings is the Angel named "Jewels"; Their heap of discrimination is Limitless Light; Their heap of other factors is Attainment; and Their heap of consciousness is Unshakable.

gru.acip: YE SHES PA DE RNAMS DAM TSIG PA GTZO 'KHOR SO SO LA (DBYER MED) PAR THIM PAS, JI SRID DGOS PA MA GRUB PA DE SRID DU (BRTAN PAR GYUR) NAS BZHUGS ZHES PA'O,,
gru.wylie: ye shes pa de rnams dam tshig pa gtso 'khor so so la (dbyer med) par thim pas, ji srid dgos pa ma grub pa de srid du (brtan par gyur) nas bzhugs zhes pa'o
gru.english: These Beings of Wisdom are drawn in to melt, indivisibly, into the corresponding Beings of Pledge, both the principal one and Their retinue.  And the text is saying that They stay there then perfectly firm, until such time as the goal of Their coming is achieved.

gru.acip: LHA PHO'I RNAM PAR BSTAN NAS RIG 'DZIN SGRUB PA PO LA DNGOS GRUB STER BA'I (DPA' BO) DANG, LHA MO'I RNAM PAR BSTAN NAS NAM MKHA' NAS DAG PA'I ZHING SOGS LA 'GRO BA DANG 'ONG BA'I BYA BA BYED PA'I (MKHA' 'GRO) MA RNAMS DANG,
gru.wylie: lha pho'i rnam par bstan nas rig 'dzin sgrub pa po la dngos grub ster ba'i (dpa' bo) dang, lha mo'i rnam par bstan nas nam mkha' nas dag pa'i zhing sogs la 'gro ba dang 'ong ba'i bya ba byed pa'i (mkha' 'gro) ma rnams dang
gru.english: With them as well are the Warriors, meaning Angels who show Themselves in male form, and who grant attainments to practitioners who are holders of sacred knowledge; in addition to Their Angels, referring to Angels who show Themselves in female form, and who engage in coming and going from the sky to realms of purity and the like.

gru.acip: DANG PO NI, DE YANG (MGON PO KLU SGRUB GYI RIM LNGAR, ,MCHOD PA THAMS CAD RNAM SPANGS NAS, ,BLA MA MCHOD PA YANG DAG BRTZAMS, ,DE MNYES PAS NI KUN MKHYEN GYI, ,YE SHES MCHOG NI THOB PAR 'GYUR,)
gru.wylie: dang po ni, de yang (mgon po klu sgrub gyi rim lngar, ,mchod pa thams cad rnam spangs nas, ,bla ma mchod pa yang dag brtsams, ,de mnyes pas ni kun mkhyen gyi, ,ye shes mchog ni thob par 'gyur,)
gru.english: Here is the first.  Think then upon the words of our Protector, Nagarjuna, who in His book on the five stages has said, Abandon every other kind of offering, And devote yourself completely To making offerings to your Lama. The act of pleasing your Lama Brings you to the attainment Of the highest form of wisdom.

gru.acip: 'O NA, DE LA 'DUD PAS PHAN YON CI ZHIG 'BYUNG ZHE NA, SNGAR BSHAD PA'I BLA MA (GANG GI THUGS RJES,) BRTZON 'GRUS SHIN TU 'BAR BA RIN PO CHE LTA BU'I GANG ZAG KHYAD PAR CAN LA, THUN MONG GI DNGOS GRUB STZOL BAR MA ZAD, GTAN DU 'GYUR MED (BDE BA CHEN PO'I DBYINGS) TE GNAS CHOS SKU SOGS (SKU GSUM) GYI (GO 'PHANG MCHOG KYANG SKAD CIG) STE SNYIGS DUS KYI TSE CIG (LA STZOL) BAR (MDZAD) PA YIN NO,,
gru.wylie: 'o na, de la 'dud pas phan yon ci zhig 'byung zhe na, sngar bshad pa'i bla ma (gang gi thugs rjes,) brtson 'grus shin tu 'bar ba rin po che lta bu'i gang zag khyad par can la, thun mong gi dngos grub stsol bar ma zad, gtan du 'gyur med (bde ba chen po'i dbyings) te gnas chos sku sogs (sku gsum) gyi (go 'phang mchog kyang skad cig) ste snyigs dus kyi tshe cig (la stsol) bar (mdzad) pa yin no
gru.english: "If we do bow to our Lama's feet," you may ask, "what benefits do we derive by doing so?"   The kind of Lama described above grants, in compassion, the shared spiritual attainments to an exceptional kind of person: to a person who is themselves like a precious jewel, blazing forth in their efforts at spiritual practice.  But that's not all.  This Lama grants to them even entrance to the realm of eternal and immutable bliss--which is to say, the ultimate state, of all three bodies: that place where they possess the holy body of the Dharma and so on.  And our Lama brings this to us in a single moment; which is to say, in but a single human life here in the days of darkness.

gru.acip: CI 'DOD KYI DNGOS GRUB STZOL BA DE BZHIN DU, SNGAR BSHAD PA'I TSAD LDAN GYI BLA MA DE TSUL BZHIN BSTEN PAS, GNAS SKABS MNGON MTHO'I BDE BA DANG, MTHAR THUG SANGS RGYAS NYID STZOL BA'I PHYIR RO, ,ZHES BYA'O,,
gru.wylie: ci 'dod kyi dngos grub stsol ba de bzhin du, sngar bshad pa'i tshad ldan gyi bla ma de tshul bzhin bsten pas, gnas skabs mngon mtho'i bde ba dang, mthar thug sangs rgyas nyid stsol ba'i phyir ro, ,zhes bya'o
gru.english: The jewel will then grant our every wish.  Suppose now that, in a similar way, we take ourselves to a qualified Lama of the kind we've described here earlier.  They will then grant us, says the text, the short-term goal of the happiness found in one of the higher rebirths, and the ultimate goal of nothing less than enlightenment itself.

gru.acip: DANG PO PHYI'I MCHOD PA LA YANG LNGA, CHU BZHI, NYER LNGA ROL MO DANG BCAS PA, MAndAL SOGS DANG, SGRUB PA'I MCHOD PA ZHAR BYUNG DANG BCAS PA BSHAD PA'O,,
gru.wylie: dang po phyi'i mchod pa la yang lnga, chu bzhi, nyer lnga rol mo dang bcas pa, maNDal sogs dang, sgrub pa'i mchod pa zhar byung dang bcas pa bshad pa'o
gru.english: The first of these, the outer offering, will be explained itself in five different parts: the four waters; the five enjoyments of the senses, along with music; the mandala and the rest; and the offering of our practice, together with an incidental section.

gru.acip: DANG PO CHU BZHI NI, BKOD LEGS SOGS RKANG PA GNYIS TE, BSHAMS TSUL GYI (BKOD) PA (LEGS) SHING MDZES PA DANG, RGYU GSER SOGS (RIN CHEN) SNA TSOGS LAS GRUB CING, DE LAS ('OD 'BAR) ZHING 'KHYUG PA'I (SNOD YANGS) PA'I NAD THAMS CAD (LAS) 'BYUNG BA'I SKYON (DAG BYED) KYI (BDUD RTZI'I CHU BZHI) STE, MCHOD YON, ZHABS BSIL, ZHAL BSIL, BSANG GTOR RNAMS YIN LA,
gru.wylie: dang po chu bzhi ni, bkod legs sogs rkang pa gnyis te, bshams tshul gyi (bkod) pa (legs) shing mdzes pa dang, rgyu gser sogs (rin chen) sna tshogs las grub cing, de las ('od 'bar) zhing 'khyug pa'i (snod yangs) pa'i nad thams cad (las) 'byung ba'i skyon (dag byed) kyi (bdud rtsi'i chu bzhi) ste, mchod yon, zhabs bsil, zhal bsil, bsang gtor rnams yin la
gru.english: Here first then are the four waters, which are presented in the four lines that begin with "Here is a vase of sparkling jewels..."  Here then is a broad vase made of jewels and other precious substances--gold and the like--which is arranged or set forth in perfect symmetry and beauty.
